# The Holy Service

## By the Divine Rabbi, our teacher and master, Rabbi Meir ibn Gabbai, may his memory be for a blessing in the world to come <note>original: "zalla-h," an acronym for "Zikhrono Livrakha Le-Hayyei Ha-Olam Ha-Ba." Meir ibn Gabbai (born 1480) was one of the most important systematizers of the Kabbalah before the Safed school.</note>

**Comprising four parts that guide a person in the holy service desired by Him, blessed be He, and they are:**
**The Part on Unity, the Part on Service, the Part on the Ultimate Purpose, and the Part on the Secrets of the Torah.**

How well-prepared a person becomes, how beautiful in his service, when he plants in the realms above and below. Through his efforts, he finds salvation and strength, stretching out his hands toward the Tree of Life <note>A central symbol in the Kabbalah representing the divine emanations</note> and all that lives forever. And not only this, but he provides a refuge for his embittered soul and mixes its sweetness from the taste of his palm at the windows of life. Following the path, you shall tread upon the swords of rest and exalt it, returning to the place where his tent was at the beginning. For the wise man who hears these books of <term>Kabbalah</term> <note>The ancient tradition of Jewish mystical interpretation of the Bible</note>, he has prepared, included, and praised them without end. For the written word brings all things near—a precious treasure and a necklace for those of great deeds. He shall inherit and possess wealth and strength in the ways of the holy service within the innermost parts of his people above and higher still; he shall rise above all. No eye has seen it beside You, and his remnant is the kindness of the Lord. Therefore, let the wise and the rulers, those who know knowledge and understand science, run to it. They shall add strength to stand before the King, the King of the Universe. For
**The Holy Service** is more precious to them than silver and gold, allowing them to enjoy the radiance of the Divine Presence in its strength, and to leave behind the illumination of the stories of the author, Rabbi Simeon bar Yochai <note>The traditional author of the Zohar, the foundational work of Kabbalah</note> and his colleagues, of blessed memory. Therefore, let the silver be increased and cut, and let them go in strength to go to the place which the Lord shall choose. From day to day, from Sabbath to Sabbath, and from month to month, to bow down before the Lord and to perform the Holy Service.

# In the Secret
# Of Holiness

**Behold**, through the vitality of this soul which our Creator on high made for us—emanating it from the radiance and brilliance of His glory, and comprised of the splendor of the supernal luminaries—the "house of the pathways" of the <term>Supernal Wisdom</term><note>Chokhmah: the first spark of divine intellect</note> was built. It was hewn from the "source of Understanding," and from there, what is called the "source of Knowledge" was carved out. It was bound by the regulation of the "Kindness of Intellect," deepening with "Strength," and Graciousness. In the "Secret of Unity," it returns through wondrous, awesome perfections in the "Beauty of Rest." 

Standing before the King, the Lord of Hosts, it gathered through their righteousness a victory in the thick darkness. The meditation of the "End of Fate" and the "Splendor" were prepared, and the foundations were perfected from the lower realms, just as the soul is comprised of the supernal arrangement. It longs to return—*who will give me back the months of old* <note>original: "מי יתנני כירחי קדם" - a reference to Job 29:2</note> as in its beginning, when the "Fate of Change" was upon its head. It moves constantly in its orbits toward the place where its portion was at the start; for its nature necessitates this, as is the nature of every thing that yearns and longs to go to a place like itself. 

The wise man possesses a toil that hovers while being deep in certain matters that revolved and left the soul in its supernal palace. To return Kindness and all absolute things to their absolute state, and to bring all goodness into our midst through supernal movement—this is the "advised counsel": to see oneself as a stranger in a foreign land. To close the gates of sin through righteousness, seeking the good at one's window, with Kindness spread before him. The act of his service moves constantly toward his ultimate purpose, digging for its place and to rest in its place. Linked to this is the hint: *as a bird that wanders from her nest, so is a man who wanders from his place.* <note>Proverbs 27:8</note> The intent is that as a winged bird, when it builds its nest as a row of its desire, Kindness and its young ones nest there. And see that the bird, when it wanders from its nest, longs to lodge and moves to rest with its wings—so too is our purity above in the "Fate of the Soul."

<margin>2</margin>
Thus, Kindness is found within this lamp, yet it wanders from its place and its degree, which is in the upper worlds. It must always move to rest upon the "Almighty." The sages of the <term>Kastris</term><note>Likely a reference to a specific group of kabbalistic commentators or a corrupted geographical name</note> said: "This bird is <term>Binah</term><note>Understanding</note>." It wanders from its nest, Jerusalem. Thus, this is the Holy One, blessed be He, wandering from His place... as it is written: "Precious is the sound of My heavens and His glory." He desired her and showed her grace. It concludes: "Like a stranger in the land," longing to rest in his place, for the cup shall not depart from himself... and the lack will be filled when the fortress of the heart and Israel are remembered. And from the "Giving," he supports with the "Gates of the Eternal World"... the Hebrews rose to their freedom. 

The soul has the power to awaken the supernal lights while it is situated in the lower realms... it awakens the supernal luminary toward it, just as it was when it dwelt there. And David... strove all his days in the <term>Tikkun</term><note>Rectification or spiritual repair</note> of our essence in "Fate," and he acted for the sake of the Name, saying: *I am a stranger in the land; hide not Your commandments from me.* <note>Psalm 119:19</note>

And he preceded this by explaining well, saying: *Deal bountifully with Your servant, that I may live and keep Your word.* <note>Psalm 119:17</note> Its meaning is the yearning to act there and to reveal to us that all his desire is from Him, and that he should not turn to another, nor should he ache or long for his own needs at all. For all our intention should be for the "needs of the High One," for such is the way of the Perfect Good. Therefore he prioritized and returned to say: *Deal bountifully with Your servant.* And it is written: "And He did good to his soul to have mercy on him," as one who detaches from your bonds to keep Your word. This is the "bounty"—I do not ask of You for my service for any other reason, such as a reward of a cup or this and that. If we were lowly people, we would consider the reward... but his intention was to rectify and to do the "Good," for he knew that this was the goal. And the heavens returned, for to it all goals are completed... and he would not delve into personal needs, nor would he rule for himself. The responsibility of "ruling" toward this Rectification is the purpose of the Torah and the Commandments. The depths of the Torah’s intention are based on this, as he said: *Open my eyes, that I may behold wondrous things out of Your law.* <note>original: "גל עיני ואביטה נפלאות מתורתך" - Psalm 119:18</note> For this is what awakens the King to serve the ultimate goal... 

He said "Open my eyes," which is a language of "revealing" secrets, as we have written. For the soul, while it is in the upper worlds, busies itself with its preparation and walks in its enlightenment, for the foundation is revealed. Its vision is the "song of the commandments" according to its lot, with clear knowledge and the perception of truths.

<margin>3</margin>
As they said in the "Chapter of the Ascents": "An angel speaks over his head, and he is open-eyed and looks from one end of the world to the other." He perceives through the veil that he is clothed in... and from within it, he breathes and looks... and the foundation, which is from one end of the world to the other, is the beginning of thought. Its end stands upon the deeds of the Torah and the wondrous reasons. As they said: "And they teach him the entire Torah," as it is said: "And he taught me and said to me, let your heart hold fast my words." And from the beginning, he is made to forget all that he saw and knew and attained. And it says there: "Once he comes out into the air of the world, an angel comes and strikes him on his mouth, making him forget the entire Torah." This is for a reason I shall explain in this book regarding the term "learning." Therefore, he said that He should "open his eyes"—those which were opened during his formation—to look at the "Good Wonders" which he once knew and attained, but which were hidden from him. He said "And I shall behold," meaning to remember and attain them so they are not forgotten again. The "Good" is not found except from above to below. This was necessary... to rectify and perform the "Holy," for there is no other way. For the "Wonders of our Torah," the "Gates of the Torah," and their reasons—which are the internal Wisdom—are necessary for the Rectification, so that the King may stand upon the Supernal Will, which is the **Unity**, as will be clarified.

<summary>This preface explores the soul's divine origins in the Sefirot and its subsequent "wandering" in the physical world, using the metaphor of a bird away from its nest. It explains that the purpose of the Torah and commandments is "Tikkun" (rectification) to return the soul to its original state of knowing the divine secrets it forgot at birth.</summary>

# The Kindnesses of the Lord

I shall mention the kindnesses of the Lord and the praises of the Lord, according to all that the Lord has bestowed upon us, and the great goodness toward the House of Israel which He bestowed upon them according to His mercies and according to the multitude of His kindnesses <note>original: "חסדי ה' אזכיר... כרחמיו וכרוב חסדיו" - an adaptation of Isaiah 63:7</note>. His abundant kindness remains with His people Israel; in every generation they have neither hungered nor thirsted from famine. In His love and His pity, He redeemed them, along with the seed of Isaac and all its strengths. 

Even so, when they were in the land of their enemies, He did not despise them nor loathe them to destroy them or break His covenant with them, for He is the Lord their God. In all their affliction, He was afflicted, and in every time of trouble, the Lord was with them. Even when He appointed evil upon us, was it not from there that freedom was fortified? From this, it shall be known and made known forever, for understanding and for knowledge, to know and understand all the days of the world and for generations to come. 

He established for us wise shepherds, despite the "Attribute of Judgment" <note>the divine quality of strict justice</note>, to lead the congregation of the Lord as a man speaks face to face, for the sake of the Lord and His <term>Shekhinah</term><note>The Divine Presence, often viewed in Kabbalah as the feminine aspect of God</note>. They continued to grow in wisdom; their lips were a healing for the eyes. Their refined perspectives were exhausted by the weak iron tools of those who lacked strength. They came prepared without money to the open dwellings of those who stood by their banners. 

Therefore, they composed books, refined by the presence of the Holy. These works included them in such a beautiful order that it glorified them, adding even more. Like the sun in its might, they straightened the paths and simplified the <term>Kulus</term><note>likely referring to the quill or the style of writing</note> to teach the weary through their good taste, revealing their foundations and secrets. These are sweet, living waters, and their value is immeasurable. Their voice goes out from one end of the world to the other; their voice is heard outside, like the sand within a room. All of them—even the infants and sucklings—seek to investigate the greatest depths and hidden treasures. And even though children and youths follow after the great ones, the words of my reasoning are engraved here. Stay with me, for in this garden nothing was wasted, for it is a precious possession to make them wise, providing another way to reach their goal, to fence in our breaches, to tell of our wonders, to strengthen our Torah, and to understand our laws. May He establish our help. 

And blessed be the Lord, the God of Israel, who has not left us without a redeemer this day: this author, who speaks peace. He is like a "button and a flower" <note>original: "כפתור ופרח" - an idiom meaning something exquisite or perfect</note>, returning our Holy Torah to its banner, clear and beautiful. He ceased the curse and made the deed heard. His words were received, opened, and prophesied like the crown of the beauty of the wise. 

Behold their arguments, traced from the remnants of our survivors, especially in his words. His hand is sufficient for him, as is his wisdom. It is a wonder, like a priest to the heart, to remember and to know. The flow of the fountain appears in its purity. With wisdom, the words are a key and an opening for the pure emanation, and for the holy accompaniment and the Tablet of Commandments. It is like a sparkling and brightening sapphire. To be on the path of grace with the Lord, its master, in the place of the Lord in the world, like the sea of excellence. He also rewarded and bestowed how to become wise through the beauty of <term>Pilpul</term><note>A method of talmudic study through intense conceptual analysis and hair-splitting logic</note>. 

Praises were offered in the place of holiness, to diminish or increase the wine of excellence, to teach by them His ways for the purity of understanding and for His kingdom. For the sake of our service, this book is a "necessity from on high." Every living being is its foundation. Even the investigator will know all their intentions, for his intention is with the Lord and our Holy Torah—the ultimate purpose of the clarification and their order. No one shall disagree with him regarding merit or any iniquities. 

A man has handed it over, a strong possession. He can prevail and ascend to the highest level, to establish the kingdom in agreement, in the heights of the excellence of the words of the press and the scribes, and the death of holiness <unclear>staining obscures several words</unclear>. This matter shall prevail further and be renewed, to elevate the holiness of the sanctuary with its emanation. May it be placed in the site of holiness and purity, to be in the ritual bath of the Supernal Light. 

This book is the ultimate structure, like a scroll of the Torah for training, and a dream, and the southern order for his house. Those who bring the <term>Kavanot</term><note>Spiritual intentions or meditations during prayer or performance of a commandment</note> and the agreement in the high excellence of the great and the bitter, the portion for all the "great and strong hand," and the ladders and the openings which he made before the eyes of all Israel. He wrote in a pure and clean language to understand its perfection. This is like his deeds; silver was spoken of concerning his preparation. The depth of his emanations was refined to the light of the mysteries of the Scripture, hinted at and beginning in faith. A dwelling tent for the recipient according to His mercies; the Lord shall profane the lips of understanding of the "tithe" <unclear>staining obscures text</unclear> forever, the source of splendor. 

And my prayer is written from the firstfruits of all... to Him, silence is praise <note>original: "לך דומיה תהלה" - Psalm 65:2</note>. A holy book, not built because of its literal meaning or distance. May it be a holy dove, and may its strength be known. May the voice of the order be holy and profane over all its decrees in the capital of our existence and the **Holy Work**. 

And I, the least of the students, have transcribed it at the dust of the feet of the wise. I worked with my own money to complete it, from my masters... I said I would build a city like the form of the Living God, so that my thoughts would be established. I said I would provide rest and tranquility along with the other sons of Seth. Some of this is in all the thoughts of my spirit. Our God spoke, providing strength despite the sorceries against me. I became wise and purified. They sought the face of the Lord who is before me. 

I have crowned this within the day, burning and consuming... known in its midst. I served before my Creator and I created the rest of the glory of this honored book. Especially the holy forest and the deeper secrets of its hidden essence, I tasted once in the female... and together their eyes. I said to you: this is my wisdom from his service before me. He ceased to hear the portion, to establish words of blessing, to print the voice of my world for the portion... may it come and help to live and hide it, like the order of the <term>Pilpel</term> <note>original: "פלפלא" - likely a pun on Pilpul (logic) and pepper</note>. 

To rely on the Divine Providence in the lightness of His holiness every day, to strengthen their hearts in the service of their Creator. And the rules of our turnings shall no longer be a hope and existence, but shall be for us a redemption and a ransom. May the Holy One descend upon us; may the Lord be the one who has mercy on His words. They were established for the day of your excellence at the time of its gates. May the merits with the burning ones stand like a second lamp, always beautiful like the firstfruits. All the laws of this book are like a prepared lamp, and like the gold of Ophir, it shall be established upon its loins. May you all be completed in the valley of the field with their agreement. May he be remembered for good, for my intention was to bring merit to the public. And so, may praise be spread in the heavens, to elevate the grace of holiness. It is good to see the coming of the Redeemer, with all who join the House of Israel. 
Amen.

-> The salvation of those who study it. <-

<meta>Continuity is maintained from the previous page's introduction of the Lord's kindnesses toward Israel. This page moves into the philosophical and mystical core of the preface, examining the purpose of creation, the nature of wealth, and the cyclical "times" mentioned in the Book of Ecclesiastes (Kohelet) through a Kabbalistic lens.</meta>

# Preface

->Preface<-

To bring forth and bring into being by His will—known to the Blessed Son alone in His significance—and known to the wise of heart that surrounding the void of causes is the illumination of the Supernal Will <term>Ratzon Elyon</term><note>The Divine Will, which in Kabbalistic thought is the highest manifestation of the Infinite, preceding even Wisdom</note> in its aftermath. For the Lord is the Creator of the ends of the earth and all that is divided into goodness and protection, just as this small span is like the span of the "end of days" <note>original: "קץ הימין"</note>. He shall choose for you length of days as a covering.

In the beginning, there is wealth and honor, for everything comes from His kindness toward His creatures. Wealth and honor are vessels through which one is bestowed upon, and they should not be abandoned. However, it is proven that following them can distance one from the Good and cause them to deny the Essence. This is what is meant by the place where nature and sin meet; through such a sin, they "kick" <note>An allusion to Deuteronomy 32:15, "Jeshurun waxed fat and kicked"</note> and turn away. All this evil is caused by the "vanity of the voice" <note>likely a corruption of "all is vanity" (hevel hakol) from Ecclesiastes</note> which prevents people from attaining wealth and honor in a holy way, distancing them from the pure heart and the Supernal Return. This return restores the "voice of good sustenance" that descends upon the Will and the wine that drips into the hearts—the purified voice from the days of Creation. For those who merit it, they shall know peace; for him, it is said that he shall pass through to do good. This means that the Supernal Return provides existence and an embrace for the secret of being. He was and shall be a sign that he shall not pass away, nor shall he seek "imaginary wealth"—the wealth of this world drawn from the "bad voice." He should not pursue it, for in following Joseph <note>possibly a reference to the Sefirah of Yesod, personified by Joseph</note>, the love is shortened and the law is strengthened. Even the wealth of the "voice which sinned" and covered him will not remain, for the Godly labor is within it. Through knowledge of the path chosen in the "good portion," one is saved from the "voice" that leads to all types of materiality. This "Joseph" includes the number eight.

<margin>5</margin> There is a deep inquiry into whether one should be satisfied with the power of the eternal world or occupy oneself with the "life of the hour" <note>temporary, mundane life</note>. It is said that it is no small wisdom to bring even that which was not initially intended through deep contemplation. Therefore, the mind and the intellect shall argue, and the good shall surround and be honored. "The righteous shall wear it," for he flourishes in righteousness. He who occupies himself with wisdom and knowledge finds that the entire world is a vessel for him. By not fleeing from it, he builds for himself that which the Supernal Promise intended—to divide and gather the "spoils of the beast" <note>metaphor for conquering material nature</note>. His love and his voice are written to remove sickness from him. He also turns his heart to understand what lies beneath this "shell" <term>Klipah</term><note>In Kabbalah, the 'shells' or 'husks' that conceal the divine sparks in the material world</note>, from the greatness of his proximity to God. It has already been hinted that the "womb" is desired and mingled with wisdom and knowledge, not merely by the law of the world's beauty, but to complete the intention and bring it from potential to action according to the Supernal and Holy Will. This is the completion of the "Good Voice," lest it be in vain. What will become of him who does good for life? He lives freely, for outside of these Supernal matters, everything is vanity and empty words. If he follows vanity, he becomes vain himself—Heaven forbid! This cannot be, for God gave man a nest even among the despised creatures. The good of the mind, which views the world with contempt, merits the "scent of the voice" and the holiness of the house. This is hinted at in the saying: "He merits his portion and his fellow's portion in Eden," while the opposite "takes his portion and his fellow's portion in Gehenna." This is also "vanity and pursuit of wind," for he followed vanity. After the loss, all is evil, for he loses the "remembrance of the spirit" <note>original: "זכרון רוח"</note> when he is stripped of goodness and perfection, and remains empty.

**To everything there is a season, and a time to every purpose under the heaven** <note>Ecclesiastes 3:1</note>. This means that for all opposites and changes in desires—between the pursuit of good and the "mediocrity" mentioned—everything has its specific species and its own end. There is a source time, meaning his intention in his desire, and all the "times" are included within the general rule of opposites.

Because the heart's will and life were once unified, but the "times" are now opposites, the Will does not participate in them at all. The indwelling of the Divine Presence <term>Shekhinah</term> is according to the preparation of the recipients. He who prepares himself for good, it shall come and awaken upon him. Likewise for him who prepares for evil. These changing "times" inform us that when good or evil awakens below, it has a root and essence above. It awakens its likeness. All opposites are under the "known tastes" of the Holy One, Blessed be He. This is the "Sun" mentioned many times in the Book of Kohelet (Ecclesiastes)—"under the sun" and "under the heavens." In that place, all opposites and changes were established, such as "a time to be born and a time to die." Know that the "good times" come from the "Good of the Tree of Knowledge," and the "evil times" come from the "Evil of the Tree of Knowledge." Above that realm, there is no nature and no opposite. Therefore, there is a place for the good and its treasure, and a place for the evil and its lack. Everything is received through the "kidneys" <note>historically viewed as the seat of counsel and emotion</note>, and no matter can force its actions. The good person yearns for the "time of the righteous," who is the "foundation of the world" <term>Yesod Olam</term>. This is a "good time," the place of birth and dances. But the sinner draws himself to an "evil time," the opposite of the "crown of her husband" which is death. All the "times" mentioned—the good and the bad—are the twenty-eight "times" <note>original: "כח עתים"</note> or aspects within the Tree of Knowledge of Good and Evil. In every cycle, the "Time of Peace" <term>Et Shalom</term> encompasses everything in peace, meaning the evil is included within the good and the perfection. For this, we must align the intention of the "good worker" to benefit all things, bringing them to the totality of life with a pure thought. This thought preceded all existence in perfection. This life is "Eternal Life." One must include the evil within the good until it is entirely transformed into good. This is the secret of "And you shall love the Lord your God with all your heart"—with both your inclinations, the good and the evil. This includes the sparks in their purity, the secret of life as will be explained in this book. Now we shall investigate the ultimate purpose <term>Tachlit</term> intended for eternal life. He begins by asking, "What advantage has the worker in his toil?" This is phrased as a question and answer. What is the advantage of all the deeds a person strives for? What is their end? The "final advantage" and "excellence" is when one merits to ascend and gain wisdom. He shall not lack anything from his toil. He says that at the beginning of everything is the "Observation," which is the end of deep inquiry. Even if he has not yet reached his full goodness and completion, reaching the goal makes the toil worthwhile. The intention is that the one who occupies himself must aim for the intended purpose. There is no "advantage" except through the Will <term>Ratzon</term>, for the Will has the power to unify the action. Regarding "the toil of man under the sun," this distances the place from the true "Advantage and Completion." There is an advantage in the source of thought and the toil that is *above* the action—the final purpose. Therefore, I saw the "matter which God has given to the sons of men to be exercised therewith." This is the quality of the intellectual soul. "I saw the matter" refers to the secret of the spreading of thought, which God gave to men to stir and strengthen them from below to awaken that which is above.

# Preface

Which will be explained in this book, with the help of Heaven. Since the intention in the creation of the worlds—all of them, and not just this world—was such that, were it not for this, the earth would be as if wasted and desolate, except for our existence and our birth within these matters. Man did not come to be a permanent resident on the earth, for Heaven forbid that he should fail to complete the Supernal Will <term>Ratzon Elyon</term><note>The primordial Divine desire that initiated creation</note>. The kindness of the Unity <term>Yichud</term><note>The mystical act of declaring or revealing God's absolute oneness</note> has no end or limit, and we must occupy ourselves with upholding it, may it be blessed, with a whole heart. The path for this was the Torah and the fulfillment of its commandments in the manner we have written, and which will be further explained. In the *Holy Palace* <note>original: "Heikhal HaKodesh," likely a reference to a specific Kabbalistic text or section of the Zohar</note>, it is taught that this world is but a small house and a short time. Therefore, one should fulfill the purpose for which he was created.

Regarding this, it is said, "I am a stranger in the land" <note>Psalm 119:19</note>, for we are those who occupy ourselves with the Upper World, and we are not meant to settle down here, but only to dwell as strangers and to do the will of our Creator through choice. In the end, his path leads to the Good, as is his nature. Even if life is but a short time, one should not waste the [Divine] intention. If one spends many days and a short period of fulfillment with great enthusiasm, then this is the path he should occupy himself with. Let the world be directed toward the completion of the Will, and do not let it be stretched away from it; if you delay, do not expect your request to be granted. For if we were occupied with being in the higher realms and with his intellect while on earth, fleeing to various places because he is a world standing within a passing world—he is only a stranger. To the stranger, his work is always the "work of Heaven," as we have established upon the tablets of our hearts. His love for Him is for the present and for service, and the intention does not ascend except through these lands and by being a stranger within them. For this world was chosen to be a place of service, and concerning this intention, we have written.

Broadly speaking, it is said of all this that the act of "nullification" <note>Hebrew: *bitul*, the ego-nullification required for spiritual growth</note> is like the "Holy" <note>original: "Kodesh"</note>; it is like the work he was occupied with on the Sabbath—uncomplicated, like the Upper World. As we have written, the intention is that according to the goal intended in the creation of the world, it was meant to complete the Supernal Will. If so, the World of Action <term>Olam HaAsiyah</term><note>The lowest of the four worlds in Kabbalah, representing our physical reality</note> is balanced, and it hints to man that the "strangers of the place" <note>referring to those who realize they are temporary residents</note> are upon him.

This is the secret of leading the **Thought** into **Action**. It is known that Action is the end and the goal of Thought. When one looks at the passing world in this way, there is a unique "voice." If Thought is accompanied by proof and accompaniment, then the awe is great. In the creation of the world, the Supernal Thought leads toward the completion of the activity and the act, corresponding to the "End of the Supernal Thought." For they ascended in power to Him, may He be exalted. This power inclines toward its root and rises upward; it is the "desired few" according to what was intended in the Thought. Then, the Attribute of Mercy <note>original: "Midat Rachamim"</note> will be the few, and the good and evil will be mixed in this Thought. But the Will is to clarify and to set the good in its place and the evil in its place. When they are all clarified and bound, the Good becomes the essence. 

In this Thought, all of this is prepared for Him, may He be exalted, not for Himself, but for those who sit before Him. In the continuation of these verses, regarding these acts, the matters were the opposite: the good was secondary and a "shell" <term>Kelipah</term><note>The "husks" or "shells" that conceal divine light and represent evil or impurity</note>, while the evil was the essence. Through transgression, one cannot be established, but is restricted and cut off. Solomon, in completing the Thought through Action, poured out his own knowledge of my ways and my birth, which are this Thought. He would return to God, for all the days he lived, he did not cease from this Thought. If he left himself as secondary, it was not within his power to finish the work of this Thought—to do the work of the King. This is the secret of his saying, "I am a stranger in the land," etc. 

The parable of the one who begets something opposite to what was intended in this Thought: Behold, the "voice of good" in the life of man is this world. God made this in Thought and handed everything over to man to be an overseer. As it is written: "See, I have set before you today life and good, and death and evil" <note>Deuteronomy 30:15</note>. You should take the general level of the Good and follow it, saying: "I am maintaining the love of the Lord your God, to walk in His ways," etc., "to live and multiply, and the Lord your God will bless you in the land which you are entering to possess" <note>Deuteronomy 30:16</note>. It is known that all this is only possible in the Land, for the entire intention is to say: even though you are a stranger in the land, you shall come to these thoughts. The Land of Israel is very great, for it corresponds to the "End of Thought" which was in it.

---

It turns toward its goal and its destruction within the level of evil, as it is said: "But if your heart turns away and you do not listen, and you are drawn away," etc., "I declare to you today," etc., "you shall not prolong your days upon the land" <note>Deuteronomy 30:17-18</note>. That is to say, the intention—which was for the Good to be the essence in your life—will not be extended. To turn the cause back toward this good, and if "Death" is the opposite, he says: "Choose life" <note>Deuteronomy 30:19</note>, to make known that the Good was the primary desire and Thought. Therefore: "that you and your seed may live," for through your choice of this life, which is named Good, you return to walk in His ways, as said above. This will be better for you and your descendants, for the nature of the Good is to be such, provided that the "Tree of Intention" is within the preparation of this Thought.

The power to do good is "the Lord your God," etc. When service is transformed toward this intention, behold, the "voice" inherits the fact that you were a "stranger in the land." You came only to do the will of your Creator. Through service, the first intention is established, but only when it is dedicated to His glory—He who is God and Spirituality, and He is eternal, as will be explained in this book with [divine] help. 

Regarding these verses, there is a "reason and knowledge" <note>Hebrew: *ta'am va-da'at*</note>. Perhaps this Unity will be lacking or exhausted from the hundreds of Torah [laws]. But let the commandments be fulfilled, for they are the great cause for us, along with the "Perfect Act" that intends them. For truly, it ascends in its weight. For everyone who is "cold" or "tepid" is a thief <note>Meaning one who lacks spiritual fire or passion in their service</note>. When hearts are empty and diminished from the Unity, he is with the "masters of the service." This is what is beautifully written: "to love the Lord your God, to listen to His voice, and to cleave to Him, for He is your life and the length of your days" <note>Deuteronomy 30:20</note> in His world, which he came to complete. 

And here is another fitting point regarding the holy Patriarchs who were strangers in the land:
*   **Abraham** said, "I am a stranger and a resident with you" <note>Genesis 23:4</note>.
*   Regarding **Isaac**, it was said, "Dwell as a stranger in this land" <note>Genesis 26:3</note>.
*   **Jacob** said, "The days of the years of my sojourning..." <note>Genesis 47:9</note>.

Since the Thought is toward the earth, and when the extension is slightly removed through their service—it is as he said, that "almost all your fathers," because of their love—to Isaac and to Jacob—to give to them. And with this, regarding the Holy Covenant <term>Brit Kodesh</term>, which is the matter we intend in this preface: It says that to the man who "writes upon our heart," He gave **Wisdom**, **Knowledge**, and **Joy**. It says that for the man who received the essence of creation, the intention was shared with him. He is the one who began to have the good rewarded to him, and the broad Good was sent to us in a vessel from Him. This is "and you shall rejoice before Him" in the kindnesses of Glory. 

To say that whoever acts for His name, it shall be well with him. And here he has the written "Knowledge" with which he was occupied, even while still within the physicality of his structure, his attachment to it and his distance from it. For Wisdom and Knowledge exist for their own sake, for through them he achieved the "taste" and the "evaluations" when standing upon their truth. By strengthening the vision which he had while occupied with Wisdom and Knowledge of the higher realms, they shine upon him while he is occupied with the lower realms, until completion. 

Furthermore, the word "longing" caused him not to return from them to turn toward the "haughty" or "lying turncoats" <note>referring to worldly distractions or false ideologies</note>, which are the "perfections" of this world. It further hints that Wisdom and Knowledge are the causes of purity and the evaluations above; this is the matter of the Unity <term>Yichud</term>. Regarding this it is said: "My son, if your heart is wise, my heart will be glad, even mine" <note>Proverbs 23:15</note>, and it is written, "Be wise, my son, and make my heart glad" <note>Proverbs 27:11</note>. For in the Supernal Wisdom was the "Vision" from the beginning, and He perfected it, and this is His Unity and His blending of the days of the body due to the Supernal order. This is the perfection of the Good which was included in him, and it is his reward. 

We have written that the matter of "to guard" here means to embrace and to cleave. It says that "Death" is that which hinders the intention and causes one to follow the body, distancing him from being in the higher realms. He went to a "lodging place" <note>original: "akhsanya," implying the physical world is just a temporary inn</note>, as you shall see. Furthermore, the word "Good" refers to that which was distant and became bad, and we did not complete it. Therefore, the word "Evil" applies to what he thought—that this evil came to him, opening a matter which is a "depth," as if it would end his days and their unity. This has a benefit: to gather and to cleave to the concepts of the "Enduring" and the "Acquisitions" in Thought. But the "mixed evil" which comes from simple folly turns the world into a "golem" <note>An unformed, lifeless mass</note>.

# Preface

A person of good intellect who shares in this path will perceive that any man who takes for himself the source of the "Lower Vessel" <note>likely referring to the physical body or the lower soul</note> and performs his service and prayers in a high manner—were it not for the revelation of the Ancient One, blessed be He—would be accustomed to this joy of the "Included Ones" <note>the souls or spiritual forces unified in God</note> until he lives through it. His voice reaches the heights, for though he is short of stature, he creates a bond and dwells there. He returns to the lower realm, the secret of the "Primal Image," which is founded one within the other, like "morning bread" <note>original: "lehem boker," a metaphor for daily spiritual sustenance</note>. For through the connection of the Crowns <term>Sefirot</term><note>The ten attributes or emanations in Kabbalah through which the Infinite reveals Himself</note>, one takes hold, and the abundance <term>Shefa</term><note>The divine flow of energy and blessing</note> flows through it constantly, providing nourishment without ceasing.

Regarding this, as is written in the literal sense regarding "taking hold" according to the Sages of blessed memory, and in the Mishnah: these are connected one with another. Even if they are the "Lower Ones" <note>the lower spiritual realms</note>, in the Torah they were like a branch of the Lower Ones. Everything is like a rope <note>a common Kabbalistic metaphor where actions on earth pull a "rope" that affects the heavens</note>. All the movement of the Crowns—even the lowest among them—is intended to make known that the Unification <term>Yichud</term><note>The mystical act of unifying the diverse elements of creation with their Divine source</note> is a high source that goes into the depth of the Torah. Its endurance depends on this great and awesome voice. Within the Torah, any disruption causes the "Spring" to cease.

Through the greatness of the Unification, one finds peace in his destiny. That is to say, when you pray, it should be a piercing light from our portion, together with the Crowns. When they pass over the Torah, then from the beginning of your words, it is established; they will gaze upon the connection of the Crowns. They will withdraw from all inner and busy matters and return to the ways of the Torah and the establishment of their rest. There, they will repair the damage with the voice of "Hear, O Israel" <note>referring to the Shema prayer</note>. This will be a time of learning... if he is a "servant," that is to say, he guards himself from the goodness of the "Samael" <note>a figure in Jewish lore representing the accusatory or evil impulse</note>, this will be held in his hand.

And further, this will be supported together, as I have written above. It is received that through this they are tied together, and the services will awaken His mercies for everyone. Through that burning desire for the way of Unity—without one’s thoughts falling away from the proper path—he returns like a cantor in the tradition... what is good and "what the Lord requires of you" <note>Micah 6:8</note>, except to do justice in his actions. If a wise man's heart is drawn to this, the help and the action will not be absent from the intellect of the wise.

The removal of the defect is easy for the intellect, to serve Him like the cantor of a house. Immediately, he says "to its end," and the cessation of your need is truly the "rectification of the laws" and the correct "taste" <note>original: "ta'am," referring to the deeper reasons for the commandments</note> with which one serves. After the path follows the way of repairing the defect, to bring close that which was distanced, and to dwell in the "likeness" that exists in the world of vision. This secret will be well-clarified in what is said: "And now, let the power of my Lord be great" <note>Numbers 14:17</note>. By mentioning these known words while praying for them, and with this intention, he brings his father into his lack... as in our words, "the heart's portion," and "may the glory of the Lord fill all the earth." Everything is repaired and prepared for those of upright heart.

One must say that you are the one who opens a way for life, as you have written. My gift is the secret of prayer and supplication, and were it not for Your will to have compassion and forgive as is Your way... and in the movement of the chapter "The Receiver"... and in His presence, it is the Ancient One who does not need a blessing. But it is written, "You shall eat and be satisfied, and you shall bless the Lord your God" <note>Deuteronomy 8:10</note>. One might ask: "Who is he that blesses God?" since the Ancient One does not need a blessing. Behold, this is a great matter and a wondrous secret concerning the nature of the commandments. For they are the "need of the High," meaning a supernal need. For they said that the Ancient One does not need a blessing, yet they relied on what is written: "And you shall bless the Lord your God." What does this mean? It refers to the Supernal heights.

When they said He "does not need a blessing," the commandments were given to make known their merit. For it is incumbent upon them to "walk before your righteousness." They need the blessing, and the commandments come from the Ancient One who does not need "righteousness" in the sense of receiving, but rather "to bless" through Him. This is a "supernal need" arising from the commandments and the services; they cause the convergence of the light and the drawing down of mercy and abundance from the Source of Holiness itself.

And it is written: "And you shall walk, and you shall be satisfied, and you shall bless the Lord your God." If so, the Holy One "needs" the blessing because the prayers and blessings awaken the Mercies, and the Great Name is blessed through them. Happy is the man who grows in the Torah and labors in the Torah, doing the will of his Creator. The intention is that he walks from our mercy in truth. The essence of the matter is the bringing down of the Will and the essence of Holiness upon the Supernal Mercies, and from there, through the "Spring," the Will and Blessing flow to the Creator. All of this is within the depth of the Torah and the establishment of the intentions, as will be explained in this book. This is the "Way of the Ultimate Life" by which the perfect servants will live all the days they dwell in the land, until they return to the "Land of the Living," the city of their birth.

For I have already informed you that the "Perfect Act" and the "Will," and the "Thought" which he brought from there—that is the "Unification" <term>Yichud</term> which he included in his soul. The intention in their creation was for this: to know the Honorable and Awesome Name. Also, with all their knowledge and their days, they should excel in their souls and desire perfection. For he knows through wisdom that it includes a perfection that has no end. Also, without the knowledge of the Torah... David our King, the anointed of God, said to his son: "Know the God of your father and serve Him" <note>1 Chronicles 28:9</note>. "Know the God of your father"—the intention is that he should strive all his days with all his heart, without ceasing, to bring knowledge toward the "Beauty of Israel" <term>Tiferet Yisrael</term><note>The central Sefirah, representing harmony, beauty, and the heart</note>. This is the ultimate goal of the service and the fruit of all the effort. This is what is meant by "And serve Him," for this is the ultimate Unification, the perfection of the "Crowns" through which He is revealed. This is what was written: "there is nothing above it." This is the whole of man and the whole world—it was only created to accompany this, to complete the "goodness" for the sake of His truth.

A person is a "tabernacle" for the Shekhinah <term>Divine Presence</term> on earth, the foundation of all the worlds and the "Glory of the Place" <note>original: "Kevod HaMakom," a name for God</note>. This is what is written: "May the glory of the Lord endure forever; let the Lord rejoice in His works" <note>Psalm 104:31</note>. Therefore, every man is obligated to seek after his ultimate end and to complete the intention for which he was created. His effort should be to live these "Ultimate Lives," which are the "Depth of Knowledge" alluded to here. For this is the level of "Desire"—to recognize one's Creator and to serve Him with a "Perfect Service" in love, to do the good and the right in the eyes of the Lord according to His will, as will be explained in this book, with the help of God.

And it is not my intention to repeat what has been said, but to strengthen our connection to this and to contemplate it, to be strengthened as "children of truth." For the ultimate point of the service of God is as I have said: "These are the Ultimate Lives." This shall be a refuge from distress and a merit to live in the "Pleasantness of the Lord" and to "visit His Temple" <note>Psalm 27:4</note>—the place from which the soul was hewn. And since the light was separated from it to live these lives... the place where the soul is hidden. All this is alluded to and prepared, and I have seen fit to set it down in a book.

# These are the Lives
And the ways that lead to them, by the hand of the Lord who is my trust and my God. For this is the end of every man and the purpose of all. I have called the name of this book:

### The Holy Service (Avodat HaKodesh)
And this is the general principle of the Service: the "war" for the Name. It is the foundation of the priestly service to the Place, blessed be He. My intention in mentioning it is not for my own benefit, but because the matters within it are precious and far from the perfection intended. My goal was that its perfection should be in "Action," according to the Supernal Will. For this, I have seen fit to write upon a book the ways that lead to this perfection, so that they may be before my eyes always in "Action." For in the "Action" of the service, the "Wisdom" becomes actualized. This is the meaning of "The Torah of the Lord is perfect, restoring the soul" <note>Psalm 19:8</note>. Its perfection is in its being "Actualized," and that is what "restores the soul." This was the intention of the Sages when they said: "Happy is he who comes here with his learning in his hand"—meaning, in "Action."

I have seen fit to clarify... to grow in perfection, to learn to know the Name. Regarding this, the Torah says to those who call it: "Where is my wisdom?"... A person should not act merely from his own mind, but from the mind of his Creator. He should know how he stands before Him.

<meta>This page continues the discussion of the "Lower Vessel" and the "Crowns," moving from the general mechanics of spiritual connection to the specific theological principle of "Divine Need." It explains that human actions—specifically prayer and commandments—are not just for human benefit but are essential for the maintenance and unification of the Divine realms.</meta>

# ->Preface<-

This is the essential principle and the commandment included within them, for we are obligated to the Omnipresent <note>Hebrew: *ha-Makom*, literally "the Place," a traditional rabbinic name for God</note> who has shared His kindness with all, from below to above. We must repair the Foundation <term>Yesod</term><note>The ninth Sefirah, representing the channel through which divine energy flows into the world</note> through the drawing down of good prayers, which was the original intent. This matter is revealed through the metaphor of a bride, and the weight of these words is great. Everything that Israel bestows through grace and good deeds serves to reveal the Wisdom in the heavens. This further hints that the commandments are a "Divine Need" <term>Tzorech Gavoah</term><note>A central Kabbalistic concept suggesting that human actions "affect" or "nourish" the Divine realm, rather than being for human benefit alone</note> and not merely for human benefit. This is the secret of the Temple service and the prayers.

In the Talmudic chapter "The Musician," it is asked: "Why were our ancestors barren?" It answers: "Because the Holy One, blessed be He, desires the prayers of the righteous" <note>original: *ha-Kadosh Baruch Hu mit'aveh li-tfilatan shel tzaddikim*</note>. And in the chapter "One who Slaughters" <note>referring to Tractate Chullin</note>, it asks: "From where do we know that the Holy One desires the Priestly Blessing?" For it is written: "And they shall put My name upon the children of Israel, and I will bless them" <note>Numbers 6:27</note. Our Sages explained that the Holy One desires this blessing because it fulfills the need of placing His Name upon His people and His world—it is for the sake of the "Place" [God] and not just for the sake of Israel.

Understand the intention of the Rabbi <note>likely referring to a specific authority like the Ramban or the Ari</note> to awaken the eternal secret. If even a small commandment is an obligation for Israel, how much more so is it a "Divine Need." The Sages of Truth <note>a traditional term for Kabbalists</note> learned from this that our spiritual awakening serves a "High Need" and contains a hidden secret. When Israel performs the will of the Omnipresent and engages in Torah and commandments for their own sake <term>Lishmah</term><note>Doing a holy act purely for the love of God, without ulterior motives</note>, they unify His Great Name and bring His Presence closer to their dwelling. This draws down the Supernal Kindness, unified in the Infinite <term>Ein Sof</term><note>God as He is in Himself, beyond all definition or emanation</note>. This unification ensures that the Divine Presence <term>Shekhinah</term><note>The feminine aspect of the Divine that dwells within the created world</note> does not depart, but remains dwelling within them with understanding. This is the vitality of the revelation that sustains the performance of the commandments. Through this, the worlds are strengthened and unified as one, testifying to the one Creator. 

The form of the Divine Presence among those below is the Sabbath and the unification of all worlds. It is the unification of the upper and lower realms. When kindness is diminished, the system falls into shadow. This is the secret of the soul and the "canopy of peace" <note>the *Sukkat Shalom*</note>—all are unified. This is the secret of the "day of his wedding" <note>Song of Songs 3:11</note>, for the spiritual awakening is like a wedding, a unification with the Bride. This is the secret of the "day of the gladness of his heart." We, the people of Israel, bring in the Sabbath with this goodness, so that our service will be a "Will" that brings vitality and completion. The perfection of Israel is a "Divine Need," a unification of kindness upon the children of Israel for the sake of the Place.

Conversely, when Israel does not do the will of the Omnipresent, they cause a separation. When the Divine Presence departs from the lower realms, her place is filled by a "distanced understanding." Our Sages said in the Midrash: "When Israel does the will of the Omnipresent, they add strength to the Power," as it says, "Through God we shall do valiantly." But when they do not, they—as it were—weaken the great power of the Above, as it is written, "You neglected the Rock who begot you" <note>Deuteronomy 32:18; the Hebrew word for 'neglected' (*tashi*) can also be read as 'weakened'</note>.

This is further explained through the story of Rabbi Akiva. When Moses ascended to the heights, he found the Holy One, blessed be He, tying crowns to the letters of the Torah. God said to him, "Moses, is there no 'Peace' <note>a greeting</note> in your city?" Moses replied, "Does a servant greet his master?" God said, "You should have helped Me." Immediately, Moses said: "And now, I pray, let the power of my Lord be great, just as You have spoken" <note>Numbers 14:17</note>. The Sages intended to show that in this matter, there is a portion that man can provide to the heavens.

<column-break/>

Just as it is a great thing to act thus for the sake of the Holy, so too is it as Rabbi Jonathan wrote: it is not proper for a person to die [to his spiritual duties] while the Temple stands. Therefore, "All that the Lord has made is for His sake" <note>Proverbs 16:4</note>. Our Sages taught us to praise Him. Afterward, one becomes worthy of this, rectifying kindness in its proper time. A righteous person merits this through complete intention in his service. By doing so, he connects the world to God. This is known in the hearts and mouths: the intention of the heart is to unify the Righteous One <note>the Sefirah of Yesod</note> with the Holy of Holies. 

The matter of sacrifices, divine service, and prayers truly performs a great action: drawing down the Supernal Will and unifying the "Sweet Mercy." Even so, the persistence of this world depends on the awakening of this service. Without this purpose, He might withhold His kindness. But the "Perfect Worker" rectifies what our God has made from beginning to end. If a man truly knew this, he would see that it is a great kindness that comes through the intention of the heart. The Great Name is unified in His glory through the engagement in commandments, even when we do not fully grasp the depth of the matter.

Therefore, realize that the best of all deeds is to act and connect with the level of the "Higher Deed." With eternal love and mercy, one should fix the "Great Measure of Goodness." This sustains the world. The righteous person draws from the "Living Vitality" to rectify the Great Name in its glory. One must contemplate this deeply.

The Sages chose this path because it is for the sake of His Name. The body lives through this language and heart. The perfection of the Name through complete intention is the ultimate goal. This is the purpose of the "Perfect Servant" in every world. His actions become a sign of the "Upper Abundance" that shares its goodness with all. This is the foundation: to honor the Perfection. 

This opens the gate of "Return" <term>Teshuvah</term><note>Repentance or literally "returning" to God</note>. The purpose of the intention in service is to bring the "Lower" to the "High." The "Hidden Waters" are revealed by the perfect worker. This is the fruit of the Torah, the commandments, and the intention of creation. Without this, the world would not maintain its form. Through the proper intention, things are transformed.

The perfect servant has the power to awaken the Supernal matters and draw down the Supernal Will, unifying the "Sweet Mercy" through his prayer and service. This rectifies the "Great Perfection." He has the power to return all things to their Supernal Place and to gather the kindness that is hidden and sealed within them. All things move in a circle; all that came down from above must eventually return there. The perfect servant has the strength to take the things that have descended and return them to their source in the heights.

<summary>This preface explores the Kabbalistic doctrine of "Divine Need" (Tzorech Gavoah), arguing that human prayer and the performance of commandments are essential for maintaining the unity and flow of the Divine realms. It emphasizes the "Perfect Servant's" role in rectifying the world and returning all sparks of creation to their celestial source.</summary>

<column-break/>

# The Book of the Holy Service
## Divided into four parts
### Which direct man in the holy service desired by the Omnipresent, blessed be He.

# The First Part
This is the **Part of Unity** <note>Hebrew: *Chelek Ha-Yichud*</note>. In it, he will mention the secrets of Emanation and Unity, and will prove the aforementioned matters that awaken the soul to it.

# The Second Part
This is the **Part of Service** <note>Hebrew: *Chelek Ha-Avodah*</note>. In it, he will mention the secrets of worship and its intention. He will explain that all types of piety and righteousness—whether for the sake of kindness and the perfection of the body or for kindness and the perfection of the soul—are derived from it.

# The Third Part
This is the **Part of Revelations** <note>Hebrew: *Chelek Ha-Tagliyot*</note>. In it, he will mention that the "Complete Servant" is the purpose of all created beings, both upper and lower, and he will explain this.

# The Fourth Part
This is the **Part of the Secrets of the Torah** <note>Hebrew: *Chelek Sitrei Ha-Torah*</note>. In it, he will explain the secrets of the "Work of Creation" <term>Ma'aseh Bereshit</term> and the secrets of the "Work of the Chariot" <term>Ma'aseh Merkavah</term> <note>The two primary branches of Jewish mysticism; the former dealing with the cosmos, the latter with the Divine throne</note> and the secret of the expanse of the Chariot... and he will explain the secrets of prophecy and its divisions, the secrets of the Giving of the Torah, and the preservation of the book.

## Preliminary Introductions:
### The First Part is the Part of Unity: Its 28 Chapters

**Chapter One**: Serving as an introduction to this part. In it, he will mention that one must direct the path toward wisdom so that they may attain true life according to the Kabbalah, for God intended for the soul to resemble His divinity and to be received by Him... according to the commandment "Love your neighbor as yourself," and he will establish this with proofs from the book.
**Chapter Two**: In it, he will explain the secrets of Emanation <term>Atzilut</term>, which is Divinity, and that the source in Emanation is unified. He will provide proofs that the Holy One, blessed be He, is the world and His image sustains all. He will prove this from the verse "The Lord is My Name" and explain that the head of Emanation is Wisdom <term>Chokhmah</term>. He will hint that the "Supreme Crown" <term>Keter Elyon</term> is not within the realm of human contemplation and will hint at the correct knowledge of the Kabbalah.
**Chapter Three**: He will hint that all of Emanation is as one ancient power, which is not within the realm of human contemplation, for it is the Infinite <term>Ein Sof</term> in Kabbalah. He will hint that it is the sum of Kabbalah... and the business of the "Ascending Man." He will explain the power mentioned in the book regarding the ten Sefirot—"ten and not nine," etc., and will prove this from the verses.
**Chapter Four**: He will explain that the Emanation of the ten Sefirot is the essence of Divinity and will prove this with clear evidence according to the Kabbalah. He will explain the verse "I am first," etc.
**Chapter Five**: To explain further that Emanation is the essence of Divinity, and he will further prove this from the intention of prayer and the blessings appropriate to them according to the verse. He will prove the verse regarding the unification of His name, that all of Emanation is unified, and will hint that all of Emanation is the Unique Name within everything and is the sum of all, and it is the division of the parts.

### Commentary

Wait for his generation and the greats of his period. Solomon wrote... King Solomon, peace be upon him, through the Holy Spirit <term>Ruach HaKodesh</term> <note>Divine inspiration or prophecy</note> as an offshoot of... arranged by the Holy Spirit for this book. The sages, builders, and those of knowledge merited it, and as... this is in the book of *Proverbs* <term>Mishlei</term> where it says, "The Lord by wisdom founded the earth; by understanding He established the heavens" <note>Proverbs 3:19</note>... by His knowledge the depths were broken up, etc. *Proverbs* corresponds to Knowledge <term>Da'at</term> <note>One of the Sefirot, often representing the union of Wisdom and Understanding</note>, which is for all... and in the book of *Ecclesiastes* <term>Kohelet</term>, it corresponds to Understanding <term>Binah</term>, as I drawn out my heart in the congregation <note>original: "Kohelet"</note> to balance the desire... corresponds to Understanding. The *Song of Songs* <term>Shir HaShirim</term> corresponds to Wisdom <term>Chokhmah</term>, and it is the chosen song... the foundation of the secret of "Grace" <term>Chen</term> <note>often used as an acronym for *Chochmah Nistarah* or "Hidden Wisdom," meaning Kabbalah</note> for the King to whom peace belongs <note>A common Rabbinic play on the name Solomon (Shelomo), which shares a root with peace (Shalom)</note>, the secret and his gift... in the Midrash "Chazit" <note>The Midrash on the Song of Songs</note>, all is wisdom and the greatness of the measures of the Temple of Wisdom to encompass... the Temple from the great business, a booth within it and a Temple in the hiddenness of the text... a portion to give. And they said again... against a small portion for his generation. And so they hinted... his greatness is the "leaven of the leaven," the *Song of Songs*, lacking forever for the King to whom peace belongs... and includes for the dead. The sanctuary include the Sabbath, a reward for his generation, and so they hinted... but the power of the cities of refuge is his tablet... and so... my thoughts... the opposite of the foundation... to say "wait for his generation," and it is known to the wise that in *Ecclesiastes* is the glory... near the King whose treasure is his, and rely on waiting for his generation and his period for rest... answer us regarding the stand with him in the verse, and this depends on the pleasure... the pleasures in the depth of the Torah and the fulfillment of the mechanisms... those of his period and written to sweeten my people... like the righteous who guard its purity and maintain the mechanisms, for he is a resident of... wisdom between the two praises they began, for they were scrolls from the beginning... desire and all salvation, and this began. And when the perfect servant intends in all his matters... the supernal glory upon its students, and above all, "May the words of my mouth and the meditation of my heart be acceptable before You" <note>Psalm 19:14</note>.

### Preface

It is explained in this book that the plain meaning <term>Peshat</term> <note>The literal or surface level of scriptural interpretation</note> here was the tradition <term>Kabbalah</term> from the side of the Torah and an explanation for the world... as it says, "The Lord possessed me at the beginning of His way" <note>Proverbs 8:22</note>. Thus, in their beginning, before the creation, there were matters written in the Book, and when He sought to create, He would look into it and create. The end of the thing being before Him like a worker, for the virtues were established. And also good further in their words... in the fourth part of this book, in the Mishnah of the "Work of Creation" <term>Ma'aseh Bereshit</term>... in any case, the tradition is his for his intention. 

The second benefit is for myself... because the trials of the Divine Presence <term>Shekhinah</term> in this portion were caused by the study of Torah. The desire is to refine the dross... and he shall never die; a vessel that shall not cease. And the compensation for his service and his unification <term>Yichud</term> <note>The act of declaring or creating unity between the various aspects of the Divine</note> for all days, all this is always active in this absolute lower world. As our Sages of blessed memory said, "Our deeds are to instruct all this," for there is no end or limit to the heavenly unification, and in the end, all the worlds will exist, and the intellect is the intention in their creation. And when he enters to know the kindness and merit of the masses upon us, and the spirit that flows in the examinations and the maintenance of the covenant to rectify this according to the learning. And in the end, when it is returned to him and known... we concluded in it the purpose of the generation... and the end will be that he has a name in the outside world.

And he relied on the number of his years, and it was like the matter that leaves an impression before the Lord, like the writing of our Sages of blessed memory. From this, he established this according to what is provided in the nature of creation, that the conclusion of the matter should be like signs in the perfect hidden storehouse... and to join his companionship after him as a blessing, to leave for himself for that day... in the book or in the building, for the life of a matter is lacking without a name, just as we relied on our Sages who wrote about it: "And the wise took Joseph for himself in his life"... the monument which is in the King's Dale, for he said: "I have no son to keep my name in remembrance," and he called the monument after his own name; and it is called "The Monument of Absalom" <note>original: "Yad Avshalom"</note> unto this day <note>2 Samuel 18:18</note>. To conclude from this that in his journeys, the end of the matter is to leave a corner of himself to be a remembrance for him, and a name better than what is spoken of him, a remembrance of a name in the way of his children.

And if he has no acquisition of a name, it is not proper; then he will cause a lack in what he intended, for he will be swallowed up and his days... from the memory of the dead. In the chapter "There are those who inherit," <note>Perek Yesh Nochalin, the eighth chapter of Tractate Bava Batra</note> it is written: "And Joab heard in Egypt that David slept with his ancestors and that Joab the captain of the host was dead" <note>1 Kings 2:21</note>. Why, regarding David, does it say "slept," while regarding Joab it says "died"? Because David left a son like himself, but Joab did not leave a son like himself. Behold, whoever does not leave a worthy son is called "dead." And even if he leaves a name in the outside world, for his name will be called upon a certain precious thing... his end and his purpose. And if he does not have such, the perfect man is not secure in a son, for "who knows if he will be a wise man or a fool?" <note>Ecclesiastes 2:19</note>. And in the tradition of Rabbi Eliezer the Great, we learn: "Leave a blessing before you and not after you" <note>A teaching emphasizing the importance of one's own spiritual accomplishments over what is inherited</note>. This is why our father Jacob did not fear what he heard from Solomon, and there was no flaw in his seed, for all his sons were perfectly righteous, as is known. 

To strengthen this, they said the shared virtues are established, and he is remembered by preparing a student for himself, for students are the spiritual sons. This is why it was taught in the chapter "The One who Brings," and in the tradition of Rabbi Akiva who said: "If one studied Torah in his youth, he should study Torah in his old age; if he had students in his youth, he should have students in his old age, as it is said: 'In the morning sow your seed, and in the evening stay not your hand'" <note>Ecclesiastes 11:6</note>. And in the chapter "There are those who inherit," Rabbi Yochanan and Rabbi Joshua ben Levi said: "Whoever does not leave a son... and whoever does not leave a student..." This is similar to Rabbi Yochanan, who used to study the Talmud and say: "Rabbi Yochanan caused this..."

<summary>This page discusses the spiritual necessity of leaving a legacy, either through righteous children, a written book, or students, who are considered "spiritual sons." It connects King Solomon's three biblical books to the Sefirot and emphasizes that teaching Torah ensures one is not considered "dead" even after physical passing.</summary>

**Chapter 19** Mentioning the question: why did the first destiny <note>The ultimate spiritual reward</note> not appear explicitly in the Torah? **Chapter 20** To prove that today is worthy of paying the first reward; proving the act and the preparation of light and food; the verse "and it shall be cut off," the verse "to enter the heavens," and the verse "a generation shall remember"; explaining them and proving from this what he brought regarding the matter of existence.

**Chapter 22** To further prove existence and physicality from the secret of Unity <term>Yichud</term> <note>The Kabbalistic concept of the absolute oneness of the Divine</note>; explaining this and proving it from all that was necessary for Naboth <note>Likely a reference to the story of Naboth’s vineyard in 1 Kings 21</note>; expanding on the explanation of this.

**Chapter 23** Regarding the pleasures of the soul; proving the opinion of the "scholars of the scale" <note>A term for rationalist philosophers who "weighed" matters by logic</note> who said that soul-pleasure is simply understanding for all; he will contradict them and prove the opposite with strong proofs, saying that this explanation is part of its essence; explaining the praise intended to rectify the Divine Glory <term>Kavod</term>, and explaining the "distant memory" of the religion.

**Chapter 24** To explain that the Divine Influence <term>Shefa</term> is composed of both speech and action, following the pattern of the "Place" <note>A name for God</note> created by Moses; he increased the generation of the "First Influence" because it is included in every creation and is worthy of it through the intention of the Name; it follows a supernal model.

**Chapter 25** To explain that just as the Holy One, blessed be He, created the body to prove the light of His actions, so He created two types of "vessels" corresponding to two types of delight; this is according to the tradition; proving the interpretation of "And Mordechai," and explaining it.

**Chapter 26** To explain that the Holy One, blessed be He, is the constant Creator of the Kingdom <term>Malchut</term> and the Order of Faith; He is the one who dwells among the supernal beings; proving this according to the tradition with strong proofs; proving the opinion of the later scholars and upholding the truth; explaining its necessity.

**Chapter 27** To explain that delight is built over against the Tabernacle of the Kingdom; the body’s preparation and how it merited this delight; the physical world; proving the worthiness of this according to the tradition.

**Chapter 28** To explain the dispute of the later scholars regarding the chapter "One who Inquires" <note>A reference to the Talmudic chapter "Shoel" in Tractate Shabbat</note>; explaining all of this in the name of a "living body whose soul ascends"; and so on.

**Chapter 29** To prove the matter of Eden, the two trees, and the rivers; everything is literal as the scripture explains; proving this with strong proofs; expanding on the description of the excellence of the Garden of Eden on earth and the ascent of the righteous from there to the supernal one.

**Chapter 31** To explain that punishment in Gehenna is not equal for everyone, but rather according to their wickedness in the "dwelling of the wicked"; proving this and explaining how this punishment occurs.

**Chapter 32** To prove the secret of Reincarnation <term>Gilgul</term> with strong proofs; explaining the end of the matter with the parable of the Name over Israel; explaining the secret of the Tree and the secret of "God shall interpret," and proving the words of the ancient heads.

**Chapter 33** To explain that Reincarnation over time has a "supernal need"; proving this after proving the opinion of the author of the *Book of Principles* <note>Joseph Albo (15th century), a famous Jewish philosopher</note> and this matter in its entirety.

**Chapter 34** To prove that the matter of Reincarnation is not equal [for all]; proving this with strong proofs according to the tradition and proving the opinion of the sages regarding Reincarnation according to what has been received.

**Chapter 35** To explain that Repentance <term>Teshuvah</term> is the foundation of the world and its rectification <term>tikkun</term>; the benefit derived from it and its high status; expanding on the proofs for this and explaining how it is possible for Repentance to remove "the mold" <note>the stain of sin</note>.

**Chapter 36** To explain that the absolute benefit of the entire Torah is reached through the specific commandment of Repentance; proving this from the verse "And it shall be... they shall come upon you," explaining them and proving the verse "For our fathers [sinned]," and revealing its secret.

**Chapter 37** To prove that the death of the <unclear>great ones</unclear> is the refining of souls; explaining this and proving there is no difference between generations; explaining its secret according to the tradition.

**Chapter 38** To explain that the King Messiah will return the crown to Israel; proving this from the words of the prophets; proving that "there is no difference between this world and [the days of the Messiah]" <note>A famous Talmudic dictum from Tractate Berakhot 34b</note> and interpreting it; expanding on this and proving what was prepared until now.

**Chapter 39** To explain that faith in the resurrection during the time of the Messiah is worthy and established for all Israel; explaining the "sect of the simple ones" and proving it with evidence according to the tradition.

**Chapter 40** To prove that the very same person who died is the one who shall rise; this is not a new creation; explaining how this is conceived and proving that the dead will receive their reward in the Land of Israel.

**Chapter 41** To explain that the World to Come <term>Olam Ha-Ba</term> is the hoped-for ultimate end; expanding on its nature; proving the opinion of "The Master of the Guide" of blessed memory <note>Maimonides, author of *The Guide for the Perplexed*</note> and the opinion of the author of the *Principles*; adding to this to uphold the truth according to the tradition of the Sages of Israel.

**Chapter 42** To prove that the World to Come promised in the Torah follows the resurrection of the Messiah; proving this with strong proofs and expanding on the matter.

**Chapter 43** Proving the opinion of "The Master of the Guide" of blessed memory, who said that those who rise in the resurrection of the Messiah...

# Index of the Book
**The Eighteenth Chapter** explains how everything is within His form, including the "void" and the "intellect" in particular. He expands on this explanation, showing that He sustains them all.
**The Nineteenth Chapter** explains that He <note>or "it," the structure of reality</note> is also comprised of good and evil. **The Twenty-Second Chapter** explains the secret of the "Song" found in the Prophets... and that it would be impossible for any intellect to establish the explanation of the Torah we have written unless the secret was revealed by God Himself. He mentions that the Torah was written with "extra" letters... the secret of the faces of the generations, and explains why it was written thus.
**The Twenty-Third Chapter** explains that He dwells in the waters and in man... these matters are explained to remind us of the Song and the Names. He brings proofs for this, including the parable of a King who had an architect <note>original: "ardikoni"</note> and explains it all.
**The Twenty-Fourth Chapter** explains that according to the "Anointed Ones" and the hearts of the "Living Creatures" <note>Chayot, a type of angel</note> who perform the Song... to verify the reason for the blessing, not in separation. **The Twenty-Fifth Chapter** explains the secret of **Fear** [Awe] and hints that it is the "Gate" to the holy service. It includes the teaching "Whoever fears sin..." and explains it; it includes the saying regarding the Sabbath and the New Moon in faith, and the verse "The end of the matter, all is heard" <note>Ecclesiastes 12:13</note>.
**The Twenty-Sixth Chapter** explains that the power of the Tabernacle is a part of its interior, and from it comes an even more inner part. He explains this at length and includes the phrase "God-fearing" said of Abraham, and the verse "And it shall be that whoever calls on the name of the Lord shall be saved" <note>Joel 3:5</note>.

**The Twenty-Eighth Chapter** explains that the Shechinah has a part called "from its midst" and a part called "inner." He expands on this through spiritual discourses and explains the bonds of love between the "Place" [God] and the Shechinah, and between man and the Shechinah... It includes the verse "And you shall love the Lord your God" <note>Deuteronomy 6:5</note> in its entirety.
The hints of the first part, called the **Part on Unity**, are completed.
