Having established the foundations of worship in the previous sections, this page outlines chapters 21 through 47. These chapters represent a deep dive into the "Part on Unity" (*Chelek HaYichud*), where the author systematically reconciles the anthropomorphic descriptions of God in the Bible (such as God "sitting," "standing," or having "mercy") with the philosophical requirement of Divine incorporeality. He frequently contrasts the views of the "speculative sages" (rationalist philosophers like Maimonides) with the "masters of tradition" (Kabbalists), defending the latter's symbolic and mystical interpretations.</meta>

# Table of Contents

<margin>Chapter 21</margin> This chapter will present the opinions regarding the "materials" <note>The underlying substances of creation</note>, demonstrating that for all things, a form of existence was prepared according to the path of intellectual speculation, the secret of the Torah, and its inner tradition; it will provide proof through strong evidence.
<margin>Chapter 22</margin> To prove that the Torah’s source is in the **Supreme Thought** <note>The highest level of Divine emanation, often associated with the Sefirah of Chokhmah or Keter</note>; it explains that it is impossible for any human to fully grasp this except through the will of the Master of Thought. It proves how every beautiful path of the tradition <note>original: "Kabbalah"</note> is found in the Torah and that anyone who turns his face from the philosophers of speculation <note>original: "chachmei ha-iyun"</note> will be caught in the "ropes of tradition," proving this with strong evidence.
<margin>Chapter 23</margin> To prove that the ultimate purpose of the Torah is **Unification** <note>original: "HaYichud," the mystical process of harmonizing the Divine attributes</note> and peace; it interprets for the seeker that this is accomplished through His blessed will and the unique concentration of power. It addresses two doubts regarding this matter and resolves them.
<margin>Chapter 24</margin> To clarify that just as it is impossible to fully grasp the source of the Torah and its explanation without the tradition, so it is with the secrets of the Torah. It explains that those who do not gather the "voice" <note>The oral transmission</note> will fail to grasp them. It clarifies that the Torah contains actual "bodies of Torah" <note>essential laws</note> and things that are like "images" <note>symbolic or shadow forms</note> which exist because of the Torah’s nature, proving this via the tradition.
<margin>Chapter 25</margin> An explanation of the secret of the "heart" and the "likeness" according to the tradition. It explores why the written Torah was not meant merely for learning but for "speaking" <note>vocalizing/enacting</note>, explaining this through Kabbalistic principles.
<margin>Chapter 26</margin> To clarify that the **Supreme Thought** is distinct from all else, and that there is no likeness whatsoever between us and Him. It sheds light on the secret of **intentions** <note>original: "Kavanot," the focused meditative states during prayer or ritual</note> and proves which attributes in the Torah are ascribed to the Name, explaining their reasons and secrets according to the tradition.
<margin>Chapter 27</margin> Regarding terms like "And He went down" <note>original: "vayered"</note> which are ascribed to the Name. It proves that these changes are for the good, and heaven forbid they should imply physicality <note>original: "gashmut"</note>, movement, or change, except in the sense that it was "pleasing to Him."
<margin>Chapter 28</margin> Regarding the positions of the "speculative sages" and the opinion of the **Author of the Akedah** <note>Rabbi Isaac Arama (c. 1420–1494), a famous philosopher and preacher</note> concerning the Aramaic translation of **Onkelos** <note>The standard authorized Aramaic translation of the Five Books of Moses</note>; the author will provide proof to evaluate and refine his opinion.
<margin>Chapter 29</margin> To argue against the *Author of the Akedah* regarding the language of the **Sefirot** <note>The ten Divine emanations or attributes</note>, nullifying his opinion and choosing the path of tradition. It discusses the text of Targum Onkelos and the secret of why Onkelos the Translator made certain pauses, and why one should not choose the literal sounds of the words.
<margin>Chapter 30</margin> Regarding what the **Master of the Guide** <note>original: "HaRav HaMoreh," referring to Maimonides and his book *The Guide for the Perplexed*</note> of blessed memory says: that the "Glory of the Lord" is a "created light." The author will challenge this, proving his own view and interpreting the verse "Blessed be the glory of the Lord from His place."
<margin>Chapter 31</margin> To prove that the epithets Onkelos uses for the Name in some verses but not in others are all based on his wisdom.
<margin>Chapter 32</margin> Explaining the Divine nicknames and which names are ascribed to the Name itself. It proves that these do not refer to any created being, strengthening this with evidence.
<margin>Chapter 33</margin> Regarding the ultimate holiness and the phrase "His Glory fills the earth," as well as the opinion of Maimonides. At the end, he will challenge Maimonides and nullify his views with strong proofs, proving his own position in all these matters.
<margin>Chapter 34</margin> To interpret the section on "mercy in the many days" <note>likely referring to Habakkuk 3:2, "in wrath remember mercy"</note> and the Name, and the author of the *Akedah's* view on it. He will challenge and refute him according to the tradition, showing how power stands on the secret of the "Holy One."

<margin>Chapter 46</margin> On the secret of the word **Flame** <note>original: "Nur"</note> ascribed to the Name. He proves the verse "Behold the place of His action" and explains that there is an **Upper Flame** and a **Lower Flame**, interpreting them according to the tradition.
<margin>Chapter 47</margin> An introduction to the **Power**; how one prepares the heart and the mind through intellectual speculation.

# The Third Part
### Called the Part on the Ultimate Purpose, in seventy chapters:

**Chapter One** seeking the ultimate purpose for all existing things. It brings the opinion of Maimonides regarding matter, that there is no purpose there other than the Will alone. It argues that the purpose is "necessary" and responds to him to maintain the proper path.

**Chapter Two** to hint at the purpose of this world and that there is an **Essential Need** <note>A need within the Divine structure itself</note> within it, specifically according to our knowledge. It explains that the need is found in this "Service," which is the purpose of the masses and the existence of the good.

**Chapter Three** to clarify that all that the researchers decreed regarding the "thinness of the intellect" and the righteousness of the soul is examined. It reviews the words of Ibn Ezra <note>original: "Ha-Ra'ba," Abraham Ibn Ezra, the 12th-century philosopher and grammarian</note> (may his memory be a blessing) regarding "experience/trial" and then critiques him to establish the truth.

**Chapter Four** to prove that human beings are more honorable than the angels in the purity of their intellectual soul. It reviews the opinion of Ibn Ezra and proves that all our vitality is through this. It explains the truth in opposition to his view and clarifies the words of the "Pious One" regarding the woman of Tekoa. It explains the verse "The Lord made all for His sake" and the verse "The end of the matter..." and establishes them according to the words of our Sages.

**Chapter Five** will mention that their status is like the form of an angel, with the power to bring forth the "Pillars of the Torah." Through their soul, they establish the holiness of the **Righteous** who is humbled by the fear of God, that "the pleasure of Heaven" etc. It will discuss the prayer of the distressed over man, etc.

**Chapter Six** to further prove the excellence of the Righteous over the "measured angel." It draws from the opinion of the Sages and mentions the Psalm "O Lord, our Master," regarding the phrase "You have made him a little lower [than the angels]," etc. It proves the saying "What is it to me to be here on the right..." etc., and concludes that the ultimate purpose of all existence is the **Righteous**, and his purpose is to "rectify His glory." It examines the evidence of Maimonides regarding the rectification of the purpose, for "who shall say to You..." etc.

**Chapter Seven** to clarify that the Ministering Angels were "grieved" <note>original: "me'atzvin," meaning they were distressed or envious</note> during the creation of man. It examines the discourse in *Pirkei De-Rabbi Eliezer* <note>An 8th-century midrashic work on creation</note> and explains it, along with the saying "Beloved is Israel..." etc. It demonstrates that the wisdom of the First Man <note>Adam</note> was greater than the wisdom of the Ministering Angels.

**Chapter Eight** to explain several verses that seem to belittle the desire for that which is the primary intention. It mentions the verse "Now if you will obey..." etc., and "The Lord will open His treasure..." etc., and the phrase "Everything that is called [by My name]..." etc., and explains them.

**Chapter Nine** will mention that all the verses indicating the lowliness of man refer to a subject limited from perfection; however, when one turns to the Torah, his hand is uppermost over all creations.

# The Section on Unity
## The First Part
### Called the Section on Unity: Containing 28 Chapters

**Chapter One:** It is my desire to set you on the right path and to show the way to the external sages <note>A term often used for philosophers or those outside the mystical tradition</note> and others, to guide them and to instill deep within their hearts and minds the true beliefs. These were explained according to the tradition received by the "Masters of Service" <note>A common term for Kabbalists</note>, who are the Sages of the Tablets. They received the Tablets—the first set—directly from the mouth of the Master of the Prophets [Moses], peace be upon him. These secrets of the inner wisdom were transmitted as a mystery so that the wise man might come to know and understand the secret of the Tablets, which are the windows through which a man can perceive his Creator and serve Him with a perfect service according to His will. This was the ultimate purpose and intention of the creation of heaven and earth. For when the heart and its intention are focused on His service, it becomes the vessel upon which the world stands and upon which every living thing depends. In that vessel, the flow of Divine abundance <note>original: "shefa"</note> was created and through it, it is sustained. The intention behind the name "Life" <note>original: "Chai" (ח"י)</note> is that it is necessary for all created beings, for without it they cannot exist. The conclusion of the matter is that the soul will find no rest or tranquility in goodness until the world is clarified for it. The source of that wisdom is the True Kabbalah, which cannot be reached through intellectual investigation alone, for it is above all investigative intellect. Investigation rests upon human reasoning, whereas this wisdom requires one to "use the dust of the feet of truth" <note>A humble idiom for learning from true masters</note> to delve into the verified truth from the mouths of the Sages. There, in that deep place, they will teach him and guide him on the straight path. It is his reward and praise, saving him from the pit of destruction, for through it the light from above is revealed. By the clarity of the waters—for through the waters they shall know God—one can cleave to Him. Since we have written in the holy Torah to reject evil and escape its clutches so that the good may be drawn toward him, he who strives and pursues that which was revealed for the sake of creation—which is the reason for the final existence—is worthy to know his Creator and serve Him. Through this true goodness, he shall live the true life. Thus, one must take care of his soul and strive to perfect it in the light of the "Light of Life," to see the face of the King, the Lord. In this way, he will come to know Him, to recognize what is written before Him, to open his eyes, and to take delight in the attainment of his Creator and His service. This completes his soul, allowing him to "walk before the Lord in the lands of the living." This is the ultimate goal of wisdom: to know Him and to toil for the benefit of the soul, for there is nothing higher. Therefore, I saw fit, before we enter the depths of the book’s intention, to provide some foundations and a gateway for every wise person into the chambers of this book. May you take this and understand the goal of His service. This is my thought regarding the supreme benefit, which has no equal; nor was it necessary to elaborate on the labor of the holy service.

<column-break/>

<header>Chapter Two</header>

# Chapter Two

Before the world was created, there was only the Holy One, Blessed be He, and His Name alone. This is as it is written in the *Chapters of Rabbi Eliezer* <note>original: "Pirkei d'Rabbi Eliezer," an 8th-century midrashic work</note>, Chapter 2, and some versions say "before He created the world itself." The foundation of the matter, as received by the Masters of Service, is that before any creatures were created, the Exalted One was a singular Life. He is the one whom the Sages of Truth <note>Kabbalists</note> call the *Ein Sof* <term>Ein Sof: The Infinite, God prior to any self-manifestation</term>. He and His Name were alone. The intention regarding "His Name" refers to a level called the "First Light." He is the First, for His precedence has no end. Thus I found in a discourse by the Sages of Truth, in the explanation of the secrets of the Ramban <note>Rabbi Moses ben Nachman (Nachmanides), a 13th-century sage and Kabbalist</note>, of blessed memory, who wrote that the Ancient One in His antiquity is *Ein Sof*. This is the meaning of what the Sages said: "I am the Lord, that is My Name," indicating that He and His Name are all one. The foundation of the Exalted One is without any hint or description... the name YHVH <note>The Tetragrammaton</note> is a hint to the order of the Assembly <note>original: "Knesset," referring to the community of Israel or a mystical structure</note>. He is a hint to all, and in Him all existences were in potential until the Simple Will arose and agreed to bring them forth from Him. Thus, the *Ein Sof* ascends in the Simple Name to bring forth all existences like ours, which were within Him in potential. They were hidden in Wisdom and Understanding, the hidden things of faith. They were potential within the creation and can stand upon their root. The *Sefirot* <term>Sefirot: The ten Divine attributes or emanations in Kabbalah</term> are bound to Him "as a flame is bound to a coal." The unity of Life is the end which we mentioned. Before this Life, there was nothing else, for these unities are the "Tablets" and the root of every matter. This Life is the power of the written word, moving from potential to actual. A parable for this: the flame is within the coal in potential, and when it goes from potential to actual light, there is no "newness" in the flame itself, but the action of the light is attributed to God now, and not before. Even when the flame emerges from the coal, there is no deficiency in the coal. Rather, the coal has a slight superiority over the flame as it existed before the flame emerged. So it is with the Exalted One. The extension of His qualities only occurred when the Will arose to bring them from potential to actual. The intention here is not that moving from potential to actual implies a change or a deficiency in Him—Heaven forbid! For I have already written that the unities are like "Tablets." This does not imply a change in the Will or the Creator. It is only spoken of in the manner of created beings. Regarding the life of the *Sefirot*, the conclusion of our discourse is that all that rises from Him from potential to actual does not result in any change in Him. This is the meaning of "He and His Name are one." Even if we speak of the coal before the flame, all is within the Unity of the Name. This does not imply any division—Heaven forbid! We only speak of the secret of Unity. Because He is unchanging, He is not affected at all. He exists in complete unity, bound and unified before the "One," for the Unity is not a unity of the intellect or the will alone. In the ten bonds of the Name, no change or division is found in the transition from potential to actual. This is shown by Rabbi Shimon bar Yochai <note>Traditional author of the Zohar</note> in the section on *Leviticus* at length, in this language: "It is taught: Ten names were revealed to the Holy One, Blessed be He... in them He is crowned... in them He is known... all of them are included and hidden in One... from this blessing they go out to life..." until here <note>original: "ad kan," a standard way to end a citation</note>.

<summary>This page introduces the mystical study of Divine Unity, explaining that the ultimate purpose of creation is for man to know his Creator through the "True Kabbalah." It discusses the concept of the Ein Sof (The Infinite) and how the Sefirot emerge from potential to actual existence without causing change or division in the Divine essence.</summary>

# Index

**Chapter 37** will achieve and prove the King's benefit regarding wealth, as it says, "as a cloud," etc. and he shall choose what is before Him.
**Chapter 33** discusses choosing whether the leader in the kingdom was a leader for Israel. It mentions the opinion of **the Guide, of blessed memory** <note>original: "Ha-Moreh Z"L" – referring to Moses Maimonides</note>, who said that they did not grasp the entirety of the matters. He [the author] will challenge him and prove the opposite of his opinion, bringing the words of our Sages: "and you shall have no other [gods]."
**Chapter 34** to prove that all Ten Commandments were communicated to Israel just as they were communicated to Moses. He will bring strong proofs for this and choose the view that there was immense benefit in this. <meta>This page continues the philosophical and mystical exploration of the Divine Unity. # Chapter Three: Part of the Unity — Chapter Four

It is received from the beginning of His primordial Grace that those who received the hidden strength held the tradition of the flaming Divine essence, each according to their capacity, regarding the name **The Holy Ancient One** <term>The Holy Ancient One: (Aramaic: *Atika Kadisha*) A name for the highest aspect of the Divine, often associated with the first Sefirah, Keter.</term>. This is because He preceded all of **Emanation** <term>Emanation: (*Atzilut*) The process by which the Divine light flows out to create the spiritual hierarchy.</term>, for in Him the "rightness" is established. His measure in His level is within the secret of the "ascending fence," where the **Infinite** <term>The Infinite: (*Ein Sof*) God as He is in Himself, beyond all definition or limitation.</term> cleaves through it and reveals the point of the letter *Yod* <note>The smallest letter of the Hebrew alphabet, symbolizing the initial point of creation or Wisdom.</note>, which is Wisdom. This was explained above. Furthermore, this is not hidden: the Infinite and the Holy Ancient One are one, as we find in the language of the tradition of **Rabbi Shimon bar Yochai** <note>The traditional author of the Zohar, the foundational work of Kabbalah.</note> (peace be upon him), that **The Crown** <term>The Crown: (*Keter*) The first and highest of the ten Sefirot.</term> is the absolute Infinite.

Furthermore, we must examine this: if the Crown is the absolute Infinite, how did all the masters of Kabbalah include this Sefirah within the count of the Ten? The Infinite cannot be defined by any number at all! According to their view, how much care is taken regarding the ten Sefirot—that one must not subtract from this count at all? Furthermore, in the place where there is Crown, there is another... After lengthening the matter, the Sages of Kabbalah noted that before all things, the "One who Divests" has no end and cannot be limited by the secret of a root or a primary cause at all, for He is the Cause of Causes and the head of all. He is the Cause that has no displacement. This is the language of **Rav Hai Gaon** <note>A leading 11th-century Babylonian scholar; his inclusion here shows the bridge between early mystical traditions and later Kabbalah.</note> of blessed memory in a response he gave to Rav Paltoi and his colleagues: "We have drawn from all the vessels of investigation from our masters, the receivers of tradition, to know if the Supernal Crowns have names by which they are called in the order of their unity... they all agree in a settled opinion that they have no known name due to their extreme hiddenness, except for the names attributed to them by way of their 'offspring' [effects]." Likewise, that which has no beginning has no known name, and they are the seven letters of the Name of the Prince... all established upon the **Glory of the Creator**.

Thus, Rav Hai Gaon says that even the three upper levels are established above the "Ten," and they are the Primordial, and one from Wisdom, and one from the High—they have no known name due to their hiddenness. And when the Gaon says they are all established on the "Glory of the Creator," one should not understand this to mean that the Emanations (the Ten Sefirot) are "created beings." Rather, they are Divinity itself, established in a complete foundation. Even when the Sages use the language of "creation" regarding them, they mean it in a Divine sense. As they said, "In the beginning, He created" refers to the head of the emanation. Regarding the verse "The Lord possessed me at the beginning of His way," they interpreted it as **Wisdom** <term>Wisdom: (*Chokhmah*) The second Sefirah, representing the first spark of conscious intellect.</term>. When it says "In the beginning," it refers to the place of its emanation. From all this, it is known that the language of "creation" used by the Gaon regarding the Sefirot does not mean they were created from nothing like the physical world, but that they emanated.

The Gaon also said that even the seven letters of the **Unique Name** <term>Unique Name: The Tetragrammaton (Y-H-W-H), the four-letter name of God.</term> are established upon the Glory of the Creator, which is the Emanation that is Divinity. There, everything was included and established, as is known to the wise of heart, to indicate the Exalted Beginning. Hearts cannot grasp it. If so, how can it be limited and defined by a boundary or the law of a "name"? It was brought into the count of the Sefirot by the Sages of Truth, who exalted it with the term **Infinite** to show that it has no end or purpose to its praise. They call it the **Root of Roots** and the **Cause of Causes** to show it is the beginning and root of all.

The holy Rabbi Shimon bar Yochai calls it the **Ancient of Ancients**, the **Hidden of Hidden**, the **Concealed of Concealed**, and later calls it the **Holy Ancient One**. All this is to teach with humility and order. As they taught in the **Book of Formation** <term>Book of Formation: (*Sefer Yetzirah*) An ancient mystical text describing the creation of the universe through numbers and letters.</term>: "Ten Sefirot of nothingness: ten and not nine, ten and not eleven." Its explanation, according to the masters of the Service, is that the Divinity is a unity of Sefirot. The word *Sefirah* relates to the word *Mispar* (number), for the vitality of the root of all is defined by the number ten. All branches, changes, and combinations are defined by the number ten. Also, the word relates to *Sapir* (sapphire) because of its light and brilliance. The phrase "of nothingness" (*Beli-mah*) is to say they are without physical essence (*Beli mahut*); they are the actual Divine Cause. And it says "ten and not nine"...

<column-break/>

...so as not to separate the first in the Emanation, which is hidden above. We do not speak of the Emanation in terms of "slanted lines" because it is close to the separated realms. In the Chamber of Unity, the "end" is established because they all divide into the Root Cause. As it says: "their end is wedged in their beginning," meaning the end of the matter is in the beginning, and from the head is the end. There is no beginning without an end, and no end without a beginning, for the beginning and the end are equal in His existence and His unity. This is what the Sages meant when they said: "The end of the action was first in the thought."

My intention is not to say that the Sefirah of the beginning and end have a physical limit or boundary. Since it is Divinity, and Divinity is not subject to limitation at all, the "beginning and end" refers to the order of Emanation for the benefit of created beings, to give them a boundary and an end, but not that the Master is limited. It says "ten and not eleven" so as not to count the Exalted Crown as a separate part, for it cannot be defined by number—there is no number in "nothingness." If so, it is not a Sefirah [in the sense of a number] and cannot be grasped by thought, for it is above them, even while being one with them. Its level over them is like the soul's level over the body. As the **Ramban** <note>Rabbi Moshe ben Nachman (Nachmanides), a 13th-century scholar and kabbalist.</note> mentioned, the Torah is like a soul. And according to the tradition of Rabbi Shimon bar Yochai, the Crown is included in the count of the Sefirot. The phrase "ten and not eleven" refers to the fact that it is with the supernal Sefirot and the essences included in it; they return to the root of the Sefirah. They do not enter the count because the Exalted Cause does not need this, for He is simple Unity. In the matter of the "Service," the Sages hinted at this in the Torah, though not explicitly in the Writings or the words of the Sages, except for those who have a tradition of the hints.

## Chapter 4

There is nothing besides the ten Sefirot that clarified the power of the Divinity. This is the matter of Emanation. For nothing exists that is outside of the Emanation... they are not one thing and another thing, but the same essence. For it is known that the Essence and the Divinity were a Unity before their expansion. Before the expansion in the Exalted Root, it was all within its "brain" [the hidden mind]. We cannot say that the Root expanded in a physical way, where one thing becomes another or things are separated from Him. Rather, the expansion of the Infinite is within the essence of the Root, inseparable from Him, until we can say that He is there and "there" is He, and all is one.

The masters of the Service received a clear hint of this from what is written in the Torah: "And he moved from upon the Shekhinah..." and "A river went out of Eden to water the garden, and from there it divided and became four heads." The "River" is the unique source. "A river from Eden"—this is where the entire Emanation was contained. "To water the garden" refers to the end of the Emanation, for regarding this, King Solomon (peace be upon him) said, "A locked garden is my sister, my bride." The river waters the garden, which is the entirety of the Emanation, through the artistry of the Sefirah that expands. As it says, "All the rivers go to the sea"—this refers to Wisdom. From there it divides, and from there downwards is the "World of Separation." Up to that point is the **World of True Unity**, represented by the four letters of the Name [the Tetragrammaton], including the entire Emanation in unity. The "four heads" in separation refer to the realms below the emanation.

The Kabbalist Rabbi **Azriel** <note>Rabbi Azriel of Gerona, a central figure in early Spanish Kabbalah.</note> of blessed memory wrote in the "Ohel HaKavod" (Tent of Glory) in the chapter "One does not stand..." <note>Referring to a chapter in the Mishnah/Talmud regarding prayer.</note> concerning the remembrance of Abraham and Isaac. He also mentioned the oath of the Name, saying "The Lord your God..." to understand the four-fold nature of the world. The root of the Rabbi's words is that "He is His Name, and His Name is He," and "His Name is in Him." It is written that in His oath... all that was said refers to the Glory of the world, that there was nothing but Him and His Name alone. Some versions read: "He and His Name alone," based on the foundation of the Kabbalist **Rabbi Bahya** <note>Rabbi Bahya ben Asher, a 13th-century commentator who integrated Kabbalah into his Torah commentary.</note>.

<summary>This page explores the paradox of Keter (The Crown) being both the Infinite (Ein Sof) and the first of the Ten Sefirot. It reconciles these views using the teachings of Rav Hai Gaon and Rabbi Shimon bar Yochai, emphasizing that the Sefirot are Divine emanations, not created beings, and that they maintain a perfect unity with the Divine source.</summary>

<meta>This page continues the investigation into the nature of Divine Emanation (Atzilut), transitioning from the discussion of the Infinite (Ein Sof) and the Crown (Keter) into the specific structure of the Ten Sefirot. It reconciles different traditions regarding the counting of the Sefirot and the emergence of the "Higher Knowledge" (Da’at).</meta>

# Part of the Unity | Chapter Two | Chapter Three

According to the tradition of the sages of blessed memory in this complete discourse, the intention regarding what I have investigated concerning the matter of **Emanation** <term>Emanation: (*Atzilut*) The process by which the Divine light flows out from the Infinite to create the spiritual hierarchy.</term> is as follows. This occurs after acquiring the attainment of the "five-fold" levels. It is known to the true sages that the distance of Emanation is from the **Higher Wisdom** <term>Higher Wisdom: (*Chokhmah*) The first spark of revelation or the "seed" of creation.</term>, for the **Crown** <term>The Crown: (*Keter*) The highest Sefirah, often considered too close to the Infinite to be counted with the others.</term> is not included in the count of the scriptures in the orders of the heart, according to the tradition of **Rabbi Shimon bar Yochai** <note>The traditional author of the Zohar, the foundational work of Jewish mysticism.</note> (peace be upon him), as we relied upon in our book on the levels of prayer. Its greatness is immense; do not let it enter your thoughts that it is otherwise. At the time of his passing, he revealed the hidden secrets, as we found written in the portion of *Ha’azinu* <note>A section of the Book of Deuteronomy; in the Zohar, this portion contains the "Idra Zuta," the account of Rabbi Shimon bar Yochai's final teachings.</note>. It is said there in these words: 

"To be a dwelling for the **Holy Ancient One** <note>original: *Atika Kadisha*</note>, and every vision above—none do not know and none can comprehend. There is no hidden place below, and all is included in all. Two heads are included in Him, and thus everything else is established. He is one in His name overall, and not in the thoughts of the heart. Upon this it was said: 'I have looked at my ways,' and after the awakening, Wisdom was found from the Ancient One, the hidden Wisdom" <note>original: *P"Ch [Pachad?] Kasia de-Chokhmata*</note>, end of quote.

And so, three traditions are pushed forward for this reason, established upon the **Book of Formation** <term>Book of Formation: (*Sefer Yetzirah*) One of the earliest and most influential mystical texts in Judaism.</term>. Those who began with it as a parable used the sign: "Wisdom carved out..." and so on. It speaks of the value of the power in one force within it, saying: "One: the Spirit of the Living God..." and his intention in this is regarding the account of Wisdom. "One: the Spirit..." means it is the mercy in the structure. **Nachmanides** <note>Rabbi Moshe ben Nachman (1194–1270), a major medieval scholar and mystic.</note> (of blessed memory) explained this: "These six are the beginnings, and the secret of these is from Wisdom."

The Torah began with it, as they said: "**In the beginning** <note>original: *Bereshit*</note>—the Sages interpreted this as through **Wisdom** <note>original: *Be-Chokhmata*</note>," which is the start of the Emanation. The tradition of Rabbi Shimon bar Yochai (peace be upon him) in the chapter of *Ha’azinu* states that Wisdom contracts into the Sefirah called **Higher Knowledge** <term>Higher Knowledge: (*Da’at*) The Sefirah that mediates between the upper intellect and the lower emotions.</term>. He said in these words: 

"These three lights shine as three, and two are for the crown of Wisdom, and these are for the throne in two garments, and all is as the Ancient One" <note>original: *Kola ke-chei Atik*</note>, end of quote.

The explanation of the "three lights" in writing is: Knowledge (*Da’at*), and the expansion of Wisdom, and Understanding (*Binah*). From them come Strength, Beauty, and Kindness. Thus we find the order of the levels: Wisdom, Understanding, Knowledge. About them it is written: "By **Wisdom** a house is built, by **Understanding** it is established, and by **Knowledge** its rooms are filled" <note>Proverbs 24:3-4</note>. After them come Kindness, Strength, Beauty, Victory, Splendor, Foundation, and Kingdom (*Chesed, Gevurah, Tiferet, Netzach, Hod, Yesod, Malchut*). What is mentioned in the *Book of Formation*, first chapter, "five... spirit," the intention is regarding the Higher Knowledge which completes the count. It is said there: 

"For the Lord is a God of knowledge—there are two knowledges: one Knowledge to be revealed and one Knowledge to be hidden, to sustain the structure as it rests in the body." 

This is further explained: by saying "ten names," the intention is to learn the emanation of the Sefirot from Wisdom, in which they were hidden. The sign of their power is "20," which refers to the Divine taking, hinting at the subtlety of Wisdom. All things were included in the Sefirah of Wisdom, which is hinted at by the letter *Yod* to let us know that it is the first in the Emanation, as we will explain. As for what was said above regarding the order of his tradition, the intention is the Sefirah of **Understanding** (*Binah*), which is second in the Emanation. It begins from Wisdom through the power of the "High Ascent" from the power of the Infinite. It is mixed with Wisdom, for the Emanation was received from it, starting in the secret of Wisdom, the "Gate of Words." As it was said: "And all is above..." and its beginning was after the Emanation at the end of the Higher Thought, by the power of the higher ones within it, and this is the secret of all intermingling. 

They are all hidden as one, and all are hidden within, and so on. "The lack of Wisdom" refers to the Sefirah of Wisdom, which includes all ten Sefirot, for from it they are all contained. This is the secret of the "high ascent" (*Rom Ma'alah*)—Wisdom is the Infinite. The intention is regarding Kindness, Strength, and Beauty, which are the "Wisdom of Binah" in the chapter where they are all contained. Therefore, they emerged in the "hollow of the source" <note>original: *Be-churei mekor*</note>. He said: "In it they dwell," to hint at what was mentioned at the start of the matter, that all Wisdom is from it, for in it they exist in absolute unity. From that essence, they are brought into unity, for they were already included there without change, moving from potential to actual. This is why it is said: "In it they dwell." 

This is what we wished to clarify in this: 
->**chapter.**<-

<column-break/>

### Chapter Three

I have already written above that the Emanation existed in potential until the Divine Will arose to be revealed. Therefore, Wisdom entered the potential of the "32 paths" of the Sefirah of Wisdom, which we hinted at (z"l), because all ten were in it in potential, as I wrote in the previous chapter. In the teachings of Rabbi Shimon bar Yochai (peace be upon him) on the portion of *Bereshit*, they said in these words: 

"And there was light, and there was light—the light that already was. This light was hidden for the expansion, to expand and to split the hidden hollow into the higher, hidden air (*Avir*). It split at first and brought forth a single hidden point from its secret. The Infinite split from its air... and revealed that point. Once that point expanded, what remained was found to be the light of that spirit, that hidden air. All that was found from it was the first point, revealed to clothe these words. Once it expanded, the light emerged and was seen—the light that expanded from the air. This is the secret of 'that which already was,'" end of quote.

Behold, they have revealed to us the expansion of the Emanations from the **Higher Crown** (*Keter Elyon*). I have already written that the world of the Holy One, blessed be He—which is the world of Emanation—was created upon three things. Because He and His Name were exalted, and His Name was hidden, He is the "High Ascent" that is in His Crown in the secret of the higher light of the clear spirit. In potential, all Emanations were within Him, and He is the *Yod* that is in the secret of Wisdom. The secret of His Name is the "High Ascent" in the Crown from the "Higher Air," which is the Higher Crown. It said that the heavens were made from everything, and it "split at first" and brought forth a "single hidden point," which is Wisdom as hinted at. 

It said that the Infinite was the air that was revealed and disclosed that point, which is Wisdom. Thus it is explained to us here: the secret of the expansion of the Emanation from the "Higher Air" in potential, and the Infinite and the hiddenness within the point. This point is the letter *Yod*, which is Wisdom, the first in the Emanation. From this revelation, the secret of the expansion of the Emanations from Wisdom will be clearly explained to us, through the end of the "Higher Thought," which is in a balanced way, as I wrote above. 

The masters of the Divine Service received that there was no element of time in this, Heaven forbid. Rather, whenever the Will arose in the Thought, it was the "end of the thought," in the sense that it was said "prior to all the air," may He be exalted. One must be very careful regarding the secret of the **Foundation** (*Yesod*) that I wrote above: that the Crown is not included in the count of the Sefirot. Then the Infinite, which is the secret of that which has no end, was such for all of existence, primordial as the Primordial One, for the Infinite has no lord above Him. He is His Name, not included [as a Sefirah] yet not outside of it. He is within the hidden realms of existence, which cannot be reached by any contemplation or thought. They are ten. 

Therefore, He had the existence of the Sefirot in this count. These are hinted at in the Zohar in their fullness. They exist with their time... which is the hiddenness in the collective of three. The "Primordial Light" is from this Wisdom. This is found in the tradition of Rabbi Shimon bar Yochai (peace be upon him) in his book, the *Tikunei Zohar*. This is also the tradition of **Rav Hai Gaon** <note>The last of the great Babylonian communal leaders (939–1038 CE), who also dealt with mystical questions.</note> (of blessed memory), who was asked about the "three lights"—they are above the five Sefirot. They are there... which is the Infinite, and so on. This is also in the *Book of Unity* of **Rav Hamai Gaon** <note>A legendary figure in early Kabbalah to whom several influential works are attributed.</note> (of blessed memory).

Behold, the three are in the collective, as He is part of them. This is what is derived from the discourse I wrote in the previous chapter: "He is included in all, and two heads are included in Him." This is the secret of the "High Ascent" in His Crown, the Primordial Light, which is the Holy Higher Crown. The holy Rabbi Shimon bar Yochai said, in the secret I mentioned above regarding the "Higher Air," that the Infinite split the air, and all of it, and so on. Behold, the Infinite split into the Higher Crown, which is His own air; it is not outside of Him. He ascended to His Name, the Source of Light. 

This was already explained above, though we did not focus on his intention here except to warn those who err in their tradition by thinking that the Crown is the Infinite itself. The intention of Rabbi Shimon bar Yochai's knowledge was that His Will is always in His level, which precedes the Crown, the "Holy Ancient One." Understand that they wrote this because He is Primordial and He is the Infinite. From his collective... the source of Knowledge, for He was prior.

# Chapter 8

A hidden opening for all hidden things <note>original: "Petiha Setima," a classic Zoharic opening</note> requires one to count blessings for all worlds, to lack nothing and to provide for all in the presence of the **Holy Ancient One** <term>Holy Ancient One: (*Atika Kadisha*) The highest, most hidden aspect of the Divine, associated with the Sefirah of Keter (The Crown).</term>. Masculine and feminine principles are hidden within it and established by it, and life flows from it. For any division, one must direct the heart toward it, and the will must look toward the blessings from that Ancient One for everyone, so that the division may be received and His will may be done.

The intention is that the **Higher Wisdom** <term>Higher Wisdom: (*Chokhmah*) The first flash of intuition or the "Father" of the Sefirot.</term> is hidden, and therefore the "Ancient One" within it is deeply concealed. Concerning this, it is said: *“Deep, deep, who can find it?”* <note>Ecclesiastes 7:24</note>. In the Zohar, the scripture calls Wisdom "Hidden Wisdom," which receives from the **Living Intellect** <note>original: "Sekhel Chai," a philosophical/mystical term for the source of vitality</note>. It is said that in Wisdom, the lack of blessings and flow is opened, and there everything is included and satiated. It receives from the hidden **Higher Mountain**; there everything belongs to the **Eternal Name** <note>YHVH</note>, providing blessings and flow to all the worlds.

Therefore, the sages said that when you pray, you must focus on Him to draw down the essence of blessing and flow to the **Influence** <term>Influence: (*Mazzal*) In Kabbalah, this refers to the "dripping" or flowing of Divine light from the highest realms to the lower ones.</term> through which He is blessed. One must associate and harmonize all the attributes in a single measure, as we have written. If so, their prayer is accepted, and He fulfills His will. It was also said there that this action is according to one's knowledge, as implied by the call to the Eternal: every vital birth indicates that the offspring is the essence of vitality. Everything receives its life from the "Influence of Wisdom," **Lovingkindness** (*Chesed*), and **Thought** (*Machshavah*). It was revealed that the intentions of prayers and blessings are directed toward the Attributes <term>Attributes: (*Middot*) The Sefirot through which God interacts with the world.</term> in the manner we wrote above.

One must choose well through the power of the "worm of Jacob" <note>A metaphor for the power of Jewish prayer, based on Isaiah 41:14</note>, to be separate from deficiency. One should pray and intend toward the non-divided parts and the Intellect, so as not to receive power from an angel or a hollow force. Hear the words of the great teacher **Nachmanides** <note>Rabbi Moshe ben Nachman (Ramban), a 13th-century philosopher and mystic.</note> of blessed memory, in his explanation of the secret of the "Six" that receive from the "Understanding" <note>Binah</note>. He gives glory to every matter of the Glorious Name. When Moses approached the cloud <note>Exodus 24:18</note>, it was in that Name. If one were to say it is a "Created Glory" <term>Created Glory: (*Kavod Nivra*) A philosophical concept where God creates a visible light to represent His Presence, rather than manifesting His essence.</term>—as is the opinion of some regarding the verse "the Glory of the Eternal filled the Tabernacle"—it would be otherwise. One who blesses and prays to a *created* glory is like one who worships idols. The words of our Sages of blessed memory point to the name of the **Divine Presence** <term>Divine Presence: (*Shekhinah*) The feminine, indwelling aspect of God in the world.</term>, which is the "Name" itself...

Furthermore, in the name of the wise **Rabbi Bahya** <note>Rabbi Bahya ben Asher, a 13th-14th century Spanish commentator.</note> of blessed memory, in the portion of *Vayera*, regarding the intention of prayer: The Blessed Name is exalted above all thoughts, rising above all levels, as it is written, *“Exalted above all blessing and praise”* <note>Nehemiah 9:5</note>, and as in the **Kaddish** prayer: *“Above all blessings, songs, and praises.”* According to the knowledge of the Sages of Kabbalah, they call upon Him in "One," and all who pray hope in Him. The intention is toward the **Unique Name** <note>The Tetragrammaton, YHVH</note>, for He is close to all who call upon Him in truth. Nachmanides also mentioned this in his poem regarding the secret of "calling upon the Bride." He informed us that prayer is directed to the **Attribute of Mercy** (*Rachamim*) which completes the **Judgment** (*Din*). This is the King... for his language proves the reality of what our teacher sought to clarify: that the divisions of the Name are unified with the Godhead, and therefore it is permitted to direct the intention of service toward them.

He also wrote in the portion of *Vezot HaBerakhah*: *“For what great nation is there that has gods so near to it”* <note>Deuteronomy 4:7</note>. Moses hinted in this verse to the excellence of Israel when they pray; they intend toward the **Higher Name** to cause flow through the Attributes, in every specific attribute they need. This is why they are called a "Great Nation" rather than a "Holy" or "Righteous" nation, because **Greatness** (*Gedulah*) is **Lovingkindness** (*Chesed*), the first of the active attributes. The verse says "gods so near [plural] to it" <note>The Hebrew "Kerovim" is plural, which the text explains as a reference to multiple Divine attributes.</note> because of the many calls to the Attributes. From this, the Sages said: "Rise from the Throne of Judgment and sit on the Throne of Mercy" <note>A common Midrashic depiction of God shifting His mode of interaction.</note>. All this is for the sake of the one who prays. Regarding the Attributes, it is said: *“You did ride upon your horses, your chariots of victory”* <note>Habakkuk 3:8</note>; the Sages explained that the Rider is not secondary to the horse, but the horse is secondary to the Rider.

And behold, **Rabbi Menachem Azariah of Fano** <note>A prominent 16th-century Italian Kabbalist.</note> wrote in the *Book of Unity* and from the tradition of the Rabbis, that it will be explained there what we have thought: that the Godhead is the very essence of the Godhead...

<column-break/>

# Chapter 9

And this is the explanation of Moses our Teacher's words, "gods so near." According to the Midrash of **Rabbi Shimon bar Yochai** on the portion of *Bereshit*: Rabbi Yose said, it is written "who has gods near [plural] to him"—it should have said "near [singular]." Rather, it refers to the God (*Elohim*) of the Beginning, the God of the Fear of Isaac, and the Final God. These titles are called "near" and "Mighty ones" as if they were close. And as I wrote regarding the title "and He forgives his relative," and "God is all around Him." No angel sees the works of Godliness, and no angel has the power to be near us, for *“the Eternal's portion is His people”* <note>Deuteronomy 32:9</note>. One might ask: are these "divisions" and not the "God of the Attributes"? This does not contradict what was written... but the scripture says that the intended goal is "YHVH is One," to show the connection from the "Influence" to everything in a proper quality.

This **Unity of the Bride** <term>Unity of the Bride: (*Yichud Kallah*) The unification of the lower Shekhinah with the higher Sefirot.</term> requires one to focus on the Higher Power, so that the branch remains in its root. This must be done with faith, like a wise person showing that the Intellect is one and there is no multiplicity there, Heaven forbid! One who calls only to the Attributes alone is "separating the plants" <term>Separating the plants: (*Kitzutz Ba-Neti'ot*) A term for heresy, specifically treating the Sefirot as independent deities.</term> of the world's God. Similarly, one who intends only for the Attribute itself denies the Higher Ascent. Therefore, one must understand according to the tradition of the masters of Divine service. The "Gods" are entirely within the authority of the **Emanator** and are not separate from Him. They are the essence of the Godhead. He is the heart for God, and our praises and blessings are toward Him, for we are His people and servants. This is the reason for the tradition of the Unity found in the verse *“Hear, O Israel”* and in the Midrash of Rabbi Shimon bar Yochai...

->**YHVH**<-

**The Head of all** in our house of the Holy Ancient One is called "God" (*El*).
**Eloheinu** (Our God) is the Ancient One from whom the male and female principles emerge and flow to all. This is the version that brings perfection to His sides.
**Echad** (One) is the Wisdom of Israel; without any preparation, it strengthens everything, and there no separation is found at all.

The intention at the "Head" generally refers to the Higher Wisdom, the secret of **Wisdom** (*Chokhmah*). "Elohim" is with the **Kuzu** <term>Kuzu: (*קוזו*) A mystical substitution for the name YHVH (using the next letter in the alphabet), often associated with the mezuzah and protection.</term> and is His emanation. As it is written, the depth of "Elohim" is known through knowledge. This is what the *Kuzari* <note>Presumably referring to a specific Kabbalistic work or the philosophical work by Judah Halevi</note> says regarding the Holy Ancient One, the beginning of the level of the ancient vision. Thus, the evidence of the later things is found in the essence of the ancient ones. 

The intention toward the Name in its creation will be explained to the wise: the "Knower, the Knowledge, and the Known" are in perfect unity. This is the gaze toward the *Kuzu*, hinting at all this. These are Mercies in the secret of the *Kuzu*... specialized for each one. They are not separate. This points to the Godhead and the bond of the Emanator with His creations—that He is Himself, and there is nothing outside of Him, just as there is no light outside of a container, and the *Kuzu* is not outside of His thought. One is not without the other. This is according to the ancient counts in the *Book of Formation* (*Sefer Yetzirah*).

"Our God, the Ancient One from whom all..." means that the "Elohim" written in the divisions is the source. "YHVH" is the container... this is the perfection of His sides. The intention of Israel's prayer includes the levels and the ranks of Jacob. And this name is called "YHVH is One," the Wisdom of Israel. This means the unity of the end of the Higher Thought, which is found at its beginning, rising higher and higher in the secret of the "Long Face" <note>Arich Anpin, another name for the higher aspect of Keter</note>. Through the intention of the heart, we call YHVH the Unique Name, which is unique and includes all Godhead in the perfection from which it comes. The intention is that the unity of Godhead... is the wonder of God, and this is the Divine service. As they said in the Midrash of Rabbi Shimon bar Yochai: to look upon and know His Holy Name... All this verifies that the Godhead is the essence of Godhead, and the titles used in the Unity were not a path for themselves... but to serve the Divine and not to serve any **created being**.

## Chapter 4

As our teachers of blessed memory said regarding the **Measure of the Divine Stature** <term>Measure of the Divine Stature: (*Shiur Qomah*) An early, controversial mystical text that describes the dimensions of the Divine "body" in metaphorical terms.</term> in this language: that which he mentioned as "our knowledge," yet he did not say "our knowledge" at all to teach about the Stature, but rather to divide it into parts <note>The author is navigating the tension between describing God in parts (limbs/Sefirot) and maintaining His absolute indivisibility.</note>. And so you shall understand: it was for the sake of His Glory, and he said "until His passing" <note>Referencing Exodus 33:22</note> and did not say "until the passing of His Glory," but rather "until **He** passed"—from all of which we learn that He and His Glory are one. This is the end of the quote. And what is the extra [meaning]? Each one is the **Infinite** <term>Infinite: (*Ein Sof*) God in His absolute, unknowable state prior to any manifestation.</term> because He is redundant and includes all the divisions found within Wisdom.

And in the Midrash of Rabbi Shimon bar Yochai <term>Rabbi Shimon bar Yochai: The traditional author of the Zohar, the foundational work of Kabbalah.</term> on the Torah portion of *Vayikra* [Leviticus], it says: "To give to you ten names to receive. They are called by Him and through Him, yet they are not finished in the perfect unity. These are the holy crowns for the King." This is our sufficiency in it; they are the support and the foundation of these 72 <note>Original: "ע"ב" (72), referring to the 72-letter Name of God.</note>. And in the portion of *Tazria*, it is written: *"Of You, my heart said: Seek My face..."* <note>Psalm 27:8</note>. Our sages taught that the **Crown** <term>Crown: (*Keter*) The highest of the Sefirot.</term> has a building, which is the **Assembly of Israel** <term>Assembly of Israel: (*Knesset Yisrael*) In Kabbalah, this refers to the Sefirah of Malchut (Sovereignty), the feminine principle that receives Divine flow.</term> to receive the Holy King. He is chased below into the place of the heart for the children of the world. He said to them: "My heart is to establish and to speak within it," for the building is the luck of the world. Then these two crowns provide for and establish [everything]; it is said of her that they are the support and she is the sustenance. "God is between you," as our sages said, "Your face, O Lord, I seek"—all of them are for the will of the Lord, and all of them are for the sake of the **Ancient One** <term>Ancient One: (*Atik*) The most hidden aspect of the Divine.</term>.

And they said in the Midrash of Rabbi Shimon bar Yochai in another place: *"Give strength to God; His majesty is over Israel"* <note>Psalm 68:35</note>. At the time when they perform acts of mercy, the Chariot is within them; He is they, and they are He, like a pillar behind a horse, and there is no separation there. And in the Book of *Hayashar* <note>Likely referring to a specific kabbalistic ethical or mystical treatise.</note> it says: "Taste and see that Israel brings a sacrifice before their Father in heaven and they are honored together, and this is the unity of God." And further there: "Know that the Lord is God; He is His Name." They should not try to be clever regarding "In the Beginning," nor did he wise them up to eat and know the One of the Unity who is unified in all His names. Thus, the ruling is clear: it is only through Wisdom that one avoids separation. They did not intend for the sacrifice to speak of His intention as something external to Himself, for that would be **foreign worship** <term>foreign worship: (*Avodah Zarah*) Idolatry.</term>. Woe to the person who makes a separation, for if he thinks God has turned away, this is the worship of a strange god.

In the Midrash of Rabbi Shimon bar Yochai on the portion of *Vayikra*, it speaks of the light descending. It says the head of the Lord seeks to establish what is required. He said: "He is the Owner/Acquirer and she is the one," and it is said further that the matter was hidden from Israel. The intention refers to the last of the ten [Sefirot], which is the connection of them all, to say that she receives all—meaning God and Israel—and they call out from her. All this speaks of the unity that occupies the Divine Essence. It is further said that she is "for God" and yet "hidden from Israel"; in the building, "He is your praise and He is your God."

The Sage <note>Likely referring to Rabbi Bachya ben Asher or a similar authority.</note> wrote and changed the style regarding the study of "Elohim and Israel," which is the secret of the Unified One that includes everything. He wrote that Israel is elevated to these two words, "praise" and "fame," concerning the matter of all the nations which He made *"for praise, for a name, and for glory"* <note>Deuteronomy 26:19</note>. "Praise" refers to the secret of the Name, and "Glory" refers to the Unified Name. Thus, they are the portion of Israel and they are the Divine Essence, and the body of Israel is within them. As it is said: *"The Lord has taken you"* <note>Deuteronomy 4:20</note>. And the name of Israel is not in the Sanctuary except as a vessel for the Lord alone, as it is said: *"For the children of Israel are servants to Me"* <note>Leviticus 25:55</note> and *"The Lord's portion is His people"* <note>Deuteronomy 32:9</note>. Your God in our final oaths is the Divine Essence. If you receive this from the Sages of Truth <term>Sages of Truth: (*Chachmei HaEmet*) A traditional epithet for Kabbalists.</term> regarding the verse *"Hear O Israel,"* the Sage Rabbi Bachya of blessed memory wrote on this: "The matter of the Unity in its truth is accepted and intended by those who know the Truth; He is the ten Sefirot that are established in one unity, all of them together, to unify everything as one, whether from below to above or above to below." All this shows that the Sefirot are the Divine Essence itself. This is the commandment of Unity—to read it not as something separate from the Essence, for that would be impossible, but specifically as Truth and to include it all.

The understanding that the enlightened one receives is sweet. He wrote in the portion of *Vayishma Yitro* on the verse "And he remembered," and it will be explained well that the external aspects are the Divine Essence. He expanded on this at length, and the enlightened one will find it in our compositions and my commentaries. Although all this is received from the mouths of the Sages of Truth, and no man has ever disputed this, for it is a matter transmitted from 

<column-break/>

ancient traditions and clarified in the **Fifth Wisdom** <term>Fifth Wisdom: Likely a reference to Kabbalah as the "fifth" level of Torah study or a specific philosophical classification.</term>. How should one speak with one who makes separations? This is for you to receive from what this Sage received regarding the verse *"There shall be no other gods for you"*—it does not say "There shall not be for you Elohim," but "The one close to My face." But "My face" shall be upon you. The intention is that they exist in a way that is beautiful and known; for the "face" of a man is not something other than him, nor is it lacking from him or separated from him. Rather, they are an essential part of the shining "Face" of God—meaning, the God of the Name.

As he wrote of blessed memory in the portion of *Bereshit* [Genesis], they are the end of the matter of the words *El Kam* <note>An etymological breakdown of the name Elohim.</note>. And the Name is the secret of the *Yod*. Remember your Creator, for the external aspect is a complete creation. And in the Midrash of Rabbi Shimon bar Yochai, Rabbi Hasa opened: "I shall call out in Wisdom, the Creator..." What is the Lord? Rabbi Shimon said: It is written of Him, "the Creator." Our God is not a created thing... not power... for His hand is not false. He is your God, and there is no other but He. It does not go up to the Foundation <term>Foundation: (*Yesod*) The ninth Sefirah.</term>... and all the rest of the kingship. He called without the Holy Name... Thus "I will call in the Name of the Lord." Rabbi Hiyya said: The Lord called, proving the wisdom that was revealed, and so it is. These are the details of the treasury of song. We said that He created it without toil; He is full without separation. She was the one sent; all the messengers are one. He said that they all ascend and connect and unify as one, and all are one, and He is God, blessed be His name forever and ever.

Thus they have explained that this Midrash teaches that the Divinity is the Divine Essence without any separation. Accepting any lack in this faith is a total destruction of the foundation. Regarding the gathering and connection of the five chariots, he of blessed memory wrote on this Midrash: "This statement alerts us to the verse *'I am the Lord, the first, and with the last ones, I am He'* <note>Isaiah 41:4</note>. This is a hint to the Sefirot, to say: I am He, the Sefirot mentioned as 'the last ones'; they are He, may He be blessed, in another guise." And so I found it explained: the "last ones" refers to the Sefirot, and they are a manifestation of "I am He" in the first. "I am He" in the first, and "I am with the last ones."

And to say that the branches and the foliage are all in His Name, may He be blessed, as it is said: *"Thus says the Lord, the King of Israel and its Redeemer, the Lord of Hosts: I am the first and I am the last, and besides Me there is no God"* <note>Isaiah 44:6</note>. He teaches us that everything is He, and there is no multiplicity in Him, God forbid. Therefore, our sages of blessed memory said regarding Wisdom and the Unity of the Creator: the Unity is the last and the lateness, for in His "latter" aspects there is no end. He is founded in all of them, and He is everything, and there is nothing outside of Him. And so I saw that this is hinted at in this verse by Rabbi Shimon bar Yochai in his Book of *Tikunim* <note>The Tikunei HaZohar.</note>; I have written it in the Gate of *Toldot Yaakov* in truth.

## Chapter 5

I saw fit to further prove and strengthen from the words of Tradition (*Kabbalah*) that the Divinity is the Divine Essence and Substance. For the masters of Divine Service <term>Masters of Divine Service: (*Ba'alei Ha'Avodah*) Those focused on the mystical intentions of prayer and ritual.</term> received the truth that the intention of the prayers is to channel the Higher Power into the attributes (*Middot*) in their entirety, filling them with blessing. It is found among the later Sages of Truth in this language: "The general rule of the blessings that we received is not a difficult thing." Regarding Rabbi Isaac ben Korab <note>Possibly a variant spelling for a known medieval kabbalist.</note>, of whom it was said he was a messenger of God, his intention was that always, all the blessings of the Patriarchs and the connections and all the gifts and blessings of the "seated" prayer <note>Likely the blessings surrounding the Shema or the Amidah.</note> are all for the dwelling and the protections of the Unity every day that has an additional sacrifice (*Musaf*). We pray this in the first three blessings and the last three blessings... and the later intentions and speech are for His praise, provided that his mind does not move from the Sefirah.

We said this in the introduction to make known the intention of prayer. It is not an external intention, God forbid, but is based on the foundation that was created; for the intention must be holy for all those intentions in the Unity. Everything said in it refers to God as the Root, for the intention of these is for the service of God, which is His primary need. And in the Midrash of Rabbi Shimon bar Yochai, they said in this language: Rabbi Hezekiah said, "Every reading..."

<meta>This page continues the discussion on the nature of the Sefirot, specifically addressing the Tenth Sefirah, Malchut, and refuting the philosophical notion that the Sefirot are "Separate Intellects" distinct from the Divine Essence. # Part of the Unity — Chapter Seven
### Chapter Seven, Page 12

That the intellect—and the last one, which is the **Contemplative Intellect**, and it is the **Active Intellect** <term>Active Intellect: In medieval philosophy, the "Sekhel ha-Poel" is the link between the divine and human minds, often associated in Kabbalah with the tenth Sefirah.</term>—and it is the **tenth Sefirah** which is called **Kingship** (*Malchut*) <term>Malchut: The final of the ten Sefirot, representing the manifestation of God's sovereignty in the created world.</term>. It conducted itself before the Holy One, Blessed be He, as the Sabbath, according to the Supernal attainment. She had a "mate," meaning the Mind from which everything stands on its own. And just as it was in the intellectual ethics that a spiritual flow was abstracted from Him onto the seven Sefirot, through Thought and by her influence. And for the sake of the simple ones, the Holy One, Blessed be He, within His wisdom that He desired, gave a mate to the lower intellect. Through His knowledge and teaching, He unified them <note>The text describes the "coupling" or unification of divine attributes as a way for the Divine flow to reach lower levels of existence.</note> with the Holy Fruit, in order to remove the obstacles. These are the sources of the masters of Kabbalah and their traditions. According to their view, the Sefirot are not "Separate Intellects" <term>Separate Intellects: A term from Aristotelian philosophy referring to spiritual beings (like angels) that are distinct from the First Cause (God).</term> that are something else besides God, may He be blessed. Heaven forbid that the masters of Kabbalah should accept this **filthy faith**! To believe that because the Name has various "lives" <note>Referring to the Sefirot as living attributes or manifestations of the Divine Name.</note>, the intentions of our worship are directed to them as if they were separate—as we wrote above from their tradition—that they are the "Separate Intellects." This is a secret of his attachment, for one is not permitted to understand or call upon any created being outside of God, may He be blessed. And likewise, regarding "Bless the Lord, O My Soul" <note>Psalm 104:1</note>... [the text here uses shorthand/abbreviations regarding the relationship of the soul and the Divine]. Just as the soul fills the body, so the Holy One, Blessed be He, fills His world. A person should not call to an angel or a created being, but only to God. For every one who calls upon the Name of the Lord shall be saved <note>Joel 3:5</note>. Thus, it is forbidden to call upon or intend toward any created being, for only through the Name of the Lord is everything accomplished... and those who receive the truth, who stand in the secret of the Great Name, know that the Holy One, Blessed be He, is all, and there is no other.

And if so, how can one say that the view of the masters of Kabbalah is flawed? Some say that the heavenly spheres are the "Chariot," and they are the Sefirot. But our teachers have already received the Divine Knowledge, and it is difficult for the eye to see such error. It is written in Chapter 28 of the second gate: "He who uses the words of the masters of Kabbalah based on his own reasoning—it shall not be so." Rather, one must be a **recipient** <term>Recipient: (Mequbbal) One who has received the oral tradition (Kabbalah) directly from a master.</term> from the mouth of a master who is an expert in Kabbalah, etc. And the greatest of the later commentators, **Rabbeinu Ramban** <term>Ramban: Rabbi Moshe ben Nachman (Nachmanides), a 13th-century sage and mystic.</term> of blessed memory, already noted this, saying that the words of the masters of Kabbalah cannot be understood or known at all through a book, but only from the mouth of a wise recipient. Human reasoning in this matter is a great mistake. For the matter of the Ten Sefirot is the core principle. Regarding what he said about the **evolution of things** <term>Evolution of things: (Hishtalshelut) The chain-like descent of divine energy from the Infinite into the material world.</term> and the multiplicity of thoughts from the **Simple Unity**, may He be blessed: the philosophical view is that from the first cause, a single intellect emanates, and from its contemplation of itself, another intellect and a sphere emanate, and so on. This would imply "two powers" <note>A term for the heresy of dualism.</note>, heaven forbid! They do not realize that everything is from the Name, as in "In the beginning, God created the heavens and the earth." The masters of the Divine Service received that this verse speaks of the lower worlds being within the higher ones, etc. The "Fruits" in the lower worlds hint at the final Kingdom. This indicates that no created thing can stand alone by its own power in the higher or lower realms. For He is great and stands over all, like a king in his palace. When a king is honored in a province, the citizens are honored with him. But the Holy One, Blessed be He, is not so; rather, He alone created the world, He alone is honored in the world, and He alone is glorified in His world. Rabbi Tanchuma said: "Because You are great and do wondrous things, You alone are God" <note>Psalm 86:10</note>. You

<column-break/>

alone created the world. Behold, according to this, the wisdom of creation is not shared with anyone else. He alone created the world, and there is no other power with Him in His creation. It is as you said: "You alone are God, You alone," etc. And if it were as this [philosopher] Rabbi thought at the end of this misguided chapter—and this is his language: "Regarding the evolution of things from the First Cause, which is the surrounding sphere, etc., and it influences the power of the spheres and their bodies..." and all the other intellects and their bodies, and from the tenth [intellect] flows all matter beneath the sphere of the moon—then, according to his view, God did **not** create the world alone!

But the view of our Rabbis of blessed memory, the recipients of the truth, is that the creation of the heavens and the earth preceded the creation of the angels. They said in the Midrash: "When were the angels created? Rabbi Yochanan said they were created on the second day... Rabbi Luliani bar Tabrin said in the name of Rabbi Isaac: whether according to one view or the other, everyone agrees that they were **not** created on the first day." Why? So that no one can say: "Michael was stretching the south of the firmament and Gabriel the north." Rather, Blessed be He, as it says: "I am the Lord, who makes all things, who stretches out the heavens **alone**, who spreads out the earth **by Myself**" <note>Isaiah 44:24</note>. The word for "by Myself" (*me-iti*) is written as "Who was with Me?" (*mi iti*)—meaning, who was a partner with Me in the creation of the world? On the first day, there was no angel! And so they said in the Midrash of Rabbi Nehunia ben ha-Kanah and in the Chapters of Rabbi Eliezer: the Holy One, Blessed be He, created the firmament and the angels... and these heavens and earth were created on the first day, as it says "In the beginning God created..." and the "Living Creatures" of the firmament were created on the second day. Rabbi Eliezer says the firmament which is above the heads of the "Living Creatures" (*Chayot*)... And the verse establishes the faith in creation, for the written word is "from Me" (*me-iti*), to let us know that creation is a part of the Creator, and that it was from Him alone, and nothing was added to Him. This is so that one should not imagine that there was any partner in creation, or that the "Intellects" were closer [to the process] because they are "influenced" [by God] as the aforementioned sage thought. As the Philosopher said, everything in the world of the Intellects flows from the First Cause—but the verse comes to negate this repulsive thought and to say that He, the Holy One, Blessed be He, is near, and He alone created, and there was nothing else with Him then. He did not receive influence from anything else, for everything was from Him, may He be blessed.

This sage did not understand that the "evolution of things" from the First Cause in a way of "cause and effect" is a branch of the "eternity of the universe" <term>Eternity of the Universe: The Aristotelian belief that the world was not created in time but has always existed as a necessary consequence of God.</term>. This view holds that everything exists by necessity, according to the opinion of the famous philosopher [Aristotle], which is a blow to the foundations of our holy religion. However, the wise men who believe in the Torah and the recipients of the truth know that everything was created with **Intention** and with a **Simple Will** <term>Simple Will: (Ratzon Pashut) The Kabbalistic concept that God creates through free will, not through logical necessity.</term>. It is not difficult for us to understand how Will can come from the First Cause while He remains absolutely simple. For this is the nature of Will: even while being in total unity and simplicity, He moves through His Will to show His actions. This is what is written: "He is in the One, and who can turn Him? And what His soul desires, that He does" <note>Job 23:13</note>. For He can do many things through His Will. This indicates His power, being the source of all existence. He is "in the One," for He did not create the rest of the world from other beings who were "branches" as the philosophers claimed. Rather, He was always in total power and life, and His ability shows His power, for I have received that He has no end... and what His soul desires, He does. For all beings are led by a Simple Will. He said that the desire was to complete the souls that He intended to bring to spiritual perfection... and this is because His power is sufficient. And because the plan of perfection and strength was sufficient to bring everything to pass, the **Intellect** is blessed...

<summary>This page argues against the philosophical view that the world was created through a chain of "Separate Intellects." Instead, the author asserts that God created the universe alone through His "Simple Will," citing Rabbinic and Kabbalistic sources like Ramban and the Midrash to prove that angels and other beings were not partners in creation.</summary>
<keywords>Sefirot, Malchut, Active Intellect, Simple Will, Creation, Ramban, Aristotle, Separate Intellects, Divine Unity, Midrash</keywords>
