<meta>This page continues the exploration of the Sefirot, transitioning from the theoretical nature of Divine Unity to the practical application of that unity through the service of sacrifices (Korbanot) and a critique of philosophical interpretations of these spiritual structures.</meta>

# Part of the Unity

## Chapter 6

Ten, and as for what is written: "You shall not make for yourself a graven image or any likeness of what is in the heavens above." The intention of "in the heavens" refers to the midpoint and upward—the stars and the constellations—and "above" refers to the **Angels**. "And what is in the earth below" refers to the element of water beneath the earth, even any small creature in the sea. And afterward: "You shall not bow down to them and you shall not serve them." For all of these are merely "vessels" like us <note>The author emphasizes that even celestial beings are created tools, not deities.</note>, and all unique worship belongs to the **Creator** alone, to recognize and believe in Him alone. This is the great secret unique to His Unity—that there is nothing outside of Him, even though all was created. Heaven forbid we should think otherwise of the Godhead, as we have explained.

## Chapter 6

From the matters explained in these essays, we shall see and recognize the known connection to the Godhead, which is a "branch" of the Divine: the service of the **Sacrifices** <term>Sacrifices: "Korbanot" in Hebrew, from the root K-R-V meaning "to draw near."</term>. This is because the sacrifice is an act of **Unification** (*Yichud*) and a drawing near of the divine powers to one another, until they ascend in a single bond to the Godhead, reaching the place of Unity designated by the Tetragrammaton <note>original: "יהו' "</note>. Through the labor of this service, they receive the fruit of the sacrifice, which is the concealment and bringing-near of the powers. As our Sages of blessed memory said: "A fire, sparks of fire" <note>A reference to the Zohar's description of divine energy as a consuming fire</note>, meaning that the fire of the altar consumes and sustains. According to Rabbi Shimon <note>Rabbi Shimon bar Yochai, the traditional author of the Zohar</note>, the sacrifice (*Korban*) is called such because it brings the powers near (*Kariv*).

Or it can be said, according to the knowledge of our colleagues, that "sacrifice" is related to the language of "calling" (*Keryon*). Why is the sacrifice directed toward the Lord? So that all may be sanctified unto Him, down to His servants. It is to rectify the "Holy Brain" in its subtle purity, a hidden sacrifice to strengthen the "Crowns" (*Keter*) <term>Crowns: Referring to the Sefirot, the emanations of Divine light.</term>. This is done to receive from the Unique One and to wait for Him in His purity, so that **Mercy** (*Rachamim*) may be found in all the worlds. This is supported by the "Ten" which represent the fullness of **Wisdom** (*Chokhmah*). On this, one must live to be healed by Mercy, and not just any mercy, but specifically for the sake of the Lord and not for "Elohim" <note>In Kabbalah, the name "Lord" (YHWH) represents Mercy, while "Elohim" represents Judgment.</note>. We require Mercy and not Judgment (*Din*). So too said our Sages of the school of Rabbi Nehunia ben Ha-Kanah: "At the time when Israel offers a sacrifice before their Father in Heaven, He is sanctified." This refers to the Unification of the Godhead and Mercy. The sacrifice draws the holy powers together until they are "one to one," as an eye to an eye. The blessings then descend and are unified within the holy firstborns, a hidden process where the sacrifice is brought near.

Furthermore, the judgment is doubled for the bull <note>Likely referring to the bull offered as a sacrifice</note>. Therefore, the secret of the sacrifice is that it descends as a "cord" to our midst and is concentrated. As it says: "Hear O Israel, the Lord is our God, the Lord is One." This is the fruit of our Sages—the Sages of the Mishnah and the Talmud—in their final traditions: that the sacrifice is a unification of the powers, which is **Lovingkindness** (*Chesed*). It originates from the Supernal Chariot, which unifies all levels down to the end of Judgment. Its "pleasing aroma" indicates that this power and all the branches of the angels and the celestial songs are based on this secret. Through this service, blessing spreads through all the worlds, for abundance and existence come from the side of Unity and the drawing near of the holy powers to the place of the **Most High God**, who is the True and Unique Godhead. This would be impossible otherwise; abundance, blessing, and existence would be withheld from anything outside the essence of the Godhead. He who separates himself from this "all-encompassing" view of the Godhead cuts off the "branch" of the Divine. The Sages of blessed memory wrote this to explain the power of the Altar of the Lord. The secret of the sacrifice is that it ascends above the Altar first, and from there to Mercy. This is why it is called an "Altar to the Lord." This is the "climbing" that elevates and unifies everything in the Supernal Level, which is the **Cause of Causes**. This is the meaning of "He offered burnt offerings on the altar." Our Sages also said: "They shall come up with acceptance on My altar, and My house of prayer I will glorify." Similarly, with Manoah <note>The father of Samson</note>, we find the reason for the Altar; he first mentioned "above the altar," and afterward it "ascended." From this abundance, it rises to Mercy, and from Mercy to the Altar of the Atonement, and from there to the Cherubim and the lower beings. This is the meaning of "And the Lord smelled the pleasing aroma."

<column-break/>

## Chapter 7

The essay continues: the abundance is the most exalted of all attainments. Beneath it, one can deeply understand the wisdom of all things. Such was the tradition of all the Sages, early and late: that the sacrifice is a unification and a bringing-near of the holy powers to the **Supernal King**, the source of everything, the **Root of Roots**. This was received from the mouth of our Teacher, the first Recipient <note>Perhaps referring to Moses or a foundational Kabbalistic figure</note>. The cycle of tradition, Rabbi Shimon bar Yochai, said in the *Book of the Palaces* (*Heikhalot*): "This is the sacrifice that rises for the Unique Unity, to satisfy each and every one as is fitting... to unify everything as one." This is a mystery in the Spirit, where "drop by drop" everything becomes included in the One as is proper. This stands against the "Adversary" (*Satan*); when the holy drops ascend, the whole is crowned and elevated with blessings. All the upper and lower beings are blessed from that Unique One. This is a desire that cannot be grasped by the worlds, for it is part of the radiance of the **Infinite** (*Ein Sof*). Everything is bound in a single bond through the chosen one. Furthermore, the sacrifice is the drawing near of the holy powers—this is the secret of the "tongues" of the service. This service indicates Unity. Herein lies the general principle of the faith of every living thing: the source of all expansion and the flow of abundance in the unification of the worlds. When the lower beings awaken through their service, the blessing is drawn down because the Unity is the place for all of this. As we wrote, the service of sacrifices teaches the binding of the holy powers and their unification. So they said in the *Zohar* of Rabbi Shimon bar Yochai: "Incense (*Ketoret*) is a bond (*Kesher*)." It is the binding of faith to the Holy Godhead, according to the true faith of Israel, to believe in the place of atonement. The Godhead is only answered through the Unique Unity, for every part is a unique portion of the Godhead.

## Chapter 7

We saw fit to introduce some of the wisdom of the Sages. In their knowledge, they wish to mention things that are impossible for a person to achieve through the path of **Inquiry** (*Chakirah*) <term>Inquiry: Medieval philosophical rationalism, contrasted here with Kabbalistic tradition.</term>. This was their error: there were in Israel sages who were both Kabbalists and philosophers, and they tried to answer the written Torah by using a "covering" to reach out to what can be grasped through general connection. They tried to prove through observation and contemplation how things move from potential to actual. They established the order of the world according to their own minds and became clever in the matter. Would that they had remained silent and been considered wise! Among them was **Rabbi Albo** <note>Rabbi Joseph Albo (c. 1380–1444), author of "Sefer ha-Ikkarim" (Book of Principles)</note>. In the second essay of the *Book of Principles*, chapter 31, he said: "When speaking of the spheres... the **Active Intellect** does not influence the existence of the effect... but rather it is according to the abundance in the matter." He wrote that the Holy One, Blessed be He, is the "Cause of all causes." But he did not write as we do. He said of the "Congregation of Israel" <note>Knesset Yisrael</note> that it is a "daughter."

In their review, they said the Sabbath indicates the renewal of the world. But the Kabbalists attributed each of the days of Creation to a different "Effect" from the separate Intellects. They called the spheres **Sefirot**. They said the first five are spiritual things and called them "Holy Crowns," and the last five were each attributed to one of the days of Creation. They called them "Crowns" according to the placement of the light of the spheres. On the Sabbath, the abundance rests. And they said...

<summary>This page explores the mystical purpose of animal sacrifices (Korbanot) as a mechanism for unifying Divine powers and drawing down blessing. It also begins a critique of medieval Jewish philosophers, like Joseph Albo, who interpreted the Sefirot through the lens of Aristotelian "Separate Intellects" rather than the Kabbalistic view of Divine Unity.</summary>

This page transitions into how the Torah and the Sefirot served as the blueprint and internal structure for the creation of the world.</meta>

# Chapter 8 | Part of the Unity | Chapter 8

<column-break/>

To teach the Torah: for when the Holy One, blessed be He, desired to create the world, as it is said: "Counsel is mine, and sound wisdom" <note>original: "לי עצה ותושיה" - Proverbs 8:14</note>, etc. The meaning is that in the **Ancient Torah**, which is Divine Wisdom <term>Wisdom: "Chokhmah," the second of the ten Sefirot, representing the initial flash of divine inspiration</term>, it included all qualities. For within it, all things were hidden during creation. Because of this, the Torah begins with the letter *Bet* in the word "In the beginning" <note>original: "בראשית" (Bereshit). The letter Bet (ב) has the numerical value of two, but the text here treats "Beginning" as the source of all.</note>, and He is the beginning of everything. The Sages explained that the "ancient ones" refer to the primordial scripts, which are the powers of Wisdom.

Furthermore, the world was created through **ten utterances** <note>The ten commands in Genesis 1, such as "Let there be light."</note>, and they are included in the general principle as it is said: "The Lord by **Wisdom** founded the earth; by **Understanding** He established the heavens; by His **Knowledge** the depths were broken up" <note>Proverbs 3:19-20</note>. The intention of the "ten" is that the ten utterances correspond to the **Ten Sefirot**, which are the general rule of the ten roots: **Wisdom** (Chokhmah), **Understanding** (Binah), and **Knowledge** (Da’at). Through these, everything exists. For the essence of Wisdom spreads into **Strength** (Gevurah), **Splendor** (Hod), and **Kingship** (Malchut), while the branches of Understanding spread into **Beauty** (Tiferet) and **Foundation** (Yesod). 

Wisdom is the general principle of everything, for "Wisdom is in its companion" <note>A kabbalistic phrase suggesting the interweaving of divine attributes.</note>, and they are the "Called Intellect" through which everything was created. As it is written: "How manifold are Your works, O Lord! In **Wisdom** You have made them all" <note>Psalm 104:24</note>. This Wisdom acts upon the upper and lower worlds through the power of Wisdom. This is what the Sages meant when they said: "He looked into the Torah and created the world."

In the Midrash of **Rabbi Shimon bar Yochai** <note>The Zohar</note>, it says regarding "How manifold are Your works": How many hidden works and holy emanations go out, and all are hidden within Wisdom. It says "You made them all in Wisdom"—meaning they were made in Wisdom but did not emerge into the light until they reached the stage of **Understanding** (Binah). When they were ready to be honored and perfected, it is as the verse says: "and by **Understanding** it is established." Therefore, "You made them all in Wisdom," but they were established through Understanding.

From all this, it becomes clear that the qualities of the **Ten Sefirot** were the "vessel" and the "place" for everything that was made and created in the upper and lower worlds. Without **Knowledge** (Da'at), there is no way to know Him at all. If so, it was necessary for the Emanation to spread out so that existence could be recognized and sustained. 

In the Midrash of **Rabbi Nehunia ben Ha-Kana** <note>The Sefer Ha-Bahir, one of the earliest kabbalistic texts</note>, they said: "I am the Lord, I occupy myself with the ten heavens alone," etc. "When I made this dwelling to delight in it, I and all the world, I spread everything within it and called its name 'All'—for the intellect depends on it, everything emerges from it, and everyone needs it," etc. It is beloved and beautiful. They explain regarding the Names of Emanation: "I was there when I made myself," and afterward, "I called to you even at the time I spread out my earth, in which I planted and supported this dwelling." Those who serve in uprightness and rejoice in them—who has seen the birth of my light?

The question was asked: "Was the Torah/World within Wisdom before it was formed?" He said to him: "Yes." It is like a **King** who sought to plant a tree in a garden. He came to see if there was a spring of water to sustain it. When he did not find one, he said: "Is it possible for it to grow?" What did he do? He dug and brought out a spring flowing with living water, and then he said: "I will plant the tree." And it stood and grew because he prayed constantly that it be watered by the spring. 

This **Tree** is what they spoke of in the Midrash: "It was a tree that has leaves," etc., from the power of the celestial stars. It is what they said in the Midrash: "A good merchant comes upon the King," and all its vitality and its beginning are suspended beneath it. That which we planted to delight all the world—from this Tree, there is existence. This is what it means that "the intellect depends on it, everything emerges from it, and everyone needs it." This Tree included the world, for without it, the world could not exist. The parable of the King finding water refers to the **Spring**, which is the source of the flow (*Shefa*) for everything. The Tree and the Spring come from the "Hidden Eden" that waters the garden to produce offspring. This Tree and its channels are the parable for the creation of the world. Wisdom saw that it was impossible for the world to exist unless there was water prepared beforehand to water the Tree—which is the world. Then He "dug and brought out water," meaning He brought down the Qualities which were the vessel of blessing through which the world would be sustained. And this is what the Midrash of Rabbi Shimon bar Yochai says regarding the portion of *Bereshit*...

<column-break/>

And behold, this matter which we have established is what is written: "His mouth is sweetness" <note>Song of Songs 5:16</note>, for He has given power to every hidden thing to be revealed. Because of the existence of those who deny <note>referring to philosophers or those who reject the Sefirot</note> the mediation of the Sefirot, they are deep within one another, and there is high and low among them. It is written that they all come from one root, and everything is within the "End" <note>Ein Sof/Infinite</note> that has nothing outside of it.

He wrote further: Regarding what you have observed about the "Living Creatures" (*Chayyot*) <note>The angels of the Divine Chariot</note>, they act not by thought, speech, or deed, even though there is nothing outside of Him. I am here to say something that might make Him seem limited—for anything limited can be measured, and in His power, there is no change or end. Yet, we follow what is written: that He acts in the manner of a "limit"—He comes, He goes, He speaks, He says—and all these terms are applied to Him.

If you say all this is according to the grasp of the human intellect, you already know that the intellect has a limit. All things found in the writings of the Sages regarding limits are actually about the "Limit of the Limitless." These "limits" are the Sefirot. All the orders of Creation and the orders of the Commandments <term>Commandments: Mitzvot</term> are arranged according to the Sefirot. The orders of the Sacrifices also testify to this. It is far-fetched to think that He speaks of two physical properties. All of this is understood without the Sefirot being considered physical or sensory; rather, the language is used because the Sages said: "The Torah speaks in the language of human beings." 

The grasp of Wisdom is through the intellect; there is a limit. But that which has no limit cannot be grasped or compared in any language. The order of the Sefirot, which is "a limit without limit," is called in *Genesis Rabbah* "the order of times." From the phrase "It was evening," we learn that there was an order of times before this <note>A famous midrashic idea that God created and destroyed worlds before this one</note>.

In the Midrash of **Rabbi Nehunia ben Ha-Kana**, he said: "The living creatures were in the firmament," hinting at the **Ten Sefirot** with which heaven and earth were sealed. Those ten correspond to the **Ten Commandments**, and within those ten are included all **613 Commandments**. It is known that these "Living Creatures" are the vessels of action; without them, no action would be possible. They are under His supervision, for they are like a "pen" used by a scribe to show His work. 

There is nothing besides the Perfect One, and everything is from Him. We use these names like "Merciful" or "Jealous" only to bring the matter closer to the human intellect. For it is impossible for the soul to grasp His true intent. As our Sages said: "The Torah speaks in the language of human beings." Thus, they are the order of all existing things, and the order of the Torah is the same. The intellect cannot exist except through them, for they are the vessels through which the divine flow (*Shefa*) speaks to the world. Until the "Ancient of Ancients, the Holy of Holies" <note>original: "עתיקא דעתיקין" - Atika d'Atikin, the highest aspect of the Divine</note> was arranged in these "rectifications" (*Tikunim*), the worlds could not exist.

The existence of everything in the world depends on the **Will** (*Ratzon*). The existence of both the lower and upper worlds is maintained as long as the "Emanated Souls" (*Nefashot ha-Atzulot*) remain within it. It has been explained that the survival of the worlds depends on these emanated souls, which are the "Heart" and the "Will." Without them, life and existence are impossible. Therefore, the emanated souls are a necessary part of the Unity...

<summary>This page explains that the Ten Sefirot serve as the essential vessels and "blueprint" through which the Infinite God creates and sustains the world. Using the parable of a King planting a tree near a spring, the author illustrates how divine influence (Shefa) flows from the hidden source through the Sefirot to maintain existence.</summary>

<meta>This page continues the exposition on the "Unity" (Yichud) of the Divine. It transitions into Chapter 8, which provides a philosophical and Kabbalistic defense of the "Ein Sof" (The Infinite) using the teachings of the early masters of Provence and Catalonia.</meta>

# Chapter 7 | Part of the Unity | Chapter 8

<column-break/>

# Chapter 7

The worshiper [strives] toward the acquisition of all virtues and attributes which, according to the Torah, lead to the proper perfection. Through these, many are included, and through them, everything lives and gives birth to the laws of the Torah. For the Torah preceded this multiplicity of virtues and attributes to complete this law. And in its separation, "the Holy One, blessed be He, desired to merit Israel; therefore, He gave them many Torah [laws] and commandments" <note>This is a famous quote from the Mishnah, Makkot 3:16, suggesting that the abundance of laws is a gift to help people achieve spiritual merit.</note>. 

And it says "many" to indicate that just as a specific reward is granted for a multiplicity of virtues and attributes at the time of death, so too—even though the General Reward in the gatherings relates to a simple root—it exists for a single purpose: the preservation of all existence and the prevention of the destruction of one part by another. Thus, all parts stand upon the position of the whole, ordered by a single, simple gaze, blessed be He. This is the secret of the "multiplicity with Him," for despite the multiplicity and diversity of those who receive [the divine flow], they do not deviate from the core. Just as the brain, in its various parts, remains unified in its simple warmth, so too the Holy Mind <term>Mind: Often referring to the Sefirah of "Chokhmah" (Wisdom) or the primordial divine intellect</term>, despite its many simple words, acts as a unified whole.

This agrees with what was stated above, that in the related "End" (Sof), there is a simple and infinite compassion and will. It is known to the Sages that "one good thing" from Him is preferred over many, for His power, His will, and His ability are one. His names and the variations are only relative to us. Just as the root of the Name is one, so too the multiplicity in the "gatherings" <note>Likely referring to the assembly of the Sefirot or the community of Israel</note> does not necessitate multiplicity in Him. Rather, His double strength toward the world and its order testifies to His oneness. 

Therefore, the order of the Table <note>Perhaps referring to the "Table" of the world or the "Set Table" of the Law</note> encompasses all rests together—life for one and a body for one. And everything that is closer to the "Hidden Individual" <term>The Hidden Individual: A poetic term for God as the ultimate, singular source</term>, blessed be He, is more unified. This was done to demonstrate the simple compassion that comes entirely from Him. Following this pattern, He ordered the law of Man, who is a "Small World" (Microcosm) <term>Microcosm: The idea that the human body and soul mirror the structure of the entire universe (the Macrocosm)</term>, whose secret is in the form of the "Great World" (Macrocosm). All of this is to indicate and awaken the mind to the "Hoped-for Unity."

And in the **Midrash of Rabbi Shimon bar Yochai** <note>The Zohar</note>, peace be upon him, they said: "One world," and it is written, "and all the host of the Lord" <note>Exodus 12:41</note>, etc. Rabbi Yannai and Rabbi Yossi said: "Fortunate are Israel more than all other nations, for they have a portion in the Holy King." Through them, the world is established so that it is not called [a place of] shame. Israel rises through the Torah because it is said "as one" to be bound together. Israel is the level that sustains the world; they are His standing and the existence of the entire order of the Unity when they perform the will of their Master.

And come and see: the general principle is that a person in this world should prepare themselves as a "light" and a "voice." The world undergoes change and addition through the wisdom of bodies, to fix a portion for every fear and addition, and strength for every body. All the aids of the body support the "Eye" <note>Metaphor for spiritual perception</note> and the "Voice." And it is established in the root of the Upper World, which is the Place and the Head that stands above. This is to bind everything together. This "light" is for the repair of the world, making it into a body, and to repair the supports of the body for everyone. 

And all the body and all those aids for the Eye are an "Anxiety of the Heart" for everything, and everything is included in it. This is to bind and awaken the active power above. Thus, everything accepted upon itself the Kingdom of the Sea to sustain it and to guard all the settlement of the earth. It is remembered by all material natures to investigate the strength and the foundation in His wisdom. To every mind, there are "Heads" and "Nests" to guard the "Prince of Powers," the Patriarchs, to guard the "skins" of Israel <note>Likely a reference to the "garments of light" or the protection of the nation</note>.

There is no "sitting" in the world that is not for the Kingdom of the House of David. The "House of the Tent" <note>The Tabernacle</note> and the "House of the King" are called the "Palace" (Heikhal) and are appointed to the **Holy of Holies**. There you find the **Ark-cover** (Kaporet), the **Cherubim**, and the **Ark**. Everything is "as one" for the whole world. All of these are the supports for the body. And all this is to express the hiddenness of the "Head" and for the honor of the One who does not resemble anything...

<column-break/>

The Lord is before him forever. In the Spirit, he shall be called "extended," and the Exalted Cause is spared. 
Is it a wonder that above the Glory, it extends from the Glory? It exists by the power of Speech to remove many obstacles that receive natural traits, engraved from the subtle nature. They are called the "supports" that carry them, and they are called the **Four Chariots** <note>The Merkavah: The divine throne-chariot described in Ezekiel's vision</note>, and they are called the **Six Horns** <note>Likely referring to the six "extremities" or the six Sefirot from Chesed to Yesod</note> which possess loftiness.

Come and see the "acquisition of skins" <note>original: "קניין עורות"</note>... there is no "sitting" in the world except in the King. In every path, all the ways that come are unified and established. In the "Clear Light," they are found there in the "Assembly of Bodies," and merit is found in it. There is no higher place to serve than the place of the "Head of the Pious One," a fountain that stands over you until it reaches the place called the **Holy of Holies** in its entirety. From there is the end of all heights. These are the "appointed ones" above, and all of this is "Flame." This "Glow" (Nogah) is forever above. And all of them belong to the Exalted King until he is found for every "Ark" from the exalted burning... until this is bound to this, and this to this, until...

And their intention in what they explained of His **Holy Name**, blessed be He, is through contemplation of its prior "nesting" until the "resting" of everything... for he created **Three Sanctifications** <note>The "Kadosh, Kadosh, Kadosh" of the angels</note> alone. Know that He alone created the world. And if the "separation" were like a division, the Holy One, blessed be He, would have placed Mercy in a far-off and circular path. As the "Master of Principles" <note>Rabbi Joseph Albo, author of *Sefer Ha-Ikkarim*</note>, of blessed memory, wrote: the opinion that He created from a "duality" or "multiplicity" must fall. If the creation existed in a way that they could not approach or grasp one another, it would be a "separated" existence. But the intention of the Name is to indicate the **Unity of the Hidden Structure**. 

After we have imagined the introduction and its entry into a true general principle, we shall give a sign for all the connection and the unification of one part with another, up to the "Cause" of the **Hidden Structure**. This is the Name that testifies to His Unity, as was said: "And we shall swear." There is in the hearts, in the name of Wisdom, a testimony to Him, saying: "**The Lord by Wisdom founded the earth; by Understanding He established the heavens; by His Knowledge the depths were broken up**" <note>Proverbs 3:19-20</note>. The exalted intention in this is that through this, He encompasses the world in a "Male Name" and a "Daughter"... as will be explained further in Chapter 17 of this part.

And this is the language of the Author, the Kabbalist **Rabbi Azriel** <note>Azriel of Gerona (c. 1160–1238), a central figure in early Kabbalah</note>, of blessed memory, receiving from the mouth of the Kabbalist **Rabbi Isaac the Blind** <note>Yitzhak Sagi Nahor, the most famous early Kabbalist of Provence</note>, etc. [And] the **Rashba** <note>Rabbi Solomon ben Adret</note>, of blessed memory, who was the third of the "Heads" <note>The chain of tradition from Isaac the Blind to Azriel to Rashba</note>. 

He added the following to stand, saying: there are ten things [at the] foundation of its secret. For I mean to say that there is nothing there but the **Ein Sof** (The Infinite) alone. 
**The Answer:** The **Ein Sof** is perfection without any lack. If you say He has power without limit (infinite) but does not have power within a limit (finite), you diminish His perfection. And if you say that the "Being" that emerges from Him exists in a way that there is an "End" (limit) in the world, then His perfection would be lacking the very power that comes from Him. 

Because His perfection has no "other," we must say that He is "within the limit" and "without a limit." And since everything exists from Him, we find here the "mediation." There is a "root" and there is a "lack." The souls receive from their nature, but from His perfection, there is "wonder" in them. When the "End" (limit) is prevented from the Messiah <note>unclear reading, possibly "from the flow"</note>, there is a "lacking power" in them. Therefore, they have the power of action in both perfection and lack. Perfection and lack are the opposites that bear the "passers-by," for one thing [leads] to another. 

And if you say that He alone [created] the world without lack, one must answer that the "intention" [of creation] would then indicate a lack in the one who intends. And if you say that He did not "intend" the creation, then the creation would have been by chance. Anything that comes by chance has no order. But we see that the created beings have an order upon order, a meaningful name. By order they are bound, and by order they are received, and the connection...

By His hands, He led us through grace, and they received them—meaning, you shall know the details. Why is there kindness in this? Because the King has provinces, and so it is the truth within everything. It is said that "Kindness protects our camp," and they are the ones who know His glory. # Chapter 9 | Part of the Unity | Chapter 10

## Chapter 9
The language and the explanation of its opening regarding the reason for it being called "of its kind" and not "of my kind," like the shell of a point and a period. To cut off the cutting of mercies and to pass through the palace so it may be called for its repentance, prepared for evil and its companion, for the movement toward the benefit of the worlds, and a moist and evil spirit before its base. This is what I have increased to explain in this chapter:

### Chapter 9
The practitioners of the [Divine] service <term>Practitioners of the service: Those dedicated to mystical devotion and the study of the Divine</term> received a tradition that the Unique Master of the world—concerning His preciousness, the Holy One, Blessed be He, says He is the **Infinite** <note>original: "Ein Sof"</note>—is not hinted at, not in a choice like in the Prophets or in the Hagiographa <note>The "Writings" section of the Bible</note>, and not in the words of our Sages of blessed memory. However, they did receive a slight hint of Him, and I have already explained it in the previous section. This hint is thrown into the realm of number, yet He does not enter into calculation at all. The Sages of Truth <term>Sages of Truth: A traditional title for Kabbalists</term> said that concerning Him, they stated as a general rule: "Do not occupy yourself with hidden things." Because He is hidden in the ultimate concealment, even the hint of Him is that He is the "End of our light," an end that the hand of thought cannot reach due to the greatness of His hiddenness.

From His hiddenness, they wrote of the virtue of the **First Emanation** <term>Emanation (Atzilut): The process where Divine light flows into structured attributes</term>, which is His Name, and He is within it. Through the chain of descent, a higher spirit is cast upon the multitude of movements and hiddenness. Therefore, they believed in the "entryway of the attributes," yet He cannot be grasped by the connection of the heart at all, as we wrote regarding what He is. Even in the First and Second Emanations, the practitioners of the service received that there is no power to draw out an inquiry, because they are outside of understanding and His world. No one has the ability to contemplate Him. Within our world and its understanding, which is from the "calculation" <note>likely referring to the Sefirah of Binah/Understanding</note> and below—which are the **Seven Days of Creation**—is where investigation is possible; but from there and above, the gate is closed.

The Sages of Truth received that this hint of ours is mentioned in the Scroll <note>The Talmudic tractate Megillah or Chagigah</note> regarding four things: one does not investigate the **Foundation**. They said: "Is it not from the day that the world was created? Ask of the first days... from one end of the heavens to the other." This implies that there is a divider and a distinction between the aforementioned Beginning and the First Day, and so on. This means "from the day," even though you might ask what is below it, what is above it, what is beyond it. Truly, these two are difficult. From the end of the heavens to the end of the heavens, you may understand, but you may not understand what is above, what is below, what is before, and what is behind.

Behold, they explained that one has no permission to ask, to forbid, or to contemplate, except from the "calculation" and below, which is "from the end of the heavens to the end of the heavens"—His world. But from there and above, the hand cannot reach. In the Midrash of Rabbi Shimon bar Yochai <note>The Zohar</note>, peace be upon him, in the portion of *Vayeshev/Adam*, they said: they were made as a higher "K" <note>The letter Kaf</note> until it reaches here. From here and above, it is closed and hidden, and no place can be found for any inquiry to emerge. What remains for the worlds is "For in Yah, the Lord, is the Rock of Ages" <note>Isaiah 26:4</note>. This is a high and concealed secret. Therefore, in His Name, up to this point, there is permission for every blessing. But from here onward, there is no permission for any blessing to be found in Him, for He is blocked and hidden from all. And whoever comes to say that from "nothingness" <note>Ayin</note> the worlds were returned—because of His thinness until that place—Rabbi Yehuda used to mock him based on the verse, "For the Lord is King over the high heavens," etc. "And from the end of the heavens to the end of the heavens"—up to here there is permission to be found, but below that, there is no permission to merit to reflect upon it.

Behold, they explained that in the First and Second Emanations, man has no permission to debate or contemplate. The reason is that whatever is closer to the **Cause** is more hidden and more like the step of "non-existence" <note>or "nothingness"</note>. Regarding the Cause itself, may He be blessed, who is the height of heights and whose virtue is above all, it is impossible to contemplate Him at all, even though He is everything and in everything, and founded in everything. Out of the warming and the shortening of our senses, His virtue and greatness become publicized and recognized through the "Thirty [Paths]" from His foundation, for He is blessed at the head of all. His greatness is known through His actions, which He performs through them, so that we may perceive Him alone and not to intellectually "know" Him. Even with the importance of His attributes emanated from His glory, He is established in the name by His power, which is founded in our understanding and His delight. They proceed from them until they reach the "Endless" <note>Ein Sof</note> of His exaltation. Behold, He is at the head of the worlds, and His virtue is in them even while being hidden from all. For out of the revelation and contemplation of these things, it is said that the **Soul** shall rule in the worlds and even every creature. But in its importance in its worlds, in the limbs of the body, the vitalities act within them, and by looking at the heart, we recognize its virtue.
<meta>catchword: and the aspect</meta>

<column-break/>

and the aspect of its understanding. Such is the parable and the analogy: before every virtue, the **Crown** <note>Keter</note> and **Wisdom** <note>Chokhmah</note> are at the head. His greatness, virtue, and fullness are found in the truth of His attributes. He is in the virtue of the soul within the body. From there, our hearts recognize His essence and greatness, which would not have been possible without His emanation. Just as it would be impossible to know the virtue of the soul and the thought within it without the limbs of the body through which it acts—for it is the spirit of life that guards it—and "from my flesh I shall behold God" <note>Job 19:26</note>. That is to say, from the traits of the body, one understands the power of the soul. This is what I wrote: that the virtue of the soul is present and stands throughout the whole body, being at their head, and its actions are through it, and it is revealed and known through its existence.

So is the parable regarding the matter of **Emanation** <term>Atzilut</term>: through the Emanation alone is the existence of the Unique Master, the Emanator, revealed and known. If so, the emanation of the virtues—which chain down in truth and in His attributes—was necessary and agreed upon in order to recognize His kingship and virtue. We must recognize in our intellect that due to the magnitude of His hiddenness and His being elevated above all, it would not be possible to recognize Him or contemplate Him if not through [Emanation]. The Ramban <note>Rabbi Moshe ben Nachman, a 13th-century scholar</note>, of blessed memory, wrote in his commentary on *Sefer Yetzirah*: "There are his names, and therefore the attributes were made, etc.," to establish them in the **Infinite** <note>Ein Sof</note>. Thus, what we hinted at in its light is clarified: the shining of the light of Emanation and its expansion in the line of the "Will" was for the purpose of contemplating Him, recognizing Him, and knowing His existence and His unity. This is what we hinted at to serve Him in this chapter.

## Chapter 10
The one who performs an action <term>The Actor (Po'el)</term>, everything he places is more than the "Name," and possesses more virtue and perfection than the "Act" <term>The Result (Pa'ul)</term>. This is the ultimate perfection. Whenever the Actor is related to the Act in existence, and His virtue is far greater than the virtue of the Act, and His existence is infinite so that he is not affected—He is unified with this Act and not separated from it. This indicates that the Actor is the Root, complete in every side, in the ultimate perfection. From Him, the one who understands will be prepared to know the existence of the Act and its perfection. None of this would be lacking if the Actor were separated from the Act and outside of it.

The "Calculated Agreement" stated that all the Sages have already agreed and concluded that it is fitting for the proven Intellect, may He be blessed, to be [free] of any deficiency, for He is Perfection itself. Therefore, they said that because the Emanation is a perfection of all sides of justice—for it is the perfection of the counted—His power, virtue, and perfection are His Will. When it was not yet created, His power was not separated from the source of the Emanation. It is a perfection without deficiency because it is within the Emanator in His unity. This is not the case with **Creation** <term>Beriah</term>, which is the "limitation," being outside the Source and blessed by it.

This distinction between the two leads us to the Actor quickly. [Creation] does not indicate Him at all because it is far from Him, unrelated to Him, not of His value, and not similar to Him. How can one know the "How" of what was before all beginnings? One must remember the virtue of the "Name" as it is without the "Name." When the creature is counted in an analogy from Him, it is not known at all. However, as the "Name" is, so is it without Him in the conduct of His existence. For only that which He emanated has a value and similarity to Him, in that which is within the Emanation. From it, we contemplate Him to know His existence and recognize His perfection.

The Emanation that exists from Him was the beginning of the emanation of His attributes, so that the power of the Emanation would be perfect. This is not the case with the power of Creation, which is deficient. If there were no Emanation derived from Him, we would be walking in a void; we would not recognize the fullness of the perfection that comes from the Infinite. For in every creature, a limit is tied and found. Not so in Emanation, for we have said that its power is to influence in perfection without deficiency, being founded in its Root, which is the Source of perfection and fullness. If so, His Emanation was from the drawing out of His elevation over His Emanation and His perfection, so that it would have a relationship, value, and similarity to Him—which is not the case with any of the created beings. Some verses from the [psalms of] "Watchman" bear witness to all this, attributed to the limbs, as it is written in the scripture: "By your life, O my God," for He is the Master of the Kabbalah, for He is...
<meta>catchword: He is</meta>

***

Using the analogy of the soul and body, the text explains that the Divine attributes are the necessary bridge for human understanding of the Creator's perfection.</summary>

# Chapter 12 | Part of the Unity | Chapter 12

<column-break/>

Glass is colored by one dye or another, and the glass changes [in appearance]; then, every face seen through the glass appears clothed in all the colors of that glass. One who is lacking in wisdom and understanding might say that the color originates from the light itself. However, the reason returned to the wise and discerning man is that he shall understand and know with a clear eye that the color is not from the light. For the light itself <note>original: "chazar ha-ta'am," literally "the return of the taste/reason," here meaning the essential nature or the reflected logic</note> does not change and is not altered; it possesses no division or separation. The nature of division and separation belongs only to the "receivers" <term>Receivers: Created beings or physical objects that catch and manifest the Divine light according to their own capacity</term>. For those lacking understanding, the simple Unity seems to be missing from the colors they perceive, as if it had been nullified.

---

<margin>According to the honor of their kind, the soul is recognized through its wondrous powers... according to the knowledge of the day and the names. Know and contemplate on a festival day the simple essence of the Actor, who is investigated in all things... the simple essence is brought closer through repentance.</margin> He is the actor of all language. Moreover, the superior kindness has permitted us to say of the Holy One, Blessed be He, that "the Lord is a man of war" <note>Exodus 15:3</note>, yet He possesses everything according to His will. From His single will emerge diverse actions in a single moment. For He is compared to the created beings, and some of His actions are called "cooking," "whitening," "blackening," or "burning." A living person who knows the reason for these divisions will think of them as diverse powers. Yet, they all emerge from a single simple essence. In one place, He provides, in another He burns; in one He brings rain, in another He acts in a contrary manner. One thing He melts, and another He causes to freeze and congeal. Is there a lack of material? These are all the result of a single act of kindness, for His action is of a single nature. Indeed, all these variations of action occur on the side of the "receivers," without this necessitating any multiplicity in the Essence of the Whole. Just as diverse actions are written of Him, the recipients experience Him through their own strengths and changes, yet this does not imply multiplicity in His Essence. His action is perceived only through the effect, like the sun and its movement. Even in human action, there is a hint of this: a single person performs diverse actions—at one moment he acquires traits, then he tears, sews, runs, or cries. Many such varied actions come from one source.

<column-break/>

...without change, for this is His being and His essence. His action is such that it brings existence into complete division from its beginning. Therefore, everything is one simple thing. Just as wisdom is His wisdom and His attributes are His, so too the soul has different names according to the variation of its actions. Sometimes it is called "admonishing," sometimes "natural," and sometimes "vital," even though it is a single contemplating essence. The simple essence and its crown are divided in the essence of the powers and their paths. The variations seen here are in relation to the diverse things being viewed from the beginning of the powers. To the Holy One, Blessed be He, there is no end, for He is the source of all honors. All that is said of Him here is to illustrate His praise, as it says in his parables: "I have told you today, even you" <note>Proverbs 22:19</note>. For He is One, above any name, secret, or sign. Listen to the words of the wise! It is true in my opinion that this is hidden in the Scripture, as in "and it shall be prepared on your lips." For after you have cut and heard the words of the wise, be careful regarding the "receiving" sages <term>Receiving sages: Kabbalists who have received the oral tradition (Kabbalah means "reception")</term> who explain the variation of actions. One must hear this from the mouths of those who know the secret, the ancient sages. Therefore, return to the study and the reception. For the intention of the Blessed One is impossible to grasp through human logic, as He is above all logic. Therefore, they hide the Essence, as it is written: "The secret of the Lord is for those who fear Him" <note>Psalm 25:14</note>. The place of knowledge is with Him. The verse "that they may be preserved in your belly" means that his mouth and heart should be equal in his words, as they were received from the mouths of sages. It says "today" to indicate the time in which it will be, a prepared wisdom like the sounding of a bell, with the intention of the heart being to be unified with Him. He made this known to us so we would know Him.

<margin>Another explanation: The more one is organized and established, the more one can understand the power of the Hero. This is the nature of the witnesses... this verse "I have told you today" means I have made known the simple essence. Regarding the future, His actions are diverse, but the internal is simple. The simple honor is the secret of "today." These two simple attributes are the secret of "The Lord is our God, the Lord is One." He is one God in diverse worlds according to the receivers. He is the God of gods who stands forever.</margin> "I have told you today, even you." Even if these diverse actions appear—changes and different powers—one should not think, Heaven forbid, that they necessitate multiplicity or division in His Essence. For the "Day" is the source of simplicity. The knowledge of the variation of actions does not necessitate multiplicity, as established above. This is the meaning of "even you"—all that has been received concerning the soul and the Holy One, Blessed be He. And in the words of R.S.L. <note>original: "Rashbi," Rabbi Shimon bar Yochai, the traditional author of the Zohar</note>, peace be upon him, they said: "The Ancient of Ancients" <term>Ancient of Ancients: A Zoharic term for the most hidden, primary level of the Divine</term>. If He is one, and in Him all things are one, they do not change. What then is the difference between one and the other? It is like a tree; the branches spread out this way and that, but they all draw from the same root. As the holy verse says: "The secret of the Lord is for those who fear Him." In the Midrash, the sages said: The heretics asked Rabbi Simlai, "How many gods created the world?" He told them a reason based on the verse "Ask now of the days of old" <note>Deuteronomy 4:32</note>. They said to him, "We see there are many names!" He replied, "It does not say 'The Gods spoke' [plural], but 'God spoke' [singular]." The Holy One, Blessed be He, said to Israel: Because you see Me in many images, do not say there are many gods in heaven. Know that I am the Lord your God who brought you out of Egypt. The intention is that the multiplicity of names like "Elohim" <note>A name of God that is plural in form but singular in usage</note> is not a division in His Essence, but according to the relationship—to the elder He appears as an old man, to the youth as a warrior. The Essence is perfectly simple, and the multiplicity of attributes exists only in the powers and the variations of action. He used the parable of voices to honor all the actions. Because they were in the Divine Essence, the verse speaks in the singular—"He spoke from the midst of the fire"—not "they spoke." Because the power of the Holy One, Blessed be He, is infinite in action, and even when manifested in a finite way, the world cannot endure it...

It emphasizes that while God may appear as a warrior, a teacher, or a judge, these variations exist only from the perspective of the "receivers" (creation), while the Source remains a perfect, simple Unity.</summary>

# Chapter 12 | Part of the Unity | Chapter 11

From his words, as in the chapter of Rabbi Levi Isaac, until the end: "Before the world was created, the Holy One, Blessed be He, was alone." The intention is to say that because He was absolute unity, there was no "thing" or "action" <note>original: "davar u-fo'al"</note> in the sense of our changing perspectives. Because there was no end-goal created to receive [His light], He was like a simple essence, stripped of everything except His own will, which is good in its own right.

The divisions we perceive arise from the perspective of the "receiver," <term>Receiver: In Kabbalistic thought, created beings act as vessels that receive and filter the infinite Divine light into specific forms.</term> for there was no world there to act upon. Everything was a simple essence. After the world was created, various essential perspectives appeared according to the changing actions received by different receivers. This does not imply a multiplicity in His essence, but only a change in the receivers.

His unity includes them all, guarding the good. When He is written [in the scriptures] as life, it is His will for all. The Holy One, Blessed be He, gives life to all. When He is written in the aspect of "the end," it is seen as a will that consumes, almost like a desire directed at the gravity of the world. And yet, the sages said, "The kindnesses of the Lord never cease" <note>Lamentations 3:22</note>. His kindness is in Him at all times, so that anger does not burn against everything. Anger and will, which seem like opposites to us, are only different from our perspective. He is always good to all, and the difference is felt by the receivers according to their actions. For one who walks a straight path, their capacity to receive will catch the good decreed by the Holy One, Blessed be He. But one who walks a twisted way receives the opposite, also decreed from God’s side, though He is only good and nothing evil originates from Him. It is like a sick person who meets a challenge on their path; their own illness causes them to stumble, yet in their heart they rage against God, thinking the change and the evil are in His essence. But no evil descends from heaven.

As in the statement of Rabbi Shimon bar Yochai <note>Rashbi: the traditional author of the Zohar</note>, "I do not see a lack in me, but a lack in the guilty." This is like the sun's heat. In the future, the Holy One, Blessed be He, will take the sun out of its sheath; the righteous will be healed by it, and the wicked will be judged by it.

"The righteous are healed" refers to the verse: "But for you who fear My name, the sun of righteousness shall rise with healing in its wings" <note>Malachi 3:20</note>. They will delight in it. "The wicked are judged by it" refers to the verse: "For behold, the day is coming, burning like an oven" <note>Malachi 3:19</note>. All this is one and the same. The sun in its essence is entirely unchanged. It is only that for the righteous, the sun provides warmth and delight, while for the wicked, it is a burning oven. The change is not in the sun, for each of these effects acts according to the different receivers. In one unified authority, it provides healing for the righteous and punishment for the wicked, according to their actions. They receive this from themselves; the change is not in Him, God forbid.

So it is with the written Name: He is good in His essence, and the perceived change is according to the one who leads. On this, the prophet's vision speaks regarding the knowledge of God: "And you shall take it to your heart that the Lord is God" <note>Deuteronomy 4:39</note>. The sun and its power are the proof. Just as the sun's heat can burn like an oven or heal, the change in actions and powers is not in the actor, but in the receivers. Take the sun as your proof that "the Lord is God" <note>original: "YHVH hu ha-Elohim," equating the Name of Mercy with the Name of Judgment</note>. The difference in Names does not necessitate a multiplicity in His essence, just as the different effects of the sun do not necessitate a multiplicity in the sun itself.

In truth, just as righteousness is one, so too the Name "Truth" is one. The Names of God are powers. Whether called "Righteousness" or "Healing for the Righteous" or "Punishment for the Wicked," it is all one simple essence without change. The change is from the side of the receivers, as it is written: "according to their actions." His proof is from the words of the Holy One, Blessed be He, to the soul... this is the secret of proper unity. Absolute unity is like the light of the sun within a flame. These things are from the side of the receivers, like the secret of the flame being seen through colored glass.

<column-break/>

As it says elsewhere, everything is included as one. Regarding the qualities of Rabbi Shimon bar Yochai: Rabbi Eleazar opened and said, "And you shall know this day and take it to your heart that the Lord is God." This is difficult. It should have said, "Know this day that the Lord is God," and then "take it to your heart." Why this order? Moses was saying: "If you want to stand on this truth and know that the Lord is God, then 'take it to your heart,' and then you will know it in your heart." Good and evil are joined as one. The Name of Mercy <note>YHVH</note> is the Name of Judgment <note>Elohim</note>; they are joined as one. And on this, "take it to your heart" to know this matter.

In the book "Wars of the Table" regarding the matter of unity, from the words of Rabbi Shimon bar Yochai: "Come and see the secret of the colors of the flame." There is a white light and a blue light. The white light is above and stays constant. The blue light is below it and is the "throne" for the white light. This blue light changes colors: sometimes blue, sometimes black, sometimes red. It changes according to what it consumes below. But the white light above never changes.

The intention is that the "Great Cycle" and the "Small Cycle" are the attributes of Day and Night. It is known that the small attribute is the secret of the blue light. It appears in different colors because of the changing ways we perceive it. This is why the verse says "the Lord is God." The source of the light is constant, like the white light. There is no change in the Divine Essence at all. It is like a cloud or a fruit—the actor is one, but the effects are many.

Therefore, the conclusion of the matter is that Godliness is simple and absolute. He does not move from action to action or from thought to thought, for He is simple in the ultimate simplicity. He is unified across all our perceived changes and attributes. Multiplicity and change exist only from the perspective of the receivers, as will be explained in the following chapters of this work.

### Chapter 12
->The change of Names and the matter of the Sefirot do not imply multiplicity<-
->in the Godhead at all; they are three perspectives<-

Sometimes He is called by the Name of Mercy <note>original: "YHVH"</note> because it signifies pure compassion, and sometimes by the Name of Judgment <note>original: "Elohim"</note> because it signifies law. These are not different entities, but a change in perspective as the Divine light spreads into different actions. When the scripture intends to show His kingship through pure mercy, it uses the Name of Mercy. When it intends to show His kingship through judgment and law, it uses the Name of Judgment. The same applies to the Sefirot <term>Sefirot: The ten attributes or emanations through which God interacts with the universe.</term> and all other Names. They all refer to one simple Essence, the ultimate simplicity. The multiplicity of Names and the ten Sefirot are only according to the changing actions perceived by the receivers.

<summary>This page explains that the perceived multiplicity of the Divine—such as different Names and the ten Sefirot—is a result of human perception and the varied nature of the created "receivers," not a change in God's simple essence. Using the analogy of the sun and the multi-colored flame, the author illustrates how one source can produce different effects (mercy or judgment) based on the recipient's state.</summary>

# Chapter 13 | Part of the Unity | Chapter 14

From the power of the Essence, the number is not complete in essence or in place except through specific perspectives of standing. Therefore, it is said: **Ten and not nine.** <note>A famous quote from the Sefer Yetzirah 1:4, a foundational text of Jewish mysticism.</note> Because the hearts of the wise needed to expand the number to **Ten**, which is the boundary in essence and in place, they also said: **Ten and not eleven.** Just as we began to explain concerning them, so too the "multiplicity" which is the "place" for that which exists arises according to Ten. It comes in the dust <note>This likely refers to the materialization of divine energy into the physical world.</note> to hint that "Place" <term>Place: In Hebrew, HaMakom (The Place) is a name for God, implying that the world exists within God, but God is not limited by the world.</term> exists through the power of the Essence.

The Ten is nothing but a single power. For there is no power less than five that would result in the Nine established in its preparation, which is a fourth to the Hiddenness from which comes the power of the eleven... <note>The text here engages in complex gematria and mathematical symbolism regarding the number of the Sefirot.</note> In the Book of the [unclear: Garden/Grudge], it is written: "Do not separate the end from the beginning" throughout all the **Ten Sefirot** <term>Sefirot: The ten creative powers or attributes through which the Infinite God interacts with the world.</term> in order to pour out flow and blessing to the lower world. He is the King who is written of as "sustaining all."

The word **Sefirah** <note>original: "ספירה"</note> can be explained as being from the language of **Sippur** <note>original: "סיפור" - telling or counting</note>, meaning that which illuminates the number within them. For in the **Infinite** <note>original: "Ein Sof"</note> there is no connection at all, nor can we say anything is lacking. We can also explain **Sefirah** from the language of "purity and brightness," as in the verse: "and under His feet was like a work of bright sapphire" <note>Exodus 24:10</note>. Or we could say that **Sefirot** comes from the language of "boundary" <note>original: "pinnar"</note>... and we can write: "Tell when the opening stands at the border." On this, our father Abraham (peace be upon him) focused in his book <note>The Sefer Yetzirah, traditionally attributed to the patriarch Abraham.</note> when he said: **Scribe, Book, and Story.**

Let it not enter the heart to say that because the wise count them, they are small parts; rather, why does he say **Ten**? Because everything established with a name has a limit. When one says "more," one reaches the point where the skin [of reality] ends, and everything around it has a boundary, a boundary for the kingship. Everything moves, and everything is divided into what is made from it as a square; once it is said three times three, they are nine. Thus you have the nine Sefirot. And since we have nine, we must say that everything established in a limit will be in the category of the "thick" [material], and everything that moves has a place.

If the Name is Ten and the Place is not Ten, this was the intention of the blessing: to direct the essence according to Ten and not nine. Upon this, the Sages (of blessed memory) based their intention when they said: **Blessed is the Place** <note>original: "Baruch HaMakom"</note>, as many do. The masters of Kabbalah wrote according to their tradition that we give names to these Ten Sefirot, a name for each one. Let the thought never arise that these names imply they are divided or separated from one another. As I have already informed you, they are weighed in the mind as perspectives.

On this, our father Abraham (peace be upon him) focused in his book when he said: **Bound like a flame to a coal.** This is a parable to say that just as in a coal there is a movement and guidance that is hidden, and there is no separation of the flame from the coal, so it is said of the **Infinite** (may He be blessed). For within Him is Wisdom, Kindness, Greatness, Strength, and Beauty—and all are from one place. Everything is in Him without separation, and all of them are hidden. This is the root of our faith. Concerning this, we mention the verse: **"Hear O Israel, the Lord our God, the Lord is One"** <note>Deuteronomy 6:4</note>. The meaning is that the Sefirot are ten but they are one power. For there is an end and a beginning, and they are all from the first **Infinite**. Even though they were emanated, they did not separate, but rather they remain with the Emanator. They are called "Emanations" <note>original: "atzilut"</note> from the language of "beside" <note>original: "etzel"</note>...

It has already been clarified that there was no change of mind in the Emanator, nor did He change in His beginning; rather, He revealed the power of His unity in the "Union of Life," and because they have a measure and a limit...

### Chapter 14

And they are ten in total, and the **Infinite**. This is the secret—that they have (God forbid) an end, and yet no end surrounds them. In the *Sefer Yetzirah* it says: "Ten Sefirot of nothingness <note>original: "belimah"</note>, ten that have no end." For that which is imprinted comes from the felt, and the felt from the intellectual, and the intellectual from the height of the hidden, and the hidden has no end. The intellectual, the felt, and the thought are in Wisdom, and the "Wise one in Understanding" <note>original: "Chakham bi-Binah"</note>. The explanation is that to **Understanding** <term>Binah: The second/third Sefirah, representing the processing or 'womb' of divine thought.</term>, which is in **Wisdom** <term>Chokhmah: The first flash of divine inspiration or intuition.</term>, there is a continuous draw... a draw from the height of the hidden... and the "Wise one in Understanding" means that he understands the draw in Wisdom through its preparation in Understanding... Therefore, he did not say in his language "Wise in Understanding and Wise in Wisdom" without a reason, but rather to show they are not separated. Behold, they are all one power, and all are the power of the **Infinite**. Other sages wrote concerning the secret of **Wisdom** which we brought above, with "nothingness" <note>original: "belimah"</note>, a full ten that have no end.
<meta>catchword: continues</meta>

<column-break/>

...the world, its foundation is called **El Shaddai** <note>One of the biblical names of God, often associated with the Sefirah of Yesod (Foundation).</note>. This is what they meant by "In His Torah He rises..." and in the Torah, the King of **Kindness** <term>Chesed: The Sefirah of expansive love and benevolence.</term> looks upon the world with the perspective of mercy. Sometimes there will be the attribute of **Judgment** <term>Gevurah/Din: The Sefirah of restraint, law, and justice.</term>, and sometimes it will be His will to sweeten the judgment with mercy. For this reason, the Torah is the attribute of Kindness.

Also, the Ten Sefirot are the generalities of the attributes called **Attribute of Judgment** <note>original: "Middat HaDin"</note>. The completion of the end is the **Seven Attributes of Construction** <term>Middot HaBinyan: The lower seven Sefirot (Kindness through Sovereignty) that directly govern the created universe.</term> which are for the needs of this world, to merit and to improve. These attributes exist within the Sefirot not in the sense of His essence, but in terms of separate perspectives. All these attributes are included within one another; in each one, there is both Judgment and Mercy to point toward the Emanator, who is the attribute of Blessing from which Judgment begins to roll.

She is the one who "rides the heights" to lead the world of Mercy from above. Therefore, the name of the **Foundation** <note>original: "Yesod"</note> called "The Visitation of God" points to them as written in the Torah, because it is tied together for the sake of Mercy. All of them are "included within one another" to show that they all come from one Root, and in Him they all live. Due to the high level of that attribute, even the perfect man was not worthy or able to reach it, for she is compelled to emanate the attribute. Certainly, that which is above her does not dwell within these attributes, for God forbid that we should attribute to them "preparation" or "guidance" except above their world. They have no "preparer" except in His very Essence.

As we have written, they are the foundation of the Torah and the attributes of the Name for the perfection of the levels in hidden and established things. From all this, it will be clarified that the necessity of His Unity (may He be blessed) is within us. These are the Ten Sefirot. I have already written that there was no change, neither in the Emanator nor in the emanated. Why? To this they hinted when they said: "Behold, I am the same as I was, and I am the same now." According to this, Hezekiah wrote... because they said "For Your sake," according to my actions.

Therefore, the name of God is written twice. He is called by every attribute: by **Elohim**, by **YHVH**, and so on, to be called by the changing attributes according to the change of perspectives and actions that flow from Him to His creatures. According to their "mixture" and the order of their reception, these things are considered.

If one were to think that there is a change in His Essence (God forbid) in the power and guidance of the attributes—which would imply He was not this way before—that would be a change in the Emanator. But when you look at this, the name of God is written three times to show that just as there is no change in Him, nor any "distance of mind" before He emanated, so everything that is fitting for these attributes remains true. He is one thing, always beyond all change and renewal. Though the change appears in the guidance and order of the Kingdom <term>Malchut: The final Sefirah, representing the physical manifest world.</term> more than it was in the beginning in the matter of the Infinite. Thus we say His powers are revealed... for the Name of the Attribute is justified in His essence. And so in the future, all these unions will be as they were before... and the understanding of the Sefirot does not necessitate any multiplicity at all. The secret is the secret of all, and everything is gathered into His absolute Unity. He is one within them. According to the change of perspectives, because of His divided actions, He is called by many names. We have mentioned the Ten Names to merit the specific attributes of the Name and to establish the emanations. Everything is from the One who is established. This is what I sought to clarify in this chapter.

It emphasizes that while God is called by different names (like Elohim or Shaddai) based on human perspective and the "receivers" of His light, His essence remains absolutely unchanged.</summary>
