The "house of my father-in-law" is the house of the Holy of Holies <note>In mystical thought, the Holy of Holies represents the innermost point of divine connection.</note>. This was the head of their lower levels for every world... and he went out in the joy of the house of the Holy of Holies, as it is written "to the Queen," and he was not to search anything from it, as it is said, "this is the tabernacle of the world." Afterwards, when it was drawn down, she was called "his daughter," "two thighs are your hips, my daughter" <note>A mystical interpretation of Song of Solomon 7:2, personifying the Divine Presence or the Oral Torah as a daughter.</note>. Further there: and because of this, they are all daughters, and all are depths, and all are purified, standing in their purity as is fitting. To us and to those outside, through the sweetness of the thighs, those outside and below are blessed, and all are the scholars of the **Oral Torah** <term>Torah She-be-Al Peh<note>The tradition of interpretation and legal rulings transmitted alongside the Written Bible.</note></term>, thus far.

Just as the **Written Torah** <term>Torah She-bi-Khtav<note>The Five Books of Moses, the literal text of the Pentateuch.</note></term> includes the six edges <note>The "six edges" or directions represent the six emotional Sephirot (divine attributes) that govern the physical world.</note>, so too the Oral Torah has six orders <note>The Mishnah, the core text of the Oral Law, is divided into six orders or "Sedarim."</note> corresponding to the six edges. And because the Names each include them all, the six orders became sixty tractates, to show that sixty teachings are directed as one, unified with one another, one branching from the other, providing strength and existence to one another. For there, the people and nations and Levites must study and refine them in their foundations... and secondarily in it day and night, as explained in its conclusions. For the Written Torah and the Oral Torah are the secret of day and night and the order of times. And they said in the chapter *Tamid*: "If not for my covenant day and night..." <note>Jeremiah 33:25; the Talmud (Tractate Shabbat) interprets this to mean that if not for the study of Torah, the laws of heaven and earth would not exist.</note> Rabbi Elazar said: The study of Torah is the rectification of day and night, as it says, "If my covenant be not with day and night, I have not appointed the ordinances of heaven and earth." And it is written concerning the Written Torah and Oral Torah that each is called a "Covenant," and they are Day and Night, and they are the ordinances of heaven and earth. And "The Lord God" is the full Name, the secret of the true Unity.

### Chapter 23

The beginning and Israel... and regarding the matter that we have understood... the secret of... one to gather the treasures of the building of the six of the Torah and the image of the six vessels of the word, the writings... and his house is complete, guarded over it, in all his house he is faithful. # Chapter 22 — Part of the Unity

I have written these things and writings, to teach them, and this is the **Talmud** <term>Talmud<note>The vast collection of Jewish law and tradition, serving as the primary text of the Oral Law.</note></term>. ## Chapter 21

->Also, that which is hidden within man and all the powers of the body are grasped by the depths of thought. From these depths, every place of holiness is established, both in general and in detail. Within these deep thoughts are included all the weaknesses of the "Vessels of the Unique Name" <note>The "Vessels" refer to the Sefirot or divine attributes that channel God's light into the world.</note> according to the way of the Elder. For the **Book of Genesis** <note>original: "Sefer Bereishit"</note> corresponds to **Holy Wisdom** <term>Chokhmah<note>The first sparked realization or 'seed' of an idea in the divine mind.</note></term>; therefore, it begins with the letter *Bet* <note>The numerical value of 2, hinting at the duality of creation.</note>. The **Book of Leviticus**, which contains the sacrifices, the order of the priestly service, the festivals, the laws of tithes, jubilees, valuations, and substitutions... corresponds to **Beauty** <term>Tif'eret<note>The central Sefirah, representing harmony and balance.</note></term> and its branches, left and right. This is the precious treasure of the Five Books of the Torah—He told them His desire. The **Book of Deuteronomy**, called the "Repetition of the Torah," corresponds to the **Final Heh** <note>The last letter of the Name of God, representing Malkhut (Kingship) or the Divine Presence (Shekhinah).</note> for those who know the secret, and its branches. Thus, there are five words, and "the Torah of the Lord is perfect, the testimony of the Lord is faithful" <note>A quote from Psalm 19:8.</note>. The testimony of the Lord and God is for the young men of Israel; their hearts live by the light of the burning heat that shall be for you and for the convert, unique in their faith in their dwelling as children of the Lord; and the Torah is "lacking" and delayed <note>A mystical concept suggesting that the Written Torah is incomplete without the Oral interpretation.</note>. And in the Midrash of Rabbi Shimon bar Yochai, peace be upon him, they said that the language of "sparing" <note>original: "chas"</note> stands in its place, not "lacking" <note>original: "chaser"</note>, for it is decreed for our freedom to look into the nullification of the inner self... and this power of our prayer... and this is from the book of the perfect ones... to remove the laws of exchange... and all the holy ones of his generations, and all the lights of his freedom... let the **Oral Torah** <term>Torah She-ba'al Peh<note>The tradition of legal and mystical interpretation passed down from Sinai alongside the written text.</note></term> be filled... everything is decreed and merit and depth and holiness for your life... for the investigation of the statute. And this is what makes His perfect ones famous in His congregation... for the sake of the trust in their holiness... and the opening for reception. And upon this, it is "spared" in its place—this is the Oral Torah; and its wonderful fats—this is the **Written Torah** <term>Torah She-bi-khtav<note>The Five Books of Moses in their literal, scribed form.</note></term>... until here. And in the dwelling of "sparing" is the Great Upper Whole, and the end includes the 248 positive commandments and 365 negative commandments... The Unique Name is the sum of the entire Torah. And the Torah is the aspect of the "Throne of the Lord" and the "House of the Voice." And because of its speech, the decree of the earth was distant from man... and in the end, he will cleave to man. And I saw a Midrash on the secret of the language: four holy letters were called **Adam** (Man), and upon them the Holy One, Blessed be He, said regarding the business of Man... a spirit to give life to the inner self of the Unique One... repentance for life... good positions... for as the Holy One, Blessed be He, is hidden in His world, so is this hidden in man. # Chapter 23 | Part: Unity | Chapter 23

The Torah, before Israel arose, was in the hand of the Holy One, Blessed be He. When Israel stood <note>referring to standing at Mount Sinai</note> and received the Torah—which had been prepared until that time—He delivered it into their hands. They had already been led from evil to good, stripping away the literal meaning <note>original: "peshat"</note> and returning it to the nature it possessed before the Holy Staff <note>or "the rod of the fall"</note>, through the letters of the Torah which were above it and its power. 

The meaning of **Sumira** <note>original: "sumira," an Aramaic term for a guard’s hut or bower</note> is a "booth" <note>Sukkah</note> and the **Divine Presence** <note>Shekhinah</note>, a place prepared for the Guardian of the Garden and the chamber from which to oversee and protect it from all harm. However, should a stranger enter it, he commits a sacrilege against the sacred. This is illustrated through the parable of the Assembly of Israel; therefore, the King to whom peace belongs said of her: "A garden locked is my sister, my bride" <note>Song of Songs 4:12</note>. Through the parable of the Temple of the Lord, reflecting the House of Israel and the House of Judah, it is said of them as well: "Solomon had a vineyard..." and this return was the place of thoughts, understanding, and transformation, held in the hand of the Holy One, Blessed be He. 

When Israel stood, He delivered it to them, for through the letters of the Torah, they act as agents and turn the wheel in His hand. From them, providence and protection spread to the whole world. They are the "great wisdom," the Torah and the Commandments <note>Mitzvot</note>, for a man is joined with his daughter, and our life bears fruit from her. This was hinted at and merited during the festival <note>likely Shavuot</note>, as it says in the Midrash on Exodus: "The Holy One, Blessed be He, said to Israel: 'I have sold you my Torah, and as it were, I have been sold along with it,'" as it is written, "that they take for Me an offering" <note>Exodus 25:2; the Midrash puns on 'take Me as an offering'</note>. 

A parable: To a King who had an only daughter. One of the kings came and married her, seeking to take her to his own land and claim his wife. The King said to him: "My daughter whom I have given you is my only one; I cannot part from her. I cannot tell you 'do not take her,' but I also cannot part from her. Rather, do me this kindness: wherever you go, make a small chamber <note>original: "kitton," a small bedchamber or dressing room</note> for me so that I may dwell with you, for I cannot leave my daughter." 

So said the Holy One, Blessed be He, to Israel: "I have given you the Torah. I cannot separate from it, yet I cannot tell you not to take it. Rather, wherever you go, make a house for Me where I may dwell within," as it is written: "And let them make Me a sanctuary, that I may dwell among them" <note>Exodus 25:8</note>.

The parable of the **ring** refers to that which was in the King's hand, and when his son stood, he delivered it to him. This is the **Shabbat**, which all the great ones of the kingdom fear and to whose will and commands they submit. As it is written: "And all the peoples of the earth shall see that the name of the Lord is called upon thee; and they shall be afraid of thee" <note>Deuteronomy 28:10</note>. Even the upper beings submit to his will and carry the sign of the Torah which is in his hand. More on this will come in the third part. 

In the Great Midrash on Genesis <note>Genesis Rabbah</note>, Section 5, it says: Rabbi Simeon bar Yochai said, "A book of lashes <note>unclear reading, possibly 'a book of stories'</note> was once traveling... they crowned him and honored him as a gardener..." <note>The text here summarizes a complex Midrash about the recognition of authority</note>. It has already been explained that the name of the Lord is added, and we are elevated by it even in all that is difficult to decree, except in the place and matter where it is explained that the "Seal of the Holy One, Blessed be He, is Truth" <note>Emet</note>, and the Torah is called "Truth."

The reference to **carpentry tools** hints at the "witness" which was the vessel of his sustenance for the whole world. Behold, the carpenter works upon the material of wood and stone according to his will through the craftsmanship of these tools. So too, the "Understanding" <note>Binah</note> of Israel acts within the space of the world according to its will, through the spiritual properties <note>segulot</note> within it. For like carpentry tools, the Torah was in the King's hand, for with it He created the world; and when His son stood, He delivered it to him. 

In the Mekhilta, Chapter 4, it says: "Speak to the children of Israel... the world was created for them, but your iniquities have separated you..." And in the Midrash of Rabbi Nehunia ben HaKanah <note>The Sefer HaBahir</note>, it says: "If not for your iniquities, there would be no difference between you and Him... they would create a world..." as it is written there. And in the Chapters of Rabbi Eliezer: "Immediately the Holy One, Blessed be He, said to the Torah: 'Let us make man.'"

The parable of the **treasures** concerns another world containing the Name of the King. The "Upper Servants" <note>angels</note> who are the mighty ones of the Chariot <note>Merkavah</note> show that they are the King's treasures which He was guarding. Once His son stood, He delivered them to him and they were revealed to him. Thus, Israel, through the Torah, achieves all that is in those treasures and they are revealed to them. 

They said in the *Midrash of the Letters* on the verse "The King has brought me into his chambers" <note>Song of Songs 1:4</note>: Rabbi Berekhya said, it is written "He declared to you His covenant" <note>Deuteronomy 4:13</note>—this refers to the Book of Genesis, which is the beginning of the world's creation, which He intended to be a crown for the wise...

<meta>catchword: laws</meta>

<column-break/>

...the Commandments <note>Mitzvot</note> which contain statutes and ordinances. These statutes are beneficial because the ordinances depend upon them, and they are proper only through them, as it says: "For it is a statute for Israel." 

**Statute** and **Ordinance** <note>Chok and Mishpat</note> refer to the **Written Torah** and the **Oral Torah**. These are the treasures that the King of Israel kept hidden until the Son—who is Israel—reached his maturity, at which point He delivered everything to him. It has already been explained that through the "seal" of Israel—those who occupy themselves with the secret and the divine manifestations—and by conducting themselves through the path of devotion and faith, which are the Written and Oral Torah, they are the treasures. Therefore, it is fitting that he should merit a "full portion," and everything comes from one source and one root. 

Therefore, "He declares His words to Jacob, His statutes and His ordinances to Israel" <note>Psalm 147:19</note>. It is known that the attribute of Jacob is **Truth**, as in "You will give truth to Jacob" <note>Micah 7:20</note>, and the Torah is called Truth—the "Torah of Truth." The Torah of the Holy One, Blessed be He, is one, and he has a portion in it. Rabbi Savikha <note>unclear name</note> said that Jacob himself is the Seal of the Holy One, Blessed be He—Truth. 

Rightfully, then, Jacob merits his attribute and the King delivers the seal to his son, for he merits the "wings of the law." The Torah, the Commandments, and Jacob are the secret of Israel's stewardship—examine this well. Israel has a "hold on the heritage" <note>a right to the property</note> to receive the Torah. But the other nations, who are from the side of the "husk" <note>Kelipah, referring to the forces of impurity</note> and the spirit of impurity, did not merit to receive the Torah: "He has not dealt so with any nation; and as for His ordinances, they have not known them" <note>Psalm 147:20</note>. 

As they said in the *Pesikta*: Rabbi Simon said, "These are the thoughts that were delayed so that the nations of the world would not clarify the Torah, and so that the 'beginning' would be kept for Israel to double our reward." Rabbi Simon said, "All Your thoughts toward us are marvelous." The Holy One, Blessed be He, was thinking and calculating thoughts from the beginning, passing over many generations and many people, and once He saw the "descendants" <note>Israel</note>, He delivered the Torah to them. 

In the Jerusalem Talmud, Tractate Rosh Hashanah, Chapter One, they said: Rabbi Simon said, it is written "Many things You have done..." In the past, You did many things. From now on, "Your blessings and Your thoughts are toward us."

Rabbi Levi gave a parable: To a King who had a **Chief Steward** <note>original: "archigon," from the Greek for a high official or record-keeper</note>. Once his son stood, he delivered it to him.

<margin>Sumira</margin>
Rabbi Yosi said: It is like a King who had a **guard-booth** <note>Sumila/Sumira</note> or a hut; once his son stood, he delivered it to him. 

Rabbi Acha said: It is like a King who had a **ring**; once his son stood, he delivered it to him.

Rabbi Meiza said: It is like a man who had **measuring tools**; once his son stood, he delivered them to him.

Rabbi Isaac said: It is like a King who had **treasures**; once his son stood, he delivered them to him.

The Rabbis said: It is like a King who had the **keys to the storehouse**; once his son stood, he delivered them to him.

The explanation of Rabbi Simon's words "In the past, You did many things" is what they said in his name in the *Pesikta*: that before the Son arose, the King Himself was calculating and managing. This is the parable of the one who guarded the treasures and the like. Once the Son stood, He delivered everything to him. This is the meaning of "From now on, Your blessings... are toward us." 

All that they thought was the portion delivered at the **Foundation** <note>Yesod</note>. All the precious customs that the King was guarding—the Torah and the Commandments—contain wondrous properties, including the Divine Will, the flow of emanation <note>shefa</note>, governance, and sustenance. These were given to the Son so he would have wisdom and knowledge to use them and to conduct himself in the way his father the King had guarded them. 

For the Torah and the Commandments contain these properties because they are engraved and emanated from the **Upper Wisdom**, which is the source of all good and virtue. Our Sages mentioned that the "Seven" <note>Sefirot/attributes</note> are the source for those who complete what is required of them. Therefore, they invited us to the fulfillment of the Torah and the Commandments, for they are the **key** to open that Source and draw it down to you, as they were written and established in the **Upper Thought** <note>the highest level of divine consciousness</note>, which is the source of all existence, happiness, and governance. By this, the Son does the will of his Master and merits all that goodness.

**Archigon** <note>Greek: archigonos</note> means the master of the house, or a temporary appointment of oversight, representing glory and understanding. Our matter is that "Time" is delayed and submits to the Torah, as it says: "In the beginning," for with the Torah, He built the world and everything in it, and it is prepared to submit to the Torah.

# Part: Unity | Chapter 25

...mighty and awesome. May your vitality and the vitality of the living be joined together. He determined that eternal life and the vitality of the world are one. You should consider the matter of Awe <note>original: "Yirah," often translated as "Fear," but in this context referring to a profound religious awe or reverence</note> to be of the utmost importance. Those like you who occupy themselves with the Torah find that it contains a sweetness encompassed by the word "Awe." Search for the Lord, and the Torah will provide you with the means.

There are positive commandments <note>original: "mitzvot aseh," requirements to perform an action</note> that encompass all negative commandments <note>original: "mitzvot lo ta'aseh," prohibitions</note>, for one who refrains from committing a transgression is essentially a "Heaven-fearer." Likewise, the negative commandments encompass the positive ones, in their proper order and strength; do not subtract from them. One who exerts himself in a positive commandment but neglects the corresponding boundary is lacking—study this well. For every transgression avoided, one is worthy of a reward according to its specific details. If a person walks the path and does not commit a transgression, they are given a reward as if they had performed a positive commandment. This is the "reward for a transgression"—if one feared and abstained from it, even if they did nothing else in the world, they have walked in His ways.

In truth, King Solomon, peace be upon him, alluded to this secret when he said: "The end of the matter, all having been heard: Fear God and keep His commandments, for this is the whole of man" <note>Ecclesiastes 12:13</note>. By saying **fear God**, he hinted that the positive commandments include the negative ones. By saying **keep His commandments**, he hinted that the negative commandments include the positive ones. He said **this is the whole of man** because it includes both paths. There is a hint here to "Remember" <note>original: "Zakor," the command to remember the Sabbath</note>, which corresponds to the positive commandments, and "Keep" <note>original: "Shamor," the command to guard/observe the Sabbath</note>, which has a numerical value <note>term: "Gematria" — a system where Hebrew letters have numerical values to find hidden links between words</note> corresponding to the negative commandments.

Man is composed of "turning toward" and "turning away." Therefore, "Remember" is for everyone, and the positive commandment must be upheld even in physical matters. These two parts of the commandments constitute the "whole of man"; if one part is missing, he is not a complete "Man." Thus, the Awe that corresponds to the negative commandments is a major part of the whole. It must be hidden within at first, for it precedes all virtues. From it, the gateway opens to the higher levels of Wisdom and Understanding. One who is crowned with Awe pardons the 365 negative prohibitions, for his existence is established through them, and this is the ultimate purpose of everything.

This is as our Sages, of blessed memory, hinted in the chapter "With what may we light" <note>A chapter in Tractate Shabbat of the Talmud</note>, where Rav Yehuda said: "The Holy One, Blessed be He, created His world only so that people should fear Him, as it is said: 'God has so acted that they should fear Him'" <note>Ecclesiastes 3:14</note>. The Midrash of Rabbi Shimon bar Yochai <note>The Zohar</note> explains it in this language: Rabbi Eleazar said, "Serve the Lord with awe." One who desires to perform the decree of his Master, the King, must first direct himself toward the fear of his Master. It then says that through Awe, one is no longer distant from the Supernal Opening. 

From this, they concluded that Awe is the beginning and the gate to **Unity** <note>original: "Yichud," the mystical process of declaring and perceiving God's absolute oneness</note>, which is the highest level of piety. Awe is the first link in the chain of Unity, moving from bottom to top, following the secret of: "The fear of the Lord is the beginning of knowledge" <note>Proverbs 1:7</note>. Therefore, one must put it before all levels of Torah study and Divine service, for it is the foundation and the whip <note>The guiding force</note> for them all through Awe. This is the summary of this chapter.

### Chapter 26

There is a type of Awe of a flesh-and-blood king, but more beloved than that is the Awe of the "Inner King." The type of "Awe" referred to here is when a person fears their Creator as long as they have not yet grasped the true level and greatness of the Creator. Such a person fears transgressing His commandments so that He will not punish them with the punishments associated with those sins which we have heard about. They also perform the commandments for the sake of their rewards, so that the promised reward of those commandments will not be withheld. This person serves out of a desire for reward and a fear of punishment.

It says in the first chapter of Tractate Sotah: "There is a Pharisee out of love and a Pharisee out of fear." This means a "Pharisee out of love" performs every commandment out of the love of the commandment in his heart; a "Pharisee out of fear" does so out of fear of punishment. Service in this way—fear of punishment—is still considered very good, for the Sages noted that he guards himself from doing any evil so as not to sin against himself. However, in the calculation of the Holy Sanctuary, this is not perfect service or complete Awe. Such a person does not truly fear God, but rather fears for himself. You should strive for "the fear of Heaven to be upon you" <note>Pirkei Avot 4:12</note> so that they merit it from Him, not fear for yourselves. One who fears and serves in the way we described is only fearing for himself, lest he be punished...

<meta>catchword: Behold</meta>

<column-break/>

...in his affairs he is lacking, and his life leads to loss when he transgresses them. There are those among the masses who turn away from sin because of the soul itself; they would feel disgraced by their desires if they did not restrain their hands. They restrain themselves from material life to discipline and punish the one who transgresses the Torah and its commandments.

Furthermore, there is an Awe common to all: the fear of the judgments of time and its developments, lest they befall him, his children, or his household, or his acquisitions and the wealth he has amassed. He fears lacking sustenance, or that his children might die in his lifetime, or that his body might be afflicted with suffering and evil diseases. Out of this thought, he keeps his hand from doing any evil. All of these are "good" traits, as he believes there is a Master above who grants reward to those who love Him. This Awe is the first stage for the masses. All rewards for the "Beginning" <note>referring to the lower world/stage of service</note> are categorized as "good" and "holy," for the Will of God is for His people to occupy themselves with it.

As stated in the chapter "The place where they were accustomed" <note>Tractate Pesachim 50b</note>: "A person should always occupy himself with Torah and commandments, even if not for their own sake (*Lo Lishmah*), for from doing it not for its own sake, he will come to do it for its own sake (*Lishmah*)." Indeed, this "External Awe" is the threshold and beginning for everything; from it, one enters the "Inner Sanctum," which is the Pure Internal Awe. 

This External Awe we have described corresponds to the "Final Attribute" <note>referring to Malchut, the lowest of the ten Sephirot/Divine Emanations</note>, the "Strict Quality of Justice" <note>original: "Midat HaDin," God's attribute of judgment</note>. Through the foundations of the heavens, which are accompanied by harsh judgments, a person is struck by the events of his time. Regarding these matters, there is a great warning for those who do not fear and who transgress the Torah and the commandments. Concerning this, it is said: "If you do not observe to do all the words of this Torah... to fear this glorious and awesome name, the Lord your God, then the Lord will make your plagues extraordinary" <note>Deuteronomy 28:58-59</note>. The reason is that this is the Attribute of Justice, and one needs a foundation to be careful and very afraid of punishments. This level of External Awe is good and very necessary. The secret is to reach the state of "Peace," for He is Mercy and the completion of all levels from bottom to top.

If this Awe is lacking, it is very much needed to preserve the body and subdue it so it does not sin. For this reason, the Torah wrote the blessings and curses—to break the strength of the body. Our Sages hinted at this regarding the verse about Isaac our father; he spoke this way to subdue the body through Awe and separate it from sin. This is what Moses said to Israel: "Fear not, for God has come to test you, and that His fear may be before your faces, that you sin not" <note>Exodus 20:20</note>. The meaning is: "Do not fear that God will destroy your existence," but rather that this Awe is a strength and a fence intended to subdue the body and its fear, making it humble before the dread of His harsh judgments and punishments, so that one abstains from sin.

After this, there is a hint regarding **Internal Awe**, for which the pure soul yearns and humbles itself. This yearning comes to the soul from its total immersion in the excellence of the Unique Name and His Wisdom. Behold, the soul is overwhelmed and filled immediately after this realization. From this level, it perceives the wonder of His power and Justice. This Awe is always "between his cheeks" <note>a metaphor for something always present and spoken of</note>. It adds a higher layer of Awe and sublime service. The person seeks to gaze upon the Holy Awe until they no longer cover <note>or "value"</note> any worldly things, considering even themselves and their own honor as nothing. Rather, they see everything as returning and standing upon the **Unique Name**.

Such a person constantly increases in holiness and purity. They sanctify themselves with the holiness of Divine service and pray that perhaps this will bring them closer to their Master, making them worthy to adhere to Him, to approach Him, to serve in His palace, and to offer incense to Him. It goes without saying that one who fears in this way will guard himself from transgressing any negative commandment or judgment, for worldliness has become worthless in his eyes.

<meta>This page concludes the discussion in Chapter 24 regarding the mystical symbolism of the "consuming fire" and the colors of the flame, then transitions into Chapter 25, which establishes "Awe" or "Fear of Heaven" as the necessary foundation for all spiritual wisdom and divine service.</meta>

The Sages, of blessed memory, said: "Be careful lest..." and may you not merit, Heaven forbid, a "thou shalt not" <note>Referring to the violation of a negative commandment</note>. Rather, return to what is good for you and for your "fruits" <note>symbolizing the spiritual results of one's actions</note>, ascending and descending each day through the restoration of the Divine Glory and its unification through good deeds, the fulfillment of the commandments, and the avoidance of transgressions. In the *Book of Brightness* <note>original: "Sefer HaBahir," one of the earliest works of Kabbalah</note>, it is stated that the "blue light" <note>representing the Shekhinah, or Divine Presence</note> is stirred to consume only by the power of Israel, who cleave to it from below. Even though it is the nature of this light to consume what is beneath it, its existence depends on the "sacrifice of the soul" <note>mesirut nefesh</note>. Thus it is written: "But you who cleave to the Lord your God are all alive today" <note>Deuteronomy 4:4</note>. This means that even though it is the nature of that "consuming fire" to eat and destroy whatever it clings to below, because you are cleaving to the Lord, your existence is a "living existence," enduring to this day.

Furthermore, they said there that the "hidden light" is the blue light, which is protected by the "white light" that shines above it. At times this blue light is called "a daughter" <note>bat</note> and at times "a fire" <note>esh</note>. When Israel does not cleave to it from below, it is called "a daughter" <note>original: "bat," which can also mean "daughter" or "end/limit"</note>, signifying a separation from the white light. But when they rouse it to join with the white light, it is called "fire," for it burns and consumes. When it is joined with its "male" counterpart <note>the higher Sephirot or divine emanations</note>, salvation is found there. For as long as it is joined with the white light, it is called "Wonder" <note>Pele</note>, for there the Divine Name is unified, and it cleaves to the white light while Israel cleaves to it from below, standing beneath it to sustain it. This is the essence of his words. From all this, the nature of Divine Unity is clarified—how it is placed in the hands of Israel to bring the faith of His presence into their hearts, knowing that even in our exile, we are not separated from the Supreme Light, as we have written above. This is what our Rabbi intended for us to labor toward in this chapter.

# Chapter 25
->On the Excellence of Service and the Path to It<-

Awe of the Lord is pure <note>Psalm 19:10</note>; it is the beginning and the starting point for the wisdom of Holy Service. It is the path to achieving the splendor of holiness and the light that draws out all other virtues. This is what was asked of Israel: "What does the Lord your God ask of you, but to fear [the Lord]..." <note>Deuteronomy 10:12</note>. From this awe, one comes to walk in all His ways, to love Him, and to serve Him. Likewise, it says: "The Lord your God you shall fear, and Him you shall serve" <note>Deuteronomy 6:13</note>, and to Him you shall cleave. This "Awe" is the entryway to "Service," and through service, one reaches "Cleaving" <note>Dveikut, a state of meditative attachment to the Divine</note>. When one seeks to perform the Holy Service to reach the upper levels, they must first acquire the virtue of Awe and purity. Only then will the other virtues dwell in their proper chamber and endure. One must not deviate from them until reaching perfection, which is the "Cleaving" that the perfected ones long for, as it is the ultimate goal.

We find in the *Tractate of the Fathers* <note>Pirkei Avot 3:9</note>, Rabbi Hanina ben Dosa says: "Anyone whose fear of sin precedes his wisdom, his wisdom will endure; but anyone whose wisdom precedes his fear of sin, his wisdom will not endure." This refers to "Action" <note>the performance of deeds</note> and "Study." For the performance of the commandments and their preservation in perfection depends on the knowledge of study, which provides the understanding and shows the way to do them, their reasons, and the proper intention <note>kavanah</note> required. This path is called "Wisdom" <note>Chokhmah</note>, for the intellect and purity are Wisdom; from it the world was born and created. Its commandments are known to the "wise of heart" <note>those with mystical insight</note>. These must stand beneath the attributes of Understanding <note>Binah</note>. If "Service" is the head, then "Awe" must be the gateway and the entrance to the Teacher and to Wisdom. One should not be surprised that this tractate suggests Awe should come before Wisdom... for the pious Rabbeinu Yonah, of blessed memory, has already explained that this does not refer to

<column-break/>

mere observation. For if a person possesses wisdom but does not know how to guard his soul from stumbling, his wisdom will not endure in his hand, even if he avoids transgressions. But when he learns with the intention of guarding himself, his study will endure. Furthermore, he explained that one whose "fear of sin precedes" is like one who makes it his primary concern, as is his habit, and his heart grows in love for it. But when wisdom precedes fear of sin, the wisdom is subdued by the transgressions he is accustomed to, and in the end, it becomes void.

The holy "Way of the Lord" is the way of Wisdom. The "Secret of the Matter" is known to the scholars of Truth <note>Kabbalists</note>: the part that ascends is called the "Negative Commandments" <note>prohibitions</note>. People are often accustomed to ignore them or not distance themselves from all impurity... which traps people in the net of desires. Because "Wisdom" precedes "Action" in the mundane world, one must reverse this to return to God. One must ensure that "fear of sin" is primary so that he may be holy in this Secret, loving the Holy One. His fruit will not be... and he will not be led into betrayal. He who puts [wisdom] into a person's mouth to feed him with bitterness—therefore, let him write it for relief and guard his face. 

Behold, Israel in the days of Josiah were all humble and saw that they were [servants of] the King... as the verse says: "He said to me, 'You are My servant, Israel, in whom I will be glorified'" <note>Isaiah 49:3</note>. This is the instruction regarding the "rejected branch" <note>idolatry</note>, that they should not bow to it at all. Those who are refined will be clarified and will wear the garments of the Holy Kingdom and Purity, as it is written: "Sanctify yourselves and be holy, for I am holy" <note>Leviticus 11:44</note>. For one who does not resemble the image and likeness of the King has no place within His ways. This is the reason for the prohibition of this path; one who defiles himself causes a blockage [of the divine flow]. For according to a person's effort below, so is the arousal above, as everything is interconnected. One must fear "The Place" <note>HaMakom, a name for God</note> through the secret of "My Sanctuary you shall fear" <note>Leviticus 19:30</note>. This is the Attribute of Judgment, and the very life of the "Attribute of Awe" depends on it. "Behold, the fear of the Lord, that is wisdom" <note>Job 28:28</note>. Since this is the "Gate," it is the beginning of all levels and precedes them from bottom to top. Therefore, Awe must precede Service to point the way toward it.

In the *Collections* <note>Likutei</note> on the third chapter, they said: "'The Lord your God you shall fear'—this includes disciples of the wise." In the chapter titled "He who sees" <note>Tractate Berakhot</note>, they said that this includes Judah, and it all leads to the same place... In the *Tractate Shabbat*, in the chapter "With what may we light," Rabbah bar Rav Huna said: "Any man who possesses Torah but does not possess fear of Heaven is like a treasurer to whom they handed the inner keys but did not hand the outer keys; how shall he enter?" This shows that the "Outer Gate" is the entrance to the "Glory of Israel" <note>Tiferet Yisrael</note>, the secret of the Written Torah, which is the "inner keys." If he lacks fear of Heaven, which is the "outer keys," through which gate shall he enter? There is no way to enter and see the face of the King, the Lord, if the "gate of his eyes" is not open. Regarding this, King David, peace be upon him, said: "Open for me the gates of righteousness" <note>Psalm 118:19</note>, and "This is the gate of the Lord; the righteous shall enter through it" <note>Psalm 118:20</note>.

This is the secret of the "Perfect Song." Awe is compared to the heavens. Rav said: "When a man is brought in for judgment [in the afterlife], they ask him: 'Did you conduct your business faithfully? Did you set aside fixed times for Torah study?' Yet even so, if 'the fear of the Lord is his treasure' <note>Isaiah 33:6</note>, it is well; if not, it is not well." This is like a man who told his servant: "Carry my wheat up to the attic." The servant went and carried it up. The master asked: "Did you mix a measure of *humton* <note>term: humton - a type of salty earth or preservative used to keep grain from rotting</note> into it?" He said, "No." The master replied: "It would have been better if you had not carried it up at all." The explanation of *humton* is that it preserves the fruits. This is the "Fear of the Lord," the Attribute of Judgment, the "Covenant of Salt," which preserves the fruits of one's labor. One must mix the *humton* with the grain, for without it, the work is not complete.

Thus we have learned that he who experiences awe in the way we have chosen, even if he cleaves to the **inner awe** which is the source of everything—for it is the awe of the Eternal King, the Source—as it is written: *“For with You is the fountain of life; in Your light we see light.”* <note>Psalm 36:9</note>

### Chapter 27

**Awe of the Unique Name** <note>The Tetragrammaton, the four-letter name of God</note> is the highest level, which refines the servant to a state of perfect worship of Unity, which is designated to represent the Great and Unique Name. **Love** is rooted in **Understanding** <term>Binah: the third of the ten Sefirot, often associated with the "Divine Mother" and the source of logic and distinction</term>, as we have alluded. 

The explanation of **Unity** is the "binding to join." Therefore, the word **Love** <note>Hebrew: Ahavah</note> has the same numerical value <note>Gematria: both words equal 13</note> as **One** <note>Hebrew: Echad</note>. In the Great Secret, it is called "One," and through its uniqueness, it binds to Him in thought. This is why the aforementioned conclusion was written. Regarding Rabbi Shimon bar Yochai <note>the traditional author of the Zohar</note>, his statement on this matter was: *“This is everything: to love the Holy One, Blessed be He; and through love, everything stands.”* As it is written: *“Many waters cannot quench love.”* <note>Song of Songs 8:7</note> Everything exists through His hints. It does not stand otherwise; this is how it was established for her. 

He spreads the "eye" <note>possibly "the covering" or "canopy"</note> above for eternity... through the hints of her Master upon her, and it does not spread... adding secrets. For this was established for her, not to be separated from Him, a flame in speech with affection, so it shall not be said of her as it is written: *“And he ceased from him.”* <note>Genesis 18:33</note> For eternity, she receives through the hints of her Master upon her, in her affection to be cleaved to everything. And she is a "constant voice"... [mystical letter associations: Koph, Samekh, Vav, Heh]. For this reason, everything is found for His glory, and everything is bound in affection. Because of this, they were commanded to hint to God to be bound in that love, and because of this: *“And you shall love the Lord your God...”* <note>Deuteronomy 6:5</note>

It is clarified from their words that the reason for Unity through Awe and Understanding is to create a "union" <note>Zivug: a spiritual coupling of Divine attributes</note>. Behold, a fixed decree is engraved, as it were, one with the other, bound together by the "Voice of the Bond of Love." Since its foundation is in love, there is no separation, for this is love, sparking constantly without interruption. It has already been explained that the soul of Israel is a chain emanating from the place of Unity and Love. Therefore, it is appropriate and mandatory for one who yearns and longs to resemble the Place from which he was inscribed, to move toward it constantly to cleave and be unified with it. For every "kind" seeks and lives to go and cleave to its own kind; its longing for it will not rest or be quiet until it returns to it. 

Therefore, let all our movements be directed toward Him. For one who was accustomed and habituated to dwell in the place of freedom—the most forgiving, light, familiar, and comfortable place—will yearn to leave the state he is currently in to return to that primeval Good, which is the "forgotten claim" <note>representing the soul's innate memory of its Divine origin</note> that was with him at the beginning. Behold, the **Divine Presence** <note>Shekhinah</note> is a "strong God" <note>El Chazak</note> from the place of Love and Unity. Therefore, she yearns and longs for Love and Unity, to be established in her "fifth" just as she was in her source. 

When she is removed from her place, she draws near to everything so she may be hidden in the "Hidden Love" and the "Hidden World." She is not separated from it... and the voice in its pleasantness nests constantly in the enduring Love and does not move from its root. The "Voice of Love" within our structure is founded on the blessing of Unity, to prevent any deficiency from it, as in the guarding of *“Hear, O Israel, the Lord is our God, the Lord is One.”* Behold, this leads to Unity and Love, and therefore *“And you shall love the Lord your God etc.”* for Unity is the love for the Unique One. They said in the Midrash of Rabbi Shimon bar Yochai: *“‘And you shall love the Lord’—this means he should bind himself to Him with a powerful bond, with a drawing of affection, so that all his worship is placed in love.”* 

Thus it begins: the supreme love is to be hidden in the power of the Unique One, and to be joined with Him in darkness, to be pure in true worship. This was the worship of **Abraham our father**, the first of the chosen ones, from the perspective of Thought. Therefore, he was the teacher of Love, for the "Voice of Love" was in him, as it says: *“You shall love kindness”* <note>Micah 7:20, Chesed is attributed to Abraham</note>. Because through love he was bound in the secret of the attribute of Love, for his soul passed through there... and therefore he was able 

<column-break/>

to be called "Our Love" <note>Abraham is often called "the lover of God"</note> by the Holy One, Blessed be He. For he is entirely "soul," and his strength is like a body not separated from the place of its grave <note>a metaphor for his total devotion</note>. Therefore, his actions and all his worship were directed toward **Kindness** <term>Chesed: the attribute of expansive love and benevolence</term> and Love. Because he was bound in love, he was called "Abraham my friend" <note>Isaiah 41:8</note>. 

From the boundary of Love, he desired our father Isaac <note>representing Gevurah/Restraint</note> to merit his friend, and he occupied himself with their work. He acted constantly as the "Life in the Holy One" to resemble his friend and to recognize the "Secret of the Water" <note>Water is the Kabbalistic symbol for Chesed/Kindness</note> that Abraham our father lived. 

So they said in the Midrash of Rabbi Shimon bar Yochai in the *Zohar*: *“‘Because Abraham obeyed my voice and kept my charge’* <note>Genesis 26:5</note>—The attribute of Kindness said: ‘All the days Abraham was in the world, I did not need to do my work, for Abraham stood in my place and kept my charge.’” Even though my work is to rebuke the world—and even those who are guilty, I rebuke them and yet I cover them—Abraham was habituated to doing the will of the "pious one" within us. This was Abraham’s business, as it is written: *“And he planted an Eshel in Beersheba.”* <note>Genesis 21:33</note> What did he do? He prepared bread and food for all who came into the world, and he would rebuke them and say: “Give thanks to the One who owns this! Serve the Lord, the God of Heaven and Earth!” He would preach the worship of the All-Encompassing to them.

It is clear that Abraham our father was from the general place of the attribute of **Kindness**, to provide for the world and to sustain it, and above all, to perfect it. Through all this, he would reach the goal of Holy Love, to spread and intend to add to his Friend <note>God</note>. For when one desires His kindness, he comes to add to it. As they said in the *Sifrei*: *“‘And you shall love’—with the love that creatures have for your father Abraham,”* as it is said, *“And the souls that they had made in Haran,”* <note>Genesis 12:5</note> meaning he converted them and brought them under the wings of the Divine Presence. And in the end, it will be joyful: *“And you shall love the Lord your God,”* so that the Name of Heaven shall be made beloved through your hands. 

And in the "Guardian," return from Your mercy, O Lord, Your love upon Your creatures. All this is to demonstrate the permanence of the Name, the secret of Love. Therefore, Abraham our father would make the Holy One, Blessed be He, beloved to the creatures. From here I understand the end of the secret of the love of all things for the place of Unity—even those things that are of the attribute of Evil, Peace, and Separation <note>referring to the diversity of creation</note>. For as it was at the beginning in the Supernal Thought, it was in Unity and perfect Love. All of this is from the attribute of the "Bond," the place of the attribute of Love. This was the attribute of Abraham our father, who merited to be chosen for the Crown of Kindness and Love because he was the first surplus. Therefore, Abraham was the master of Kindness and the master of Love. 

We learned in the ninth chapter <note>of Mishnah Berakhot</note>: *“With all your heart”*—meaning with both of your inclinations, with the **Good Inclination** and the **Evil Inclination**. And in the *Sifrei* we learned: *“With all your heart”*—that there should be no division regarding the Omnipresent. All this is because its root is in Unity. For the Evil Inclination is from the powers of Evil, Peace, and Damage, and a person needs to love the Name through it and to unify it to Him. For He desires its merit to return all things to Unity. This is the boundary of Love, and one should not distance this through division and separation. Especially when he himself is blessed... he shall not distance any division in himself, for the Will was to disconnect everything and it shall be made straight by man, as is explained. This is the love that one must love with his two inclinations, and that is what is meant by *“With all your heart.”* 

To demonstrate this absence of division in Unity, we learned in the chapter *HaRo'eh* <note>Berakhot 54a</note>: *“A person is obligated to bless for the bad just as he blesses for the good,”* for it says, *“And you shall love the Lord your God with all your heart etc.”* This hints at the "separation of time," to show and publicize the kindnesses that are hidden in all things, to unify them and return them to Unity in their concealment. For this reason, one is obligated to bless Him for every single attribute—and this is the Awe of Unity, and it is part of the boundary of Love. This is the reason for the transition from Unity to Love: *“And you shall love the Lord your God etc.”* This very intention is what is meant by the path of Unity and Love, since there was a transition in this...

### Chapter 28

**Love** also has a part called "External"... and this is called "Internal." And regarding the King who prevents her, He sends darkness to the place from the side of its three-fold nature...

<meta>This page continues the exploration of spiritual "Awe" (Yirah), specifically distinguishing between external fear of punishment and the "Inner Awe" that leads to total devotion. <header>Chapter 36 | The Section on Unity | Chapter 37</header>

### The Unity: Chapter 37

The path we have described, and this **awe**, is exceedingly exalted, for there is no purity below the **shell** <term>Kelippah: literally "husk" or "shell," referring to the spiritual forces of impurity that conceal the Divine light</term>. This is what the sages meant when they said that the ultimate goal of wisdom is repentance and good deeds. This is the **awe** that a person should feel from their youth. It is told of two students who stood before their master; he asked them, "What is the purpose of the wisdom you study?" They replied, "To increase the honor of the Creator." He said to them, "You have answered well, for the beginning of wisdom is the awe of the Lord." <note>Cf. Psalm 111:10</note> This **awe** is the start of the **inner awe** that is compared to clear glass; one must enter within it to see how Divine Justice returns to all deeds and everything in the world.

No one merited this level except for our father **Abraham**, peace be upon him, at the time of the **Binding of Isaac** <note>The Akedah: Genesis 22</note>. Because he was filled with this awe, he was able to withhold his own compassion and overcome the natural law of mercy to fulfill the Divine decree. Even in his imagination, he did not hesitate or question; he simply accepted, went, and acted, all to perform the will of the Creator. This is called the "tradition of Justice"—to do the will of the True Desire, to cling to it, and to hold onto his inner inheritance. Thus it is written of the levels of this awe: *“The awe of the Lord is pure, enduring forever.”* <note>Psalm 19:10</note> It is called **pure** because it stems from the purity of thought; there is no mixture of foreign or external motivations within it.

Therefore, he who cleaves to this **awe** does not allow any mixture of self-interest. He does not fear for the sake of any physical end or reward, as one might in "external awe." Once you have reached this stage, you will see that this **awe** never falls or diminishes. The reason for **inner awe** is the soul's deep desire to cleave to the **Upper Thought**. This is the meaning of "The reward of humility is the awe of the Lord." <note>Proverbs 22:4</note> In every place where one perceives the greatness of the King, one feels a great awe, lest he should fall from his rank and not be accepted into the King's palace to serve Him or behold His face.

Through this **awe**, a person adds holiness and purity to their soul. He watches over himself constantly so that no flaw or blemish is found in his thoughts or his speech. He stands in the King's palace, always judging himself, purifying his actions through the clarity of his deeds. He knows that these deeds are the King’s desire. This **awe** has no "shadow of loss," for it is constant. This **awe** will always increase and soar, being at his right hand in all his ways to achieve **Unity** with the King. As it is said in the verse, "to walk in all His ways," so that he should not recoil in fear, even while performing the deeds of a servant. As it is written: *"Happy is the man who fears the Lord,"* <note>Psalm 112:1</note> find rest in His commandments and find great strength. Our sages of blessed memory explained: "He finds joy in His commandments, and not in the reward of His commandments." This is because the commandments are the King's royal garments and jewels. The King is enriched by them, and it is His desire and His glory that his servants should be adorned by them. His servants should know and desire them, for they are the King's treasures. Through them, the servant draws closer to his Master.

It says in the verse: *"And it shall come to pass, that whosoever shall call on the name of the Lord shall be delivered."* <note>Joel 3:5</note> And how can one "call on His name"? By imitating the attributes of the Holy One, Blessed be He. Just as He is called "Merciful and Gracious," you too should be merciful and gracious. Just as the Holy One, Blessed be He, is called "Righteous"—as it is written, *"For the Lord is righteous; He loves righteousness"* <note>Psalm 11:7</note>—you too should be righteous. Just as He is called "Pious" <note>Chassid</note>, you too should be pious. Therefore, when a person calls on the name of the Lord in this way, he is delivered. And it says: *"Everything that is called by My name, for My glory I created it."* <note>Isaiah 43:7</note> Furthermore: *"The Lord has made everything for His own purpose."* <note>Proverbs 16:4</note> Thus, the one who possesses the **awe of the Name** knows that he was created solely to call upon the Name of the Lord. He is always prepared to complete the intention of his creation. This is his strength and his constant potential. He is always careful and in awe lest he fail in anything he does. He does not turn away from his obligation, but is always pursuing his perfection.

At the end of the chapter of "The Pious Man," <note>a reference to a Talmudic or ethical tractate</note> it is said: "A person should always be clever in his awe." This means his cleverness should be directed toward this **inner awe**. This will remove all hidden obstacles from him, and they will assist him from Heaven. Once his ultimate goal is to stand in awe of the Place <note>HaMakom: a name for God implying He is the "Place" of the world</note> and fulfill the intention of his creation, he is provided with the means to do so. This is the secret of the "Length of Days" and the "Life" mentioned in the verses: *"The awe of the Lord increases days"* <note>Proverbs 10:27</note> and *"The awe of the Lord leads to life."* <note>Proverbs 19:23</note>

<meta>catchword: The/Those who...</meta>

<column-break/>

### Chapter 36

Instead, he should always cleave to the ways in which the King’s will is known. We have no other task in all our years but to do His will, to draw near, and to cleave to Him. He should be like the **incense** before Him—pure, holy thoughts and holy knowledge. Faith should never leave his mind. He should look with alacrity and haste to fulfill the commandments. He should pursue them to be adorned by them and to be remembered through them, so that he does not miss any of his obligations, whether physical or spiritual. He knows that his Master’s word is a foundation and a burning fire for those who love Him, not just out of fear of shame or lack. He even strives to perfect his soul and body so that he may perform the task even better. He is like a person who is riding toward the **Glory**, the Glory from the upper house, with a burning love.

Regarding this, the sages said that the Patriarchs are the **Chariot** <term>Merkavah: a Kabbalistic concept where the righteous person becomes a vehicle or "chariot" for Divine presence</term>. This is because their conduct was not like that of later generations. Their soul and body became a chariot for the Name in the world below. Our father Abraham, peace be upon him, after the Binding, saw that his actions were for the sake of heaven because he was crowned with this **inner awe**, which is even higher than **love**.

The level of **love** is why he was called *"Abraham My friend."* <note>Isaiah 41:8</note> But he reached the fullness of this **inner awe** according to his uprightness. The proof for the level of this inner awe is what was written concerning Abraham after the Binding: *"Now I know that you are a God-fearing man."* <note>Genesis 22:12</note> Abraham then named the place "The Lord Will See" <note>Adonai Yireh</note>, as it is said, *"On the mount of the Lord it shall be seen."* This means that the will of the Master of the world was revealed before him. The command was: "Take now your son, your only son, whom you love..." He did not hold back. This was not because he was forced, but out of his great love and humility. This is explained in the *Guide for the Perplexed* toward the end of the third section.

It is clarified there that the point was not merely the physical act itself, but the desire to serve and to attain this **inner awe**. This is the highest level of Abraham’s house. He did not seek to be saved from judgment, but rather to be worthy of the King's secret, for his will was cleaved to the attribute of Truth. This is the **awe of the Lord which is pure**, cleansed of all dross. This matter is the "hidden and inner work," not the "external awe." Because he reached this, the work of the Binding was established for generations. Even so, it is protected from the "shells" as we have written. By doing this, he was repairing and strengthening his connection to the King with all his might. His awe was intended to firmly plant his heart in the Place and to draw the Divine Will toward him. It was written for him as a merit and a sweetness in the true assembly, reaching the level of inner awe—the awe of our father Abraham.

The sages said at the end of the chapter that whoever acts out of **love** is greater than one who acts out of **fear** <note>Sotah 31a</note>. Rabbi Shimon ben Eleazar says: "Greater is the one who acts out of love." But we do not interpret "fear" here as the common fear of punishment, or the fear of hell and suffering. Rather, it refers to the **awe of the Majesty** of the Place—the awe of His greatness, His grandeur, and His dread that is cast upon a person. Even though we have written that this awe is higher than love, and we will further explain that the "Awe of the Kingdom" is the highest level, this does not contradict us. This awe is not a single level, but has many grades. One person might fear and guard himself from transgressing commandments because he knows the punishment for them is severe, which is a lower level called "external fear." But the one we discuss is **inner awe**, which is the goal of the soul—being in awe of the Divine presence itself.

<summary>This page defines "Inner Awe" (Yirah Pnimit) as a sublime spiritual state beyond the mere fear of punishment, using Abraham and the Binding of Isaac as the ultimate model. It explains that true awe is about becoming a "chariot" for the Divine will and performing commandments as "royal garments" rather than for personal reward.</summary>

It concludes the discussion on serving God out of love, using Rabbi Akiva as the ultimate example.</meta>

<header>Chapter 28 | The Section on the Service | Chapter 1</header>

...all kinds of honor. And as we have merited to learn regarding Rabbi Akiva, as recorded in the chapter "One who sees" <note>Talmud Berakhot 61b</note>, at the hour when they took Rabbi Akiva out to be executed, it was the time for the recitation of the Shema. They were combing his flesh with iron combs, yet he was accepting upon himself the yoke of the Kingdom of Heaven with love. His students said to him: "Our master, even to this extent?" He said to them: "All my days I was troubled by this verse, 'With all your soul'—meaning, even if He takes your soul. I said to myself: When will I have the opportunity to fulfill this? Now that the opportunity has come to me, shall I not fulfill it?" He prolonged the word **One** (*Echad*) until his soul departed with that word. 

And according to the Midrash of Rabbi Shimon bar Yochai <note>Rashbi, the traditional author of the Zohar</note>, may peace be upon him, in the *Book of the Palaces* <term>Heichalot: early Jewish mystical texts describing the heavenly realms</term>, regarding Understanding and Wisdom <note>original: "Binah and Chokhmah"</note>... it is said that the Divine Presence <term>Shekhinah: the feminine, indwelling aspect of God</term> stands at the entrance of the Palace, and they all stand ready to prostrate themselves. They bestow spirit upon those who are silent and surrender their souls to You in mercy. They raise their deficiencies upward. All those who perform acts of kindness in the world are the ones who travel, strike, and enter. They see the Palace and are crowned there, all of them becoming crowned within the Supernal Divine Presence. Regarding this it is written: *"For Your kindness is great above the heavens."* <note>Psalm 108:5</note> And because of this merit, it is written: *"Many waters cannot extinguish the love, and rivers cannot sweep it away; if a man were to give all the wealth of his house for love, they would utterly scorn him."* <note>Song of Songs 8:7</note> These are the words of the sage.

One who serves out of love sustains the world, because love encompasses the 990 worlds of acts of loving-kindness, which are the pillars of the world. For one who occupies himself with the Torah out of love performs a kindness specifically for the Holy One, Blessed be He. And regarding the Torah, it has already been explained that it is a **Tree of Life**. 

He learns that all the Priests and Levites stand ready to bow down wherever they are honored, and they bestow upon the silent ones through our mercy. With these, he also includes the intention of **Unity** through the verse of the *Shema*. Regarding the Service <term>Avodah: specifically referring to the Temple service or prayer</term>, he said that they surrender their souls for it with their spirits. This is the "service of free men," and it was the service of Rabbi Akiva and his companions who ascended on high through their jubilee. 

Regarding acts of loving-kindness, he said: "All those who perform kindness in the world are the ones who strike, etc., and ascend to be crowned within the Supernal Divine Presence." The "Constellation of Kindness" <note>original: "Mazzal Chesed"</note> tips the balance toward kindness from above the highest heavens. This is the unification of the Holy One, Blessed be He, with great love, according to the secret of "becoming a God to me" with my portions. Thus it is explained that service from love is what is specifically designated for the "Great Kindness." Service in this manner is the explanation of the entire Torah, which is included in the teaching that the Levites belong to the Lord. We are commanded to be under the Great Name through His kindness: *"And you shall love the Lord your God with all your heart, with all your soul, and with all your might."* <note>Deuteronomy 6:5</note>

When it says **"With all your heart,"** it corresponds to the Torah in general, which includes the positive and negative commandments. These correspond to the **Good Inclination** and the **Evil Inclination**. One who serves from love must unify them and serve in the Name of the Lord, the Unique Name, out of love. This is "loving with both your inclinations," as in the matter of lifting the inclination upward.

Regarding **"The Service,"** it says **"With all your soul"**—meaning even if He takes your soul. This obligates us to surrender ourselves to death for the service of the Unique Name and Love. As we have merited to see with Rabbi Shimon bar Yochai and his companions, who were unified through them; their souls rejoiced so that they could not and would not fear any danger.

Regarding **"Acts of Loving-Kindness,"** it says **"With all your might,"** which we have merited to understand through the commentary of the *Rokeach* <note>Rabbi Eleazar of Worms, a 12th-century mystic</note> as "with all your money." Thus, there are three pillars corresponding to the three things with which a servant must serve the Name: **Heart**, **Soul**, and **Wealth**. These are **Torah**, **Service**, and **Acts of Loving-Kindness**. 

Kindness corresponds to the attribute of Kindness and the Unity of "The Lord is our God, the Lord is One" <note>original: "Y-H-V-H Eloheinu Y-H-V-H"</note>, which is Kindness like His Name. Similarly, one is obligated to unify Him with all one's heart, soul, and might. This is the Service and the Love than which there is no higher level. This love of kindness is more profound than the awe of the Lord. This is what we wished to discuss regarding the matter of Love.

With this, the first part of this book is completed, which is called **The Service of the Holy**. Praise be to the God of Glory who chooses glory. May He be blessed and exalted above all blessing and praise. Amen.

->The Section on Unity is finished and complete. Praise be to the One God.<-

### Called "The Section on the Service," consisting of 44 chapters.

### Chapter One

I have already written in the introduction to this book that the **Service is a Divine Need** <term>Tzorech Gavoah: the mystical concept that human actions "benefit" or complete the Divine realm</term>, according to the necessity of its secret. I mentioned there many proofs from verses and the teachings of our Sages, of blessed memory. Furthermore, it is a tradition in the hands of the "Masters of the Service" <term>Kabbalists</term>, passed from mouth to mouth, that this was the purpose. It was handed over to the pious and the "Wise of Action" <note>practical Kabbalists</note> to draw the Divine Will from the upper realms to the lower realms through their service and their good and pure prayer, doing what is good and right in the eyes of the Lord.

For behold, the "Ears" and the "Awakening" occur through the awakening of those below. The source flows toward the intended purpose through his labor, returning to the Unique Name through his action, as it is written: *"Who rides the heavens in your help."* <note>Deuteronomy 33:26</note> Our Sages said in the Midrash of Rabbi Nehunia ben HaKanah <note>The Bahir</note>: How much does one act kindly with his Maker through the study of Torah! For anyone who studies Torah performs a kindness for his Maker, as it is written: "Who rides the heavens in your help." In truth, man is the help, providing aid to Him who is above him, sustaining the Blessed Name. From this we see that the **Service is a Divine Need**, for through it the upper realms are awakened and moved by human action. This is the **Repair of the Glory** <term>Tikkun HaKavod: the restoration of Divine harmony</term>. 

They said in the chapter of Rabbi Akiva: "Woe to you if you do not help Me." Through the assistance of those below, the Levites and the heavens are sustained and blessed, and the Great Kindness of Unity is increased. This is the reason for the various Services; they were the awakening of the lower beings. As we have merited to see in the Midrash of Rabbi Shimon bar Yochai, in these words: "At the time when one rises and kisses the Good." When an action is done below, it awakens an action above. Regarding this, they established: "And you shall give a sign." All those who perform actions below do so to cause their awakening below to arouse the above. Therefore, "Who rides the heavens in your help" is written. 

The "Good" mentioned here is the **Righteous One**, the Foundation of the World <term>Tzaddik Yesod Olam: a specific Divine attribute or Sefirah</term>, for it is written: *"Tell the righteous that it is good."* <note>Isaiah 3:10</note> When a person acts, he awakens the "Good" to be aroused. Then the Divine is ready for them, and everyone experiences joy. There is joy above and joy below in the world. He who is able to gladden the Heart causes the "Good Kindness" to be aroused toward the children, and he arouses it—as it were—within Him. 

Know that according to the deed below, so is its likeness done and awakened above. Through a small amount of good, the "Righteous One, Foundation of the World," who is called "Good," is awakened. By his good deeds, it is as if he makes that very thing and that Unity on high. As it was said, "And he kissed the Good," which refers to the **Repair of the Glory**. This name is filled by the action from above through the intention of the heart. This is why it is said that the "Good" resides in the residence of the Almighty...
