# Chapter 28 | The Section on Unity | Chapter 28

He should behold and turn to dedicate himself, for anyone who trembles and fears because of an occurrence of the **Divine Overflow** <term>Shefa: the spiritual energy or "flow" from God that sustains the world</term> in his house. Furthermore, one must know the Place <note>original: *HaMakom*, a traditional Rabbinic name for God, suggesting He is the "place" of the world</note> when he sees that [the trial] is meant to rebuke him, and it is a merit for the living essence. To achieve this, he pursues His commandment and seeks His love. One must know that he who seeks, not for the sake of the cycle of worldly honor or the good of his own heart, but to raise the glory of the Holy One, Blessed be He—such a person is considered as one who intends to merit love for us. This is like an intermingling of the delights of the King of the body, for how beautiful and how pleasant is "love among delights" <note>Song of Songs 7:7</note>. According to this love, the way is not merely for elevation—in Gematria <term>Gematria: a system of Jewish numerology where letters have numerical values</term> it is... meriting love, for from it love descends, though not like the lower, physical love. 

And this is the **Palm Tree** <note>original: *Tamar*</note> which is strange; afterward it reaches not just to the waters below, but to the Supernal Love. The Palm Tree is "above the heavens," as it says in the verse: "For Your kindness is great *unto* the heavens" <note>Psalm 57:11</note> and it is also written "For Your kindness is great *above* the heavens" <note>Psalm 108:5</note>. This is the "Unity" that allows one to rest all his actions for the sake of His name. Behold, they explained that love in this manner is the most chosen path. His face is a reflection, and one should awaken the love that fills his heart with things that have no measure. One should be good with his whole being so that love is established below. 

They said in the Chapters of the Fathers <note>Likely referring to Sifre, a legalistic commentary</note> and in the orders of the 13th chapter of the *Sifre* on the verse "to love the Lord...": You might say, "I am studying Torah so that I may become rich," or "so that I may be called Rabbi," or "so that I may receive a reward in the World to Come." Therefore, the text says "to love": whatever you do, do it only out of love. Rabbi Eliezer ben Zadok said: "Do things for the sake of their Maker, and speak of them for the sake of Heaven." 

Observe from their words that even one who serves for some purpose eventually reaches his service, but he is not considered [truly serving] except for himself, for his service is only for hoarding and storage. But the song and the intention should be that his service is for the sake of Heaven—which is the **Unification** of the Great Name in thought and action. He who isolates himself for this purpose is called "one who loves the Place." He who serves from this love has his service counted, and he does not intend for any personal end, but only for his own ways. It says that there is no end to his service except to do His will, which is the Unification, which is the clear boundary. He should not pity himself, but rather find himself in total surrender in every way, never turning back. Through this, he attains the goal of service and love. This is the love intended by the verse "And you shall love the Lord your God..." All this was the path of **Abraham our Father**, peace be upon him. He loved the Place, and the service and love of Abraham our Father were what was intended by the verse: "And you shall love the Lord your God with all your heart, and with all your soul, and with all your might." 

They said in the Midrash of Rabbi Shimon bar Yochai <note>the Zohar</note> regarding this language: "Love" is a love that stands in **Kindness** <term>Chesed: the divine attribute of expansive benevolence, associated with Abraham</term> in all measures. It passes over everything and does not stand upon the body or upon money. Why? Because the heart is elevated to the heights of the soul and the money, to the point where one does not look at physical excess. 

Prepared for the good, he stands in the Section of Unity to establish an altar for the whole world. Because of this, he stands in the attribute of Kindness, as it is written: "Kindness to Abraham" <note>Micah 7:20</note>. He is prepared to be unified in his elevation... and not only that, but through him, everyone is blessed with the flow of Kindness. Regarding "And you shall be a blessing," do not read it as "you shall be a blessing," but rather "they shall bless each other through you." Here they explained that the one who loves the Place is the one who is enriched by the attribute of **Truth**, for he enters into it from every side. He rules over all things, upper and lower. This is the secret of the existence of the Kingdom... and its entourage. They said regarding the love for the Place that one should not pity his own body, his money, or his children. This is learned from Abraham, who in his love for the Place, through ten trials, [gave of] himself, his son, and his wife.

<column-break/>

And there is no one who brings upon himself [trials] regarding his body and his son as difficult as they were for Abraham. Even regarding his money, he was not sparing, but would use it to cause others to recognize the love of the Place. They said that because of this, he merited the attribute of **Kindness**, which is the secret of Love. Afterward, it was said: "Kindness to Abraham." Thus, the one who loves and serves in this way is unified with Him and adds to the flow. He does not need to intend for himself or serve for any [personal] end, for it will come and be drawn to him automatically. For one who serves in this way is warned to act, and he causes blessing in all things, from the beginning of thought to its end. From his blessing, he too shall be blessed... and not only that, but all his worlds are blessed through him. They proved this from what is written: "And through your seed shall they be blessed." Do not read it as etc. 

Our intention is that those who intend and direct their goodness toward the attribute of Kindness and its standing, even in their service from love, their intention is for the blessing that comes to the end of the thought. This is what is meant by "they shall be blessed through it." The intention is that he too is included in the blessing without intending it for himself. This is what they said in the chapter *Helek*: "Learn out of love, and honor will eventually come" <note>Talmud Nedarim 62a</note>. Within the treasure houses of love for the Place, how much more so is this the way.

We have already written that the love for the **Name** is established, and from it is derived the statement "Support me..." which causes overflow and freedom in all the holy attributes included in the **Great Name** <note>The Tetragrammaton, the four-letter name of God</note>. And these were the fulfillments of the Will. Behold, this great foundation is pressed toward the attribute of the Name... and if so, from his love for the established Name, the love is strengthened for him. This is also why it is possible for love to fall between the Great Name and man in that same foundation, just as it is common between man and the established Name. This is the secret of the verse that says, "My friend, I loved kindness for men," as the Holy One, Blessed be He, says... and you might say that from the believers of love, it is "Kindness to Abraham" by way of the attributes... because they are the unifications of the Great Name. He loves it because Unification in this way creates a "Spirit House" <note>a dwelling place for the Divine</note> and He loves him. This is the path we wrote of. Those who love it have this "Kindness," which is the expansion of love between the Great Name and Israel. 

And also, from another side, it is possible for love to fall between the Great Name and Israel, and that is **God's love for us**, because we are a "portion of Him" <note>Deuteronomy 32:9</note>. He has a relationship with us. We have already written that the souls of Israel are called by way of the Names and Faith... and the soul of Israel is the name of the Holy One... just as there is a relationship and "the eye of the Lord is toward those who fear Him." Because of this, the love was very strong between the Name, which is the "portion," and Israel, which is the "inheritance." As it is written: "When Israel was a youth, I loved him" <note>Hosea 11:1</note>, and "I have loved you, says the Lord" <note>Malachi 1:2</note>, and "He loved Jacob" <note>Malachi 1:3</note>. It is also written in the Torah: "To love you, and to bless you, and to multiply you..." and "The Lord your God turned the curse into a blessing for you, because the Lord your God loved you" <note>Deuteronomy 23:6</note>. And it is written: "Because of the Lord's love for you..." 

This love grew and prevailed so much that it rose to the level of **Passion** <term>Chashak: a deep, binding desire or longing, often considered higher than Ahavah (love)</term>, which is the crown of love and its ultimate end. This is what they said: "Not because you were more numerous than other peoples did the Lord set His passion (*chashak*) upon you and choose you" <note>Deuteronomy 7:7</note>. And it is written: "Only with your fathers did the Lord set His passion to love them" <note>Deuteronomy 10:15</note>. The reason is that the soul of Israel is carved out as a "beloved companion" to the King. For they are beloved friends. She is the "wife" of Israel... it is written that when they journey on the straight path, they cause love and passion between the two of them.

In the Midrash of Rabbi Nehunia ben HaKanah <note>the Sefer HaBahir</note>, it is known by a parable of a King who had a beautiful wife, and she bore him sons. They turned to evil ways. He hated them and removed a portion of their inheritance. She said to them: "My sons, why do you act so? Do not make your father hate you." And she reminded them of their mother’s youth... until they returned to their father. He saw them and loved them as at the beginning. From all this, Israel is obligated to turn themselves toward the love of the Place, as it is written: "And you shall love the Lord your God with all your heart and with all your soul." And they explained in the chapter *HaRo'eh* <note>the final chapter of Talmud Berakhot</note>... in the *Sifre*, we hear: "A certain person says, 'I love...'"

# Chapter 2 | The Section on Service | Chapter 3

The rectification whose essence shall be to rectify just as he rectified for Abraham, who was himself [rectified] and received the blessing from on high, as has been explained. His physical matter, when not occupied with the business of God, was a void <note>original: *bitul*, meaning nullification or negation</note> for Abraham, who would come to distribute the teaching of the glory of the Holy One, Blessed be He. "What will You give me?" <note>Genesis 15:2</note> and therefore it shall be within the new, etc. And the secret of his preservation is known, which shall be beneficial to those known as the "wise-hearted." 

Like the portion of Abraham our forefather, even though during the days they are occupied with the ways of prophecy; and so too for the master of the righteous who are referred to as "their own knees" and who ascend via the "knees of heaven." And he assisted the Service <term>Avodah: specifically refers to the sacrificial service in the Temple or, post-Temple, to prayer</term> and its Divine Presence <term>Shekhinah: the feminine, indwelling aspect of God on earth</term> from its path... and this is the "Living Water" that the Living One rectified. They took action and were called the "Sages of Action" <term>Chachmei Ma'aseh: scholars focused on the practical application of mystical secrets or wonder-working</term> based on what we wrote above regarding the secret of "my making," in the secret of "And David made a name" <note>2 Samuel 8:13</note>, and the secret of the rectification of the Glory and its unification with that which is above it... the elevation of the world and the Kindnesses.

The "Sages of Action" are the Prophets, and this is the secret of "For Your sake, O God, Blessed be He," which shall stir. And mainly regarding the fruits, they returned to the paths so that he would be a good guardian, like a cycle in the Assembly of Israel. From Him comes Kindness. And Rabbi Isaac the Kohen, son of Hama, said: "The firmament whose name is *Arvot* (Clouds) was purchased; he sows the deeds of the righteous upon it and it flows with fruit." The firmament of *Arvot* is the [foundation] of the world and its base, for all good sustenance comes from the head of the White One to all sides and mixes with it. And through the "Nine Principles" of the firmaments, He shall be exalted... and also for the secret of the Foundation <term>Yesod: the ninth Sephirah (divine attribute), associated with procreation and the funneling of divine energy</term> and in it until the secret of the world... and the tearing at night is a secret, and it is the secret of "tasting the fruits" during its preservation, and to exempt his life-force and the cause of all... the deeds of the righteous that ascend in the perfection of intention in prayer... and this is its fruit.

Kindness, remembrance... "remember us" in the aspect of this book... and from the material of Rabbi Phinehas ben Jair they returned to the secret of the Tongue. All the intention of the Holy One, Blessed be He, is for this one upon that one... to provide sustenance... its fruits. Even the Holy One, Blessed be He, over the heavens... and the life of the Holy One, Blessed be He, is His fruits. They explained it through the names of the righteous... the way of the Great Glory, ascending and cleaving to the pioneer... through the righteous and the good among Israel, that He should be blessed and guard them... and this is in the rectification of the Holy One, Blessed be He. Behold, they explained that even though through the days He rectified the pure and clear overflow, the Holy One, Blessed be He, blesses his intention... Kindness of the righteous and the good, for they increase and strengthen power in the Supernal Might <note>This refers to the mystical concept of *Tzorech Gavoah*, where human deeds "strengthen" God’s ability to interact with the world</note>... by their deeds. And they strengthen the grace of the Holy One, Blessed be He... a root below that descends from above... so that His Shekhinah is among the lower beings... and everything depends on the Service and good deeds, for they are what draw the Shekhinah downward and establish her in the place of the Holy Temple. And this great secret is unified in His glory, which is what our Rabbi intended to prove in this chapter.

### Chapter 3

->I saw fit for our Rabbi, of blessed memory, to explain what he desires from the verses asked:<-

General Principle! It is that the Services are also a necessity for prophecy, just as we discussed from the scriptures and the words of our Sages of blessed memory in the previous chapters and as we mentioned in the introduction to this book. And from this place... what is the benefit for the Holy One, Blessed be He... why does it help Him? Does it give Him anything or harm Him? ... "If you are righteous, what do you give Him?" <note>Job 35:7</note>. "The word of the Lord is pure" <note>Psalm 18:31</note>... why is He a shield for you? He is a shield for all who take refuge in Him. At first thought, it seems there is no addition to Him... but when he harms it, then he helps it...

<column-break/>

And he said that he did not ascend from the earth for nothing, so that the Sages of the One did not nullify your portion... so that you should not know any other besides Him. Therefore, he mentioned the "last of Egypt" in the middle. So I found in the Midrash on Psalms on the verse "When Israel went out of Egypt," Rabbi Joshua ben Levi said: In the merit of the Tabernacle, Israel was redeemed from Egypt, as it is said: "And God saw the Children of Israel" <note>Exodus 2:25</note>, and it is written: "And Moses saw all the work" <note>Exodus 39:43</note>. And you have a place from which to learn... "that I took them out of the land of Egypt" regarding the Sages of His tongue in the Torah... this is the language of the Midrash. And this is the verse "The spirit of Moses to him," and it is written... and many are the gatherings that testify to this... and I have already mentioned it regarding the verse "And He spoke to Nathan and his words."

And regarding the verse "And He spoke," he wrote in this language: From here you shall understand that the Holy One, Blessed be He, [dwelling] in Israel is not for a need of assistance, but for a necessity of prophecy. For once Moses... publicized through the Glory, the Name of the Glory receives an addition of the Holy Spirit. And that is "May the glory of the Lord endure forever; may the Lord rejoice in His works" <note>Psalm 104:31</note>. Therefore, Israel has the power to be His helpers, adding strength to the Supernal Might according to their deeds, as it is written: "You neglected the Rock that begot you" <note>Deuteronomy 32:18</note> and it is written: "With God we shall do valiantly" <note>Psalm 60:14</note>.

And to indicate that the Shekhinah in Israel is a necessity for prophecy: when there was prophecy, he even prayed for the Temple, that it should be a Tabernacle and a Throne for the Supernal Glory to dwell in. He said in his prayer: "See that Your place be there" for the sake of the Lord, in the House, so that the kingdom should not be in a house other than His. For it is not the glory of the kingdom to be on the outside rather than the inside. And all the blessings... and because the Temple is a throne for the Supernal Glory... this is what he meant by "For the sake of the Lord." For when the Shekhinah dwells in the Holy Temple and rests upon Israel, as it is written, then the Great Name is honored in His glory, and then the House crowns King Solomon and radiates light upon him from the Source. For when the Shekhinah dwells among the lower beings, the Supernal Shekhinah also dwells among the upper beings. 

And because this matter of the Shekhinah resting in Israel is a necessity for prophecy, this is the reason for the Services that were in the Temple—the place of the Shekhinah—to sustain her and hold her among the lower beings, so that she might be fixed in the Temple. Through this, the upper blessings are aroused from the beginning of Thought until the end. And the secret of the unification of the Great Name in its word: the Service is from the power of the upper Attributes... and as it dwells among the lower beings, it is a necessity for prophecy. He knew the end of everything, he would pray for the Temple to be the place of the Shekhinah... and in her return below, she would also return above. And then the intention in creation [is fulfilled], for so the Sages of blessed memory said: "Originally, the essence of the Shekhinah was among the lower beings."

And in the first chapter of Berakhot, Rav said: Even Daniel was only answered for her sake, as it is said: "Now therefore, O our God, listen to the prayer of Your servant and to his pleas, and make Your face shine upon Your sanctuary, which is desolate, for the sake of the Lord" <note>Daniel 9:17</note>. It should have said "for Your sake," but rather it means "for the sake of Abraham, who called You 'Lord'." And they hinted... for the creations that preceded their blessing... our forefather, the God of the Shekhinah from her place that was among the lower beings at the beginning... and they caused separation and sorrow. And when she departed from the lower beings at the beginning, she also [departed] from the upper beings...

And Abraham our forefather, even though he knew the essence of the matters—that they began to rectify and "restore the crown to its former glory"—he would publicize His existence and call the name of the Holy One, Blessed be He, in the mouth of every creature. He would teach them to acknowledge the divinity of the Single Lord, etc., to Him alone. This is the wisdom of the gathering... until he came and rectified that which the generations had distorted. Through his occupation, he was a throne of glory for the Shekhinah, and she was among the lower beings by virtue of his good deeds. And just as he rectified below, so too he rectified above, and matters returned to their former state and their inheritance. Daniel [prayed] for this before the Holy One, Blessed be He, through the virtue of Abraham and his merit, to seek mercy and to pray for the Temple... so that the Shekhinah would return to her former state, so that all things would return to their rectification and their unification above as well. For so Abraham rectified, and everything is by the judgment of what he said: "For the sake of the Lord." And because the whole was praying for...

### The Section on Service | Chapter 2

### Chapter 1

The faith that shall be in the secret, and all his deeds are in faith according to His will; for just as you, by the will of her actions, serve Him with good deeds, so shall they do His will, and live and fear, saying "And he shall produce for you," etc. <note>original: ויפק לך; likely a reference to Proverbs 8:35 or 12:2, "obtaining favor from God"</note>. Included in this is the saying: "A yoke is good," <note>original: עול שק טוב; likely a play on 'the yoke of the kingdom of heaven'</note> the language and both of them... their eyes hang upon them, a portion of them to serve the scales of his freedom and his choice in the nullification of the eternal crown <term>Keter: the highest of the ten Sefirot or divine emanations</term>. Serve Him forever, the wine within it in the sickness of your yoke and its rising, and upon this and their service of them, and their eyes and the life of the beginning, awakening upon him to join him, this in the beginning to join the holy secret as is proper.

"And you shall do them" <note>Leviticus 26:3</note>—not according to the version of the wine <unclear>chamar</unclear>. Rabbi Shimon said: "And David made a name" <note>2 Samuel 8:13</note>. Did David actually "make" it <note>the Name of God</note>? This means that because of the freedom and you shall make the scales of freedom and for the poor of the Kingdom <term>Malchut: the tenth Sefirah, associated with the Divine Presence on earth</term> as is proper. All occupation <insert>of the commandments</insert> is for the sake of the Above, and there was no king in the world who merited this glory. In the end, [it is] like the skull <note>original: gulgalt; a reference to the 'Golgalt' or skull in the Zoharic description of the Divine head</note> of the night... until the holy Presence is supported on His throne with the flavor to ascend the crown through the Tetragrammaton <term>The four-letter Name of God</term>, as if it were possible to say that "He made a name" literally. So too, "and you shall do them" is written; and behold, you see that you are joined to make them, to connect the holy secret as is proper. All those blessings from above are gathered in them through your rectifications as is proper. Thus far. 

Behold, they have chosen the ultimate glory, for by performing the commandments below, they provide <note>original: yefarnes; literally 'to provide sustenance' or 'to nurture' the divine realm</note> above and awaken their counterparts to rectify with their deeds the Glory that is above. They elevate the Service through these ten [commandments] and five. Through these good deeds, the upper realms are awakened to join and unite with one another. This is the matter: all and the life of the way of doing the choice... "And David made a name," and in this rectification of the Glory... you rectify and unite as yourself... serving always without a break, causing the doing of kindness and its rectification—this kindness is the Will and the Supernal satisfaction. Its absence [comes] through nullification, but [doing so] awakens the blessing and the abundance from the expanse that spreads until the end. This is included in the blessing, which is the "all" <note>original: kol; often a reference to the Sefirah of Yesod</note>... in the Supernal Glory.

And all this will be clarified, for the righteous <term>Tzadikim: holy people whose actions maintain the world</term> through their service and good deeds manifest strength in Might <term>Gevurah: the Sefirah of strength or severity</term>, for they draw the light and the abundance from the Source until the "end" of the Kingdom. As our Rabbis of blessed memory said in the Midrash Chibat <note>possibly a reference to a specific Midrashic compilation or 'Chibat Yerushalayim'</note> on the verse "And David made a name": Rabbi Yehuda in the name of Rabbi Yehuda bar Simon said: "Whenever the children of Israel do His will, they add strength to Might." <note>original: מוסיפין כח בגבורה; a foundational kabbalistic idea that human deeds empower God</note>. This is what we say, as if it were possible, that by performing the Torah and commandments, the light is improved from the "Eye" to the "Crown," and from the "Crown" to the "Luck" <note>original: mazal; in the Zohar, this refers to the 'Beard' of the Divine Countenance from which grace flows</note>... they give Him strength and power.

And so the Divine Presence becomes empowered in its assistance to Israel, for it is an expanding and drawn-out power. We have learned the saying: "All who find strength." Rabbi Yochanan said: "So it was that the righteous would elevate the strength of the secrets of Jacob our forefather... and stood to pray, saying: 'And God Almighty give you mercy...'" <note>Genesis 43:14</note>. From here we see that the righteous, through their service and prayer, prepare strength in Might... because they draw down to it the light and the abundance from the expanse to kindness, and it is rectified and established there... the image of the world of the backward light. The Righteous one below awakens the "Righteous One" <note>the Sefirah of Yesod</note> above, and the creators rectify and make the Glory that is above and add... just as from below, so from above. The Righteous One on high is clarified like the righteous ones below... as it is said, "Give strength to God." <note>Psalm 68:35</note>. 

And in the Midrash of Rabbi [Shimon]... "There is one pillar from the earth to the firmament, and 'Righteous' (Tzadik) is its name," after the name of the righteous and the pious and the upright in the world... and if it were not for him, [the world] could not exist. And he sustains the entire world, as it is written: "And the Righteous is the foundation of the world." <note>Proverbs 10:25</note>. And if he did not exist, the world could not be sustained. Therefore, even if there is only one righteous person in the world, he sustains the whole world. This pillar is what they said in the second chapter of [Tractate] Hagigah:

<column-break/>

Rabbi Elazar ben Shammua says: "It stands upon one pillar, and 'Righteous' (Tzadik) is its name, as it is said: 'And the Righteous is the foundation of the world.'" <note>Hagigah 12b</note>. This is the foundation of the earth... the pillar is in the middle and upon it... for it is "all in the heavens and the earth." It is the one that supports the heavens upon the earth and joins them to be one. It is called "Righteous" after the name of the righteous people in the world who awaken it with their good deeds... and it is clarified that through them, light and abundance flow to it from the Source of all. These are the righteous in their lives. And he sustains the entire world... and the Kingdom of the House of David. And if, God forbid, they were to be corrupted by the awakening of the lower ones according to their evil deeds... the world could not be sustained. When the righteous are found, it becomes empowered and is called "Righteous" ... even if there is only one righteous person in the world, he sustains the world, for he is the counterpart of the Righteous One above. The Righteous One above sustains and bears the world as long as the righteous one below performs his service properly.

It has been clarified, then, from what we have written in this chapter, that the Service is a "High Necessity" <term>Tzorech Gavoah: the idea that God or the divine order 'needs' human ritual/moral action</term> and not just a human necessity. The Glory is also joined in a bond of delight... through the awakening of the lower ones by the choice of their deeds. Since the matter is so, the Service must be without interruption. For through the neglect of service and the lack of deeds, a flaw will be perceived in His Glory, and this [diminishes] the blessing and the abundance. Since there is no foundation... if they neglect the service and lack deeds, the unity [is harmed]. Therefore, the study of Torah is equivalent to all the commandments, and it is the great cause of unity; for one who occupies himself with the Torah is literally dealing with the Name of the Living God... as it is written: "This book of the Torah shall not depart from your mouth, but you shall meditate on it day and night," <note>Joshua 1:8</note> and it is written: "I have set the Lord before me always." <note>Psalm 16:8</note>.

### Chapter 2

Service as a High Necessity is a great foundation in the holy faith, for it strengthens the hearts and settles them upon the Service and the Unity. The occupation with it is the true life, and through it, the true servant will exist. It is necessary to introduce and prepare his heart to internalize it and to prove it further, for this is the whole of man.

He said that the great later sages, in the true truth—the Ramban <term>Rabbi Moses ben Nachman (Nachmanides), 13th-century philosopher and kabbalist</term>, of blessed memory, wrote at the end of the portion of "When you have begotten children" <note>Deuteronomy 4:25</note>... in this language: "Know, my son, a great principle: that according to the plain sense of the matter, the writing concerning Israel is a human necessity and not a High Necessity. However, it is like the matter the verse states: 'Israel, in whom I will be glorified.'" <note>Isaiah 49:3</note>. 

And Joshua said: "And what will You do for Your great Name?" <note>Joshua 7:9</note>. Many verses come [to support] this, as well as the thought of of blessed memory. Here he thought they were [essential] obligations. And it is written: "And I will remember My covenant." And specifically according to what we have understood from his students, the Kabbalists who received from him, they said in this language: "The writer says that according to the plain sense... writing about Israel is a human necessity. But in the way of the secret, it is not so, but rather it is a High Necessity, as it is said: 'Israel in whom I will be glorified.' The Honored Name says: 'Because of your sacrifices and your service, I am glorified in the beauty of My strength.'" And Joshua said: "What will You do for Your great Name?"—meaning, if the enemies destroy Your name, which is great... what will You do for Your great Name? We have no place here. 

And so too the thought of of blessed memory... and his life hinted at the Assembly of Israel. And so "And I will remember my covenant" mentions the hints. And this matter is explained there. And the Kabbalistic sage, our master Rabbeinu Bahya <term>Rabbeinu Bahya ben Asher, 13th-14th century Spanish commentator</term>, of blessed memory, wrote there in the portion of "And I appeared" <note>Exodus 6:3</note> on the verse: "And they shall know that I am the Lord their God, who brought them out of the land of Egypt, that I may dwell among them." <note>Exodus 29:46</note>. He says that the bringing out was for the sake of "that I may dwell among them," for if not for this, He would not have brought them out. This shows that the dwelling of the Divine Presence (Shekhinah) among Israel is a High Necessity, and this is also the secret of human necessity. And this, in my opinion, is what the Sages of blessed memory said: "I am the Lord your God who brought you out of the land of Egypt... and without Me you shall not know [any god]... and besides Me there is no savior."

-># Chapter 2: The Section on Service — Chapter 3 | Page 26<-

Who said that His kindness will not change from the Glory of God because of His lack; for the division of the vessel that receives your portion, etc. <note>original: חילוק כלי המקבל; a common philosophical metaphor suggesting that while the Divine light is constant, the human "vessel" determines how much is received.</note> Rather, you should know that there is an "other," and therefore he mentioned the lack caused by the cutting off of darkness. And so too is His portion in the Midrash on Psalms <note>Midrash Tehillim</note> regarding the verse "as the inheritance of Israel," those who inherit the desires of Joshua, so too Levi; to say that in the merit of He who dwells in His inheritance, Israel—who inherit wisdom and fear—increase the children of Israel. And it is written: "And he saw all the work" <note>Exodus 39:43</note>. And you have another place to learn from, that He granted them their portion from the cutting off of His inheritance to dwell within it, based on the general language of the Midrash's trial. And this is what is written: "for a habitation for Himself" <note>Psalm 132:13</note>, and it is written: "Here I will dwell, for I have desired it" <note>Psalm 132:14</note>. Many gatherings <note>scholarly opinions</note> have commented on this, and I have already mentioned them regarding the verse "And He spoke" and the like.

And regarding the verse "And He spoke," he wrote in this language: From here you shall understand that the Divine Presence <term>Shekhinah: the feminine, indwelling aspect of God</term> among Israel is not for the "need of the commoner" <note>human benefit</note> alone, but for a "High Need" <term>Tzorech Gavoah: the idea that human actions affect or "complete" the Divine realm</term>. For since the Unique Name spreads through the Glory, the Glory receives an additional measure of the Holy Spirit. This is the meaning of "May the Glory of the Lord endure forever; let the Lord rejoice in His works" <note>Psalm 104:31</note>. Therefore, Israel has the power to strengthen or add power to the "High Might" <note>the Sefirah of Gevurah/Power</note> according to their involvement. Regarding this, it is written: "You neglected the Rock who begot you" <note>Deuteronomy 32:18</note>, and it is written in the sections regarding the effort of the servant's strength.

To show that the Divine Presence in Israel is a "High Need," Daniel prayed for the Temple that was being established, and by the power of the Supernal Glory that would come after their prayer: "Cause Your face to shine upon Your sanctuary which is desolate, for the sake of the Lord" <note>Daniel 9:17</note>. He taught: By the power of Your House, the Queen <note>a reference to the Shekhinah</note> shall be established in the Holy House, for the Glory of the Queen is loath to be outside of His presence forever. And when the blessing is for another—since the Temple is a throne for the Supernal Glory, which is the Divine Presence—it is in this secret that he said "for the sake of the Lord." For the indwelling of the Divine Presence rests in the Temple and rests within Israel. Through His goodness, the Great Name is magnified in His Glory, and the Glory is a crown for King Solomon, looking upon him from the Source. For when the Divine Presence is occupied with purity among those below, the Supernal Shekhinah also flourishes among those above.

According to this secret, the order of the Divine Presence in Israel is hinted at, and this is the reason for the "Services" <note>sacrifices and rituals</note> that were in the Temple, the place of the Divine Presence: to draw it down and hold it among the lower beings so it would be fixed in the Temple. When the lower things end, the upper things distance themselves from the Temple due to ethics and rebuke. The Great Name then returns to its previous state. The Service is one of the attributes of the Divine Presence among the lower beings, and from here stems its secret: that it is a "High Need" among the lower beings. One who knows this will pray for the Temple, that it may once again become the place of the Divine Presence, that it may dwell and return to its place. By its return below, it also returns above. This is what is written regarding the "Blessed One," for thus they said: the primary essence of the Divine Presence was originally among the lower beings.

In the blessing of the first chapter, Rav said: Even Daniel only requested this for the sake of Abraham our father. And now listen: Daniel, do not separate your servant <note>from prayer</note> with a thousand supplications—"Cause Your face to shine upon Your sanctuary which is desolate, for the sake of the Lord." It should have said "for Your sake," but rather it means "for the sake of Abraham," who called You "Lord" <term>Adon: Master/Lord</term>, etc. And they hinted that his blessing is the merit of the Foundations <note>the Patriarchs</term> that preceded their recognition. They understood the portion of the Divine Presence, that its place should rest among the lower beings to shepherd the flocks and the rivers of influence and the miracles. When it departed from the lower beings, it also departed from the upper beings, and the connection was severed. To restore this recognition, he <note>Abraham</note> began to repair and "restore the crown to its former glory" <note>a phrase meaning to return a tradition to its peak</note>. His mouth publicized the Unity and called upon the Name of the Holy One, Blessed be He, before every creature, teaching them about His essence in the Kingdom, the mystery of Unity, and that to Him alone belong dominion and kingship. In the end, he repaired the kindness of the sins of the generations, and his occupation was the secret of Glory for the Divine Presence, to settle it among the lower beings through his good deeds. Just as he repaired it below, he repaired it above. Matters were ordered for the Divine Presence as a "Special Treasure" <note>Segulah</note>, to be with power before the Holy One, Blessed be He, as recipients of blessing. His merit was to ask for mercy and to pray for the Temple to be built, so the Divine Presence would return to its place below, so that all things would return to their repair and foundation above as well. For thus Abraham repaired it, and all was through what he said, "for the sake of the Lord." And because Daniel was praying for

<column-break/>

the repair that was his essence, so that it might be repaired as Abraham repaired it—who was himself <note>the embodiment of this repair</note>—everything was a "High Need." It was explained elsewhere that this was not for himself, but for the sake of Abraham who called Him "Lord" in the secret of the "paved white stone." This is the meaning of: "The kindnesses of the Lord never cease... they are new every morning" <note>Lamentations 3:22-23</note>. The secret of its existence is "appointing a companion," as is known to the heart of understanding.

By his strength, Abraham His beloved hinted at matters involving the "blessings of a prophet." So too for the majority of the righteous, who are called the "knees of themselves" and are emanated through the "blessings of Heaven." This is the established Service and the sustenance required from God. The water is placed in the outer vessels of the kingdom, the external actions. These are called the "Sages of Action" <term>Chachmei Ma'aseh: those who focus on the practical performance of commandments</term> because of what we wrote above: according to the depth of the secret of the "Name." This is the secret of the repair of the Glory and its unification with the Supernal Name—the Righteous One <note>the Sefirah of Yesod</note> who sustains the world and the foundations. The Sages of Action are those decreed for this. This is the secret of the "kidneys that advise" <note>a Talmudic idiom for intuition/conscience</note> and produce fruit. He returns to the order of the "Good Guardian," like the cycle in the Assembly of Israel. They mention the sage Rabbi Phinehas the priest, son of Hama: The firmament whose name is *Aravot* <note>the highest heaven</note> has the deeds of the righteous sown upon it, and the secret is "it produces fruit," end of quote.

The firmament of *Aravot* stands in the heart of the world and its unity. Just as the brain nourishes everything from the white of the heart, so everything that enters is mixed there. Through the deeds of the righteous, it is joined and becomes a crown for the Name. The world knows this because it bows at the sign of the Commandment and the power until its peak, and to its "Righteous One." This is the secret of "producing fruit" in the secret of its existence. To remember our days—and the power of all this is the deeds of the righteous that ascend in the perfection of intention, which are formed and categorized in the firmament of *Aravot*. These are its fruits, as they mentioned. We have already mentioned this in the introduction of this book.

In the Midrash of Rabbi Tanchuma, the Holy One, Blessed be He, said in this language: All the intentions of the Holy One, Blessed be He, are one upon the other. They hinted at this "tree" one upon the other through a verse that proves its fruits. So too the Holy One, Blessed be He, placed the water as His chariot, like the water of that tree. The "House" and the "Tree" of the Holy One, Blessed be He, are Wisdom and Understanding <term>Chokhmah and Binah: the second and third Sefirot</term>, like the living waters that flow from the Great Source through the great pipe, ascending and clinging to the Tree. Upon this, it flourishes through Israel, who are the righteous and the good, so that the Understanding <note>Binah</note> shall be between them, measured according to their deeds by the law of the Holy One, Blessed be He.

Behold, they have explained that through the water and the sound of the ordered abundance, the Holy One, Blessed be He, is "mounted" upon it. His waters stand in the mercies of Wisdom, and His secret is chosen by Israel, who are the righteous and the good, for they increase and strengthen the power of the "Might" <note>Gevurah</note>. The provision of the province is in their hands through their deeds. For this reason, the commoner is at the "right hand" of the Holy One, Blessed be He. This is proof of the Unity: for when it dwells below, it also flourishes above. Since it returns above, the Divine Presence only dwells below through the word. If so, the Divine Presence among the lower beings is a "High Need." Everything depends on the secret of the Services and the good deeds, for they draw the influence downward and establish a dwelling place in the location of the Temple. Through this, the Great Name is exalted in its Glory. This is what we needed to prove in this chapter.

## Chapter 3

I have seen in the words of our Sages, of blessed memory, something that appears from its plain meaning to contradict what has been received and established! This is the principle that the Services are a "High Need" as well, as we have proven from the verses and the words of our Sages in the previous chapters and in the introduction to this book.

This is what they said in the Midrash "Yelammedenu" regarding the section on the Peace-Offerings <note>Shelamim</note>: What desire does the Holy One, Blessed be He, have when you slaughter an animal? Does He say "I shall eat"? Are you "saving" Him? Does it "harm" Him if you do not? Does He care? If you are wise, you are wise for yourself. It is not written "to give to you," but rather "to refine the creatures." There it says "The Lord is blessed," etc. Why? To be a shield for you, as it is said: "He is a shield to all who take refuge in Him" <note>Psalm 18:31</note>.

At first thought, this seems to say that He does not care if one slaughters or eats, and it is all for the person's own benefit. It suggests that nothing "harms" Him or "saves" Him, and nothing reaches Him at all. This is as it appears from the plain meaning of the verses: "If you are righteous, what do you give Him? Or what does He receive from your hand? Your wickedness affects only a man like yourself" <note>Job 35:7-8</note>.

Faith in the One who exists in the Mystery <note>original: "סוד" (Sod); referring to the hidden, mystical dimensions of the Divine.</note>, and all His works are in faith according to our will. For just as the act of the **Upper Offering** <note>The spiritual archetype of the sacrifices performed in the Temple.</note> is meant to ascend through one's good deeds, so too they fulfill our will and live, as it is said, "You shall decree a thing, and it shall be established for you" <note>Job 22:28</note>. It is explained from this further when they spoke of the *Cup of Lebanon* <note>Likely a reference to a specific Kabbalistic text or the Sefirah of Binah/Understanding.</note>; and when you change them from life, and "you shall answer them," you shall "salt it with salt" <note>A play on the ritual requirement to salt sacrifices.</note> for the one who awakens His lights in His rising, and He in His riddles, **as it were**, acts according to his heart <note>original: "כביכול" (Kivyakhol); a term used to avoid being overly literal when describing God's "actions" or "feelings."</note> for the action of a bit of matter through these acts of service and his faith.

And regarding this: "And you shall answer them," and they answered, and their afflictions, and his mysteries, and his profanity; and they awaken upon you to be honored by these without being requested from His hand. The Holy One <note>God</note> looks and examines: "And you shall do them" <note>Numbers 15:39</note>. And it does not say "as one who carries." Did Rabbi Shimon not say: "**And David made a name**" <note>2 Samuel 8:13</note>? Did David actually *make* the Name [of God]? Rather, because he walked in the paths of freedom and performed the commandments of freedom, he attained the Kingdom as is fitting. **As it were**, he "made" the Name above. There was no king in the world who merited this dwelling place and helped... like a skull for the moon, and take a mask for the Holy One, blessed be He, until He supported His holy Name upon the Throne. As it is known to the sorcerers, according to the explanation on the right side, **as it were**, a voice actually "made a Name" there. Thus, the calculation stands and the sickness of the tax shall be removed, and I have built thus: "And David made a name."

And regarding this: "And you shall answer it" is written, and the living and gracious shall be sent to act for them, to sanctify the Holy Name as is seen fit. All those above are found among you according to their proper arrangements, as is fitting for a Priest. Behold, in these matters lies the ultimate choice; for by performing the commandments below, one prepares <note>original: "יזנוס" (likely a scribal error for "יגנוס" or "יזמין", meaning prepares or invites)</note> [the way] above, and they awaken their counterparts to repair the **Upper Glory** through their actions. It is accounted to the doer as if he actually *made* it. And through your good deeds, the upper realms are awakened to connect and unite with one another. Regarding this, the Zohar says: "And they awaken upon you," etc. This matter, in this way, is the making of the "Book of the Crown" in Lod, since "David made a name."

The entire repair of the Glory includes the "Kindness of the Glory," which he repairs and unifies in the depths of the Torah. We fulfill its commandments, and through his service, the servant always sustains it on weekdays. In the end of all, the tax shall ascend, and this kindness shall repair it; this is the **Offering**, the upper hidden thing. Your merit in His glory and His hiddenness thus awakens the blessing and the expansive flow that spreads to its end. It is also like the general blessing, which is "for strength is Might" <term>Gevurah: the Sefirah of strength, judgment, and power</term> in its repair within the "Glory of Freedom." All this will be explained, for the Righteous, through their service and their good deeds, **add strength to the Divine Might**. They draw down the light and the flow from the Source to the House of the Kingdom <term>Malchut: the Sefirah representing the physical world and the Divine Presence</term>.

As our Sages of blessed memory said in the Midrash on Lamentations <note>Midrash Eicha Rabbah 1:33</note>, on the verse, "He has departed from the daughter of Zion all her splendor": Rabbi Azaria said in the name of Rabbi Judah bar Simon: "When Israel does the will of the Place <note>A title for God, "HaMakom."</note>, they **add strength to the Divine Might**, as it is said: 'In God we shall do valiantly' <note>Psalm 60:14</note>." The secret of this is in his firstborn; for through the performance of the Torah and the commandments, they draw the light from the **Nothingness** <term>Ayin: the infinite source</term> to the **Crown** <term>Keter: the first emanation</term>, and from the Crown to the **Garden**—facing the Assembly of Israel, which is "two thousand" <note>A common Kabbalistic reference to the "two thousand years" the Torah preceded the world.</note>. They add strength to grace and valor. For this Might shall be inaugurated and warmed.

We have learned their saying: "The Cup of Lebanon" and all the "smiling of strength." Rabbi Yochanan said that thus the Righteous would strengthen the power in the Might... until now in these days. And he preceded with prayer, as if to say: "May [the Lord] grant you mercy." Everything depends on this: the pious and the righteous, through their service and prayer, **add strength to the Might** facing His voice, to tell you that they draw down upon it the light and the expansive flow below, and they unify it with its light, facing the "Form of the World," the Light which resides in your eyes.

The Righteous one below awakens the **Righteous one above** <term>Tzaddik: in Kabbalah, this refers to the Sefirah of Yesod, the cosmic connector</term>. They strengthen and build the Upper Glory, adding to and warming its strength—this one from below and that one from above. The Righteous one above connects like a horse to the form below, strengthening its power as it is a "cloud over God." It is written in the Midrash of Rabbi Bahusya: Thus the Holy One, blessed be He, suspended one **Pillar** from the earth to the firmament, and its name is "Righteous" <note>Tzaddik</note>, named after the righteous people. When there are righteous people in the world, it connects... and he sustains the entire world, as it is written: "**The Righteous is the foundation of the world**" <note>Proverbs 10:25</note>. Not only that, but the world cannot exist [without it]. Therefore, if there is only one righteous person in the world, he sustains the world. This pillar...

<column-break/>

Rabbi Eleazar ben Shammua says: The world stands upon one pillar, and its name is **Michael** <note>The archangel often associated with the Sefirah of Chesed (Kindness) or the sustenance of Israel.</note>, and "The Righteous is the foundation of the world." This is the sign of Ecclesiastes; it is the "Land of Existence" reaching to the firmament that stands in the middle. Concerning it, it is said: "For all that is in heaven and earth" <note>1 Chronicles 29:11</note>, and the end of the **Holy Constellation** <term>Mazzal: usually 'luck' or 'destiny', but in Kabbalah, it refers to the flow from the highest Sefirot</term> with the earth and the covering to give life to all. The verses refer to it by the name of the righteous.

When there are righteous people in the world who awaken them with their good deeds, which "warm" his strength, it is made so; for they make light within it, and the light and flow from the **Source of All** are gathered into it. Within it, he pours out his flash. He sustains the entire world, the "Constellation" and the "Kingdom of the House of David." God forbid <note>original: "ולא שם ושלום", likely "חס ושלום"</note> that it should be otherwise from the start. Through the awakening of those below, according to their evil deeds in the "generation's constellation," then it shall be "void," etc. The world cannot exist, and then it is called an "evil time."

But he said that according to the deeds of the righteous, it grows strong, and it is called "Light" in the name of His compassion. Even if there is only one righteous person, he sustains the world, for he is the counterpart of the **Righteous One above**. The Righteous One above sustains and bears the world for the sake of the righteous one below when he performs his service properly.

It shall be explained, then, from what we have written in this chapter, that **Service is a Divine Need** <term>Tzorech Gavoah: the concept that God 'needs' or 'desires' human action to manifest His light</term>, and not for the need of the commoner alone. This is explained regarding the Glory in the "Prayer of the Cloud," etc. This is through the awakening of those below through the service of action. Because the Glory is such, it requires the attainment of its service through the "finding grace"; for with a little service or a lack of deeds, the Miracle becomes "precious" in His glory, and the flow of blessing and abundance is withheld.

Since there is no limit to the law and time, for there is no cessation in service—as the lack of deeds causes separation—therefore, the **Study of Torah** is equal to all the commandments. It is the great cause of Unification, for in the repair of the Torah, one is literally occupied with the Name of the Lord <note>The Tetragrammaton (Y-H-V-H)</note>, as will be further explained in the "Section on Ecclesiastes," the completion of this book. As David said: God said to Joshua, "**This book of the law shall not depart from your mouth**; but you shall meditate therein day and night" <note>Joshua 1:8</note>. And it is written of David: "O Lord... answer us in the day when we call" <note>Psalm 20:10</note>, always.

Holiness, for it strengthens the hearts and draws them toward service and Unification. Those who delve into this are [accessing] the **True Life** through which everything truly lives. I say that the greatest of the later Sages in the True Wisdom <note>referring to Kabbalah</note>, the **Ramban** <note>Rabbi Moshe ben Nachman / Nachmanides (1194–1270)</note>, of blessed memory, wrote on the portion of *Ki Tavo* regarding the verse: "And I will dwell among them" <note>Exodus 25:8</note>, that there is a **Great Secret** in this matter. And in the **Unification**, according to what his students who received [tradition] from him explained, they said: "The Cup of Lebanon." Regarding this cup: according to the plain meaning, it would seem that the Divine Presence among Israel was for a "human need" alone. In the way of a parable, it is not so; rather, it is for a **Divine Need**, as in the matter of "Israel, in whom I will be glorified"—the word of God. Regarding the Glory: "Because of your sacrifices and your service, I am glorified in the Prayer of the Cloud."

And Joshua said: "And what will You do for Your great Name?" Meaning, if the enemies destroy our name, what will You do for Your great Name which is ours? For we have nothing else here. And so, "even for a refuge for Him." "Here I have desired to dwell." This points to the **Assembly of Israel** <note>Knesset Israel / Shekhinah</note>. And likewise, "the earth is His footstool." All this is explained.

And the Kabbalistic sage, **Rabbenu Bahya** <note>Rabbi Bahya ben Asher (1255–1340)</note> of blessed memory, wrote there in that portion on the verse: "The Cup of Lebanon; and they shall know that I am the Lord who brought them out of the land of Egypt, that I may dwell among them." This says that the Divine Presence was [contingent] upon the condition of "dwelling among them," for if it were not so, He would not have brought them out. This shows that the indwelling of the Divine Presence in Israel is a **Divine Need** as well as a human need. This, in my opinion, is what the verse says: "Save by Your hand... to bring out of the land of Egypt... and I am the Lord... and there is no savior beside Me." And he said...

Rabbi Eliezer said to him, but Rabbi Akiva said: "Behold, it says 'which I command you <insert>today</insert> shall be upon your heart' <note>Deuteronomy 6:6</note>; from here you learn that the entire passage requires focused intent." And they further said there: "Read 'Hear, O Israel: The Lord our God, the Lord is One'—up to this point requires the heart's intent." These are the words of Rabbi Meir. Rava said: "The law follows Rabbi Meir." And in the chapter "One may not stand" <note>Referencing the fifth chapter of Tractate Berakhot in the Talmud</note>, our Rabbis taught: "One who prays must direct his heart to Heaven," for even without this, it says, "You will prepare their heart; You will cause Your ear to hear" <note>Psalm 10:17</note>. And they said further there: "From where do we know that a person should focus his heart? From the verse 'You will prepare their heart.'"

And they said further there: "If one did not focus his mind from the beginning, they would weigh him by his measures to succeed until he focused his mind." And they said further there: "One who prays must focus his heart in all the blessings, and if he cannot focus in all of them, he should focus his heart in at least one." Rabbi Chiyya said in the name of Rav Safra in the name of a master from the house of Rabbi: "In the blessing of the Patriarchs" <note>The first blessing of the Amidah prayer</note>. And in the chapter "The Morning Prayer," Rabbi Elazar said: "A person should always measure himself—if he can focus his heart, he should pray; and if not, he should not pray." And they said further there: "And when you pray, know before whom you are praying; know before whom you stand, and because of this, you will merit the life of the World to Come." And this knowledge—before whom we stand—is hinted at there in the verse regarding the Unique Name <note>The Tetragrammaton, the four-letter name of God</note> of the Lord, who is worthy and the Creator, as will be explained in the chapter. And the knowledge that constitutes service is worthy and complete, and the intent of knowledge is that there is no will other than that which dwells in service. And they said in the Teaching of the Name: "Any priest who does not know for whose sake he splashes the blood or for whose sake he burns the incense—his service is not service." And prayer is called "service," for the Sages said in the Sifrei: "'And to serve Him with all your heart' <note>Deuteronomy 11:13</note>—what is the service of the heart? This is prayer."

# Chapter 4

The intent in the sacrifices <note>original: נשיות (Nashiyot), likely a scribal error or a specific mystical term for "offerings of fire"</note> is that they do not say this or that without the unification of the Great Name; rather, the sacrifices are offered to draw close the realms of action. And in prayer, through speech in the mystery and the special virtue of "the fruit of our lips" <note>Hosea 14:3; prayer as a substitute for sacrifice</note>. Through the name of intent and through proper focus, the spiritual levels relate to and unite with one another, and there is no end to the law for one who increases intent in service, according to the path explained in the chapter. And they said in the Midrash *Shomer Tov* <note>The Midrash on Psalms</note> regarding the Psalm "My heart is steadfast": "And King David came and sat before the Lord." But is there "sitting" before the Omnipresent? For a person only prays while standing, as it is said, "And Phinehas stood and prayed" <note>Psalm 106:30</note>. Rather, there is a "sitting" that one has in prayer when he focuses his prayer. "His face is toward you, You incline Your ear," until you begin to ask from Him; if your heart is focused in my prayer, be assured that your prayer is heard, as it is said, "You will prepare their heart; You will cause Your ear to hear."

And so it says elsewhere, "You will prepare his heart," etc. And do not wonder at the silence <note>Referring to Jeremiah's prayer</note> when he prayed for Israel, for it says "Do not pray for them" etc. Yet when he prayed, he focused his heart, as it says "With all your heart, prepare their heart" etc. For when Israel focused their heart, the Holy One heard their prayer and desired the Name. And so the multitude says, "And the priests arose and blessed the Holy Name with a loud voice." As the Sages said: "And so it was with Rabbi, to focus my heart before Him so that it would be heard," as it is said, "My heart is steadfast." Thus they explained that internal and hidden intent in prayer is the prayer itself, for all acts of service depend upon it. When the priest would offer the sacrifices and focus on the name with proper intent, he would bind and bring close all the spiritual forces into the Infinite (*Ein Sof*), and the blessing would spread through all the worlds. And they said in the Midrash on the language of the Aramaic translation: "Understand in our time to write it; call it 'intent of words,' and for the burning of the sacrifice upon them, to bring out through them our righteousness." And from this, it is permitted to involve our labor in these. And they said further there: "In its time, write it without a mediator <note>original: שושבנא (Shoshvina); best man or intermediary</note>, and bring the sacrifice and burn the incense of spices and focus the words to be accepted in the inner chamber." It is written: "You shall decree a thing, and it shall be established for you." And regarding the matter of prayer, they said in this language: "Whoever has every desire and longing for the Head of Life <note>A title for the Divine</note>, the commandments of holiness require asking his request and forgiving from the depth of the heart, in order to be settled in the House of Peace and merit a heart with good will." Furthermore, the sage Rabbi Shimon bar Yochai said in the *Book of Palaces* <note>Sefer Hekhalot</note> in this language: "Come and see, all those who pray without such intent..."

<sig>N P A Z</sig> <meta>catchword: and is careful</meta>

<column-break/>

The parable in the dream: they shall give to the totality of the commandments. Elsewhere, in *Leviticus Rabbah*, it is explained: "Prepare this animal," which is according to him to write all the strictures of the "swept away exchange." The Master <note>Likely referring to Maimonides or a similar authority</note> said: "The commandments were not given to Israel except to refine the creatures through them." For why should the heart be concerned? And what does it matter to Him? For to all places until now, it seems that the meaning of every stricture of "swept away exchange" is placed upon the totality of the commandments and their weight. And the end of its weight, according to the Midrash *Shomer Tov*, where Rav said: "The Omnipresent did not give the commandments to Israel except to refine them through the weight of strictures. The Lord is 'swept away' <note>original: גרופה (Grufah)</note>." Behold, all this investigation is focused on the totality of the commandments, but it did not satisfy the opinion of the Master. Furthermore, its release from its taking focused on the matter of prayer, the verse of the "Last Table," and its weight is explained in *Leviticus Rabbah* in the section following "My Friend, My Friend." Just as Rabbi Isaac the Outsider <note>original: החיצוני (Ha-Hitzoni)</note> said: "The Holy One, blessed be He, is destined to perform a service for the righteous in the future to come; and anyone who did not eat of the forbidden fats in this world merits to see them in the World to Come." This is seen from what is written: "The fat of a carcass and the fat of a torn animal may be used for any work, but you shall surely not eat it" <note>Leviticus 7:24</note>. Since one abstains from its fat, he will enjoy it in the future to come. Therefore, Moses warns Israel and says, "This is the law of the burnt offering," and so on, until here. Behold, the understanding of the intellect and the focus is in a special place which is part of the established portion, and its mouth is found for my longing; and I have removed from it the movement which is the business of the soul. And I have extracted from the core that it lives and completes my longing from this name, and its release from the service that lives and rests for him from the cessation of the focused intent, and it is hidden in a special place which is part of the sweet portion according to the opinion of the Master. And since this intellectual investigation is a secular tribe and this Torah is in it, it is a wonder like his words; all that the Sages of Truth <note>The Kabbalists</note> received regarding the reason for this commandment for things that are in the covering of the world was hidden from the eyes of the Master. And in the Midrash *Shomer Tov* they said in this language: "Ask what is prepared for the way of God: water, grace upon heat, how and how much." And does it matter to the Holy One, blessed be He, whether one benefits from praise or consumes from the preparation? Rabbi Berachiah, in the name of Rabbi Jacob, wrote: "The fat of a carcass and the fat of a torn animal—if he does not eat it in this world, he is worthy, for the wickedness is greater than the laughter of the future World to Come that follows; and its law is to eat and be simple over all of them."

And they said: "The way of God is perfect; the word of the Lord is refined" etc. <note>Psalm 18:31</note>. This hints at what was explained above in the mystery of "refining the creatures," which is the connection between those above and those below, and the relation of one to the other. And for the Holy One, blessed be He, these and then do not matter to Him—whether one slaughters, etc. For everything is for the sake of the Chosen One, hidden, refined, and pure from all generalities and disqualifications. And when it comes to the refinement, he said: "They shall be for us from all the commandments, and they shall water us from the refined fruits, the voice of which is the perfection and source of the upper ones for us in these; and they are performed so that His glory and merits these perfections of the voice." If so, there is nothing in the commandments of no value <note>original: אלף (Elef); literally 'thousand', here meaning 'small worth'</note> that did not intend a purpose and utility in the wisdom of Heaven, and more so for the Great Name in His glory, as is known to the saviors of perfection. And the teachings show that there is nothing not grasped in the Torah that did not intend a utility, and in it is the relationship of the commandments as a whole. And they prepared to say: "These first ones of His death are to your hearts for all explanations" etc., for "it is not an empty thing from you" <note>Deuteronomy 32:47</note>. And all types of perfections and repairs are attached to things that are in them and in what is drawn from them. And it was said that it is founded there on the life of the World to Come, and as it is said, it "lengthens the days of God"—to say that they are also in the draw of the life of the world.

It also explores the philosophical and mystical reasons for the commandments, arguing that they serve to refine the human soul and connect the physical world to the divine realms.</summary>
