# Chapter 3 | The Section on Service

<meta>catchword: The King</meta>

As it is explained in the holy chapters, those things which prevent attachment to the Upper Things <note>Spiritual realms</note> are like a mountain or a barrier. Through attachment, the union of the lower beings with the upper beings is achieved. If one prays without the proper heart, it is like water that lacks a source. It is proper to say, as the Sages of the Mishnah wrote, that the space of the Tefillin <note>phylacteries</note> must be remembered, for the attachment is uniquely realized through the Mitzvot <term>commandments; from the Hebrew root 'tzavta' meaning connection</term>. The connection mentioned between their performance and their fulfillment is what links them to the Unique Name <note>The Tetragrammaton, the four-letter name of God</note>.

For the Mitzvot we mentioned, even a small amount of their fulfillment is also for the sake of the Divine Glory. For a downward inclination stands below, preventing ascent even above to the holy Sanctuary. Consider the one who commits transgressions: he awakens the "External Forces" <note>original: "chitzoniyot"; in Kabbalah, these are the 'shells' or forces of evil</note> which are the depths of gloom. They cast impurity <note>original: "zohama"</note> and defile the Sanctuary. Regarding the "evil" that occurs when the righteous one and his soul are changed, the reason is not simple. His intent should be not to awaken the "Voice" <note>The Divine attribute</note> to suffer damage, Heaven forbid, but rather to distance it so it may enter the inner Sanctuary, purified and refined from dross. As it says, "Take away the dross from the silver, and there shall come forth a vessel for the refiner; take away the wicked from before the king..." <note>Proverbs 25:4-5</note>. This good intention guards one from violating a negative commandment.

Everything is almost like a path through which the creatures are refined. Through it, they become blessed and honored, and all things are made good. Furthermore, there is a separation and a removal of the "glow of the husk" <note>impurity</note> through the Refined Word, as it says: "Every word of God is refined" <note>Proverbs 30:5</note>. From all this, it will be clarified correctly that deeds—whether good or bad—all reach the High Place. As it is written: "They add strength to the Supernal Power," while evil, as it were <note>original: "kivyakhol"; a term used to avoid literal anthropomorphism</note>, diminishes the great power of the Height. Everything is prepared and clarified.

The Master, the Guide <note>Maimonides</note>, in Part 3, Chapter 27 <note>of The Guide for the Perplexed</note>, details that this refining is not the ultimate end in itself, but it has already been explained by him at the beginning of his discussion there. He thinks that the "External" species have no part in this except in their birth. Rather, everything he intended regarding them was for another purpose, and that is the benefit found there. This is what he said there: "What does it matter to the Holy One, blessed be He, whether one slaughters from the throat or from the nape?" <note>A famous Midrashic quote suggesting God is not affected by the mechanics of rituals</note>. He meant to say that the commandments were only given to refine the creatures, as it says: "The word of the Lord is refined."

The existence of this statement is general, yet it should not be found to be identical to their words as they were openly explained. For we are standing now upon a force that interprets their words in this way, and it does not separate from the holiness drawn upon it. This is because all the Mitzvot possess a beneficial purpose for the kingdom, for nothing is in vain. As He said: "I did not say to the seed of Jacob, 'Seek Me in vain'... I the Lord speak righteousness, I declare things that are right" <note>Isaiah 45:19</note>.

That which requires explanation is this: anyone whose opinion is similar in this matter—that it is possible for a commandment to be given without a reason or benefit—such a person has a logic of vanity. However, there are Divine reasons for which it is said "I have a desire for the commandments." For example, the slaughtering of animals for the sake of good food—the benefit is clear. We are destined to eat, but the fulfillment of the laws regarding the "throat" or the "nape" <note>the specific anatomical locations for ritual slaughter</note> is to "refine the creatures." And so it will be clarified to you from the parable of "slaughtering from the throat or the nape." I mentioned this small point to you because in all their words, of blessed memory, they did not say that the "throat" or "nape" are the same, but the truth of the matter is as I have brought. The logic for eating animals is for a specific purpose, together with the quality of the deed, which cannot be achieved except through slaughtering and the like. And the "nape" was omitted to avoid a cruel death, as they fixed the power of the knife... <note>original: "ad kan l'shono" (until here are his words)</note>. This is the law for the state of this saying, and he produces its meaning according to his opinion, as they already said: "What does it matter to the Holy One, blessed be He, whether one slaughters from the throat or the nape?"

Now come and see how they produced this in the Midrash: "What does it matter to Him if one eats what is pure or eats what is impure? The words of the Torah are only to refine them." Here they were speaking generally about some commandments to hand over everything <unclear>illegible</unclear> and did not intend another purpose; these are only divisions. And the proof from their words, of blessed memory, is that the King...

<column-break/>

...And these are the words of Eliphaz <note>one of Job's friends</note> regarding obligation. And after that, Elihu says: "If you sin, what do you do against Him? Or if your transgressions are multiplied, what do you do to Him? If you are righteous, what do you give Him?" <note>Job 35:6-7</note>. This is for a man like yourself; your wickedness [affects] a man like you. And Solomon the King said: "If you are wise, you are wise for yourself" <note>Proverbs 9:12</note>. From all this, it would seem that the good or evil of a person does not touch the High Place at all, but only affects the one who performs the deed.

But the opposite of this has already been clarified from our words, and that is the truth in which there is no doubt. It is the true Kabbalah <note>received tradition</note> held in the hands of the Sages of the Truth <term>Kabbalists</term>, passed from man to man. Regarding the matter of physicality, they said in the Midrash of Rabbi Shimon bar Yochai <note>The Zohar</note>, peace be upon him, in this language: "Come and see: all those who cling to the Lower Side <note>the realm of impurity</note> are diminished and they cling to that which is darkened." They said the matter of "Inside" and "Bodies" <note>referring to souls and physical vessels</note>: the lights of the King are over them, and the bodies are for the God of the Earth to rest upon. And they do not come to be bound, and he does not cling to Him... Go and see from this other world, for all those who are in the shadow of the King, they are refined and judged. So too, a person who is refined in this world ascends to the other world to be called...

And regarding this it is written: "And you shall be holy to Me" <note>Leviticus 20:26</note>. A person should only cling to His holiness to be joined to Him, and not turn away from his thoughts forever. If they merit it for their souls, they will cling to the Bundle of Life <note>original: "tzror hachayim"</note> and live forever. For they have been found, and the Lord is for their bodies. Regarding this it is written: "For if you keep [the commandments], you shall not die." And it says: "If you keep them, they shall be life to you." But regarding the flesh, it is written: "The dust returns to the earth as it was." This refers to the Side <note>original: "sitra"</note> to which he clung.

Israel is from the Side of the Right <note>The side of Mercy and Holiness in the Sefirotic map</note>. If they cling to the Side of the Left <note>The side of Judgment and potential impurity</note>, they touch that Side, and their bodies and their souls... in the world of Judgment and the world to come. This only happens because he clung to the Side of the Left, which is "another god." And if he merits, it is written: "For you are a holy people to the Lord your God" <note>Deuteronomy 7:6</note>.

Behold, in these words it is explained that the lower being himself, by eating what the Torah forbade, turns to the Left. For he said: "Israel is from the Side of the Right," which represents all holiness and the service of all the fathers <note>the Patriarchs</note>, which is the [holy] eating. As this will be clarified from the secret of the "Sides" and the impurities... And from this, all cling to the Midrash of Rabbi Shimon bar Yochai, especially in the portion regarding "Plagues" <note>Tazria/Metzora</note> and the chain of forbidden sexual relations.

And from them in this language: Rabbi Yitzhak said, "The deficiency is only for the one who does not cling below, but for the one who is found above." And he does not cling except to that which is found below like himself... And in Lamentations Rabbah <note>an ancient homiletical commentary on the Book of Lamentations</note> they said in this language: Rabbi Yehuda bar Simon said in the name of Rabbi Levi bar Tarfon: "When Israel does the will of the Holy One, blessed be He, they add strength to the Supernal Power <note>original: "gevurah"</note>, as it is said: 'And now, let the power of my Lord be great' <note>Numbers 14:17</note>. But when they do not do the will of the Holy One, blessed be He, as it were, they weaken the great power of the Height." And they said further there: "When Israel does not do the will of the Place, as it were, they weaken the great power of the Height, as it is written: 'You neglected the Rock who begot you' <note>Deuteronomy 32:18</note>."

I have already written about this "as it were" regarding the Height. From all this it is clarified that good and evil, Mitzvot and transgressions, do not touch the performer alone, but also the great power of the Height, as it were. And the statement "What does it matter to the Holy One..." etc., and "They were only given to refine..." is not against what we have said. Rather, it will be clarified and understood by the Sages of the Truth from what I have written. The service is for the need of the High Place as well, for the preparation for them is a "time of desire." And "what does it matter to the Holy One" does not mean He is not affected at all. For with this intention, all the verses [of Job] were brought... "Your righteousness and your wickedness do not touch Him" only in terms of the performer. But the good and evil in the context of the straight Will—that the Glory should stand to overflow upon the Upper Heads—this is the beginning of the Thought in the meditation. For such was the pure Will, and His holy desire is for a total necessity.

To bring this about and to be perfected in this intention, and to confess his secret in it, all the Mitzvot and services were given. And in our intention toward them, besides the general intent and the matter of Jacob, through them one always perfects the intention toward the Name. This is the unification of the Great Name in His Glory, which is also for the need of the High Place. This is the matter of the Mitzvot and the depth of the service—intentions focused on the intention of the King...

<summary>This page argues against the philosophical view that God is indifferent to human actions, asserting instead the Kabbalistic principle that Mitzvot (commandments) have a theurgical effect on the Divine realms. It contrasts Maimonides' view of commandments as tools for human refinement with the Zohar's view that human deeds either "strengthen" or "weaken" the Divine power (as it were).</summary>

<meta>This page continues the exploration of "Service out of Love" (Avodah me-Ahavah), contrasting the philosophical views of Maimonides (the Rambam) with the interpretations of Rabbi Joseph ben Shem Tov. It examines whether the ultimate goal of religious life is personal perfection and reward in the afterlife, or a higher, more selfless union with the Divine.</meta>

# The Section on Service / Chapter 8

Or what is considered so because it is the truth, and the ultimate good will come because of it and through him. One who merits on his own the level of a "Prophet" <note>A state of high spiritual attainment</note> by calling out to his "Beloved" <note>God</note>, since he served only out of love, will eventually reach the highest of heights according to the level of his intellect. Indeed, the Torah and the statutes are proven by the words of the Sages who said: "The labor of the Torah must be for its own sake" <note>original: "lishmah"</note>. And behold, in the writings of [Maimonides] of blessed memory, it is discussed etc. Is it not to be valued etc. And since this is what the Scripture says, "He greatly desires His commandments" <note>Psalm 112:1</note>, and to return to reveal and not in the matter of His commandments—this is the primary intent in the Will of God "for His Name's sake" <note>meaning, for the sake of the Divine Himself</note>. And because the whole "Song of the Turtledoves" <note>A poetic reference to the Song of Songs</note> is a voice and a call for this matter, it explains that he rejoices in this, warning that "I am sick with love" etc.

This is what emerges from his words in the eighth chapter (and it is also the language in the commentary on the Tractate of the Fathers <note>Pirkei Avot</note> in the Mishnah of the denier). And look into the chapter "Helek" <note>The tenth chapter of Tractate Sanhedrin, famous for Maimonides' principles of faith</note>, and what emerges from his words there is that he [Maimonides], may his memory be a blessing, intends that the one who "serves out of love" does not aim his service at any end other than the service of the Place <note>original: "HaMakom," a common rabbinic name for God</note> and standing before Him. Ultimately, such a person is called one who "serves out of love" according to his words, and all the sages who came after him followed this path.

However, the sage Rabbi Joseph, son of the Kabbalist Rabbi Shem Tov ben Shem Tov <note>A 15th-century Spanish Jewish philosopher and commentator</note> of blessed memory, took another path in this, as he wrote in the book *The Eye of the Reader* <note>original: "Ein HaKore"</note> and in the book of the Master Teacher <note>Maimonides' Guide for the Perplexed</note>. The second level of knowledge is known in the [study of] traits, where he said that to a wise man, matters should be honorable in his eyes for their own sake, which is not like his usual way, for they are the [essential] action. He [Rabbi Joseph] removed the preciousness and the good to be like his level, for "sick with love" etc. and the matter is for your intent. How far is your intent from his intent? Woe to the early sages of Israel whose intent in "service out of love" was according to the words of the Academy <note>The traditional school of thought</note> that the Rabbi wrote of. After him, everyone's intent in "service out of love" was the intent of the Academy—the satisfaction of the "ultimate love," as I wrote in the chapters on Love in the first part of this book. 

The intent of those who aim [properly] in the Sages' saying "Be like servants [who serve not for reward]" <note>Ethics of the Fathers 1:3</note> is to say that one should not aim for the expectation of the good, which is "service out of love" for the purpose of an end for oneself, but rather for a [higher] need as mentioned in the fifth chapter later in this book. This is what the entire holy generation relied upon. This was their intent in my book. Those who hold this view, the "pious of your nation" and the "men of vision" will not be awakened in the service of your God in this inner matter, for they have nothing in it but words, no less a matter than his intent in their service. And he who denies the smallness of knowledge, let him look into our writing in the first chapter of this book in the chapters on Love, and he will know our seal upon these faithful foundations and how the intent of service and the commandments is directed.

The sage Rabbi Joseph, son of the Kabbalist Rabbi Shem Tov ben Shem Tov of blessed memory, sought the intent of the service and the commandments as it appears from his words in the book *The Eye of the Reader*. He stated there that "the good of the tongue" is from the fourth level—the level of one who performs these commandments for their true end, which is so that the "Divine Nature" may be added unto him, and he may become a holy "Man of God." This is for the purpose of perfection and the life of the soul, which merits inner purification to "stand with the King" and to know tranquility and to enjoy the "Radiance of the Divine Presence" <note>original: "Ziv ha-Shekhinah"</note>. Ultimately, he added this for the life of the World to Come and the Resurrection of the Dead. This servant will adapt the word "service" in its truth. It is written for the heart of everything that he desires to "cleave to his God" <note>original: "dveikut"</note> and to take a stronghold and delight in all that he desires according to his nature... seeking the ultimate perfection... looking at everything according to its nature toward the First Perfection...

<column-break/>

Abraham our Father clearly loved God. Specifically, in the "Binding of his only son" <term>The Akeidah; the biblical story of Abraham offering Isaac</term>, his compassion did not prevent him, nor was he saved from evil by abandoning the Binding. He went on his way because it was already clear to him that the [Divine] Will is a matter of request and petition... it was not from a lack of power to prevent it... but he intended for his only son... that everything is ultimately for a good purpose and the expression of perfection... in a way that the vision of the lackings resembles the Divine more than the lack. 

He [Abraham] was measured in his conduct in a way that reached the final end for which he existed, to continue his existence by cleaving to his Creator. His thought of Him did not give him a reason to abandon [the command]. Sometimes it is sought in every place to say that His holy hand prevented his precious son because He knew... his level was like that of the angels of heaven. He clearly knew that he would receive a reward for the Binding of his son, and he hoped and desired to do such a thing... and this was the ultimate level according to his [Rabbi Joseph's] opinion. 

However, in his delighting in the "Radiance of the Divine Presence" during his standing in His providence... these commandments which are a physical body... and who is like him... the goal and end and perfection... even though He, may He be blessed, commanded us in them so that we could stand before Him. This is the use of the general excellence. But what is proper is that our sages, those who serve for the sake of the "end" that reaches us... were it not for this, we would be like those who serve for the sake of the "table." From our attachment to Him, everything is based on this.

It is proper to remember the matter: if one reaches the level of wisdom... these are his words and his opinion regarding the intent of service and the commandments. And if they do not reach my understanding, or any of the things that the wisdom of our predecessors requires, they will receive the words... for the upright were supported for the sake of existence. 

I say that the "striving and merit for the life of the World to Come" is not the true ultimate end intended by the service and the commandments. Rather, there is a true end which is even more exalted and noble in itself. The striving and merit for the World to Come follows from it incidentally. Therefore, the servant must aim in his service toward that true, essential ultimate end, which he will achieve, and all other levels will follow. The striving and merit for the life of the World to Come is just a cause and intent of "service out of love" for a secondary need.

In the matter concerning the understanding of our Sages "so that it will be good for you" <note>Deuteronomy 22:7</note>... our intent in our journey regarding the World to Come is that from the thought of the righteous and the level of glory... which awakens the joy that rests upon him. And in the words of the Rabbi who proved to him [Abraham], the Holy One, blessed be He, even said "Who is like Me in the world..." for all the attributes and their perfections were given to us... and what is the reason? Because we are mistaken... for the world... and as explained by all the people of "Helek" <note>The chapter on the World to Come</note>... 

It will be clarified from this to the wise that the merit for the life of the World to Come is [one] way, but the later thinkers [aim] for a more exalted end, which is the "Greatness of the Great Name," to be unified in His glory until the "Infinite" <note>original: "Ein Sof"</note>. This was the purpose of creation and the intent of service and commandments. One who serves for the end of meriting the life of the World to Come—and in the way that the Sage Rabbi Joseph of blessed memory went—he too reaches "service out of love." And we would be serving according to the "Way of Truth" <note>A common term for Kabbalah</note>, for this servant will be whole, aiming for the ultimate end of life, aiming in his service at the "True Unity" <note>original: "Yichud Amiti"</note> which is the hidden body and the eye and the foundation of the way...

<summary>This page analyzes different philosophical and mystical motivations for serving God, specifically debating whether "Service out of Love" aims for personal spiritual reward (the World to Come) or a higher, selfless unification with the Divine Essence (the Infinite/Ein Sof).</summary>

## Chapter 4

One praises God in his prayer with the desire of the heart and with clean hands <note>A reference to Psalm 24:4, signifying moral and ritual purity</note>. He seeks from Him that which is hidden, to weigh it <note>original: "le-matkala," referring to the mystical "Balance" or "Scales" mentioned in the Zohar</note> with the desire of the spirit and his portion. And then, the Heavens are sanctified, to be made holy above all. It is like the Sanctuary of the Holy of Holies; with the **bending of the tongue**, all words are gathered to know how to bind the "bonds" <note>The "bonds" or "knots" refer to the connections between different divine emanations or Sefirot</note> of the incense, and to unify the Unification through his will, with a heart properly searched, in order to attach every drop of spirit to spirit. All becomes one, to be entirely one as is fitting, above all.

Furthermore, it is said that with the **bending of the tongue**, the mechanisms of hidden things are prepared—those things that are darkened <note>original: "de-matchashkha," referring to the concealment of divine light</note>. One directs them with the spirit of heaven to unify them as in the Sanctuary, to bind the bonds of the incense, and to unify everything in a single Unification. These are the "preparations of the hidden" <note>original: "chovkhei taman"</note>, as it is said: "to devise artistic designs" <note>Exodus 35:32; here interpreted as "thinking deep thoughts"</note> above all.

The secret of the matter is to say: the **bending of the tongue** in a whisper <note>original: "le-chishu"</note> to a "Certain One" <note>A coded reference to a specific Divine Name or level of the Godhead</note> above, so that the bride <note>The Shekhinah, or Divine Presence</note> may be extracted from the darkness. Through the desire of the heart, a voice is prepared to cleave the drop and the intent, and to unify them above in the manner of a flame. Just as a "Certain One" <note>The human practitioner</note> emerges from them below, so it is necessary from below to above to bind the bond properly, spirit to spirit, so that they may merit the chosen light. The "diminished thought," the "voice," and the "word"—these four bind the bonds to the **Crown** <note>Keter, the highest of the Sefirot</note> of the incense, binding them all as one to elevate the entire spirit to a single higher portion. In this manner, they are made, and all four ingredients <note>referring to the four components of the incense or the four elements of speech</note> are mixed within them, serving as a peg to strengthen them in all the preparations of the higher bonds. 

Thought is the portion of the will of Unification; it elevates the voice. The voice is used to find words to bind the bonds from below to above, like clouds rising. A whispered voice ties the bonds and draws down blessings from above to below, so that these four—Thought, Will, Voice, and Speech—become a support. This is the sign of the incense: to be bound to the "Flame" <note>original: "le-galvei de-nabla"</note> so it may be tied as a whole. All of this is done for the life-force of the "bonds of bonds," to smell them, and immediately they are properly supported and sealed in all the portions of the world. He who is sealed in this world merits the World to Come, above all.

This teaches that prayer is a deep secret for the "Repair" <note>Tikkun</note> of all the upper and lower worlds, linking the upper things to their foundations in holiness and in proper Unification. This includes the thought of the heart. When one prays to Him with an upright heart, it is attributed to the Divine Will. For grace and favor were found in the intent of the Higher Beings, and in the understanding of their direction, there is power and strength. Love is awakened for the high souls, and comfort comes to them—a "comfort of kindness" <note>Chased</note> upon their return from the heights of the desert <note>A metaphor for the spiritual exile or the void</note>. Through the **awakening from below** <note>original: "it'aruta de-letata," the foundational Kabbalistic principle that human action triggers divine response</note>, there is an awakening above. When the awakening from below is in holiness, purity, and perfection, so too is the awakening above triggered in their likeness, bringing strength and help to the one who awakens the proper thing. 

It appears that there is power in those below to awaken the higher things according to their deeds and their speech, whether for good or, heaven forbid, for evil. If for good, it brings grace; if for evil, it brings a "darkened voice" <note>original: "kol tamal"</note> and blackness. The root is above, but according to what is awakened below in its likeness, so it is awakened above—whether little by little or for generations. For the power of the voice is great; it improves the source of all who wait. The upper things are measured according to the awakening below. Regarding those who awaken, it is said at the end of another chapter <note>referring to the Talmud, Tractate Yoma 38b</note>: "If one comes to defile himself, they open the way for him; if one comes to purify himself, they assist him." If one defiles himself a little, they defile him a lot. If he defiles himself in this world, they defile him in the World to Come.

The Sages taught: "'Sanctify yourselves and you shall be holy' <note>Leviticus 11:44</note>—if a person sanctifies himself a little, they sanctify him much; if he sanctifies himself below, they sanctify him from above; if in this world, they sanctify him for the World to Come." This means that according to the awakening below, so they awaken above. The power and cause of those who awaken—whether they be profane or holy, impure or pure—depends on this. For impurity exists in action and in speech, and so too does holiness. It is awakened above, as it is found in the Midrash of Rabbi...

<column-break/>

# The Section on Service
## Chapter 4

...with the **bending of the tongue** to say "Repair" <note>Tikkun</note>. One should not merely awaken or say what is written or remember the voice alone, or the word alone. For a word below is a word above. It is called "Remembering the word." "The Lord remembered the word" <note>a paraphrase of biblical themes of divine remembrance</note>; the word of the Lord was precious. From the "waters as smoke," the word rises and pierces the firmaments until it reaches its place of repair. Then an awakening of life-giving dew is triggered... as it is written: "And on the morrow, all was evil" <note>referring to the consequences of improper speech or intent</note>.

According to the secret of "Truth and Grace," prayer is a "Service of the Heart" <note>original: "avodah she-ba-lev," the classic rabbinic definition of prayer</note> performed with intent and unification, for the benefit and completion of the soul through directed and proper speech. The voice elevates the grace of the prayer. Thought and speech are essential for prayer to be complete. These are: **Thought**, **Direction**, **Voice**, and **Speech**. Thought is the proper intent that awakens the Will. Direction prepares the voice through the letters of the action, which is the speech. The voice, which includes everything, rises above and awakens the higher things. They are arranged and counted according to their likeness above. 

For indeed, above, the "Holy Thought" <note>Machshavah Kedoshah</note> gives birth and brings out the pure Will from the Supernal Mind. And the voice is what leads it into the world of the expressed, through thought and heart. This unifies the "One" and binds "Kindness" <note>Chesed</note> above. Similarly, we find in the tradition that the completeness of the voice and speech in their vitality has the power and the hint to awaken things through the "Voice of Life." Through their perfection, the voice reveals them and binds them together. Thus, the blessing and the flow always descend from the "Head of Thought" to its end. Its unification is the "Speech." The Blessed One, through the blessing of the prayer with proper intent, gives power to the higher things, which are then repaired and linked through Him, being in His likeness as we have written.

This is the secret of prayer. Our Sages of blessed memory said in the chapter "One must not stand" <note>Tractate Berakhot, Chapter 5</note>: "Rabbi Eleazar said: Prayer is greater than good deeds, for there is nothing greater than the good deeds of Moses our Teacher, yet he was only answered through prayer, as it is said: 'Speak no more to Me,' and immediately afterward: 'Go up to the top of the cliff.'" And Rabbi Eleazar also said: "Prayer is greater than sacrifices, as it is said: 'To what purpose is the multitude of your sacrifices to Me?' <note>Isaiah 1:11</note> and it is written: 'When you spread forth your hands, I will hide My eyes' <note>Isaiah 1:15</note>." 

The Rabbi, Rabbenu Azriel <note>Rabbi Azriel of Gerona, a 13th-century Kabbalist</note> of blessed memory, wrote in his commentary: "The secret of the **bending of the tongue** and the **bending of service** is to attach the soul to the Great Thought in the matter of the Direction (Kavanah), and to connect the directed actions. For this reason, the Early Pious Ones would wait one hour before praying." And the Rabbi, the **Me'il** <note>referring to a specific rabbinic authority or text, possibly the 'Me'il Tzedakah' or a similar title</note> of blessed memory, said: "The essence of the service of the 'High Ones' <note>the angels or spiritually perfected individuals</note> and those who direct His Name is the Will. It is found in everything called prayer and blessings, to make their thought wise through the letters, as if they were cleaving above to speak the Name in its existences, and to include the Ten Sefirot in the 'Chariot of the Bond' <note>Merkavat ha-Ketirah</note>." This is done with the word of his mouth and his speech, with his intent, with his heart, and with his speech properly directed. He asks of Him to speak a word of Wisdom, to reveal the hidden things to Understanding <note>Binah</note>. 

Until here are his words. From the words of all the holy ones, it is clarified for us that the essence of **Service** is **Intent** (Kavanah). When the service is based on the intent with the proper letters, it is a service that rises to the Divine Will, completing the intent within it. This is the true "Higher Unification" through which the worlds are perfected. And with this, the intention of this chapter is completed.

---

## Chapter 5

The later authors come to explain the means by which hearts find rest and opinions are cooled. Through it, they shall know how the "External Services" <note>ritual actions as opposed to internal meditation</note> follow the path to perform the "Service of the Holy." Since **Intent** is the essence of Service, as I have written, it is fitting to delve into it and to determine it for the best, and to return to it the eyes of the wise. 

This is the "Portion of Thought" as it is conducted in the world above. From the words of the later authors on this: For **Maimonides** <note>The Rambam</note> of blessed memory wrote in the tenth chapter of the "Laws of Repentance," in this language: "One who serves [God] out of [pure] thought, who occupies himself with the Torah and the commandments and walks in the paths of wisdom for no worldly reason, not out of fear of evil nor to inherit the good, but rather..."

It emphasizes that human action below (it'aruta de-letata) is the necessary catalyst for drawing down divine blessing and achieving mystical unification.</summary>

Even if he does not prepare himself, provided that Israel performs their services and directs their hearts toward this, the Holy One, Blessed be He, would agree and assist them. I desired <note>original: "Ratziti"</note>—and this is a language of "smoothness"—the one who shepherds me. They interpreted in the Midrash regarding the word "I desired": what does "I desired" mean? Rabbi Yonatan said: they tremble <note>original: "meparkesin," suggesting a rhythmic movement or struggle</note> so that they may pasture Me through the merit of the daily offerings every day. 

And in the Midrash of Rabbi Tanchuma: "My bread for My fire-offerings" <note>Numbers 28:2</note>—this is the end of the phrase. And Rabbi Berachiah taught: "And let them take for Me a contribution" <note>Exodus 25:2</note>. Thus said the Holy One, Blessed be He, to Israel: "Raise Me up through your prayers." And "He lives through me," for in their merit, grace is drawn into this world in its desolation. For in it is My heart placed, so that My name may be known, and from it, it is fitting to take My contribution, as it is said: "And this is the contribution which you shall take" <note>Exodus 25:3</note>. They take My contribution and His capacity to receive is for the sake of the Compassionate Teacher, to distribute it to the righteous. Through the <term>Silsul</term> <note>A term for refinement or elevation through song/prayer</note> of Israel who raise Me up, the whole world rejoices in their merits. It "trembles" from them <note>original: "meparkes," referring to the divine response to human action</note>, until here. Behold, they explained that the Heart, which is the **Heart of the Heavens**, trembles through the prayers and merits of the righteous who raise it upward and sustain it with their speech; and this is the ultimate purpose of their service, not any other end. 

Even a "small trembling" occurs even when their intention is not fully for this, for there is a "Need of the High" <note>The Kabbalistic concept that human actions "affect" or "nourish" the Divine realm</note. Because this acceptance is the desire and the Supreme Horn <note>A metaphor for strength or eminence</note>, they said there at the end of the matter: "Take My contribution from him." And it says: "And this is the contribution which you shall take... gold and silver and copper," to say that the Acceptance <note>God's reception of the service</note> desires nothing but the service for the purpose of increasing His glory. This is His desire and His will with the righteous who know this and do it to fulfill that Will, and not for any other end.

Since the intention in the manner we mentioned was the core of the service, they said at the end of the tractate *Menachot* regarding the Sanctuary: regarding the burnt offering of a bird it is said "a pleasing aroma," and regarding the burnt offering of cattle "a pleasing aroma," and regarding the meal offering "a pleasing aroma." This is to teach you that **whether one does much or one does little, provided that he directs his heart to Heaven.**

Behold, the goal of all services is to direct the heart—the secret of "Voice and Darkness"—to wash them toward Heaven—the secret of the **Crown** <note>The Sefirah of Keter, the highest divine emanation</note>. That is to say, one learns through this to elevate the Supreme Will; the perfect servant directs himself to this and not to any other end. 

Regarding a service that is not for its own sake, the intention does not ascend for acceptance. For this, our Rabbis of blessed memory directed in the first chapter of *Yoma*: it is a law that they do not delay... neither with the priest nor with the atonement, but rather the priest... and they do not say "The Lord is present" except for the House... to help him direct [his heart] in it. And they explained there that the priests would sing before Him "The Name," so that He would enter the House. That is to say, increase in your service so that it shall be for acceptance; place your will in it, and let your labor ascend to the Presence... and you shall choose. For service that is not for the sake of Heaven, and does not hope for the "Darkness" <note>Referring to the hidden divine essence</note> with the proper intention and acceptance of our King, does not ascend to anything.

<column-break/>

Its goal is greater than all services because it is the drawing down and the flow of the "Holy Spirit" from the Eye to the Garden in a more perfect way. For it has such great power, more than all the sacrifices, being composed of the **Chariot** <note>The *Merkavah*, the divine assembly of powers</note> according to the known matters of the Chariot above. With the proper intention, the incense was a "bond" <note>original: "kitura," a knot or spiritual connection</note> for the Nazirite... and because these are precise details, they have this power as the doors of supplication. The Holy One, Blessed be He, is moved and forgives, and he asks that they bless Him for this intention, for in it he receives the satisfaction of the "Holy Aroma." 

The Sages of Truth <note>The Kabbalists</note> received by tradition that "the end" is the **Kingdom of the Crown** <note>Keter Malchut</note>, which is the "Wall of Israel." Therefore, it is associated with the Lord, for He is the God of Israel. This is the secret of our mercy, and it is written: "For then I will be called..." as it is said in Isaiah. And this is said through the "Awakening from Below" <note>Human initiative that triggers divine response</note>, which draws upon the Impressionable Power, which is Wisdom, as mentioned in the Chariot of Ezekiel, peace be upon him. 

And He said to me: "Ishmael, my son, bless Me!" And he prayed. This is the matter: for the perfect prayer draws the blessing from the Source. This is what He hinted to him by saying "Bless Me"—meaning that he should pray in a language that draws the blessing down to the Kingdom of the House of David. The language of the prayer and its subject matter prove this: "May it be Your will before You," and do not say "to You." It is like a gift. This is our will: the "End of the Will." It is the end of all paths, and from it, he receives. Therefore, he was afraid and said "from before You," so that Your mercy may suppress Your anger. 

May the "Right Hand of the Lord" be exalted, prevailing over the "Left" in the manner of the joyful Judgment, transforming the Attribute of Justice into the Attribute of Mercy. May Your mercy be revealed, and above it, the "Holy Spirit" shall be included, adding blessing. May the good flow descend—the flow of the "Horn"—upon Your attributes, as it is written: "Like the **good oil** upon the head, running down upon the beard, the beard of Aaron" <note>Psalm 133:2</note>. It descends according to His attributes. When the Holy Spirit is blessed and flows, it is through the path from the Head until the end of the Great Name, clarified in His glory. This is the "filling of the Name." 

And when He says "My son, bless Me," it refers to the extension of my prayer to this end, for this is the "Supreme Horn." Since the request for mercy for Israel is also a blessing for the High—for the assembly of Israel is like a bride joined with her husband—he continues in his prayer for this as well, saying: "and deal with Your children [with mercy] etc." And we also say according to our way: when the Great Name is blessed and exists in His glory through prayer, there will follow the transformation of the Attribute of Justice into the Attribute of Mercy for the need of those below, and they too will be blessed by our blessing. As it is written: "And with Your blessing, let the house of Your servant be blessed." 

Thus, prayer in this way is an offering that includes the High, and it is the Supreme Will. The Holy Sages of Truth, who know that prayer with intention is for a unique purpose—the increase of His glory, which is a "Need of the High"—were accustomed to pray a [special] prayer after their regular prayers. They would awaken the Supreme Will for the purpose of increasing His glory, and for no other end. For such a prayer is the most choice, as it includes the "Need of the High," which is the goal toward which the servant turns all the days of his service. This is the **Service of Love** which is "not dependent on anything"—meaning that the passion of the servant for this goal is a passion not dependent on receiving a reward at all. Rather, his love in his service is entirely for the "Need of the Holy One, Blessed be He." Through his service, he opens for Him the flow of this purpose, which is that the Great Name be blessed and increase in His glory, so that His Will shall be one. 

This is what we learned in the chapter "One who Recites": Rabbi Eleazar, after finishing his prayer, would say: "May it be Your will, O Lord our God, that You place our lot in wisdom, strength, peace, and friendship." The intention is: when our lot is in Him, then His Great Name—which is the "Lot of Israel"—will always be a lot of grace, and his success will be unified with that which is above. He said "May He dwell here in wisdom and strength," so that he may be blessed from it above, and His "Right Hand" will be strengthened. And this is the "Holy Aroma."

And He said to me: 'Ishmael, my son, bless Me!' And He nodded to me with His head." 

What we learn from this is the importance of prayer that follows the path we mentioned. It is greater than the intentions within the sacrifices, for it is like the "Incense of the Spices," where all the levels are perfumed and bound together, gladdening the heart, as it is said: "Ointment and incense rejoice the heart" <note>Proverbs 27:9</note>. He said to him "Ishmael, my son, bless Me" to show that prayer on this path and with this intention...

# Part on Service, Chapter 6

The works and the commandments follow the principle we have explained generally: the perfect and all-encompassing servant, who contemplates the Name with a constant and enduring love, must do more than simply aim to unify the Great Name in His glory through his service. He must also ensure that he holds no personal motive in that unification—not for the needs of the body, nor even for the needs of the soul. Even though all good and success, whether physical or spiritual, are gathered and drawn from this unification, he must focus on the love he maintains in his heart and aim toward Him alone. One should not allow secondary causes to disrupt this focus. Those who weigh their own interests in their minds are far from the true purpose of service, for they do not know the correct path or the light. God forbid they should covet the inner wisdom accepted by the Sages with ulterior motives. Indeed, the servant must not fear punishment nor seek a reward for the soul; rather, his thought and intention should be that the Great Name be unified in His glory, to bless Him. This is because unification in this manner is "good in His eyes" and constitutes the fulfillment of His will.

The one who merits this knowledge and reaches this goal is the one who completes the intention of unification. This is the person of whom the Sages spoke in the chapter titled *The One Who Recites* <note>original: "Haya Koreh," referring to the second chapter of Tractate Berakhot in the Talmud</note>: "Pious is he who grew up in the Torah, toils in the Torah, and provides gratification to his Creator." For the servant who aims for this goal in his service provides gratification to his Creator. When he merits to sustain the Name in His glory, all things are blessed and united. Ultimately, they take refuge under the "spirit," for the Divine Presence <term>Shekhinah</term> <note>The feminine, indwelling aspect of God</note> descends and the Holy Spirit rests upon her. Nature is then elevated and blessed from the Source. This is the secret of the Great Name, the Source of Blessing.

According to the celestial order, a "secret" is required to unify the realms above. The servant must aim as we have written, for no other purpose, even though all other goals depend on and flow from this one. This is the secret of prayer in the singular language—all without delay or hindrance. He places his needs before God, the Master, but while asking, he also aims to serve, thereby refining himself to receive the blessing. Furthermore, all prayers and good words are part of the "unification," as is known to those "wise of heart." One who focuses on them and makes them known through good prayer within the unification brings his sustenance into the "Tale" <note>original: "Birah," possibly referring to the celestial palace or structure</note> and the arrangement of the Sanctuary.

The specific blessings follow this true intention, as will be explained in the tenth chapter of this section with Heavenly assistance. Regarding the chapter on "simple righteousness" <note>original: "Tzedakah Peshuta"</note> by Rabbi Yannai: the core of our intentions is nothing other than the Will of the World. "It is revealed and known before You that my will is to perform our duties through the Torah." He did not even write according to the "nature of nature." This informs us that through simple righteousness, one unifies His "Sister" <note>A common kabbalistic metaphor for the Shekhinah</note> all his days and elevates all services and commandments to this level. This was the foundation of his intentions; he was an offering to the Name. In all his Torah study and service, he never aimed for the pleasure of his own body; his entire intent was for the "Need of the High" and nothing else. This is the "Pious One" <note>Chassid</note> created through the excellence of his intentions.

True fortune belongs to the prophet who did not aim for himself at all, like the servant who excelled above all the sages of his generation, such that the pious said of him: "My heart is like Rabbi Atir" <note>likely a scribal variation or specific reference to a Sage known for pure devotion</note>... The one who serves for this purpose is one who serves out of love, "cleaving to the Place" <note>Hamakom, a name for God</note> and doing His will. To this, the Sages of blessed memory alluded when they said: "One who prays must direct his heart toward Heaven." They said "my heart" to mean "The Lord is for me, my heart is for Him." One must aim to unify that heart in its perfection; this is the complete Unification. One must aim for this unification as a "Need of the High" and not for any other purpose. As it is written: "You will strengthen their heart; You will incline Your ear" <note>Psalm 10:17</note>—this refers to one who aims for this goal and refines his thought and soul. Tiferet <note>Beauty/Harmony, the central Sefirah</note>.

<column-break/>

# Chapter 6

->With Heavenly assistance and by the breathing of His spirit upon us, from what is written in this holy book in this language: The Sages of Truth <note>Kabbalists</note> alluded to a great secret in this service by saying: "The Presence of the Shekhinah in Israel is a Need of the High <note>Tzorech Gavoah</note>," a great principle in service and in providing gratification. Thus far. And the man who has understood this—why would he direct his service and action toward other things? Why would he relate to his Maker and His pious ones except to see the attainment and the beauty <note>Tiferet</note> of the Shekhinah? These are the true holy ones who acquire their souls, who know their Creator and cleave to His service. Therefore, the Sages must know that the goal toward which they aim in their true service is to return the Grace of the Name, blessed be He, to His letters, to include all the Attributes <note>Middot/Sefirot</note> within Him, and to reach the ultimate Absolute Unification. The intention of all intentions is that it be "good in the eyes of the Lord," in the way that will be explained in this place with Heavenly assistance.<-

# Chapter 6

We have already written in the first part of this book that the reason for the creation of man was to be the "Upper Inclusion," to repair and adorn, and to demonstrate through his own inclusion all the levels included in the Great Name, blessed be He. In his desire and understanding, he knew that this was the original Will: that this secret be handed over to Man, who was created in the Image and Likeness. By awakening the lower realms through his good deeds and service with the proper intention, he awakens the upper realms. He is the cause of that awakening, so that the Great Name may be unified in His glory. This is the ultimate goal of all services and commandments, as well as the intention, the diligence, and the entire Torah.

It is fitting that this should be for the sake of this high level, so that the fear of Him in our hearts becomes the Absolute Unification. For He is the One who unifies alone... and this is the true service required by a prophet. For this, the service must be directed; one should not aim for any personal benefit or any other goal at all. This is the order of intention, and upon this the Shekhinah and her purity depend, as the author hinted in his brief but all-encompassing words: "The essence of the service of the wise and the thought of their oil," etc. You should scrutinize the core of the intention in the language of the Sages... for the servant must think and aim in his service to unify the Great Name, to recognize Him in His letters, to include all levels in Him, and to extend them in his thought until the Infinite <term>Ein Sof</term>.

They said: "Scrutinize," to hint that the thought should be clear and empty of all external things, the intention cleaving above in a constant attachment, to say that they act for the sake of the One without any blemish of separation, sustaining the Great Name alone. I have seen the Sages of Truth say regarding this matter: "This is the title of the Midrash in this book for Israel: The Great Name, and the righteous, the pious, and the wise pray and unify the Great Name." They unify the Name through the Attributes that are explored in their hearts, not with foreign thoughts. They repair all the <term>Sefirot</term> <note>Divine emanations/spheres</note> and bind them to one another until the Crown <term>Keter</term>, the source of thought, which leads to His infinite compassion. This is the sustenance of the Name within Israel. This is the secret of all Israel seeking this Name through the merit of pure thought in the ten Sefirot... and this is the secret of the Unification in the morning and evening: "To declare Your kindness in the morning," etc. Anyone who unifies the "limbs" <note>metaphor for the Sefirot</note> through the Attributes and elevates all the Sefirot into one constant, enduring leadership is then cleaving to the Great Name, blessed be He.

From this it is explained that the perfect servant, who unifies the Great Name in his thought and proper intention, cleaves to Him. This is the secret of "Scrutinize." Because the intention of the perfect one was for this goal—which is essentially the essence of the Upper Glory—and because this praise is in the Source in his hand, he must focus his service toward the Absolute Unification, the intention of its inclusion, and its becoming "All."

It emphasizes that human actions "awaken" the upper realms, allowing the Shekhinah to be blessed and the world to be sustained through pure intention.</summary>

# Chapter 6 | Part on Service | Chapter 7

Its virtue is greater than all other forms of service, because it is the extension and the chain connecting the vitality of the Holy Spirit from Eden to the Garden in the most perfect manner. It possesses a power greater than all other sacrifices, as it is integrated with the Chariot <note>The "Chariot" (*Merkavah*) refers to the celestial structure of the Divine realm described in the visions of Ezekiel.</note> through the known vessels of the supernal structure. Regarding the intention, the thought remains focused on the **Need of the High** <note>This technical term, *Tzorech Gavoah*, suggests a mystical idea that human worship somehow provides a "necessity" or completion to the Divine realm.</note>. Because the incense has a power equivalent to the perfection of Wisdom, the Tradition, and the secret of the *Sachel* <note>original: "סוחל" - a reference to one of the specific ingredients of the incense, here interpreted mystically</note>, it is through this intention that one receives the breath of the Holy Spirit. 

The Sages of Truth <note>A traditional title for Kabbalists</note> received the secret of the incense as the "Crown of Sovereignty," which is to say, Israel. For this reason, the Sages linked it to the concept that "God is the portion of Israel." It is written: "For to the Lord belongs the kingship" <note>Psalm 22:29</note>. This is the same theme found on the Day of Atonement, concerning the "Lot for the Lord" <note>Referring to the two goats in the Temple service</note>. This secret was revealed through the petition of Moses, may he rest in peace, and it is the same secret mentioned regarding the Chariot in the vision of Ezekiel, where it says "and he spoke to me: 'Ezekiel, my son, bless Me.'" 

This refers to Prayer. The essence of the matter is that perfect prayer opens the source of blessing from the Primeval Origin. This is what the Sages hinted at when they said "Bless Me"—meaning, one should pray in such a way that the blessing is drawn down for the needs of the Kingdom of the House of David. Regarding the time of prayer and the Standing Prayer (*Amidah*), it was said: 

->**"May it be Your will before You"**<-

One does not simply say "before You," but uses the term "May it be," which implies that "Will" (*Ratzon*) is the ultimate goal. For the Supernal Will is the source from which all paths emerge and from which everything flows. The end of this request is "that Your mercy may suppress Your anger." This means that the Mercy of the Lord should prevail over His attributes, so that the "Angel of the Face" <note>A high-ranking angelic being who stands in the presence of God</note> may be occupied with transforming the Attribute of Judgment into the Attribute of Mercy. Then, Your mercy will be revealed from above, the Holy Spirit will be disclosed, and blessing will descend. 

A "flow of goodness" and a "flow of wisdom" will descend upon the Divine attributes, as it is written: *“It is like the precious oil upon the head, running down upon the beard, even Aaron's beard”* <note>Psalm 133:2</note>. This represents the flow of Grace and Kindness as it descends according to the Divine attributes. When the blessing and the flow of the Holy Spirit arrive in this manner, it begins at the "Head" and reaches the "End of the Garment," magnifying His glory. This is the "Peace of the Name" that is mentioned. This is also the secret of "Bless Me"—it is the "End" that draws from the "Ultimate End," for the Supernal Desire and Will are there. 

Since Mercy is requested for Israel, there is also a "Need of the High." For when that specific "Level" is known to look upon these children, she is unified with her Husband <note>A Kabbalistic metaphor for the unification of different aspects of the Divine, often represented as the "King" and "Queen" (Sovereignty)</note>. Therefore, one draws this down through prayer, saying: "And deal with Your children with the attribute of mercy." 

Furthermore, according to our path: when the Great Name is blessed and His glory is unified through prayer, it follows that the Attribute of Judgment is transformed into the Attribute of Mercy for the sake of those below. They, too, are blessed by His blessing, as it is written: *“And with Your blessing let the house of Your servant be blessed forever”* <note>2 Samuel 7:29</note>. This is because prayer, performed in this way, ascends entirely to the High and is a "gratification" before Him. 

The holy Sages of Truth, who know that prayer with the correct intention aims at the unification of the Great Name in His glory—which is the "Need of the High"—were accustomed to offering a specific prayer after their regular prayers. Through this, they would awaken the Supernal Will. Such a prayer is most choice because it is entirely for the sake of the High. This is the goal toward which the servant should turn, directing all his service toward it his whole life. This is the "Service of Love." The one who serves for this goal is the "Lover" who does nothing for his own benefit, but all his love and service are for the sake of his Beloved. He occupies himself with his service to bring about this goal: that the Great Name be blessed and unified in His glory.

This is what was intended in the chapter *The One Who Recites*, where Rabbi Elazar said: "May it be Your will, O Lord our God, that You cause to dwell in our lot love, brotherhood, peace, and friendship." The intention here is not for personal benefit, but for the "Sovereignty of Israel," which is always His lot. He asked that the Attribute of Mercy dwell there, to be a source of blessing for the masses, and that they may dwell in their portion and behold the pleasantness of the Lord.

<meta>catchword: The Incense</meta>

<column-break/>

Even if one does not intend it for his own sake, how much more so when Israel performs their service and intends it for this purpose. Then the Holy One, Blessed be He, rejoices and calls them "My Beloved" (*Ra'ayati*) and uses the language of "My Kin" (*Kerovai*). 

It is said in the Midrash: "What is the meaning of 'My Beloved' (*Ra'ayati*)?" Rabbi Jonathan said: "Those who provide for Me" <note>The Hebrew word for "beloved" is linked here to the word for "pasturing" or "providing."</note>. Just as a companion provides for his friend every day until the end. It is also said there concerning Rabbi Hezekiah: See what is written, *"That they take for Me an offering"* <note>Exodus 25:2; original: Terumah</note>. Thus said the Holy One, Blessed be He, to Israel: "Raise Me up (*Terumah*) with your prayers." And who is "Me"? It is the one you will meet when you depart from the world, the One in whose glory I rejoice. For those who know My Name are worthy to take My offering, as it is said: *"From every man whose heart prompts him, you shall take My offering"*—from the one who honors Me. 

Rabbi Rahumai said: It is explicitly stated that Israel raises Me above the whole world through their merits, and from them, the "All" is sustained. Thus they explained that the "Heart of the Sages" provides sustenance through the prayers and intentions of the righteous, who raise Me up and cling to Me in joy. This is the ultimate goal of their service. 

This goal is the Supernal Desire and Will. For this reason, we say that the end of the matter is for the glory of His Name. From this perspective, one should pray. Afterward, the text says: *"And this is the offering (Terumah) which you shall take from them: gold, silver, and copper..."* This implies that the Holy One, Blessed be He, desires the service and prayers founded upon the glory of His Name. This "building" and its intention among the righteous completes the Divine Will.

It has been clarified that intention is the essence of service. As it is said at the end of Tractate Menachot: It is said of the burnt offering, "a fire-offering of pleasing aroma," and of the meal offering, "a fire-offering of pleasing aroma," and of the bird offering, "a fire-offering of pleasing aroma." This teaches you: **Whether one does much or one does little, it is all the same, provided that he directs his heart to Heaven.**

Thus it is clarified that in all services, one must direct the heart to the secret of the Name of Love. This is because the Supernal Will is the goal. Service with this intention is what creates "Gratification" (*Ratzon*). This is what our Rabbis, of blessed memory, intended in the first chapter of the Mishnah: "Be not like servants who serve the master for the sake of receiving a reward, but be like servants who serve... for the sake of Heaven." 

Rashi, of blessed memory, explained: "But rather, you should be awakening [the Divine] before Him." If He desires it, let Him act. That is, let your service be a "gift" to establish His Name and raise His Will. From this, it is clear that service which protects the "Wall of Heaven" is the transformation of intention and goal that we have explained, which ascends to the High.

### Chapter 7

The prayer that is intended for the goal that the Great Name be blessed and His glory sanctified, so that His Will and Desire are fulfilled as we have explained—this is what the Holy One, Blessed be He, longs for and expects from the righteous who know this secret. 

The Sages said in the first chapter of Tractate Berakhot: Rabbi Ishmael son of Elisha said: "Once I entered the innermost sanctum <note>The Holy of Holies</note> to offer the incense, and I saw **Akatriel Yah, the Lord of Hosts** <note>Akatriel is a mystical name of God, often associated with the "Crown" (*Keter*).</note>, sitting upon a high and lofty throne. He said to me: 'Ishmael, my son, bless Me.' I replied: 'May it be Your will before You that Your mercy suppresses Your anger, and Your mercy prevail over Your attributes, and may You deal with Your children with the attribute of mercy, and stop short of the limit of strict justice for them.' and He nodded His head to me." 

From this we learn the secret of prayer. It is greater than the incense among the sacrifices. For even though the priest offering the incense reaches all the high levels and unifies the known forces—as it is said, "oil and incense rejoice the heart"—nevertheless, the Lord said, "Ishmael, my son, bless Me," to show that prayer with this direction and intention...

It features the famous story of Rabbi Ishmael blessing the Divine manifestation Akatriel, illustrating how human prayer can evoke Divine Mercy over Judgment.</summary>

### Chapter 6

The nature of Divine service and the commandments follows this path: the general principle and the power of anyone who serves perfectly toward the ultimate, precious goal—the Name—is to bring about enduring outcomes. Aside from the necessity of focusing one’s service on unifying the Great Name in His Glory, one must have no intention in that Unity for one's own needs at all—neither for the needs of the body nor even for the needs of the soul. Even though all these benefits naturally flow from the intention of Unity—for all goodness and success, whether of the body or the soul, are gathered and drawn from this Unity—the perfection of thought lies in the Unity itself, to focus on it alone without allowing the thought to stray into the physical act itself. 

Since it is fitting for the Children of Israel to understand and merit this, and they are all "Kings of the Ultimate Purpose" of all service, they shall know the correct path. For if they do not guard their inner intention—which has been received by us and the <term>Sages of the Secret</term><note>A traditional term for Kabbalists, scholars of Jewish mysticism.</note>—the worshiper's work is diminished. One must not intend anything for the sake of the soul, which would profane the act; rather, his thought and intention must be that the Great Name be unified in His Glory, to bless Him and thank Him. This Unity should be simple in his eyes, and the inclination of his will and the desire of his mouth should be for the blessing and the Unity which he has merited to know. 

One who pursues this goal completes the intention with uprightness. This is what the Sages said in the chapter *These are those who are Strangled* <note>A chapter in the Babylonian Talmud, Tractate Sanhedrin 92a</note>: "Pious is he who is great in Torah, whose labor is in Torah, and who brings <term>contentment to his Creator</term><note>original: "נחת רוח" (Nachat Ruach). A central concept in Jewish ethics meaning to act solely to please God without ulterior motives.</note>." Such a person is exempt and focused in his service on "raising the <term>Shekhinah</term><note>The Divine Presence, often viewed in Kabbalah as the feminine aspect of God that is in "exile" and needs to be reunited with the Holy One.</note>." We have heard this from the mouths of our Sages of blessed memory: to be exempt from all self-interest and to focus on the Unity of the Name in His Glory, through which all things are blessed from the beginning to the end. 

A person can, through the "gift of the spirit," cause the Shekhinah to rest, and thus the Holy Spirit <note>original: "רוח הקודש" (Ruach HaKodesh)</note> dwells, the Name is exalted, and blessing comes from our mouths. This is the secret of the blessings and the reality of all existence. This is the general rule of Intention and Unity. According to the <term>Secret of Unity</term>, the worshiper must "live above"; his focus must be as we have written, not for any other purpose, even though all other goals are revealed to them and thought of through him. 

This is the secret of reward from His side—it is included within the whole. But service should be for His benefit, to bless the Shekhinah with joy, intending for the sake of the Name rather than personal gain. Furthermore, all actions and matters from the perspective of reward—as known to the "Sages of the Heart"—are but a ladder for his prayer during the time of this Unification of the Name. It is a hidden matter, and in its appearance, it sanctifies the Holy One. These blessings will be explained with focus in the tenth chapter of this section. 

In the chapter *He who Folds*, it is said that anyone who has a thread of grace upon them <note>likely referring to the Talmudic concept of a "thread of grace" (חוט של חסד) extended to those who labor in Torah at night</note> is acting according to the Will of the World. He knows before Him that we have labored in our wisdom and His Torah. I have not written this as a small matter. It is known that a specific Unity is required for His vitality, elevating all services and secrets in His existence. This returns to the piety mentioned regarding intention: that all his Torah and service had no intention for his own essence at all, but all his intention was for the <term>Divine Need</term><note>original: "צורך גבוה" (Tzorech Gavoah). The mystical idea that human actions provide a "necessity" or completion to the Divine realm.</note>.

This is the advantage and the matter of our labor in Torah. I did not write of his conduct in a small way. His life was a complete life, directed toward the <term>Guide for the Perplexed</term><note>A reference to Maimonides (Rambam) and his seminal philosophical work.</note>, not intending for himself at all. Glory was bestowed upon him by all the sages of his generation, until they said of him that he taught the house of Rabbi <note>referring to a high level of Rabbinic authority</note>. His life was a pure path to the heavens. One who pursues this goal, his thoughts and blessings merit the Name in its place, and he performs His will. This is what the Sages hinted at when they said: "One who prays must direct his heart to Heaven." They used the word "heart" in these matters to mean "mercy," and in this, one must focus and unify the heart toward the Unity. This is the Perfect Unity. One must focus on the goal of Unity, which is a "Divine Need," and not for any other purpose. From this, you shall understand how to sanctify Him; the intention is to subdue the self, and success follows from this intention.

<column-break/>

In His existence and His perfection, He is the Holy One, Blessed be He, as written in the Holy Book on the first day. The <term>Sages of Truth</term><note>The Kabbalists.</note> hinted at a great secret of service in the *Zohar*, of blessed memory: that there is a "Divine Need" in Israel, and without it, there is a great falsehood in service and the performance of the commandment. 

The man who has become wise in this and knows it—why would he abandon it? Others will add to his words. Why should he find favor in the eyes of time, and why his sages? For it is forbidden to seek wisdom and publicize the wisdom they acquire for their own end. The "Correction of the Perfected" is for the sake of those who know the secret of their intention and intend to serve Him. Therefore, the Sages must know that the <term>Kabbalah</term> <note>The received mystical tradition.</note> upon which the later worshipers should focus in their service is the vitality of blessing the Great Name through our own vitality, to include all the letters and to unify Him in the Supernal realm—the Absolute Unity. The one who serves with this intention is the "Good Servant" in the eyes of the Lord, as will be explained in the sixth part with the help of Heaven.

---

### Chapter 6

We have already written in the first part of this book that the reason for the creation of man in the <term>Image of the Supernal Glory</term> was to repair and give thanks, and to order all the levels included in the Great Secret, so that he would have the power and capacity to reach the end. For such was the Will from the beginning: that there be a sage from the "Secret of the Perfect Secret" of the Glory. Through his arousal below, through his good deeds and his service with the proper intention, he awakens the supernal matters. He ascends and assists in that arousal so that the Great Name may be unified in His Glory. This is the purpose of all services and commandments, the body of all deeds and teachings, and the entire Torah.

The commandment given to him was for the sake of the glory of the levels of the Secret of Perfection, to unify Him in the Supernal realm—the Absolute Unity. For the Unity and the intention toward it are required, just as a connection necessitates unity. This is the "Service of the Fifth," which is a "Divine Need." For this reason, we require service and commandments directed toward this, so that the worshiper does not face any other goal at all. By applying the thought and the focus, he acts according to the perfect intention and the pure thought. 

In this way, the Sages of blessed memory spoke regarding the dedication of the "Perfected Holy Ones" to the primary service of the thought. The masses may think of His Name for their own favor, but the proper intention in service is for the worshiper to surround and focus his service on unifying the Great Name, recognizing his intentions, including all levels, and perfecting his thought unto the <term>Infinite</term><note>original: "אין סוף" (Ein Sof). The infinite, unknowable aspect of God in Kabbalah.</note>. 

They further hinted that the thought should be turned away from all other things, cleaving above with constant focus. This is to say that the worshiper acts as a vessel for the end of the Unity, to bless the Great Name. I have seen the Sages of Truth say regarding this matter: "In their love, they separate from the ten levels." The Great Name of Israel, the righteous, the pious, and the sages intend and unify the Great Name, considering the Name as the level of the "Engraving in their Hearts" through pure thought. Thus all the <term>Sefirot</term><note>The ten divine emanations or attributes in Kabbalistic theory.</note> are moved and bound one to another until the thought reaches the "Source of Thought" in the Infinite (*Ein Sof*), for His exaltation. 

This shall be the Perfect Unity in Israel. This is the secret that "All of Israel are bound to the Name of the Lord," and the secret of thought within the Ten Sefirot. This is the secret of "Those who cleave to the Lord." This is the secret of the Unity in the morning and the evening, like the service in the palace of the King. One who unifies the "branches" in man elevates all the Sefirot in one special, enduring thought, to bless the Great Name forever. 

From this it is explained that the perfect worshiper, who unifies the Great Name in his thought and with proper intention, cleaves to Him. This is the secret of "And to Him shall you cleave." Since the intention of this "Perfected One" is the goal for which he was created—in the image of the Supernal Glory—as has been explained, he must focus his service on the Wondrous Unity, as is fitting for his creation.

It emphasizes that man's actions on earth awaken and unify the supernal Sefirot, fulfilling the ultimate purpose of creation.</summary>
