They would pray to God a single, general prayer that included the **Divine Need** <note>Hebrew: *tzorech gavoah*. This refers to the kabbalistic idea that human prayer "completes" or "assists" the flow of Divine energy in the upper worlds.</note>, for this is the ultimate purpose of proper disposition and piety.

### Chapter 9

One must understand the nature of prayer and its intended order. The prayer-offering is like the arrangement of the voice. There is no doubt that the standard version was established with wisdom and poured out with discernment, for the **Enlightened ones** <note>Hebrew: *Maskilim*, often used in this context to refer to those with mystical insight.</note> were those who knew the "wing of righteousness," as I alluded to in the chapter regarding those who stand properly in the holy congregation. 

They established for Israel both short blessings of enjoyment and the formal prayers. It is well known that the **Men of the Great Assembly** <note>The supreme legislative body of Jewish leaders at the start of the Second Temple era.</note> lived in the days of Zechariah and Malachi, and they were great sages. It is said in the chapter of the Talmud titled "One who reads the Megillah" that one hundred and twenty elders—among whom were several dozen prophets—established the **Eighteen Benedictions** <note>Hebrew: *Shemoneh Esrei*, the central standing prayer of the Jewish liturgy.</note> according to their proper order. 

They included the "Sanctification" <note>Hebrew: *Kedushah*</note>, containing the mysteries of the Divine receptions and the "vessels" in a subtle hint, so that the ultimate purpose of the blessing would be reached from its source. This is the path of kindness and the "Voice." One should know that their intention in the order of the "Voice" was to benefit and restore the "eyes" of those who serve with deliberation. This removes doubt from a person regarding their path and is more essential for the perfection of the **Holy Service**.

It was said in the chapter "One should not stand" <note>A chapter in Tractate Berakhot of the Talmud.</note>: Rav Yehuda said, "A person should never ask for his own needs in either the first three blessings or the last three blessings." Rabbi Hanina explained: "The **first three** are like a servant who arranges praise before his master; the **middle ones** are like a servant who asks for a reward from his master; and the **last ones** are like a servant who has received his reward from his master and takes his leave to go on his way."

The secret of this matter is that everything is intended to dig deep and subdue the "Source." One must first join all his words to **Unify His Name** <note>Hebrew: *Yichud*, the mystical act of declaring or visualizing the oneness of the different aspects of God.</note>, for this is the correct path to obtain one's needs. Without this, one will not reach the goal at all. In all prayers and blessings, the worshiper must unify in his thought the **Great Name** in His glory and His "wrapping" <note>Hebrew: *hit'atfuto*, a reference to the Divine Light enveloping existence</note> unto the Infinite (*Ein Sof*). 

It is said in the Midrash *Shocher Tov*: "Because he has desired Me, I will deliver him." Rabbi Joshua ben Levi said in the name of Rabbi Phinehas ben Yair: "Why is it that Israel prays in this world and is not answered? Because they do not know how to pray using the **Explicit Name** <note>Hebrew: *Shem HaMeforash*, the four-letter Tetragrammaton.</note>." This means they do not know the secret of the internal permutations of the letters of the Name. Such was the tradition received by the wise **Rabbi Azriel the Levite** <note>Rabbi Azriel of Gerona (c. 1160–1238), a pivotal figure in early Spanish Kabbalah.</note> of blessed memory, at the end of his "Gate of Holiness."

It is proper that the intention in this be correct. We must understand that the path to a "time of favor" is to appease His ways, so that the individual establishes a "vessel" to receive blessing into his house and fulfill his will. This "speech of knowledge"—praying with the Explicit Name—is a path and a disposition that cannot be achieved without the intentional knowledge of the **Unification of the Name** in its various manifestations and powers. 

The Sages established the **first blessings** as a moral path to agree upon this Unification. There, they unify the Name with the proper intention. The first blessing, which is the **Blessing of the Patriarchs** <note>Hebrew: *Avot*</note>, includes all the "faiths" of the Great Name and all the virtues. As we wrote in the book *The Worm of Jacob*, this blessing is the "Shield of Abraham," meant to include everything in the "Upper Right" <note>In Kabbalah, the Right side represents *Chesed* (Lovingkindness) and is associated with the patriarch Abraham.</note>. Afterward, they unify the thought in the "Right of Glory" with "You are Mighty" <note>The second blessing, *Gevurot*, representing Divine Power and the "Left" side.</note>. Then, they unify everything in the "Middle Pillar" with the blessing of the **Holy One** <note>The third blessing, *Kedushah*, representing the balance or beauty (*Tiferet*).</note>. 

The one who performs this Unification must fix his focus there, including it in his thought and binding all other virtues to the "Holy Virtue." His intention in the Unification of the Name should be to include everything in the **Infinite** (*Ein Sof*). This is the "Foundation" that pours His goodness into the "Kingdom," which is the secret of His Great Name and the source for all souls. The "Perfected One" will be graced to understand and include the **Holy Presence** (*Shekhinah*) from level to level until the end of all levels, so that it becomes attached to the whole, spreading through the whole, and including the whole. This teaches that He is everything, and He alone, and there is nothing besides Him. This Unification is the "source" that sustains everything and leads to the acceptance of your mercies. 

Therefore, they established the **middle blessings** as thirteen blessings where mercy is requested; that is the place of Unification and power. And in the Midrash of Rabbi Simeon bar Yochai <note>A reference to the *Zohar*.</note>, of blessed memory, it says as follows:

<meta>catchword: word</meta>

<column-break/>

Every night, the "Watchers of the Voice" of the night and the voice of the evening keep watch. The "Perfected One" merits this, and it is written concerning this that he "denies the business" and awakens the hints regarding the completion of the Glory. Because they know the end of the will of the **Mighty One** to visit his pious ones, the "Voice" requests mercy before his **Upper Offering** and looks into this, saying: "Unify the deed!" 

"May You be whitened with mercy, and may You be covered in Your 'Eye,' and may You be wrapped in our place." This is the secret of the **Perfect Unification**. It turns sin into "a secret of fear," and He who knows answers us. "Awaken Your disposition," which is the attribute of the "Disposition Above" in the "Constellation." Prepare to see the "Base" that prepares the "Flute" <note>Likely a mystical metaphor for the channel of Divine flow.</note> of the **Kingdom** (*Malkhut*).

"Be present before You the attribute of Your Goodness," for it is the attribute of Your Goodness that is worthy to pass over all my "goodness." In our iniquities, there was the attribute of humility. Its intention is to unify the source of the sanctuary of the attribute of Goodness. The intention in all this is that the **Great Name** should stand in His Glory and wrap Himself unto the Infinite. This Unification is to bless Him so that He becomes One. 

He would request that the Great Name stand in His Glory using the language of "becoming clothed" and "becoming wrapped," etc., so that He is unified in His glory by Himself. For "I have nothing in the lower worlds" <note>Meaning God's essence is not dependent on the lower realms.</note>... but He is sustained in the souls of some of the "Deeds" for the "Divine Need." 

May the acceptance be like the statement of **Rav Safra** <note>A Babylonian Talmudic sage.</note> regarding the "Upper Crown." "May the light of My face be from Your treasures, O Lord," to show that his soul is in peace, like the "upper wick" and the "lower wick" <note>Hebrew: *Petilah*, a metaphor for the soul's connection to God, like a flame to a wick.</note>. This awakens the hint that He should pour out mercy and His great light through the attribute of His Goodness and be unified in His glory. For "He has nothing in the lower beings," and it is for their sake that the peace returns—the peace of the **Upper Wick**. 

From this comes the concept of "Peace in the voice of the place," the attribute of **Peace** (*Shalom*). This is "Peace, the Righteous One, the Life of the Worlds," connected to the attribute of the **Kingdom of the House of David**. In the books of Rabbi Hamnuna, the Deputy High Priest, it says regarding "And give you peace": "This is the peace of the Kingdom of the House of David," which was the "Holy Chariot" and "Of peace there shall be no end." Rabbi Jonathan says: "This is the peace of the **Torah**," as it is said, "The Lord will give strength to His people; the Lord will bless His people with peace."

This is the **Perfect Unification**. This is the secret of one who enters to pray for the "Peace of the Kingdom," which is the **Kingdom of Heaven**. The pious ones did not focus their prayers on themselves, but rather they would request in their supplications for the Divine Need, for this is "all my desire and all my salvation." 

When they spoke of the **Lower Wick**, it was a hint toward the "War and the Contention" that exists in their councils and their repentance. For there exists the "Good Inclination" and the "Silver Money," which are the portions of life below, the smallness, the wars, and the accusations. Through the presence of peace and the attachment to the "Upper One," peace is drawn from the **Upper Wick** to the **Lower Wick**. Then, those who accuse Israel are silenced. 

This is the secret of "doing justice at all times," according to the "time of evil." For when justice and peace are awakened below, they are also awakened Above. There is peace in everything, even among the "External Ones" <note>Hebrew: *Chitzonim*, referring to the forces of the "Other Side" or demonic realms.</note> who dwell in the depths. For He makes peace among them below when they occupy themselves with the Torah. Their intention is not for the sake of dispute in word or money, but rather to prove the "Ancientness of their Desires"—to clarify and whiten the holiness. Thus, peace is awakened Above as well.

This applies to those who **study for its own sake** (*Lishmah*). One who occupies himself with the Torah "for its own sake" does so for the sake of the Name standing in His Glory. It also applies to those who **study not for its own sake** (*Shelo Lishmah*), if they do so for some other purpose. Even then, one should pursue peace among them so that peace is drawn Above. Thus, peace is found among them for this purpose, which is the **Divine Need**. 

He would return and pray for those who do not study "for its own sake," that they should come to study "for its own sake," so that the "Upper Purpose" should be drawn from it—which is the Unification of the Great Name in His Glory. This is difficult, for these pious ones, whose prayer was the "height of success" for others and not for themselves, would hint at what was established for us—all that He has graced us with. They would also show this after the conclusion of their prayers, which include all the blessings...

It emphasizes that true prayer focuses on the "Divine Need" and the attribute of Peace (Shalom) to harmonize the upper and lower worlds.</summary>

### Chapter 8

The nature of good and evil and what causes them. There is a kindness, and I have achieved my portion through my actions in this world. My "portion" means to bless the Source for my sake. Behold, there are those who bow and are cast down, but your heart shall live. It has already been explained what our sages said in this regard: "At the moment of the departure of the righteous, the Holy One, blessed be He, shows them their reward." <note>This refers to a Talmudic tradition that the righteous glimpse their afterlife reward just before death to put their minds at ease.</note>

For example, they showed **Rabbi Abbahu** thirteen crowns <note>Original: *ketarim*. In the standard Talmudic version (Avodah Zarah), it is "thirteen rivers of balsam," but this manuscript uses "crowns" to develop a mystical interpretation.</note> of balsam. He said, "For whom are these?" They said to him, "For you." He replied: "Indeed, I thought I had labored for nothing and spent my strength in vain" <note>Quoting Isaiah 49:4</note>.

Behold, Rabbi Abbahu was a great sage, a pious man, and a master of good deeds. Through his good deeds and his wisdom, he would draw down and begin the flow of thirteen crowns, and the "good oil" <note>A metaphor for Divine emanation or *Shefa*.</note> hidden in the **Ancient Mystery** would pour out upon the crowns beneath it. Through him, the Great Name was blessed and praised in its Glory. For this reason, they showed him that his reward was thirteen crowns of balsam in **Eden**, to allow him to delight in them. He listened and rested, and his heart lived, for he had been occupied with the rectitude of the Place <note>Hebrew: *HaMakom*, a common rabbinic name for God, emphasizing His omnipresence.</note>, teaching it through the Supernal Law, which is the ultimate purpose of the Service and its intention in its preservation.

He further said: "May the coolness of our souls come before You as a pleasing aroma." "Coolness of our souls" is an expression of satisfaction or "spirit of rest." That is to say, that which You rest and cause to dwell in Glory through our speech. We alluded to the songs and the libations that ascended to the heights <note>Original: *karka*, possibly referring to the altar or the firmament.</note> to come before You, so that the Good One might rejoice in it, in the sense that the Great Name returns to its Glory. Do not let it enter your thoughts that this is a matter of "window and separation," Heaven forbid! Rather, the thought and the deed must always be aligned, aiming toward the Perfect Unity.

->Chapter 5<-

**The "settled" prayer is the most chosen and desired.** This is the prayer that ascends entirely to the High Place, as we have said—meaning, to bless Him, and not to involve one's own desires or what seems "good in his own eyes" regarding mundane needs. The sages said that **Rabbi Yohanan**, after finishing his prayer, would say: "May it be Your will, O Lord our God, that You cause love and brotherhood to dwell in our lot, and peace and friendship in our borders."

The intention here is to direct Will and Mercy toward the **Glory** <note>The *Kavod*, or Shekhinah (the Divine Presence)</note> that is with us in exile. He would bring before Him the intention and the knowledge of his thoughts, and the knowledge of the children of the covenant. This is like what they said in the Midrash on Ruth: "And she came softly, and uncovered his feet, and laid her down." <note>Ruth 3:7. The text interprets this allegorically as the Community of Israel seeking union with God.</note> She who lies at his feet is like a pearl set between his legs. This refers to the **Assembly of Israel** <note>Hebrew: *Knesset Yisrael*, a mystical personification of the Jewish people and the Shekhinah.</note>, which carries the burden to straighten the awakening toward Him. She is the "garment" that shall not be kept away. May You be with us in our exile, and may You be in our awareness.

Regarding this, the holy ones said: "Do not look at my blackened appearance" <note>Quoting Song of Songs 1:6</note>. This refers to the thoughts of the children in exile. They curse and sin every day against You, and I have no mouth in exile to awaken [mercy], therefore, stay until forever. This is why the lamp appears to him.

It is said in the Talmud (Tractate Berakhot): "A prisoner cannot release himself from prison." This hints that the **Glory** <note>The Shekhinah</note> requires help, and that an awakening of Will and Mercy is needed so that it may leave this "prison" of exile. This is what is written: "And the Lord your God will return with your captivity" <note>Deuteronomy 30:3</note>. According to this, it does not say "He will bring back," but "He will return" <note>The grammatical nuance implies God returns *with* the people, sharing their exile.</note>. And he did not suffer in his knowledge when he spoke of the fury of the suppressors... a "Correction of the Scribes" <note><term>Tikkun Soferim</term>: A traditional scribal emendation in the biblical text to preserve the honor of God.</note>. And in its rest, in the verse "established always," his knowledge did not suffer in that which is written. It is the way of the pious and the men of action to be troubled in their thoughts and in the assembly, and to seek and pray for the ways of rest and for the Sanctuary...

<column-break/>

### Chapter 7: The Part of the Service

That which awakens the soul to the commandments is "My Beloved" and "His Friendship." "Friendship" refers to the **Righteous One of the World** <note>The Sefirah of *Yesod*, the foundation and channel of Divine flow.</note>. "Peace" is the Foundation (*Yesod*) and the Secret (*Sod*). "And I will give peace in the land" <note>Leviticus 26:6</note> is the end of their existence, the Foundation.

And he continued to draw down the "majesty of strength" and the "secret," and "expansion in our borders" like students. This too is a "Divine Need" for the wicked man <unclear>X</unclear>, for their intention within it is grace and the secret for the **Shekhinah** <note>The Divine Presence</note> in her exile, through the "Upright Intellect." Every path of the "Crown" (*Keter*) and its expansion in our exile... the general principle regarding "students" is "the students of the Lord" <note>Isaiah 54:13</note>, who are blessed by them. You shall be enriched by them through the **Righteous One** who sustains the world—these are the students who influence her through him.

He continued and said: "And the end of our goodness for the future." The hope that increases his deeds and his service bears fruit in the end. This means that the Great Name shall be blessed and unified in its Glory through his service, for this is the sought-after purpose. There will be an expansion in **Eden**, which is also a Divine Need, so that his action is felt above. "And establish us with a good reward and a good memory in Your world." For You are good—these are the ones who answer for peace with the intention of the Service. This is the preparation, the radiance, and the spiritual assets.

The holy collection of **Rabbi Shimon bar Yochai** <note>The *Rashbi*, the central figure of the Zohar.</note> in the *Book of Palaces* <note>The *Heikhalot* literature, an early form of Jewish mysticism.</note>, in the Palace of the Foundation, says: "Behold, there is in the hidden side of holiness a first crown... the Good Memory that does good, deep to bless it within itself and in the world to come."

And he included: "And unify our hearts to fear Your name." This is to lean away from thoughts of the night. The beginning of the unification is the "weak part" that is recognized and remembered, to draw life from the upper, inner "weak part" <note>The text uses a cryptic term for a stage of emanation.</note> and let them hang there. The point is that the thought, by day and night, should be directed toward Him without the mixture of foreign thoughts. Rather, the thought should always wander above, in the **Unification of the Great Name**.

He further included in these words: "Establish us with a good reward and a good memory in Your world." These are the good answers to draw down the Divine Life, which is the Service for the ultimate purpose of the reward. He said: "For in Your book is the portion of life." This is a hint toward the transition to the Life to Come, to reach the portion of Heaven in existence. "The unification of your hearts" refers to what we would ask for in our lives, despite the brevity of our lives, through our service. This is to "rectify the Glory" through our good deeds. Then the Honorable Name will be called upon us, and it will be found so in the Unification, and they shall not labor in vain.

He gave a taste of this in the covenant of "And He said to me: You are My servant, Israel, in whom I will be glorified" <note>Isaiah 49:3</note>. But I said: "I have labored for nothing, I have spent my strength for emptiness and vanity; yet surely my right is with the Lord, and my recompense with my God." <note>Isaiah 49:4</note>

In the verse "You are My servant," they hinted to us that the reason we intended the Service and the "Divine Servants" are those through whom Israel exists. They are included because in the service of life, which presides over wisdom, they shall rule over all creatures so that the Great Name may be glorified through them—through the service with the musical intentions. They are the chosen ones... and this is the "crown for the King to whom peace belongs," a crown of glory and the treasury of the Holy Spirit from the Source. All this comes through the awakening of Israel below through good deeds.

In the Midrash of **Rashbi** on "Israel in whom I will be glorified": "To be glorified—through what? Through the deeds of Israel below, He is glorified above."

The intention in this is the ultimate goal: that the Great Name be blessed and unified in its Glory, for this is His will. As long as one is alive, he lives this Divine Life. Despite all this, they are in doubt about themselves, for perhaps they did not reach all that was necessary... and their labor would amount to nothing. This is why they said: "I said I have labored for nothing." But when they transition from the portion of this short life to the life that is near and coming, they are informed that their labor bore fruit. This fruit is the "rectification of the Glory" which they established through their speech in this life. The reason "God" is blessed is for what they did today. How will they achieve and know this? The Holy One, blessed be He, shows them their reward at the moment of their departure from the world. From this, they know that the rectification of the Glory they established in this world was a [valid] work. In the way we have chosen, He made for them all the Glory... and that is what is meant by "my right is with the Lord," which hints at the giving of the reward.

# Chapter 10: The Service of Prayer #

And the people rested and gathered the manna "day by day" <note>Exodus 16:4</note>, precisely so—except on the Eve of Sabbath. Thus, the Holy One, blessed be He, is found to be the source of blessing every single day. Regarding this, it is written: *“You open Your hand and satisfy the desire of every living thing”* <note>Psalm 145:16</note>. What is this "desire" <note>Hebrew: *ratzon*</note>? It is the desire drawn down from the **Holy Ancient One** <note>Original: *Atika Kadisha*, a high level of the Divine in Kabbalah</note>. When one requests it, it proves the desire for sustenance to be found for all, and grace for those who lack. Day by day, it is the seeker of the "blessing of faithfulness." When the blessing of faithfulness is found above, the blessings manifest below. Until here.

Behold, they have explained that the request for sustenance every day below is for the purpose of the **Glory** <note>The Shekhinah or Divine Presence</note> being blessed above. The true worshipper must direct his intention toward this goal, and not primarily for his own needs. If he only intends for his own benefit, he does not properly maintain the custom of the upper realms through his actions. In that case, he is merely dealing with his own lack and focusing on himself, which has already been clarified as insufficient.

**The Blessing of the Years** <note>The prayer for a successful harvest</note> and **The Blessing of the Gathering of the Exiles**: One should contemplate our King regarding the Redemption, as it is the fourth blessing <note>In the sequence of the middle petitions</note>. Why is it placed among them? According to the discussion in the chapter "One who reads the Megillah" <note>Talmud Megillah 17b</note>, this refers to our return and the beginning of the Redemption. Even though they call it "redemption," it refers specifically to the redemption from the troubles that constantly come upon us in exile. For the blessing of the Gathering of the Exiles, the rebuilding of Jerusalem, and the Sprout of David <note>The Messianic line</note> each have their own specific blessing. Why then is this one established as the fourth? Because the name "Redemption" is associated with it, they established it as the fourth. In the Talmud, they explain that this refers to the redemption from the hardships of the exile.

Furthermore, the conclusion of the blessing proves this. One must know that they established these two blessings regarding the exiles: the gathering of the exile of the body and the gathering of the exile of the soul. At the beginning of our prayer, we mention the body, that it should be saved through His mercies. Afterward, we pray for the redemption of wisdom. Therefore, they explained that the redemption of souls involves returning from the exile of the bodies; the exile of the body comes first, and the exile of the bodies <note>perhaps referring to the collective</note> comes last. Thus, the masters of the **Service** <note>Theurgy/Prayer</note> have divided these based on the mystery and the pathways of the **Torah**.

For the redemption of souls, which is a profound necessity, as they said in the Midrash of **Rabbi Nehunia ben ha-Kanah** <note>The Bahir</note>: this is the reason that in this section we pray for the light in the world. Regarding the redemption of the souls compared to the redemption of the bodies: it is written, "Sound the great shofar for our freedom," for this is the shofar that brings servants to freedom. And just as there is a spirit in their words, "and gather us together," this refers to the redemption of the **Shekhinah** <note>The Divine Presence</note>; thus, there is a high spiritual necessity here as well.

**The Eighth Blessing: The Blessing of Judgment.** The essence of judgment is as we mentioned before: that judgment should be according to the Torah and that there should not be unjust judges, so that evil does not have a hold. When He reigns, the authority and the foundation are in this blessing: "And Rule over us, You, O Lord, alone." Since the exile of our community is due to the strength of wickedness, it is written that when the wicked perish, the Kingdom of Heaven is revealed over us, and there will no longer be a yoke of foreign labor upon us until the Kingdom of the **House of David** returns to its place. This is a profound matter. It is what is written: "Afterward the children of Israel shall return and seek the Lord their God and David their king" <note>Hosea 3:5</note>. This teaches that these matters are linked, and they will be redeemed because they seek Him. In the chapter "One who reads the Megillah," they said that once the exiles are gathered, judgment is executed upon the wicked, and the haughty are humbled, and then the righteous flourish. Once the wicked are finished, the generations are completed, and judgment is executed upon them according to His record, through the help of the Lord and the movement of the deceased, who will merit measure for measure.

**The Ninth Blessing: The Blessing of the Heretics.** This is a prayer against the **Minim** <note>Heretics or sectarians</note>, that they may be uprooted from the silver <note>possibly a metaphor for the purity of Israel</note> and that the "thorns" which hold back the return of the Kingdom to its place may be removed. For when the spirit of the heavens increases:

-> To clear the upper and lower waters, for my soul is alive <-
-> To destroy and uproot the kingdom of wickedness, to cut down all the horns of the wicked <-
-> Above and below: A blessing that the horns of the righteous shall be exalted <-
-> The song of the blessing of the righteous, which is a support in the help of the Lord. <-

<column-break/>

**As if** <note>Original: *Kivyakhol* — a term used to speak metaphorically about God</note> the Holy One, blessed be He, returns with His people and remembers them with blessing. The verse mentioned in the blessing of the "broken piece" <note>referring to a specific prayer or the state of the Shekhinah in exile</note> is to awaken the blessing from the depths. For the lot of wisdom and the spreading of the days and the holiness of the Sanctuary—in the future, the Holy One, blessed be He, will heal the blow He struck and set His eyes and His memory upon them. His memory will ensure they are not passed over from the world. It will be "lacking in your heart," meaning the diminishment in the mystery of the moon’s lack in the light of the sun. But then the light of the sun shall be sevenfold, like the light of the seven days <note>Isaiah 30:26</note>. The mystery is that the Name will be unified in its Glory. Those who are designated as "wise servants" are found in the Kingdom. The light of the seven upper days will be joined to the sun, and the flaw of the moon will no longer be revealed. Everything in the upper realms will be revealed in its name upon you, and "the Lord shall be one and His Name one" <note>Zechariah 14:9</note>. And on that day of the Lord’s blow, He will heal the captivity of His people. The "blow" is the blow to wisdom that causes the "eyes" of the moon to wander and the Sanctuary to be defiled; this is the secret of our sorrow and the exile.

For this mystery, we pray in this blessing for sustenance, which is the "portion" of our King. Regarding the blessing of the "Minim" <note>Heretics</note>, our intention is that sustenance comes from the power of the "Table," as it is written. The blow of the destroyer and the exile—this is the intention in the expansion of the blessing for sustenance. Therefore, we ask afterward for the boundaries of the dawn from the exile and the blows that exist in the foundations of the world. This is why it is said, "And bring up a complete healing," etc.

**The Blessing of the Years: The Blessing of Pearls.** One must intend that the Honorable Name be blessed above so that the blessing may be blessed below, and the years may be blessed. For when the blessing is found above, it is also found below. Therefore we say, "Grant dew and rain for a blessing upon the face of the earth." The mystery of the Upper Wisdom is divided into the upper completion, and afterward it descends to the face of the world, as it is written, "He establishes the world" <note>Jeremiah 10:12</note>. He impresses the whole world with Good, "and fill our hands from Your blessings," so that the world may be blessed. Then the flow will be filled from His Goodness—and there is no "Good" but the **Righteous One** <note>The Sefirah of Yesod</note>, as it is written, "Tell the righteous that it is Good" <note>Isaiah 3:10</note>. When the world is blessed, all lack is gone. The blessing spreads below, and the buyers, the harvests, and the fruits are blessed. "And fill our hands," etc. May the Name deliver us from every evil thing, etc. They receive in their prayer that there should be no "abandoned" ones or "days of retribution," so that this grace, which is the Sanctuary of the Lord, should not be profaned. Now there is a restoration in the cord, and a line shall be stretched out over Jerusalem <note>Zechariah 1:16</note>, the line of the tabernacle, the final peace of the Righteous One upon their world.

**The Blessing of the Gathering of the Outcasts.** This blessing is with the intention that the flow from above should be reversed until it reaches the power that sustains the world, so that the blessing spreads downward to the lower beings. The one who awakens the blessing from below causes it to be awakened and found above. The complete intention is to intend for this: that the Name be blessed above. For even though the person praying needs all this for the survival of the body—for he cannot stand and serve unless he is healthy, God forbid, and has his needs—nevertheless, the intention should be for the sake of the **Glory**. He does not ask only for himself, but rather he asks so that the "reward" is the return of the blessing to its Source. For this he asks: that through his prayer below, the Glory is blessed above. The ultimate purpose of requesting these blessings is to enlighten himself and bless Him. It is not by chance that by asking for the needs of the body below, the upper blessings are awakened and found. For it is desirable that they return above, and if the blessings below are not awakened, more and more is withheld from returning above.

Regarding the matter of the request for food, they said in the Midrash of **Rabbi Shimon bar Yochai** <note>The Zohar</note>, peace be upon him: "I will rain down for you bread from heaven," etc. <note>Exodus 16:4</note>. Rabbi Yose opened and said: *“The eyes of all look hopefully to You...”* <note>Psalm 145:15</note>. All the inhabitants of the world wait and lift their eyes to the Holy One, blessed be He, for sustenance. So too, all the "children of faith" should seek every day and present their needs before the Holy One, blessed be He. Why? Because through all these things, the "exiles" of a person's needs for sustenance cause Him to be blessed every single day and to provide drink for all. The reason is to learn that "Blessed is the Lord day by day" <note>Psalm 68:20</note>. One should be found with the Lord, to pray before the Holy One, blessed be He, and to reveal his "exile" <note>his needs/displacement</note> regarding his sustenance every day, so that blessings may be found every single day above. For this reason, a pious person must intend this intention from day to day, to labor, and not to mix one day's request with another...

# Chapter 9

And these will be exalted by His names, as it is written: *“With whom did He take counsel...”* <note>Isaiah 40:14</note> and His holy Name shall be filled according to His will and for His entire assembly in measure. Contemplate the use of "Judgment" in its essence. To awaken this Name, they established at its beginning and wrapped it in its results: "To You is the crown," and "Our salvation is before Him." They were even more stringent in the chapter *One Does Not Stand* <note>Talmud Berakhot, Chapter 5</note>, following the way of Rabbi Simlai: "A person should always **arrange the praise** of the Holy One, blessed be He, and afterward he should pray." From where do we know this? From Moses, as it is written: *“And I pleaded [Va'etchanan] with the Lord...”* <note>Deuteronomy 3:23</note> and it is written there with these words of praise: *“O Lord God, You have begun to show Your servant Your greatness and Your mighty hand...”* and afterward it is written: *“Let me cross over, I pray You, and see the good land...”* <note>Deuteronomy 3:24-25</note>. 

And according to the midrash of Rabbi Shimon bar Yochai <note>The traditional author of the Zohar</note>, peace be upon him, they said: The "Pomegranate" <note>A symbol for the soul or the community of Israel</note> enters the inner chambers to be praised before its Master with its crowns, and afterward it asks for its needs. This is why Moses first said, "You have begun to show..." and afterward, "Let me cross over." Rabbi Yehuda said: What is the reason that he praises first and afterward requests? It is so that the "Attribute of Day" <note>Mercy</note> may be integrated into the "Attribute of Night" <note>Judgment</note>, and the "Attribute of Night" into the Day, so that the whole becomes one as is fitting. 

The goal of all this is one: it is what we have explained, that "arranging the praise" of the Holy One, blessed be He, means **unifying the Great Name** in His Glory and including all within the **Infinite** <term>Ein Sof: The Boundless or Infinite aspect of God</term>, which is the "end of the blessing and the beginning of its pool." It is to clarify that He is the "Place of the World" <note>A common Rabbinic epithet for God: *HaMakom*</note> and prepares the vessel to attend to His ways. For He acts as a "Mover" among the lower beings and ascends to perform His action, and they perform His will. They brought proof from Moses our teacher, peace be upon him, that the worshipper must arrange the praise of the Holy One, blessed be He, and afterward ask for his needs. 

Behold, those who established [the prayers], peace be upon them, followed this path in their prayer. They began from below to above, bringing the Attribute of Night into the Day and vice versa, as we explained regarding the "Old Man" <note>A reference to a specific passage in the Zohar</note> who said that the "pool" includes everything from above until its cessation. Such is the Kabbalah, as we wrote in the book *Tola'at Yaakov* <note>A classic Kabbalistic commentary on the liturgy by Meir ibn Gabbai</note>. He mentioned "The Most High" there, hidden in the head, and prepared the way of light to draw down the Holy Spirit and the flow of grace to the end. This is the **unification of Day and Night**, to include the holy within the holy, and its light and glory [descend] from level to level until the end of all levels. 

This is the meaning of: "May His Name be magnified and sanctified..." <note>The Kaddish prayer</note> which is the order from below to above. "Greatness" (*Gedulah*) and "Strength" (*Gevurah*) correspond to the Patriarchs and the "Mighty Ones." For "who is a God in heaven and on earth" who can do like Your works? This refers to the **Shekhinah** <term>Shekhinah: The Divine Presence, associated with the feminine aspect of God</term> from above and the ruler of the earth from below. The intention is that He is One in all the Heavens—which is the "Beauty of Israel" <note>The Sefirah of *Tiferet*</note>—corresponding to the holiness of the Name. And His holiness is like the "Holy One of Jacob." "And on earth"—this is the "Land of the Living," the Sefirah of **Kingship** (*Malchut*). Behold, He is One in the upper heavens and earth, and He is the ruler and the height, according to His will, in the lower heavens and earth. After arranging the praise of the Holy One, blessed be He, which is the complete unification, and in the manner of "they blessed," "they prayed," and afterward "Let me cross over," it is clarified that this is the path one must take to prepare the vessel and the way through which one finds their request. This is the "arrangement of praise" that is the Unification, following the path we explained. It will be further clarified from what we wrote in the section on "The Order of Prayers" with the Holy Spirit; and "your eyes shall behold" with the Supernal Wisdom. This is what we intended to explain in this chapter.

### Chapter 10

->The middle blessings in which all blessings are included<-
->Also in them is a hint to the Unification which is a high need<-

Our intention in these follows the path we have explained. We have already written that the blessing of "Years" was intended to grant holiness corresponding to the "Holiness of Jacob," which is the "Attribute of Truth." We wrote in the book *Tola'at Yaakov* that the intention of the prayer is for the middle blessings. Regarding this, it is said: *“The Lord is near to all who call upon Him, to all who call upon Him in truth”* <note>Psalm 145:18</note>. They said in the Jerusalem Talmud, in the chapter *The One Who Sees*: "To what is this comparable? To a mortal king... but the Holy One, blessed be He, is not so. A person enters the synagogue, stands behind the pillar, and prays in a whisper, and the Holy One, blessed be He, listens to his prayer." As it is written: *“And Hannah, she was speaking in her heart...”* <note>I Samuel 1:13</note>. The Psalmist said: *“In the Lord I have put my trust; how can you say to my soul, 'Flee as a bird to your mountain'?”* <note>Psalm 11:1</note>. The "Pillar" is the Lord, the Great Name, and that is the intention of the middle blessings.

Behold, the first blessing is **"You graciously grant knowledge to man."** This hints at the Sefirah of *Da'at* (Knowledge). It was established at the head of the requests...

<meta>Catchword: Our ways</meta>

<column-break/>

# Part of the Service # Chapter 10

...our ways, to show that this is the root from which everything else follows. It transforms the entire order of blessings, for it is what provides for those who have life or those who lack. The intention in this statement is that the one who approaches [God] should first request the knowledge to understand His "Oneness" and to align ourselves with supernal matters, upon which the Unification depends. He requests that He provide us with knowledge and intention, and that his mouth be opened to speak and to place the Great Name in His Glory there. This is the ultimate purpose of the service and indicates the final goal of his intention and his cleaving (*Devekut*) to Him. 

Our way is not to explain the literal meaning [of the words], but rather the knowledge of Him and the reaching of His perfection, which is the foundation. The sages said, based on the verse: *“But let him that glories glory in this, that he understands and knows Me, that I am the Lord who exercises lovingkindness, judgment, and righteousness in the earth; for in these things I delight, says the Lord”* <note>Jeremiah 9:23</note>. He said that perfect knowledge is in the matter of the **Unification**. This is the meaning of "understands and knows Me"—that through the intellect (*Sechel*), one reaches the level of the Foundation (*Yesod*). Whoever brings the world closer to Him, his name is "Lord" (*YHVH*), and that is the "Knowledge" which is the Foundation of the Chariot with its "Legs." For "the Lord exercises lovingkindness, judgment, and righteousness." This refers to the "Attribute of the Patriarchs" on earth, which are the "Living Waters." Behold, the "Chariot" is complete when the "Peace of the Legs" is joined with "David," who is the fourth leg. This is the "World" which is the Unification, like the "Work of the Chariot" (*Ma'aseh Merkavah*). For when the four are the "Foundation of the Chariot," they belong to the Name of the "Heavens of Heavens." They are the foundational flow so that the Unification exists in everything and is integrated within them. Their unification is the Will and the Supernal Strength. Behold, perfect knowledge is the Unification; therefore, they established the blessing of Knowledge at the head of all the blessings and requests.

**The second blessing** is the blessing of **Repentance** (*Teshuvah*). This blessing was established after the blessing of Knowledge, which is the Unification. This is because it is natural for a person to err and sin. Sin causes "separation" and "division." In the Holy Unification, which is the source of all holiness, one draws down the flow. His return to the proper order is for the "Master of Knowledge" to return to the worship that was abandoned. In its place, it causes the Holy Names to move away from their children, and there their nakedness is revealed. When the Divine Presence (*Shekhinah*) is brought close, it returns to its place in the mystery of "Return," and He will have mercy on us.

**The third blessing** is the blessing of **Forgiveness** (*Selichah*). "Forgive us, our Father." The reason for this is that due to the weight of sin, the Glory is not yet fully forgiven. For sin and transgression cause "darkness," and into that darkness the "Plague" enters. Therefore, these two blessings [Repentance and Forgiveness] are needed so that you may return. Because the "Lights" are separated, the Light of Heaven—which is the "Beauty of Israel" <note>Tiferet</note>—must be brought toward the King. It is said: "For Your Name's sake, O Lord, pardon my iniquity" <note>Psalm 25:11</note>. And it is written: "Help us, O God of our salvation, for the glory of Your Name; and deliver us, and forgive our sins, for Your Name's sake" <note>Psalm 79:9</note>.

**The fourth blessing** is the blessing of **Redemption** (*Geulah*). In these three [previous] blessings, we appeal to the "Glory of Your Name." This is because the *Shekhinah* is the "Name of Glory" which is with us in exile. Therefore, we pray that He redeems us, so that He redeems Himself. This is why it says, "For Your Name's sake," for this is the prayer of the exiles. 

And they said in the Midrash on Psalms (*Shocher Tov*): "Bring us salvation." Rabbi Eleazar said in the name of Rabbi Jose: It is written, "Your salvation is ours." And they said further there: "O God of our salvation." This is one of the places where the salvation of Israel is actually the salvation of the Holy One, blessed be He. In the chapter *One Who Dies* <note>Talmud Sanhedrin</note>, regarding every distress that comes upon the community, Rabbi Meir says: "It is as if the Redemption were for Me and for you." As if it were possible (*Kivyakhol*), "I was redeemed with you," as it is written: *“...whom You redeemed for Yourself from Egypt, nations and their gods”* <note>II Samuel 7:23</note>. And in the Sifrei: "He saved us with His hand." Rabbi Akiva says: Were it not for the verse being written, it would be impossible to say it—**as if it were possible** (*Kivyakhol*), Israel said before the Omnipresent: "You redeemed Yourself."

**The fifth blessing** is the blessing of **Healing** (*Refuah*). This also has a "high need," for when the lower creatures are healthy, as if it were possible, their health affects the Supernal Essence. In the chapter *The One Who Reads the Megillah* <note>Talmud Megillah 17b</note>: Why did they see fit to say "Healing" as the eighth blessing? Rabbi Hama said: Since circumcision is on the eighth day and requires healing, they fixed it as the eighth. Behold, the "Right Hand" requires healing. In the chapter *The Trial is Finished* <note>Talmud Sanhedrin 46a</note>, Rabbi Meir said: When a person suffers, what language does the *Shekhinah* use? "My head is heavy, My arm is heavy." And in the Midrash on the Song of Songs (*Hazit*), Rabbi Joshua of Sikhnin said in the name of Rabbi Levi, Rabbi Tanchuma said: The Talmud of these [sages]... if one of them is suffering... as if it were possible...

It emphasizes that Israel's redemption and health are, in a mystical sense, the redemption and "health" of the Divine Presence itself.</summary>

...to reveal His kingship and to clothe Himself within it by resting upon the world. When the soul is consumed like a shadow <note>original: "כטול" – likely referring to the protective shadow or the soul's ephemeral nature during ascent</note> for its own expansion, it travels deep until it reaches the Crown <note>Keter, the highest of the ten Sefirot or divine emanations</note> of the male principle, where the soul must be exchanged and clothed. There, the soul is satisfied and established as it ascends. And it says further there: "The soul's steps are remembered," and to establish the soul is difficult and requires precision, like a shadow intended to give life to the soul and to look upon it with a steady gaze, to trust and be established in it. It ascends to the "Offering" <note>original: *Korbanka*, a mystical term for the proximity achieved through sacrifice or prayer</note> through it, to be sustained and to stand always, all through the days, before the Ancient of Days <note>Atik Yomin, a term for the most ancient, hidden aspect of the Divine</note>. This is the ascent of the soul's steps, to stand as one with its Brother. Until here [ends the quote].

Because the secret of the ascent of the breath <note>original: *neshimah*, referring both to physical breathing and the soul</note> is hidden and sealed, and as was explained in the secret of the aforementioned higher intelligence in this blessing, which corresponds to the secret of the Place of Intelligence, so that the breath may delight through there by divine will and not drown in the Masculine River <note>term: *Nahar Dikur* – in Kabbalah, a spiritual flow that can be overwhelming to an unprepared soul</note>.

As for the phrase "And they shall praise and bless Your great Name," this is because the purpose of the existence of the days through which the Name passes is to praise and bless the Great Name and the Higher Source, so that He may be unified in His Glory. This is the entirety of His service.

As for the phrase "Forever, for He is good," because there is no interruption to the Divine Unity, so must the praise and thanksgiving be without pause. For this, the perfected person yearns for the continuity of the blessings, to unify without end.

**The third blessing is the Blessing of Peace**, corresponding to the "Righteous One, the Life of the Worlds" <note>referring to the Sefirah of Yesod</note>. Peace is written concerning the land of the waters, the peace of the Kingdom of the House of David. Through this, peace is found in the secret that when this peace returns, all goodness and blessings are completed, for He is the one who gathers and mixes the flow. He brings forth a scent for the "White One" <note>symbolizing the Sefirah of Chesed or the pure divine light</note>, a holy secret through the spinal cord, pouring out like a pitcher... and this is His expertise, "He who blesses His people Israel with peace."

As interpreted from the words of the Zohar: "A cup of blessing... peace, peace to the world, peace below, peace to all sides, peace in the upper assembly, and peace in the lower assembly." The language is only settled if there is peace in the lower assembly and peace below, to embrace the lower peace, which is explained as a voice in the upper assembly. This hides the secret for all the lower living beings. All is gathered into the core. The higher realm is established at its beginning to complete the fullness over all its hosts, perfect in all who walk in the higher callings of the hopes, all becoming one end: peace, goodness, and blessing, etc. Take a man who begins to emerge from foolishness; he does not speak, but rather his bones emerge from the community to be consumed. Those primary bones are the ones who precede... to wait for the blessings, to work for the Unification, to complete it. He is a man who is a steward to the King. And it is found in one manuscript: "From the moment the intelligence of peace is paused, and it returns to all the links of the incense and the Unification and the blessings and the holiness and the addition of holiness, the calling goes out to all the foundations, saying to them: 'Write for this one a blessing, portions for the horn of his dwelling.'" For those who are hidden and carved within the secrets of heaven, let us say: "Understanding in the connections and the binding of knots," and let them all be filled with a single Unification. These shall be the dwellings of His name, without mundane thoughts, to be written and placed and made known above, and to be revealed above and below. Until here [ends the quote].

The secret of the matter is that when the one who prays knows the order of the higher things and their movements, and directs his heart in prayer with the proper intention—an intention that connects the lower Palaces <note>term: *Heichalot* – the spiritual dimensions or 'palaces' through which prayer ascends</note> to the heights—his intentions reach the place of the upper lights, and he unifies the Great Name in His glory. This is the secret of the full Name: *YHVH Elohim*. If he passes through these intentions and directs his heart to this, he is prepared for his prayer to be established, prepared within the Great Name to unify it in His glory. This is the Unification that the Palaces perform at every level.

In the book *Talumot Yitzchak* (Mysteries of Isaac), we have elaborated on the secret of this matter, the order of things, and the intention regarding the book of the Palaces of below and above. We have already written in the second chapter of this part that the one who focuses in his prayer on the Root, without any distraction, clings to the Great Name. And in this book of the Palaces...

...in the language of "Blessed," which cascades down. He saw with strength and placed it in the desire to uplift truly, as the altar is arranged in the south and the libation in the east. So too, everything is bound in one Unification to be revealed with power. All those who know how to order their prayers as is fitting are bound together, and the "Blessed ones" connect with them. He is clothed in strength and designated, and all his ascents are in this world and the world to come.

Thus, one who knows how to order his prayer in a way that the lower Palaces are elevated and bound with the secret of the Name included in the upper Palaces—through the secret of the Unique Name—is also illuminated and praised through them. He shall walk in radiance, and he is connected in this world and the world to come.

# Chapter 12

I must recount all the blessings of the prayer <note>referring to the Amidah</note>, which were ordained by the Men of the Great Assembly <note>the legislative body of Jewish sages at the start of the Second Temple period</note> through the Holy Spirit. The "Blessing of the Heretics" <note>term: *Birkat HaMinim* – the 19th blessing added later to the original 18</note> is an established blessing, as they said in the chapter *The Morning Prayer* <note>Talmud Berakhot, Chapter 4</note>.

However, the reason for the number eighteen was to point toward the Holy Unification that is unified in a single source. This number equals "Chai" <note>original: *Chet-Yud*, meaning 'Life' and equaling 18 in Gematria</note> to point toward the "Eighteen Lives of the Worlds," which are destined to be judged together with the upper heavens, in the secret of "For all that is in heaven and on earth." And because there are eighteen mentions of the Divine Name <note>original: *Azkarot*</note>—unique names included in the Name of Mercy—this is the secret of the Holy Unification that seals all things. As they said in the *River of Peace*: "And the seal is voice."

They said in the chapter *The Morning Prayer*: "To what do these eighteen correspond?" Rabbi Hillel, the son of Rabbi Shmuel bar Nachmani, said: "To the eighteen mentions of God's name that David said in 'Ascribe to the Lord, O sons of the mighty' <note>Psalm 29</note>." Rav Yosef said: "To the eighteen mentions of God's name in the Shema." Rabbi Tanchum said in the name of Rabbi Joshua ben Levi: "To the eighteen vertebrae in the spine."

The Rabbi, R' Yehuda HaLevi <note>the famous 12th-century philosopher and poet</note>, wrote: "These three sages do not disagree, for each of them desired to exalt the prayer and support it upon a strong pillar, to sink into it further meaning and strengthen it like nails." The general rule is that they correspond to the "God of the Worlds." Rabbi Hillel said they correspond to the 18 mentions in the Psalm *Ascribe to the Lord*. Rav Yosef said they correspond to the 18 mentions in the *Shema* <note>The central declaration of Jewish faith</note>. Rabbi Tanchum (and Rabbi Yose adds) said they correspond to the 18 vertebrae in the spine because the Prince of the Worlds decides below between the ten toes of the feet, as explained in the *Book of Creation* <note>term: *Sefer Yetzirah* – the earliest extant book on Jewish esotericism</note>. For the order of the names waters all the pathways, and they are sustained, and He establishes, knows, subtracts, waters, gives birth, and gives life. This is the nature of the "One who revives the dead."

As for the **Blessing of the Heretics** which they added to the blessings, it can be said to correspond to the "Four-Letter Name of the Distant Glory" <note>referring to a lower manifestation of the tetragrammaton</note>, which is not the four-letter Name itself but below it. Or it can be said to correspond to the "Smallness" within them... This corresponds to the "small constellations" in the Torah, which are the most distant of all. Against them, they established the prayer of the heretics, which is the place of the claim of the "Kings of the Nations," as hinted at... and he should strengthen another matter they intended, and the wise one shall see with his eyes and his heart shall understand. Until here [ends the quote].

Furthermore, in this number [18], there is a secret concerning the ascent, as they were established to correspond to the **eighteen thousand worlds** of His. And they said in the *Secrets of the Sabbath* that the Merciful One rides upon His light cherub and moves across 18,000 worlds, as it says: "The chariots of God are myriads, even thousands of *shinan*" <note>Psalm 68:18</note>—do not read *shinan* but *she-einan* (that are not) <note>a play on words suggesting 2,000 are subtracted from 20,000, leaving 18,000</note>.

The secret of the matter is that the Merciful One, in His qualities, gives life to the Creator to uplift the world, for the power of contemplation is in Him. The secret of the hidden "twenty" minus "two" <note>original: "רמתיים קרי יח" – a mathematical allusion to 20,000 minus 2,000</note> equals 18. Through the intention of the 18 blessings, one completes the 18,000 worlds in the universe. "Worlds" (*Olamot*) comes from the language of "Hiddenness" (*He'elam*). The secret is that we ask in the intention of prayer to be lifted up. Furthermore, from the language of "Worldly concealment," as He is hidden in the secrets and the universes.

According to another of the sages who spoke in this language: "One must know that there are blessings corresponding to the 18,000 worlds that surround the Crown [Keter] of the Most High." There are 18,000 worlds on the Eastern side, 18,000 worlds on the Western side, 18,000 worlds on the Northern side, and 18,000 worlds on the Southern side. Thus, their total number is **72,000 worlds**.

# Chapter 10

When we are found worthy and the wicked are punished, the "horn" <note>A biblical metaphor for strength and pride</note> of the righteous is elevated—this is the secret of the **Horn of David**. We shall stand upright before the Eternal Life in a single radiance, for those who separate themselves from the fleeting world <note>original: "חלופו של עולם" - referring to the transient nature of material existence</note> merit this. This is the intention behind our petition for the uprooting of the "bandits" <note>original: "מלסטים" (listim) - a term often used in midrash for spiritual or physical oppressors</note> and the wicked. This is the explanation of the elevation of the lowly and the virtue of the high and the low.

**Blessing 9** <note>In the standard Amidah, these are usually blessings 14 and 15; the manuscript uses its own numbering for the middle section</note>: The blessing of the **building of Jerusalem**, the dwelling place of His supreme glory. For the Temple is the "meeting house" for the Righteous One and Justice <note>referring to the mystical union of the divine attributes of Yesod and Malkhut</note>. Through the building below, the building above is also constructed, for when the Divine Presence (*Shekhinah*) dwells below, the supreme *Shekhinah* dwells above, as one depends on the other. This is hinted at in the phrase "Open for Him, O Lord." If you merit the "doves' holes" <note>A reference to Isaiah 60:8, symbolizing the return of exiles or prayers to the Temple</note>, it refers to the nest of the Holy Temple, the Tabernacles (*Sukkot*) that surround the Kingdom. Here is the holiness of this Festival. When we merit it, the "horn" is raised, for the **Jerusalem of Above** is the "Peace of Jerusalem," and one must mention it. Behold, the sacrifice of the righteous is the secret of the **Horn of David** being raised in Jerusalem, granting us an inheritance and merit for all.

**Blessing 10**: The Blessing of Salvation (*Yeshuah*), which is the sprouting of the Kingdom and the raising of the **Horn of David** to the "Head," the place of salvation. He grants a "horn of salvation" to His people, a day hinting at the return of **David their King**. His voice, which was silenced in the dream of exile, shall break through. Our petition "for Your salvation we hope" indicates the **Salvation of Above**, for that is the essence of our hope. We direct our hearts to His ways and the peace of the paths of prophecy. We look toward the Salvation Above, for the primary intention is planted on high; His salvation is found within our salvation.

As they said in the *Midrash Tanhuma* regarding the Eighteen Benedictions: What is written? "Rejoice greatly, O daughter of Zion... behold, your king comes to you; he is righteous and *nosha* (saved/victorious)" <note>Zechariah 9:9</note>. It does not say "savior" (*moshiya*) but "saved" (*nosha*). Likewise, it says "Return to the daughter of Zion, He is your savior." Is "savior" written here? No, it says "your salvation," as if He Himself—if it were possible to say—is the one being saved. Rabbi Meir said: "And the Lord saved Israel on that day"—it is written "and He was saved" <note>original: "ויושע" (vayosha) interpreted homiletically as "and He was saved" rather than "He saved"</note>, as if He were saved along with Israel. For as long as Israel is in exile, it is as if He is in exile. Until here [ends the quote]. And they said further: It is written, "to him who orders his way I will show the salvation of God" <note>Psalm 50:23</note>—not "My salvation" but the "salvation of God" <note>original: "ישע אלהים" - implying God's own salvation</note>.

And in the previous chapter regarding the afternoon prayer (*Mincha*): once Jerusalem is built, David comes, as it says, "Afterward the children of Israel shall return and seek the Lord their God and David their king" <note>Hosea 3:5</note>. This hints at what we have written.

**Blessing 11**: The Blessing of Prayer. One who prays must fear the word of the Lord and intend in this blessing that He hear his voice—the voice of a "prophet" <note>original: "נבוך" - likely a scribal error or variant for "נביא" (prophet) or "נבון" (understanding)</note>. That is to say, all that we have requested in all the middle blessings, we request with understanding. Just as we ask for forgiveness, blessing, and health, we ask for the strength to stand and for our intentions to be made like a "pure creation." In this blessing, we beg that He **hear our voice**, just as He hears the "intention of the heart," if it were possible to say. They said: "He passed by him and showed him mercy," to bless him, but only for the sake of understanding.

Rabbi [Menahem] said: For what reason did our teacher Moses desire to enter the Land of Israel? Was it to eat of its fruits or satisfy himself with its goodness? No; rather, Moses said: "Many commandments were commanded to Israel that can only be fulfilled in the **Land of Israel**. Let me enter the Land so they may all be fulfilled through me." Prayer follows this same intention; when we bless in this manner, the Answerer is Above, and it is accepted with favor.

They said in the first chapter of *Berakhot*: "Things that stand at the height of the world, yet people treat them with contempt." Rashi (may his memory be a blessing) explained: "Things that stand at the height of the world" refers to **Prayer**, which ascends to the heights. This means that when the intention is directed in the way we have mentioned, the prayer ascends and is crowned upon the head of the Righteous One. This is the meaning of "standing at the height of the world." With this, the intention of the middle blessings is completed.

# Chapter 11

The three final blessings are **Service** (*Avodah*), **Thanksgiving** (*Hoda'ah*), and **Grant Peace** (*Sim Shalom*). We have already written that the first three blessings correspond to the intellects and the perfections of the soul, while the middle ones address our needs and blessings according to the secret we explained. The first of the final three is the "Rina" <note>Song of joy/prayer</note> corresponding to the High Priest, while the last is "Hallel" <note>Praise</note>, and "Peace" corresponds to the "Peace of the Crowns." These three final blessings are intended to mirror the first three: these correspond to Kingship, and those correspond to Wisdom, which is—

<column-break/>

# The Service: Chapter 11

—forgiven. They said in the Midrash of **Rabbi Shimon bar Yochai** <note>The Zohar</note> (peace be upon him) at the end of the mentions: After one finishes his requests, he should grant peace to all sides in his dwelling... and then return to be strengthened with blessings forever.

The Blessing of the Service (*Avodah*) corresponds to the power of the "Ancient of Days" <note>term: *Atik Yomin* - the most hidden aspect of God</note>. This is because the service of the **sacrifices** brings satisfaction there, and the Holy Spirit descends from there upon the House of Kingship. This is the secret of the **Ma'amadot** <note>term: *Ma'amadot* - groups of laypeople who stood by during the Temple offerings to represent the entire nation</note> who stood over the sacrifice; they are the "sustenance of the body." It was said in the chapter "Three Times a Year" in the tractate *Ta'anit*: Rabbi Jacob bar Aha said in the name of Rabbi Assi: "If not for the **Ma'amadot**, heaven and earth would not endure."

The secret is that the *Ma'amadot* establish the "Body," which is the secret of the Heavens, and they influence strength and power into the Earth. Thus, they are established in the habitation of the Heavens, for they receive from every high level and influence every lower level; this is the "sustenance of heaven and earth." These are the ones of whom it was said in the chapter "One who expounds": "He established standing and quiet rows for the righteous in the time to come."

And in the Midrash of Rabbi Shimon bar Yochai (peace be upon him): "The righteous shall praise Your name; the upright shall dwell in Your presence" <note>Psalm 140:14</note>. This refers to the heavens... after the "refuse" is removed, once they have been purified of the "scum of the calves" <note>referring to the sin of the Golden Calf</note>... this is the secret of the "upright shall dwell," referring to the joy of the righteous. The Holy One, blessed be He, will provide for them from the "bread of the mighty" <note>original: "לחם אבירים"</note>... all this refers to the ability to stand in the rank of the "living," so that they may be blessed by the radiance of their King. This is why it is said of the righteous: "These are the righteous who are included and receive all their sustenance from the 'fire' of other righteous ones." Until here [ends the quote].

They mentioned the Service along with "And let our eyes behold" <note>referring to the prayer for the return to Zion</note> to show that prayer is itself a form of **Service**. As it says in the *Sifrei*: "'To serve Him with all your heart'—this refers to prayer." Since the service of sacrifices is gone, this is what is written regarding Israel, "and they shall return to the glory of their houses." This is the secret of the **Unification of the Great Name** in its dwelling. So too, prayer contains all of this. This is why we seal this blessing with "Who restores His Divine Presence to Zion." This is the secret of the **Kingdom of the House of David**, which prepares and fills the "Eternal Building," the secret of Zion for the Kingdom. This is the secret of the one who "serves" within this blessing.

**The Second Blessing** [of the final three] is the **Blessing of Thanksgiving** (*Modim*). It corresponds to the "Pillar of Truth" <note>referring to the attribute of Yesod or Hod</note> from all the *Ma'amadot* that sustain heaven and earth. It is from here that the "Living" <note>the righteous</note> are sustained. Within this is the **secret of bowing**, to draw down the light and to acknowledge the wisdom of the hidden powers.

In the *Book of the Palaces* (*Hekhalot*), it says regarding the intention of the wisdom of these two blessings: "The building is constructed through the union... and the service is above all." And they said: "Everything that lives shall thank You," to show that the purpose of life is so that one may speak and give thanks to the Great Name, blessed be He. The "form" of this blessing corresponds to **Hod** <note>Splendor/Majesty, the eighth Sefirah</note>, because it represents judgment, and one must be careful of it; we must increase its greatness through thanksgiving.

There is another reason for mentioning "the living" in the form of this blessing. It is because the "Palace of the Heavens" <note>referring to a specific spiritual realm</note>... as our teachers (may their memory be a blessing) said: One must acknowledge the "Life of the Worlds." This spirit enters and all the waters... and all these are found in the "Horn" of his merit as a "memorial of judgments." Then this spirit breaks through and is remembered in the light of the "Face of the King of Life."

Because this Palace corresponds to *Hod*, we say in this blessing: "We shall forever give thanks to You and tell of Your praise, for our lives which are delivered into Your hand." For life is what flows downward to the world... and we speak of "our souls which are entrusted to You"—this part of the blessing is to increase and give thanks for them, for they are destined to ascend through there to take delight in the **Precious Kingdom**, according to what they have prepared through their deeds in these days. They said further there: "All those who are attached to their Master, the righteous, are called 'living' even in their death, for they are attached to the Life." And all the souls ascend and are pardoned in this Palace... to be crowned for their merits and for having feared Heaven... and for performing the commandments of the Torah...

### Chapter 13

**The preparation of the soul** through the received tradition <note>original: "קבלה" (Kabbalah)</note> obligates us to believe that the Lord <note>original: "יי'" - the Tetragrammaton</note> is the source of all power and the Name to be praised. Let no one be deterred or say, "Why should I believe in this tradition more than any other?" For anyone who tries to know their Creator and His awesomeness through logic alone will find it impossible. This is the intent of this tradition: to believe in the root and the foundation of everything. 

One who does not listen to this wisdom—which is the tradition I have received—is not considered a "Wise Kabbalist" <note>term: "חכם מקובל" - one who has mastered the received mystical tradition</note>. A wise person is one whose words show that they have received the tradition from a master, even if they must struggle greatly to grasp it. Our great Master <note>referring to Maimonides, the Rambam</note> (may his memory be a blessing) stated that a tradition received from a wise master should be believed more than anything else, for there is no other way to truly know the Creator and serve Him. 

The later generations have already received from the **Sages of Truth** <note>original: "חכמי האמת" - a common term for Kabbalists</note> that Elijah the Prophet (of blessed memory) revealed himself to the court of a certain master and handed over the secrets of the Wisdom of Kabbalah. That master then handed them to the father of the **Ravad** <note>Rabbi Abraham ben David of Posquières, a 12th-century critic of Maimonides and early mystic</note>, to whom Elijah also appeared. The Ravad then passed them to his son, the pious **Rabbi Isaac the Blind** <note>original: "רבי יצחק סגי נהור" - a foundational figure in early Kabbalah</note>, to whom Elijah also appeared. He then passed them to his two students, Rabbi Ezra and Rabbi Azriel. From them, the tradition reached **Nahmanides** <note>original: "הרמב"ן" - Rabbi Moses ben Nahman</note>, and from him it spread to the pious ones who followed him until this day. From there, it was revealed to us, to the famous master who was a vessel full of wisdom, who almost at the end of his days swore to serve God in truth according to this wisdom. For this is the True Wisdom, and if one does not exert themselves to believe in it more than other things, they are missing the true source of life and return.

<column-break/>

->**Chapter 13: Part of the Service (Page 32)**<-

I have not heard of any wise men who disputed these words after they were revealed. If some students turned to "evil waters" <note>a metaphor for heresy or incorrect philosophy</note> and strayed from the words of these great figures, it was because they thought they could understand everything through the plain meaning <note>original: "פשט" (Peshat)</note> and ended up in the mire. When they were called to judgment, they found that they had only upheld the superficial layer and neglected the inner spirit. 

Regarding the great philosopher **Maimonides** <note>original: "הרמב"ם" - Rabbi Moses ben Maimon</note>: there is a story that late in his life, he found the "pearl" <note>the mystical truth</note> and cast aside his previous philosophical works. One of the Sages of Truth, who explained the secrets of Nahmanides, wrote that Rabbi Jacob went to Egypt and transmitted the Kabbalah to Maimonides. It is said that Maimonides was very happy with it and taught it to his students until the end of his days, saying that all his previous famous books were incomplete. **Rabbi Isaac Abarbanel** <note>a famous 15th-century statesman and commentator</note> also wrote at the end of his commentary on *Pirkei Avot* that he heard that Maimonides wrote in a letter to his colleagues at the end of his life: "A person came to me and told me things of great sense, and had I not been at the end of my life, I would have corrected many of the things I wrote." There is no doubt these were matters of Kabbalah.

This resolves the difficulty for those who think the great Master Maimonides was only a philosopher. He returned to the root of wisdom. If someone asks, "Who from the house of the Kabbalists would do such a thing?"—implying that he retracted his rationalist works—the answer is that he did so to point toward the true path. It is impossible to achieve true soul-attachment <note>original: "דבקות" (Devekut)</note> without these hidden matters. One must have great faith, for in the end, it leads to action. This is the secret of the "Burnt Offering" <note>original: "קרבן עולה" - an offering entirely consumed by fire</note> which is about the perfection and purity of intention in service, as I explained in the previous chapters. Truly, there is no place for those who doubt; even if a wise man doesn't understand at first, it is because he needs time and great diligence to be refined and brought out of his confusion.

I have informed you of what was said regarding the foundation of the words of our great Master <note>Nahmanides</note>, who exerted himself to believe in Kabbalah more than anything else. It appears his words are consistent, and even Maimonides eventually agreed that the tradition received through the generations—the **Oral Torah** <note>original: "תורה שבעל פה"</note>—is the true foundation of faith.

### Chapter 14

**We find** in the law of the **Sacrifice** <note>original: "קרבן" (Korban)</note> that it is entirely founded on the rectification of the soul. Specifically, the **Burnt Offering** (*Olah*) was entirely consumed by the fires on the altar. There were also the two "Daily Offerings" <note>original: "תמידין" - the Tamid offerings</note> brought every day. These were not brought for a specific sin, but rather to fulfill the **Supreme Will** <note>original: "רצון העליון"</note>, which is the secret of **Unification** <note>original: "ייחוד" (Yichud)</note>. Our intention in prayer should be this alone. This is the true intent of the service that we established in the previous chapters. When the perfect servant intends this during the offering, the service is accepted, for the body is merely a vessel for the internal spirit.
