->### Chapter 12 | Section | The Service | Chapter 13<-

Corresponding to the 70 essential and chosen Names found from King Solomon <note>original: "שלמה המלך"</note>, and the verses "And He traveled," "And He came," and "And He stretched out" <note>Exodus 14:19-21. Each of these three verses contains 72 letters, which Kabbalists use to derive the 72-letter Name of God</note>. These are the **72 Names**, and every single world has its own fixed Name. There is a portion of "Motivations" drawn from the Prime Mover, may He be remembered for life, which flow from the world of all Names and bring out the "Hidden Ones." These are the worlds; they receive from those Names. There is a portion of the "Blessings of the Lord"—you shall call them blessings—for all the blessings that sustain the entire world come from them. For this reason, the **Men of the Great Assembly** <term>Anshei Knesset HaGedolah: The leadership body of the Jewish people during the early Second Temple period, credited with composing the standard liturgy</term> instituted the blessings for us to pray to Him, may He be blessed, in order to draw the flow of abundance from Him. This portion of blessings is drawn and found from the **World of Wisdom** <note>original: "עולם של חכמה"</note>, up to this point.

One must know that in prayer there are four levels, corresponding to the four wings of the Living Creatures <note>A reference to the celestial beings in Ezekiel's vision</note>, and prayer possesses an exalted height. 

The first and highest level descends from time and the world until the Morning Prayer. This Name is the aspect of the **Soul** <note>original: "נשמה" (Neshamah)</note>, and its movement is like a celestial sign without any circle. 

The second level reaches the "Occupied Realm," and by its power all the stars and constellations were subjugated and would obey, though not with total straightness.

The third level reaches near the sphere of *Araboth* <note>The highest of the seven heavens in Jewish cosmology</note>, and by its power the "First Kings" were subjugated, and they would hear the cry of this people.

The fourth level is of great significance; they would enter until the sphere of the Moon, and by its power all the ranks of Israel are subjugated. One "Living One" fills them, and they were hidden in the "House of Levels" at the four corners of the Kingdom <note>original: "מלכות" (Malchut)</note>. 

In the time of the "Return of the Throne," and in the time of the Sages of the Talmud, and in these times of Israel's exile, the merit of the innocent is diminished because of the lack of grace; for though they were once heard, these things have been forgotten. For this reason, the King <note>likely referring to David or Solomon</note>, peace be upon him, heard of this and sought mercy before the Name, who hears the prayer of the Mighty, to write this book of the **Ordered Prayer**. He did not despise it, nor did it cease from here.

The Sages, of blessed memory, said that one's prayer is only heard when offered with the community <note>original: "צבור" (Tzibur)</note>, for all prayers require the many, with one heart, one agreement, and with focused intention <note>term: "כוונה" (Kavanah) - the meditative focus or mental directedness required during prayer</term>. For a prayer that is joined to others must ascend, and it reaches the source of prayers. To the extent that these obstacles are diminished, the reception of the prayer is diminished. 

Unique individuals among the Righteous and the Pious of old would raise their prayers even higher as needed, and the "Companions" would perform actions and raise seventy "Houses." For I have received from the **Sages of Wisdom** that thirty lines ascend to that place. This is part of the "Hidden Wisdom" that the Men of the Great Assembly instituted—that prayer should abound in blessings to prepare the "Pool" until there is a blessing to ascend the five levels, so that it may find favor and be enriched by the will of the **Righteous One, the Life of the Worlds** <note>A Kabbalistic title for the Sefirah of Yesod</note. In the book *The Rod of the Worm of Jacob* <note>original: "מטה תולעת יעקב" - likely referring to the work *Tola'at Yaakov* by Meir ibn Gabbai</note> I found these levels and the agreements within them. 

And behold, they were completed when they came to establish the Honor in this world through the "Anointing of the Grapes," and its throne is in External Wisdom. Its foundation is the level that ascends higher and higher by way of this world, supporting the journey until it reaches its place to be bound there, the "House of her Father." From there it came and descended through those levels, and through there it shall ascend and return to its place. The one who prays must achieve the path of the "Mountain" and receive from her through his prayer and service, passing along the path we have described with the intention we have stated. Then his soul will ascend on that path without delay or hindrance, and he will find the delight that is within it, and the Glory will be praised and beautified through the Living God of the Worlds.

### Chapter 12
### The Section

He also returned to ask about the chance occurrence to the innocent flesh who are choice in faith, to strengthen the hand of faith and true service. These are his words in Chapter 137: 

"I have also informed you that his teacher, the 'Small Rabbi' <note>likely a humble epithet for a great scholar</note>, of blessed memory, who was a greater rabbi than all the men of his generation and was also my teacher—though I did not see him with my own eyes—he used to say: **'I pray with the knowledge of this child.'** This is to say, the pious ones of the King, the Kabbalists, pray sometimes to one **Sefirah** <term>Sefirah (plural: Sefirot): One of the ten divine emanations or attributes through which God interacts with the universe</term> and sometimes to another Sefirah, according to the subject of the prayer. And some say that this is the meaning of what the Sages, of blessed memory, said: 'One who wishes to become wise should turn south, and to become wealthy

<column-break/>

should turn north.' This means he should direct his intention toward the 'Attribute of the Right' <note>Chesed/Mercy</note> or the 'Attribute of the Left' <note>Gevurah/Judgment</note>. Also, in the **Amidah prayer** <note>original: "תפלת י"ח" - the 'Eighteen' benedictions, the central silent prayer</note>, they have a known intention for each and every blessing for its specific salvation. All of this seemed very strange in my eyes, even though Elijah was a Kabbalist like him. 

I responded to this in the 'Eighth Article of Faith.' I have already heard questions among those who branch off from the book regarding the version of the Kabbalists, where they would say 'shameful things' about those who keep the watches and the meditations on the angels of the World of Action. 

It once happened to me while I was in Syracuse that the elderly sage **Don Joseph ben Shoshan**, of blessed memory—who was a sage in the Talmud and other sciences, a great Kabbalist and pious man, meticulous in the commandments—stood up there. He was a great scholar. Once I asked him: 'How can you change your focus? In one blessing you intend for one Sefirah, and in another blessing for a different Sefirah? Furthermore, one could add words that the Name might complete for them!' 

And he answered me, 'Elijah, let the tradition be thus: for though there is the **Cause of Causes** <note>original: "עלת העלות" - God as the Ultimate Source</note>, this matter is like one who has a legal dispute and asks the King to perform justice for him. If he asks the King to personally sit in judgment, they say to him: "This is not good; go to the Steward appointed over these matters," for he is the one who handles the instruments of the law. If he did not ask the king to give him something he didn't have, the king would immediately tell him to go to the Steward. If he wants wine, he should immediately seek the Cupbearer. If he asks for something difficult, he says "go to the Master of Tongues," for they have the power.' 

So it is in the matter of prayer: it is always directed to the Cause of Causes, but the portions of the 'Stewards' appointed over the heavens provide the holiness and the completion of the Sovereignty <note>Malchut</note> to us for every specific request. As is explained regarding the blessing 'Upon the Righteous,' one should intend for the Sefirah called the **Attribute of Loving-kindness** <note>Chesed</note>, which is the attribute of mercy. And in the blessing 'Against the Slanderers,' one should intend for the Sefirah called **Power** <note>Gevurah</note>, which is the attribute of judgment. 

He was very strict about this. And there is one thing I have: a warning to be careful of the 'dwelling of the Kabbalists,' and it is very good. Afterward, he who brought us into all this—is it not good? For prayer literally requires intention, and He knows its power. This is a straight path... as it is written: 'Cast your burden upon the Lord and He will sustain you; trust in Him and He will act.' 

And so it was that **Rabbi Isaac** said to me in the name of my teacher: 'It is enough for me that the sacrifice [of prayer] be for the One who established the world itself.' I asked him about the matter of Kabbalah, for it is difficult. He said to me: 'Fix yourself in the Five Books [of the Torah] and Wisdom, for I have not received this from the mouth of a wise Kabbalist, nor have I seen it in the compositions on these secrets. Furthermore, even they [the books] only reveal a handbreadth of wisdom while covering many handbreadths. It is easy to err in this matter. Therefore, when I send to you, I will deal with the scroll but not with this specific matter.'"

<meta>This page transitions from the specific structure of Divine Names and prayer levels discussed on page 33 to the broader philosophical and musical harmony of "Service" (Avodah). It explores how human action resonates with the celestial spheres, using the analogy of musical instruments.</meta>

-># Chapter 15 | Section on Service | Chapter 15<-

From the nature of existence, the astronomers <note>original: "חכמי הכוכב" - literally "sages of the stars"</note> have said that there is a "resonance" between two instruments tuned to the same pitch and scale. When one produces a sound, the other is stirred by its voice, for they are lowered into the same frequency. Because there is a shared measure between them, the ear of the listener perceives that the honor of the sound is prepared and awakened by the culture of the first voice. This is what our Sages, of blessed memory, interpreted regarding the verse, "Awake, my glory" <note>Psalms 57:9</note>, for the "Pleasant Singer of Israel" <note>King David</note> was skilled in the **art of music** to achieve this awakening. This principle applies to the construction of the entire universe; it is like the first instrument which has a fixed order and value in all our systems, both upper and lower. Through them, the work of the world’s composition and its action are carried out. Corresponding to them, the "shores of the earth" are arranged like the children of the **Microcosm** <term>Olam HaKatan: "Small World," a philosophical concept where the human being mirrors the structure of the entire universe</term>, which is divine, to receive their influences properly. However, when the small instrument <note>the human being</note> finds peace in its systems, movements, and temperament according to the proper value, and stands upon the secret of truths—beholding it in its totality and its parts—then his soul satisfies them. Then the "shores of the Great World" <note>the Macrocosm/Universe</note> are awakened toward them, drawing near and becoming prepared. For there is a "straightness" required to act, and this causes an effect in such a way that the leadership of the powers is stirred over everything in the most restful way. For so the King established His world: that the entire world, small and large, is bound by a law that connects our smallest parts to the celestial parts. In this way, they aim together to receive the **abundance** <term>Shefa: The divine flow of energy or blessing from the upper worlds to the lower worlds</term> from the Blessed One. This is exactly what the Blessed One said through the prophet: "And it shall come to pass in that day, I will respond, says the Lord, I will respond to the heavens, and they shall respond to the earth; and the earth shall respond to the corn, and the wine, and the oil; and they shall respond to Jezreel" <note>Hosea 2:23-24</note>. He said that the Blessed One is the one who "responds" to our will, to the voice of the small resonance, well-aimed in the way of the "shore." As it is said: "Before they call, I will answer" <note>Isaiah 65:24</note>. He gives the goodness of the heavens, which are the upper and most inclusive guard, through the spreading of the nature of His will. They, in turn, answer the earth, which is second in the sequence, with good intent. The earth then answers the grain, which is the third "shore," and they answer Jezreel, which is the fourth "shore"—the sowers who plant holy things upon His trust. I have answered according to the way mentioned. And behold, I will teach you the general rule in the scripture, for they are the "stars" in the tongue and in the middle, finally in the way of "Truth shall spring out of the earth; and righteousness shall look down from heaven" <note>Psalms 85:12</note>. And how much did our Sages aim for in the Midrash? They said: "Those of the God of my father were not established in my bosom..." In the place where it is written, "I have engraved the heavens and the earth," as it says, "If My covenant be not with day and night..." <note>Jeremiah 33:25</note>. In the place where it is written, "I have engraved the heavens and the earth," as it says, "Thus saith the Lord, who giveth the sun for a light by day..." <note>Jeremiah 31:34</note>. In the place where it is written, "I have engraved the sea," as it says, "When He gave to the sea its boundary" <note>Proverbs 8:29</note>. In the place where it is written, "I have engraved the mountain," as it says, "Who giveth light for His glory." In the place where it is written, "I have engraved the deep," as it says, "When He set a circle upon the face of the deep" <note>Proverbs 8:27</note>—using a "verbal analogy" <note>original: "גזירה שוה" (Gezerah Shavah) - a Rabbinic tool of hermeneutics</note> between "law" (Chok) and "circle" (Chug). Rabbi Levi said in the name of Rabbi Shmuel: In every instance of "dedication" (Chanukkah), it is said: In a place where I did not engrave it upon the straightness of wickedness, it is as written, "Woe unto them that decree unrighteous decrees" <note>Isaiah 10:1</note>. Rabbi Levi gave a parable: To a place of a legion that is praised for its buildings—what did the King do? He tilted a "commander’s line" <note>original: "קוסטרלוכא" (Castellatio?) - likely referring to a surveyor's tool or a military plan</note> in it for its instruction. So said the Holy One, Blessed be He: The Torah is called **Stone** <note>original: "אבן" (Even)</note>, and the Evil Inclination is called **Stone**. The Torah is called stone, as it says, "the tables of stone, and the law and the commandment" <note>Exodus 24:12</note>. The Evil Inclination is called stone, as it is written, "And I will take away the heart of stone out of your flesh" <note>Ezekiel 36:26</note>. Let the "stone" <note>Torah</note> come and instruct the "stone" <note>the heart/inclination</note>. Rabbi Isaac said: Everything written was to rebuke man; the world is vanity, for it is written, "And the pit shall be destruction..." Everyone who occupies himself with the Torah, which is the **Tree of Life**, for it is said: "She is a tree of life." This is the "shore" upon the power of what we have said, which is the "fixed order." Know that every "shore" of the celestial systems and their parts, in their totality and their form, is according to the **Divine Torah**, by which the world was contemplated and completed, as I wrote in the first Gate.

<column-break/>

This is for the secret of the traditions <note>original: "קבלות" (Kabbalot)</note>, as I have written, for grace and the attainment of **Service** <note>original: "עבודה" (Avodah)</note> are for him. When one labors properly, even if he does not intend it for himself, honor will ultimately come, and grace will be like blessings upon our heads. For the King’s will is in the nature of the Service according to the "straight way," as will be explained. This is what is meant by "And you shall serve the Lord your God" <note>Exodus 23:25</note>. One who serves for the ultimate purpose—and this is what we mentioned—it does not bypass us. I say that from the Service, the intention is that the Blessed One will be the Great Abundance, and from Him, the blessing spreads to all existing things, to all their generalities. Since the abundance coming from the Source is the "Upper Sustenance," it draws one to gather it. Because this is the essence of existence, it was clarified that the sustenance—which is awakened above by the awakening of the servant's service below—is the ultimate goal. And because the beginning of the Great Name is in His glory, He removes and casts away everything that is "kindness," and extinguishes every plague and every disease through the nature of the Decree, which is "I will take away sickness from the midst of thee" <note>Exodus 23:25</note>. For doing good in the eyes of the Lord—which is the **Unification** <term>Yichud: The meditative act of unifying the different aspects of the Divine</term>—burns away the spirit of impurity above so that it does not enter the Sanctuary. In this way, there is no impurity in the Sanctuary, and every evil that was drawn from it is also clarified below from the "Sodomites" <note>meaning those who disrupt the unity</note> through the Unification. And because bereavement and barrenness are also drawn from that <note>evil side</note>, he said that through this Service, the abundance will protect and prevent this. This is what is meant by "There shall nothing cast their young, nor be barren, in thy land" <note>Exodus 23:26</note>. And because the year naturally consumes from its beginning and upon the flesh—for this reason, all flesh is called "grace"—and it extinguishes days and completes years and their cycles, for it is the essence of death. He said: "the number of thy days I will fulfill" <note>Exodus 23:26</note>. And he said that the completion of one's days is through sustenance, as it says, "Honor thy father..." and as it is written, "there shall nothing cast their young, nor be barren, in thy land; the number of thy days I will fulfill." What did the pious one intend by providing the attainment and the drawing of Service? As he said, "I will send My terror before thee..." and "I will deliver all thine enemies..." and "I will send the hornet..." <note>Exodus 23:27-28</note>. For in the performance of the **Upper Offering**, the powers of the "intellects" above are brought, and they also flow downward; they shall not depart from you, for this was the intention in their creation. To this was added the aspect of the land and the distancing of nothingness, as he said: "And I will set thy bounds..." <note>Exodus 23:31</note> and "I will deliver them into your hand." For the land that was prepared for those who labor and merit is the place of the Service; it was intended to correspond to the Upper "Land of Life." With the removal of the obstacle and the burden, the resting upon the Service will also be blessed. These are the good things, not in every matter. Therefore, perform the Service! For from the Service, in the way that has been explained, all their plagues are struck down, for it was the interruption that prevented the Source from which all perfections flow. All this is from the nature of the true Service, as I have written. Indeed, how can it be conceived that it is as I wrote—that the awakening of the "Awakener" below through our Service in the way explained awakens the upper generalities above? What is the similarity between us and the Upper Births, such that because of it, they say that when these upper attributes move, the "shores" of the voice also move toward Him, and He hears and acts for him? This will be explained according to what I say. Before this matter is explained intellectually, I will first acknowledge what the sage **Rabbi Isaac Arama**, of blessed memory, wrote in his work **Akedat Yitzhak** <note>The "Binding of Isaac," a famous 15th-century philosophical-homiletical commentary on the Torah</note>, in the portion of *Bo*, in the first chapter on the "Foundation of the World." He said in these words: A established and accepted foundation for the belief of the intellect—and its taste belongs to the elders whom our holy Torah and perfections lead in her way—is that there is a great day and a strong tradition. For between the actions which groups of people perform, whether good or evil, and the accustomed nature of the world in its generalities and details, there is a link. For it is said that their actions generally affect the existence and strengthening of the nature of all beings. Their reception and their effect can be established or ruined by them. This matter which we behold necessitates that the "Numerical Trust" <note>calculable certainty</note> is like the construction of the universal chariot. There, he called this a "Great World" and this a "Small World" <note>Macrocosm and Microcosm</note>. Because he places them in all their love, their generalities and their details, as is drawn from all the sages, it is appropriate that a great relationship be found between the two.

For the secret of the **Infinite** <term>Ein Sof: The Boundless or Infinite aspect of God</term> stands for it and others from the endurance, without the worshiper intending it for himself.

### Chapter 16
**Regarding the nature of service to the Unique Name with Intention**

That which we have paved and jumped through regarding the needs of the commandments is to reach the **Source** and to draw out the outcomes of blessing from the "Will" that clings until its end. From this, it spreads to all the causing places through their service. For when the Great Name is blessed, the constant worshiper brings blessing into his service. This is what our Sages, peace be upon them, hinted at when they said, "He who is blessed shall be blessed by the God of Truth" <note>original: "Elohei Amen"</note>. This is to say that the power of the one being blessed is in the goodness of the blessing before its end.

For the one who serves with the **Proper Intention** <term>Kavannah: Directed heart-centered focus during prayer or a commandment</term> is the one who yearns for the Name in his intention, and ultimately gives grace and kindness through the secret of "In God we shall do valiantly" <note>Psalms 60:14</note> and the secret of "Ascribe strength to God" <note>Psalms 68:35; a central Kabbalistic concept suggesting that human worship "empowers" the divine flow into the world</note>. In the chapter *Elu Ne'emarin* <note>Tractate Sotah</note>, Rabbi Isaac ben Levi said: "Anyone who blesses is blessed, and a priest who blesses is blessed," as it is said, "I will bless those who bless you" <note>Genesis 12:3</note>. The explanation is that the **Priestly Blessing** causes blessing in the upper worlds, and from there it spreads to those who are initiated in the secret of "Thus <note>Hebrew: Koh</note> shall you bless." This means they draw the blessing to the word "Koh" <note>a name often associated with the Shekhinah</note> by its nature, so that Israel shall be blessed by their blessings. And this is why it says "And I shall bless them," meaning the Priests will rectify the scriptural "And My Name is upon them," to rectify their blessing so that those above and below are blessed.

They do this according to the blessing, to cause the "Causes" to dwell. It is written, "Those who bless you are blessed," and "Your blessing is upon those who bless you." And in the Midrash on Ruth, on the verse "And behold, Boaz came from Bethlehem," they greeted him with the Name and his holiness, saying to the reapers, "The Lord be with you." The reapers answered him with a "supplement of praise" from the Source of Life. They explained that the **awakening** that rises from the worshiper draws blessings to the "Head of the Righteous" <note>the sefirah of Yesod</note>, and ultimately he intends for him a "supplement" in the secret of "Ascribe strength to God." This is the "Prepared Righteous One" in the secret of "The God of Israel is He who gives strength and power to the people." Through this, his boundaries are expanded. This is part of the "Service of the Gift," the service proper to Him. Regarding this secret, it is said, "And you shall serve the Lord your God," and this service is his existence in intention, as it says, "And He shall bless your bread and your water." This is the "luck" that God allows to bring the person into the Garden of Eden "to serve it and to guard it." The intention is that they should be called by it, and it gives him strength and supplemental growth from the world of joy.

"And I will dwell in the midst of the children of Israel and I will be their God." This sacrifice is called an **Olah** <term>Olah: Literally "that which ascends"; the Burnt Offering</term> because the intention in it is that the **Assembly of Israel** <note>Knesset Yisrael</note> shall ascend to the place of its high priesthood, which is its complete existence. All their intention was so that they would worship with the proper intention and order that we have written here. This is the **Opening of the Gates** to draw the flow of blessing above, the cause of the dwelling of the Great Name within His powers until the Infinite. This is the secret of "doing good for those who do His Name." They also draw down the blessings that are according to His will, performing His will just as He performs the will that is upon Him, without intending for oneself. For glory and goodness come of their own accord to those who perform the Torah for its own sake <note>L'shma</note>, for the nature of service in this way necessitates it.

As they said in the Midrash Yelamdenu <note>Midrash Tanhuma</note> on the portion of Pinhas: Rabbi Judah bar Rabbi Simon said, "No man ever spent the night in Jerusalem with a sin in his hand." How so? The morning sacrifice atoned for the sins of the night, and the afternoon sacrifice atoned for the sins of the day. Thus, no man stayed in Jerusalem with a sin in his hand, for "Righteousness lodged within it." And in the Midrash Hazita, Rabbi Judah bar Rabbi Simon said: Israel offered two daily sacrifices every day, one in the morning and one in the afternoon. The morning one was for sins done at night, and the afternoon one was for sins done during the day. Until there was no man in Jerusalem with a sin in his hand. Rabbi Judah did not mean anything else by saying "The morning one was offered etc." except that the acceptance of the daily sacrifices and the obligation...

...with strength <note>Hebrew: *Gevurah*; one of the ten divine emanations representing severity or judgment</note> and I found in the guarding and melting <note>original: "ומסס ככ"ס", likely a shorthand for "melting like wax"</note> and as wax melts, and melting in its laws and revelations of the aspect of all the generalities. And they are all included in every refuge and hiding place within the 613 commandments <note>original: "תריג מכות"; the 613 mitzvot or divine decrees</note>. And they all relate to those commandments. Through this path, one of them will exist and be sustained for a high existence—meaning, as a likeness. This is the secret of "It is a time to act for the Lord" <note>original: "עת לעשות ל"י"; Psalm 119:126, often interpreted as a call for spiritual action</note>. The structure of the Torah in its totality is like the structure of the **Primordial Man** <term>Adam Ha-Elyon: A Kabbalistic concept of the divine structure that serves as a blueprint for both the universe and the human body</term>. Its closure <note>referring to its internal logic</note> is that there are 248 positive commandments <note>original: "רמ"ח מצות עשה"</note> and 365 negative commandments <note>original: "שס"ה מצות לא תעשה"</note> in the Torah. They correspond to the high structure: 248 limbs <note>original: "איברים"</note>, which is the Great Name expanded into 246 letters <note>original: "רמ"ו חותיות"</note> and their combinations with the first letters of the alphabet, totaling 248. These are the 248 limbs in the Primordial Man.

In its revelation, it is a matter of the general lights from the side of the 365 negative commandments. Therefore, for whoever sins against them, there are 365 veins <note>original: "גידין"</note> in the high realm, and corresponding to the 613 [commandments], these are set against those. The structure of the lower sanctuary <note>referring to the human being or the Tabernacle</note>, which is made of flesh and blood for the rectification of the Glory, has 248 limbs and 365 veins. Thus, they are constructed and directed between the worlds. The structure of the lower sanctuary is like the structure of the upper sanctuary. 

Since the intention in these is the rectification of the Glory alone, the commandments and the orderings are arranged from the high order to complete this. If it were not for this name, the hiddenness and the likeness with the Glory—which is one and rectified through them—would not be. He shall be rectified, but his beauty will not be elevated in the rectification that is the "all," and the "all" within him. The Glory will not be aroused except by the arousal of everything that is with him and there, in a likeness in visions. Because this is there, a likeness with their foundation, and then it is connected and relates between them and from the heavens. 

After these things and the visions of space, I say that after we have seen the High Wisdom to rectify the lower likeness in the form of the High Likeness—as the Sages of Truth <note>Kabbalists</note> received in the "Section of Man" from the hidden parts of the **Chapters of the Chariot** <term>Pirkei Ha-Merkavah: Early Jewish mystical texts focused on visions of the Divine Throne</term>, and as was explained in the first part of this book—from this, the Sanctuary, His dwelling place, will be understood as a likeness of the structure of the Primordial Man.

It will then be explained what this likeness is, and its similarity with the High Likeness, which was made according to its pattern and likeness. It relates to it, and is prepared. For when this likeness moves in its actions, the High Likeness also moves and is sanctified, and flows and passes toward it. Thus, an arousal is awakened in it from the arousal awakened below through our service. In the way that has been explained, the high kings will be aroused above. For the Torah and the commandments are from the Wisdom, being placed in these structures, part after part in its completion. When they are linked to the source of the Torah and the high light, there will be an opening to open the source, which is its nature, through the completion of actions in perfection. 

The form of the rectification by the lower perfection, which is included in the upper likeness according to the measure of the structures, is rectified one with the other—as was explained above. From this comes the nature of Service for the sake of the Name for which we hope, which is the Unification <note>Hebrew: *Yichud*</note> alone: to open the high source and to draw from it the pools of blessing unto the end of Thought, and what spreads from there to the revealed lower realms. These, too, do not intend for themselves, for it is the High Will to be satisfied through that service.

From what we have explained, it will be clarified that these structures have a "secret of the thread" <note>original: "סוד החוט"</note>, which the Sages of the Loom <note>likely referring to expert mystics</note> say is found in it. It is like two vessels, or like two pieces of wood <note>original: "עץ" translated here as wood/pieces</note> in one manner, and one has a secret to move it. When the sound of the speaker reaches one, the sound of its counterpart in the second vessel is aroused, because there is a secret of a thread between them. So it is with the thread itself in these structures: even when the lower line is moved, the upper line will be aroused by the letters of the Torah and the intentions. This is the cause of their existence, the secret between them. For the perfect speaker brings his words to the high things, and they are heard and pass to him. A commandment is delighted in its arrival to them, as is explained in the literal visions of the spiritual likeness. They are active from wisdom, and in their totality are called by the Name of God <note>original: "אל"יי"</note>, and His light is now. And as our Sages of blessed memory said: "I rule over man," and "Who is this to him..."

All this is from the aspect of the "secret of the thread" and the connection that exists between them. Therefore, the Upper ones will hear and answer the Lower ones.

This is what he said, and in his words, it relates to the structures. In the whole verse, it is said "I will respond, says the Lord, I will respond." It should have said, "And it shall come to pass on that day, says the Lord, I will respond to the heavens," etc. But it comes to hint that the arousal of the world comes from this lower likeness, which arouses the High one and opens the Source. Then the High paths are blessed. This is hinted at in the first "I will respond," saying that the source of existence responds to the calling—that the arousal of the world begins from below, and from there the flow and the light come to the high heavens, which is His Great Name.

Regarding all this, he calls to us the rest of the visions of blessing in a proper and straight path until the end. This is what he said: "And they shall respond to the earth, and the earth shall respond..."

From their source, the Great Name in its powers. For without this, there is no place for the flow and the blessing at all. After that, the blessing spreads to the lower beings, as it says: "And the earth shall respond, etc." And this is the secret of "And the earth shall sprout." "And they shall respond to Jezreel" <note>original: "יזרעאל"; literally 'God will sow'</note>—call them Jezreel after those who arouse, for they cause the unification <note>Yichud</note> by what they "sow." If they did not elevate [their deeds] above through their good movements, which are the commandments—which is what we said regarding the arousal of the High Likeness by the call of the lower one, as I wrote above.

And they said in the Midrash: Rabbi Pinchas HaKohen said, "The Holy One, blessed be He, is called 'The One who Sows' <note>original: "זרוע"</note>, for He sows the deeds of the righteous upon Him, and He produces fruit." And he said, "He shall live," for strangers will not inherit them, as was the case in the time when they were in "Hiding of the Face" <note>original: "בהסתר פנים"; a state of divine withdrawal or suffering</note>.

All this is the secret of the perfection and the drawing of the thread of arousal that returns the world from the side of the lower perfection. For the Torah and the commandments are the middle [path] that connects the lower likeness with the upper one, because of the relationship it has with both of them—as will be explained above, in all its aspects, its head, its middle, and its service.

## Chapter 17
### The Service

The fear that service is for a High Purpose <note>original: "לצורך גבוה"; a Kabbalistic concept suggesting that human actions affect the Divine realm</note> and not only for the need of a common person has already been explained. For there is an end to the portion, and an end, and honor, and the understanding of the Torah and its commandments. That which your tradition mandates for the chosen time and for piety—these actions are enduring. The one who is forced <note>or "compelled by devotion"</note> considers it a constant acquisition, reciting its obligations and using your exceptional knowledge to perform them and double their requirements. Understand that this matter is our goal and our direction. Those who serve uprightly are the place, the boundary, and the existence of every celestial being. Through them, the vessel is prepared to pour out the overflow <term>Shefa: The divine energy or "flow" that sustains all existence</term> and the blessing. This is because the "Shells" <note>original: "הקלפות" (Kelipot); the forces of impurity or spiritual barriers</note> and the specific "Fifth" <note>likely referring to a specific level of the soul or cosmos</note> are sufficient for every lack. For this reason, man was created so that the Blessed One’s connection would not be interrupted for Himself, and certainly not for others. For if there were no blessing in the vessel, it would be dependent on others; how much more so in this specific case, where it would interrupt itself and others. Therefore, the direction of the preparation and their intention was toward the "Sacrifices" <note>original: "קרבניות"</note>, which is the place of existence. Without it, no being could be found, and after being found, its existence would be impossible except through it, for it is the vessel to pour the blessing into all the worlds. This was also explained in the first part.

The third aspect of the intention: that one should intend in all of their service that it ascends to the High One—meaning, for a High Purpose—and there is nothing in it for oneself or for one's own benefit at all. Even though the servant must prepare in their service the unification of the Great Name <note>original: "ויחוד השם הגדול"; the meditative act of unifying divine attributes</note> in His glory, for this is the ultimate goal mentioned above—that service is for a High Purpose. In addition to this, the entire intention must be for that unification alone, to bless Him and nothing else. This was already explained at the end of the fifth part.

The fourth: for the souls of the upper species are made in the likeness of the whole, and our intention is directed toward the likeness of the **Upper Chariot** <term>Merkavah: The "Divine Chariot" or throne, representing the structure of the divine emanations</term> and the firmament. As explained in chapters 18 and 19 of the first part, "Let us make man" <note>Genesis 1:26</note> was done in our world in our likeness. It has already been explained that this suggests the arousal of the unification of the High One, so that there would be power and capacity in man's hand to descend and repair the Upper Glory. For this reason, he was made in His likeness. Included in this is everything contained within the Upper Likeness, as it is said: "Everyone who is called by My name, I have created him for My glory, I have formed him, yes, I have made him" <note>Isaiah 43:7</note>. This would not have been possible if his body had not been made and repaired as a sort of reflection of the world that was created with the perfection of the likeness. Since all beings originate from the "End" <note>referring to the physical manifestation</note>, the entire intention is that through him, action and mercy and the existence of all beings are achieved. Because this happens by chance and by force, it is necessary to raise the structure of Man to the place of **Emanation** <term>Atziluth: The highest of the four worlds in Kabbalah, where the divine light is most pure</term> and Unification. There, he has a portion of the "Good Emanation" and the Kingdom <note>original: "מלכות" (Malkhut)</note>, which is not the case for any other created thing that lacks this source. Since the purpose of creating Man was for a High Purpose—to repair the perfection—he was therefore made in His likeness. And since this purpose was not for the sake of [lower] beings, there is no grievance against him, even in his power. The reason for this matter is in its secret: for the one who unifies and brings peace has the power in his hand to arouse through his actions the thing that is of his kind and likeness. For this reason he was made: to prepare that which he is. The thing that he arouses through his actions must be unique and unified, to be the source of the overflow, the blessing, and all goodness and perfection, for this is the nature of Divinity. If he had not been created in this likeness, but only in the likeness of the general world, there would be no peace or path for all this, and the intention of his creation would not be fulfilled. Therefore, the Upper Wisdom saw fit to prepare him in the "Repair of Glory." Through this, the intention for him ascends as being for a High Purpose; he is the repair of the glory of "All Living" <note>original: "כל חי"</note> from the root of the whole, and from the repair of the upper and lower realms. As explained in chapter 17 of the first part, from this follows the overflow and the existence of all beings, for they are dependent on the repair of Man. Therefore, he finishes and mentions that he should be in a likeness similar to the existence of the High One, and not just like the general world.

The fifth: for the [service] <note>OCR reads "קערה" (bowl), likely a typo for "עבודה" (service)</note> in its entirety, with its 613 commandments, depends on intention. That is to say, it is included in all **Ten Sefirot** <term>Sefirot: The ten attributes or emanations through which the Divine interacts with the universe</term> which are Divinity. It is like the "Chariot of the Soul" in the plan of the Creator. Action is in the deed of the sinner, and in the ten there are thoughts that depend on and sustain the "Crown" <note>original: "כתר" (Keter)</note>, and some in "Wisdom" <note>original: "חכמה" (Chokhmah)</note>, and some in "Understanding" <note>original: "בינה" (Binah)</note>, and some in "Kindness" <note>original: "חסד" (Chesed)</note>, and some in...

<column-break/>

## Chapter 15
### Section

The first: a contemplation upon it, its structure, and its preparation. They are carved upon the orders of the world, for he is the "Great Vessel" of the entire ladder, which is the "Small World" <term>Microcosm: The idea that the human being is a miniature version of the entire universe</term>. Within it, in its place, His excellence is above it. Therefore, His commands and when He wrote the Divine Torah by the hand of Moses... with the "Crown" <note>Keter</note>, it was invalidated there... that the correct way in this and the order of his service is to repair within it the natural decay of his heart’s creation. For by nature, he is mired in selfish interests. But by the decree of the Father, he will not judge his brother harshly, to soften and break the hardness of his heart so he does not receive [sin?], and does not descend... in the writing of the rest of the Tablets... in every **Sefirah**, and not on the day of His sanctification. "And now, if you will diligently obey..." etc., "you shall be My own treasure..." etc. <note>Exodus 19:5</note>. For by a person repairing himself, he is found through his own perfection. And if he puts aside the orders of the world which are general, such as water and earth—which are the first row—and the later ones are the second row, and he is the third row and the fourth row, which is the repair of the... Kingdom <note>Malkhut</note>... and those who order the rows shall be directed in service and be acted upon by them. They all stand at their watch, and their intention is in the Name... and if they rebel against their order... it was within the powers of man in the way most suitable for him... the Divine Torah is over the worlds. Therefore He said, "If you walk in My statutes..." etc., "and keep My commandments..." etc. <note>Leviticus 26:3</note>. All this is in being a substitute for the Name... "You shall serve the service of God" <note>Exodus 23:25</note> as the chosen of nations, because the matter depends only on the dedication to the Name... to place these vessels. As will be explained in the order of the 70 [nations?] with the help of God. Therefore, when man sins, he diminishes [the flow]. He is called the **Tzaddik, Foundation of the World** <note>original: "צדיק יסוד עולם"; a concept from Proverbs 10:25 meaning the righteous person sustains existence</note>, being the guardian of the order and law of all these matters in their proper form. So I have written: the King is accepted in His ways... the hand of the thoughts, and he will count them. These are his words, of blessed memory—this is the end of the matter.

It was clarified that even if all of them are in a prepared structure like a High King, who would decree for Him and who would listen to Him? And to believe that there is a connection between the merciful actions and the nature of the Kingdom <note>Malkhut</note>, until through its repair it is established and strengthened, and conversely, it falters and is corrupted. The general explanation: it does not establish that the hosts of our actions should answer, and be aroused to fear, to act out of goodness. What is the thing that divides the hearts? For when they agree together and intend to receive the overflow from the Believer, may He be blessed, this and that have the power to arouse Him and bless Him. And there is no proof from the scripture... and there is nothing in existence where the dependency of the overflow and blessing is from the side of agreement and intention together. The end of a vessel of clay—its thought is not a matter for testing. For a vessel of clay that moves, the intention and the value is... all the vessel of its power is full... there is power if there is will... which the secret of the source corrupts and we arouse... not the God who was created... by the names given to it, the form and value are arranged in goodness for all to be filled by them... the division and desecration... Therefore he said that when the lower structure is aroused, then the Upper One will serve, because the existence of [the flow] is not truly possible [otherwise].

And what he said, that thus the King of the Universe established His kingdom—that the entire world, small and great, should be as living, he said... and its parts in service... it is not known from where he got this, and for this they were afraid... But the scholars of the wisdom of humility <note>likely referring to Kabbalists</note> [placed] the structure of man above the celestial spheres <margin>Midrash</margin> and the angels, and from his holiness in the section of the "Chapters of the Upper Chariot." And there also in our understanding... for it is on a shaky foundation. And the Midrash he brought... what he said, the "arousal of the lower beings" and hearing one another—the summary of the matter is the principle of speech. Therefore, he raised the understanding of all that interrupts... to prove under the authority of the explanation what is above him. And if it falls under the language of the general rule... as I wrote here so that it would be directed toward the truth of what will be explained regarding this great matter in the chapter [to come], with the help of God.

# Part on Divine Service: Chapter 17

**To serve** His service entirely, and so on. A further difficulty arises regarding his <note>Maimonides'</note> opinion when he divides the matter: it is understood from him that ultimate Good and Pleasure are for the life of the World to Come <note>original: "העוה"ב" (Olam Ha-Ba)</note>, while rest, suffering, and distress are merely obstacles—and this constitutes the delight of their cessation. This is the measure of the general opinion of the Rav <note>Maimonides</note>, of blessed memory, and what the Rabbi <note>Nachmanides</note> in *The Gate of Reward* <note>original: "ספר התגמול" (Sefer Ha-Tigmul, usually referred to as Sha'ar Ha-Gemul)</note> saw fit to respond to it.

For the opinion on "The Good" according to the Ramban, of blessed memory, is that ultimate good and evil are not merely a matter of receiving "good" as a reward for kindness or "evil" as a punishment for transgression in a physical sense. Rather, it is the act of the Wise One; God cannot be "satisfied" or "dissatisfied" by human actions such that they would add to or subtract from Him. However, the reward of the entire world and their punishment in this world is all ultimately found in the "End of Days." These are two distinct inquiries aside from the common custom of the world: the general reward and punishment among nations, and the specific reward for individuals.

The path of awakening the elements in this world—and the selection of the unique entry into the world of souls—these are wonders. In opposition to the spheres <note>the celestial bodies</note> and the existence of the miracle, when one weighs the parts, it is a proper thing in the governance of those who always look toward the portions given to them to aid society. This is true if the "Good" is completed upon the soul, as is written in the portion of *Acharei Mot* regarding the matter of "Excision" <term>Karet: a spiritual punishment where the soul is "cut off" from its divine source</term>. This provides great confidence in the endurance of souls after death and in the granting of reward in the "World of Souls."

The conclusion from his words there is that because immortality is a necessary consequence for the soul—since it has no causes for destruction—it should be, in our eyes, an indestructible law. Even if it were not to have life <note>the active reward of the afterlife</note>, what he wrote is that the merits of the one receiving reward sustain the whole; for this is a natural necessity. Therefore, it <note>spiritual reward</note> does not appear explicitly in the Torah. Instead, the "Goods" mentioned are because the physical actions of the body are not the primary path of punishment for the one receiving reward. Regarding the "Goods," he sought to say that the commandments are a service within us. Therefore, the Rav decreed that the reward of the whole Torah is, as it is written, like "Crowns."

Furthermore, the Rav added in his explanation in the section *Im Bechukotai*, speaking of the "Goodness of the Language." We have already chosen the view that all these blessings are heavenly; the arrival of rains, the high value of peace, and protection from enemies are not strictly within the "natural" order. He places fear in their hearts to flee from a sinner because of our sins, and [provides] steadfastness and patience; otherwise, everything would be the opposite: destruction, hunger, and difficult suffering. All of this is the opinion of the Rav, of blessed memory, in *The Gate of Reward*.

It has already been included in *The Service* <note>the name of this book</note> that the Rav was the greatest of believers and a distinguished teacher, even if he denied the Wisdom of Kabbalah <note>original: "חכמת הקבלה"</note>, which is the Wisdom of Truth. I, too, wonder at his path—that the promises of the Torah are literal, even though he was great in wisdom. The Sages have already said that Kabbalah <note>here meaning "tradition"</note> is the existence of the grave in nature <note>referring to natural law</note>. This was his intention in his foundations. In his opinion, the promised goods and the traditions in the Torah should not be thought of as the primary intentions at all, nor are they necessitated by the performance of commandments. There is no [natural] link between the performance of the commandments, the heights of peace, and the swiftness of the rains when the land is full, and the eternal, overflowing reward. Rather, the Rav, of blessed memory, sees the existence of all this after the commandments as a miracle; the nature of the whole is not the cause.

However, according to the tradition of the Torah as received by his students, the opposite appears to be true in many places, and this is the Truth: the Higher Beings are blessed through the "awakening of the lower beings" <note>original: "התעוררות התחתונים"; the idea that human actions trigger divine flow</note> through their service. From them, the blessing spreads to the givers. One should not say this is a "miracle" according to the True intention, but rather the "Nature of the Service" necessitates this, as has been and will be explained with God's help. Were it not for the Rav's intention to restrict the ancient Kabbalah to its literal meaning as an answer to the masses of scholars, he would have responded to the disputants and involved himself in his secrets for the sake of the "Chosen Few" who stand in the secret of our God. In the end, the heart is occupied, and knowledge is remembered.

Truly, regarding what the Rav said—that the immortality of the soul is a natural thing in its birth, and for this reason the Torah did not mention spiritual reward—some of the later sages have already challenged him. Among them is the sage Rabbi Joseph Albo in the *Book of Principles* <note>original: "ספר העיקרים" (Sefer Ha-Ikkarim)</note>, Fourth Treatise, Chapter 29. He wrote about it in this language: "This too is a divine matter, for is there any immortality more natural to the soul of a person who is purified than that which the Torah said: <meta>catchword: Behold I have set</meta>

<column-break/>

**before you** today life and good..." and so on, as explained regarding "Life." He said that if the remnant of the soul is something famous and known, why does the Torah not mention it as it mentions the life of the kingdoms of the world? Especially among the blessings and the physical curses with which the Torah is filled.

Furthermore, according to the opinion of those who say that spiritual reward is for the soul alone, since it is not a "natural" thing for the soul to be sustained forever, it would be proper for the Torah to tell us this according to reason. The Rav <note>Maimonides</note>, of blessed memory, would nullify his own argument by what he wrote elsewhere, saying that occurrences in the world are natural. This would be a contradiction in his part, for he promised physical, elemental rewards to man throughout the Torah, which are also natural and necessitated by nature. For a "type of nature" exists at the time of receiving [the Torah], as was explained in the previous chapter and will be further explained with God's help. The Rav pursues this. And as I wrote above, there is no doubt that the "Good" of the soul's service is compared in its quality to the body, by virtue of its attachment to its Source, its good deeds, and its service to its God, creating a Unity.

It is said that these promised "Goods" that result from the performance of the Torah and the commandments are like the example written there: that they will arrive and return to the one who serves in a constant state, in the place where he was previously a transgressor. The soul is left connected to the body so that its immortality and the punishment following the Torah and its commandments—which are their cause—will be realized. And even if the one receiving the reward was that Cohen <note>priest</note> who was warned physically, he says this should be considered a consequence of the commandments and the steadiness resulting from them in nature.

From now on, one cannot refute the Rav from the perspective of the senses; for it was necessary to mention them in our days to bring them toward the spiritual reward, distinguishing them from the physical at the end. We do not mention it because the spiritual is more concealed. For we have mentioned our opinion that the spiritual is the cause, and in the end, it will be arranged. He further questioned there, saying: "What is most difficult in all this is that he said the spiritual promises were not mentioned because of the physical promises, which are not the essence of the reward at all."

And regarding what he said—that according to those who say spiritual reward is for the soul, and since it is not natural for the soul to endure, etc.—this is the opinion of the Rav, of blessed memory, and it is the Truth. Such was the intention in the creation of the first man (Adam), were it not that it is truly "Truth of Truths" that in the future the world will return to its original state. Therefore, the dead will endure in the end, for the nature returns to its place. Thus, there is no need to mention it. Furthermore, aside from this, according to the Rabbi, he <note>Maimonides</note> did not believe this because the philosophers distanced themselves from it, and he was forced to believe in a God who changes for the sake of the Truth, as a stabilizer for the followers of philosophy after the source of their knowledge, aiming for the Higher Will.

And what Rabbi Joseph ben Shem Tov, of blessed memory, wrote in the book *The Eye of the Reader* <note>original: "עין הקורא" (Ein Ha-Kore)</note>, Treatise Four, in this language: "Divine labor for our Rav <note>Maimonides</note>, of blessed memory, in all that they wrote and exerted themselves on his behalf. He understands and knows that the existence of spiritual perfection following the Torah's commandments is because the soul, by nature, will not reach annihilation upon the departure of the body, for she is the one who excels in it. Rather, she is counted in it through a bond of existence, not in a way that is fitting, for by nature she is in labor for pleasures and food. He, of blessed memory, did not restrain even the fact that remaining in punishment follows the commandments in his opinion, even though she is sealed in herself, and the damages to perfection occur when the commandments are not performed naturally, according to the words of the Sages. This is explained from all of this."

I have already written above that the Rav, of blessed memory, knew the "Matter of the Service"—that the gaze toward the Truth of perfection is directed at the body, and certainly that wisdom is the essence of the Service. This will be explained in Chapter 17 regarding the hidden things: that the existence of spiritual perfection through the Torah's commandments is like her nature. And even if it is not a "natural intellect" of the fathers, it is a "natural intellect" of these [souls], and he is distinguished from the higher group.

This is the measure of the Rav's general opinion in this matter, along with what is proper to respond to it and to argue on his behalf: that the opinion of the philosophers, according to the Rav, is like a... <meta>catchword: to (distinguish)</meta>

# Part on Divine Service: Chapter 10

<column-break/>

# Chapter 10

In this selection, the speculation of the intellect and the voice of blessing are as follows in this chapter:

### Chapter 10

The power of contemplation will realize that the teacher <note>likely referring to Moses or the Torah itself</note> illuminates this, his writing, and clarifies for him that this Torah is a source of strength before the children of Israel. It serves as a protective covering for the foolish and the simple against all types of harms and pitfalls for those who fulfill it, preventing them from straying from the sacred service. I have seen fit to examine, clarify, and include the physical depictions <note>descriptions of physical rewards like rain and harvest</note> that were included in the Torah, and to analyze the contemplation which is the remedy for lack, and to remove the complaints of those who argue that the Torah did not explicitly mention the ultimate spiritual rewards—which are the life of the World to Come <note>original: "חיי העולם הבא" (Chayei Ha-Olam Ha-Ba)</note>. In fact, many have stumbled over this and have written much on this wisdom. I would like to explain why these were not explicitly mentioned in the Torah, except in a minor way, and why they were omitted from the masses. However, to precede my own words, I will present what is commonly known regarding this, which is generally divided into three opinions.

The first opinion is the view of the Rambam <note>Rabbi Moses ben Maimonides, 1138–1204, a preeminent medieval Sephardic Jewish philosopher</note>, may his memory be a blessing. He said regarding this reason that because the Torah was intended to be given to a large nation and a multitude, its initial arrival presents matters in a way they can grasp and accept. The Torah aimed to ease them into physical matters before moving to lofty matters, so they would be able to bear and receive them. This is similar to the argument of the Sages, of blessed memory, that "the Torah speaks in the language of human beings." Since a person’s life and time are physical, they would not initially grasp the levels of the intellect and its supreme loftiness. Therefore, the Torah concealed these from them and revealed to them what they would long for—those physical successes in the future. This was his opinion, may his memory be a blessing. 

However, later scholars, may their memory be a blessing, have already come and challenged this, establishing for themselves a different path. For the Rambam said that the physical promises are fulfilled and hint at the foundation of the spiritual reward <note>original: "הגמול הרוחני" (Ha-Gemul Ha-Ruchani)</note>, for how could a person take life from that which is not explicitly mentioned in the world? If the good is hidden and not mentioned at all, how could they strive for it? Furthermore, they pointed out that since the foundations of the soul are deep within the unity of God and our own unity, these are matters the masses cannot grasp. If the masses cannot grasp anything but the physical and the simple, how can they grasp other non-physical things? There is no doubt in this: they cannot grasp the spiritual reward just as they cannot grasp the existence of a spiritual entity.

And regarding the matter of physical rewards, there is the explanation found in the *Sefer Ikkarim* <note>original: "ספר העיקרים" (The Book of Principles) by Joseph Albo, c. 1380–1444</note>. It says that the Torah promised us these physical rewards to say that if we perform the commandments with joy, sincerity of soul, and wisdom, God will remove from us all things that prevent us from performing them—such as illness, war, and famine. Instead, He will increase for us all the good things that assist our hands in performing the Torah—such as abundance, peace, and an increase in silver and gold. This is so that we do not waste our days on the needs of the body, but rather have the free time to study wisdom and perform the commandments so that we may merit the life of the World to Come. According to this path, when we are rewarded with these good things, we are not meant to return to our physical desires, but to use that peace to focus on the Divine. 

Yet, this is not entirely sufficient. For while it explains the path that leads to the goal, the goal itself <note>spiritual salvation</note> is still not mentioned explicitly. We are still not "assured" of it. This would not be the case if the goal itself were mentioned, for then we would be certain of the path leading to it. There is no doubt that the King’s intent is the survival and the ultimate goal of his subjects. If so, he should have included the spiritual reward and explained it at length, rather than leaving us in doubt of attaining it. 

Consider this parable: A king told one of his servants who was small in his eyes to go to a certain place and commanded him to go to a far-off land. There, he was to do the king's work and serve his service. The king would ensure that while he was engaged in his work, he would be safe from hunger and would enjoy his youth. Yet, the servant is still not certain that upon completing the work, the king will return him to the high place and the status he held originally. Only if the king promised to return him would he be certain. The king's provision of food and comfort during the journey is merely to enable the work, not the final reward for the labor itself.

<column-break/>

...His service and His unity, may He be exalted above, and those who do His will and act within these matters and thoughts perform wondrous, glorious, and excellent deeds. This shows that he is wise and discerning. His wisdom and understanding consist of his cleaving <term>Devekut: the meditative state of being "attached" or "glued" to the Divine</term> to the Living God. He shall long for Him, and there is no greater wisdom or understanding than this. For he will see the fruit of this thought and its purpose. This wisdom is not like the sweetness and pleasantness of other types of knowledge and sciences, for all of those are external to the soul and do not benefit or allow their practitioners to "see life."

Regarding the secret of the will of the Creator according to the tradition of the Torah, it is based on everything we have written on this matter. It says: "And you who clung to the Lord your God are all alive today" <note>Deuteronomy 4:4</note>. And it says: "Behold, I have taught you statutes..." and "You shall keep them and do them, for this is your wisdom..." and "For what great nation is there that has God so near to it..." and "What great nation has statutes and judgments so righteous..." <note>quoting Deuteronomy 4:5-8</note>.

First, it states that through the attachment of thought to the powers of the Great Name, one is prepared to "cling to the Lord your God." Because those who are pure and have this relationship and powerful trust—this cleaving—that is the essence of spiritual life. It is the very "death of life" <note>likely meaning the transcendence of physical life</note> within you. 

When it says "Behold, I have taught you statutes," it means you should be confident in what I have told you. For these are the spiritual statutes and judgments through which one lives. These were given to be taught because without prophecy, it is impossible for a person to grasp them at all. Our entire capacity to understand is limited, as we are separated from the "Supreme Thought" which was not granted to us. As I have already mentioned, it is known that the supernal wisdom is the Torah.

It says "to do so in the midst of the land" to teach us that these are to be performed in the physical world, for the Land of Israel is the designated place for the commandments and their service, as that land is a specialized dwelling for Him. "And you shall keep and do them" refers to the fact that they should be cherished, for through them, the cleaving to the Name of Heaven is achieved. 

It says that the performance of the Torah and the wisdom within it are constant; it is the beginning and the completion. This refers to the wisdom <note>original: "חכמה" (Chokhmah)</note>. And the "understanding" <note>original: "בינה" (Binah)</note> is the actual performance. The "attachment" <note>Devekut</note> is that from which your actions will flow—out of love for Him and His staff. It will be "seen as wisdom in the eyes of the nations," for it will be clarified to them through miracles that they cannot logically fathom. They will wonder at the beginning, for the portion of the Lord is His people; God alone guides them and performs wonders, removing every lack and every "Egyptian plague" from you. They will see this and say, "Surely this is a wise people." 

And what is the thing they will wonder at? It is that God is "near" to them. This refers to the miracles that occur regarding their water and their sustenance. When the nations hear that the service consists of keeping commandments—some of which seem to have no logical reason even in their eyes—they might say, "This is not a wise people at all." But because of the miracles they see from Him, which they cannot logically explain, they will be forced to admit that "you have wisdom and understanding" even in the depth of those commandments. This is the "cleaving." It is not known to them through the imagination of their power, but through the perfection of the matter. When you perform the commandments, which are the "Supernal Building," He will act and hear you whenever you call to Him. This is the meaning of "For what great nation is there that has God so near to it." This is the explanation for why it says "this is your wisdom and understanding in the eyes of the nations."

And it says "What great nation..." as a reason for what was said before. That is to say: how could there be another nation that sees God as close to us in every way? All of this is included in the concept of "We will do and we will hear" <note>the Israelites' acceptance of the Torah at Sinai</note>. However, regarding those who are "distant," this does not apply to them at all. They are like those who speak of "distant gods" because there is no power in them, neither to do good nor to do evil. They do not have "righteous statutes and judgments" like this entire Torah. The purpose of these commandments is intellectual perfection, through which all intellectual powers and the hidden wisdom are served. All these wisdoms are found within us in their perfection, and we attain them through the intellect here, being seen as "wise and understanding in the eyes of the nations." And you should believe that the intention...

# Part on Divine Service: Chapter 18
