# Chapter 18

...drawing it out, were it not for all the goodness and virtues, and they became fully obligated to give thanks and gratitude for this. For the "Great Voice" <note>original: "הקול הגדול" (Ha-Kol Ha-Gadol); a reference to the divine voice at Sinai, associated in Kabbalah with the sefirah of Tiferet</note> is what He, may He be blessed, lacked <note>This suggests the "Voice" acts as a vessel for divine expression</note>. And we included within it all the blessings destined to be renewed in every generation, as will be explained in Chapter 23 of Part 3 regarding Sovereignty <note>original: "מלכות" (Malchut); the lowest of the ten sefirot, representing the manifest world</note>. For the order and providence over every single thing does not follow this order except to make known that this reward is drawn forth and necessitated by absolute Grace.

And according to the guidance of the Ramban <note>Rabbi Moses ben Nachman (Nachmanides), 1194–1270</note>, may he rest in peace, so too every word <note>original: "מלף", likely a variant or typo for "מלה" (word) or referring to the letter Aleph</note> is filled with every tongue of meaning and every tongue of words, decreeing decrees and judging judgment, and scattering power like a portion. All the goodness and perfection found in this Torah, and the fulfillment of its commandments, are drawn forth and necessitated by "all"—meaning that its commandments are a "Torah of Grace." For to say they are the key to His voices is to say they are the preparation to inherit the source of all goodness through them, and to be careful because they rectify from that source.

Furthermore, this is in their nature; by the opening of that source through the utterance of speech <note>original: "מלל" (milal)</note>, a flow of light and blessing is drawn forth, showing the establishment of the source upon its body. Through this movement, we are written and graced from there, affecting the laborers, for the nature of the service necessitates this. I have already written that the "Holy Sovereignty" <note>Malchut</note> is like a vessel to pour out the abundance, and by necessity it must be sent. Without it, it is impossible in any way, for everything is according to its word and its power. When one draws near, nature is awakened toward it and descends below. For when it rises with a primary intention, nature is awakened toward you and descends below.

And in the Midrash of the Ramban, may he rest in peace, they said: "The cup of the tongue is in the secret of the Good upon the tongue." It decrees a word from the Good... many voices to flow. And according to the sweetening of the choice, it comes to rest in the heavens, and the majority is covered for miracles... and the word is like a flow at the head of the King, hinting at the precious things of the holy pressure. It sweetens the flow for every tongue, the glory of the King that is prepared within them... according to His attributes, according to His attributes <note>original: "על פי מדותיו" (al pi midotav)</note>... and the crowns of the King are before Him to sit in praise. Come and see: every flow and every generation in this world is the King's vision given to us through those holy hours, which are the brain of the Holy King. And regarding the flow, it is written: "ordered according to His attributes, according to His attributes." And it was all "according to the hand of Aaron and his sons" <note>A reference to Numbers 4:27</note>. Thus, according to His attributes, it descends and flows to all worlds to be connected by the rein of the whole.

And this is the secret of "This is the Good Fruit," standing upon the Voice. And from the power of the lower chariot, they would ascend. These were necessitated—this is the principle of Cain and the redemption. This sign is a structure in the closure and the walls of Cain, for these are the attributes of the whole. Until here <note>original: "ע"כ" (ad kan); marking the end of a quote</note>. Behold, they have explained all that they meant by "Blessed is His Glory." And they said from the "Spoon and the Bowl" <note>original: "ממין וקערת" (mamin u-ke'arat); references to the offerings of the princes in Numbers 7, interpreted here as spiritual vessels</note>—the "Bowl" is the heart's voice of yearning, and the "Spoon" is the written voice within it, as in "And the Lord spoke to my heart." The "Incense" is the perfume offered upon the head. The "Bowl" is the service ascending from below in praise. And through the "Spoons," they are the Voice. From there, joy and light spread to all who intend. Were it not that a word came to them, they would not be able to pray to consume the good. For they truly give sustenance to all worlds in the secret of "The eyes of all look hopefully to You, and You give them their food in its time" <note>Psalm 145:15</note>.

And they said in the Midrash of the Ramban: What is "its time"? "Its time" refers to the Righteous One <note>original: "צדיק" (Tzadik); often referring to the sefirah of Yesod</note>, for His Sovereignty is called "the time of the Righteous." And all its children are anointed from that which is "its time." All the lower ones of tomorrow... and this is what we have established... "And You give them their food in its time," as was established... for through this, everything is covered by "its time," and from here all worlds are blessed... in blessing, then the Name is established above and below. Until here.

And in the Midrash of Rabbi Nehunia ben HaKanah <note>referring to the *Sefer HaBahir*, an early Kabbalistic work</note>, Rabbi Rahumai said: I have seen the righteous and the wholesome, that they were making me wholesome over every action through their merits. And behold, she is blessed with milk, and the Voice provides for it. I have already written this. And the "Great Cause" is through the study of Torah and the fulfillment of commandments. Because she is thus, all the blessings and goodness in the Torah come by way of narrative, and their explanation is by way of the "Foundation of the Whole" <note>original: "יסוד כלל" (Yesod Kelal)</note> included in what I have written. It is in its essence. Conversely, when we abandon the Torah and the commandments, there follow and are necessitated...

<column-break/>

...And because of this "Good," in the opinion that there is a "nature to the service" <note>term: <term>Nature of the Service</term> (teva ha-avodah) — the idea that spiritual actions trigger natural consequences in the divine and physical realms, like a law of physics</note> to give good thus, and to grant good within it, there is no doubt to be pondered. He said, just as Rabbi [so-and-so] said, the reward of the good is not delayed. Why then did he mention the physical promise, when the spiritual promise is the essence of the reward? For the physical reward is not the essence of the reward. Indeed, it was not mentioned as a "promise" at all, but rather to reveal and tell what is necessitated and follows from the nature of the service. All the goodness and perfections are drawn after the commandments by nature—a part of their nature is within them.

This is the revealed way. The Torah opens with this by saying: "If you walk in My statutes, and keep My commandments and do them" <note>Leviticus 26:3</note>. "If you walk in My statutes" refers to one who labors in the Torah. "And keep My commandments" refers to the fulfillment of the mitzvot. "And do them" refers to the "Higher Correction" <note>original: "התקון העליון" (ha-tikkun ha-elyon); the sefirotic alignment</note>, the correction of the Flow that is corrected through the study of Torah and the fulfillment of commandments—a correction that you yourself "make" <note>A wordplay on "do them" (va-asitem), which can be read as "you made them," suggesting man "makes" the divine flow active</note>. After this, all that follows and is necessitated from this is: "I will give you your rains in their season" <note>Leviticus 26:4</note>. This is the "Good" and the completion.

As for the "Fruits and the Curses" intended for pleasure and order, in the Midrash of the Ramban, of blessed memory: "And you shall do them"—it is written "them" <note>original: "אתם" (otam), which can be read as "atem" (you)</note>, as if you made your own rains, to rectify the Holy Name. From here, all those blessings come to the world, and their intention is through them. They were rectified in a fitting manner. Furthermore, "Your rains" includes every single drop. Furthermore, it is a reward for the correction of your work, which is the Holy Name.

It is written: "And they said, the way of the Lord is to do righteousness and justice." Now, since it is written "the way of the Lord," why does it say "to do righteousness and justice"? Rather, it is to prepare the paths of our God; through this, one "makes" righteousness and justice.

And the Kabbalist Rabbi Joseph ben Gikatilla <note>1248–1305, author of *Sha'arei Orah*</note>, of blessed memory, wrote in the book *Sha'arei Orah* (Gates of Light), regarding the attribute of "The Bride" <note>referring to Malchut</note>, in these words: "Know and understand that the sefirah of *Binah* (Understanding) and the sefirah of *Malchut* (Sovereignty) are directed toward one another. When the flow of Sovereignty is rectified through the correction of the Foundation <note>Yesod</note> by the fulfillment of the Torah and the commandments, then the sefirah of *Binah* shines forth to pour out all kinds of abundance and blessing through the channels <note>original: "צנורות" (tzinnorot); the spiritual conduits between sefirot</note>, until the flow of Sovereignty is blessed and filled. Then, all the people of the world are found in peace and joy, and the blessing is distributed into all types of sustenance, and the blessing is filled to seek... and this is the secret of the order of all the blessings: 'If you walk in My statutes,' 'then I will give your rains in their season,' and 'the earth shall yield its produce' throughout the entire passage." Until here.

This is what we have said: the "Correction of the Glory" <note>original: "תקון הכבוד" (tikkun ha-kavod)</note> is achieved through the fulfillment of the Torah and the commandments. The commandments draw forth all those goodnesses mentioned in the passage from that correction. This is not considered a "promise" <note>original: "יעוד" (ye'ud)</note> in the usual sense, for the reward that follows is by the very nature of that thing. It is dependent upon it; there is no place or need for a promise, except to reveal the justice and the narrative—that it is drawn forth and necessitated from that reward by nature. This is the case with the fulfillment of the Torah and the commandments: they are the "Keys" themselves to the source of all goodness, for they are dependent upon them.

In our current reasoning regarding the "opening," it is a preparation. If this action were not in the nature of fulfilling the commandments, we would have said there is no relationship of good or evil between the fulfillment of commandments and those physical goods, and they would not be drawn to them by nature. This is far from the truth of the responses of those who depend on the dregs of the Torah, saying it is better for the wise to be foolish sometimes... but the truth we know regarding the reality of the nature of fulfilling the Torah and commandments is that all those goods are drawn to them. Therefore, what appears in the Torah in this matter is a narrative and a revelation of the subject. For that which is the way of things to draw forth and come by nature—to promise it is permitted, but there is no [absolute] need for it.

From this, we know how much good those who do right cause, and how much harm the corrupt and their sins cause. The King <note>Ramban</note> summarizes all we have said by stating: "He who commits a transgression, let him say 'he shall be sated with bread' <note>likely a paraphrase or specific homily</note>... for the Name is the Master of Grace, providing and arranging the decree. Rain shall grow, and his name and his students will naturally succeed at the beginning. And the laborer shall be sated with bread, for this is drawn and necessitated by the nature of the service and the tradition." And if he abandons it... he did not understand his land...

...for you a vessel to investigate the existence of God and His unity. However, your heart was not fully set on this, but rather on setting us apart to believe generally that there is a "Raven from the Heavens" <note>original: "עורב מן השמים"; likely a metaphorical reference to divine providence or the story of Elijah</note> and He sent for its sake... and as the Rabbi of blessed memory <note>Likely referring to the Ramban or another authority</note> wrote in the sermon "And Your Sign" <note>original: "וסימנכון"</note> regarding the relationship between place and grace, upon which the existence of God and His unity are based, and that it is not a mere chance occurrence. 

The light brings this forth because from You they fled in Egypt <note>A reference to the Exodus</note>, and upon it, several matters were removed that are beyond doubt, in addition to what they received from the Patriarchs. This is part of what we saw fit to mention in this matter, according to what these Sages of blessed memory included and assisted us with in their views. After the introduction to the Covenant, we saw fit to clarify the truth of these two rewards according to the view of the Torah, and according to what the Supreme Wisdom endeavored—of which they speak—to remove a certain stumbling block. I saw fit to establish a chapter on its own regarding the essential reward, which I have already opened to explain its nature... to explain the spiritual reward. And I have mentioned it in the way of truth.

# Chapter 18

We have already established in several places that the nature of **Divine Service** <term>Avodah: specifically referring to the Temple sacrifices and the performance of commandments</term> is the foundation for attaining the **Source** <note>original: "המקור" (Ha-Makor); the divine origin of all flow</note> and for drawing the blessing from the **Head of Thought** <note>original: "ראש המחשבה" (Rosh ha-Machshava); a Kabbalistic term for the highest sefirah, Keter</note> upon the soul, and from what the Sages of blessed memory wrote regarding those who gather together to cause this through **Unifications** <term>Yichudim: Kabbalistic meditative intentions intended to unite divine attributes</term>. 

And in the Midrash of Rabbi Shimon bar Yochai <note>The Zohar</note>, peace be upon him, they said: "And I will exalt Him with all... to let Israel know why they bring a sacrifice." They further said there: "The Lord is near to all who call upon Him" <note>Psalm 145:18</note>. What does "in truth" mean? We have established that it is to let Israel know how holy and fitting the sacrifice is, and not just in the presence of the opening. And who lets Israel know that the Holy God is within Himself? As it is written: "And who is like Your people Israel, one nation on earth?" <note>2 Samuel 7:23</note>. On this we established: anyone who does not know the Holy Name properly, his service is not considered service, for it is all separate from him. **Higher Service** is the unification of the desire so that the upper and lower beings may be blessed through it. 

This matter is repeated in the Midrash of Rabbi Shimon bar Yochai in many places. The intention in all this is to teach us what we have already summarized many times: that the study of Torah and the fulfillment of its commandments draw the **Light** and the flow of **Blessing** from the Source of Life to the upper and lower worlds. This is the cause of all good in the physical portion, for the flow causes this. For the Torah is the **Great Name** and its essence. In the Midrash of Rabbi Shimon bar Yochai, we learned: "The Torah is called a Rainbow" <note>original: "קשת" (Keshet)</note>, and "There is no water but Torah." The Great Rainbow is the source of all goodness and portions, for it is the absolute Rainbow itself. It is fitting that the Torah, which is the actual Rainbow, should draw to it all that is near; for by this, it testifies to its Source. This is hinted at by King David, peace be upon him, when he said: "The testimony of the Lord is sure" <note>Psalm 19:8</note>. Behold, in all its wealth and happiness, it exists through the actual Great Name, as I wrote in Chapter 23 of the first part of this book.

Because this is so, all goodness and success in the Kingdom <note>original: "מלכות" (Malchut)</note> are necessitated by it. For when the King establishes it in the seven... it nourishes not according to the Source from which it is drawn, for if the Source is withheld, it is fitting that it be withheld, as we have written. From this, we can understand the request regarding the blessings mentioned in the Torah for those who walk in the law of the Lord. This is the most exalted point: all those goods are not merely a "promise" in the way a master pays a servant for their work, giving them such-and-such in exchange for their labor. If the good came only as a promise, it would be external to the service and not necessitated by its nature. This would be a great flaw in the status of the Service. It is not so when the good flows directly from the Service and is necessitated by its nature; for this indicates the Name and the glory of the rank of the Service and the one who serves. Our Torah is included in an upper rank that is beyond measure... and our service to our God is a true service, chosen above all. The Supreme Wisdom saw fit to implant it and fix it in the darkness and the tabernacle.

# Chapter 17

Behold, there is a doubt that the sciences of those times were not conducted in the proper way or according to the faithful judgment that our Sages possessed. For they all denied the **future reward of the soul** <note>original: "גמול העתיד לנפש"</note> after its separation from the body. They distanced themselves from this because they could not provide a near and tangible sign for it. When our Torah came among those sciences, just as it surpassed them in rank, so too it encompassed and aided them—meaning, it provided what they were unable to give. 

Just as the Torah could handle the matter of the many... for the partial matter is attached, which the ancients could not do. Thus, the eye can see clearly that the matter belonging to the Torah of truth is eternal. Had it only promised the reward of the soul after death, its importance would have seemed lesser <note>Because it couldn't be proven during life</note>. But the Torah did not limit its promises to the World to Come; rather, it extended its narrative to matters of this world that are beyond doubt. 

Rabbi Yosef ibn Shem Tov <note>original: "ר' יוסף סביב"; a 15th-century philosopher</note> wrote in the book *Ein ha-Kore* (The Reader's Eye) that the foundation of this is missing... not to suppress those goods, but to spread the memory of the ultimate end. It was proper to mention both this and that. I have always thought that this language... except for what he could doubt. But what removed him from the eighth doubt is that he believed this doubt could be resolved by saying at the beginning of the matter: "in the same way, the body and our death... in the matter of the soul's existence." But they deny its nature until it is fitting... that the one who prevents it will have a more complete loss. All the Torah's promises regarding physical matters are to show that there was a "clinging" <term>Devekut: communion or attachment to the Divine</term> to the Divine matter. If one is assured of the laws of the body, there is no doubt that he will be assured of this clinging. 

Since this clinging is what the Torah holds as the rank of the ultimate reward, then its mention in the Torah is a complete and perfect reward. Rabbi Abraham ben [Daud/Bibago] <note>original: "ר' אברהם בן כי חכמי"</note> wrote in his book *Derech Emunah* (The Path of Faith), Part 2, Gate 5: "This answer is not without doubt. For if the perfection of the soul were famous/known, then it would certainly be publicized." But Abraham our Father and his descendants were the products of the existence of God and His divinity. Just as the Torah presented us with the existence of God by saying "I am the Lord your God," which was already a known concept, it should have also mentioned the soul's survival. 

However, this is nothing, for if the existence of God was known in the time of Abraham, it was also known at the time the Torah was written. Yet Israel, who came out of Egypt, needed to hear this from the Almighty because in Egypt they were heretics regarding these two principles. As they said in the Midrash *Exodus Rabbah*: "At first, Pharaoh said to them: You speak lies, for I am the master of the world, and I created myself and the Nile." Thus, they returned to their own essence. 

But regarding the survival of the soul, they were then powerless. I must also say that the survival of the soul was mentioned in the Torah because the consensus to bring an actual proof for it—as the text testifies—comes from the matter of the "clinging" that man has, which is the choice of the assured. From this judgment, there are four questions to which there is no answer, and it is better for the Sages to be silent about them, as the Rabbi <note>Maimonides or Ramban</note> wrote. But the existence of God and His unity were not mentioned there for the same reason... and this is what was created, for behold and all will be...

### Part on Service, Chapter 19

...which is entirely simple, and from it extends, as it were, the double sphere of its existence. These are the **Second Effect** which flows from the **First**, and from it extends the double sphere of the fixed stars. This same path applies to the other spheres. For the wise man, according to his absolute detachment from the First Cause, there are likewise commandments for the angels. As they said in the chapter *Chelek* <note>The tenth chapter of Tractate Sanhedrin in the Talmud, which discusses the afterlife and the nature of the soul</note>, "The righteous are greater than the ministering angels." If so, then his degree was sufficient to make up for the lack in others, and he was given existence by being almost god-like. As it is written: for the sphere of his existence, being almost god-like in motion—which is the specific action suited to them because of their small degree of perfection—this action, which is motion, is sufficient to sustain them, establish them, and give them grace. For the lack of deeds is necessary for their existence and standing. 

This existence is more worthy through grace, for the value of the "lower" to the "possessor" is like the value of the "double" to the "double." This is the secret of the things. This is the grace of the sphere to find its absolute state, as it is written: "And God set them in the firmament of the heaven to give light upon the earth" <note>Genesis 1:17</note>, decreeing for it this existence and eternity. If this is true for the perfection of the Holy One, blessed be He, how much more so is it proper that existence be granted to man? In His wisdom, He decreed their actions, as seen in the section of "that certain person" <note>Likely referring to a specific Midrashic figure or anonymous teacher</note>, and in *Leviticus Rabbah* on the portion *Acharei Mot*, and in the *Midrash on Proverbs*. 

Rabbi Levi said in the name of Rabbi Shimon ben Menasya: "The apple of the heel <note>The fleshy part of the heel; here used to represent the lowest, most physical part of the body</note> of the First Man <term>Adam HaRishon</term> would dim the orb of the sun." Behold, the upper perfection of Man is influenced by the duration of his existence compared to the orb of the sun—that is to say, one who lives a beautiful life. For the First Man, through his choice and the integrity of the Holy One, blessed be He, was literally the integrity of all creatures. How much more so should the "apple of the heel" of the First Man dim the sun's orb? This is the meaning of "the apple of his heel dims the sun's orb"—meaning, by how much more so [is the rest of him greater]. 

The essence of the matter is this: the matter of the First Man was necessarily of a level of perfection that serves as the foundation of foundations. His existence and eternity are greater than the sun's orb. This is the "action of the apple of the heel," which hints at the merit of his physical matter, his holiness, and the "countenance of his face" <note>A phrase referring to divine or radiant light reflecting from a person's features</note>. By this, he surpassed the sphere, which was higher and simpler and purer than the substance of the sphere itself. It was right that he should have existence, for he was more worthy according to what was designated for him in the service of the Holy One, blessed be He. This was the intention of his creation: existence and eternity. For the service he performs for Him alone must be without interruption. This is also hinted at in their words regarding "the apple of his heel" and the "covering of his foot." For with the term "designated," he called the horse in *Keritot* <note>A reference to Tractate Keritot in the Talmud</note>, and gave to the integrity of the Holy One, blessed be He, grace from his service in perfection. From him, existence is extended to all created beings. 

And they saw that further grace would be needed to return to the existence of the sun's orb, for it suffices for the existence of the lower beings. They took the parable of the "apple of the heel" to the binding of the "refused" <note>unclear: פגול (pigul); possibly referring to disqualified sacrifices or rejected states</note>, all that was mentioned for the chosen ones. For this deed is the foundation of existence for all creatures. And the intention is that they knew that the sphere, being physical matter, requires a "soul-action," which is the persistence of motion, to achieve its perfection. The time of motion was the source of existence for all lower creatures. Similarly, man, being physical matter, needs a physical action—namely, the **practical commandments** <term>Mitzvot Ma'asiyot</term>—through which he achieves perfection, which is existence. The intention necessarily included in divine service is more essential and more eternal than the service of the sphere. From this, existence is further repaired for all creatures, until they no longer need the action of the sphere for their existence. This is the meaning of: "The apple of the heel of the First Man would dim the orb of the sun." 

The same applies to all things mentioned regarding the beauty and perfection of the First Man before the sin, as will be explained in Chapter 10. From what we have written, it will be clarified that the intention was the beginning of physical existence for these commandments... they could not hear it because it was against their wrath. And how could they promise the beginning of grace in the body? He wishes to prove existence for man and his dream, for they must admit that because man possesses physical matter...

<column-break/>

...to a foundation that is not his perfection through contemplation alone without action. This is clarified by the spheres: because they possess matter, it was necessary to bring forth for them some physical action, which is motion, so that through that action they might achieve the perfection hidden within them according to their nature. Therefore, it is necessary that regarding the thing intended for the perfection of all—that which possesses matter and a rational soul—it be a matter composed of physical action and soulful contemplation. 

They said that without soulful contemplation, the soulful perfection is repaired by being joined to those physical actions to serve God in deed. This is the fulfillment of the intention to do good and its existence for His sake, and not for one's own consumption or any other intention. Therefore, you know it will be clarified that the cause of the soul's perfection, its completion, and its existence in eternal delight in the World of Souls, is upright—it is through physical actions, which are the **practical commandments**. These are the "Great Part" in completion and the attainment of perfection. This is the great cause in the management of the soul as long as it enters and causes its service while being in the "cover of the body." 

This uprightness helps the soul in its existence through deeds, just as the soul helps the body in its existence through its intention, by the power of existence in this world. This prepares both of them to help and benefit each other. The actions hinted at before Him flow to the relief of the lack and the decay attached to it. From all this composition, its strength and ability will increase... and as long as this grace and this will persist, there is no power of destruction to habituate the composition at all. As they merited to see, as long as the incense was tied to the body, it was the cause of its existence; if its measure changed, there was fear of destruction and separation. Just as this itself is the existence of the sphere—for from its action, which is motion, to dwell and be joined to it, it is also peace to it—this is from the power of its existence. Since there is no interruption to this action, there is also no interruption to its existence according to the Will. 

So too, Man, by being constantly attached to his service, his existence will endure. This is why the practical commandments were given according to the number of man's limbs; a hint of one vision against the hint of his limbs for holiness. For every single commandment intends existence for that specific limb which corresponds to it. He sought for the commandments a "cancellation for the world" <note>unclear: בטול לעולה</note> and an obligation for the body, for the commandments for the limb correspond to it as the body does for him. Just as the commandments are existing and eternal, they are the causes of perfection, which is grace for the body that fulfills them. 

This was the intention of the Sages of Truth, peace be upon them, when they said in *Leviticus Rabbah* Section 12: "Rabbi Hezekiah said regarding the matter: The words of the Torah are a crown for the head, a necklace for the throat, a poultice for the heart, a collyrium <note>an eye salve</note> for the eyes, a cup of roots for the bowels." <note>This Midrash illustrates how Torah and commandments provide physical and spiritual health to specific parts of the body</note>. "A crown for the head" is from "for they shall be a wreath of grace for your head" <note>Proverbs 1:9</note>. "A necklace for the throat" is from "and chains about your neck." "A poultice for the heart" is from "the precepts of the Lord are right, rejoicing the heart" <note>Psalm 19:9</note>. "A collyrium for the eyes" is from "the commandment of the Lord is pure, enlightening the eyes." "A cup of roots for the bowels" is from "it shall be health to your navel" <note>Proverbs 3:8</note>. "A balm for your limbs" is as it is written: "for they are life to those who find them, and healing to all their flesh" <note>Proverbs 4:22</note>. Behold, the light of their words confirms what we have said. 

This same discourse was already brought in *Midrash Zomer Tov* <note>Midrash Shocher Tov / Midrash Tehillim</note>: "The heavens declare the glory of God" <note>Psalm 19:1</note>. At the time of the hidden things, after existence—meaning that man dies by nature—nature is subjugated and conquered by the Torah and those who keep it. For the Torah preceded nature and was created for the sake of those who keep it. Furthermore, it wanted to prove the existence of the body and its eternity after the Holy Spirit... and it agrees with what we explained above. For we have already said that the destruction of the body and its decay comes from the lack of existence... and this is almost this and that in its intention. There is nothing in all the practical commandments that is merely a "mark" or "sign," but rather they are the "existence of the body." Their intention is through grace and the perfection of health, existence, and eternity for their possessors, as we mentioned. And the **Covenant of Circumcision** <term>Brit Milah</term> is weighted against all the commandments...

It cites Midrashic sources to show that the First Man (Adam) was more radiant than the sun and that the Torah acts as a physical healing and sustaining force for the human body.</summary>

### Chapter 18: Part on Service (Continued)
### Chapter 19

And do not find it difficult... as they said in the Midrash regarding the "firmament" and the "seven heads" <note>Referencing the levels of the heavens in Jewish cosmology</note>. The secret of the verse is that through His wisdom, He informed us that one who serves the Most High God does so through the "rectification of faith" and the "reception of the Daughter" <note>term: Reception of the Daughter (Kabbalistic reference to *Malchut* or the *Shekhinah*, the feminine aspect of the Divine)</note>. For every person who elevates the "Upper Word" and the "Foundation of Rectification" in the "Valley of Blessing" <note>original: *Emek HaBeracha*</note> ascends through the metaphor of "cleaving to the center" which we mentioned, and the measurement that is above all worthy intentions in their service.

As in the Midrash of Rabbi Shimon bar Yochai (peace be upon him), his master Eleazar opened: "A garden locked is my sister, my bride..." <note>Song of Songs 4:12</note>. This "locked garden" is the Assembly of Israel <note>term: Assembly of Israel (*Knesset Yisrael*), the mystical personification of the Jewish people and the *Shekhinah*</note>, which is called a "locked garden" to say, as Rabbi Eleazar noted: just as a garden eventually requires a person to awaken and water it, so too does the Assembly of Israel need one to speak, awaken, and water it. This reception of the "garden" is called a "covenant." Just as the garden needs one to awaken, water, and dig, so is the entire secret: for the Lord has established a covenant through our strength. It is written: "He watered it and cleared it of stones," etc. <note>Isaiah 5:2</note>. 

The intention is strengthened in this way: the secret of the Lord’s grace is poured into the "chosen one" of the matter, bringing down the "rain of kindness" and blessing upon the "Upper Earth," which then gives its life-giving produce. With the heart’s agreement, the scripture says that the entire "debt of fate" <note>original: *chov hamazal*</note> is extended and obligated by the goodness of the service. This is the secret of all the rectifications of the "Nebo" <note>unclear: possibly a reference to prophecy or a specific celestial station</note> and its completion: "And you shall do them," "And I will give your rains in their season" <note>Leviticus 26:3-4</note>, as I have written above. 

From the "Firmament of the Firmament" <note>original: *merak rakia*</note> spreads the secret of the Upper Rectification. One might think it has no end, but the "Tablets of the Seven Heads" show that the "Rectification of the Glory"—which is the "Depth of the Torah" and the "Fulfillment of the Commandments"—is the source of all good things and blessings. Its form contains no goodness or blessing for the world except through these upper realms. Through understanding and usage of His "Glory," the body of the idea is refined, and its "wine" is poured out through the opening of "Judgment" and its beauty. Together, they bring life to all through the Lord's mercy. 

The secret of the verse and the thought is that we should be in a state where the upper heavens receive, as in "And you shall hear in the heavens" <note>1 Kings 8:32</note>. Through the "Supernal Connector," the "garden" receives the "water and wine." In their celebration of life, they are similar to the "High Places," where "Manna" is hidden for the righteous. There, in the "Cleft of the Included," is the secret of those who find the Lord. Between the Right and the Left <note>note: The sefirot of *Chesed* (Mercy) and *Gevurah* (Strength)</note>, the light spreads to those who receive from the "Mediator" upon the "Righteous One, the Life of the Worlds" <note>term: Life of the Worlds (*Chai HaOlamim*), a title for the sefirah of *Yesod*, the channel of divine flow</note>. The secret of the "Kingdom of the House of David" <note>term: *Malchut*, the final sefirah</note> is revealed, and when it reaches there, the secret spreads to the lower realms. It is said, "Judgment is opened and the beauty of the world dwells."

And in saying "and righteousness together," he hinted at all this good flowing from above to below. For the secret of the reversal of the "Rectification" is maintained by the servants of the Lord in the "Valley of Blessing" and the fulfillment of the commandments, as in the secret of "and righteousness you shall bring forth," etc. This means that righteousness opens the merit through the "Rectification" of the "Disciples of the Profane" <note>unclear: *talmidei chol*</note>, moving and journeying through the upper realms and being proven and heard in the lower realms. This is why it says "together for life in His mercy"—meaning the "Rectification" is established and ordered, and all this will be drawn and obligated from it naturally. 

When the "Rider of the Horse" <note>note: A metaphor for God or a high angelic power controlling the celestial spheres</note> is revealed in his preparation, and through the movement of the "Rider of the Horse," there is no lack or weakness in the union of forces. Those who complete the intention in the "Upper Rectification" through their service—which is the "Unification"—are included in the secret of: "And he called him El, the God of Israel" <note>Genesis 33:20</note>. As explained in the "Chapter of Labor," He called Jacob "El" <note>original: *El*, a name for God</note>. It has already been said that he is a "god" in the upper realms and a "human" in the lower realms. This is the secret of the "Rider of the Horse" in his preparation. This is the secret of the "Unification" caused by the service of all, as hinted in "In your preparation." This opens the "Upper Rectification," which is the "Rectification of Glory." It is the "Consolation" that rises through the hand of Israel; through the hand of Israel below, it is elevated above. In saying "The Heavens," he hinted that what is drawn and obligated comes from the "preparation" and the "unification" caused by the servants who direct their hearts to the "Upper Source," which then flows upon the "Obligated." They receive the "Heavens," which are added from the "Righteous," meaning he rectifies for them. This is the secret of the "Heavens" that bestow all the good and blessings received from above. For this is maintained by the "Nature of Service," and this is what our Rabbi intended to prove in this chapter.

## Chapter 19
---
->The investigation of why the Torah and the commandments do not [seem to] benefit us [regarding mortality]<-

<column-break/>

The metaphor we hinted at regarding life after death is focused on the "Eternal Covenant" and the intention of "Receiving the Torah." The tradition is as it was written. In general, as the excellence of the Torah and the "Place" <note>note: *HaMakom*, a name for God</note> increase, its complexity is removed. The "Kingdom" is its model, and its foundation was upon it. When standing upon the truth of all this—to know the Holy Torah, which is the "Upper Knowledge," and according to the "True Reception" <note>note: *Kabbalah HaAmitit*, meaning the authentic mystical tradition</note>—it is the "Wisdom of God" to keep the existence of the receiver alive through mercy. Without it, it is impossible to stand before the lack in anything, whether by Moses or anyone else. 

Death is not natural to man at all, except through this [lack of connection]. When one stands upon the "Nature of the Torah," it gives man mental existence and eternal life with no death at all. The "Satan" is simply the reversal of this "Divine Nature." This reversal is "Judgment," which is covered by the "Upper Wisdom." Since this was the Torah's intention, there should be no place for the "foundation of death," for there is no death where there is "Divine Existence." Rather, it should be a "Right Hand" of long, eternal life.

Afterward, they shall merit the level of those like Elijah (of blessed memory), who did not taste the taste of death at all, such as those mentioned [in tradition]. For the scriptures and the "Reception of the Torah" <note>original: *Kabbalah Shel Torah*</note> are like what we say in prayer. Our Holy Rabbi (peace be upon him) said there: "You shall do with your wisdom in your life." Regarding those who did not taste death, he mentions the son of Jacob <note>possibly Joseph or Benjamin</note>, Serah bat Asher <note>note: In legend, she lived for centuries and entered Eden alive</note>, and it is written that the "Daughter of Pharaoh" <note>Bithiah</note> became a servant to the Ark <note>insert: She entered [Paradise] alive</note>, and Elijah, and the grandson of Rabbi Judah the Prince. Some say even Rabbi Joshua ben Levi <note>a sage who famously tricked the Angel of Death</note>. 

Behold, these are valid witnesses that the "bridle of death" only exists because it was [historically] established, but it is a "Change of Nature" and contrary to the "Intention of the Torah." For the nature [of Torah] is to give life to its doers. This is worthy of being explained to anyone who needs it, and may God stand by me.

I say that those who "act wise" regarding nature <note>note: referring to secular philosophers</note> say that death is "natural" to man. Their reason is that everything that is "generated" must "perish." Since man is generated and composed of the "Four Elements," he must necessarily perish. Even if all the "Wise Men of Greek Wisdom" <note>term: Greek Wisdom (*Chokhmah Yevanit*), referring to Aristotelian philosophy</note> use their intellects, they are among our own people who "turn judgment into wormwood" regarding the Law of the Torah and its intention. 

But the "Sages of the Torah," the masters of the "True Wisdom" <note>Kabbalah</note>, believe that death is **not** natural. They spoke the truth: "There is no death forever." The great master, Nachmanides <note>original: *Ramban* (1194–1270)</note>, of blessed memory, said in the Section on Genesis (page 10): "Know that composition does not [necessarily] indicate decomposition." This is contrary to the "thinkers of thoughts" <note>philosophers</note> who believe that creation indicates a beginning and an end. But according to the Sages of the True Wisdom, the world—even though it is composed—will exist as long as God desires. This is clear truth. 

If so, the idea of "perishing" is against the "Covenant" and the simple principle of the "Opinion of our Sages." We should not believe or establish matters based on the words of those "foolish philosophers." 

Before I come to the core intention, I say that these "Masters of Logic" among our people who say man dies "by nature" would nonetheless admit in their logic that the "Spheres" <note>term: Spheres (*Galgalim*), the celestial bodies in medieval cosmology</note>—despite being composed of "Body and Soul"—are eternally alive. Even though they are "generated," they do not "perish," according to the [Divine] Will. If they decree this for the Spheres, even though they are generated and composed, why would they not decree eternal life also for man, who is also generated and composed? 

Is it only because the "investigators" say that the "Matter of the Sphere" is not like the "Matter of Man," claiming it is pure, refined, and not composed of opposites, while man is dark, thick, and composed of opposites? Even so, we say that the "Soul of Man" is more refined and more excellent than all the Spheres! For the soul is an "emanation" of the "Upper Light." It is not merely the "Result of the Actor," as in the opinion of the author of *The Kuzari* <note>Rabbi Judah Halevi</note>, who says that the "First Effect" <note>term: First Effect (*Al-Aql al-Awwal*), the first creation in Neoplatonism</note> was divided from the "First Cause" according to their view of what the Self can endure...

# 39 - Chapter 4 - The Part on Service - Chapter 4

Existence was revealed to them, for these were worthy. As long as our existence is defined by service—the service of the Blessed Name that was decreed—it was as a reward for that service that He gave him <note>Referring to the archetypal Man or the practitioner</note> existence in both body and soul. This is because service is the "living water" <note>A metaphor for spiritual vitality that never ceases</note> which has neither interruption nor limit. Just as the reward for the body is that it is perishable and changing, so too is the soul compared to water. One might say that just as it fills and attains the "Upper Things" <note>term: Upper Things (*Elyonim*), referring to the spiritual realms or divine emanations</note> which are our foundation, its perfection increases. It is "sweet and good for the eyes to see the sun" <note>Ecclesiastes 11:7</note>. He said this because the "Upper Light" strikes all generalities, and its existence is derived from its heart <unclear>kofat kofat</unclear>. This is the light that the Rabbi spoke of as being "sweeter than honey" <note>Psalm 19:11</note>, which is a parable for the pleasantness and delight that flows from that Light. 

And when he said "good for the eyes," it is a metaphor for their perceptions of the pleasant Upper Perceptions. Regarding the word "to see," and "to see the sun," this refers to the cause of eternal existence—to see the sun is to see the spiritual life. He who has not yet merited it should ensure that the light is always "upon his head," like "oil upon the head" <note>Ecclesiastes 9:8</note>, so that it is never lacking. This is a metaphor for the service and praise that fills that light so that it never departs from him, for not everyone merits its continuous presence. Death is described as "hiding His face" <note>Psalm 104:29</note>.

In the Midrash *Genesis Rabbah*, section 11, Rabbi Yehuda bar Simon <note>original: "bar Kiyamanu" - a likely OCR error for Bar Simon</note> said: With the light created on the first day, a person could see from one end of the world to the other. But when the Holy One, Blessed be He, looked upon the deeds of the Generation of the Enosh and the Generation of the Flood <note>The generations associated with the breakdown of morality in Genesis</note>, and saw that their deeds were corrupt, He stood up and hid it from them. As it is said: "From the wicked their light is withheld" <note>Job 38:15</note>. And why did He hide it? To reserve it for the righteous in the world to come. As it is said: "And God saw the light, that it was good" <note>Genesis 1:4</note>, and "good" refers only to the righteous. From where do we know He hid it for the righteous? As it is said: "Light is sown for the righteous" <note>Psalm 97:11</note>. And when He saw the light was prepared for the righteous, He rejoiced, as it is said: "The light of the righteous rejoices" <note>Proverbs 13:9</note>.

Rabbi Levi, in the name of Bar Nezira, said: That light served for thirty-six hours—twelve on the eve of the Sabbath <note>Friday daytime</note>, twelve on the night of the Sabbath, and twelve on the Sabbath day. When Adam sinned, God sought to hide it, but He showed honor to the Sabbath, as it is said: "And God blessed the seventh day" <note>Genesis 2:3</note>. How did He bless it? With light. When the sun set on the night of the Sabbath, the light continued, and they sang praises to the Holy One, Blessed be He. Why? Because they remained on the bank of the river <unclear>ha-moreh</unclear> in that light all day and all night. But when the sun set at the close of the Sabbath, the darkness began to grope its way in. At that moment, it is written: "His light was upon my head" <note>Job 29:3</note>. Levi said: With that light, Adam was able to see and place his strength in it... and he said "Perhaps the darkness shall bruise me" <note>Psalm 139:11</note>. Until here.

Listen: according to the opinion of Rabbi Levi, the light did not continue except until the sixth day when man was created, because the intention within it was to establish our permanence in life. But its continuation was shortened, though He gave honor to the Sabbath. At the conclusion of the Sabbath, the light was hidden—which is the "Sabbath of the Waters"—and its removal is the cause of death. It is clear, therefore, that the light created on the first day is "Existence." The existence of Man was primary, and our life from all the things that were in potential and for the benefit of man followed all the things in the Work of Creation. Even the Upper Generalities were created first to be more perfect than him. The body was created last <margin>Action, Formation, Creation</margin> so that all the generalities were included in the creation of man, to show that he is the sum of everything and the root of everything. Even his being created last shows that he was the intended goal of their creation, and the Name <note>God</note> created them for him. All this was within him by the power of the soul (*Neshamah*) which was linked to him from the Source of Life, which is higher than the angels. This was the meaning of his existence. If he were by nature destined to die and perish, then the Upper Beings created for him would be superior to him. 

<column-break/>

As demonstrated by the statement of Rabbi Levi, he would be more elevated than them. If so, the things created for the sake of the Goal <note>Man</note> would be greater than the creature itself. However, since the "Last" <note>Man</note> is the intention of all created things, his soul must be sustained in life. By this logic, when the Light is the intention, it provides existence and removes the causes of perishability from him. For the soul of existence that was linked to him gives to him and saves him, being elevated to the "Orit" <note>Aramaic: Light/Torah</note>. For the soul comes to him from the Source of Water to give him life and sustain us in life. This is what is written: "And He breathed into his nostrils the breath of life" <note>Genesis 2:7</note>.

The word "And He formed" (*Vayyitzer*) is written with two *Yods* <note>The Hebrew letter 'Y'</note> to hint at the two forms within him before the soul: the *Nefesh* <note>term: Nefesh, the lower/animal soul</note> and the *Ruach* <note>term: Ruach, the spirit or animating breath</note>. For his existence is not complete with the body alone; he needs a soul from the Holy Height, which is a spirit from the spirit of the Source of Water. This is why it says "He breathed into his nostrils the breath of life" in a double sense. These names will help you understand. One "nostril" receives the body, and the other receives the soul, and he rejoices in the existence of his soul passing through the body. This is why it says "a breath of life, and man became a living soul." The Targum of Onkelos translates this as "and it became in man a speaking spirit" <note>Aramaic: *Ruach Memallela*</note>.

According to what we explained above, it will be clear to the wise that the speech and existence of man are guided by the *Nefesh* and *Ruach*. The essence of this was his thought, for the "Living Soul" mentioned in the Work of Creation is translated as "Living Soul" (*Nafsha Chaya*), but here it is translated as "Speaking Spirit" (*Ruach Memallela*). The reason is to distinguish between the speech of the spirit and the speech of the soul: one is external speech, and the other is internal speech, which is contemplation and the perception of Upper Matters, which brings joy. This is why one is translated quietly <note>Refers to internal thought</note>. That is to say, the "Breath of Life" is called a "Speaking Spirit" because it is the power that speaks in vitality, for it is the prince that comes to speak before the King, the Lord of Hosts.

In the *Midrash on Ruth* regarding the soul, they said: "My soul yearns for You in the night, even my spirit within me seeks You" <note>Isaiah 26:9</note>. "My soul yearns for You"—these are the tied crowns <note>spiritual levels</note> that praise Him. A person has *Nefesh* and *Ruach*. The *Nefesh* is to sustain the body, and the *Ruach* is to awaken him and make him wise in the ways of the world. If he merits more from Above according to his ways, he receives an additional spirit. As a person goes through this world to enjoy its presence, the *Nefesh* is established in the body. But when he involves himself in the Spirit <note>spiritual pursuits</note>, it rests upon him. If a person merit to complete himself through these powers, a holy awakening from Above rests upon him, crowning him and making him wise with the "Upper Wisdom" (*Chochmah Ila’ah*), and he is invited into the Palace of the King. That awakening is the "existence" of the spirit upon him. This is the "Living Soul" (*Neshamah Chaya*), which does more than just sustain; it is called *Ruach* because it gives him wisdom to perceive.

Thus, when they are linked and saved through wisdom—the *Nefesh* and *Ruach*—to perceive the Name in this world, then according to his deeds, he merits a higher level. By the power of his service and perception in this world, he reaches the "Upper Sister" <note>A mystical reference to a high spiritual level</note>, which is the Service and the Unification (*Yichud*) of the Unique Name. They assist him and pour upon him an "Additional Spirit" (*Ruach Yeteira*), which is the Holy Breath of the Living God. This is the Holy Soul (*Neshamah*) that connects him to the Upper Wisdom to be in the Palace of the King, to stand and serve before Him and to bless His Name always. For the nature of the soul is to give him eternal existence in body and spirit, so there is no interruption in his service or his life. This is the measure that remains forever. This was the intention: that the Spirit should not cease, for the Soul is from the Spirit of Life. And even if the body faces death, the person himself lives through the sweetness of the Holy Soul, for holiness does not dwell in a place of impurity.

# The Service Chapter 19 | Section: Chapter 19

The act of the living—as it is written: *Sing for joy in the Lord, O you righteous* <note>original: "רננו לצדיקים"; Psalm 33:1</note>—and suffering through the strength of praise to God <unclear>bakari</unclear>. As the lap of praise, these are the daughters of prayer. There is a generation, and there was Moses, over whose handiwork flies had no power. This "generation" is as it is written: *Her gates have sunk into the ground* <note>Lamentations 2:9; a midrashic idea that the gates of the Temple were hidden/preserved rather than destroyed by enemies</note>. Of Moses, the Master said: Since the First Temple was destroyed, the Tent of Meeting was hidden away—its hooks, its bars, its pillars, and its sockets. Where were they hidden? Rav Hisda said in the name of our Teacher: beneath the tunnels of the Sanctuary. And these objects, though it is fitting that death and perishability should rule over them, they are the handiwork of the Holy One, blessed be He. For the work of the Holy One and His preparation are perfect so that they may endure. And through what did they endure? For with this intention <note>term: intention (*kavanah*); the focused spiritual aim during an act</note> they were fashioned, and through the attribute of his trust, which is the attribute of the Covenant of Circumcision <note>term: Covenant of Circumcision (*Brit Milah*)</note>, as was explained above. 

This secret is hinted at by the prophet Isaiah (peace be upon him) in his saying: *Your people shall all be righteous; they shall possess the land forever, the shoot of My planting, the work of My hands, that I may be glorified* <note>Isaiah 60:21</note>. It is known and accepted by those who know wisdom <note>referring to Kabbalists</note> that the guardian of the Covenant, which is performed in fitness, holiness, and understanding with the true intention, is called a "Righteous One" (*Tzadik*) after the name of the **Righteous One, the Life of the Worlds** <note>A divine title associated with the sefira of Yesod</note>. Therefore, Joseph was called "Joseph the Righteous" because of his persistence in guarding the Covenant. Because the **Upper Righteous One** inherits the Land of the Living—for it is His to give life to the earth—the one who guards the Covenant merits the inheritance of the land in his lifetime, for he draws life from the Righteous One, the Life of the Worlds. 

And when He said, *the shoot of My planting*, His intention was to give them this title based on this quality of guarding the Covenant. Behold, he is called "the shoot of the planting of the Lord," and the planting of the Lord shall not perish nor be uprooted. This is because that planting was, even at its time, prepared for its destiny. Therefore, it is just that they should inherit the land forever and not die, for they were intended for permanence in their planting. And as for saying *the work of My hands, that I may be glorified*, it means the intention in that planting was that the Divine Purpose should be clarified through it. Perishability only exists when the ultimate purpose is absent; but in a thing that is enduring, the Name of God is present.

Furthermore, there is a hint in the phrase *the work of My hands, that I may be glorified*—this is the great secret that we have already elaborated upon at the end of the discourse on the commandments of Law and Service regarding the "Divine Need" <note>term: Divine Need (*Tzorech Gavoah*); the concept that human service sustains or "glorifies" the Divine realms</note>. He said it is right that they should inherit the land forever and endure, because the intention in them fulfills a Divine Need, which is that He should be glorified through the Service. As it is said regarding the priest, *I have placed My glory upon him*, drawing light and abundance from the Source, the Source of Glory (*Tiferet*). This is the foundation of the great secret of His Blessed Honor. If so, it would provide a suspension of death to give endurance to the body, as the soul is cleaved to it, and it becomes a lodging place for the soul's perfection. This was the intention in the making of the Copper Serpent, which was not delayed in its effect <unclear>akmir</unclear>. Even according to those who say man dies by nature, Circumcision sustains him, just as His promise returns him to existence. These are the secrets of what I have seen to prove and verify the endurance of life that follows the intellect, even according to those who follow the hidden things from the sages in the mouth of Amos, whose hands and feet cannot find the way to prove Divinity. This reward comes to benefit the existence that is according to the Knowledge of the Torah and its true receivers.

## Chapter Twenty

He is *near to the Lord, to all who call upon Him* <note>Psalm 145:18</note>. This final rule is that a person stands in his recognition on the first day, for he has a destiny in the world. And the Sages of Truth said regarding one who is not nourished by His blessed nourishment and His preparation, and who "eats the light" that is drawn from Him so that there may be permanent existence in the man—who is the purpose of creation—through the service he performs. Regarding this, it is said of the "Son of Jesse," and they said in the Midrash that four entered <note>A reference to the *Pardes*, the four sages who entered the orchard of mystical knowledge</note>: Ben Azzai and his companions... and it was said, *And God said, "Let there be light"* to tell him it is holy, and He saw in every work... He told him a parable: it is like one who was freed and found a crown... and he returned to his house because his son was worthy of the thirty years that were given in thought... and the families were opened... until here. Behold, that which is wrapped is the light hidden within the revealed.

<column-break/>

As we say in the fourth chapter of Tractate Nedarim: Rabbi Shimeon says, "Great is circumcision, for it is weighed against all the commandments in the Torah," as it says, *For in accordance with these words I have made a covenant with you* <note>Exodus 34:27</note>. And it says further there: "Great is circumcision, for it is weighed against all the commandments in the Torah," for it says, *The Covenant which the Lord made with you concerning all these things*. Our Rabbis of blessed memory intended in the Talmud to show that the purpose of it is trust in God, which is all the good within it—eternal life, endurance, and joy. Therefore, so that this Covenant might be sealed, it is compared to the Covenant of the Rainbow, for it is one covenant for the whole world that shall not cease. For God desired to warn of understanding and otherwise, and *He made a covenant with all flesh* from the days of the Flood that *there would never again be a flood to destroy the earth*. But the cutting of Circumcision was written and "cut" into the body of each of the pious of the species to show that it is the ultimate holiness for body and soul in the endurance of the body.

Even in things whose nature is to perish, and were therefore "cut," we find promises for them because they were intended for holiness. Salt is His will <note>referring to the "Covenant of Salt"</note>, as has already been stated according to the tradition of our Rabbis. Therefore, the section on salt is connected. And in the Midrash: *Death is in his lips, he breathes out his will* <note>A play on Proverbs 16:14 or similar</note>. Rabbi Meir says: until now they have no permanence, and they did not rise, and they did not establish, but they are living and enduring. According to his words, it is a logical inference (*Kal Vachomer*): if the materials of the Tabernacle <note>term: Tabernacle (*Mishkan*)</note>, which any skilled person can read about, were given endurance and completion and are living and enduring forever—called "portions of life"—how much more so for the things you remember... *I will sing of mercy and justice* <note>Psalm 101:1</note>. Rabbi Yohanan in the name of Rabbi Meir says: in the future to come, they will strengthen themselves to collect from the wicked, for in them is mercy for the living righteous and judgment for the wicked.

His intention in this is to say that the "fruits" <note>human actions</note> sustain the wicked temporarily from death, even though their sins rule over them. They are destined to give an account for having killed themselves by the "fruit of redemption" which is meant to give life to the poor through the commandment of *Challah* <note>the portion of dough given to the priest</note>. This is seen in the work of the Tabernacle, etc., of endurance, which will convict the wicked in the future.

And Rabbi Levi's intention was regarding the "accents of suffering" <note>possibly referring to the cantillation marks of the Torah</note> that stand for the world and for all eternity. How distant are these words from the eyes of the "Sages of the Census" <note>likely rationalists or scoffers</note> in their knowledge. When they see the words of our Rabbis, they are revived in the Law (*Halakhah*), or they press and choose "under their tongues" and explain with a forced interpretation distant from the intent of the matter. In our days, with philosophy, to the truly wise, these things will be forgiven... for the intention from the beginning was to elevate all things to give them endurance in fixed vitality, so that the Divine Light would shine upon them. For behold, the Sefirot and the markings... one power appears, the Divine Presence (*Shekhinah*). It was in the hearts of the ancients... because their preparation was holy, which is "fire in the soul for the body," and there is no place for perishability there at all. Because the vitality of the Divine matter is their foundation, these things saw no place for the fate of destruction and ruin... but in cleaving, it goes up and up. All the more so the part included in the "Image and Likeness" <note>Genesis 1:26</note> which was prepared for endurance by being a dwelling for the Divine Presence.

And as for the doubts our Rabbis had regarding the "book with the book" <note>a phrase about the sanctity of Torah scrolls</note> because of the Divinity and the words of Torah written in it... because it is attached to the Book and all that is included with it. So says Solomon: *He who walks with the wise shall be wise* <note>Proverbs 13:20</note>. The Holy One said to the First Man... for his laws are like a cleavage: "Listen to Me and be like Me—just as I am living and enduring, so he is living and enduring." Until here is the hint regarding damage to the soul and the soul to the Book, and the nourishment of the body from death, for the Divinity is with it since it cleaves to it and is almost Divine... it is fitting that vitality should rule over it just as the light rules... and the scriptures will be fulfilled together. As they understood, life did not depart from the handiwork of the righteous, and certainly it was fitting that death should not rule over them if not for the sin, as we say in the first chapter of Tractate Sotah: *that not Rabbi Hanila bar...* <note>A catchword linking to the next page; likely referring to a specific Talmudic sage and a discussion on the death of the righteous</note>

It highlights the Tabernacle's components as proof that holy objects do not truly perish, but are hidden or preserved by Divine light.</summary>

He is not unable—meaning, the hands of the Holy One, blessed be He, were not prevented from creating it by His will. For had everything existed by necessity <note>The author is likely arguing against the Aristotelian view of a "necessary" world, asserting instead that God created the world through free "Will" (Ratzon)</note>, He would have been constrained. After this, he brings proof that He is the Creator of all by His will, saying: *Thus says the Lord, the Holy One of Israel and his Maker: Ask Me of things to come; concerning My children and the work of My hands, command Me* <note>original: "אמר יי' קדוש ישראל ויוצרו האותיות שאלוני... ולבניהם ולהודיעם"; Isaiah 45:11</note>. You shall know and ascend—that is to say, the works of My hands are free and I have power over them. This would not have been possible if my thoughts and my creative power were not "present" <note>unclear: "חל"; possibly referring to the divine presence or agency resting upon the creation</note>. He is the measure of the Holy One, blessed be He.

Also, regarding the prevention of its lowliness and what the people of the generation were asking me regarding His memory and His action, I said in truth: "My God, I made the earth with absolute Will." And also you have heard these divine words, that its life is balanced. I created Man in a law of perfection so that he would have eternal existence. And after the holy soul that I breathed into him from My mercy is reminded of the "later things" <note>likely referring to the ultimate spiritual purpose or the afterlife</note>, he shall ascend from the "possible" to "existence." For death is only a matter of existence for the body.

He gave them proof of this by saying: *My hands stretched out the heavens, and all their host I commanded* <note>Isaiah 45:12</note>. Behold, they are equal and composed of body and soul. This is also true of the heavens. The wise man, despite being composed of parts, his soul shall live forever. This was the intention in their creation, except that it was hindered by the sin of Adam. His intention is further shown in saying *I made the earth*—referring to the body. As our Sages of blessed memory interpreted: *He summons the heavens above* <note>Psalm 50:4</note>—this refers to the soul; *and the earth, to judge His people*—this refers to the body. 

And regarding them, *I created man*—the soul that was in the form of Man. For the skin, the flesh, and the bones are merely the "garment" of the human. As it says: *You clothed me with skin and flesh* <note>Job 10:11</note>. The intellectual part is called "Man." The vitality of the body, which connects to the soul, is like what we have discussed regarding the vitality of the "husks" <note>term: Husks (*Klipot*); in Kabbalah, these are the shells of materiality or evil that conceal the inner divine light</note>. When they are joined as one, the whole is called by the name "Nut" <note>The "Nut" (*Egoz*) is a classic mystical metaphor for the soul (the fruit) surrounded by protective layers or shells</note>. But the separation of the "waste" is called a "Husk" for the nut. The skin is what I have clothed in this matter, as is written in this chapter.

### Chapter 21

-> Just as the supernal Torah is the written form, <-
-> So the Torah written upon it reflects the wisdom from above. <-

This was the secret of the Unique Name <note>term: Unique Name (*Shem HaMeforash*); the four-letter name of God, YHWH</note>. The Torah is visible because it teaches and applies to the existence and standing of the Eternal Lord, as will be explained in Chapter 28. The first part of this book concerns the Perfect Torah, the heritage which Moses placed before the Children of Israel. it points to the place from which it was engraved—the supernal spiritual Torah, which is the secret of the "Beauty of Israel" <note>term: Beauty of Israel (*Tiferet Yisrael*); the central divine attribute (Sefirah) associated with the Torah and the Tetragrammaton</note>, the Unique Name. 

This is the secret of the Tree of Life. In the Midrash of Rabbi Shimon bar Yochai <note>term: Midrash of Rashbi; the Zohar</note>, it is said: *The Lord gives strength (Oz) to His people* <note>Psalm 29:11</note>, and "Strength" is nothing other than the Torah, as it is written: *It is a tree of life* <note>Proverbs 3:18</note>. And the Torah is nothing other than the Holy One, blessed be He. The body of the Torah was truly with the Lord. Those who engage with it and hold fast to it are engaging with and holding fast to the Name of the Lord and to existence in Him. Because the upper Torah is bound to the strength of the Lord and is called the "Strength of Life," one is strengthened by this life. It is called by His name, the "Strength of Life," for the totality of the "Strength of Life" stood between life and death.

It is impossible for any living person to say that life belongs only to one who has not sinned at all in the body, but rather to live their natural life required by their composition. For this would be no more than a simple degree of the Torah. Regarding the Elders of Judah <note>historical reference to righteous figures like Rabbi Yehuda ha-Nasi</note>, they are in a hidden state where their vitality is at our level. Our Sages of blessed memory said that other righteous men who did not sin did not die but are alive in the Garden of Eden, as we have written elsewhere. One should not say that the portion of life belongs only to the soul of the righteous in the "World of Souls," for that is a necessity of its own nature as it walks uprightly. Rather, they are justified in being called "living" while still in the body in the world mentioned, drawing from the vitality of the heavens, because they are attached to the "Strength of Life" which is the Torah. Whoever cleaves to Him, death has no dominion over him.

In the Midrash of Rabbi Shimon bar Yochai (peace be upon him), in the portion of *Behar Sinai*: "Whoever merits the Tree

<column-break/>

of Life shall drink of it in this world and shall rise in the time of the World to Come." As it is written: *all the more so for a man...* This is the singular intent of the Torah, even if the recipient only receives its revealed aspect. Since this is true, the Torah does not mention spiritual reward explicitly. The intent of the Great Name was to restore the noble powers to how they were before the sin, including the physical composition. His intent through the Torah is as explained in the previous chapter: that this composition was prepared for life and the endurance of the soul within the body. Man was meant to literally delight in the works of Creation, taking from it without any toil or labor. 

If humanity had not sinned, life, goodness, and perfection would have flowed continuously from the "Source" to all who came after him. But through sin, the deeds of man became subject to death, and no one is clean. Just as one who cleaves to the Tree of Life draws down the staff of life and good, so one who cleaves to the Tree of Knowledge <note>The "Tree of Knowledge of Good and Evil"</note>—where the "Evil" resides—draws down the staff of death and evil. For the Name he holds onto is for those who cleave to it. 

When Israel stood at Mount Sinai to receive the "Freedom" <note>A play on words: the "engraved" (*charut*) commandments are read as "freedom" (*cherut*)</note> that was the Torah, the Holy One, blessed be He, desired to merit Israel and to repair that which was distorted in their composition—to return the "Crown" <note>term: Crown (*Atarah*); referring to the divine aura or the Sefirah of Malchut</note> which was the cause of all good, life, and peace. This is what was mentioned in the previous chapter. It is as He said: *Now, if you obey Me faithfully and keep My covenant, you shall be My treasured possession among all the peoples... you shall be to Me a kingdom of priests and a holy nation* <note>Exodus 19:5-6</note>. 

He came to warn them not to sin in the way of their first father <note>Adam</note>, who brought death and changed "Knowledge" in the soul. God said to him: *Because you listened to the voice of your wife...* <note>Genesis 3:17</note>. Since He came to repair the world and to hold it within the intent of the Torah, Israel answered with their voice to accept all His commandments. This is His "Voice." Had they accepted the "Bad Voice" in the land—referring to the physical composition—it would have revealed death to them and all who follow.

*And you shall keep My covenant*—not in the sense of the physical joining of a covenant <unclear>kadoshim</unclear>, but as Rabbi Isaac said: "He who pulls his foreskin" <note>A Talmudic reference to one who tries to hide his circumcision, symbolizing a betrayal of the covenant</note>. It is written of such a person: *he has broken My covenant*. It says in the *Book of Principles* <note>likely *Sefer Ha-Ikkarim* by Joseph Albo</note> that they sinned in these matters. Thus it is written: *But they, like Adam, have transgressed the covenant* <note>Hosea 6:7</note>. And it is written: *He broke the covenant of peace*. But I will establish the Holy Covenant upon the world through choice, through service, and through ancient matters. The trust of the Lord shall establish all.

*And you shall be to Me a treasured possession (Segulah) among all the peoples.* The "treasure" of kings is not kept for its utility or its beauty alone, but because the Divine Presence <note>term: Shekhinah</note> rests upon them. It was to be attached and bound to the Name through constant service. You too, if God delights in you, shall be attached to Me. Cleaving to Me is "Living Life," where there is no death at all. I am capable of this; I am not distant, and it is not impossible for Me to give you physical endurance in these lives. *For all the earth is Mine*—I created the "later" and physical things from which the human body is built. I am the one who can make their composition eternal through your actions. For listening to My voice and keeping My covenant is the "salt" <note>A metaphor for a preservative</note> that sustains things that are naturally prone to decay. Everything is built on the life-force that I share with the creation. He who created it shall sustain it forever.

I will guard you not only from "damagers" <note>demonic or harmful forces</note> but even from death itself. All the more so since I have composed you as My *Segulah* from all the nations. You shall be like the heavenly beings in your physical life. He added further: *For all the earth is Mine*, for He shall stand over those who cleave to Him always in the delight of service—this is the meaning of *Segulah*. Even though the whole world is Mine, I desire the *Segulah*. He said to them: "All the earth is Mine, and you shall lack nothing." For he who merits the "treasures of the heart" does not need to toil; rather, your work shall be done by others...

It defines the human as essentially an "intellectual soul" and explains that through divine attachment (deveikut), the physical body can achieve a state of eternal endurance.</summary>
