# Part 4 | Chapter 4 | The Service

And so Enoch conducted himself in holiness before the Lord, and he is no longer among the dwellers of the earth, for he was transformed and ascended to the firmament by the Word of the Lord, who called his name **Metatron, the Great Scribe** <note>Metatron is a primary angel in Jewish mysticism, often described as the celestial scribe who records the deeds of humanity</note>. In the *Midrash Ruth HaNe'elam* <note>A mystical commentary on the Book of Ruth</note> it is written: *“And Enoch walked with God; and he was not, for God took him”*—meaning he was removed from this world of human beings. Enoch was changed and transformed into a holy minister <note>original: "קד" - likely an abbreviation for "קדוש" (holy) or "קדמון" (ancient/primordial)</note> to strike in his place as is fitting, becoming Metatron, the great minister appointed over his kind, under whose authority are many lower angels and celestial ministers.

And in the *Book of Hekhalot* <note>The "Book of Palaces," an early work of Jewish mysticism</note>, Rabbi Ishmael said: I said to Metatron, “Why are you called by the name of your Creator with seventy names? And why are you greater than all the princes, higher than all the angels, wiser than all the servants, more honored than all the prophets, and more powerful than all the legions in greatness, conduct, and glory?” 

He answered and said to me: “Because I am **Enoch, the son of Jared**. When the generation of the Flood sinned and rebelled in their deeds, saying to God, ‘Depart from us,’ I was taken from among them to be a witness against them in the highest heights, to remain a witness for all eternity.”

Behold, Enoch is a witness for the ages, for he did not sin; therefore, he merited all the holy glory. Ultimately, he sustains all the inhabitants of the world. Had the first man, **Adam**, not sinned, he too would have been worthy of all this holy glory. For what the first man lost through his sin, **Wisdom** <note>Chokhmah</note>—which had been established within him to sustain him—was returned and merited by Enoch through his attachment to God and his good deeds. Because he removed himself from sin and guarded himself in holiness, he merited all the glory and holy permanence.

And the holy teacher, **Rabbi Shimon bar Yochai** <note>The traditional author of the Zohar, referred to here as RSB"Y</note>, revealed this great secret in the *Midrash Shir HaShirim HaNe'elam*: He responded to those who say that death is "natural" to man because his body is composed of physical elements that must eventually break down and cease, as if God were unable to create him in a way that he would be living and enduring forever. 

Furthermore, they detailed this view that creation implies death. But it is not so; the intention of his creation was for perfection. God preceded them with what is necessary to know on this matter, as the verse says: *“I form light and create darkness, I make peace and create evil; I am the Lord who does all these things”* <note>Isaiah 45:7</note>. This means that He, may He be blessed, sustains opposites even though He Himself does not change. Death is a deficiency, but God intended for life and goodness and permanence, as was explained above. Our Sages of blessed memory said that God made it so that men should fear Him, as is known to the "wise of heart." The reason he did not deviate was to draw from the Light the attribute of Peace, and from the Darkness the attribute of Evil. Although His name is strong and no change can be established in Him, He is the cause of these opposites without being defined or multiplied by them. 

The heavens thunder from the beginning... he said that He already entrusted the repair of death and evil—which are drawn from the "hidden darkness"—into the hand of man. Man was commanded to fix the evil and the loss so that his own wickedness would not touch him. This is explained in the same way we explained it previously. 

And after investigating this great principle and foundation, he cried out against them and said: *“Woe to him who strives with his Maker!”* <note>Isaiah 45:9</note>. This is to say, it is a disgrace for a created being to say "What are you doing?" to God, or to cast a blemish upon creation. They say of the first man that he was not made to endure because he is a composite being that must eventually break apart, asking "How can a physical thing stand forever?" This would be a great deficiency in God's power and action, as if He had no power to grant him eternal life and permanence. They essentially say: "Why did He bring us into the world for vanity and terror?" 

They even say of His action: *“He has no hands”* <note>meaning, no power/agency</note>, claiming the world follows a set of necessary laws rather than the Divine Will.

<column-break/>

These people, by their own force, have turned away from **Wisdom**. When Wisdom is removed from a person, it becomes the cause of death. The soul and the spirit were intended to sustain the entire body, but they are destined to separate from it. This is what the scripture hints at in saying: *“But from the Tree of Knowledge of Good and Evil you shall not eat, for on the day you eat of it, you shall surely die”* <note>Genesis 2:17</note>. This "surely die" refers to the departure of the "breath of life" <note>Nishmat Chayim</note> from him. This is one death, and the ultimate separation of soul and spirit is the permanence of death. 

Death became necessary from the side of the "Obstacle" <note>referring to sin or the Sitra Achra</note>. When the holy voice of Wisdom is removed, the feet of man "go down to death." He who breaks the fence will be bitten by a serpent. This is like a king who destroys his own palace; when the kingship is removed, it becomes a place of death.

In the *Midrash Rabbah*, they detailed these matters further... <unclear>illegible phrases regarding the value of hidden things</unclear>... he shall live for eternity and not be separated by rebukes.

As it is written: *“I said in my heart concerning the estate of the sons of men, that God might clear them, and that they might see that they themselves are beasts”* <note>Ecclesiastes 3:18</note>. This means that there was a doubt concerning the children of men. When man sees the appearance of the heavens and the intention behind the creation of man, he wonders why man is lower than the ancient celestial beings. Even if man has a higher purpose, why should he lack the perfection given to those eternal beings who were created for his sake? 

The phrase "they are beasts to them" <note>Hebrew: *hemah lahem*</note> means that man places himself in that category; he was not meant to be so. For the Lord God intended to give him permanent existence, but through his sin, he was removed from that state. He was a "living soul," but he became like the "beasts that perish" <note>Psalm 49:13</note>. 

It has thus been clarified that man was not created to die; had he not sinned, he would have lived and endured forever. This is the opinion of the Sages of Truth. They said in *Vayikra Rabbah* (Chapter 20) and in *Midrash Kohelet*: Rabbi Isaac said that the First Man was intended to live and endure forever. He was told: "You were worthy to never sin and to live and endure forever." And in *Exodus Rabbah*: "O Lord, my God, my Holy One, we shall not die." Before the first man ate from the tree, he was not subject to death. Only because he faltered was it written of him "you shall surely die," to prove to all creatures that the Lord is just in His judgment.

In the teachings of the RSB"Y <note>Rabbi Shimon bar Yochai</note>, they said: Look and see, man was made to serve the King, to attach himself to Him, and to live through Him. All upper and lower beings were ready for him. He was given the "Tree of Life" and the "Tree of Knowledge." If Adam had guarded the command, he would have lived permanently. But he did not guard the command... and was punished.

All these sources teach us that if the first man had stood in his original intention and guarded the watch of his Creator, he would have lived and endured forever. His sin was the cause of his loss and the separation of his physical composition. Behold Enoch—of whom it is said *“And Enoch walked with God; and he was not”*—he returned to the state of the first man before the sin, and he is greater and more exalted than all the high princes of heaven.

# Part 4 | Chapter 21 | The Service
### Page 40

To his life and for good, etc. Just as the transformation from evil arose for the children of the East, all the more so from Adam. This was the primary intention of the Giver of the Torah, may He be blessed, and upon this condition, the recipient accepted it. Because this is the truth, the Torah did not explicitly mention the ultimate reward <note>The author argues that because the Torah's purpose was to restore natural immortality, "heavenly reward" didn't need to be stated as an external prize; it was the inherent result of the restoration.</note>. The intention of the Great Name in writing the Torah was to bestow goodness and life upon all things, just as it was originally—purely an act of Grace. 

It was already explained in the previous chapter that when Adam was first created, he was prepared for eternal existence in both body and soul. He delighted in the works of creation and took from them without toil or weariness. Had he remained worthy, existence and goodness would never have been removed from him. However, when he sinned, he brought death upon all who followed him. Through his sin, everyone was moved toward death, and there was no one left who could cling to the **Tree of Life** <note>original: עץ החיים (Etz HaChayim)</note>. Instead, humanity became attached to the **Tree of Death**, which necessitates passing away.

At the Giving of the Torah, when Israel stood at Mount Sinai to receive the Ten Commandments, the Torah was established as a repair for what Adam had corrupted. The Holy One, blessed be He, desired to grant merit to Israel and return them to the state of being "servants of the Lord," which is the source of all good and permanence. This is the meaning of the verse: *"Now therefore, if you will obey my voice indeed, and keep my covenant, then you shall be a treasured possession (Segulah) unto me above all people... and you shall be unto me a kingdom of priests, and a holy nation"* (Exodus 19:5-6). He promised to give them life and peace, showing them the way to return to His Will.

Understand this wisdom: God said to Adam, *"Because you listened to the voice of your wife."* Since the Torah was written to repair the world, it commands all to listen to *His* voice and accept His commandments. This "Voice" is the structural foundation of the world. Through the sin, death was caused for Adam and all descendants. Regarding the phrase *"And you shall keep my covenant (Brit),"* it is not apparent that Adam initially transgressed a covenant. However, in the chapter concerning monetary judges, Rabbi Isaac said: *"Adam was one who 'stretched his foreskin' <note>A Talmudic idiom (Sanhedrin 38b) suggesting Adam tried to hide his circumcision/covenantal mark to distance himself from God</note>."* It is written here, *"They transgressed the covenant,"* and elsewhere it says, *"He has broken My covenant."* Rabbi Nachman said he was an "apostate in principle," as it is written that they abandoned the covenant of the Lord. The truth is that sin added "uncircumcision" <term>Arlah: a spiritual barrier or impurity</term> and defilement to the world, harming the Holy Covenant.

Regarding the phrase *"A treasured possession (Segulah) from among all nations":* this is a level of kingship that is not subject to decay or loss. By cleaving to the Torah, the people achieve a perfect attachment (Dvekus) to God. Thus, you will not experience loss or destruction, for those who cling to Me are in the state of Eternal Life where death has no dominion. 

*"For all the earth is Mine":* I created all earthly and speaking things, including the human body. Though the body is composed of elements that tend toward decay, my Will can sustain it. Obeying My voice and keeping My covenant is the "salt" that preserves things that would otherwise perish. Everything was created through My Name; when My Name is shared through your actions, it grants the created world eternal existence. 

Furthermore, *"For all the earth is Mine"* refers to the fact that one who is constantly attached to God in service <note>original: עבודה (Avodah)</note> becomes a "treasure." Just as one might worry, "What shall we eat?" God answers that the "whole earth is Mine." The soul will lack nothing, for it inherits the "property of the Father" without the labor usually required for physical tasks, which may be performed by others. Know this in wisdom.

<column-break/>

No one has power over him—meaning the hands of the Holy One, blessed be He, did not create him by mere whim, for if it were just by chance, all would be material. This "House" <note>The human body</note> is for the Name, and it is right that the Creator of all, by His Will, made the matter of the "Holy One of Israel" and his holy knowledge. Even before you began, He knew all thoughts. If there were any lack in His wisdom, there would be a separation from the Divine possession. 

What the sages rely upon is that the "Essence" <note>original: עצמי (Atzmi)</note> made the judgment by Will. Regarding the physical things that are temporary, I created them—meaning I created Adam with the potential for eternal existence through Holy Wisdom. I agreed that by My Will, he would be saved from earthly decay and rise from destruction to permanence. 

The proof for this is the verse: *"My hand also has laid the foundation of the earth, and my right hand has spanned the heavens"* (Isaiah 48:13). Behold, they are composed of "body" and "soul" (matter and form) and yet they are eternal. Even though they are composite, Wisdom keeps them existing forever. 

Our Rabbis, of blessed memory, interpreted: *"He shall call to the heavens from above"*—this is the soul; *"and to the earth, that he may judge his people"*—this is the body (Psalm 50:4). Without the Divine creative power, the body would be nothing but skin, flesh, bones, and sinews. But it is a **Holy Garment** <note>original: מלבוש הקדש (Levush HaKodesh)</note>. As it says: *"You have clothed me with skin and flesh"* (Job 10:11). The totality is called "Adam" only when the body is joined to the soul. Death is nullified by the Wisdom of the hidden God. This is the intention of this chapter.

# Chapter 21
Just as the **Supernal Torah** <note>The primordial, spiritual Torah</note> is the "Written Vision," we have said that it encompasses the highest Wisdom. It is the "Unique Name" (Tetragrammaton) and is called "Torah" because it instructs (*moreh*) and reveals the commandments, statutes, and the law of the One, as explained in Chapter 15. 

Similarly, this physical Torah that was placed before the children of Israel points toward the place from which it was gazed upon—the Spiritual Supernal Torah. It is Israel's reception of the Unique Name. In the Midrash of Rabbi Shimon bar Yochai (the Zohar), it says: *"And the Lord showed him a tree"* (Exodus 15:25)—the Tree is the Torah. It is the "Tree of Life." The Torah is the Holy One, blessed be He, literally. Those who perform its deeds and hold fast to it are holding fast to the Name of the Lord.

Because it branches out from the light of the "Supernal Living One" <note>The Sefirah of Binah</note>, it is called the **Tree of Life**. In the realm of **Understanding** (Binah), it is also called the Tree of Life, meaning that with it, there is no death or destruction. It is a "Torah of Life," a purposeful existence, for it was emanated from the Source of Life. It was drawn down so that those who perform its commandments would have permanence. 

We should not say that it only "lengthens the life" of one who hasn't sinned, but rather that it affects the very body of man to prevent the "natural death" that usually results from being a composite of elements. This is why Enoch and Elijah, and other righteous who did not sin, though they "died" in a sense, are alive in the Garden of Eden. One who cleaves to the Torah, which is the Tree of Life, is not ruled over by death. 

As it says in the Zohar on Parashat Behar: *"What does it mean to be 'cleaving' (aduku) to the Torah?"*...

It posits that the Torah is not merely a book of laws but is ontologically identical to God’s Name and serves as a preservation "salt" against physical decay.</summary>

# The Service | Chapter 4
## Part 4 | Chapter 4

One should direct their intention, both in the performance of all the commandments and in refraining from transgressing any of the prohibitions warned of by the Blessed Name, toward enslaving oneself to Him in all ways—both right and left <note>Refers to the "Right" (mercy/positive acts) and "Left" (judgment/restraint).</note>. One must lead their body upward to this worthy rank, for it was for this purpose that man was chosen based on his form and his mystery. This was alluded to in the verse, "Man is born to toil" <note>Job 5:7</note>, and Solomon said, "All the toil of man is for his mouth" <note>Ecclesiastes 6:7</note>, and so on. Let this suffice regarding these three pillars <note>original: שלש פינות (three corners/foundations)</note> which stand as the columns of the world, upon which all of existence in its entirety depends. 

Through the Torah of the Blessed Name and the fulfillment of its commandments, one recognizes and knows that for this they were created, and that this was the will of the Blessed Name in creating this lower world. Nor is it a disgrace or a slight to the glory of the Blessed Name that His ultimate intention would be for the benefit of the lowly human species. For the elevation and the change occurring in the recipients <note>i.e., humans being improved by God's light</note> is not a flaw in the nature of the Giver. He is the Absolute Good, and He desires to bestow His goodness and complete grace upon all creatures in general, and upon man in particular. This is absolute kindness on His part, for the Simple Will <note>A philosophical term for God's unchanging nature.</note>, when bestowing goodness, does not change despite the variations in how the recipients receive it. 

Humility and lowliness on the part of the Supreme Giver are actually the essence of His majesty and dominion, for there is no greater kindness than when the Blessed God turns toward the lowly to do good for them and to bring them back from the state of death to the state of life, so they may share in the delights of the celestial beings and beautify the canopy of His glory. This is what King David, peace be upon him, marveled at when he said: *O Lord, our Lord, how majestic is Your name in all the earth, You who have set Your glory above the heavens! Out of the mouth of babes and sucklings You have established strength.* <note>Psalm 8:2-3</note> Behold the order of the levels and ranks upward; he explains that the Blessed Name bestowed His glory upon the heavens, which are at the highest rank, yet this strength is established through the "babes and sucklings" below in the lowly rank. For it is there that the supreme rank is found; the whole does not depend on the heavens, but on lowly man. 

He further says: *What is man that You are mindful of him, and the son of man that You visit him? Yet You have made him a little lower than the angels.* <note>Psalm 8:5-6</note> He ordered these levels against one another because of man, as it is written: *The birds of the heavens and the fish of the sea.* <note>Psalm 8:9</note> Here is the secret of the rank in the creation of man compared to the celestial beings: because man was created in the **Image of God** <note>original: צלם אלהים (Tzelem Elohim)</note> even though he is lowly below. In the creation of man, the two ranks—upper and lower—were completed, as we explained regarding the mystery of man. Behold, man carries both ranks, and for this the scripture says: *For the work of a man He will pay him back* <note>Job 34:11</note>, and so on. 

He marveled further at these ranks, noting that while the Blessed Name is at the ultimate peak of the highest rank, He still supervises lowly man and shows him the path he should walk, informing him that the supreme protection and governance are bestowed upon him. This is what the Blessed Name said to our teacher Moses, peace be upon him: *Behold, I send an angel before you to guard you on the way* <note>Exodus 23:20</note>. For the angel and the supreme governance are humbled and made lower before this holy rank that stands on the earth but whose head reaches the heavens. This is the most honored rank of all the upper and lower levels. Therefore, the Holy One, blessed be He, and His heavenly court were before him and below him <note>Interpretive note: The author suggests that the human soul, when perfected, reaches a state that the divine focus serves and orbits.</note>. The secret of this rank, which is holier than all holiness and the bearer of the **Throne of Glory** <note>original: כסא הכבוד (Kisse HaKavod)</note>, was man. Behold, the Blessed Name in His goodness and complete will created this world so that the rank of human beings would come into existence, so they might attain pleasure and supreme wisdom and merit what is worthy for them through His complete goodness and the will of His soul and the mystery of existence...

# Chapter 21 | The Part on Divine Service

## Chapter 21

...and so too your friends and your vineyards, etc. As it is said: "You shall be called the priests of the Lord, the ministers of our God shall be told of you" <note>Isaiah 61:6</note>. And it says: "And you shall be to Me a kingdom of priests" <note>Exodus 19:6</note>. For the choosing of Israel as His own is because of their wisdom, for they eat from the "High Table" <note>term: "High Table" (Shulchan Gavoah) — a metaphor for receiving sustenance directly from the Divine, like priests eating from altar offerings</note>. This love from the Merciful One is toward me and toward those who were priests, ministers who serve. This service is itself the "Lordship." And it says, "A kingdom of priests and a holy nation" <note>Exodus 19:6</note>, in the sense of "You shall be holy" <note>Leviticus 19:2</note>, meaning you shall be removed from all affairs of the body for the sake of Divine Service and the Foundation. This is the path to the preservation of the body, for the soul is the essence and is elevated through its cleaving [to God]. The body is not the primary essence; it is merely a garment or an outer shell for the soul, and the soul sustains it with its life-force. In the end, everything will be repaired and sustained. This was already explained in the chapter on the "Excellence of the Dwelling" in this book. If so, in its divisions, holiness is the preservation, and these physical matters are sustained. Thus our Sages, of blessed memory, detailed it in the chapter titled "Helek" <note>The eleventh chapter of Tractate Sanhedrin in the Talmud</note>: "It is said of him, 'He who is left in Zion... shall be called holy' <note>Isaiah 4:3</note>—just as the Holy One lives forever, so too do they live forever."

Behold, all this was to repair the damage of his sin, for he <note>Adam</note> would not have seen corruption if he had listened to the voice of the Lord. But because he listened to the voice of his wife, these other creatures and the teeth of death rose up against him and all who came after him, and he became like the beasts that perish. But when Israel received the Torah, they restored their standing to its original state, and the world was perfected, and their sorrows and wars ceased. As it says in the chapter "Ein Ma'amidin" <note>Tractate Avodah Zarah 22b</note> and in the Midrash: "I said, 'You are angels/gods'" <note>Psalm 82:6</note>. Had Israel waited at the bottom [of the mountain] and not performed that act <note>the sin of the Golden Calf</note>, there would have been no exile and the Angel of Death would have had no power over them. For what does the verse say? "And the writing was the writing of God, engraved <note>original: "harut"</note> upon the tablets" <note>Exodus 32:16</note>. Rabbi Yehuda and Rabbi Nehemiah disagree: Rabbi Yehuda says it means "Freedom <note>original: "herut" — a wordplay on "harut" (engraved)</note> from the kingdoms [exile]," and Rabbi Nehemiah says it means "Freedom from the Angel of Death." They were entitled to every kind of good and happiness that flows from the reception of the Torah. By "freedom from kingdoms," the intention was that they would be exempt from the tax of the kings along with what they would receive. By "freedom from the Angel of Death," the intention was regarding the preservation and the spiritual levels that would be visible in them as a "holy nation," as we have established there. And so it says regarding the gift of Oholiab <note>a master craftsman of the Tabernacle</note>: he asked from the Creator that they should be alive and exist forever. Behold, because of their great cleaving to all the paths of life and the good, they reached a level of greatness and were honored with the "crowns" we mentioned above in our wisdom.

And they said in the Mekhilta: "Even the sword of the enemy... on this condition Israel stood at Mount Sinai: on the condition that the Angel of Death would not rule over them, as it is written: 'I said, you are gods...' But you corrupted your deeds; 'Indeed, like Adam you shall die'" <note>Psalm 82:6-7</note>. And in the Midrash on Ruth: Their minds were at ease, and Israel was crowned from behind and crowned with engraved crowns. Once they performed the act of the Calf, they were stripped [of them]. Previously, their "freedom" was written on the tablets of stone, filled with all kinds of beauty. They returned from the Angel of Death, they returned from the subjugation of kingdoms, they returned from all the evil diseases of the world. Once they sinned with the Calf, they broke it all and descended to the world's common state, like other people. And they said: "I said 'gods'—I intended for you to be like the ministering angels..." What beauties and merits were given to Israel! But now, the crowns are empty, to be taken by the Destroyer <note>original: "mashchit"</note>. Then a cry went out over them: "Woe to them, for they have moved away from Me!" <note>Hosea 7:13</note>. Woe to them, for they did not remain in their faithfulness to their Creator. Behold, the Torah is a book that removes death, for the Torah is life and there is no death in it. And it is also freedom from the kingdoms, for the Material <note>original: "Homer"</note> awakens its power above, which is all darkness, and that is the Angel of Death, and that is the power of the nations. And that power is the appointed prince over them and they are under his authority below. But with the fulfillment of the Torah, there is no power for anything that is dark to be awakened at all, and no power will rule over those who keep it. Therefore, the nations would not rule over them below, but rather they [Israel] would rule over their enemies.

Furthermore, they said in the Midrash on Exodus: "What is this? If the Angel of Death comes and says before the Holy One, blessed be He, 'Why did You create me in this world?' He says to him: 'I sent you over every nation in the world, except for this nation, over which I have no authority, for I have 'engraved' <note>harut</note> my laws upon the tablets.'" And regarding what they said, "They broke it all and descended to the world's state," etc., the Midrash on Exodus (Parashah 32) says: "What is the matter that you told? The tablets were written in such a way..."

<column-break/>

...they broke and the good was lost. For the material and the darkness and the angel of darkness—all of these are [usually] masters over all, but here [at Sinai] they were not. So we find in the Prophets that when Israel transgressed at the place of "the wandering of the star," <note>unclear reference, possibly a corruption of a place name or astrological event</note> it was as if they died, and that was their downfall. They were then captured in exile among the nations who come from the side of that [darkness] in which they sinned. And so it was with the First Man: when he sinned, he was stripped of the "garment of light" that was upon him and became subject to death.

In the first chapter of [Tractate] Avodah Zarah: "In the days of the Good, and in our first state, they did not sin. Had they not sinned, they would never have moved [from life], as it says: 'I said you are gods... but indeed like Adam you shall die.'" They asked there: "If you say they would never have died, how would the commandment 'Be fruitful and multiply' be fulfilled?" They answered: by the merit of the commandments. From this, we see that in every place where it mentions "living" in the Torah, such as "a man shall do them and live by them" <note>Leviticus 18:5</note>, it refers to the physical preservation of the body. If they had merited, they would have lived forever. This is the Great Secret: the life that is drawn to the body through the performance of the Torah and the commandments. It says: "And you shall keep My statutes and My laws, which a man shall do and live by them." It seems to me that this was the intention of Onkelos <note>The famous 2nd-century translator of the Torah into Aramaic</note> when he translated it as "life of the world" <note>original: "chayei alma" — usually meaning the afterlife</note>. This is not like the "living" mentioned regarding Reuben <note>Deuteronomy 33:6</note>. For when it is said regarding Reuben, the commentators already explained that it is impossible to explain it as anything other than the World to Come. But if we say the intention here is only the World to Come, that was not the primary intent of the verse. Rather, even though he translated it that way, he meant it as the foundation for what follows. So too, what our Sages derived from "and live by them"—that it refers to the World to Come—and "that your days may be long"—in the world that is entirely long—and "that it may be well with you"—in the world that is entirely good—all these derivations were only because the commandments are spiritual. They wanted to connect the unique excellence of the soul's preservation to the life of the World to Come.

However, the plain meaning and the primary intent of the Torah is about life in this world. Therefore, it does not explicitly mention the "reward of the soul" <note>spiritual afterlife</note> anywhere, because it was obvious that by its nature, the Torah sustains the soul with spiritual life. Its main innovation <note>original: "hiddush"</note> is that it could have removed death [from the body]. The intention for Israel was "and live by them" in the World to Come, as well as "long days" and "goodness." This means that if the body and soul had been prepared to receive the reward of the commandments in this world, then the body would not have been treated as mere matter. Furthermore, the Great Secret is the preservation of the soul and its dwelling in the body through the practice of Torah and the fulfillment of its commandments. It says: "And I will set My Tabernacle among you, and My soul shall not loathe you" <note>Leviticus 26:11</note>. The hint here is "My Tabernacle," which is the Shekhinah <note>the Divine Presence</note> that dwells within to preserve the soul. Just as the soul sustains the body, so the Shekhinah is the "soul" of Israel. As long as it dwells among them through their perfect service and good deeds, they are alive and sustained in excellence, greatness, and supernal pleasure. And it says "My soul shall not loathe you"—this is like what is said, "And He breathed into his nostrils the breath of life, and man became a living soul" <note>Genesis 2:7</note>. This means: My soul, which is the Holy Spirit, will not find you repulsive so as to vomit you out or reject you, separating from the body. Rather, it will remain bound to it forever. The intention was that they would not die, but would be alive and exist forever. Because of this, the "reward of the soul" is not explicitly mentioned in the Torah as a separate promise, because there was no need; the goal was to spiritually refine and sustain the soul and body together forever. This is what we have explained in this chapter.

### Chapter 22

->**The one who occupies himself with Torah and fulfills its commandments with intention**<-
->**is joined to the Supernal World, which is the secret of the Male and the Female**<- <note>A Kabbalistic reference to the balance of Divine attributes</note>

It explains that the sin of the Golden Calf reintroduced death, but the Torah remains the "elixir of life" that can spiritually refine the body and soul.</summary>

->Chapter 23: The Part on Divine Service<-

...if to include everything, and this is sufficient for the one who understands. With this, all doubts are resolved, and it has been clarified what the intention was from the beginning of time regarding the removal of the [physical] skin; it will surely happen, and death does not prevent this. This is what we sought to clarify in this chapter.

# Chapter 23

The philosophers <note>literally "scholars of research"</note> debated the names of the soul. They said it is the "passive intellect," the "knower," and the "living force," because it receives more than a "wild ass's colt" <note>a reference to Job 11:12, meaning a person born without knowledge</note> who does not know or understand. As long as the body continues to grow, the soul grows in wisdom. This indicates that the soul does not dwell in the spirit alone; for if the soul were merely a product of the body's physical temperament <note>term: "Mizag" — the balance of bodily humors/elements</note>, it would follow that the body, through its maturity, would naturally produce its own knowledge. But as seen in the words of Maimonides <note>original: "the Rambam"</note> in Chapter 8 of the *Eight Chapters* <note>Maimonides' introduction to the Ethics of the Fathers</note>, where he discusses the wisdom of the soul: Know that besides the one soul previously mentioned, it was rooted in matter, and the intellect does not descend [automatically]. If the soul does not reach its ultimate purpose, its existence is considered "in vain." 

Our Sages, of blessed memory—who received wisdom from the mouths of the true prophets—said these things according to their literal meaning. They knew the truth clearly: that the soul is separate from the body, and from the soul the body receives its completion. This is testified to us by the verse: "And He breathed into his nostrils the breath of life" <note>Genesis 2:7</note>. This informs us of the place from which it lives. They knew that it is a "portion of God from above" <note>term: "Helek Elokah mi-Ma'al" — the mystical concept that the human soul is a literal spark of the Divine</note>.

In the chapter "The Prayer" <note>likely referring to a section in the Midrash or Talmud</note>, they said: A light is placed at the child's head [in the womb], and it looks from one end of the world to the other. It is taught the entire Torah... and when the time comes to enter the atmosphere of the world, an angel comes and strikes it on its mouth, making it forget the entire Torah. 

Why is it shown the world from end to end? This matches what we explained about the soul's capacity. The Sages explained this through the way of the Kabbalah <note>original: "Kabbalah" — here meaning the received tradition</note>. They said the light on its head is a hint to its soul, which shines with Supernal Wisdom. By saying it is taught the entire Torah, they are teaching us that wisdom and the Torah are the soul's fulfillment, so it may exist if it merits to serve God.

In the Midrash, it is said concerning the soul: Even before they descend to this world, they are all grown before the Holy One, Blessed be He, in the exact same image they will have in this world. And if they were not holy, they would not descend to the world. They also said in the Midrash on the portion *Pekudei*: An angel shows the soul Paradise <note>original: "Gan Eden"</note> and shows the righteous sitting there with crowns on their heads. The angel says: "Know who these are... these were formed like you in the womb, and they went out into the world and observed the commandments of the Holy One." Then the angel takes the soul to Hell <note>original: "Gehenna"</note> and shows the wicked being punished by angels of destruction... and the angel says: "Be righteous and not wicked, so that you may live." And when the time comes to go out into the world, the angel strikes it and makes it forget...

<column-break/>

...all that it saw, and leads it out into the world. Because of this, the infant cries upon entering the world. Until here [is the quote].

Behold, it is clarified that the soul is prepared to receive wisdom, and every person is wise and knowing before coming into the body. The reason the body is not wise from the womb is because the angel strikes the mouth and removes the knowledge, making the person forget the greatness of the Creator. The reason for this—as has already been clarified in this chapter—is that the world is prepared in the likeness of the "Upper Glory." A person's task is to repair that Glory through Torah and the delight of those who occupy themselves with it. This is achieved through the study of true wisdom received from the prophets and by fulfilling the commandments.

If a person entered the world already knowing and remembering everything they had seen and learned in the womb, there would be no room for human effort in "repairing the Glory," nor would there be prayer with true intention toward the Unity [of God]. The soul is brought into the person to engage in the Unity and in Divine Service, which would not be possible if everything were already known by nature. To allow for choice and merit, the child must forget.

Throughout life, a person looks to restore what was forgotten in the womb and to remember what was once known. Through the struggle to regain this wisdom, the person's soul is refined. This is why a person must toil in the words of Torah.

It has been clarified, then, that the soul does not start as a "blank slate" <note>literally "not as a thing of no knowledge"</note>, but was a very thin spiritual entity, full of intellect and wisdom before descending. The "Divine Service" is to work to regain that wisdom. 

Maimonides, in Chapter 6 of the *Laws of the Foundations of the Torah*, says: "When we say 'in our image and likeness' <note>Genesis 1:26</note>, it refers to the form <note>term: "Tzurah" — the essential intellectual nature of a thing</note> that knows and attains conceptual ideas." He says further: "The soul knows and attains the truths... and knows the Creator of all." In Chapter 8 of the *Laws of Repentance*, he says: "The 'soul' mentioned in this context is not the life-force needed for the body, but the 'Form of the Soul,' which is the knowledge it acquired according to its capacity." He explains that the "crowns on their heads" mentioned by the Sages refers to the knowledge they attained, which is the "crown" that accompanies them into the afterlife. 

Thus, the knowledge the soul attains and the refinement of its actions are the "vessel" and the "crown." This is the secret of what the ancients said about bringing the soul from potential to actual through the wisdom of the commandments.

<meta>The previous page was labeled Chapter 23, but the heading on this page identifies it as Chapter 22. The text continues the theological investigation into the purpose of the soul's descent into the physical world, moving from the definitions of the soul to the ethical and mystical implications of its existence on Earth.</meta>

->Part of Divine Service, Chapter 22<-

As I have written, etc., and for my daughter <note>referring to the soul</note> like a lamp lit from below, and through this, the power of the **Ark of the Covenant** <note>original: "Aron HaBerit"</note>. For from the Ark of the Covenant [souls] emerge, and were it not for the "House," etc. Our Sages of blessed memory <note>original: "Zal"</note> in the chapter *Ein Dorshin* <note>Hagigah 12b</note> said: *Arabot* <note>the seventh and highest heaven</note> is that in which there is Righteousness, Justice, and Charity, the treasures of life, the treasures of peace, the treasures of blessing, and the souls of the righteous—meaning those who completed [their mission] and ascended in peace to their **Shekhinah** <note>the Divine Presence</note>—and the spirits and souls that are destined to be created—meaning to dwell in the bodies of human beings. And we have explained *Arabot* in the well [of wisdom] in Chapter 2, regarding the "Lesson" <note>term: "Lekach"</note>, that it is the "Righteous One, the Life of the Worlds," and from it, the Ark of the Covenant begins. 

If so, why were they created? For they [the souls] see [God's light in heaven], and perhaps it would be better for them to dwell there. But this doubt is resolved by the addition we wrote: that the souls need their completion <note>term: "Halamutan," perfection or integration</note> by being a "lamp from above" and a "lamp from below" to complete the **Glory** <note>term: "Kavod," often referring to the manifestation of the Divine</note>. Its vitality is inclusive of everything, and this is a "higher need" <note>original: "tzorech gavoah"</note>. If they did not go out, this purpose would not be achieved in the spheres, and the intention of their creation would not be tested. Rather, this reason exists in several essences in the explanation of the Names of "the God of the Heavens," so that there should be no turning back from the good way. It would have been more pleasurable than death, for it was meant "to produce grapes, but it produced wild grapes" <note>a reference to Isaiah 5:2, meaning the soul was meant for good but may fail</note>. This is also a wretched doubt for the living. 

The removal of this doubt is in the explanation that the Torah and the Commandments were given to that which is within the "Protection" <note>meaning the physical world/body</note> to repair that which they corrupted. The Torah was handed into the hand of man, and he shall "choose life" and complete the intention of their creation—and what is this repair? It is for the **Glory** and its completion. And if he sins, he shall repair it through **Repentance** <note>original: "Teshuvah"</note>. In the tractate *Arakhin*, Chapter 8 <note>actually Eruvin 13b</note>, it was taught: For two and a half years, the House of Shammai and the House of Hillel disagreed. These said: It would have been more comfortable <note>better</note> for man not to have been created than to have been created. And those said: It is more comfortable for man to have been created than not to have been created. They voted and concluded: It is more comfortable for man not to have been created than to have been created; but now that he has been created, let him examine his [past] deeds <note>original: "yefashpesh b'ma'asav"</note>. Others say: let him scrutinize his [ongoing] deeds <note>original: "yemashmesh b'ma'asav"</note>. 

See what we have written on this, for those who say it is better not to have been created speak from the perspective of the "Wrath" and the **Satan** who stands at his right hand to accuse him and twist him toward the "husk" <note>term: "Kelipah," the shell of evil/impurity</note>, the opposite of why he was created. It would be better for him to stay there [in heaven] and not come to increase transgression and multiply sin against his God. [Man's] purpose is to unify the "Wise One" <note>God</note> and to separate [evil] from within, but [sin] is the opposite of what was intended in their creation. And those who say it is better to have been created do so because [God] did not create the Evil Inclination <note>original: "Yetzer Ha-Ra"</note> for it to rule; rather, the power and the path given to man are the main purpose. This is a benefit to himself, to merit [the world to come], and these [commandments] guide him in the straight path to complete the intended purpose, which is the repair and perfection of the **Glory**. They voted and concluded it is better not to have been created, because removing sins from the path is very difficult, and they may fall into evil. But now that he is created, "let him examine his deeds"—let him check himself for transgressions he has already committed and destroy them through repentance, and by this, he shall repair. The Torah and Commandments will add to the health he has received... and "some say let him scrutinize his deeds"—meaning to cast his eyes upon his ways and not be mindless at all, being careful in his actions. He should remember and take to heart the intention of his creation, which is "Observance and Service," and complete it. 

Regarding this matter, they said that his life is for completion through prayer at every single hour, so that his mind should not be distracted at all, so that he may take to heart that he is a "vessel of Glory" and a dwelling for the **Shekhinah**. He should sanctify himself in his actions and purify himself in his thoughts. This is what they meant by "scrutinize his deeds," and from all his scrutinizing, it will be found that it is "better for him to have been created." We find in Chapter 4 <note>of Pirkei Avot</note>: Rabbi Yaakov says, "This world is like a **corridor** <note>original: "prozdor"</note> before the World to Come. Prepare yourself in the corridor so that you may enter the **banquet hall** <note>original: "traklin"</note>." He used to say: "One hour of repentance and good deeds in this world is better than all the life of the World to Come; and one hour of satisfaction <note>original: "korat ruach"</note> in the World to Come is better than all the life of this world." This holy secret is everything we have said in these high traditions. For in saying "Prepare yourself in the corridor," it refers to the repair of the soul, which must be inclusive of both the "higher" and "lower," as explained above. And in saying "One hour is better, etc.," he comes to awaken the prayers...

<column-break/>

...behold the reason for the soul’s coming, which is the purpose we brought above. For the reason for its coming is for its own standing. And I have placed a thought in this: in "shame" <note>meaning the "bread of shame," receiving without earning</note> one will not be protected from the straight path. For by saying "one hour [of repentance]... is better than all the life of the World to Come," he resolved the first doubt. For the reason for the soul's coming is to unify the "Unique Name" and so they may delight in the coming of the "Ark of All" from above to below. Behold, the soul is comprised of all "Distinctions" <note>term: "Havdalin," levels of spiritual reality</note>, and this is the striving for the **Glory** as we wrote, as it has been explained. While it was in its place before its arrival, it was part of all that light of the World to Come, and its vitality exists because it already came from the "Six Days of Creation." 

As they said in the Midrash, and all the "Two Writings" <note>possibly a reference to the two tablets or two versions of a text</note> are by the Holy One, blessed be He, until "everyone knows grace." And its fruit is not as Rabbi Yosef Albo wrote in Chapter 38 of the *Investigation* <note>Sefer Ha-Ikkarim</note>... regarding the performance of commandments as a "sale." He did not understand the "Observance," nor the explanation of the Ramban <note>Nahmanides</note> upon it. Behold, the soul in this world serves the intentions of **Unification** <note>original: "Yichud"</note> and the spreading of perfect existence. The Glory is not diminished, and in the way we have explained everything, choosing to complete all this—behold, one hour of his pleasure in completing this perfection is better than all the life of the World to Come [that existed] before, because all of this is achieved while it is there [in the body]. 

There is a reason for this. Repentance, which he mentioned, protects the soul just as the merchant protects himself from the sun. The reason is that in the World to Come, God is a metaphor <note>meaning God is the source</note>, and behold, he is careful and does not turn away with his dwelling, and there is no "Repentance" there. Furthermore, there is an added excellence and a difficult blow: "good deeds," which are the way to complete what was meant for its perfection. And this is better in the first [this world] than in the second [the next world] because physical matter is built upon the Name through thought.

And behold, the second doubt is resolved, and its vitality—which we mentioned in the explanation of the first doubt—in his language, he resolved the two doubts. By saying "One hour of satisfaction in the World to Come is better than all the life of this world," it is said regarding a specific doubt. For after the soul's creation into a living man to unify the Great Name, to perform His service, and to repair the **Glory**—which is the place of the intended purpose—it would be fitting that the pleasure of the service, the unification, and the repair of the Glory should be greater than all those doubts. Should it not be the law that the one who serves should live in purity? 

And it includes names for every chapter... "You shall be holy" <note>Leviticus 19:2</note>, and likewise, "This is the thing you shall do to them to sanctify them to serve as priests" <note>Exodus 29:1</note>. Regarding the verse "You shall be holy," they said: it is a high degree, for "I the Lord your God am holy." The intention here is what we said: since the soul comes from the "Holy Shekhinah," the intention is the repair of the Glory. It would be fitting that it remains in death so that the holiness may be elevated through the "Pause" <note>term: "Hefsek," the break from physicality</note> which the Holy One, blessed be He, [ordained]. For this, he said: "One hour of satisfaction in the World to Come is better"—referring to this purpose, which is the repair of the Glory when the soul is inclusive and complete. This is not the case while it is alive in this world, for although it guides and repairs the Name, the Glory is not yet inclusive of all the "Distinctions" until the soul separates from the body and returns to the place from which it came, which is the **Ark of the Covenant**, as we wrote above. This is the "Satisfaction" <note>original: "Korat," meaning cooling or tranquility</note>. And they said "satisfaction" based on the verse: "Happy is he whose labor is in the Torah and who brings satisfaction <note>original: "nachat ruach"</note> to his Creator." Also, the soul that ascends to what the Prophet said: "No eye has seen, O God, besides You" <note>Isaiah 64:3</note>—which it cannot perceive until it strips off the "Grease" <note>meaning the physical fats/matter</note> and clothes itself in the "Garment of Holiness" of good deeds.

> According to the Midrash of Rabbi Shimon bar Yochai <note>original: "Rashbi"</note>, peace be upon him: "No one is far from Him... as long as it dwells in this body. But once it strips off this body of this world and clothes itself in another garment which is in the likeness of this world, then it sees and returns, and clothes itself at the 'Gate of the Expanses of the Worlds,' that which it could not see or establish while in this world at all. And when it is clothed in the 'Garment of Truth' <note>original: "Nishtala de-Kashut"</note> that belongs to that world, how many beauties and how many delights are there!"

This is the intention of saying: "One hour of satisfaction in the World to Come is better than all the life of this world." And this is sufficient for what [remains]...

<summary>This page explores the purpose of the soul's descent into the physical world, arguing that although it is better for the soul to be in heaven, it enters the body to repair the "Divine Glory" and earn its reward through Torah and repentance. It reconciles the classic paradox from Pirkei Avot regarding whether this world or the next is "better" by explaining the unique spiritual achievements possible only in a physical state.</summary>

<meta>This page continues the discussion from Chapter 24 regarding the soul's labor in the physical world and begins Chapter 25, which focuses on the "spiritual garments" the soul acquires through its actions and intentions.</meta>

# Chapter 24: The Part of Service / Chapter 25 | 43

One who labors below—and let the intention be that in his way he serves the Name of the King—this is the **exaltation of holiness**. It is the **Secret of the Union** <note>term: "Sod HaYichud," the mystical unification of Divine attributes</note>, and to him, it is a sequential secret, and for Israel, it is a surrounding secret, crowned in "nursing" <note>term: "Yenika," receiving spiritual sustenance</note>, receiving and drawing close to His radiance according to the **Secret of the Causes** <note>the principle that human action triggers divine reaction</note> and the Union in times of distress.

And after this, he returns and writes: one becomes unified with his Creator through the study of Torah. For anyone who studies the Torah, his Creator bestows "grace" <note>term: "Hesed"</note> upon him, as it is written: *“There is none like God, O Jeshurun, who rides the heavens in your help, and in His excellency on the skies”* <note>Deuteronomy 33:26</note>. This "riding of the skies" refers to dwelling in inner chambers, as we translate the verse *“Who rides in the highest heavens of old.”* And regarding the **Cup of Kingship** <note>likely referring to the Sephirah of Malkhut</note>, we are strong in the highest heavens. The correct understanding is that this alludes to the **Radiance of Glory** <note>original: "Ziv HaKavod"</note> which emerges in secret... 

At the end of Chapter 19, he calls to those who are weary from the burden of the crown and their labor in this world, and the depth of the spirit's spirit. It is possible that with **pure intention** <note>term: "Kavana Lishma," doing a commandment for its own sake</note> one unifies the Name in His glory, and to him descends the **Will** from the Source toward the abundance and the **Great Light**.

Whoever occupies himself with the Torah for its own sake brings **peace to the Upper Assembly** and to the **Lower Assembly** <note>original: "Pamilya shel Ma'ala u-Pamilya shel Mata," the heavenly and earthly entourages</note>, as it is said: *“Or let him take hold of My strength, that he may make peace with Me; and he shall make peace with Me”* <note>Isaiah 27:5</note>. **Rav** said: It is as if he built the **Upper Palace** and the **Lower Palace** <note>term: "Palterin," from the Greek "praitorion," used in Rabbinic texts for a royal palace</note>. **Rabbi Yohanan** said: He protects the entire world, as it is written: *“And I have covered thee in the shadow of My hand”* <note>Isaiah 51:16</note>. **Levi** said: He even brings the **Redemption** <note>original: "Geulah"</note> near, as it is said: *“And to say unto Zion: Thou art My people”* <note>Isaiah 51:16</note>.

The Holy One alludes here that laboring in the Torah for its own sake and establishing the proper intention in one's path causes his permanence and the source of vitality of the **Great Name**. He establishes peace in the Upper Assembly—for peace is the secret of the "clinging" of all within the **Assembly of Israel** <note>term: "Knesset Yisrael," a mystical term for the Shekhinah</note>. And in the Lower Assembly, it is the secret of the "graceful beauty" so that they do not prosecute above... All of this is according to the preparations he made in his standing, and his merit to receive from his "waiting." 

These are the six pillars of the Sanctuary. He builds the Upper Palace, which is the Union of the Name in the construction of our "outer" parts, and he builds the Lower Palace, which is toward the surrounding and the upper land. Thus, he protects the whole world and brings the Redemption near, both above and below. In this totality, all who merit to explain the depth of the Torah for its own sake are joined as one.

<margin>Rashbi <note>Rabbi Shimon bar Yochai</note> Chapter 2</margin>

And like a king speaking in a decree, in this way the intention is caused through him, and in the way it is transmitted to the intellect above. Thus, the action is refined, and all this perfection also falls upon this—to intend in the performance of the **Commandment** <note>term: "Mitzvah"</note> and the entire Union. He should intend the vitality of the **Great Name** with the intention that will be clarified later. Through this, the action below is elevated... just as we learned above that the thought is received above. One's service depends on being refined, and this is the secret of performing the commandment through thought.

As we established in the previous chapter, **Rabbi Hanina** said: "Anyone who occupies himself with a commandment through thought is not brought bad tidings," as it is said: *“Whoso keepeth the commandment shall feel no evil thing”* <note>Ecclesiastes 8:5</note>. And **Rabbi Assi**—or some say Rabbi Hanina—said: "Even if the Holy One, Blessed be He, decrees a decree, he [the righteous person] can nullify it," as it is written: *“Where the word of a king is, there is power; and who may say unto him: What doest thou?”* and immediately following: *“Whoso keepeth the commandment...”*

Since every human action, intention, knowledge, and wisdom are dependent on **Thought**, and His "garment" is fixed and placed before all—the **Infinite** <note>original: "Ein Sof"</note>—one must equalize everything to fix the thought and the intention in every word and deed. For he says that he unifies the Great Name in our vitality and intention. Whether in speech, action, or proper thought, one must equalize all to fix all upon the Infinite and to unify His Name within it. This is the ultimate purpose of all Divine service.

In the book of **Heikhalot** <note>The "Palaces," a genre of early mystical literature</note> at the beginning, [it says]: "I am the Holy Source of Rabbi Shimon bar Yochai, peace be upon him; behold the incense that sustains the upper and lower [worlds] entirely." This commandment must be fulfilled within His domain.

->For this reason, one should always whisper: Upon this, the tree of death was struck, and the fixation of all his thoughts.<-

<column-break/>

And like a burden, and you did not fulfill it in speech at all, but rather as it is written: "For every commandment is in its fulfillment." And through service in speech and action with intention in this way, behold, the deed, the intention, and the knowledge are brought to perfection. The intention below is like that which is above. This is the perfection, the objective, and the effect, as has been well clarified in all of this, and it is the primary focus of this chapter.

### Chapter 25

This **Soul** <note>term: "Nefesh"</note>, just as it needs every "vessel"—which is the **Body** in which it is mounted—in our perception and in all its actions and attributes (which are its powers), so too its completion in the perfection of deed, calculation, knowledge, and wisdom requires a connection. Without the completion of this vessel <note>the body</note>, it is impossible for the soul to be completed at all in that perfection which is its ultimate goal: to be included in all generalities and perfected with a **Higher Perfection**, prepared to be completed in Glory.

As has been clarified, it is impossible for the soul to receive the **Light of Glory** and the delight of its creation and the enjoyment granted to it for its thousand years of service without a "vessel" acting as a **mediator** <note>original: "memutza"</note>. Only then can it contain and absorb the light. This is what is bestowed in the light of the completions: if its thought, deed, intention, knowledge, and wisdom were [properly aligned], the soul would merit all levels of this delight, one above the other.

Therefore, for its service, it requires **two types of vessels**. One will be more "mighty" <note>original: "kabir"</note> than the other, and the relationship of vessel to vessel will be like the relationship of delight to delight. The first vessel is prepared through the fulfillment of all the **Commandments** and the occupation with **good deeds**. This is a vessel formed from the "ten [Sephirot]" in their general intention...

In the performance of every "Positive Commandment" <note>original: "Mitzvat Aseh"</note> for the sake of the Glory, one makes for themselves a **Spiritual Garment** <note>original: "Malbush Ruchani"</note> in the form of the body in which the soul was mounted. He will then enter the **Orchard** <note>term: "Pardes," referring to the celestial paradise</note> of dwelling and suckle from the radiance of that world, clothed in it, refined and clear, delighting in the pleasure of its repair. This garment is woven from all his deeds. Through labor in action, he merits to refine the soul to delight in the pleasure of its repair.

As the verse says: "Humility is to live and to be saved for the children of the King, the Lord of Hosts." When the soul was in its life, it was given a measure of holiness, and from Sabbath to Sabbath, we pray to be included in a garment that is even more refined and more spiritual than the first, to delight in the **Upper Delight** <note>original: "Eden HaElyon"</note>. This is impossible to merit except through the "Second [Garment]" acquired through the **Great Depth** of the intention of the Torah, the fulfillment of the commandments, and the intention within them at the time of their performance—the intention in service that causes "clinging" <note>term: "Devekut"</note>.

As we explained in the *Book of the System* <note>original: "Sefer HaMa'arekhet"</note> and made known the perfection of the secret of the "Effect," we find then that the soul requires **two types of garments** to merit **two types of delights** according to its service:
1. The first is made from the complete performance of the commandments and their fulfillment in actual deed.
2. The second is made from the **spirituality of the intention of the thought** appropriate for them.

With the first intention, one merits to delight in the **Lower Delight** <note>Eden of below</note>. With the second intention, one merits to delight in the **Upper Delight** <note>Eden of above</note>.

Regarding the **First Garment**, they wrote in the Midrash of Rabbi Shimon bar Yochai, peace be upon him: "Anyone who prepares himself in this world, the Angel of Death cannot strip him of his garment and this body, for that spirit is saved from this body by the Angel of Death and is clothed in another body, pleasant to the eye... and there is no power to the spirit except in that body." This is as we wrote above in Chapter 23.

Regarding the **Second Garment**, the holy fellowship of Rabbi Shimon bar Yochai wrote in the *Book of Palaces* <note>Sefer Heikhalot</note>, in the **Sixth Palace**—which is the **Palace of the Eagle**, the place of the light of thought and intention: "When the righteous who merit to gaze upon their Master arrive and stand before Him, every soul that ascends and reaches this Palace is met by a designated official to be buried <note>gloss: probably 'to be crowned' or 'clothed'</note> in the ultimate garments. The soul that has already performed the commandments of the Torah in this world in an 'active garment' to arrange them—so it is made for him in this Palace above, a garment to be clothed in, in that world. And when the soul ascends, that official takes that garment of hers and goes with it down to the word of the soul and blesses..."

<meta>This page continues the transition from Chapter 23 into Chapter 24, focusing on the "Service of the Heart" and the mystical mechanics of the soul. ### Chapter 23: The Part of Service | Chapter 24

When the soul is in that place from which it originated, this is its pattern <note>original: "dugma," meaning a microcosmic reflection of the macrocosmic divine realm</note>, just as we have written. For this reason, it is called "precious" and "praised" there, and it is described as a **"speaking spirit"** <note>original Aramaic: "Ruach Memalela," a term used in the Targum to describe the human soul's unique capacity for speech and reason</note>. This refers to **Inner Speech**, which consists of action, thought, knowledge, and wisdom, all of which are included within it. When its rest is brought to completion through the perfection of its deeds, it becomes complete and inclusive of all, like a "son of fire" <note>likely an allusion to the angelic or fiery nature of the soul</note>, enabling it to speak before the King of the Universe.

As was explained above in Chapter 20, in the Midrash of Rabbi Shimon bar Yochai (may he rest in peace), he said: "Come and see the structure: this 'living soul' <note>original: "Nefesh Chaya"</note> is holy and supreme. All the 'holy land' emerges from there in the female principle. We call it 'Soul' <note>original: "Neshamah"</note>, and there is none that ascends higher to the eye of the King, being revealed before the Holy King. It enters through all the gates, and none may hinder it. For this reason, it is called a **speaking spirit**, for every place it breathes into, it stands before the King."

Now, these "Gods of God" <note>referring to divine attributes or powers</note>, along with the entirety of the Torah, require both the "Part of Glory" and the "Part of Action." Behold, the Torah and the Soul are included in **Speech** and **Action**, mirroring their place of origin, their dwelling place. For Moses our Teacher said that the soul's outpouring is perfected and completed below, returning to its place with an addition of status and glory—higher even than that place from which it first came. This is the ultimate purpose: by coming into the body, the soul can ascend to a higher level than it occupied before its descent, when it was merely one of the general collective, as explained in Chapter 22.

King David (may he rest in peace) hinted at this when he said: *"The Torah of the Lord is perfect, restoring the soul"* <note>Psalm 19:8</note>. It is perfect when those who occupy themselves with it do so completely. As we wrote, the power of the Torah—which includes action, thought, knowledge, and wisdom—is contained in speech and action. These are called "Supreme Thought" because they originate from it and return to it; in it, they find their perfection and are elevated without any separation or cessation of the "Divine Voices." If one occupies oneself with that wisdom in that very way, then the hidden world above is blessed. Through these two—the perfection of the soul's thought and the proper intention <note>term: "Kavana," the focused heart-aim required for prayer and rituals</note>—one achieves the pattern of supreme perfection and repair <note>term: "Tikkun," the mystical process of mending the world</note>. 

One must learn without any separation, just as the foundations are established above. For external speech that is joined with thought, and thought that leads to human action, constitutes a "Complete Man." Speech and thought without action are not whole, and the "Repair" does not ascend properly. Therefore, in the books and the minds of the scholars, the practical commandments were established as the "Body of the Soul." 

Part of this "Part of Glory" is included in the service of the prayers and the proper meditation intended to ascend for Divine favor. We have already hinted at this regarding Speech. Specifically, it is included in the study of the Written Torah and its explanation, which is the Holy Talmud (the Oral Torah), and the inner understanding <note>original: "Tevunah," the Sephirah of understanding</note>. By contemplating them, one attains the "Body of Knowledge and Wisdom" mentioned in the verse *"For there is no action..."* In the chapter concerning "How one receives lashes" <note>A reference to the Talmudic tractate Makkot</note>, the sages hinted at the study and investigation of the **Wisdom of Kabbalah**, which is called "Wisdom" for the wise. It is said: "Being wise of heart from within a matter." This hints at the Oral Torah; one who occupies themselves with it with the proper intention (as explained at the end of this part) unifies the Great Name in His Glory, creating "much spirit" <note>satisfaction/pleasure</note> for Israel.

In the Midrash of Rabbi Shimon bar Yochai, they said: "How was David able to succeed? Through his blessings, he would prostrate himself day and night, 'mining' and searching. What was he mining? The paths of the Above. He would join himself to the Holy One, Blessed be He." This is why we say: *"A person should always engage in Torah, even if not for its own sake (Lo Lishma), for through 'not for its own sake' comes 'for its own sake' (Lishma)."* What is this "for its own sake"? It is the Torah when she is adorned, crowned, and inclusive of all the commandments. It was said that the Torah is the "fiancée" <note>original: "Arusa"</note> of the Holy One, Blessed be He, as it is written: *"An inheritance (morasha) for the congregation of Jacob."* Do not read it as *morasha* (inheritance), but as *me'orasa* (betrothed). When Israel occupies itself with Torah for its own sake, she is the fiancée of the Holy One. And when she is His fiancée, she becomes an inheritance for Israel.

### Chapter 24

<column-break/>

...to this, when the soul finds its "good," the scripture calls it a "waste" <note>likely referring to a soul that does not fulfill its purpose</note> if it remains idle. But the rest of the soul is the "rest of all," as we wrote from the words of the Master <note>referring to Maimonides</note> above. God forbid one should think otherwise, for such a thought is a great ruin and a subversion of the Torah in its entirety, "turning the bowl on its face" <note>idiom: to completely distort or overturn a matter</note> regarding the thoughts and investigations into Torah study, commandments, prayers, and the sounding of the Shofar. 

However, we have already found in the words of the Master (Maimonides) that which agrees with this truth. In the 3rd chapter of *Laws of the Foundations of the Torah*, he wrote regarding the "Great Chamber" <note>likely referring to the study of the Chariot or Metaphysics</note> that the Holy One, Blessed be He, bestowed this upon the inhabitants of this world to reward them with the life of the World to Come. Yet, his opinion there is not fully aligned with the ultimate purpose of the "Great and Small Chambers" <note>terms: "Ma'aseh Bereshit" (Physics) and "Ma'aseh Merkavah" (Metaphysics)</note>. For the Torah is not merely for the inhabitability of this world, as has been explained; rather, it adds to the life of the World to Come. In his commentary on Tractate Makkot, he said that this concept is among the foundations of the faith: that when a person fulfills even one of the 613 commandments properly and with "Correct Intention," without any worldly motive, but purely for its own sake and out of love, they merit the life of the World to Come. If only these were his only words on the matter!

We already wrote in the previous chapter that the Soul, in the mystery of the letter *Aleph*, includes the higher realms. Therefore, it is a pattern of the place from which it came. Thus, it possesses the power of **Speech** and the power of **Action**, just as they exist in that source. It has been explained that the purpose of our union with the body is for "Action," to repair the "limbs" and our conduct. That perfection must manifest in speech and action; without this, there is no "Repair" and no "Perfection."

In the Midrash of Rabbi Shimon bar Yochai, on the verse: *"For there is no action, nor account, nor knowledge, nor wisdom in the grave (Sheol) where you are going"* <note>Ecclesiastes 9:10</note>: "Come and see: In the grave, there is no action or perfection to be found. A person cannot be called a 'Man of Action' or say anything to the Master of Thought there. 'Account' refers to the speech of the world, for all the calculations of the calendar and the cycles of the moon are for the world of the living. 'Knowledge' refers to the spirit that possesses the guards that hang in thought, called the 'World to Come'—Thought and Understanding (Binah) all hang from it. All the 'forces' are included in the soul so they may ascend. For anyone who did not strive in this world to eat of its fruits through action, account, knowledge, and wisdom, his end is to be locked in the grave (Sheol), where none of these exist. When a person departs this world, as it is written: 'The Grave (Sheol) is below.' One who was prepared and merited the Holy Power should strive in this world before departing."

Behold, they have clarified that in this "Power"—which is the end of Supreme Thought—there is Action, Account, Knowledge, and Wisdom, for it is inclusive of all. We have already written that Wisdom is a part of them, and it includes them, and it is the "Body." It must be unified with Thought, for through it, everything is repaired. "Account, Knowledge, and Wisdom" are included in that "Sabbath" <note>a mystical state of rest/perfection</note> above. It must also include the soul below. When one is called "inclusive of all this," one examines these powers. Through this power, it is said "In the image of God He made him." One becomes a microcosm of the upper and lower worlds. 

Therefore, **Action** and the fulfillment of **Mitzvot** (commandments) are the great foundation for the repair and perfection of that "Part," according to the secret of: *"And David made a name"* <note>2 Samuel 8:13</note> and *"And you shall do them."* For this reason, the Prophets are called "Men of Action," because through their good deeds they repair and "make" the Divine Glory. Thus, the power of the Lord grows great. This was explained in Chapters 8 and 20. Through this "Part of the Soul," and through all that we have explained, one stands upon the truth of our intention. The soul, before it was born into the body, was already inclusive of the power of Action, Account, Knowledge, and Wisdom—but it lacked the "Wisdom of Knowledge" that opens the gates. This is what we wrote at the end of the chapter.

-> **Speech and Action, as you have learned, are included** <-
-> **in all of them, for the Body is that which breathes within them.** <-

It interprets the soul's descent as an opportunity to gain a higher spiritual status than its original state through the study of Kabbalah and the performance of Mitzvot with holy intention.</summary>
