<meta>This page continues the discussion from Chapter 24 regarding the soul’s journey and its "garments"—spiritual forms it takes based on its deeds. It transitions into a philosophical debate between medieval scholars like Rabbi Aaron HaLevi and Rabbi Joseph Albo concerning whether the soul is "perfect" without a body.</meta>

### Chapter 26: The Part of Service | Chapter 26

<margin>44</margin>
And this is the middle path upon the armor, taking them from the Garden of Eden below, and clothing that chosen luminary within it. It feels as though its existence will endure forever, for the body and the soul are divided according to their various levels. After its separation from the body, the soul clothes itself in *Malchut* <note>original: "Kingdom," the lowest of the ten divine emanations, often associated with the Divine Presence</note>, for the Divine Presence <note>original: "Shekhinah"</note> serves it according to its service. There are two types of "Kingdoms" that one must understand in order to merit the higher Divine Presence, which is more exalted, praised, and pure. This is because the light of the "Kingdom" in which it was clothed while serving below now clothes it to take delight in the upper Eden. However, the soul strips off and puts on garments according to the place it serves and delights in, as we wrote in the previous chapter.

There is a hint to this in the Torah regarding the service of the Day of Atonement <note>original: "Yom Kippur"</note>. The High Priest enters and exits in five white garments; he wears them both inside and outside, sometimes serving in golden garments and sometimes in white garments, as mentioned in the appropriate place. The changing of the garments corresponded to the change of locations. So too in the Garden of Eden. Scholars have wondered at the writing that says after the soul separates from the body, it puts on spiritual garments appropriate to its service, according to the place where it takes pleasure. Even in the "Booth" <note>original: "Sukkah," likely referring to a spiritual canopy or the "Tabernacle of Peace"</note> of this world, it will be clothed in a very thin garment that has a visible reality after it is placed. This level is not found until thirty days after death. But in this world, within the Presence of the Holy One, Blessed be He—this is the secret of what is written regarding Joshua the High Priest: **"I will give you paths among those standing here"** <note>Zechariah 3:7</note>. This means his status after his passing was to be sent into the Kingdom of God like the other "standing ones"—the angels. 

As for the vision of seeing the Holy, because he was alive, he returned from Sabbath eve to Sabbath eve for his vision, as mentioned in the chapter "The One Who Counts." <note>likely referring to a Talmudic passage regarding Rabbi Yehuda HaNasi</note>. It is told of a certain pious man that he said his teacher sat in a place of wine <note>a metaphor for deep mystical wisdom</note>, and that the "foreign" language <note>original: "La'az"</note> of the early righteous was good. I have also written that in a dream, one's garment might appear as flesh. Rabbi Chasdai bar Yoshiya died, and they said to him that he appeared in the form of a human being <note>original: "Ben Neveira"</note>. He asked what his "house" was, and was told it was the house of the son of Yoshiya. All this indicates that when one dies, the soul is clothed in a subtle, spiritual body that can be seen by the "pure of eye." When it ascends through the higher levels, even if the other righteous have not reached this supreme level, the soul still clothes itself in the Kingdom, which is its dwelling place according to its service, to inherit and be inherited by that great, crowned light. This state of "enslavement" <note>meaning devotion or attachment</note> exists in all the other worlds, in the garments of the soul as explained. This is meant as a metaphor for its excellence, as some sages have mentioned.

I have seen in the words of the Rabbi, Rabbi Aaron HaLevi (may his memory be a blessing), things that seem to judge the opinion of those who say the soul has no perfection without the body. In his commentary on the "Blessing of the Moon" and in the chapter "They Used to Test" in Tractate Berakhot, in the chapter "The Morning Prayer," he said the following: "The intention of the dream is that the soul is never complete without the body, much like the celestial spheres. If the perfection of the soul were possible without a body, there would be a place for an intellect that is separate and more perfect than the spheres, which possess bodies. However, the soul *needs* the body. Regarding this, it is said that the souls of the righteous are hidden under the Throne of Glory. The term 'hidden' <note>original: "Geniza"</note> is only used for something that requires something else—meaning they need a body, for their perfection is not complete without it." These are his words there.

However, the sage Rabbi Joseph Albo (may his memory be a blessing), in the *Book of Principles* <note>original: "Sefer Ha'Ikkarim"</note>, fourth treatise, chapter 30, wrote against this, saying: "Behold, you see how many difficulties there are in this view. First, this opinion tends toward the view of the materialists who say the soul has no existence without the body and therefore always needs a body to sustain it. Second, if you say the Divine soul has no existence without a body, how does the soul exist immediately after death when it separates from the body?" He argues that its existence then would be

<column-break/>

a deficient existence, as it would have no full pleasure or attainment of any level at all. 

He further wrote: "Furthermore, this contradicts the opinion of our Sages, who say that souls were created before they were placed in the spiritual body, as we have already said: **'With the King in His work they dwelt there'** <note>1 Chronicles 4:23</note>—this refers to the King of Kings, the Holy One, Blessed be He. The soul dwells in the 'Booth' of the righteous like a king. For all souls were created on the first day, as it says: **'And the spirit of God hovered'** <note>Genesis 1:2</note>—this is the spirit of the first man <note>original: "Adam HaRishon"</note>." On the surface, these words indicate that this is the case. 

Our answer to this is based on contemplation. It will become clear to us that the opinion of our Sages is correct. Their intention was to show the truth. As he wrote there regarding the "Resurrection of the Dead," that this is the ultimate goal they can achieve in terms of perfection—each soul according to its knowledge and imagination. Our current bodies, made of the four elements, will change to receive another form. This was an ancient saying, that there is a simple, light foundation for the soul to be prepared to receive a more "praiseworthy" body, like the "sight of a bird" <note>likely a metaphor for clarity and lightness</note>. This is similar to the moon, which is a body that receives light. We see examples of this in this world with many living creatures whose body chemistry changes to receive a different form. Some of them need to eat a special food for this—this is the concept of the "Tree of Life." Whoever ate of its fruit made his body ready to receive this eternal form and live forever. This is hinted at in the Account of Creation—that the intention was for man to exist forever. If so, it was possible for him not to lack this perfection, as was the original intent of his creation.

According to this view, the Rabbi <note>referring back to Aaron HaLevi</note> would say that when you evaluate this high level and perfection, his first intention was for the soul's holiness and lightness to be acquired forever above. But by walking through the world in body and soul, a more wonderful level and greater honor is added. When the Sages said: "The Holy One, Blessed be He, makes them wings," as Nachmanides <note>original: "Ramban"</note> explained in *The Gate of Reward* <note>original: "Sha'ar HaGemul"</note>, they meant that the soul is given a "white" <note>pure/spiritual</note> body so it can endure. As long as the soul has not reached this perfection, its existence is "deficient" while it is under the Throne of Glory—meaning, even though it is in the Garden of Eden in spiritual delight, it is "deficient" only because the ultimate intention has not yet been completed through the body to reach the greatest level of perfection. This is undoubtedly what is meant by the "return" and the pleasure there.

One should not conclude from the Rabbi’s words that being "hidden" <note>under the Throne</note> means the soul has no full pleasure or attainment at all, as the author of the *Book of Principles* wrote. This is similar to what we wrote above in Chapter 23 regarding the phrase "One hour of satisfaction in the World to Come is better than all the life of this world." The reason wisdom came into the body was to acquire the "Unique Name" <note>the Tetragrammaton</note> and so that the vision of all reality from above to below could be judged. This brought the body a goodness and perfection it would not have had in its original place. While the soul there delights in the radiance of the Divine Glory, its existence is called "deficient" only in comparison to the *ultimate* perfection it achieves through its journey in the body. This is what the Sages meant—not that the soul lacks consciousness, but that it has not yet reached the "perfection of the intent" of creation. This is the secret that our teacher included in this chapter.

### Chapter 27

# Part [of Service] Chapter 25

To bow and be blessed always, and to prepare the true nature constantly and to be sanctified. And it shall not depart, until every individual soul every month [receives] the Holy Spirit <note>original: "Ruach HaKodesh"</note> to find relief, as they established its strength and it is sanctified, and its purity and radiance return. This is so we may merit His kingdom <note>original: "Malchut," the final of the ten divine attributes, representing the manifest presence of God</note> to be conceived, to dwell, and to be established. Its existence and its renewal are in its restoration. These words of "Tirka" <note>likely a reference to a specific kabbalistic term or local textual variant</note> and their purity are like the weapons of its restoration. This is through the grace of assistance in its beginning, and the Holy One is exalted from within the holy space, and so on, to remove the impurity and the garment of the soul, to breathe into it and to establish a house and a kingdom for the offering by their hand, to strengthen its existence always at every time before Him, occupying itself with merit, a portion to rejoice in the joy of its existence and the merit of its portion.

And we have already written the end. And one who, Heaven forbid, [turns] his face from the ethics of the kingdom, behold, his matters are investigated. He shall not look upon his heavens, nor upon the dwelling, nor knowledge, nor wisdom. In the image of the intention, there is a voice included, and it is naked of all good and is compared to the place of the stain of the gates. It is light, and the memory of the stain is all light nakedness here, and there is no merit to the account, for it is an act of accounting, knowledge, and wisdom in its place. 

As it was said by the rabbis in the section on Phinehas: <note>original: "Parashat Pinhas," a portion of the Zohar</note> "One who does good for his fellow, these are simple garments, until he prepares his garments properly, and his precious things from there." This is so they may merit the existence of these levels to make for him a coat of skins <note>original: "Ketonet Or," referencing the garments God made for Adam and Eve</note> to enlighten his mind and to stay his hand to remove the burden. These voices will be there, and when holiness is found in his soul toward his freedom, these garments will be his, and he will be distanced from the gates of Gehenna <note>the place of spiritual purification or punishment</note>, for in his comfort he is protected from the voice of destruction. 

And there is a hint to this in the kingdoms: "the rest of the blow and the movement," and "this is from the king's ministers in royal apparel of blue and white." <note>referencing Esther 8:15</note> And "Mordecai went out," which points to the wisdom that belongs to the incense of myrrh and their clothing. Furthermore, the precise nature of the "royal ministers of the world" is a royal garment according to what one achieved in his service in this world. The level of the holy ones is blessed above all that leads, leading to an upper level and leading to a lower level in good delights. This is directed toward the preparation of the deed in thought and its refinement. 

"And a great crown of gold" <note>referencing Esther 8:15</note> points to the Crown <note>original: "Atarah," another name for Malchut</note>, the Crown of Splendor <note>original: "Ateret Tiferet"</note> which the righteous are crowned with. And "the secret of his name" is further: "the light of the Lord, the light of delight," which is inclusive of all wisdoms and points of sustenance for this secret. And in the hidden things there is a fire that does not consume. The peace and the joy belong to him in the attributes of the joy of the righteous. 

And they hinted at the joy of the King in the precious garments. And in the "whiteness of the heart," which is the stain according to his service, he is the messenger. For with Joshua the High Priest, they "removed the filthy garments from upon him," <note>referencing Zechariah 3:4</note> and that is the secret of the "filthy ones." And "they clothed him in his [proper] garments," which is the garment of the joy that rests upon him as he separates from the body, according to what he achieved in his service. And "to the Lord who stands," points to the standing ones who are crowned by it—the righteous who are bound to the chamber of the Lord. 

And it was said in the first chapter after Rabbi Elazar: Rabbi Hanina said, "In the future, the Holy One, blessed be He, will be a crown on the head of every righteous person, as it is written: 'In that day shall the Lord of hosts be for a crown of glory'" <note>Isaiah 28:5</note> and so on. And it is clear from the essence of our words on this matter that just as the soul acts through its powers in the physical limbs and prepares the actions that are done through it, so too it needs a body, which is the spiritual garment that it prepares through its service. It will receive and come and endure the spiritual [light], and there are the high faces. And one does not need to understand two types of garments, as we have explained. And with this, the intention in this chapter is completed.

# The Service | Chapter 26

We shall keep this and it is sanctified as it is [done] by many, and it is prepared. For it is joined to everything above it in the likeness of a body and a garment, and the upper one is in the likeness of the soul to it. In this manner, all the worlds are [structured], and there is an "Upper One" over all the powers, the Master of all. The upper beings are like forms for the soul, and the soul of the world is clothed in a very thin garment, and they are perceived as those who strip it away. Also, the Torah is perceived from the upper beings as being composed of several garments: some are external and some are internal. The internal ones are the secrets of the Torah, and the internal [parts] of the bodies of the Torah are called the "bodies of the Torah," and their soul is the actual Torah, the garment of the Queen. 

As it was said by the rabbis: <note>original: Zohar, Behaalotcha 152a</note> "Come and see, the upper world and the lower world are weighed in one balance. The lower world is made in the image of the upper world. Regarding the upper angels, it is written: 'He makes His angels spirits, His ministers a flaming fire.' <note>Psalm 104:4</note> When they descend to this world, they clothe themselves in the garments of this world. If they did not clothe themselves in the garments of this world, they would not be able to endure in this world, and the world could not endure them. If this is so for the angels, how much more so for the Torah, which created them and all the worlds, and their existence is because of her. When she descended to this world, if she had not clothed herself in these garments of this world, the world could not have received her. Therefore, this story of the Torah is the garment of the Torah."

"See, those who look only at the garment, which is the literal Torah, and do not look at what is beneath the garment—they have no portion in the World to Come. Thus David said: 'Open my eyes, that I may behold wondrous things out of Your Torah' <note>Psalm 119:18</note>—that which is beneath the garment of the Torah. Come and see, there is a garment visible to all, and those fools, when they see a man in a beautiful garment, they look no further. But the essence of the man is his soul. In this manner, the Torah has a soul and a body. The 'bodies of the Torah' are the essential commandments. This body is covered in a garment, which are the stories of this world. The fools of the world look only at the garment, which is the story of the Torah. And they do not know more; they do not look at what is under the garment. The wise, the servants of the High King, those who stood at Mount Sinai, look only at the soul, which is the root of everything, the actual Torah. And in the future, they are destined to look at the 'Soul of the Soul' of the Torah."

"Come and see, likewise above there is a garment, a body, a soul, and a Soul of the Soul. The heavens and their offspring are the garment."

When the time comes for them to descend to this world, in the knowledge of the soul, they prepare for the things of this world. Those spirits strip off that radiance and the thin garment they possessed, and they clothe themselves in the radiance and garment of this world, making their dwelling in this world in a physical garment. # Chapter 27: The Part of Service / The Service Chapter 28 [Page] 45

...for the righteous, for the intermediate, and for the wicked. He said to him: "If so, what is the meaning of 'the dead know nothing'?" <note>original: "אינם יודעים מאומה"; a quote from Ecclesiastes 9:5</note>. He replied: "By the life of the world! It is established that the righteous, who are called 'living,' contemplate and know that they will die, and they add to the expansion of their understanding <note>original: "Binah," the divine attribute of understanding</note> that there is a judgment and a Judge. Thus, 'the living will lay it to his heart' <note>Ecclesiastes 7:2</note>. But the wicked, who are called 'dead,' do not know, nor do they pay attention, nor are they found to possess anything of the deeds of that world. It appears that such a person does not know the deeds of the World to Come because he does not belong to the 'children of life.' That World to Come is hidden and hinted at; it is a world where the wicked among men dwell as mere images <note>original: "dyoknin," referring to spiritual silhouettes or shells</note>. They do not know what is destined to happen at the end of the world, though they strive to know the glory of their Master in the kingdom of that world."

And the king's goodness increases for those who repent, for "the living will lay it to his heart" <note>original: "ישית אל לבו"</note> constantly, as long as the breath of God is in his nostrils, to contemplate the matters of that world—the world of desire—and to strive always for its attainment. One who stands, strives, and contemplates it, to know it, possesses it in potential. Through this effort and contemplation, he conducts his time in repentance and good deeds, through the knowledge of that world: its gates, its palaces, its proofs, and all its forms and structures, which are miraculous, perfected, and armed with the supernal secrets hinted at in these forms. At the end of his perfection, he will behold and contemplate the matter, for "God has made one thing opposite the other" <note>Ecclesiastes 7:14; a core kabbalistic principle that the physical world mirrors the spiritual</note>. Through them, he is filled with wisdom; he occupies himself with this through the power of his service, which he loves without end, sufficing for every matter he will actually achieve. We see that those who dedicate all their time and those who come before Him in this way are considered "living" even after death, while others are "dead" even during their lives.

We further learned that the souls of the righteous exist in hints as their physical images; they recognize one another and know the end—they know what will be in the future at the end of the world. We also learned that those who strive to know and attain the hidden wonders are those who will be praised there. Every "key" <note>original: "klapter," possibly a corruption of the Greek 'kleis' or a specific technical term for spiritual access</note> is given to them at the beginning. This soul builds itself from the power of its striving and the way it spent its time. In truth, their world is a world of longing, and they clearly attain in the next life what they looked upon at the end of the world. For their intention and direction in the fear of death clarified the matter; the secret remains with the living, and his heart will tell him of himself and he will acquire it.

It was further added that this joy in the midst of the World of Souls <term>Olam Ha-Neshamot: the intermediate realm where souls dwell after death but before the final resurrection</term> corresponds to how the souls and spirits perform their service. From the words of our great master, the Ramban <note>Rabbi Moshe ben Nachman, or Nachmanides, a 13th-century sage</note> of blessed memory, in his work *The Gate of Reward* <note>original: "Sha'ar Ha-Gemul"</note>, it appears that the Upper World is the Upper Garden of Eden, called the World of Souls. All of this is true, for the souls delight in this, and with assistance, they create a dwelling, as will be explained in this book. We further learned that during the time the body is in the grave, the soul does not rule by its own power and does not merit its place until the body is buried and settled in the grave. Then the soul ascends and returns to its rest. It seems that when the body is settled and returned to its dust, the soul ascends in rest, even if it was the life of a sufferer and was buried in a simple wooden coffin.

This was already a dispute among the Sages <note>original: "Amoraim"</note> in the chapter "A Man May Ask" <note>Talmud, Tractate Shabbat, Chapter 23</note>. They said: "What did Rabbi Achai bar Yoshiya say? 'All those who say that the dead person knows until the cover of the grave is closed...'" Some say until the flesh rots, as it is written, "But his flesh upon him shall have pain" <note>Job 14:22</note>. Others say until the coffin rots, as it is written, "And the dust returns to the earth as it was" <note>Ecclesiastes 12:7</note>. According to the one who says "until the coffin rots," as soon as the body is chosen, the spirit immediately returns to God who gave it. This is the opinion of the Author, as we wrote in the map. According to the one who says "until the flesh rots," it seems that as long as his flesh is upon him, it is not yet processed, and the soul has no rest because it is still tied to the body and the mastery of its own flesh. This is also the opinion of the Sages in *Midrash Ruth* regarding the soul. In the Midrash of Rabbi Shimon bar Yochai <note>the Zohar</note>, they explain this further. One sage derives his proof from a verse mentioning "spirit" <note>original: "Ruach"</note> and the other from a verse mentioning "soul" <note>original: "Nefesh"</note>...

<column-break/>

...to say that they disagree in the end, yet they do not truly disagree. It is not as it appears on the surface. Regarding this, the Talmud says: "This person and that person..." This will be clarified and refined in Chapter 28 following this, with God's help.

### Chapter 28

They said in *Midrash Ruth* concerning the soul in these words: Rabbi Alexandrai said: "At the hour a person departs from the world, the *Nefesh* <term>Nefesh: the lowest level of the soul, associated with physical vitality</term> follows the body and remains within it. But the *Ruach* <term>Ruach: the middle level of the soul, associated with emotions and spirit</term> flies from it into the Garden of Eden and visits the place of the Throne, awakening it. Then the dead know and speak with one another, and the dead know by proclamation the end of the world and many other things."

The *Nefesh* never separates from the body, neither in life nor in death. Like this example: the *Nefesh* says to its body, in the language of the verse: "Do not entreat me to leave you... for where you go, I will go" <note>quoting Ruth 1:16, personifying the soul's attachment to the body</note>. This is the life of the *Nefesh*, and it does not separate... [the text here describes the soul's refusal to leave]. When the person lies on his bed, the *Ruach* ascends, and the *Nefesh* remains while the body is destroyed. During that destruction, it visits and keeps watch over its time... the *Ruach* leaves the body and wanders in the clouds above.

The secret is: if you deal well with your soul, it will not be separated from you after life, for death shall part me and thee. But at the final burial in the grave, the body is consumed and rots, while the *Ruach* and the power of the *Nefesh* constantly offer incense... they do not separate from the body during life, but they do separate to live in the essence of the "Living World" <note>original: "Chai Ha-Olamim"</note>.

We have already written in Chapter 4 of the first part and Chapter 2 of the second part that man possesses a *Nefesh* and a *Ruach*, and according to his deeds, he merits a higher level. In this world, the soul finds comfort in returning to its place without delay. The *Ruach* goes to the Garden of Eden, as mentioned in the Midrash I quoted. The *Nefesh* remains with the body until the flesh is consumed and rotted. This is the meaning of "Death will separate"—it refers to the time the flesh exists before turning to dust. Once it rots, that is the "death" that separates the *Nefesh* from the body. Then the *Ruach* is in Eden, and they are visited... the *Nefesh* is bound with the *Ruach*, and the *Ruach* with the *Neshamah* <term>Neshamah: the highest level of the soul, the divine spark</term>.

In the Midrash of Rabbi Shimon bar Yochai, it is added: "The soul of God is bound in the Bundle of Life" <note>original: "Tzror Ha-Chayim"</note>. The wise man proves this by saying that they are partners in the attachment. We find that all is one: the *Nefesh* in the *Ruach*, the *Ruach* in the *Neshamah*, and the *Neshamah* in the Throne. Thus, the soul is bound in the Bundle of Life.

What we have brought explains what we wrote in the previous chapter regarding the different views. They do not disagree in the hidden sense. He who says "until the body rots" intends what we said in *Midrash Ruth*—that when the body is chosen, the *Ruach* goes immediately to Eden. This is the power of the verse: "And the dust returns to the earth as it was, and the spirit returns to God." He who says "until the flesh is consumed" intends the *Nefesh* which remains with the body until the flesh rots, as mentioned in the Midrash itself, citing the verse: "But his flesh upon him shall have pain, and his soul within him shall mourn" <note>Job 14:22</note>.

And as for what they said in the chapter "A Man May Ask": "For dust you are and to dust you shall return" <note>Genesis 3:19</note>, he said to him: "That refers to one hour before the Resurrection of the Dead." This refers to the remaining bones which are stripped of flesh, where the *Nefesh* is no longer bound and does not remain with them. We find that the *Nefesh* has no rest until that hour. Then the truth is revealed, which is the opinion of our Rabbis, proving that regarding the bones it is said "in the embroidery" and at the time of dust—one hour before the Resurrection of the Dead.

## Chapter 27

There, as in the Tractate *Temurah* <note>original: "תמורה"; a volume of the Talmud dealing with the exchange of consecrated animals</note>, in the chapter "There are in sacrifices," Rav Yehuda said in the name of Rav: "The reason one is released from this world..." And at the end of every section, he would speak beautifully like this, saying: "An orchard and a pomegranate tree, planting fruitfulness..." In a pig’s snout <note>likely a metaphorical reference to a short moment or a specific spiritual state</note>, in a brief moment, it is said there is a Garden of Eden. And because it is difficult [to grasp] the pleasantness... that it should be forever as has already been explained, for this is in the choice of places in this world... its truth itself. And it is not all that is beautiful for him to achieve in his creation, for the place is prepared and ready, upon which and from which for his sacrifice... to the perception. This is the "cleaving" <note>original: "Dveikut"; mystical union with the Divine</note>, for just as he has a small tear [to connect to] the Lord to join the Garden of Eden—and in it is the Tree of Life and the Tree of Knowledge with four rivers as the verses explain, which wrap this in the Work of Creation <note>original: "Ma'aseh Bereshit"</note>—so too above there are hidden places and firmaments like the curtains of the Garden of Eden and the Tree of Life and the Tree of Knowledge with four rivers in the secret of "and from there it divided and became four heads" <note>Genesis 2:10</note>. And the Upper Garden of Eden is in the secret of "the Lord to His God," a full name <note>referring to the combination of the names YHVH and Elohim</note> in the secret of the seven heavens. And there, at the beginning... the Lord. And this likeness is the Lower Garden of Eden in the secret of "the Lord God," a full name like the Upper one. And it is the Palaces, and there are seven, and there in the assemblies everything is the Lord, etc.

Adam the First Man <note>original: "Adam HaRishon"</note> would see from afar [the name] Elohim and perceived wondrous gifts in the secret of the Upper Garden of Eden. And from there, because they desired and ascended above in those changes... in the assemblies, the Garden of Eden and the Tree of Life and the Tree of Knowledge were prepared for the life written [in the Torah]. was but to die. And when he departs, he is to cleave to the height where he was, until he strives from his kingdom and his body, and her body in the star joins and [unclear] and praises. It was upright in its food... and therefore it is hard for it to remove and to endure that great Upper light, whose greatness and revelation cannot be estimated, until it has become accustomed to perceive in the Lower Garden of Eden, which is the delay of life. And this world of the soul prepares it for that hidden outer world. And eventually, it becomes [unclear] and gazes into the void.

And a hint to this is hinted in His holy Torah in the matter of prophecy and Moses, the master of all prophets, peace be upon him. For he did not ascend from the lowliness to the upper height in the secret of what is called "the Vision" <note>original: "HaMachazeh"</note>. The entire opening of his prophecy was in a mirror that does not shine <note>original: "aspaklaria de-lo nahara"; an opaque lens, often associated with the level of prophecy lower than the direct vision</note> from the heavens, as the word says: "And an angel of the Lord appeared to him" <note>Exodus 3:2</note>—the secret of the holy angel. And that which accustomed him to hold on, he ascended to the level of prophecy in the Great Name <note>the Tetragrammaton</note> to which no man had ascended before. Thus the precious way is made for the pure soul, so that it does not transition [too] harshly from this lowly world to the place of the holy, the pure and shining light, for it could not bear it until it acclimates for some time in a certain middle place between the living. This perfection is the Garden of Eden which is in the end. And when the light of the soul arrives, it merits to come before the King, the Lord, to see and to delight in the glory. And this is what is elevated to the Bundle of Life, which is the Upper Garden of Eden.

And this is the arrangement that was said, that this is the Lower Garden of Eden here. And this is what is immediately after the separation from the body, called by the masters of wisdom the "World of Souls" <note>original: "Olam HaNeshamot"</note>. And they said in the Midrash of Ruth: Rabbi Yehuda bar Simon said: "Fortunate are these to gaze upon what is prepared in that world where they serve there." For one cannot know this or use a parable to know it, for this is the one of his wisdom. Rabbi Jeremiah used to say: "As long as the body has not rested in its place, its soul likewise [does not find rest]." And he eventually gazes at the light to know that level of the souls [where it] sits. There it goes according to the verse, "and the lying down of his body shall be," and it is destined... [unclear]... and I found in it those who need to stand. And the book of the fathers in that [place] says: "And these and the puffing out of their breath, when it comes to him, he gazes into his grave, understanding it." And then to pardon and to prepare for him supports and a grave. And He is destined to favor him and cover him, and he is found upon him. And He brings up all that was in his hands once he has rested and been buried. That soul, in its name, ascends into the Upper Academy <note>original: "Metivta Ila'ah"</note>.

They said this, and behold, sleep is good for the one who enlightened you. One day, Rabbi Pinchas was sitting at the gate of the city of Kur, and there was a matter to establish for him. Now a certain man came to him and said to him: "My master, for I need such-and-law in this, and I will give you [unclear] of silver so that you may strive in the Torah, all of them in its way." He said to him: "And are all those... the path of life, I have known them? And they are destined and stand here." And he knows them from the living. And thus it is said: "For the living know that they shall die" <note>Ecclesiastes 9:5</note>—these are the righteous. "But the dead know nothing"—these are the wicked. He said to him: "By your life, my master! Do not the wicked know in this world? They know their own pain, and they know the pain of others, and they know what they did in this world, and they know the glory of the righteous..."

# Chapter 29, Part of the Service, Chapter 30
## Chapter 29

To sustain and understand all of them: all of this honor, stature, and delight is the lot of the souls of the righteous in the Lower Garden of Eden <note>Hebrew: *Gan Eden shel Mata*. In Jewish mysticism, this is a terrestrial-adjacent paradise where souls rest before ascending higher.</note>, where they enjoy every day the "Dew of Life" that our God sprinkles upon them from the Tree of Life and from the river that flows out of Eden to bless them. The quality of this "Dew of Eden" is known by tradition to be that which will eventually revive the dead, as will be explained. In all this, I intended to show that during the "Kingdom of the Weeks" <note>likely referring to specific cycles of time or spiritual stages</note>, they shall abide in the Divine Presence <note>Hebrew: *Shekhinah*; the immanent aspect of God that dwells within the world.</note>. Through it, they attain and know the past, the end, and the future concerning the states of the dead and the investigation of all the glory and praise that sustains them, as well as the merit to ascend and appear before the King, the Lord, in His holy place in the Upper Garden of Eden.

And they further said in the *Hidden Midrash on Ruth* <note>original: "מדרש רות הנכנס"; referring to *Midrash ha-Ne'elam* on the Book of Ruth, a section of the Zohar</note>, using this language: Above this gate, there appears a great and luminous gate. From the time they are before this, three gates are lacking, and thus he has three names upon him. It is opened to him through mercies and kindnesses, and with the writing of "good days" in his being. When the Sabbath enters, seven mercies are stirred for him, and a voice from Eden calls out through all the firmaments, saying: "Open the gates, that the righteous nation which keeps faithfulness may enter" <note>Isaiah 26:2</note>. Because all the spirits in the Garden of Eden surround all the beauty of the seventh [level], standing there and interwoven within it. A great trembling occurs in the region of the firmament that is over the gardens of Eden, and they open to seven kingdoms <note>original: "מלכויות"; here referring to spiritual realms or spheres of influence</note> that support the "chariot-rider" <note>a reference to the *Merkavah* or Divine Chariot</note> to enjoy the beauty of the Explicit Name <note>Hebrew: *Shem Ha-Mephorash*; the tetragrammaton or the essential name of God</note>, built of pearls. And all those spirits of the King who died within it are precious in that Garden of Eden, in the likeness of those of the world whose forms are within them, appearing as refined flesh in that hour, moving through the innermost parts. They are made above in the established place, and they flow to this place, and are covered in silver clouds with sweetened laughter. They stand at this gate among all these festive gates, and they are combed like the silver of the soul in life, and they ascend upward. And so it is in every firmament, seventy-seven [levels]. At the hour when the spirits begin to ascend, they are spiritual and descend precisely between the waters of life, ascending and descending in the company of the place of their separation. These spirits join with the other merits, and the place is not hidden in its construction. In the "Psalm for the Sabbath Day," at the hour when they study and skip "May the pleasantness [of the Lord be upon us]," for the sake of the heave-offering <note>original: *Terumah*; a gift or sanctified portion</note> separated for them on the Sabbath, these spirits ascend from there, and others descend; these ascend to live and those descend to their place. And so it is always on the Sabbath and forever. Until here [is the quote].

From here, the secret of the "Ascent and Separation" <note>original: "סוד העליה ופרידה"</note> shall be explained as mentioned in this composition. The Sages have seen fit for me, from my own heart, to show myself to the firmaments, etc., in the general vision and my dream. For my King and my Vision, etc.—this is the secret of the delight I wished to speak of regarding the pleasure of souls and the matter of the Garden of Eden. And do not wonder or be amazed at the way of wrath, and may He have mercy according to the portions of His Torah.

### Chapter 30 | Section on Divine Service | Chapter 31 | 47

These three matters are almost divided; if so, it is logical that what is prepared for the **righteous** on earth comes from the body, whether now in the measure of the "bounty of holiness" <note>original: "מגד הקדושה"; a phrase implying spiritual spiritual abundance</note> to which they were drawn by their level, or the punishment prepared for the **wicked** in Gehenna <note>the traditional Jewish realm of purgatory or spiritual purification</note>, which is drawn from the "bounty of impurity" that they followed during their lives. Furthermore, we have learned that Gehenna is "below" on the earth, according to the plain meaning of the scripture "that he saw in his understanding and dwelled in Jerusalem" <note>referring to Isaiah 31:9</note>, which speaks of the lower realms but hints at the upper ones. Just as there is a **Garden of Eden** <note>Paradise</note> above and a Garden of Eden below, so too there is a Gehenna above and a Gehenna below. The dwelling of the upper Garden is spiritual, prepared with radiance as a continuous delight and pleasure for the souls of the righteous, just as it is below on the earth. 

Similarly, from the "Holy and Pure Fire" above, a "glowing coal" descends from the Throne. The fire below consists of those "purifiers" <note>original: "טהרלי'"; possibly a corruption of a term for punishing angels or spiritual forces</note> which represent all the impurity we mentioned previously. This is called the "Upper Gehenna." This was hinted at in the Mishnah, Tractate Tamid, Chapter 38: "They would bend behind the hearth because Gehenna was from the firmament." This is the secret of the words of Rabbi Pedat, who said there is no difference between the fires, as Rabbi Yohanan said: "Even in the name of Rabbi Yose, all the 'peace' <note>Hebrew: *Shalva*</note> in it is the fire of Gehenna." As the verse says: "For Topheth has been prepared since yesterday" <note>Isaiah 30:33</note>. Gehenna was fitting to be mentioned on the second day of creation <note>Monday</note>, which is the day of "divisions and changes," and for this reason, it does not say "and it was good" on the second day. There is no secret in all holiness that does not have "evil and destruction" separated from it, which is called "the burning of the Lord and His wrath" that "shall rest upon the head of the wicked." This is the "Lower Gehenna" which was prepared to punish the wicked, each according to their evil deeds, just as the "Lower Garden of Eden" was prepared to enlighten the righteous, each according to their deeds. Therefore, these enter through one gate, and afterward the paths divide: this one goes to the Garden of Eden, and this one to Gehenna. 

In the Torah, the "Secret of the Husband," the "Mountain of Vineyards," when it draws them to be "grafted to the brothers of the orchard," two paths lean and turn, from this side and from that side. We say: "From these to those." One path is to go to the Garden of Eden, and one is to go to Gehenna. Whoever is fit for the Garden of Eden goes through the "Righteousness" and they accompany him with a thousand deaths <note>perhaps a reference to the transition of death</note>; whoever is fit for Gehenna, they take him and lead him into Gehenna. We have supported this end and this book: it is "below on the earth," and that is what we have discussed in this chapter.

## Chapter 31

There is no single punishment for the wicked in Gehenna; rather, the punishment for each is according to their choice and human intellect. For this reason, Gehenna contains a place consisting of seven dwellings <note>original: "מדורות"; levels or compartments</note>. Our Sages (of blessed memory) gave them names as mentioned in the chapter "One Who Builds" <note>Tractate Eruvin</note>. Rabbi Joshua ben Levi said: Gehenna has seven names: **Sheol, Abaddon, Beer Shachat, Bor Shaon, Tit HaYaven, Tzalmavet, and Eretz Tachtit** <note>These terms translate roughly to: The Underworld, Destruction, Pit of Corruption, Pit of Tumult, Miry Clay, Shadow of Death, and the Netherworld</note>. Each of these is a dwelling unto itself, though collectively they are called Gehenna. They correspond to the seven names given to the **Evil Inclination** <note>original: "יצר הרע"; the internal urge toward selfishness or sin</note>, as mentioned in the chapter "The Flute" <note>Tractate Sukkah</note>. 

And according to the words of Rabbi Shimon bar Yochai regarding the "Chambers of the Side of Impurity," their seven names are: **Evil Man, Impure, Enemy, Stone, Stumbling Block, Uncircumcised, and the Northern One.** These are the seven names corresponding to the seven levels that consume everything through "foreign thought" <note>distractions during prayer or holy acts</note>. Corresponding to these seven names are those called "Gehenna," where the guilty of the world are found. These are: **Pit, Chasm, Duma <note>the angel of silence/death</note>, Miry Clay, Sheol, Shadow of Death, and Netherworld.** All these are levels corresponding to those others. The one who is chastised is judged with "prior justice" for turning away from the upright path to the evil that was drawn from the whole. He is enslaved in Gehenna, which is also drawn for everyone according to their sin. For as we wrote, all that is holy in the souls is like glass in a dwelling of splendor, and it is all one, but for each person in their place or dwelling according to the secret of their punishment. There are levels that are "hard" and levels that are truly "harsh," as they said that if the first dwelling is like fire, the next is even more so. Similarly, they said in the world of "Labor" or "Affliction," that one should not think the punishment for a light transgression is the same as the punishment for a severe transgression. For it is not just that the punishment for "rounding the head" <note>a minor prohibition regarding haircuts</note> should be as

<column-break/>

the sin of a "pit of defect" or "dressing in garments with a drop of bitterness." Ultimately, the punishment that meets the measure is severe for the one who passes into "Foreign Service" <note>idolatry</note>. In Tractate Eduyot, Chapter 2, we said: "The judgment of the wicked in Gehenna is twelve months." And in the Midrash of Rabbi Shimon bar Yochai regarding the "Chambers of the Side of Impurity," there are seven palaces which are the seven dwellings of Gehenna. These twelve months are called so because just as life is possible through the Lord who is exalted, so there are twelve months for the "husks" <note>original: "קליפין"; spiritual shells or forces of evil</note>. It is possible for a person to imagine that they will be consumed there, and the heat there will govern them. 

Exactly as we wrote in this matter: since the soul is separate in its refinement, Gehenna and the "Great Sin" that rules over it must be clarified. For behold, the soul is a spiritual entity, yet it takes on a "form" that cleaves to it, level upon level, as we wrote in this part and in the first part. And behold, it rules over matters for some time. We are forced to explain this regarding the holy spiritual matters within the soul's kindness. However, the tradition of our Sages (of blessed memory) is that there is "Wisdom" in a place of wasteland, along with the tradition of "purity" and passing through the fire of Gehenna as we wrote. There is nothing in the words of the Sages regarding Gehenna being a place of punishment for sinful souls that is merely a "parable" or "allegory." Rather, the intellect and its image are meant to inform us of the vitality and the side of that "error" which hinders those who transgress the King's commandments. When the soul finds itself in the refinement of Gehenna, it receives punishment there according to its sin, based on the "image" and "likeness" it adopted. 

But how is such a thought possible? That a "spirit" or "soul" could be rewarded or walk through waters or be governed by order? For these names signify souls that are "thick" or "harsh," yet this is a "thin, minute spirit" that is not a body, is separate, and cannot be grasped in any physical place. How can it be in a "fire" that burns? From the subtlety above the angels, the Place called Gehenna was created. It includes even the "thinnest of the thin" which is not a physical body in the soul, yet it carries these thin matters. Just as the intellect in pure and clear souls is of the utmost subtlety, so too there is a creation that is "thinner than thin" to make the guilty souls "bend" and to refine what has become "hardened" and "thick" in the place of Gehenna. 

This is like what was said: just as we know that the soul of a man dwells within him and is remembered in his body—as some researchers say—so we must know and believe that there is a "spiritual power" between the soul and the body. This "matter" can explain how, in its refinement, it is clarified between itself and the "Holy Empty Space" that was created. There is a secret to this in the "Book of the Points" <note>original: "ספר הנקור"; likely a reference to a work on Hebrew vowels/points or a specific Kabbalistic text</note>, providing a reason for the Sabbath alone. It says that because the soul is holy, it goes from the "Measure of the Balance" <note>original: "מדת פלסור"; a term for divine equilibrium</note> to the "Opening of the Gateway," which is the foundation of which it is said, "The Lord is with you, you shall not be consumed." It has the power to "tear" and "consume" the shells <note>original: "קליפות"; the forces of impurity</note> until they are very thin. This is because the place from which souls emerge receives from the "Three Foundations," and it was a "fire consuming fire." 

We must state the reason why souls stay in the "Lower Gehenna," since the drawing of that fire is from the "Upper Foundation" of the "Upper Gehenna." The preparation and refinement of the lower realm is still in its strength and might to "tear" and "consume" the souls. This is the essence of his words and his intention, and it is a correct and sufficient reason. There is yet another reason for this matter which is very sufficient and removes all doubts and confusion. It is a "Secret of the Master," correct for those who delve into the "Higher Wisdom" <note>Kabbalah</note> that we have merited to receive from the later Sages. It has already been explained in this book that the soul was created for the body and is clothed in a "garment" <note>original: "גניז"; a covering or ethereal body</note> similar to the "Lower Garden of Eden," which mediates between the thin soul and the coarse body. And the Creator made a second matter for the spirits, as explained in this part, regarding the "Spirit of Kindness." But he himself, in his material nature, adds himself to whatever "fire" he pursues. And the scripture did not explain the way of the return of this power...

# Chapter 30 | Section on Divine Service | Chapter 30

Impurity is hidden; it desires to hide all that is good within the **Evil Inclination** <term>Yetzer HaRa: the innate human drive toward physical pleasure or selfishness, which must be channeled toward good</term> that entices and creates the desire in people to sin, to transgress the will of their Creator, and to lose themselves in evil deeds. According to the **Sages of Truth** <note>original: "חכמי האמת"; a common term for Kabbalists</note>, the "Voice" <note>The "Voice" here refers to a divine spiritual frequency or the flow of holiness</note> is where impurity, every plague, every illness, and death reside—along with the tearing and cessation of that holy Voice. From this source, people draw impurity upon themselves. It is hidden from them like a flash of lightning, for they are drawn toward it, even though it sits below the holy place. Thus, the wicked—who sell themselves to follow that "Voice" of impurity—labor within it. Conversely, all the **righteous** who are drawn after holiness, purity, and good deeds draw upon themselves goodness, life, and peace. Their reward is in the **Garden of Eden** <term>Gan Eden: Paradise or the celestial realm of the righteous</term>, continuing toward the "Good Voice." For the righteous man is drawn after his Source, while sins—God forbid—stem from a different source.

Even though human life is lived in the balance, the longing and the authority are in the hands of man to incline himself toward kindness or otherwise. As it is written: *“See, I have set before you today life and good, and death and evil”* <note>Deuteronomy 30:15</note>. Behold, these two paths are handed over to man without any external compulsion. The first path is "the Day," which represents all holiness and purity, the secret of the holy **Atzilut** <term>Atzilut: the world of "Emanation," the highest of the four spiritual worlds in Kabbalah, closest to the Divine</term>. By following it, one draws life and merit upon himself. The second path is "Evil," which represents all that is profane and impure; following it draws death upon the person. 

The coming verses explain all this. To prove the way of the Good, it says: *“In that I command thee this day to love the Lord... to walk in His ways, and to keep His commandments and His statutes and His ordinances”* <note>Deuteronomy 30:16</note>. This is the Good, because purity and the commandments are drawn from Atzilut, which is the foundation of the heritage that leads to "cleaving" <term>Devekut: a state of meditative attachment or "cleaving" to the Divine</term> to Him. As it says at the end: *“To love the Lord... and to cleave unto Him,”* for the Good is drawn from the "Voice," and it results in "life and multiplication." 

In the introduction to this book, I explained a wonderful matter regarding this through a parable. If the "Enticer" leads one to the Evil path, and the soul does not listen, but rather turns away and bows down to other gods and serves them—all of which is drawn from the side of Impurity—this is the Evil. All the letters in the Torah are meant to distance man from this stumbling block. The text proclaims: *“I announce to you this day that you shall surely perish,”* which is the death that is drawn from that side. Afterward, the Heavens and the Earth are called as witnesses that these two paths are handed over to man's power and authority. Those called "Living" are those who choose life, as it says: *“I have called heaven and earth to witness against you this day... therefore choose life, that thou mayest live, thou and thy seed.”*

It is clear from all this that both paths are in the hand of man. One who is drawn after the side of holiness and purity fulfills the reason for the commandments and receives a reward. One who is drawn after impurity experiences the "taste" of transgression and receives his "reward" accordingly. This is what is meant by the phrase: *“The reward of a commandment is a commandment, and the recompense of a transgression is a transgression”* <note>Ethics of the Fathers 4:2</note>. Just as from the holy side there is a place of reward for those who listen, there is likewise from the side of impurity a place for those who defile themselves, which is **Gehenna**. This is the meaning of the saying: *“He created the righteous, He created the wicked; He created the Garden of Eden, He created Gehenna”* <note>Talmud, Tractate Baba Batra 16a</note>.

There is an interpretation in this language regarding the various paths: Here, for the sake of holy rain, and likewise for the sake of seeing how all things are found and sown in the clouds. There are **seven circles** corresponding to the **seven pillars** of the Evil side, and they all stand to judge and entice. Those who cling to these circles and do not guard their ways in this world—whoever comes to be defiled in this world—they find him and lead him through many levels and many appointees. They all stand ready to bring the person close to the "Kingdom of the Father" <note>Abba</note> to clothe him [in holiness]... but for one who comes to be defiled, they lead him like a flower cast away, leading him through many levels...

<column-break/>

...and how many appointees there are! They all stand to find those people who draw near to them and loiter after that [impure] side. The holy [author] explained that according to the "wings" <note>likely referring to the wings of the soul or spiritual inclinations</note> mentioned above, whichever way a person inclines himself and cleaves, he draws that upon himself—whether good or evil, holiness or impurity. That is his "reward." He acquires for himself the holiness and purity that sanctify him, and after his death, he is elevated to the place he was drawn to in life, which is the Upper and Lower **Garden of Eden**.

However, if he turned his efforts toward impurity, it draws him in, and that is his "reward." They punish him according to his deeds and thoughts. The place drawn from that side is the Upper and Lower **Gehenna**. Just as there is a Garden of Eden below in this world to remember the righteous according to their deeds, so too is there a place below in this world for the wicked, called "Gehenna" in the language of our Sages. They said in the Tractate *Erachin*: *“Gehenna has three gates: one in the desert, one in the sea, and one in Jerusalem.”* <note>Talmud, Tractate Erachin 32b</note>

They further taught in the school of Rabbi Ishmael: *“‘Who has a light in Zion’—this refers to Gehenna; ‘And a furnace in Jerusalem’—this refers to the gate of Gehenna.’”* <note>Isaiah 31:9</note> They also said: *“There are two palm trees in the Valley of Ben Hinnom, and smoke rises from between them, and this is the gate of Gehenna that the children of Israel prepared in exile.”* Behold, these are its locations and conditions. Therefore, the words of the Sages are not merely a parable; if they were a parable, they would not derive laws of forbidden and permitted matters from them. They said in the first chapter of *Beitzah*: *“Raki said that the transport of fire is permitted on the path of Gehenna.”*

It is said in the *Midrash Ruth* regarding the verse *“I have set before you [life and death]”*: Just as in Jerusalem it is written, *“Says the Lord, whose light is in Zion and whose furnace is in Jerusalem,”* everyone knows they are like a structure of awe. Zion and Jerusalem are with one another, paired like **Male and Female**. All is holy to Him; they are not parables. There is nothing in the world that does not hint at these two "Living Beings," which are called the **Evil Inclination** and **Holiness** in the soul. By bowing down to the Name, as it is written: *“Therefore in the valleys [of fire] honor the Lord,”* <note>Isaiah 24:15</note> man honors his Creator.

There is another gate where the name **Zion** is found beneath the earth, two thousand cubits by two thousand cubits. It is a standing place of thin, weak fire. That gate is called *Kanon* <note>possibly a corruption of a term for a hearth or brazier</note>, and it spreads toward Jerusalem, the place of the Temple Mount, the place where every male stands to see the face of the Master, the Lord. The reason for this is that they are beneath the Temple Mount. There, the "Sun of Truth" <note>original: "שמש אמית"</note> is double the strength of a powerful furnace. This is comparable to the **Orlah** <term>Orlah: the foreskin, which in Kabbalah represents the "husks" or "shells" (Kelipot) that block holiness</term> that hovers over the **Covenant** <term>Berit: the sign of the covenant/circumcision, representing the channel of holiness</term>. Therefore, every male who has the sign of the Covenant upon him stands there before the Lord to atone.

The "Sold Gate" <note>original: "שער המכור"; possibly a technical name for a specific entrance to the underworld</note> is called "Uncircumcised" (*Arel*). When one bows down at the time of sin, the fire stands over the **Great Abyss** <note>Tehom Rabba</note>, which is the fire of Gehenna. This is the conclusion of their words. What we hear from their words clarifies what we are striving to explain in this chapter: that Zion and Jerusalem are paired together... for they are spiritual vessels. Just as "Light" and "Furnace" are Light (Male) and Candle/Female—the "Daughter" and the partner of **Lilith** <note>In Kabbalah, the female personification of the demonic or impure side</note>—these are the secret of Gehenna, the "Filth of the Shell." They have a hold on the family of Gehenna which resembles the Night, and they comprise the side of Impurity. One is near Zion and the other near Jerusalem. Man honors his Creator with the Name, as it says: *“And you shall love the Lord your God with all your heart”*—meaning with **both of your inclinations** <note>the Yetzer HaTov and Yetzer HaRa</note>. If a person is drawn to that which is honorable, the matter is transformed. But they are in the likeness of the *Orlah* (foreskin) which hovers over the *Berit* (Covenant), which is the secret of the world's attachment. Therefore, when one mentions the "Other Gods," there is no place for the Covenant, but rather the *Orlah* and the bowing into the Great Abyss, which is the secret of the "Wrath" of...

# Chapter 32 | Section on Divine Service | Chapter 32

His station, for they hiddenly placed him above with the ark of Pharaoh to curse him. This is through **Supernal Wisdom** <term>Chokhmah Ila’ah: the second and most hidden of the ten divine emanations (Sefirot), representing the first flash of divine intellect</term> and not as written at the end of the *Tikunim* <note>original: "תיקונין"; likely referring to the *Tikunei Zohar*, a foundational Kabbalistic text</note> in which there are "processions" and the secret of what he was. He—peace be upon him—was "other," as in the verse: *“But the Lord was angry with me”* <note>original: "ויתעבר יי' בי" (Deuteronomy 3:26)</note>. The **Sages of Truth** <note>original: "חכמי האמת"; a common term for Kabbalists</note> said that this word "angry" (*Va-yitaber*) is related to the word for "impregnation" (*Ibur*) <term>Ibur: a mystical concept where an additional soul enters a living person's body to assist them or fulfill a specific mission</term>. It is the glory of the *Ibur*. Similarly, they returned to what is written: *“visiting the iniquity of the fathers upon the children”* (Exodus 20:5), for this is a doubling of the *Ibur*, as He visits the wicked two or three times. This is the matter of "myriads." The "blows of the *Ibur*" are pressed like clay, a great elevation regarding this matter. It is difficult to describe with any word to one’s companion except by way of a sieve, for it is a tradition from the mouths of the Sages, and the Sages from the mouths of the Prophets, reaching back to Moses "mouth to mouth."

The master, **Rabbi Bahya** <note>Rabbi Bahya ben Asher (13th century), a famous Spanish commentator known for integrating Kabbalah into his Torah commentary</note>, of blessed memory, wrote in this language: "You must know that this matter is the kindness of the Omnipresent toward Israel, for the souls exist after the selection of the world of concealment." As our Rabbis of blessed memory said: "All Israel has a portion in the World to Come." This matter is sent forth in the metaphor of the interpreter who said: *“Behold, God does all these things, twice, three times, with a man”* (Job 33:29). We should consider it a fine thing, as these are the paths through which existence is maintained. What is written as "twice, three times" implies the necessity of choosing life after this current living state, in order to do good for them. This is also according to the tradition itself, which said that it is a requirement to fulfill the words of our God <margin>33</margin> at the "corners of the earth," that it might "shake the wicked out of it" (Job 38:13). This refers to the covering: *“It is changed like clay under the seal, and they stand out like a garment.”* He says that its structure in the scriptures is to take hold of the corners of the earth and shake the wicked from it, and afterwards to establish you beneath it. The earth "turns" from them like clay under a seal, for it turns and joins with the forms of thoughts, and every void and lack is fulfilled, while the wicked within them are like "worn-out garments."

And they said: "All choices are threefold." The wise man can deduce the changes of the exile, which is one standing of this matter. Thus far their words. The **Sages of Truth** said that the end of the matter depends on "the wicked man who fares well and the righteous man who fares poorly." They explained in the Midrash of **Rabbi Bakhnuka** <note>A pseudonym or rare reference often found in older mystical midrashim</note> that the sage asked: "Why does the wicked fare well and the righteous fare poorly?" It is because the righteous man was already a wicked man in the past, and he suffered, and now he has his punishment. This judgment is carried out through the **Sefirot** <term>Sefirot: the ten creative powers or attributes through which God interacts with the universe</term>. This is a correct thing, for judgments are only made upon those eighteen and older. But if a man comes after his growth and says, "I have already reached the number," his companions said to him: "How long is the scripture required?" He said to them: "Go and see Moses the Seeker, who was called to account for his son." And they say he added a thousand generations of children in his hand and he grew, and he was cleansed of the stains of the scriptures and erred for more years. And regarding the one who did not show his level and erred, it is written "after the kindness of the bonds of his vow." They wrote concerning the "shame" of the generation as follows: "The generation that is written 'passed' opens a door for the entire generation." This is what we say: "generations turn" within the structure. And the Holy One asked and led them in every single generation.

Regarding what he said about "until a thousand generations," it does not mean that the souls will not be refined until a thousand generations have passed, but rather to say that they will be prepared in this world until a thousand generations, which encompasses all the days of the world. But without doubt, in every day, the generations are refined. For they said in the Midrash that just as it is with the Messiah, so a generation will come where the souls in the body will be exhausted, and then the Messiah will be able to come. Then the "nest" will be for the individual, and he will merit the month of Elul, for it is written "strengthened in all generations." With this, the scriptural matter in this chapter is completed.

### Chapter 33

This matter of the "final reincarnation" <term>Gilgul: the transmigration or reincarnation of souls</term> was a kindness from the Omnipresent, Blessed be He, toward Israel, without doubt. There is yet a deeper and truer reason, which is already explained in this section: that the inheritance of the woman is always in the "cracking of the property," which is the "thorn of glory" and the repair of the cold. It is impossible for a person except through the "blossoming dust" and the guarding of glory according to the order of truth. Even his soul—and not because it was for the sake of "repairing the cold"—deserves to be attached to the lowest level. The good within the matter of the soul that his companions learned is the "inheritance of life," and he merited life to wear the "thorn" that followed him. Thus, it changes and settles, just as they returned to the point of the death of Solomon, through which they were repaired. This is the simple meaning of what is written regarding the soul:
<sig>58</sig>

<column-break/>

to judge at the end, meaning the death of the righteous, that he may be "gathered to his people." And the end falls before us. For every soul that hopes is shaken and bowed and not gathered; it is said "to live and be nourished." "And the soul of my lord shall be bound"—everyone shall receive it, for the gathering subtracts and captures it within the **Hollow of the Sling** <term>Kaf HaKela: a state of spiritual wandering or purification where a soul is "slung" between different forces until it is ready for rest</term>. He "devises means, so that the banished one be not expelled from him" (2 Samuel 14:14). Everyone suffers their destiny, for souls have a cycle of action, and it is enough for them to be joined and not lacking. Their actions are received, and one cannot die in his death. "He devises means" and repairs this in the verse: "in the days of your youth," perhaps you will repair that which you distorted, so that you are not banished from Him and you return to your Root. There is in the "devising of means" and "devising thoughts" the idea that the destiny of the matter depends on the **Inner Thought** <term>Machshavah: the highest level of human or divine consciousness in Kabbalah</term>, which does not return to anyone but Him, Blessed be He. For this is the glory of the *Ibur*, whose root is in **Supernal Wisdom**, the secret of Thought. Even the "longed-for judgment" could not stand over it; it is destiny, and you cannot know it.

In the Talmud regarding destiny, four verses are written about it. The Sages said it is like a king who prepared a crown for his son, a light and easy crown. He said, "This is for my son's head." When he was finished, he said to him: "And he shall be cleansed," for he is already worthy. He told him to repair it in Thought once more, and "He devises means," etc. The Master, the author of *The Belief* <note>likely referring to Rabbi Shem Tov ibn Shem Tov or another philosopher-kabbalist</note>, wrote in the book *Kiyyum* in this language: "The law is not called such except for the reincarnation of children in place of their father and your friend," etc., so that they do not mix. <margin>4</margin> From the mixture of Germany (Ashkenaz) they were mixed, and that which is written "twice, three times with a man." Also, the testimony is as if internal, like a procession, and in ten, and for eating—such as transgressions and the like—internally and those who were stoned, for they did not examine the exchange. The feet of their fathers did not stand in their "nest." From the distant past, there are ancient generations in every single generation, children and possessions. The explanation of his words according to what was explained before the Sages of Truth: He said that therefore Israel is publicized with the "Face" <note>original: "פרסוף פנים"; likely referring to the *Partzufim* or Divine Countenances</note> to say "how much." Therefore, when these were transferred with those, for every reincarnation, he needs "six for his children," from the name of every exchange of "his father and your friend," a hint to revive the "Ancient Judgment."

From the "mixture of Germany," he hints at those who were mixed into the bodies of the nations: "your actions are like clay, twice or three times with a man," like the matter of their offspring. Also, the reincarnation of one Jew into another, such as those sent for forbidden sexual unions, which today is a "cleansing of the name"—meaning laundry—and those who appear as "mamzerim" <term>Mamzer: a person born from a biblically prohibited relationship, often discussed in mystical terms as a misplaced soul</term> among them are the "exchange of children" who did not stand in their "nest." They are from those 974 generations <note>A Talmudic concept of generations that were planned but not created until later</note> that stood to be brought forth, and the Holy One, Blessed be He, did not create them but rather distributed them in every generation. These are what the Torah calls "children and possessions."

The Master [Rabbi Bahya], of blessed memory, further wrote: "And so I saw the wicked buried, who had come" (Ecclesiastes 8:10), for they do not desire the death of the wicked, but that he live among us. "And your people shall all be righteous" (Isaiah 60:21). The turn will go in the internal countenances through "laundry," for it is "rust" that must be removed. The explanation of this is in the "residue" which explains that they were originally there, and further worthy a second time by way of reincarnation in the bodies of Israel, as it is written: *“And so I saw the wicked buried, who had come... from the holy place”* (Ecclesiastes 8:10). That is, they came by way of mixtures. These are the "proselytes" (*Gerim*), for God does not desire the death of the wicked but rather their improvement through His ways. From them comes the "blow of mixtures," so that the hoping soul does not perish among the nations, for it is not similar to them. It is like a thorn being removed from the mixture. One who came like them will go like them; and one who came from the mixtures will return to the mixtures, as it is written in the Torah. Thus far his words.

The holy illuminator, **Rabbi Shimon bar Yochai** <note>Rashbi: the traditional author of the Zohar</note>, said in the book of *Tikunim*: "And if a thousand years are completed, it shall be for the **Shekhinah** <term>Shekhinah: the Divine Presence, often described as the feminine aspect of God dwelling in the world</term>." And in its wearing out, there is no silver or gold, nor shame before the Shekhinah, for He is holy. *“Behold, God does all these things, twice, three times, with a man”* (Job 33:29). The secret is this: in its structure, it is a "trespass" if it is not the first reincarnation. If it was refined, "happy is he"—this is the second reincarnation. "Within the dweller"—this is the third reincarnation. Thus far. This matter is spoken of by all the Sages of the Academy and the Talmud, from the elders back to Moses. Furthermore, the Supernal Wisdom saw fit to gather mercy and return it in the "Holy Mixture" and the "Palace of Myriads." From there, its fruit shall be revealed, a choice vine for the recipient of wisdom in the secret of the "Entering Spirit." From there they refined it by saying, "Behold, the world was," and the Sages of Wisdom said that it is like "what was, was," and he considered it "worthy of innovation." For these were not in the beginning. And so, "He devises means," etc. Here is the glory and honor; the Whole watches and the matter is prepared. From there it ceased, meaning...
