# Chapter 31 | Section on Divine Service | Chapter 32

He is distanced by its hand and diminished at the time of the power of his good source, and let the **evil occupation** be within him; his luck is stolen and they are separated. Even one who guards himself may become entangled and removed from the **Radiance of the Firmament** <term>Zohar HaRaki'a: the spiritual light that illuminates the soul's understanding</term>. He makes his skill like torches of fire, and through his walking, his face is directed downward as proof. God forbid that anger should turn toward the evil side because of the small portion within him, which is the foundation of evil. At the hour of its cutting off and its concealment, its power acts as a barrier of evil and bitterness. He himself acts out of an evil spirit from that source, becoming entwined in the belly of the abyss to couple with the holy spiritual spirit. In this way, the reward of the labor of the soul leads it to its source, which is that level within the **Holy Realm**. 

However, that level may prosecute against her, burning with the likeness and tangled growth of vitality according to her separation; a spirit from it rests upon her. If her transgression is not erased, she is cast into the **Sling’s Hollow** <term>Kaf HaKela: a state of spiritual wandering where the soul is tossed between conflicting forces, unable to find rest</term> and returns to the heart to waste away. But if she performed **repentance** <note>original: "תשובה" (Teshuvah)</note> and they disciplined her until the mixtures from the source of that level were refined, she is given life to build that which was destroyed. This returns the **cycle of the soul** <note>original: "הגלגול" (Gilgul)</note> to its source. The soul spreads out there in the baldness of spiritual prominence, and in the falling of the guards, the soul guards there. She is not alone in her explanation; from the beginning, the source is above her, and the lowly garments she wore are now meant to be wasted and returned to their distance. She becomes clothed in the garments prepared for her through her merits. In this way, she merits to return to the **Divine Presence** <note>original: "השכינה" (Shekhinah)</note>. 

This is the secret of the soul needing to ascend to the **Supernal Garden of Eden**; she strips off those garments and passes over their supernal bodies, just as she passed over their lower bodies. No spirit from the "cold window" <note>likely a metaphor for the realm of spiritual lack or shells</note> shall be cast to return through her. Behold, the soul, being from the holy places, cannot possibly emit anything other than the spiritual garments that constantly strengthen her with her essence. The essence of her judgment is the knowledge of **Good and Evil**, weighed between the Children of the Garden and the Tree that stands in the kingdom of the rest of the evil power. Through forms and visions within her, she may be swallowed up and the holy spirituality forgotten. Her evaluation is like the lower miracles, for there was no power in the lower miracles to destroy. In the upper worlds, she is called "absolute," and then she merits to enter the Supernal Garden of Eden. Before she enters, she must look through that "window" in the Crown to remember the source, so that she may be embraced and drawn near to the Holy. If she has merit, the holy appointee enlightens her and clothes her in a garment of light worthy of her existence. If not, the fear of the source clothes her, for it is a decree. She does all this by encountering every day those angels who offer praise, singing and sanctifying, and she is accompanied by the strength of his words. 

Thus, because the soul is from the holy places, the light of her journeying is the journeying of holiness. The "evil and bitter spirit" has no permission over her, and time has no dominion over her, for the **Source of Impurity** has no power over anything that is from the side of Purity and Holiness, unless a spirit lower than her is invited upon her through her evil deeds. This is the truth attained by the voice of the holy spiritual connection, which is the **Chashmal** <term>Chashmal: a celestial "glowing amber" or aura mentioned in Ezekiel's vision, serving as a boundary between divine light and the physical world</term> mentioned between the two holies. There, the fine spiritual soul is placed between the physical body. Since she is from the realm of the **Knowledge of Good and Evil**, she is tied to it and merits toward the evil if she is drawn in action after the evil—which is the nature of the "diluted knowledge" over her. She then receives from the external "evil," and is stuck and suspended in the consciousness of the soul that is a threshold for her. This is her life, tied to the level of "the end of all flesh" to be held by it. The "Sun" <note>perhaps referring to a specific angelic force or celestial body</note> seeks to devour and swallow her because she must justify what she "stole" from it. For everything returns to its source; in this world, being joined to a body, she must return what was taken. She shall not rise twice, for she was already judged.

<column-break/>

What I have explained regarding the matter of the soul and the capabilities of the "Forsaker of Souls" within it: May the Holy One, Blessed be He, save us from the judgment of **Gehinnom** <note>original: "גיסנה" (Purgatory/Hell)</note> and may our portion be in the Garden of His Kingdom, and may we merit the life of the **World to Come** <note>original: "העולם הבא" (Olam Ha-Ba)</note>, to shine in the light prepared for the righteous.

### Chapter 32

The **Sages of Truth and Justice** <note>Kabbalists</note> received the tradition that the soul which has sinned and rebelled against its Creator—dishonoring its paths—is sent back to the life of peace to repair its iniquities and return its debts. Even if it did not willingly follow the commandments and holiness, it is returned. In the **Midrash Rut HaNe'alam** <note>A mystical commentary on the Book of Ruth found in the Zohar</note>, they said regarding this: It is like a man who sows a grain of seed; it did not grow as expected, so he takes it and plants it in another place. And so it happens many times, as it is written: *"Behold, God does all these things, twice, three times, with a man"* (Job 33:29). 

In the chapter "A Man Sends," this is hinted at. Our Rabbis taught: *"And the spirit returns to God who gave it"* (Ecclesiastes 12:7). He gave it to you in purity; you must return it in purity. This is like a king of flesh and blood who distributes royal garments to his servants. The wise among them folded them and placed them in a chest; the foolish among them went and did work in them. After some days, the King requested his garments. The wise returned them polished and white; the foolish returned them dirty. The King was happy with the wise and angry with the foolish. Regarding the wise, he said: "Let my garments be washed and stored, and they shall go to their homes in peace." Regarding the foolish, he said: "Let my garments go to the laundry, and they shall be imprisoned." 

So too does the Holy One, Blessed be He, say regarding the bodies of the righteous: *"He shall enter in peace..."* (Isaiah 57:2), and regarding their souls: *"The soul of my lord shall be bound in the bundle of life"* (1 Samuel 25:29). Regarding the bodies of the wicked, He says: *"There is no peace, says the Lord, for the wicked"* (Isaiah 48:22), and regarding their souls: *"And the souls of your enemies He shall sling out as from the hollow of a sling"* (1 Samuel 25:29). 

Behold, this matter is hinted at here, for the intention of the verse is to inform us that the corrupted soul is slung like a stone and returned to this world. In the **Midrash of Rabbi Nehunia ben HaKanah** <note>The Sefer HaBahir, one of the earliest Kabbalistic works</note>, they said: Rabbi Mehuya asked, what is meant by the verse *"The Lord reigns forever"* and *"from generation to generation"*? Rabbi Phineas said: *"A generation goes and a generation comes"* (Ecclesiastes 1:4). Rabbi Akiva said: Why does it say "a generation goes and a generation comes"? It means "it has already come." 

It is like a King who had servants; he clothed them in garments of silk and embroidery. They ruined the garments and he cast them out. He took the garments and washed them until no stain remained. He then bought other servants and clothed them in these same garments, and he did not know if these servants were good or not. Thus, they returned in the garments that had already come into the world. But the King always guards them. *"And the dust returns to the earth as it was, and the spirit returns to God who gave it"* (Ecclesiastes 12:7). 

Furthermore, they said there: When Israel is good, the word of the Place is "to come" and "I will give you holy seed." But when Israel is bad, the seed is that which has "already come" into the world, as it is written, *"A generation goes and a generation comes"*—meaning one that has already been here. The explanation is that according to the plain meaning of the verse, it should have said "a generation comes and a generation goes," but by saying "a generation goes and [then] comes," it hints that the one going is the one coming back. This is the meaning of "Generation" (*Dor*) from the language of "dwelling" (*Dur*) in a land. 

There is also what the woman of Tekoa said to King David: *"For we must surely die, and are as water spilt on the ground, which cannot be gathered up again; neither does God respect any person; yet does He devise means, that His banished be not expelled from Him"* (2 Samuel 14:14). Furthermore, it is written *"Surely die"* (*Mot Namut*)—implying death after death. This hints at the soul that sinned in its first incarnation, as it was said: *"For in the day you eat of it, you shall surely die"* (Genesis 2:17). Regarding this secret, He said to him: *"For dust you are, and to dust you shall return"* (Genesis 3:19), for the soul causes the return. 

The master Kabbalist, **Rabbi Bahya** of blessed memory, wrote: *"And to dust you shall return"*—the intention follows the secret of the verse mentioned regarding our life, that there is no rest for the soul. This is what they said in the Midrash: "To dust you shall go" is not what is written, but "you shall *return*." From here we find a hint for the **Resurrection of the Dead**, which was already mentioned. And it is possible to say "to dust you shall return" means returning to life, for the world is like dust. *"As water spilt on the ground"*—so is the soul spilt; it goes and is not gathered to its place because it drips...

# Section on Divine Service | Chapter 33

We have further learned regarding the universal body and the form of the radiance of the **Supreme Wisdom** <term>Chokhmah Ila'ah: the first spark of divine intellect</term>, which draws the spiritual "branch" down. By its nature, it possesses **free will** <note>original: "בעל בחירה" (Baal Bechirah)</note> even when constrained within the physical body, in order to temper it. This is undoubtedly a high spiritual level, to the point that the "Kings" <note>likely referring to the "Kings of Edom" or primordial spiritual forces</note> took it to heart. As we have learned, this was crowned in the **Tradition** <note>original: "קבלה" (Kabbalah)</note> to provide perfection to the souls. Conversely, the "External Kings" <term>External Forces: the "Other Side" or Sitra Achra, representing spiritual impurity</term> seek to bow down to it. Because man possesses more free will than the **Ministering Angels** <note>original: "מלאכי השרת" (Malakhei HaShareth)</note>, his choice is doubled when he is chosen from the external bodies. 

Furthermore, some say that the souls of the "externals" <note>those outside the holy realm</note> wander and are reincarnated into the bodies of living creatures. It is known that the ancients spoke of this, as it is written: "From where does the soul come?" It returns to its source, and so on. This is the matter of **reincarnation** <note>original: "גלגול" (Gilgul)</note>, which is a path known to his companions, where the king returns to his path and his dwelling. This is a secret of the **inner soul** of the Tradition. It is necessary for us to know that this matter is almost entirely based on the "Image" <note>the *Tzelem*, or spiritual archetype of man</note>, unless one receives from the Prophets regarding His will. 

As clarified by our words, the knowledge of the "chosen one" comes from the initial expansion. From this, one understands the secret of the body. If the wisdom was hidden from them and they did not attain it, they would search for the root of wisdom and would not accept its height to improve upon the external qualities. They would ask: "From what place does the wisdom that was chosen in the body come?" These are truly the secrets of wisdom that are hidden within the **womb** <note>original: "עבור" (Ibur)</note>. If they knew the truth, they would be silent and wonder. 

From the way of the pure and the opposite: for one who says that man is like a beast, this is a rebellion against His authority. God forbid one should suggest that the Ministering Angels would bow to such a thing! This was only written regarding the First Man (**Adam**). The reason the Tradition mentions the light of the First Man is that even the Ministering Angels mistook him and sought to say "Holy" before him. What did the Holy One, Blessed be He, do? He cast a "deep sleep" upon him so they would know he was human. This is mentioned in the *Chapters of Rabbi Eliezer*. Regarding the "bowing to creatures," the **Translators** <note>likely the Aramaic Targum</note> said that when they saw him, they thought he was their creator and intended to bow to him. Now, there is no mistake in this statement; it does not mean the angels are part of the forbidden "external" class. Reincarnation is a deep matter, and though it may seem far from human honor to be within a beast, this is a secret known to all the Sages of the Tradition. Aside from their tradition, they have support in the words of our Sages, as will be explained in the next chapter, with the help of Heaven.

# Chapter 34

As we explained in the first **rectification** <note>original: "תיקון" (Tikun)</note>, we learned that everything lacks light. As we wrote, the most external part of the self is subject to **reincarnation** <note>original: "גלגול" (Gilgul)</note>. Now, the soul wanders through the world, for there are transgressions that weigh so heavily that the soul is forced into the material world of Israel, and there are transgressions where the power of **Judgment** <note>original: "דין" (Din)</note> forces it outside, meaning into the nations of the lands. 

There are also transgressions so severe that the power of Judgment causes the soul to be reincarnated into a **beast**. This is a "True Judgment," well known to those who understand the external secrets. The wisdom of the "Sufis" <note>Here used to mean "mystics" or "those with hidden knowledge"</note> and the initial thinkers is that the soul is reincarnated into a beast, a tradition held by the Sages of Truth. 

They said that the place of the **Altar** <note>original: "מזבח" (Mizbe'ach)</note> below is aligned exactly with the **Temple** <note>original: "בית המקדש" (Beit HaMikdash)</note> above. Michael, the High Priest of the celestial realm, stands there and offers up...

<column-break/>

...and recently, in the literal sense of the "Righteous," meaning the **sacrifices** <note>original: "קורבנות" (Korbanot)</note> that are brought every day below, they are equivalent to the souls of the righteous. For they have brought the essence of the species back to its path. Those who were lowered from their level through their conduct are brought back to the earth to be refined. If they are strong in spirit and directed even slightly toward their source, and if their sins have been thinned out, they are ready for reception. 

The Temple is aligned with the Temple above, so that in the directed intention, there is no "Satan" and no "Evil Occurence" in the eating of the holy meat. Therefore, the cloud of the sacrifice rises without deviating. Do not say "a sacrifice," but rather "When a man offers from you a sacrifice to the Lord." The secret is that the sacrifice of the animal is linked to the **Righteous** <note>original: "צדיק" (Tzaddik)</note>, who draws it from above to here. 

Furthermore, He will have mercy and prepare the creations and the portions of man in the primary animals that are reincarnated. When there is no more lack, from the "death that is not death," it ascends higher and higher. When one desires to eat meat, it is because he is elevating the portion that is worthy of ascent. This is the meaning of "because your soul desires to eat meat"—meaning, through your desire, you intend to elevate that which is found within the species. Therefore, the eater must be one who elevates the "inner spark." The food is prepared for him as "living food." But if the eater only intends to satisfy his hunger, then the food gives strength to the lower forces instead of ascending to the proper heights. 

Those souls that are reincarnated in this way are a matter of truth, and the Sages are careful with them. This is the secret of the "inclusion" and the "sweetening." After all their deeds, the external side is prepared for them. The righteous who maintain the soul of Israel are as if they sustain the whole world. 

Regarding the generations who took the blows from below, even the "Masters of the Primordial," they have no way to purify themselves from all obstacles. However, the matter of the "finding" is known. What the Sages said—that the Torah was given on the day the "crown of the slave" was broken—means it is now permitted to eat meat. The Sages of the Tradition wondered: if the great eat the small, and the beast is like the man, why should the greater eat the lesser? If it were not for the "elevation of the sparks," it would be better for a man to eat the grass of the field rather than turn a beast into his own flesh.

The author of the book *Ha-Yichud* wrote that the language "eat this" and "do not eat that" regarding birds and beasts refers to those that are close to the mystery of the soul. Through the sacrifice, the soul is unified with its root. This explains why the Torah forbade us from eating things that "darken the soul." 

Sometimes a righteous soul is found within the flesh of a pure beast or bird. It is reincarnated into that body, and therefore the Torah commanded us to bring it as a sacrifice, so the righteous soul may ascend through the sacrifice to the "Will of the Lord." If you look at the daily occurrences, you will see the truth in the saying: "I have placed the soul in the blood." The Sages also mentioned this in *Tractate Eduyot*, Chapter 6, regarding a rooster that was stoned in Jerusalem because it had killed a person—they treated it as a human because a soul was within it. The Sages of Truth said that the beast was killed because it was deserving of it, having been judged for a capital crime. This is what is said in *Eduyot*. I have already expanded on this, for there is nothing more wonderful in his eyes than the wisdom of the soul.

# Section on Divine Service | Chapter 33

Regarding **Adam the First Man** <note>original: "אדם הראשון" (Adam HaRishon)</note>, it is written of them: "and she was naked and bare" <note>quoting Ezekiel 16:7, applied here to the primordial state</note>, because they were not yet completed through the commandments. They were "naked" of the nullification <note>meaning they lacked the spiritual covering provided by selfless devotion</note> and were in a state of poverty. But after they were refined from the **filth of the serpent** <term>Zohamat HaNachash: the spiritual impurity introduced into humanity by the primordial serpent</term>, they were already shifted into a chosen place from which he was taken. There, for his congregation, he prays to complete it, as it is written: "and your nation stands over you."

If the person does not complete that **rectification** <term>Tikkun: the process of repairing the world and the soul</term> and transgresses what he was commanded in the Torah, he causes a "purchase of possession" <note>an attachment to the material or "external" shells</note> and separates the Divine Unity. He ruins his generation and leaps into errors and happenstance, for the burning of the evil within the "matter of evil" clings to him. He then moves, by the grace in his hand and authority, to deepen it and discipline it. After he fails due to the **primordial blemish** <note>original: "פגם הראשונית" (Pegam HaRishonit), the original sin of Adam</note> and does not repair what he was created to repair and complete, he must, by all means, repair it. For he has no other way, and it is impossible in any other manner at all.

This is the "pressure of the **Supreme Wisdom**" <note>original: "חכמה העליונה" (Chokhmah Ila'ah)</note>: that he should return to the days of his youth for merit and complete the repair through a new structure, as in a third time. In this regard, it is said: "God works all these things, [twice, three times with a man]" <note>Job 33:29</note>. Sometimes one receives punishment and suffering in this world as a result of the transgressions he previously committed. He prays to repair what he twisted through **repentance** <term>Teshuvah: literally "returning" to God</term> and by abandoning his path. Through this, he is repaired and merits to be clothed in the **Radiance of the Divine Presence** <term>Ziv HaShekhinah: the perceptible glow of God's indwelling presence</term>, to shine in the light of life.

According to the law, it is said that he is punished for his past, and this is the "Book of the Covenant" of the teacher. If he is released from his illness, he attains all the "acquisition of glory," which is the ultimate purpose for which he was created. There is no perfection without this at all, nor even a half-measure. For through what would he be repaired? He must fill the deficiency. It would be "sweet" for him, but he did not prepare on the "Eve of the Sabbath" <note>a metaphor for preparing in this life for the world to come</note>. Therefore, it is established that it is impossible to complete and show the deficiency except by his returning to the "days of his youth" time after time, until he clarifies that which he worked for and chose. This was the "rectification of the Glory" and the essence of the purpose. 

**Joseph** <note>likely referring to a specific commentary or the biblical figure as a symbol of the soul's ascent</note> rejoiced in the soul’s elevation toward the **Redemption**, which it receives through the appeasement and ease of his soul. He is sanctified from the radiance of the **Shekhinah** <note>the Divine Presence</note>, and through this, he understands and elevates the loss and the Will that was upon him. As long as it is not completed by man, it is as if it was never created. He must come and come again to complete it, for such was the Will from the beginning—time after time—until he completes the "word of the Lord," the actual word of the Lord.

The **Holy Zohar** <note>the primary text of Jewish mysticism</note> on page 91a says in the *Book of Tikunim*: "Furthermore, they look for food, clothing, and a dwelling, which is the Sabbath." It is a simple dwelling, not one that dwells in its measure and busies itself, etc. And there is no one who weeps for the "food" which comes from the side of the Shekhinah. On this Sabbath, the "garment of Enoch" <note>referring to the angelic transformation of the biblical Enoch</note> is like his clothing and his wrapping. The **Tefillin of the hand** <note>phylacteries worn on the arm</note> are placed there, as in "A prayer for the poor man when he is wrapped" <note>Psalm 102:1</note>. There is a delay in its matter. If a man is complete, he will not build the completion [externally], but rather everything is released into life. If he has no "Soul of the Face," then the Shekhinah is "wrapped." And "God works all these things, twice, three times with a man."

By what is said here, the intention of Adam was for the first **reincarnation** <term>Gilgul: the transmigration of souls</term>. His "helpmeet" was for the second reincarnation. The cause of this was the third reincarnation with "balance in his tongue." I have already written earlier in the previous chapter a bit about this matter. This is the opinion of the Holy [Zohar] and its intention: to teach through these words what we have strived to explain in this section—that the **Divine Service** <note>the performance of commandments and prayer</note> is a **need of the High** <term>Tzorech Gavoah: the idea that human actions affect or "sustain" the Divine realm</term>. This is what is meant by "they go," etc., and "there is no one who weeps for the food which is from the side of the Shekhinah," etc. In the heights of his knowledge and his tradition, according to the principle of what the perfect servant must seek, ask, and intend in his service—it is for the "need of the Glory," which is the "food of the Shekhinah."

This is revealed in two things: First, he made it the essence, saying "another who invites the food of my warmth." And regarding this, it is said later that he "forgot his name." Second, the "existence of the commandments," as he said: "In its death, this is the death of Enoch," etc. The hidden meaning of these essences is the **Unification** between the two "beloveds" <note>the masculine and feminine aspects of the Divine</note>. He said, "and the Sabbath busies itself," which is the completion of the "food" when it is within man, intending for this purpose which is a "need of the High" and not for a "commoner's need." Regarding the verse "supported from him," as I explained in this section, the measure of reception is awe. One must intend first and as the main thing for His joy; because of it, all goodness and perfection are drawn down, which is the "need of the High." After we have clarified what was intended from the beginning—namely, that reincarnation was necessary time after time until—

<column-break/>

—they completed the "acquisition of the Glory," which is a "need of the High." This is what he meant by saying: "And if God's worker does not build the Shekhinah..." and "Not every man..." and "In what was said thus..." This means that because he did not prepare, he will need a reincarnation for the sake of **rectification**. This is what we sought to know: [the soul] prays and completes it. 

Regarding what we have composed in the explanation of the matter of reincarnation, I will write what I have heard from the inquiry of the Sages, of blessed memory, regarding the answers concerning its matter. You already know that every thing returns to its root. If it is specifically elevated, it adds to it. What is diminished from it? As it is written: "And the spirit returns [to God who gave it]" <note>Ecclesiastes 12:7</note>. This is when the person is silenced [in death] and clings here. When his soul ascends and is established, a spirit from a place that is not in the future rests upon it. It is not worthy of rest and the "Holy Tranquility," for while the soul was in the body, it descended and was lowly. 

It must be delivered into the hand of the **Primordial Level** <note>original: "מדרגה הקדומה" (Madreget HaKedumah)</note> from which it came. The "Unique One" is exalted over him and his soul, as our Sages of blessed memory said: "He descends and trusts in it and guards it; He takes permission and takes the soul." To the extent of this level, it desires to cleanse from it what was attached and what was "stolen" upon it. He will rejoice and acquire it—this is its glory in which it is clothed. It is not within his power to conquer it, but he merits to nourish it in the "Hadassah" <note>Myrtle</note>, which is the actual **Lower Garden of Eden**, to take our portion of spiritual ease. 

And so, look, there are several levels of the **Lower Garden of Eden** and the **Upper Garden of Eden**. In the Upper Garden of Eden, through the power of the pious and the goodness that fills it, one merits to ascend to behold "the pleasantness of the Lord and to visit His temple" with a great addition beyond what it had before it was created: the spirit of the **World to Come**.

Sometimes the Angel [appointed] over him eases his suffering, and he merits judgment to open. After the one who breaks from his dwelling is elevated according to that order, he returns to the "days of his youth" and is materialized in the body worthy of it. Through this, the punishment by suffering is ceased. Sometimes this is through **Levirate marriage** <term>Yibbum: the practice of a man marrying the widow of his childless brother to continue the lineage</term> or through another close relative. Sometimes the "Potter" <note>God</note> can, according to his initial deeds, choose a bit from him, and he merits the light in its totality. This is the case if he is "completely built" according to his continuation after these middle levels. 

There are those who are "hot" <note>passionate or impulsive</note> and intended by himself in strength; he merits the Holy, but not until the end, being repaired at the last. There are those for whom it suffices [to return] to the "Ancient One" one time to be filled with mercy until he is more than "built." The permission in its coming and returning is sometimes "built" according to the smallness of the first ones; he comes "built" in a soul from the "vomit" <note>a difficult metaphor for a rejected or lower state</note> and receives a space from his choice. It is possible that he will return and repair. Suffering is decreed upon him, and he is repaired against this. It is proper to give to the face of the lack, with deficiencies in a body that is more holy, yet he still comes "built" and moves through suffering and the experiences of the world. 

And behold, he goes up another time so as not to be missing, after he is awakened by way of **reincarnation**. He takes every limb there to explain it, whether in a "structure of height" or a "structure of reincarnation." Sometimes reincarnation occurs because one was without a "spouse" <note>original: "פלף" (likely a typo for "אלף" or "חלק"), referring to a soulmate</note> in this world, and not because he is another from the chain. Any matter regarding his companions is because the deficiency is within him, and it is not proper for the "Perfect One" to be seen over the "Blemish." Most times, the constant sound returns and is reincarnated in the reincarnations of "building" and its varieties. 

The divisions of reincarnation are impossible to fully grasp, for the essence of it is hidden in the **Supreme Wisdom**, which is the **Thought** <term>Machshavah: the highest level of divine emanation</term>. Even **Moses** did not grasp it in its perfection, which is why it is said of him: "The righteous who suffers," etc. This is the secret of reincarnation as it was said to him regarding the reincarnation of **Rabbi Akiva**: "Silence! Thus it arose in Thought" <note>a famous Talmudic quote where God tells Moses not to question the suffering of the righteous Akiva</note>. 

Behold, the paths of Glory for the souls of this body by way of reincarnation were not under the dominion of a king. But it is in the hand of man to draw this lack to himself or that lack. He did not dream, and the ancient exchange of one against the other was a wonder. After these words and hints are established in the heart, regarding what was written against what we have understood and brought in the matter of reincarnation—and as was explained later in Chapter 28 of the Fourth Light—according to the calculation of these times. From here comes the essence of the tradition and the knowledge of reincarnation. Because they are those whom you have heard, it is understood according to the Torah: the soul, while it exists, is nothing but a guardian of itself, as we have said. Therefore, from his tribe and family, they are perfumed and given strength in the body of his initial deficiency, and thus he is repaired. It is possible that he will be grasped in actual flesh in a human body and be bound.

# Section on Divine Service | Chapter 35

3

The perfectly righteous <note>original: "צדיקי גמורים" (Tzaddikim Gemurim)</note> do not dwell there. What is the reason? Rather, this level is sweetened in the **Supreme Crown** <term>Keter Elyon: The highest of the ten Sephirot or divine emanations, representing the Divine Will</term>. The Crown of the commandment of the Sabbath is sweetened by it. And who is it? **Repentance** <term>Teshuvah: Literally 'return'; the process of returning to one's divine source after straying</term>. It is for this reason they are called "Masters of Return" <note>original: "בעלי תשובה" (Ba'alei Teshuvah)</note>. And these are sweetened in the other Crown corresponding to this one. For this reason, these dwell in the Supreme Crown and those dwell in the Lower Crown. This is why you cannot travel to your places from the supreme place to the surrounding deep until that place is called "Righteous." And the perfectly righteous all have their destination in the place where they dwell for this world. Therefore, these are upper and those are lower. Yet all of them have a portion in Repentance, and all of them have a portion in the Righteous, for whose sake the world is sustained, etc.

And in the chapter on the **Day of Atonement** <note>original: "יום הכפורים" (Yom Kippur), referring to a section of the Talmud</note>, it is said: Great is Repentance, for it reaches to the **Throne of Glory** <note>original: "כסא הכבוד" (Kisse HaKavod)</note>, as it is said: "Return, O Israel, unto the Lord your God" <note>Hosea 14:2</note>. **[Marker]** For the rectification reaches until the influence of the "branches," which is the Throne of Glory for the "Living Being" <note>referring to a class of angels</note> that is above it, and it is called "Mercy" in the Crown of the mouth. From there, one receives and draws down the light below, and it is called the "Voice of the Messiah." Great is the righteous of the world; his levels are in Wisdom and the awe of the Atonement of the burnt offering, and it is a **[Marker]**. 

He revealed that Repentance brings redemption to the world, as it is said: "And a redeemer shall come to Zion, and to them that turn from transgression" <note>Isaiah 59:20</note>. And it is written: Thus he rectified and improved the dwelling of the Glory, and the verse says, "and rides upon them." It is known that by cause of the "horn" and the separation, the sustenance is from the "sweeteners," and the wrath is sweetened. For sin brings death. And when he returns and improves, he calls upon the children so that they may merit. For this is the secret of Repentance, and it is the source of Life as explained: **[Marker]** that which is above it. If one clings to it, behold, they cling to Life, in which there is no death. This is why it says there: "Great is Repentance, for it lengthens the days and years of a person." And because he strengthened himself in Repentance, he learned from where the redemption comes; it is the edge of the Supreme Rectification and its sustenance. When one merits these things, **Mercy** <note>original: "רחמים" (Rachamim)</note> prevails over **Judgment** <note>original: "דין" (Din)</note>, and he receives a portion from the Sanctuary, etc. There is no protest or accusation there, for there is no one to arouse the "Kings" <note>referring to the forces of harsh judgment</note>, as the accuser has been removed. This arouses Mercy upon the world in general and for him in particular. This is what is said there: "Great is Repentance, for even if his days were [numbered], they forgive him." In the entire world, if he returned out of love, he clings to it, for there he is truly attached.

From what we have explained further, there was reason to doubt the matter of Repentance: how is it possible for Repentance to be effective in removing the sin and erasing the transgression that was committed in action? Who can undo what has been done? If he practiced foreign worship <note>original: "עבודה זרה" (Avodah Zarah) - idolatry</note> or killed a soul, how can Repentance repair such a great distortion? In truth, if the transgressions remained in their place, they would never be undone at all. But when one does Repentance, it is considered as if they were never done. The sin is gathered up and does not enter. The debt is considered as if it was never borrowed. And the soul returns to its place, which is the "Body of Repentance." 

And even more difficult than this is what was said in the chapter on the Day of Atonement: "Great is Repentance, for intentional sins are transformed into merits" <note>Talmud, Yoma 86b</note>. This is an exceedingly high level. In the Midrash, they were in doubt about this "sweetening." Rabbi Yochanan said: Not only that, but for every transgression a person commits, the Holy One, blessed be He, forgives them or turns them into merits. However, when we look deeply into the fact that transgressions cause separation and damage the "Plantings" <note>a Kabbalistic metaphor for the divine emanations</note>, ruining and pushing away the Throne and uncovering the "Nakedness of the Father," this destroys worlds and ruins the supreme orders, as we have written. Know and understand that by returning in Repentance, he repairs them. And this is why the Holy One, blessed be He, in His holiness, mentioned in the first part of this book: behold, he will rectify everything he did. The soul returns to its place and is covered by its children and its rectification. This is the secret of the "Unity of the Smallness" revealed in His glory; the crown—the crown of the "barren woman"—shall return to its former place as it was before the sin. Behold, this is like a complete building; he too is considered a new creation, as if he was created now and never sinned. In this act, the Name is sanctified, and the spring is drawn forth, and the emanations of light and blessing are found in the Great Name. His glory shall be uplifted, and the Glory shall be rectified. By the inclination of the "Smallness," the King is joined to all of this. This is considered a great merit for him, for Repentance caused all of this, and thus intentional sins are made into merits. 

According to this, the level of the Penitent is like the level of the Righteous who never sinned—

<column-break/>

—never sinned. Indeed, he has a great advantage over him, because he enters and is bound above, higher than the level of the Righteous. For every person is bound and clings to the Chariot <note>original: "מרכבה" (Merkavah)</note> according to their deeds and ways. The Righteous is bound and enters through the "Uprightness of the World," which is the "Righteous One" of the worlds. But the Penitent is bound and enters through the "Supreme Repentance," which is the "Source of Life" <note>original: "חיי המלך" (Chayei HaMelech)</note> in the hidden places. He draws down and influences water and food from the place where he is stationed, above the place of the Righteous. The Righteous then shines and is illuminated from that place to sustain his world, as the Midrash proved above. 

One must know that through the "Subjugation of the Evil" <note>original: "אכפיא דסטרא אחרא"</note>, the Holy One is exalted and glorified. This is the essence of the matter: when the "Other Side" <term>Sitra Achra: The side of impurity or evil in Kabbalah</term>, which is the main source of evil, is subdued and broken by him—and all impurity is surrendered and lowered—then the Supreme Light and the Glory of the Holy One, blessed be He, is glorified and exalted in all the worlds. This is what our Sages, of blessed memory, said in the chapter "The Trial is Finished" <note>Talmud, Sanhedrin 43b</note>: Rabbi Joshua ben Levi said: "Whoever slaughters his impulse and confesses over it, the Scripture considers it as if he honored the Holy One, blessed be He, in two worlds: this world and the world to come," as it is written: "Whoso offereth the sacrifice of confession honoreth Me" <note>Psalm 50:23</note>. The meaning of "offering" is breaking it and subduing it. Those who establish the "Will" and the world of "Anger," he subdues them for what he transitioned. 

In the case of the Master of Repentance, the things he returned from—those he was accustomed to with all his strength, desire, and satiation—he did not do them. In the Midrash of Rabbi Nehuniah ben HaKanah: "I will make you know," etc. Come and see, I will teach you. For a person who covers his sins and does not explain them before the Holy King and request mercy for them, they do not give him an opening to the gate of Repentance. Because if he repeats his folly, and they were certainly to give him a "Life of Good" upon them, his debt would be increased upon the judgment. This is especially true if he is a son of the "Other," for all gates are closed to him. But he opened and was accepted by God. Therefore, they spread out to show his honor, for the King is to be graced with mercy over the judgment. And therefore it is written, "And the sacrifice of confession shall honor Me." What is "shall honor Me" <note>original: "יכבדוני" (Yechabeduni)</note>? The double "N" <note>the word ends in a plural-sounding suffix</note> refers to two honors: one below and one above; one in this world and one in the world to come. 

Thus, by his jewelry and the spreading out of his sin, he makes Mercy prevail over Judgment. This is his luck and the Glory of the Holy One, for the strengthening of Mercy over Judgment is the power of the "Binding." The "Smallness" is surrendered and broken, for it has no place to be aroused. Once it is surrendered above, it is also surrendered below. Thus, the Glory is honored above and below. This is what it means: "two honors, one below and one above." 

The continuation of the Glory follows the Master of the rectification of Repentance into the Supreme Glory and the World to Come, which is entirely great. It is like being heralded before the King in person. This is his "life in this world" and "life in the world to come." And they said in the chapter on the Day of Atonement: "What is a Master of Repentance like? For example, if a transgression came to his hand and he separated from it." Rav Yehuda explained: "In that same place, with that same woman, and in that same time." Behold, this is a Master of Repentance! For even though the habit was there, and it was sweet to him, and it was in his hand, and he was ruled by his wing and his desire—yet he subdues it. "Whoso offereth the sacrifice of confession" intends to subdue and lower and remove all the impurity that intends to satisfy its Master. Behold, he has a great spring, and he stands in it. This is the one who uplifts and honors the Holy One, blessed be He. In this, his level is very great. 

Behold, the level of the Perfectly Righteous who never sinned is great because he never entered and the Accuser never was crowned in him. He never tasted the sweetness of transgression, nor did he come to the point of needing to subdue it so that the Name would be exalted and glorified in His glory, as the Master of Repentance does. And so it is heard: "In the place where the Masters of Repentance stand, the perfectly righteous cannot stand" <note>Talmud, Berakhot 34b</note>. In these two things—which are the foundations of Repentance—the "Other Side" is subdued and the Holy One, blessed be He, is exalted and unified in His Glory in His dwelling. This is what we have said. 

And second, when he regrets what he did and is bitter and groans over his former deeds, he confesses and shows in himself that those sins were evil, and that they are truly the "Other Side" which is pure evil. By confessing his sins and subduing them—since sin is pure evil and has no—

## Chapter 34

May your wisdom be present, for all His ways are justice. And regarding those who left their fatness upon the soaps <note>This likely refers to a process of spiritual purification or refining one's character</note>, the mystery is "white as snow," for His garment is like "clean wool." Through their fall, there is repentance. They further said that the matter of judgment is to include the law—the judgment that is the "Book of the Lord from Sinai"—and all the fine details of the commandments found in the words of our Sages, of blessed memory. This is for the knowledge of those who return, so that it shall not be flawed, for the benefit of souls mixed within bodies. Through their incantations, the attributes act, and He shall further rectify, for she is the mixture.

The Rabbi, author of the **Book of the Image** <term>Sefer HaTemunah: An early, influential Kabbalistic work that discusses the Hebrew letters and cosmic cycles (Shemitot)</term>, divided the words, as "salted" <note>original: "מלוח" (maluach)</note> is at the end of the tongue. It is fitting for him to rectify the "magic of water" forever, through the mystery of ascending to the cutting of the foundations. For him, a beautiful death is a sphere, as it is written: "and you shall take to your desire as within." It is full of study, and the misguided shall live, and wisdom shall be disqualified by your hand. Let all be white because of their merit. They explained my words thus: the reason His hands are ready to build the righteous is so there will be no hunger. They are "Pearls of Life," for they are worthy of life. Therefore, they established that the Sages gave fine flour for every expression—Moses mentioned the partition of the chosen ones. 

Upon every mouth, the sweetness of deaths, etc. And in the "Taking of the Community," it was written: "and its fat for your desire as within." One must place the seal of His hidden wisdom upon the path of kindness <note>original: "חסד" (Chesed)</note>. Through him, the mystery was excused, and through the hand of kindness, it is "white" to him, for we have salted it and its spices shall be. They shall live for the Midrash regarding the building. Furthermore, they received that from the "salted" <note>original: "מלוח" (maluach)</note>, we declined the Torah to the "God of the spirits of all flesh," for it hinted at the power of the sphere, a mystery in all flesh—meaning, in the powers, the sides, and the incantations. They returned to "all flesh," meaning every soul. They said that for this light, the one learned in Torah becomes a firstborn servant of the Will, coming so they are not torn or cast away. It was also mentioned that when the letter *Qof* precedes the *Yod*, it is the "time of the blows," for they are like the salt. And as God spread it for him, his hands were filled within, for the "mercy of salt" rolled into the soul. Blessed be God for his sake; in rectifying the saltiness, He performed kindness, preparing their characteristics and their rulers, which are hidden from human knowledge. 

The source of the Torah contains the intellect to seek and investigate in poverty. His generation doubled His seal: "In that which is too wonderful for you, do not seek; in that which is hidden from you, do not investigate" <note>A classic Rabbinic caution against over-speculation into the divine mysteries</note>. Do not turn away, for these are words of tradition, and it is good for us to accept the time of tradition—a style of knowledge. How blessed is God for the one who speaks from the Hebrews and from the scholars. I have learned the kindness of His power and in His hand. For my teacher, it is written: "The salt is everything," so that salt should not come into his hand. The sphere of the Hand of the Lord, a pillar of tradition, knows. Therefore, every person is obligated to bring his heart into wisdom with his intellect, to seek after Him, to know through refining, and to leave everything to you. For thus they shall see kindness and there shall be a mixture. He shall lead them to the upper sides and the outcomes of the commandments forever. He shall shake the attributes of the transgressions and rectify them, for his thoughts and his supporters shall graze upon the touch of the holy. They shall include the letters **Y-H** <note>The first two letters of the Tetragrammaton, often associated with the hidden realms of Wisdom and Understanding</note> to explain and achieve the general perfection. This is known at the proper time to the masters of the True Wisdom. And that which awakens us to speak of it is the matter of the sphere and the salt; they shall have mercy through the fall from the Torah of Grace.

## Chapter 35

**Repentance** <note>original: "התשובה" (HaTeshuvah)</note> is the existence of the world and its foundation. Were it not for Repentance, the world would not have been created. Just as the pillar of a building cannot stand without a foundation, so too the standing of the world and its existence would not return if Repentance were not established for its preservation. For it is the medicine that heals in the upper depths, to bring them close to the Good God. Their salts are the nourishment, and the commentary sweetens the salt—it is compassion. It empowers the soul and strengthens it. This is why the world was written for its sake. 

In the third chapter of **Pirkei De-Rabbi Eliezer** <note>An 8th-century Midrashic work on the creation and history of Israel</note>: Before the world was created, there was only the Holy One, blessed be He, and His Name. It arose in His thought to create the world, and He would "sketch" <note>original: "מחריט" (macharit)</note> the world before Him, but it would not stand. They gave a parable: To what is the matter comparable? To a king who wanted to build his palace. If he does not sketch with a stylus its foundations, its exits, and its entrances, he does not begin to build. Thus, the Holy One, blessed be He, sketched the world before Him, and it did not stand until He created Repentance. The explanation of the matter is in the hidden mystery: for the markers are the path of kings.

<column-break/>

In the Torah of the Lord, those who contemplate His attributes are the ones who sustain the upper existence. They constantly join from the outside to the foundation of the Great Name in His glory, preparing a building for their pairs, one with another. There is no exchange of the Holy Spirit there, nor separation. This is the perfect existence in its splendor and its elevation, for in the ladder of the scripture, it is according to its creation. For this reason, they surround it; the first [attribute] hovers over them, ruling around them, and completing the kindness and the touch of blessing upon them. There is no touch of nakedness there, nor flaw or separation, for they are the unifications of the ladder, and His scepter... they sweeten the flour together for the sea. In their portions, they shall be cleansed, and the ladder of their grace is in the hidden ones through the Will of the Creator. 

They are guided by His will, and because of them, through the balance and its structures, He turned His evil into softness, and it reaches to the upper heavens. For this reason, the Glory ascends from upon them and is revealed from them like the measure of the receiver. Those who separate between the water and the salt are angry at the building, and the living spirit is sent away, for the portion is received as a mystery. In their longing, wisdom is filled. The upper Voice prevents its blessings from being received, for the blessing of life is present only in a place where it is remembered and gathered. The blessing is prevented from the foundation because the attachment is not desired with it. 

There is a mystery of "saltedness" and "salt" upon its cup—the mystery of all life, water, and soul. Therefore, "the little Rachel" <note>A Kabbalistic reference to the lower Shekhinah or the soul of Israel</note> shall have mercy on her children, for "he loved her." He should have said "because her husband loved her," for he ascended from upon her. Regarding the children, it is written: "and from their dew and the strength of their touch, she shall have mercy on the children because he loved her." 

When the Holy One, blessed be He, sought to create the world, He would sketch the world before Him, but it would not stand because of the sins that would eventually spoil their deeds and cause the ruin of the upper blessings and their destruction. But through the Name, it shall be established and the world shall return, until He saw in His wondrous wisdom to rectify this, and He created Repentance. 

In the **Midrash of Rabbi Shimon bar Yochai** <note>The Zohar</note>, regarding "You shall forgive": When the Holy One, blessed be He, wished to gaze upon the world, and from that which was prepared in the lower dwellings for the Ancient of Days <term>Atik Yomin: The highest 'face' of the Divine in the Zohar, representing pure mercy</term>... all those wise ones look into the hidden wisdoms, and they are all blessed with the taste of the matter. They rejoice in those who look at one another in the visual light, those who did not act for repentance and forgiveness... as it is written: "The upright shall behold His face." And they are all blessed and water one another until all the worlds are found. All the worlds are written as one, and then the Lord is called "Kindness" and His name is "Kindness." All the rulers of the world multiplied to the hidden Ancient One... and then the wise ones whisper to the wise ones. At that time, judgments are awakened in the world, and the Throne of Mercy and the Ancient of Days is hidden. Then the mystery of the spirit is revealed, as it is written: "I beheld until thrones were placed, and the Ancient of Days sat." The thrones were placed to show the upper crowns, to bring out the life... they did not exist in their standing. And who are they? The kindnesses. And the Ancient of Days sits, and then He is revealed, and then the guilt of the world is forgotten, and they are forgiven through judgment. 

Just as the ruin of their thoughts ruins [the world] through their evil deeds—which strikes above, and then the Glory departs from them in the mystery of "you shall not take the mother bird with the young"—and the children go into exile as well from the side of their fullness; so too, when one is sanctified and returns from his evil deeds, abandons his ruined ways, knows, returns, and is rectified as is proper—the Voice ascends and strikes until the Mother. And "she has mercy on the children," for she saw them occupied with the rectification of the deed. The scent that ascends from the person who returns in complete Repentance—then He dwells upon them in His holiness. This is the mystery of "He shall return the stolen object that he stole," for in his lack, the blessings and the unification above are diminished. This is the "stolen object that he stole," and he returned and rectified that which he distorted... he returned the stolen object and turned to his rectification. Then "she has mercy on the children" and returns to her husband as at the beginning. By causing this through his repentance, the Holy One, blessed be He, is the Master of complete Repentance. Regarding this, they said in the chapter [of the Talmud]: "In the place where the Masters of Repentance stand, the perfectly righteous cannot stand." 

In the Midrash of Rabbi Shimon bar Yochai: "Worthy are those who sustain the existence of the upper realm... and worthy are those who sketch Repentance, for those who return are not cast away... for a place is prepared for the Masters of Repentance that is not even prepared for the perfectly righteous..."

### Chapter 36: The Section on Divine Service

The word "talent" <note>original: ככר (kikar)</note> implies the language of a "piercing" or "opening," like a kind of ring or hanging object. It suggests that which returns and encircles its place. This represents strength, captivity, and rest—specifically the individual rest where the ultimate purpose is reached. This is the "voice" that arrives from the entirety of the transition, a voice like the Divine Glory. It dissolves and melts, as we have explained. Through the "mouth of longing," things are sent and elevated together. Within the "existences of sending," He shall be exalted to gather and return all the exiles included within the "daughters of protection."

Among these are the exile of the soul and the exile of the body. For this reason, the verse doubles its language, saying: "The Lord your God will return your captivity and have compassion upon you" <note>Deuteronomy 30:3</note>. This indicates that from the goodness of the soul and its exile—which was divided by the judgment of change and goodness—He will gather you so that the body also returns from its exile. This will be the "Complete Redemption," which is established for him as the "pleasure of the heavens." The word "outside" <note>original: חוץ (chutz)</note> implies its own profanation or hollowness, just as the verse "if the Jubilee shall be" <note>Leviticus 25:54</note> diminishes what it requires but also adds to it. Thus, it is explained that it will be in the likeness of the "Sabbatical Reed" <term>Shemitah: The seven-year Sabbatical cycle, which in Kabbalah also refers to cosmic cycles of time</term>, and its meaning is like "if an atonement is laid upon him" <note>Exodus 21:30</note> or "If you lend money to My people" <note>Exodus 22:24</note>.

Regarding the matter of "Returning to the Palace," it shall be known and blessed. It is written to say it is "founded," for the "eyes of the female" are the Sabbatical cycle, the place of the "feet." These are the "Feet of the Divine Presence" <term>Shekhinah: The feminine, indwelling aspect of God</term> which lacks a place. The "exile of death" is where the exiles descend and arrive; when they arrive there, "His feet shall stand." This "voice" of ours is like the calling of the "Holy Migrations." We were written in a hidden place, and the structure was joined upon us in its totality—the place of the "Building" facing the "Known Hidden One," which is the "Kingdom" <term>Malkhut: The final sphere (Sefirah) in the Divine hierarchy, associated with the physical world and the Queen</term>. They said that the "place for his soul" is the "dust of the floor of the Tabernacle." We were written into the "hidden land," and it became a "land of gloom" <note>Job 10:22</note> until the exiles reach that point and are drawn forth. This is our standing and the "Glory for the Abode of Grace."

This is the secret of the verse: "If your outcasts be at the utmost parts of heaven, from there will the Lord your God gather you, and from there will He fetch you" <note>Deuteronomy 30:4</note>. And the verse "The Lord your God will circumcise your heart" <note>Deuteronomy 30:6</note> refers to the evil within this matter, following the nature of generations in which mankind stumbles and becomes ill. For from there is the "foundation of the leaveners," which is the "uncircumcision" <term>Orlah: Literally 'foreskin,' but used here to mean a spiritual barrier or blockage of the heart</term> that causes sin and defiles the heart so that it cannot contain any holy thing. Now, the Holy One, Blessed be He, comes to circumcise that spiritual barrier and remove it from the world, like the "swallowing of death forever." It is written: "And I will take away the stony heart out of your flesh, and I will give you a heart of flesh" <note>Ezekiel 36:26</note>. The purpose of this "heart" is that the secret of "inclining toward evil" will no longer be within it to cause sin, for they will rest. Instead, one will do what the intellect requires according to the Torah. He will not turn from the intellect to the right or the left, for our "sustenance" will return to its first state—as it was before the first sin, and not just the first state, but a time of natural perfection.

This is the meaning of "The Lord your God will circumcise your heart... to love the Lord your God with all your heart and with all your soul, that you may live" <note>Deuteronomy 30:6</note>. For these things further indicate that the "rod" has been removed—which is evil and death—and that "life and good" have been called forth. This is a life without death and a good without evil. In the *Book of Palaces* <term>Sefer Hekhalot: Early mystical texts describing the heavenly realms and divine palaces</term> it is written: Another "talent" <note>kikar</note> after the holy luminary of the Tree. In its completion, they shall show mercy and rejoice. Then all who are dying in their appearance shall be drawn upon His feet, and "His feet shall stand." The voice shall pass through as a "mingled spirit," for the "uncircumcision" <note>spiritual barrier</note> hinders it. Then Israel shall glory in their God at the "Head of this Building of Heaven." The spiritual barrier shall be beneath, unable to touch the Sabbatical cycle. From that point forward, that barrier shall be uprooted and pass away from the world. Then "Israel shall dwell in safety, alone" <note>Deuteronomy 33:28</note>, in the "Segulah" of the "Eye of Jacob." No accuser shall be found against them or against the Priest.

<column-break/>

This matter is regarding the "Superior Support," which is the cutting off of the "mouth" here. These things establish the "Supreme Unity," which adds to the good in a constant flow without any interruption. It returns us continually to "Your Table." This "voice" itself is found in "Proper Thought." It is the circumcision performed for you in the distance. This is the meaning of: "And the Lord your God will make you overabundant in all the work of your hand..." <note>Deuteronomy 30:9</note>. Just as these things exist in "Thought," which is the attribute of Unity—the first and the last together without interruption—so too He will return them and grant them in perfection. The "Voice" is drawn from the "Rectification" and the "Unity" of the Voice without interruption and in the "Fit Choice."

It is written: "For the Lord will again rejoice over you for good" <note>Deuteronomy 30:9</note>. This means there is indeed a flow and an arrival, for "The Lord will return to rejoice over you to bless you." He will not only rejoice "for good" according to the attribute of His goodness, but He will do so continuously and rest upon it without interruption. This is the meaning of "as He rejoiced over your fathers"—finally to bless them with Him.

"If you shall hearken to the voice of the Lord your God..." and "If you shall return to the Lord your God..." <note>Deuteronomy 30:10</note>. This further clarifies that hearkening to the voice of the Lord and keeping His commandments is the "Superior Support." This is the secret of the "Return," where they are revealed at the "Eating Table." It says that these six "Corners" <note>The six emotional Sefirot</note> elevate to a higher level by virtue of their Repentance <note>Teshuvah</note>, in the manner explained above. This is the matter of the entire section concerning the future: "And you shall return to the Lord your God... and hearken to His voice... when you shall turn to the Lord your God."

And the "Last He" <note>The final letter of Y-H-V-H, associated with the Daughter/Kingdom</term>—this is Repentance where she rises from her exile with her children, of which it is said "with the drawing up" etc., with each one returning to its place and being rectified. For this secret reason, Repentance is mentioned three times: to hint that by its "returning" below, it returns above. ### Chapter 37

The Sages, of blessed memory, have a great secret concerning the explanation of the Redemption and the Good found in this Repentance. This is revealed in the hidden parts of the *Book of Brilliance* <term>Sefer HaBahir: One of the earliest and most important works of Kabbalah</term> concerning the matter of "Our House." Regarding the first section, Rabbi Yose said: The "Generation" does not belong to him until all the souls in the "Body" are exhausted. For it says: "For the spirit shall fail before Me, and the souls which I have made" <note>Isaiah 57:16</note>. The Sages of Truth have received by tradition that all souls were deposited before the soul enters in the secret of "Conception" <note>Idbur</note>. This is what they meant by "until all the souls in the Body are finished." Then the "Kingdom" <note>Malkhut</note> will merit to be "sent forth."

The "exhaustion" they spoke of refers to the "Body of Protection." In the secret of the scriptures, the world of Israel is devastated, but not to go alone so as not to involve them. What is the delay? "Their laughter inherits them" in the heights, for they are "inheritors before the Thought," but not all of them. That is, they have not yet been refined and clarified. They must be refined. This is what is meant by "it shall fail" <note>original: יעטוף (ya’atof)</note>—it delays and holds back the Redemption. This comes from the language of "enwrapping to whiten." When these souls are refined, the "Enwrapping" <note>barrier</note> upon them will begin to fall. This is the verse in its entirety, and this is the opinion of the Sages of Truth.

It was said in the Midrash of Rabbi Hamnuna the Elder on the verse "And the soul" <note>Genesis 12:5</note>: The "Good Souls" say it is a merit to go out and come into this world, and if those "Good Ones" do not come, then the "Son of David" <note>the Messiah</note> will not come. This is why we say the Son of David does not come until all the souls in the "Body" are finished <term>Guf: In Jewish mysticism, the 'Guf' is the celestial treasury of souls</term>. All these souls in the "Body" are established, and it says that the souls in the "Body" are "light." Then the Kingdom will merit to be sent forth. This is the "Son of David" who merits the "Last Residence." For my soul shall come to be taken as the "Last Firstborn" upon the rest. And the opinion of Nachmanides <term>Ramban: Rabbi Moshe ben Nachman, a 13th-century scholar and Kabbalist</term>, of blessed memory, is that in every writing, it is written "your beloved one" and "your God"...

# Chapter 36: The Section on Divine Service

In them, it is good to reveal the sand of their heat upon them and to be generous toward them. Not only toward them from their own perspective; for in this way, He promises and heralds all goodness. The reward rises and advances through the **forty-nine roses** <note>original: מ"ט ע' וורדין. These likely refer to the 49 Gates of Binah (Understanding) which a penitent passes through to reach the 50th gate of divine mercy.</note> over the transgressions of the past, and a **cup of consolations** is his in the corners. He must further prove his perfection in divine service and the power of his capability regarding its intricacies. He reckoned every new merit—all his labor became merits for him, and all his merits were found to be truly meritorious. Likewise, even from the desires of the **wicked one** <note>original: רש"ע</note>, though the sinner began as a denier, he can become someone distinguished. Is there a deficiency in the commandments that they should be as merits? Why does the denier of the distinguished find a transformation? From here we learn that since he began [working] on his merits, he acts with loving-kindness toward them, so they are accounted to him as merits.

For us, the specific principle is that the "measure of goodness" is greater than the "measure of punishment." Surely the **Master of Repentance** <term>Baal Teshuvah: A person who has "returned" to religious observance after a period of secularism or sin.</term> always has his heart in awe. Repentance is the "added ruler"; they are higher than all the courts and all the moral rebukers. It is a comprehensive elevated state, and its lack creates a great month of **Gehinnom** <note>The realm of spiritual purification or "purgatory" in Jewish thought.</note>. This is not by strict judgment, for it is a transformation; it is like an arrow according to a double bribe, for He established the whole—the repair of the upper and lower worlds and their existence.

As the sages said regarding the awe of **Rabbi Shimon bar Yochai** <note>original: רש"ב ע"י. A 2nd-century sage credited with the teachings of the Zohar.</note>, "If a man shall open a pit..." <note>Exodus 21:33</note> what is written regarding the liability? "The owner of the pit shall pay." Who is it that compensates for the deficiency of the creature and the improvement of the world in a public alleyway? How much more so does Repentance act to guarantee life! Why is life granted to him? This is as it is written: "And they shall give," and it is written, "The humble shall be transformed." He has a refuge in the building of Repentance. It is as if the servant worked for **the fifty** <note>original: ל"ו ממט. Likely a reference to the 50 Gates or the 36 hidden righteous ones.</note> and is certain of them within the House of Repair. He rests in Repentance, for Repentance repairs the world; it moves and repairs itself and the entire world through it. This is all we wished to explain in this matter and in the inquiry of the intention in this chapter.

### Chapter 36
->Inquiry of the intention in this chapter:<-
->The discipline of ethics regarding the portion of joy<-
->The orders of Repentance written in a luminous view<-

As its name implies, it is explained here that the offspring who come from rebellion against the whole Torah—their iniquity is sealed and more than just a sin. These are the portions that were written, for the offspring of the entire Torah and its intention is that the **Great Name** shall be in His Glory. He is the repair of the Glory, which is the path of our blessings, like the goodness of the prayers that was with us. It arrives through Repentance, as one who passes through. Furthermore, it adds to the life of the **Lord** and rises above the fear of the "branch of lashes" in the Torah, to be for him "and He shall have mercy upon you" <note>Deuteronomy 13:18</note>. It is to do good with mercy, to bring the distant close, and to gather the scattered upper and lower beings.

Therefore, it is called **Teshuvah** <note>Repentance; literally "Return."</note>. This is the **Higher Repentance** <term>Teshuvah Ila'ah: In Kabbalah, this is the return of the soul to its source in the divine mother, Binah.</term> which is hidden in the world. The **Sages of Truth** <note>The Kabbalists.</note> returned to this reason because the doors of pure knowledge open to the inner power of agreement and recognition of the vessel of cessation. The language of *Teshuvah* is related to the language of "returning" <note>original: בתובה (likely a scribe's error for "returning" or "writing").</note> and is pleasant for our taste. Furthermore, it serves as a witness and life and goodness for all who "turn from transgression in Jacob" <note>Isaiah 59:20</note>, and He will not abandon his children. For this reason, it is also called *Teshuvah*, as was explained in the previous chapter.

From the language of "The Merciful One," which is the wisdom of the spirit and the movement of the **Upper Unity** and the repair of the Glory when the lower beings awaken through the Holy Spirit in the sense of deeds, as was explained at the end of the section. Similarly, the explicit language is "And He shall return and gather all the exiles." For He had the power of "servants to the wrath," and all the power of the deeds was the cause. This is the portion called **Repentance**, and it moved all the benefit for us; therefore, it is called the **Higher Name**. Since the first blessing contains the beginning of the benefit to return all the wicked and those who turn away from everything, I saw fit to write clearly according to the way of **Higher Wisdom**. It is worthy for it to be said to reach the "Living One," for this is the intention of the Torah. For if there is a logic of "how much more so," then the Great Name, blessed be He, prepared us and designated all the good things within us for Him. Also, the essence of goodness and doing good and its success is within the success of prayer. This is the movement of the body and the house, as will be explained from that verse which includes and says: "And it shall come to pass, when all these things are come upon thee, the blessing..."

<column-break/>

"...and the curse" <note>Deuteronomy 30:1</note>. It was written to "bring it back to your heart among all the nations whither the Lord thy God hath driven thee, and thou shalt return unto the Lord." Because of the time of these words and according to the occupation and the flow of the upper chapter, it was appropriate to write thus: "And it shall come to pass when all these things come upon you... and you shall return to the Lord your God." For the deficiency in the blessing is as it should be, for it is my "seal." What is the blessing compared to the curse? From it arises strength, and upon it is the power of the sufferings. One must return from the cause, which is the transgressions, to be saved from them. Even the curse—there was a need to mention it for this very reason. Also, "bringing it back to your heart" <note>A phrase meaning to reflect or repent.</note> is not without reason; it means "return Repentance to yourself," and then "return unto the Lord your God with all your heart." It is well known that there is no Repentance if there is no standing and returning of the heart, for transgressions are the cause of suffering and exile.

Furthermore, it says: "Then the Lord thy God will turn thy captivity, and have compassion upon thee, and will return and gather thee." This is a pleasant doubling, for it refers to the first goodness. Furthermore, "will return and gather thee" is the same as "will turn thy captivity." Why did the scripture need to say "will return and gather thee from all the peoples," only to repeat it and say "If any of thine be driven out unto the outmost parts of heaven"? <note>Deuteronomy 30:3-4</note>

Furthermore, the doubling of the power in the verse of Repentance: after it says "and thou shalt return unto the Lord," it says again "and thou shalt return and obey." The reason it is written is that it explains that they shall all return. It says, "when they shall come," the blessing and the curse. This was to write in the secret of the exile, the "return" and "bringing back to the heart," speaking of the powers of our blessings. Our trust is in the goodness and the hope for the Great Name in His Glory. When Israel performed the will of the Place <note>A name for God.</note>, then that goodness was present, and our hope increased through us. We merited that goodness, for it is the "essence of the blessing"—the blessing designated for us in the Torah, which is praised and necessitated by Divine Service and Unity, as I wrote at the end of the eighth part.

They returned and were built after the evil, for the "Cloud of Knowledge" then overpowered everything absolute. It gave place to the "Darkness of Sin" and transgression to strike and take root—that which we have iniquitously committed. All the curses and judgments in the world come through its flow, for we missed out on all the good. This is our logic: we were hidden in exile among the nations, where every deficiency is found within them. And also our "Greatness" <note>The Divine Presence.</note> goes with us into exile, in the cancellation of looking toward the deficiencies. This is what it means: "even though You have received me in my sickness, my iniquities"—for your iniquities are the curse designated in our intention after all that. When we claim for all that is in our generations, for all our helpers are according to the "Nothingness" we have turned toward, we were also promised that when one returns to his heart among all the nations where the Lord has driven us, that is the "designated time of the curse." For the evil is the cause that hinders us from the portion of our sin; so too our holiness is in yearning. After everything, our awakening will cry out, and he will not be a "heartless one," but he will understand with his good heart. Even the evil one can, in his path, repair the distortions, elevate the deficiency, and return the exile to its border. This is what we took upon ourselves as a foundation: to move in Repentance to return. It is written "Repentance is above," and that is what it means: "And you shall return unto the Lord your God." The secret of the goodness of Israel is "unto the Lord your God," for our Repentance reaches the **Higher One**, and then He too will return to the children.

Because the essence of the blessing and the "bringing it back to your heart" is not a curse; for there is in the power of all that is designated in the Torah—both good and evil—the ability to stand upon life. Everything depends on the power of your choice <note>original: סורך (your turning/choice).</note>, to say: "The blessing and the curse which I have set before you... and you shall return to your heart and the Lord your God shall return." I have already written that transgressions are the cause of preventing the **Higher Good**. When they are removed, she turns toward them with grace and peace. Woe to the "Heat" <note>A reference to divine wrath.</note> and the "Nakedness" in the place of the "Seal." Then the "Close Arrow" is distanced and rests in exile until the turn. For her Master returns, and as one who thinks of playing, he will repair the distortion. Repentance will return to the children, life will be good, and everything will return to its place. Regarding this, it is said: "The Merciful One shall return," and the **Higher Good** shall be upon the children. Also, the "Lower One" shall then return to the hidden world.
