### Chapter 38: The Section on Divine Service ###

Creation has not yet come to rest, nor is it finished; it is ongoing and will eventually reach every facet of existence. Behold, nothing is neglected or abandoned until the merit of judgment is revealed. The "First Dominion"—the dominion of the Supreme Will and Desire—shall not abandon its rule <note>original: "וממשלת הרצון והחפץ העליון". This refers to the kabbalistic idea that God's primary will remains the underlying force of reality despite the appearance of disorder.</note>. It will cast away what is redundant. As it is said regarding the time of Rabbi Yohanan: all the good things and consolations written by the prophets are for the covenant and his praise in the days of the King Messiah, which were not fulfilled during the time of the "exile" <note>The OCR reads "בריחה" (fleeing/escape), but the context suggests "גלות" (exile) or the state after the fall.</note> or before the sin of **Adam the First Man**. 

The opinion of Samuel, however, is that in these matters, the prophets did not envision anything except the return of the world to its original nature and custom, as it was before the beginning of creation's [decline] and before Adam the First Man sinned and was purified. As it is written: "Nature shall return to its old state" in the days of the King Messiah, for then the Supreme Intention shall be completed. Until now, the "Action" has been spreading according to the intent of the "Rider" <note>original: "רוכב", referring to God as the Rider of the Chariot/Heavens.</note>, just as He saw Adam and the Messiah. Now, the Holy One, blessed be He, is bringing the time of God to remove [evil] from the world, and His intention in creation is not yet complete. This was the will of the **Men of the Great Assembly** <term>Anshei Knesset HaGedola: The ruling religious body of the early Second Temple period who standardized Jewish liturgy.</term> (peace be upon them) in the prayer of *Nechem* <note>A prayer for the restoration of Jerusalem.</note> and in their saying, "Therefore we hope to You, O Lord our God, to see quickly the glory of Your strength," and so on.

The intention is to hint that the Great Name and the "writing of His strength" <note>original: "וכתיבה עזו". Likely referring to the Divine Name as a source of power.</note> will spread before our eyes and be revealed in the world. Until now, they were hidden in the upper realms, and there was no true "placement" or "greatness" due to the corruption of the lower beings. This is the "Revelation," and the [goal of] the Prophets is to remove the **idols** and the **husks** <term>Kelipot: Literallly "shells" or "husks"; in Kabbalah, these are the forces of evil/impurity that conceal the divine light.</term> that prevent the light from reaching the "Higher Man" <note>Adam HaElyon: The primordial celestial form of humanity.</note> from the earth. For they lived by faith in God, but it was taken from them when the lower beings turned away. 

When the "Minister" who is above is removed, then the whole "Tree of [Idolatrous] Service" will be cut down. This is also discussed in the tractate regarding the corruption in the world. All of this is written to "repair the world under the Sovereignty of the Almighty" <note>original: "לתקן עולם במלכות שדי". A central phrase from the Aleinu prayer.</note>, which has not been repaired until now. His intention for the world was not lacking, but rather the intention of the "Minister" who resembles "My Witness" <note>original: "ורומות עדי". This is a difficult passage, possibly referring to the angelic prince of the nations.</note> in the world by way of passage. When the Holy One, blessed be He, removes him from the world, then the world will be repaired under the Sovereignty of the Almighty, and "the Sovereignty shall be the Lord's." "And the Lord shall be King over all the earth; on that day the Lord shall be one and His name one." 

Then the world will return to what it was before the sin of Adam the First Man. "All children of flesh will call upon Your name"—something they did not do until now, for they called only upon the name of impurity, God forbid. Then that which is written will be fulfilled: "For then I will turn to the peoples a pure language, that they may all call upon the name of the Lord, to serve Him with one accord." The scripture says "all the wicked of the earth," for if these remain, they would turn away and mislead His kingdom. Their existence until now was through the "Son of Impurity," but when the Holy One, blessed be He, cuts him off from the world, then all the inhabitants of the earth will recognize and know that "to You every knee shall bow" and "to the glory of Your name they shall give honor." Previously, they gave honor to "Other Gods," but then they will all accept the yoke of Your Sovereignty. 

The corruption of the world will end because "the Sovereignty is Yours," and You will reign in glory forever. This is the "Renewal of the World" and the restoration of the "Crown of Beauty" to its dweller, just as it was before Adam the First Man sinned. Then all the worlds were joined and ascending in one bond—the Great Bond in one Unity (Yichud) through the writing of His strength and the "Takhsh" <note>original: "בתחשו". This may refer to the "Tachash," the mysterious multicolored animal whose skins covered the Tabernacle.</note> of Adam the First Man in the order of Unity. But the worlds became corrupted; the internal parts went out to the exterior, and the external parts were forced inside. The spirit of impurity spread through the world, causing the corruption of the creatures. They separated the Holy Unity until it was hidden away. 

Therefore, the King Messiah will repair everything, for then the Holy One, blessed be He, will remove the spirit of impurity from the earth. Nothing will be lacking; the [visions of the] prophets will be repaired and fulfilled, and all will aim toward the **Unity** (Yichud). When the "Separating Screen" is removed, the [original] intention of creation will be revealed. This is the measure of what our Rabbis understood regarding the "Gates" in this chapter.

## Chapter 39 ##

-> The innovation in the vision of the Truth, surrounding <-
-> the giving of life at the time when the Holy One, blessed be He, is destined to return souls to dead bodies. <-

<column-break/>

This matter is similar to how things were in the days of Adam the First Man. That is to say, the "Lower Staff" corrupted everything and imprisoned nature. However, there is a doubt regarding what we have written here, based on what our Sages said: "The righteous stand in their clothes." Rabbi Hiyya bar Abba said in the name of Rabbi Yohanan: "All the prophets prophesied only for the days of the Messiah; but as for the World to Come, 'no eye has seen, O God, besides You.'" This contradicts Samuel, for Samuel said: "There is no difference between this world and the days of the Messiah except for the subjugation to the [gentile] kingdoms alone," as it is said, "For the poor shall never cease out of the land." This seems to follow the view of Samuel mentioned above. Let us consider his view: he interprets the matter of the King Messiah's days in this way, and these are our words [on the subject]. 

This refers to how the world functions today. This view was discussed by the **Ramban** <term>Ramban: Rabbi Moses ben Nachman (Nachmanides), a 13th-century Spanish scholar and kabbalist.</term> (may his memory be a blessing) in the chapter on "This World," etc.

## 13 Kingdoms, Kings, and Their Wars ##

He said there, using these words: "Let it not enter your mind that in the days of the Messiah any part of the world's custom will be canceled, or that there will be some innovation in the Work of Creation. Rather, the world follows its custom." It will be recounted later that Samuel's intention was not that the Holy One, blessed be He, would change anything outside of nature, but that things would return to being a blessing, just as they were at the beginning of creation. 

Behold, it is known that at the start of creation, the world was already naturally set for goodness and grace, and its boundaries were set toward perfection, reducing the [influence of] the "External Ones" <note>The forces of the "Other Side" or evil.</note> as much as possible. It was also intended that humans would be wise and living, as we have already written. From this, it was revealed to him that the nature of the world changed for him and for all who followed him, and man was destined to die. As the scripture notes by saying: "And now, lest he put forth his hand, and take also of the Tree of Life, and eat, and live forever." Our Rabbis said in the chapter *Ein Dorshin*: "When Adam sinned, the Holy One, blessed be He, placed His hand upon him and diminished him." That is to say, a wise man has a high degree, living [in] all possible worlds. 

But He diminished him to the grave. This is indicated by the "crushing" of Adam and his taste. So too, the ground itself was affected, as it is written: "Cursed is the ground because of you; in toil shall you eat of it... thorns also and thistles shall it bring forth to you." Behold, the earth itself, in following its Maker, withdrew the power that was implanted in it at the beginning of creation. 

In this way, the scriptures will be reconciled which testify that in the future to come, the virtues and the good things will return to their natural state and perfection, as they were at the beginning of creation before they were diminished by sin. This is what Elijah meant by saying, "And the tree of the field shall yield its fruit"—meaning the fruit of the earth will be given just as it was at the beginning of creation, without distinction. And "the heavens shall give their dew," which had been withheld because of Adam's sin. All things will return to their settlement, as we wrote at the beginning of this chapter. 

All these things were shown to Rabbi Yohanan and Samuel—the scriptures regarding the diminishment and corruption caused by sin, and the restoration of their Unity and perfection. As he says later, "the lips of the Lord," the "spirit," etc., indicating the diminishment of the lights that were eclipsed because of sin. The "spirit" comes from the "Minister" to serve his lack. We are the "lowest of the earth," indicating the fruits of the earth and the fruits of life. The curse of the ground, which was cursed because of sin, is why he continues that "even the eunuch shall sing and live" and "every tree is in him." He chose this and sang: "For the Lord has redeemed Jacob, and will glorify Himself in Israel." For then all things will merit their repair, and all "approximations" will be settled. The impurity of the "driven sin" <note>original: "החטא הנדח"</note> will be gone. This is what he mentioned by saying, "I have blotted out, as a thick cloud, your transgressions... Sing, O heavens!" For the holy sin caused the diminishment and corruption of the upper and lower beings. 

When [the world] returns to its Inhabitant, according to the original intention of the Supreme Wisdom, the perfection that is drawn to Him is Will and Joy. This was the intention He had for them during their creation. What is written here in the words of the Prophets and those who bless with the Holy Spirit regarding this matter—this is the intention, and this is the fruit itself. There is no doubt that Samuel's view will rise... [as it was] before the sin. For the sin preceded the joining of the bond of the worlds and the drawing down of the Almighty (Shaddai) in the beginning, and the change of the nature of the world, and the merit along with this Supreme Will and Intention.

It reconciles the views of Talmudic sages Samuel and Rabbi Yohanan, suggesting that the "renewal" of the world is actually a restoration of its original divine perfection.</summary>

# Chapter 36: Section on Divine Service | Chapter 38 #

"Return to the Lord your God... you and your children, with all your heart and all your soul" <note>original: "ושבת עד יי' אלהיך... בכל לבבך ובכל נפשך", quoting Deuteronomy 30:2</note>. This refers to the **Will of Increase** <note>original: "לרצון יוסף". The word 'Yosef' (Joseph) also means 'to add' or 'increase,' suggesting a surplus of divine favor.</note>, meaning that when you return, the preparation of Israel will be refined, and they will return fully to the Lord. And "The Lord your God will restore your fortunes" <note>Deuteronomy 30:3</note>. The sages said this is to give hope to all Israel. "With all your soul"—this means when all the "wings" of Israel return to their roots, they will be refined and merit divine favor and goodness.

Regarding the end of days and the arrival of the **Son of David** <note>The Messiah</note>: this depends on the exhaustion of all the forces in the "Body" <term>Guf: In Kabbalistic thought, the *Guf* is a celestial storehouse or "body" where all souls exist before they are born into the physical world.</term>. As it is written in the *Book of the Palaces* <note>The *Heichalot* literature, early Jewish mystical texts</note>, the holy Sage **Rabbi Shimon bar Yochai** (peace be upon him) said:
In the secret of the **Palaces**, all souls and all bodies stand ready for life, like a throne hoped for to unite the worlds. For this reason, goodness is found in the cutting off of all "living things" <note>original: "חיכון", perhaps referring to the biological life force</note> that emerged from that "river that flows and goes out" <note>original Aramaic: "נהר דנגיד ונפיק", a common Zohar phrase for the flow of divine emanation</note>. Because of this, the Palace does not stand empty forever; it is meant to be filled from the Sanctuary above. If this Palace stands empty and nothing emerges from above, then the King adds and breaks through this Palace above to awaken the Palace below. This continues until the Sanctuary gates of the souls are completed, and the Palace is finished, reaching the time of goodness and mercy.

And the voice of the souls that were refined through the connection of "Will" with the goodness of the Palace is the secret of what they said: "For this reason, this Palace... which emerged from that river..." This Palace is in the likeness of the "Body" of all souls. It contains a hint that when the body and its forces—like the throat and all the souls destined to be revealed—are finished, then the end will come.

There are levels like the **Crown** <term>Keter: The highest of the ten Sefirot or divine attributes.</term> in the power of the Holy One. It is written here that the "Wing of the Supernal Adam" <note>A reference to *Adam Kadmon*, the primordial spiritual archetype of humanity</note> alludes to the body. He will return to merit the Divine, and the "Body" will be entirely empty for all of them. The Temple below is a small chariot for the one above. To this, the verse hints: "The Holy One is in your midst, and I will not enter the city" <note>Hosea 11:9</note>. The Sages interpreted this: The Holy One said, "I will not enter the Jerusalem above until I enter the Jerusalem below." There is no path for the power from below and outside to enter until the **King Messiah** is revealed. Then the souls that were in the sanctuary will be refined, and his Palace will no longer be empty. This will be linked from above through the power of prayer, and the King Messiah will be the light.

The secret of the matter is that the fall of **Adam the First Man** caused a disruption of the orders and a destruction of the upper worlds. Through the cunning of the Serpent, knowledge was corrupted, and Adam transgressed his station. He followed the "Knowledge of the Serpent" and the "Husk" <term>Kelipah: Literally 'shell' or 'peel,' referring to the forces of spiritual impurity that conceal divine light.</term> instead of his own wisdom. He brought upon himself abominations. This is because the "Tree of Knowledge of Good and Evil" contains the "Evil" side, which serves as sustenance for the "Naked Soul" <note>The soul stripped of its divine garments due to sin</note>. Because of Adam, these forces act as a source of death and destruction. 

When a person is as Adam was originally, he is connected to the holiness. But after the sin, he and all his descendants are ruled by the "external forces" <note>Demonic or impure forces</note>. Even his "garments" are influenced by the Kingdom of Evil. Furthermore, the "Holy Seed" was mixed with impurity because Adam followed the "Naked Ones" <note>The Serpent/forces of impurity</note>. This necessitated the "Cycle of Souls" <term>Gilgul: Reincarnation; the process of souls returning to the world to repair previous sins.</term> to refine the body. Adam the First Man abandoned the "Book of the Covenant" and did not follow the **Tree of Life**, which would have drawn holy lights to complete the purpose of his creation. Instead, he clung to the Tree of Knowledge in its aspect of Evil. Thus, it is written that the soul was "tethered" to these forces, and the body was made subject to the authority of the "Husks." The source of blessing and the spring were corrupted. This corruption was meant to spread through the world for a thousand generations. However, the Word of the Lord intervened for refinement and purification.

<column-break/>

That "filth" <term>Zuhamah: Spiritual impurity or 'slime' introduced by the Serpent's interaction with Eve.</term> was supposed to be purged from the world to return it to the state it was in before Adam the First Man sinned, achieving the intended purpose of creation. But when the people returned to their corruption and made the **Golden Calf**, the filth returned. The souls were again confused and became "Naked Souls" clothed in human bodies. These are the "brazen-faced" ones in the generation. Through them, the spirit of impurity spread through the world, disrupting the orders of the generations. They inherited evil from their fathers, serving idols and transgressing the Torah. They trusted in vanity and tasted the "forbidden," polluting the forces of the "Palace" with impurity. This disruption will not depart until it has spread through the world.

Then the "Spring of Joseph" <note>The source of increase/Messianic light</note> will open to refine the world. Every thing will return to its place. The "bitter" will be separated from it, and he will "sweeten" the path so that goodness will be repaired. Until everything is repaired, it is impossible for the King Messiah to come. Regarding this, the Sages decreed: **"The Son of David will not come until all the souls in the 'Body' [Guf] are exhausted."** 

The Sages of Truth <note>The Kabbalists</note> said this aligns with what is said in the chapter *Helek* <note>Chapter 11 of Tractate Sanhedrin in the Talmud</note>. Rabbi Yohanan said: "The Son of David will only come in a generation that is either entirely meritorious or entirely guilty." In a generation that is entirely meritorious: as it is written, "Your people shall all be righteous" <note>Isaiah 60:21</note>. In a generation that is entirely guilty: as it is written, "He saw that there was no man, and wondered that there was no intercessor" <note>Isaiah 59:16</note>. It is necessary to know that with the exhaustion of all souls in the "Body," the spirit of impurity will pass from the earth, as explained in the following chapter.

### Chapter 38 ###

->**The King Messiah shall be revealed speedily in our days.**<-
->**He shall return and arrange the Temple Court; this is the 'Return and Goodness.'**<-

The "Supernal Thought" <term>Machshavah Elyonah: The primordial divine plan for existence.</term> is the ultimate intention of creation: that the world should be preserved in holiness and purity. This was the state of Adam the First Man before the sin. As it is written: "And I will dwell in Jerusalem and walk in the midst of my people." He shall appear and oversee the world. After he "swallows up death forever" <note>Isaiah 25:8</note>, there will no longer be "impoverished people" in this world. Many verses support this, which I have written about elsewhere. 

Peace shall be granted to the world, meaning it will return to the state it was in before the sin of Adam the First Man. The King Messiah is destined to restore the world to its original beauty. Our Sages of blessed memory noted that in the account of creation, the word *Toledot* <term>Toledot: 'Generations' or 'Chronicles.' In Hebrew, the word is usually spelled 'deficiently' (תלדות). Throughout the Bible, it only appears with the full spelling (תולדות) in two places: the creation of the heavens and the earth, and the genealogy of Perez, the ancestor of the Messiah.</term> is spelled "deficiently" except in two places: the "generations of the heavens" and the "generations of Perez." 

Rabbi Judan said in the name of Rabbi Abun: Why is it spelled fully in the case of Perez? Because the six things taken from Adam the First Man will return through him. These are: **his Splendor, his Life, his Stature, the Fruit of the Earth, the Fruit of the Tree, and the Luminaries.** These six things are destined to return in the days of the King Messiah, who descends from Perez. 

Furthermore, Rabbi Berachiah said in the name of Rabbi Samuel: Even though these things were created in their fullness, when Adam the First Man sinned, they were corrupted. They will not return to their perfection until the "Son of Perez" <note>The Messiah</note> comes. In the Midrash, it is written: The earth is destined to produce "delicacies" just as it did in the days of Adam the First Man. Just as the earth produced fruits on the same day they were planted, so too in the future. As it is said: "He has made a memorial for His wonders" <note>Psalm 111:4</note>. This teaches that on the day a tree is planted, on that same day it will yield fruit. This goodness will increase in the days of the King Messiah for the sake of the world.

<meta>This page continues the discussion on the final restoration of the world. # Chapter 40: Section on Divine Service | Chapter 41 #

The resurrection and the restoration of the **Divine Presence** <term>Shekhinah: The indwelling presence of God in the world, often described in feminine terms.</term> occurs through the initial cleaving to the essence of the Divine Presence. At that time, the Name shall return to establish and build the structure upon it, so that nothing shall be lacking from the whole. With "chariots and horses," the body returns to its dust—but not as it was before. At the end of the matter, it will arise in the purity of the ages, together with the purity of the righteous. For the decree of the Divine Will <note>original: "גזירת חס הרצון", likely "the decree of the [Divine] Will"</note> necessitates the resurrection of the dead.

The explanation of this, according to what we have received from the **Sages of Truth** <term>Chachmei HaEmet: A traditional title for Kabbalists or mystical scholars.</term>, is that the Holy One, Blessed be He, purifies within the body one small bone called the **Luz** <term>Luz: In Jewish tradition, an indestructible bone (often identified with a vertebra or a bone at the base of the skull) from which the body will be reconstructed at the time of resurrection.</term>. It is this bone that waits in the grave, and upon this bone, the entire body will be rebuilt. It is never destroyed, remaining like ice. In the language of our Sages of blessed memory, they said in Chapter 34 of the *Chapters of Rabbi Eliezer*: "Rabbi Shimon says: All bodies crumble into the dust of the earth until nothing remains of the body except the 'Luz' bone itself, which does not decay. It mixes with the dust..." This is a firm foundation for how the body is reconstructed. Upon it, the shells of resurrection shall be formed, so that nothing is superfluous, but everything is reconstructed through the power of Divine Knowledge.

The catalyst for resurrection will be through the **Dew** <note>original: "טל", referencing the 'Dew of Resurrection' mentioned in Isaiah 26:19</note>. As they said in the *Chapters of Rabbi Eliezer*, Chapter 33: "From the place where it descends from the head of the Holy One, Blessed be He, in the future, He will shake His hair and bring down the dew of resurrection, reviving the dead." As it is written: "I slept, but my heart was awake... for my head is drenched with dew" <note>Song of Songs 5:2</note>. This dew enters the hair until it reaches that specific bone, and it will soften it like leaven in dough <note>original: "כעיסה דא", Aramaic for 'like this dough'</note> within the dust. It will then spread to all sides, drawing to it all the limbs, sinews, and flesh from below.

In the Midrash of **Rabbi Shimon bar Yochai** <note>Referring to the Zohar</note>, it is taught: After the bone has been in the dust for a long time, it merits resurrection. It is made like a leaven for the body, as it is written: "His dew is a dew of light" <note>Isaiah 26:19</note>. It will mix with the other bones and soften like dough. Afterward, skin, flesh, and sinews will be drawn over them.

In another place in the Midrash, Rabbi Elazar said: "Woe to those foolish spirits who say that the dead will not live again! How can they be made anew?" Let those foolish ones wait and see. Their understanding is far from the Creator. At the end of days, even the dust will be gathered. Look at the taste we have already: the bodies that held holy spirits and souls and labored in the light of the Torah—they are hidden in the dust until the time when the world is renewed. Rabbi Chiya said: "Not only that, but that very body shall truly arise," as it is written: "Your dead shall live" <note>Isaiah 26:19</note>. It does not say "they shall be created," which would imply a new creation, but "they shall live," implying the very bone that was preserved in the body under the earth, which never rotted or dissolved in the dust. At the appointed time, it will expand and be made like a leaven in the dough, spreading to the four corners, and from it, the body and all its limbs will be completed. Afterward, the Holy Spirit will be placed within them.

Rabbi Elazar said: "This is certainly so." That bone is softened as it is written: "For Your dew is a dew of lights." As for the righteous who are buried outside the Land of Israel, tunnels are made for them through which they roll until they reach the Land of Israel <term>Gilgul Mechilot: The 'rolling through tunnels,' a traditional belief that the righteous buried outside Israel travel underground to the Holy Land for resurrection.</term>. There they will stand on their feet. This is because the **Luz** bone itself possesses holiness and purity, and thus it merits the Land where the Divine Presence stands. This is what is written: "Behold, I will open your graves and raise you from your graves, O My people, and I will bring you into the Land of Israel... and I will put My spirit in you and you shall live" <note>Ezekiel 37:12-14</note>.

In the Midrash of Rabbi Yochanan ben Zakkai, he asked Rabbi Chizkiyahu: "Why must the dead that the Holy One, Blessed be He, will revive, be resurrected specifically in the Land of Israel?" He answered: "The Holy One, Blessed be He, swore to build Jerusalem and never to destroy the graves hidden within it." For Rabbi Jeremiah said: "In the future, the Holy One, Blessed be He, will sanctify His world and build Jerusalem, bringing it down as a structure from above." At that time, the soul of Israel will no longer experience shame. Jerusalem is built so that it will never again be called "forsaken" nor the land "desolate." Just as God swore after the Flood that waters would never again destroy all flesh, so too He has sworn regarding the restoration of Jerusalem.

<column-break/>

As it is written: "For this is like the waters of Noah to me; as I swore that the waters of Noah should no more go over the earth..." <note>Isaiah 54:9</note>. From here we see an oath. In the future, the Holy One, Blessed be He, will sanctify His world so that the shame of Israel shall not arise, nor shall it occur in the building of Jerusalem and the Holy Temple. Therefore, souls are only received in that place for the sake of "Eternal Life," so that their existence may be eternal in the body. This is what is written: "He who is left in Zion and remains in Jerusalem shall be called holy" <note>Isaiah 4:3</note>. This is the place of holy life.

Rabbi Chizkiyahu said: "The Holy One, Blessed be He, is praised as Holy; Jerusalem is Holy; the Wall within it is Holy." As it is written: "Holy, Holy, Holy is the Lord of Hosts" <note>Isaiah 6:3</note>, and "Holy is He in your midst." Since the first "Holy" refers to life, so too those who remain are "Holy" and alive. Therefore, to revive the bodies, the soul must be received in the Land which is holy, so that life may exist in the "House of Life" <note>original: "בבתי חיים", a traditional euphemism for a cemetery or the afterlife</note> through the soul of the Holy Land.

If this were not the case, the righteous would not need to travel through tunnels under the earth until they reach the Holy Land. They enter there and arise so that the construction of their life is mediated by Holy Providence. If they were resurrected in the lands of impurity, they would not be prepared for this. The holy teacher, the **Ramban** <note>Rabbi Moshe ben Nachman (Nachmanides), 1194–1270</note>, of blessed memory, wrote: "All those bodies that decayed in the earth are reconstituted from the bone by the power of the soul, until they delight beneath the Throne and are refined by the 'Dew of Lights.' They will emerge from the Holy Mountain and there receive their souls, so they may be established in the World to Come."

In the final chapter of tractate *Ketubot*, Rabbi Chiya bar Joseph said: "In the future, the righteous will sprout and arise in Jerusalem," as it says: "May they blossom out of the city like the grass of the earth" <note>Psalm 72:16</note>. "The City" refers specifically to Jerusalem, as it is written: "For I will defend this city." The bodies of those resurrected will be gathered into the Holy Land after they have traveled through the tunnels and ascended within it. Just as the first creation was from the Holy and the Attached, at the time of resurrection, the "Crown shall return to its former glory" <note>original: "עטרה ליושבה", a common idiom for restoration</note>. The words of the great elder, the Ramban, and the words of his student, **Rabbi Aharon HaLevi** <note>1235–1303, author of the 'Sefer HaChinuch'</note>, are verified: Those who are resurrected will never die again. This will be further explained regarding the nature of their life, as our masters have taught regarding the matter of resurrection. May it be built and established quickly in our days, Amen.

### Chapter 41 ###

The **World to Come** <term>Olam Ha-Ba: The afterlife or the post-resurrection era of spiritual reward.</term> is the ultimate purpose toward which the righteous aim. It is their preservation and their crown; it is the world of recompense and the final reward for the commandments. The Torah shall be internal to those resurrected. This principle is rooted in the Torah and bears fruit in many places in the words of the Sages. The Prophets also alluded to this matter. It is a concept accessible to all who seek the hidden and true world. One could speak at great length about it. The Prophet said: "From of old, no ear has heard, no eye has seen a God besides You, who works for those who wait for Him" <note>Isaiah 64:3/4</note>.

In the chapter "One Does Not Stand" <note>Tractate Berakhot, Chapter 5</note>, Rabbi Chiya bar Abba said in the name of Rabbi Yochanan: "All the prophets only prophesied concerning the Days of the Messiah; but as for the World to Come, 'No eye has seen it, O God, besides You.'" It appears that the essence of that world, which is true life, is visible only to the "Eye Above." In the Midrash of our Rabbi <note>referring to the Zohar on Ecclesiastes</note>, it is stated that the World to Come is the "Afterward." Because this world cannot grasp it, no prophet could envision it or prophesy concerning it. We learn that the World to Come is not merely the time of the resurrection, but what follows it. In the Midrash on Ecclesiastes, it is said: "This world is for labor, and the World to Come is for receiving reward." Some say that neither the world nor the reward was seen by the prophets. All agree that the reward hidden for the righteous in the World to Come is the "End of Recompense," which the prophets did not perceive. The differences in opinion among the Sages are merely matters of metaphor and expression. According to Rabbi Helbo, the "World to Come" is where the reward is gathered...

# Chapter 39: Section on Divine Service | Chapter 40 #

From the majesty of **Rashbi** <note>Rabbi Shimon bar Yochai, the traditional author of the Zohar.</note>, peace be upon him: All the souls of the righteous are hidden and concealed beneath the **King’s Throne** <term>Kisse HaKavod: The Throne of Glory, representing the highest level of the created spiritual universe.</term>. May their crown be ready for them to return to their places. This refers to the "Assembly of Israel" <note>original: "כנסת ישראל", the Shekhinah or the spiritual personification of the Jewish people.</note>. "My soul yearns for You in the night, and with my spirit within me I seek You" <note>Isaiah 26:9</note>. This "visitation" <note>original: "פקודתך", meaning a divine command or remembrance.</note> surely refers to the **Matron of the King** <term>Matronita: An Aramaic term for the Shekhinah, depicted as the Queen or Mother.</term>. "Watch over my spirit and my life"—watch over it for me.

The intention regarding the **Assembly of Israel** is that there is a place where the souls of the righteous gather, a place that is established and lacks nothing. It is a crown of life. Concerning this, it is written: "The King’s visitation" <note>original: "פקודתך", relating to the divine supervision over the soul.</note>, signifying that she shall rule. This is called **Chesed** <term>Chesed: The attribute of Loving-kindness or Grace.</term>. This refers to the Throne of the lower depths. As our **Sages of blessed memory** said: The souls of the righteous are hidden beneath the Throne of Glory. This requires a clear investigation into the "parts of the soul."

This includes the "Hollow Space" <note>original: "מקום חללו", perhaps referring to the primordial vacuum or the space where creation occurs.</note>, for searchers have found them bound like a candle in the clarity of the lights of the **Lord God**. This is like the "Organ of Prayer," the voice of the good purpose and prayer. Why then did they descend from their rank and honor? It was for the sake of their bodies, which crumbled and returned to the dust. The secret of the "End of Days" is for those who possess the **Knowledge of the Brain** <note>original: "דעת המוחים", referring to hidden mystical wisdom.</note>. It has already been explained that the purpose of the soul’s descent to this world is for it to hold onto the "Honored One" and elevate it, so that it might exist in a purified and intellectual state, ascending from every blemish.

This was the intention in the first creation: when the "Spring of Blessing" and the Source was opened, it was meant to wash away all impurity that was drawn after it and became caught in the filth and laughter of the world. The **Evil Inclination** <term>Yetzer Hara: The drive toward physical desires or selfishness.</term> confuses everything until the righteous person is awakened for their needs and life. For since death and these angels are prepared for all generations, there is no escape from it. Without death, the higher intention for the soul would not be fulfilled, and the Glory would not be rectified as it should be. The soul requires the garment of the body to refine itself, and this causes the "Time of Death." For the pure soul cannot dwell in a dwelling of impurity while the filth of the serpent is within it. This is what our Sages of blessed memory said: "A person is only called 'Human' by their soul." For the true human is the Soul, and this body is merely a "shroud" for the soul, which grows dark and bitter until it spreads and flies away from the body and returns to its place.

To correct the errors and the filth of the serpent, the **Higher Wisdom** saw fit to remove the "Accuser" <note>original: "קטרוג", a spiritual force of judgment or the Satan.</note>, which is the materiality called "the skin of all flesh," and to uproot it from its place and close the mouth of the "Evil Side" to destroy it. Then the body shall be called "faithful," and it will be hidden until the Holy One, Blessed be He, raises the body from its dust, after its impurity and stench have passed away. For because of the Evil Inclination—which is the cause of the body's filth—the body was a source of these deaths from the beginning. Therefore, before the souls ascend to their place, the body must pass through death to be purified, refined, and to rise from its filth. Then, the soul will descend and dwell in a body that is less than its previous place of rest, for it will be clean from impurity and stench. Thus, it will be ready for the **Divine Service** and the rectification of the Glory in perfection, without any obstacle. For the "Obstacle" will have departed from the world.

Then the worlds will merit to be illuminated by the Higher Light, and the Higher Intention will be realized according to the will and desire intended in creation. For **Adam the First Man**, the handiwork of the Holy One, Blessed be He, was created in perfection. He breathed into him the "Breath of Life," and he attained things in the higher realms that the ministering angels did not attain. But through the "Serpent's trickery," he sinned against his Creator, and impurity spread through the world, bringing death and all the evils and troubles that have found our ancestors. But when the time comes for the filth to pass from the world, in the time of the Resurrection, they will live a strong and eternal life.

<column-break/>

This will be like the **First Creation**, for that creation was the work of the hands of the Holy One, Blessed be He, and not through the fruit and offspring of male and female. So too, the final resurrection shall be the work of His hands. Our Sages of blessed memory hinted at this in the first chapter of *Treatise Ta’anit*, saying that the "Key to the Resurrection of the Dead" is held in the hand of the Holy One, Blessed be He, and not given to an agent. He will descend and remove the "filth of the serpent" from the faces of the dead. At that time, they will know perfect knowledge of the Lord. The "Matron" will return to the King, and the filth of the soul, which is the **Evil Inclination**, will be removed; it will be burned and destroyed from the earth. Then they will recognize the Great Name. This is the meaning of the verse: "Knowledge of the Lord shall increase like the waters cover the sea" <note>Isaiah 11:9</note>.

In the chapter *Chelek* <note>A chapter in the Talmudic tractate Sanhedrin discussing the afterlife.</note>, they said: "Rabbi Meir says: From where do we know the Resurrection of the Dead from the Torah? As it says, 'Then Moses and the children of Israel will sing' <note>Exodus 15:1</note>. It does not say 'sang' [past tense], but 'will sing' [future tense]—from here we find the Resurrection of the Dead in the Torah."

In the Torah of **Rashbi**, peace be upon him, it is written: "Then Moses will sing." This refers to the time when Israel will return to look upon the "Face of the King." For Moses and the children of Israel are the "Righteous of the World" who were alive on the level of the soul. They will be invited to live in the body and will be called the "Chosen of the Holy One, Blessed be He." For it is written: "Then Moses will sing."

Rabbi Shimon said: "The Lord will again set His hand a second time to recover the remnant of His people" <note>Isaiah 11:11</note>. This means that the merit of the righteous will protect them and refine them in the "Land of the Living." Israel will then be established and the world will be stood up on the foundation of their deeds.

And if you should say: "Since they are already established in the 'Bundle of Life' <term>Tzeror HaChayim: The treasury of souls in the afterlife.</term> and delight in the higher pleasure, why do they need to descend again into a body?" The answer is: In the beginning, when the world was created, they were like sparks of light, and they were intended to live in bodies forever. But because of the sin, death was decreed. Now, the Holy One, Blessed be He, desires to fulfill His initial plan, for "there is no righteous man on earth who does good and does not sin" <note>Ecclesiastes 7:20</note>. If you say they died because of the Serpent’s counsel, then they must rise and be "Masters of Knowledge" for the King.

Concerning this, we have learned: "Moses died." But is it possible to say he died? Rather, it means he was hidden from the eyes of the world, for he was the first and the last. His physical form returned to the dust like the first creation, but his soul remained in the "Land of the Living." When it says "Then Moses will sing," it refers to the day of the future song.

Even though it has already been explained in the "Clarification of the Souls" that they will live and rise, there are reasons why the Holy One, Blessed be He, revives them. It is like the renewal of the work of creation. All the levels of the worlds will rise, because in the future, the Holy One, Blessed be He, will rectify the attributes that were diminished. Even those who died "at the hands of the serpent" <note>Referring to those who were so righteous they only died because of the universal decree of death brought by the primordial serpent, not for their own sins.</note> will rise to be the "Legions of the King." Even Moses our Teacher, whose level is higher than all, will return in the Resurrection of the Dead, as proven by the verse "Then he will sing."

Furthermore, there is an intention regarding **Moses our Teacher**, peace be upon him: he is included in the **Secret of the Ibbur** <term>Ibbur: Literally "impregnation"; a Kabbalistic concept where a soul enters a living person to assist them or fulfill a specific mission.</term>. This is the intention of this chapter.

->**And this is the intention in this chapter**<-

This wonder requires an explanation of the reason for the "decay" of the bodies. Why must the bodies rot in the dust until the time when the Holy One, Blessed be He, revives them and rouses them from their dust? And why must the soul subordinate itself under the body that arises without the Accuser? This is the reality of the Resurrection. "Then Moses will sing" refers to the first creation... <note>The text breaks off here.</note>

<meta>This page continues the investigation into the nature of the afterlife, specifically debating whether "the World to Come" refers to the immediate state of the soul after death or the physical resurrection at the end of days. It seeks to reconcile the views of Maimonides and Nahmanides on these stages of existence.</meta>

After the Resurrection, the righteous person receives his portion immediately from the "Hand of Kindness." According to this view, "the World to Come" is interpreted as the "World of Souls." This is a significant point regarding the memory of the commandments and the ultimate cessation of physical life. If one considers the state after the Resurrection of the Dead, the purified body itself will be called "the World to Come." The reason the Master of Reward, blessed be He, pays a good reward to those who fear Him in the World of Souls—called the Garden of Eden—prior to the "Great Reward" and the "Hidden Good" is that the latter occurs after the Resurrection. At that time, the Reward and its ultimate purpose will be near; everything will belong to both the body and the soul, and they will delight together just as they earned it together.

He further wrote in that chapter, at the end of the passage: "I was sent," as support for these words. What we wrote regarding *Midrash Rabbi Tanchuma* <note>A collection of homiletic teachings on the Torah.</note>: "Behold, the Holy One, blessed be He, established it." Rabbi Berechiah taught: "He strikes the living; they shall all live in the World to Come, yet they did not know that voice." "The World to Come" is translated into Aramaic as *Almaya d'Atei* <note>The world that is coming.</note>. This teaches us that before the world was created, it arose in the Divine Thought to create it, to restore it, and to flee... <unclear>glul phatz</unclear>. See, no creature could endure it. The Holy One, blessed be He, turned away because they could not bear it; He took its restraint and placed it in its stead, hidden and prepared for the "End of the Heel" <term>Ekev: Literally "heel," but here referring to the end of history or the final generation.</term> when they shall merit the end of the "Satiety" and it will be restored to them. This refers to the "Final World." This is what we mean when we say "the World to Come" has *already* come—since the beginning of Creation. As King David said: "How great is Your goodness, which You have hidden for those who fear You, which You have performed for those who trust in You" <note>Psalm 31:20</note>. This concludes the language of the Midrash.

The **Ramban** <term>Nachmanides (1194–1270): A leading medieval Jewish scholar, philosopher, and kabbalist.</term>, of blessed memory, wrote on this in his *Sha'ar HaGemul* <note>The Gate of Reward: A treatise on the afterlife.</note>, and these are his words: "The definition of the World to Come is that it has *already* come." This is the meaning of the Aramaic translation. Some call it the "Fortune of the World to Come," implying it is waiting and coming. Furthermore, the "End of the Heel" is the Light, and that light arose in Thought and was created before this world. This is to say it is the "Last Sephira" <term>Sephira: One of the ten divine emanations in Kabbalah.</term> which one attains and through which one is elevated. Thus ends his language.

There is one who explains this Midrash to mean that the World to Come is a continuous force and state—meaning, it is for every person after death and before the Resurrection. Regarding this, it is called the "World that Comes." There is also a later Midrash stating that the soul is elevated through it, and it is also called the World to Come regarding the "fruit of his portion," of blessed memory. But this was not the intention of the Midrash, nor was the Ramban’s explanation intended as such. For one requires tradition received from man to man, and the recipient must broaden it according to his own understanding and path, following the words of the Sages. One should not be foolish regarding intellectual matters. Before the world was created, it was a "Prepared World" that arose in Thought—it was the Divine Wisdom to create the Light. This Light is the "Prepared One," and this "Prepared One" exists for the end. Their saying "it has already come" is like saying "Let there be light," meaning it already existed—that is, before the Blessed One, in His mercy, created the "Hidden Good" for the righteous.

As for what our Great Teacher <note>Referring to Ramban.</note> said—that it is "waiting and coming"—we have a tradition that this hints at a continuous power that never ceases. It is the expectation of the event’s occurrence, from which it is named. This power exists for the time of Preparation, always ready. The Light was the essence of what was perceived. It is the "Last Level" through which one is elevated, and through which one will be elevated after the Resurrection. This is what the Midrash meant by "giving to them in the Final World," which is a hint to the "General World" after the Resurrection. This was their intention in the Midrash: they hinted at the "World of Souls" that comes to a person immediately after death.

Consider this wise man: how did it enter his mind that our Great Teacher could mean a hint that would contradict his own true opinion? For in every place where our Sages mentioned "the World to Come," their intention was the state *after* the Resurrection, not the state of a person immediately after death. This was proven in the *Sha'ar HaGemul* with clear evidence. He should be rebuked for passing over his own words and warnings in Chapter 28—that no man should approach the words of the Sages of Kabbalah unless he is a recipient of tradition from the mouth of a Sage who is a master of Kabbalah. He remains far from the words of our Great Teacher in his Introduction to the Torah. I have already written about him regarding this in the "Chapter of Differences," using this same language. He also wrote in that chapter, at the end: "There are those who mention in the prayers more than the Sabbath... for the 'Waiting Good' to receive the reward for the fear of God." This is intellectual—following the path we wrote—regarding man after death.

<meta>This hidden tag marks the transition between columns.</meta>

<column-break/>

"Arranged for You, and there is none besides You; nothing but You, and who is like You?" <note>Part of the "Ani Ma'amin" or "Ein Keloheinu" liturgical tradition.</note>. Our Sages explained these as four levels of reward: "There is none arranged for You, Lord our God, in this world; there is none besides You for the life of the World to Come; there is nothing but You for the Days of the Messiah; and who is like You for the Resurrection of the Dead." These are the periods designated for receiving reward. Afterward, they explained the "Choice Reward" from this world, which was mentioned first. To say "nothing but You" refers to our portion in the Days of the Messiah, and it says "thus it will be visited in the World to Come," which is the eternal state following the Resurrection of the Dead.

He mentioned the World to Come after "This World" because it is "waiting." This agrees more with the view of the **Rambam** <term>Maimonides (1138–1204): The preeminent medieval Jewish philosopher and codifier.</term>. If it were according to the view of the Ramban, he should have mentioned the "Garden of Eden" which is in this world—as it is the level that follows This World—rather than the "Heel" which is the very last of the levels. But since he did not mention the Garden of Eden at all, it appears the term "the Heel" includes all the levels that come after death.

That arrangement is not difficult for our Great Teacher, but rather agrees with his view, even though it follows the Rambam. There are several reasons for this. One is that the "World to Come" is the goal of all hope in one's service and choice, and his labor in the Torah of this world. Thus, it is described as the "Complete World," and such is the language of the Midrash. The Sage wrote according to the conclusion of the study: just as the service was through Resurrection, so shall be the reception of the reward. Since the service was with both body and soul in this world, so the reward must be in both body and soul. This is impossible in the "World of Souls," but it is possible in the "World to Come" that follows the Resurrection. For this reason, the Rambam mentions them, and there is no place to mention the Garden of Eden here.

Furthermore, the intention of the "Waiting Good" regarding the Great Teacher is the extension of the soul and spirit through the power of Kabbalah before all else. This inclusion within the body clings to the "Secret of the World to Come" after the Resurrection, so they may exist today in body and soul through the merit of the commandments. This intention applied even in This World, were it not for the Sin <note>The Primordial Sin of Adam.</note>. Now, by decree, it must return to its ancient state in the World to Come. According to the Sage, this is why it says "at the end it shall be forgiven." This is the help that our Teacher included in this chapter.

---

->### Chapter 42<-

Understand this, all Israel: they have a portion in the World to Come, as it is said: "And your people are all righteous, they shall inherit the land forever, the branch of My planting, the work of My hands, that I may be glorified" <note>Isaiah 60:21</note>. The "World to Come" mentioned here is the one that follows the Resurrection of the Dead; it is not the one that comes to a person immediately after death. The author rejected the idea that "inheriting the land forever" meant anything other than the eternal life in the presence of the Creator, which has no measure or limit.

In the first chapter, and in the third chapter of *Sha'ar HaGemul*, Rabbi Jacob said: "There is no commandment in the Torah whose reward is mentioned alongside it that does not also refer to the Resurrection of the Dead." Regarding the honor of parents, it is written: "so that your days may be lengthened and so that it may be well with you" <note>Deuteronomy 5:16</note>. Regarding the "Sending of the Nest" <note>The commandment to shoo away a mother bird before taking her young.</note>, it is written: "so that it may be well with you and you may prolong your days" <note>Deuteronomy 22:7</note>.

Now, consider one who climbed a building to fulfill this commandment; he ascended and sent away the mother, and took the young, but on his return, he fell and died. Where is the "length of days" for this man? And where is the "goodness" for this man? Rather, "so that your days may be lengthened" refers to the world that is *entirely* long, and "so that it may be well with you" refers to the world that is *entirely* good.

If one were to say this refers to the World to Come that immediately follows death, there would be no need to mention "goodness," for there is still a doubt and an error regarding the "length" and "goodness," since he is destined to rise again in the Resurrection. In that context, that spiritual world is not truly "long" <note>Because it is temporary until resurrection.</note>. Since there is this doubt, it is not the end of his wonder. Where then is the "length of days"? This claim only makes sense if applied to the World to Come after the Resurrection of the Dead, which is the "End" after which there is no destruction. It is for his goodness and his life that he is forced [to live], as they said: the Resurrection of the Dead is not the end, but the world that is entirely long and entirely good. This says that this world follows the Resurrection and is dependent upon it.

<meta>This page continues the theological debate regarding the nature of the afterlife. Specifically, it contrasts the view of Maimonides (Rambam), who argued for a purely spiritual existence in the World to Come, with the views of Ra’avad, Nahmanides (Ramban), and the author of Sefer Ha-Ikkarim, who emphasize a physical resurrection where the body is refined to a higher state of existence.</meta>

# The Service
# Chapter 41

### The Service
### Chapter 41

Physical actions like eating, drinking, and sexual relations are used [in this world]. Upon the separation of the soul from the body after death, eating is far from the unique quality enumerated by our Sages (may their memory be a blessing) as a "banquet" <note>The "Seudah" or banquet prepared for the righteous in the afterlife.</note> and a time of blessing. Regarding eating and drinking, it would be a slight to the body and physical form to say that this is how those in the World to Come will function—as a body and physical form—even if they were sustained like Moses or Elijah <note>Biblical figures who were said to have transcended physical needs for periods of time or permanently.</note>. Maimonides <note>Rabbi Moshe ben Maimon, 1138–1204.</note> says it is impossible to say such a thing. He gives the reason that if physical powers were abolished from them, it would be only temporary; there is no purpose in their existence if they are not used. Since they used their limbs before the separation, it would be a waste for those in the World to Come to have them if there is no eating, drinking, or other physical nourishment. He says that the presence of organs without function would be like a collection of diseases <unclear>liket</unclear> and would lead to shame and disgrace, leaving one empty-handed—as can be derived from the scriptures. Therefore, the Creator does not perform actions in the world in vain, Heaven forbid. Consequently, every intelligent person should believe that in the World to Come there is no body or physical form, but only the soul. This is his general opinion and the upshot of his words.

However, the Ra’avad <note>Rabbi Abraham ben David, a 12th-century critic of Maimonides.</note> (may his memory be a blessing) already challenged him, writing that Maimonides' words are "close to someone who says there is no resurrection of the dead for bodies, but only for souls." According to Ra’avad, the opinion of the Talmudic Sages was that the righteous are destined to stand in their garments, using an argument "from the grain of wheat" <note>A Talmudic analogy: if a grain of wheat is buried naked and grows with many coverings, surely the righteous buried in clothes will rise clothed.</note>. Thus, they instructed their children to bury them in white garments and not black ones... and the righteous should believe that they will merit to live through their physical bodies. Likewise, the Sages said that they "stand in their blemishes and then are healed," and all these things prove that they stand in their physical forms. For everyone who departs from the group, their bodies will be strong and healthy like the bodies of angels or the body of Elijah, and the "crowns" <note>A reference to the teaching that "the righteous sit with crowns on their heads."</note> will be understood literally, not just as a metaphor. 

Also, Rabbi Meir ben Todros HaLevi <note>Known as the Ramah, 1170–1244.</note> (may his memory be a blessing) wrote a letter of complaint to the Sages of Lunel against Maimonides, presenting a great and precious argument. He said: "I am distressed by what he wrote, which seems to deny the resurrection of the dead, for he interprets the 'World to Come' as being without body or physical form. If so, there is no 'Resurrection'." Rabbi Aaron HaLevi replied to him regarding the World to Come, saying this is a danger to the words of the Master [Maimonides], for in the Chapter "Chelek" <note>The 10th chapter of Tractate Sanhedrin.</note> we take from his words that the World to Come belongs to a person immediately upon their separation from this world, and he calls it the "World of Souls" which one merits instantly.

Furthermore, the Master [Maimonides] believes in reward... and it is not a denial at all. If so, there is no place for Rabbi Aaron’s letter against the Master on this point. The opinion of the Master [Maimonides] is that all this is against the view of the Talmudic and Midrashic Sages and against the true Tradition <note>original: "Kabbalah."</note> received from Moses at Sinai. However, we have found in the book *Sefer Ha-Ikkarim* <note>The "Book of Principles" by Joseph Albo, 15th century.</note>, Chapter 28 of the Fourth Part, that the "World to Come" mentioned in this context is not a general term. It is used generally for every level of reward for souls after death, but it is used specifically for the greatest level possible for the soul of the righteous: the level of light after the Resurrection of the Dead. That specific level is called "Life of the World to Come." Therefore, the Sages say "All Israel have a portion in the World to Come," meaning that in the World of Souls, everyone has a place after death according to their deeds. Indeed, even the "nations of the world" have a portion and some level in the World of Souls. But the final, great level, which is the "Life of the World to Come," is not merited by everyone, only by the perfectly righteous, and only after the Resurrection of the Dead. He said the proof for this is the Sages' statement that "the nations of the world have a portion in the World to Come." If the "World to Come" only referred to the level after Resurrection, how could they say even the nations have it? For that level is prepared only for the perfectly righteous. Thus, we say the term is used for both the World of Souls and the World to Come after Resurrection. The confusion and wonderment regarding this arise because each matter has a tradition; the dispute is not over names but over the essence itself...

### Part
### Chapter 41

In the chapter "The One Who Sells the Ship" <note>Tractate Bava Batra, 74b.</note>, Rabbah bar bar Hannah said in the name of Rabbi Yochanan: "The Holy One, blessed be He, is destined to make a banquet for the righteous from the flesh of the Leviathan... and they will make a trade with it." The words of Maimonides in the *Laws of Repentance* are like a heavenly wind compared to what he wrote elsewhere, where the Sages called it:

<margin>
->Behold<-
A metaphor for this goodness prepared for the righteous is the "banquet." We have already explained Maimonides’ view, and he said: "Heaven forbid that those bodies should return to the dust." He thought it would have been better for Maimonides to remain silent on such matters. In his opinion, while the perfectly righteous in this world are not denied a good reward according to their deeds, the primary reward is spiritual and for the soul alone in the World to Come. According to his view, whenever the "World to Come" is mentioned in the words of our Sages, the intention is...
</margin>

...to them, that the World to Come for a person begins immediately after death upon the separation of the soul from the body, where there is no eating, drinking, or physical pleasure. This is what he wrote in the *Commentary on the Mishnah*: that there is no body or physical form, only the souls of the righteous wearing crowns. There are no physical bodies as they exist on earth. However, regarding the idea that they return from the graves and receive reward and "standing" and pleasure and life—the early Sages said that in the World to Come there is no sexual relation, but it is like a "passing through" where there will be spirit. They said "the righteous sit," in a physical sense, without toil or weariness, meaning they have knowledge from which they benefit—this is the "radiance" and these are their "crowns." This is like what he said... and behold, he speaks of the Resurrection without... against Maimonides. Thus, these ten [points]... this is what they said... from the Divine Presence <note>original: "Shekhinah."</note>. The Holy One is there, and they do not know a physical body. One should believe with this that there is a physical reward in this world for the perfectly righteous. The reason is for the sake of the Holy One and His faith in the world... in the days when we suffered, then even more so... or so they might acquire more spiritual life which they could not achieve in their lifetimes. Furthermore... but what he wrote in the chapter "These are the [ones who have a portion in the] Mishnah," and according to what... the Dead and another nourishment after they live and are prepared for a greater level in the World to Come, according to what we received regarding physical life from the Holy One. According to his opinion, even based on their statement "The World to Come has no eating etc.," it is because there is no body or physical form... for then the body and form would be in vain.

Since he thought that the Midrash of Rabbi Shimon bar Yochai <note>The Zohar.</note>... remember this. <meta>catchword: Behold</meta>

<summary>This page analyzes the debate between Maimonides and other scholars like Ra'avad and Albo regarding whether the World to Come is a purely spiritual state or a physical resurrection. It concludes that "the World to Come" can refer to both the immediate World of Souls and the ultimate state following the Resurrection of the Dead.</summary>

<meta>This page continues the theological exploration of the "World to Come" (Olam Ha-Ba) and the Resurrection of the Dead. The previous page discussed Maimonides' view that the afterlife is purely spiritual, while this page explores the counter-argument: that the physical body is refined and preserved in a state of holiness for the truly righteous.</meta>

# Chapter 42
# The Section on Service
# Chapter 43

...the perfectly righteous <term>Tzaddikim Gemurim; individuals whose lives were entirely dedicated to divine will</term>. One might say that those who remove the physical vitality of the World to Come <note>This refers to the transition from a physical biological life to a spiritual-physical hybrid existence</note> do so to diminish the existence of the whole Torah... just as the perfectly righteous, whose existence is entirely a Torah of kindness, even in their physical choice and their portion of the Torah. They will merit a level in the World to Come according to their Torah. And if so, why should they not merit the Resurrection of the Dead?

Furthermore, one might say that those who remove the physical vitality of the World to Come from the "remnant of the flesh of the soul" <note>A poetic way of describing the body as it relates to the soul</note> have a portion in the future world during the time of Resurrection. They will remain standing and will not die. It has already been explained that Rabbi Hanina (may his memory be a blessing) established that in the future to come, "Death will be swallowed up forever" <note>quoting Isaiah 25:8</note>, as it is said, "The Lord God will wipe away tears from all faces." What does Rabbi Hanina do with the phrase "from all faces"? He interprets it as "from the faces of Israel and from the faces of the nations." For it is written, "For the youth shall die at a hundred years old" <note>Isaiah 65:20</note>. This does not support Rabbi Hanina's view. What does Rabbi Joshua ben Levi do with this? He applies it to the other nations of the world...

In this world, because of the "Satan" <note>In this context, the personification of the impulse toward physical decay and sin</note>, the Israelites are held captive. But in the future to come, the Holy One, Blessed be He, will make them less susceptible to destruction... they will be like "holy flesh" and will not be subject to the Angel of Death. This is what is meant by the saying that one whose "sin is finished" is entirely pure, and he merits that his soul resides in the *Zebul* <note>The name of one of the seven heavens, often associated with the Temple or the dwelling of the righteous</note>, as it is written, "I have surely built a house of habitation (*Zebul*) for You" <note>1 Kings 8:13</note>. Thus, in the view of Rabbi Hanina, in the future to come, the walls of the world will fall <note>A metaphor for the breaking down of boundaries between the physical and spiritual realms</note>. And Rabbi Hanina, who holds that there is death in the world, admits that those who are "perfectly righteous" are not included in the category of death.

Even if one says that these rewards will not occur at the Resurrection of the Dead, nevertheless, those who merit them in their lifetime will not die and will have a portion in the World to Come... it will return in a cycle <term>Gilgul; the concept of reincarnation or cyclical return</term>. According to the words of the Sages, one does not return except during the days of the World to Come after the Resurrection, not immediately after death. Both Rabbi Hanina and the other Sages agree that there is no "biological life" in the future to come <note>Meaning life as we know it, driven by physical hunger or decay</note>. This is also the view of the Sages of the Kabbalah <note>The Jewish mystical tradition</note>, who said that this portion will return when the soul is clothed in it. Death will not exist for Israel at all when the world reaches its perfection.

We have already explained this in the preceding chapter. Consider the generation that accepted the Torah; it was a decree that they should have been freed from death. For in the World to Come after the Resurrection, the Holy One, Blessed be He, restores the original Will <note>The primal state of creation before sin entered the world</note>. The decree of death and the exile from the Garden of Eden will be removed. The souls in the body and soul will be as was intended before the sin [of Adam]. When the generation was at Sinai, that "Satan" was removed from them... and it was a great success, for that Divine Will turned the bowl on its head <note>An idiom meaning to completely reverse a situation</note>, and perfection was found in their lack. It was the "Old Serpent" <note>The serpent in Eden, representing the source of mortality</note> who was the cause of the interruption of the world and its corruption. But in the end, everything will be included in the Rectification <term>Tikkun; the process of repairing the world</term>... to justify the righteous and to bring them to their dwelling. It was originally intended that man would live in body and soul for a long time, achieving great benefit and reaching perfection in the World to Come after Resurrection, living in pleasantness and great radiance. This was the original Will, and they merited the elevation of body and soul to be eternal. This is the "standing" of humanity—that the soul and body do not cease to exist in that purity and radiance...

<column-break/>

...in this world as empty and lowly, and even worse for those who have died. Even though they had some vitality in their emptiness, the ultimate intention was that they would not be subject to the "bitter death" which is the result of sins. Regarding this, for their benefit, the generation that received the Torah reached a level where the "Satan" of heresy was removed from them.

Indeed, the existence of the soul when it is linked to the Supreme Knowledge is like the existence of the angels. Its influence on the body makes the body like the soul. Even when the soul is in the body, it can be rooted in the spiritual source. For the "Secret of the Soul" prevents the decay of the body, until the life of the body becomes eternal. This is like the stay of Moses on the mountain for forty days and forty nights <note>Exodus 24:18</note>; if he had stayed there forever, he would have been sustained by that divine existence for all the days of the Holy One, Blessed be He.

This is what happened to the righteous who entered Paradise while still alive, as the Sages mentioned in the *Tractate of Derech Eretz Zuta*: seven entered Paradise in their lifetimes: **Enoch**, **Elijah** (may his memory be a blessing), **Methuselah**, **Ebed-Melech the Cushite**, **Hiram King of Tyre**, **Ya'abetz the son of Rabbi Judah the Prince**, **Serah daughter of Asher**, and **Bithiah the daughter of Pharaoh**. These individuals achieved life while still in the flesh because they were strengthened in their bodies and their souls were made permanent... they will enter the Garden of Eden in body and soul and will exist there... they will be nourished by the radiance of the Divine Presence. This will be further clarified in this chapter and in Chapter 30.

### Chapter 43

<margin>Maimonides 4</margin> The second part: the cessation of time until the end of the Messiah's reign. This is the end of man's achievement of merit.

All the authorities have ruled on this and contemplated it. They placed their focus on the end of human existence... and some explained the words of the Torah at their conclusion to match the words of the Sages. This is what the later believers did, as explained in their books. Maimonides, at the end of his words, was moved to speak against those who disagreed with him... but even in his forced explanations, he spoke against the words of the Kabbalah... he spoke against those who spoke of the time that follows the Resurrection. He saw this as a great mistake... but it is proper to wonder about this... for the Sages of Truth <note>The Kabbalists</note> know that this is so, and it is written regarding the matter that they will be established... as it says in the chapter *Helek* <note>The 11th chapter of Talmud Sanhedrin which deals with the afterlife</note>: "Know that our Sages said that in the future, the world will be destroyed and then renewed..." This refers to the cessation of the physical form...

As I have already explained in Chapter 35, they will not be physical until the time of the Resurrection... and so it seems to us and to others. These people will merit the simple existence of their souls, and they will be nourished and sing and praise... and the status of that life is higher than life in this world. This is the life of the World to Come, where the souls are like angels. However, this was not the view of **Rabbi Akiva**, who held that the body and soul are combined... and the language used is that in the future, the Holy One, Blessed be He, will grant the righteous "wings" <note>A metaphor for spiritual mobility and transcendence</note> so they may exist forever. This is the life that the Holy One, Blessed be He, designated for the righteous in the World to Come. As the Midrash teaches us, in the World to Come, His "wing" will be spread over all of Israel, and they will see the Divine and live forever, "for eye to eye they shall see the return of the Lord to Zion" <note>Isaiah 52:8</note>.

The tradition means that the generation that is now present will continue until that day. I have already written that the tradition regarding the "portion" refers to the future to come. This is not because of any external addition, but because of the nature of the soul itself. As we have written, the existence of the souls is linked to the Divine...

It also begins to contrast Maimonides' view of a purely spiritual afterlife with the Kabbalistic view of an eternal, refined physical-spiritual existence.</summary>
