# The Service: Chapter 42
## Chapter 42: The Section on [The Portion of the World to Come]

->**The Book**<- <note>original: "Ha-Sefer"; referring to a previous section of the work</note> was mentioned in the third part. And behold, if we take it according to the simple understanding of the deficiencies included in the Name of the Lord <note>original: "Y-H-W-H"</note>, as I have taught and as we have already summarized, in the future to come, the Name shall be revealed upon you. It shall dwell within them to sustain them with eternal existence. And regarding the Name of the Lord in truth, there shall be the life of existence and the indwelling of the <term>Shekhinah; the Divine Presence perceived in the world</term>. This is necessary and required by the Name of the Lord, for it shall be within the <term>Tzaddikim; the righteous who have aligned their lives with divine will</term>, because they testify to Him there, and He becomes publicized through them, as we have written above. 

Furthermore, Rabbi Elazar said: In the future, the righteous will have "Holy" proclaimed before them in the same way it is proclaimed before the Holy One, Blessed be He, as it is said: "And it shall come to pass, that he who is left in Zion, and he who remains in Jerusalem, shall be called holy" <note>Isaiah 4:3</note>. This refers to the existence mentioned in the Name, as we have written. "And he who remains in Jerusalem shall be called holy"—this is because <note>original: "le-phis-is," likely a corruption of "le-phi-kakh"</note> they shall be holy and sustained by the Name. 

Similarly, it is stated in the chapter "Helek" <note>The eleventh chapter of Talmud Sanhedrin, dealing with the afterlife</note>: Rabbi Eliezer said, "The righteous whom the Holy One, Blessed be He, is destined to resurrect shall never return to their dust," as it is said, "And it shall come to pass, that he who is left in Zion... shall be called holy." Just as the Holy One is eternally existent, so too are they eternally existent. And if you ask: what of those thousand years in which the Holy One is destined to renew His world, as it is said, "And the Lord alone shall be exalted in that day" <note>Isaiah 2:11</note>? Rather, what do the righteous do? The Holy One makes them wings like eagles and they float upon the face of the waters, as it is said, "Therefore we will not fear, though the earth be removed" <note>Psalm 46:3</note>. 

His student [Ma'oz] explained that this refers to the World to Come—the era of Resurrection. This is the "World of Rectification" <term>Olam Ha-Tikkun; a restored and perfected state of existence</term>, where they will be able to persist in both body and soul. They shall never return to their dust because they will be like the supernal radiance and the clear light which is their very life. This is what the Sages meant by saying "they enjoy the radiance of the Divine Presence." This is the beginning and the true fusion which grants eternal existence. We have already seen that the scripture records the survival of their bodies in these most holy matters. One who is nourished by the "thin" <note>referring to refined, spiritualized matter</note> will have their body become increasingly pure. 

The people in the wilderness, by being sustained by the <term>Manna; the heavenly bread provided to the Israelites</term> which appeared in the mornings—being a product of the light and the divine action—rose to higher and higher levels. Just as the soul ascends through its deeds, they merited a level even higher than this. By the knowledge of their Creator, they did not need the "product" of the light but were sustained by the light itself. Through this, they merited the Divine Presence. So too our ancestors, who believed they would be sustained in the body—the body of the World to Come—through that eternal light. This is the supernal existence, a permanent blessing placed within them. 

This is the wonder of our teacher Moses (peace be upon him) when he passed through, prayed, and ate. Regarding the Manna, the verse informs you that "man does not live by bread alone, but by every word that proceeds from the mouth of the Lord does man live" <note>Deuteronomy 8:3</note>. Its meaning is not that the physical mouth is the medium for taste and nutrition to sustain life, but rather the intent of the verse is to inform you that bread and law are not the ultimate end of taste and nourishment. Existence is sustained only by the "will of the mouth" <note>the divine decree</note>. To bring them to this final realization, He gave them the Manna, which is "that which proceeds from the mouth of the Lord." It was "bread from heaven," and those who directed their hearts to it were sustained by the word of the Lord and His Lordship. Therefore, they were directed toward the light itself, and they merited the soul's attachment to the "Light of the Secret" until they were sustained in body and soul eternally. 

In that World to Come, where they merit to enjoy and be nourished by the Light of the Secret, they will acquire eternity and merit existence in body and soul. This is what the Sages meant by saying they do not return to their dust, for they are "the work of My hands, in which I glory" <note>Isaiah 60:21</note>. This is the true union, for they are no longer like temporary "works of My hands" or like a script that fades. As for the "wings," the Great Rabbi <note>likely Nachmanides or Maimonides, though here used to support a physical-spiritual hybrid</note> explained them as the body becoming light and ascending, while the physical elements <term>Yesodot; the four elements of earth, air, fire, and water</term> are nullified in their coarse form. 

It is clarified, then, that the "World to Come" mentioned by our Sages (of blessed memory) when they said "All Israel has a portion in the World to Come," refers to the era after the Resurrection. Even though they said "the pious of the nations of the world have a portion in the World to Come," this refers to the light of the World to Come. But how do the pious of the nations merit the Resurrection? For the Sages already said that the Resurrection of the Dead is only for the righteous.

->**To the righteous**<- <note>Catchword for the next page</note>

<column-break/>

For a pure and clear soul at this level, it is possible to call this Torah "the World to Come," which surrounds and encompasses the Day of Judgment. There is no World to Come for [a person] to receive life immediately... <note>The text here enters a complex debate regarding Maimonides' view</note>. This requires investigation regarding the deficiency of the one who understands the World to Come only as the state after the Resurrection. 

The opinion of Maimonides (of blessed memory) and the scriptures regarding the "deficiency of the Nazirites" <note>likely an OCR error for 'those who die' or 'the deceased'</note> is that after the Resurrection of the Dead, the soul will eventually strip off the body and die again. This would mean that the soul's return to the body is a temporary event. However, if the verse says "forever," it hints that during the time of the cessation [of this world], it refers to the judgment placed upon the laws of the world... and they merited the reward of the Torah and the commandments in both body and soul. 

By saying they were "planted by the same reason," it means He gives existence and continuity to the body and soul together in the "World of the Body." The reason He decrees this continuity is because it corresponds to the Supernal Flow <note>the emanation of divine energy</note>. In the secret of "the eyes of the Lord shall be satisfied," one must examine the absolute reason for our physical nature. As explained in the first part of this book, when the spirit prevails, it flourishes and increases and exists in its particularity. 

The body was not given merely for "good" but to be a vessel for the soul, not as a separate physical action. For vessels are made for a purpose—they are the "vessels of the Chariot" <term>Merkavah; the divine chariot or throne representing God's manifestation</term>, the chariot of the Rider in the Heavens, from the secret of Emanation <term>Atzilut; the highest of the four worlds in Kabbalah</term>. It is therefore necessary that these "vessels" <note>the bodies of the righteous</note> exist eternally, because they are integrated into an eternal existence and order. Their existence does not depend on physical organs that decay, but on their cleavage to their Source. They merit the ultimate purity. 

Scripture gave them this time to nullify the "evil" <note>the physical inclination</note> that prevents this attachment. Since the soul in its lower state is like the emanations, it must be decreed that existence is not lacking for it. This was the assurance and the fusion of the Divine Presence and the Light. We compare those who walk in the "perfect way" to the statement in the first chapter of Rosh Hashanah: "Rav used to habitually say: The World to Come is not like this world. In the World to Come, there is no eating, no drinking, no procreation, no business, no jealousy, no hatred, and no competition. Rather, the righteous sit with their crowns on their heads and enjoy the radiance of the Divine Presence, as it is said: 'And they beheld God, and they ate and drank'" <note>Exodus 24:11</note>. 

Look and see: if the World to Come has no body, how can such things be attributed to it? By saying "It is not like this world," etc. Who does not know that Rav's intent in all this was not to say there is no body there at all? To say so would be to utter empty words. Rather, if we accept that there is a body and a resting place there, Rav's teaching is very great: even though there is a body, there is no "materiality" <note>no physical density or biological needs</note>. Because the body does not need eating or drinking to survive, but rather survives through its attachment to its Source. The Supernal Light dwells upon them, and they exist in order like "the light of the King's face is life." 

This is why he said "the righteous sit"—this "sitting" is the aforementioned permanent existence. "And their crowns are on their heads"—this is the Crown of Tiferet <term>Tiferet; the kabbalistic attribute of Beauty or Harmony</term> that sustains them. This is the joy referred to in "eternal joy shall be upon their heads" <note>Isaiah 35:10</note>. They become like the "Chieftain's Council" because the wonders below are a reflection of the wonders above. 

This doubles the proof of the verse that Rabbi Abba said to Rabbi Yohanan: In the future, the righteous will be called by the Name of the Holy One, Blessed be He, as it is said: "Every one that is called by My name, and whom I have created for My glory, I have formed him, yea, I have made him" <note>Isaiah 43:7</note>. The "Righteous is the foundation of the world" <note>Proverbs 10:25</note>. All who are certain and included in this are sustained by their connection to the Master. Those who are so attached are called "Righteous" after His Name, for they are the channels connecting the Heavens to the Earth. It says that there they become in the likeness of the Supernal Glory, for the Supernal Glory includes everything. So too the righteous one above is included, for every thing is rectified and included above, as all this was explained well in the first part of this [book].

<summary>This page argues that in the World to Come, the righteous exist in a refined physical state sustained directly by divine light (the Radiance of the Shekhinah) rather than material food. It challenges Maimonides' view that the afterlife is purely spiritual, asserting that the body becomes a holy "vessel" for the soul.</summary>

It explores how the physical and spiritual realms, currently separated by sin and exile, will be perfectly integrated through the "Torah of Kindness."</meta>

# Part of the Service: Chapter 43
## Chapter 43

->**Intellect**<- and let the Oral Torah be kindness, and let this world be as it is written, "and Your love [is toward the heavens]." The upper ones and the second tablets <note>Referring to the second set of Ten Commandments given after the Golden Calf</note> are like a "Koph" <note>The Hebrew letter ק (Koph)</note>, meaning that, as it were, He returned and renewed the foundation and His Torah by His will, in the manner of the **Crown** <term>Atarah; the crown, often signifying the final emanation of the Divine, Malchut, which relates to the physical world</term>. And the Crown sits within him, though its ornament is missing from this world. But in the World to Come, after the Resurrection, it will be a Torah of kindness upon kindness from the Merciful One, like a body and a set power that is established, and they shall delight in it in both body and soul. 

To return to the praise and its fulfillment: Israel extended the simplicity of the Torah's home into the "Voice," which is the Oral Torah. The Crown—the Crown is missing its writing to teach them that the simple meaning will be detailed through it, and it will be fulfilled. This means the Merciful One intended that it should be mixed with the rejection of Wisdom, Honor, and the rest of the worldly wisdom, as opposed to the wisdom of the holy vessels and incense. For the increase of lower wisdom—which is the wisdom of Solomon <note>King Solomon, traditionally the author of Proverbs, Ecclesiastes, and Song of Songs</note>—is the form of service and kingship. But the form of the Merciful One is from the wisdom of the holy vessels, meaning from the upper, holy Wisdom. This is the beginning of the measurement of Voice and Understanding, meaning the Torah, for its increase is the kindness of the vessel... 

And this is the secret of the Service and its intention: that it needed to be established, lacking, as if with its swords in the mouth of the divider. Just as its aspects are measured portions that cause the return of the "Koph" signs <note>original: "Simanim Koph"; likely a symbolic reference to the shape or numerical value of the letter</note> in the choice of the Merciful One, and it shall be complete. For they will merit to delight in the light of the Holy One, Blessed be He—the end of what was lacking in its ornament—in the world of promises, which is the lower Garden of Eden. And in the World to Come, after the resurrection of the dead, they will merit an even higher protection, which is the surrounding of the Merciful One and the sound of the proper writing for the righteous in the time to come. Behold, they are pure in everything—in body and soul—in the lower Garden of Eden as well. 

And in the chapter "Layn" in the tractate *Arachin*, it is taught: Rabbi Judah says, the glory of the lower Sanctuary was like a spring... <note>Original: "ma'ayan." This refers to the idea that the holiness of the Temple flowed and expanded</note> do not read "the sukkah of the weak," but "nature," and all the portions that are lacking so that you may merit to gain wisdom upon wisdom in its prepared house, and not for the World to Come... "upon a ten-stringed instrument and upon a lute." <note>Psalm 92:4</note> The secret is that the Mishnah <note>The core text of the Oral Torah</note> in the Sanctuary of the Merciful One was in every ring of the building's wisdom. And for its song, it is mentioned as "increasing," and above, the **Shekhinah** <term>Divine Presence</term> is upon the "eighth," which refers to the levels of the building. 

In the World to Come, the "eight" will be complete like the whole eagle <note>Perhaps an allusion to "renewing youth like an eagle"</note> and the law will be chosen. For the World to Come involves both body and soul, since the Sanctuary and the Glory are aligned. And according to the explanation of this Mishnah, after Rabbah bar bar Hana <note>A Talmudic sage famous for his fantastic, allegorical travel stories</note> said: "Once we were traveling in the desert and we saw those 'Dead of the Wilderness' <note>The generation of the Exodus who died in the desert; Rabbah bar bar Hana claims to have seen them in a miraculous state</note> lying on their backs... and a light went out from them... and I did not have a bit of the World to Come <note>meaning he couldn't grasp their level</note>... for they have the power to walk and to act and to sing to Him... Israel is destined to know the law through them." 

Our Sages of blessed memory already said: "Wisdoms cry out in the street." And our Teacher <note>likely referring to Moses or a specific Kabbalistic authority</note> received it in the wilderness, which was a hidden place... and the righteous is like the foundation of the dwelling in the upper Wisdom, which is the Wisdom of God, and the lower Wisdom, which is the Wisdom of Solomon. This is the secret of the story of the "joints of the thighs" <note>referring to Song of Songs 7:2</note> in the holy song that Solomon sang. The secret is the purity and the appointment as the duration of time flows to those who delight. This is during the "time of favor." In the time of exile, it is not perceived above, because the intent and the "silvers" <note>original: "Kesafim"; can mean money, silver, or "longings"</note> are like silver that separates between those who are accompanied by sin. For those who delight, this is a hidden glory, and the "silvers" prevent sin. The time is set... and the time of its purity is like silver, and the intention will fall... they will find the secrets of their hearts... as it is written, the flow and the existence as the duration of time moves to all the worlds... to know how they will be merits and their taste in the World to Come after the resurrection of the dead, which is the "resurrection of every place" and the secret of the totality. This is the end of the reward for the Service and the commandments. And the flow of life will be the Shekhinah within them, in body and soul. 

And this is the vision of the Prophet: he saw the "thigh" <note>Ezekiel 1:7 or Song of Songs 7:2</note> to the Merciful One, that it would be exalted, and the body would remember after the soul. The lower parts are like the soul, which is a hint to Wisdom... compared to the body, which is the lower part of man. And the soul corresponds to the soul, which is more spiritual... and a hint to the involvement. Therefore, his cooking is like "silvers" for kings. And the "thigh" corresponds to the lower companion, for the thigh—

<column-break/>

**The end** and the aftermath of the soul was also the end and the aftermath of the upper Building. And the **silver** <note>Kesafim/Silver/Longings</note> corresponds to the Upper, to teach that delight is permanently fixed on the Upper Wisdom in the World to Come after the Resurrection. Israel is destined to give judgment upon them, because from now on, the choice and the sign are above. For in exile, the end of everything is in the "Hiding of the Face" <term>Hester Panim; a state where God's presence is not clearly visible</term>, and the Holy One, Blessed be He—as it were—does not go up to His goodness in the Jerusalem below. The flow is delayed by the sins of Israel, for the Shekhinah is with them in exile. For the Mother <note>A common kabbalistic term for the Shekhinah</note> does not abandon her children, and in every place they were exiled, she was with them. Just as they caused her to go out and be established among the nations in exile—which is the "prison house"—so they must cause her goodness and benefit to return from him. 

As our Sages of blessed memory said: "A prisoner cannot release himself from the prison house." <note>Talmud, Berakhot 5b</note> The Redemption is in the hand of Israel... and when they awaken Repentance below, the Upper Repentance is awakened above—the secret of the **Jubilee** <term>Yovel; the 50th year when slaves were freed and land returned to original owners</term>, which brings servants to freedom. For so it was in the exile of Egypt, in the secret of "and their cry went up to God." Then the redemption of the king, the **Messiah**, will grow great. The Crown will return to its wearer, and the Upper Shekhinah will return to the creatures. 

Afterward will be the Resurrection. Those who are resurrected will never return to their dust. They will exist in body and soul, for such was the intention from the beginning in the life of the Merciful One: that he should live forever, as we have already written. Sin caused him and all the world the deficiency of death. But after the Resurrection, when the Evil <note>original: "ha-Ra"</note> is consumed from the world, there is no more death... because the destroyer has gone away. And because there is no **Evil Inclination** <term>Yetzer HaRa; the drive toward selfishness or sin</term>, there is no sin. And where there is no sin, there is no death. For there is no "mixture of elements" that leads to decay—unlike the opinion of the Greeks and the naturalists <note>original: "ha-teva-im"</note>. Their false opinion says that anything composed must decompose and separate. But from the beginning, the intention in this composition was that it should never separate. Sin caused it to separate. In the World to Come after the Resurrection, there is no sin, so there is no death. 

Therefore, there are no curses or impurities, and there is no "Sacrifice" <term>Korban</term> in the time to come, nor the Daily Offerings, nor the Additional Offerings. However, the **Thanksgiving Offering** <term>Korban Todah</term> will never be nullified. For Sin-Offerings and Guilt-Offerings are brought because of sin and iniquity; since there is no sin, why would there be Sin-Offerings or Guilt-Offerings? At first, there is only "Good" ... as it is written: "Enter His gates with thanksgiving..." <note>Psalm 100:4</note> and "Bless His name." 

Rabbi Isaac said in the name of Rabbi Levi: "All sacrifices will be nullified in the future, but the Thanksgiving Offering will never be nullified." As it says: "I will offer to You the sacrifice of thanksgiving" <note>Psalm 116:17</note>—one refers to the prayer and one refers to the sacrifice. And so it says, "the voice of joy and the voice of gladness... the voice of those who say, 'Give thanks to the Lord'"—this refers to the prayer of thanksgiving; "and of those who bring a thanksgiving offering to the house of the Lord"—this refers to the physical Thanksgiving Offering. 

The secret of the matter is that from below, there was the cause of distancing the "Upper Earth," the smallness, and the separation in the Unity. According to the center, the Sacrifice was to establish the world and to cause the Presence to return, to bring those who were far near, and to support every limb and part of the Sanctuary. But in the future to come, when the accusing Evil Inclination is consumed and "sinners vanish from the earth," there will be no more need for sacrifices. For the attribute of Justice will be elevated into Mercy. "And the Lord shall be King over all the earth; in that day shall the Lord be one, and His name one." <note>Zechariah 14:9</note> 

As we explained regarding the "Heel of Jacob," we will go further into the secret of this matter—look there. And because there is no sin, there is no death, as we explained. Those resurrected will see the Shekhinah increase upon the light of the Merciful One, which is the "Good" prepared for the righteous at that time. They will delight in it in body and soul, as we have written. This is what our Sages hinted at when they said, "so that it may be well with you"—in the world that is entirely good; "and that your days may be long"—in the world that is entirely long <note>Talmud, Kiddushin 39b</note>. This does not refer to the death of the soul, whether after death in this world or after the Resurrection. For if the body had no part in that good or in the "length of days," there would still be the question: "it is well for this one's days, but where is the length of days for the other?" 

Behold, the body is deep in its judgment, for its measure is like the Sabbath. Not everything is caused by the "night"... as we have explained and as we believe: the reward will be for the body as well. Just as both of them acted together, so they will delight and "eat" of their goodness together. "So that it may be well with you and your days may be long"—all these words are for their preparation and their existence... and the Upper Desire, for three...

<summary>This page explains that after the Resurrection, the physical body and soul will be eternally reunited and sustained by the "Torah of Kindness." It argues that death is an unnatural result of sin, not a physical necessity, and that in the future, all sacrifices except the Thanksgiving Offering will cease because the Evil Inclination will be destroyed.</summary>

# Part of the Service | Chapter 43

<meta>catchword: The Gold-Stain</meta>

To Him, and He will save us, etc. And as stated in Midrash Rabbah: In the future, the Holy One, Blessed be He, is destined to be the head of a **dance** <note>Hebrew: *Machol*; also implies a circle</note> for the righteous in the time to come. This is a sign for the circumcision <note>likely referring to the covenant</note> for good. It is written: "And He will hover over it like God" <note>original: *ka-Elohim*</note>, according to the secret of the seven, and to the scholars, for "This is God, our God forever and ever; He will lead us *al-mut*" <note>Psalm 48:15</note>. This means leading us through "worlds" <note>Hebrew: *olamot*</note>, healthy worlds, worlds among those worlds. As it is written within the worlds of the hidden ones. 

According to Onkelos <note>The famous 2nd-century translator of the Torah into Aramaic</note>, this refers to "the world in which there is no death" <note>A wordplay on *al-mut* (forever) as *al-mavet* (no death)</note>. *Almut* is like "two worlds" <note>dual form</note>. And we were given through action, and we were given through action; so too in the Jerusalem Talmud, it is brought that a "circular dance" <note>original: *machol agulah*</note> has no beginning and no end, which is a parable for the pleasure that has no end or limit. For this reason, the World to Come after the Resurrection is called "a world that is entirely good" and "a world that is entirely long" <note>meaning eternal</note>. 

Then the righteous will achieve the ultimate perception, for the Divine Presence <term>Shekhinah; the feminine, indwelling aspect of God</term> will be in the center, as it is written: "And a voice like a dance." And the Divine Presence hints at that inward excellence. They said: "Every single one [of the righteous] has [the light] hovering over him." And in the chapter "One who sells a ship" <note>A section of the Talmud, Bava Batra 75a</note>: In the future, the Holy One, Blessed be He, will make seven canopies for every righteous person. And you shall see the light of the eyes in every crown of beauty, all of which are included in the seven canopies, all of them for the service of the heart. 

And in Midrash Rabbah (Parsha 83): In the future, the Holy One, Blessed be He, will make a feast for His righteous servants in the time to come, and everyone who comes to all the feasts of this world will merit to see it in the World to Come. And in the Psalms it is written: "The secret of their greatness is a thousand mountains," and if the mountains are counted, they belong to the King. 

And in the fifth chapter of *Chasidut*: Rabbi Eliezer [says]: [the light] will sprout from the earth in heights, which is the will in the orders of a thousand, etc. And it is prepared for the great banquet of the righteous, the feast of the world. And also in the chapter "One who sells a ship": In the future, the Holy One, Blessed be He, will make a feast for the righteous from the flesh of the **Leviathan** <note>The primordial sea monster</note>. And in the *Alpha Beta* of Rabbi Akiva, it teaches that in the future, they will say before the Holy One, Blessed be He, at the banquet of the righteous in the Garden of Eden: "The soul is Yours!" 

It is written regarding the "Succah" <note>booth/canopy</note> of the world, that the wicked shall not consume it, but they shall see the canopy of the righteous, etc. What remains from all this is that all the righteous in their canopy, delighting in the future in the World to Come, are there in **body and soul** in the Garden of Eden. For the intellect will be pure and will reach the "First Light," which is the **Higher Wisdom** <term>Chokhmah; the second Sefirah, representing the flash of divine inspiration</term>. 

According to the tradition of Rabbi Nehunia ben HaKanah <note>A 1st-century sage to whom early Kabbalistic works are attributed</note>, there is the Throne of Glory, the managed dwelling, the protected place, which is the House of the World to Come. Its place is engraved in Wisdom, as it is written: "And God said, Let there be light, and there was light." And John <note>likely a reference to a specific sage or a corruption of a name like Yannai</note> said: they are the sick, as it is written, "and there was light," and concerning the heavens it is said "that it was good." And the Holy One, Blessed be He, took it and **hid it** for the righteous in the time to come, as it says: "Oh, how great is Your goodness, which You have hidden for those who fear You" <note>Psalm 31:20</note>. 

No creature can look upon the First Light, as it is written: "And God saw all that He had made, and behold, it was very good." This means the Holy One, Blessed be He, saw all that He had made was very good, radiant and silvery; He took from that "goodness" and hid within it all fifty gates of Wisdom and wrote them in this world. This is what is written: "For I have given you a good lesson (Lekach Tov), do not forsake my Torah" <note>Proverbs 4:2</note>. "I have given you a good lesson"—if you involve yourselves in it, do not forsake it. This refers to the master of the Oral Torah. 

He said that the wise man should not limit this quality to this world, for this quality is included in "this world," but it is also the light by which they will merit the life of the World to Come, which is the "Hidden Good." From then on, they sought the humility of the Holy One, Blessed be He, as it is written: "He hid it in a bull/ox..." <note>alluding to the Shor HaBar</note>. In the future, the body that was taken from the First Light will be in the light, and they will be refined through it... to teach them, as it is written: "Hear, my son, the instruction of your father..." and "approach His teaching." 

And with this vision of humility, the divine humility is understood through the light that was hidden and is found, as it is said: "Hidden for those who fear You." This remains in his heart as an exalted thing, similar to how you return in this world and guard Your Torah and fulfill Your commandments and sanctify Your Name in greatness and unify it in the morning and evening. This is the secret of the "Standing Prayer" <note>The Amidah</note> in which the righteous are crowned, and it is at the head of all mysteries. Its place is engraved in Wisdom, for it is "Wisdom from Wisdom." It is the light taken from the First Light, and it is the achievement that the righteous will attain, and they will be able to ascend to the All. It is the Light hidden there, and the light that God wrote from it is **the Gold-Stain** <note>Hebrew: *Ha-Ketem*; referring to a high level of spiritual purity or a grade of gold</note>.

<column-break/>

And even if they will be as souls in their existence—Heaven forbid [that they are only souls]—it is from their delight in these matters greatly. As in Midrash Rabbah (Parsha 4): "And they beheld God"—this teaches that they nourished their eyes from the Divine Presence; they beheld God as a man looks at his fellow while eating and drinking. Rabbi Yochanan said: They went and reached the light of the face of the Living King. 

As children of the World to Come, that Light will hover over them, and thus they will always be without interruption. For this reason, existence will be constant without cease, because the soul, in its tranquility, bestows upon the body return and straightness, and sustains it through its own existence. We have already explained "names," and this is an absolute truth accepted by the people of truth and the Pardes <note>Those who study the mystical "orchard" of Torah</note>. All of this adds vitality to the general body. 

And many times this is not hidden, and he returned for his sake in everything, and you shall see... and then it will be known who is obligated in the future, and from this, they will not be shocked or shaken by the days of judgment, saying "The songs of the upright are righteous." And concerning this: "Because you have not abandoned my kindness which I hoped for from you." 

And when he comes back, he explains the matter equally and constantly regarding that time. And there is a staff and a support... and also the people explained "The scepter shall not depart from Judah." And so in everything... and then it will be known regarding the days of judgment. And all that Moses brings and goes... and then it will be known. 

And as for what the Sages of blessed memory said: "The World to Come has no eating or drinking, but souls sit with their crowns on their heads..." This follows the opinion that there are two "Worlds to Come": one for a person immediately after death in "this world," and the "World to Come" after the Resurrection. The latter is entirely after death, and the righteous are in a world of proximity according to his view. 

As he proved from the statement of Rav: "The World to Come has no eating or drinking," he interpreted that since there is no eating, there is no body or corpse. But we have already explained this statement according to the author's view, which is the opposite of his view. Everything established in the statements "the righteous sit," etc., does not indicate that the World to Come is a world of spirits without bodies, etc., as those who prove a world of souls without bodies argue. They do not mention "the righteous" regarding the *soul* of the righteous, but rather the *souls* of the righteous. 

And in the writings regarding the World to Come after the Resurrection, where there is a body and a corpse, they mention "the righteous." They said that Rav said in the name of his teacher Rabbi Eliezer: "The souls of the righteous are hidden under the Throne of Glory," as it is said: "And the soul of my lord shall be bound in the bundle of life," etc. And in the chapter "One does not expound" (Chagigah): "The heavens contain Righteousness, Justice," etc., "and the souls of the righteous and the spirits and breaths that are destined to be created." 

And in the Sifrei: "God of the spirits of all flesh"—this refers only to the spirits of the many. And concerning his flesh, Rabbi Yose the Galilean said: "Let this sign be in your hand—as long as there is water in the pipe, the structure stands." [God] in whose hand is the soul of every living thing, and "into Your hand I commit my spirit." And the scripture says concerning the soul: "And the soul of my lord shall be bound," etc. 

Listen, my son: for the righteous, between the wicked and her... the Holy One, Blessed be He, is not [the same]. And in the Midrash on Song of Songs: ...the souls of the righteous. Behold, all this is clear: that the matter refers to souls without bodies, which is the "World of Souls" that Maimonides (the Rav) calls the "World to Come," because it follows immediately after death in this world. 

However, the "World to Come" after the Resurrection is not like that; rather, it is used by the "Men of the Service" <note>referring to those following the kabbalistic/liturgical path</note> to mean **body and soul**. For in the World to Come after the Resurrection, they will ascend in body and soul, like Elijah of blessed memory. And what will be in the time of Moses, Saul, etc... the higher secret in which the righteous will be sustained in body and soul. And they sought and mentioned "the righteous" to testify to the existence and permanence of body and soul in the delight of those worlds without end or limit. 

They said concerning Moses the Prophet: Rabbi Malka said, Rabbi Elazar said: In the future, the Holy One, Blessed be He, will make a dance for the righteous in the Garden of Eden, and He will sit among them, and every single one will have [the light] hovering over him... to say: "On that day, it shall be said to all the righteous: Behold, this is the Lord for whom we have waited!"

<summary>This page discusses the nature of the World to Come, distinguishing between the "World of Souls" after death and the ultimate reward after the Resurrection, which involves both body and soul. It emphasizes the "Hidden Light" and a "circular dance" led by God as symbols of eternal, infinite pleasure for the righteous.</summary>

<meta>This page transitions from the conclusion of the "Part of Service"—which discussed the spiritual reward and the eternal nature of the soul—into the "Part of the Purpose." It begins a deep philosophical and Kabbalistic inquiry into whether humanity is the center of the universe or if the universe has an independent divine purpose, specifically engaging with and critiquing the views of Maimonides.</meta>

<header>Chapter 1 | The Part of the Purpose | Chapter 1</header>

for our benefits and our pleasures, and [to think so is] a corrupt and foolish imagination, like the stories of liars. The essence of this evil thought regarding his bed <note>likely a reference to physical procreation or base desires</note> and his portion: "If not for my covenant, I would not have created day and night" <note>original: *lo bera'ati yomam va-laylah*; Jeremiah 33:25</note> etc. And he strengthened it as a symbol for dwelling. And if the celestial spheres existed for the sake of man, then all species of animals and plants would also be the primary intent. Just as the angels are necessary from the start, [the text] clarifies the error within this view. For it is said that according to the logic of the intellect that directs this "Purpose"—meaning the existence of the human species—there is no necessity that could sustain it from its completion. If its resting place were entirely for him, it would not be possible for anything to exist except for man. And if one says that the matter is prohibited and difficult, can one bring man into existence from his completion as a parable? One must ask: what is the benefit in all these things if their law is the "Purpose" for everything, without the Master <note>Hebrew: *Akisar*; likely a corruption of a title for the Creator</note> directing from His completion? And even if everything were for the sake of man, and the purpose of man is, as it is said, "to serve the Name" <note>to serve God</note>, the initial question remains: what is the purpose of his transient existence? For his service adds nothing to the Creator, and all that He created and achieved is for a "Minor Purpose." And if we knew the lack, nothing else would exist at all.

And if one says: this is not for our tranquility but for our perfection, for that is the "Good" for us, and it was for our perfection, then the question remains in its place. If the purpose of our existence is this life of perfection, it is impossible for the "Director" to avoid the conclusion that the matter depends on the investigation of the Purpose. Rather, thus did He decree; thus His wisdom decreed. And this is the Truth. And so you find the Sages of Israel in their interpretations within our boundaries saying: "You are the ultimate merit from the womb, and recognize Him to stand before You, for who can say to You, what shall You do?" And if He is exact, what will He give to you? Behold, out of nothingness He chose one purpose: a Will for all according to His power. 

And the truth is that it is impossible for man to exist without the Heavens, for he is a soul and requires a place, and the place requires service. It is impossible to exist without a servant, for this world is the "World of Action" and requires service according to the view of "to guard it and to keep it" <note>referring to Adam in the Garden of Eden</note>, and to repair the one who needs repair, which is the pattern of this world, as will be explained. Therefore, he must exist. And if there was a holiness in his folly and his service, there is a direct need, and his perfection completes the one who needs his perfection. He should strive to draw near to the "Necessity of Being," for the angel, in seeking the Purpose, is compelled by his own nature. And the Purpose ends in great significance if thus His wisdom decreed. It is known that the purpose of all existence, both the upper and lower worlds, is the "True Man" <note>Hebrew: *Adam Ha-Amiti*; a Kabbalistic term for the spiritual archetype of humanity</note>. These [worlds] were made and included for the sake of the body, and that is the True Purpose, as will be explained later. And what was killed of them was found for his help, and this is the support of the gathering of the Sages of Israel and the words of prophecy. It will be clarified in a true way according to our study of the law of the "Wars of the Lord" <note>likely referencing Gersonides' work *Milchamot Hashem*, or a general theological struggle</note> with His people, on the peace of his mind. This is a story of the surplus of help and the horse, all of which should be a small part of the Likeness—which is the "Essential Man," a supreme example, built and perfected in the likeness of the "Supernal Chariot" <note>term: *Merkavah*; the divine throne-chariot from Ezekiel’s vision</note>. This is the greatness of the sages of the heavens. 

This noble and holy knowledge is the grasp of truth for the Rabbi, of blessed memory <note>referring to Maimonides (Rambam)</note>. You will find the natural knowledge—knowledge that is for the commoners—and after it the "Premises." For after he arose and we believed that the world was necessitated through the way of "chain-like descent" <term>Hishtalshelut; the Kabbalistic process by which the infinite Divine Light descends to form the physical world</term> and the necessity of power, it leads some to believe that everyone who is closer and closer to the First Cause will be higher in degree and more general than those who are not as close. This leads to the conclusion that Man, who is at the end of the levels and the lowest of all, would be the most inferior and of the least degree of all existing things that preceded him. They go so far as to say that his soul has no value or relation to the celestial sphere at all. From this, they reject the idea that Man could be the ultimate Purpose of the higher beings, for he is inferior in degree and honor in their eyes. This shaky premise and corrupt knowledge has its source in the "Evil Nature of Knowledge" <note>referring to Aristotelian or secular philosophy that lacks mystical insight</note> which has darkened [the truth]. From there, the deniers thought to uproot the foundations of religion and truth. Their delay follows the Rabbi, of blessed memory <note>Maimonides</note>, and his words are wrapped around our people, surrounding their judgment. Most bitter and evil is that he met the Angel only to dwell in heresy with the "Ugly Kushite Maidservant" <note>A harsh metaphor used by Kabbalists to describe Maimonides' embrace of Aristotelian philosophy over mystical tradition</note>. And so they did, for they sought for themselves laws from their own imagination and declared them, ceasing to act like [proper] creatures, and they fell upon the Rabbi, of blessed memory.

<column-break/>

This necessitates that the Will of the Blessed One should be the purpose of the commandments, and that the "Face of Man" should be perfected in the world that comes from the True Light. And if there were angels and earth, it would be searched like an ox. Then the light of the moon would be like the light of the sun, and the light of the sun would be sevenfold, like the light of the seven supernal days. Two kings would bow down in the "Crown of Kindness" <note>referring to the Sefirot of Keter and Chesed</note>, which is the Perfect Unity. The "Vision of the Face of the Earth" will be such that "the breach is healed" and there is no lack in their hearts. Would that the glory of the Lord be forever! Would that the Lord rejoice in His works, they being established before Him as was the intention from the beginning of creation, and as we have written above. "He looks at the earth and it trembles" <note>Psalm 104:32</note>—perhaps this is a hint to the generation of the sword. "I will sing to the Lord as long as I live" etc., for the purpose of the present, enduring waters is so that the service and the calling shall be without pause or relief. And at that time, the establishment of the sages of the wisdom of the Children of Israel [will occur]. For in the time of establishment, much wisdom that was silent will spread from there to be heard by all the nations and islands. And he said: thus the lack of action will be given to the thirds of the earth, for the "Satanic Inclination" will be uprooted from the world. Those wicked ones will be no more. The Great Name will be supported in His glory, as it is written: "And the Lord shall be King over all the earth; on that day the Lord shall be One and His Name One" <note>Zechariah 14:9</note>. 

He concluded his intention in this chapter, and so he completed this part from these two... which until now were valued. This is his value and his standing, for the glory of His name and His presence to shine in the light of His countenance with His beloved ones and those who know Him, walking and returning and standing before Him. Amen.

# The Third Part Called the Part of the Purpose

### Chapter One

The Actor/Creator created according to the perfection of His purpose. The existence of the upper and lower worlds is the action of the Name [God], who is the most perfect Actor. It is necessary that it be for the most perfect Purpose and for the most complete of purposes. This is the time proper for the word: to seek and find a purpose for the action of the Lord and these eternal works of His hands in their entirety. If we succeed in this quest according to the details of the True Wisdom <note>meaning Kabbalah</note> in explanation, and we know this matter correctly from its foundation in the "Holy Service," [we will see] how great it is to complete the Purpose for which we were created.

I say that the Rabbi of blessed memory <note>Maimonides</note> wrote in the third part of the book *The Guide for the Perplexed*... <note>original: *Moreh Nevukhim*</note> that he did not find... meaning he wrote regarding the quest for the "Ultimate Purpose" of all existing beings. He said in his name: "Whoever thinks that the purpose of this existence was the human species alone—this view was not, in his opinion, according to the craft of the world in its entirety." Since He placed... and so they find the purpose of existence in its entirety, and in the emergence of the human species alone to serve the Name. And all that was made was not for his sake, to the point that above, the stars do not serve...

# Chapter 44 | Part of the Service | 44

The Will <note>Hebrew: *Ratzon*; refers to the highest level of divine desire or the sefirah of Keter</note>, the choice of the chosen, was such that the Good is accustomed to connect and spread. For within the internal Realm of Sovereignty <note>the sefirah of Malkhut</note>, they see from afar; and this is his perception of the first, supreme Light. Regarding this, they hinted by saying—as written in Chapter 10 of the *Sefer Yetzirah* <note>Book of Formation</note> and in the chapter *The One Who Sells the Boat* <note>a section of the Talmud, Bava Batra 75a</note>—that the Holy One, Blessed be He, made ten canopies for the first man <note>Adam</note> in the Garden of Eden. Every matter of the Garden that was in the House is even more so called and proven. And further: because within the lower crown <note>the lower sefirah</note>, he would delight and glory in the upper crown; and that is the end of the repetition. And behold, the space of the Will in the body and in the soul would perceive that great joy. Also, in this world and the resurrection of the dead, they will achieve that acquisition and merit to delight in the first, good Light, hidden for the righteous in body and soul. From the gateway of what I desired regarding the matter of the World to Come, I have sealed [this section]. May they be comforted in the way of truth and merit to benefit from the power of His awe and His persuaders, to return to the Light of Life, the life of the World to Come. Amen.

### Chapter 44

->Joy continues upon the pleasantness of fulfilling the divine Will<-
->of the Deity, and fulfilling the intention through the performance of His commandments.<-

And the Good shall be raised over the face of Yah <note>a divine name</note>, and in this way, as the heavens were formed, so did impurity and sadness settle upon the heart. For in the exile of the impure and the distancing of the Divine Presence (*Shekhinah*), etc., the consequence of praise is like a void, and it is delayed from reaching the heart. For from the beginning, the intention in these acts of service was that it should return so that it would be awakened in His will; for regarding the work of His hands, it is to be improved. This is the secret of the Will and the Desire in the existence of the chosen ones, because of their likeness, as was explained above. This is the secret of "A wise son gladdens a father" <note>Proverbs 15:20</note> because he walks in an upright path and takes the kindness of Isaac. Wisdom and the secret of the Holy One, Blessed be He: since he was ruling under the Great Name in His glory, and the impurity departed, it was directed upward. "The Lord shall rejoice in His works" <note>Psalm 104:31</note>, and behold, the joy is in all His glory, may He be blessed, and it adds revelation to the [divine] wrath. This is the secret of "the heart shall rejoice," "from you and through you," this refers to the Holy One, Blessed be He; and "to you" refers to the Assembly of Israel <note>Knesset Yisrael</note>. There, the constellation of the mouth and the throat, and the power of the Great Intellect, is sealed at the end of the verse. In Your mercies may You be remembered, for in the service, the Will of the God of the heavens is there in the "oil and incense that gladden the heart" <note>Proverbs 27:9</note>. The King, peace be upon him, did not dream it; rather, "I rejoiced in it with this joy," which is the joy of the Kingdom of Heaven. All the intent at the start was the supreme intention in their hearts in unity. -># Chapter 58 | Part of the Purpose | Chapter 2<-

It was written in the heart to know the Lord, by Judah the son of Eleazar, for by this the worlds are completed. One should not say that the Holy One, Blessed be He, created anything lacking, Heaven forbid, or say that the parts of the universe are without a Knower. Peace be upon the end of all things, for everything returns to His hand. The world is a complete whole, though it changes through every power <note>original: *koach*; refers to divine or natural forces</note>. As a metaphor, one might say the "generations of the heavens and the earth" <note>a reference to Genesis 2:4</note> are like a single work of art that proclaims His wisdom. Heaven and earth were both created through the "Upper Crown" <note>term: *Keter Elyon*; the highest of the ten sefirot or divine emanations</note> which is the end and the measure of the Will. 

One must not say, Heaven forbid, that He regrets the creation of this world. Rather, it was created with "K-I-Z" <note>likely a numerical code or abbreviation for a specific divine name or timing</note>. To settle the matter of heaven and earth, all were created by the Upper Crown, which is the end and the measure of His Will. Rabbi Shimon bar Yochai <note>term: *Rashbi*; the 2nd-century sage to whom the Zohar is attributed</note> commented on the verse "And it was evening and it was morning" <note>Genesis 1:5</note> that the world itself was forged in a "show of war" <note>a metaphorical struggle of creation</note> with the intention of being called "World" <note>Hebrew: *Olam*, which also shares a root with "hiddenness"</note>. 

From this cause, the reason is revealed and known to those who remember Him, to receive the totality of existence. One must further know that the "Upper Perfections" were the final world, filled with the revelation of Unity. The sages stood at this fullness, for there is no perfection and no Unity except through Him. So too, there is no perfection of the world except through the perfection of the Essence. Since the world requires service <note>term: *Avodah*; refers here to ritual and spiritual labor</note> to the Unique One, it rises to the "World of Discernment" <note>original: *Olam ha-Nivanim*</note> through the intentions of service. Service cannot exist without a place, and because the lower world is the prepared place for service, its creation was necessary. 

As the Midrash of Rabbi Shimon bar Yochai says: "There is no deed <note>original: *ma'aseh*</note> without a building." When there is a deed of human effort to strive in the upper joy, it is called an "Upper Deed" for the sake of its purpose, which was the first in [Divine] Thought. This world is the "World of Action" <note>term: *Olam ha-Asiyah*; the lowest of the four worlds in Kabbalah, representing physical reality</note> and it is necessary for the perfection of the "World of Discernment," which is the end of the Upper Thought. We have already expanded on this in Chapter 2 of the first part of this book.

As the sages said regarding the end of the world: "It was only created for the merit of the Torah," as it is written: "The Lord by wisdom founded the earth" <note>Proverbs 3:19</note>. Rabbi Berechiah said: "In the merit of Moses," as it is written: "And he saw the beginning for himself" <note>Deuteronomy 33:21</note>. Rabbi Huna said in the name of Rabbi Matna: "In the merit of three things the world was created: in the merit of Hallah <note>the portion of dough given to priests</note>, in the merit of Tithes, and in the merit of First-fruits." Why does the text say "In the beginning (*Be-reshit*) God created"? Because "beginning" refers to nothing other than the tithes, as it is said "the first-fruits of your grain." "Beginning" refers to nothing other than Hallah. "Beginning" refers to nothing other than the Torah, as it is written "The Lord possessed me in the beginning of His way" <note>Proverbs 8:22</note>. 

Thus, the purpose of existence is clarified: the Torah sustains the world, and the world requires a servant to honor the "Tree" <note>the Tree of Life or the Sefirotic system</note> and to complete the end of the Upper Thought. These are the hidden matters of His glory, and they crown the name of Israel. All this is to say and to return the "End" to the "Beginning." Look at what the Lord said: "If My covenant be not with day and night, I have not appointed the ordinances of heaven and earth" <note>Jeremiah 33:25</note>. This means if not for the Torah—about which it is written "you shall meditate in it day and night"—I would not have created heaven and earth. 

This world was created for the sake of the Servant. Jacob and David knew they were "servants," and they are mentioned because they were the "Perfect Servants" who completed the end of the Upper Thought. Jacob rose to his "double dwellings" <note>a reference to Jacob’s spiritual reaching</note> when he worked for Rachel. According to Rabbi Eliezer, all the attributes spoken of regarding the "seed of Jacob" do not refer to Jacob himself, but rather to the "Land" <note>often a code for the sefirah of Malkhut</note>. He is the one who unifies the "End" with the "Beginning" through his service. This is what was said of David in his time, as we wrote in the first part of this book. Our words will be clarified further. The purpose of existence in its totality is the place where service is required, which is its goal and a high necessity. This is our intent in this section.

### Chapter 3

All that was stirred by my pen with simplicity at first, as I sought in my soul to understand the "Revealed Matters" <note>original: *Nigla'ot*; exoteric knowledge</note> and the "Hidden Matters" <note>original: *Nistarot*; esoteric or Kabbalistic knowledge</note> in relation to the "Dwellers of the Heights" <note>angels or celestial beings</note>. Everything is nurtured and refined by His Name, and in Him, the life-force spreads. For if not for the light of the Divine Presence <note>term: *Shekhinah*</note>—that sweet light—they would not be able to rise or grow.

<column-break/>

They receive from the sphere <note>term: *Galgal*; the celestial spheres in medieval cosmology believed to be intelligent beings</note> that prevails over them, and thus they are sustained. There are those who believe that all wickedness and perfection is known to them at their start. But they all reach their exhaustion and desolation regarding the final goal. This group knows that they have not risen to the level where they can provide the reward for human labor from the stars and the spheres, and they shall not rise further. 

The Sage <note>likely Maimonides</note> said: "Behold my smallness" in relation to the power found in those celestial beings, according to the decree by which the world is governed. Some things are renewed and changed, and there is a perfection in many things that will never be separated. Even if they are examined or if they are in their joy, the matter is far from our understanding. For in all their paths and their warmth and their coldness, they do not move by their own will, but are shaken by the wind, and they suffer what was created because of their rest. 

Behold, this is a simple metaphor for their Creator. Whatever is achieved by their movement is a sign of their ultimate perfection and the intention of their creation. But we, the "Philosophers" <note>used here perhaps ironically or to mean "seekers of wisdom"</note>, in our knowledge, there is no "movement" in our warmth, nor is there the Divine Will. I am far from those who exist by themselves, who are like heavy weights or precious pearls, even from the stars that endure. For the light of Truth has not shone upon them. How much more do they rise and become equal to the created things? For even according to their own view, human knowledge is far from the knowledge of the spheres. 

I have found among all the Jewish Sages of the Torah a wisdom in their knowledge. It is written there that the knowledge of the stars and the spheres is a step below the rank of angels. Human knowledge, however, is not part of this, for they are the recipients of the [divine] illumination. I did not understand the wisdom of what was written in the "Book of Splendor" <note>likely referring to a specific commentary or the Zohar</note> and in Chapter 3 of the *Foundations of the Torah* <note>by Maimonides</note>, where it says man is less than one-hundredth the value of the spheres. 

Surely, in his view, his own knowledge was less than theirs. If they had been clarified and refined, and if man were greater than them in knowledge, he would have admitted that man is superior to them. For he knows that the sphere is defined by a physical body, whereas the soul is greater. He wrote this in *The Foundations of the Torah*: there is no difference in this regard between a man, a sphere, and an angel. He wrote this so that one should see and fear and tremble before the pure Essence. This was also said of the "holy ones" and the "great ones," and regarding the "pure sources." 

The Rashban <note>likely Rabbi Shimon ben Nachman, or a variant of Ramban/Nachmanides</note>, of blessed memory, whose tongue was powerful, was zealous for the honor of man. He was amazed at those who would not place man above the angels. He said that human beings are more honorable than them. He wrote this in the portion of *Mishpatim* <note>Exodus 21-24</note>. He says: "Behold, I am sending an angel before you." He translated this regarding the stars, and then opened his mouth to say that human beings are more honorable than the Ministering Angels. He said the angels were created for the sake of human beings, and his proofs are well-aimed. He spoke only of the angels who serve at every moment in the "Chariot of Life" <note>original: *Hayot ha-Kodesh*; the high-ranking angels in Ezekiel's vision</note>. 

Furthermore, there is a proof that he was not wrong. I will set it before you. Behold, the text says: "Behold, I send an angel before you to guard you on the way." He says that if the angel were superior, the verse would not say "to guard you." And I did not know that our father Jacob, and also our master Moses and King David, ever said such things. The "Hand of our God" is with us always. Israel said: "If the Lord does not guard the city, the watchman stays awake in vain." He guards them like a shepherd guards his flock. 

When Isaac opened his eyes, he saw that even the angels are "messengers" and human beings are "servants." And it says "And a kingdom shall be removed..." and "The prince of the kingdom of Persia stood against me, but Michael, the great prince..." <note>Daniel 10:13</note>. Michael is called a "strong prince," yet Israel is more precious than him. How can they be equal in honor? For the angels must "guard" the one who is smaller in rank. And the text says "be careful before him" <note>Exodus 23:21</note>. Why? "For he will not forgive your transgression." We know that man does not have the power to forgive, yet the angel is given this role. And the Prophet says "The angel of His presence saved them." And he says to him: "What..."

-># Chapter 1 | The Section of the Purpose | Chapter 1<-

After many scriptures and the words of our sages have reached us regarding the excellence of life and so forth, for concerning the upper and lower creatures and their existence in the height of perfection, scriptures were included and stated that indicate the opposite of this. These refer to the permanence of the **Shekhinah** <note>term: *Shekhinah*; the Divine Presence perceived as dwelling within the world</note>, which points to their inner essence. In general, these indicate His existence without explanation or grace, and they are the correct path for the wise. How far is it for us to maintain them relative to one another? This is only due to a "calling of perfection" and a laziness to maintain, know, and strengthen their reasoning, turning the void of their error—which is written in the division of the "Good Portion"—into something famous. Even these, like the power of a candle’s orbit, revolve around the verse regarding "suffering evils." For such is the law of the philosophical investigators in these sixty opinions, and their blasphemies are more terrible than the opinions of fools. There is no grace in their eyes for what the Rabbi <note>original: *Ha-Rav Zal*; likely referring to Maimonides (Rambam)</note> of blessed memory revealed regarding knowledge and the secret.

For philosophical matters are critical in the Torah; yet to add to the law of its leaders is to make an error of all secrets and a seal for all who come. It shall not be so at all, Heaven forbid! For this is **holy** and that is **profane**; this is **pure** and that is **impure**; this is **light** and that is **darkness**. As our sages said: "A horse is not a weak blind thing" <note>a metaphor for the strength of traditional wisdom over external systems</note> that tastes the essence from the fall and the rescue to live. Heaven forbid we should say that there is no wisdom in Israel except for philosophy! They do not know that the wisdom of the holy letters is unique to her, for philosophy is merely the **peel** <note>term: *Klipah*; literally a "shell" or "husk" that hides the inner "fruit" of holiness</note> of the holy and strange tongue. It is beautified like a soul in a body to show the philosophical elements, as if the original were taken and nullified to show a change.

This was a strong point for the structure of the spirits in their strength, to say that the error of the exterior is complete—even more so, Heaven forbid, regarding the Tree of Knowledge from which one may not eat in Eden. Instead of a heap that compels, they explained all the known weaknesses. Since many are diligent to look into the scriptures, they are complete in the novelty and the "Composition of the Light" <note>likely a reference to a specific work or the Zohar</note> before you, like a servant. Spare all the weaknesses in writing, Heaven forbid, for if that were the intention in creation and the cause, they would be proven wandering and lacking. Leaving them abandoned leads to the nullification of some; they wither and the blood is forgotten. In this, the intellect and the secrets of the purpose of His strike fell, and the abundance was covered and nullified due to a secret relevant to all life. And so the matter goes and returns, for it shall bear bread and a complaint and the known time. This is a premise that is entirely about the secret of the "Unique Influence" separated from the generality of the line of wisdom.

For years, our path was to see His glory above the inner part and the wisdom of living in the surroundings. A perfect one is provided for those who sit before Him—may the Lord be their hiding place. Philosophy, compared to that Intellect, is like "external wisdom" <note>term: *Chokhmah Chitzonit*; secular or non-Torah disciplines</note> which is a species of the physical/material. It is a derivative that burns its holy and essential bitterness to relate in its likeness. Their power above is what connects and seeks to spread and uproot. All this is known to the wise of heart. This was completed "one against the other" <note>Ecclesiastes 7:14</note>. It is written regarding those "wise in their own eyes": they shall take a void, for it enticed them to seal it. Thus, its likeness entices and removes; it takes its master into a void because it castrates, as in the matter of the proofs and the physics of the mourners. For their whole way—as will be explained at the end of this chapter—is from the greatness of their doubt. They wrote according to their heart and did not honor the pursuit of the "Flow of Life" <note>the spiritual life-force</note>, the forgotten one, which is accepted in its time. This caused them to take omens in the creatures and to be satisfied with the "children of strangers" <note>Isaiah 2:6</note>. The corruption of their methods proves this. The Prophet was crying out against the wise men of his generation, for there is no doubt they were all riding and going toward the investigations of bitterness. They tore themselves apart and were humbled by proofs and difficulties from prophets. Instead of grace, they gave birth to heresies and the destruction of the foundations of the Torah, as is seen from the words of some authors in their perception.

They say "they are learners" and so forth, as a relief for the repair of the Sabbath... to arm oneself. From this, we would deny the Maker of the world and acknowledge the corners of the sanctuary and the voice of the beginning. It is said: "House of Jacob, come, let us walk in the light of the Lord" <note>Isaiah 2:5</note>, etc. For the voice is everything, and matter is above this. To live in the creations of this day—this is the King Messiah. Now the "Mountain of the House of the Lord" shall be beautiful in the Holy of Holies, above every mountain of lack that they placed there. It is called the "Mountain of Sages," for to the generality of our holiness, Jacob called it "House," and it is the "House of the Lord," to say that the victory of the precious light is like the mercy of the mountain, and there is no separation for it...

<column-break/>

...profane grace to the creatures. He was exalted in His name and His mercies, and all of them are virtues. Wisdom flows to them; the **Kingdom** <note>term: *Malkhut*; the tenth sefira, representing the manifestation of divine rule</note> is a daughter who comes in the "unification of grace." And it says: "and He shall judge many peoples" <note>Micah 4:3</note>. And they said: "Come, let us go up," etc., for the nations did not receive the Torah and did not toil in the glory of the Lord. Yet in the end, they will merit to receive the light and to know Him. "House of Jacob," etc., meaning they are to be praised for the weaknesses they had initially. A light was taken for them, and in the end, they went. The general rule is that they were wrapped in a place and they tell of it... they will recognize the light and return to the path of righteousness for all the House of Jacob. For at first, your standing was upon the "Peel," but it reached the level of glory and its closeness. Tomorrow you shall be covered by its glory, and your eyes will be in His Torah and His commandments. You shall say to one another: "Come, let us walk in the light of the Lord," specifically in His Torah and His **inner wisdom**. For this, the general connecting vessel and its openings were prepared. It is to make known that "at this time," etc., meaning the House of Jacob takes its virtue with you. They are called "with grace"; take the naming of the names. Your hands have been empty of it since the day of grace you received at Sinai, and also when hearing and receiving the investigations of the wisdom of the Greeks and their external opinions. For they were "divided from of old," meaning every perfection of knowing the whole comes from the "Wisdom of the East" <note>original: *Kiddum*; can mean ancient or Eastern</note>, which is the external wisdom—the peel of the holy and alien tongue. It is called "East" (*Kedem*) because it preceded all living things, and the **peel precedes the fruit**. The foundation is known to the lack, and its name is its sickness. All kinds of falsehood and dwellings of their division shall be destroyed.

"And they are satisfied with the children of strangers"—these are the helpers and the shepherds who were born from their proofs and their false syllogisms, along with all their distant paths. For it is difficult in the matter of their dwelling, for there is no vision and no evil. For the cry is in its essence, and that evil shall not spread to become and to turn the essence of life. Distant things shall be drawn and prevented from surrounding the details of the image and the essence, as is known from the proofs of "that certain Greek" <note>likely referring to Aristotle</note> and his intellectual syllogisms. It was in his mind that in their spread and their division, his intention was nothing other than the mechanical investigation that does not know God. They chose and were exalted, and he was covered from every memory of the "living existence" from the wisdom according to its spread. It became known as "living" through the philosophers of my people, for in it is the "unification of our God" in His proof and His generality. They received from him that this is the essential knowledge in the "Unique One," based on what the scripture of blessed memory said: that "existence is for honor and not for life." But the unification received from the mouths of the holy ones, according to which they knew that He is not an image and has no end—for once it is clarified at the end of this chapter, the matter will be as follows: they have neither knowledge nor understanding in the Unification. This caused what was sought, for the "children of strangers" are like flesh. Until Jeremiah the Prophet (peace be upon him) in his book said: "In the time of greatness, small and great shall recognize and know the Lord" <note>Jeremiah 31:33</note>. This is the "Great Plain Meaning" and His unification. And this is what he said: "And they shall no longer teach every man his neighbor and every man his brother, saying, 'Know the Lord,' for they shall all know Me, from the least of them unto the greatest of them" <note>Jeremiah 31:33</note>.

### Chapter 2

This world corresponds to the "fourfold living creature" <note>term: *Chayah*; the celestial being from Ezekiel's vision of the Chariot</note> which is also called a "world." In it is the **Lower World** according to its kind, that world and its preparation. Thus they said in the Midrash of **Rashbi** <note>The Zohar</note> on the verse "Look at the world": Its beginning is in its likeness; the "World to Come" is intellectual and not in the likeness of man. The **Upper World** is a distant place, divided by its stars. The **Lower World** is of its kind; it is the usage and the receiving in its portion, etc.

Behold, he did not include that which is called "World" as all the signs. According to the language that receives "This World," it is an **Upper World**, and within it, in ancient times, was a **Lower World**. Just as this lower world is the end of existence and the permanence of the matter, and it is the end of the divisions—for the "Small World" <note>term: *Olam Katan*; the Microcosm/Man</note> is the end and the conclusion of all creatures and the last of them—and just as the last world is strengthened by matter and contains something of the Upper World, so this second world was drawn and spread by means of the last world. It spread throughout the whole, and from it, and in the wisdom of the "Small Chapter" and the whole...
