<note>original: "המלאך" (The Angel)</note>

A guardian who waits for <unclear>the end</unclear> <note>original: "לת'"; likely an abbreviation for "to the end" or "to the Torah"</note>, for the King establishes this as a law of service for everyone over him; if he does not keep watch, he is liable. This is for his merit, and he can be exempt, yet he requires a guardian from without. In the King's nature, as it is written, he requires protection <note>original: "היק' ולין"; possibly "the palace and the night"</note>. The guardian is only capable of the protection entrusted to him by the King for everyone, and he requires external things and has power over them. This is the meaning of: "The King smote the children of the world, reign over your children to guide them in the way..." and so on. This is to say, it is as if his authority is in his own hand, like his own property, ruling over other matters once he has guarded his own children. For sometimes this is not in his power, depending on the authority of the kingdom over him. Eventually, it returns to him, for he is in his own place. Behold, these are moved by the Heavens, and here he transgresses the established law, for it is not in his power except according to the law that was missing from his protection. In that case, the one being guarded is greater than the guardian, just as the King is of greater status than his guard <note>The text explores a paradox: usually, a protector (like a shepherd) is superior to the protected, but a King is superior to his bodyguards</note>. However, this does not apply to the "Power of Israel" <note>A name for God</note> who conducts the world.

The conduct of the Angels <term>Melakhim; divine messengers or spiritual forces</term>, who are forbidden from that name <note>The name of the unique Guardian</note>, is because they are included in all that and are strengthened. No power or angel exists except that which has power over its specific place. But this is the Great Power that belongs to everyone, and in Him is one cause that directs everything, because there is no intermediary between them. As it is said: "And I bore you on eagles' wings and brought you to Me" <note>Exodus 19:4</note>. The intention is to say that they are higher than the messengers of the work; they are in My presence, and the will of the Omnipresent is without an intermediary. This is what He meant by "And I brought you to Me," to show the answer to his intent—that it was not through receiving holiness from what they saw in the conducting messengers. The generalities of the conduct of the world depend on the power of the Sabbath <note>original: "בשבת"</note>, and this is why He said, "You have seen what I did to the Egyptians." Behold, this is the joy and the protection that cannot be measured by an intermediary. This is called the Name of the Omnipresent, who conducts with this "Guardian of Israel" <note>original: "שומר ישראל"</note> and the King of the Sabbath. This high degree is called "Shepherd" and "Guard," and nowhere is an angel called "Guardian" or "Shepherd" or "Guard." This Name belongs specifically to the Name of the Support itself. However, it says, "For He shall give His angels charge over thee, to keep thee in all thy ways" <note>Psalms 91:11</note>, which indicates the reception of the recipient between one type of protection and another, within the distinction between the Creator and the creature. Even if the name "Guardian" were applied to an angel, Heaven forbid that we should say the guarded is greater than the guardian <note>Addressing the philosophical problem of hierarchy</note>, for everyone knows an angel is a creature. Rather, this is because a specific person's charge is a "watch" <note>original: "משמר"</note>—this was created for the sake of that.

As for what further appears—that an angel is called the "Prince of Israel" and yet Israel is more honored than him—our Sages of blessed memory already explained that he is not called so except because he is appointed to plead for their needs and their honor <note>Referring to the Archangel Michael as the celestial advocate</note>. And from where do we know he pleads for them? It is written in the Midrash on Exodus <note>original: "שמות רבה"</note>: "The Prince of Israel." The Holy One said, "This one will benefit himself in everything." And at that time, Michael, the great prince who stands for the children of your people, would plead for the needs of Israel and speak in their defense: "Shall the Lord benefit? And the Lord of Hosts shall say, until when will You not have mercy on Jerusalem?" And it says, "And there is none that holdeth with me in these things, but Michael your prince" <note>Daniel 10:21</note>. Furthermore, we have already said that these things are only said during the time when Israel are righteous and doing the will of the Omnipresent. But when they are not doing the will of the Omnipresent, they are subservient to the idolatry of the nations, which are under the rule of the Princes who are their lords and their gods. During the time when Israel was doing the will of the Omnipresent, they were connected to the Name, so they did not come under the rule of a prince <note>original: "שר"</note>. Then he would return to plead for them, and even Michael their prince. This is what made Israel honored—the Name was with them to save and to help, as it says, "And behold, Michael, one of the chief princes, came to help me" <note>Daniel 10:13</note>. In the Midrash on Exodus, it says: "Not to any messenger, but rather 'the King of your children.'" The Holy One said to Israel: "If you had merited it, I Myself would have acted for you, as I did for you in the wilderness, where 'The Lord went before you...'" <note>Exodus 13:21</note>. But now that you have lost your merit, I am handing you over to a messenger, as it says, "Behold, I send an angel" <note>Exodus 23:20</note>. This is similar to the rest of the Princes at the time they committed idolatry, until the power of the merit caused them to see the world turned upside down—those below were above and those above were below. The opinion of Rashi <note>Rabbi Shlomo Itzhaki, 11th-century commentator</note> is that this angel is Michael.

A guardian, for if he were our lord, no deeds would prove it, and he would not be ashamed <note>original: "כי חלונו... לח היה כיסס"</note>. ### Section on the Purpose — Chapter 4

Because he was the messenger of the Name <note>original: "שלוח השם"; referring to God</note>, and from the perspective of his mission, he is greater, yet not from his own essence. Therefore, the defense is that one bows to the Godliness mixed within them and calls them "Lord," not for their own sake.

### Chapter 6: The Section on the Purpose — Chapter 6

It is known that all the stars of heaven are the retinue of the Kingdom <note>The Hebrew term *Malchut* refers to the lowest of the ten Divine emanations, often associated with the physical world and the presence of God in it.</note>; for if His glory is not on earth, His glory is not in the awesome heavens. This hints that the heavens were created for the sake of the earth, as it is written: "to serve the earth." In the *Midrash Rabbah* on the Book of Exodus, it says: "Whatever is below is from above," for the lower reflects the higher. This is what we explained regarding this matter in Chapter 1, hinting at David's words in the Psalm: "O Lord, our Master, how majestic is Your name in all the earth" (Psalm 8:1). 

It is said that the connectivity of the parts of existence and the intention of its creation is the unification of the Great Name <term>The "Great Name" (Shem HaGadol) refers to the tetragrammaton, the essential name of God, which represents the source of all existence.</term> through His glory. This is why it says, "O Lord, our Master," using two names: the Tetragrammaton and the name of Mastery <note>original: "יי' ואדנות"; referring to the names YHVH and Adonai</note>, for everything is His desire and everything was created for Him. This is the ultimate purpose of service: to draw down the light and the "Good Time" <note>likely referring to divine grace or favor</note> upon man. This is the praise of the sun and the power of the foundation of the earth, which is full, and the end of the matter is that we should be built in the image of the Great Name, according to the secret of His hand, to rectify the upper crown, as we wrote in the first part.

This is the meaning of "How majestic is Your name," meaning the human soul is made in the pattern of the letter *Samekh* <note>The letter Samekh (ס) is circular, symbolizing wholeness or divine protection.</note>. How great is it that through man's actions and service, the hand of the one who walks becomes the conduit for the flow and the light that comes from the Supernal Source to the heavens, which is the Great Name. Thus His glory is established, and His name becomes known in the land—that is, in the lower realms—which was not originally the case.

In the Midrash of Rabbi Shimon bar Yochai <note>Rashbi: The traditional author of the Zohar, the foundational work of Jewish mysticism.</note>, it is said concerning the phrase "You who have set Your glory above the heavens": this refers to the kindness <note>original: "חסד" (Chesed)</note> that You placed upon the heavens. It implies that the human soul, through its deeds, brings the Divine Presence to dwell among the lower beings. The essence of the soul is like a flame, and though it is in a body of nothingness, it has the power to ascend and connect to the source in the desert <note>A reference to the Israelites receiving the Torah in the wilderness.</note>. All worlds are sustained by His name. 

Therefore, "How majestic" refers to the strength that cannot be overturned by any violent power, to pass it or move it. Thus it is said in the Midrash: "How can a human, through his thoughts, open the Supernal Source and draw down the light and flow?" Regarding Jeremiah, they said "His support is in all the land," meaning his power was in the lower realms. To give strength and power to the Great Name through service—this is what is meant when they say that when Israel does the will of the Place <note>original: "המקום" (HaMakom); a common rabbinic name for God, implying He is the "place" of the world.</note>, they add strength to the Supernal Power. This is the secret of "You who have set Your glory above the heavens," as we explained above.

"Out of the mouths of babes and sucklings You have established strength" (Psalm 8:3). This is interpreted as referring to the children in the house of study <term>Tinokot shel Beit Rabban: Young children learning Torah, whose innocence is considered spiritually powerful.</term>. As it says in the chapter "All the Writings" <note>A chapter in the Talmudic tractate Shabbat</note>, Rav Hamnuna said: "Jerusalem was destroyed only because they neglected the children in the schoolhouse." For it says, "Pour out [Your wrath] on the children in the street." Why? Because they were "outside"—meaning they were missing from the schoolhouse. It is also said there: "The world is only sustained by the breath of the children in the schoolhouse." 

In the Midrash of Rabbi Shimon bar Yochai, it says: "Go and see your young goats," these are the children of the schoolhouse, for the world is sustained by them, and they provide strength to the community in exile. This is the secret of "You have established strength" to counter the "adversary and the avenger." In the Midrash, "Your adversaries" refers to the four kingdoms <note>Traditionally: Babylonia, Persia/Media, Greece, and Rome.</note>. This also hints at the supernal powers and the children who crush them. It says that even if a person is not perfect in the higher wisdoms, if they focus their service and direct their heart to the Supernal Light, it is enough to give strength and praise in the exile. Even if one's prayer is broken, if the intention is there, the flow from the Source is not withheld. After this, he speaks as one who holds a high level, saying: "When I behold Your heavens, the work of Your fingers..." (Psalm 8:4). Why does he say this? Because in his heart, he feels as small as a monkey compared to the angels, yet his soul is great.

<column-break/>

And he dreams that he is at the inner edge... compared to the *Malchut* (Kingdom). This is the truth that has been investigated since the world began regarding the perfection we mentioned in this chapter and the chapters preceding it. But when we reached the perfection that is the essence of the matter, it was found that the soul is ever-ascending, to the point that it was said there is only a "small amount" between the soul and God. This is the meaning of "You have made him a little lower than the angels" (Psalm 8:6). 

From here we find an answer to what the author of *The Guide for the Perplexed* <note>Maimonides (Rambam), the famous 12th-century philosopher.</note> wrote in Part I. Do not err or be misled by the celestial spheres and the angels. In his view, he distanced us from them, saying "Behold, the nations are like a drop from a bucket," and he compared the spheres and the stars to separate intellects. But the truth is as we have said. We have stated that man is greater in status than all of these, even though the *Guide* describes man's perfection as being lower. 

The core of the matter is explained in the Midrash regarding the Ministering Angels <term>Malakhei HaSharet: The angels who serve God in the heavenly court.</term>. When the Holy One, Blessed be He, intended to create man, the angels said: "Master of the Universe, what is man that You should remember him?" (Psalm 8:5). He replied to them: "Let the one who possesses the wisdom come and speak." They said: "Master of the Universe, the Torah, which has been hidden for 974 generations <note>A midrashic tradition that the Torah existed for 974 generations before the world was created.</note> before the world was created, You seek to give to a human of flesh and blood?" 

Moses then came to receive the Torah. The angels said: "What is a human born of a woman doing among us?" He said to them: "I have come to receive the Torah." They said: "The Torah is a hidden treasure... You want to give it to Israel? What is man that You remember him, and the son of man that You take note of him? Rather, 'set Your glory [the Torah] above the heavens!'" 

The Holy One, Blessed be He, said to Moses: "Give them an answer." 
Moses said: "Master of the Universe, in the Torah You are giving me, what is written in it? 'I am the Lord your God who brought you out of the land of Egypt.' Did you [angels] descend to Egypt? Were you enslaved to Pharaoh? Why then should the Torah be yours?" 
"Again, what is written in it? 'You shall have no other gods.' Do you live among the gentiles who worship idols?" 
"What else is written? 'Remember the Sabbath day.' Do you perform labor that you need rest?" 
"What else? 'Honor your father and your mother.' Do you have a father or a mother?" 
"What else? 'Do not murder,' 'Do not commit adultery,' 'Do not steal.' Is there jealousy among you? Is there an Evil Inclination <term>Yetzer Hara: The human drive toward selfish or physical desires.</term> among you?" 

Immediately, the angels conceded to the Holy One, Blessed be He, and said: "O Lord, our Master, how majestic is Your name in all the earth," and they no longer said "Set Your glory above the heavens." At that moment, the level was established that no prophet could reach, and no human could attain except for Moses. This is the focus of the world: man ascending toward God. Through the intention of Divine service, which is the highest of levels, it is said of him: "And he was there with the Lord" (Exodus 34:28) and "But as for you, stand here by Me" (Deuteronomy 5:28).

This is why they said that the Ministering Angels opened with praise and said: "What is the perfection of the one born of a woman?" until they saw his soul among the holy souls. This is why it says "between us," for certainly he would ascend higher than them, and he would be able to take the Torah and bring it down and ascend with the upper beings. The Holy One, Blessed be He, said to them: "Because we have been dealing with the secret and the hidden, the names that are the foundation, they [the souls] will judge with you." But when we deal with the whole Torah that speaks of man, that is "Your glory" which we wrote about, and this is why he came to receive the Torah.

They came with two strong arguments to prevent the Torah from being given to flesh and blood. One was the eternal nature of the soul, which belongs to the spiritual realm; it seemed to them that it was sufficient for the soul to remain in its natural intellectual state, without needing the physical reception of the Torah. The second was that even if the Torah exists for the benefit of the created world, the soul—being a spiritual entity—does not need these physical commandments. They argued that the Torah should remain "simple" <note>In philosophy, "simple" (pashut) means non-composite, purely spiritual, or unmanifested in physical form.</note> before God. Since the angels are "simple" (non-physical), they felt the Torah was more suited to them. I have written about this in several places... as we wrote in Chapter 2, Section 7.

->### Chapter 5: The Section on the Purpose — Chapter 8<-

For it was already explained at the end of the introduction of this book that the assigned portion and the branches correspond to the "upper wings," as was also explained at the beginning of Chapters 17 and 18 of the first part of this book. This concerns what was mentioned there regarding the conditions and the rectification of the services intended for the High One. It also includes all the decrees, forms, and measures as explained there. Furthermore, it discusses the consensus regarding the apparent contradictions in other discourses concerning the rectification and the importance of all the limbs in the secret of the "Balance" <term>Tiqun (Rectification) and Teqel (Balance) are central concepts in the Zohar, referring to the harmonious arrangement of Divine energies.</term>, and in relation to the soul in every tablet in its creation and its fall. Likewise, all the languages and movements written in the entire Work of Creation <term>Ma'aseh Bereshit: the kabbalistic study of the biblical creation story.</term>, as we wrote at the end of Chapter 20 of the second part of this book. 

Its secret is that "I shall return" <note>original: "אשיבי" (ashivi); likely a reference to a specific kabbalistic permutation</note> is within the secret of the First and the Firmament. Like the whiteness between [the letters], so is "Let there be light," "Let there be a firmament," "Let there be luminaries" <note>These are the creative utterances from Genesis 1.</note> — our understanding of the light and the light for a "living soul" <note>original: "אבינו" (avinu) appears frequently here; while it literally means "our father," in this context of linguistic analysis, it likely refers to "our root-understanding" or is a scribe's shorthand.</note> in the deep language of the Work of Creation, in the firmament, in the luminaries, and in the living creatures of the earth. Our understanding of the essence of the Name [of God]; our understanding of the language of "Creation" (*Beri'ah*) as in the Work of Creation and in the light, where "God called the light" in its revelation. Our understanding of the "Living Creatures" (*Chayot*) <note>The high-ranking angels described in Ezekiel's vision.</note> which are above all; for in all of this, the language of "Formation" (*Yetzirah*) was not mentioned. 

However, regarding the statement "And the Lord God formed (*vayiytzer*) man," and what is written "And the Lord God formed from the ground every beast of the field," they have already said in *Genesis Rabbah* (Section 17) that this was for "subduing" <note>The Hebrew root for "formed" (Y-Tz-R) is homiletically linked here to "subduing" or "shaping" a material.</note> and as a "correction" of the material. "Formed" is a language of subduing. And the reason seems to be that all the works of creation are established and proceed for the sake of these souls, which are the very covenant of creation—as if to say, "If not for My covenant day and night..." (Jeremiah 33:25). They were frightened of the sea and the foundation of the earth, as they resemble worlds and He forms their value and good deeds. His mouth is His primary light, for in His depth He is always with the children of God <note>original: "יה" (Yah); one of the names of God.</note>, acquiring Torah and clothing Himself in every Law-giver, whether He adds or innovates in the practice of the Torah and its attributes. 

The foundation of the term "Formation" (*Yetzirah*) used here is clarified by its Master in the Midrash of Rabbi Shimon bar Yochai (may peace be upon him) on the verse: "Everyone that is called by My name, and whom I have created for My glory, I have formed him, yea, I have made him" (Isaiah 43:7). This is because the Upper Glory contains within it the stages of Creation (*Beri'ah*), Formation (*Yetzirah*), and Action (*Asiyah*). However, man was created for the "Rectification of the Glory," and therefore all these linguistic terms were included in him. As explained in Chapter 17 of the first part of this book in the name of the "Alphey Alon," among all created things, who can grasp the Ultimate Purpose? Therefore, the term "Formation" did not appear in the Name for this specific person, a "Wise Rabbi," to teach him what he is... to equate him to other creatures who lack the power of free will. 

And so, perhaps they will say concerning the time of success to increase the level of the Righteous and the Chosen: for all creatures are vessels and "rectifiers" that are drawn toward him. For according to the view of Rabbi Eliezer and Rabbi Abba, we can say that the creatures are to the Righteous as the ministers are to the King. They are the ones who plan and act for the King from the class of ministers, and they were created in a "lesser" way to serve them in His kingship and His providence. It is proper to understand that the nations are far removed from the levels of the Torah. It is clear that all creatures are drawn toward the Righteous, even in the "rectification" of his food and drink, as is known regarding the levels of the Righteous and the generations in the glory of the *Sefirot* <term>The ten divine emanations/attributes through which God interacts with the world.</term> and the "Connections." 

It is written of them: "And God set them in the firmament of the heaven to give light upon the earth" (Genesis 1:17). This follows the words of the Ramban <note>Rabbi Moshe ben Nachman (Nahmanides), a 13th-century sage.</note> (of blessed memory) who wrote at the end of Chapter 23 of this book, and his language is: "And finally they said of the stars that they give light upon the void." From this we learn their purpose: so that he may benefit from it, but only to recognize the "Taste" that cleaves to it—meaning, the luminaries are like pearls. As it was said of man, "And have dominion over the fish of the sea," its meaning is not just that he was told to do so, but that the intention is for him to return to us. Furthermore, all creatures came for the sake of the Righteous, for his benefit and assistance. And what is written "to give light," etc.—all "to give light" is a claim to strengthen the argument that the intention of the world is for the Good. The world exists so that they might be in their fullness, with "taste" and "intention," for the sake of Faith—meaning, for the sake of man. So too wrote the Sages of blessed memory regarding the "Treasuries," and he added more in the book *The Kuzari* <note>A famous philosophical work by Rabbi Yehuda Halevi.</note>. This is what is meant by: "The entire world was created only to accompany this person" in his creation. For this reason, He blessed him, providing him with all 

<column-break/>

that is necessary and rectified for his existence, so that he may be always free and prepared for the Upper Life and the rectification of the Glory. This was the focus of his ultimate purpose. 

Our Sages of blessed memory already said in the *Sifrei* that the celestial beings were created to serve the earthly beings. This is literal. Rabbi Shimon ben Chaksis said: "The heel of Adam was so bright it would have obscured the orb of the sun." Do not wonder at this: in the world, a person makes a disc for his servant, and another for himself—who makes the finer one? Obviously, he makes the finer one for himself. Thus, Adam was created for the service of the Holy One, blessed be He, while the sun was created for the service of the creatures. Thus, the heel of Adam obscured the sun. 

He who has eyes will see that the Righteous are not intended for themselves. For all the nations [of creatures] were not born for their own sake; so too all creatures did not come for their own sake, for they are nothingness in themselves. Rather, all creatures are a "garment" for the Light, and man is meant to "know his Creator." As it is stated at the end of Tractate *Kiddushin*: "I was created to serve my Creator." 

The statement that the "orb of the sun is for the service of the creatures" is proof against the view of the Great Rabbi <note>Likely referring to Maimonides (Rambam), who held that celestial bodies have their own purpose and intellect.</note> who said they are intended for themselves and have their own power. [Our view is] that they are laws and *Sefirot* until they are elevated. 

Explicitly, our Sages said that the upper beings were created for the honor of the lower beings. In a certain place, the Holy One, blessed be He, said to the Host [of Heaven]: "Go and speak to the Assembly of Israel: 'I created constellations in My world, and for whose sake did I create them? For your sake, O Israel.'" 

And in *Genesis Rabbah* (Chapter 1), on the verse "Open the tent": "With 'Good' you opened for the travelers," and the conclusion is "With 'Good' you opened for the Righteous." They said: "If not for the Righteous, I would not have created heaven and earth," and "I would not have established the sun," as it says: "In them He has set a tent for the sun" (Psalm 19:5). "I would not have created the Torah," as it says: "The fear of the Lord is pure" (Psalm 19:10). Our Sages of blessed memory commented on this. There, it says that one who supports himself through the intention of the Torah, even a single Righteous person, is the "foundation of the world" <term>Tzaddik Yesod Olam: The concept that the world exists by the merit of the righteous.</term> from the class of the "Luminaries." This is the gate we intend to prove.

### Chapter 6

In the Vision and Will of the Name, [humanity's service is] more than the service of the Angel and the Firmament. For the service of the Righteous is precious in His eyes, and they are the sustainers, as explained in the second part of this book regarding the "Intention." This was explained regarding his turning toward the remainder. 

They did not say "The Holy One, blessed be He, desires the service of the angels," but rather "The Holy One, blessed be He, desires the prayer of the Righteous." It is said in the Midrash of Rabbi Shimon bar Yochai (may peace be upon him): "All who pray at night are called 'Kings,' 'Place,' and 'Matronita' <note>Matronita: A kabbalistic term for the Shekhinah, the Divine Presence.</note>." And they said: "God of gods and Lord of lords." 

It says, "Open to me, my sister, my love" (Song of Songs 5:2), and by this law, help is given through the rectification of the Righteous. There is no portion like that of the Youth <term>The "Youth" (Na'ar) often refers to the angel Metatron in kabbalistic literature.</term> who was formed at the beginning of the Torah. All of them, according to their Creator, are for His providence; all of them are for praising Him, and all of them praise before Him. The Intellect sends its parable over them. It is very urgent; He did not want a house for Himself from any of them. 

In the *Pirkei Hechalot* <term>The "Palaces" literature: early Jewish mystical texts describing the ascent to the Divine throne.</term> (Chapter 9), they sang and said to them: "Lift your eyes to the firmament, toward your house of prayer. At the hour you say 'Holy' before Me, I have no pleasure in all My world that I created except in that hour! Your eyes are as good news in My house, and My Shekhinah is with you at the hour you say 'Holy' before Me." 

And in the *Sifra*, they said: "This is the entire generation that I created, to say and to strengthen the obligation of My children." Furthermore, I found in the book *Alphon*: Rabbi Ishmael said, "The merit of Abraham and Israel before the Holy One, blessed be He, is greater than that of the Ministering Angels. For at the hour that the Ministering Angels seek to sing a song above, below they change the Name of Glory in the 'Blessed be the Name' and the 'Nissim' of the Holy One. The Holy One says to them: 'Be silent! Every King and every Living Creature, every Wheel (Ofan), and every Minister and Seraph—seek in My world until you find the praise of the songs and dwellings of Israel.' For every nation has seventy songs, but Israel sings 'Three' to the Sons of Jacob <note>Likely referring to the Trisagion or "Kadosh, Kadosh, Kadosh" (Holy, Holy, Holy) prayer.</note>. These are the songs and praises of Israel. The Ministering Angels wait until Israel finishes their songs in order to finish [their own] in the glory of the Radiance. For Israel is the foundation of His glory."

### Chapter 6 | The Section on the Purpose | 62 Chapter 7

My material nature is among the lower beings, and not only that, but they are able to withstand them. To create life for all creatures, they stood and did not perish immediately. Grace <note>The Hebrew word is *Chesed*, referring to the Divine attribute of Loving-kindness or Mercy.</note> stood and called out names for all the creatures, by the power of the verse "And the man called names..." and so on. At this point, the Ministering Angels <term>Malakhei Ha-Sharet: The angels who serve in the Divine Presence.</term> praised the Creator, saying: "If we had vessels like his eyes in the branch of the tree of Man, who takes a garment for himself, we would not be able to withstand it." And the Great Grace in Heaven desired him, and so on. How greatly did our Sages of blessed memory exaggerate in explaining this Mishnah which was taught in the Ethics of the Fathers <term>Pirkei Avot: a foundational collection of Jewish ethical teachings.</term> in Chapter 4: "Rabbi Elazar ha-Kappar says: Those who are born are destined to die..." and with the quill of a wise man regarding the creation of these creatures in the **Chapters of Rabbi Eliezer** <term>Pirkei de-Rabbi Eliezer: an 8th-century midrashic work on the Torah.</term>, concerning the high degree of Man, who preceded from his height all created beings, both upper and lower. Yet the angels were few and hindered his creation for this reason.

However, the primary intention we have written here is to explain that "Man" <note>Hebrew: *Adam*</note> is likened to the "earth" <note>Hebrew: *Adamah*</note> in the daughter of the river <note>original: "בת יארה" (bat ye'orah), likely a poetic or cryptic reference to the Nile or a source of life</note> for the first of the world, who feared for him lest he be left behind. He denied it and its punishment, and the "wormwood" <note>a symbol of bitterness or sin</note> shall dwell in Man through the sickness of Grace—this is the sickness of the "Evil Eye" that was planted, from which they eat. "You shall be like God" <note>Genesis 3:5</note>—just as He makes, creating worlds and destroying worlds, so too you are able to create worlds and destroy worlds. Just as He gives life and sustains life, so too you can give life and sustain life, as it is said: "For God knows..." and so on. Your wisdom shall spring forth in its measure, etc., as it is found there. And he ate from the tree which was tied to this purpose, etc., and to give life. For there came into his hand a number of things to destroy worlds and to revive the dead—that is, that he should take his strength for himself. And if they recognized the master of their time, for in the hand of Man is the Creator of worlds, and he shall live now, our King, and you shall increase. He took "to give life" and fled from him, and Cain and his soul, and Grace turned away after him. The secret of the persuasion and the counsel [of the serpent]—this is not the place for it, and we have not seen fit to dwell on it at length. Its secret will come in the second part of the book in the secret... and the intention of merit in this tractate shall be that Man, who remembers Grace, is a blessed Grace. And if not, his reception is like the name of the Sabbath, for they stumbled and transgressed the mind of their Creator, and he shall be lacking.

### Chapter 7

A good and logical opinion, close and more worthy to the Name [God], and already it was taken as a portion. **The Holy One, Blessed be He** <term>Ha-Kadosh Baruch Hu: the standard rabbinic title for God.</term>, for the righteous stand from Him, as his companion, as it is explained in the first chapter: He traveled to create the world like a king with the Ministering Angels before him. He said: "Let us make Man," and so on. And they said to Him: "What is his life?" meaning, to tell all of Your creatures that they stand from Him, the Holy One. "For the Lord knows the way of the righteous," etc., to make known the way of the righteous to the Ministering Angels. "And the way of the wicked shall perish"—its ruin is from there without instruction. For the righteous stand from Him, and therefore "Man" is for the name of the "Roots" <term>Shorashim: likely referring to the Sephirot or foundational spiritual principles.</term> who stand from Him. If it were not for the fact that the righteous stand from Him, the Attribute of Justice would not have written the Torah. And also the other first portions stand from Him, without them hindering us in our coming, for the righteous stand from Himself to be glorified. As our Sages of blessed memory said in the chapter regarding **Monetary Laws** <term>Dinei Mamonot: Chapter 4 of Tractate Sanhedrin in the Talmud.</term>, Rav Yehuda said in the name of Rav: "When the Holy One, Blessed be He, sought to create Man, He first created one group of **Ministering Angels**. Some said: 'Let him be created,' and some said: 'Let him not be created.'" And this Grace was done—what are his deeds? He spoke in the Name, etc. And thus they said before Him regarding his deeds: "When I hide the wise in him, you shall be created," etc. And there is no doubt that He desired the one destined to sin, as they said in every place: "And the way of the wicked shall perish"—its ruin is from there, etc. And since God Himself created him, he was destined to be killed because he was clarified as a man, as if he were punished and they began to cast him down from his high degree and push him from his glory. For He knew that he would sin because of the schemes of the "Other Side" <term>Sitra Achra: the kabbalistic term for the realm of evil or demonic forces.</term>. And they said that the heavens and his shoulder... to make known the tradition, and the illness, and the glory that they pour out as holy from the world. The Ministering Angels said before the Holy One, Blessed be He: "Master of all worlds, what is Man that You are mindful of him?" <note>Psalm 8:5</note>. Grace comes to explain why. There is none like him upon the dust. He said to them: "Why do you sanctify such-a-one in these matters? He is permitted as we have written." The Holy One, Blessed be He, had His eye upon him and said to them: "Why do you sanctify..."

<column-break/>

...touching upon this matter. The Holy One, Blessed be He, "lives." Where do we understand from that the Holy One, Blessed be He, was clarified? Therefore, [the souls] of Israel are those whose life is not the heart of our building, and a portion for men forever. And I have already written what... and furthermore it is expounded at the beginning of the name, for just as His thought was to make them great, to give them an inheritance that was their first essence, yet they would not be able to earn a reward for it—just like making oneself. And in this matter He labored, and they were not tested by the Name. Thus was His thought and His goodness to complete them with the perfections of the deficiency, and that is the honorable "Reception" <note>Kabbalah</note>. And in order to earn a reward before Him by making known His will through the giving of the Torah and the commandments, they would not be able to be forgotten and say to Him: "What have You done for us?" For by leading us, this was for us. For in this first perfection, which is prevented against your will, the final perfection is impossible to precede it. It is not all a husk <term>Kelipah: a 'shell' or 'husk' representing evil or material concealment in Kabbalah.</term>. This is so, for just as they are in perfection of language, and not what we completed in speech—for who shall say to You what You shall do and make? It would not be right. How is it possible for you? For from Your hand it was yours, for You wrote for him a way in which he might justify his soul. And he would not be able to be difficult and say it was a matter of his own intellect, and he would justify himself. And by his return to the sickness of this deficiency, your counsel was seen for you, the opposite suffering, and he shall be justified.

And furthermore, You gave an inheritance from Your remnant, a small matter, and He returned the intention and the foundation of the Angel of the Torah by giving him a way to do good for him when we are... his sin and his sin. And that is what is said: "Like You," and "You gave to us, O Lord our God, in love, the **Day of Atonement** <term>Yom Kippur.</term>," etc. And he rose to do from the abundance of the Reception <note>Kabbalah</note>, and he knew that in general, it is the purpose. And that is the Rectification of the Glory <term>Tikkun HaKavod: the restoration of Divine honor or the spiritual structures of the universe.</term> after the soul has sinned. For that is the purpose: the deficiency in the existence of these. And He began to complete the intention in His teachings. He shall not be satisfied with his service, and his heart shall be confident in his Torah and in his good deeds. And he shall know that our life to complete the intention through service is very, very great—which is not the case for one who thinks this is the purpose but does not pass to any [further] purpose. That is to say: Repentance—for with this there is no "will" [desire], but he shall atone for everything that arises, however he may live.

# Chapter 6

<margin>
It further appears that just as the Torah preceded the world, according to the words of the Rabbi <note>likely referring to Maimonides or another central authority cited in the manuscript</note>, its perfection requires the establishment of the Divine Glory. This too is a "High Necessity," as I wrote in the text of the second part, Chapter 4. According to the Rabbi's knowledge, because he operated within the foundation of the traditional wisdom of the "Radiance of God" <note>Hebrew: *Karnayih*; a mystical reference to the emanations of Divine light</note>, which anticipates the revelation of His Glory, he did not write what he wrote here. For regarding the matters of awakening and the secret of the Sovereignty and His greatness, he did not speak in such terms at all. And after seeing how much the Sages of Israel vowed in their opposition, being stringent with themselves...
</margin>

The book, as it is written: And when the end begins, it pertains to its antiquity as well. A beginning in itself is not necessitated, as per the words of the Rabbi, for its perfection requires the establishment of the Divine Glory, and this too is a **High Necessity** <term>Tzorech Gavoah: A kabbalistic concept suggesting that human actions "complete" or "satisfy" a requirement in the Divine realm, allowing God's light to manifest.</term>, as I wrote in the text of the second part, Chapter 4. According to the Rabbi's knowledge, because he was grounded in the foundation of the traditional wisdom of the Radiance of God, which anticipates the revelation of His Glory, he did not write what he wrote here. Regarding the matters of awakening and the secret of the Sovereignty and His greatness, he did not speak in terms of "captivity" at all. And after seeing how much the Sages of Israel vowed in their opposition, being stringent with their tradition, "hearts of wide measure," etc. For he saw and said to you: "What will you ascend and not be crushed? What will He give you?" Since this is so, they chose a path away from this, following the tradition of our Sages of blessed memory that it is "will" alone. Therefore, from that broad perspective, the entire foundation of the Order reversed his opinion from "surrounding" to the "division of kindness" in his portion. And the voice said: according to the logic, the voice diminished and lessened. They were very satisfied with the emptiness of his hand and foundation; they justified and acted with His strength, His might, His excellence, and His few deeds; his ascent and his hand—everything is before Him. Until, in the end, they returned to: "The preeminence of man over the beast is nothing, for all is vanity" <note>A quote from Ecclesiastes 3:19, often used in the morning liturgy to express human humility.</note>.

I said, therefore: "**You have distinguished man**," etc. <note>A reference to the *Attah Hivdalta* prayer from the Yom Kippur liturgy.</note> meaning that all we have said is not to be tested by man’s own measure, for he is devoid of value compared to the evening and death; his voice is like the silence of the perfection of the sun's heat. As it is written: "Man is in honor but understands not; he is like the beasts that perish" <note>Psalm 49:21</note>. And they returned in the chapter to say: there is no difference between him and a dog unless you distinguish him as a beast. All this was in the days of his youth, in his physical form and in the service of the Psalm.

But You <note>God</note> accepted man from the beast from the beginning of creation, and You recognized him. This was not a mere coincidence, but a **great good**, for he stands before You to minister in Your Name, to serve You, and to unify You. For the recognition of His power and His holiness belongs to You—the service and the "Psalm" for the sanctification of Your Glory. The revelation of His greatness through his service proves that the "residence" <note>The indwelling of the Divine Presence</note> is the purpose of his existence. This is the "Acquisition of Glory," which is a **High Necessity**, as we wrote.

And they said: "From the world to you, what will you stand?" Meaning, this is a general matter, for who knows the depths of the hidden thoughts of the mind to say to You: "What is this that You have done?" or "What is the reason You have prepared the upper beings in the hands of the lower beings?" As they said in the Midrash regarding Rabbi Shimon bar Yohai <note>The traditional author of the Zohar</note>, peace be upon him: "Israel themselves make the heavens holy," etc. And on this point, "You are My witnesses, says the Lord" <note>Isaiah 43:10</note>. As it were, with us the heavens are called holy. If Israel were not down below to sanctify, the heavens would not be called holy above. And concerning this, "as it were" <note>Hebrew: *Kivyachol*; a term used to avoid being overly literal about God</note>, the Holy One, Blessed be He, said: "All of Israel are sons of Kings," and when they are below, My hand is recognized over all. All this is from what I have written as a memorial; as it were, He is the "Life of the Worlds," the One above, and there is no other to be the "Good Protector." There is a secret in Israel: through the essence of His will, the place "increases strength in the Supernal Might" <note>A mystical phrase suggesting human prayer strengthens the Divine attributes</note>, as we have already written at length in the second part of this book.

And in my explanation of what is similar to it: "To You I lift up my eyes, O You who dwell in the heavens" <note>Psalm 123:1</note>. Were He not dwelling in the heavens, He would not be called "the Dweller." And so it says: "We have placed His excellence and His understanding in the heavens above the earth," etc. With all this, the lack that was upon Him—it is His, and there is no one to ask or answer Him. For there is no "reason" in the Will, except that the Purpose is known to My Creator, the Lord; and that is the **Unification of the Great Name** in His Glory, which is a **High Necessity**.

And it is not what they said: "What will he benefit? What will He give you?" which seems to be the opposite of what we said. For this has already been explained in the second part of this book. And the Rabbi, Abraham ibn Ezra <note>A 12th-century philosopher and biblical commentator</note>, wrote: "Jacob is His lot," as it is written. For this will be the explanation or the conclusion of the words regarding the good qualities of man and His will to touch the heights at all. Rather, it is in the sense of the Will of the One who removes all garments <note>reaches the essence</note> and guards the honor of the Glory. This refers to the man who humbles himself like a "mop" <note>a metaphor for extreme humility or self-nullification</note>, which is the Unification of the Great Name in His Glory. For such was the Simple Will and the Intent, which we must believe is absolute. He and His life are one. All hangs upon the "Upper Head," for according to the awakening below, so it will be awakened above. This has already been explained in its perfection in the appropriate places. There is no need to repeat these words here. In your great wisdom, you will know this, for who is like Him...

# Part: The Purpose
## Chapter 6

<margin>
Known Necessity
</margin>

And the greatest doubt that could be raised in this matter is this: it appears as a "deficiency" in the simple sense of the word. They did not see the answer in the soul. But according to the level of **Kabbalah** <term>Kabbalah: Here referring to "received tradition" or mystical wisdom.</term>, to ascend to the heights, the awakening is more appropriate for Israel. Their service, their value, and their desirability to Him are greater than the service [of angels]. This will come in the explanation of the one who receives the Torah to clarify the matter from their essence and their mind—which already determined this for their great name. The Holy One, Blessed be He, desired that He should be the one who answers them, and eventually a response will be found for them.

And the taste: See what is supported by His answer. It is that man is great in level and in wisdom. From the time of his creation and his service, He was swift and prepared him in His service. Yet He had not yet brought him to the point that he was already in the "two gates" before the punishment. This is what He said: "I have always been," etc. Or He said to him: "I have not forgotten him from the day he was formed from every body," for the strength of the Name of the Lord is revealed. This is what He meant by "the place of His Glory" and "His Glory is His excellence." And though their path is remembered concerning them, there is no response to satisfy their sins, as it is written: "Because the Lord your God is with you," etc. Meaning, this is the awakening of the Will to understand them.

We all admit that the wisdom given to His creatures—of man—there is no doubt that they were prepared to thank the Lord in their broadness. The ancestors preceded, as it is written in the argument: "I began with you from the land of Egypt." And He said: "The circumcised nations" regarding the perfection of those who are remembered to be the "Dwellings of Glory" for the Lord. They already said: "Before the Torah was created," the life to clarify the Glory of the Lord. "The Lord possessed me in the beginning of His way" <note>Proverbs 8:22</note>, before the existence of what is written: "Your throne is established of old" <note>Psalm 93:2</note>.

Rabbi Moshe and Rabbi Jeremiah, in the name of Rabbi Samuel bar Isaac, said: "That which is written concerning Israel—it is the word." A parable of a King: and so it is, my master, that the Holy One, Blessed be He, decreed to merit Israel in the future to receive the Torah. He would not have written it if not for the Children of Israel, but rather "to the Children of Israel," etc. And if the "Seven Foundations" were as it is written: "I am the Lord your God who brought you out of the land of Egypt," etc., He explained to them that it is Ancient, close to all. From their joy, it was also for the sake of **Might** <term>Gevurah: The Divine attribute of strength, judgment, and restraint.</term>. And that is the acceptance of His Sovereignty over them, to serve Him, to unify Him, and to fear Him. In the end, He was all-desiring and all-knowing in His creation and in the existence of the holy "Thirds."

And in the Midrash on Exodus: Rabbi Moshe bar Isaac said: "I am the Lord your God"—it was for this purpose that I brought you out of the land of Egypt, so that you would accept My Godhood upon you, along with everything I have written. And as a "Good Guardian," I speak in My greatness, only to stretch out His Will in His greatness, that He diminished the service of Abraham concerning the Torah. For were it not so, it would be His Kingdom.

And regarding this, it is written: "Who is like Your people Israel, one nation in the earth, whom God went to redeem for Himself as a people" <note>2 Samuel 7:23</note>. Rabbi Akiva says: "Were it not for the verse being written, it would be impossible to say it," etc. As it were, Israel said before the Holy One, Blessed be He: "You have redeemed Yourself!" And so I have explained and written all this. It has become clear from all this that the tradition and the receiving of the Torah—it was all for a **High Necessity** as well. All other opinions are merely "flavorings" for the peace of the world. All this is based on this: even the Messiah will come to them here, etc. It is included in the necessity for them to thank the Holy One, Blessed be He, for His wondrous deeds.

This is what he said: "Who has merit before the Holy One, Blessed be He?" "Lord, our Master, how majestic is Your name in all the earth!" If these were "empty," meaning, and they knew in truth that the service of man is more desirable and closer to the Lord than their service. For our existence is a **High Necessity** and not merely for "peace." For on this they were created, as we have written. And after it is unified, it is a High Necessity, as was explained in the section "Purpose" of this book. One must not come to the unifier with empty hands, for there is the secret of the Purpose found. If so, the Unification and the Service together are the Purpose of the Being.

And as I wrote in Chapter 4, "The Holy Spirit," it will not be seen that the reward is "Great Grace," for so His wisdom decreed, as it is written in Chapter 37. And if so, it will be clarified that the Purpose of all was to delight the Lord and to be satisfied in His Glory. There is no question remaining against the words of the Rabbi <note>Maimonides</note>, of blessed memory, that the Service and the Unification are a **High Necessity**, and not for his own sake and benefit was the Glory created, so that he might have the power to know Him and to make Him known. This is as explained in the first part and the second part of this book.

# Chapter 7 | The Section of Purpose | Chapter 7

<columns>

In his very existence, man is meant to always unify the Name <note>the Four-Letter Name of God, the Tetragrammaton</note> in his heart and with his mouth. For this, he must toil and constantly labor through pressure and doubt. He must be willing to expend his wealth, for in their death, what they sent ahead is missing, and so it is for them. The fact that Israel mentions the Name after only two words, while others mention it after three <note>Original: "ישראל מזכירין את השם לאחר כ' תיבות ויש לאחר ג'". This refers to the *Shema* prayer ("Hear, Israel, the Lord...") versus the angels' prayer ("Holy, holy, holy, is the Lord...")</note>, serves to make known that the "smallness" of Israel is greater in the Name than the holiness of the [angelic] portion. For as the partitions <term>Mechitzot: Spiritual barriers or layers of reality that separate the created world from the Divine source</term> decrease, this "smallness" increases. Just as it is in the whole, the fewer the partitions, the greater the capability. Thus, Israel is accustomed to this closeness after only two partitions, while others [the angels] only after three.

The explanation for this is that the foundation of the Name is withdrawn after they encompass the seeker within the three general principles, and there are three partitions surrounding Understanding <note>Hebrew: *Binah*</note>. The Levites, who are among them and lead them, derive their life-force from there, from the beginning. The congregation stands between Him and them, for the Creator dwells within the Assembly. The second point is the "voice of His glory" <note>Hebrew: *Kol Kevodo*</note> from a single source, as they have no existence of their own but are comforted and, at the appointed time, are sanctified to the Lord and live; this is an existence in itself. Among the three witnesses <note>Hebrew: *Sahadi*</note> in the general sense, he who exists stands in goodness and evening, and in the binding with the weight in the portion with them.

Therefore, these are the partitions that separate Him from them, which always withdraw Him; according to their endurance of the Holiness and the "weight of His glory," they publicize this further when they conclude: "The Lord of Hosts, the whole earth is full of His glory" <note>Isaiah 6:3</note>. For He is the One who brings into being, and through mercy, the acquisition of existence is drawn forth. It is not that the partitions exist of their own accord. As the Sages said: "When they finish, they descend," for the One who sustains them through the distribution of power, and through the power of the "Light of my weight," He influences them constantly. This is their existence and their capacity, for they would sleep without this life-force.

By saying "the whole earth is full of His glory," they hint that all the partitions included in the whole earth are contained within Him; He is hidden and exalted above them all. He is the life-force for the dwelling. This relates to the conclusion of the "fullness of the salt," which is the mediator of life. These gatherings and those preceding them hint at what they have performed, as described in the books: "Seraphim stood above Him; each had six wings" <note>Isaiah 6:2</note>. With two he covers his face, with two he covers his feet, and with two he flies. He covers his face to correspond to the Merciful One, so as to be face-to-face with the Wall <note>a metaphor for the Divine presence</note>. In the mixing of their will to cover their faces, it is because he who is born has his face turned toward the dread of their standing before Him. With two he covers his feet, corresponding to the known intelligence that the feet are the place of support and sustain the owners. This means they have no "feet" of independent existence, for the One who grants them residence is the one who sustains them. With two he flies, corresponding to the internal intelligence, showing that they are part of the "place" <note>Hebrew: *Maqom*, a name for God</note>. They move toward the higher binding because they show they are in flight and dependent on Him for their existence. They are given the power to fly to receive from Him and to be brought into being toward Him, according to their ability to be covered above and according to the hint of their binding, so that they may attain from Him according to their perfection. It is thus clarified that in the general intelligence, these are the partitions and the sign for their nearness.

The wise of Israel at Sinai attained their station after only two partitions. This is what they explained regarding the two words "Hear" <note>Shema</note> and "Israel." These hint at the two parts of the Torah: Study <note>Hebrew: *Iyun*</note> and Action <note>Hebrew: *Ma'aseh*</note>. The word "Hear" indicates Study, as it implies listening and understanding. It refers to the Written Torah and the Oral Torah. Hearing precedes true wisdom. The word "Israel" indicates Action, which is the fulfillment of the commandments <term>Mitzvot: Divine decrees or religious duties</term> in practice with the proper intention.

<meta>catchword: its secrets</meta>
<sig>ג 1</sig>

<column-break/>

Its secrets and its reasons are the perfection of Study. And the word "Israel" points to Action, which is the physical fulfillment of the commandments with the proper intention. This is why they chose "service" in the portion of the mediator. The proof for this is the invocation of this inclusive Name, which is the "answer in constant action" during the life of the person. There is no higher virtue in service and the fulfillment of the intention than the combination of the tongue of "Israel," which strengthens the blessing for the person who acts with rest and places his intention there—meaning that the entire structure ascends on high. If the intention is added, "The Lord is kindness." It has thus been explained how and what Israel attains of the Name from only two partitions.

Regarding the fact that the ministering angels do not say song above until Israel says song below: this is because the song of Israel is the essence of everything, for the reasons we have written. Furthermore, it is to make known that the "awakening" that rises from below arouses the exaltation above. By saying song below, they give strength and arouse the upper beings to say song. For those who were created to sustain and detail the perfections wait until these [Israel] give permission. This is the awakening they arouse below in their measure, and therefore they say song below first.

It is thus explained that perfection, which is the foundation of everything, is closer to the ways of Israel among the lower beings than to the angels. This is expressed thus: at the hour they wish to say song, Shamiel <note>The OCR reads *Shemiel* (שמעיאל), likely a variation of an angelic name associated with "Hearing" (Shema)</note>, the great, honored, and awesome Prince, stands over the kingdoms of the lowest firmament to fly and to bring in the voice of thanks, praises, and melodies attained from the earth, from all the synagogues and houses of study, to place them before the *Aravot* <note>The highest of the seven heavens in Jewish cosmology</note>. From there, permission is given to the ministering angels to say song above only after Israel says song below, as it is written: "Exalt the Lord our God and bow at His footstool" <note>Psalm 99:5</note>—these are Israel; "Exalt the Lord our God and bow at His holy mountain"—these are the ministering angels. All the angels of every firmament, when they hear the voice of the songs and praises of Israel, they remain silent in holiness.

Furthermore, his existence requires strengthening because he is a composite being <note>made of body and soul</note>. He must bring his portions toward existence "with all your heart"—with both your inclinations <note>the Good Inclination and the Evil Inclination</note>. For one must discipline them and direct them in the perfect service. As they said, we have seen the submission of his physicality to his spirituality through strength, as we wrote regarding the Unification of "The Lord our God," for this is the essence of his existence. Thus his existence is valued before the angels. Israel must mention the Name while they are among the nations. Even when the nations of the world gather against Israel to distance them from the Holy One, blessed be He, they still acknowledge Him, as it is said, "From among the nations they raise a voice," and they declare it twice every day, saying "Hear, Israel..." 

Because his existence requires this, He said to them: "Why do you praise Me with intellectual studies alone? That is already established." He did not say this out of a lack, since in everything they serve Me and are unified by Me. After all, the perfected person is closer to Him than anything else in his existence and service, and therefore the necessity in his existence was great. This is to let him know that he is greater than they [the angels] in writing and in power. They stood and were unable [to speak] because they sought Him as if He were composed of matter <note>Hebrew: *Chomer*</note>, and that no perfection could be taken from him because the matter would hinder him. But he comes to make known that his matter does not hinder his perfection.

# Chapter 7 | The Section of Purpose | Chapter 7

<margin>
The Unification of the Voice: they desired the Torah from Him, etc., and Israel to recite the Shema, for they are like the wings of a Cherub in divinity, to know that the Lord, He is God.
</margin>

<columns>

...[to praise] Him with the distinct voice of the stringed instrument, to praise Him with supplications, and afterward to inform them that his [man’s] status is greater than theirs [the angels’]. This is because they have already desired the glory of the Holy One in their divine realms—pure compared to other places—due to their limited knowledge of the heights above them. They took the "Heavens as a throne and the Earth as a footstool" <note>Isaiah 66:1</note> as the level of the separate intellectual beings. According to this, the wise of heart knew that the Unification <note>original: *Yichud* — the proclamation of God's absolute oneness</note> that the survivors <note>the Jewish people</note> have agreed upon as attributed to the Name is greater in value, more precious, and more desired by Him than the "Sanctification" <note>original: *Kedushah* — the "Holy, Holy, Holy" prayer</note> of the angels. 

There is no doubt that the song is more excellent and the place more praised when they are awakened and brought close before Him; this is the "Sanctification" with which they praise. As the Pious One <note>likely referring to a specific scholar or the author of a classical text</note> noted, "one calls to another and says: Holy..." <note>Isaiah 6:3</note>. The one who intends the Name... intended that the Unification spoken of unifies the Great Name, as in the verse "Hear, O Israel." When performed with the proper intention, it surely carries a reward for the commandment... In the first part of it, and with strength until Chapter 15 of this section, everything is a voice more desirable and accepted by Him than any part of the Sanctification song, despite its excellence. 

This is the preciousness inherent in the way of unifying this Great Name, as explained in the book *The Benefit of Jacob* <note>original: *To'elet Yaakov*</note>. There are those who are careful in the order of the verses, walking also in Unification through the divisions of the Name in the song of Sanctification. This is added value, for the Unification of the "Threefold" <note>referring to the three repetitions of "Holy" or the structure of the prayer</note> was said only to Israel, an excellent division known through them. For this reason, He handed over to them the order of His service and His Unification—an excellent and praised path of service. Such a Unification in the Threefold was not attained or known by any angel until it was revealed through wisdom. Because of this, they were judged as excellent... according to the words of the Sages in the *Sifrei*... "The Lord is our God," and here we are partners... to say to God... for the sake of Israel every day, twice, and in the Unifications of the voice. Through these Threefold [praises], it becomes known and revealed that divinity depends on the Unification of the Voice. And so they act and unify, as it were, for Him. There is no doubt that the voice of these angels and the speech of the angels is less than this. This is why it was not said in the prayer except to Israel. For this reason, those who understand... to know that "the Lord, He is God."

It is known to the wise of heart that the Unification intended is the Unification of "The Lord is God," which is the Unification in the verse of *Shema*... meaning "The Lord our God, the Lord is One." And it says "to know," meaning what purpose would a high created being desire if not to attain knowledge? And regarding this knowledge, it is said... "and Israel to recite the *Shema* twice..." as they requested the Torah from Him, etc. Israel reciting the *Shema*... as it is written: "Hear, O Israel," the sages of the Lord our God answered together and said, "The Lord our God, the Lord is One." And so it says in his walking... Another explanation for "Hear, O Israel": from the time that Jacob our father <note>original: *Yaakov Avinu*</note> was near death, he called to all the tribes and said to them: "Is it possible that after I pass from the world, you will worship another god?" Since they were constant, they answered: "Hear, O Israel <note>addressing their father Jacob, whose other name was Israel</note>, the Lord our God, the Lord is One." And He said in a whisper: "Blessed be the name of His glorious kingdom forever and ever." And Israel says now: "Hear, our father Israel, that very thing you commanded us is still in our mouths: The Lord our God, the Lord is One."

Regarding "Hear, O Israel," the Rabbis said: At the hour Moses ascended to the heights, he heard the ministering angels <note>original: *Malachei HaSharet*</note> saying it to the Holy One, Blessed be He, in praise, and he brought it down to Israel. And why does Israel say it in a whisper? Because the matter is like someone who stole jewelry <note>original: *Kiyumim* — ornaments or precious items</note> from the King’s palace and gave it to his wife, telling her: "Do not adorn yourself with this in public, but only inside your house." But on Yom Kippur <note>The Day of Atonement</note>, when they are pure like the ministering angels, they say it out loud in praise. Thus far [the Midrash]. We return to saying that the Unification of the Threefold was not handed over or revealed except through Israel. 

<column-break/>

The Unification of the Voice: they desired the Torah from Him, etc., and Israel to recite the *Shema*, for they are like the wings of a Cherub in divinity, to know that "the Lord, He is God." And the power of the statement "Hear, O Israel" to the sages of the Lord your God—immediately they all answered in His Unification and said the Name... that He is One, and Unification is in everything, and He is separate from them, and they are witnesses to Him. In this, He is God, as in the statement: "You are My witnesses, says the Lord, and I am God" <note>Isaiah 43:12</note>, as explained above. For this reason, they said this speech is the "Acceptance of the Yoke of the Kingdom of Heaven" <note>original: *Kabbalat Ol Malchut Shamayim* — a core concept of Jewish liturgy</note>, as they said... mentioning the Name explicitly with pleasantness... as it was mentioned in the Temple.

And by way of truth: because the "Kingdom of Heaven" is not mentioned explicitly in the Unification of the Voice except by hint... therefore it is whispered... and they will speak to mention eight times, etc., that there is a Unification of the Supernal Kingdom. And indeed, as to why Israel was commanded to recite the *Shema*, it is related to what Jacob our father (peace be upon him) said at his death, concluding with praise before Him... for the Unification was already accepted in their hands from the tribes, in whom there was no error or blemish. It was established to be said in a whisper... so as not to [arouse jealousy] in the Unification of the Voice. 

And as explained in the book *The Benefit of Jacob*, some said the ministering angels used to say this praise before the Holy One, Blessed be He, and Moses brought it down to Israel. This is what they meant by: "That which you sanctify Me with in the upper worlds, He is unified through Me in the lower worlds." For they [the angels] do not say it except by way of "Holy" <note>Kedushah</note>, but Israel unifies the Great Name for Him in His glory, as is known to the wise of heart regarding the intention of this praise... for Israel's service was more desirable than the "Sanctification" [of angels]... And Moses brought it down to Israel to wrap themselves in the praise of God and the glorious Unification. 

From this, the intent of Moses became clear: when it is day, it is the "Sanctification" in which they nullify the Great Name... which is not the case when it is in the hands of the angels. Because of everything in them, they are sweetened in the morning watch... and there is no place to publicize the Unification because it does not ascend with intent. For the "Shinanim," "Seraphim," "Keterion," and the celestial spheres above—all on Yom Kippur, and also while there is "Finding of Favor" <note>original: *Ratzon*</note>... there is no sin. And when there is no fear of the "Mixed Multitude" and the world is corrected and beautiful, then they unify in public. For it was said there is no sin or theft there, etc., for the Unification... brings the Name more delight than the songs of the angels. This was the great benefit of his dwelling [in the heavens].

And they also said in Chapter... "Your service is more precious than theirs." As they said... Israel is more beloved to the Holy One, Blessed be He, than the ministering angels, for Israel says song before the Omnipresent at every time and every hour. Some say they [the angels] only say song once a day, some say once a week, some say once a month, some say once a year, some say once in a sabbatical cycle, some say once in a Jubilee, and some say once in eternity. 

Furthermore, Israel mentions the Name after only two words, as it is written: "Hear, Israel, the Lord..." <note>Shema Yisrael, YHVH...</note> while the angels mention the Name only after three words, as it is written: "Holy, holy, holy, is the Lord..." <note>Kadosh, kadosh, kadosh, YHVH...</note>. And they do not say song above until Israel says song below, as it is written: "When the morning stars sang together, and all the sons of God shouted for joy" <note>Job 38:7</note>. All this comes to inform us that the praise of Israel is more desirable and sweet to God, whereas the praise of angels has a fixed time. Furthermore... they do not always go day and night... like the secret of "David's Harp." This is hinted at in the verse saying, "O God, do not keep silent... do not hold your peace" <note>Psalm 83:2</note> and "give Him no rest" <note>Isaiah 62:7</note>. If so, "You who remind the Lord, take no rest for yourselves." Moreover, since the service and song of Israel contains the secret of the gathering and Unification of the Great Name in His glory, it depends on them. And just as there is no end to His Unification, so there is no end or fixed time for the service—that is, the ultimate purpose of excellence in piety.

</columns>

# Chapter 8 | The Section of Purpose | Folio 66

The sixth section, which is the changing one, indicates the acceptance of the toil <note>original: *ha-la'ot*—likely referring to the 'yoke' of the commandments or the effort required in divine service</note> and likewise the tasks [pertaining] to Him in life. "And this is the Torah which Moses set before the children of Israel" <note>Deuteronomy 4:44</note>. And "to listen to His voice" <note>Deuteronomy 30:20</note> is not to be done through an intermediary <note>original: *sarsur*—a middleman or broker</note>... but rather through the agency of his disciples, as it is written "and to His voice you shall listen," which is the acceptance of prophecy. He chose them for Himself to inform them and to know His will... and He let us hear His voice through His prophet, the bridegroom <note>a poetic reference to Moses</note>, and his disciples. As He promised to Abraham our father regarding "walking in His ways" and "to be a God unto you."

"To walk in His ways": these are two [paths].
"To keep His statutes, His commandments, and His judgments" and "to listen to His voice": these are another two.
And corresponding to these, He designated for them four things in the blessing of the souls and their survival from illness.
"The Lord, the exalted and majestic" who exists through all the days of the world, which indicates the eternity of holiness from then and before. He will no longer give them over to [other] matters, but rather to you alone, to be for Him a treasured people <note>original: *am segulah*—a chosen or special nation</note>, as he said to you: "to be for Him a treasured people," connected and clinging to Him more than all the other nations.

And corresponding to "walking in His ways," He said "and to keep His commandments," because according to the way one behaves in His ways, to be like Him, so too is His will; these are His perfections which are performed for them and not for others. From the "Rest" <note>original: *menuchot*—states of spiritual rest or divine emanations</note> in the matter of telling His words to Jacob... and they are the great reward and the inheritance that is not a humiliation <note>the reward for following the Torah is substantial and honorable</note>, which He did with the nation of His choice to bring them quickly to life.

"My commandments," from which all iniquities and shames are removed, which will not be missing from them... and he will establish the action corresponding to "keeping His statutes." And to say that the matter of all the changes which are at the beginning... and to state the matter of the love and the bravery over all the names which He made... to mention the matter of the greatness of His Great Name, which is the praise and the name and the glory known to the unique ones of the intellect. From there, the Torah, the life, and the spirit are drawn, which are kept and extracted. And through it, one merits His place there, for "His house is in His holiness," as we have written. By being attached there, he will be saved from all those above and below. And the nations will praise His Name and His honor... and over all the nations they will be uplifted... this is the portion of the Torah mentioned in His dwelling.

And likewise, regarding all the things to be forbidden to them and to be permitted from the works. And corresponding to "listening to His voice," it says "and your being a holy nation to the Lord your God," as the Word says through the agency of the Holy One, blessed be He, to them: "And you shall be to Me a kingdom of priests and a holy nation" <note>Exodus 19:6</note>, to be constantly before Him in peace... and the hearing of His voice, and He gave them the heavenly life. For there is a movement <note>a spiritual awakening</note> that is "hearing," for He is their mercy, prepared and ruling... and He placed upon you His providence according to His will... so that you would not be added to [the influence of] the stars or the "gods of the eyes" <note>idols or astrological forces</note> within the Torah. And when one is before Him in the blessing... the nations were revealed in the creations, and they are the ones who fall under the power of Time. Therefore, they are forgotten before Me. And that is what is said: "He passes over transgression," which is the Time that separates from the soul... and the straight one will be found.

And the reason why the soul is "under Time" is because it is from the [physical] essence, but it is given to you to be detached and spread out, which is "Above Time" <note>the spiritual soul can transcend the linear nature of physical time</note>. <insert>As is clarified from what we have explained, for all the missing ones [the nations] receive their perfection from their creator... while for Israel it is impossible for them to acquire any perfection of the soul unless there flows upon them from the Name the perfections of the heights, and these are the perfections that are in the harmonies of the Glory.</insert>
