<header>Chapter 8: The Section of Purpose</header>

The obstacle facing him is "matter" <note>original: *chomer*—referring to the physical body or material substance</note>, for his material nature prevents him from the perfection of his wisdom. For the intellect which a prophet possesses, as mentioned, allows him to know higher matters. God hints at their beginnings, and all of this is simple and can be rectified. Through God, he ascends, yet [others] were unable. Despite this division, their material nature guided them according to their portion... in his composition, everything was entirely perfection and wisdom. For even while existing within "matter," he perceived the details of the generalities and knew their essence and nature. Regarding all that was built, as we explained, the "higher ones" <note>celestial beings or spiritual concepts</note> called them by names that agreed with their natures, to entrust the power to know their matter. And this is the meaning of "and that was its name" <note>referring to Genesis 2:19</note>—meaning the name he called every living creature first. Behold, this was a great perfection and wisdom, accompanying the completion of lower things which are designated to perceive spiritual matters. 

This is the secret of the "calling of names"—meaning, he placed them to call out their life-force and to know their actions. This is a perfection, and all the more so could he complete himself, elevate his "matter," and refine it. The names also hint at this, for he called names for the cattle, the birds, and the beasts of the field. Even now that he is within "matter," though his matter is not the end, he "called him a name." This refers to the completion of the "Blackness" <note>possibly a reference to the 'dark' or unrefined state of physical matter</note> and the ultimate understanding in his wisdom. 

In the Midrash of Rabbi Shimon bar Yochai <note>the Zohar</note>, Rabbi Hiyya said: Adam knew that his wisdom ascended higher than the ministering angels... he knew what was known to the streams <note>metaphor for flows of divine wisdom</note> more than all other inhabitants of the world. But after he sinned, all the flows of wisdom were diminished from him. What is written? "And the Lord God sent him forth from the Garden of Eden to till the ground" <note>Genesis 3:23</note>. And it further says there: when he heard the holy decrees from heaven... it was made known to Moses how close he was to his material nature... <note>The text here contains several difficult Aramaic-derived phrases regarding the soul's descent</note>. It will be clarified, then, that the greatest of the prophets excelled in wisdom and knowledge from the beginning, and they are even more exalted than the name [of angels], and this is the reason for their closeness to God more than the ministering angels. This is why they [the angels] hindered his creation, as our Sages of blessed memory wrote. And what is our "matter" that we should choose it in this chapter?

## Chapter Eight

Regarding his "matter," the "Holy Covenant" is written, which from its plain meaning... to prove the opposite of what we have discussed. Whether in our service to Him or in vision, at first he stands in prayer: "even those who dwell in houses of clay" <note>Job 4:19—referring to human bodies</note>... whether in his weakness... "behold He puts no trust in His servants... how much more so the abominable and corrupt" <note>Job 15:15-16</note>. Regarding these verses which call out to him, one must understand them in their uprightness and truth, so that their plain meaning does not contradict what we have said. 

For above, it spoke with "armed reasons" <note>rigorous logical or theological arguments</note>... it hints at the surface of the deep... it says "he shall not remember his distance"... he seeks from his sickness... and they can do it. For even though he was made of "matter" in his opening, he was struck by it and his words were against it, though he had done no violence. This follows the principle that he was a "ladder" in two parts, in speech and in action, according to his knowledge... to prove and to make known that a lie was made... he will not be ashamed. And it is sustained that they shall live before Him... for those who seek God... regarding the perfection of "matter"... for it is possible in the correction of his world, His will is to do good. It will be clarified that His purpose is to merit them and not to obligate them... and because there are forces in the elements and in the changing "matter"... and he explained further that this lack in the claimant... said it is great if it is not in its breadth... and the Holy Spirit was... as they said "and a wind passed over the surface" <note>Genesis 1:2</note>. And he explained further that at first He formed this lack... and did not merit the level of the Holy Spirit... and in goodness he reaches perfection...

<header>Chapter 7</header>

In the "Torah of the King," in our two aspects, in his orders, and rest, and abundance... His kindness shall stand and He will not remember his initial distance from before my eyes, for our "matter" is our training... and it is known to the wise. He shall stand and not remember the distance... and this is his matter, resting before my eyes. And behold, from all these levels, the *Keter* <note><term>Keter</term>: The "Crown," the highest and most hidden of the ten Sefirot or divine emanations in Kabbalah</note> was such that it was impossible for *Binah* <note><term>Binah</term>: "Understanding," the third Sefirot, often associated with the process of discernment</note> to know it or hear it, because it was below, it would not be heard. And it was the strong Will, which was the voice and the power that hindered it... to hear, and the "matter" of the *Atarah* <note>The "Crown" or *Malchut*, the lowest Sefirah where divine energy enters the physical world</note>. All this effort was to complete his creations... all this lack was to merit them before Him and to remember them by necessity... to justify His judgments and not to obligate them. 

How can my righteousness be lacking? Therefore, "My judgment is always..." <note>referring to the constancy of divine justice</note>. All this is to justify His judgments, as it says: "The Lord desires, for the sake of His righteousness..." <note>Isaiah 42:21</note>... "I have no pleasure in the death of the wicked" <note>Ezekiel 33:11</note>. And righteousness is like our righteousness, in His perfection without measure. And in righteousness, in power, and in the precision... and if so, the wise... said finally "remember"... and sustain the distance between God's righteousness and [human] righteousness, like the space between the necessary and the separate. Even if we say that righteousness is not withheld from Him... for which way is the rest? And the wicked are far from it. 

If from the weight... and the righteousness of the Place <note>God</note> shall stand, for His perfection is His action and His correction... as kindness is told. In His service... meaning they have no righteousness of their own, and at their beginning, they are moved... to seek it and sustain it. The awakening upon it will be to justify it... and sustain the "acquired" for the later ones... to say that in our righteousness... and a portion of My great kindnesses upon you will sprout... for they are bound to His kindness and our righteousness. And behold, with all their greatness and level, they need His righteousness and His influence to live. The general rule is that it is impossible for them to exist... even the "dwellers in houses of clay" from their matter... they are distant from the revealed things, for it is impossible for them to justify themselves by themselves unless the flow of righteousness is poured upon them... to save them, meaning they shall be righteous and merit before Him. And through righteousness, they shall be elevated above the higher powers, as will be clarified with God's help.

And behold, righteousness is fixed... in His boundless wisdom. And the "Abundance" <note>the flow of divine energy</note>, which is the reversal of His lack to the perfection of His creations, is a voice... from His knowledge and His Will which is exalted above every creature. If so, how is it possible at every end... that he should be more righteous than He? And we have the greatest of the prophets <note>Moses</note>, and it is said of him: "And You made him a little less than the angels" <note>Psalm 8:6</note>. The obstacle to righteousness is the lack of the flow of grace from the Higher Will over all, and there is nothing above it. He will also be higher than the "matter" of the creations that are below the favored Will. And so the "Law of Judgment" writes according to the higher chapter... and he is the one who designates what is his "treasure" <note>segulah</note> on the day of the assembly... "And now, if you will diligently listen to My voice and keep My covenant, you shall be My treasure <note>segulah</note> among all the nations, for all the earth is Mine" <note>Exodus 19:5</note>. 

This informs us of the general principle we explained above... to know the Will of the Creator. And that Will, it is impossible to know it unless He Himself makes it known... and they shall do it and merit to receive all perfection from Him. And regarding the knowledge of His Will, He said: "And it shall be if you diligently listen to My voice..." and He said: "You shall be holy" <note>Leviticus 19:2</note>, to direct them that they should become perfect for His sake and merit through their cleaving to Him by means of the Torah, which is drawn from the Primordial Will. And that is what He meant by "And you shall be My treasure..." and He said "You shall be for Me..." and the meaning of *Segulah* is a bond and a cleaving to His Great Name. For everything, even with high power and boundaries, is called "Earth" in relation to that which is above.

# Chapter 9: The Section of Purpose

From all the intellect, proofs were not lacking; they informed him, and he would humble himself before it and accord it honor. A wise man is to be shown mercy, and no kingdom is greater or more powerful over its actions than the first. This submission is according to the intellect, for these words of his elevate him to what he is. This dominion takes hold of all that is in the likeness, which serves as the culmination of the intentions of the Great Name. The end <note>original: *Siyum*—the conclusion or completion</note> is: "O Lord, our Lord, how majestic is Your name in all the earth!" and "Who has set Your glory above the heavens." This serves to answer and testify to what we have explained. Because this dominion, which is of the entire likeness, is greater than the first for the reason we wrote, it was publicized in the Book of Genesis by saying: **"Let us make man in our image, after our likeness; and let them have dominion over the fish of the sea, and over the fowl of the air, and over the cattle, and over all the earth."** This was said through the light of Solomon's deeds, that he should rule over all the works of His hands—over the sentient living beings and over the dead bodies, the earth and its foundations.

And if this is not so, what does "and over all the earth" come to teach us? It is to show that the matter is as we have written: that the dominion and the evidence which existed over the living creatures is compared to the first, as man is elevated in his holy image. The higher intellects <term>Separate Intellects: purely spiritual beings that, in medieval philosophy, were thought to guide the movements of the stars and planets</term> would submit and humble themselves to him. This proof, for the reason we wrote, shows that one must guard the "likeness" so as not to change it. Regarding this, the Torah speaks of "Positive Commandments" and "Negative Commandments"—they stand as guards, for they are rewards. They feel and recognize the honor and the kingdom of the likeness of the King over them. This is also the human soul, which is more refined and pure than the path, and they accord it honor. For that light and its powers are not felt except by this, as we have seen. They remembered the role which is swallowed up within the Torah and the commandments. This is according to the contemplation of the life of the soul in man, unless it appears to him as a likeness of his imagination, which would not stand for his merit to achieve submission to him.

The "Second Dominion," which is indicated by the phrase **"and over all the earth"** in the sense we wrote, is the greatest of all. One of the hidden books states that it guards its role and strengthens its creation. Much honor is upon it <gloss>behold</gloss>, and they placed this at the highest level, as God has already uniquely designated them. Therefore, it is appropriate to say that its division is to do the will of its Creator. And the will is such that it is impossible even to sit, and it adds that everything created is subjugated to those who keep the Torah. Indeed, the "First Dominion" is that which Joshua used to rule over the hills, as stated: "God of this," and the angels and the completion of the proofs. Do not misunderstand; your fear there is what prevents you from tolerating the antiquity of the First Adam. For his intellect was such that all creatures would prostrate themselves to him, as we wrote above. This submission and dominion were not against its will, but to do as he willed for his service, and not to cancel its nature and customs, in the sense of: "They shall not hurt nor destroy in all My holy mountain." The third type was ruled by the "First Glory" <note>likely referring to a high angelic rank or the Shekhinah</note> regarding the living creatures, and the wonder which the Lord showed to be done in the land of Egypt. And "the earth opened its mouth" and swallowed those who rose against him <note>referring to the rebellion of Korah in Numbers 16</note>. Also, the lightnings bring and are able to complete His strike in antiquity, and no man stood before them. We have written more on this to explain the count of the lower ones who are obligated. 

"In the Lord and in Moses His servant"—Moses's works were over the great angels, after the stars. Look, therefore, with intention at the reason for the appearance of the moving lower beings. The owners of the higher "bringers" bring them with fire and with its blessing. This is a great power, to say that they are the most harmful of all creatures. This is because the dominion that removes and leads the lower existing things—while the power of the "Higher Machine" <note>original: *Ha-Mekhonah ha-Elyonah*—the celestial mechanism or system of spheres</note> stands over them to rest them and move them—is the wisdom of the Separate Intellects and their kinds, and they are in fire and its blessing.

<column-break/>

Behold its strength and its delight; not upon a single one of them is there a rod, and the dominion of the Higher Machine is removed from them alone. To what is this comparable? To one who perceives and looks with the power and knowledge of his might at the "Highest Wheel" <note>the *Primum Mobile* or the outermost celestial sphere</note> in the world, moving from the force of the "Living Creatures" <note>original: *Chayot*—a high order of angels</note> that move it with all the strength of a bound, hidden power, without the power of the days that were chosen. And he paused its strong movement by removing the "glaze" <gloss>radiance</gloss> and the antiquity of those lights. Behold, the wheels <note>the celestial spheres</note> shall not pass through it to prevail; all the more so was it to be believed at that time. For when he is the treasure of the individuals in the lower elements, he is perfected and proven from the commands. He divides them, and by this, he would humble and look upon the intended ones. It is known that movement is perceived from the higher ones, and they are significant within them and move by their power. The Great Rabbi <note>likely Maimonides</note> wrote about the contradiction of power in the element of Water, looking at the Heavens and facing the Fire. 

On this, he wrote in these words: "It entered his mind when I knew this, that these four intended spheres—even though the interior of them all is alike in all places—they themselves have for each sphere a foundation from the four elements, with honor which is the beginning of the intentions of the foundation. It is the mover of those movements of equality." In the movement of the elements: the sphere of the Moon moves the Water; the sphere of the Sun moves the Fire; the sphere of the other stars moves the Air, etc.; and the sphere of the fixed stars moves the Earth. It is known that these spheres are joined and moved by the power of the Separate Intellects, through the power of the emanation upon them from the One who is above them all, blessed be He. Solomon said this must be added to the tradition: that when the Name is honored, Man is the precious one. For the sphere of the "Living Creatures" that moves the day—what of the light? It stood still from its movement, for it was only commanded by his mouth. And they applied this to the rest of the spheres. For his hand [Moses] was over the encircling of the higher and lower ones above. And also for him, the "Horn" <note>symbol of power or radiance</note> is that which performed the sign of the serpent, and they were all spread out and wondered. For God chose a path and an order, and sent a blow from the blow of the pestilence, descending from the heavens. For "whatever the Lord pleased, He did in heaven and in earth," which follows the ways of the Creator. Thus, in the rivers and in the six things that were in the land, he had the authority to rule over the plant of heaven. 

Behold, in man, there was the creation of the Higher Glory in its movement, and this touches also upon the higher beings. In general, this language of "differentiation" that we mentioned is to complete the lack. The intellect is for the "eyes of our future." This is what Rabbi Eliezer mentioned when he said: "From where do we know that every single plague that the Holy One, blessed be He, brought upon the Egyptians in Egypt was of four plagues?" <note>referring to the Passover Haggadah</note>. And it was supported by the fact that he placed the lower foundations there. Through the power of its reason, while the higher one was moving, they moved it with fire and its blessing, as we mentioned. Likewise, Rabbi Akiva said it was of five, for the lower elements were filled, so the plague that occurred and dwelt—the voice looked upon their higher powers that move it. He would draw it to the light and settle it and stand it still from its movement. Because there are four [elements] plus the "Fifth Element" <term>Fifth Element: the *Quintessence* or Aether, the substance of the celestial spheres</term>, which are the higher spheres that move the lower ones. Thus, "every single plague... was of five plagues." For he sees that the purpose of the moving spheres was for the sake of the lower ones. Their movement for these elements was a plague of separation of power, by the change of movements and the removal of the standing places; they would stand still without doubt. To what is this comparable? To a machine <note>original: *Melakhah*—here likely a mill</note> of water; as long as it has something to grind, the power covers and passes the ancient [parts]. But if something happens to the grinding, it dries up and all stand still. Our opinion is that the power of the lower ones exists for the sake of the lower ones <note>likely meaning the higher exists for the lower</note>, just as the daughter of the Torah was said to be for the sake of those on the earth, according to the plain meaning of the text, and as was explained in the name of the purpose of the sphere.

<summary>This page explores the concept of human dominion over nature, arguing that a perfected human intellect (like that of Moses or Solomon) can control both earthly elements and celestial spheres. It uses medieval cosmology to explain the Plagues of Egypt as the suspension of the natural movements of the celestial spheres that govern the four elements.</summary>

# Chapter 9: The Section of Purpose, Chapter 9

<margin>His name and...</margin>
His Creator, and the great change in the foundations. As it is explained in the Midrash <note>A traditional Jewish method of interpreting biblical texts through stories and homilies</note> regarding the verse: "But your iniquities have separated you from your God" (Isaiah 59:2). If not for your sins, there would be no separation between you and your Father in Heaven; it would be as the matter of a man's own daughter. It is told that Rabbi Zera used to converse with the heavenly beings and they did not turn away; if not for sins, the world would have been perfectly aligned, and man would have been able to enter the presence of his Creator. For it is written, "And He breathed into his nostrils the breath of life" (Genesis 2:7), and the breath of life comes from the Almighty Himself. If not for your sins, this pure soul would have remained in its state, and the difference between us and our Father in Heaven would be minimal, as it is written: "You have made him a little lower than the angels" (Psalms 8:6). This "little" implies that there is nothing between man and the Blessed One except for sin, which causes the deficiency. For if man had preserved his soul in its initial purity, there would be no separation between him and the God of the universe in terms of the creation of the world. For the human body and its soul, which was breathed into it from His own breath—as in the matter of "He breathed into his nostrils the breath of life"—possess a quality that no other creature, high or low, has the power to achieve. Therefore, one must acknowledge man’s superior standing.

The Scripture further suggests that the deficiency lies in the physical body, for the soul is not a body but a spirit. This is the ultimate and most praised perfection, for we would have been able to endure the afflictions of the soul and the blood. This is why it says, "And crowned him with glory and honor" (Psalms 8:6). For our supreme glory, which encompasses all, is the foundation of all his understanding, influenced by the Supernal Wisdom. To this, they applied the term "Glory" (*Kavod*), which is the primary honor, encompassing the meaning of the <term>Ten Utterances: the ten creative commands through which God brought the world into being</term>. Every single benefit found in them derives from the Glory, which is the "Wisdom" mentioned in Scripture. Behold, "Glory" refers to the beginning, while "Honor" refers to the end—the observation and contemplation of them.

"Honor" is what we say regarding the beauty of the soul, in the likeness of the Higher Being in its construction. Far be it from us to suggest it is identical to the Divine Essence, but it is a part of that Glory mentioned in the verse as being "high above all glories." It is a separate portion, as it says, "You have made him to have dominion over the works of Your hands; You have put all things under his feet" (Psalms 8:7). This dominion is the essence of the glory given to them, and they are revealed in its construction. Even the heavens were placed under him, because they also recognized and remembered his superior status, being influenced from above. This is found in the wisdom of the Torah and the fulfillment of its commandments. The intellect and the consciousness are the essence of what he was formed from, for "kind recognizes its kind." His glory and his existence are high glory, just as glory is called "life."

Regarding the other "glory" mentioned in the context of the stars and heavenly spheres: these are foreign to the Kings <note>referring to the divine or angelic forces</note>, according to the words spoken about the Glory which is "Wisdom." They do not know His ways except through His strength and his proximity to His glory. But when they are perfected, they attain that glory. Behold, Joshua stood in his path and his honor, and he did not lack the benefit of the punishments <note>or "powers"</note>. This is paid back as it is said of them, "and the thousands are for its keepers." Even the souls that were trapped in impurity, I have said in Chapter 8 that Rabbi Elazar stood on his feet and would awaken the creatures of God. See those creatures—how they were afraid, thinking he was the Creator himself! And also regarding the heavenly hosts: the Midrash says on the verse "You have made him a little lower than the angels" that this refers to Joshua, who said, "Sun, stand still at Gibeon" (Joshua 10:12). Behold, see how they said "You have made him a little lower than the angels," and not like the stars and the hosts who were divided. They received their portion and they inclined to it. One should not err and say that if the upper beings are subject to him, then they are his servants; for we have already explained that the Blessed One made us hear through His miracles that the cause of the soul's perfection is not the Glory alone, for it is not according to a natural intellect but through the mentioned matters. We remained in existence with the intellect. 

And the perfection of the soul is more worthy of strength than the lower wisdom. To what is this comparable? To a king who arrived at the gates of his kingdom. Through his great deeds, he manifested the greatness of the kingdom, and in his glory, they feared him, for all those who possess knowledge see and know that it is right for them to give glory to the kingdom, for this preparation belongs to them...

<column-break/>

...the exile and its nature. For the desire of Glory is to justify its creation. That which is forced comes from his own strength, and he is its source. Truly, His hand is supreme over all creation, for His glory in the world is revealed through him more than any other. This is what the man of God prayed for: to recognize his creation and his soul through these verses we have mentioned.

And it is almost as if the difficulty were to bring it close. And the sages, of blessed memory, said: "Will a man say to his Maker, 'What are you doing?'" Is it possible for a mortal born of woman to merit anything through his own deeds? For he is but a species of the earth. If he does not perfect his virtue, it is as if it is said of him: "What are we that He should remember us?" When a mortal is born in poverty, how can he say of himself that he should merit and be justified with the proper holiness and be preserved in the eyes of his Creator? If His will does not save him, his justification will return to his own eyes. This is what will be inherited for himself. For the intellect prepared in the heart—the source of the Haggadah <note>the non-legalistic, narrative tradition</note>—its hand is difficult for our species. 

<margin>Behold, in His holy ones He puts no trust (Job 15:15)</margin> 
The separated beings <term>Separated Beings: angels or pure intellects that lack physical form</term> are beyond him, and he would have no existence in himself if that existence were not influenced upon them from Him. And even with all their levels, they are not pure in the eyes of God. He looks and sees always without doubt. Even though it is written: "And in man He puts His trust," and "The world exists forever," it is not from our own strength, but He speaks to increase the ultimate perfections. This verse is difficult and sinful; therefore, one needs the Divine perfections to be influenced upon him from his Creator, etc. It will then be possible for him to resemble the Creature to his Creator. Then his status will be revealed over all the creatures, high and low, as we have seen. This is what our Rabbi intended to prove in this chapter.

### Chapter Seven

We have already written in several places that the dream, in its connection to the Glory and when separated from the physical senses, is where one receives matters of wisdom. It is through the soul and the spirit. Regarding this matter, all the scriptures come together and complete our understanding of our childhood and our perfection relative to the higher beings. As King David, peace be upon him, said in the Psalm whose explanation I began, and whose conclusion is in this chapter: "When I behold Your heavens..." (Psalms 8:4), "What is man that You are mindful of him..." (Psalms 8:5). As I explained in this chapter, the beginning is "flesh and spirit," because of the state of the righteous who complete their connection to their Creator with strength, wisdom, knowledge, and understanding. The righteous who guard against all evil will be elevated above all creatures, high and low, as we wrote in the previous chapter.

A person is honored and written in the likeness of the Glory, as is explained in the first part of this book. When he walks in the paths of wisdom, through the Torah and its commandments, he merits to become one who is influenced in His likeness. Here, the word "King" is used for one who "breaks a fence to make a path for himself," for the building of perfections is what he has established. As it is written: "His kingdom rules over all." Behold, the decree for that day is established over everything; he strikes everything and rules over everything. 

In the Midrash of the High Priest <note>possibly referring to a specific section of the Zohar or a midrashic collection</note>, Rabbi Shimon bar Yochai says: First, he ruled over the upper beings, as it is written: "And Solomon sat on the throne of the Lord as king." Finally, he ruled over the lower beings, as it is written: "For he had dominion over all the region on this side of the River." Finally, he ruled over Israel, as it is written: "I, Kohelet, was king over Israel." Finally, he ruled over Jerusalem, as it is written: "The words of Kohelet... king in Jerusalem." Finally, he ruled only over his bed, as it is written: "Behold the bed of Solomon." Finally, he ruled only over his staff, as it is written: "What profit has a man in all his labor?" and "This was my portion from all my labor." 

Behold, the sages returned to everything they evaluated regarding him. This is in the awareness that says: "Twelve months... then the king was walking on the roof of the royal palace..." and he returned to the throne of his kingdom. From there, he had great wealth, even over the upper beings, through our soul and over the lower beings. But when he sinned, the "serpent of knowledge" ruled over his fall, and he took from him and burdened him, descending level by level from what he had been created for. He no longer ruled except over his staff—which is a dry piece of wood—according to his merit. From this, those who know the hidden wisdom <note>the Kabbalists</note> will understand. How much sin causes! Before he sinned, in his glory, there was no separation between him and his Creator.

# Chapter 10: The Section of Purpose, Chapter 10

Their actions as a whole, and the establishment of heresy in the "Chosen City" <note>likely referring to Jerusalem or a spiritual state of perfection</note> is near. There is no proof from the philosophers regarding the prevention of change after a specific quality has been established, for the reception of a miracle is within their nature. For they <note>the philosophers</note> say and decide on a different beginning for religion. Therefore, one who acts upon the lower worlds cannot act upon the upper worlds unless everything is under his authority, as is the case with a special quality that acts upon matters according to his will and the will of his Creator. This is because he calls out to them in a moment of mercy and remembers them in their time of danger, whenever they desire, and they recognize that there is none beside Him. 

This is the principle of the permanence of reward—both pleasant recompense and punishment. Regarding what they <note>the philosophers</note> denied concerning Divine Grace, this special quality is maintained through the "Right Hand" <note>original: *galgal hayemani*, likely referring to the sphere of mercy or the right-hand path in Kabbalistic thought</note>. For one must know that the righteous and the perfect servants of God are the ones who "lay the earth's foundations" and are its grace and its kindness. For the Lord has one special property that sustains and establishes it, as it is written: "The righteous is the foundation of the world" (Proverbs 10:25). From the place of the spheres, the worlds are completed. 

Those possessing understanding and wisdom see that the spheres are inclined to stand, for there is power in Him to sustain the world without the influence of the goodness upon them; in their completeness, they return even more and exist for them. One of their contemplations regarding total perfection is to sanctify the Name of God and to manifest His glory and His infinite power, and to publicize His wonders. He is the cause of the existence of all the spheres. How could a place be given from which heresy might spread? He is the cause of the primal Will within them; however, this is not possible and cannot be imagined unless as a whole. 

The commentators and the Sages said that this "standing still" is what the Scripture refers to in the Psalm: "Who set the earth on its foundations" (Psalm 104:5), meaning that the sun shines from the place where it is established to praise the Holy One, Blessed be He. So too, our Sages of blessed memory <note>original: *Chazal*</note> explained regarding the hour that Joshua stood at Gibeon and wanted to silence the sun. He did not say "Sun, stand still at Gibeon," but rather "Sun, be silent <note>original: *dom*, which means both 'be still' and 'be silent'</note> at Gibeon" (Joshua 10:12). For as long as it moves, it offers praise to the Holy One, Blessed be He, and as long as it praises, it has the strength to move. Therefore Joshua said to it: "Be silent." The Sun replied: "You tell me to be silent? Can a small person open his mouth and tell the greater one to be silent? I was created on the fourth day, and you were created on the sixth, yet you tell me to be silent?" Joshua replied: "A small free man who has an old slave—is he not permitted to tell him to be quiet?" He reminded the Sun of our father Abraham, who "acquired heaven and earth," and not only this, but that the Sun had bowed down before Joseph, as it is written: "And behold, the sun and the moon and eleven stars were bowing down to me" (Genesis 37:9). The Sun then said to him: "Tell me who will offer praise to the Holy One, Blessed be He?" Joshua replied: "Be silent, and I will offer praise." Some say Joshua told him: "Is there no other song? As it is written: 'Then Joshua sang...'" (Joshua 10:12). 

Behold, we are precise in noting that he said "be silent" (*dom*) and did not say "stand" (*amod*). The sun stands when it ceases its song. In the Midrash of Rabbi Shimon bar Yochai <note>The Zohar or related mystical commentaries</note> concerning the "Prince of the Sun," it says that the sun's praise of the Holy One, Blessed be He, is the secret of the "new song," as it is written: "Sing to the Lord a new song... make known His deeds among the nations." I have already written of this in the book *Olamot Yaakov* <note>The Worlds of Jacob</note> at length. Again, I found in the Midrash of Rabbi Shimon bar Yochai regarding the edge of the firmament and the sound in the spheres: one hears the sound of those firmaments in their divisions, traveling with the sun in its path, and the sound is powerful. No son of man can withstand it except for Moses our Teacher, whose soul was sustained by the King, and Joshua, whom he <note>Moses</note> had empowered. Joshua heard the sound of the movements and the turnings. What is written? "And he said in the sight of Israel: Sun, be silent at Gibeon." What is "be silent"? It means: "Silence your song, and by the silencing of your song, your movement will cease." 

One should not say that the movement from East to West is essential to its existence; rather, the Sages have already said that the song is its existence. When the song ceases, the movement ceases. This is what is meant by "as long as it praises, it has the strength to stand"—meaning to move. The song and the praise are its existence and the existence of the others, not the movement alone. Otherwise, he should have said: "Sun, stand still at Gibeon." But in saying "Be silent," he referred to the silencing of the song which comes from the power of heresy <note>or perhaps 'negation of self'</note>, which is the true existence. When it was silenced, it stopped and did not move, for there is no movement except through the power of the song. By the silencing of the praise, the sun was arrested so that the world could be sustained according to its necessity from its place, and its strength...

<column-break/>

...in the song, as will be explained. According to our way, there are actual sounds produced by the circuit of the sphere. The Guide <note>Maimonides, in *The Guide for the Perplexed*</note> in Part 3, Chapter 10, mentions one of the ancient opinions spread among the philosophers and most sages, that the movement of the spheres produces sounds. He says that this was the opinion of the Sages of Israel as well. Some sages ask: "How great is the sound of the sun as it moves through the sphere each day?" He <note>Maimonides</note> notes that the Sages' view in this matter was influenced by the belief that the spheres are fixed and the stars rotate within them <note>a reference to the debate in the Talmud, Pesachim 94b</note>. Thus, he followed the opinion of the Greeks as it appears from his words there, but this is no proof. It is not proper for his Excellency <note>Maimonides</note> to cast doubt on the ability of the stars, for they have a voice that is powerful and pleasant, even though they are fixed in the sphere. Furthermore, the sphere itself, which is the source of the circuit, has a voice that is powerful and pleasant as it revolves. 

The Scripture explicitly says: "The heavens declare the glory of God..." (Psalm 19:2). It seems his words are very much in agreement that the heavens speak. It was not only to Joshua that the heavens spoke; rather, as the verse says: "Day unto day utters speech" (Psalm 19:3). One must understand what is written: "The heavens declare..." and then what it says: "There is no speech and there are no words, their voice is not heard" (Psalm 19:4). This means in relation to the inhabitants of the world, who do not hear the glory and the holy sound that they have, and they do not perceive it. This is like the analogy given by the ancients regarding the "prisoner in the mill": because we are accustomed to it from birth, we have become habituated to this matter. They gave a parable of a person born in a mill-house, who stays there all his life; he would not perceive the sound of the grinding at all. 

I have seen in the *Book of the Kuzari* <note>By Rabbi Yehuda Halevi</note> that this language is used: "A person needs to awaken the holy spirit within him." Regarding what they say about the "Holy Spirit" <note>Ruach HaKodesh</note> and its descent upon a person: "And it was when the musician played, the hand of the Lord was upon him" (2 Kings 3:15). This is because of the joy of the Torah from above, from the source of life, and the legs moving in melodies and the song of the ministering angels and the song of the spheres. Now, while the soul is in the body and hears music, it is settled within itself and prepared according to what it was accustomed to when it was attached to its source. The movement of the spheres and the centers of balance and the arrangements are worthy of having the "Holy Spirit" rest upon them, to be conducted according to their primal foundation. 

It further seems to me that when it says "There is no speech and there are no words, their voice is not heard," the intention is to inform us that speech, talk, and sound are all one; there is no separation between them. For above, it says "Day unto day utters speech" and "Night unto night reveals knowledge," and it did not mention "sound" there. It then explains that they do not have speech without sound; thus it says "There is no speech and there are no words without their voice being heard"—meaning, without the sound being heard. There is no sound heard without the speech and words. It suggests that sound and speech are found together. In the lower world, one might find a forced sound without any speech or words at all, but in the upper world, there is no sound at all without speech, and this is never found one without the other. 

In the Midrash of Rabbi Shimon bar Yochai, they said: "There is no sound without speech, and no speech without sound." With this, the literal meaning of "The heavens declare the glory of God" and "Day unto day utters speech" aligns with "There is no speech and there are no words without their voice being heard." We have no need to establish principles except according to the words of our early Sages, the receivers of truth <note>the Kabbalists</note>, and not according to the spirit of the kings and the prophecies of the philosophers who researched the necessities of logic. Every group follows its own path, but we drink from the Torah and the received tradition. 

The Sages have already said: "The sound of the sun travels from one end of the world to the other, and the creatures are within it but do not perceive it." This is the meaning: it refers to the "Daily Sphere" <note>the *Primum Mobile* in medieval astronomy</note> which moves all the spheres in its circuit from East to West. It is called "daily" because it only has this daily movement from East to West. However, the other spheres have two movements, Eastern and Western, and therefore the "day" is named after them <note>the daily rotation</note>. They explained "declaring" (*mesaprim*) as an illustration for them, like a complete illustration of the movement that moves one after the other... and its strength...

# Chapter 11: The Section of Purpose

Their statement implies that time is necessarily created, for the end of the cause of time and the time subjected to it are for everything that exists. All things are subjected to time; they shall neither live nor be diminished <note>original: *yir'on*</note>. This is like a servant, and I have already stood as one acting in practice after that which his grandfather Abraham and Moses gathered and led; behold, it is the inheritance of his fathers. For the Father, the word "existence" means he shall labor, pray, and sacrifice through total contemplation. From this contemplation, a humble acquisition is made, and the world cannot endure without it. He said its existence is the "custom" <term>minhag: the established natural order</term>. He bears the whole world, as it is written: "The Righteous is the foundation of the world," and without this, he could not hold up the world. We have already written this. Also, an "End" came to him, and there is doubt in the precision, yet He sustains the world below; the sustenance and the bearing of the world was the logic we wrote, by which this lowly world is sustained. The "End" is hinted at in their saying: "The beauty of the heel of Adam the First covered the orb of the sun" <note>A Midrashic hyperbole suggesting that even the lowest part of the first human—the heel—outshone the physical sun, emphasizing the superiority of the soul over the celestial bodies</note>. ### Chapter 11

Regarding the wisdom of what was agreed upon concerning the levels of this Purpose, we have already written above in the chapter that this "Wonder"—meaning the standing of the soul alongside the other Intellects—is acquired and attained. See the perfection in the hearts of men and their struggle in such a choice; this shall not be erased, nor shall it be lacking from the prophecies that come in other frameworks. As for what the book says, as we wrote in the previous chapter, the "End" is to complete the Unification and to fix it in the hearts of men. They shall explain wonders even in your presence. The ultimate purpose is so that the Great Name may be exalted and glorified through His servants, and be honored in His glory, like the Angel of Wonders. "I will thank You, for I am fearfully and wonderfully made" <note>Psalm 139:14</note>.

Also, the "End" of the reason was the Supernal Will, that wonders should be performed even among the upper created beings. We have already written in the explanation of this part that the intention of the verse in saying "The Righteous rules" <note>2 Samuel 23:3</note> is to see with open eyes. For by receiving the word in all upper creatures, they are diminished and subdued, sacrificing to His will. This "End" causes the Fear of Heaven upon the earth. Also, in the soul, by the Holy Spirit, they hinted at this by saying: "I know that whatever God does, it shall be forever; nothing can be added to it, and nothing taken from it; and God has done it so that they should fear before Him" <note>Ecclesiastes 3:14</note>.

They explained: "I know that whatever God does"—this refers to all that was created and made during the Six Days of Creation through the power of this Name, which is *Elohim*. "It shall be forever"—always in its upright nature that was established, not changing its function when it is present for the reason that He protects it at the time of its creation. For every action points to the perfection of its actor, and the law of the

<column-break/>

judgment is that the most perfect of actors shall be the actor who acts with ultimate perfection. This "Perfect One," to which nothing can be added or subtracted, is thereafter whole in its life. The "End" said of it: "nothing can be added to it," etc. This is to show the perfection of Creation, as it is said of every detail, "that it was good." If you find addition or subtraction, it is not good and it is not [complete]. Regarding its totality, it is said: "And God saw everything that He had made, and behold, it was very good" <note>Genesis 1:31</note>. Thus, the work of God is perfect in detail and in its entirety, with the ultimate perfection in the gift of life and existence.

This is the "Good" that is awakened. Because this requires knowledge of the intention and the truth of the part, a living Being would not add this in love through the performance of wonders for this Holy One. He said, "I know," because he was destined to conclude: "and God has done it so that they should fear before Him." This means He made the creatures—details and wholes—perfect in ultimate perfection; behold, by His simple Will, He performs the [interruption] on earth and in the heavens, and enters the soul for a more praiseworthy purpose. This is so that His fear shall be upon the faces of all creatures, and they shall admit that He is everything, He created everything, He is capable of everything, and He is perfect. "And God has done it so that they should fear before Him," for while the creation follows its nature, and the sustenance of the creatures is with it, the "Hand of the Messenger" acts upon it and strengthens it. They shall be terrified to rebel against the eyes of His glory. For this, He publicizes His plagues and His power, showing He is the unique Craftsman. He said He created between the outcomes and brought them from potentiality to the sight of all. Would that they knew and understood that His hand made every part, and they would believe in Him, include Him, and fear God. This occurs through His prophets and His servants who stand before Him. May He be exalted in His world and honored in His glory. He said: until this, all the creatures shall know and be capable. Because of their doubt and confusion, He opened the door to fear.

This observation leads to understanding the act of wonders and those who cleave to the height and the Holy Spirit that comes through this act. They said: "Sing of the wonders and of the sea," as it is said: "And [Israel] saw the great work..." etc., "and the people feared the Lord, and they believed..." etc. <note>Exodus 14:31</note>. In their difficulty, when they saw the wonders which are the chapters of the Supernal Presence (*Shekhinah*), they spoke of the "breaking of the voice." Because they saw the section of the merits of faith—that they believed in Him—he came to say a Song, and the Divine Presence rested upon them. All that we have written on this matter is hinted at in the saying: "Who is like You among the mighty, O Lord? Who is like You, majestic in holiness, awesome in praises, doing wonders?" <note>Exodus 15:11</note>.

The intention is that from what they saw on high and at the sea, they knew there is none like Him among the upper "mighty ones," which are the angels. For they are within a limited name according to what is said to them by their Creator, and now none of them can do great and awesome things for us in the lower realms. But You—Your Name is truly the Lord (*Y-H-V-H*); this points to true existence and that He is the source of prophecies. He who is at the head can overrule them to remove them from their nature. "Who is like You," as it is said, "in holiness"—He who is sanctified by one who is glorified. This refers to the performance of wonders in the upper realms, for there their names are diminished; they surround and crown Him. He said further that He is "awesome in praises," and they receive Him and the Crown. He said that the reason for all this is His "doing wonders."

It shall be explained, then, that the purpose of the wonders is very great. The greater the wonder, the greater the purpose. In the "End," the wonders will be publicized even in the heavens, for He is the Holy One of the soul, entirely hoped for in the lower realms; and above all, this and His honor must be shown. Now I shall change to the side of the agent, who is Abraham; the "loss of the agent" <term>hefsed ha-po'el: a philosophical concept regarding whether an agent is changed or diminished by its action</term>, etc., as Gersonides <note>original: *RaLBaG*</note> argued. Furthermore, he revealed his opinion in the book *The Wars of the Lord* <note>Gersonides' primary philosophical work</note> according to what he said. He spoke of the agent in all wonders in general, that he suffers the agent, meaning he should be built. He argues that the loss of the agent indicates that its existence preceded its being, and this cannot be; he is not the one who performs them. Also, since it would be by law in a known chosen pit, a known knowledge, even if he had an agent, the General Agent—the Natural Agent—is more perfect and enduring than another agent that exists by the power of loss and a non-enduring thing.

<header>The Section of the Purpose, Chapter 10</header>

## Chapter 10

And since this "Harmony of the Lute" <note>original: *hakinor*; a metaphor for the musical harmony produced by the movements of the celestial spheres</note> has spread across the entire length, one might speak of this movement as a model of the lute. This is because all parts of the "sea" <note>likely referring to the celestial ether or the vastness of the heavens</note> were equal in their nature relative to the Sun. Through the Sun's movement, day and night are drawn together, reaching a single purpose. Regarding this, one might ask why they have a voice that is heard by day just as it is heard by night. The literal meaning of this is mentioned specifically regarding the firmament, as noted by commoners. However, regarding the literal sound itself, the scholars of the Talmud <note>Sages of the Oral Law</note> placed it as a distant matter concerning the hearing of sound from afar. This is what they meant when they said: "the end of its sound... the prophets against their will..." What does it mean to say, "their labor is turned to your service," etc.? There is a story regarding the King of Egypt, etc., and suddenly his voice traveled about three *parsa*s <note>a Persian unit of distance, roughly 4 kilometers</note>. And even so, how much greater and more praiseworthy is it to describe what was intended to be said to all the people regarding the Work of Creation. Even though it is asked from where the "birth" <note>likely a reference to the "birth" or emergence of natural phenomena</note> comes—meaning that which passes through—and it is decided that there is no "birth" there, and one wonders about the "sound of birth," etc. All of this is argued regarding a rotating sphere <term>galgal chozer: the medieval concept of a revolving celestial orb</term> and a fixed sound, unlike the varying opinions of the Talmud.

As we have written and worked through the teachings of the Master <note>likely Maimonides or another prominent sage</note>, may his memory be a blessing, these points are supported. His eyes and his grace were upon the necessity of his words when he sought the cause of every fixed sphere and rotating constellation <term>mazal chozer</term> that has no support. It is said: "Were it not for the sound of the sun's sphere <term>galgal chama</term>, the sound of the masses of Rome <note>referring to the noise of the bustling Roman metropolis</note> would be heard; and were it not for the sound of the masses of Rome, the sound of the sun's sphere would be heard." It is well known that their sound travels from one end of the world to the other. To what can the sound of the sun's sphere, the sound of the masses of Rome, and the sound of the soul be compared as they rule over the body? We have already written that the literal meaning is praiseworthy.

The simple meaning is excellent: this "sound" occurred at the time of the Giving [of the Torah], and the words are to be taken literally according to the tradition of Rav Saadia Gaon <note>RSG: a major 10th-century philosopher and communal leader</note>, may his memory be a blessing. This decision is famous in its prophecy and the wonders of the Holy One, Blessed be He, which He performed with the celestial systems that possess power. Every kindness He performs is like His own handiwork. According to this, it is not by His power alone, for all parts of the nations, etc. And this adds to the matter and the wonder of this praise for the Sun's expertise and its preciousness, for it is like a public proclamation of the judgment of the hands of the Holy One, Blessed be He. Because of the Sun, heretics acted out and sent many [arguments] for themselves. But it is well known that it trembles and is bound to His Name, making it known to all the inhabitants of the world that it is like a kitchen-fire <note>meaning a servant or a tool</note> set by Him. It serves to rebuke, to announce, and to make known the preciousness of the great kindness He has performed.

Were it not for this voice of His, along with the glory and the atmosphere as we wrote above, it would be like the roar of the masses of Rome who strive to stand and sustain themselves in the world, as that portion is known and publicized through the spirit of the decree. In saying "Kindness," they announce and entice to sin. To the profane, the refuge itself proves the opposite of their opinion. How much is included in the praise of the "Sound" when it says this thing is strong: to assign one generation after another, a "decree to Sarah," and its movement "to Isaac," and standing "to Jacob," as a law for Israel as an "Eternal Covenant." For the "Decree" and the Torah and its study belong to it, the Judgment. It will not be filled by the name of "time" at all, for it is by nature eternal. And as is further included in the saying: "For all the parts of the nations," etc. This adds to the proof and publicizes that "there is none besides Him," and He is the one who returns and stands in His health and His servants.

And regarding this change, this is the **"Sound of the Pearl"** which our Rabbis, of blessed memory, mentioned in the first chapter of Tractate Bava Batra: "Abraham our Father had a precious pearl <term>margalit</term> hanging from his neck; any sick person who looked upon it was immediately healed. When Abraham our Father departed from the world, the Holy One, Blessed be He, took it and hung it in the sphere of the sun <term>galgal chama</term>." This pearl serves as the agent through which He announces and publicizes His connection <note>original: *zivugo*; union or alignment</note> to the world. For from the rising and the strength of Abraham our Father, there were heretics who denied Him. Every person "sick" with foreign ideas and untrue beliefs who sees it is healed from the sickness of heresy through the kindness of the wisdom of true opinions. He hung it in the sun's sphere to say that this healing is within it, and it adds to the publicity of the Kingdom and its endurance in the world, in the manner we have written.

One might ask: concerning the kindness of the Sun with Abraham, why was this pearl not mentioned from the time of the announcement of Abraham's sun <note>metaphor for his influence</note>? Why was it not included in the story of Isaac? One may say that without a doubt, this was its central point from the beginning of its creation... as we wrote above, and it was not merely a random event.

<column-break/>

## Chapter 10

It is found that his teaching was a unique virtue <term>segulah: a supernatural property or special charm</term> regarding the Benefactor and His power. And it did not cease... for the pious ones who clarify wrote regarding the division of the light. Their portion was for Abraham our Father, and through all his tradition and wisdom, the truth was reached and peace sufficed for us and others. He took proofs from the broad world... for he publicized the general principles and His being "The Last One," as will be explained in Chapter 27 of this section. Thus it is, and thus it was from the pearl itself, being attributed to him. No one preceded them in this. And it is said that he spoke of His connection to it and its placement, and he would be the one to publicize the divisions we wrote for him.

There is a necessity for this: according to the "End of the Rectification," there must be an end and a cessation to life. If he had hung the pearl on the neck of Isaac, it would undoubtedly have an end and a cessation after his voice passed. Also, it would have been a place for error. Therefore, He hung it in the actual Sphere, which was once a place of error <note>referring to sun worship</note>, but now He makes it a witness. Were it not for the "sound of the masses of Rome," kindness would be missing to sustain for them at least the announcement to accept with them and to overturn their opinion, as is the literal meaning of the "sound of the sun's sphere" which announces and publicizes His endurance, to complete all those who dispute. This is the delay of rebellion... to add the depths of truth and justice until the generation, etc. This shows that what is written shall be fulfilled: "For then I will turn to all the peoples," etc., and it is written: "And the Lord shall be King over all the earth; on that day the Lord shall be one and His name one."

To return to the matter of the sound of the sun's sphere being with the sound of the masses: they said that when it is revealed, it is like the "Mercy of Mercies" <note>divine compassion</note>. Regarding the science of the "Lute" <note>music/harmony</note>, the charm of the body and the "virgins," his voice is praised through the sun's sphere. There is a parable in the words of the clarifiers... the Master [Maimonides] received this sound literally. He meant to say that the sound is drawn from the movement of the fixed sphere, etc. According to the Greek view, the central point of the sun's life is the continuation of everything. He [the Master], of blessed memory, accepted his view and established it according to the "Time of the Other Glory." He intended to interpret it literally as the "sound of many waters, like the sound of the Almighty <note>original: *Shaddai*</note>." It is already known from our study of the "Chapters of the Chariot" <term>Ma'aseh Merkavah: Jewish mysticism regarding Ezekiel's vision</term> that the "Four Creatures" <note>Chayot</note> are the four directions. In their writing, according to his view, they explained the details of his "births"; they are the four directions intended for the movement of the sphere. They are our spheres, our wisdom, and our intelligence, and everything is rectified. He said they have a "sound," and so too the sphere has a literal sound.

How did the Master [Maimonides], of blessed memory, see that the intention is always to deal with a foundation of nothingness? For a "fixed sphere and moving constellations" is not the truth according to his own opinion. This is a matter for the dreamers. For according to the Prophet and the Sages, the sound is literal... even if we believe in a fixed sphere and moving constellations, the sound is real.

Behold, this dispute was proven in the Talmud, Tractate Pesachim, in the chapter "One who was [Defiled]." They did not mention the intention that the Master abbreviated in his illness. The "Sages of the Nations of the World" said one thing, and the "Sages of Israel" said another. All of them said these are the reasons for their words: "The sun never travels in the South." They were called "wings." According to their words, if the sphere was rotating, the kingdom would be in every direction... Scorpio in the North. From the day of the wonder of Rav Chisda bar Yaakov, his imagination was merely general and not the core principle. Furthermore, he did not say "The Sages of the Nations of the World are more correct than the Sages of Israel" <note>A famous phrase from Pesachim 94b regarding the sun's path at night</note>. We have already diverged from the intention... to establish the truth on its pedestal.

Return to the literal meaning... for Abraham our Father, he bought... from his thought and his merit. This was not difficult for Abraham our Father, for the heavens, etc. And Rabbi Yehoshua ben Korcha has already said: the sun was created through the merit of Abraham.

# Chapter 11: The Section of the Purpose ## Chapter 11

All these inquiries will ensure that one is not troubled by the changes in nature, temporary miracles, and wonders in the world. They <note>The Sages</note> spoke in metaphors to say that the Source, which fills all kinds of matters, allows anyone who merits to be attached to it to draw forth from His ways according to the calculation of the Divine Will. From the beginning until the construction of the hidden realm, the Worker of Wonders is the one who remains unique to it. This choice is primordial; therefore, there is no change in His Will, nor is there any novelty in His knowledge or Will. This "Firstborn Will"—which is the root of the matter—always desires goodness and perfection with precision. For even if nature was always fulfilling the Will before Him, it is through their existence that they come and add "oil" <note>a metaphor for divine light or sustenance</note> consistently without doubt, for there is no end to His life and peace. And this was the ultimate

purpose in creation: that the world should proceed from joy, following the path of nature, and through it, this joyful purpose is revealed. Our Sages, of blessed memory, sufficed by saying—as we explained above regarding the "Covenant of the Holy Man" <note>referring to the primordial Adam or the ideal human state</note>—that he is destined to live. This is the insistence of the Supreme Wisdom: it is the Will to enliven wonders in every sphere, above and below, to sustain them. Behold, this is that perfection and spirit. And look: just as He created all the initial powers to return to their place—which is the Eternal Intellect that persists in existence—so too, the action of the created being is understood through Insight. The explanation is that the Intellect is the majority, and the word of my Name <note>God</note> sustains it. He said that this is for the sake of the purpose of thought, which is that perfection and that existence which is eternal, heavenly, and persistent without doubt.

And this is because it is for the sake of the Purpose that He remains Himself. And it has already been explained by Rabbi Yonatan <note>likely referring to the Midrash in Genesis Rabbah, though usually attributed to Rabbi Yochanan</note> regarding the "Covenant" that the Holy One, Blessed be He, made with the sea: that it should be split before Israel. It was conditional from the start of its existence, as the Master of the Torah changed the nature of the sea. Likewise, regarding Jeremiah and Eleazar: the Holy One, Blessed be He, did not make this condition with the sea alone, but with everything created in the Six Days of Creation. As it is written: "My hands have stretched out the heavens, and all their host I have commanded." "I commanded" the sea to split before Israel; I commanded the fire not to harm Hananiah, Mishael, and Azariah. There are those who teach—not among those who imagine evil, but those who find merit—for the recipients of the Torah. These are the holy Sages of Israel. Truly, they are not surprised, for they know these are His own words. And when he renews things for you, it is according to His Will.

This Intellect exists within His creatures, and its nickname and all its knowledge are found in these chapters and in the second chapter of the Book of the Torah. They have already responded in the name of Rabbi Isaac Abarbanel <note>a famous 15th-century statesman and philosopher</note>, of blessed memory, and he aimed well with a good literal explanation, as he wrote in his work *Chemdat Avot* <note>"The Desire of the Fathers," a commentary on Ethics of the Fathers</note>, Chapter 3. Regarding the "last thing created," man: behold, he did not remain a mere thought, as indicated by the word "End," for "the end of thought" <note>is the beginning of action</note>. Thus said Abraham regarding the examination of the Will; it is said there that "with love He desired to create heaven and earth" and all that is in them. And in His prior knowledge of things destined to be, a time already emerged where nature exists as it truly is, on the condition that it would occur for a person at the specific hour of his birth. This was not a change in the Action, nor an innovation of Will or an innovation of an actual deed, for everything was revealed and known before Him, etc., as he wrote there. In my opinion, this was not a trial of the Will or of Knowledge, for I have already written above that what emerges from this Source is a "Created Will." One truly knows there is no change in Him, nor any novelty or knowledge, except according to the Will of the speech from Him to all; rather, He decrees it and watches over it. This resolves the confusion of the "Perplexed" <note>a reference to Maimonides' *Guide for the Perplexed*</note>. And the Rabbi, Rabbi Joseph ben Gikatilla <note>a 13th-century Kabbalist</note>, of blessed memory, in the book *In the Name of the Lord* in the second gate, wrote to save this principle: He has no change of Will when He impressed nature during the works of creation. Therefore, they were forced to say things that the Holy One, Blessed be He, did, etc., meaning He, may He be blessed, compels the elements and the seven spheres, giving them the power to receive this thing. And it is His Will for all generations and times to be a witness that there is a Ruler over them who can bring about any wonder He desires with humility. For these seven spheres would not be ordered without Him giving them the power at the time of creation to receive His gaze through His choice. This is not a change in Him, for it was already impressed in nature at the moment of creation. Accordingly, He stood in His glory over the ability of the finite creature, such as this world and nature, in its passing through the midst of...

<column-break/>

the End <note>the Infinite, or *Ein Sof*</note> which the Rabbi <note>Gikatilla</note> mentioned, for there is nothing in this except a decree of the Lord, may He be blessed, which was intended within the nature of the Actor and is not without distinction. I believe that because the Actor of the action is the Actor, and through the knowledge of contemplative inquiry, He first received there the "Triple Extension" <note>likely referring to the dimensions of physical space or a metaphysical triad</note> with infinite power. And through this, His power is hidden within it and testifies to this. For there would be no creation if the "End" <note>Infinite</note> did not decree over the creation and over the power of the Ruler. This is the intention of the "Created Commandment"—a witness to this before the eyes of all the world's inhabitants. We have already explained clearly that He draws near to those who look, as his words prove in the "Gates of Light" <note>*Sha'arei Orah* by Gikatilla</note> and as we mentioned in Isaiah’s name. It seems to me that their intention in saying "the elevations of the Lord" followed the path we shall explain. For just as miracles and wonders testify to the Creator who exists, the wonders persist, and they are the streams that bring between them from the beginning. They will be recognized and moved forever by those wonders, without passing away; it is that which will be stronger than those extensions. He will not break a covenant, nor will the streams pass through all the wonders and the coming of the writing. Thus, when the Holy One, Blessed be He, created the world, they <note>the creatures</note> were hidden so that His creations would always be before Him. This was intended for when they do His Will and keep His charge. We say that this was the Purpose of creation: that which is revealed and felt. For as long as they do not do His Will, it returns to what is appropriate for existence, for so He gave power and life, as it is written that they are "theirs forever," and the wonders persist.

However, in the "Second Prophecy," they were not sustained in the end because they transgressed the law of the "streams" and broke the covenant. They said, "Let us cut off," and they followed the powers of the heavens and entrusted the government to the stars and constellations. When they saw the governance in part and the rest, they did not listen to their covenant and did not fulfill the intention of their creation and their souls. They received the foundation and denied His actions, thinking there are light forces that could cancel the law of existence and its flow to the wisdom and the past from which they came. To show this, and upon the power of the enduring strength forever, because they transgressed the distinction and violated the law and covenant, the wonders ceased as a Will to complete the wrath against the existence of the world. Through His power and knowledge, the only intention is to instruct through Him without clear difficulty. The foolish will hear and see the persistence of the "streams" <note>natural laws</note> as the wonders continue; they will see what is established and compelled. And just as this pure Intellect was the imagined Purpose with all of Israel and all their labor in precious things—for they are the seed that remains—and the remaining Purpose in them is to be part of the general Purpose and the Secret. For they fulfilled and repaired what the Canaanite princes distorted. For at the time they stood and desecrated, the Prince of your God, our Father, followed Him fully. And this was the vessel in the chapter, and it is the preservation of the entirety of creation. This is every man's duty, and all that is incumbent upon everyone else to complete and repair, he was busy completing. They considered that he entered into the "Intellectual Action" which is the preservation and totality of the world with its creatures and their movements in the Covenant of the Secret, in that bond. And know that they were the generations of service and the intention in creation and in the Name for completion. And in Chapter 4, regarding what is written: "And it was evening and it was morning, the **sixth** day." Why is there an extra "the" <note>Hebrew letter *Heh*</note>? This teaches that the Holy One, Blessed be He, made a condition with the works of creation and said to them: "If Israel accepts the Torah, you shall persist; and if not, I shall return you to *Tohu va-Vohu* <note>chaos and void</note>." Until here <note>end of quote</note>. Behold, they explained that the purpose of creation is the perfection of service and righteousness. The path to this is this Torah, which they are to keep before Israel. They said that on this condition, the purpose came to the whole and to Israel. Those who uphold the Torah—they and everyone else among the survivors—are worthy of existence, for the wonders persist in the fulfillment of the Purpose. Otherwise, there is no Law, and there is no time of taking for them to return to the remainder and the past from which they came. This was the intention of Jeremiah's words and the path we shall explain. It is for the precision of the generations you have forgotten; they were the voice of the service in the "Sphere of Adam HaRishon" <note>the cycle or celestial influence of the first man</note>. For the purpose of the Torah is to bind one's actions to the "Right Hand" <note>mercy/divine power</note>, and accordingly, nothing shall change.

# The Section of the Ultimate Purpose
## Chapter 11

The **Active Intellect** <note>original: "HaSekhel HaPoel" — in medieval philosophy, this is the spiritual force that bridges the human mind and the divine</note> has a portion in the decrees associated with the holy, and even more so with the dwellings of the righteous who guard themselves in purity and holiness. We have written there that the souls of the wicked originate from the **Left Side** <note>The realm of harsh judgment and spiritual impurity</note>, and therefore they are subject to suffering. In this regard, the **Active Intellect** holds a law regarding the Ishmaelites and their king, whose shame stems from their windows <note>unclear: possibly referring to celestial windows or influences</note>. This is because the portion of the wise is within the "intermediate" decrees. Their glory shall be called out, and in their dwellings they are like the decrees of Israel. He has no hand in these matters, God forbid, and it is said that he has no hand in the decrees even in their sickness; he has no portion there. 

Then, through the manifestation of wonders, we cry out—not suddenly or by chance—for nothing from Above is an accident. Rather, it comes from the source and the hope in God, as we have written. Concerning the matter of prayers, it was said in the **Midrash of Rabbi Shimon bar Yochai** <note>The Zohar</note> (may his memory be a blessing) on the verse *“The Will of the Lord”*: It says one should be found in all their business to be found for life. They are all open—meaning, then, to one whose peace or brotherly love is removed, or whose kindness or light is removed. Rather, let every trial come, and if he is forced to be moved to sustain Israel, everything is restored. It is as if he transfers holiness through ten exchanges <note>original: "ashron chalifin," likely referring to the ten Sefirot or divine emanations</note> that are red here, etc. And when he is found as if those times or a full weapon or a sword are full of blood, then he acts as a protective shield for the children, to be found nine with seven. Every opening is a path for all kinds, and then it is grace. 

The cloud passes <term>behind the Am Ha'aretz</term> <note>literally "people of the land," here referring to the uninitiated or those without mystical knowledge</note>. For when the singular light appears with great mercies, in which there is no mixture of judgment—which is the **Head of the Supreme Thought**—all the agents of judgment are subdued. This reaches the "End of Thought," and they are not sinned against in the world when there are strengths and many colors in the bush. We give him the world, and if so, everything depends on **Unification** and merit. He who knows how to unify and bind the beginning of the thought with its end, and the book with the scribe, for the Kingdom of Power is his, and he rules in the upper and lower realms. Their union flows and is carried from the Holy One, Blessed be He. For in His turning, He releases from my songs, and one light of mercy reaches until the **Source of the Horn** <note>original: "Mekor HaKeren," a metaphor for the source of divine power</note> from which the world was planned. With the opening of the Head with the End, so he can call at any time he desires. 

When wonders are found in his teeth <note>unclear: possibly "years" or "repetition"</note> from the root of those three masters of the source of thought at the beginning of the world, in the secret of *“In the beginning God created...”* and so on. Just as if it were prepared in the Will of the Voice for him, for he is above the calculations and the good ones. From there onwards, with the change of the created beings, the thought is what he stands as, existing by the Will of the Essence itself. And look, for we have seen in haste that it was the Will of God in the body, because he was cleaved to the **World of Mercies**; these have no boundary, no end, and no purpose. 

So it is for the one who reaches the **Source of Will** <note>original: "Mekor Ratzon"</note>, and from there in the branches of the powers of governance and the Sabbath of the world, because he is above its knees. And this is the foundation of the Wisdom that is blessed from His action in the hidden and the lower realms. In the secret of what we said: "A pious man decrees and [God's] Will is fulfilled." This is revealed and opened for the action of fifty <note>Referring to the Fifty Gates of Understanding</note>, and in the book *Sefer Imrot*, it is said concerning the source from the covering of the Will. It is written: "The Will of the existing ones," "The Will written in the scroll of the whole," to act according to His Will. And it is as we said: "He will fulfill the desire of those who fear Him." 

One who is wise in this can understand every place where it is written concerning signs and wonders and greatness and comforts and the purification of the world's dross. Behold, the first creation was for the sake of the Purpose, and now that it has been written and returned a second time, He creates everything for it. And they shall know that all the power of the Thinker is through the Lord. And almost from the beginning of the creation, it was considered according to the... they ceased the "thread of life," and it is the yearnings. And the dissenter sought the end of his end toward the wisdom and the reason. Furthermore, the detail of the argument is like this: All that was created, the verse [seeks] to return us to the revealed of His kindness. This... his soul fell to give him for the life of the creation and for the ability and peace. The old hand to the Purpose of its life, and to this, it leans with necessity further.
