So that this principle may be clarified in general, and through this generality, the Immediate Actor <note>Refers to God as the direct cause of events</note> and the Overseer shall come into all His actions, both in the upper and lower realms specifically. This is a known matter in the records according to their folly and the lowliness of their value compared to His value, for they placed them under the dominion of the constellations <note>The belief in astrological determinism</note> and others, according to the opinion of the Sabeans <note>An ancient group often cited by Maimonides as the archetypal idolaters who worshipped celestial bodies</note> who think and observe all these beings. And in the chapter "The People of the City," <note>Referring to the Babylonian Talmud, Tractate Megillah, folio 31a</note> they said: Rabbi Yochanan said, "Wherever you find the greatness of the Holy One, Blessed be He, you find His humility." This matter is written in the Torah, repeated in the Prophets, and stated a third time in the Writings. It is written in the Torah: *For the Lord your God is God of gods and Lord of lords, the great, mighty, and awesome God, who shows no partiality and accepts no bribes.* And it is written immediately after: *He executes justice for the orphan and the widow.* It is repeated in the Prophets: *For thus says the High and Lofty One...* and it is written after: *...with the contrite and humble of spirit.* It is stated a third time in the Writings: *Extol Him who rides upon the clouds...* and it is written after: *A father of orphans and a judge of widows.*

And the end of this answer is almost a necessity for the recognition of their deficiency and the lowliness of their rank, and the lack of glory and awe, and the matter of superiority for others over them. If so, the scriptures do not compete when they are written about all the lowly ones, to judge all deeds with the attribute of <term>humility</term> <note>Hebrew: anavah; here referring to God "lowering" His attention to the physical world</note>. And when mentioning these regarding the essence of the principle, it is a response to the knowledge of the deniers and the sect of the philosophers and those who follow them, who say that He, may He be blessed, has no knowledge or <term>providence</term> <note>Hebrew: hashgacha; the concept of Divine supervision over the world</note> over these beings due to His loftiness and their lowliness. For truly, their logic is deceitful when they say and legislate that He does not engage in specific affairs, claiming that proper preservation is only through general providence. This is the knot of the opinion of these destroyers. 

And they describe Him thus even though He is exalted, yet His providence is seen through His humility, in the name of the greatness of His rank and loftiness. They said that wherever you find in the words of the Torah and the Writings His greatness, may He be blessed, and His loftiness reaching to the God of the heavens, it is branched upon the knowledge that He oversees the lowly ones. And the interpreters of wisdom said regarding every merit and deficiency—as Ben Sira said: "What are fathers if they are lost?" <note>Likely a reference to Ecclesiasticus/Sirach regarding the transience of human generations compared to God's eternity</note>—that it is fitting for Him. Therefore, let our hearts consider: wisdom once said that despite all the height of His exalted rank, His humility is with Him, and His eyes and heart are directed toward justice and righteousness in the land. 

And to establish this, one should say it is close to his heart: learn His <term>individual providence</term> <note>Hebrew: hashgacha pratit; the belief that God cares for individuals, not just species</note> from the laws of judgment. For a judge should not hear arguments through an interpreter. And also, the testimony of witnesses should not be accepted through an interpreter unless the judge understands that language, even if he does not know how to speak it. As the pious ones said, "everything is from His mouth and His writing," as we push back in Sanhedrin and Makot. All this is to distance falsehood and to judge a righteous judgment. So too is Providence, which is Divine Judgment, not remembered through an intermediary, but He Himself, in His glory and essence, is the Judge and the Overseer. 

And providence over these lowly things is not a deficiency in His law, God forbid, nor a lowliness of rank; rather, it is loftiness and perfection for Him. And beneath Him, in general, is the Master of the Gatherings, as they said: *You have affirmed the Lord this day to be your God, to walk in His ways, to keep His statutes, His commandments, and His judgments, and to obey His voice.* And it is written that He would not be an overseer in this lowliness if He did not listen to all this and attend to His ways and keep His statutes. For I have received that through these statutes and judgments, they acknowledge the providence of the Blessed One. And it is written there as a loftiness for them, and their loftiness is in His providence over them. And this is why it says *You have affirmed [He-emarta] the Lord,* which is a language of loftiness, like *the top of the branch [Amir].* 

And how fitting it is further that providence over a portion of the beings is not through an intermediary, which would be a deficiency. Even though it was written in the past, *And I will send an angel before you... for I will not go up in your midst,* the prayer of Moses was added so that they would not be handed over to his power alone, for he [Moses] was the weight of the chosen place. And that is what he said: *If I have now found favor in Your eyes, my Lord... let my Lord go in our midst.* Behold, he requested that the glory of the Divine Presence <note>Hebrew: Shekhinah</note> be in their midst, and not that they be...

Therefore, they are born to all who dwell on the earth, for every genus and secret belongs to the people of the world. In this context, it refers to human rational inquiry vs. divine revelation.</note>, because they rule in the land.

With this, he was diligent for his King, and like the names before him, they wrote the secret of the world, and from him come the proofs. We have found that just as the creation of the general world, which is the <term>Macrocosm</term> <note>Original: "העולם הגדול" (The Great World). The universe at large.</note>, was His will—not by any external tool—so too the specific creation, which is the <term>Microcosm</term> <note>Original: "העולם הקטן" (The Small World). A common medieval philosophical term for Man, who reflects the structure of the universe.</note>, is also the purpose. He also brought out tools to use, and there is what the prophet said, matching one to another: *I the Lord have called you in righteousness* <note>Isaiah 42:6</note>. This was the calling of the creation in the "forgotten wall" <unclear>...</unclear>.

That is to say, the purpose of the calling is to make known the **Divine Will**, etc. And let Jacob know that the **Zohar** <note>Original: "זוסל" (Zohar). The foundational work of Jewish mysticism.</note> says it is impossible that the creature could add to or strengthen its Master. And the law is in hand. In the essence of the matters heard in creation, they shall be strengthened and warmed in the hand of the children of Adam; there is no weakness or frailty in them if they are balanced at all. This is not the case with matters investigated by the intellect, for when they rise in the teacher, there is a doubt whether they will return or even hold in their existence. 

*I will give you as a covenant to the people, for a light to the nations* <note>Isaiah 42:6</note>. The matter of the provision of prophecy is to increase peace and lack in the way of perfection, to open blind eyes to see from afar the light of the horns <note>Or "rays"</note> of the matter—to know what the Lord demands of His servants and His people. To bring the one who overcomes into the light; for the knowledge of His will, attained through **Prophecy**, is the "Grandmother of Actions" and the guard of the proper taste. 

His calling is the "Fence" from the house of the foolish who are called "intellect" and the "lesser ones." From the belly of the abyss, they bring perfection and its masters, and they follow after his investigations. There they are inherited in darkness, for the light of truth shall not sleep without the shadow of the mouth of Truth. His words shall live and flow, the matters spoken to him and the living of prophecy, to reach the portion and to know them. For if through prophecy: *I am the Lord, that is My name* <note>Isaiah 42:8</note>, for He shall verify a thing. 

He came to say that the Name—He who is the Creator of these two creations mentioned by Isaiah and the intended intellect—He is His name and He is His secret. There is no human thing influenced except from Him, from His holy foundation, not from a created or separated speaker. And it says: *And My glory I will not give to another.* All these three things come for His glory and His creation. We are prevented from using it to open the desires which are the secret of the foundation... to know that all this is influenced from Him, and His excellence is above all this... to His Great Name.

...upon the two opposing views together. For this view of the **Chain of Succession** <note>Original: "השתלשלות" (Hishtalshelut). According to the first way, the master of this view follows the "Researcher" <note>Usually referring to Aristotle.</note> regarding the joining of the sun to the strengthening of his creatures. All that "Chain" which is by **Simple Will** <note>Creation by choice rather than by mechanical necessity.</note>—behold, all that they say regarding the succession of things is by way of necessity. 

Behold, **Rabbi Isaac Arama**, may his memory be a blessing, in Gate 49 of his book <note>*Akedat Yitzchak*</note>, brought from there the words of **Rabbi Eliezer the Great** <note>Author of *Pirkei de-Rabbi Eliezer*.</note> and mentioned it in Chapter 6. According to the way we wrote above, afterwards are the "Hidden Things" influenced by the "Nearby Intellect," which comes because of a beam. This was not clarified, nor did it rise to the Will. For this matter of the **Eternity of the World** and its thought spread prophecy by way of necessity. 

In the general existence of the improved luminary, it says its conclusion. And to know that all the things written... these shifted. And after what appears to him in these places, there is a prefix of the "Eternity" and he made known the weaknesses there. These are the wandering opinions of the day. The world was a kingdom in their writings, and they are not to be blamed, for they are the light of truth. He did not build upon them to say them in the explanation of the opinions and the guides, according to this Torah which Moses set before the children of Israel. 

They gave them ways according to research and the craving of prophecy, and they attuned themselves to their own knowledge. But the answer to those who dimmed their eyes to the **Light of the Torah** and Prophecy—which guards all those righteous deeds and proper knowledge—is that they followed in the footsteps of strangers. They copied words and clarified matters of doubt. 

Behold, in that which Prophecy specifies and roots out all these opinions... as Isaiah said in the verse: *Thus says God the Lord, He who created the heavens and stretched them out...* <note>Isaiah 42:5</note>. # Chapter 13 | The Part of the Ultimate Purpose | Chapter 14 | 71

### [Right Column]

In this, the intention of the verse is to include everything within the inner intention. Forgive the vessel of intention <note>The author likely refers to the human mind or soul as a "vessel" for divine intent.</note> upon which the **Complete Prostration** <note>Original: "השתחוות גמורה" (Hishtachavuah Gemurah). In Jewish philosophy, this represents the total negation of the self before the Divine Will.</note> is observed as a law. This is the level of thought referred to as the "Face," for the inwardness of thought relates to all matters of vitality.

This is the power of the one who is "sent," who acts from the side of their world and their rank. Regarding this, he possesses double strength, like a "storm horse" <note>Original: "סוס הסערה" (Sus HaSa'arah). This likely refers to a swift, divinely inspired force or a metaphor for a soul "storming" the heavens.</note> to diminish or to increase the vitality of a matter, such as choosing the path through the principles of the logic of compositions. Regarding prayer and outcry, it is already decided: "Do not pray, do not deepen his judgment." Every person who prays finds their prayer changing, for the matter of their prayers brings satisfaction to them.

However, the servant of the King <note>Referring to Moses.</note> was present, and it is written that the **King’s Scepter** <note>Original: "סרביטו של מלך" (Sarbito shel Melekh). A metaphor for Moses having direct access to divine power without needing a middleman.</note> was intended to do all that he desired without a doubt or a "storm horse" of lack, neither at the beginning nor at the end. He was not like a mere servant.

My opinion on this is that the intent of the verse is to show that it is known that the will of each individual does not always align with the signs and wonders that must be performed according to the decree of the time. The purpose was not merely the level of the wonders, but the benefit of the rank. For these were "dream-like" events that did not possess the same permanence as the first level. In any case, because of the pressure of the hour and the blessing, the star of my honor, which is the Holy One, answered my explanation.

He said that the matter of the wonders is better explained by saying that all "Faces" were present, and there is a place for prayer even in our movements and our merits. Just as the intention was not merely the level of the wonders, so too it was not merely the level of the beginnings. By the judgment with which God sent me to achieve, it was not to increase the claim of the "shaggy one" <note>Likely a reference to Esau or a metaphor for chaotic forces.</note> until it was corrected.

According to what you wrote, the "trembling of the star" <note>Astrological or celestial influence.</note> relates to the written word of the land. We do not speak with him beforehand. Our Sages, of blessed memory, intended that his level was like the "Faces" of the wonders, as the verse says: "With all the signs, etc." This follows the meaning of the verse, for these levels are the signs I have written in this place. As I have set before Him, it is better for that person to be last.

As for the difficult opinions, one can answer them from the acts of Joshua. Even though his intention in the **Complete Prostration** was the level of thought, it was established that after the splitting of the sea, he stood through the knowledge of his name. This was blessed through Moses, for the splitting of the sea was known to him by a hint, as it is written: "And the Lord said to Joshua: This day I will begin to magnify you in the eyes of all Israel" <note>Joshua 3:7.</note>. For just as I was with Moses, I will be with you. You shall come to the writings, as it is written concerning the Jordan: "You shall stand still." This was a "near hint" to everyone, for it is better to understand the Tabernacles <note>Original: "סוכות" (Sukkot).</note>.

Even if he did not come with prayer and outcry, it is found in his opinion that even though he was never equal to Moses, the song of the wonders was at the highest level of all paths. From his rank, it was not withheld from him. Thus, he sought the "Ma'oz" <note>Strength or fortress.</note> of his rank in the Complete Prostration. After the ultimate purpose was reached, the level of the vision of the paths according to his opinion was immediately apparent. He said the intention of the verse is that signs and wonders should not be as a decree of honor to a man, nor should they be added to. Through the standing of Moses, even though it was not made known to him, it was not through prayer and outcry.

<column-break/>

### [Left Column]

Regarding what the Sages, of blessed memory, said: "And he remembered, they shall call to the Levites," they already said in general in the *Chapters of Rabbi Eliezer* <note>Pirkei De-Rabbi Eliezer, a 9th-century midrashic work.</note> that the speech was strong and he was a witness. However, the Sages said that they should stand for honor, that they should be seen and quieted by us through the miracle.

And what is written: "And there was no day like that before it or after it, that the Lord hearkened to the voice of a man" <note>Joshua 10:14, referring to the sun standing still at Gibeon.</note>—the intention is that during the standing of the sun, the standing of the spheres was achieved through his voice. For if it were not the will of God, they would not have stood. And even though Joshua spoke through **prayer and outcry**, there is still room to divide and say that it is not fitting for a prophet to have this vision of the level of Moses. Therefore, he was not required in his miracles to use prayer and outcry, for the vision of prayer is a matter for the "negated ones" <note>Those who must plead because they lack inherent authority.</note> because they are the purpose and the necessity for the performance of business.

As it is written: "He will answer my prayer." My Sages did not know anyone but them, for their duty was upon him. Therefore, what is done through prayer and outcry is not fitting for the rank of Moses, as I have written. As the servant said to the prophet of Israel: "They heard and they trembled." They have no portion except for the salvation as it is completed.

And regarding the matter of the "withholding and closing" <note>Referring to the closing of the heavens/drought.</note>: why did he not decree that the few fruits be sweetened, or that every pit be filled with water? Behold, **Elijah, of blessed memory**, decreed upon the heavens and they were closed. He said: "As the Lord God of Israel lives, before whom I stand, there shall not be dew or rain these years, but according to my word" <note>1 Kings 17:1.</note>. Also, regarding the "Jar of Flour" and the "Jug of Oil," that which the wise man makes light of is a perfect gift in the tradition of our Sages.

As we have in his merit the "Holy Stands," and it is said: "I have commanded a widow there to sustain you" <note>1 Kings 17:9.</note>. He knew her, and the sustenance was for the other, for thus said the Lord God of Israel: "The jar of flour shall not be spent, and the jug of oil shall not fail." He did not need prayer or outcry for this.

Also, the prophets of Israel crossed the Jordan, and God's name was taken for them in their land. They revealed and struck the water, and it was divided hither and thither, and they passed through as if on a path. And regarding the "Salting of the Waters" <note>2 Kings 2:21, referring to Elisha healing the spring at Jericho.</note>, even though it is written that he went out to the spring of the waters and cast salt there and said: "Thus says the Lord: I have healed these waters; there shall not be from there any more death or barrenness." This was within his power, as our Sages said in the *Mekhilta* <note>An early collection of midrashic interpretations on Exodus.</note>, and he did not require prayer and outcry.

And Joshua also spoke to the poor ones, and they rose and went up and the water dwelled. This was also within his power, as they said in the *Mekhilta*, and he too did not require prayer. In all these equal cases, not one of them fell into "doubt or storm" at all.

Truly, one must return to what you wrote regarding the prophets who acted through the "Paths" according to their law. They did not require prayer and outcry, except for those we mentioned at their beginning. They required prayer for the "Writing of Permission" <note>A term for divine authorization to change nature.</note>, which is the opposite of prayer. For example: the uprooting of the sun for Joshua, or the "voices and rain" in the days of the wheat harvest for Samuel, or the fire descending on the altar for Elijah, of blessed memory, or the reviving of the son of the Shunammite woman for Elisha. These are the doubts upon which the commentators have argued.

The secret of the matter is as he said: we have already written that the "Scepter of the King" is the secret. For the person who performs everything is the Honor <note>Original: "הכבוד" (HaKavod) - The Divine Presence or Shekhinah.</note>. This is the foundation of all intention and the order of the place of perfection. From the Upper Honor, which is the **Upper Wisdom** <note>Original: "החכמה העליונה" (Hachokmah HaElyonah).</note>, it flows to the upper beings and the spheres. These are the "Deeds" that come through the unique ones who are perfected by all perfections. They descend to say, "Take for them," and they do not stand for prayer, such as Elijah, of blessed memory, who was among the perfected ones.

It highlights that the most significant miracles were performed through direct divine will rather than pleading.</summary>

# Chapter 12 | The Part of the Ultimate Purpose | Chapter 13

### [Right Column]

...in this, for regarding it he said above that the "evil portions" <note>The author is discussing the division of divine influence and how it can be affected by human action.</note> belong to him; these are the portions in the movement of the celestial sphere. And according to the Midrash of **Rabbi Shimon bar Yochai** <note>original: "רשב"י ע"ה" - Rabbi Shimon bar Yochai, the traditional author of the Zohar.</note>, may he rest in peace, this is revealed to you... and so too: "The heavens, etc., six days shall give," to support you, and "satisfies the desire of every living thing" <note>A quote from Psalm 145:16.</note>.

What is written above this? "The eyes of all look hopefully to You, etc." All those who are "high" <note>Refers to spiritual beings or elevated souls.</note> lift their eyes to **the Holy One, Blessed be He** <note>original: "קב"ה" (Hakadosh Baruch Hu)</note>. Similarly, all the children of faith look every single day to the King and His days to give them their sustenance and to cast their burden upon Him. For this reason, anyone who concludes his prayer before the Holy One regarding his sustenance, "Blessed be He" is said every day through him. The reason for the matter is: "Blessed be the Lord day by day" <note>Psalm 68:20.</note>. One should not merely set his table, but should distribute before the Holy One and cast his burden regarding his sustenance every day, so that blessings may be found every single day Above.

For this reason, one should not seek to eat his sustenance as a "free gift" from one day to the next, nor should he mix one day with another. Rather, he should receive it day by day. "And they shall gather a day's portion on its day" <note>Exodus 16:4, referring to the Manna in the desert.</note>, except for the Eve of Sabbath, so that it may be found in its preparation. Then the Holy One is found full of blessings every single day. Then it is written: "You open Your hand, etc., full of desire." The Holy One is found within the **Holy Ancient One** <note>term: "עתיקא קדישא" (Atika Kadisha) — In Kabbalah, this refers to the highest, most primal level of the Divine Will.</note>, and from Him issues "Desire" <note>original: "רצון" (Ratzon) — Divine favor or will.</note> to lead the sustenance to all, and a portion to each person according to his days, every single day. This is the source of the power from which all faith is nourished. These branches are praised in the language Above.

And I have already written this at length according to the method of this book, and the wise shall understand it all according to its intent in this chapter. It is because it has already been explained in the book *The Worm of Jacob* <note>original: "תולעת יעקב" (Tola'at Yaakov) — A famous Kabbalistic commentary on the prayer book by Meir ibn Gabbai.</note> and in this book that prayer with **intention** <note>original: "כוונ" (Kavannah) — Meditative focus or spiritual intent.</note>—in the way we have described—activates the Supernal Source, the secret of the "Desire." The blessing and the flow of abundance then spread through all the worlds. This happens when the Great Name is blessed first, and every single day they fulfill these matters from the Source. This is the secret of "Blessed be the Lord day by day."

Therefore, prayer for one's livelihood and sustenance is necessary every day, even if his food is already prepared for him. The reason is so that the blessing may be established Above every day, and that every day may be blessed from the Holy Source of "Desire." This is the meaning of "gather a day's portion on its day"—so that he does not look to the next day, but rather his eyes are fixed Above, praying for his sustenance so the blessing is established Above, for this is the intended purpose. This was the secret of the Manna that fell every single day, as it is said: "And they shall gather a day's portion on its day."

If so, behold, the preparation of food and the prayer for it every day is to extend the blessing Above and to unify the blessing for each specific day in the Supernal places. Through this, the Great Name, the Source, is blessed. This is the "Desire," and then the Holy One is found full of blessings. This is the ultimate purpose sought in asking for food every day. When the Great Source is blessed, the blessing spreads from Him to all the worlds. Thus, livelihood is provided by the Holy One, Blessed be He—meaning its completion is found Above so that the Name may be blessed.

Regarding this, in the chapter "Yom Tov" <note>A tractate of the Talmud, also known as Beitzah.</note>, it brings a saying about **Shammai the Elder** <note>A famous scholar of the 1st century BCE.</note>: All his days he would eat in honor of the Sabbath. If he found a fine animal, he would say, "This is for the Sabbath." If he later found a finer one, he would eat the first and leave the second for Sabbath. But **Hillel the Elder** had a different trait, for all his deeds were for the sake of Heaven, as it is said: "Blessed be the Lord day by day."

It mentions there that this is like the verse mentioned in your Mishnah, and they say: "Blessed be the Lord day by day." This is because Hillel the Elder was a "receiver" <note>term: "מקובל" (Mequbal) — A mystic or one who has received hidden traditions.</note> and knew in truth that every year and day, the Supernal ones receive their food and sustenance from the Supernal Thought. Every day provides for its own from what it receives from the Sabbath. As they said in the Midrash of Rabbi Shimon bar Yochai, and as we wrote in the book *The Worm of Jacob*: every day was prepared and would eat in honor of the Sabbath, even from the first day of the week. Anyone who conducted himself thus knew that today he had already received his food from the Sabbath day, and he would direct his intent to it and not leave it from day to day, for all the days are already blessed from the source of sustenance. But Hillel the Elder, even though he knew 

<column-break/>

the ultimate truth, nonetheless it was appropriate to say "our portion forever," and he would provide for each day separately. This is the meaning of the verse, and it is the way to awaken the blessings from below to the Above in these matters, to perform its function. The reason is that each of these matters is influenced by the Supernal Sabbath to provide for its day. This is "Blessed be [the Lord]," an awakening and vitality from below to give it grace and life, and to bestow what it received.

Finally, they said of him that "all his deeds were for the sake of Heaven" <note>A famous Talmudic dictum regarding Hillel's philosophy.</note>, meaning his intention was that the Supernal Heavens—the Name of the Holy One—should be blessed. This is the secret of the verse: "Ascribe strength unto God." As he said, "Blessed be the Lord day by day," all his actions were intended for the sake of the High, not for himself alone. As we wrote in the second part of this book regarding the way a person should intend when performing a deed: he would pray for his sustenance every day so that the Great Name would be blessed. This is "Desire," for all his deeds were for the sake of Heaven, as we have written. I have elaborated on all this to make known that sustenance comes through the Holy One, and in the manner we described above. Indeed, the intention is not just to admit that the Great King is the provider, but that He is the Master of Sustenance and is found in the world—specifically in Israel, who are His children, for their providence is not through an intermediary. This is like the words of Rabbi Shimon bar Yochai in his commentary on the Torah. And regarding his "wars," the tribe manages through its biological nature and returns it through the perceptions of the good intellect. This is the Divine knowledge of the secret and the additions of the Torah, and this is what he intended to prove in this chapter.

# Chapter 13

Behold, regarding what they claimed about the excellence of **Moses** <note>original: "משה ע"ה" - Moses our Teacher, peace be upon him.</note>, that [other prophets] were not on the level of Elijah and Elisha, who were able to perform constant miracles and great wonders. They claimed that "there did not arise another in Israel like Moses" <note>Deuteronomy 34:10.</note> in this regard. This claim stood in their strength... until they said that the action of miracles and wonders is not achieved through [mere] intention, and that the "reception" <note>The prophetic tradition.</note> is not canceled. Despite all this, it will be explained according to the secret of the level of Moses, for they would only act for the need of the hour.

Furthermore, they said there is no [other prophet] like him, etc. However, the degrees and similarities... there was nothing like him in miraculous excellence... and this intention was appropriate to be said regarding all the signs and wonders. They also said that the eyes of the text were to distinguish between Moses and other prophets, whether in the intention or the level of the soul.

They further said "no one arose like him, etc." to say that "the Lord knew him face to face," <note>Deuteronomy 34:10.</note> for the precision and level of his visions were at the level of "Clear Vision" <note>term: "אספקלריא המאירה" (Aspaklaria HaMe'irah) — A prophetic vision that is direct and clear, unique to Moses.</note>. Indeed, they said further "for all the signs, etc." specifically stating that those signs and wonders which the Lord sent him to do in the land of Egypt were according to the need of the time and the necessity of the matter. For there, the Holy One would speak to him through miracles "mouth to mouth," while he was dwelling in the land of Egypt, which was not yet settled as a double field <note>A metaphorical or technical description of the spiritual state of Egypt compared to the Land of Israel.</note>. As it says, "I have not made Myself known to them," which was a great influence upon the foundation.

Furthermore, he said, "the Lord knew him, etc., for all the signs and wonders that He sent." Through this, the purpose was achieved... and if so, the excellence was not in the miracles themselves, but in the awakening that He performed with him for every miracle, even though the Foundation was not yet awakened toward him. And from what he said, "which the Lord sent him," you know and see that all of them did not rise to his level. This was Moses' specific intention and the strength of his level—that he did not rise except to introduce knowledge and the reception of his Creator... and the signs He sent him to perform.

And if there had not been a specific time for Israel to be moved by miracles, and he had not been needed to make the sun stand still by his hand—as happened in the days of **Joshua** <note>original: "יהושע" — Moses' successor who famously caused the sun to stand still.</note>—would he be any less great than Moses because of this? It is known that this is the opinion of **Abravanel** <note>Don Isaac Abravanel (1437–1508), a famous Jewish statesman and philosopher.</note> in the portion *Zot HaBerakhah*. And he follows the path... in the gate... of his book. This is the language of his claim: "And we have not returned from the secret of the text that there shall not arise another prophet like him... and wonders... for He will not add strength... on the day of Judgment..."

# Chapter 14 | The Part of the Ultimate Purpose | Chapter 14

**Rabbi Nehemiah** says he was gracious to all creatures, meaning they removed from their minds the notion that he was born with a common nature. Rather, he was gracious to all creatures to show he possessed a superior temperament from the moment he was born. Because **Moses, our teacher** <note>original: "משה ע"ה" — Moses, peace be upon him.</note>, was destined to negate the influence of the celestial "stars" <note>The author refers to the spiritual forces or astrological influences that distance people from God.</note> and to unite them with the **Unique Unity** <note>The absolute oneness of God.</note>, he achieved this through his intellect and his merit, distancing himself from the world’s physical powers and the foreign evils which take the form of these stars. He sought to bridge the gap that separates created beings from the absolute Spirit. 

As a preparation for all this, he acted in the assembly with the sign of the covenant <note>circumcision</note>, which is why the sages hinted that he was born already circumcised. And the Sages say: "At the hour he was born, the entire house was filled with light." This was a sign that he was destined to receive the **Torah**, which is called "Light," and to illuminate the entire world with it. This is the intent behind the phrase "that he was good" <note>Exodus 2:2</note>, which I have explained is linked to the first utterance of Creation: "And God saw the light, that it was good" <note>Genesis 1:4</note>. 

It is known that the light of the first day was the primordial light of man, through which one could see from one end of the world to the other. Through the influence of the **Written Torah** from above, this light shines. We have already explained the value of this light in the upper realms. Our Sages said regarding the light created by **the Holy One, Blessed be He** <note>original: "הקב"ה" — Hakadosh Baruch Hu</note>, on the first day, that Adam could gaze and see with it from one end of the world to the other. They said in the first chapter of Tractate Hagigah that this refers to the "Face of the Chariot" <note>A mystical reference to the divine throne</note>, through which one perceives everything created by that light. 

Not all sages and prophets are equal in this perception, but the **Master of the Prophets** <note>Moses</note> perceived it all. As the Sages said in the name of **Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi**: "Fifty gates of understanding were created in the world, and all were given to Moses except for one, as it says: 'And You made him a little less than the Divine'" <note>Psalm 8:6</note>. By ascending in his perception above all other prophets regarding the Torah written by his hand, he attained a level worthy of the Torah's own excellence. 

Since this is so, one must believe with a faithful heart that just as Moses’ intent was higher than that of all other prophets, so too his soul and his preparation were higher than those of all other prophets. This is a necessary principle of the Torah; for you must know that the greater a thing is, the greater its substance and purity. This Torah which Moses gave to the children of Israel is above human intellect, for it is divine law. Since we have written that its purpose is for his soul's perfection, it required a soul and preparation more established and more wondrous than what is normally possible. 

If you consider the life of Moses, even though the Torah does not explicitly attribute to him every great action found in other prophets, he possessed a power from this "portion" that surpassed them. We can understand his rank through the physical signs. His intent was to order the lower worlds, which are moved by the upper powers that lead them with strength and clarity. This is the great power of the Torah, which originates in the upper realms. One must believe that while God’s action works through the lower elements, Moses was the vessel for the upper realms. 

I found this mentioned in the **Midrash Rabbah** on the book of Deuteronomy. Moses himself saw what I have written, as they said there in this language: <note>The following is a translation of the Aramaic Zohar/Midrashic passage</note> "What was his might? It was not merely to stand before Pharaoh with a staff, but to see the release of the 'portion' and its forces, to understand the secret of his mission. When the staff was cast down, the 'head of wisdom' was written so they would know its order. It was a serpent to hide the whisperings... and on this, it stands and is known that the staff had power on the earth, but its roots were above. Moses was able to make the staff swallow their staves because his source was higher. On this, he performed two signs: one above and one below. One above—that the staff ruled over those 'rectifications.' Pharaoh saw and looked, realizing that the staff ruled on the earth, ruled above, and ruled below." And through the merit of this Unity, they spoke in this language...

<column-break/>

...regarding the existence of the **Tablets**. Therefore, this Moses was the one worthy of receiving the complete Torah through his hand. Everything that elevated his status above other prophets served as a revelation and a wonder regarding the level of this Torah. Moses was prepared, established, and perfected from the power of the vision. 

In the **Midrash Rabbah** on the verse "A good man obtains favor from the Lord" <note>Proverbs 12:2</note>: "Good" refers to the righteous. For others, the "taste" <note>the prophetic flow</note> was interrupted, but for Moses, it was not. Regarding the blessings of Jacob, Ezekiel, and Samuel—the flow was interrupted. But for Moses, the flow was never interrupted. Why? Because he saw the "Two Faces" <note>A reference to a high level of divine encounter</note>, as it is written: "And she saw him, that he was good" <note>Exodus 2:2</note>. 

In the first chapter of Tractate Sotah, on the verse "And she saw him, that he was good," it is taught: **Rabbi Meir** says his name was "Tov" (Good). **Rabbi Yehuda** says his name was "Tuvyah" (God’s Goodness). **Rabbi Nehemiah** says he was born already circumcised. And the Sages say: At the hour he was born, the entire house was filled with light. It is written here: "And she saw him, that he was good," and it is written elsewhere: "And God saw the light, that it was good" <note>Genesis 1:4</note>. 

We intend to clarify that in Moses, the intent of Creation was completed. He was its ultimate purpose. Therefore, he was born perfect in every kind of completion. **Rabbi Meir’s** opinion is that the verse "And she saw him, that he was good" means his very name was "Good." As explained in several places, he was worthy of being called "Good" because the physical part of his body reflected this name; it indicates a thing that is perfect in its essence. The Torah does not usually follow the path of merely giving names, for a name often does not match the thing called, but here it says "that he was good" to show he was perfect in himself and in all his parts. 

It seems to me that the word "Good" was not said during the creation of the first man in the same way, because the intention of creation had not yet been finalized in the formation of the generations. Rather, it says: "And God saw all that He had made, and behold, it was **very good**" <note>Genesis 1:31</note>. This refers to the intent of Creation in its entirety. According to Rabbi Meir, this refers to the ultimate purpose the Creation was destined to achieve, which is the Torah. 

The Sages said: "'Behold, it was very good'—this refers to the Angel of Life; 'and behold, it was very good'—this refers to the Angel of Death." Why is the Angel of Death called "very good"? Using a parable: it is like a king who prepared a feast for his servants and set before them a table full of all good things. He said: "Whoever eats and blesses the King, it shall be well with him. But whoever eats and does not bless the King..." So it is with one who occupies himself with commandments and good deeds; he is called an "Angel of Life." But one who does not... is called an "Angel of Death." 

Thus, the purpose of the spheres is to honor the King, and the purpose of Creation is the collection of commandments and good deeds, which is the Will and desire of God in Creation. This is only possible through the Torah and because of Moses, who was destined to receive it as the ultimate end. Therefore, when he was born, it was said "that he was good," to explain that this "Good" was not merely a physical quality, but a spiritual completion. **Rabbi Yehuda** viewed this "Good" and perfection as a spiritual acquisition, which is why he said his name was "Tuvyah" <note>literally "The Goodness of God"</note>. His intent was that this "Good" is not considered complete unless it ascends entirely to the Glory. 

Because Moses was destined to complete this most exalted perfection possible, it is said his name was "Tuvyah." This represents the love of the Most High through our cleaving <term>Dveikut: the mystical state of 'cleaving' or attachment to the Divine</term> to Him. Moses ascended to this wondrous cleaving, as in the matter of "But as for you, stand here by Me" <note>Deuteronomy 5:27</note>, without any separation or change from that attachment.

It contrasts Moses' unique prophetic "cleaving" (Dveikut) with other prophets, utilizing Midrashic and Talmudic sources to explain his superiority.</summary>

<meta>This page transitions from a discussion on the unique nature of Moses' birth and soul to a broader investigation into the mechanics of divine providence, specifically focusing on the role of human initiative ("Awakening from Below") in triggering heavenly abundance, such as rain and resurrection. # The Section on the Ultimate Purpose
## Chapter 13

The supreme good is to provide rain through the process of **awakening from below** <note>original: "התעוררות מלמטה" — a Kabbalistic concept where human actions on earth trigger a corresponding divine response from above.</note>. This is the secret of the verse: "But a mist went up from the earth" <note>Genesis 2:6</note>, which represents the awakening from below, followed by: "and watered the whole face of the ground." This secret will be further explained based on what we wrote in the fifth chapter regarding the secret of the phrase: "Blessed be the Lord day by day." Just as the fountains of wisdom can be stopped—meaning the flow of sustenance and the "hiddenness of life"—it is said that the "Good" is closed and barred due to the corruption of those below. 

Therefore, one must engage in prayer to awaken **Mercy** <note>original: "הרחמים" — often referring to the divine attribute of Tiferet.</note> above, to repair the corruption, and to open the flow. This necessitates praying for rain even if it has already been promised, as in the phrase "And I will give your rain" <note>Leviticus 26:4</note>. This is because the preservation of the ultimate purpose requires an awakening from below, like a chain reaction. This draws **Kindness** <note>original: "חסד" — Chesed</note> down upon the world in the name of *Hebron* <note>Likely a symbolic reference to "union" (hibur) or a specific mystical location.</note>, joining prayer and petition to the Torah. 

This was necessary because Moses represented the "Lower Foundation" <note>original: "היסודי התחתון"</note> as much as the Upper, and he is the one who "consumes the sacrifices" from upon the altar before the Lord. Similarly, regarding the preservation of life, there was a doubt concerning the "Living Soul" <note>original: "החיה"</note> and the oath "as you have kept them alive," regarding the need for prayer to return and restore souls to their place from their Supernal Source. 

In the Midrash of **Rabbi Shimon bar Yochai** <note>original: "רשב"י" — the traditional author of the Zohar.</note>, they said the following: Rabbi Isaac asked: When is it written "they shall yet increase and rejoice" and "the former heights"? It refers to Jerusalem when her "staff returns to her hand" due to the greatness of days. When she praises her "Constellation" <note>original: "מזל" — Mazal</note>, then the staff is in her hand. Rather, Rabbi Isaac said that the righteous are destined in the future to revive the dead, as it is written: "and his staff shall return to his hand" <note>Reference to 2 Kings 4:29-31</note>. It is also written: "And you shall place my staff upon the face of the youth," yet I did not merit this. Does this mean the righteous want to act on their own to be the "Creator"? This is the sign of the "staff on the face of the youth," where there was "no voice and no response." 

It appears we require two things: prayer and calling out to the Lord. This is because this world is not yet worthy of these high levels due to its fallen state, until the "Future to Come" <note>original: "לעתיד לבא"</note> when the broken pieces shall return to their wholeness and be satisfied according to their will, as they were before the curse of death. Then, the broken will not need to be entrusted to prayer to return the dead, for they will be from the hidden realm and so attached to their Creator that the dead will not even feel their own bones. This is the secret of the "abundance" that will be poured upon them then. 

Moses will return until they merit their inheritance, existing as living souls. How will this matter affect them? It will suffice to revive the dead. We see the reason for this in the story of the man who was revived by touching the bones of the prophet <note>Reference to Elisha in 2 Kings 13:21</note>. He stood up on his feet because there remained within the prophet's bones a residue of the Light and Holiness that revives nature, stemming from the holy body that was refined through the "Living Matter" of eating, until it sufficed to revive whoever touched them. Indeed, the great righteous ones are greater in their death than in their lives. To revive the bones mentioned in the Torah, one must connect through prayer, as it is written: "He went in, therefore, and shut the door... and prayed unto the Lord... and he went up, and lay upon the child, and put his mouth upon his mouth, and his eyes upon his eyes..." <note>2 Kings 4:33-34</note>. While the mere touch of his bones sufficed for the other case, here in the "shrunken and destroyed brain," prayer was required to access the Supernal powers. This was done for the sake of the **Glory** <note>original: "הכבוד" — the Kavod, or Divine Presence.</note>, as we have written elsewhere. This provides a proper reason for why the names of the prophets are associated with their miraculous works.

From what we have written, it will be clarified that the intent of the scripture is not merely to say "whom the Lord knew face to face" <note>Deuteronomy 34:10</note> regarding signs and wonders alone. Heaven forbid we limit it to that! Rather, it refers to the prophets' chosen status and their elevation in degree and their proximity to the Throne, as will be explained in full in the coming chapter.

## Chapter 14

The Torah of the Lord is perfect, founded upon **Supernal Action**, woven and influenced by **Holy Wisdom**. Let it be seen that what exists in the Supernal Will through the "Union of Reception" <note>original: "זיווג הקבלה"</note> will be most complete. Every sphere is drawn until it becomes a messenger for the Almighty's will and His commandments, so that every perfection and virtue may be found within it, and no illness or gathering <unclear>defect</unclear> shall be missing.

<column-break/>

Those who influence, as mentioned in the Name—heaven forbid one should think they descend from heaven initially just for you and your anointed ones. Rather, the spirit descends from heaven to "consume it and its fifty" <note>Reference to Elijah calling down fire in 2 Kings 1:10</note>. Look closely at the "Wonderous Action" where soul bonds with soul; there is no need for speech, such as in the splitting of the Jordan, where it is written that Joshua took his cloak, wrapped it, and struck the water, and they stood up. Similarly, with Elisha healing the "bad waters." 

And who can restore us through the **Names of the Names** <note>Divine Names used in mystical practice.</note> and through swearing by the lower agents in the upper realms? This is done slowly out of respect for the **Glory** <note>The Kavod</note>, which is the "burden" through which we mentioned the language of prayer and crying out to draw down the Will. This draws upon their bodies the "foundation of the Glory within the Glory." 

Like the oath of Elisha, all the created prophets whom the **Glory** created—who are "opposite" to it—act out of respect for the Glory. This is the **Kindness** <note>Chesed</note> that flows upon them from the Supernal Source, because they all recognize the level of the **Intellect** <note>original: "השכל"</note> that is shed upon them from above. Therefore, by the staff of His will, and because of what is within the soul, the prophets were directed to act in the name of wonders—both in deed and in the intellect through prayer. This is not required for the "Perfect Agents" regarding lower matters, which are "extra." To command them to return is done by the "decree of the word," in the bonding of soul to soul as we wrote. These are like the oath of Elisha for the sake of the "Ox" <note>unclear reference, possibly a symbol of strength or a specific angelic face</note>, and his death... and the writing of the "beams and rain" brought down in the days of harvest. 

The **Messiah** is part of the cause of these wonders for the Supernal matters. Time and again, time is drawn toward the movement whose place and foundation is the Celestial Sphere. If so, through the support of time, the Sphere is praised for its movement, which "Sabbaths" time. This is what the Sages, of blessed memory, meant by saying that things depend on the power of the **Constellation** <note>Mazal</note>. The "Holy Torah" in the mouth of the pious was used to call unto the Lord, etc. Because that tranquility exists in the upper realms and in our support of them, it was for the sake of the **Glory** that prayer was necessary, as we explained. 

Also, in the "Writing of the Rain" by **Elijah**, of blessed memory, there was a new wonder. For it was not in its nature to follow the way of rising rain—vapor rising from the earth and descending from below to above. For this, he needed to prostrate himself, as seen in the scriptures: "And Elijah went up to the top of Carmel; and he cast himself down upon the earth, and put his face between his knees" <note>1 Kings 18:42</note>. He said to his servant, "Go up now, look toward the sea..." and he said "Return" seven times. 

One might wonder: why was all this effort needed? For God had told him, "Go, show yourself unto Ahab; and I will send rain upon the earth" <note>1 Kings 18:1</note>. It would be proper that after being promised and given a sign of rain, he should not need the toil and the intense prayer. The scriptures suggest two reasons: first, that Israel had returned [to God] and cried "The Lord, He is God! The Lord, He is God!", and second, that Elijah was sanctified... it was part of God's attribute of Kindness to fulfill His word and give rain immediately after the act of the fire. 

And yet, we do not find among the prophets that they would be praised for something and then still require prayer for it to be established and fulfilled. The answer to this doubt is that we find Elijah praying even earlier when he said, "As the Lord God of Israel lives, before whom I stand, there shall not be dew nor rain these years, but according to my word" <note>1 Kings 17:1</note>. The plain meaning implies he was focused in prayer. When he decreed upon them, there was sufficient power to last... even while all Israel worshipped Baal... but when they cried "The Lord is God," the Supernal influence was restored. When God told him "I will give rain," Elijah prayed to fulfill his oath and to ensure the rain came through the proper channels of prayer. The Rabbi <note>likely Maimonides or another major commentator</note> exempts this... and there is another double reason for the matter, which is to link the chain...

# Chapter 14: The Section on the Ultimate Purpose
## Chapter 15

By the merit of the "Rod of the Torah" <note>This refers to the Torah as a source of power or guidance.</note> from Heaven, as we have written above, and by the merit of the Earth upon which the Torah was given—through which He prepared the secret of their "mouth" for the essences, the secret of the "Way of Life." This is also by the merit of the attribute of the **Kindness of the Name** <note>original: "מדת חסד השם" — The divine attribute of Chesed.</note>, because the Torah was given from the voice of the flame called "Kindness" and "Living Waters." And as it is stated there, by his merit, they joined together in passing through the land, for his face was like the "face of the moon." <note>A traditional comparison where Moses' face is likened to the sun and Joshua's to the moon; here it likely refers to the reflective glory of the prophet.</note>

In this way, the "Crown of the Vessels" <note>likely referring to the spiritual tools or Sefirot</note> dawns upon every unique inquiry, connecting to its root through His Torah, which includes both him and them—their influence and their leadership. From there, his prophecy was woven. All of them, in their excellence and agreement, are sent forth, explaining the secret of the letter *He* from the "Simple Square" <note>A Kabbalistic reference to the four-letter Name of God expanded into ten degrees.</note>—ten levels, each described in its own degree, each according to its own calculation. For "in all My house, he is faithful" <note>Numbers 12:7, referring to Moses.</note>.

Regarding the "Center" of Rabbi Saadia Gaon <note>Saadia Gaon (882–942) was a foundational Jewish philosopher and linguist.</note> (may he rest in peace), here Judah says regarding the "Oven" <note>The text here is likely a corruption of a philosophical term for the "Source" or "Central Fire."</note>... it is possible to be praised in ten ways, as it is written: "In all My house, he is faithful." It does not say "My house" alone; the word "Silver" <note>original: "כסף" — possibly a metaphor for desire or refinement.</note> adds to the matter. All of this is forgiven him, to be tested by those who seek internal enlightenment through him, as we have written.

**Kindness and its Concept:**
Nachmanides <note>Rabbi Moses ben Nachman (1194–1270), also known as Ramban.</note> (of blessed memory) wrote in the portion of *Ki Tisa* that it is possible for the Torah and tradition to be a hand... I have explained it as "Kindness." According to what I have concluded later, your mind should know that from him to another, "Kindness" knew the Lord "face to face." For the Torah preceded the creation of the world, according to the tradition of our Sages, and it was entirely written in **black fire upon white fire.** <note>A famous midrashic image suggesting the Torah's essence is spiritual light, with the letters being "black fire" and the parchment "white fire."</note> This "Kindness" represents the reception of the ultimate understanding before the eyes of all Israel, learned from the mouth of the "Almighty" <note>original: "הגבורה" — Gevurah, often used as a synonym for God in this context.</note>. The Rav <note>referring to Nachmanides</note> (of blessed memory) already wrote at the beginning of his commentary on the Torah that Moses was like a scribe copying from an ancient book.

This script is meant to clarify that the inheritance of the "Staff" is the great trial of Will and the unique "Shining Face," doubling life and goodness. His life and "Kindness" knew the Lord "face to face." No man has reached this level since the day man was created. This is known from what preceded our words and will be further clarified in Chapter 22.

Regarding "all the signs and wonders," the Rav <note>Maimonides</note> (of blessed memory) wrote that it is a compelling proof that there never arose in Israel a prophet like Moses in all the signs. This is to say that he "knew the Lord face to face" through those signs and wonders. According to what was mentioned, there are two reasons: the "Tablets" and the "Possessions." Just as the "Almighty" by its power made the staff unique... so too in his signs and wonders, which included his knowledge. There has not arisen one like him, as we mentioned earlier.

<column-break/>

The error and the custom that occur in leadership: in every generation, the knowledge of the "Scholars of Inquiry" <note>Philosophers/theologians who use logic and observation.</note> changes, and the later ones always disagree with the earlier ones. The ancients thought they had found the "Ultimate Proof" for their investigation, while the later ones found an "Ultimate Proof" for its opposite.

Regarding what our Sages (of blessed memory) wrote specifically, everything Nachmanides wrote... he wrote that all of them were "cut off." Everything said about all that exists under the "Sphere of the Moon" <note>The sublunary realm in Aristotelian physics, which was considered the realm of change and decay.</note> at the center of the Earth is true beyond doubt. However, the author of the *Perush* <note>Commentary</note> disagreed with what was mentioned regarding what is above the Sphere of the Moon.

The scholar Rabbi Isaac Abravanel <note>A 15th-century statesman and philosopher.</note> (of blessed memory) elaborated on this in his commentary on the Book of Kings, in the portion regarding the buildings of Solomon. "Who would believe his report?" regarding how he disagreed with those flawed words. It is known that the simple element is close to the fundamental element, and it does not enter the "Wisdom of Powers" except in small measure.

Some scholars believe they can act through natural means in natural ways, as we have heard concerning the Sages of Israel. This is proof that they knew and achieved wisdom in all its "Inclusion" and the "Chariot" <note>original: "מרכבה" — Ma'aseh Merkavah, early Jewish mysticism.</note> and the "Kingdom." Their knowledge and wisdom are not of the same type as the "Greek Wisdom" <note>Aristotelian philosophy</note> which is based on victory and logic.

It is well known that the "Guide of the Perplexed" <note>Maimonides (Rambam)</note> (of blessed memory) at the beginning of his work stated that there is no wisdom in Israel except for the Greek wisdom... but this loss of the later generations was in the "Intellects." It is impossible for them to know this perfection... whether in natural, mathematical, or divine sciences, in the way the Greeks knew them. They all went according to their reasons in the Talmud and commandments, but did not reach the knowledge of the Sages in natural matters... like the matter of the "King in his Palace" <note>A famous parable from Maimonides' Guide for the Perplexed (3:51) describing different levels of closeness to God.</note>.

He also mentions the opinions of the Chaldeans and the Sages of Egypt and how he came to explain the words of the Torah and the "Hiders" <note>Those who hide secrets.</note> so they would agree with their opinions. But we have chosen to explain that our nation is a nation of Truth and Wisdom, as it is said: "Surely this great nation is a wise and understanding people" <note>Deuteronomy 4:6</note>. But when the wicked of the flawed religions thought to consume our Sages... our wisdom and understanding were hidden, and we became mixed among them. Just as the kingdom was uprooted from us, we were "mixed among the nations and learned their works." <note>Psalm 106:35</note> So it was said concerning the copying of flawed opinions. When we were raised on the knees of the "Fathers of the Flawed," the philosophical matters became to us as if they were the firstfruits of our Torah, but the matter is not so.

Many of the later scholars agreed and revealed this. Among them was the scholar Rabbi Joseph ben Shem Tov <note>A 15th-century Spanish Jewish philosopher.</note> (of blessed memory), who, despite being very clean and righteous in philosophy, wrote in his book *Ein HaKoreh* as follows: "It is proper to ask of you and give a correct reason why the Sages held onto it..."

### Chapter 15

It will be clarified in what follows that the intellect is tied to the choice of his hand. To the Greeks and the flawed ones, perfection is merely their vitality. It has already been explained in many places in this book that the **Ultimate Purpose** of the soul is its permanence and the raising of the **Will of its Creator**. This was the intention in its creation. In this part, we wrote that the Holy Will cannot be known through philosophical inquiry or custom. If it were a matter of chance, then "the righteous would be the foundations." Through their philosophical inquiry and their intellect, they think they reach the Will itself, but they are far from the Supreme Will. All they strive for in their goodness, they remain ignorant of, adding only distance from Him.

# Chapter 14: The Section on the Ultimate Purpose
## Chapter 14

<margin>
Numbers Rabbah, end of the portion of Shelach, Part 80.
</margin>

...in all the earth and among all the nations, etc. And it says that although we see wonders and great, awesome deeds performed by his successor after this time, the scale of those he performed previously was infinitely greater than those performed afterward. All this was intended to show that whatever Joshua, the disciple, performed, it was as if he lacked his own independent prophecy; rather, he performed wonders through the power he received from Moses. From this point forward, all other prophets are compared to him, and all their prophecy and power were what they received from him, as they revealed what they heard through the wonders of his prophecy. It was said of them that the day they were created was more wonderful than anything Moses did, even though they followed his inheritance and likeness. 

The Sages said: **"The face of Moses was like the face of the sun, and the face of Joshua was like the face of the moon."** <note>A classic Rabbinic metaphor from the Talmud (Bava Batra 75a) explaining that Joshua’s leadership was a reflection of Moses’ greater light.</note> Just as the light of the moon is not its own and it has no illumination except that which the sun reflects upon it, so too was the prophecy of Joshua and the prophecy of all other prophets. Everything they revealed of the wonders of prophecy was entirely handed down according to the capacity and power of Moses. Therefore, it is fitting to attribute everything to him. 

However, what Moses himself did is not comparable to any other prophet, for no prophet before him reached his level, nor did any after him. It seems to me that when it says, "Before all your people I will do wonders," it refers to the opening of the darkness and the swallowing of the earth <note>Refers to the rebellion of Korah in Numbers 16, where the earth "created" a mouth to swallow the rebels.</note>. This is what is meant by "which have not been created," for it says, "If the Lord creates a new thing" <note>Numbers 16:30</note>, using the language of "creation" <term>Beriah</term> <note>original: "בריאה" — In Jewish thought, this refers to "creation ex nihilo," something entirely new in the world.</note>. These wonders were related to the very creation of the world, as it is written: "there is nothing like it." This was the essence of that vision and wonder. Therefore, it is written: "wonders which have not been created in all the earth and among all the nations," to inform us that this wonder would be greater than all the wonders performed by his hand, or that would ever be performed by his hand or anyone else's. 

And therefore He said, "I am doing this with you," because this was a testimony to his perfection and prophecy. Likewise, everything written regarding the excellence of other prophets was great, yet they eventually passed away. But "there has not arisen another prophet in Israel like Moses," whom the Lord knew face to face. 

The path should be understood as follows: because the level of Moses’ prophecy was the ultimate level of the Torah, his prophetic visions served as evidence of the Torah's excellence. It was impossible for anyone, at any time—past or future—to stand at his level. This is the intent of the phrase "there has not arisen" <note>original: "ולא קם"</note>. The word "arisen" applies to both the past and the future; since the Torah is the absolute truth, it says that even though many will arise until the end of time, none will reach his level. This was necessary for Moses due to the excellence of the Torah. 

In the likeness of Rabbi Shimon bar Yochai <note>Rashbi, the traditional author of the Zohar.</note>, he speaks of these divisions, for of him it is written that he surpassed other prophets, but he specifically spoke of these wonders. Therefore, he was "anointed with the oil of joy" <note>Psalm 45:7</note> from the source of the prophets. These words include all who came before him and all who came after him—none were at his level. This is the intent of "there has not arisen" in the Holy Spirit. 

This matter depends on the degrees of the Torah. We benefit from a place that no other prophet's soul has benefited from. Each of the prophets attained a level of prophecy and perception according to the refinement of his soul, and each was attached to his root through his Torah, drawing his prophecy from there. But the high degree of Moses' level surpassed all other prophets because his soul and light were above the level of the forms of other prophets. This is what the early Sages received: that the "form" of Moses was grasped from the "Great Luminary" that ascends to the heights without limit. Therefore, it is correct...

<column-break/>

<margin>
Chapter 7 of the "Eight Chapters" <note>Maimonides' introduction to the Ethics of the Fathers.</note> explains the distinction in levels between the prophecy of Moses and the prophecy of other prophets.
</margin>

...regarding the addition of the eighteen extra parts... and his portion is for the world and his portion is for eternity. And because of this, Israel did not rejoice from the day... why? 

Regarding the plague of the "Swarms" <term>Arob</term>, they said this language implies things coming from the west and the east as one. All the "Holy Beings" <note>original: "בני קדש" — likely referring to angelic classes like the Chayot.</note> are like the "Holy Living Creatures" of the Chariot forever, and all those subordinates are made holy like spaces in a single hand. They were for the Lord, and it was upon them to wrap themselves. They gave and bestowed wisdom to the disciple of wisdom, for "wisdom is lost from its wise men," etc. And it is written, "I have forgotten my foundation" in the Twelve Prophets... for those heavenly hosts are appointed above over the matters below. 

Regarding the plague of the "Firstborns," they said: every firstborn is dedicated to the service and the ritual of the colleagues... Behold, through these we see that a plague among the lower beings was also intended for the "Supernal Beings" <note>Angelic or celestial powers.</note> appointed over them. A strike upon the lower foundation was a prevention of the "Mazzal" <note>original: "מזל" — a constellation or spiritual channel of influence.</note> appointed over it, removing it from its task. Correspondingly, among the spiritual beings above who are appointed over the lower ones, each was disturbed and removed from their dominion and gaze, all to show Pharaoh and Egypt that there is a Ruler above the supernal beings and the lower beings. 

For this reason, it was necessary to perform wonders among the lower beings and correspondingly among the supernal beings, so they would recognize that He created everything and everything is in His hand to humble them and to show His will. As we said previously, we have already written that the relationship of the "Ministers" <term>Sarim</term> <note>Spiritual patrons of the nations.</note> is such that even the diminishments they suffer through the attribute of Kindness are attributed to that Kindness, for He is their God. 

One should not say that other prophets were greater than Moses because they performed wonders in the supernal realms while he performed them below. This is the opposite of what we have written. Just as in the days of Moses, he was greater than other prophets in the level of prophecy, so too they did not equal him in the level of wonders. Especially as the scripture says, "and they also did" <note>Exodus 7:11, referring to the Egyptian magicians.</note>, while regarding Israel and Moses it says, "for all the signs and wonders," etc. As will be clarified, they exist according to the first Existence (Blessed be He), for others do not equal him, as "the face of Moses was the face of [the sun]." 

Even according to the second existence, although other prophets acted upon wonders in the supernal realms, they do not equal the quality of Moses in height and origin. For the truth is that Moses' power was "Universal/General" <term>Kollalut</term> from the Heavens, known to the "wise of heart," as will be explained. Also, in his days, [wonders came] from those Heavens, while in the days of Joshua they passed through the Earth. The secret of all this will be explained from the level of each one’s prophecy. 

The general rule of his humility is that he was hidden from them for forty years. Also, the pillar of fire and the pillar of cloud—what other prophecies are as great as these? He reached a level above this, which was not shown even to the knowledge of the "Stranger" <note>likely referring to non-prophets or those outside the covenant</note>. This was from the mouth of my teacher, regarding the prophets and the supernal beings, as will be clarified from the words of Rabbi Shimon bar Yochai (Rashbi). 

Furthermore, the day [at Sinai] was unlike any before or after it, when we stood before the Lord our God to hear the Holy Voice, the voices of prophecies. That which was written regarding the Standing at the Voices <note>The Revelation at Sinai.</note> is more wonderful and greater than any measurable vision. Remember what was renewed in the heavens and the earth through the hand of the Prophet [Moses], more so than through the hand of all other prophets, peace be upon them. 

Moreover, all the wonders performed later, even by others, are attributed to the "First One" who began to open the source of performing wonders through the stars. For he is the known "Striker." The first one through whom the Great Name was created to act upon the famous waters... this was an additional branch to the excellence of prophecies. If so, everything Joshua and the other prophets did from the "Seventy Elders" is all attributed to Moses our Teacher, for he is the ultimate doer. As is explicitly stated: "Behold, I make a covenant: before all your people I will do wonders such as have not been created in all [the earth]..."
