# Chapter 15: The Section on the Ultimate Purpose
## Chapter 15

It shall be made known to all men, as is known from the foundations of the exclusive properties belonging to unique individuals, just as I have chosen for you from their statement: **"One does not hand over the secrets of the Torah except to a counselor and one who is wise in crafts."** <note>Original Hebrew: "Ein mosrin sitrei Torah ela le-yoetz ve-hacham." This is a quote from the Babylonian Talmud, Tractate Chagigah 13a, emphasizing that mystical knowledge must be restricted to those with high intellectual and moral character.</note> This is the necessary reason for the cessation of these pleasant orders from the Nation; nothing remains of them except small points of interest and hints that appear in the Talmud and the Midrashim, and even those are but a few grains of husks. They are like soft shells, so much so that men delved into these small shells and thought there was no "heart" <note>Meaning an inner core or spiritual essence.</note> beneath them at all. This continued until those philosophers followed us, all of whom are damaging in the words of the philosophers, and they inclined toward their views—which was not permitted within the community of the religion of the servant and the messenger. <note>Referring to Moses as the servant of God.</note> For the portion of the philosophers is distinct from ours, as there was never a sect or a wisdom that was not given to Jacob; for in garments <note>likely meaning the "outer layers" or metaphors</note> were the Torah and its stories for the assembly of the Lord.

As will be explained in the chapters following this, God willing, the hints and allusions that appear in the Talmud and Midrashim did not come to hint at what the Rabbi <note>referring to Maimonides, the author of the *Guide for the Perplexed*</note> attained and what entered his mind to choose and explain, as will be clarified with the utmost explanation to one who understands the Rabbi’s intent. Such a person will see and understand what is explained in them according to the details of the true wisdom received from us. Since the Rabbi did not begin by following his own opinion or forming theories when he started his words—theories which would not fall under the hand of the intellect at all, for some are far above it—it is impossible for a vision of such greatness to be achieved by a human mind alone.

The Oral Torah was not permitted to be written down for the reason the Rabbi stated, but it is a sublime study. At the beginning of the third part <note>of the *Guide for the Perplexed*</note>, he said that the Sages' statement regarding the degrees of the secrets of the Torah, which are explained and mentioned to the masters of speculation, is very distressing. They said at the end of the verse regarding what Isaiah wrote: **"Before the Lord shall be their sustenance, to eat to fullness and for a stately covering"** <note>Isaiah 23:18</note>—the Sages said: **"for a stately covering"** <term>me-khasseh atik</term> refers to things that the **Ancient of Days** <note>Atik Yomin, a name for God</note> covered. If these secrets of the Torah regarding God were brought before men, what we said is that the Ancient of Days hid them so that the masters of speculation might attain them through their inquiry. 

Later, he <note>Maimonides</note> found a place of permission to rely on his own opinion regarding the secrets of the Torah, the "Work of Creation" (*Ma'aseh Bereshit*) and the "Work of the Chariot" (*Ma'aseh Merkavah*), which in his view are the **Science of Nature** <note>Physics</note> and the **Science of what is after Nature** <note>Metaphysics</note>, following the Greeks and their heretical groups. But this was not the intention of the Sages when they said He "hid" them. Rather, they meant to inform us that it is impossible for the intellect to grasp the secrets of the Torah—and certainly not for a common person—until the Ancient of Days Himself arises with him, and He is the one who hides them. 

The Sages also said that there are names written in the Torah that were hidden, and according to this, the inquiry of the masters of speculation is still hidden from them. And in the chapter "One does not expound" <note>Tractate Chagigah, Chapter 2</note>, it is said: **"One does not hand over the secrets of the Torah except to one who has a heart that worries within him"** and to a **"master of crafts"** (*hacham charashim*) and **"one who understands a whisper"** (*nevon lachash*). All of this is what the Rabbi explained, saying that those who are skilled in powerful deeds are called "masters of crafts" because their portions were all made in silence (*cherashim*) and are not matters revealed or forced upon the masters of speculation. From this, it follows that one called a "master of crafts" has ascended to the level of perfect speculation, and then he is prepared for the tradition of the secrets of the Torah. He, in his strength, attains it based on the statement **"One does not hand over,"** which implies it is impossible for any intellect to grasp them unless he is great in speculation and holiness, and they are handed over to him mouth to mouth. 

After the Sages of blessed memory distinguished this, they were careful with the Name. This agreement was hidden from the collective of the Children of Israel. This is why the Jews are confused, for those who took grains from there found it was revealed and famous to the gentiles, the Samaritans, and the Christians. This will be clear to whoever understands the Rabbi’s intent and his explanation of the Name. See that his explanation is truly known, for the Rabbi’s details regarding the secrets of the Torah, the "Work of Creation," and the "Work of the Chariot" are far from them. He himself admitted this in the introduction to the third part, though not truly as I have said, to inform us of the preparation of speculation.

<column-break/>

**"In all My house, he is faithful"** <note>Numbers 12:7</note>, and **"There has not arisen a prophet since in Israel like Moses..."** <note>Deuteronomy 34:10</note>. If a person had a mind like his mind, and wisdom like his wisdom, and an attainment in the matter like his attainment, he could distinguish between the holy and the profane, and between the pure and the impure. Yet, even with all this, he needed to receive that which was impossible for him to attain despite the breadth of his mind. Even a thing learned from our own mouths—for the intellect desires to attain what is above it—the disputes and differences among the philosophers in their opinions, their investigations, and their intellectual proofs are sufficient for us to know their true nature. They are far removed from sensory experience and the clarification of things. The philosophical matters will become known to us; they have no portion or memorial in them.

What is even more bitter and evil is what appears from his <note>Maimonides’</note> words in the 63rd chapter of the first part, where he seems to lack a vision of the "Greatness" <note>the Divine</note> despite being perfect in logic and the like. For he took all that he merited in the end, because his prayer was lacking... <unclear>textual corruption</unclear>... there is a difference in the world regarding the "All." Afterward, he says that it is "Kingdom" (*Malkhut*), and he says something else about the division. It entered the mind of the Rabbi that the existence of God is a proof for him, whether by tradition or whether the enlightened one lacked evidence. The Rabbi then provided another understanding—this is the "Wisdom," meaning the **Necessary Existent**. This lack brings to him the logical necessity that there is a Necessary Existent, neither absent nor defined. When he intends the proofs with which he establishes the existence of the All-Wise, all is doubt. For in the Rabbi's view, one needed to learn from the mouth of prophecy the proofs and demonstrations with which to establish His existence, for he would not know them otherwise. 

How could he say, "What shall I say of the division?" For if he had known them, peace be upon him, there is no doubt he would have been compelled to admit to his prophecy, as there are no proofs of His existence except through clear intellectual demonstrations. In the Rabbi's view, he knew them then, and in his view, the power of Moses' proof was improved, for he established the existence of God through demonstration. Perhaps those proofs of God's existence are what he learned from the mouth of prophecy, referring to the "forged" matter according to one view, to prove that these are heard truths. If so, the scripture describes him as not being perfect in logic. Yet the Rabbi himself, in the chapters on Prophecy, established that perfection in ethics and logic is required above all else. He said that the intent of the saying **"Prophecy only rests upon one who is wise, mighty, and rich"** refers to this. After this inherited perfection, one who was destined to answer the calls of prophecy would not be hindered by any general thing. 

The Rabbi established that this "loss" should not be attributed to Israel, who had received traditions from the Patriarchs, saying they would doubt the existence of God. In my opinion, the love of wisdom and the tradition was lost from them due to the necessity of their exile, as it was said: **"The wisdom of its wise men shall perish"** <note>Isaiah 29:14</note> during our exile. It then appeared in the house of study of the Greeks, and the order of the philosophers made it known. 

This was already preceded in Chapter 71 of Part 1, where he said: "Know that the many sciences which existed in our nation regarding the truth of these matters perished with the passage of time and the loss of the traditional walls around us." Since these matters were not permitted to be revealed to everyone, as we have explained, the only thing permitted to all people was the text of the books alone. You already know that even the **Received Talmud** was not composed in a book in earlier times due to the principle spread throughout the nation: **"Words I have told you orally, you are not permitted to write down."** <note>Gittin 60b</note>. This exile caused the Torah, which was truly in Babylon, to eventually have many opinions, hidden meanings, and enduring doubts regarding the explanation of the composition. The author's intent was forgotten, leading to constant dispute among men, and it suffered from the ignorance and stumbling of the few. This thing is not in your great heart, as we explained in the end of the *Al-Muzi* <note>Likely referring to a specific work or commentary</note>. They hinted that the matter of the Torah would be brought... and if the Talmud was entirely received from the scattered ones to be made public and famous to all men, why did we turn away? He said, it is a crime for one to sell any of these secrets of the Torah.

Because this investigation and the awakening restraint—this mention of the seven—shall be explained in the *Book of Prophecy* <note>original: "Sefer ha-Navuv," likely a transcription error for "Sefer ha-Nevuah," Maimonides' lost or projected work on prophecy</note> and its explanation according to its strength in the *Book of the Torah*. These actions are not held to be given to the sages, for they are not for the destructive <note>original: "le-makhlim"</note>. For this reason, the teacher concluded that this indicates the greatness of your proficiency in the **inner wisdoms**—meaning the **mathematical, natural, and divine sciences**—for these are the various parts of **theoretical philosophy**, as the **Philosopher** <note>Aristotle</note> explains at the beginning of the second book of the *Metaphysics* <note>original: "Sefer ha-Nev," likely referring to the *Metaphysics* or *De Anima*</note>, and as our holy teacher <note>likely Maimonides</note> said of him, that he is the most exalted, etc. Because of them, clouds begin... a little of the end of the enduring. For many will be satisfied to ask from what the moon descends... and who knew it, who was wiser in natural matters, or his wisdom, or Hillel and his like. Most of the sages of Israel possessed a wisdom that was more complete, and it remained strong until the time of its destruction <note>Referring to the destruction of the Temple and the loss of oral traditions</note>. 

For this reason, **Averroes** <note>original: "Ben Rushd," the famous 12th-century Andalusian Muslim philosopher</note> was lacking in his commentary on the book of **Physics** <note>original: "Sefer ha-Teva"</note>, for everything the ancients wrote before his wisdom is not worthy of being tested by a **demonstration** <note>term: "Mofet" (Logical/Mathematical Proof)</note> according to the principles that established his law of explanation. Why did he desire the section of change to descend to the truly natural, in natural and internal matter? According to his interpretation, they showed you until the beginning to say: Hear! For his wisdom completed the science and the investigation. Most of the sages acted toward him in this manner and called him the "Second Beginner" after the matter of his wisdom. This is from a composition for whoever desires the books of the ancients... the dullness of the investigation into the crafts of the **wisdoms of the Torah**. 

It is a far-fetched thing that all his affairs would live with a sage who is established in the sciences... **natural philosophy**... and it shall not grow great in this latter time, the investigation of the depths, our stories. They have weak and forged claims regarding this, for from the day the land went into exile, there has not been found in Israel a man of greatness, a sage established in these matters like him. And the **House of God** <note>original: "Beit El," perhaps referring to a specific scholar or the Temple structure</note> said: it is not worthy to think thoughts only about this day. They thought they possessed wisdom after the recognition of this wisdom was given to the sages... and that they were a strange nation to say they were attached to knowledge, and his generation, and this is their wisdom, and this is his folly for tomorrow. For the **Chariot of Ezekiel** and Isaiah <note>term: "Ma'aseh Merkavah" (The Work of the Chariot), the highest form of Jewish mysticism involving visions of the Divine throne</note> is missing from our day... the hidden thing shall be proven, and this is a small part of the wisdom of our sages. This is revealed to whoever splits the investigation into the books of the Torah according to our chapters... and looked at the time of the beginning of the sages until they were all covered... Ezekiel... known to most of the sages of the **Kuzari** <note>referring to the classic work by Judah Halevi</note> and the excellent ones, and the more he lives, the more he is considered clean of error according to his opinion... Ezekiel. This is clear to whoever understands the scripture, but he hinted at it by saying: "And I have made the voice known" in an explanation, for because of his honor I permitted him to mention it. Remember the sage who interpreted the **Spirit of the Lord**... he who clarifies his eyes had a mistaken book before him, and they interpreted the entire word... that it was regarding the making of laws and judgments, and they returned... and established in his Torah... for **"it is your wisdom and your understanding in the sight of the nations."** <note>A quote from Deuteronomy 4:6, used to argue that the Torah contains the highest forms of philosophy</note> 

And the Rabbi of blessed memory, in his words... after fortune, for in the streets he fled, he strove to give a reason and a proper taste to this selection, and he aimed well and interpreted... for it was not from before him to be a return to the intent... and for my heart in general in his interpretation of all of them. Therefore, I said: Remember our memory. And this is because they said: "And who hid it?"... to learn... a taste for the matter because "the voice of your wisdom and your understanding," etc. For when the nations see that his wisdom is holy to the Lord... because in poverty the portion of the statutes... and he shall give... he was like a child who knew the living God and knew how to please Him with strength... a writing greater than this. For he looked and his hand was heavy in this great matter... for his desire was the ultimate purpose in the *Book of Life* <note>original: "Sefer ha-Chayim"</note> to know the laws of the constant... and their cause... and the laws and investigation of many sources. And he said great doubts and exaggerated in speaking of it in the distance, if you had heard...

...for in the existence of the world in the branch and in the writing in the form of the [logical] flow, his investigations to the end... as ten and ten of Israel used to do in beautiful grace... wrapped in a **Prayer Shawl** <note>original: "Tallit"</note> and they called the Lord with the **Twenty-Four Attributes** <note>original: "K"D Middot," likely referring to the 13 attributes of mercy or a variation involving the 24 books of the Bible</note> and the mention of the **Seven Blessings** <note>original: "Sheva Berakhot"</note> which the sages established... as explained in the Tractate... and according to the plain meaning... to say "The Lord... His spirit"... and behold, the earth is small... blessings... the truth of the waters and they were waters in hours... they would hold to a single sage.

Behold, these are the famous matters and accepted traditions... and the pouring out of our [wisdom] is an existence... for the Lord was with His people... and he would hold back. He who acts to test us with a great pen and his knowledge in the **craft of the stars** <note>term: "Melekhet ha-Kokhavim" (Astronomy/Astrology)</note> and the knowledge of the constellations... as was done by the ancients, like Josephus **Ben Gorion** <note>original: "Ben Gorion," referring to the medieval "Josippon" history book attributed to Josephus</note> according to what is in the tradition. He who delves deep to decide the majority of his dialectical reasoning in **Divine Wisdom** <note>term: "Chokhmah ha-Elohit" (Metaphysics)</note> and the abundance of our habit in the knowledge of the cause of the ultimate purpose of the **Separate Intellects** <note>term: "Sekhalim ha-Nivdalim" (The incorporeal angels or planetary intelligences of medieval philosophy)</note> and their fullness and the paths of their subjugation and the connection... and the manner of complete understanding... as mentioned all of this... to publicize the powers of the decree... that wisdom deepened... for he would speak of these in visions and in riddles, like the investigations of his secrets... to the philosopher...

# Chapter 17 ## The Section on the Ultimate Purpose

To attain a clear language for himself, so that he might explain the book *Pardes Bar Perach* <note>The title likely refers to a "Garden of Flowering," a common metaphor for Kabbalistic or philosophical inquiry</note> according to the various parts, clarifying from his right hand <note>a metaphor for strength or primary focus</note> all the matters of the language of beauty. They brought his statement according to the wisdom of the Greeks, for this was distinct in the German language <note>original: "Ashkenaz"</note>. And he said, "I do not remember the language of Morso" etc., and they replied that "Greek wisdom" refers to something else entirely—not the spoken language, but rather the **scientific wisdom**, specifically the **wisdom of astronomy**. Regarding the slight slighting of Greek wisdom that was mentioned concerning Rabban Gamaliel <note>A leading 1st-century sage and head of the Sanhedrin</note> and his household, it was explained that they were "close to the monarchy" <note>The Roman authorities</note> and therefore spoke in the "Greek wisdom" used in the king's palace. This is not at all the same as the **theoretical sciences**, which are for everyone.

Thus, the complaint mentioned by the earlier ones—that the Torah is the completion for every Jew, so why is there a need for these other sciences—is answered. These sciences are necessary for human perfection; for a person must be a "perfected human" <note>possessing universal reason and ethics</note> before being a "perfected Jew." This is both appropriate and mandatory. Afterward, he compared the situation to a father and so on. There was a fear regarding "Greek wisdom" that it would lead to idleness, as Ishmael saw it as a wisdom without utility, and studying it was a matter of wasting one's time and life. 

The reason for learning it is that any matter permitted for study should not be studied without purpose. The answer is that it has already been clarified that there is no truth received outside of that wisdom. There is no doubt of its truth, just as the believer knows that the words of wisdom do not contradict the matters of religion in any absolute way. The **Master** <note>Maimonides (the Rambam)</note>, may his memory be a blessing, already elaborated on the matters of the world's composition. If these early opinions were known, they would not be considered "wisdom" at all, for true things are brought forth through wisdom, through the power of wisdom and demonstration. 

However, because of the "evil neighbors" <note>corrupting influences or poor teachers</note> who mislead, we have already replied that this does not stem from the wisdom itself, but from the poor disposition and lack of character of those individuals. It is impossible for sages to be found who have not delved deeply into the **wisdom of the Torah**, for if they knew its secrets and principles, and only then engaged slightly in the theoretical sciences, the perfection of the intellectual would not escape their hearts. They would remain steadfast on both sides. These are the students mentioned by the Sages who "did not serve their masters sufficiently" <note>A Talmudic phrase describing students who learned facts but not the deeper reasoning or character of their teachers</note>. Regarding them, the verse says: "Catch for us the foxes" <note>Song of Songs 2:15, often interpreted as a warning against those who spoil the "vineyard" of wisdom</note>. For I have found a grievance from the words of the **Rambam** <note>Maimonides</note>, that the truths and perfections based on the "Ancient Orator" <note>Aristotle</note> would lead to doubts and confusion. One should not be concerned by this, for they are negated by their small number. As for the "many" who were in doubt, it is according to what the Sages said: "Students who did not serve sufficiently..." 

One should not prevent any student, for a small amount of wisdom is necessary alongside the community. Regarding the statement that one should not teach Torah to a student who is not "proper," as they expounded on the verse "As clear as the day," the honor is not for the person but for the **Torah itself**, the honor of the sages and their greatness. 

<column-break/>

The judgment is given not to neglect the Divine Eloquence, which is the most exalted. For in his soul, a person speaks if he aims to achieve the path of the righteous in depth. This is the explanation brought by the **Master** <note>Maimonides</note> regarding "The Holy Rabbi" <note>Rabbi Judah the Prince, editor of the Mishnah</note>. How could it be that another good man would not be found? It was not out of anger toward the sages, but rather out of the master's concern to distinguish the "other good man." For a powerful guide leads to two outcomes: because the intellect is the doubt of the action. That which is intellectual in action is nothing but the intellect itself. For example: in the case of a house being built, the action is the finished house, but the intellect is what conceived the house. One first conceptualizes the house, then builds the house as necessitated by that thought. 

Thus, when one understands and conceptualizes first, if the house was built according to the way it was conceptualized, then one is considered a "wise builder." What existed before was the thought, and the action follows. Thus, you see that the action begins the intellect in a simple way and completes the whole. It is appropriate that the action be performed first. Man is a "speaking living being" <note>the standard medieval definition of a human: a rational animal</note>; the intellect begins to be formed from the imaginative and developmental faculties. Therefore, one who weighs things in his intellect should first know the laws of the **speaking soul** <note>the human rational faculty</note> and then move to the other parts.

Therefore, a Jewish person, as a believer, possesses a nature similar to what proceeds from his faith. He should start with the first form, which is simpler, and grow in his faith. Thus, we find that the stories of the Torah are the primary language that follows the course of nature. The "Israeli" community is elevated first by the "Covenant of Man" and then perfected by the "Jewish Law" which he believes in. It is appropriate for every Jew to begin first with the perfection of his upbringing and his parables, so that he understands the tradition and the principles of faith. Afterward, he should strive as much as possible in the **theoretical sciences** <note>Philosophy, physics, etc.</note> according to his ability. Then, he should strive even more in wisdom as a Jew, with the Torah as his priority. 

He should not have too much leisure to turn to other parts, for this is the **true and straight path**. One who does the opposite will already find his intentions distorted. Those who delve into the "simple" without the "theoretical" will find that their hands are filled with confusion and errors because they did not suffice themselves with the secrets of the faith. Therefore, the Sages of old made a decree and said: "One should not study theoretical sciences until he knows the ways of faith." This is what they meant by saying: "One should not enter the **Pardes** <note>The Orchard of esoteric/philosophical wisdom</note> until he has filled his belly with bread and meat"—which refers to the study of the **Divine Torah** before other studies.

The conclusion is that it is appropriate for every inquiring person striving to attain theoretical sciences to seek a teacher who is an expert in the truths of the Torah's secrets. Such a teacher can tell his students, when they reach difficult questions in their research that do not agree with the principles of Torah and religion: "This inquiry is an error, its end is loss." For if the teacher is not an expert in these matters, the student will only hear the inquiries of the philosophers. 

The meaning is not that investigation is forbidden. It has already been explained that what was forbidden was "Greek Wisdom," which is different from the **wisdom of investigation and speculation**. The latter is not "Greek Wisdom" but rather **human and universal wisdom**. It is even more appropriate for Israel, who are a "wise and discerning people." 

Consider what **Solomon**, peace be upon him, said. He composed three books: *Proverbs*, *Ecclesiastes*, and *Song of Songs*, corresponding to the levels of wisdom. Solomon was given three names: **Solomon, Kohelet, and Jedidiah**. "Solomon" corresponds to the Seven Wisdoms <note>The Liberal Arts</note>; "Kohelet" <note>The Preacher</note> refers to the gathering of the elements and their composition <note>Natural science/Physics</note>; and "Jedidiah" <note>Beloved of God</note> refers to the truth of one who knows and attains the Divine, who is a "friend" to the Creator. 

Furthermore, "Fear of the Lord" is the beginning of the matter. Fear of God is the **Divine Wisdom**. Know that the "Fear of the Lord" mentioned by the sages of our nation is not an empty or simple fear, but a fear rooted in the truth of investigation. For Divine Wisdom removes a person from worldly imaginings and brings him to the perfection of the intellect without doubt. Through it, one resembles the Creator. He should strive for the attainment of the body in a way that allows for the intellect, fulfilling the verse: "My words shall be... etc." as I said above. He should strive to be upright and compassionate toward creatures, to be merciful and gracious, and all the attributes that lead to perfection. This is the **true ultimate purpose**.

Finally, he proved the truth of wisdom at the end of his words. Each person is defined by their intellect, and the intellect is expressed through intellectual actions. Intellectual actions consist of the understanding of the sciences. Investigation through demonstration is what one strives for at the end; thus, one must learn wisdom.

<summary>This page argues that while specific "Greek sophistry" was historically discouraged, universal theoretical sciences are essential for human perfection and do not contradict the Torah. It emphasizes a structured educational path: starting with Torah and faith ("filling the belly with bread and meat") before advancing to the "Pardes" of philosophical investigation.</summary>

# The Section on the Ultimate Purpose

### Chapter 10

And the explanation in our name according to the Torah as it is, and specifically regarding the "Breadth and Diminishment of His Chariot" <note>A reference to Ma'aseh Merkavah, the mystical study of the Divine Chariot</note>, and also not because he lacked a tradition in it from a teacher, as is necessary in this wisdom. For he has an established foundation in the book *The Redemption of Tradition* <note>original: "Geulat HaKabbalah"</note>, where he sought to be wise through theoretical premises. The core of the matter is that the investigation will be different from the text, and the Scripture will be a separate thing. For the purpose of the study for one who reflects upon the secret of what is written in the Torah, the Prophets, and the Writings <note>The Tanakh</note>, and the Words of our Sages of blessed memory <note>original: "Chazal"</note>—the carriers of the divine wisdom that is in our hands—it will become clear to him without any doubt that their intention in these matters was not what the Rabbi <note>Likely referring to Maimonides or a similar rationalist philosopher</note> intended. This is what will be clarified in his words, with God's help, and this is what I intended to prove in this chapter.

### Chapter 10

->**The philosophers and what our Sages called "Greek Wisdom"**<-
->**And regarding the benefit of its study according to its appearance and its occurrences**<-

In the world and according to the custom of kings, as they wrote, to investigate beings and to take pride in the intellect of their creation. Among the philosophers of our people, it is called the "Wisdom of Investigations" <note>original: "Chokmat HaMechakrim"</note> because they sought wisdom according to their own opinion. In the Greek language, "Philosophies" means the "Love of Wisdom." However, for every member of the House of Israel, it is revealed and prohibited from what they said in the Talmud, Tractate Sotah, in the chapter "The Beheaded Heifer" <note>Tractate Sotah 49b</note>. And at the beginning of the first chapter of Sukkah, they said there: 

When the Hasmonean kings were at war with one another, Hyrcanus was inside <note>Jerusalem</note> and Aristobulus was outside. Every day, those inside would lower coins in a basket, and those outside would send up animals for the daily burnt offerings. There was an old man there who was familiar with **Greek Wisdom**. He said to the besiegers: "As long as they are engaged in the Temple service, they will not be delivered into your hands." The next day, they lowered the coins in a basket, and the besiegers sent up a pig. When the pig reached halfway up the wall, it stuck its claws into the wall, and the Land of Israel shook over an area of four hundred by four hundred leagues. At that time, the Sages said: "Cursed be the man who raises pigs, and cursed be the man who teaches his son **Greek Wisdom**." 

Regarding that time, they established what is said: "From the time the first Temple was destroyed, the fragrance of the balsam was lost and the fat was taken from the earth" due to the sin mentioned. But is **Greek Wisdom** actually prohibited? For it was taught that in the Land of Israel, one might ask: "Why use the Syrian <note>Aramaic</note> language? Use either the Holy Tongue <note>Hebrew</note> or the Greek language." And Rabbi Yosei said in Babylon: "Why use the Syrian language? Use either the Holy Tongue or the Persian language." Thus, the Greek language is one thing, and **Greek Wisdom** is another.

But is **Greek Wisdom** truly prohibited? For Rabbi Yehuda said in the name of Shmuel in the name of Rabbi Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel: "There were a thousand children in my father's house; five hundred of them studied Torah, and five hundred studied **Greek Wisdom**." They replied: "The household of Rabban Gamliel was different, as they were close to the monarchy" <note>The Roman government</note>. As it was taught: "Cutting the hair in the *Kumi* style <note>A Roman fashion</note> is a forbidden heathen practice." However, they permitted Avtalyon ben Reuven to cut his hair in the *Kumi* style because he was close to the monarchy. Likewise, they permitted the household of Rabban Gamliel to study **Greek Wisdom** because they were close to the government.

Perhaps Rabbi Abraham Ibn Ezra, of blessed memory, followed the way of the philosophers and was lenient in this matter. But the author of *The Way of Faith* <note>original: "Derekh Emunah"</note> wrote in the second treatise, the third gate, in these words, to solve the difficulties: "The **Greek Wisdom** mentioned is not the wisdom of demonstrative investigation <note>Logic/Philosophy</note>, for the wisdom of investigation is an intellectual wisdom belonging to all of humanity. Rather, it must be an ethnic wisdom belonging specifically to the Greeks and not to any other nation." He already explained that even if some of these sciences are found in their books, they were stolen from the Hebrews <note>A common medieval Jewish claim that Greek philosophy originated with the Prophets</note> and translated into their languages. All these sciences are "human wisdoms," not "Greek Wisdom." 

The specific **Greek Wisdoms** are different sciences, which even the philosophers criticize...

<column-break/>

...them. He already said in his book, in the third section, that the opinions of the ancients regarding the stars were in the place of the sun... <note>A possible reference to astronomical models</note> without a doubt the scholars of **Greek Wisdom** were named so so that they would not follow the intellect and demonstration. They were accustomed to ethnic habits that existed for thousands of years... the wisdom of their religion, sacrifices, and hidden worships... or it was the wisdom of sorcery, involving seductive and false arguments... imagining celestial spheres... and that is the "Greek Wisdom" which is wicked. They would pass down their divinity in a hidden way and mandate divine status for a foreign stranger whom they worshipped, arranging prayers and sacrifices in their abominable ways. This is one type of Greek wisdom.

And there is a second type, which is the wisdom of rhetoric, where they would speak in strange riddles and refined language. This was called the "Wisdom of Parables and Riddles" <note>original: "Chokmat Meshalim ve-Chidot"</note>. This was the intention of the decree, in my opinion. And behold, these are the two parts of **Greek Wisdom** that are prohibited to the children of Israel.

However, concerning that which is extremely necessary, is it prohibited for a Jew to learn it? For it was already explained in that gate that if it is doubtful, then the Greek language might provide a solution... but it should not be thought that the Sages were endangered by this. Regarding this part, Rabbi Jonathan said: "Why is a reward given for the study of **Greek Wisdom**? Because it provides a 'graceful presence' before the nations." But it is impossible for them to be sustained by it, for it is like "the two handbreadths of the heart" <note>A metaphor for internal struggle or limited space</note>.

The second wisdom is the wisdom of politics, which is found in their circular laws and riddles, as is known of Titus who was a peacemaker... speaking in parables and nuances. This is what they permitted to Rabban Gamliel and his household, who were close to the monarchy, to study and to speak with it. As it was said, they studied it in the king's house with the Persians and the high-ranking officers. This is what they meant by **Greek Wisdom**—the wisdom of diplomatic conduct used to speak with the authorities so that the Sages and the leaders would not be disgraced. 

Specifically, it was said that before the time of Titus, it was even more necessary. And we see that it is appropriate for whoever says this was the intent of "Greek Wisdom." For the sophists were engaged in it to rule over the masses. In the time of Titus, a royal decree was issued so that everyone would know that anyone proficient in this wisdom would be esteemed in Titus's eyes. It would be explained that the monarchy of the time favored this wisdom... Rabbi Joshua said that one should avoid **Greek Wisdom** because of the "informers" who were close to the monarchy and would accuse a man if they wished. Because of **Greek Wisdom**, it is implied that there is no doubt one could speak to the government and hand over his fellow to the authorities. This was said in the days of Titus. 

The Tosafot <note>Medieval commentators on the Talmud</note> already brought this and said it was a great honor for the old man <note>from the siege story</note> to teach **Greek Wisdom** to the sons, but how could he do this? They said it was like a "whispering of the lips" or "Greek nuances," and they did not find the specific nature of this wisdom. But the Elder, who intended to subvert the knowledge of the Divine Wisdom <note>the Temple service</note>, was the first. And so in the days of Titus, they were the first in wisdom, and through the knowledge of this wisdom, he was esteemed by the kings and honored for being of a different nature. This is what the Rashba <note>Rabbi Shlomo ben Aderet, a 13th-century authority</note> explained at the end of his words: "**Greek Wisdom** is used in the palaces of those close to the monarchy, who speak the wisdom of Homer and Titus." At that time, it was not prohibited as a language, but as a specific ethnic wisdom. This is the proof that being "close to the monarchy" refers to the Greek language. And since the Greek language was already permitted...

### Chapter 17

In this, our eyes see and the voice of the awakener calls, for the king of all perfection is the intellect <note>original: "HaSechel"</note> within the Written Torah and the Oral Torah and the commandments of the Torah. Through their signs, the wise man is tested, and he draws close to understanding the supreme virtues and the heights of the Torah that he has studied and engaged with. For one who lives freely to act according to their truth—if it is through the internal received wisdom <note>original: "Chokmah HaPnimit HaMkubalah," referring to Kabbalah</note> and the sealed secrets within it—behold, this is the True Perfection. Through it, he is a "man," and he does not merely need to be a man of flesh and blood. From this and through this, he is called a "holy, mighty man." For it is good to speak and to study it for all who are unrefined <note>original: "pra'im," literally "wild ones"</note>, though not among them as an equal, for with a man of wisdom, those wise in that wisdom are greater than him. And it declares and spreads to the simple that they are called "man" <note>A reference to the Talmudic dictum that Israel is called "man" (Adam) while idolaters are not, here applied intellectually</note>, and excluded are the wicked—why are they not called "man"? And what is it? They are a "man" through that wisdom, according to the knowledge he has learned and included for them, and through it, he becomes a "man," etc.

And in the Reproofs, Chapter 2, on the matter of Ben Dama <note>A nephew of Rabbi Ishmael mentioned in the Talmud, Menachot 99b</note>: Because Ishmael's shop... after Ishmael my son, he said to me: "Our God, all the promises are in the heart." And what is the perfection of extra wisdom? They applied this verse to him: "And who shall break the Holy Torah from his mouth," etc. And all this is an exhortation to be careful lest his thinking incline away from grace and from walking and studying the Greek Wisdom <term>Greek Wisdom (Chokmat Yevanit): Historically interpreted as either the Greek language, subtle Greek rhetoric, or Aristotelian philosophy</term>. And he provided for Rabbi Shmuel bar Nachmani; Shmuel bar Nachmani said that Rabbi Jonathan said: "This verse: 'It shall not depart' <note>Joshua 1:8: "This book of the law shall not depart out of thy mouth"</note> is not a duty <note>original: "chovah"</note> nor a chariot." And he said that it is the "foreign language" <note>original: "alel chana," likely a corruption of "Lashon Yevanit"</note> referred to as the "Greek language" that seduces, etc. And this is not in the thought at all, and one should not prevent the matter reflected by Ben Dama. 

Is it close to nature? Why would Rabbi Ishmael withhold the Wisdom of Kabbalah from him? Had he strictly observed the Commandment of Rabbi Ishmael regarding the Torah, he would have approached the Kingdom of the Torah. If he had no portion in the generality of the Torah—furthermore, even if Ben Dama had learned the entire Torah—he would still have lacked its written beauty and rectitude. And if Ben Dama asked because he pitied the "Internal King" <note>The Intellect</note>, the demonstrative one, and pitied those who study and know this wisdom—for it is necessary in their paths—whatever he did and pitied, according to his speech, they were decreed from his wisdom. Behold, every man whose Torah is upon him stands in his freedom. And Ben Dama understood that the Torah had to contain things "against the Torah" <note>contradicting literalism</note> which might lead the possessor into errors and heresies. Ben Dama thought that after he had finished the "Order of the Book," it was permitted to learn and teach it [Greek Wisdom]. And Rabbi Ishmael said to him: "Heaven forbid!" <note>original: "Chas v'shalom"</note>. He meant to say that we must be careful of linguistic refinements, and not what was written, and if he were to say that the study of the commandment of heresy is uprightness <note>meaning, studying heresy to refute it</note>... even if he had the power of things against the Torah, the wise man who engages in it should deepen in his heart the foundation of the existence of the Good. They gave him a paper to check what is mixed in from the "outside," etc. 

And regarding the claim of the "Greek," for the Torah is the daughter of Time and its existence, and there was an order of times and its correction through the existence of the Result <note>original: "ha-alul," a philosophical term for the Effect/Creation</note>. For this reason, it opens with the creation of day and night and the engagement in things to stir life in the depth of the world's settlement; for in all our ways and without the order of times... and in the books of its matter and its righteousness, it is a fundamental principle. If his claim is a treasure, it shall not be hidden or permitted; it is like a small vessel that should not be mixed with missing things. There you shall learn his teaching, the wisdom of the spy, and to study Greek Wisdom—where should he go with them? And do not say from within it, and so he says, "Let them be only thine own" <note>Proverbs 5:17</note>, etc. Specifically through them, you have permission to speak in other languages. But Greek Wisdom in general is a matter of missing things. And the Rashba <note>Rabbi Shlomo ben Aderet, 13th-century sage</note> who said in Chapter 2: "Because I did not call him a man except... Arabic and Hidden." He maintained the commandments in our time. And Rabbi Shmuel bar Nachmani and Rabbi Jonathan, who said in this chapter, "Do not rest," etc., were not disagreeing with Rabbi Ishmael. Rather, Rabbi Ishmael mentioned the rebuke of studying all day and night according to the literal meaning of the verse "It shall not depart," and the writing of "My son," etc. The opinion of Rashba and Rabbi Jonathan is that it is not a "chariot" nor a "duty" to learn the blessing. All agree that the study of Greek Wisdom—for the "Greek" was included in "missing things" and the rebuke there was to warn and distance one from it—is a sign of creating the depth of the Torah, which is the Shabbat and the creation. It is the depth mentioned, which is the birth of the world and its existence. And the study of Greek Wisdom is—

<column-break/>

### Chapter 17

It is a depth in the heart of the generous soul, sent without time, without a heart like a sieve. And it was not for this that he relied on the words of Rabbi Ishmael. And from the words of Rabbi Joshua, it was seen that the study of Greek Wisdom is forbidden, even if you have studied the entire Torah. This is the "Demonstrative Intellectual King" within him, which is necessary; thus we have agreed.

And the claim that says "everything that contains a reward is permitted," etc.—this is the "Kingdom" that was said... in the wisdom of the Table <note>Likely "Chokmat HaShulchan," possibly referring to table manners/ethics or a specific text</note>, "evil sages," etc. And this is far from greatness, until the study of it is forbidden to the recipients of the True Religion <note>original: "Dat HaEmet," Judaism</note>. Because after there is a blessing in the covenant, it is permitted to him, unless it leads to heresy, such as the matter of the "Renewal of the World" <note>Creation ex nihilo vs. eternal matter</note>, providence, the Torah of Prophecy, nature, the writing of the Torah, the intellect, the abandonment [of the world by God], and all the things written about this. For the Torah and the rebuke stand upon them, and they are tested by their results. 

And this is the Greek Wisdom that has no share in the True Religion. He said that it was "weakening" her, and if it were forbidden, he would have been prevented from writing, or even if he happened upon the entrance of his house. And even the things from which he might be saved—those that do not contradict [the Torah]—aside from the "Forbidden Gates" <note>dangerous philosophical concepts</note> that will pull their students [away], he said that things which uproot the foundations of the religion lead to heresy. As we have seen from the claim against the "Lovers of the Philosophers": for in grasping their "demonstration" <note>logical proofs</note>, and if the Kingdom was not found, they knew heresy. In their essence, they are close to those of whom it is written: "None that go unto her return again" <note>Proverbs 2:19, often applied to heresy</note>.

And the Sage Rabbi Isaac Arama <note>15th-century philosopher and author of the Akedat Yitzchak</note>, of blessed memory, wrote in the book *Yad*, the books of the *Sefer Ha-Ikkarim* <note>The Book of Principles</note>, in this language: "They fabricated a quarrel and seized it, they loathed it upon us..." This is what happened in the early days and what he heard in his time until now. For this is the "accidental" anchor <note>original: "ha-igon hamikri"</note>—that their wisdom is also our wisdom, until it was integrated into the people as a whole... like the "clothed scroll" that he silenced, and he clothed the Levites more than all the nations upon the face of the earth, who in our light saw the light in the Torah. And now they have abandoned us... until: And you shall test the Human Wisdom <note>philosophy</note> received in the Torah, for it was a divine wisdom and holiness in a thin body. And there is nothing in this that opposes us, because our knowledge comes from one source, which is the Supreme Wisdom within us, which brings to light the mysteries of the True Religion. It is refined and supported in its principles and its excellence, even when hidden by the "frothing of the waters" <note>likely referring to the turbulence of secular thought</note> and its perspective. And it received its kingdom and the Torah of the straight path to answer the desire of its Owner <note>God</note>, walking in the way of service. It removes one from turning from the Torah to the right or the left. The inclinations of nature shall be corrected by it, and the crooked thoughts of the masses shall be dispersed. And from the clarity of the attributes, they shall be revealed—and all this is proof of its being true.

And as is known to these [people], one must not forbid, etc. And even though his rulings are many, the law has already been decided by the mouth of the "High Court" <note>original: "Pei Heh," possibly an abbreviation for a specific authority</note>, etc. And it is not as he thought, for there is no "reward" in it, except in the matter of the shame of study—for through much [study], you will find a little of his foolishness. At the end, they teach Torah to every man, there is no doubt. But if the study would lead them to an obstacle, to raise thoughts against the Torah, we find that we do not teach them anything else. And the law gives this—not to be "scrupulous" in the wisdom of the "son of Belial" <note>a lawless or wicked person</note>, etc. And they showed him... and this is the secret of the intention of the "Connection of the Pleasantness" and the sight of the knowledge of the True Wisdom—for wisdom was meant to perfect all the states of man, which is the True Perfection, drawn from the engagement in the Torah and the existence of its rest. For "he who keeps the commandment shall know no evil thing" <note>Ecclesiastes 8:5</note>. It is what draws one to the depths of merit and distances them from ugliness and the trivial. 

Above all this, the True Wisdom is understood, and it causes the "Cleaving" <term>Cleaving (Deveikut): Spiritual attachment or communion with the Divine</term> by which the intention of creation and the ultimate purpose of the human collective are completed. And the philosopher marvels at the "Partial Collectives" who divide themselves to act and to be a middle path... toward His kingdom, for which he was created. Specifically, the "Wings of the Received Wisdom" <note>Kabbalah</note> of the Torah. And if there were a generation from the "generations" who thought they were the "teachers of the vine"... it was because of their poor choice and their being empty of the Divine Wisdom and the support—

### Chapter 10 | The Section on Purpose | Chapter 10

In the Talmud <note>Gemara</note>, regarding **Greek wisdom**, it was said to him: "Go and study it at a time that is neither day nor night," for it is written: *You shall meditate on it [the Torah] day and night.* From this, it would seem a person is forbidden from teaching his son **foreign wisdoms** <note>original: "Chokmot BaGoyim"</note>, because it is written *you shall meditate on it*, etc. Rabbi Yehoshua raised a difficulty... [regarding] the wisdom of God <note>original: "Chokmat Hashem"</note>... this refers to one of the foundations. However, the second part, which is the **Wisdom of the Celestial Spheres** <term>Astronomy|The study of planetary motion and the zodiac</term>, it was said that they decreed against it because of the "foundations" <note>likely referring to political establishments or informers</note> through which they could hand over and understand power and the *Shekhinah* <note>Divine Presence</note>... they are accustomed to those symbols and could use them to sell out or inform. Yet, they did not forbid it entirely, for to inform and betray does not require a specific language, as every tongue and language bears witness to this. Furthermore, in the days of Rabbi <note>Judah the Prince, 2nd century CE</note>, when they spoke of the "masks" <note>social/political pretenses</note>, they did not need the Wisdom of the Spheres, for a different language was common. If so, this part was not included in the decree. Rather, the decree was upon the **Essential Part**, which is referred to in its path as the "Religion of Heresy" <term>Minut|Sectarian beliefs or early Judeo-Christian deviations from Rabbinic law</term>. The language of our Rabbis, the **Tosafists** <note>Medieval French and German commentators on the Talmud</note>, who said that our Rabbi [Judah] understood the nature of the division, but they understood the religions. This is included in "seeking schemes" to cast them into total abandon. Our Sages of blessed memory <note>original: "RZL"</note> did not teach actual wisdom alongside the Wisdom of the Spheres and language, except regarding the intellectual part and the knowledge of **Heresy** <note>Minut</note>, from which it is known that he suppressed religions through forgetfulness. Wisdom founded in other laws is permitted from time to time, as will be explained further... it is clear in itself that intellectual research... is worthy of being received and heard. For these are intellectual proofs, and there is something above them for which there is no sufficient intellectual reason, as it does not fall under the net of human intellect... many ancient things were changed and confused, for it resembles the portion of the **Arabian Sages and Proofs** <note>likely referring to the Kalām or Islamic scholastic theology</note>. As the master of "Sealed Wisdom" <note>King Solomon</note> hinted in his riddles: *For the lips of a strange woman drop honey, and her mouth is smoother than oil.* This will be further explained when the time comes. This part is sufficient to decree against it systematically... and they received a little from the words of our Rabbis the Tosafists regarding Pliny <note>possibly a reference to Pliny the Elder or a similar classical authority</note> on the systems they accepted. Furthermore, when they asked about the "House of my teachers"... there was no fear there of wisdom or informants. They did not consider the external matter... the Sages only decreed against that which excludes one from the community... and what he wrote in the style of the Sages is not comparable, for the intention of the Sages was for one whose end goal is human study only... for he is like a wild person... but for one who clarifies things through the "tools of the Torah" and has books in hand... there is no room for innovations... as the Sages said regarding the **House of Rabban Gamliel**: "They permitted them to study Greek wisdom" <note>because of their need to interact with the Roman government</note>. But the truth is that actual wisdom, and specifically every science based on demonstrative systems... they questioned: "Is Greek wisdom forbidden? But we learned..." Perhaps they studied it because it is fitting. "Greek wisdom" was the version in the Mishnah, and the explanation is that the intellectual path... such as the **Wisdom of Logic** <note>original: "Chokmat Gichon," likely a corruption of Higayon/Logic</note>... it is fitting that a portion of wisdom should rejoice and be part of the whole. To this, they raised a difficulty: "But we learned..." and they added: "The Greek language is one thing, and Greek wisdom is another." When they spoke of Greek wisdom, language was not included. And what they questioned was whether it was unworthy to learn; but since it is perfection, and since being a "Man" is a calling of perfection... these are the foundations... he did not leave room for "Nationalist" studies except before the foundations... he is a "Sage" because he prepares for the creation... and even though he is a Jew... these are nothing but "foreign words" <note>original: "Divrei La'az"</note>. Furthermore, if it is unworthy to be learned, it is forbidden, for we are only permitted to argue and debate in matters that depend on it.

<column-break/>

This is the matter of his wisdom for man as a human being. Any end that he learns and knows is worthy for him to know. But it is worthy and important in all his wisdom... it is a secret alone, worthy and mandatory to know. Indeed, in this generation, it is worthy to learn it, and this wisdom is clear despite the sufficiency and smallness of their words, for they needed the **Wisdom of Logic** <note>original: "Chokmat HaHigayon"</note> to bring their students to the fundamental levites on the platform <note>Duchan</note>, etc. Also from **Arithmetic and Geometry** <note>original: "Mispar ve-Handasa"</note>, they have great teachings from the depths of the sciences, and they said: "All truth is in its heart." In the **Wisdom of Astronomy** <note>original: "Chokmat HaTekunah"</note>, they have works... and in many other places, great details... and in the part of the Mishnah, the virtue of the teachers is their number. In the **Natural Sciences** <note>original: "Chokmat HaTeva"</note> and the secret of existence, they have teachings and measures that were not witnessed. The **Scholars of Research** <term>Chokmei HaChakirah|Philosophers</term> called them "servants of power," etc. In the **Divine Science** <term>Chokmat HaElokut|Metaphysics or Theology</term> and the "Divine things," there are deep and hidden matters like the *Book of the Palaces* <note>Sefer Hekhalot, an early Jewish mystical text</note>, the *Book of the Measurement of the Height* <note>Shiur Qomah, a mystical work on the Divine "dimensions"</note>, and the *Book of Brilliance* <note>Sefer HaBahir, a primary Kabbalistic work</note>. In the name of Divine Wisdom, they arrange it, and they are sages, and no intellectual researcher can contain it. It is worthy to know the portion of the High Wisdoms and all that was known to them from it... to strive in its vitality, etc. And also in saying: "Anyone who is able to understand and ascend"... the smallness of the birth of the **Divine Torah**, which is a blessed thing to learn for all the wisdom within it... paths and founded sciences from every language to merit its virtues... like knowing the commandments of the Festival <note>Chag</note> and the matters of the Temple Service <note>Avodah</note> and other things. These are like "tools" for us to clarify the action... along with the length of the dwelling... and they mentioned in the **Wisdom of the Laws** <note>original: "Chokmot Halakhot"</note> that are revealed in our wisdom... and the loss you mentioned, the Sages in the paths of this wisdom, etc. Also, it is mixed with the **Wisdom of Whispering** <note>original: "Chokmat HaLachash," likely referring to incantations or magic</note>... and against the intellect and for the sake of religion, it is worthy to follow it... to be a student and to offer in His name. Through this, he has the power to learn every wisdom, for its precision and quantity and variations... which is the "Storm of the Desires," etc. And even though it is from the **Universal Torah** <note>original: "Torah HaKolelet"</note> that every man should be an intellectual and be wise and complete in his perception, behold, it is worthy and mandatory for him to learn wisdom, for through it a man perceives and merits... and they will be like the **Intellectual World** <note>original: "Olam HaSechel"</note>... and through the effort of goals and difficulties... they will ascend... the pleasure that the Universal Torah... the intellect with the virtues... his laws, etc. In another tablet, the "Kindness of the Intellect" <note>Chesed HaSechel</note>—these are the two divisions.

### Chapter 17

And after these "vain words," he comes to challenge them in the next chapter:
However, the one part which is the **Wisdom of the Religion of the Torah**... and that the Legislator <note>Moses</note> gave the statutes to his state... it is settled and stands... and the decree was not upon it. To exclude it... it is clearly written in the Torah: *Take heed to yourself, lest you forget the words*, etc. For this, the faces of the beginning of the statutes will be recognized... and he who permitted their study [did so] as a "fence around the laws," to say that the service which was lacking... and knowing the manner of the service so that he could not err and do otherwise... for there are beautiful arguments... and a partial religion was born from them... our Sages did not come to decree against this part at all. And if this part is not proven... that the wisdom which was intended for signs would give it strength for the religion... for he has no proof for it... they were worse than him in wisdom... to distort the laws in his way... it was the opinion heard in the **Jerusalem Talmud** <note>original: "Yerushalmi"</note>... they asked Rabbi Yehoshua: "Is one permitted to teach his son **Mishnah**?"...

### Chapter 17 | The Section on Purpose | 77

...as a remembrance of the place of existence, and as it is written: *Your kindness is better than life; my lips [shall praise You].*
The true [scholar] will be tested, for the parable has no reward from it, but the reward of the one who tests <note>original: "HaMenaseh"</note>.
In the **Book of the Reed** <term>Sefer HaKaneh|A 14th-century Kabbalistic work on the reasons for the commandments</term> and at the beginning of the **Book of Wonder** <term>Sefer HaPeli’ah|A major Kabbalistic text structured as a commentary on the first chapters of Genesis</term>, and in the writings of **Nahmanides** <note>Ramban</note>, it is explained to us that there is a deficiency in the wisdom of others <note>non-Jewish philosophers</note>, as if they lack the fruit and the essence.
The books which are the mystery of the tradition <note>Kabbalah</note>, he knew them, of blessed memory, even those of the philosophers. For there are the **Book of Power**, the **Chapters of Power**, the **Book of the Measure of the Stature** <term>Shiur Komah|An early mystical text describing the anthropomorphic dimensions of the Divine</term>, and the **Book of the Zohar** <note>The central work of Jewish mysticism</note>.
The purpose is for the thread and the connections; and the **Book of the Pious** <note>Sefer Hasidim</note> mentions the deficiencies and their many types.
From what the Geonim <note>the leaders of Babylonian Jewry</note> mentioned, and in the writings of **Nahmanides** who followed them, they were all used among the sages, and all the "crooked" was mixed in. We went to the books and did not find anything that adds to the light of the truth. For the **Book of Creation** <term>Sefer Yetzirah|The oldest known book on Jewish esotericism, attributed to the Patriarch Abraham</term> was the companion of **Abraham our Father**.
They were like those among the foundations of holiness. And **Jeremiah** was occupied with it [at the time of] the destruction of the House of Mercy <note>the First Temple</note>, as written in the **Book of Confidence** <note>Sefer HaBitachon</note>. Ten [years] he toiled there until he complained to his companion **Rabbi Mikha the Gaon**, of blessed memory, in the **Book of Unity**, and also his holy companion...
to the Name in the **Book of the Garments** <note>Sefer HaMalbushim</note>, which are the mysteries of the depths. Therefore, he was occupied with the **Book of Creation** by himself. A **Heavenly Voice** <term>Bat Kol|A divine resonance or echo of God's voice</term> went out and said: "Get yourself a companion." For your sake, you took Mikha his son, and they occupied themselves with the **Book of Creation** for three years, until they were refined. It is written: *Or according to my words you shall see,* etc.
And so it is with the aforementioned, and all this is the end. And he mentioned that from them [the secrets] were found from the time of the Second Temple. Afterward, they went into exile and were not emptied from their place, holy and pure, but became like a worn-out vessel. They were not copied and were not found among the tablets.
In every generation, the sages are zealous, occupying themselves with them and explaining their secrets, as they received them personally. Afterward, I will summarize: he is the one, and they spoke of his many wisdoms found in our lives. The books mentioned by the sages in the chambers of wisdom—some are regarding the "Hall of the Chariot" <note>Hekhalot literature</note>, and also letters whose depths are revealed according to the investigative intellect.
Through them, the hands of the masses are weakened from the judgments of truth. But the essence of wisdom is truly thus: for in it is found, etc. And if it is clarified in the lives of the philosophers, it is impossible to stand upon the truth in any of those who mentioned the Name. For the fear of the Name is the beginning of wisdom, as with [the study of] books, as will be clarified in each of them.
Here, if we test those whose wisdom and philosophy is forbidden, [it is] empty and void. All those who were negligent in it and found... and what they relied upon... the Sages of blessed memory said regarding other wisdoms, etc. Behold, the truth is this: the knowledge of these [others] is not found except by the one who knows.
He said this and his companion, as will come further in Chapter 2, that the one who failed in it... regarding the vitality of the wisdoms. **Maimonides** <note>Rambam</note>, of blessed memory, whose greatness we have mentioned, etc., was great and his wisdom was from him in failure.
And they did not distance the wisdom of **Maimonides**, of blessed memory, because of its high place... from what he wrote in the **Guide for the Perplexed** and in the **Book of Knowledge** <note>Mishneh Torah: Sefer HaMada</note> to point toward the truth.
He did not arrange it for him, and they all became like a wall. He placed his two hands [on it] and it was not built... he destroyed and caused a crash upon the foundation of opinions, which is the Greek root. His students said: "May the right hand live!" But they did not have the power of one thought. And this is the end: we came to learn every wisdom, and to take [from them], and to find wisdoms and philosophies, etc.
Behold, in the words of the companions and the legends regarding his desire, double what was expected from him, which is the power to exaggerate the praise of the philosophers and their wisdom. Although he dripped all of their folly, and opened the hidden matters of the Guide, there is no comparison or value to the chosen one <note>the Torah</note>.
There is nothing greater than it to learn from... the Ten Splendors <term>Sefirot|The ten divine emanations in Kabbalah</term>. However, the way is to remove the thorns from the path, and to search and to crush the small ones.
In my opinion, from the beginning, he took the heavens <note>philosophical heights</note>, etc., and in the end, they became like broken pits and damaging things for him. They were desolated before him, and this became a spirit for the world of the intellect, etc.
The world of the intellect, its perception and its perfection is in constant action. There is no lack in it compared to our thoughts. One should not seek [it in] time or its creation. It is constantly preparing and bringing forth great wisdom, and there is no change in this. Nor will he deny the grace that comes into action, but his tools are only those which were the result of the premises of the grace... and there is nothing in the particular except what is in the general. And this is more than that which was expected. And all this is hinted at <meta>to our sages of blessed memory</meta>.

<column-break/>

Who philosophized about all the attributes attributed to the True Perfection and attributed them [to God]. And their wisdom is for evil. I have written it according to the Will Above. Afterward, for this man is a day that is in the intellect, etc., which is higher than all investigation. For the **Israelite Intellect** is generally from the intellect of the order of the tablets, just as it is generally there in the soul.
As is known to the Sages of the Heart, this Israelite intellect is refined in the Torah and its commentaries and its secrets. The dialectic of the external wisdom is also to know much of the wisdom of the [celestial] spheres. This is what the philosopher did not attain. And every Israelite is the one called "Man" <term>Adam|In mystical thought, 'Adam' often refers specifically to the spiritual potential of Israel</term>. This is the meaning: they were intentional in this great account... may his hand be doubled... what he was wise in.
And the saying: "You are called 'Man' <note>Adam</note>, and the nations of the world are not called 'Man'." For after this, he is a vessel of the prophetic intellect. It is worthy for him to bring it out in this labor, the Name and the spirit. In their wisdom, the philosophical one, they are emanated and investigated from the spirit of the [celestial] Chariot, as is known to the Sages of the Heart.
The intellect of the philosopher and his creations are below the human intellect, for he is occupied with the physical and does not desire, and he did not understand. In his hearing from the story, he is like a king who rules and prepares according to his investigation and his pleasure.
The beauty is that he has no portion or completion in the Essential Wisdom. It is worthy for him, if so, to receive [knowledge] to know the wisdom of the prophecy. And there is our peace in his opinion and in the writing of the spiritual laws, etc., as in the **Book of Power**, etc., and like the **Book of Creation** by **Abraham our Father**, peace be upon him, which leads by the hand to the gates of the spiritual forces... the essence of the constellation...
And the **Book of the Fountain of Wisdom** and the **Book of the Zohar**, and much of it is clarified. For the wisdom of the power is a wall that is impossible to bring out by way of the human intellect, unless there is something higher than it. Even if there are revealed aspects in it, they are not comparable to the inner parts.
In his way, I found help for the revealed verses for those who possess the oral tradition, according to the tradition that I support. And this is all a hidden dream, founded upon the portion of *Beshalach* <note>Exodus 13:17–17:16</note>. And this... and she bore a son at the appointed time, etc., to the scribe. And afterward it is written:
"I have seen a death and a staff... <note>original Aramaic: "mit u-mateh"</note> but I saw its movement and it did not rage. It was hidden to be reconciled and joined. And it was found to be disciplined in its beauty. The sweetness of the upper water I did not see written, its rebuke thus comes in the blessing." It is written: *Better is a rebuke...* <note>Proverbs 27:5</note>
"The long one in the time of its existence, surely thus it was joined and did not go out. A long spirit and then the drop of my coming from the side of beauty. Its sweetness is clear at its feet and it will be forgotten upon the strike," etc. This is the building of the upper holy word that is revealed.
Until here. And in it are found the faces of the seventy... from his book. Here, this holy author, to the exclusion of the hint and the "how" and its existences. He explained it thus. And it will be seen that there are wisdoms that he wrote to choose them for the day of advice... for the day of advice that is explained in the spirit.
The Name, the companion... which is mentioned in the Zohar. Do not seek it for another. And he teaches that those [secrets] are more honored than all the hints that are hidden in relation to the intellect. And if it is found in **Abraham our Father**, they were in his eyes like the "Garments of the King" and his Torah, etc.
Behold, because he is abstract, so that no intellectual thing will be dependent on the intellect of the philosopher, from what comes in the words of those who came to us to explain. For they are not tied to the intellect and its sister, to be refined more than it is refined in everything. Then every wise man... he will rejoice.
And afterward: "Double me!" according to the Kabbalist, for the intention of the holy one, peace be upon him, in this work... and it is known to the Sages of the Heart. For the wisdom from below is from the wisdom from above. It is the Name to lengthen... the end of the intellect... the face and his glory in it according to the sun.
The wisdom from the wisdom, as they said in the *Shiur [Komah]*: the male from below is from the male from above. And afterward, it is hidden and concealed according to the names. The male from the male, as they said there.
And afterward: the ranks of the soul that descend... as is known from the vessels of the living creatures <note>Hayyot</note>, which are bound in the garment... his pair to him. For the soul causes... and according to the sun in the soul... as he said... that is drawn from it...
The spirit of life and in the soul. And as it is written: *And he put his mouth upon his mouth,* etc. <note>2 Kings 4:34</note>. And they said there in the Midrash: "When it was clarified to him... I saw the upper word... the place where the letters were written in it," etc. And if he turns his spirit to him. And according to the sun in the bond...
