### Chapter 10 | The Section on the Purpose | Chapter 10

For when the most perfect [individuals] join together all the parts of wisdom which are, by their nature, true wisdom—including the first principles and ancient knowledge that the philosophers deepened with their intellects—all of this is established. A wise person is superior at the start of his path compared to a mere researcher or a learned scholar. For investigation, speculation, and knowledge are a special virtue <note>original: "segulah"</note> that does not remove the perfect man from his perfection, nor does wickedness mix into their knowledge. 

Yet, for some, everything is overturned until a false witness arises. This is because the student who lacks the foundation of perfection—the principles of the Torah—finds that the "cup" <note>referring to the cup of knowledge or destiny</note> does not stop according to his view. His eyes are not enlightened by the light of the Torah, which is the necessity of the **Divine Will** in the perfect man. This light is meant to refine the masses, making them pure and polished after intellectual research. 

Without this, one reaches the end of perfection and finds that everything the intellect denies leads to saying, "we are sick." Death's fury stands before such a person, leading him to deny and speak perversely against the Name <note>God</note> and His Torah. He will not rely on His testimony and will see himself as liable for all sufferings, and his wickedness will dwell within him. 

Regarding the overturned secrets of wisdom and its roots: bread will be forgiven to complete his intellect and his merits in his speculative concepts. He wrote that it is "awesome" <note>fearful</note> to say that a day of perfection was given to his opinion, which consists of harsh words in the rebuke of the wisdom of Israel. For if demonstrative intellectual research <term>hakira hamofetit|Logic-based philosophical inquiry used by Aristotelians</term> adds to the discovery of truth, it is only a spirit and a source for knowing that there is a **received wisdom** <term>kabbalah|Tradition or mystical lore</term> from Sinai. A student should learn it from its masters, and he will taste that it is good. His face will shine with the light of truth, and he will not open himself to the doubts of existential proofs that follow from the "fear of the evil" in the eye of knowledge. 

The wisdom of the Kabbalist <note>the receiver of tradition</note> should be purified before the teachers of our sages. For the tradition is true wisdom from Him, may He be exalted. It is impossible for it to contradict the truth. The perfect man, after being prepared, should ascend the ladder to engage in the wisdom of **Kabbalah**, which is the very likeness of the Torah. It is impossible for the strength of true wisdom—which aligns with the religion from every side—to falter. It aligns with the intent of the Torah, the Will, and the Desire for the service of prayer and the commandments. 

After standing upon this, he shall strive to increase his learning and bring forth "offspring" and intellectual possessions, removing any deficiency from his hand according to the external intellect. For since his hand is ready to achieve this wisdom, he can be free for all of this according to the **Divine Intellect**. He should engage in the dialectics of this wisdom in the way of truth, in which the holy ones and the sages lived. 

There is no desire to prioritize "external wisdom" <note>secular philosophy</note> over the Torah. Preventing the study of the philosophers at first is necessary because it uproots and destroys the details of the true religion. Its path is a path of thorns and crookedness, a voice of vanities that leads to heresy. When such a person comes to study the Torah and sees in it external matters that seem to contradict his [secular] wisdom, he will deny them unless they are explained according to his heretical views—as happened with many of the philosophers among our people. 

However, true wisdom provides the measures to find rest for the soul. The opposite is true: the reward of truth and righteousness spreads to the merits and spiritual views in the hearts of the students, even if they study the Torah first. For the Torah is the resting place for the mysteries of the Torah and its principles. One can leave the details aside to establish the causes of Divine Wisdom. Every student has a "taste," because the Torah is the end and wisdom is the end. To draw near to the light of the Torah, one must know the intent and the Will as they were sent in the tradition from Sinai. Then he may enter to stroll in the **Orchard** <term>Pardes|The four levels of Torah interpretation, often referring to mystical study</term> of wisdom. This is not something that can dwell in writing alone, like a body or a husk. Rather, he should stand and prepare the virtues and the materials to understand everything clearly and according to their truth. His intellect will not be confused after he has prior knowledge of the matters to which the secrets point. This priority belongs to the Torah.

<column-break/>

This applies to the nations and to the sages. Regarding this, it is said: "Let everything be established with righteousness and integrity." He will rejoice because he stands upon the distinct principles of our religion. Then everything will be sustained in his hand. If a student says he knows and perceives, yet his error is discovered, say to them: "Your heart is like an overturned garment." The path of this true wisdom stands upon the principles of the Torah. Why would they prepare the truth that is based on the "horn of the prophet"? 

This is wisdom and merit above all external, intellectual wisdom. For the "portion of Jacob" <note>the Jewish people</note> is not like theirs. Everything is a voice, and the eye of wisdom is for the sake of knowing Him and perceiving His Will—something impossible for the external intellect. It cannot be achieved through demonstrative research alone; it is beyond its reach. 

This wisdom is most appropriate for Israel, who are a "wise and understanding people." All of this stands against those who believe Israel's status as a "wise and understanding nation" refers to their mastery of abstract intellectual sciences. If that were the case, strange creatures would enter the congregation of the Lord. Who wrote that logical proof precedes the secrets? Israel is a wise and understanding nation because of their engagement with the Torah and the fulfillment of the commandments. As the scripture cries out: *Observe them and do them, for this is your wisdom and your understanding in the sight of the nations, who shall hear all these statutes and say, "Surely this great nation is a wise and understanding people"* (Deuteronomy 4:6). 

If you say this status refers to the fulfillment of the Will of the Place <note>God</note>, it brings knowledge to the soul. All the nations will see and fear those who fulfill these statutes, even if the reason is unknown to them; the answer to them is the **Divine Will**. I have already elaborated on this at the end of my book, *The Thoughts of the Lord*, regarding what the intellect lacks. 

Heaven forbid that intellectual wisdom should be denied to Israel! Rather, it was a portion of the other wisdoms because they are human, and they excelled in them more than the nations. This was revealed in Israel during the time we wrote to justify the great philosophers of our people. However, the wisdom of Israel is internal and Divine, received from the mouth of the Almighty <note>original: "HaGevurah"</note>. As it is written: *He tells His words to Jacob... He has not done so for any other nation* (Psalm 147:19-20). 

Their wisdom is true, as it is written: *And God gave wisdom to Solomon.* This wisdom does not exist outside of this nation; it is unique to Israel. If it were merely a human end, it would be equal to all. But it is a Divine portion, taken by the **Holy Spirit** <note>Ruach HaKodesh</note>. The intent in my words and my books is not merely what occurred to my mind or my colleagues' minds to explain logically. 

**Fear of the Lord** is the wisdom of perfection. One who knows it finds the secret of His hand. The wisdom of Divinity and the fear of the Lord are one. They added: "Every woman her wisdom," for they already established for us that there is no wisdom where there is no fear [of God] walking within it. 

The **Master of the Guide** <note>Maimonides, author of The Guide for the Perplexed</note>, of blessed memory, brought forth in his writings several statements that seem to oppose "fear" and prioritize the intellect, which appears entirely in the form of [secular] wisdom. We have already written about this in Chapter 7. Everything that is founded on the beginning of His name, may He be blessed, will lead to the fear of the intellectuals and increase their wisdom. 

How can a thing that is settled and proper be the end of their perfection if it was brought from Him? However, when they research them and follow only the intellect, they become foolish. This is the path and the religion of the philosopher whose eyes were not enlightened by the light of the truth. But if one takes his preparation from the **Wisdom of the Hidden** <note>mysticism</note>, the light of the Torah will shine upon him, and he will truly lack nothing. For he is whole and righteous, aligning with the intent of the Torah in the refinement of the body and soul. We do not need the external sciences for this, for the received testimony provides perfection in every place, as the Divine and Divine Wisdom have mentioned to us.

It asserts that while intellectual research has value, it must be preceded by the fear of God and traditional Jewish teachings to avoid heresy, even when interpreting works like Maimonides' Guide for the Perplexed.</summary>

<meta>This page continues the historical and theological defense of the transmission of the Oral Torah and the mystical tradition (Kabbalah). ### Section on the Purpose | Chapter 18

...who received the Torah from Sinai and handed it to Joshua, and Joshua to the Elders, and the Elders to the Prophets, and the Prophets handed it to the **Men of the Great Assembly**. They said: **"Make a fence for the Torah."** <note>This refers to the opening of Pirkei Avot (Ethics of the Fathers), the foundational text of Rabbinic tradition.</note> And Joshua is remembered among men for the sake of the Great Assembly throughout their generations, those who received the Torah into the Great Assembly as is explained. And regarding what they mentioned in the "House of Merit" <note>likely referring to a specific chamber or court</note> and the "Clarification," they descended from these levels at first, and seemingly these were elevated through the **Holy Spirit**.

In this distinguished chapter, **"The Holy One, Blessed be He, acted righteously with Israel"** <note>original: "tzedakah asah HaKadosh Baruch Hu im Yisrael"</note> by revealing the exile in small measures while the "Exile of Merit" still existed. This section is a preserved and pure examination within the exiles. The generation of Hezekiah [was sent] to Babylon while the blow of the "Exile of Merit" was still present; these are the secrets of the Torah. These are the later Great Ones, for most of the Sages of the Torah were exiled with **Jeconiah** <note>A king of Judah exiled to Babylon eleven years before the final destruction of the First Temple.</note>. As they said: "The Holy One, Blessed be He, acted righteously with Israel by preceding the exile of Jeconiah to the exile of Zedekiah, so that the **Oral Torah** would not be forgotten."

Thus, they dwelt in the Torah in Babylon from the destruction of the Temple until this very day. Neither Edom <note>Rome/Western powers</note> nor Greece ruled over them, nor did they decree against them every time. For the hand of this **Wonderful Leader** was not too short to perform wonders and to supervise this small portion of Torah and wisdom for this kingdom. This is the "fence," and for this reason, it was refined and treated with kindness, as it was in the beginning by the hand of the Almighty, may His name be blessed, who provides His merit to him. This is the Providence in all generations that follow the exile, a matter of His righteousness, may He be blessed.

So it was in a hidden time, like the secret of **Simeon the Pious**, who was of the remnants of the Great Assembly. Through him, our Sages entered into "good life." The end of the foundation was received by Jose ben Joezer of Zeredah and Jose ben Johanan of Jerusalem. Regarding him, they said: "Foolishness is better," because of Jose ben Joezer and Jose ben Johanan. For this reason, Judah [the Prince] concluded the "Clusters" <note>original: "eshkolot," a term for the greatest scholars who possessed all virtues</note>, explaining that "everything was in them." Until the time of the two Joses, there was no dispute among the Sages of Israel, as they spoke words exactly as written, as mentioned below. From their mouths and the mouths of the first ones, they departed regarding the "laying of hands" on sacrifices during festivals, according to the custom of Chapter 8 of the tractate *Derashot*. Finally, there was the last dispute that existed in Israel regarding the words of Torah.

And so they said in the Jerusalem [Talmud]: From them, **Joshua ben Perachiah** and **Nittai of Arbela** received it. From them, **Judah ben Tabbai** and **Simeon ben Shetach** received it. From them, **Shemaya** and **Abtalion** received it. These and those returned and received from them. Thus, through them, they handed over the tradition of the Torah and wisdom to **Rabban Yochanan ben Zakkai** and his like, from the master of the house in goodness. **Rabbi Eliezer the Great** ben Hyrcanus and **Rabbi Joshua ben Hananiah** received from Rabban Yochanan ben Zakkai, and from all of them, **Rabbi Akiva** received. **Rabbi Simeon bar Yochai** <note>The traditional author of the Zohar.</note> received from Rabbi Akiva. This was after the destruction of the Temple.

This is the ancient [tradition], according to the voice of the master of the printed Midrash called the **Book of the Zohar**. This is also mentioned, and it concerns the Kabbalah in that Kabbalistic work; for the Rabbi and his colleagues are of it in the "End of Days." And like the word *Bereshit* <note>In the beginning</note>, which is called the **Book of Tikkunim** <note>Tikkunei Zohar</note>, using the language of the Jerusalemites, Rabbi Simeon and his colleagues turned to it. Their entire purpose was "to perform valor and a connection for the supernal, essential illumination for the masters of the Torah's healing." Rabbi Simeon and his colleagues were chosen through the **Six Spirits** <note>original: "ruach shettayin"</note> and all the assistants of the Supernal Academy and the Lower Academy, and for the Seven Mountains... for the education of the Three Wisdoms and the **Faithful Shepherd** <note>original: "Ra'aya Meheimna"</note> and the lessons of David and Solomon...

And because of this, the reception and the **Shekhinah** <note>the Divine Presence</note> were refined to make this composition by the hand of a holy one and to dedicate it. Through it, the upper and lower beings shine, to find in it "rest for the Shekhinah in exile," and freedom for you and for the whole... And it comes blessed in the "Hiddenness of the Ancient One" <note>original: "genuza d'atika," a high level of divinity</note>, the power of darkness in every time. Thus, all who believe in their God and the merit of the commandments of their poverty gather in this composition, like the priest and the goat for the Lord. The refined ones shall come into it, and for our redemption... for the Tikkunim (Rectifications)...

And all those sealed with blessed kindness in the world, the "Treasured Ones," gather to him, of whom it is said: "For whom the Lord loves, He rebukes," and to give kindness to His right hand until the congregation of the composition. They stood with us today, and regarding them it is said: "And those who turn the many to righteousness shall be like the stars forever and ever." This Providence is the wisdom of Ecclesiastes, preserved in many...

<column-break/>

...the Torah to its owners, everything explained according to a certain order to explain and to enable the understanding for the creation of that **Holy Composition** <note>The Zohar</note>, as we have received, to agree on the distinguished work by the hand of his student, our Holy Rabbi, until he received from him. And the intent and purpose in every place is "It is time to act for the Lord" <note>A common justification for revealing hidden secrets when the tradition is at risk.</note>. Perhaps, as is known to the wise of heart, the survival of the Torah is hidden within it, wrapped in the holy book.

Therefore, it was revealed in this bitter and long exile, for there is no "pleasure" for the Torah except in the occupation with the **Wisdom of the Torah**, which is the true, received wisdom <note>Kabbalah</note>. For from it, the Will of the Almighty is known in His service and His Torah. This was also the reason in the famous exile of **Maimonides** <note>original: "Ha-Rambam"</note>, of blessed memory, who was the "Key" and divided the wisdom of the scripture. Now, upon the unfolding of the law of the "Voice of the Exile," this Holy Composition was sent after being covered and hidden. When it was revealed to the world, many sought it and said: "Do not prevent it," since he promised... these shall join together, and the "Treasured Ones" gather to it...

Were it not for this, in this time, the feet of the innocent wise men would have almost slipped, and the number of those engaged in the "Holy Service" would have diminished, those who are swept away to be enticed by the "tearing of the string" <note>metaphor for deviation</note> toward the sciences [external wisdoms]. For the **"Greek Flower"** <note>Aristotelian philosophy</note> blossomed in the hearts of the Sages because of this "Little Maidservant" <note>Referring to Philosophy serving the Torah</note>, which is prey, prey, torn by philosophy. It originated from the Greek tongue, while the Hebrew tongue is like a blossoming leaf outside.

To occupy oneself with this, to arrange it in the exile, that Holy Composition was revealed... to return to shining and to remove foreign opinions. Open your eyes! And the war began to be remembered after it was absent. The "Scorpion" <note>perhaps a reference to the dangers of secular logic</note> teaches its lesson. In this continuation, everything was in the **Holy Name** that is embraced... its time draws near, and the **Spirit of the Lord** shall pulse within us. It is an enduring offering from the power of our exile, after it was fulfilled in them: "And her end is like her beginning."

Nevertheless, the "foreign wisdoms" could point to the [Divine] Name... to use this in relation to the **Shekhinah** in her exile... and further, "Heaven forbid that I should be far from you, my Master, my Master." The power of the wisdom was revealed from the composition... they shall be publicized in the highest waters until they shine into the rivers at the end of his days. And "a living man's joy is his wiping away [of tears]..."

Behold, he made it known that this composition would be like a **Crown and Wisdom**... from it, and in the final generation, it will be revealed for the sake of supplications. Through it, Jacob will have a "nearby healing" for our time and our protection, the goodness of the Redemption. The merit of the "Exile of Kindness" and the true, received, partial wisdom shall be remembered for the Lord... because it was the Supernal Will to create that Holy Composition, which is a vessel full of the pearls of the **inner Torah**, the details of wisdom, the **Secret of Divinity**, the mysteries of the Unity, and the comfort of the Lord, blessed be He.

For it is written and stands: "Voice, and they did not fear it," for Heaven forbid that the Place [God] should allow one who is enticed by folly and through whom the "Good Ones" are bitter... for there is a "Shadow of Wisdom" in Israel, for they are the philosophers... and you will find that "Pure Gold" is lacking in this. The matter is necessary and refined: it is to return and find in it "rest for the Shekhinah in her exile," and a teacher for her and for the masses. This is the necessity, and specifically the necessity for the exalted one, which is drawn through all time, and specifically in the time of exile, where it is most needed.

The hand of some of the Sages shall not be too short to supervise this... and He blew into them a spirit for the reception of the generation of Hezekiah in Babylon, while the "Exile of Jeconiah" still existed as the ladders of the Torah for these exiles, so that the **Oral Torah** would not be forgotten, nor the orders of the Torah, the reasons for the commandments, and the Work of the Chariot <note>original: "Ma'aseh Merkavah," early Jewish mysticism</note> within the Oral Torah, for all of it was there. And so, through this being revealed by the righteousness of the Holy One, Blessed be He—as they said: **"The Holy One, Blessed be He, acted righteously with Israel by revealing the exile in small measures while the 'Exile of Merit' still existed."** His righteousness has no end or cessation, and He provides this "War of Righteousness" in every generation and supervises...

# Section on the Purpose | Chapter 18

<column-break/>

### Chapter 18

We say that insofar as the **Intellect** is created and living, and whoever turns toward that light, it is necessary for him to have a source that draws him in. All the wisdom I possess is but a hole to peer into the light of those lives. This is especially true regarding the matter of the Sustainer and that light, which are distant from there. Return and merit the existence where the proof does not turn away from its simple meaning. In this regard, it is written: "I have searched," and the wisdom found in **Ecclesiastes** is life, and it is called *Return*. For this reason, it is written in Ecclesiastes that the nature of the Source is such that it resides in that which is better than it.

That *Return* refers to the peering of the **Intellect**, specifically the **Divine Intellect**. That *Return* represents the "conclusions" <note>original: toldot</note> that are merited from the "premises" <note>original: hakdamot</note> from the mixtures. Therefore, the name "merit" is used there according to its custom, for the Intellect is similar to the source and the **First Cause** <note>The philosophical term for God as the primary cause of all existence.</note>. It is called the Intellect, and as the verse sings, the entire second matter is the "nursing" of the Intellect. From the beginning of the name "Intellect," he returned and refined its merit. Just as the source is peered into, one must bless the dead and the living forever; every judgment is refined. This means to say the world is blessed because the premises of life do not allow for a rise upward, nor to take their lives from there in the judgment of the one who perceives what is included. In general, they were refined and thin, and this is what is written: "and Return," and "forever every judgment we shall refine."

The word "refine" <note>original: nedakdek</note> is used to hint that the **Object of Intellection** <note>original: muskal</note> must be as the Intellect itself, intended to examine its cut—that is, to draw it out. In general, they merited their hearts to feel its movements. All the deaths of hope that we merited will bend the judgment like a thief, and they are good with him from every side. This is what we wanted: that there is room to leave over and to snatch away, to remember a matter like this in the chapter.

### Chapter 18

We have already written in the previous chapter that the **Book of External Wisdom** <note>referring to secular or Greek philosophy</note> is for itself, and it is not connected from one wisdom to another. It is like a traveler who lives in a time of confusion, or like a small ship <note>original: mifleget hasfinah haktana</note> struggling in the depths to do its kindness, stuck like a mast that is pushed toward another wall. This is not the case for our tradition; it is not detached from its source. As it is written: "It shall not be forgotten from the mouths of his descendants," and it is written: "My words which I have placed in your mouth shall not depart from your mouth, nor from the mouth of your children, nor from the mouth of your children's children, says the Lord, from now and forever."

So too, God labored to do kindness for us from of old. The **External Wisdom**—which is received by those who follow their own sight—was not refined along with the light that is forced upon that wall. For there, the researcher pushes himself in his writing, and this is his intention regarding chance. Perhaps it does not reach the reception of the "House of Merit." It is like a place of standing water, whereas the Torah and its derivations are like the reception from the mouth of the Prophet. The **External Wisdom** is etched into the soul of the Torah. When they spoke of the "Oral Commandments," he was handing over and teaching the reasons, the secrets, and the memory of the commandments orally. This includes the **Work of Creation** <note>Ma'aseh Bereshit: Jewish cosmogony and mystical physics.</note> and what is called the **Work of the Chariot** <note>Ma'aseh Merkavah: The highest level of Jewish mysticism, dealing with the Divine throne.</note>, which is the secret of the hidden Unity according to the Intellect. This came to his aid. 

Our Sages said: "The Torah includes and the Divine Wisdom includes," and they gave a shield as it is said: "The wise man has his eyes in his head," etc. In this way, the Torah was used, which includes many things, reasons, and secrets. These are the **Wisdom of Kabbalah** <note>Kabbalah here refers to "that which is received" or the mystical tradition.</note> founded for the Elders. The Elders handed everything to the Prophets, and they deepened the clarity for the recipient from among the clean men. Thus, everything was handed over to the Priest, the teacher, who is a "Tree of Life" for all who hold onto it. The traditions of the Torah and Wisdom were heard by the **Men of the Great Assembly**, and there the reception reached its strength, its understanding, and its tables. For the holy inner meanings and the secrets, throughout that entire time, were refined. Up until the time of the Great Assembly, it was not written down; nothing was spread out, whether great or small, from the Written Torah or the Tradition. This **External Wisdom** was not like what was handed to Moses at Sinai from the mouth of the Almighty. Regarding these hidden things, all was handed to the Sages of the Great Assembly. And finally, we understand...

<column-break/>

### Chapter 10

...and to raise the grace of our inquiry, to ask: what is the life of the Intellect? What is spoken in the thoughts that sometimes rest and are sometimes profaned? In the hour that the memory rests from the mouth of the Holy One, laws and droplets [of wisdom] flow. For the Glory <note>original: Kavod - often referring to the Divine Presence</note> rests even from the mouth of the Holy One. Our Sages chose this because the Glory rests even from the mouth of the Holy One, and the "ancient ones" <note>referring to early traditions</note> held fast to this wisdom and influenced them. When they are "profaned" <note>original: mechalot - perhaps meaning common or secularized</note>, they are simply contemplating and understanding, deriving from the premises great wisdom and the secret of the "Inner Intellectual Connection," which is joined in action. 

"Let man become a living soul" — this refers to the "Speaking Spirit" <note>The human capacity for rational speech.</note>, because from the beginning of his creation, man was meant to be an "Intellect in Action" <note>Sechel ba-po'al: A philosophical term for the mind when it is actively thinking and perceiving truths.</note>. It was chosen that they should not inherit anything except for the "revealed works," for there is no death for them. Their sustenance is only their wisdom, to pour upon them influence and expansion so they do not achieve evil ends for themselves.

We return to the idea that from their "existence," we found Rabbi [Judah the Prince] called by the name "Rabbi the Speaker," as he came with the help of the Torah of the Holy One. Through his religion, they hold the curse within them. And Rabbi Ami bar Hanina [spoke] through his study and his speech, for from their existence, we understood this place. Rabbi Tanhum bar Hanina taught us that the occupation of the angels was due to their study—meaning, there is a place for error in what they said: "From our existence we have come to think of subtle matters for ourselves." 

One must realize that they have nothing of their own. All their perception and excellence comes from what time has given them from their source, not from themselves. This is the meaning of the "Measured Spirits," the masters of the clearings, regarding the seventy laws. All of this follows the "Upper Word." In this manner, His providence [watches] over the reception of both the commandments and the curse, which is the **Internal Wisdom**. For the premises derived from it will be contemplated and will give birth to later conclusions. Regarding the matter of "hearing His words," let him take for himself, for nothing is empty or void of its Intellect. 

This is hinted at when they said: "One who adds in wisdom..." <note>likely referring to Ecclesiastes 1:18, "he who increases knowledge increases sorrow"</note> for they did not learn to open their Intellect at all, nor to use the "Intellectual Matter" and the human thought in anything from the Wisdom and the secrets of the Torah. For this, the Scripture hinted: "Do not mix the words of your heart." It is enough for him to have the "Internal Thinker" from within himself, and by the expansion of his Intellect, he will be saved from death and heresy.

Whoever fulfills the "Commandment of the Spoken Word" that we mentioned, it shall be said of him that he is "living," for he resembles the **World of the Intellect**. From this perspective, the perfect man is called "Master of the Divine Intellect," for the Torah and the Divine Wisdom are written together. One thing is needed for the other. The believer needs it to sweeten our questions. The drawing out of the premises from within them will build and give birth. Philosophers are not "substantial" except for what they clarify from the **Divine Intellect**. Therefore, even the conclusions they reach are remembered as his, and he raises them. Then they will recognize their Master, and no filth will cling to them as they travel toward the World of the Intellect. 

Thus, the Intellect and the Religion <note>original: HaSechel ve-haDat</note> delight in each other. Indeed, it has been said: **"The Intellect and the Law are two sisters."** This is refined in the knowledge of the "Thoughts and the Traditions" according to the External Intellect. Therefore, the Intellect lingers with the Religion of the deaths, and they distance themselves. In the end, a "foreign language" will be created for anyone who did not want to see the lights of the Torah and the thoughts from the **Supreme Wisdom**, which is above all Intellect. 

Therefore, the one who prays to his God labors according to the External Intellect, for he shall not leave it at all, so that his intention will be the **Divine Intellect**. Upon this Intellect and the Religion that comforts him, he clings to the truth. The Intellect and the Religion are indeed two sisters. 

Regarding all of this, King David (peace be upon him) hinted when he said: **"For with You is the source of life; in Your light do we see light"** <note>Psalm 36:10</note>. He said that the "Source of the Higher Lives" is *with You*—meaning, it is not a separate thing. He said it is like a small ornament that he spreads over us to another; it is not separate from the Light, and it is not a foreign thing. This is the "God of the Great Intellect," the Life that sustains everything, and He is the Source of Life. "In Your Light"—this is the Divine illumination within the Torah. "We see light"—and they said of it: a light that already existed, and it is the Life that was mentioned.

# Section on the Purpose | Chapter 19

->**Chapter 19**<-

At the end of his days, in the years the sun stands still, he became more heavily burdened in his return and alluded to it. From this, my heart sees the entanglements of the secret among the nations, which swept toward him and took hold of him. When shall I find rest and ease? There is the secret of the cauldron <note>original: kalachat; possibly a mystical reference to a vessel of transition or turmoil</note> that took hold of him, and the secret of the upper realm, a charm for the destroyer, and the secret of the suffocator. It is a scheme from within the longing for death, and this is because he was enticed without lack afterward; therefore, that which stands upon the heart is a reminder to the veteran, for she is a "daughter of harlotry" <note>An allegorical reference to Proverbs, where the "strange woman" represents heresy or foreign ideologies.</note>. The secret of my merit of peace-offerings <note>original: zachti shelamim; a reference to Proverbs 7:14</note> stands upon the fulfillment of his forgetting, in order to give a reason for his words. The Intellect is half of the entire dance, for the holy dance is upon the edge of the tongue. "I have merited peace-offerings" refers to that which is taken, and the secret of "I have merited peace-offerings" is a building for all the responses that prosecute the world. Such a building was for the Levites, in order to open the world constantly. He who is boorish and lacks a heart—he is the one written about in the hints of the Midrash of Rabbi Machoniel ben He-Chakham regarding the "Third Wisdom." There are midwives for the "Fifth Evil," which is the bride <note>or "exhaustion"</note> in her writing. From there, he brought wise men as spies beneath our understanding of the world. There are times when it is like glass, and from there they are the ones who deduct all kinds of spoils and constellations. The Prince of Human Delights and the foolishness of the body—from there comes the bitterness and the blackness <note>refers to "black bile" or melancholy</note> leading to transgressions, and the gravity of the choice to bypass them. From there come evil thoughts and reflections, and from there comes life to the bitterness of the heart and the bitterness of the eyes. From there come those who are crushed and shriveled. From there, that which is not healed in its clay is written by the authors of clay, and from there comes "Wisdom without Clay" <note>original: chokhmah bli cheres; likely referring to spiritual wisdom vs. material philosophy</note>.

He was riding upon one order and going there, but the cause and effect was to learn his wisdom. That which caused him to fall from his kingdom was the lack, yet his wisdom stood by him in his faithfulness. Because of it, in my thought, the women who stood for him were all in anger <note>original: af</note>, as it is written: "she shall yearn." Concerning Solomon, for "wisdom is better than strength," it is the "Fifth Wisdom" of Solomon which was written for him in the pan <note>original: machavat</note>, as it is written: "And the Lord gave wisdom to Solomon." Regarding this, it is said: "A man's wisdom illuminates his face" <note>Ecclesiastes 8:1</note>, and it is written: "Solomon's wisdom surpassed the wisdom of all the people of the East" <note>1 Kings 5:10</note>, to walk in the paths of kindness. He was going toward the mountains, refining his speech, ascending and measuring to learn their wisdom, which caused him to deviate from following the Lord. For the multitude of the refiner did not draw near; he took hold of it and was enticed with the people and came with his worn-out garments in his palm. Through this, he came to all sorts of heresy to beget and give rest, and through the enticement to merits, etc., he led me in the matter, and through it, I was caught in the proofs. I transgressed what is written in the Torah: "Keep your way far from her" <note>Proverbs 5:8</note>—this refers to heresy. For she is weak in taste, a shame to the horns of thought. He was prostrating himself with the soothing words of his mouth, and they set it up for him so that he would not need to kill or deaden himself for the Torah and the commandments. The spirit of turning returned with strength to my "Small Wisdom" <note>Chokhmah Ketanah</note> and my "Understanding" <note>Tevunah</note>. The wisdom and understanding mentioned here were three parts: "Wisdom opened her books," and afterward, "I searched them," etc. And he said to my thought: "to my understanding"—this is the "Fifth Inner Wisdom of the Soul," which is the **Kabbalah** <term>Kabbalah: the received mystical tradition of Judaism</term>. This understanding is meant to diminish the other wisdoms that are not his wisdom. In the end, one must not do good by them nor sin after them, for the multitude of the "Five" brought the daily learning. In the end, they are **External Wisdoms** <term>External Wisdom: secular sciences or philosophy, often viewed as spiritually dangerous in this context</term> and deficiencies, which are heresy, because they are sourced from the "Evil Portion" within the cauldron that turned against him. In his Midrash on Rabbi Shimon bar Yochai, regarding everything, all twelve are chosen, but they are difficult to give. They are prepared in the "Left" for the "Nail" which is the Holy Crown called Wisdom. Regarding this, our Sages mentioned, and from there, ten wisdoms struck these in the world, and they were included to be hidden in Egypt, each one spreading throughout the world. Were it not for the "Fifth Wisdom" that spread in the world, then all would be the portion of the "Repentant Wisdoms" from the Ishmaelites, told to the Final Wisdom. Since its source is the "Blind One," it was strange and backward to the stiff-necked people, for it is like a spark in the kingdom to act wickedly. This is why it says: "For the lips of a strange woman drop honey, and her mouth is smoother than oil" <note>Proverbs 5:3</note>. This is a parable for the Egyptians, according to the intellectual matter influenced by the opening of her smooth tongue in her teaching, and they—

<column-break/>

—entrap the soul. This is the word. And the end is "bitter as wormwood," bitter as the bitterness of death. "Her feet go down to death; her steps take hold of the netherworld" <note>Proverbs 5:5</note>. This was mentioned as the logic of what I prefaced above regarding the "Bitter Torah." It hints at the spirit, for in its "secret ways" it is crushed, so that the spirit of the fullness might be added. He calls the one who walks in the secret ways of his heart—where investigation and the purpose are—an "Old Spirit" walking in a container. He calls the **Kabbalah**, which is the "Fifth Wisdom," "bitter" because no sufficient intellectual reason is known for it, as it is above the Intellect. As it says: "Her feet... her steps..." it rouses a doubt that the intellect should properly have here: Why did the Lord do so, writing a path that is not right before a man and warning him to dwell in His name within it? The answer is: because he who says "from among the nations they shall be melted," it appears that according to the general intended perfections found within it, there is both a thing and its opposite from the spirit—which are to do good and to do evil, to reward and to punish. The weak ones did His work before Him. "God has made even this over against that" <note>Ecclesiastes 7:14</note>. These are all: He created the righteous, He created the wicked; He created the Garden of Eden, He created Gehinnom. If the intentions were not in the way these secrets were understood, it would not matter who is righteous or who is wicked. For the "Separated Wisdom" <note>Chokhmah HaNivdelet</note> from the "Created Portion" is not here to do the will of its Creator. It does not say that the primary cause was to complete the "Exalted Three." Rather, that "Strange Woman" is the standing of heresy. In her choice, the woman—the Prince of Wisdom, which is the Torah and the spirits—is in the tongue of the replacement of the Holy Levites, which is the "Smoothness of the Portion of Israel." The reason is that they are "His portion," behold their God. As she says to him, "the reward of rest is from rest." But if, Heaven forbid, he deviates toward her light and his heart is enticed after the "Strange Woman," then she is in the "Way of Bitterness" among the nations. It is her doing, as she says, "the reward of transgression is another transgression." Afterward, it will be clarified what we wrote in Chapter 19: that it is forbidden for us to investigate or search after any wisdom, whatever it may be, from the wisdoms of the nations. For they are sourced in the place that was that "Portion" intended for its proofs, which are against the "Preservation" that we were witnessed upon. Since the wisdoms—as they have been explained to us—are sourced in the "Evil Portion," their nature is the "Wickedness of the Mind" that bakes them, even in their fullness. This is especially true of the Greek concepts, which are the **Wisdom of Demonstration** <term>Wisdom of Demonstration: Aristotelian or logical philosophy based on proof</term> and the secret of knowledge that follows the "stubbornness of the heart," for it is drawn from the "Intended Created Wisdom," the **Wisdom without Clay** <note>original: chokhmah bli cheres; likely meaning wisdom without a spiritual vessel</note> that follows your own evil stubbornness. For this is for the nations. "And you shall not follow after your own heart" <note>Numbers 15:39</note>; the Torah told us to investigate our knowledge according to the futility of the standing and the mechanism of the columns. The one who knows the hidden things quickly from the springs of the **External Intellect**, as will be mentioned in the chapter following this one, God willing.

It is known that the virtue of Truth is the highest level at the end of the derivatives of evil and the Prince. The "Separated Wisdom without Clay" and the "External Wisdom," as we have written, are aimed against the "Included Kabbalah." This is the "Famous Wisdom," the Wisdom of Solomon, and the Kabbalah of the **Niddah** <term>Niddah: technically referring to laws of purity, but here likely a mystical state or "separation"</term>. A man of the bellows, for she always prepares a prosecution against it. Even though "one kingdom does not touch its fellow even by a hairsbreadth," I have made friends to sing to quiet the strife and contention in the "Man of Beauty" <note>Tiferet</note>. The wrath is the window to destroy and to deny and to uproot the taste in the eyes with a "high hand" <note>boldly</note> without life. The evil was also done out of anger because of the companions; there is the King who walks this path to bring near the "External Greek Wisdom of Proof" that I have mentioned. It is truly investigated as that which was inherited, uprooting the principles of the Torah and the Faith. **Wisdom that was emanated from the Inner Wisdom is the "sure testimony of the Lord."** For everything is "this over against that," this corresponding to that, above and below. Regarding this, the Master of the Tablet warned, saying: "Keep your way far from her"—this is the "Upper Strange Woman"; "And do not come near the door of her house"—this is the "Hidden External Wisdom." This is what we have elaborated upon to prove in this chapter.

And just as this conduct and every good existence proceeds correctly, as we have written, it is already clear to all of us and revealed to anyone who observes. The appearance of the longing for success sounds like returning and turning cycles. This is because we have already written concerning the good in the second part of this book, regarding the tradition of the later sages <term>Acharonim; the rabbinic authorities from roughly the 16th century to the present</term>—the sages of truth, may their memory be a blessing.

This division generally applies to every generation. The "House of Judgment" <note>likely referring to a celestial or authoritative rabbinic body</note> rested upon it, yet it lacked the source of the wisdom of Kabbalah. His heart <note>referring to a specific, though unnamed, sage</note> lacked this line, and his own division was revealed to him. Similarly, the heart of the Ramban <note>Rabbi Moses ben Nachman, a 13th-century philosopher and Kabbalist</note> was illuminated by the light of Rabbi Isaac the Blind <note>original: Sagi Nehor; the 12th-century father of Provencal Kabbalah</note>, and his division was revealed to him. And they took from the Levite, Rabbi Ezra <note>Ezra of Gerona, a key 13th-century Kabbalist</note>, his division, and they took it according to the judgment of their time. 

It was lacking from him, according to the calculation of the rows that followed him, along these lines, and so it goes in a cycle. This is because that "harvest" is placed within the heart of every generation. For the Holy One, Blessed be He, revealed His division to those pious ones so that wisdom would not be forgotten from Israel. Behold, this chapter contains some of the secrets of the later generations, just as it contains the traditions of the early ones. Nothing was lacking until the end, except for one thing: the wise man whose heart was like a ladder for their heart... 

And concerning the burden of the division of all those who tread the path, the portion of Aristotle <note>The Greek philosopher, often viewed with suspicion by Kabbalists for his purely rationalist approach</note> is named "the obstructed." For those who take hold of it and those who rely on it are wandering and obstructed by his wisdom, which is built on a forged perspective. According to our obligation to resolve every doubt with humility, we must return to the opening. For the sages, according to our eyes, established their reasoning and then returned to the book. From then on, they belonged to the heart of Joseph <note>possibly a reference to Joseph Karo or an allegorical "Joseph"</note>.

They walked in the ways of the path of Kabbalistic research. He desired to find the end and the limit of the days. But they were lightheaded in their dreams, following the books of the researchers and the wisdom of the "mixed multitude" <note>original: erev rav; a biblical term for those who joined the Israelites in the Exodus but were later blamed for inciting sin</note>, and all of it was empty words. They obstructed the foundations with the Torah of the "lonely one" <note>possibly referring to a specific heretical or secular philosopher</note> to learn from, and her opinion spread. They caused destruction and broke open the hidden things.

It is upon me to reveal to him the words of the great wisdom of the past. As long as we are in the midst of the exile, the books mentioned in the versions of "External Wisdom" <note>secular sciences and philosophy</note> will cause this small thing to be moved. It was destined to be received publicly before every eye, yet all of this was due to the exile. On my account, this was the reason the heart of these wisdoms was not revealed. For the sages from whom this division was drawn have revealed to me that it was written just as we wrote it, at the center of the Second Temple. Everything that deviates from the center and the exile from the study of the exchange of Kabbalah... until it returned and was drawn to the later generations. For our Master said to us, "We have been made righteous," yet it was not so in our exile. As we have written for his days, this is the conduct and the general rectitude, were it not for the intention of this chapter.

### Chapter 19

Solomon, the King, peace be upon him, founded the Book of Proverbs <note>original: Mishlei</note> at the end of the chapter. Behold, the secret of the "Son of Man" <note>meaning a human being</note> is to flee from the "Strange Woman" <note>An allegory for heresy, foreign philosophy, or the "Other Side" (Evil)</note> and the smoothness of her tongue, which is like a pit. He turned to speak at first and to warn about the end, so that all would not be enticed by her mouth. Do not be comforted by her, but be wise and intelligent, for the Lord gives to all within it. These are the arrangements of the "Foolish Woman" <note>Another allegory from Proverbs</note> on his tongue, who returns as a light. He clarified that she is "Tohu" <note>chaos</note> and a lie.

The explanation: A "Strange Woman" <note>Proverbs 2:16</note> has a light, but the powers of reason will twist it. She is the hidden "harlot." The shell of this bread is bitter. He turned back to the merchant... and the books they chose from them were only from the longings of idolatry and the vanity of the commandments. They will not say anything about her except for the actual death she brings. For what he wrote about the song that was born here was to gird God. These are the crowns that go out, and upon this is the removal of the yoke of all the labors. What was mentioned in the words of the branch? This is the reason that covers from you these "breaches." He said: "Who is the rod that hit me? Until when will there be testimony?" And he said further, "Until when?"

<column-break/>

With the word "The Simpleton" <note>referring to Proverbs 9:4</note>, it is open and revealed to knowledge. This is because she is the opening and the invitation to the sons of man, as we wrote in the tastes of the foundations. She is the "last one" and the cause of the clouded wisdom. Therefore, the "Primordial High One" <note>referring to a high level of divinity</note> passes through the way of the ethical ones. "Whoso is simple, let him turn in hither," and to him that void of understanding, she says: "Stolen waters are sweet, and bread eaten in secret is pleasant." But he knows not that the dead are there; and that her guests are in the depths of hell <note>Quoting Proverbs 9:16-18</note>. 

This is the secret: The one whom the Lord rebukes, He corrects. He punishes the simpletons and the rebels because their seduction is in the smoothness of her tongue and the sweetness of her lips. For she is the place of evil and the place of the "deviants." So are the children of man enticed like fools. For she is like the ostriches; her mouth is smooth as milk through the ornaments she spoke of. From the "redness" <note>symbolizing judgment/severity</note>, peace be upon him, it was explained in the portion of *Emor*: write her desire to slaughter him with pearls of emptiness. This comes to his heart. And because the Merciful One warned with "My son, My son," and corrected in the matter, and took his well for him, he brought death upon himself and his descendants.

Corresponding to the four "simpletons" he mentioned, there are four curses. One is a slave to the Lord and decrees upon his middle, and a crown upon her deadly daughter. She travels to the "Cauldron" <note>the place of spiritual transition or punishment</note>. Correspondingly, "forty shall he strike him" <note>Deuteronomy 25:3</note>, which is a bitter thing.

As Rabbi Simeon bar Yochai <note>the traditional author of the Zohar</note>, peace be upon him, said: This language in the Zohar describes how she seduces with a shield of strength to virginity. She produces the "husks" <note>Klipot; the shells of evil</note> that are like a needle between us, wandering without purpose. When they are gathered to their unique source, which is separated into many sides from the Creator, her "feminine hole" is never built. It is like a dead woman who is not on the side of holiness. She is like the smallness of the heavens to the word of the "Other." She is a tree without a female to investigate her.

In the fire of holiness, there are those who dwell on every side, whether on the right or the left. They are stuck in the "Smell of the Spirit." But she is the "Evil Scent," who speaks in her palace and her ornaments are spread out. She breaks out in the quietness of the spirit. Her stubbornness causes her to have no "Holy Spirit" within her. She is the beginning of the world. And she stands at the opening of the evil, a holy "sinner." There are times for her, and she seduces and frightens from the path of order to the bitterness of the lips, like wine to the deviants from the Torah. After she is revealed, her path reaches toward simplicity. She causes all power and strength to be corrected toward her. She is a "deviant" and a "law" in her house. She is a runaway. She is corrected with the redness of a rose to sin. She is "Alilin" <note>an Aramaic term for charms or pretexts</note>. Six corrections are prepared for the rain. She is "Alilin," a weariness of understanding. Everything from her is to know the opening that is corrected in her opening, and not with strength.

She is seen in the "Four Sides," entering the hidden expanse. And oh, the redness of the rose! From the voice of all that is sweet to the world, she is corrected in four corrections which correspond to the "Storm" <note>a reference to Ezekiel’s vision of the Chariot</note>. After her, she covers her master and passes with a cup. What did she do? She was corrected in the "Cypress" with cunning. She went up to the "Elephant" and canceled the desire. In the place where the "deviant" is prepared, she is better than her palace. She is a tail of freedom and cessation, drawing near to it. She is the one "crown" of the stranger. Holy strength for the receiving of the heart... to the children of the Creator. She is a hope that trembles with gold. She causes eyes to be filled with sickness. She increases the "Bitterness of the Sea" in the drop of the serpent. She kills him... and casts his children into Gehenna <note>Hell</note>.

This was the sin that the children of man were warned about, regarding the "sweetness" that is within her. And it was so, in the time of Solomon's old age, that his wives turned his heart <note>referring to 1 Kings 11:4</note>. This is the portion of the women that he wrote about. Understand the secret of Solomon's wisdom. In it, there are many turnings of the cycle for all his actions. "For she has caught me with her lips." I did not write "to her lips" but "with her lips"—with the lips from above and from below. He sank into the "bitter soup" of the poor. This is the Torah of the "heavy one." I merited to raise those thousand wives among the creatures. They should not have returned to lift up your hearts, for this is the merit. This is the place of the son and the "harlot." It is the sign of the key for the children of man... "and after your eyes," for this is harlotry. And it says that it was corrected for him to understand her.

<meta>This page continues the philosophical and kabbalistic critique of secular "external" wisdom, specifically addressing the limits of human reason as discussed by King Solomon in the Book of Ecclesiastes. It bridges the previous discussion of Solomon’s symbolic "wives" with the broader danger of relying on logic over divine revelation.</meta>

### Chapter 20:

The modern thinkers focus on the primary principles, and each one strives and acts with cleverness to destroy, topple, and overturn the strong foundation upon which both sides build their walls of inquiry. Using **sophisms** <note>sophisms: fallacious arguments that look true but are actually misleading; from the Greek 'sophisma'</note>—which are proofs lacking the closest doubling to their eyes—they rise up, yet they fall in their journeys. For what the others considered a proof of existence in their principles, the moderns considered a proof of its absence. Through the poverty of these evils, they draw forth and pour out to their ultimate shame. The work has risen, and the wall of their divisions is broken. For if the foundation of the principle is strong, it will be the same for the perspectives of external ignorance; all the more so in matters that are **above the sphere of the moon** <note>original: "למעלה מגלגל הירח." In medieval science, the "sphere of the moon" was the boundary between the changing physical world and the eternal, unchanging heavens. Human reason was thought to be limited to the physical world below this sphere.</note>, which the hand of man cannot reach. Not every proof applies to them, and the discussion of them via the path of the student and the consensus—which is prevented from standing upon the truths—is severely lacking.

The secret of these things has already been revealed to you in the book of **Ecclesiastes** <note>original: "ספר קהלת"</note>, which is the furnace of external faith. It is taken in two paths of inquiry, saying: *“I applied my heart to know wisdom, and to see the business that is done on earth, even though one sees no sleep with his eyes day or night. And I saw all the work of God, that man cannot find out the work that is done under the sun; because though a man labor to seek it out, yet he shall not find it; yes, even though a wise man think to know it, yet shall he not be able to find it.”* <note>original: Ecclesiastes 8:16-17</note> For he had already given his heart to know wisdom and the voice of inherited wisdom via the path of intellectual, demonstrative contemplation.

*“And to see the business that is done on earth”* refers to seeing if one can grasp, by way of demonstrative inquiry, the nature of separate things and their composition in this world, and the sphere of contemplation and inquiry. For even *“day and night he sees no sleep in his eyes,”* and so on. My heart saw much wisdom, which is intellectual contemplation, *“and I saw all the work of God, that man cannot find.”* For even if they toil before Him, all these things are hindered by the depth of the concept. For the foundations of nature are the work of God, measured by His wisdom, as it is written: *“The Lord by wisdom founded the earth...”* <note>Proverbs 3:19</note> and *“His understanding is infinite.”* <note>Psalm 147:5</note>

The concept is hidden because man, being merely human, cannot dwell in the natural darkness and the separate matters to be a life-force for him by their power. For time and the existence of its days are mostly weak. *“Because though a man labor,”* etc. This refers to what man lacks in his own power, namely the toil in his inquiry by way of the student and the consensus, and this is his deficiency regarding what is **above the sphere of the moon**. He says that all the more so in this case, even if a man toils as much as he can to seek by way of the student and the intellectual consensus, he will not add anything in this inquiry of his to seek. He says, *“and he will not find,”* for it is impossible from the perspective of human nature.

He mentions **sophisms** <note>original: "סופיסמס"</note> because the one who inquires into them is not from the soul nor from the prepared intellect; rather, he is a man who inquires into nature from this side. He went to investigate these matters through these inquiries, and he knew them initially in his investigation. This was intentional, so that he would recognize the excellence of the wisdom written for him in the place where he would stand upon the truth of everything he had previously been foolish in while inquiring into it from the side of the senses and the side of the intellect that makes him a man. He is the one who says in another place: *“Then I saw that wisdom has an advantage over folly, as light has an advantage over darkness.”* <note>Ecclesiastes 2:13</note> For the "darkness" of folly consists of the inherited wisdoms of investigation from the perspective of being human. Therefore, there is an advantage and a great excellence to the contemplation of the wisdom written for him, since he stands upon the truth of all that he was foolish in before. Had he not investigated before, perhaps he would have stayed at a distance and not recognized the advantage of wisdom. He might have said that even as a mere man, he could achieve and know this. Therefore he said: *“Even if the wise man thinks to know”*—meaning, even if the man who has become wise through the wisdom that comes from the side of the intellect and contemplation says he can know and grasp what he has become wise in—he says: *“yet shall he not be able to find,”* for he has already stood upon this from all experience. And though this renewed wisdom is meant to be a source for the secret of nature...

<column-break/>

...And as will be explained here, he performed a deed after it to complete his window, which is a window within him, and to fill his wisdom. For so it was fitting for him, but he followed after other things until he too said and wrote: *“When I turned my heart,”* etc. And he said: *“Then I saw that wisdom has an advantage over folly, as light has an advantage over darkness.”* Its explanation in the Midrash of **Rabbi Shimon bar Yochai** <note>original: "רסבי" (Rashbi). A 2nd-century sage to whom the Zohar is attributed.</note> is that from folly comes the benefit of wisdom; if it were not for folly, wisdom would not be known or recognized in the world. Its excellence is recognized only by contrast, just as the benefit of light is only recognized through darkness. If there were no darkness, light would not be recognized and its benefit to the world would not be evident.

Therefore, the "advantage of wisdom" does not mean it is just for a person or for his own benefit, but rather that wisdom shines for the world and does not become entangled in errors. The text says further: *“To provide light and clarify,”* and it increases its light. The advantage is for the benefit of wisdom itself, and for the building of its goodness, so that its purpose is exceeded. Thus there is an "advantage to wisdom" specifically *from* folly. If there were no folly in the world, there would be no "wisdom." This is the way that all beauty comes out of the unsightly. The "advantage of wisdom" comes through the ordering of its opposite, which brings out its goodness and builds the benefit of wisdom through it. Therefore, wisdom is more precious than all folly, even a little bit, which is a mixture for wisdom, and it is called "wisdom." And it is not written: "my heart was led by wisdom," but *“and to lay hold of folly.”* <note>Ecclesiastes 2:3</note> Behold, it is clear that folly is joined to wisdom for its repair and perfection.

This was the wisdom of Solomon, for Solomon's vision was to pursue it to complete the window—which is why he followed after it more than was proper. Thus, it is said that the wisdom which is the excellence of the intellectual secret is "folly and madness." It is so in comparison to the true, received wisdom. Because many would agree with it, every man must be careful not to be tripped up by the "foreign tongue" <note>original: "לשון נכרית." This refers to foreign philosophies and secular ideologies.</note>, for the "Great One of Wisdom" <note>Aristotle</note> called to her, and the foundation was placed upon her. And it is said: *“Keep your way far from her, and do not go near the door of her house.”* <note>Proverbs 5:8</note>

The Torah has already explained the inquiry from the side of man and the inquiry from the side of intellectual contemplation—from the side of the matter and the thinker in the books of the Torah and the reasons for the commandments—and regarding the student and the observer. The foundation of the warning is in the statement: *“And you shall not explore after your own heart.”* <note>Numbers 15:39</note> This refers to inquiry from the side of the intellect. Regarding inquiry from the side of man, the foundation is in the statement: *“And after your own eyes.”* This matter comes specifically in the commandment of **Tzitzit** <note>original: "מצות ציצית." Ritual fringes worn by Jews, intended to remind the wearer of the commandments.</note>, which is one of the "received" commandments that have no logical reason according to the intellect of the investigators. One might say: "If I do not see it with my eyes, I will not believe," and he would say in his heart that he will not do the commandments.

In the Midrash of **Rabbi Shimon** <note>Rabbi Shimon bar Yochai</note> on the portion of *Shelach Lecha*, he said: *“The heart is the one who wants to go after...”* but only after the heart, this is for the heretics. And they said the "eyes" are those that stand over it, as it is written: *“Upon one stone are seven eyes,”* <note>Zechariah 3:9</note> and it is written: *“The eyes of the Lord are toward the righteous.”* <note>Psalm 34:16</note> But regarding these, it says: *“Do not explore after your heart and after your eyes,”* so that you do not merit the afterlife. The meaning is that seeing and thinking about the Torah and in the fulfillment of its commandments—all of this is drawn toward the good. And the divine power adds to us, saying that there is a "divine portion," and *“the Lord’s portion is His people.”* <note>Deuteronomy 32:9</note>

But the remote inquiry and thinking and secret that is drawn from all the "secret of the tree of knowledge" does not result in the "portion of Jacob." Rather, all of this is in the philosophical "exterior," which goes after the bitterness of the heart and the sight of the eyes, as will be explained. This is what was fitting to be intended in this chapter.

### Chapter 21

The zealot... and so many of our people thought that our kingdom was accepted because... I found it to be holy and... and they struggled to establish it after him. But he too stood in the benefit of his matter...

- Rashbi: Rabbi Shimon bar Yochai, the traditional author of the Zohar.

It warns that relying solely on intellectual inquiry can lead one away from the commandments and the divine portion of Israel.</summary>

<meta>This page continues the philosophical critique of human reason, specifically moving into Chapter 2 of the "Section on the Ultimate Purpose." It transitions from the general fallibility of secular logic to the specific danger of using such logic to interpret the Torah and commandments, emphasizing the necessity of received tradition over independent speculation.</meta>

-> ### Chapter 2: The Section on the Ultimate Purpose — Chapter 2 <-

True perfection, for which we strive, is the attachment to the Holy One, Blessed be He, so that He may be with all of us, as it is written: *"And I have separated you from the peoples, that you should be Mine"* <note>original: "ולהבדיל אתכם מן העמים להיות לי" - Leviticus 20:26</note>. From this, the prohibition against coming to investigate matters of the Torah and its commandments through the audacity of the intellect is also clarified. The intellect often chooses wisdom based on natural philosophy, yet all of this [the Torah] exists within His Supreme Wisdom. Our Sages, of blessed memory, alluded to this in the Midrash of **Rabbi Shimon bar Yochai** <note>original: "רשב"י" (Rashbi); the 2nd-century sage to whom the Zohar is attributed</note>, peace be upon him. He spoke regarding the "cup of language," saying: *"You shall not make for yourself a carved image"* <note>original: "לא תעשה לך פסל" - Exodus 20:4; part of the Ten Commandments</note>. Sufficient is what this mouth has opened to declare Your glory; how much one is obligated to bless and enlighten them through His conduct, to show them how careful one must be not to err or derive difficult conclusions from what one does not know and cannot grasp. It is written: *"You shall not make for yourself a carved image or any likeness."* Despite this, to exact punishment for the "cup of their error," people fall into their own brains and imaginations when they return to their merits. This imagination alone reveals that God's kindness toward His covenant is clearly lacking in their imagination.

As **Rabbi Yehuda** <note>original: "ר' יהודה"</note> taught: How beloved is kindness to Him! "God is [heard] in your voice." He did not speak in a mere metaphor. In the Book of the Lord, five lines are written, for the "Sages of the Lord dream of His voice." This is because of the staffs that were before them among the eight sons of the "tongues" called to count. The "flight of the world" is within, and the "living flight" of our songs will prepare the white spaces that include all. It is a holy dialogue; you have no word in the Torah that is not included in His Holy Name. Because of this, it is so that they should not err in His Name nor lie in it. One who lies regarding the King is not permitted to enter the King’s palace, and from there he is removed to his end.

Our Sages of blessed memory said: Behold, it is written, *"You shall not make for yourself a carved image"* <note>original: "לא תעשה לך פסל"</note>, and yet it is also written [to Moses], *"Carve for yourself two stone tablets"* <note>original: "פסל לך שני לוחות" - Exodus 34:1. The author is playing on the Hebrew word PS-L, which can mean "idol/carved image" (Pessel) or "to carve/hew" (Psel). The Sages use this to distinguish between man-made idols and God-sanctioned transmission.</note>. To the Sages, this means: "The Lord shall be distinguished for you." Do not be lacking in your Master’s tradition, for "The Sages of the Lord are your portion." Regarding those who fall into imagination to exact punishment from themselves, when they return to judge themselves before Him, how abandoned they become! They are brought close and then overturned into **Gehenna** <note>term: Gehenna <gloss>A place of spiritual purgation or suffering in the afterlife</gloss></note>. 

The Kabbalistic Rabbi, **Rabbi Shem Tov** <note>original: "ר' שם טוב" - likely referring to Shem Tov ibn Shem Tov, a 15th-century Spanish Kabbalist and critic of philosophy</note>, wrote about this: It is better for a person to understand the words of the "Grace of the World," those holy beings on high who see the King's face. Remove yourself from error and the folly of abstractions and common knowledge. Their taste is lacking, for the "Masters of Configurations" <note>original: "בעלי התכונות" - historically refers to astronomers or those who believed in using celestial alignments to create talismans</note> intend to make images as a vessel to receive powers from the celestial host and to be aligned against them for use. But there is no permission to make these images unless it is in the way that it arose in the celestial sphere. In their pressure, they think they know how to combine the external things of the world through water and fire, and they respond to them according to the Name. They thought these works were prepared and ready to receive the portions of the divine and its host. But in the words of the **Tur** <note>original: "הטור" - likely referring to the legal code Arba'ah Turim or a related commentary</note>, it is famous that everything lacking the "holy Merkavah" <note>term: Merkavah <gloss>The "Chariot"; a central school of early Jewish mysticism focused on the divine throne</gloss></note> is far from the Lord. It is written, "My Name is in him." It is a sin to think one can make a likeness of these forms through our own inquiry. Such people do not provide cover at all; rather, they think the external form will serve the constellation. The material would then be like a buried root, and through the conducting power, it would be prepared for the "absolute force" <note>original: "כח המוחלט"</note>. But the thinker has no readiness for this; he only diminishes and mixes the absolute force with his own deeds and nature. Therefore, he errs and is uprooted from the world, for he **replaces the King with a servant** <note>note: This refers to the sin of "Avodah Zarah" or foreign worship, where one worships the intermediary (like a star or angel) instead of God</note>, exchanges good for evil, and lies about the totality of everything.

This is also the secret of the "difficult matters" in the Torah. They are given as hints to the essence of Divinity and hidden wisdoms. It is necessary to understand their physical form and their explanation in relation to the hidden imagery within them. The hint in them is like signs permitted for use. When you have no other path, the secret is not prepared to rule over matter and forces. His wisdom is an internal, special virtue, like the images of old.

In the first chapter of **Ethics of the Fathers** <note>original: "מסכת אבות"</note>, they brought **Rabban Gamliel** <note>original: "רבן גמליאל"</note> saying: *"Make for yourself a teacher (Rav), and remove yourself from doubt; and do not tithe by estimation"* <note>original: "עשה לך רב והסתלק מן הספק ואל תרבה לעשר אומדות" - Pirkei Avot 1:16</note>. It is fitting for me to say that this perfect man intended to add a safeguard so people would not err regarding the secrets of the Torah and its nature.

<column-break/>

[The teacher explains] the commandments for all. "Make for yourself a teacher" means to receive the tradition from him, so that they do not become foolish as we have explained. For one who walks this path in the name of the "King of Speculative Intellect" <note>original: "השכל העיוני המופתי"</note> finds his life in doubt. He easily falls into the arguments we mentioned that occur in every generation—the "philosophers" <note>original: "למתפלספים"</note> who deny and lack the depth of knowledge and secrets. For whatever one proves with a "demonstration," another may reveal the opposite. This is why he warned: *"Make for yourself a teacher and remove yourself from doubt."* 

The **Jerusalem Talmud** <note>original: "בירושלמי"</note> says: "Any Torah that does not have a father’s house <note>original: "בית אב" - meaning a clear lineage or tradition of transmission</note> is not Torah." In the Midrash, they said this means one should not try to learn the essence on one's own, but rather from others. If one learns from others, his learning stands in an exalted place. But one who learns only from the verses by himself, his learning does not stand; his heart is not confident, even if he praises himself. 

The explanation is this: One who receives his wisdom from others—it stands forever and cannot be contradicted in any way, for so he received from his teacher, and his teacher from his teacher. This knowledge transcends the hour, reaching what is impossible for the human intellect to discover or grasp on its own because it is above it. For this, one needs a teacher to receive from. This is the "removal of doubt," because he is certain that what he received is the truth. 

He further explains this by saying: *"And do not frequently tithe by estimation"* <note>original: "ואל תרבה לעשר אומדות"</note>. This means one should not apply his own mind and speculative guesses to the statements of the Torah and the reasons for the commandments. Do not rely on the multitude of "accidents" and intellectual inquiry. They hinted at this using the laws of **tithing** <note>term: Tithe <gloss>Hebrew: Ma'aser. The practice of giving a tenth of one's produce to the Levites or the poor</gloss></note>. If one increases his tithe beyond the law, that which he takes out becomes **Tevel** <note>term: Tevel <gloss>Produce from which the required tithes have not been properly removed, making it forbidden to eat</gloss></note>. 

The Master said: "One who increases his tithes makes his fruit corrected, but his tithes are *Tevel*." Similarly, one who increases the use of human intellect regarding the "accidents" of the Torah becomes confused. Even if in the matter of tithing he physically fixed the grain, it is not the same here. For what he brings forth in his inquiry is *Tevel*, and it is a grave sin to "consume" it, bringing the danger of death upon himself. He has distorted the tithe and made it the opposite; he has defiled the intention of the Torah because he understood it as the opposite of the True Will.

It is known that things which appear to the "accidental knowledge"—the primary knowledge of memory—are misleading. He who receives knowledge through the "faith of the inclined" <note>note: likely referring to those who rely on sensory or logical inclinations rather than revelation</note> sees only what is revealed to them. But the hand of the inclined has no power over the essence. It is impossible to speak of it unless you learn and receive it. The researcher who speaks of what is hidden from faith is far from the truth; "it is deep, deep, who can find it?" <note>original: "עמוק עמוק מי ימצאנו" - Ecclesiastes 7:24</note>. 

The receivers of tradition have already counted the errors that occur in the first type of knowledge. These are the errors of folly. Because the primary gaze at the "hidden essence" cannot fall upon the truth except by chance. This is because "hear-say" is often faulty, and the truth is hidden behind a partition, especially regarding the five senses. In this, the estimation of "it is better for me" is often crooked. Because external intellect considers the "thought" to be everything, and many times one thing acts as a covering, exchanging good for evil and lying about the whole. This is the first trap for one who walks in doubt. It is written of such people that they "stagger." It should not be so; one must hear the Voice and fear the Voice to be strengthened. 

The second error happens when the masses exchange a dream-vision for reality and conclude in their hearts that a magical transition is a lie. This is because their knowledge is not from the source, but is a "child of the stranger" <note>original: "בת הכוזר" - possibly a reference to external or foreign philosophies</note>. In this way, all paths of royal inquiry occur, and one must distance himself from this development which fills every generation with the opinions of men and their free-thinking inquiries...
