...explaining the necessities and the end of all deaths <note>This likely refers to the "death" of the ego or physical limitations in the face of the eternal</note> and their completion, and his tablets likewise. As was written in the words of **Rabbi Yohanan** and **Rabbi Hanina** and **Samarkos** <note>original: "סמכרס"; likely a corruption of a sage's name or a philosophical reference</note> and we have relied on the Torah portion of *Lech Lecha* <note>original: "פרשת לך לך" - "Go forth," Genesis 12:1</note> and the nuances of the commandments. Abraham’s friend said to him: The Holy One, Blessed be He, told him that he who is meticulous with the commandments and walks with the Creator regarding all his actions, "Go forth from your land," etc. And what the scripture says, "And Abraham was seventy-five years old" <note>Genesis 12:4</note>, from this we can see his perfection...

And so it appears from what is written in the Midrash <note>Ancient homiletic interpretations of scripture</note>, that Abraham our Father was forty-eight years old when he recognized his Creator, but when the Omnipresent spoke to him at the "Covenant Between the Parts," <note>original: "בין הבתרים"; the foundational covenant between God and Abraham in Genesis 15</note> he was seventy years old. Then he returned to Haran and stayed there five years, making him seventy-five when he left. When I received the "fifth level" <note>A reference to a stage of spiritual ascent</note> of rising from level to level and world to world, until he achieved perfection and holiness... and it was clarified to me that by the strength of his investigation, the first true light was understood and attained. The thoughts that come from us are like those that followed him; they will be established and stand, and no other power will dominate or rule over them, for he alone is honored in this. And when he achieved his desire, I understood the sanctuary with all my strength, to walk in them and cling to Him.

And the Midrash of **Rabbi Simon** <note>Possibly Rabbi Shimon bar Yochai</note> asks: on the verse "and he kept My charge" <note>Genesis 26:5</note>, how can this be? It means to say that as long as Abraham was in the world, I <note>God</note> did not need to perform My work, for Abraham stands in My place and keeps My charge. Even though this was his work—to return the world to its proper path—even in his place, I found it. And because he returned and found the blessing to do the will of his Father in Heaven, all this ascended to Abraham. The scripture says, "And he journeyed toward the south," <note>Genesis 12:9</note>. What did he do? He set his time and his sign for every person, so that he might return them to the right path. He spoke to their hearts: "To whom are you bowing? Worship the Lord, God of Heaven and Earth," and he would preach to them about the Creator. And now there is no other explanation for "the gate," which is to say that the Omnipresent, blessed be He, occupied Himself with Abraham and multiplied his reward, as found in the parable...

This was not so for him; for he clung to his Creator and followed His words and performed His work. He emerged from the general category of the nations, as the Sages of Truth interpreted: "Go from your land"—that is, he was told to turn away from the evil deeds that came from those times, and this is the blessing.

And from what I wrote on the page regarding the intention of **Rabbi Isaac** in the discourse which is a parable to a man traveling from place to place, who saw a **palace** <note>original: "בירה"; a famous Midrash from Genesis Rabbah 39:1 where Abraham sees the world as a palace and asks who its master is</note>. He saw that Abraham was occupied with the most hidden and supreme things, even there. They praised him according to all the vessels and all the ancient things of the body... but it only ascended to his understanding to merit the creatures and bring them under the Divine Presence. He was a traveler moving from place to place and from level to level, as we wrote regarding "tearing oneself away from his place" <note>A metaphor for transcending one's natural habits or environment</note> in the wisdom of the place of Godliness. The true Godliness from which he attained perfection is the unity of all creation, which is the soul of all worlds, the soul of souls, and the light of the supreme providence and abundance...

This world was created with the letter *He* <note>original: "ה"</note> and the World to Come was created with the letter *Yod* <note>original: "י"</note> <note>A classic Talmudic/Midrashic concept based on the Name of God</note>. This is to say to those who argue against it and deny all this: he brought them to the truth of this cause. The creation was as if it were hidden, and the intention was not that they denied the beginning and the end—for there is no doubt they admitted to that—but rather they removed providence and oversight from the creation, falling into their own knowledge. From this, they became worshippers of the "Queen of Heaven," <note>original: "מלאכת השמים"; a biblical term for celestial idolatry</note> for they believed that God gave the power to the stars and the constellations. He told them that there is a Master who is the First, who is the Master of the days... and he would preach to them about the Creator. This itself was their intention when they said: "Abraham's soul yearned for the King's garden." If a King walks in dark alleys, etc. And they have another wonderful intention in this, which is the hidden necessity of Godliness and His unity...

He acknowledged Him when he was in the furnace <note>A reference to the legend of Abraham being thrown into Nimrod's furnace</note>, as it is said: "Until I find a place for the Lord." And perhaps he was warned about the mixture of these divine concepts, to guard them as one would the words of prophecy. For there was no place for him in this [secular wisdom] alone. Abraham our Father, of blessed memory, followed the path of divine science and its practice, and he prepared himself with his Creator. All these necessities were according to what he attained from that science and that contemplation. Through all this, he ascended to the level of **prophecy**, for this is the fruit of his actions and his perfect service. By his merit, he completed the path for others, the intention of the Master of the Palace toward them. And God looked upon him and said to him: "I am the Master of the Palace." Their intention in what they said elsewhere: **Rabbi Elazar** said, "To what is this compared? To a King who says to his son... I am the King's son." Then there is the one who says, "I am the Master," and not you, certainly. And this is the difficulty of one who says to the King, "I am the Master and not you." So too, the generation of the Flood said what they said... "What is the Almighty that we should serve Him?" <note>Job 21:15</note>. But Abraham said, "I am dust and ashes" <note>original: "עפר ואפר"; Genesis 18:27</note>. And as we wrote, it is possible to arrive at this through the path of investigation and human contemplation. But the Holy One, Blessed be He, desired for him to live through all this. If so, you are forced to say that we have achieved this through the wisdom that was given to him, alongside what he reached through the intellectual wisdom of the world. This is what the *Sefer Yetzirah* <note>The "Book of Formation," an ancient mystical text attributed to Abraham</note> tells us, stating that there is nothing higher than the First Intellect... and this is our explanation for this chapter.

### Chapter 22

We have already written in several places in this book that the entire Torah is woven from the **Supreme Thought**. It is the divine wisdom that attaches to the Supreme, which provides and flows to all. Regarding it, it is said: "For My thoughts are not your thoughts" <note>Isaiah 55:8</note>. And they likewise said in the Midrash of **Rabbi Shimon bar Yochai**, peace be upon him: "Furthermore, there is a subtle thought... it is the foundation and the beginning of the word." It transforms from thought to thought into the Divine Will and into the Intellect... and the abundance of its repair is in the firmament. 

Thought then descends to the senses and becomes physical, so that the eye can perceive it and it can be captured by all. This thought turned into the **Written Torah** and the **Oral Torah**. This thought stands, exists, and is a fountain. It is the contemplation that the Written Torah and the Oral Torah—the "Two Sisters"—are the great intellect that was woven from the Supreme Thought. These two Torahs we received from the mouth of the "Almighty" <note>original: "הגבורה"; a term for God</note>: the one that is written is the Written Torah, and its explanation is the Oral Torah. They were carved from there, and their place and source are there. The source of all is the Thought, which is hidden from every eye that might perceive it in a vision. And as that light is found, it was created by His Will... He wanted to manifest from it two great lights: the Written Torah and the Oral Torah. They are like a gift that he bequeathed to us, an inheritance and a providence for our souls... And just as the Written Torah was mentioned as being from His mouth, so too was the Oral Torah necessarily from His mouth, for it is the "mouth of the King" <note>original: "פי המלוכה"</note> which is the life of the Torah. For what was before the Children of Israel was given by the right hand of that Source... to point toward its place and its portion for good and sweetness.

Wisdom was built upon him, and the Holy One, Blessed be He, provided him with two kidneys that flowed with wisdom and knowledge. These are the "lower divine wisdom and knowledge," not the human speculative ones, as **Rabbi the Guide** <note>The Rambam / Maimonides</note> and his followers wrote. From this holy book, he stood upon the fifth divine wisdom and the secret of the sphere, from which he gained the wisdom of the celestial movements. He attained the essence of these matters through judgment, rising above the common masses until his wisdom and attainment in these matters were recognized as surpassing all others. He became a source for them. This is what was said in the Mishnah <note>Referring to the Talmud, Tractate Bava Batra 15b</note>: **Rabbi Eleazar of Modi'in** said that Abraham our father had a great astrology [or wisdom] in his heart, and all the kings of the East and West would rise early to his door. This wisdom is the dominion of the Holy One, Blessed be He, and he stood by His will and gave from his wisdom until he was with the Knowledge that established the prophecy, which is the secret of the primordial spirit he mentioned.

He taught that the fools think this is the way to be merit-worthy in the assembly of researchers, but through this, they reach the seal of the wise. He spoke of the understanding of the additions <note>original: "תוספות"</note>, and this is his attraction to them as well, by way of a received tradition <term>Kabbalah</term> to you and from the excellence of his wisdom. He said to him: "Go forth from your land" <note>Genesis 12:1</note>. His discovery and his covenant were not from human knowledge, but from the fact that he had already flowered. Israel asked about it, and the Sages said his discovery and his covenant have weight in the saying: He was immersed in the circles of the stars. He said: If they were his circles, they would have been in the city of the days. Through the lines of speculation, the researchers were shifted by this, and it was placed before him as his source. As for what all the people of the world say regarding the kingdoms, this is the summary of their knowledge. **Maimonides** <note>The Rambam</note>, of blessed memory, wrote in the "Laws of Idolatry" <note>Hilkhot Avodat Kokhavim, Chapter 1</note>: "As soon as this giant was weaned, he began to wander in his mind. For it is impossible that it should rotate itself." He had no teacher or anyone to inform him; rather, he was immersed in Ur of the Chaldeans among foolish idolaters. His father and mother were idolaters and he worshipped with them, but his heart wandered and understood until he reached the path of truth. Thus, Abraham recognized his Creator. Regarding Abraham our father, it was not that he had a final path of being foolish; rather, they were close to error, and they were full of every blessing and evil, but in his merit. As was said in **Bereishit Rabbah**, **Rabbi Isaac ben Hakorsheh** said regarding Abraham: In the merit of Abraham. And how could they be saved even for one moment? From where [does he learn this]? "Because" <note>original: "עקב" (Ekev). The numerical value of the word "Ekev" is 172. If Abraham lived 175 years, and he recognized God at age 3, he served God for 172 years</note>. And so says the Midrash. He obeyed My voice. **Rabbi Isaac**'s explanation is that his intention was towards the essence. He was a servant of the Creator, and he did not receive it from a teacher, nor did he enter the covenant of the Lord until later. Truly, the truth is clear: from Adam until Abraham, it was through the soul and the tradition of the **Kabbalah** which those ten generations received. Prophecy existed in them, but he did not receive the intellectual message until the Sages of Truth said he was a master of the **Diklos**. Through this, he attained understanding in his soul. There are many intellectual ideas that require quickness, and I have found regarding him that they were studied and gathered. The **Scribes** <note>The early Rabbinic authorities</note> said: "What is the reading of the **Megillah**?" <note>The Scroll of Esther</note> And in the chapter titled *Helek* <note>A famous chapter in Tractate Sanhedrin (99a) dealing with the afterlife</note> it brings: "'Because he has despised the word of the Lord'—this refers to one who learns the Torah but claims it is not from Heaven." According to another interpretation: "The entire Torah is from Heaven, except for this one verse, which the Holy One, Blessed be He, did not say, but Moses said it of his own accord." This is the meaning of "despising the word of the Lord." According to yet another interpretation: "The entire Torah is from Heaven, except for one <term>Gezerah Shavah</term> <note>A formal logical tool used by rabbis to link two laws based on identical words</note> or this particular logical derivation." And in the **Jerusalem Talmud**, in the final chapter of *Peah*, it is said: "Even what a veteran student is destined to innovate before his teacher was already told to Moses at Sinai."

All of this we have mentioned to show that the Prophet and all the good things we have written are the truth of the <term>Rule of Investigation</term> <note>Hebrew: *Memshelet HaChakirah*; referring to philosophical or logical inquiry</note> and the ultimate purpose. That which the Sages, of blessed memory, placed under the rule of investigation—calling it "the blackness" <note>likely a metaphor for the limitations or "darkness" of the human mind compared to divine light</note>—is a claim regarding things that it is impossible for the human intellect to grasp on its own, such as the perfection of the soul upon which everything depends. The intellect can clarify the divine aspects through the details of the matter, which cannot be grasped otherwise. For this reason, we were merited with "the Law of the Lord which is perfect, restoring the soul" <note>Psalm 19:8</note>, and we were warned of His will through His prophet in the vision of His house. For she <note>the Torah</note> is that which teaches and reveals things that were hidden and concealed from the thought of human calculation. 

To demonstrate this perfection, in the <term>Midrash</term> of **Rabbi Shimon bar Yochai** <note>The Zohar</note> on the verse "Investigate the Torah," they explain that they returned and revealed what was written: "Do not plow with an ox and a donkey together." The intention refers to the "mixed help" which is combined from the Higher Wisdom, which brings light out of its mysteries. This is the Torah which Moses set before the Children of Israel—investigating and including within itself the teachings of the ultimate purpose. For "one stands against the other," as we have written above. This is what was intended by the following:

## Chapter 23
There is a massive doubt concerning what we have written. This is because we already wrote above in Chapter 20 that it is forbidden for us to weigh any matter of the Torah in our own minds or to follow intellectual speculation to investigate its secrets and reasons. We proved this with strong evidence, showing that one who does so is considered a "heretic." Yet, in the previous chapter, we proved that the excess of the Torah's intention—which is the essence of everything—is correct. And it is this: the purpose of the Torah and its aim is to achieve the **Divine Will**, which is our very existence. The path to this is impossible for any human intellect to confirm or grasp unless the Master of that Will makes it known to us.

If our existence is to follow a proper path, as we have written in this book, God must guide and discipline us. If so, there is no room for human investigation at all, nor is there a straight path for one who walks it if he abandons God for the human intellect. If that were the case, choice would be in vain, and man would not be able to secure the ultimate purpose or achieve the Divine intent through the union of his intellect with the knowledge of God's will. For the "Perfect Torah" is the revelation of His will, which He Himself chose to make heard and known. Who could grasp His will if He did not reveal it in His own glory and essence? 

This is the meaning of "The Lord descended upon Mount Sinai" and "God spoke all these words, saying." We heard from His mouth all the general principles of the commandments, the <term>613 Mitzvot</term> <note>The total number of commandments in the Torah</note>, which comprise the entire Torah and are the fruit of the Divine Will. He made us hear the general Torah in its entirety and its details through His prophet in the vision of His house. Furthermore, everything that the prophets and the Sages were destined to innovate, to enact, and to teach in every generation was revealed in part to Moses, as we wrote in the previous chapter. Everything was included in the Torah, for the Divine Will preceded the writing of the Torah. God did not want to change anything for the sake of intellectual investigation. This is a powerful reason to follow the straight path, which is the intended purpose. This reason is sufficient to forbid and distance oneself from investigating the reasons for the commandments based on human opinion or intellectual research. 

However, after these words and conclusions, there is a difficult question

<column-break/>

and a massive doubt regarding what has been proven here. It concerns what is found in the **Oral Torah**—the **Mishnah** and the **Talmud**—which is the explanation of the commandments. There, laws are proven through the ways of logic and analogy, which are the very essence of investigation and intellectual reasoning! Every time there is a dispute between the Sages of the Torah—who are wise, discerning, and primary thinkers—the dispute between the sides is based on their reasoning (*sevarah*). One says "the reason of Rabbi So-and-so is such," and another says "this is the logic of his words." Is this not a large and very honorable part of the laws of the commandments, founded upon the path of investigation and reasoning? This is the very thing we proved was forbidden according to the intention of the Torah!

Furthermore, consider the decrees and stringencies enacted by the Prophets and Sages in every generation to build "a fence around the Torah." It was incumbent upon them, by the Master of the World, to do this. This is what is included in the Torah where it says, "And you shall guard My charge," which they received and interpreted as "Make a guard for My guard." They were given permission to innovate strict decrees, and this is what is passed down to us by the authorities who came after. This is a second major category, and in it too, disputes fall between the perfect authorities—one says "this is for this reason," and his colleague does not agree, or one decrees one way and the other does not.

Additionally, there are many matters concerning human conduct that are conducted according to investigation. These involve no addition or subtraction from the commandments but are for the benefit of people in matters of Torah, tradition, enactments, and customs. The Sages and Prophets in every generation agreed to permit all of this. Not only that, but it is written that God agreed with them in their authority. As we say in the Tractates of **Shabbat** and **Eruvin** (Chapter "Osin Passin"): **Rav Judah** said in the name of **Samuel**: "At the hour that **Solomon** enacted the laws of *Eruvin* <note>A legal mechanism to allow carrying on the Sabbath</note> and the washing of hands, a <term>Bat Kol</term> <note>A heavenly voice</note> went forth and said: 'My son, if your heart be wise, my heart will be glad, even mine'" <note>Proverbs 23:15</note>. 

And there in the same chapter: "I have stored up for you twenty generations—these are the words of the Torah and these are the words of the Scribes." The "words of the Scribes" are those things innovated in every generation to build a wall and a fence. In the chapter "Ein Omdin," it says: "'For your love is better than wine'—the Congregation of Israel said before the Holy One, Blessed be He: Master of the Universe, the words of your beloved ones (the Scribes) are sweeter to me than the wine of the Torah (the Written Law)." And in the **Midrash Chazit**, they write that the words of the Scribes are more beloved than the words of the Torah. For example: if one violates the law of *Tefillin* <note>Phylacteries</note>, which is from the Torah, he might be exempt; but if he adds a fifth compartment to the *Tefillin* to override the words of the Scribes, he is liable. 

**Rabbi Tanachum bar Hanilai** in the name of **Rabbi Judah** used to pray: "May it be Your will that I do not fail in the path and the fence of reading the words of the Sages." He restrained himself because of "thieves"—meaning if he were to violate a positive commandment, he would be like a servant who rebelled and became liable for his life. They understood the words of the Scribes to be more stringent than the words of the Torah.

Behold, the Sages say in the name of Wisdom that Wisdom was given to them, and their instruction comes from it regarding all that they decreed and enacted. Not only that, but these matters are the very essence of the Master of the World's intent, even with the legal arguments based on investigation and reasoning, which we previously argued against. 

Furthermore, it is difficult to understand their statement regarding all the legal opinions and Torah reasonings: "These and those are the words of the Living God." We learn in *Eruvin*: "Rabbi Abba said in the name of Samuel: For three years the House of Shammai and the House of Hillel argued. These said the law is like us, and those said the law is like us. A heavenly voice went forth and said: 'These and those are the words of the Living God, but the law follows the House of Hillel.'"

The **Rashba** <note>Rabbi Shlomo ben Aderet, a 13th-century Spanish scholar</note>, of blessed memory, wrote in his Responsa: "If these words were not written, I would not have dared to say them—the words of the Scribes are the words of the Living God." This is hidden and there are many interpretations. The conclusion is that when the Torah was given, every single word was given with seventy facets of meaning, including reasons for prohibition and reasons for permission, for impurity and for purity. The law follows the consensus of the Sages in every generation, and the decision is made according to their intent. This is correct according to the law and the path of truth, and there is a secret in this matter. And if it were...

-> # Chapter 22: The Section on the Ultimate Purpose # <-

The rest that encompasses all. In the Midrash of **Rabbi Shimon bar Yochai** <note>original: "Rashbi"; the 2nd-century sage credited with the Zohar</note>, peace be upon him, it is said that the sound of the **Shofar** <note>The ram's horn blown on holy days</note> goes forth to those who are outside the land of Israel, and it descends to give them life. This is because they have no merit of their own, but through the rebuke, all of Israel returns to God. For this reason, at the time of the resurrection for judgment, they began to hope for the word as it is written: "**Engraved** on the tablets" (Exodus 32:16). Do not read it as *charut* <note>meaning "engraved"</note> but rather as *cheirut* <note>meaning "freedom"</note>. This is a literal freedom for all who labor in the Torah.

And in the Midrash **Exodus Rabbah**, it is taught regarding the word "engraved": **Rabbi Judah**, **Rabbi Nehemiah**, and the **Rabbis** disagreed. Rabbi Judah says it means "freedom from the kingdoms" <note>freedom from foreign political subjugation</note>. Rabbi Nehemiah says it means "freedom from the **Angel of Death**." The Rabbis say it means "freedom from suffering." All of them intended to point toward the source from which the Torah was carved, to make known that all of its essence is from Him. For the nature of the **source** <note>The Divine origin</note> must be found in that which emanates from it. It is known that the source is the fountain of life and goodness, and there is no deficiency or impurity in it. Therefore, the ultimate end, the boundary of death, and the shadow of death are far removed from there, and they have no portion in the Source of Life.

Because the benefit is great in the place where merits and rewards exist, there too life is eternal. The Counselor <note>God</note> has no cause for death or suffering, for those are not the result of merit. This Source is the All-Inclusive, for the nature of the Source is to benefit those who receive it according to their purity. Every part of it is sent there because we were carved from the place of perfect existence.

If so, the engraving of the Tablets was not meant to be revealed except by His will. What emanates from Him cannot be known or understood until it is proven that it is from His presence and by His will. He Himself must make it known. For this, the **Oral Law** was necessary, along with receiving from the mouth of the **Almighty** <note>original: "Gevurah"; a rabbinic name for God emphasizing His power</note> the explanation of the Torah and the acquisition of the **Written Scripture** before the Oral Law. Just as it was hidden, so He wrote all the words as an explanation for their engraving and their sealing, for the benefit of "freedom" in its place.

As the **Sages** <note>original: "the Work"</note> said, the essence of what was written—its light and wisdom—is for the benefit of the listening and thinking mind. Its explanation is the dwelling place for the active force. Man can only know this through the "Upper Oral Law" <note>The divine wisdom behind the spoken tradition</note>. Its essence, the soul of its dwelling, can be grasped by a human in writing, like a sign for a traveler. This is the very path for the necessity of the **Written Torah** and the **Oral Torah**, which we received from His mouth. The benefit of the Written Torah is that it was written in the most excellent and exemplary way, while the Oral Torah is entirely "with us and within us."

Regarding what was written by the "Writing of the Spirit" <note>Divine inspiration</note>, see what was written in Chapter 2 of this book, regarding the statement of **Maimonides** <note>original: "Rambam"</note> on this matter. When it arose in that Pure Thought to write the script and give it to us for our benefit and our proof—and even though it was in His Glory, blessed be He—do not think that human investigation can reach its ultimate heights. It is far off, for its wonder is great, and it is more precious than what can be attained by the human mind, which grasps only broken fragments. Human inquiry often brings faulty divisions and storms of confusion. But through the "Voice" <note>Revelation</note>, it becomes known. Then the goal of the writing is achieved—not just for physical rest, but for the sake of the Name.

I do not say this so that you should uproot or deny the words of the Torah, which is the beauty of all things. Denying it is the denial of everything, even in matters of faith. The Name is the one who displays its public wonders. See from these pure things that the Torah is a witness to His rest, to behold the Lord of All, for He is literally His Name. It is the **"Testimony of the Lord is faithful"** (Psalms 19:8). If so, one should receive it from Wisdom and for the sake of freedom. If someone comes to say a law that does not listen to this, we do not listen to him, for he is likely a liar. Similarly, intellectual investigation, once it denies the Torah as the "Testimony of the Lord," brings a thousand proofs to strengthen its own narrow straits. But the "Testimony of the Lord" has set your table—the **Table of Perfection** <note>A metaphor for the complete and divine system of the Torah</note> which is set before the humble.

<column-break/>

He did good and unified it to show a straight path for every species and offspring. No confusion or proof-seeking is found in it, nor any storm. You can then arrive at this through the path of intellectual research and knowledge, for the proofs and evidence point to this. The "Perfect Torah" is perfect from its beginning to the place where the source of all intellect ends.

This is why the "Root of Roots" for faith is in the tradition: "**In the beginning God created...**" (Genesis 1:1). Even in the rest of the words of the Torah, He informed us of its entire existence from His own mouth. He did not leave it to the intellect, which is full of great reversals and fluctuations. Even though he <note>Moses</note> stood in prophecy, God did not want the Torah to be lacking by coming from the mouth of Moses alone. Therefore, it is added that "Moses spoke," but it was done through the "Mouth of the Lord." Moses became the intermediary for all who received it. This was so that there would not be anything in the Torah for the One God that did not come from the Master of the World.

There is a matter they have already received. They said in the Midrash of **Rabbi Shimon bar Yochai**, peace be upon him: "**Moses would speak and God would answer him with a voice**" (Exodus 19:19). What does our group say about these essential words? "He answered him with a voice"—meaning with the voice of Moses. When it was a "Voice" <note>Revelation</note> to be spoken by Moses, it was revealed to them. But even regarding the voice of which it is written, "And God spoke," it is also written, "Moses would speak." This was so they wouldn't say to Moses, "You speak with us..." (Exodus 20:16). Therefore, "Moses would speak and God would answer him with a voice," so that it would not be found that there was any deficiency in its teachings. It should not be thought that Moses spoke the Torah from his own heart. The Sages said: Did he speak from himself? No, rather he spoke from the mouth of the Almighty. Even when it seemed to be from himself, it was because he was the "Voice" to say "And it was," and so he told the word.

Consider these things regarding what we have said. There was a question against this from what was said in **Tractate Megillah**, in the chapter *Bnei Ha'ir* (31b), regarding the Mishnah: "We do not interrupt the **Curses** <note>original: "Klallot"; the sections of rebuke in the Torah</note> in the **Priestly Torah** <note>The book of Leviticus</note>." They asked in the Gemara: From where do we know these things? **Rav Ashi bar Nachmani** said in the name of **Samuel**: Scripture says, "My son, do not despise the chastening of the Lord" (Proverbs 3:11). **Rabbi Shimon ben Lakish** said: Because we do not say a blessing over retribution.

**Abaye** said: This was only taught regarding the curses in the Priestly Torah <note>Leviticus 26</note>, but regarding the curses in the **Repetition of the Torah** <note>Deuteronomy 28</note>, one may interrupt <note>i.e., stop for a different person to read</note>. What is the reason? Abaye said: Those <note>in Leviticus</note> are in the plural tongue <note>spoken as God's direct warning</note>, while these <note>in Deuteronomy</note> are in the singular tongue. Those were said by Moses from the mouth of the Almighty, but these were said by Moses "from his own mouth."

Since it appears from the simple meaning of the words that the curses in Deuteronomy were said by Moses, it would imply there are things in the Torah from Moses and not from the Holy One, Blessed be He. This contradicts what we agreed upon. But I take his statement "Moses said them from his own mouth" to mean: he did not say them purely from his own human heart. Rather, they were spoken through his "prophetic voice" from the mouth of the Almighty. The difference is that those in Deuteronomy come from the "Voice of Mercy." Because they are from the attribute of Mercy, Abaye said one may interrupt them, for there is no issue of "not blessing over retribution" in the same way. But the curses in the Priestly Torah were said from the mouth of the "Power" (*Gevurah*), which is the Voice of Judgment. Therefore, one does not interrupt them.

Furthermore, they said in the Midrash of Rabbi Shimon bar Yochai: "Rav said: For the future generations, everything was said from the mouth of the Almighty. It was also said that everything was from the mouth of Moses himself." These are the curses in Deuteronomy. They were "clothed" in Power. All of it is "Moses speaks and God answers him with a voice." "Moses speaks"—this is the voice of Moses. "And God answers him with a voice"—this is the Power/Judgment, making the voice heard.

They also believe that the Sages and students were destined to engrave, research, and tell until the end of all generations. Everything was revealed to Moses. They received it as a certainty to let us know that everything the Sages innovated—even their disputes—was already fixed and written in the **Higher Wisdom**. They measured it exactly as it was measured in that original engraving. Nothing goes outside of it, for everything is included within it.

Truly, in Tractate Megillah, in the chapter "The Holy One," it says: "God revealed to Moses at Sinai the **Inferences of the Torah** and the **Inferences of the Scribes** <note>original: "Dikdukei Torah" and "Dikdukei Soferim"</note>, and what the Scribes..."

### Chapter 23

For every time, season, and value, one evaluates it according to its extension toward the future in its relative proportion. The description of the magnitude of the **Will** is expressed by the word "Power," intended to awaken the blessing. This relates to a decree of strength against the material fruit of haste, the Will, and the depletion that mingles with it during the **Day**. You will find in all the holy books a clear explanation and writings on the decree that contains the secret of the word **Day**, for the word "Day" is the essential root of it. The description of the completions and the allusions in this section regarding the **Torah**, the **Prophets**, and all its homiletic study <term>Midrash; interpretive traditions</term> is that one engages with them at **Night**, because that is the nature of the word "Night." This "fragrance" <note>an allusion to spiritual intuition</note> is attained by the one who reads it with perfection. However, not all investigations in the **Gemara** <note>The component of the Talmud comprising rabbinic analysis and commentary</note> are there for that purpose. Therefore, it is said, "And 'Living' <note>original: 'Chai'</note> it shall be called for men," and this refers to the firstborn, hinting that "the Lord is with you then."

After one sanctifies the new repetitions each and every day to show that the good flows constantly, there is no cessation of that **Great Voice**. Therefore, there must be no cessation of the "lender" <note>likely referring to the transmission of tradition</note>, the time, and the "lending" of the lines, the disputes, the **Pilpul** <term>sharp dialectical reasoning</term>, and the insights of the wise and understanding. For the Blessed One knows the story and sustains the "hand" of the voice—the secret from which everything comes, all that they debated and sang. Everything is included in that voice as its fragment; there is no innovation from one's own mind until the stage of evaluation and the ultimate order. To me, the first doubt is hidden in this.

However, the connection to the second doubt is according to what was said: that the source, which flows constantly, has "faces" and light. From it come the variations, the small matters, and the turning faces that change according to the motion, the voice, the contradiction, the preservation, the forbidden, and the permitted—as is known to those "wise of heart." The **Great Voice**, from which there is no cessation, comes from the source, and everything comes from it. The totality of all the changing "children" <note>interpretations or outcomes</note> contains no deficiency at all. According to the greatness and appointment of that voice, things spread out from every side to be fashioned. The entire voice, from the firstborn and the writings, everything takes its own portion—this one receives the cause, and this one is pure—according to the place of his standing and his capacity. Everything comes from one place and goes to one place.

In the **Midrash of Rashbi** <note>Rabbi Shimon bar Yochai</note>, peace be upon him, it asks: Why do you not have the word of "vision" in the Egyptian script? This one thinks this way, and another thinks that way, because they saw at every "woman of the mountain" <note>likely a corruption of 'at the mountain' (Sinai)</note>. To prove the power of the branching voice hinted at by "perfection at night," all who are near eat from it. And it is written: "Everything goes to one place" (Ecclesiastes 3:20). The intention is that all things emerged from the Voice; they are the branching—the exalted, the lowly, and the wicked—until the wonder that is the Sea, as it is said, which is the "one place" that receives from there, etc. The words are completed, and there is none in our generation who knows this writing. And they said: "All to One." We have written this to say that although these scriptures and titles seem like separate authorities, it proves they do not come from a single place of honor in a way that suggests change; for in Him, there is no change despite the greatness.

Regarding the source of the soul, each of the sages maintained his own opinion, and the pure ones merited to be sated by the Torah through choice. Because study is not proven in a physical body, just as things are rectified every day Above, so must one rectify and act with them below. For this they said: "Why did the researcher engage with the Four?" <note>Refers to the four who entered the 'Pardes' or orchard of mystical inquiry</note>. And behold, you have a heart to reach everything that the pure vessels awaken. According to the measure of the beauty of the path of rectification and completion, one counts to God. In this way, it is said: "**These and those are the words of the living God**" <note>original: "Elu v'elu divrei Elohim chayim"; a classic Talmudic dictum regarding the legitimacy of conflicting legal opinions</note>. Because that which was is distant, and "deep, deep, who can find it?" (Ecclesiastes 7:24). This matter depends on the writer, for it is impossible to stand upon it. The one who strips away the cause according to the rest of the evaluation is strong. All these things require mutual intention and are joined together—this one blesses the other in our likeness. We have come to understand them, and even if it is impossible to sustain the divine face that contradicts, by agreeing to one of the two opinions. Therefore they said, "These and those are the words of the living God," and everything is one source in its intention. For all their paths are good words, yet the **Halacha** <note>Final legal ruling</note> follows the **School of Hillel** alone. In this, our doubt is hidden, and the intention of what we desired to work with in this wonderful chapter is completed.

<column-break/>

### Chapter 24

Just as it is with the Creator, who is One, in the power of every creature upon Him—you shall strengthen yourself to perceive the **Supreme Will**. But He must provide a path and a place for our hiddenness, and He Himself will make known His will and the place for it. This is the introduction: He became known to us to inform us of His will, to save us through the secret of His voice—which is the **Torah and the Commandments** <note>original: "Torah u'Mitzvot"</note> that He gave us, commanding us to keep and to do.

Just as it is in the small part of it, so it is in knowing and absorbing the sacred manner and the investigation, which is the *plain meaning* of the Torah and the Commandments mentioned above, to awaken understanding. If He Himself does not explain it according to His will—as will be clarified in the chapter on the Torah—then the **Secrets of the Torah** <note>original: "Sitrei Torah"</note> and the **Reasons for the Commandments** <note>original: "Ta'amei ha-Mitzvot"</note> are but a small portion for every creature. One must strengthen oneself to perceive and know them until He Himself makes them known.

Just as the portion of the "firstborn" <note>referring to the spiritual elite or early recipients</note> was necessary to receive the mouth of the Torah and the Commandments—for there is no overturning the face of the Torah—to receive from His mouth the Secrets of the Torah and the Commandments. And just as with the **Great Voice**, the voice that should not be without the "disputes and sittings" <note>referring to the dialectic of study</note> at night, these are the charges and the diligences and all that was destined to be innovated in all generations, events, memories, and commentaries. All of this is without the "will of the world" toward His servant in the understanding of His house. So it is with the **Secret Voice** in its totality: all the secrets of the Torah, the reasons for the commandments, and their mysteries. All these, the scholars and the sages were destined to debate and innovate within them, all without the "will of the world" to cease in his nullification.

In the **Midrash of Rashbi**, peace be upon him: "And so, every single word was a lender with all those reasons, and all those words go and flow to the rivers, and they dwell in the mysteries of the **Tefillin** <note>phylacteries</note> in this socket." The voice goes out according to the mouth, and for this, it is shown that everything is calculated in its letters in the dwelling of that word—into **seventy branches** <note>The "70 faces of Torah" representing the multiplicity of truth</note> that emerge from the hidden store of the wise. For thus said the Master: "Understanding is difficult." There is a book there, and Master Yosef said: "In the plain sense, we do not need this, for it is plain in the storm," as it is written: "**And like a hammer that shatters the rock**" <note>original: "U've-fatis ye-fatu sela"; a reference to Jeremiah 23:29, describing how one divine word shatters into many interpretations</note>. Behold, they have explained that speech creates things and branches; speech is also full of reasons, mysteries, and secrets. This great thing was so because speech is His Blessed Will, and through it, everything is one. All this was spoken to make known that everything flows from one source, which is the **Supreme Utterance**, the place from which the Torah and Commandments were established, as was explained previously.

After this is verified, if there were any doubt, it would then be necessary to explain the Torah and the Commandments, to clarify their secrets and reveal their reasons in a manner and with "faces" that prove the written Secret we have mentioned. This is almost impossible unless one can be in the company of those who know them through **Tradition** <note>original: "Kabbalah"</note> from the mouths of those who truly know. A man receives it according to his capacity from the mouth of a sage, from the mouth of a prophet, and prophet from prophet, until the **First Tradition** of those who understand and the "Breastplate of the Intentions" <note>likely an allusion to the High Priest's Choshen</note> who received the Glory from the mouth of prophecy, etc. It is said according to the wisdom of the "distributed" that was spoken by them. The **Great Voice** is a "pleasant stream," for even though it was according to many sages, the Voice is truth itself. It rectifies the Religion and the Torah in one holiness, and without "good ones" to the one place came **Moses**. Not with "early ones," but with these. There are voices and storms that were less, and the heavy weight of all of them.

And we said the mystery: that since in the **Secret Voice** in its totality, and "Life is dear to him," the intention of his eyes and the secrets, both are in it. They are clarified, and if they were to be explained thus in the **Pentateuch** <note>the Five Books of Moses</note>, it would have been necessary to engage in the "returnings" <note>logical responses</note>. The engagement and the study are according to the "lending" and the manner of performing the deed, similar to what is in the Ark, and afterwards in its reason and instruction. This is the perfection of the blessing of the Day, for this holy intellect is the essence, which is the world itself.

Wisdom is the word that is better than any other in the building of the portion of the "Tongue of the Torah." For the Torah also has things that are like a **Garment** <note>original: "Levusha"</note>; these are the stories without Law, which contain neither commandments nor Torah, and she clothes herself in them. And there are those words that are her **Body** <note>original: "Gufa"</note>; these are the depths of the bodies of the Torah, which are the Commandments and the Sayings that are her essence. And there are things and matters in their very selves which are her **Soul** <note>original: "Nishmata"</note>; these are the Secrets of the Torah and the Reasons for the Commandments.

In the **Midrash of Rashbi**, peace be upon him: "The Torah has a garment to be seen by those outside. And those fools see only the garment of the Torah... they do not look further to see what is under that garment. The body is more important than the garment, and the soul is more important than the body... In this body of the Torah, there are those called the 'Bodies of the Torah' <note>essential laws</note>. These bodies are clothed in garments, which are the stories of this world. The fools of the world look only at that garment..."

### Chapter 23: The Section on the Purpose — Chapter 23

It is possible to uphold the words of reasoning and justice, for they said: "Both these and those are the words of the living God" <note>original: "Elu v'elu divrei Elohim chayim"; a famous talmudic maxim from Eruvin 13b regarding the disputes between the schools of Hillel and Shammai</note>. Our Sages of blessed memory said that "justice" here is like the act of Phinehas <note>referring to the zealous act of Phinehas in Numbers 25</note>... and the Sages also asked: why was it necessary for the Holy One, Blessed be He, to say "these and those are the words of the living God"? Because it seems impossible to uphold the words of both opinions at once... But if I have written an introduction regarding one matter and you do not uphold the words of its companion, then the "words of the living God" do not stand. One cannot simply say his own words to reject another's. Reasoning, therefore, will not lead to such blasphemous words, for they are sufficient in this matter. Rather, the reason is fitting and aligns with the path of research and integrity, as the Rabbi <note>likely referring to Maimonides or Albo himself in the third person</note> of blessed memory hinted. And in the first chapter of Tractate Hagigah <note>Hagigah 3b</note>:

"The masters of assemblies" <note>original: "Ba'alei Asufot"</note>—these are the disciples of the wise who sit in assemblies and engage in the Torah. These declare impure and those declare pure; these forbid and those permit; these disqualify and those validate. Perhaps a person might say: "Since these declare impure and those declare pure, these forbid and those permit, these disqualify and those validate, how can I learn Torah from now on?" Therefore, the verse states: "They were given from one Shepherd" <note>Ecclesiastes 12:11</note>. One God gave them, one provider <term>Parnas; a community leader or provider, here referring to Moses</term> spoke them from the mouth of the Master of all works, Blessed be He, as it is said: "And God spoke all these words, saying..." <note>Exodus 20:1</note>. You, too, make your ear like a funnel <note>original: "afarkeset"</note> and acquire for yourself a heart to hear the words of those who declare impure and the words of those who declare pure, the words of those who forbid and the words of those who permit, the words of those who disqualify and the words of those who validate.

Behold, the Sages of blessed memory established that despite all the divisions of opinions and the contradictions that oppose one another, "One God gave them and one provider spoke them." This concept alone is very far from human intellect, almost impossible for it to accept, unless one is drawn to it by the path of the Lord, the path of enlightenment and the foundation of the light of truth. This will be clarified immediately upon explaining the opening of the verse to which we merit. We rely on the crown of the first verse according to what he said, which is that His Supernal Wisdom—which was the source from which the Written Torah and the Oral Torah <term>Torah she-be-ktav and Torah she-be-al-peh</term> were drawn and engraved—does not cease. Rather, it flows and comes constantly. If it were to cease for even a moment, all created beings would return to their non-existence, for existence depends on the unity of the Great Source in His glory, etc., the existence of all creatures. Concerning this it is said: "For with You is the source of life" <note>Psalm 36:10</note>, and they are lives that have no interruption or end, and their removal has no rest or cessation. Because the nature of the source must be established in that which turns from it, even if the lines in the Torah appear as one, no cessation should ever be seen in it. Rather, it should be a flowing spring to indicate the Source from which it was drawn.

Mentioning this, that we are drawn from this Torah, is because that "Great Voice"—as we have written—did not cease. For after He wrote them for us and made us hear His holy commandments, which are the general principles of every detail, it did not cease from there. Its specific flows continue until... as it is said by the Sages and is the intention of Targum Onkelos <term>The authorized Aramaic translation of the Torah</term> on the verse, where he translated "a great voice that did not cease" <note>original: "kol gadol v'lo yasaf"; Deuteronomy 5:19, where "lo yasaf" can mean "did not continue" or "did not cease." Onkelos chooses the latter.</note>. There is no cessation to the Great Voice, for the Voice calls out forever in its creations. Everything that the prophets and the sages in every generation innovated, renewed, and enacted, they received from that Voice that did not cease. Within it were included all the divisions, decrees, voices, and everything destined to be innovated. In every generation, that Voice is like the sound of the Shofar, or like a scribe whose ears and mind are focused on the sound of the Shofar, such that he feels no dream from his own mind or intellect, but only what he received from that Voice... they bring it now from potential into reality. Everything is included in what was said: "All these words the Lord spoke," for all the laws are part of the "great voice that did not cease," as we have explained.

This itself was the intention in the Midrash Tanchuma on the verse: "And God spoke all these words, saying..." <note>Exodus 20:1</note>. This means that even what the prophets were destined to prophesy in every generation, they received from Mount Sinai. For He said to the House of Israel: "Both with him who is standing here with us today... and with him who is not here with us today" <note>Deuteronomy 29:13–14</note>. It does not say "standing

<column-break/>

with us today," but rather "with us today." These refer to the souls destined to be created, who had no physical substance yet, so "standing" was not said of them. Even though they were not present at that moment, each one received his portion. And so it says: "The burden of the word of the Lord to Israel by the hand of Malachi" <note>Malachi 1:1</note>. It does not say "in the days of Malachi," but "by the hand of Malachi," for the prophecy was already in his hand from Mount Sinai, but until that hour, permission had not been given to him to prophesy.

Similarly, Isaiah said: "From the time it was, there I was..." <note>Isaiah 48:16</note>. Isaiah said: "From the day the Torah was given at Sinai, I was there and I received this prophecy, but 'now the Lord God has sent me, and His Spirit'—and until now, permission was not given to me to prophesy." And not only did all the prophets receive their prophecy from Sinai, but even the Sages who stand in every generation—each and every one received his own from Sinai, etc. Again, it says, "All these words the Lord spoke to all your assembly... a great voice that did not cease." Within this, understand that what the innovators produced in all generations, they received from Sinai from that Voice. It was not merely according to their intellect, research, or their own truth, but with the help of the "Hand" <note>divine assistance</note> that was with them... according to the mouth of the law which they shall teach you, "you shall do; you shall not divert from the matter which they tell you, right or left" <note>Deuteronomy 17:11</note>.

One is liable for the death penalty if he does not listen to them, because this Caller is a "Great Voice" which "did not cease." "And the man who acts willfully, not listening to the priest... or to the judge, that man shall die" <note>Deuteronomy 17:12</note>. This was so because the source of visions and the foundation is preserved in the hand of the innovator, as in the matter: "You are My witnesses, says the Lord, and I am God" <note>Isaiah 43:12</note>. As we explained in this book, today the Supernal Voice is what contains all things destined to be innovated... to be brought into action through the innovators who arise... as in the matter: "It is a time to act for the Lord, they have voided Your Torah" <note>Psalm 119:126, often used to justify rabbinic enactments</note>. Everything goes back to the Sages, of whom it was said: "Place upon me the words of Levi." As it was said: "I have made a covenant with your brothers," for the law is pleasant and sweet in the heat and heart... all things are the "Voice," for the Great Voice is essentially all the words of the Sages; they received it from Him. And this is what they meant by "calling to thoughts in general and to events..." until it stands, as we wrote in Chapter 22 of the first part of this book, with the help of Heaven.

It was further clarified from the latter words: "and him who is not here standing today"—these are the souls destined to be created. For whoever was heard at Mount Sinai and received his portion from that Voice is worthy to be heard. If so, all the prophets come through their reception, for they did not stand there [physically] and were not given to receive the testimony... and there is no prophet who prophesies who did not... for they did not come to the help of the Lord... and they received from there, in truth, their unique qualities... between holy and profane, and between impure and pure. Behold, that Great Voice is what opened and awakened each person in his source. It is the fence and the boundary of learning, even the "Gate" which is the Oral Torah for the Lord, which is the Written Torah. It was a chain of transmission; therefore it is said: "And you shall guard My charge" <note>Leviticus 18:30</note>. This is the reason for the "fences" and "boundaries" that the Sages judged... "Make a charge for My charge" <note>Yevamot 21a; the mandate to create protective rabbinic laws</note>. For everything is "one corresponding to the other," above and below.

Because that Voice has no cessation, and the Source of the Voice is here and comes to teach this path found with me in the holy Talmud... Ravina and Rav Ashi <note>the 5th-century compilers of the Babylonian Talmud</note> [marked] the end of the [formative] period in Babylonia. This was the path of the sages of the generations... look to the "Tree of Life," the holy one, on the verse "My beloved is white and ruddy" <note>Song of Songs 5:10</note>... in the souls of Israel... in the gathering of Rabbi Meir Almosnino <note>16th-century Sephardic rabbi</note>... to speak... to my second knowledge... in those days... and he was diligent in his dust, and made his books four for his Torah, and my tastes in prophecy... and at night a deep secret in the orders of judgment... a lyre from the inner parts of our wisdom and reasoning...

->**Chapter 25: The Section on the Purpose**<-

It is proper, as mentioned above, for one to know Him, to order Him, to crown Him, to instruct Him, to hint at Him, and to establish Him. We have hinted at this, just as it is said: that the Kingdom <note>original: *Malchut*; the final of the ten Sefirot, often associated with the physical world and divine presence</note> is prepared to be struck, to awaken from within itself the holy actions of its thought and its longing, and to be appointed over His service. And this day and the cup are ready for us to receive <note>original: *L'kabel*; likely a reference to receiving the Sabbath or divine light</note>. Let its clarity be the goodness of your heart; you shall transform it and place it as her sickness, and awaken it little by little to be strengthened in the holy prayer.

Its ultimate goal should be pursued very slowly at first, starting with simple matters to reach the level of a person who possesses nothing but the simple law, to know that his intellect is like something precious. At the beginning, one is still among the "children of understanding" <note>original: *Bnei Binah*</note> and researchers who provide a taste for deeper matters through study. You shall sing to him parables and ethical traits that will serve as signs and hints toward the hidden and awesome things within his heart. This is what is called **Kabbalah** <note>literally "received tradition"</note> in its true sense—matters that have been tested in seclusion and in the homilies of our Sages of blessed memory. Books that guide these matters have been mentioned, such as the *Midrash* of Rabbi Shimon bar Yochai <note>referring to the *Zohar*, the foundational work of Jewish mysticism</note>, may he rest in peace, and in the commentaries on the *Aggadah* <note>non-legal rabbinic lore</note>.

The Holy One, Blessed be He, will double the secrets of the Torah and the truth of the traditions and His light in the books of investigation into the law, to remember the Name of the Lord <note>original: *H'Y*; abbreviation for Hashem Yitbarach</note> who said "Let there be," and the world was made through depth alone. When you see him diligent and living, and you direct his voice to Him, then you will see "face to face" in every examination, and you will speak to him "mouth to mouth." You will grant him the benefit of the face of the hint there, and give it to the "wise of heart." It shall be a path; do not hide a thing from him, and do not treat him merely as one who speaks of the secret of the Palace <note>original: *Hekhal*</note> every holy evening.

Rather, let him exert himself in the essence of the Torah and its soul, which are the hidden things and its secrets. They are the secrets of the world and its Creator, in truth and holiness, for those who master the Torah. This is the "whole of man" <note>Ecclesiastes 12:13</note>, and these are the letters of the service of the Name. All of these are the secret of the Palace of the Torah. In the writing of the hidden things, the intention is to be established in the point and light of the *Kelipot* <note>original: *Klipot*; literally "shells" or "husks" that conceal divine light</note>. This shall be an atonement for his sins—a step taken lest he stand upon the vanity of the idol. This is a study, and know that this path will direct the light of the vanity of the end to every wise person who is uniquely dedicated to his Son. He shall prepare his holy face toward him, the secret of making him beloved through knowledge, understanding, and wisdom, to illuminate this path for the children of His holiness. Amen, may it be so. May our letters be sufficient in His service.

# Chapter 25
It is written: *And God said, "Let the earth bring forth grass..."* <note>Genesis 1:11</note> etc. And it is written: *Let us make man in our image, after our likeness* <note>Genesis 1:26</note>. The portion of the Teacher <note>referring to Maimonides' *Guide for the Perplexed*</note> said to compare it to my soul; He created it in His cessation, *in our image, after our likeness* in the ancient mountain, which was the intellectual argument. *After our likeness*—a likeness in essence, for the research of the intellectual comprehension cannot be entered by the senses, nor is it a deed of the body. The foot has no place there, for they have no physical form... and this is the opinion of the Rabbi <note>Maimonides</note> regarding the intent of "Image" and "Likeness."

Then the intent of the Torah is to let us hear what the wise man can understand through his own perception. But if the secret of labor is like the secret of the Lord, then he has received the light of the Torah and yet does not know the intellectual secret. Know that the wise man in this matter is only "man" insofar as he is a man of intellect. For He placed the intellect in its garment to distinguish him from the rest of the animals. However, the language of the scripture does not fully support the Rabbi's intent, for the phrase *Let us make man in our image* indicates the preparation and making of a thing according to the pattern of a form, alongside a purely spiritual and intellectual secret.

This brings us to the matter of the "Whole" <note>the cosmos</note> and grants power to all. But the matter is among the secrets of the Torah, and the prayers hinted at the Holy Soul, the "Soul of the World," which is complete from the Upper One in a holy manner. This stands as a hidden thing, as explained in the *Midrash* of Rabbi Shimon bar Yochai, may he rest in peace, in these words:

*Rabbi Shimon stood and said: I was looking at the time the Holy One, Blessed be He, sought to create man. He moved the Upper and Lower worlds and established and engraved the forms. Finally, the desire rose to the Upper Will, and freedom was spread to all sides. He opened until he grasped the point of the body and sought its light, which surrounds the point of the spark from the spirit, and it was established in the East.*

*The East was established for the North... and it was called complete. The South for the West, to spread in holiness. Then the West rose up...*

<column-break/>

...wings. They have already explained the South, East, North, and West in the previous chapter. The South is the wind of the *Sandalphon* <note>an archangel in Jewish mysticism</note>; then the East approaches the West, and the West is contained within them. The King desired and said: "Let us make man as grass," in our image and after our likeness, according to this form of four knots. It rose and was established, and the East was sealed in the West, and He brought it out. Regarding this, we recite the "portion of praise," a matter of the Sanctuary. The wise man of kindness stands over this exceedingly wonderful secret, and he shall return to the secret of the Assembly <note>original: *Knesset*; possibly Knesset Yisrael/the Shekhinah</note> in its cycle, in their likeness. This is his desire for the Crown <note>original: *Keter*; the highest Sefirah</note> more so in this.

And just as the internal clarity within him was from the four upper directions, so too at that moment the lower seven *Sefirot* <note>the divine emanations</note> were from the four lower directions. This is what they said in the *Chapters of Rabbi Eliezer*: The wise one took from his essence... from the four corners... measure for measure... this corresponding to that <note>original: *zeh l'umat zeh*; a key concept that the physical world mirrors the spiritual world</note>. And what they said about the "first portion" lacking for the Holy Temple, corresponds to what they said: Rabbi Berechiah and Rabbi Helbo in the name of Rabbi Samuel bar Isaac said: The specific place of creation was where he was initially intended to be placed in the world. The Holy One, Blessed be He, said: "I am creating him from the place of his atonement, and there he shall stand."

And in the *Midrash* of Rabbi Shimon bar Yochai <note>the Zohar</note>, it is taught that He sought to create... the Temple below... and from the dust of the Temple above... for the stones and dust of the lower world were not to be destroyed, but rather the knots of its foundation are upon it... and this is the truth they made known. Everything is revealed through the Upper Intent. The souls are full and testify to their intentions above, which were made and established to build the Unique Chariot <note>original: *Merkabah*</note>. Your feet shall stop this, for this is the death of the *Kelipah* <note>the shell/evil</note>. The "Marrow" <note>spiritual essence</note> is within, and the "Shell" is the garment of the spirit within. This corresponds to that; it was made and established for the rectification of the world, as it arose in the Pure Thought.

For all the writings and these intentions are in the *Diyokan* <note>divine image/countenance</note>. Therefore, it is said that the closing of your feet shall be like a name for all souls. And in the *Midrash* of Rabbi Shimon bar Yochai: "He told us how many shells <note>*kelipin*</note> are to the East, and the whole world is in the shell of *Nogah* <note>a 'translucent' shell that contains both good and evil</note>. Beneath it are the levels of the abyss until the end of all levels. All of them are within one another, and this one is above that one... a shell that covers the point."

The First Point is a light... it has no foundation from the spreading... it is the heart... for the rectification and essence of the law. This hides the point that was made into a Palace <note>*Heikhal*</note> to clothe the precious point that is unknown to creatures. This Palace, which is to cover the First Point, is established as a light that has no measure. Despite all this, it is thin and fine, a covering for the First Point, which is hidden and stored. It spread a spreading to that Holy Light, and that spreading and that First Light—which serves to cover that Palace—is a thin and fine light, more than all of them. It did not spread in all, nor was it clothed in all, until this was made as a covering... not a "death" and not a "shell." Rather, the "Marrow" <note>essence</note> of the garment became the "Marrow" for another level. In this manner, it was made so that below, in this world, there is nothing but Marrow and Shell, Marrow and Shell. This is the rectification of the world.

Regarding this, the scripture says: *Let us make man in our image, after our likeness*—meaning, according to the secret and form of all the Upper Existences. In them, one is within another, and one is a garment for the other: the Marrow within and the Shell directed toward it. Far be it from being a literal "shell" <note>evil</note> there, but they are lights that have no end in their purity and fineness. The outer one is merely a "garment" for the Marrow, being slightly less refined than the one it covers.
