# Chapter 24: Part 24 — The Purpose — Chapter 24

The tradition of the Torah is upon him, as we have written. The members of the "House of the Cave" <note>original: *Bnei Bei Me'arata*; a reference to the circle of Rabbi Shimon bar Yochai, the traditional authors of the Zohar</note> share in this to increase grace upon them, to fill the lack of those who are wanting, and to elevate the one who receives this kindness. Initially, she <note>the Torah, personified as a woman</note> awakens them and gives to you little by little, like words of a secret, until she suddenly reveals herself to the one who receives her. Immediately, she is exalted and elevated through their song. From this, the sought-after goal is found. Sometimes she speaks with them from behind a curtain <note>original: *pargod*</note> until they hear her voice, but she remains distant. At another time, she speaks from behind a thin veil until you become accustomed to her and she places a longing within them. They remain in that state of longing for her always, day and night, never resting and never turning away from the entrance of her house. By her permission—for they have entered into her love—she brings them inside to her palace <note>original: *hekhal*</note> and reveals her inner arrangements to them. She speaks with them face-to-face, without any dividing screen or partition <note>original: *shavarta*</note>.

After this illumination, she truly instructs the heart to perceive wisdom, and you shall be purified and dwell therein. It is said that the difficulty of loving the Torah should not be painful, as it is written: *and those who love Me shall inherit substance* <note>Proverbs 8:21</note>. One should learn until he becomes exactly as we wrote above and in other places in this book. You shall dwell in it, for it is more precious than fine gold. For the Torah, in her light, serves the gates of Understanding <note>the Sefirah of *Binah*</note>. At the end of the first section, her image is further described in the high name of man. Everything is according to the interpretation of the Ramban <note>original: *Ramchi*; Rabbi Moshe ben Nachman, a 13th-century sage and Kabbalist</note> along with other people of the world. In our estimation and in our foolishness, we learn, and these secrets were handed down in their simple form at length. They depart every day in our lives... <unclear>illegible phrases</unclear>... and we are not ashamed to conduct ourselves so. Even though we see that the light of the Torah can be exhausted on the lips of those who crown her... and it is worthy to inherit from her lightning-bolt-like clarity.

She does not act for you except for the benefit of those who learn her and to be recognized by them. To provide a hint for those who place their prayer in Zion... she is destined for our residence in her Garden of Eden. From the beginning, we knew her through the words of the lip, part of our lot in her Garden of Eden. That hint—out of all the hints she provides—is for the master of the house who is always standing at every watch. He knows that hint which is spoken after it. Almost constantly she makes an opening, and before it is opened, her palace is hidden. They do not look except at the hint... and his soul follows after her. He knows the secret of the hint she gives him regarding the "reincarnation" <note>original: *gilgul*</note> of the soul, to rouse his fortune so it is not stolen from him. For he is full of Torah, not for the sake of reincarnation, but for the sake of the hint. She knows how to empty her secrets so that they do not go into hiding at the end of her house every day. She reveals herself like a thief—that Divine Presence <note>original: *Shekhinah*</note>—to his heart from within the palace, hinting to him with signs. Immediately, she prepares her correction and her change. All those legalistic judgments <note>original: *dinin*</note> do not know and do not look; only he, through his hints, and his soul follow after her. And for this reason, the Torah is not for reincarnation, but she is found and brought out through the hints of the "thief" <note>the subtle revelation</note> to be revealed at the time she is written to be emptied.

So it was at the beginning: all the hidden things that were taught were stolen in a moment through her hints to him. If he knows, it is good; and if not, she returns to him and says, "There is my face." The Torah says to turn back toward her beauty; they said to give "the simpleton" a drink <note>a play on Proverbs 9:4</note> to be called a "Grandfather" <note>a term for an experienced mystic</note> and to be changed in his life. It says: *Whoever is simple, let him turn in here.* Behold, my eyes draw near to her; she desires to battle with him from behind her curtain. She speaks to him from the mouth of the palace until he looks further. And he does not strengthen his study to change in the secret, from the end of her subtle words, until she becomes a revealed light. The light of the Torah is revealed to her children face-to-face, and she reveals to him all her hidden mysteries and every hidden palace that was in her chamber, hidden with holy words. Then he is blessed with peace for the sake of the Torah; they return to her dwelling. Every legal judge <note>original: *dayan dina*</note> hides it for him, and she does not suppress any message from him. She says to him: "Truly, the word I hinted to you at first was such-and-such a judgment, and such-and-she was all of it." He enters with her into the palace... and this is what we seek from her: even in simple secrets, just as she is not found and not handed over, the sign of kindness comes. And because of this...
<meta>catchword: because</meta>

<column-break/>

...being exempt for his service. I knew more, yet I did not look at her clothing but at her soul, for the sound of her clothing is like her likeness. The "Wise of the Supernal Works" are those who stood at Mount Sinai; they do not look at anything except the soul, which is the essence of everything—the Torah itself. And compared to what is to come, they are meant to look at the soul of the wisdom of the Torah, etc. We have written this discourse in our flame-like explanation of the second part of this book, in the section on property, and at the end of the introduction only. I say that there is nothing there but this: the portion of wisdom and the lowered state of the Torah's command. The whole thing is the source of Ancient Wisdom <note>original: *Chokhmata Atika*</note>, which is constant. And as for Understanding <note>original: *Binah*</note>, he did not merit it in the secret of the Torah and its root. Woe to him! For in this, everything is chosen. And in the secret of the Ramban, peace be upon him: those who look at the literal meaning of the Torah look only at her garments. When the Torah was written, it was not for them... for they say there is only the literal sense <note>original: *peshat*</note> in the Torah and the Talmud in various places, without any secret to be seen within it. It would be better for such a person had he not been created in the world, that he did not learn the secret of the Torah. When the Torah was written in her garments, it was returned to him without the secret of the world. He reveals its matter in the world and the length of the exile. Thus far.

The secret of the matter is that the Torah is truly the "Torah of the Lord" <note>original: *Torat Hashem*</note>, meaning that His Name is the Name "Lord" <note>the Tetragrammaton, Y-H-V-H</note>. His Name is in the whole and in the parts. Even the help within it exists in the revealed and the hidden. It is the way of the world to have both and to engage in them together. In this lies the perfection of the Torah, the Divine Service, and the Kabbalah <note>the received tradition</note>. Behold, they are stories, commandments, and warnings. The stories in the Torah are indeed stories, and the services are within the commandments of the Torah. This means that all the stories of the Torah contain secrets of secrets, great creation and wisdom, and within them are resting places and warnings. The Kabbalah <note>the mystical tradition</note> hints at its existence and the receptions of holiness, which are the secret of the Great and Unique Name. One needs a certain depth in every matter of the Torah regarding all of this. This is the "Torah of the Apple" <note>likely a reference to the "Field of Holy Apples," a Kabbalistic term for the Divine Presence</note>. This section, if one does not establish its explanation in this manner with the Great Name—and it is known that His Name is "Our God"—behold, he lies against the Name, the intention, and the help. 

In the letter of the Ramban, may his light shine, Rabbi Isaac opened the book of the structure of the Name of the Lord and sanctified it in its loftiness, as it is written: *Holy, Holy, Holy*... Thus, the holy literal meaning is both inner and revealed. In my eyes, everything is both hidden and revealed. The Torah, which is the Supernal Holy Name, is hidden and revealed. Every verse in the Torah and every section of the Torah is hidden and revealed. As it was taught: Rabbi Judah the Pious said: "Righteousness is like many elders of the world." And who stands up and says what is written: *And she covered her eyes*... <note>referring to Tamar in Genesis 38:14</note>. All these details do not prove that the Torah is hidden and revealed? And at the end of this matter, he repeated: Every section in it is Torah; the Torah is bound to the Torah, and everything is hidden and revealed. The entire Torah is found in this manner. You have no word in the Torah that does not hint at the Supernal Holy Name in a hidden and revealed way. Because of this, the hiddenness of the Holy Torah is upon you... and it is not to be revealed to the rest of the world in a place where it is not written in the Book of the Construction of the Name of the Lord. It begins with its lineage, like in the Temple. Behold, here is Moses, as is fitting, looking toward his intention. And regarding this, everything is hidden and revealed.

And the tradition is: anyone who subtracts a single letter from the Torah or adds a letter that is missing in the Torah, it is as if he caused a blemish in the Holy Name that sustains all worlds. We have already written in the *Gate of the Thirty* of this book that the Torah includes all the laws, which is the dwelling of the secret of the 22 letters <note>original: *kaf-bet*; the Hebrew alphabet</note> of the Unique Name. Just as the Unique Name is in revealed and hidden forms—as we wrote in Chapter 15 of the first part of this book—so too the help within it is in revealed and hidden forms, as we wrote above. It will be realized, therefore, from this that the help is truly the form of the Great Name. If, God forbid, a letter is missing from it or a letter is added to it, it is not the "Torah of the Lord," because then it is not the Torah of the Great Name. And since it is like the form of the Great Name, it is truly the Hidden Name in its addition, which is more sanctified, as we wrote—that within the Name it is the Holy of Holies. These are the depths of the matters and her holy secrets... and this is by keeping the "Purpose" <note>original: *Tachlit*</note> they spoke of. They should not be mixed with this. Rather, when they examine their explanation through the Great Secret and through the collections of secrets...

# Chapter 27: The Section on the Purpose — 85

The Creator, may He be blessed, cannot be grasped by any other being. Language has no title, no comparison, and no expression that can describe His essence, whether in the upper or lower worlds, for He is not subject to any boundary; He is not a body, nor is He a power within a body. If so, why does the Torah contain a collection of "imaginary creations" attributed to Him, such as hands, feet, eyes, and ears? These are physical terms and names for parts of the body. One must know and contemplate according to what we have received from the <term>Masters of Divine Service</term><note>A term for Kabbalists who focus on the inner spiritual effects of their actions.</note>. They strove to explain that all those things refer to the "Above," for they all uprightly testify to the greatness of the Creator of the beginning, whose wisdom and power have no end.

Regarding the simple essence of that holy Being, may He be blessed: the "foot," "eye," or "attachment" <note>original: *levayah*</note>—even though it is written that all are built in the "image of God" as explained in the previous chapter—it must never enter one's mind, Heaven forbid, that an eye is like a physical eye or a sense, or that a heart or hand is like a physical hand. Rather, He possesses <term>Sefirot</term><note>The ten divine emanations or attributes through which God interacts with the universe.</note> and insights according to this order, structure, and form.

However, these are inner matters, the "inner-most of the inner," from which the light and flow originate and spread. They are the power for all "joints" and for every life force. A "hand" exists in the place of a hand, but its form is not like a physical hand’s form, as it is written: *To whom then will you liken God? Or what likeness will you compare to Him?* (Isaiah 40:18). Wisdom is within all, and His intent and description are not a physical likeness at all, despite the terminology used. Out of concern for the intention behind the structure of these connections, the sages surrounded these hidden matters with the imagery of titles and hints toward supreme, fiery things that human knowledge cannot know or grasp upon entry.

There is a likeness to Him in His "countenance"—that is, in His essence and structure—but not a likeness of physical appearance. As it is written of Jacob: *His distance is thus,* <note>original: *rachoko ken Yaakov*</note> referring to the external order of his essence and the Torah of his distance and their nature. <note>This likely refers to the Kabbalistic concept of Jacob as the "Small Face" or the central pillar of the divine structure.</note> According to the secret of the "Secret of the Enclosure," He did not come in a body, Heaven forbid; rather, these are hidden and revealed teachings, similar to the "nourishment" for the <term>Work of the Chariot</term><note>Ma'aseh Merkavah: The earliest form of Jewish mysticism, focusing on the visions of the Divine Throne.</note>. Just as Joseph interpreted a dream to resolve a lack in the connections, this matter is a companion to the imagery of the Name, a sign of the inner, designated matter. This "eye" is not a physical eye; this "hand" is not a physical hand; this "foot" is not a physical foot; and so it is with the rest of the teachings.

We have already explained in various places in our books that the holy purpose is the "Repair of the Glory" <note>original: *Tikkun ha-Kavod*</note>. It resides in the structure of the Supernal Chariot. One cannot reach this purpose at all through the power of studying the Torah and performing the commandments without saying that the end of the study is the life of its fulfillment. Since all physical creatures require this, the Perfect One made the form of this structure. Even the Supernal Glory was repaired according to the secret of the "Image of the Likeness of Adam" <note>The Primordial Man, Adam Kadmon</note> to include all things, both upper and lower. Since He is the inclusion of everything, the Glory was repaired in His structure.

This was also the teaching of the holy Rabbi Shimon bar Yochai, peace be upon him, in his composition <note>The Zohar</note>, where it is written in the original language:
*All these are the Ancient of Ancients* <note>original: *Atika de-Atikin*</note>. *Furthermore, they joined in this together. He is beautiful; He does not change. He changed only to be repaired in these repairs, an image to include all images, an image to include all praises, an image to be seen in its colors. Without an image, He could not be known. The image exists in a hidden eye, and through it, crowns and ornaments are joined for the perfection of the Whole. Because of this, the image of Man is the image of the Upper and the Lower, to be included within it. And because the image stands as the inclusion of Upper and Lower, the repairs of the Holy Ancient were established, and the repair of the Lesser Countenance* <note>original: *Ze'ir Anpin*</note> *was established in this image.*

Thus, we find that the Supernal Likeness exists according to our wisdom and requires its "repair" <note>original: *Tikkun*</note>. Therefore, it was repaired. Within this repair, one must know that the "Attributes" <note>Middot</note> are ancient in their connections. For example: the attribute of the Eye is Greatness; the attribute of the Ear is Hearing; the attribute of the Hand is Action; the attribute of the Foot is Walking. These are the "chosen attributes" mentioned in the teachings. One should judge the matter of the Attributes like the "chosen ones," just as there is a name and value between Him and us in the matter of the teachings, so too there is a name and value between Him and us in the matter of the Attributes.

It was already explained in the previous chapter regarding the secret of the Supernal Likeness, that this

<column-break/>

does not refer to the physical matter of the body, but to the inner powers and the Torah. Just as a "man" is not defined by his physical matter but by his inner spirit, so too the names of the teachings are not names for physical parts, but for their prophetic insights. I have investigated these matters and written them in one connected composition. All these things, in their perfection, follow the "Image of Man," as proven by the statement I wrote above. This is the secret of the "Chariot of Man" recognized in the Supernal Chariot and also in the lower one. It is not that there is any physical form similar to Him at all, Heaven forbid.

In the order of the "Sections of the Chariot," the secret of the matter is this: there are levels and inner chambers, and all of them together are called the "Soul of Man" or the "Secret of Man." It is not like the form of a physical man, Heaven forbid; rather, it is a parable for the way, the order, and the inner nature of the "Beings" <note>original: *Havayot*</note>. They are hidden in the ultimate degree, like the essence in a person which is inner, hidden, and concealed within the skull of the head. It is not seen, for it is "Holy within the Holy," and the essence inside is covered and hidden. So too is the parable and example of the inner nature of the Supernal Beings. The hidden ones are called the "Skull of the Head" <note>term: *Gulgaltā de-Reisha*</note>, which is the head of those [mysteries]. The early sages did not explicitly mention the inner workings. The more something is inner, hidden, and stored away, the less it is mentioned or revealed, in order to demonstrate its high rank and importance. Even Solomon, with the "Song of the Temple," only mentioned the essence through a wondrous hint when he said: *His head is like the finest gold* (Song of Songs 5:11). He spoke of the "cheeks" and the "hidden eyes."

To be the repair of the beauty of the "Face" <note>original: *Partzuf*</note>, the scripture expanded on His supernal lordship. From these come the verses mentioning "ears," such as *the ears of the Lord*, or "eyes," such as *the eyes of the Lord*. Between the "hands" and "feet" and the hidden parts of the Supernal Chariot, they join and exist in one connection and one secret. He is exalted by the name "Man" <note>Adam</note> because it includes all the names and the most comprehensive supernal lights.

Corresponding to this, in the world of separate beings and the lower composition, there are names called by the name "Eye"—these are the "Eyes of the Supernal Desire." Some are called "Ears," some "Hand," some "Hands," and some "Feet." All of them are one, in the general and the specific, under the name "Man," due to His importance; for He includes all the Attributes and all the sections of the Chariots, as we have explained. This was the intention of this chapter.

### Chapter 27

->He descended upon it. And they said in the Midrash of Rabbi Nehuniah ben<-
->HaKanah, peace be upon him, regarding the "weapon of the house" and the division, as it is written: "And He descended"<-

And he ascended and diminished... descending and bestowing the "appointed glories" there, drawing near through the sacrifice <note>original: *korban*</note>, which is why it is called a "sacrifice" [drawing near]. At the end of the matter, they said: "From where does He descend?" As it is written: *a pleasing aroma to the Lord* (Leviticus 1:9). *The Lord is a pleasing aroma... Hear O Israel, the Lord our God, the Lord is One.*

Every "descent" attributed to the Above refers to the drawing down of the Light, the Holy Spirit, and the Flow <note>original: *Shefa*</note> into all matters of the Secret of Emanation <note>term: *Atzilut*</note> from the beginning to the end. This is what they meant in the Zohar: "The Lord is One and His Name is One"—the unification of the lights. They are all included in the Great Name, and all that is within it is in this Name, so that everything is unified. His further intention in this verse is the Unification.

When we ascend from below to above, it is called an "ascent." This is the elevation of the Glory from level to level until the place from which it ascended. This is the secret of *Blessed be the glory of the Lord from His place* (Ezekiel 3:12), for He is the Supernal Place who sustains them all—the secret of the "Maker of Man," as has been explained. The secret of *And God went up from upon Abraham* (Genesis 17:22) is that the "God" mentioned here is the secret of that which is below, which became lower at the beginning of existence. It is the secret of the "Letter Qaf" <note>original: *Kof de-Atvan*</note> which is above the Supernal Chariot, the secret of the Groom and the Woman. Jacob is a parable for the flow and the beauty of Isaac. The intention is that the Glory was planted there, returning through the powers of the Patriarchs to speak with Abraham... God ascended from upon Abraham, for the lower beings are dependent upon the upper beings.

# Chapter 28: The Section on the Purpose

And because of this, the entirety of the body served as a shell for it, and so on; and likewise, all things proceed from the movement of the Thought until its conclusion, until they were included in the "Branch of Man." This Man consists of a shell and a spirit, a body and a soul—all positioned "one opposite the other," <note>A reference to Ecclesiastes 7:14, a key concept in Kabbalah meaning that for every holy element, there is a corresponding physical or "other side" element.</note> as will be explained above. In this book, the reason for our being servants to the "Kingdom of the Chariot" <note>The *Merkavah* or Divine Chariot, representing the structure of the spiritual realms.</note> is explained, and we have praised it. Know that what we have explained regarding the nullification of the physical form and likeness is absolute wisdom.

The essence of perfection relates to this revealed form and likeness. From it comes the life-force of the <term>Holy Living Beings</term><note>original: *Ch"v*, likely an abbreviation for *Chayot Ha-Qodesh*</note> along with the worldly realms <note>original: *Khaladim*, a term likely used here as a substitute for "God" or to refer to the temporal world/Heled.</note>, and not—Heaven forbid—with the foundation, nor with the void and the song. "And He blessed the man" <note>Genesis 1:28</note> in his entirety, among all the worlds, through the blessing of his life-force. It is written: "This is the book of the generations of Adam, on the day he was created" <note>Genesis 5:1</note> in the Holy Thought, to make Man according to this holy principle, through the power of the seal of the <term>Holy Living Beings</term> with life-force in the hearts. This Man, along with the worldly realms and everything included—the brain and the shell, the Torah and the body—exists in a state of unity. 

This is not only full from this perspective, but in the manner we have written: that which is more internal is like the Torah to everything it has acquired. It is like a shell and a body to it. This and that are intertwined, and the Divine Names are joined together, power added unto power. The second reason is the essential one: the detail of every human is like the brain and body to the Name of the Will, which covers it. This <term>Holy Living Being</term> is the totality of the Torah which covers the body. If the likeness of the moving body exists through the power of the body—written in the language of the <term>Holy Living Beings</term>—it is sustained by the body. But within the Foundation of Holiness, the body would be lost and absent, for without the Divine <note>original: *Khaladim*</note> and the order proceeding from the Torah of Man with the Name of God <note>original: *Y"H*</note> as it is written, the foundation of the <term>Holy Living Beings</term> would be established. He shall not open his mouth against this Man in his entirety, in the worldly realms, by the blessing of his life-force, for the sake of his rest and the nourishment of the brain and shell, spirit and body—power added unto power for every <term>Holy Living Being</term>. 

The occurrence of the Torah belongs to the <term>Holy Living Beings</term> with the Foundation, because it is not a shared cause, but rather entirely light and an inner line. There is no end to their simplifications and their parts within the wisdom of the Torah. This is because his way is to translate <note>Referencing the Aramaic Targum</note> for the worldly realms, and in our connection to the Divine, "And He blessed" the worldly realms and the man in his entirety, by the blessing of his life-force. In the likeness of the worldly realms, now for the grace of the <term>Holy Living Beings</term>, it is translated: "And he lived..." This contains a great intention and wisdom which guides us to what we have written. 

Regarding the hint in "And the Divine <note>original: *Khaladim*</note> blessed" and "And he lived," and the worldly realm was elevated in its totality—this too is a great intention and wisdom. For his way in all the Works of Creation where the Divine <note>original: *Khaladim*</note> is mentioned is to translate it as the Name of God <note>original: *Y"H*</note> to indicate its permanence and to compel the understanding that the Attribute of Justice is like the Attribute of Mercy. As our Sages of blessed memory said: "It arose in His thought to create the world with the Attribute of Mercy." It is good that this should be separated in the Covenant of Kindness. Finally, the translation of "And the Divine blessed the man" is entirely holy, even between the "House of Rest" <note>possibly a reference to the grave or a state of spiritual repose</note> and the rest of the world, included in the blessing of his life-force. It was not translated as "And she said," but rather as the blessing of the life-force with the Divine Will, so that the Name of God shall be established. This is to say, the unique spark of the life-force is included in the Divine <note>original: *Khaladim*</note>, like the Sphere of God, intended so that the Name written within the Divine—the blessing of his life-force—is like matter upon his mouth, a holy drop. 

For the damage is the "scent of the garment," which is the flesh of man and not the eternal world. This is what is written: "You have clothed me in skin and flesh" <note>Job 10:11</note>. Furthermore, the "Covering" <note>original: *Kippur/Kafar*</note> is the garment of man. Thus, man’s inner essence is an inner spirit, and the Torah dwells within him as a bond and a guard. I have carried this upon myself: "And the Divine blessed the man in his entirety... by the blessing of his life-force." His thought is the secret of the Chariot, so that it may be seen and recognized when it breaks forth to investigate the world, as it is written: "The world is sealed with bread." The wicked are not of this world; the Spirit of the Holy Speaker investigates the world. His soul is for the purpose of the world, and upon this: "You have clothed me in skin and flesh," flesh to flesh for the world. The Temple is below, as it is written, a covering for the world, a garden in the throne to yearn for Man. Therefore, regarding Man, it is written over him: "The Divine blessed him... with the blessing of his life-force." The true kindness of the Divine is the spirit of man—life, lest she see the completion of the forms over the totality of the generations, from the beginning to the end. This is what they said in the Midrash regarding Rashi, of blessed memory: "The spirit of man is the shell of the world..."

# Chapter 25

Why does it open with an opening that begins in the West, and not with the general principle of the above and below? For the lower to the upper, and the upper to the lower—these are the "lowly openings." When we prepare below, the whole is as one in their dreams; it is found outside and corresponding to the "witness." Here they guided us to the secret of the dream in their visions. Furthermore, the totality of "Male and Female" is known, as it is written: "A dream," and "upon a dream," like the matter of male and female in the womb, for the spirit of lying down and the power of sin shall you understand. 

"And He blessed them and called their name Adam" <note>Genesis 5:2</note>—this is so that there would be a totality of "Male" both above and below. Furthermore, they said in the Midrash of Rabbi Shimon bar Yochai <note>The Zohar</note>, of blessed memory: Wisdom opened and said, "And the Divine blessed the man in his totality," like their power to bless the world for the "Dream." He made him in the image of the upper and the lower. He is a totality of the whole, and the whole is in order, shining from the heights of the upper realms to the ends of the world. The "Coldness of the Worlds" stands before Him, everything is according to the law of His statutes. It is life for the completion, like the "Early Worlds" of which it was said, "And the Divine blessed the man in his totality"—life within the totality of the Divine. These are two levels of the totality: male and female, master of all and the covering. Thus, they are "Two Faces" <note>A Kabbalistic concept that the original Man was created with two faces, male and female, later separated.</note>, living and missing, to be called "Man" <note>original: *Adam*</note>, as it is written: "Male and female He created them." And all of this is from all sides. 

It was said that Man is the inner life-force and the Perfect Torah. Regarding him, it is said in the "Wheel of the World": "By the blessing of his life-force." If so, how can that which you said at the beginning be sustained—the necessity of the Divine totality, as the power of the brain and shell, spirit and body? It shall be sustained as he said, and it was. For I have already written in the *Book of Principles* of Jacob, that such knowledge is like a lip to the imagination, an image of his world for him. Higher than this is a refined light, this one and that one; this one is arranged like that one. That is to say, this one touches that one, and that one touches this one. 

In this chapter, the holy secret of the Book was supported: it was explained that the "Torah of Man" in its totality is an arrangement for the wise man. From this comes the spirit, soul, and blood, in the order of the "Living" <note>original: *Chayot*</note>, and this is the "Living to the Living." It will be explained to you then that they established the life-force in the boundaries of the brain and the Torah to the Spirit. The Spirit is in the likeness of a body and shell to the Wisdom. And the Spirit is in the likeness of the brain and a riddle to the Soul (*Nefesh*). And the Soul is in the likeness of a body and shell to the Spirit. This is the entire internal totality. There is a power of brain and shell, and through it shall be sustained: "And the Divine blessed the man in his entirety... by the blessing of his life-force." 

The Midrash says that the "Spirit of Peace" belongs to the "Tongue of the Covenant," the blessing of his life-force. The body is for the "Dream," a full opening, a mouth for him as the lower one for the prayer. Part of the calling of "Man" spread into his secrets, like the Sanhedrin. He is the light of one of all the generations. By the investigation of his wisdom and his generations, they spread into the writing of secrets. This is the light of one without a generation. Upon this, "the Divine created the man in his totality... and male and female He created them," etc. The spirit is called "Chosen" between them. The Lord <note>original: *H'*</note> investigated the "Son" and the "Daughter," and upon this, there is power, and thus, "Male." 

A great spirit shall be the life-force for the calling of "Man." They spread into his generations below, speaking in secrets. This one and that one are the dwellings of this Man, and the understanding of the Name of God <note>original: *Y"H Y"H*</note>. These are "Male and Female He created them and He called their name Adam." It was explained that the "Male" in the body is for the living foundation of the Lord, "the Divine [created] the Man, dust from the earth." What is the difference between one man and another? Behold, the Name of God <note>original: *Y"H*</note> is called "Man." And the Soul (*Nefesh*) is called "Man." If so, why is it called a "Line"? Rather, as it was said, "And the Divine blessed the man in his totality," through this it shall be. And it is written that he is called by his totality, this "Henoch" <note>Enoch</note>. 

According to this Midrash, it is difficult: why did he not explain the principle of the "Image and Likeness" from which the life-force of the Divine comes? The reason for this is that he said these are from the Scripture, and their meaning is the simple interpretation. The necessity proceeds from it, because the necessity is composed of the whole, like matter and death and the spirit of the internal man. Life is worthy to arise and to be drawn to that Name. Its fullness is hidden; there is no end to their simplifications. There is life of knowledge and wisdom in all to understand the secrets of the necessity. They could err and forgive what they grasp in the "Secret of the Divine" within the masses, as we have written. In the end, we return only to our words, to a great secret: the Likeness is according to the whole intention of the Torah. He shall be great and shall live in the totality of his brightness.

<meta>This page continues the investigation into the nature of divine manifestations and the linguistic choices made by ancient translators to preserve God's transcendence. It transitions from the physical "shell" of man to the "glory" of God as described in the Torah.</meta>

### Chapter 33: The Section on the Purpose ###

He ascended and did not descend, and he shall ascend further to the place of His glory—this is the secret of the "Challah" <note>This likely refers to the "Sod HaChallah" or the secret of the dough offering, often used in Kabbalistic texts to describe the separation of the holy from the mundane.</note>, and this is the "Challah" for... All that is written shall be claimed, and he shall say his psalm: "Take in your support all who die for Egypt," and "like clay," etc. And it has already been moved from the "all" and shifted, taken like myrrh and frankincense, concerning that which the event itself relied upon. As it is written in the <term>Targum</term><note>The Aramaic translation of the Bible, usually referring to Targum Onkelos.</note>: "I shall appear before the Living God," and he explained and saw, etc. He should not have written "And indeed," as <term>Ramban</term><note>Rabbi Moshe ben Nachman (Nachmanides), a 13th-century philosopher and Kabbalist.</note> (may his memory be a blessing) scrutinizes in its place. For if the language of "appearing" were attributed to the "God of Israel," it would remove what is written: "And they saw the God of Israel." One should not translate in a way that implies praise in this description, for in this matter the Targum's meaning was that the <term>Shekhinah</term><note>The Divine Presence, often described as the immanent or feminine aspect of God in the world.</note> of the Lord is what passed by, etc.

The intention there was specifically regarding the usage and the hearing, and it should have said, "And they sang to the Lord God," not to weep over the transition to the Glory. As he envisioned then, he also said: "And he saw the [glory] of the Lord," etc. And there are those who intended that it is only said when referring to His essence, and for this reason, they left it as "His Glory." However, he said concerning the reward of "His psalm," which belongs to Him, that all shall gaze upon the Glory toward the *Shekhinah* intended for you, as is said in another place: "The Lord your God [goes] before you in the desert." "His psalm"—this is a language of "near and far," for he did not say "it shall happen" nor "his psalm" nor "his *Shekhinah*." And from this matter, it is said to all these: "with your mouth." "And I will cause you to dwell," etc. In this, and at the end, and in the chapter concerning all these matters, without his way being to reveal himself like a <note>original: *poly-phisicus*? The OCR "פלוגיסקיס" suggests a Greek or Latin philosophical term for "manifold nature."</note>, nor in obscure or perfect matters.

And his claim is nothing, for even the generalities are not intended, because the Glory appropriately links the generalities. His reason further is that they should seek for its explanation from the underworld, for the intellect knows the "evil" <note>referring to the *Yetzer Hara* or material inclination</note> in all matters and includes them. To this end, he devoted a chapter on its own, and regarding this scripture, to show that all this is impossible to teach except through the wisdom of the Torah, which is the ultimate wonder. And according to the way of our Great Rabbi <note>Likely referring to Maimonides or Ramban.</note>, although many despise this according to the Tradition <note>original: *Kabbalah*</note> in his hand, from which it is impossible for us to turn right or left. No permission is given to any opinion to look upon the Holy Scripture (peace be upon him) except in the way he walked in his translation of the city, from the mouths of the "Fathers of the World" according to their tradition from Sinai. From this, he brought light into what is "Knowledge," and looked to the end [to ensure one does not] labor in vain. One who understands comes to the whole, and is destined to give an account for his pride. This is the God of the Torah of Truth.

## Chapter 29

"I will make all my goodness pass before you" <note>Exodus 33:19</note>—Onkelos translated this as "I will make all my **Glory** pass," not "all my goodness." And the verse "And I will put you in the cleft of the rock," Onkelos translated as "And I will protect you with the word of my **Glory**." This explains the reason for the suffix "to Him" and the "Behold" in any place in the desert, for that is where He dwelt. And we also find this suffix regarding the guarding of the righteous and His providence over them: "And all the congregation said to stone them with stones, and the **Glory of the Lord** appeared in the Tent of Meeting to all the children of Israel" <note>Numbers 14:10</note>. And they said in the <term>Midrash</term><note>Ancient homiletic interpretations of the Torah.</note>: A parable of one who throws a stone there, and the cloud precedes it. And in the chapter "These are guarded," it asks: Is it possible for a human to throw something toward the one whose Glory is riding [above]? They threw it upward! The intention was not the Glory itself, but because they were denying the *Shekhinah* and His providence with him there, the sages said they threw it "upward." And the righteous ones, who are our portion in the world, they said "to stone them with stones," and the Glory was revealed to protect them in the <insert>loops</insert>

<column-break/>

and to guard and to change and to remind who the righteous are. We find, then, that this suffix refers to protection and providence even within it. It would have been appropriate for Onkelos to translate "my Glory" and "the death of your people," and not change His dwelling place, nor establish any falsehood. The deep [meaning] of the *Shekhinah* is "Evil." From where [do we know] that he was able to translate "my guard" and "this with you"? Because he saw that it was not a matter of rescue or removal, nor any movement of the matter, etc., for the mention of it "ascends and does not descend." If so, the proofs in it are movements of transition, and it is not to be attributed to the Glory according to our opinion and understanding.

For he attributed it to His "Word" (*Memra*), which is the return and the dwelling, which are movements of transition. And He afterwards returns to the word "which," and "all," for "it shall not return to Me empty, but it shall do that which I purposed and prosper that for which I sent it" <note>Isaiah 55:11</note>. Behold, this "return" applies to them, and "they saw them." And it is written: "By the coming of His word, He healed them," and "He sent His word and healed them." Even though Onkelos did not intend for the language to be a redundant statement or a sworn oath, as the Master, the explainer, wrote, "in your faith." For it is from the explicit [text], saying "rejoice with the voice of God," which speaks from the midst of the fire, and he translated: "the voice of the **Word** (*Memra*) of the Lord was revealed." This belongs to the Kingdom of Sheba regarding the *Memra*.

And he said further, as is said in another place: "The Lord your God who goes before you," etc., and "A thousand," etc. Why did he say "Glory" and not "Word" (*Memra*) and not "Presence" (*Shekhinah*)? For we find "The Lord your God is He who goes with you and will not fail you," and from this the translation is: "The Lord your God, His **Word** (*Memra*) leads before you." If so, even in what is written, "The Lord your God, He passes before you," he could have translated it as "His Word" or "His Glory," just as we found above that this suffix refers back to Providence and Protection. And it will be clarified from where he was able to translate "His Word" and "this with you."

And he said further: There was no place for "Glory," etc., unless it was written, etc. And from this, he had no [reason] in it; he should have translated "And He was exalted," etc., as Ramban (may his memory be a blessing) scrutinizes there. The Master's intention there is distant and not from its place. And regarding the matter of the Satan, he shall take... since he increased the word in that which he has no power over, etc. And the intention of the Master <note>Likely referring to Maimonides/Rambam.</note> (may his memory be a blessing) regarding "His Glory" is the "Chosen Virtue" <note>original: *Segulah*, a special divine property</note> received in the True Wisdom <note>referring to Kabbalah</note>. For when you come to confirm it, the eyes of the wise are directed toward it...

And what he established further: that when one intends the "Glory," it encompasses the matters and the specifics, and the *Shekhinah* has already [rested]... And behold, this reasoning was taken by the Master in the book *Duties of the Heart* <note>original: *Chovot HaLevavot* by Bahya ibn Paquda</note>, chapter 25... and the Master [critiqued] this in the name of Wisdom as well in the final chapter. And it was received regarding this Master how he took this reasoning from him. It appeared to him from the book that it is the *Shekhinah*, until he said that Onkelos (peace be upon him) could not translate "my dwelling with your death," for these do not intend the True Soul, but rather the matter of Protection, etc. It does not intend a suffix, for the intention there is also regarding the usage and the protection. And there are those who say that everything [refers to] "I will send an angel before you to guard you on the way and to bring you to the place which I have prepared" <note>Exodus 23:20</note>. The law is that they intended (peace be upon them) not the translation of the "Angel."

And he sought the providence of the *Shekhinah* and said, "among my sons," and "let us go and be seen by you." And he translated "my dwelling" as "between you." And he (peace be upon him) said: "If your Presence does not go," etc. And the intention in writing "from the *Shekhinah*" is "to my dwelling." And the secret (peace be upon him) of all flesh—unless it be the Angel according to the opinion of other commentators, for he is a created being. But the Creator who measured it is then to comfort you, standing in our place, and He sends by way of the *Shekhinah*. But according to the Truth <note>i.e., according to Kabbalah</note>, this Angel is the **Redeeming Angel**, and he is the "Angel of God" without [possessive] connection. Rather, the "Sin of the Calf" caused him to say to them, "And I will send before you an angel," equal to the [regular] messengers. And he warned: "For I will not go up in your midst." Concerning the *Shekhinah*, it would not say "For I will not go up in your midst." The choice is that the *Shekhinah* is the Protection and the Providence, and it is the "last" <note>The final Sephirah, *Malkhut*</note> to guard you on the way. If so, even concerning protection and providence, he could translate "My *Shekhinah* shall die with you." If so, he shall guard you to show by reasoning that these matters and their outcomes should not be questioned, nor should one have power over them or contradict them at all. It is impossible to settle them in their proper way except through the Received Tradition (*Kabbalah*) which Onkelos had.

# Chapter 27: The Section on the Purpose

In these matters, one should follow tradition and not simply speak of "right and left" <note>original: "ימין ושמאל"; here referring to literal physical directions attributed to God</note>, nor should one imagine that the text can be left to stand merely as a parable. It is not permitted to speak by mere human reasoning regarding the details of matters that have already been investigated to provide "good taste and knowledge" <note>A phrase from Psalm 119:66, often used to mean sound judgment or logical explanation.</note> in the translation of this scripture. One must add understanding to it through the weighing of the intellect and the intent of the heart in our writing, following the style of the scriptures.

The intention, as the **Master Guide** <note>Referring to Maimonides and his work, *The Guide for the Perplexed*.</note> frequently mentions there, is that they call out to the Lord "from His right hand" <note>Deuteronomy 33:2</note>, which refers to the **Shekhinah** <note>The Divine Presence</note> of the Lord. These reasons are well-known according to the linguistic roots and the sense of the language, even without hidden traditions, as they contain great and wondrous secrets. This is because the general principle is to avoid attributing to Him (may He be blessed) matters that would contradict His honor.

Initially, one must consider every case according to its context. When the scripture assigns to the Lord (may He be blessed) an action or a state like "rested," "sighed," "came down," "went up," and the like, the translator distances the literal meaning. They will say "the Lord revealed Himself" or "the Glory of the Lord was revealed." For example, where it says "And Israel saw," it is translated as "The Glory of the Lord was revealed to them and Israel saw." All of this is done for the sake of the honor of the Creator, as is the custom in all languages when speaking of the great. It is known that "for His honor" and "for His greatness" are used according to the weighing of the intellect. As the verse says: "The glory of the Lord filled [the Tabernacle]" and "The glory of the Lord shall dwell." This "covering" does not refer to a physical place.

Regarding the expression "for the sake of My glory," it refers to a hidden matter. The verse "Let Your glory pass before me" <note>Exodus 33:18</note> does not mean His actual "face," as will be explained in its proper place. However, when the text deals with **Providence** <note>Divine supervision or intervention in the world</note>, the translator uses the term **Memra** <note>original Aramaic: "מימרא"; literally "The Word" or "The Speech" of God</note>. For example, "The Word of the Lord was with him." This term "Word" is used from the beginning to the end. Just as it says "By the Word of the Lord the heavens were made," the Targum translates the voice of the Lord as the "Word of the Lord."

When it says "I will be with your mouth," it is translated as "My Word shall be with your speech." This is to say that the style and intention is to provide a sense of security and trust, as if to say His Word is His action. When one swears "by the Lord," he is swearing by that comforting promise.

Furthermore, when the intention is the revelation of these matters, the translator uses the term **Shekhinah** <note>The indwelling Presence</note>. For example, "The cloud of the Lord was over them." It is written, "The Lord shall dwell in your midst," which is translated as "The Shekhinah of the Lord shall dwell." This is because the intention in all of them is to describe a state that is not a physical movement, and therefore it is attributed to the Shekhinah.

The general rule that emerges from this is that their intent in almost all these matters is to provide a reason why we do not translate literally. When the text says "And I will come down," it cannot be translated as a literal descent, but as "I will reveal Myself," because the intention is the revelation of His Presence.

# Chapter 28

Regarding the concept of **Glory** <note>Hebrew: "Kavod"</note>, I have already informed you that it refers to a certain internal perception. Because God is free from all that is seen in prophetic visions, one cannot attribute physical movement to Him. We have seen the objections of **Ramban** <note>Nachmanides (13th century), who often disagreed with Maimonides' philosophical explanations for the Targum's choices.</note> (may his memory be a blessing) on this. According to the first logic, the translator Onkelos intended to distance anthropomorphism.

It appears that **Onkelos** <note>The 2nd-century convert and scholar credited with the standard Aramaic translation of the Torah.</note> did not follow a single rule for all languages but used many different terms: some to distance physical descriptions, some to distance physical actions, some for the sake of honor, and some to make the specific subject matter understood. I say that if there is a tradition in our hands regarding what these terms hint at, it is sufficient for understanding the difference.

# Chapter 27

"And God went up from him in the place where He spoke with him" <note>Genesis 35:13</note>. He explained that "God" here refers to the Glory that was with him in the place where He spoke with him. This is written to indicate the **Unification** <note>Hebrew: "Yichud"; the concept of God's absolute oneness and Jacob's unique connection to it.</note> that was revealed to speak with him in His transcendence.

This was not as precisely noted with Abraham, because with Jacob, the bond of Unification and support was more established. He is the "Man of Truth" who represents the people of Israel. His stature is greater than that of our ancestors before him. In him, the form of Unification was completed. Therefore, it is said of the People of Israel that "the Lord is in our midst," and "the Shekhinah of the Lord shall be revealed."

Our Sages (may their memory be a blessing) in their explanation said it was like a herald. I found in the book *The Love of the Lord* regarding the orders of prayer: they said at the beginning of the **Haftarah** <note>The selection from the Prophets read in synagogue.</note> for Sukkot, in the name of Rabbi Meir: "Behold, the Lord comes forth from His place and will come down and tread upon the high places of the earth" <note>Micah 1:3</note>. He "comes forth" from one attribute to another: from the **Attribute of Judgment** to the **Attribute of Mercy** over Israel. From His "place"—meaning the agitation of Judgment which is fear and sighing—to Mercy.

And when they are convicted by Judgment, He "comes forth" from the Attribute of Mercy to the Attribute of Judgment. This happened in the merit of Jacob... for he was in a place of drawing forth from the source, and that was His "place" and His being. But He went out from there and turned to the Attribute of Judgment.

In the commentary of **Rashi** <note>Rabbi Shlomo Yitzchaki, the preeminent medieval commentator.</note>, it says that they were shaken... and he said: "Who is like the Lord our God?" He explained that the words are not about the Essence Himself, but about His actions and His wisdom. There is no physical movement or change of place here. This is the way of the Torah—to use human language to describe the Creator of all, speaking to people according to their ability to understand, as will be explained further. This is enough to understand the distinction.

# Chapter 30 | The Section on the Purpose | Chapter 31

In Chapter 30, "Blessed be the glory of the Lord from His place" <note>Ezekiel 3:12</note> is discussed according to His excellence and the essence of His fullness in existence. See how there is none like Him, and praise is due to Him as one who relies on what was received from the prophets. It addresses the creation of the world through our reasoned judgment alongside the "vital names" <note>Names of God that imply life or action</note>, the "accidental" <term>accidental: in medieval philosophy, a non-essential property or characteristic</term> false appearances, and that which contradicts the truth in its simple sense. This is the delight they take when they sanctify Him with a blessing and say, "Blessed be the glory of the Lord from His place" and "Blessed be Your glorious name," etc. The one who blesses and prays to the "Glory of His Glory" is mentioned here.

And regarding what relationship He (may He be blessed) has to the term "Glory" in Himself, it says "for the sake of His glory" and "on the matter of His glory," which refers to His power and the dread of His awe. As in Chapter 27 of Part 1 <note>of Maimonides' *Guide for the Perplexed*</note>, where the Master <note>Maimonides</note> says that for Onkelos <note>The famous 2nd-century translator of the Torah into Aramaic</note>, all these are words in the Hebrew and Aramaic tongues. He previously exerted himself in presenting premises that every attribute the Scripture boasts of which might lead to "corporeality" <term>corporeality: the state of having a physical body, which philosophers argued cannot apply to God</term> should be called according to its true meaning. Whenever they apply metaphors to Him full of names indicating a type of movement, the meaning of this movement is the distancing of any lack in the Creator—meaning, it refers to the **Shekhinah** <note>The Divine Presence</note> or Providence. Thus, he translated "And the Lord descended" <note>Exodus 19:20</note> as "The Lord revealed Himself," and did not say "The Lord went down" <note>original: "ונחת"; Onkelos avoids the physical verb for descending</note>. Rather, he used terms of revelation.

This is all consistent with his explanation. However, he translated for the **Sages of Truth** <note>original: "חכמי ח"ד"; likely referring to the Kabbalists or those with esoteric knowledge</note> the "pillar of cloud" as an established force of truth, which is a very profound matter and points to the perfection of the latter's fullness and his good philosophizing and understanding of his words. He opened for us in this translation a great matter regarding the nature of prophecy. Initially, this scribe said, "And God spoke to Israel in the visions of the night, and said, 'Jacob, Jacob...'" <note>Genesis 46:2</note>. When we look at the beginning of this, saying it was "in the visions of the night," the clear narrative which is in the material of the "visions of the night" is not diminished or weakened by its language. This is a report of what was said, not a report of an event that happened physically.

From here you will be awakened to the fact that there is a great difference between what is said in a "dream" or "visions of the night" and what is said in a "vision" or "sight" <note>Hebrew: "מחזה ומראה"</note>, or what is said plainly as "The Lord spoke to me." The Sages further explained that "God" <note>Elohim</note> refers to the fact that He reigned over Isaac, and did not suggest that he should be called a "wise man of established truth." These are his final words.

And in Chapter 48, regarding everything that comes to pass... he explained its meaning like the "vision of the morning" which belongs to Him (may He be blessed)—meaning, it is He and His will, and it was strong like the matter of the "encampment." When he mentions that He accepted him, if He accepted, he always says in his translation "The Lord heard" as "It was heard before the Lord." Regarding the "cry" being heard, it means the acceptance of the prayer. This is consistent with his explanation, not that he placed it in one location or another.

However, our Great Rabbi **Nahmanides** <note>The 13th-century scholar and mystic</note> (may his memory be a blessing) challenged him on all of this. He lengthily replied with correct answers showing there is no firm basis, for these things are visions. It is possible to speak of them and be amazed according to the intellect, and they should be considered according to the traditional wisdom in our hands, as he hinted at the end of his words. What wonder is there that the Master Guide <note>Maimonides</note> thinks there is a report of what was said versus a report of what happened? It is surprising that he said "the Lord would not do such a thing." Perhaps the Master will reveal in this that the change was imaginary in Jacob's mind as he went down to Egypt. For every place where revelation occurs, it was "in the visions of the night," which in his opinion was a "sleep of descent" and prophecy was changed, and it was not from the observation of the intellect because he did not see it in a waking prophecy. If it were so, he would have translated it as "revelation," but because it was "in the visions of the night," he translated it as "vision." Some of his commentators said: how did this Master not notice the narrative of the Torah? It was not just Jacob's narrative. Perhaps there was room for the Master's thought... mention is made of bringing their fathers from a full night to the Torah. Behold, the Master Guide attributes to Onkelos things that never entered his mind, and in several places, he confused the lack of his food <note>metaphor for lack of understanding</note> and there is no...

...intent in the "visions of the night" from there. We are here to tell the outcome of the true wisdom in all this according to the tradition of our Great Rabbi <note>Nahmanides</note>, as I knew from the chapter preceding this.

### Chapter 31

Regarding the investigation of the "Custom of the Torah" <note>A concept that the Torah follows certain linguistic patterns</note>: it did not employ the traditional secret wisdom in that regard. Certainly, the translator of the Torah from the days of Rabbi Eliezer and Rabbi Joshua—and the scriptures written in our name—the wise will call His **Shekhinah** <note>Divine Presence</note> and His **Memra** <note>Aramaic for "Word" or "Logos"</note>. Some scriptures did not mention it by name. Similarly, scriptures that used the language of revelation said "in the name" and "were revealed" through the sight of an angel, such as the striking angel, or in language of equivalence as with Jacob. Even scriptures that use the name of the "First of the World" <note>God</note> which he translated with language of revelation, and other scriptures he translated with language of equivalence. Or scriptures that use the term "descent," which he translated with language of revelation, while others—such as "I will go down with you to Egypt" <note>Genesis 46:4</note>—he translated as "I will go down," which was not from him a distancing of corporeality in its precision, as the Master Guide <note>Maimonides</note> found difficult. If not for this, why would they act to force the names in some places and not in others?

Our Great Rabbi <note>Nahmanides</note> expanded on this in his critiques of him, to which there is no answer. Why attribute to Onkelos things where the Torah did not sin? Why distance that which he distanced? For who will attribute and who will distance outside of her <note>the Torah</note>? For she is "a tree of life" and "a good lesson, her ways are ways of pleasantness and all her paths are peace." The perfection of prophecy and life are clarified through the path of life. If error were found in her paths, Heaven forbid!

For he did not find it difficult that "Let us make man" <note>Genesis 1:26</note> was translated in the language of men. Its explanation was "one in the head" <note>meaning, a single act of creation</note>. "Let us make man in our image and likeness"—it was said so that it would apply to the upper and lower beings. Why was the language of the scriptures not difficult regarding His saying "In our image and our likeness," just as he questioned the word "Let us make"?

As the Sages said in *Genesis Rabbah*: Rabbi Samuel bar Nahman said in the name of Rabbi Jonathan: "At the hour when Moses was writing the Torah, he was writing the work of each and every day. When he reached this verse, 'And God said: Let us make man,' Moses said before Him: 'Master of the Universe! Why do You give an **opening for the heretic**?' <term>opening for the heretic: a phrase or idea that could be misinterpreted to support non-monotheistic beliefs</term>. He replied to him: 'Write! And whoever wants to err, let them err.'"

The Holy One, Blessed be He, said to him: "Moses, this world that I created—did I not establish great and small within it? If the great comes to take permission from the small, he might say, 'Why should I take permission from one smaller than me?' They will say to him: 'Learn from your Creator! For He created the upper and lower worlds, and when He came to create man, like a king among his works, He consulted...'"

Just as it was difficult for him regarding the writing of an "opening for the heretic" to err and warn of "two authorities" <note>the heresy that there are two gods</note>, why was it not difficult for him regarding the scripture that indicates "continuity"? And He (may He be blessed) as well—why did He not guard against all this? But everything is from Him; in this, He "misled" the heretics but wrote language that creatures would speak, to teach them to walk in His ways and achieve perfection toward Him.

So I say regarding the "Soul of the Torah" which I wrote above in Chapter 20, regarding the secret of "Let us make a spirit," etc. Had He written "I will make," it would have been a "logical inference" <term>Kal Va-Chomer: a 'light and heavy' logical argument</term> that the Upper World, which was made so, would be diminished. The Torah is recorded and engraved from the light of Above, and it cannot be changed. Heaven forbid that He should make His Torah a "forgery" <note>original: "פלסתר"</note>. The same applies to this doubt regarding "In our image and likeness." As mentioned, it points to what preceded it and all other things hinted at further on. Afterward, this wondrous matter comes out correctly, through which the eyes of the perfect sages are opened to say that all this is to align it with the Great Wisdom received in his hand. Everything done in this was with intention and Providence, for they did not appear in the Holy Torah in only one way. It mentions time and nine for all, sometimes for revelation, sometimes for a generation, and judgment. And this is the place...

<meta>This page continues the deep theological inquiry into how the term "Glory" (Kavod) is used in the Torah, specifically debating the interpretations of Maimonides (the Master of the Guide) and Nahmanides regarding Divine manifestations. # Chapter 30 | The Section on the Purpose | Chapter 30

Furthermore: one must distinguish a great difference of heart between the statement "while my glory passes by" <note>Exodus 33:22</note> and its context until "I have passed by," and the statement "Show me, I pray Thee, Thy glory" <note>Exodus 33:18</note> regarding the essence and truth of God Himself. This "Glory" is attributed to Him, may He be blessed, in the same way as the context of "until I have passed by," which refers—according to the simple meaning of the verses—to what is written: "but My face shall not be seen" <note>Exodus 33:23</note>. This is because the text says, "thou canst not see My face, for man shall not see Me and live" <note>Exodus 33:20</note>. Just as this refers to His essence and truth, so too does the other refer to His essence and truth. Regarding this, the text continues, "and I will cover thee with My hand until I have passed by" <note>Exodus 33:22</note> to hide Himself. According to the Master <note>Maimonides</note>, why would God need to "cover him with His hand" and protect him from seeing a "Created Glory" <term>Created Glory: a theological concept where God creates a special light or visual phenomenon to represent His presence without being His actual essence</term>? God forbid! For if seeing "face to face" were possible, it would be known from the living God. Behold, a barrier exists for the Created Glory to exist. For the Master’s opinion is that "Place" <note>original: "Ha-Makom," a name for God</note> is attributed to the Created Glory, and not to movement or the displacement of location, as he explained in Chapter 28 and as we wrote above.

From this, one might be confused by the translation <note>the Aramaic Targum</note>: "And the angel of the Lord appeared to him in a flame of fire," and it says, "the angel of the Lord," which refers to the Glory. If these intentions are meant to address the lack of physical perception and the lack of intellectual perception, there is yet another answer: If Onkelos <note>the famous 2nd-century translator</note> did not intend to attribute the status of Created Glory here, he should have translated it as such. But in the end, he translated it as "behold, I saw," etc. Our Great Rabbi <note>Nahmanides</note>, of blessed memory, already challenged him on this. Furthermore, in the Master’s <note>Maimonides'</note> view, there is a "stumbling of the foot" and a place for error in his statement that "Glory" refers to that which is called "Glory" in every place. And to this, he divided them, and all of them are one. As it is written: "and the glory of the Lord filled the tabernacle" <note>Exodus 40:34</note>. And it is written: "the priests could not stand to minister because of the cloud, for the glory of the Lord filled the house of the Lord" <note>1 Kings 8:11</note>.

There is a statement about "Created Glory," and this was the intention of our Sages, of blessed memory: to guard and incline toward the hidden meanings. In the "House of the Ages" <note>the Temple in Jerusalem</note>, they were to experience the light of the Glory. But the Perfect One, may He be blessed, spoke of His Glory and His Essence: "And let them make Me a sanctuary, that I may dwell among them" <note>Exodus 25:8</note>. And He said regarding the building: "I will meet with thee there, and I will speak with thee from above the ark-cover, from between the two cherubim which are upon the ark of the testimony" <note>Exodus 25:22</note>. And it is written: "And there I will meet with the children of Israel, and it shall be sanctified by My glory" <note>Exodus 29:43</note>. And the Lord, may He be blessed, said: "And I will dwell among the children of Israel" <note>Exodus 29:45</note>. This is proof that the attribute of the *Shekhinah* <term>Shekhinah: the Divine Presence that dwells within the world</term> in our midst comes to rest upon us, and there is no fear regarding the "Created Light" which emanates from Him. As it is said: "And they shall know that I am the Lord their God, who brought them forth out of the land of Egypt, that I may dwell among them; I am the Lord their God" <note>Exodus 29:46</note>. On this, it is explained that the intention is for the Created Light to dwell among us. However, the verse does not say "to make the Glory dwell among them," but "that I may dwell among them; I am the Lord their God."

The foundation is that when He speaks from between the Cherubim, it is a connection settled and prepared for the Light of Glory, and it is hidden above the Created Glory, above all supreme honor. From the strength of that Created Light, the Glory becomes a "throne" for the Creator. If so, according to this view, the one speaking with Moses from above the ark-cover between the two cherubim would be the Created Light and not the Creator Himself, Heaven forbid. This is because if his heart were strengthened to believe it was specific to the Glory of His greatness, his intention would be "and I will speak with thee," etc., and he would increase the power and perception of the Created Light. We have already seen this from one of the commentators on the words of the Master of the "Guide," and from his own language it is explicit in Part 1, where he uses this phrasing: "And so 'Living Ears' between the Holy One, Blessed be He, who is the 'Agent Intellect' <term>Agent Intellect: in medieval philosophy, the bridge between the Divine mind and human reason</term> and, as it were, they are one," etc. How many difficulties are there in the Master's words and intentions—a place for error and a "stumbling of the foot" regarding the holy faith!

Furthermore, they would be astonished by each of the services, for it is written: "Blessed be the glory of the Lord from His place" <note>Ezekiel 3:12</note>. The translation of Jonathan ben Uzziel <note>an early Aramaic translator of the Prophets</note>, peace be upon him, says: "Blessed be the glory of the Lord from the place of the house of His Shekhinah." If you follow the intention regarding the "Glory," it refers to "My Glory" and His truth, and it would be like "Show me, I pray Thee, Thy glory," which the Master interpreted in this way in that verse. Behold, I will mention that he says "and the house of My Shekhinah" appears as a commentary; these are the words of Jonathan ben Uzziel, agreeing with the opinion of the Master <note>Maimonides</note> in several books according to...

<column-break/>

Behold, according to what he explained, all parts of the matters which belong to Him, may He be blessed, are attributed to His names. All the verses that our Sages, of blessed memory, agreed upon—calling Him "Grace" and "Kindness"—belong to Him. And the parts of "Glory" within them: this is the Glory divided from Grace. This belongs to Him by virtue of His creation, so that you might bring it in. If so, why would He be distant from Him in His place and in the places given to Him? Rather, this belongs to Him through great wisdom and intention, to distance "corporeality" <term>corporeality: the philosophical error of imagining God has a physical body</term> in the opinion of the Master of the Guide <note>Maimonides</note>, of blessed memory. For why would he distance and attribute "Place" even to that which the Holy Torah did not distance, nor spare him from?

All these matters are explained to those who receive the truth <note>a reference to Kabbalists</note>. Jonathan ben Uzziel, who translated "The Glory," did so because of Haggai, Zechariah, and Malachi <note>the last of the biblical prophets</note>. Indeed, from their wisdom, we learned the translation of the Torah from the mouths of Rabbi Eliezer and Rabbi Joshua, peace be upon them. They learned the translation of the Torah of Jonathan ben Uzziel, which they returned to the mouths of Haggai, Zechariah, and Malachi. It is written there regarding it, and the translation of the Torah is "to the Place" of which they spoke. And the statement of Rav Hisda: when he saw, Rav Huna said, Rav Hisda said: As it is written, "And they called the glory of the beauty of the nations," explicitly, etc. "And they read in the book, in the Law of God"—this refers to the Scripture; "explicitly"—this refers to the translation. And so, "they pushed the Shekhinah and Jonathan."

Thus they clarified that the translator holds a tradition by their hand, based on the "reception of the weights" <note>original: "mitan ha-kvulim," possibly referring to traditional measurements or chains of transmission</note> which were undoubtedly received from Sinai, but they were forgotten and then later returned to Jonathan. Their foundation is through the hands of the Sages, peace be upon them. Thus they clarified and supported the intention. With great wisdom, the ancient translator of the Torah assisted, for he was a "Righteous Proselyte" <note>meaning a convert to Judaism</note> and held ancient traditions. If so, everything the commentators wrote in his translation is exactly what we wrote in the section on "Epithets" <term>Epithets: names or titles used to describe God without implying physical form</term>. Everything is known to him by tradition. I am not lacking, peace be upon him, the intention of our Sages... and the wisdom of the Recipient <note>the Kabbalist</note> in all this, according to the standard of my Great Rabbi, Nahmanides, of blessed memory, and according to what the Sages of Truth <note>Kabbalists</note> received, which he returned to the Holy ones in Chapter Five and in the Name.

### Chapter Thirty

Which shall be called "Glory" in every place and in every matter concerning the *Shekhinah*. Everything the translator said has already been discussed, leaning on these matters. This is because everything you divide is attributed to the Glory, Grace, and the ancient Jonathan ben Uzziel. If the translator were forgotten, the Light would be placed today for another prophet, after it was delayed... in the Torah. And they were heavy upon him, and he called it the "Standing at Sinai." And he said: "May the Lord be my intention and His glory shall dwell," guarding for the Lord, etc. On this, he continued his commentary, and so now in his words: "And the Lord passed before his face," he translates: "And the Lord caused His Shekhinah to pass before his face and called out." Behold, the entire order will be the "Glory of the Partition" <note>original: "kavod bi-ferat"</note>. If his heart ceased regarding the name of the Hidden Glory before the face of our teacher Moses, peace be upon him, his commentary would return "before his face" to mean "in front of him," as it says, "and the gift passed before his face." This is a good and beautiful interpretation.

However, keep hold of the interpretation of Onkelos, of blessed memory, who said the verse: "And it shall come to pass, while my glory passeth by." He already explained that the thing passing is alone attributed to Him, may He be blessed, and not to His very self. Regarding that Glory, he said: "until I have passed by" and "the Lord passed before his face." If we were to explain the word "passed" as being derived from a similar root like "dirtied," Onkelos always follows the foundation of the statement: sometimes it is called "Shekhinah," sometimes "Glory," and sometimes "The Word of the Lord" (*Memra*), according to the context of each place, etc.

And he wrote: "And the Sages said: the Glory of the Lord was upon Mount Sinai," and "I will dwell in the midst of the children of Israel." And so, the Shekhinah dwells within us. Everything attributed to the "Action" is attributed to the Glory; it is like the matter of the Shekhinah, meaning His created Light in this place, the standing of the one who makes use of the order for every place according to its context. And in Chapter 7 he says: and so with "The Glory of the Lord," sometimes they mean the "Created Light" which is the Shekhinah, which God makes visible in the manner of a miracle: "And the glory of the Lord settled" <note>Exodus 24:16</note> and "the glory of the Lord filled" <note>Exodus 40:34</note>. And sometimes they mean His very self, may He be blessed, and His truth, as it says: "Show me, I pray Thee, Thy glory." The reason is that "he cannot see Me and live." The source is that the Glory refers to the Essence itself, and he says "Thy glory" to magnify...
