<meta>This page continues the technical analysis of how the Aramaic translator Onkelos handles Divine names and physical descriptions of God. It follows a discussion on the differences between the Sages' interpretive tradition and that of the Karaites, focusing here on the linguistic "barriers" created to protect God's absolute unity and transcendence during moments of revelation.</meta>

# Chapter 31 | The Part of the Purpose | Chapter 31

This is to indicate absolute unity. He, peace be upon him <note>original: "a"h" – a common honorific for the deceased</note>, also repeated himself by using the epithet for the name **Elohim** <note>God</note>, as our Great Rabbi <note>referring to Maimonides (Rambam)</note> wrote regarding the Torah portion *Yitro* <note>Exodus 18:1–20:23</note>. He translates the name **Elohim** in every instance as the Tetragrammaton <note>The four-letter name of God, YHVH, often translated as "The Lord"</note> to indicate the Divine Unity. Since he <note>Onkelos</note> came to explain the Torah, he was required to clarify which of the holy names refers to the **Honored Name** and which refers to the **Precious Holiness**.

In places where the Torah mentions the name **Elohim**, he uses the name **YHVH** <note>The Lord</note>. Everywhere the name **Elohim** appears, he translates it as "The Word of the Lord" <note>original: "Memra d'YHVH" – an Aramaic term used to avoid describing God as having physical speech or presence</note>. This is to hint to us that this is not the Great Essence itself, but rather a term whose plain meaning is internal. As the Sages said: "One who mentions his master's name must include an epithet." He uses these ancient epithets for the word **Elohim** to include them together.

In places where the Torah mentions the name **YHVH**, he uses the name **Elohim**. Everywhere the name **YHVH** appears, he inserts a "partitioned" epithet. We find this in the Giving of the Torah, because the Torah was given through His Great Name. Therefore, his <note>Onkelos's</note> wisdom was clear when he translated "And the Lord descended in the sight of all the people" <note>Exodus 19:11</note> as "The Lord revealed Himself." He said this and called it "to the Lord." Similarly, for "And the Lord descended upon Mount Sinai" and "And the Lord said."

Regarding "And God spoke all these words" <note>Exodus 20:1</note>, he translated it as "And the Word of the Lord spoke." He translated "And Moses brought the people out to meet God" as being toward the "Word of the Lord," to hint at what we have considered there. This hint points toward His unity, for Israel heard the voice from the midst of the fire. There, they said that the Divine Word left **Elohim** <note>God</note> in that state. Onkelos translated this as: "And then He shall reveal Himself with you from before the Lord."

Since there is no epithet for the name **Elohim** in his Aramaic dialect—as we have written—he must translate **Elohim** using the name **YHVH**. Perhaps one might think he erred in the arrangement of the verses; therefore, he inserted a "partition" <note>original: "mechitza" – a conceptual barrier to prevent a physical understanding of God</note> and said, "from before the Lord." This refers to the Voice we considered and heard, which was speaking with you. This was a law they could not endure until they said, "You speak with us" <note>Exodus 20:16</note>. This was his method in some places to establish a barrier, even in places where the meaning is clear from the scriptures and there is no room for error. For example, it is written: "Finally we have seen that God speaks with man and he lives." He should have translated this as "He was revealed from before the Lord," but since it said above "And we heard His voice," he translated it as "and His Word," which is equivalent. There are many such cases.

Our Great Rabbi <note>Maimonides</note>, of blessed memory, already hinted at this in our lessons, providing enough for one who contemplates his words. However, the **Glory** below is addressed throughout the entire portion using the straightforward name. Where the text writes "And the Lord called to Moses," it is translated as "And the Lord called to Moses." "And the Lord said to Moses" becomes "And the Lord said to Moses." In every place where the mention and the speaking are directed "downward," the translation is literal, without a "partition." 

Regarding what is written in the portion of Moses, "Moses spoke and God answered him with a voice" <note>Exodus 19:19</note>, they gave a portion to the "Ancient of Days" <note>original: "Zakan Kadam YHVH" - a mystical reference to an aspect of the Divine</note> who answered him. Our Rabbi, of blessed memory, hinted that this existed before the "Descent," and that is how he translated it. This follows the order of the portion. It seems to me that he translated it this way because this Voice also reached Israel. This was also the opinion of our Rabbis of blessed memory. We have already understood the method of translating it thus.

As for the teaching of Rabbi Simeon bar Yochai <note>the reputed author of the Zohar</note>, peace be upon him, they said regarding the phrase "Moses spoke and God answered him with a voice": Moses spoke to the voice of Moses, and God answered him with the voice of all prophecy. For the Voice is the whole; "He answered him with a voice" means the Voice is Moses. One was not obligated to translate "God" without a barrier here, as that would weaken the intention regarding the "Secret of This World."

It was part of his <note>Onkelos's</note> wisdom that throughout the entire Torah, regarding the words mentioned as blessings for the Sages, he placed no barrier. This is because he had received the tradition regarding the place of their prophecy. As he noted in his translation: "Do not let these things be hidden from you." Regarding Jacob, he translated without a "Voice." It is proper to say that he informed us of the subtle difference between various prophecies. If the prophet had a "partition," it would be a place for linguistic error—as if the attainment was of a created thing—heaven forbid! They were strict in their explanation to ensure no one erred in thinking our attainment was higher than that of the Patriarchs.

This is forbidden in the scriptures, to decide for the people of your generation out of shame or theft. The Sage <note>Onkelos</note> translated it to be quiet, for it was said from the Sanctuary. It says "God spoke to Israel in visions of the night"...

<column-break/>

...and he taught the Sages of the Tradition <note>original: "Chachmei ha-Kabbalah"</note> the names **Elohim, Elohim**, and it is **Elohim**. This is from the "Illness of the Heart," and it is "The God of Bethel" <note>Genesis 35:7</note>. All of these are hints that the **Glory** <note>Kavod</note> is associated with the attribute of Judgment <note>represented by the name Elohim</note>. Because He is the speaker, he translated it plainly, for this is not an epithet that he would dare to change. The Exalted One is above all; it is a "language of descent" <note>referring to God's presence descending to the world</note> according to the secret of "I will go down with you to Egypt" <note>Genesis 46:4</note>—the Divine Presence <note>Shekhinah</note> was with them. 

If the Sages had placed a barrier here, it would have been a place for error, as if one were placing a "foreign thing" alongside the Foundation—heaven forbid! For he went down and said "My Word" <note>Memra</note>, and it is the Word and it is the Glory, for He is the speaker. If it were a foreign thing outside of the Glory, heaven forbid, then "strengthen your king from the foreigners," as the Guide <note>Maimonides, in the *Guide for the Perplexed*</note> thought in chapter 48. For the Sages of the Tradition would not speak of "atonement" regarding **Elohim, Elohim**.

Regarding what is written, "An angel of God said to me in a dream of Jacob," and it says the epithet "one of the foreigners"—it is actually the Great Angel, the sign of the **Glory**. The Sages of the Tradition said "The God of Bethel," and he is called a "Guarding Angel," as his nature was explained in Chapter 30. He is the one of whom it is said: "And an angel of the Lord appeared to him in a flame of fire out of the midst of a bush" <note>Exodus 3:2</note>. Because he is the "Angel of His Presence," the face of the bush itself was impressed with him. The Exalted One's work is "to the Lord," as it says, "And the Lord saw." This is what was said regarding Isaac, and what was said: "And God appeared to Jacob," for the language of "Sleep" here refers to the **Glory** through the power of the Patriarchs and their joy. 

He is the "Glory" within him. "And the Angel of God moved" <note>Exodus 14:19</note>, and they honored him. The conclusion of these matters is necessary: "For it is proper to say God to the sons of God." Facing him is the custom of the foreigners, and its secret is known to the Sages. It was not said regarding him "And a man wrestled with him" <note>Genesis 32:25</note>, yet Onkelos translated it as **Elohim**, for "I have seen God face to face" <note>Genesis 32:31</note>—"I have seen angels." If what was seen in the soul was from the foreigners, his soul would have turned his face from him. He wrote "to the blessings" for the sake of the three, and for the three. 

What is the matter of "His face" being consistent with the "Standings of the Lord"? Jacob said, "For I have seen God face to face." Also in the portions concerning Abimelech, **Elohim** is mentioned, and Onkelos inserts a "partition of three." Those who want to claim it is the literal name erred. It is written, "The Lord was with him," and he translated "The Word of the Lord was his help." It is known to the Sages of Truth that even for the Holy Patriarchs, the **Glory** was not the Great Name <note>YHVH</note> in its absolute sense, but rather the Name through which they gazed upward—the Prophets. Regarding the matter of "And My name YHVH I did not make known to them" <note>Exodus 6:3</note>, the wisdom of the scriptures hints at this. 

He translated "And behold, I am with you" <note>Genesis 28:15</note> and placed "My Word" in his assistance. Certainly, this was the speech from the Great Name. Through the Honored Name, he should have translated "And behold, the woman is with you," or "it is good to receive truth with you." But he was careful and translated "And behold, My Word is your assistance," so that he would not say the Name is in the Glory. "And behold, I am with you" without a barrier—this was his way because it was written at the beginning "And behold, the Lord stood over him." People might err and think it was the Great Name itself; therefore, he translated "And he called to the Lord." So they would not err and say that the speech did not come from the Great Name, he translated "And behold, I am with you" as "Behold, My Word is your assistance," to indicate that the Speaker is the Great Name in His attribute of Justice.

In the portions concerning Abimelech and Laban, he is careful to be precise with the Name in his wisdom, according to what the Tradition revealed to him. There is a difference between them and the "Dream of the Bush." It is said of them, "And God came to Abimelech in a dream by night" <note>Genesis 20:3</note> and "And God came to Laban the Aramean in a dream by night" <note>Genesis 31:24</note>. He translated these in his response as "And a word came from before the Lord." This is very wondrous! It was not enough for him to say "And the Word of the Lord said" or "And He revealed Himself," but he was careful, as the Guide <note>Maimonides</note> thought. If "The Word of the Lord" alone were sufficient, he would have used it; but he added a partition to the name and said "A Word"—which is one partition—"from before the Lord"—which is a second partition. This hints to us that this was a "created thing" <note>original: "davar nivra"</note> that came from before the Lord. 

Such was the tradition of the Great Elder <note>Onkelos</note> which stands in the secret of the Lord. In the school <note>Midrash</note> of Rabbi Simeon bar Yochai, it is explained that every prophet's prophecy is a source of blessing for Moses. In the intention of "facing God," that word refers to the blessing of the word "to be revealed upon him." And when it says "By the mouth of the Lord," he translates "By the Word of the Lord." There is no "death of the soul" there, for all of it was from Him through the **Word** <note>Memra</note>, for he included in the prophecy that which was not part of it before.

# Chapter 33 | The Part of the Purpose | Chapter 33 Page 89

And this "surrounding" is by way of a metaphor for the distance of His existence, blessed be He. Through this, His "countenance" was diminished <note>This refers to the concept of God limiting His perceived presence so that humans can endure the revelation.</note>, as our Rabbis of blessed memory said. The explanation of these words is that in his lack and the complexity of the matter regarding the truth of His existence, etc., he means to speak of the unique quality of the purpose of existence as "existence" itself. That is to say, in the explanation of "no man shall see Me," <note>original: "lo yir'uni"</note> it means that the truth of His existence, blessed be He, cannot be attained by any other existence besides Him. The interpreters of the Rabbi's <note>referring to Maimonides</note> secrets explained it thus. This was the view attributed to the Rabbi in his response, separate from the inquiry of the <term>Intelligences</term> <note>The "Separate Intelligences" were considered pure intellectual beings or angels in medieval philosophy.</note> when Moses intensified his request: "Please show me Your glory." <note>Exodus 33:18</note>

To attain everything in a response other than Him is attributed to Alexander <note>likely Alexander of Aphrodisias, a Greek commentator influential in medieval Jewish philosophy</note>, and thus the interpreters of his secrets explained. They went on to say, regarding <term>Onkelos</term> <note>The OCR reads "Anpelos," a common transcription error for Onkelos, the 2nd-century translator of the Torah into Aramaic.</note>, that he lacked the sense to know because Moses attained the existence of all the <term>Separate Intelligences</term> that are included. Thus did the interpreters of his secrets also explain.

One must investigate the Rabbi's view that Moses's request in the phrase "Please show me Your glory" was an attempt to attain the <term>Essence</term> <note>The "whatness" or true nature of a thing.</note>. If so, he achieved two levels of attainment: the essence of the first sphere and all the other spheres. This is necessary according to the Rabbi's view, for otherwise, he would not have attained a true grasp of His essence, blessed be He, while still failing to grasp the essence of the Separate Intelligences. And if the attainment attributed to the "back" <note>God telling Moses he can see His "back" but not His "face."</note> was an attainment, how was the attainment of the essence attributed to the "face" achieved? Rather, he certainly attained the essence of all the Intelligences according to the Rabbi's view. If so, what was the new attainment he received when God "passed all His goodness before his face," as it is said, "I will make all My goodness pass before you"? <note>Exodus 33:19</note> And why was he not satisfied with the knowledge he already had from the question of the "back," as He said, "And you shall see My back"?

It appears from the Rabbi's view in Chapter 54 <note>of the *Guide for the Perplexed*, Part 1</note> that the statement "I will make all My goodness pass before you" refers to the act of the first vision, where Moses said, "Please make Your ways known to me." Regarding the request "Please show me Your glory," he was told: "You cannot see My face." Generally, according to the Rabbi, they reveal the limit of what is possible for a human to attain. What Moses attained was something no human reached before him or after him—these are his words in that chapter. According to the Rabbi, Moses did not leave with his thoughts empty, nor was the Rabbi mistaken in this attainment of the included Intelligences. This is necessary because the attainment of all other existence is difficult for him, as in the statement "I will make all My goodness pass," as we explained from his words there. However, it is still difficult: if he had not perfectly attained the Intelligences, how could he have asked for something deeper, which was the knowledge of His essence, blessed be He? And if he had already attained the essence of the Intelligences, what was the purpose of the further vision granted to him?

<column-break/>

...according to the order of the Sages and the standing of the recipient. Everything Onkelos aimed for was according to what the Rabbi explained in his words. I have begun to understand that the views the Rabbi mentioned, which were not attributed to him, Onkelos has no part in them. If the Rabbi speaks according to his wisdom as a philosopher, he would say that at first, Moses only attained the "existence of an existent" by way of <term>demonstration</term> <note>A logical or mathematical proof.</note>. But this is far from the intellect—that Moses, peace be upon him, would only have such an attainment, which is not an attainment of the Truth according to his high level. Rather, they are true attainments of all reality, which he attained from everything God created.

What then was the lesson that was made known to him regarding the Patriarchs in the statement: "I appeared to Abraham, to Isaac, and to Jacob as <term>El Shaddai</term>, but by My name <term>YHVH</term> I was not known to them"? <note>Exodus 6:3</note> It is clear from this statement that the level of the Patriarchs was hidden before the request "Please show me Your glory." We cannot say that the Patriarchs did not attain the truth of existence at all, seeing only a distant "existence of an existent" by way of demonstration. For Abraham, who argued with the nations and proclaimed the firmest faith in God to them—if he had only attained the truth of His existence at first by way of demonstration, he would not have been more believing than anyone else with a firm faith. How could he proclaim to others to believe in Him if he did not possess a demonstration of His existence? How would they accept his faith from him? The truth is that Abraham is the "Head of Faith," who reflected in his soul, entered the covenant, and increased his belief. The Rabbi knows this, etc.

However, one can harmonize his words: at the vision of the Burning Bush, Moses attained a level higher than the attainment of the Patriarchs. If this is not mentioned elsewhere in the Rabbi's words, it is because he attained only His existence alone, through the intellect and not through names. When he said "Please show me Your glory," it was not about attaining the truth of the Essence—which was withheld from him—but rather about making known the truth of Existence according to the whole truth, as the Rabbi innovated. He wrote that when Moses asked "What is His name? What shall I say to them?" <note>Exodus 3:13</note>, it was so he could provide a definition. The Sages said that the righteous ask for "proofs." One person says God is "Holy," another says "Eternal," and so on. The secret of the vision is the "Necessary Existent" <note>A philosophical term for God: a being whose non-existence is impossible.</note>. This is what a demonstration leads to—that there is a Necessary Existent. When He informed him of the proofs that establish His existence for all their wise men, He said, "This is for you," and Moses understood what he was told and they accepted it; this is the meaning of "Hear, O Israel."

Thus, Moses would say through the power of the Name, and they would accept it. Among their intellectual judgments, what would be the proof of this "Necessary Existent"? From this, the Rabbi's view is clear: Moses did not initially attain the level mentioned in Chapter 54 until he needed to be informed of the proofs that establish His existence. In the Rabbi's view, these were intellectual demonstrations. Perhaps, in the Rabbi's view, these proofs of His existence were difficult for Moses to learn even from the mouth of the Almighty. This was taken from him without his knowledge, the existence from the <term>metaphysical</term> <note>The OCR reads "amopisitiko," likely a corruption of the Greek/Latin-derived term for metaphysics.</note>. If Moses's hand did not reach this, why did he ask "What is His name? What shall I say to them?" It appears he sought the intellectual demonstrations by which His existence is established. This was recorded in his soul. It appears that according to the Rabbi, the Patriarchs also possessed these. It must be harmonized that their words were intended to establish the faith with the greatest intellectual rigor; for if they did not have demonstrations in hand, but only hearsay of His existence, the people would not have accepted the faith from them.

# Chapter 34: The Section on the Ultimate Purpose

### Chapter 34

This surplus belongs to Him, may He be blessed, in another path from which that action proceeds, etc. For when nature is refined in its preparation, etc., it was left to the aspect of mercy, as it is said of Him, may He be blessed: "Merciful," etc. <note>Exodus 34:6</note>. And how could it enter the mind of the Rabbi <note>referring to Maimonides, often called "The Rabbi" in philosophical texts</note> to say such a thing? For it appears that the Master of the Prophets <note>Moses</note>, peace be upon him, did not consider in his prophecy, etc. And these "ways" of His—of blessed memory—are His attributes and His actions, to the point that He called them for us "the way of His governance." And these are the attributes. And the existence of these attributes is to say, regarding the intention of God, to say at the end of his words: ultimately, the purpose of human excellence is perfection within it <note>original: "hashelmut bo"</note>, as much as is possible. That is to say, by **imitating our actions to His actions**, etc. 

For it appears from all this that regarding Moses, peace be upon him, the state of divinity was not merely something that followed the vision shown to him, may He be blessed. Rather, he attained greatness—meaning, the attainment of these "ways"—because everything was within his power, even to achieve a Divine likeness through a complete vision. And the ultimate goal of wisdom was these attributes. And what would the Rabbi, of blessed memory, say? For behold, the enumeration of the "ways" and the actions are at the peak of perfection when they say "before Him as He walks" <note>likely a reference to walking in God's ways</note>. Its interpretation is the knowledge of them and the observation of Him, may He be blessed. And He, may He be blessed, did not show it even to Moses himself; rather, what was seen by him was according to his preparation in these "ways" which he grasped "after" Him <note>original: "acharayv," referring to Moses seeing God's "back" in Exodus 33:23</note>, may He be blessed. And he would walk in them to be like Him.

And in our contemplation of this, we find a world placed in His likeness, may He be blessed, through these words. For Abraham our father, peace be upon him, grasped His actions, may He be blessed, which are His "ways." And this is because he, peace be upon him, was perfected through his **ten trials** and through his prophesying a prophecy from Him. And through this, He, may He be blessed, was pleased with him and "the souls they made in Haran" <note>Genesis 12:5; traditionally interpreted as those Abraham and Sarah converted to monotheism</note> and all those who draw near to the truth. Abraham was a "prince of the sycamore house" <note>original: "minzar beit hashikmim," likely a metaphorical or local title for a leader</note> and he was a prince to your wives. And such is the opinion of our Sages, peace be upon them. And they received the Torah. 

And in our contemplation, there is the power to pass it to those who are sick in the land <note>perhaps referring to spiritual sickness or ignorance</note>, and the intent is not merely great mercy, but that creatures enter **under the wings of the Divine Presence** (Shekhinah). For this is what is explained in the "Secret of the Living One." He, peace be upon him, was the "Secret of the Intermediary Agent," a partner with the Master, may He be blessed, in creation. For he was within the worldy spheres. And there is that which points to the indwelling in the created being, for he, peace be upon him, would grasp "after" His actions, may He be blessed, which are the Forces. For he was distant in his understanding of them. 

Also, when he contemplated, he, peace be upon him, was comforted by the action found from Him. For he gave a dwelling to every living thing in the world, and he was prepared to host, bringing them into his house, **feeding them and giving them drink**. And regarding Moses, it says that the refinement of his understanding, which is nicknamed "the light," was that he, peace be upon him, grasped from "after" His actions, may He be blessed, as explained in the Midrash of Rabbi Hanania ben Hakanah, peace be upon him. And he further said of the rest who came: he provided his bread and his wine to all the people of the world, and he would host them and speak to their hearts: "Whom do you worship? Worship the Lord, the God of heaven and earth!" And he would preach to them until they returned to Him. For regarding this it is said of him: "And he kept My charge" <note>Genesis 26:5</note>. And it is known that all this was "walking with God" in the way of action and providence.

And truly, it said he is "Slow to Anger" <term>Erekh Apayim (slow to anger): one of the thirteen attributes of mercy</term> in the statement concerning him, when Abraham said to Lot: "Please let there be no strife... for we are men who are brothers. Is not the whole land before you?" <note>Genesis 13:8-9</note>. And "Kindness" <term>Chesed: the attribute of loving-kindness</term>... and how greatly he was perfected in the Name from his beginning, to return to the sun <note>unclear: possibly "to return to the source"</note>... and as seen specifically in the **War of the Kings**, when they rebelled... for his mercy was in the dwelling, and his whole intent was directed toward Abraham because he was lifting the banner of faith of the King of the World, and making His faith special. And they provoked him in this, and they "took Lot and his possessions, the son of Abraham's brother" <note>Genesis 14:12</note>. And he, peace be upon him, raised his hand against them to erase their memory. And he counted one of them, his refinement and his hand. And this was not for the sake of gaining silver or for social leadership and silver, but rather because of his reception from "God Most High, Creator of heaven and earth." For those were rebels who spread out against Him... the way of perfection was in the law of Providence, which satisfies the perfection that is explained. There is a refinement of external understanding which is preserved from all this, for Abraham our father, peace be upon him, grasped "after" His actions and His ways, may He be blessed. And we have already revealed to you that His saying "Make Your ways known to me" <note>Exodus 33:13</note> is that He should make him know the secret of the Chosen One.

<meta>catchword: entering</meta>

<column-break/>

And His actions for each one individually. For those who bestow and those promised their reward change based on whether they are natural to him or whether they proceed from God as actions that receive. And so, the knowledge of the "End" <term>Takhlit: the ultimate purpose or goal</term>, ultimately, for the things that bestow will be clarified from their own side... and it is more publicized before the Face... their essences are more than their existence, the first being upon... And there is no doubt that their difference is known from their own side alone to all knowledge in a different way, knowing them from the aspect that they are the **actions of God and His ways**. And from the noble purpose that one should be perfect in rational matters as is fitting.

This is the Guide... and for this, one must believe that before the **Standing of the Chosen One** <note>the Revelation at Sinai</note>, he was perfect in the knowledge of all existing things from all their aspects, which are the ways of God and His actions. If it were not so, how could he have ascended to the level of prophecy? Moreover, the Voice is accepted in the wisdom of the **Book of Creation** (*Sefer Yetzirah*) <note>an ancient Jewish mystical/cosmological text</note>... because it is a special book for knowing the secrets of existing things from the aspect that they are the ways of God and His actions over the worlds. And furthermore, this is a tool that would exist after the Holy Standing. 

And there is no doubt that the reception <note>Kabbalah/tradition</note> was in the standing of Moses in his level, and like the level of his prophecy, higher than all who preceded him and all the prophets who lacked his degree of prophecy. And he was the one who understood on that day... which included what was between him and them in prophecy. And as for the standing of the Holy Voice, it was the end of his perfection at his preparation... and what this includes in general was not added to him afterward—anything in the level of prophecy or the degree of prophecy to which he ascended then. And who is forced to the matter of the Torah which was written by his hand? For he was already perfected before the existence of the Awesome Voice in the wisdom of wisdom, at the ultimate hiddenness. For from there is the "Tablets of the Chosen One," every foundation built of sanctified craftsmanship. 

And in such as this, following God... and there are those who will understand it from him. And every single day, continually from there, it is received in the House of Study of the Lord, yearning to understand himself toward prophecy until the day of his death. The level and the double perfection, the day of the **Giving of the Torah**, because all his faith and the revelation of our degree in truth and in prophecy, more than anyone who preceded us or those who come after us, was an adjustment... for the excellence of the Torah which was written by his hand. 

Therefore, the reward that comes in comfort in all kinds of worlds preceded the reception of the Torah. And because the nature of existing things and their order is fixed in the soul... he took there things found from the **philosophers**. But for us, the believers, because the book that was decreed in their mouths—and there is no other vanity in His wisdom for all their understanding—it made known to him that they inform of them... 

Let us say that the intellect of Moses, in the name of the Divine Spirit that was attached to his understanding, could grasp more than the intellect of all the philosophers combined. And this gate is small in your eyes, the grasp of Moses, compared to what one must hold: that he was a recipient in all this from the standing of his father, peace be upon him, who was a recipient from Jacob our father, peace be upon him, and also from those after him who preceded him in the level of prophecy by priority of time. 

Furthermore, one must know and believe that the Divine Abstract Being would not appear to the perfect man to bring him "news" unless he had already grasped Him in all this—that is, in the grasp of the nature of existing things and the order of the soul's reception and their knowledge from every aspect of God's ways and His actions... And let this be the final word: that the day of the soul's law and its yearning is to be existentially eternal. For how could it enter the Will of the Perfect One [God] to act not according to the established order? And how could one grasp the Supreme Spiritual Reception if he has not yet been perfected in grasping the natural and the sensory, which are the boundaries of the limited and its heads? And all this is said in the nickname "Divine." 

And we say that it was for the sake of His Glory's will, may He be blessed, that He spoke from the "Face" to a high level—it is much more. Furthermore, consider returning to the opinion of the Rabbi [Maimonides], of blessed memory, in his saying that the statement "Make Your ways known to me" <note>Exodus 33:13</note> is that He should make him know the particulars. And he said that the things through which there is knowledge of them and making them known are the **actions proceeding from Him**, may He be blessed, etc. For these are like the actions proceeding from Him, may He be blessed, at the ultimate purpose in the nickname of these, etc. Behold, it has already been clarified that the things and the attributes which are the actions proceeding from Him, may He be blessed, in the world... which He intended in the action of His actions...

<meta>This page continues the discussion from the previous section regarding the distinction between the knowledge of God attained by the Patriarchs versus that of Moses. It specifically engages with the philosophy of Maimonides (referred to as "the Rabbi") concerning how the "Truths" of God are understood through His actions and attributes rather than His essence.</meta>

# Chapter 21: The Section on the Ultimate Purpose — Chapter 22

Regarding him <note>Moses</note>, peace be upon him, there was no permanence in the languages, nor was it as he thought in the excess of our knowledge through the names, where he said, "And I appeared... but by My name, the Lord, I was not known to them" <note>Exodus 6:3</note>. We have read this as a conclusion of the law, just as "I was known to you" and not to all of them as a specific property like the masculine. It follows the path of the ultimate purpose, like the rank of the specific property, and not like the whole of the purpose of his speech, according to a simple limit that the Patriarchs did not attain and which was not revealed to the prophets among them, peace be upon them. How, then, could he rise to the rank of the proper order?

But there are points concerning them, for through their intellect they attained the existence of God as it was before the division of the work. And in the work of "He who exists," they attained it in a way that was easier and more complex for the vision of the story, by way of **intellectual demonstration** <term>mofet sichli: a logical proof based on reason rather than tradition</term> and intellectual precision. For the two understandings are like the intellect which is between the vital intellect and the partial intellect. And also the Patriarchs, peace be upon them, attained the rank of simple connection—the existence of God—in a way that was easier and more complex than the way of intellectual demonstration. And the difference between them was like the object of the intellect, which is at the rank of the connection; that is to say, like the intellect of the rank of the name according to the philosophical way.

And until this point, the Rabbi <note>Maimonides</note>, of blessed memory, must admit according to his demonstration and his principle and his premise in our holy Torah, which comes from the receivers of wisdom and the order of the great ones of the generation in its foundation from Jacob's heritage, peace be upon him. And were it not that the cup of time gives but a little due to the burden of the world upon the understanding, the window of possibilities and the drawing near of the circles of God's power <note>original: "sevivah"</note> would be according to their demonstrations and the proof accepted from Him. And because the holy vision of the Lord would tarry for them, he rebuked them for their strength, like the people of Egypt. And as he entered this, he [Moses] strengthened himself, peace be upon him, in his words and said to them: "Is it not from the goodness of your faces that you are prepared?" and he said, "Do not stand still from the strength of the tradition." That is to say, they lacked the power to prove this to them. And there is no doubt that the elders of Israel and their leaders were holding fast and receiving and being comforted by his words, for the entire tribe of Levi held fast to the tradition of wisdom, peace be upon them, and they studied their Torah as is known from the tradition of our Sages of blessed memory, for whom there is no lack of wisdom, time, or prayer.

And furthermore, behold it is written: "And the children of Israel groaned because of the labor, and they cried out, and their cry for help rose up to God because of the labor" <note>Exodus 2:23</note>. It appears that all the people previously believed in His existence and His powers, for if not so, how could they cry out and pray before the Holy One, blessed be He, from their distresses and their truths? And if they were in doubt of His existence, how could it say, "and their cry rose up to God," etc.? But the truth is that he said "the children of the prophet" <note>referring to the Israelites as heirs to the Patriarchs</note> to the people, for they were the recipients of the tradition that through repentance and the merit of their fathers, their inheritance would be settled. And there were those among them who attained His existence, but the premise was through demonstration, while all the rest of the people were through tradition. And this is what is said according to the opinion of the Rabbi <note>Maimonides</note>, that we have eaten a great thing, praising those powers, may He be blessed, as attaining the ultimate purpose.

With what you said regarding the revelation, that signs and powers are for all His glory, the descent and the order, and the early sages of Israel were not in intellectual agreement according to their vision of them, according to their wisdom which could annihilate them, so that they would not be shifted like a proper demonstration, which is the praised and exalted demonstration without measure. And after the time of their dependence on them in the printing and the greatness of the generation of the Torah, those were the strong demonstrations that publicized everything similar to Him; it is impossible for Him to be called to those who doubt Him and to all of them together.

Furthermore, the Rabbi of blessed memory said: "The general rule of the commandments, and this which is at the beginning of our laws, is after Him, may He be blessed." And that the majority of them are in the attainment of the knowledge of Him, as He said: "Make me know, I pray Thee, Thy ways" <note>Exodus 33:13</note>. And were it not for more than Him being known through His attributes, for in the compound material and its precision, etc. And he passed over the first request, which was "Make me know, I pray Thee, Thy ways," and it was said to him: "I will make all My goodness pass before thy face" <note>Exodus 33:19</note>, etc. Consider His saying "all My goodness," for then He hinted at the understanding of Him in His entire existence, which is said of them: "And God saw everything that He had made, and behold, it was very good" <note>Genesis 1:31</note>. That is to say, in showing them the simplicity of their nature and their order there in wisdom, and he knew how they entered into Him, both in general and in particular. And to this the prophet hinted: "In all My house he is faithful" <note>Numbers 12:7</note>, meaning that he is like an agent acting upon it, as it is written.

<column-break/>

**Truths**, for the living opinions that are vital truths will not be sustained if the attainment of the actions—which are the Divine things known from all—and the proofs for the matter that depends on our attaining them are His actions, may He be blessed. They were as a single matter, He made known His actions after Him. He said of them: "the knowledge of them," and the way of their covering is correct. Behold, it has already been clarified that the things in which there is knowledge of them, and which made them known, are the actions proceeding from Him, may He be blessed. And the sages call them **attributes** <term>middot: divine characteristics or ways of acting in the world</term>, and they taught the Thirteen Attributes, etc.

Furthermore, he said: "However, the verse mentions these Thirteen Attributes, and even though the glory attained by his attainment—meaning all His actions—for these actions that proceed from Him, may He be blessed, according to the law of the ignorance of human beings and their attainment, besides their being truths..." The intention of our prayer is the end of the struggle, and your saying "so that I may find favor in Your eyes" and "see that this nation is Your people," whom I need to bring into the actions; therefore, seek in the way of My actions in your preparation.

And behold, the opinion of the Rabbi in all this is as an object of the intellect in the scale of reason, and he found it so. For he already said in the chapters on Prophecy that whoever prepares himself for prophecy must be perfect in wisdom and in attributes. And this is what he said in Chapter 33: "However, the beauty and the perfection of prophecy, and the perfection in attributes and in speech, are necessary in every way." From this he said, "Prophecy only rests upon one who is wise, strong, and wealthy" <note>A famous Talmudic dictum interpreted philosophically by Maimonides</note>, and we have already explained this in the Commentary on the Mishnah and in the *Great Source* <note>Mishneh Torah</note>, etc. And it is known from the words of the Rabbi in the chapters that his intention regarding "wisdom" that he was able to possess was the **science of astronomy** <term>chokhmat ha-techunah: the study of the celestial spheres and their order</term> and intellectual permanence.

And if so, one must ask according to the Rabbi's opinion: if the Master of the Prophets <note>Moses</note>, peace be upon him, who was chosen for wisdom according to his holy disciples—was his wisdom and his attainment and the wisdom of the things proceeding from him not the wisdom of demonstration and complexity? If so, it is impossible to say it was of another kind, for according to the Rabbi, the wisdom of demonstrating Him, may He be blessed, is through the science of existence. If so, since the proof and the wisdom of demonstration is the negation of everything that is impossible for the human intellect to attain in the wisdom of existents and their distance, for all who came after him from among those who philosophized from his wisdom and from his mouth... and thus all who established him from the Sephardic philosophers <note>referring to the Spanish-Jewish philosophical tradition</note>. And all who came after him did not cease from coming and being within the matter of my book, to descend to the ultimate depth of his mind regarding the literal meaning. And from these in the language, they only brought up what a prophet brings up at the head of his mouth.

And it is impossible that there should be a parable for the matter according to the law of the visionary above their vital intake. And this and that were for him when he understood the nature of existence and the order written regarding God and His goodness, may He be blessed, to them; if so, in general and in particular. For then it is impossible, and the praise of the external intellect of man is not so. Therefore, Moses had to ask, "Make me know, I pray Thee, Thy ways." And if this were impossible by the law of the external intellect, He would have answered him without doubt. Also, Moses, peace be upon him, would not have asked this. And it is known that the attainment of those things proceeds from the knowledge of God and His order. And whoever is ignorant of them, his ignorance is because He is not known except through His actions.

And it is found, if so, that both this one and that one did not know God, for behold Moses, peace be upon him, said: "Make me know, I pray Thee, Thy ways," and your saying indicates that He, may He be blessed, is known after Him, for through knowing the ways we know Him, as the Rabbi said in Chapter 37. And it will be clarified from his words that whoever does not know the nature of existing things and their order, etc., does not yet know the wisdom of existents, which is the ultimate purpose of the wisdom of the intellect and the knowledge of the All, may He be blessed. And if so, what was the wisdom of his preparation when he said "Prophecy only rests upon a wise man," etc.? We all know that one who does not know the ultimate purpose cannot be designated for a greatness as high as the rank of prophecy, even if he be wise in the science of existents. And one still needs the continuity of his fellows in them. And if so, how did Moses rise to the greatest rank of prophecy when he, peace be upon him, was not hidden in wisdom? And he said in the Torah by his hand: "all of Israel arrived at the rank of prophecy" in our preparation and in his action. He spoke clearly so that the receiver would be perfect in the ultimate purpose of attributes, in wisdom and in prophecy. And the defective wisdom is at the end of the doubt in the separate [intellects]. And this is what is doubted in this language, and it is that Moses knew all existing things from their beginning to their end, but he did not know them in every aspect—only them **and His essence**.

<summary>This page explores the philosophical tension between knowing God through tradition versus intellectual demonstration, focusing on Maimonides' view that God is known only through His actions (the 13 Attributes). It argues that Moses attained a unique level of wisdom by understanding the "order of existence," which is the prerequisite for the highest form of prophecy.</summary>

<meta>This page continues the exploration of the "Ultimate Purpose" (Tachlit), transitioning from the intellectual attainments of the Patriarchs to the unique prophetic status of Moses at the Burning Bush. It utilizes Midrashic interpretations to explain why Moses chose the desert and the symbolic meaning of the "Mountain of God" (Horeb).</meta>

# Chapter 34: The Section on the Ultimate Purpose — Chapter 34

And the Sages said: "Change, change, change" <note>This likely refers to a cycle of spiritual transformation or the changing nature of existence</note> regarding the recognition of the kindness that permeates all deeds. He accepted these transformations upon himself and performed them for all the powers of the world. So too for Isaac and Jacob, whose **kindness** followed his path; they returned and merited the **crowns** <note>original: "כתמים" likely a transcription of "כתרים" (crowns), referring to spiritual attainments</note> to bequeath from them that perfection. They accepted their transformations upon themselves in completeness and removed their merit from the "accusers" <term>tachmanim: those who calculate or withhold</term>. Because they [the Israelites] had abandoned the ways of their fathers and rejoiced in the idols of Egypt and busied themselves with them, and their "arms were weakened" <note>an idiom for losing spiritual strength</note>, I turned toward them to look upon my people and to contemplate my words. He turned his attention back in repentance and understanding, lacking nothing to cause him to rejoice and be answered.

And as the Midrash states: "And he led the flock to the backside of the desert" <note>Exodus 3:1</note>. Rabbi Yosi says: From the day Moses was chosen, the Holy Spirit never departed from him. He saw through the Holy Spirit that this specific desert was holy and prepared to receive the "rest of heaven" upon it. What did he do? He turned the flock "behind the desert" in every sense—not like a desert of the plain, but so they could enter into it. Rather, he "turned behind the desert" and came to the Mountain of God alone.

Rabbi Yehuda said: This is comparable to one who receives a clear explanation; anyone who dies for it starts the work freely. Thus Moses, called "the humble man," bore the burden with one another... <note>original: "סה"ר" - likely an abbreviation for a secret or a specific mystical source</note> "And he came to the Mountain of God, to Horeb." After he bore the burden, the "horses" were storming at the beginning with one another, and that day he was providing **kindness** to the light of Moses. Since Moses saw it, he entered into it and stood at the gate. This teaches that they [the divine forces] eventually agreed with one another.

Rabbi Yosi said: Moses knew that this mountain was the Mountain of God, as it is written: "And he came to the Mountain of God." What did Moses see on that mountain? He saw birds that were **spreading** <note>original: "פירמיס," likely a corruption of "פורשים"</note> and extending their wings above, but not entering it. The Rabbi said: He saw the spreading of wings, and the wings of Moses [were] at Moses' feet... he entered alone, as it is said: "For Moses, peace be upon him, was prepared for prophecy from the foundation of the chosen treasure." This is stirred by the phrase "And she saw that he was good" <note>Exodus 2:2, referring to Moses' birth</note>. This is the secret of what is written: "All the house..." and "after her..." which teaches that her merit was distant.

And they said further: "Behind the desert" and not "in the desert." They said that they should enter into it, etc. This is a hint to Moses that Israel is called "Holy to the Lord" <note>Jeremiah 2:3</note>, prepared to receive the Torah in the morning and to be humbled in soul and to be poor, as it is said "with cattle and morning," and "He desired," etc. And it says "it was beloved to the one who receives it clearly," etc. And it says "they were close," etc. And that day he was "providing," etc. It is known from the way of existence that this was a hint to the **Final Heh** <note>The last letter of the Divine Name YHWH, representing the Shekhinah or the physical manifestation of God's presence</note> and the end, as it is said of them: "The Mountain of God, Horeb" — the "Sword of the Lord" <note>A play on words between Horeb and Cherev (sword)</note>. The "Mountain of God" is written without a connecting phrase, and the end is connected to "And an angel of the Lord appeared to him in a flame of fire."

For this reason, the mountain was "providing" <note>drawn toward him</note>, for even more than Moses wanted to cling to it, the mountain wanted to be drawn after him and to cling to him, for its desire was toward him. This is like the matter of "Draw me, let us run after you" <note>Song of Songs 1:4</note>, for he is here called a "man of God," a general term for his longing and standing. And their saying "he saw birds that were spreading," etc., and "not entering," etc., "spreading and building from there and their wings were at Moses' feet" — this hints at the nations who do not enter into the "flesh of the covenant" and did not receive the Torah.

The mountain is "Horeb," and here we find elsewhere in the Midrash: "Mount Sinai, for fear descended from it to the nations." From the Holy One, blessed be He, it is a praise, but in the future, He will destroy them and they will not consume it, because they did not want to merit the **Crown**. In the future, they will fall at the feet of Moses.

Furthermore, in the Midrash: "And an angel of the Lord appeared to him in a flame of fire." What is the reason for "a flame of fire"? To say in a "vision" <note>original: "בכיסון," perhaps a variant of "חזיון"</note>... Rabbi Yehuda said: In "strengths," not like Moses. For whoever draws near to fire is usually harmed, but Moses drew near to the fire and was not harmed, as it is written: "And Moses drew near to the thick cloud where God was" <note>Exodus 20:18</note>.

Rabbi Abba said: It is necessary to look into the words of the Sages regarding what is written "from heaven" and "birds." From where do we see this? ... Rather, these are hints from the Creator to him. Rabbi Yehuda said: To ask Moses... for he stayed in ten ranks. Behold, it is written: "In all my house he is faithful" <note>Numbers 12:7</note>, and it does not say "in My house," but "in **all** My house."

<column-break/>

And he continued. By way of hint: the thought rose before Him that their desire awakened **Repentance** <term>Teshuvah</term>, and it stopped. The power of awakening was from afar until the end, and God did not withhold their portion. This is the "hidden world" <note>original: "העלם הגנוז," referring to the concealed realms of the Godhead</note>, for there the supreme Name, as it were, strengthened Isaac and Jacob and the children of Israel, for so they did. The "seed of God" brought them close to the knowledge of the word, corresponding to the "Accidental Attribute" <note>likely referring to the world of phenomena</note> and the **Unity** <term>Yichud</term> of these. The luck of the matter is the awakening of Repentance and the merit of the Patriarchs above and below. Kindness, which is bestowed in His honor, will be forgiven.

This is the hiddenness of everything: for the awakening of perfection and Unity rises from below through the power of Unity above. The Unity above was a desire and a completion below from their "Might" <term>Gevurah</term>. And regarding the "luck" above... then it is free to hide this below. This is the secret of "And it was known."

And as in the Midrash: A parable of a king who had a basket <note>original: "קפה," likely "קופה"</note> and produced from it several tools and hid them. Their knowledge was not increased, and his strength rested upon them and he taught them... so they will be wise from what they understood and lived until they were comforted and returned to their sins. The Merciful One had mercy on them as at the beginning... and it was known, etc.

This is the secret of "Because of your transgressions your mother was sent away" <note>Isaiah 50:1</note>. It points to the "fury of the voice" and the luck of the awakening, God forbid, to awaken them to the path, for "the teacher is good." He is perplexed as well as the "Cantor" <note>original: "חזן"</note>... and this is the voice of the end. And their produce is with them—"fruits"—for they are merits below and above. They all finished being servants to Him in soul and spirit, by their own will, like the sense of "The children of Israel said from the crossing."

Behold, the matter is to make known that trust clings to the "Saving King," who is great enough to reward their souls and revive them from their exile, and to save their scattered parts, to give them a straight path to perform the service of **Kindness**. Its splendor shall be the essence within it, along with the humility of the body and the soul. And your "thinking" <note>original: "חסככם," perhaps "your savings" or "your restraint"</note> is like His mercies and His kindness. He wanted the stature to rise and be blotted out from their ascent. The wicked man is wicked... and they shall be written "behind the desert" until all the tribes are finished... "And an angel of the Lord appeared." Were it not for the "flame," it would not be from within the bush. This is a hint to the receiving of the **Crown** <term>Atarah</term> corresponding to the movement of the assembly.

And the Sages hinted: regarding the wicked, they will eat strength... and this restraint is a hint to Israel... the "Crown." And it was not said "because he will believe" every curse and excess... but all this is the restraint and our life, like the matter of "But you who cling to the Lord your God are all alive today" <note>Deuteronomy 4:4</note>. Clinging <term>Dveikut</term> depends on this... it is not necessary to say he will forgive and not disqualify you, but he will give them "existence" <term>kiyuum</term>, and He is our life today.

This refers to the "Stature" that rises... and this existence is a great distance to see... why is the "throne" <note>original: "הכסה"</note> not fit or snatched? For does it not consume and burn from the world? ... To hint that God distanced the Name... for He is the one who sustains and maintains the stature... and will not be disqualified while they live for the sake of the **Crown** and its commandments. For this, he has wisdom and existence. We have already informed you how many times: that the Holy One, blessed be He, created the Crown.

"And He called to him from the midst of the bush" — for he who maintains the Torah, the Divine Presence <term>Shekhinah</term> is with him, and God is within him to sustain him. Do not read it as "to him" <note>original: "אליו"</note> but "upon him" <note>original: "עליו"</note>... and for the merit of the end of existence, one must open the "Married Crowns" to the power of Understanding <term>Binah</term> to attain this existence. As at the beginning: at the beginning one must establish the body and cleanse it from evil deeds and strive to adorn one's soul and awaken Repentance, raising up thoughts that were stuck in the "mire" of sins. He shall not disqualify the "distorted" until their merits are paved. For he who establishes **Kindness** takes it upon himself to attain it and see the "Holy of Holies." For this, one needs "seventy prayers" for the sins that dull and close the heart.

# Chapter 33: The Section on the Ultimate Purpose — Chapter 33

Those who are separated from the "dreams of their wrath" <note>likely referring to worldly delusions or physical impulses</note> seek to see His Glory—that supreme level included in the outcomes of the "solar" <note>metaphorical for the manifest/physical world</note> degrees, which are blended together. He sought to awaken the spiritual nature of the "back" <note>original: "אחוריים" (achorayim), referring to God's effects or the physical world</note> and the spiritual essence of the "face" <note>original: "פנים" (panim), referring to God's true essence</note>. It is said: "I will make all My goodness pass before you" <note>Exodus 33:19</note>, for while I go before you, you cannot perceive My interior, but only the back. His request was to walk with Him to perceive the spiritual "face" in the wake of the mercy shown to the people. Behold, in Your speaking with us, etc. And it is necessary to decide on this knowledge: what was the understanding that Moses achieved in the statement "And you shall see My back" <note>Exodus 33:23</note>? And also regarding the mention of the Name, it is said in the statement: "I will be gracious to whom I will be gracious." And behold, they admit by necessity that if there were not a "Voice" of the Essential Name for the Creator, the matter of the congregation would prove it; just as there is holiness in the Name, so there is power in it, even in His thoughts as written—for it is not for the profane.

And the attributes through which He turned His "face" to him, and the matters where it says the **Divine Presence** <term>Shekhinah: the indwelling presence of God in the world</term> dwelt in His essence as it passed before him. He said: "Inform me of the judgment of the world," even though he was refined in his qualities. This is the "opening" toward His kingdom, and this is "incense" <note>possibly a metaphor for prayer or spiritual elevation</note> to say "by my spirit." Were not all the chosen ones shown mercy? Behold, this statement shows that in the Torah, the "Voice" is the supreme "Nest" <note>a mystical term for a source or dwelling</note>, the crown uniquely described by the title of "Glory." If so, what was his plea when he said, "Show me Your glory"? According to their view, the agreement was that it was withheld from him when He said, "You cannot see My face." Yet, the "Voice" <note>the prophetic perception</note> had already achieved that understanding previously. Furthermore, it is difficult according to their view: if the attainment of "Show me now Your glory" was regarding something external to the fifth perception <note>likely referring to the five senses or levels of the soul</note>, why does it say "And the glory of the Lord shall be seen"? And "this one cannot see My face, for man shall not see Me [and live]"? He only received "the face" by tradition, as it was said to him, "they shall not see," and "My face shall not be seen." All these verses are necessitated by these opinions because they wish to refine in their minds things that the intellect must refine beyond any doubt. Therefore, I marvel at the work of the service of the "Voice" and at the explanation of the "Clear Vision," which is the Vision of the Glory, to send a window of metaphors. They said that this is a type of oil and answers for the time of the world upon him and his lack, in the statement "Show me now Your ways." And in the delay of "Show me now Your glory," there are answers to judge the world according to the tradition received with the help of the Teacher of the world forever.

## Chapter 34

"And it came to pass in the course of those many days, that the king of Egypt died; and the children of Israel sighed by reason of the bondage, and they cried" <note>Exodus 2:23</note>. This cry coincided with the death of the king because it is the way of kings upon their death to declare **amnesty** <note>original: "דרור" (deror), meaning freedom or release</note> and to forgive taxes and burdens. Also, the new king who reigns usually says to the prisoners: "Go forth and be free," and they return to their former ways. For they expected the tribes would be granted freedom; they hoped that their salvation would come through the wisdom of the "nobles of the workers," for their existence was established and not taken away. But when a new king arose over both of them, and the matter was evil for them, they were not awakened to the kingdom and no decrees were made. The Sages explained these things: that the "Voice of Jacob" <note>symbolizing prayer</note> breaks through and ascends, and it has the power to awaken the upper realms. As in the matter: "Awake, why do you sleep, O Lord? Arise, do not cast us off forever. Why do You hide Your face?" <note>Psalm 44:24-25</note>. For the dwellings of the House of Jacob had ceased because He had abandoned them, and Egypt was destroyed because of him, yet not his labor. "And the children of Israel sighed by reason of the bondage"—he means to say that through the labor, the kings made the children of Israel heavy, as it is said. From this, do not flee, for it is better for them to serve the Lord than to labor in submission to Egypt. And then "their cry came up to God by reason of the bondage"—the labor of the fruit of proper service. He repeated this to say that by their remembrance and their speech, it was a proof for the servants. Also, grace and favor were set upon them to save them in the final wrath, which they did not admit was to their merit. He called out in His name to him, to return and destroy all who rose against him, and to save His servant who is dedicated to His name. For withholding this is like raising a hand against the King and touching the apple of His eye. As in the matter: "Not unto us, O Lord, not unto us, but unto Your name give glory" <note>Psalm 115:1</note>. And they said: "Anyone who enslaves those below, it is as if he enslaves the One above."

## Chapter 33

It is known in the histories that the "Path of the Perfect" is his way, as led in Chapter 24. This name is an inheritance in love until the ultimate perfection. It will be clarified, then, that he even knew how to advance following the root of his path and in their reversal. If so, to judge by these examinations, the deed is great; and if the intention is deeper regarding His kingdom, after all the examinations, even the law of the Torah is to inherit through the knowledge of His Torah and His ways. And he did not place "destruction" <note>original: "קטב" (ketev), often meaning a demonic force or destruction</note> there. He did not remember the aforementioned, for I joined with it when the salvation of my kingdom spread over him. Regarding the choices, we did not diminish nor know until he sent: "Show me now Your ways and Your goodness." All the more so because the Torah is according to the will of all the choices, supreme in all the acts of our deeds. His love was established in them with the creatures to fulfill "and you shall walk in His ways" <note>Deuteronomy 28:9</note>. This was before He revealed to him the first level of the degree of intention. He said: "In our distress, He is from us." Also, what is written: "And he took the Cushite captive," etc., and he returns to the wicked—why is the wicked man evil? Because he looked at the toil and was able. Also, what is written: "And the shepherds came and drove them away; but Moses stood up and helped them, and watered their flock" <note>Exodus 2:17</note>.

Behold, he will have pity on all his [people], and the souls of our Sages will add goodness in exchange for acquiring his exalted ways, because he is exalted in the "Secret of the Degrees." All of it is in the cycles and completions, they are led with **Kindness** <term>Chesed: divine grace or loving-kindness</term> according to the opinion of the Rabbi <note>likely Maimonides or another major commentator</note>. And if he did not know, even this was established, and he turned with them among the creatures. And his way would be that the intention in His kingdom was according to what he thought... and the "Brilliance" <note>original: "אלעער" likely "הזוהר" (Zohar) or "הארה" (illumination)</note> indicates the known assistance in His Torah, etc. They returned to "That I may find grace in Your eyes," which indicates the assistance in His creator, etc. God knew that he did not profane, for He knows Himself. They returned to the known, as in our Chapter 24, and afterwards in this chapter [33] and in Chapter 60 of our book. The author of the *Book of Principles* <term>Sefer Ha-Ikkarim: a 15th-century work of Jewish philosophy by Joseph Albo</term> in Chapter 3 of the third part of his book wrote about this and said that this was written only as a "remainder" to the one who knows the advantage of the level over the one who does not know it. Aside from this, my opinion and your plea indicate the knowledge of His existence, may He be blessed, and he made it known. And it is necessary that if so, behold, what I have written in the "Afterward" of "Show me now Your glory" and what he thought in his saying "You cannot see My face."

The end of the matter: in every part of them, there are repetitions. And behold, before us is what we have written by his hand... wisdom is hidden in the verses, also not intended for the "window of intention" in our histories. And our answers are upon him. They said that they were... a "veil" <note>original: "מסך" (masach)</note> over "Show me now Your glory" regarding the bitterness of the pieces. Everything is according to the law of the "Productive Torah" which includes the one who looks at the first without a report. For the "Wrath" of that level was not achieved through the perception of the "Dismissal," for the inclusive decree—the "Voice"—to their knowledge, is in its placement. And it is redundant in level... from being caused by the "First Cause" without the five. And since it is inclusive in its forms from the "Hidden," it was a partner with the "Dismissal" like a type of its inclusive portions, which is the choice of the intellect and absolute simplicity in the inheritance. If so, this level is composed of two simple spiritual matters, supreme above all the "chosen levels." This matter of **Kindness** is its being included in its portions and from the "Hidden." And its opposite belongs to it, shared with them in kind and expertise. These two matters are intended in the Torah as "Face" and "Back." And regarding this matter, it is possible to say of it "For man shall not see Me and live." But regarding the examination of the levels intended by the "Back"—indeed, the attainment of the "Face"—He said to him: "Take the intention of the one who perceives the Name in recognition." And this, according to their opinion, is the intention of "And you shall see My back, but My face shall not be seen." And according to their opinion, this does not reach to judge the metaphors according to all its inclusive portions.

# Chapter 34: The Section on the Ultimate Purpose — Chapter 34

A holy place and a stumbling block for all the people of the world, and that which is prepared for shame and for the cessation. 
Why does the "Striker" <note>Referring to God acting through the attribute of strict justice</note> not bring good tidings, comfort, show grace, and have mercy? For the Lord is the source of life-giving moisture. 
The Merciful One's compassion is with these, and in the "spreading out" <note>term: pashitut; the Kabbalistic concept of Divine simplicity where God's essence is undifferentiated</note> it is with the ultimate simplicity. With this, 
His power is within these compositions, and He does not change or multiply within them. And he calls these 
"Elohim," which is the Attribute of Judgment <note>original: middat ha-din</note>, coming from the word for "bitterness," to hint that it is a necessity for the world to discipline 
the transgressors and to complete the judgment upon the wicked. Because of this, everything is obligated to Him, for "Elohim" 
is within it and is its preservation, for He is the life of all the transcendent worlds. And He said to the "inner part," 
for this secret is held within the High Thought <note>term: machshavah elyonah; the highest level of Divine consciousness in Kabbalah</note>, which is outside of this learned 
measure. For this reason, it is not called "where" <note>original: ayah</note>, for it is written: **"the eye of the hawk has not seen it"** <note>Job 28:7</note>, and it is called 
a "penalty" <note>unclear reading</note> before everything, because it was beyond the comprehension of Moses, our teacher (peace be upon him), for 
he did not grasp the essence of that "Thought." And from his blessing, he shall teach us regarding the bonds of the Kingdom <note>original: malchut</note>, 
the secret of the Kingdom of the House of David. And for this reason, he said "Woe to my God," and he said: **"Who am I, and what is my house, that You have brought me thus far?"** <note>2 Samuel 7:18</note> for he merited the attribute of Holiness. And behold, he responded regarding 
his rectifications to the Merciful One, and the Merciful One [answered] regarding his teaching: "Why does the Striker not bring good tidings?" 
He answered him, as if to say: **"Put off your shoes from your feet"** <note>Exodus 3:5</note>, meaning that the time has not yet 
arrived until all the obstacles are finished—the obstacles that prevent the transition because of the weight 
of sins and transgressions which act as a screen and hide the Radiant Glory <note>original: ha-kavod ha-me'irah</note> 
and block the Gates of Mercy. And as they receive the revealed "houses" and the "chariots," their

# Chapter 35: The Section on the Ultimate Purpose — Chapter 35

Distinguished, as he was until now, and as he was designated by the phrase, **"and I have known you by name."** <note>Exodus 33:17</note> Furthermore, the matter of the request that he asked, saying: **"And show me favor,"** <note>Hebrew: *v'chanantani*; Exodus 33:19</note> and **"be gracious to me,"** they assisted him as well. All of this is included in the statement: **"and I have known you by name."** As it is written, peace be upon him, regarding the level of prophecy: just as all the holy ones and the ministers <note>Referring to angels or high-level prophets</note> were at the level of knowing His Unity <note>term: *Yichud*; the absolute oneness of God</note>, so too did He inform him of a level above them all. If this knowledge had not been granted to him, his greatness at the beginning of his prophecy would have been for naught, until it was said previously that this knowledge did not ascend to this level in perfection. For indeed, nothing was added to the quality of his prophecy beyond what he had prior to this, which was the level of the giving of the Torah, where he ascended to the highest of the levels of prophecy. This was necessary for the sake of the Torah’s secrets that were written by his hand. For when he said, **"Show me favor,"** he said, **"You said, 'I have known you by name...'"** and they said: **"and I shall know You by name."** <note>original: *ve-eda’acha be-shem*</note> 

Behold, he did not ascend higher than the topmost level, which was for the sake of the people's sin. Rather, what he sought was that he should be elevated to the level of knowing His Unity in accordance with the quality of his prophecy. This was added to him now, beyond what he had perceived and known of the Unity prior to this. This is the meaning of: **"and I have known you by name,"** which is like saying "by His great Name in prophecy," as it was before the parable. Furthermore, regarding the matter of His Unity, he was granted what no prophet before or after him ever perceived. 

And he said: **"Show me, I pray Thee, Thy glory."** <note>Exodus 33:18</note> Because he saw the pleasantness of his requests, a time of favor was opened—and a "favor" that was not merely for himself, but was very appropriate and prepared. For he examined himself and found that the physical matter <note>referring to the physical body or material world</note> could be overcome and there was no obstacle. Perhaps all of this was within what he had prepared in the heavens, for it would be inclusive and praiseworthy like one of the different distinguished [entities]. 

Initially, in an intellectual sense regarding the purity of his speech, he spoke to Jacob and did not lack the soul; he was blessed and brought tidings of wisdom and the attainment of the Great Name and His Glory. No man among all humans achieved this, and all his life this was not withheld from him—that he attained what he requested, even things that others had not yet attained. And now, in his vision, peace be upon him, because there was no obstacle to his power, he made this distinguished request, which was worthy and honorable, saying: **"Show me, I pray Thee, Thy glory."** His intention, peace be upon him, was that since he had asked to know His ways <note>Exodus 33:13</note> as a foundation, and as it is explained in his words: **"Inform me, I pray Thee, Thy way, that I may know You,"**—and "Your way" follows this, for he spoke of a unique way among His ways, which is the unification of His great Name that includes the Ten Sephirot <note>term: *Eser Sefirot*; the ten divine emanations in Kabbalah</note>. This is the first level of the true illumination: that He is One in His Name and His Essence, and He is not multiplied in His Being. He is One in Name and in Soul, to which one must be subordinate. **"And I have known you by name"**—for this knowledge is the distinguished one worthy of his level. 

Peace be upon him, as it was completed in the Torah in the verse, received by tradition and hinted at in the portion: **"Hear, O Israel: The Lord our God, the Lord is One."** <note>Deuteronomy 6:4</note> And there they received it from him, each one according to his wisdom and attainment. In his perfection, peace be upon him, he knew and looked into how to divide this distinguished and refined knowledge, revealed in the portion of the commandments. He, peace be upon him, sought to attain His Essence, may He be blessed. As he said: **"and I have known you, so that I may find grace in Your eyes,"** <note>Exodus 33:13</note> he asked that he might attain perfect knowledge at the peak of perfection in this way. 

This is what he meant by **"Show me Thy glory."** For according to the Unity, according to pure thought and the abstraction within it—not separated from Him but fixed within Him—no separation or interruption can be imagined. This must be at the peak of perfection in his finding of His glory. For a person asks and considers in his heart, and through this, this knowledge rises—which is the Unity in its total perfection—and this is what occurs in practice. This is why he asked that He show him His glory, as if with the sight of the eye. And if there is any physical obstacle, it does not exist at his level. 

This was also in the test of **"And I will show favor,"** for the thing will appear and he will recognize it in perfection. From there and onward, he will ask about the thing that is the source and established in his intellect, even when it is hidden from his eyes. Ultimately, he will stand in perfection upon the knowledge of His Unity: that He is One in His Divinity and is not multiplied in name, but He is One in His simple being. This is the distinguished purpose that he sought from the Great [God]. And he saw...

from the place where he intended the secret of the great hints. And I do not know <note>original: *ve-lo yada’ti*</note> the matter, because according to the Source, he will revolve the wheel, and with mercy he will show... etc. This is the secret of the revelation of the **Ancient of Days** <note>term: *Atik Yomin*; a Kabbalistic term for the highest, most ancient aspect of the Divine</note> mentioned before Him, whose wheels are revealed upon him. He will unify the Great Name in His glory. This is the secret that He would inform him of this way of Unity. 

There is an implication in **"And I will show favor"** as well, that He would inform him of the Great Name in its glory constantly, as it was until now. This is the first mention, as they hinted in the verse: **"And You said, 'I have known you by name,'"** as we wrote above. And in his saying: **"and see that this nation is Your people,"** <note>Exodus 33:13</note> this hints at the lights of the stars that were the need of the people and their benefit. This is the "cleaving of friends," <note>original: *davikut ha-re'ut*</note> meaning that He should be with them "Face to Face," as he hinted in saying: **"and you have also found grace in My eyes."** <note>Exodus 33:17</note> 

And He, may He be blessed, answered him regarding this first request concerning the Name, saying: **"My presence shall go, and I will give you rest."** <note>Exodus 33:14</note> The purpose he took was the "Presence" <note>original: *Panim*; literally "Faces"</note> which are with mercy, the "Unified Faces" upon which it is said "in a time of favor." For "My Name is within him," <note>referring to the Angel in Exodus 23:21</note> and he is the "Angel of His Presence" <note>Isaiah 63:9</note> hinted at as being in the level of the Shekhinah <note>term: *Shekhinah*; the Divine Presence</note> within. 

This was the Attribute of Judgment, and they had drawn near through the sacrifices, but he "separated the Chieftain" <note>referring to a disruption in the divine flow</note> as a sheltering helper, and there was anger with them over this.
