And it was "Face to Face" that I would tell from the beginning. 

And behold, in this, He was obligated to answer him as He did: **"Behold, I send an angel before you,"** <note>Exodus 23:20</note> and to say **"for My name is within him."** It is a "time of favor" because He will send them with that mercy and His Name is within him. 

Moses our Teacher, peace be upon him, said after this: **"If Your presence does not go with Your people and with Your glory,"** <note>based on Exodus 33:15</note> meaning that You should be with us Face to Face, **"do not bring us up from here."** For then there would be an interruption. What is the meaning of what You said, **"My presence shall go"**? That it would be like a dream? For a dream is what creates an interruption. This was hinted at when He said to him: **"Behold, I am sending an angel before you..."** because "My Name is within him." But after they sinned with the Calf, the divisions of the world would be strict; He would not stop them, for if I were Face to Face in your matter and in your glory, he would go with us. 

Or perhaps it was given to him for the time of the [sin of the] Calf, for in his mind, peace be upon him, was to request before Him for this—that it should be Face to Face. This is the meaning of: **"And how shall it be known here..."** <note>Exodus 33:16</note> that it is not just in Your going, but we shall be distinguished, all of us, in Your midst as a structure. This hints at his own "Face," which was the previous level of Your Shekhinah, and hints at His glory, the "Face" that does not shine for others, but only in a unique Unity. 

And his saying hints at all of this—that which is turned to be in your midst with us. And if he did not intend this secret, he should have translated it as "in the midst of Your Shekhinah." For above, when they spoke of His glory, in the phrase **"My presence shall go,"** he translated it as "My Shekhinah." Inside are "Faces" that do not shine in the garments of mercy. 

And when he began regarding "Face to Face," which was in his request "in Your midst," Your Shekhinah was angry at what he asked. In the beginning, my heart... see that being "Face to Face" is in one Unity, and a special Unity that was distinct. That is to say, the distinct and hidden would be revealed from the Ancient of Days <note>Atik Yomin</note>... in the revelations of the structure in the Unity of the Great Name in its glory. 

And this is according to the divisions known in prophecy, as I was until now at a high level. And I will not keep back or diminish from my greatness because of the sin of the people. And because he did not act, peace be upon him, for his own name but for the sake of the people, he had to return and ask. And thus he said "my heart and the midst." And for the need of your people, that He should be with them "Face to Face." And because all of this depends on the revelation of the "Distinct One," he said: **"and we shall be distinguished"** <note>Exodus 33:16; the Hebrew word *veniflinu* also means "wonderous" or "distinct"</note>. 

But "anger," etc., because he divided the matter into a separate thing, and favor in those distinct things... that our portion should be in the distinct and in the perfect Unity our portion. And this is against what He said: **"And I will send an angel before you,"** so that their portion would be like something separate upon its separation in Unity, as we explained above. 

**"Also this thing,"** if it were "Face to Face" which you spoke with them, for You said "for I have known [you]." And behold, it was done according to what he asked for the good of the people, and he blessed them with perfection—that there should be "Shining Faces" within "Faces that do not shine" in a different Unity.

And **"I will show favor"** <note>v'chanantani</note> at this time, in the hour of my first request, which I asked—that the Great Name should be inclusive for him.

# Chapter 34 | The Section on the Ultimate Purpose — Chapter 35

And this is regarding the state of separation, for the cause of explanation and anger toward our teacher <note>Moses</note> was like a unique separation. Even the God of the world would be as a separate thing in the phrase **"I Am"** <note>original: *Ehyeh*</note>, as is the meaning of His saying: **"For I will not go up in your midst."** <note>Exodus 33:3</note> Had this rebuked God been the Source <note>The Ein Sof or ultimate source</note>, He would not have spoken thus. Then Moses, peace be upon him, said: "If this is so, let it not be! Let me not be a burden to my people, for this is not 'knowledge'." For the nature of true knowledge is that it must be fixed upon one thing and one matter, a lasting existence that does not change. If it changes, it is not true knowledge.

In the beginning of the matter, Moses said to Him: **"See, You say to me..."** <note>Exodus 33:12</note> as if to say, "These words of Yours release one another." There is no argument from any of those who receive tradition in this present matter, for You wrote in Your Torah: **"whom the Lord knew face to face."** <note>Deuteronomy 34:10</note> This is what He meant by: **"and You have said, 'I have known you by name.'"** <note>Exodus 33:12</note> That is to say, the Name <note>original: *HaShem*</note> was known to him in the greatness of His glory. You were always known to him in His glory as has been the case until now. But then, He sought to contradict this because of the deed of the Golden Calf. For Moses, peace be upon him, feared after God said to him, **"Go, go down,"** and according to what He said to him, **"And I will send an angel before you,"** and **"I will not go up in your midst,"** etc. Afterward, Moses took pride in the silver <note>likely a metaphor for the merits or the refined state of his prayer</note> that earned him the right to know Him by the Great Name in His glory. And this is why he said to Him: **"And You have said, 'I have known you by name.'"**

As I have already explained, there is a secret in these two parts, and my eyes are upon them. This is not the end of your degree, for you are still in the state of being "before Him" until you are "in my eyes." This is what is meant by: **"and you have also found favor in My eyes."** <note>Exodus 33:12</note> This "also" serves to include more. He already said this, and it is what he received as a response for the good of the community. Abraham also said: **"Now, if I have found favor in Your eyes, please let me know..."** <note>Genesis 18:3/Exodus 33:13</note> and so he merited. Every hidden path is linked to **"finding favor in my eyes,"** for "finding favor" is a great thing. It is through this that he becomes the Luminary and the Unity <note>term: *Yichud*; the state of divine oneness</note>. In the context of what is written: **"For all that is in heaven and on earth"** <note>1 Chronicles 29:11</note>, this "all" refers to the specific tie between the heavens and the earth.

**"Now, if I have found favor in Your eyes"** as You have said, **"please let me know Your ways."** <note>Exodus 33:13</note> By the pattern of Your ways, show me how to grant strength and be unified with You. **"That I may know You"** <note>original: *ve-eda’acha*</note> means: "Teach me and let me understand." For through the Name, by informing me of the secret of Your existence and making us understand, He unifies Himself in His Name in a time of favor. **"That I may know You"** implies that when He is divided in the "Name of Anger" without any teaching of His Name, He is the true Rebuker. The increase of favor is because he does His will; for by the Supernal Will, he exists. The Unity with the Name revealed in His glory comes through finding favor in His eyes and doing His will. This is why it says: **"that I may know You, so that I may find favor in Your eyes."**

**"And consider that this nation is Your people."** <note>Exodus 33:13</note> You must remember them, for they are as nothing except for the good that comes from them, and that comes from You. Therefore, You must be with them "face to face." For the sake of Glory and the sake of existence, I ask for the knowledge of His ways. For one who is said to be "in Your ways" is sustained by Your life, for that is what you seek. With Your people Israel, he hopes even more for this, and so all his requests were granted. He attained "The Lord is One" <note>Adonai Echad</note>. You are the one who knows the truth of my strength and my will, for His will was also to bless them and give them life in every detail. For He knows that the favor holds great provision for the upright, and he seeks mercy for them. There will be a time when he seeks a place for all this, regarding the questions we raised about the assumptions. 

This is because once he is in a state of connection and knows that the Name will return in the revelation of His glory, that is the way to attain all his desires—for He is the source of all goodness and comforts. It is necessary that this perfection be found for himself with ease and with providence over the whole. From above it will be drawn down, and it will also be found below for those who cause this truth. Delve into his request before Him, that He might make it known to him. That is to say: "How is He unified in His Name for good?" So that he might achieve from Him what he had not achieved before or after—to be in the light and to return to God. To this, the scripture appears to say to the Holy One, Blessed be He: "May it be Your will to let me know the intention of Your conduct," meaning the reason for doing what You did. This is the unification of His Great Name for good. In the matter of **"and you shall do what is good and right,"** <note>Deuteronomy 6:18</note> our intention is His Unity. It is written: **"Trust in the Lord and do good,"** <note>Psalm 37:3</note> for Unity above is "doing" and "rectification." After the Unity, it says: **"And I have done what is good in Your eyes."** <note>Isaiah 38:3</note> Their saying "Go to the blessings of the verse" refers to the elevation above, which is the Perfect Unity, as is known to the wise of heart. He shared His mercy so that you might find these mercies, for through great mercy, everything is transformed for its owner.

<column-break/>

There is another doubt like this as well, which must be agreed upon. Furthermore, why was He not satisfied following Him with the "Aleph" <note>note: referring to the letter Aleph in the word 'Ehyeh' (I Am)</note> that existed until it fell away and was missing? And should the God of them be slow to return and enter? And through this, he would be separated from Him, and the God of forgiveness would accept him from there. He spoke of the "separators," and those who receive would not attain it from Him. If so, why say to the one who sent His God? Heaven forbid that such a thought should enter our minds. 

Rather, resolve this: this request was made in the face of the "spreading of thought," which is from the signs of the Name, both hidden and revealed. Although it is through a receiver, one must know that this is necessary to perform for the whole—to God, who fills everything, specifically and generally. Through the spreading of thought, the secret of His measure increases. When he grasps this weight upon his secret, then he knows and attains in the secret of the Name what everyone attains from this—the "before" and "after." As He said to him: **"And I—this I have not made known to you,"** and my Name is as I have made known to you, which is before and after. 

**"I Am That I Am"** <note>original: *Ehyeh Asher Ehyeh*; Exodus 3:14</note> is a doubling of the end before they ask and it spreads out. This is when the intellect stands by itself as a whole, its essence not yet spreading into the "How" and "Where." That is to say, "Asher" (That/Which) implies the whole for the sake of, and because of, He is the "All" from there. "Atum" (Closed/Hidden) means that from all the receptions, He is the Great Name that established us. As is told in the Supernal Wisdom that was in every heart, because of this, He said **"I Am"** (*Ehyeh*), which is the sum of all the light. 

It is said in the Midrash: **"I was a nursling (*Amon*) beside Him"** <note>Proverbs 8:30</note>—do not read *Amon* but *Amen*. The intention was focused on what is written: **"Truly (*Amen*), everything was from the Holy One, Blessed be He."** He is the sum of all. It is as if everything were still in the silence of the high degree, and there was not yet a word in His glory. Until seven "times" <note>stages or emanations</note> were drawn further out, and a thin, inner revelation was revealed in the world. Yet everything was still hidden, though it was more ready to be revealed and drawn out from that point on. This is what is meant by **"That I Am"** (*Asher Ehyeh*). It is the flow and the unity that existed between the First and the Second. This is the secret of *Asher* (That), for it is the spirit that is distinguished from the Divine, and from it, everything is received. In the scripture, He is called "The Name *Ehyeh*," and He says **"Asher Ehyeh"** because the reception of the Name was from Wisdom.

Everything was ready to be drawn out and revealed in detail according to the Will. Then it moved to distinguish and complete the "spreading out." Afterward, it is as if—at this moment—everything is drawn out in detail. For this reason, He did not say **"Asher Ehyeh"** <note>to the Israelites</note>, for the time for the completion of the revelation and the drawing out had not yet arrived. Therefore, He said: **"Thus shall you say to the children of Israel: 'I Am (*Ehyeh*) has sent me to you,'"** <note>Exodus 3:14</note> to indicate the specific part of the matter. After it was drawn out and everything was fixed in its designated place—as implied by "and he went down to Pharaoh" in the context of the signs—He then returns to Moses: **"Thus shall you say to the children of Israel: 'The Lord (*YHVH*), the God of your fathers, the God of Abraham, the God of Isaac, and the God of Jacob...'"** <note>Exodus 3:15</note> Here, everything is specified, including the perfection of the Great Name. 

I have written this at length, and there is more to be gained from the secret of the Holy Name that is with us and revealed. In the Name, as in the "Good Vision," its meaning is that it is one. He received from the mouth of the Almighty the Unity of the Hidden Name and its revelation through the prophecy of wisdom. Vision is associated with those who fear Him, according to the revealed argument and the breadth of his knowledge and strength. We have written these Holy Names with help, and our goal is to accompany and direct the desires by hinting at the secret of the "Wisdom of Opening" <note>original: *pituach*</note>. This is the "knocking of the Supernal Thought" and to awaken the intention at the beginning. Regarding the vision of the intertwined things... that we wrote in this fullness and in part of it, according to the intention of the book. It is solely to awaken the intention regarding the questions **"Please let me know Your ways"** and the question **"Please show me Your glory"** in the coming chapter, with God's sign.

# Chapter 38 | The Ultimate Purpose — Chapter 38

And it is drawn down, moving from the right side downward, <note>This refers to the flow of Divine emanation from the Sefirah of Chesed (Kindness/Right) toward the lower worlds.</note> and through these, one contemplates and reveals one thing upon another. This is the perfect unity in the revelation of the Higher Name over the lower. And then the skin of Moses' face <note>Exodus 34:29</note> shone through the secret of the ancient, subtle light that returned to him. We should rejoice in the dances before Him, from above them, by way of revelation and the refinement of the *Manna* <term>Manna: the spiritual food of the wilderness, here used as a metaphor for divine sustenance</term> standing within us. This was what sufficed for him when seeing the "back" <note>Exodus 33:23</note> and what was included in his request where he asked: **"Make Your ways known to me, that I may know You,"** as will be explained. His degree reached the end according to the level of his glory which was at the beginning, and He wrote concerning him more than all the holy ones and those who inherit the Leviathan. <note>A metaphorical reference to the righteous in the world to come.</note> And in the book *Tola'at Yaakov* <note>original: "Tola'at Yaakov" (The Worm of Jacob), a 16th-century Kabbalistic work by Meir ibn Gabbai.</note> I wrote the secret of calling upon the 12 attributes <note>Though usually 13, the manuscript here specifies 12, possibly referring to a specific arrangement of the Divine names.</note> and the intention behind them. There are no other ways in the writing, for each one has its place, and all is kept for one intention: the Way of the Lord, which is the perfect Unity. This was the "end" that he sought.

**And Moses hurried and bowed...** <note>Exodus 34:8</note> to include the beginning, to return with a blessing as He passed before him. He heard the voice calling the attributes, and from all of it, he bowed. The matter is correct for the children of those who fear Him: "All my ways are in our midst," as it is written regarding the *Shekhinah* <term>Shekhinah: the Divine Presence residing in the world</term>. Even though the *Manna* was among you, what the speaker and the first spoke was in the place of the Unique Name. All of it was to teach about the Unity, for this is included in that, and that in the name *Yah* <note>A shorter form of the Divine Name YHWH.</note>, and the Name includes from beginning to end, as is known to the "wise of heart."

I saw fit to explain from my holy offering <note>The author likely refers to his own previous writings or a specific commentary.</note> what was written in these words: Know that after Moses understood in his intellect the secret of the 12 attributes—which are not limited—to return the words of the subtle, exalted level... the level of the *Kabbalah* <term>Kabbalah: here meaning "reception" or the received tradition</term>. The final word among the three "Beauties of Mercy" is not the "Merciful One" who was there in the words at the beginning. This was the intention of the statement: **"If I have found favor in Your eyes, let the Lord go in our midst,"** <note>Exodus 34:9</note> for a prophet has no power to prophesy and to forgive, nor to bring the earth into the great path. Regarding the "Building of the Sullam" <note>The Ladder</note>, according to the "Secret of the Smitten," it will be explained that it is known that the Lord is the one who supports us. So too: **"The Lord will not remove His Godliness"** regarding the holy teachings. And afterward, he explained the two internal intentions of this matter, for they are few.

**And forgive our iniquity and our sin, and take us for Your inheritance.** <note>Exodus 34:9</note> He said to Him: "Grant me the intention of the Covenant," which was intended to produce and limit his knowledge toward the "Living Head" through the "Foundation of Glory." This is the "Covenant of the End" in the blessing of your longings, to return the level of Greatness to the Name, so that the wicked one may say: "Behold, all your people have seen wonders," etc. He intended to show in a general tongue the level of *Tiferet* <term>Tiferet: Beauty/Harmony, the central Sefirah</term>, the King who includes all. And he said: **"Forgive, I pray You, Your people."** You knew everything according to the doubling of the language, for who is the one who says His *Shekhinah* is upon him? His *Shekhinah* is close, within, "face to face" in His name and His goodness.

# Chapter 38 | The Ultimate Purpose — Chapter 38

...to be gracious, in my humble opinion, to our seal that was given: **"And I will show mercy on whom I will show mercy,"** <note>Exodus 33:19</note> even though we mentioned it as "given." This is the measure to inform him that these are His attributes, blessed be He, and that there be no difference. **"I will show mercy"** and **"He will be gracious to us"** are within His name and His goodness. In this, he will achieve the end of what he sought to achieve—for His holy Unity is perfected. He shall see and achieve, yet the whole shall not be seen. The great "Final Glory" belongs to Moses, about whom I wrote for the first time when he was at the standing at Mount Sinai. And now, to make all this known:

->**And the Lord descended in a cloud**<- <note>Exodus 34:5</note>

And this is the "Cloud of Glory." **And He stood with him there** to make known the permanence of the goodness of His foundation by saying: **"And He called out the name of the Lord before you."** He called out the name of the Lord because the worship of the Great Name is through His honored Name. This alludes to the peace. "And he called by His name to the Lord"—the call of the Name, the Lord.

**And the Lord passed before his face and called out.** The light would ascend when He said: "If all My goodness passes by, the created beings will be destroyed." Therefore, the Lord "passed" with His intention, for the Glory of the Name passed before Moses' face. I saw fit to clarify from my holy offering what was said in these words: "I have prepared a bit," and its intention is for one of the hidden things in this deep matter. It says "And He passed," referring to the Supernal Glory, the power of the "Key and the Lintel" <note>Metaphors for the opening of divine flow.</note> from the level of the "Last Writing," which is a "Voice" known to those who understand.

Analyzing the depths of the grammar, he said that the first **"Lord"** (YHVH) has two cantillation marks: a *Shofar Holekh* and a *Pashta*. <note>Cantillation marks are musical notations for chanting the Torah; Kabbalists interpret their shapes and sounds mystically.</note> He said the "Ancient One" and His "Might" are required; it is only from the "Cave of Learning," and it is the sign. Therefore, it is the "Shofar of Salvation" for Israel who walks in exile—thus the *Shofar Holekh* <note>Holekh means "going" or "walking".</note>. He did not give a reason for the rest of the children, but there is the *Darga* <note>Another musical accent.</note> mark. From the general rule, according to my limited intellect, it indicates the great clarity of the soul of the "Third Glory," which was honored before Moses' face.

So I saw in the commentary of the wise **Rabbi Judah the Pious**, may his memory be a blessing, regarding the word **"And He descended."** He did this because Isaac blessed Jacob... to show that the sign of the Holy Torah given to Isaac belongs to Jacob. He wrote this regarding the word **"And He called."** The accent follows the custom and the form of the foundation of the word, which calls out to the understanding mouth. **"The Lord, the Lord"**—the calling out of His words, and in these He is gracious and merciful in His name and His goodness. The portion of the "Hidden One" and the "Removals" is from the womb until the end of the complete Foundation (*Yesod*), where the foundation of Kingship and Mercy over Israel exists. Through this, Kindness (*Chesed*) and Support will be strengthened. Therefore, he explained "Mercy" and "Salvation," for His great Name will then be blessed and not forgotten—meaning, through these words within Him.

Even though we use the word "Mercy" and the word "Judgment," one should not think that the Name has two opposite attributes within Him. It is not so! Everything is One, unified in the ultimate unity. Our intellect cannot grasp this clearly, and we lack the power to understand these matters at their source. Now, the word "Mercy" performs the righteousness of judgment. They said that "The Lord is difficult by day from His place," and He covers Himself as if in a sanctuary between the attribute of Mercy and the attribute of Judgment. These are two matters of teaching.

As we say, **"The Lord, God"** <note>original: "YHVH El"</note>—the name *El* is specifically for the attribute of Judgment. One must know and look deeply to prove them, for there is no intellectual comparison. He is One, and there are no others. We say this with our mouths to establish it clearly. And the truth of what is possible is that this is what Moses sought: to know and to see that "He should go"—He who is within His name and His goodness, as will be explained. It is written that the seal of every creature is upon Him, and that is what was made known to Moses. He desired his existence to be what it had not been... though the "Seeing of the Face" was denied to him.

Regarding the doubling of the Name, the Holy Psalmist <note>King David</note> said, when teaching about the Name: **"The Lord, the Lord"**—the verse’s accent and intention are for a perfect fear. I have come to mention the words... there is no translator for the "Strong Shield." He prepared the word for the "Womb of Mercies" ... regarding the "Mercies of the Beginning." And he poured kindness... in every creation, "Merciful," and my sins... and the end is not like flesh. I have turned to show mercy to you. He informed us of the secret of the names... he is the first, and the "Ancient of Days," to show the connection of the 12 <note>attributes</note>. He spoke to Moses concerning the secret of the descent of the words.

# Chapter 35 | The Part on the Ultimate Purpose | Chapter 35

**Right Column**

Interpret his glory. And regarding the second question, the Master (peace be upon him) asked <note>original: "ע"ה" (Alav HaShalom) – a traditional honorific for the deceased, likely referring here to a specific commentator like Maimonides or Nahmanides</note> to interpret His glory. Indeed, that which He answered in prophecy, He wished to show him through the sight of the eye. This matter is known to the wise: that the power of attainment through "face to face" <note>original: "פנים אל פנים" (Panim el Panim) – a technical term for direct, unmediated prophecy</note> involves "shining faces" and "faces that do not shine." For he attained through this and understood through this, and now he sought to see with the heart a literal vision. He called His face "the Glory," as it says, **"Show me Your glory"** <note>Exodus 33:18</note>; for the word "Your" <note>Hebrew: "Et" (את)</note> hints at the final ones, and "Your glory" hints at those at the end. To stir this intention, the word "Your glory" <note>original: "כבכך" - likely a scribal variant for "Kevodecha"</note> is missing a letter *Vav*. He called his request a "vision of the back" and a "vision of the face." He told him that this is impossible by the law of any created being. And He said, **"I will make all My goodness pass"** <note>Exodus 33:19</note>; He said "His goodness" because the Hidden Good is between Him, and it is the "All" within Him. He said He would make him pass through everything as if standing in a sphere before His face. He did not mean "to pass" as in "to save," but rather that the Great Name <note>The Tetragrammaton</note> would cause the Good to pass through all things. And so that he would not die from the sight—perhaps his physical composition would fail—He hid him and covered him. This would be the proclamation upon your face from the morning, for He would elevate his place above your face and stir you with nothingness, etc. And He said, **"And I will proclaim the name of the Lord before you"** <note>Exodus 33:19</note> literally; meaning, a literal path of the attribute of leadership and the attribute of mercy. You shall know how they act with mercy and grace through My name and My essence. This shall suffice for you to satisfy your longing regarding what you included and wrote in your desire: **"Make Your ways known to me,"** etc. And the rest follows the path I explained above. Regarding the difficulty you found in the words **"I will be gracious to whom I will be gracious,"** etc., it means: **"You cannot see My face"** <note>Exodus 33:20</note> from the back. To this, the Master (peace be upon him) aimed: you cannot see the face of My Indwelling Presence <term>Shekhinah: the Divine Presence as it manifests in the world</term> together with the face of Divine Leadership, the face of the surroundings. And write this: for there is no "face" to the Shekhinah, and the Shekhinah is not "this." And regarding any being, "face" and "back" are reversed in reality; the back is the posterior. Concerning this, He said, **"And you shall see My back, but My face shall not be seen"** <note>Exodus 33:23</note>. The meaning of "Back" is what Onkelos <note>The famous 2nd-century translator of the Torah into Aramaic</note> (peace be upon him) translated as "that which is behind Me," for **"no man shall see Me and live."** This is the ultimate sustenance: "living life." The intention is the vision and the vitality, for even the intellectual vitalities and the sages who possessed eternal life could not see My crown <note>Keter: the highest of the Sefirot</note>, nor could they say that before it is sent, its composition is separated. And what He promised him and what we heard Himself say: **"for no man shall see Me,"** He did not say "for He shall distance Me," lest the prevention be a sickness. There is no such thing, for it is not withheld from him "and live." As it is written: **"And they saw the God of Israel,"** etc., and also **"And he saw the Lord."** Behold, **"a place is with Me"** <note>Exodus 33:21</note> is missing a word. **"As My glory passes by,"** and I will set you in a **"cleft of the rock"**; the passing by means from His resting place. For this He intended: **"I will remove My hand,"** and this is what is said about "upon your face." It stands to work there on the "Unique Name" <note>The Tetragrammaton</note> without division. When the Glory passes, you shall cut the wings of the rock. Onkelos translates "rock" as "a cave," for it was the cave where Moses and Elijah stood in the mountain of the Torah. This was a connection to show him as if hidden by a "palm" <note>referring to God's hand in Exodus 33:22</note> in the words from the midst of the cracks, to return and reveal the secret to his choice. The "Back" could not stand before the Torah because it is written, **"for no man shall see Me and live."** And his "living" stood with him according to his degree, and from there we see how great was the power of his excellence over all the prophets. Because of the Torah, so that he would not break through to see the mystery of his desire, He said to him: **"And I will cover you with My hand until I have passed."** Note that it says **"until My glory has passed"** and not "until I have passed," to say that the Place of His Glory and His Glory are one. And to remove his place, His Glory spoke. And as it is written: **"Behold, a place is with Me,"** the word "with Me" implies a prayer to Me, and there is nothing secondary to Me. And the text reveals what you desired after you sought to see the "Place" that he could not reach, and they endangered the essence. And also a place of purity and vision and strength; and within his house, from every "place," a time of mourning and trembling before the sight of the eye. All the goodness in this, he shall gather it there. **"And I will remove My hand,"** and the distance of the back, and My back—this is to teach that He showed him the **"knot of the phylacteries"** <term>Tefillin: ritual leather boxes containing Torah verses. Midrash says God showed Moses the back-knot of His own spiritual Tefillin.</term> and its seal, for it is a universal knot. It returns everything, and it is the knot of the decree of "Do Not," for it was the "Fourth Leg" in the Supernal Chariot <note>The Merkavah: the divine throne-chariot in Ezekiel's vision</note>, and through it the greatness of the cycles ascends. From that place, he was given a portion and told to see "His back," to investigate the first and the last things and everything...

**Left Column**

...said, **"The form of the Lord he beholds"** <note>Numbers 12:8</note>. In this book of mine, I have explained "His back." **"But My face shall not be seen"**; he did not say "it shall not be seen" because there was an intermediary preventing him from seeing, but rather that it is impossible for him. "They shall not be seen" means that the internal faces are hidden from everything itself. And Onkelos translated: "and you shall see that which is behind Me." This is literally the "back," to follow that which is below by the placement of the backs, which are the back of the faces. The backs are difficult, and for one of the other backs which are to the posterior, it is difficult. Also, "Face" in Arabic means "direction." Turn your back to the backs; they are in relation to the Upper Faces from which the Name of the Faces emerges. But that which is below them—this was not withheld from him; it is only the Inner Faces, which are the "Faces of the Faces." And the matter of this is deeper: in his wisdom (peace be upon him), he grasped the vision of the Face. For he knew that if he attained his vision, nothing of what is "Before" or "Behind" would be hidden from him. Therefore, even if we say that until now he did not attain the vision of the World of the Back, which is the "Back of the Backs," it should not be taken literally as something kept from him. For he knew that he would not be kept from it, yet he would still not emerge to see the King Himself. But he desired to see the King, whose vision would allow him to see all His ministers and servants, for they are all with the King in His work. It was written to him: "You shall ascend to see My face and all the Internal Faces," for they are called "Faces before Faces." And when he attains the "Backs" which are "Faces" in relation to what is below them, then all the "Backs" are included in their vision. Along with this, it says, **"The form of the Lord he beholds,"** to see all the things termed "Backs." And in saying **"And I will remove [My hand],"** He meant to exclude all the things termed "Faces" from him—the "Faces of the Faces," the "Faces." This was withheld from him even after his prayer and his pleading; it was not granted to him. All is one matter, for the Face of the Holy One and His Back are one thing in Him. That is to say: they are not outside of Him. And as in the Midrash of Rabbi Hanina <note>A 3rd-century Talmudic sage</note> who asked: Master of the Universe, I have received this from Moses... it is known that the knowledge of the Name as it is written... and the Sages said: "Regarding 'Show me Your glory,' he sought to know why there is a **righteous person who prospers** and a **righteous person who suffers**, a **wicked person who prospers** and a **wicked person who suffers**." <note>This is the classic question of theodicy: why do bad things happen to good people?</note> And they did not inform him. That is, they did not inform him of what he sought. Would it enter your mind that Moses did not know this secret? For so said Moses: "Behold, I know the names of my fathers, but I do not know how the Thought spreads through them." I know that 'the Name' is one... I knew my God. And he sought to know of God, but they did not inform him. Behold, we understand that two answers are true. The first: "I will be gracious..." and in the Psalm of Solomon: "Your ways and Your knowledge." For the head of His three knowledges and His purposes, as explained above, is the knowledge of His Foundation—it is one with His Name and His Essence, without any division, for He is His own vessel. And the knowledge of His parts, the "Thought," and how it spreads through all His parts in a single unification—regarding this, it is said "without any change or variation." For by knowing this, one would know why the righteous man prospers and the righteous man suffers, etc. For this "Path," this was hidden from him as a secret. It has already been explained in the Great Midrash and is received by those who "stand in the secret of the Lord." This is what they meant by saying they "did not inform him"—meaning they did not inform him of what he sought, which is the knowledge of His "spreading parts" and the reasons for their expansion into His attributes. This is the "Vision of the Face." It was withheld from him because "Thought" is not attained by another. This secret depends on the "Supernal Thought," for it is the mystery of the "Transition" <note>likely referring to the passage of divine energy</note> which is the source at the beginning of the Thought of the Water of the Seas. And as explained regarding Rabbi Akiva <note>The 1st-century sage who "entered the Orchard (Pardes)" and returned in peace</note>, that he ascended in Thought to stand upon the limits of Evil and Good. Its meaning: from the path of how the Pure Thought spreads. But all this is a Truth without any change or variation, and he could not grasp it at all. This is what is meant here: "He sought to know its parts, and they did not inform him." And this is what they also said in the Tractate Berakhot, disagreeing with Rabbi Meir: for Rabbi Meir said "Two things were given to him and one was not given to him, as it says: **'I will be gracious to whom I will be gracious...'**"

# Chapter 36 | The Part on the Ultimate Purpose | Chapter 37

...as a broad and powerful eastern portion, and all of them are like a crescent moon in the levels of all wisdom. Like milk, and not the voice of the blemish of the small ones, their thickness is actual darkness, and every grace is in the cleanliness of the paths from the rivers of light, according to their preparation for their levels. And for here, they are prepared for their existence, given to their levels, hinted at in the burning voice. And we read of the "openings" upon the gate of <note>original: "לסוריא" (Le-Suria) – possibly a reference to a specific gate or a mystical region</note> where they gathered in a line, like those arranged for the <term>Shekhinah</term><note>The Divine Presence or the feminine aspect of God that dwells within the world.</note>, being saved as the law of the 135 heroes surrounding it. They said that what they attained was the "perfection of the moon" upon them, in its colors, a mixture of thoughts. And there is the royal garment, and it makes known to the wise of heart. And they were the ones who tasted and merited to reach the heart; they did not perceive the Glory itself. And the knowledge of the "burning" they kindled, of which it is said, "it shall not depart from him" <note>likely referring to the eternal flame or divine inspiration</note>, and also "known," and so on. He said "truth and humility," and they brought it upon the Hand. And they perceived the "Lord," for he did not say "and I will see my Lord," but rather "the Lord," and they fought because He is as written. -># Chapter 38: The Section of the Purpose<-

### Chapter 38

"The Lord is a Man of War." <note>Exodus 15:3</note> Names are called "man" at first in their heat, and for the death of his sins, they are called by these names. For from the breast to the stature, and because they were also written in the likeness of the upper beings, they are "The Lord" <note>original: *YHVH*</note> below. 

As in the school of Rabbi Nehunia ben ha-Kanah: Rabbi Shapira asked: "What is the meaning of the verse 'The Lord is a man of war'?" He explained: Do not ask me about simple words, listen to him. It is a parable of a King who had three beautiful dwellings, and each one was better than the other. He said, "I will give you this one whose name is **Aleph** (א), for it is beautiful; and this one whose name is **Yud** (י), for it is also good; and this one whose name is **Shin** (ש)." What did he do? He made a "Well of Wonders" and from there a Name was made. Then he made from there a "House." They said to him, "Until when will you rejoice in the Blessed One?" He said to them, "My children, the **Aleph** is the head, for it is found there. The **Shin** includes the whole world." Why does the **Shin** include the whole world? Because it is written: "The Son of Repentance" <note>original: *Ben Teshuvah*; the letter Shin has three branches, often compared to the three patriarchs or the three paths of the soul returning to God.</note>.

And because the word **Man** (*Ish*) was difficult for them, he explained it through the letters, saying that in the binding and unification of these letters—which are established together upon this Name—the **Great Name** is called by it to indicate the unity of the Divinity. The spirit of the Divinity which he established in the language of the scripture and the tradition is that "The Lord is One and Unique," and there is no Name except Himself. He is the entire expansion that indicates Holiness. He did not call it by His name alone, may He be blessed, and for this reason, he avoided calling the Unique Name "The Lord is a Man" by its essence, but rather used the term "Man" (*Ish*) as it relates to "Woman" (*Ishah*), for it is more inclusive. In its letters, it includes everything. Through wisdom and through the cause of the "Salt," the end of the name **Adam** <note>The Hebrew word for Man/Humanity.</note> includes all things from the beginning to the end. All this is written in the words of prophecy with a wondrous hint.

<column-break/>

And regarding the "Death of Security," the "Death of the Abundant" who does good for us and elevates us—as in the school of Rabbi Shimon bar Yochai: "I saw the sparks of perfection." Above, when the Name sits upon the **Throne**, but before He sat upon the Throne, perfection was not found. For it is written: "And upon the likeness of the throne was a likeness as the appearance of a **Man** (*Adam*) upon it from above." <note>Ezekiel 1:26</note> This teaches that "Adam" signifies totality and the perfection of everything.

They asked there: "If so, it is written 'The Lord is a man (*Ish*) of war' and it is not written 'Adam'?" He said to him: These words are the same. He said to her: To find the perfection of everything and its structure, He is called *Ish* (Man/Husband). But everything is the perfection of all and the totality of all, and because of this, He is called *Adam*.

Furthermore, there is the "Structure of the Countenance" <note>The *Partzufim* or Divine Faces in Kabbalah.</note> where **six wings** emerge from the *Aleph* and are joined in the "Crown of Might" (Gevurah). They are joined in the "Attribute" and become one body. When they enter the body, it is called *Ish*. And if he is an *Ish*, why do you grant him "Six" <note>The six directions or Sefirot of the emotional core.</note> more than his vessels and the "Thread of the Throne"? "The Lord is a man of war," for it is written that *Ish* is the totality of all.

Rabbi Yehuda said: I was told this was in the precious teachings of Rabbi Isaac, son of Rabbi Shimon. He said to him: Understand the root of the head. It is written: "This shall be called Woman (*Ishah*), for from Man (*Ish*) she was taken." Understand what this "Man" is—it is the **Source**. And there you said that it stands for him. Here is the general rule: This joins with "Fire" (*Esh*) like a ruler and the "Rod of the Lower Leader." It appears and is clothed in the **Ten** [Sefirot]. He is called the "Vision of the Head" before him. Thus, the "Hair of the Head" passes from him to be covered, and he is understood below in all his parts. Because of this, he is called **Pure**, as it is written: "Who can bring a clean thing out of an unclean?" <note>Job 14:4</note>. And it is written: "If a man's hair falls out from his head... he is pure." <note>Leviticus 13:40</note>

The "Head" washes him in the colors of the *Keren* <note>Horns or rays of light.</note>. Thus the **Skull** and the Head of the "Redness" are all like a rose. The hairs are red like scarlet, and from them, the "Lower Crowns" are filled to awaken "Judgments" in the world. Thus the hair and the "Arms of the World" pass from him, and everything is covered and called by His name.

Further there: This "Man" (*Ish*) is within the totality of "The Small Face" (*Zeir Anpin*). Every wise person wants to discern the calling of this "Man," and here in the name of the "Battle," it is written: "The Lord is a man of war." In his "Six" [Sefirot], he is a "Man of Death" <note>Meaning a mortal-like manifestation for the sake of judgment.</note>, and he does not rest in the battle until his hair passes from him. For from here, they are "flames" and all those "crowns" that are seen in the hair are broken. It is written: "In that day the Lord will shave with a razor hired..." <note>Isaiah 7:20</note>.

"And there was fire." They hinted at the **six kinds of wings** from the structure of the Countenance. When they join in all the **Might** (Gevurah), they are called "Gevurot" (Mights/Powers). And it is written: "And I will dwell among them," to indicate perfection. When they join into one body, he is called *Ish* (Man), and they indicate the "Hardness of Judgment" and the "Strong One" who oversees the world. These "Mights" are the "Gate of this Judgment" and the "Constellation" over the Judgment. From it, Judgment is observed and led in the "Smallest Place" of the "Lower Crowns." When the "Hair" is full, the "Hairs of the Head" from which the lower ones are separated and cut off, they wander and are washed in **Upper Kindness** (Chesed). Then the "Kindness" turns to **White**. In the secret of the "Correct Myrrh," these "Waters of the Sukkot" <note>The festival of Tabernacles, associated with water drawing and mercy.</note> dwell in the "Constellation of the Leap Year." This is the "Clothed One" from the school of Rabbi Nehunia. This breaks the "Oaks," for he includes the perfection of everything in "Fire."

Since they said that this "Man" (*Ish*) is within the category of **Fire**, the foundation of the "Gate of his Head" is this, which is the source of the "Lower Connections." Therefore, they are "cut off" and "wandering," according to the length of our God.

Behold, in my coming near, the secret of the verse "The Lord is a man of war" is to say that within "Man" He dwells and builds His wars. This is not something separate from Him, for He is the Ruler. Let it not be thought that there is change, Heaven forbid! For the end of the verse says: "**The Lord is His Name**"—there is no change in Him; everything is One, giving life both in the time of war and at other times. The Name was written to indicate His constant life in the existence of the "Fire."

<keywords>Man of War, Divine Name, Aleph, Shin, Nun, Rashbi, Nehunia ben ha-Kanah, Judgment, Mercy, Zohar, Divine Countenance</keywords>

# Chapter 36: The Section of the Purpose
->Chapter 36<-

In the Midrash of Rabbi Shimon bar Yochai <note>original: "Rashbi"; the traditional author of the Zohar</note>, peace be upon him, who wrote concerning the concept of **Wisdom** regarding the verse: "And God saw all that He had made, and behold, it was very good" <note>Genesis 1:31</note>—these are the angels who are prepared to receive the "Good." We have acted well, as it is written, etc. And after a generation, he returned to let us hear thus, etc., so that the **Thought** <note>Machshavah; a high level of divine emanation</note> should be beneath His **Throne of Glory**, in which He gladdens us. Similarly, one who errs in this is like one who errs in the sanctity of the Great Holy Crown. 

Behold, the Sages have explained that in their thoughts, they are likened to the arrangement of the heavens. Everything returns at once to the Great One, who is the Holy One, Blessed be He, to receive them—meaning, through unification with Him. For even though everything in the world was caused by His hand, as it is written, "the work of His hands," it means that everything that exists was attained and clarified. For after that generation, he was bound to the Secret, for he mentioned the **Higher Torah** of the Holy One, Blessed be He, as we find in the *Book of Honor* <note>Sefer ha-Kavod; likely a reference to a specific mystical treatise</note>. Similar to this, before the Purity of the Unique One, He derived strength from it. This is because he is the light of that **Unification** <term>Yichud: The mystical practice of unifying the different aspects or Names of God through prayer and intention.</term>, for he understood and heard from the "moving connector," and specifically the "Voice from the Stream" <note>a metaphor for divine flow</note> belongs to them. Thus, his prayer would be accepted, as it is said, "the work of His hands," and afterwards, "The Great Attentiveness." 

And after He hears the prayer, "Blessed be He who pardons and forgives." His connection in the Midrash of Rabbi Shimon bar Yochai, peace be upon him, elevated the heart like a widespread house, into which prayer is written—and to Him is the prayer of the generation of children. For it is a logical inference (*Kal va-Chomer*): if the living are bound together, then He surely "hears prayer." This is not just a prayer of hands, as is written regarding "and to you" with the letter *He* <note>referring to a specific orthographic variant in a mystical context</note>. The hint concerns the two points of prayer in the "Beginning" <note>Be-Reshit</note>, as it is written: "to the house of my prayer" and "to Him is the prayer." Specifically, with the voices of wisdom and the tongue which contains **Mercy**, He "hears prayer" from the dedication, and it is unified there. 

"Unto You all flesh shall come" <note>Psalm 65:3</note>, for through the Unification he made the Voice heard—Heaven forbid anything in the world should be excluded—through the "Openings of the Stream" so that he might recognize it. Because he made it heard below, it causes it to be heard and connected above. This is a "double hearing," and it returns to "hearing prayer," according to the verse: "to the voice of the Lord your God." The end of this is "If you will surely listen (*Shamoa Tishma*) to My commandments." And it calls out, "If you will surely listen to the voice of the Lord your God," to awaken the commandment of hearing below, so that you shall hear and be connected to the **Voice of Voices** in the assembly of Israel, the "Voice of God." 

This adds to the statutes of the **Great Name**, for the "Attribute of the Tongue" is the one that mingles. When it is part of the hearing below, the "Attribute of the End" above is also elevated through the word "Hearing," and it awakens the Seal. According to the order of the blessings, so does this attribute rest. In the secret of the Kabbalah, the "Attribute of 26" <note>The numerical value of the Name YHVH</note> is like an **empty vessel** that can hold, whereas a full one cannot hold. The Holy One, Blessed be He, is a "vessel that holds when full, but does not hold when empty" <note>A classic Talmudic paradox from Tractate Berakhot 40a: human vessels hold more when empty, but God "fills" those who are already full of Torah.</note>. You might ask why it says, "If you will surely listen (*Shamoa Tishma*) to the voice of the Lord your God"—repeating the word "listen." It means: if you listen to the old, you will attain the holy; and if you repeat it in your heart, you will never cease to hear.

The intention of the scripture is that every attribute returns to the **Crown** (*Keter*). In the "void of the empty vessel that holds," its purpose for another is that it receives from the source of Wisdom. Just as the Tablet had ten sayings and ten commandments, according to the verse, if one is "empty of all good," he returns to being a vessel. But if—Heaven forbid—one is "full of all good" for the sake of another, in his freedom and his wisdom, then he "does not hold" and instead flows out to others. All of the Holy One, Blessed be He's creatures are meant to sustain one another, filling each other and adding strength to strength. This is why the Sages said: "He saw all His creatures sustaining one another—the day from the night, etc." By being "full," the attribute of the Holy One, Blessed be He "holds" if the ladder is full of Torah and commandments. Behold, it holds and completes the Upper Image in its time, and he establishes it in its requirement. 

Some say: mention the **Great Name** in His glory, and He "strengthens the power in Might" (*Koach ba-Gevurah*). This is the secret of what the Sages said: "The Holy One, Blessed be He, increases strength in the Might" <note>A Kabbalistic concept that human performance of Mitzvot actually increases the divine capacity to act in the world.</note> so that they may be hung by the scepter of His radiance. We have already explained this in the second part of this book. The "empty vessel" neither holds nor completes, and it does not add strength to the Might. This is the secret of the verse "If you will surely listen" (*Shamoa Tishma*). "If you listen" below, if you occupy yourself with the flow of the Torah and the preparation of the Name—this is the "Repair" (*Tikkun*) and the binding to the structure of the Great Name. Then the heavens will perceive the hearing of His voice, and it will be heard above, completing the Unification of the Voice in the act of "Hearing" and the "Remembrance" in the preparation of the Great Name. When his intention is unified toward the **Infinite** (*Ein Sof*), and after he has made it heard in the "old," he will hear in the "new."

<column-break/>

This is to hint that this "Hearing" requires the logic of the verse: that the Unification and the Hearing above have no cessation and no end. Therefore, the one who occupies himself with it must always return to the "old" hearing and listen, and his voice should not "be heard as old." If you do this, you will "hear in the new," which is the praise that spreads and connects above. This is the Torah and the commandments, which are the Path and the Great Repair leading to the Unification. Thus, they never cease, and one should not separate from them even for a moment, returning to his essence above. As it is said: "And you shall meditate on it day and night" <note>Joshua 1:8</note>, for the "Spring of Unification" flows constantly and never stops. 

Regarding all this, they said at the end of the tractate *Moed Katan*: "Torah scholars have no rest, neither in this world nor in the World to Come, as it is said: 'They go from strength to strength; every one of them appears before God in Zion'" <note>Psalm 84:8; Berakhot 64a</note>. The meaning of "rest" here is "cessation" or "nullification," like "and the masters of the night rested." They go on forever. By David's name, it is said "and he rested," meaning he ceased and was weary. But because I said that the scholars of the beginnings occupy themselves with the Torah fully, as in this world, so too in the "Holy Things" that are coming—for these are the "knots" and the "strength of the voice" that fill the Upper Unification to show that it has no cessation. Therefore, they have no "rest"—meaning no cessation or nullification from the Torah—which causes them to be swallowed up in the Unification, whether in this world or the next. 

This is similar to what was said about Joshua the son of Nun <note>Moses' successor</note> at the end of the chapter *Ha-Mocher*: "if they had not been deleted," etc. Rabbi Yannai said, "His hands were great for him." Perhaps they also hinted at this in the connection: "If you do not hear the old, you will hear the new." For if one makes it heard in the world of the living, he will also hear in the World to Come, hearing "innovations" (*Chiddushin*) in the secrets of the Torah and the reasons for the commandments and the wonders of the Unification. This is sweeter than the "old hearing." And it is further renewed in this verse that we have established: they shall see "eye to eye," as it is said, "to see God in Zion." 

This is the secret of the "Sending of the Mouth" <note>likely referring to prophetic speech</note> which is the Unification we explained in the previous chapter. From the heights of these "Sendings," one goes "from strength to strength," which is the secret of "with God in Zion," adding "Strength to the Might," just like the "old" and the "new." To indicate the complete Unification, he said to his friend: "May my prayer be part of the boundary of the heavens," which is the secret of the "Full Name." Furthermore, for the "Words of YHVH" are with the heart of a person in the heavens, in the prayer for the generation. For this, he said: "Hear, O Lord, my voice, and let it be connected to the 'Sound of the Shofar' of my prayer." This is the secret of the unique "Hearing" of the Great Name, which is the "Remembrance" and the "Unification," as we have explained. 

In order to add strength to the structure of the "House of Kingship" <note>the Sefirah of Malkhut</note> and the source of the scriptures, he said: "And now, hear, O our God, the prayer of Your servant." Let Him hear and be connected in prayer. If you intend for this, it is the Prayer, and it is "Supplication" in the secret of "and to His Friend he shall supplicate." The prayer of the righteous and their supplication ascends and is heard above, causing "Hearing" and "Joy," and awakening the Upper Blessings so that He may hear and be comforted. By making the Voice heard to the Name, they cause Him to "rejoice." 

After he explained the "portion of His mouth" for the sake of the building, and the righteous shall know in the future, and to increase His "binding"—he first spoke regarding the "spreading of the colors" <note>referring to the Sefirot</note>. These higher faces are all ours. He said, "And after your face..." and afterwards concerning what was mentioned about the "portion of the mouth" for the "Dwellings of the Place," which is the "Name." And this is "for the sake of my God," so that the "House of Kingship" should be full. He draws near a little to your path, from His arrangements and His secrets that were not revealed. 

To bring it to the First Lady <note>The Matronita or Shekhinah</note>, he said: "My Lord the King, such a palace was built for the sake of the Matronita, so that she should not be outside, and she should not rise outside of her place." In this, he said "Your face" regarding the portion of the Name "for the sake of my God." And thus they returned to the Midrash of Rabbi Shimon bar Yochai, peace be upon him. To awaken this secret, it is written there: "And she came with intention and with a wondrous completion." 
"Incline, O my God, Your ear and hear; open Your eyes and see" <note>Daniel 9:18</note>. With the addition of the letter *Lamed* in these letters to awaken the status of the Holy One. "Hearing the Voice" is the secret of the "Standing" and the "Remembrance" of the Great Name in His glory. Just as the letter *Ayin* <note>meaning "Eye"</note> of these letters is awakened to remind of the Kingship, the "Higher Voice," and the "Judgment," as it is written: "All the eyes..." "All eyes... hear." 

<summary>This page explores the mystical dynamics of prayer and "hearing," explaining how human study and supplication "add strength" to the Divine Might (Gevurah). It uses the metaphor of an "empty vs. full vessel" to describe how spiritual capacity increases through the continuous unification of the Divine Name.</summary>
<keywords>Rashbi, Unification (Yichud), Throne of Glory, Hearing, Matronita, Great Name, Strength in Might, Vessel paradox, Shekhinah</keywords>

<meta>The previous page concluded Chapter 36, focusing on the mystical "Higher Torah" and the unification of divine thought. This page skips forward to Chapter 41, shifting the focus to the "Throne of Glory" (Kise ha-Kavod) and its relationship to the physical and spiritual cosmos.</meta>

-># Chapter 41: The Section of the Purpose<-

The body acquired existence and eternity from Him, so that He might grant it to those He protects. For this reason, the world’s stability and its place bore witness, for the nature of the Source is expansive... <note>The Hebrew text here contains some abbreviated or corrupted OCR strings like "סימשח", likely referring to the joy or expansion of the divine flow.</note> and regarding the King of Kings, she awakened the idea that the Holy One, Blessed be He, was the "place of the world" <note>A classic Rabbinic concept: God is not in the world, the world is in God, hence the name "Ha-Makom" (The Place).</note>... as I have clarified regarding the concept of Place, along with what has been explained elsewhere regarding its status.

### Chapter 41

The Lord has established: **"The Lord has established His throne in the heavens... The heavens are My throne and the earth is My footstool"** <note>original: "Ha-shamayim kis'i ve-ha-aretz hadom raglai"; Isaiah 66:1</note>. It is received by tradition that the "Great Living Creatures" <term>Chayyot: The high-ranking angels described in Ezekiel's vision of the Divine Chariot.</term> each have a throne, for there is a throne above a throne, and no throne is separate from the One who sits upon it. 

The meaning of "the heavens are My throne and the earth is My footstool" does not refer to these physical heavens or this lowly earth. Rather, it refers to the "Heavens" which is a Name of the Holy One, Blessed be He, and the "Earth" refers to the desire <note>original: "chefetz"</note> that exists in the Name, for all the general lights are included within it. The Throne is one thing and the One who sits upon it is another? Heaven forbid! The Sages of Truth <note>A traditional term for Kabbalists.</note> have revealed to us that this is a hidden matter. The intention in the "Chapters of the Chariot" <term>Merkavah: The "Chariot" refers to the mystical study of the divine realm and the structures through which God interacts with the world.</term> is to teach the existence of the Throne and the loftiness of its nature. 

By "His Throne," they mean that which "rides" upon it, which is its very vitality, not something external to it. To show that all the structures of the physical and spiritual Names are intended by His throne, they said: The Holy One, Blessed be He, is "High and Uplifted," and His Throne is "High and Uplifted." And even His garments are "High and Uplifted." He sits upon a "High and Uplifted" Throne.

The Holy One is called "Righteousness" <note>original: "Tzedek"</note>, as it is written: "to remember Righteousness." His Throne is also called "Righteousness," as it is written: "Righteousness and justice are the foundation of Your throne" <note>Psalm 89:15</note>. The Holy One is called "Justice" <note>original: "Mishpat"</note>, as it is written: "For the Lord is a God of justice." So too is His Throne, as mentioned: "Righteousness and justice are the foundation of Your throne," meaning that from there, souls sit for judgment.

The Holy One is called "Truth" <note>original: "Emet"</note>, as it is written: "The Lord God is Truth." His Throne is also called "Truth," as it is written: "And a throne shall be established in mercy, and He shall sit upon it in truth" <note>Isaiah 16:5</note>. The Holy One is called "Glory" <note>original: "Kavod"</note>, as it is written: "Who is this King of Glory?" and He sits upon a "Throne of Glory" in a "Temple of Glory," as it is written: "A glorious high throne from the beginning." 

The Holy One is called "Holy" <note>original: "Kadosh"</note>, and His Throne is likewise called "Holy," as it is written: "God sits upon His holy throne" <note>Psalm 47:9</note. Behold, these descriptions are allusions to the mysteries of the Throne, which is called by the King's own Name. Just as the Savior said in his statement, "For My life is from Him and I shall dwell in Him," the Throne is not a thing separate from God. This strengthens the secret of the "Included Names" mentioned in the secret of the alphabet, through which one understands these visions.

Furthermore, they said in the *Chapters of the Chariot*: One verse says: "His throne was sparks of fire" <note>Daniel 7:9</note>, and another verse says: "Until the thrones were cast down and the Ancient of Days sat." This seems contradictory—is it one throne or two? One for Him and one for David <note>meaning the Messiah</note>. These are the words of Rabbi Akiva. Rabbi Yossi the Galilean said to him: "Akiva! How long will you treat the Divine Presence as profane? Rather, one is for Justice and one is for Charity." But did he accept this? Rabbi Elazar ben Azariah said to him: "Akiva! What have you to do with Aggadah? <note>Aggadah: Non-legal, homiletic, or mystical teachings.</note> Go to the laws of Leprosy and Tents! Rather, one is for a throne and one is for a footstool—a throne to sit upon and a footstool for His feet, as it is written: 'The heavens are My throne and the earth is My footstool.'"

Among the ancient maskilim <note>original: "maskilim"; wise/enlightened ones</note>, there is no real dispute here, only a difference in language. In the truth of the matter, all the masters of tradition agree on one view: the secret is that "One for Him and one for David" refers to the High Throne, which is the mystery of the letter *Vav* and the mystery of the *Khaf* <note>Letters of the Hebrew alphabet used here as mystical ciphers.</note>... and the secret of "Justice" is the secret of the power of the *Aleph*... and the one who said "One for Justice and one for Charity" intended to explain that he sits in judgment and in righteousness. And the "Footstool" that Rabbi Elazar revealed is a mystery in clear language, as he brought proof from the verse "The heavens are my throne and the earth is my footstool." From this, it becomes clear that the intention is not these physical heavens and earth... and the one who understands the Chariot...

<column-break/>

They said that the "Heavens" are the composite heavens and the "Earth" is the lower earth. What is called "Throne" is not a separate entity, but a secret. As the verse says, "The Lord has established His throne in the heavens," the intention is to hint that the Higher Throne is "high above the high," encompassing and surrounding every single firmament like a throne. 

There are seven "chairs" or levels seen by the "Living Creatures." In the sphere of *Arvot* <note>The highest of the seven heavens in Talmudic cosmology.</note>, in the right and second spheres, there are three thrones, and in the "Sovereignty" <term>Malchut: The lowest of the ten Sephirot, associated with divine manifestation in the world.</term> there is one throne. This is the Higher Throne mentioned in the verse "A glorious high throne from the beginning." 

In the sphere of Jupiter <note>original: "Tzedek"</note> there is a throne; in the sphere of Mars <note>original: "Ma'adim"</note> there is a "Throne of the Throne"; in the sphere of Venus <note>original: "Nogah"</note> there is a throne; in the sphere of the Moon <note>original: "Levanah"</note> there is a throne. These are the "Thrones of Sovereignty." The Ruler over them is exalted over all. 

These were not created before the creation of the world; rather, they are what the "Knowers of the Chariot" spoke of as the Throne that is high, uplifted, and exalted far above. It is carved from the "High and Uplifted" light... as seen in the "vision of the sapphire stone"... and this is the mystery of the Throne we mentioned, the secret of the "Included Bride." The Throne is "High" and it is carved in every firmament. 

This is what is meant by "the heavens are My throne and the earth is My footstool"—not that the physical heaven is a chair and the earth is a stool. There is a teaching in the *Covenant of Metatron* that the "Man" of the earth is composed of the Holy Living Creatures and the Throne of Glory is the footstool of the Master of Worlds. Just as there is an intention above, there is an intention below... 

They said "Thrones of Truth" because the intention refers to the lower floors on the pavement of the lowest firmament near us, which is the Sphere of the Moon. This is very well known to those who delve deeply into the Chariot of Ezekiel. 

The explanation for why it says "Throne" in the singular sometimes and "Thrones" in the plural other times is that "Thrones" refers to the Higher Throne, the secret of the "Living" one, while "Throne" refers to the other thrones called "Thrones of Glory," such as those of the Moon and the Sun. According to the first speaker, the mystery of the Throne refers to *this* one, and the second refers to the Lower Throne. The first is prepared for the "Glory" to dwell upon, and the second is the "Footstool." 

Regarding the verse "He sits upon a high and uplifted throne," this is the second throne. As for the "Ten Levels" included in the Great Names, each one is a level unto itself, and each one is reflected and increases in its wisdom. This is the use of the language of "Throne" and "Support." 

The "higher" is like a soul and the "lower" is like a body, and all are founded and established together. This is what Ezekiel intended with the "Throne of Glory"—a likeness of a covering and a dwelling for the Glory. They established that "Throne" is a name for the level of the "Head," a circular head for His Holy Throne... 

Furthermore, the Sages of Truth have a tradition that in the Throne of Glory is the place of the "Living" from below to above. From there, the prayer of the repentant is received, and it is the "Opening of the Gates" of the Throne. For through that secret of the Living Creatures, there is like a "hand" that is extended and stretched out to receive the "Crown of Holiness" and the flow of influence. This is His Throne, as it is written: "And they had the hands of a man under their wings" <note>Ezekiel 1:8</note>. In the *Arava* of the heavens, the hand of the Holy One, Blessed be He, is spread out under the wings of the Living Creatures to receive the repentant.

It reconciles different scriptural descriptions of the Throne and emphasizes its role in receiving human repentance.</summary>
