<meta>This page continues the theological investigation into the nature of the Divine Presence (Shekhinah) and the Divine Glory (Kavod). It specifically engages with the philosophical framework of Maimonides (the "Rav"), who argued that physical descriptions of God in the Bible actually refer to a "Created Light" rather than God’s actual Essence, to avoid the problem of anthropomorphism.</meta>

57 Part of the Purpose, Chapter 57

And it is called *Shekhinah* <term>Shekhinah: the Divine Presence dwelling within the physical world</term> because of the *Mishkan* <term>Mishkan: the Tabernacle, the portable sanctuary in the desert</term>... the Rav [Maimonides] of blessed memory <note>original: "Ha-Rav Z''L"</note> explained that the presence of the *Shekhinah* in a place refers to the "Created Light." This is a divine light that was created to demonstrate the greatness of the Name [God] when it appears in a specific place, as it says: "And I will dwell in the midst of the children of Israel" <note>Exodus 29:45</note>. The place of the Lord and the appearance of the Glory of the Lord were visible to all the observers as part of His Providence. It is His intellect and His quality.

And also His providence is manifested in a way that is not limited by place, for the spiritual is not contained or surrounded by space. Regarding the verse "The Lord has established His throne in the heavens" <note>Psalm 103:19</note>, it means He "sits" in the heavens in a manner appropriate for Him, as the prime mover. The *Shekhinah* of God refers to His kingship and His dominion over the entire world, for the Supreme King rules over all. Therefore, the "Glory of the Lord" is not distant, but rather it joins with the Name of the Lord. Thus, it says that the *Shekhinah* dwells with His glory upon the cherubim. This interpretation of the "Created Light" is what the Rav [Maimonides] emphasized, even as he elevated the concept. 

The "Created Light" of God serves to indicate His providence, may He be blessed. This is a deep subject worthy of contemplation. A second interpretation, which is quite common in various places, explains that the "Created Light" is perceived by the mind's eye when the intellect connects with it. This is how the Lord "dwells" within the sanctuary. Why was this intellectual terminology used? As I explained above, the perception of the intellect is what grasps the divine, without any physical change or multiplicity. This is what Maimonides meant when he commented on the verse "Is the Lord among us?" <note>Exodus 17:7</note>. He argued that the *Shekhinah* refers to this Created Light, which is more hidden from us than anything else. 

And he said that "And He dwelt" means to have a good and beneficial fear of God. From this interpretation, the Kabbalists took the term "Shekhinah of God." They also questioned what is seen in the "Created Light." The logic suggests that it is the universal intellect. Our sages understood that the light mentioned in the Work of Creation—"And God said, 'Let there be light'"—is the light of the intellect. If so, it is hidden and concealed from the eyes of flesh. 

<column-break/>

55 Chapter 55 Part of the Purpose 55

...all the glory which produces fruits for you from the flowing and refined delicacies, as explained regarding the kindness of the Lord. These refined matters are beloved to me, and he shall be glorified for his kindness and mercy. Redeem yourself and grant kindness, and walk in His ways. To seek the Lord and to cleave to His portion is the secret of the "Repair of the Inclusion" <term>Tikkun Ha-Kelul: a Kabbalistic concept of restoring harmony to the divine attributes</term> which is found in the "Sweet Service" <note>referring to Torah study or prayer</note> and the preservation of grace, according to its repair above. I have already expanded on this explanation in the second part of this book.

Furthermore, regarding "following the Lord" and "doing good to one's heart," it stands for a person to walk after the *Shekhinah*. I have already learned that "walking after the Lord" is nothing other than walking after the attributes of the Holy One, Blessed be He: "Just as the Holy One, Blessed be He, clothes the naked... so should you." <note>A famous Talmudic teaching from Sotah 14a on imitating God's kindness</note>. It is all about kindness (*Hesed*). The primary desire for the kindness of the Lord is measured by all that exists in the world. 

Regarding the blessings of the *Tefillin* <term>Tefillin: phylacteries worn during prayer</term>, we intend for the *Shekhinah* to resemble the Supernal Image, to repair the Glory. These are the blessings intended in their repetition... "to order the Lord our God." And this is my work written in this chapter.

## Chapter 55

The Glory (*Kavod*) about which it is written, "And the Glory of the Lord dwelt" <note>Exodus 24:16</note>. "His Glory" is something unique to Him, and Heaven forbid that His unique Glory should be a created thing outside of Himself. The term "The Lord" follows its primary judgment. It has already been explained in the Kabbalah, and it will be further explained, that there is a place for error if one assumes that the Glory dwelling in the Tabernacle and the Temple is a separate creation.

The second interpretation of the *Shekhinah* is that it refers to the Divine Presence as the power of the "Inclusion" <note>the synthesis of divine attributes</note>. The *Shekhinah* in Israel was the superior *Shekhinah* known to the "Masters of the Name" <note>Ba'alei Shem: mystical practitioners</note>. This is what was said regarding the construction of the Temple: "I have sanctified this house... to put My Name there forever; and My eyes and My heart shall be there perpetually" <note>1 Kings 9:3</note>. From here we see that because His Name dwells in the house, His providence, His "eyes," and His "heart" are there perpetually. Because His Name is in Israel, they are supervised by Him. 

This is what is meant by the "Tefillin of the Torah." This is the secret of what is said: "And I will hide My face on that day because of all the evil..." <note>Deuteronomy 31:18</note>. When God is distant, people are in pain due to the "Hiding of the Face." The "Face of Life" is nothing other than His Presence. If the *Shekhinah* were a separate created thing, then the removal of the *Shekhinah* would not be a removal of God's actual providence. But all this is the testimony of the Living God: the *Shekhinah* is not merely a "Created Light," for there is nothing more to the "Created Light" than a separate entity. 

Rather, when His "Face" shines, the kingdom is rejoiced by them. The sages of truth <note>referring to Kabbalists</note> have already revealed this secret in their explanation of "You shall have no other gods before My Face" <note>Exodus 20:3</note>. This means: do not have other gods in the presence of My *Shekhinah*.

To the strength for their subjection. "Awake" and "Arise"—these are the two modes of our conduct, "Our Merciful One" and "Our Magician" <note>This refers to the different ways God interacts with the world, sometimes through overt mercy and sometimes through hidden, seemingly "magical" providence.</note>, thus far his words. Rabbi Shimon bar Yochai <note>original: "RSB''I"</note> on the verse "The eye of the Lord is toward those who fear Him" <note>Psalm 33:18</note> and it is written "The eyes of the Lord wander..." <note>Zechariah 4:10</note>. It means he rose above the "eye" of the evil inclination. And it is written "He who has a bountiful eye [literally: a good eye] shall be blessed" <note>Proverbs 22:9</note>. And if he is after the One, he will be in the lower colors; there is a "returning eye" and an "initial eye." These are two levels, but here there is no eye that changes, for both are on one level, and all of it is return. Therefore, it is "Eye" in the singular and not "Eyes" in the plural.

And the purpose of the eye is not to be a physical eye, but rather to be constantly open, constantly existing, constantly shining, unlike the lower eye which has colors—redness, whiteness, and darkness—because it is not always open, and the eyelashes guard the eye. Regarding this, it is written: "Awake, why do You sleep, O Lord?" <note>Psalm 44:24</note>. "Open Your eyes, O Lord, and see" <note>Daniel 9:18</note>. Then, when the awakening occurs below for strength, the eye is mixed with redness, and that redness descends below to receive it. From here, the Lord's eye moves away from those who distance themselves from Him. And if the King desires to bestow Grace [Chesed] upon them, He will return to them. Concerning this, it is written "He who has a good eye will be blessed," and it is written "House of Jacob, come and let us walk in the light of the Lord" <note>Isaiah 2:5</note>. From here, the mystery of the colors mentioned in this place will be clarified: they are all one, for the Divine Presence [Shekhinah] responds according to the blemish of the sins and the left side. A cloud is placed over the eye, which is the mystery of the judgment mentioned by our predecessors, and from there the light is hidden from the heart when the thinker focuses on the Upper Eye. This darkening is caused by human thought, for everything is according to the recipients. For me, etc., it is turned and reversed, for it is not all a darkening. This is the remainder of what I saw fit to bring at the end of this chapter.

### Chapter 55
**The Sages said:** The "Manna" is also the mystery of the portion dedicated to the King of Peace <note>A common Kabbalistic reference to God</note>, for everything is included within it and returns in sweetness. The explanation of "behold" is the mystery of the eyes, and they are my "beloveds" who will eat the fruit of His choices. His presence increases only for the sake of the union, as it says: "I have come into my garden, my sister, my bride; I have gathered my myrrh with my spice; I have eaten my honeycomb with my honey; I have drunk my wine with my milk" <note>Song of Songs 5:1</note>. And in the Midrash: "My companion [Re'ati]"—what is "my companion"? Rabbi Jonathan said: "Those who sustain Me," for they sustain Me with two offerings every day. And in the Midrash of Rabbi Nehunia ben Ha-Kanah: "They sustain Me here, and they sustain Me there." 

And in the Midrash of the Ramban [Nahmanides] of blessed memory, on this same verse: A woman who comes to lean on the delights of the King from here and further, "No stranger shall eat of the holy thing" <note>Leviticus 22:10</note>. Who is the "stranger"? One who does not recognize the Name of the Holy One below and has no portion in Him; he shall not eat of the holy thing, for he has no path to the eternal sustenance. But "Eat, O friends" <note>Song of Songs 5:1</note>—this is the eating of the upper world, for they are the friends who exist in the place where they eat every day of that which is hidden. Come and see: whenever there is a blessing found below, a blessing is found above for the King. Below, it is from His bounty, and if he is not found to perform his duty, and if he is found to perform his duty, he eats his meal. This is what is written: "I have eaten my honeycomb with my honey, etc." Is it His meal? Rather, the King said "Eat, O friends," and their entire meal should be more than a sacrifice. In this way, they honor the Head, for whatever one does for Him, he does for the sake of the Ancient Holy One. Therefore, the King's meal is mixed with the meal of his servant. In this way, Israel sustains the righteous ones who are humble. Thus far his words. And the aforementioned "sustenance" is the mystery of the overflow of everything, which is watered by the light that shines from the beginning to the end, which is the "honor of the dwelling" that is called by the Great Name. The "Great Soul" is the mystery of the living water, the water of the world, and He placed it

in the sanctuary for the sake of the whole, and according to the accepted path in this book. And in the Midrash: all the "eating" and "drinking" mentioned in this book are nothing other than Wisdom [Chokmah]. For the true, traditional Wisdom is the food that sustains the soul and gives it life. Likewise, compare it to the Upper Wisdom, for from it comes the life of everything. Whatever is "eaten" from it through the refinement of thought and its clinging to the sources is nothing other than the Torah, which brings the whole world to one place, for Wisdom is the "Primeval Torah." Just as through physical eating and drinking the soul and body are sustained below, so too, through the light and the flow that comes from the Source above, the whole is sustained from beginning to end. This is the mystery of the "eating" mentioned regarding the realms above. 

And in the Midrash of Rabbi Shimon bar Yochai, when Rabbi Shimon was walking on the way, he opened with: "My beloved is like a gazelle" <note>Song of Songs 2:9</note>. He said to him: "Peace be upon you." He said to him: "You have done a new thing in the heavens." He said to him: "Through the sacrifices you have acted," and he said words that refreshed his mind. In one moment, he returned to his place in peace. "And I have one thing I wish to ask you, which I found in the 'Heavenly Ledger': In the world to come, there is no eating or drinking, yet it is written: 'I have come into my garden, my sister, my bride; I have gathered my myrrh with my spice; I have eaten my honeycomb with my honey; I have drunk my wine with my milk'?" 

Rabbi Shimon said: "And what did you answer?" He said to him: "I said that this refers to the 'eating' of the world to come, which is not physical eating and drinking." 

### Chapter 57
Rabbi Shimon said: Come and see how much the Sages have labored to explain this. ## Chapter 57

**Concerning** the purpose of our intention, and thus we have received its literal and mystical meaning <note>original: "Peshat and Sod"</note> from the prophets who were chosen to be like a legal decree. This may be the literal meaning and this the secret, regarding what is said "on high" <note>meaning, in the divine realms</note>. They acknowledge that relative to the "Great Name" <note>The Tetragrammaton, YHWH</note>, it is only because He desired us. It is He who said, "Let us make man" <note>Genesis 1:26</note>. Understand the matter we have written: from all this good, which is a mighty inheritance, He honored him among the many. This is like a king who built a palace through an architect who saw it through, but it did not please him until the end. He was then angry with the architect; thus, "He was grieved at His heart" <note>Genesis 6:6</note>. Another interpretation: This is like a king who made a decree through his scribe, and it turned out poorly. Against whom should he complain? Against the scribe. Thus, "He was grieved at His heart." The "King" is the secret of the Great Name; the "Scribe" is "Man" <note>original: "Adam"</note>, who is the seat and the throne of glory upon which He sits. He made him through the "architect" <note>the creative forces/Sefirot</note> as we have written. He saw him, but he did not please Him because the intention was not completed, nor was the prepared light drawn from the Source—for this is the purpose of the intellect—and then He was angry with the "architect." Rabbi Asher added to the parable that the King made the palace to profit from it and be glorified by its honor, but he did not profit, nor did the Light from above rest upon it, but rather it was lost. In its loss, a "husk" <note>original: "Kelipah," a force of spiritual impurity</note> rose above the "Grape-clusters" <note>the holy realms</note> because the lower realm caused a separation between a man and his wife <note>metaphorically, between God and the Shekhinah</note>. No blessing rests there unless there is a single union. And regarding "they rebelled and grieved His holy spirit" <note>Isaiah 63:10</note>: "rebelling and defying" are the group of the "Satan," and the Targum translates "His holy spirit" as "His holy prophets" <note>referring to the spirit of prophecy</note> because of the holiness of the Holy Spirit. Through their actions, they caused the Holy Spirit not to rest among them. In the power of the light and the flow, the whole "accounting" <note>the divine administration</note> functions like a pillar of smoke at the entrance of a furnace. Because they overturned the word—for the generation of the flood was from the side of the soul of deceit—"He turned to be their enemy; He fought against them" <note>Isaiah 63:10</note>. This is the secret of the verse: Attribute of Mercy turned into the Attribute of Judgment <note>original: "Middat Ha-Rachamim turned to Middat Ha-Din"</note>. Everything is according to their deeds. Such is the way of the world: if they were not corrupted by their actions, they would have lived in peace. And these matters are taught in the *Chagor* <note>a section of text or study circle</note>: Rabbi Shmuel bar Chiya said in the name of Rav: "The Holy One has a place where He weeps, and its name is *Mistaraim* <note>original: "Hidden Places," based on Jeremiah 13:17</note>." Why? Because of the "Body" <note>of the Divine</note>. Rabbi Shmuel bar Yitzchak said: "Because of the exile of Israel, who were removed from their place and brought to the nations of the world." Rabbi Shmuel bar Nachmani said: "Because of the exile of the Kingdom of Heaven." But is there any weeping before the Holy One? Did not Rav Papa say, "There is no sorrow before the Holy One," as it is said, "Splendor and majesty are before Him" <note>1 Chronicles 16:27</note>? There is no contradiction: one refers to the "outer houses" <note>original: "Batei Barai"</note> and the other to the "inner houses" <note>original: "Batei Gevai"</note>. In the "inner houses," there is no sorrow. But what about the verse, "My soul shall weep in secret places" <note>Jeremiah 13:17</note>? That refers to the time when even the "Angels of Peace" <note>original: "Malachei Shalom"</note> wept, as it is written: "Behold, the valiant ones shall cry without; the angels of peace shall weep bitterly" <note>Isaiah 33:7</note>. Some explain that this refers to the "Name," and the "inner houses" etc., and this is the version of the Master of Kabbalah, Rabbi Todros Ha-Levi <note>a 13th-century Spanish Kabbalist</note>, and he wrote in this language: "Some explain it refers to the Name, and in the 'inner houses' there is no weeping." This is a scribe's error, for it is impossible, since the verse and the proof are for the future. He asked: how can it be said the "Angels of Peace" weep? Behold, the "Erelim" <note>a high class of angels</note> are identified with them... but this Midrash's intention is according to the Way of Truth <note>meaning the Kabbalah</note> and the secret of the matter. For the "inner houses" are the inner Crowns <note>the Sefirot</note> of the Upper World, and there is no lack or evil there, only light.

<column-break/>

And now we will clarify the statement "Splendor and majesty are before Him" and its relation to "His place." For the "Place" that is above the level of the "Living Creatures" <note>original: "Chayot," referring to the angels of the Chariot</note>—where they have no permission to enter—is called "His Place," which is designated for Him alone, and no strangers enter. Everything there is joy, and there is no weeping or bitterness of heart. But the "chambers" and "thresholds" are called the "outer houses," where the powers of the "Chariots" <note>original: "Merkavot"</note> and the "Hosts" exist. From there come the weeping, the prayer, the exile, and all kinds of grief and sorrow. For there, the "Face of Mercy" is hidden, and the "Attribute of Judgment" <note>original: "Middat Ha-Din"</note> prevails. The decree of the "Secret Places" refers to the "hiding of the Face" mentioned on high, and the places where the Face of the King and Mercy are hidden. Concerning this, they said: "The Holy One has a place where He weeps, and its name is *Mistaraim*." Thus it is clarified: one refers to the "inner houses" and the other to the "outer houses." However, they questioned whether there is weeping in the "inner houses" at all, citing the verse "And He called to his Father," etc. Even in the "inner houses," the text proves this. We have clarified the holy names associated with this matter, which will prove that even in the "inner houses"—which are the most primary levels—there was weeping during the destruction of the Temple, both above and below. Even the "Angels of Peace" wept, and tears flowed from above to below. Regarding "I will weep and shed tears," Rabbi Eliezer said: "He sheds three tears: one for the First Temple, one for the Second Temple, and one for Israel who were exiled from their place." Like the lower eyes, the eyes of the "Small Face" <note>original: "Zeir Anpin," the more manifest aspect of God</note> have three colors: white, red, and a dark white. These represent the three bitter tears that descend—meaning they are not withheld—and these are the "overflows" derived from Judgment. This weeping was over the destruction of the Temple on high, the Temple below, and the exile of Israel. In the chapter "The Beheaded Heifer" <note>original: "Eglah Arufah," a section of the Talmud</note>, it is mentioned that the Holy One, when He remembers His children who are in pain among the nations of the world, lets fall two tears into the Great Sea, and their sound is heard from one end of the world to the other. In the *Zohar*, it is said: "The Holy One, blessed be He, struck His two eyes together, and from the colors of white and red, two tears emerged." Every house of the Holy One and the "Holy Ones" <note>the righteous</note> will weep for Israel. These two tears are found on the day of Judgment. What is "the wisdom of the heart"? It means those who will be seen in the light of the "Hidden One" <note>original: "Mechasseh"</note>, to bring out the great wisdom and fill the spirit of Israel. Generally, understand that the "Indwelling Presence" <note>original: "Shekhinah"</note> is grieved on high because she is the source of the flow. In the chapter "The Beheaded Heifer," it says: "Every single day, the 'Watchers' stand on the platform and say: 'Awake, why do You sleep, O Lord?' <note>Psalm 44:24</note>." Does sleep exist before the Omnipresent? Has it not already been said: "Behold, the Guardian of Israel neither slumbers nor sleeps" <note>Psalm 121:4</note>? Rather, because Israel is placed in sorrow while the nations of the world are in tranquility, it says "Awake, why do You sleep?" In the Jerusalem Talmud, Tractate Ma'aser Sheni, it mentions those who "Awaken" Him, saying "Awake, why do You sleep?" Does sleep exist before Him? Since it says He neither slumbers nor sleeps, why does it say "Then the Lord awoke as one out of sleep" <note>Psalm 78:65</note>? This is only "as if it were possible" <note>original: "Kivyachol," a term used to qualify anthropomorphisms</note>, because when Israel is in trouble and the nations are in tranquility, He is like one asleep. This is also the meaning of "until the shadows flee." According to the "Way of Truth" <note>Kabbalah</note>, there is no difficulty: on the level of the "Long Face" <note>original: "Arich Anpin," the most transcendent level of God</note>, there is no change or shadow, only great mercy. There is no sleep there, for the "Eye of Mercy" is always open. Of this it is said: "He neither slumbers nor sleeps." There, He is the "Guardian of Israel" <note>referring to the higher spiritual Israel</note>. However, below, in the place called "Small Face" <note>Zeir Anpin</note>, there are "eyelids," and right and left, and front and back. These are the "branches" from the Long Face, to the right and left. There, the eyes are not always open like the eyes of the Long Face. Of this it is said: "Awake, why do You sleep, O Lord?" "Neither slumbers nor sleeps" refers to the "Seal of the Shekhinah" which...

**His Presence** <note>original: "Shekhinato"</note>—**and His soul was grieved by the misery of Israel** <note>Judges 10:16</note>. The intention is that He was present in the misery of Israel, following the principle: *In all their affliction, He was afflicted* <note>Isaiah 63:9</note>. According to its plain meaning, the Sages interpret this in the context of a final judicial sentence: When a person is in pain, what language does the Divine Presence <note>original: "Shekhinah"</note> use? "My head is heavy for me, my arm is heavy for me" <note>Mishnah Sanhedrin 6:5; it expresses God’s deep empathy even for the suffering of the guilty</note>. And the time drew near... [philological discussion of the word "grieved" and "shortened"]. Regarding the verse, some translate it as "He was weary," following the context of His mercy and His soul. The actions were transformed... like a legal decree. The meaning would be a "shortening" or "limitation" that occurred because of the severity of the decree... and he gave them movement and allowed them to perceive... He considered mercy for them and satisfied His will by having pity on them.

<margin>The Great Master <note>likely R. Bahya ben Asher</note> wrote here that the "Soul" <note>original: "Nefesh"</note> mentioned refers to the Divine Presence, for she is the "Soul" of the divine attributes. It says, "My soul shall not loathe you," because since she is within us, she will not distance herself from us.</margin>

**And my soul shall not loathe you**—regarding the "Soul" of the divine attributes, which is the Divine Presence. Since they are her "prey" <note>metaphorical for those sustained by her</note> and they are connected to her, and she is the single crown that receives them all. If you grasp this, it is necessary for the cycle of existence. For the entire foundation of man is that he exists within the secret of the "Measures" <note>term: Middot - the divine emanations or attributes</note>. This is the matter written: "In one seven" <note>likely referring to a cycle of seven years or attributes</note>. According to its plain meaning, the language contains hints... and in the expansion of Rabbi Shimon bar Yochai <note>the traditional author of the Zohar</note> on this: "And I will set my dwelling among you" <note>Leviticus 26:11</note>. He explains: Since My dwelling is among you, I will not separate from you... "And my soul shall not loathe you"—this is the Great Master's statement about Himself. The general principle in our saying "the soul of every living thing" <note>from the liturgy</note> is that He gives souls and spirits, for all are included in one another. Therefore, when we say "soul," we mean the Essence. This is what the verse establishes in this chapter.

<column-break/>

**Two authorities** <note>original: "Reshuyot"</note>—for in their days they were receiving [foreign influences] and would rebel against the Holy One, blessed be He. When it was written about them, they were angering their Creator for generations to come... they were drawn after shameful things. And "My soul" relates to the gate. They were claiming "on high" <note>in the spiritual realms</note>... as it is written: **My spirit shall not strive with man forever** <note>Genesis 6:3</note>. This means: My spirit, which I have influenced into man, shall not be diminished for the sake of the shame they have brought. I will not prolong their days because of the shame of their sins... but rather, a hundred and twenty years I will give them to repent. And if they do not, I will bring the flood and the decree. Afterward it is written: **For he is also flesh**—meaning, there is no reason to be agitated in the world by saying that people are only held by my vision... for I have already mourned for the first man <note>Adam</note>... they crossed the covenant.

According to the way of the Sages <note>original: "Rabbotenu"</note>, the intention regarding "My Spirit" <note>original: "Ruchi"</note> refers to the Holy Spirit, which is the "Soul" of the generation. How the spirit of the Lord is elevated here... as it is mentioned: *The spirit of wisdom and understanding, the spirit of counsel and might, the spirit of knowledge and the fear of the Lord* <note>Isaiah 11:2</note>. The intention is that Adam caused the covenant to be flawed in the world, which consists of the **four shells** <note>term: Kelipot - the "husks" or forces of impurity in Kabbalah: the stormy wind, the great cloud, the flashing fire, and the translucent glow</note>. Corresponding to these are the four holy spirits which include all the virtues. These are the attributes of Wisdom, Understanding, Knowledge, Might, and Kindness. The intention of the Exodus from Egypt was to cause the Divine Presence to dwell among them... as it is written: **And they shall know that I am the Lord their God who brought them out of the land of Egypt, that I may dwell among them** <note>Exodus 29:46</note>. Thus it is explained that the purpose of the Exodus was the indwelling of the Presence within them.

## Chapter 62
**The Name:** Which he did not come to bring forth. "His soul" is written... it refers to the soul of David. These things point to a single matter... let the Name of the Lord be blessed. His Name is upon Israel, that His Presence may dwell within them. Every "Soul" attributed to the Place <note>term: HaMakom - a rabbinic name for God</note> is the secret of the light of His attributes... the body of the Divine Presence.

## Chapter 63
**Living God:** Who is among the wise of the generation... the Great Name from the foundation of His glory. It is prepared in its holiness... "My soul yearns" to bring into the "Living God." This is the secret of the "Living God" mentioned by David... Who is the Lord? He is Life itself, and not from anything else.

<meta>This page continues the exploration of spiritual perfection (Shlemut) and the "Purpose" (Takhlit) of existence. # Chapter 66
### Chapter 66
From what we have written, it will be clarified that the perfection we mentioned has reached its foundation only through the performance of the **commandments** <note>original: "Mitzvot"; the 613 religious duties in Judaism</note> and their actual fulfillment. For the Creator necessitated the perfect design of the **Chariot** <note>original: "Merkavah"; the visionary chariot of God's throne, symbolizing the structure of the divine realms</note>, mentioning and dividing it as we have explained. Since all the instruments of action are the primary cause, the intention behind them was the actual service and the pursuit of the **purpose** <note>original: "Takhlit"</note> for which they were created. This is the foundation. It is said that unless they were like a forged judgment, the physical delights of action would be the largest part of the Torah, because their fulfillment is required in actuality at all times. For the merit and preservation of life is only in the intellect and the voice of Zion, the primary ladder of His ways always.

As is known, there is an advantage to the purity and preservation of the word. Just as the fulfillment of the positive commandments in action is the cause for the preparation and preservation of the world, so too is the fulfillment of the negative commandments <note>prohibitions</note> and the preservation of the Chariot against any blemish or power of transgression, preventing it from being stolen from us. This is the virtue and the preservation of the foundational principle of the Torah in its generality, with its nuances and details. For when the perfect person subdues his **inclination** <note>original: "Yetzer"; the inner drive or impulse</note>, forcing it and humbling the "Great Anger," His glory is unified and exalted in His world. This is the chapter of virtue and preservation. In this way, the "negative" is transformed and merged into the "positive." This is the secret of the attribute of Justice being sweetened by Mercy, which is the source of its preservation in the world. This is the fruit of all the services: the **Crown** <note>the highest Sephirah/attribute</note> will repair the evil and the "shades" to mend them so that all becomes good.

A person might mistakenly think that his rise depends only on his time and wisdom of the Law, but it is written: *"And you shall love the Lord your God with all your heart"* (Deuteronomy 6:5). As written in the chapter *Ha-Ro’eh* <note>a section of the Talmud, Berakhot 54a</note>: "with both your inclinations—the good inclination and the evil inclination." For the duty of mending all paths toward Fear and sweetening them is cast upon us, just as they were in the **Higher Thought** <note>the divine plan</note> before they descended. For then, they were an absolute and exalted good. Therefore, even in our current state, when we remember the "evil," we must clarify the good and the mercy within it so that no part of it remains neglected. This is the secret of **reintegration** <note>original: "Hashlamah"; the process of making something whole again</note>... as we wrote in its place. 

Since all of this is the perfection of the merit of action, this part on virtue was established to show that its fulfillment is the ultimate purpose and the intention, just as the actual fulfillment of the commandments belongs to the side of **Kindness** <note>original: "Chesed"</note>, the secret of Great Wisdom. In the *Sefer Ha-Kaneh*, I saw this aspect explained: all the commandments are intended to lower the divine flow from the high and perfect path to the lower world. The commandments of action and the negative commandments are all directed toward the path we have written; their purpose is the preservation of the Foundation, which turns in its changes upon its essence. This is a correct secret and a perfect necessity.

In the wisdom of the chapter of Rabbi Akiva, Rabbi Eleazar said: "When Israel prioritized 'We will do' over 'We will hear,' a Divine Voice went out and said to them: 'Who revealed to my children this secret that the **Ministering Angels** <note>original: "Malakhei ha-Sharet"</note> use?' For it is written: *'Bless the Lord, O His angels, mighty in strength, who do His word, to hear the voice of His word'* (Psalms 103:20)—first 'doing' and then 'hearing.'" For whoever is refined in their essence and tied to action as a major part of this perfection—this is their necessity and their name, more so than their intellectual comprehension. This is their preservation, looking upon those causes that give life. They are different from their Creator in strength and power... as it is written: *"He declares His power."* They express this through the physical bodies, while the comprehension and the priority within them belong to the submission and the wisdom that precedes the submission of the intellect, as the soul says regarding the physical existence, being prior in the knowledge of the generation. For He is the speaker to all nature through these flows, holy in His knowledge.

According to the way of learning, it is proper that **action** should precede **hearing** <note>understanding</note>, for action is what is prior from above to below in the order, so that the intention and purpose are in the deed. This is why Israel prioritized "We will do" over "We will hear." This is what they meant by "Who revealed to my children this secret?" For it is a great secret that the purpose of action is prior in the way we have written. And as the Rabbis of blessed memory said in this language: "When Israel stood before Him and were willing to sacrifice their lives for the Holy One, blessed be He, their preservation was in 'doing' before 'hearing' in its holiness, and afterwards 'doing' and 'hearing' in the lower world..."

<sig>N G 3 18 Purpose</sig>

<column-break/>

...in the likeness of the **Chariot and the Throne of Glory** <note>the structure of the divine manifestation</note>, to teach about the Inner Higher End which is called by this name. There, eye is for eye, hand is for hand, foot is for foot, and so with all the external parts. The Sages of Truth have a sign for this: we have learned that "one limb supports another limb." For the perfect person completes himself to establish the lower action. And our crown and the crown of our salvation will be hidden in our limbs... and he perfects and completes all his limbs to resemble the structure of the **Macrocosm** <note>original: "Ha-Shalem ha-Gadol"; the "Great Perfect One" or Primordial Man</note>. Then he is perfected in His likeness. For when every limb within him is perfected through the specific commandments assigned to us, he is then in the likeness of that Form which was established in His image. 

Through the teachings, a person must establish the structure of his limbs to match the Higher Structure. For this reason, hands and feet are mentioned in the Torah... to show that a person should direct his hands and perfect them in the way that "hands correspond to hands," and so too with the rest of his limbs. He should always be mindful of his internal part and his soul, and the doors to the Higher Life.

As a sign, all his limbs in the laws of the commandments come as a Chariot and a Throne of Glory toward the Higher Likeness. Regarding this, the Sages of blessed memory said: "The **Patriarchs** <note>Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob</note> are themselves the Chariot." For they became a Chariot for the attribute of **Kindness** <note>Chesed</note> because Abraham's actions were straight, and he sanctified His name and the truth of His image. He worked with his "right hand" in perfection. There is a hint in this when he said: *"I have lifted my hand to the Lord, God Most High"* (Genesis 14:22). It was revealed to us through his limbs that he was established according to the Higher Name, and his memory was revealed as holy and pure. Thus he became a Chariot for the attribute of Kindness. In this way, Isaac was a Chariot for the attribute of **Fear** <note>original: "Pachad"; associated with Gevurah or Judgment</note>, and Jacob for the attribute of **Truth** <note>Emet/Tiferet</note>. 

And King David, may peace be upon him, of whom it is written that his kingdom was fitting, for it says: *"And David made a name for himself."* He was the **fourth leg** of the Chariot <note>The Chariot is often described as having four supports: the three Patriarchs and King David representing the Sephirah of Malkhut (Kingship)</note>. This was fulfilled as I have written. This depends on the level of intention and the "Wheels" of the Torah. 

The ancient Form which He prepared and perfected is glorified through the Torah. It is the **Form of Man** <note>original: "Tzurat Adam"</note> that he repaired and perfected in secret. All the visions symbolize the "Man" who is God, the "Man" sitting upon the Throne—He is the Chariot. As Rabbi Yannai already wrote: "The name of the Holy One, blessed be He, is combined with the name of Israel." It is written: *"And I have sworn by My holiness"*... and Rabbi Yehuda bar Simon said: "Do we have a verse more explicit than this? *'And upon the likeness of the throne was a likeness as the appearance of a man upon it above'* (Ezekiel 1:26)."

This is exactly what we wrote: that the intentions prepare and perfect the design for the building of the Great Whole. They stand as the Likeness with its foundation. This is the secret of the perfect ones: this Form is recognized through the perfection of their actions. Thus they merit the level of the Intention that flows from that Form which we have sent. It will return him in the likeness of its form, which is the Form of Man, to let it be known that he has a likeness and a structure in His image. For the Form is recognized as a great and mighty matter, much greater than the "Perfect Whole" over the "Incomplete." Who can speak of this? Even the great verse brought by Rabbi Yochanan does not lack this meaning: one could say "He is Man," and not "as a man," but it says "And I saw," referring to the separate emanations. Only one who has ascended to the level of the Intention... for this, Rabbi Yehuda brought a verse from which the matter is more clearly explained. 

We will divide this into Chapter 28... and there is more to this. All perfection reaches the person who completes his likeness and purifies his limbs, which are established in the likeness of those who comprise the Chariot. Thus, these are in the likeness of those. You have a place for this preparation, to return us to it, for our necessity is great in the Higher Likeness. He prepares the Higher Limbs—hands and feet—to match the hands in this place, so that the actions of the children of man will be completed, to sanctify their hands, their feet, their eyes, and their ears, until they merit to be joined and unified as one. Then they are "kind with their kind," for they are the "sustenance" of the whole. This is the **Cleaving** <note>original: "Deveikut"; mystical union with God</note> spoken of: "To give the cleaving of the Lord... which is not found in anything else." The form of cleaving and attachment is as it is written: *"But you who cleave to the Lord your God are alive every one of you this day"* (Deuteronomy 4:4). This is what our Rabbi intended to work on in this chapter.

# Section of the Purpose Chapter 68 | Chapter 64

...as in the balsam, and you shall separate them between the species and the whole. This is the **secret of the wet wings** <note>original: "Sod ha-knafayim ha-luchiyot"; refers to spiritual emanations that are still receptive to divine flow</note> and the wings of the **Holy Names** which clothe themselves and are called "garments." These are the secret of the "coats of skin" <note>original: "Kotnot Or"; referring to the skins God made for Adam and Eve, often contrasted in Kabbalah with "coats of light"</note> which the King of the Chariot <term>Chariot: the Merkavah, or the divine assembly surrounding God’s throne</term> caused to be inherited by Israel at the time of the exile, as it says: "I have washed my feet, how shall I soil them?" <note>Song of Songs 5:3</note>. This means: Behold, hear the wings called the "Sabbath Garment" within the realms of the **uncircumcised shells** <note>original: "Klipot ha-arelah"; the spiritual "husks" or "shells" that conceal divine light</note>. And behold, I have left them face to face without any cause, and I have no desire for them. Why are they drawn by your evil deeds to turn away? I will hide my face from you, and it will be fulfilled that the fruit of your thoughts has left you with the fantasies that have misled you.

I have seen the feet of the secret of the **Understanding** <note>original: "Binah"; the third Sephirah or divine attribute, associated with the Divine Mother</note> which brings peace, the feet that tread down the uncircumcision. I will lie down, and your deeds caused her to be enslaved under it, and they placed my dwelling in darkness. However, when the Master of the world is appeased and the Torah is strengthened, and everything is sweetened for Him in the **Unification** <note>original: "Yichud"; the meditative act of declaring God's oneness</note> of the secret of the pious **Spheres** <note>original: "Sephirot"; the ten attributes through which God interacts with the world</note>, held fast in the mirror of the **Living Creatures** <note>original: "Chayot"; the high-ranking angels who carry the divine throne</note>, then the wings appear to provide honor to the King and the Bride, like a woman to her husband. There is no evil spirit there, and the secret of holiness is sweetened, saying: "Spirit and wind in your palms for your life." This means from the hidden place they shall not behold our beauty, for you are an abomination. This is what I have been shown to pass through the palm mentioned in the place of the **Name** <note>original: "Sod Y-H-V-H"</note>, etc., in the hidden intention at the end of the chapter.

### Chapter 68

Behold, the **Guide** <note>original: "Ha-Moreh"; referring to Maimonides' philosophical work "The Guide for the Perplexed"</note> in Chapters 30 and 60, if he did not mention the change of the administrations according to their species... the end of the matter is his saying that all that is now in the language of human beings—see there—is because all that is possible for human beings is according to their preparation and their initial thought. It is worthy of explanation. Even if one is assisted by the hands of the souls that are bound to him, which are his wisdom entirely, this is the lack at the beginning of the thought of his rest. For then it is in the thought alone, and this is why it is not called by the name "Yah" <note>a shorter form of the Divine Name</note> in the brain... and this is the end of the matter that the masters of the **Spheres** <note>original: "Galgalim"; literally "circles" or "celestial orbs"</note> use as an excuse. This is worthy to be known by the first wisdom that did not mention these changes, for they did not see the form of the world in its entirety so as to serve it. 

The light of the Torah is that there is evidence for these powers, for the form in its quantity is chosen: "In the beginning God created" <note>Genesis 1:1</note>. Behold, it testifies to the primordial Divinity from man, and from this it is called the "Testimony of the Lord," as it is a testimony to the Divinity of the **Name**. And the sages and the **Tradition** <note>original: "Kabbalah"</note> correspond to the writing of the world, which is distant in our eyes in its chambers. Upon the sea, they fulfilled the testimony of God. This distant memory is the center of the knowledge of evil, capable of the movements of the Manna. Upon this, the preparation and its words are focused. The middle ones in the house of the Master have no relation to these preparations, yet they point to Him through their movements. Why was this said of me? To delay in the matters that point to the souls bound to Him.

But these matters are among the gates of the Torah which cannot be understood through logic or human investigation, but only through the **Wisdom received from the Prophets** reaching back to Moses at Sinai. It has already been explained in our previous words that the **Small Man** <term>Microcosm: the human being as a reflection of the universe</term> is sweetened in his making and preparation in the likeness of the **Great Man** <term>Macrocosm: the divine structure of the universe</term>, who includes all the general forms in the Great Name, called in metaphor "the Man sitting upon the Throne."

It will further be clarified that in the true movements there are memories and turnings in their house, spiritual and subtle to the ultimate degree. These are the **Parts of the Chariot** <note>original: "Pirkei ha-Merkavah"</note>. From them comes the thought of "behind" and the spreading of the existence of **Trust** <note>original: "Bitachon"</note>, which is the delight in our knowledge. They are called the "Handles of the Feet" <note>original: "Yedot Raglayim"</note>... not like the physical palms of hands, but in their preparations. These are symbolic of the female and male... and as it were, a complete image from the side of the form and preparation, as clarified in the secret of the Sanctuary. Indeed, in the preparation and the turning in this death, to indicate that he is worthy of the secret which returns and achieves through the revealed powers, so it shall be in the soul alone.

<column-break/>

The secret of the **Reincarnation** <note>original: "Gilgul"</note> is the preparation of them all to join the Body. These are entirely the secret of my visions, for he is in the life itself. Therefore, he is called "Living Brain," and he is the **Source of Life**, as it is written: "For with You is the fountain of life" <note>Psalms 36:9</note>. When they cease in the portion of life, it is the secret of his death... and they create life for him forever. This is the secret of "giving them into trust," etc. And conversely, "you who are alive today." Regarding you it was said: "Wash and be clean before you today the life." This "Good" is the **Way of Life**, and also the **Way of Death** in his saying "and this is the death and the evil." This is the secret of the wicked males who are outside, from whom death and evil are drawn, corresponding to life and good. As it is clarified in the scripture: "I have set before you life and death, the good and the evil" <note>Deuteronomy 30:15</note>. To cleave to the scripture and to be within its vitalities. 

He said to them that they have committed two evils against Him, for in Him is the **Fountain of Living Waters**, corresponding to the life that they shall acknowledge there... and life is the cleaving to His eternity, which is my kingdoms that are perfected below... so that they may be in the ultimate freedom, which they do not understand today. Corresponding to the existence and the knowledge that there are hidden kindnesses there, which are drawn into the union. Because of this, sin, iniquity, and their purity were drawn to them. The secret of the one who cleaves to life: behold, the secret of the great good is that which **Jacob** achieved in dreams and the holiness of the vitalities. This is the truth, to hold onto the Divinity of the **Wisdom of Israel** as a gift and a chain. From the evil within it, one shall acquire the vitality and the attainment of the "Permission." We have been comforted by the "forged wisdom," the **Wisdom of the Nations** <note>original: "Chokmat ha-Kutim"; literally "Wisdom of the Samaritans," used here for non-sacred philosophy</note>. 

And regarding the union... "I have said I shall live forever." For above it was said that the "Fear of God" and nothing else is strong and great, and the order of the Service is almost the skeleton... the **Beauty of Israel** <note>original: "Tiferet Yisrael"; the central Sephirah associated with balance and the patriarch Jacob</note>. This is the attainment of "Anger," for **Understanding** <note>Binah</note> caused it through the corruption of their deeds. Say now, in the "Time of Favor" for the lover of the heavens, that through prayer he shall be answered... and I said, "He is the life of my heart forever." Everything is in one **Unification**, for this is the secret of the choice waters in the place, etc. This is the measure of what we have seen fit to explain in this chapter.

### Chapter 69

"In the shadow of Your wings let us be hidden" <note>referencing Psalms 17:8</note>. "And you shall be hidden in the secret of Your wings, Selah." The secret is that "there is one law for the maidservant" under his wings. The intention is regarding these lacks, for she is a covering for the higher ones. For she is the "dawn and the frost," the Great Name... "The Lord is in His holy Temple." 

Regarding the secret of the **Rashbi** <note>Rabbi Shimon bar Yochai, the traditional author of the Zohar</note> on the verse "Upon the earth we have heard songs": It is not like the rest of the world. "Songs we have heard" in the secret of the night. Songs at night, songs, and we shall rise. For she rises at night, she rises at night in the exile. At night and during the day she is far off and not found. And when she is there to praise the Holy One, Blessed be He, and to be protected... then there are songs at night.

"Songs to her Creator, He will not be cut off." It is written: "He will change the servants." Those who are strong are released. And he spreads his palms to the established one and the foundation of your right hand... the secret of the **Jacob**, the secret of the **Seal of Solomon** <term>Seal of Solomon: a mystical symbol of protection and divine authority</term>. And under the crown... and He shall take in his hand the choice of your peace... and then she is pious with the grace of **Abraham**. He separated with the secret of the "gathering," and the wall that surrounds you. After that, he spreads his palms... when the Grace of the assembly is received. When **Jacob** is joined, then he pours out goodness to the perfect one, according to the test and refinement in his palms which belonged to Abraham. 

The secret of it is that the corruption of the creations and their deeds in their exiles is in the **Unification**. The lack within it shall be repaired, for there are the "Husks of the Uncircumcision" <note>Kelipot</note>.

-># Chapter 66 - Part of the Purpose - Chapter 67<-

This is the conduct appropriate for one who is not yet a master of intellect in their work. It is well known that conduct through the application of **intellectual concepts** <note>original: "מושכלות עיוניות" (moshkalot iyuniyot); abstract philosophical or scientific truths reached through reason</note>—in both their deficiency and their abundance—surpasses the practice of ethical traits. Without a doubt, the wisdom of the Torah is more inclusive and universal. Furthermore, standing upon the **demonstrative intellectual concepts** <note>original: "מושכלות עיוניות מופתיות"; truths proven through logic or mathematical demonstration</note> is a very exalted state, much like the wisdom of the paths of the Torah, the knowledge of its true meanings, and the performance of its commandments.

You can see this by observing those who contemplate the **Ladder of Sciences** <note>original: "Sulam ha-Chokhmot"; a traditional curriculum moving from lower to higher knowledge</note>—namely, the Mathematical, the Natural, and the Divine sciences. Within the general Mathematical sciences, which include Arithmetic, Geometry, Music, and Astronomy:

*   **Arithmetic** <note>original: "ha-mispar"</note> alone, along with research, provides the foundation for paths of intelligence. It is essential when one encounters precise numbers in the Torah, such as values and appraisals, or the analytical wisdom needed in the Talmud to examine the various opinions and requirements of the Law to understand the true nature of the craft.
*   **Geometry** <note>original: "ha-mitpach" / "ha-handasa"</note> provides even more variation in understanding measures and dimensions, and the knowledge of specific laws found in the Talmud.
*   **Music** <note>original: "musika"</note> provides proof for recognizing and knowing the melodies used by the singers <note>The Levites in the Holy Temple</note>.
*   **Astronomy** <note>original: "chochmat ha-kokhavim"</note> and the recognition of the changing celestial cycles are vital for the Sanctification of the New Moon and the Festivals. This teaches the scholar the spirit of the calculated reward.
*   **Natural Sciences** <note>original: "tiviyot"</note> reveal many matters; it is impossible to understand many commandments of our Torah without them. For example: the matter of blue dyes, the laws of ritual immersion, the behavior of birds in their domain, matters of purity, and the various species. In my opinion, these are the "perfumes" needed to grasp the Torah and stand upon the **Tradition** <term>Tradition: Kabbalah, often referred to as the received mystical tradition</term>.
*   **Divine Science** <note>original: "chochma ha-elohit"; Metaphysics</note> is necessary for us to understand the essence. According to its principles, one who balances this wisdom achieves their fullness, specifically regarding what is received from the Prophets and the words of the visionary.

In general, when one includes all that is encompassed by the visionary research, following the nature of knowledge and intellectual conduct, and joins it with what is seen through the **Tradition** <note>Kabbalah</note>, they reach a worthy state. This standing distances "filthy opinions," removes foolishness, and pushes away many types of heresy that might occur regarding the principles of the Torah. Generally, standing upon these concepts means recognizing His Unity and the unique nature of the Intellect. It does not contradict the concepts of the Torah; rather, it "opens the eyes of the blind" and helps one grasp the matters of the Torah.

Thus, the proper conduct regarding the knowledge of **demonstrative proofs** <note>logical certainties</note> has been clarified. They are the "deeds of the heavens" for many who lack the heart for the Tradition of the Lord. I have proven that the study of Arithmetic and Geometry is necessary for knowing the laws and recognizing the calculations within the Talmud. It is a great lack when the interpreters of the Law are not learned in mathematics and geometry. If there were a book in Israel composed of all this, it would be a "work of man" in the hands of the sages. Without it, they rely on the logic of the Law itself, but they lack what the scientists have calculated. If that composed book were lost, the lack would be great.

**The Science of Music** is also greatly needed for the songs on the Platform <note>the *duchan* where Levites sang</note> to awaken the souls, as is known to the "wise of heart." This wisdom was specifically entrusted to the Levites. The intention of the Temple service also requires Music, as known to the scientists. This matter is of high degree, as written regarding the Incense.

**The Science of the Stars** (Astronomy) is also a great necessity for the laws discussed in the Talmud... specifically the calculation of cycles and births <note>of the moon</note>, which is required for the laws regarding the changing seasons.

<column-break/>

...forever. Therefore, knowing the way is a general requirement for him and is part of his perfection. This is to say, even if the commandments are minimized, one must still possess them as a duty... and this is the "Perfection." For the **Seven Commandments** <note>Likely the Seven Noahide Laws or the seven liberal arts/sciences</note> are acquired according to the place from which one gains them. Thus, one must acquire them for himself... it should include the revealed perfection for every nation... to understand the true depth of the intended advice. This matter is precious and rare; none stand upon it except for the "few sons of the ascent" <note>original: "bnei aliya muatim"; a Talmudic expression for the spiritually elite</note>. It is impossible for me to mention this except for those who wish to understand the Tradition... as we mentioned in our previous words.

Behold, the human has been established in the likeness of the Upper Realm. His perfection and the repair of his creation depend on the knowledge of the "Ladder of Wisdom" in the Upper Glory, which repairs the Lower Glory and upwards. Without this repair, even the physical "Glory" remains a mere gate. It is clear that this repair is according to the Torah. Therefore, the one who is "balanced" and ascends must also possess this inclusive perfection...

The required wisdom is like the "Scent of the Wine" <note>a metaphor for the inner essence of study</note> of the acquisition of deeds and the study of the Law. This applies to what is received in the traditional Lineage, according to the nature of the Torah. That is to say, one should occupy themselves with the knowledge of its explicit laws and the knowledge of its Talmud. Yet, one remains "unformed" <note>original: "golem"</note> until they reach the completion and the repair. This is the intention behind these matters... as clarified by the **Divine Philosopher** <note>original: "ha-chakham ha-elohi"; likely referring to Maimonides</note>. This book, in this place, is the completion of the line of perfection, reaching the Upper Perception and repairing this "Glory." This is the goal: to rise in the way and the repair of one's own essence... reaching the divine will, which is the repair of the Glory. This is the ultimate "Complete Virtue" which was the intention behind the creation of man.

And this is the hint: "Israel... we will do and we will hear" <note>Exodus 24:7</note>. That is to say, first the "Doing" (completion of action) and finally the "Perfection" which is included in the "Hearing." In "Hearing" lies the secret of knowledge according to the Tradition—the **Oral Torah**—and the intention within it according to the **Received Wisdom** <note>Kabbalah</note>. This is the path we have written, and it is the exalted matter of the "Ladder" written in this chapter.

# Chapter 66

# An objector might raise a claim and awaken an argument, saying:
# "Behold, this perfect Torah includes
all these matters—the four roots of the Divine generations and their generalities, as we have written. If so, why is the conduct of the **demonstrative sciences** <note>secular/rational sciences</note> such a rare practice, achieved by only one or two in a generation? Furthermore, if one who is 'balanced' reaches a smaller degree in the 'generations' than the degree achieved by merely performing the commandments, wouldn't these scientific conducts be in vain? It would mean the 'generations' of the Torah are sufficient."

Rabbi **Joseph ben Shem Tov** <note>A 15th-century Spanish Jewish philosopher and commentator on Aristotle and Maimonides</note>, in his book **Ein Ha-Kore** <note>"The Eye of the Reader"</note>, answered this claim. In his view, the intellectual conceptualization of the demonstrative sciences is a great and necessary path toward perfection. He said that the perfection of the intellectual is like the "rank of the soldier" compared to the rest of the army. This conduct is his perfection and is necessary for him... it is like the "light" and the "research." This is similar to a person who speaks; if his words are clearer than those of others, why should he be considered like a person who speaks without any understanding or realization? Therefore, his words are directed at this premise... and the knowledge of these things...

<meta>This page continues the discussion on the ultimate purpose of human life, transitioning from the role of intellectual sciences to the core debate between the value of Torah study versus the practical performance of the commandments. It seeks to reconcile the two by explaining how action serves as the final realization of divine flow.</meta>

-># Chapter 15 — The Section on the Purpose — Chapter 15<-

<margin>The purpose. [Section] 72.</margin> Behold, although in the supernal realms "hearing" <note>original: "shmiah"; here referring to internal understanding or receiving divine flow</note> precedes "action" according to the order of emanation—where the purpose of action is to reach hearing, the Crown, and the downward flow—here below, the Sages prioritized "action" over "hearing" to demonstrate a specific secret. This is because when a person desires to merit drawing closer to the Most High, their agreement to act awakens the intended purpose; the action becomes the completion of the entire law in its proper order. This agreement prepares the heart to be a vessel for receiving the presence of the Place <note>original: "HaMakom"; a traditional Rabbinic name for God, implying He is the "place" of the world</note>, blessed be He.

As our masters scrutinized: Once, Rabbi Tarfon and the Elders were reclining in the upper chamber of the house of Nitza in Lydda. This question was posed to them: Is study greater or is action greater? Rabbi Tarfon answered and said: Action is greater. Rabbi Akiva answered and said: Study is greater. They all then answered and said: Study is greater, because study leads to action. 

The masters of the *Tosafot* <note>original: "Ba'alei ha-Tosafot"; 12th–13th century medieval commentators on the Talmud</note> wrote there that a distinction must be made: if a person has not yet learned at all, heaven forbid that they should engage in action first. One must teach them first, because "an ignorant person cannot be a pious one." However, if one has already learned, then action is better than study. This interpretation settles the matter: the words of Rabbi Tarfon apply to one who has already studied—for them, action is greater—while the words of Rabbi Akiva apply to one who has not yet studied. 

Yet, we must turn to the view of Rabbi Akiva and the Elders over Rabbi Tarfon. Why should the pious be so eager to follow Rabbi Tarfon's claim that action is greater? We see from Rabbi Yohanan's example regarding whether to pause study for the sake of a commandment, such as putting on *Tefillin* <note>term: Tefillin (phylacteries); leather boxes containing Torah verses worn during prayer as a physical sign of the covenant</note>. It was concluded that study is greater than action because study leads to action—meaning, the initial step of study is superior. However, some argue that for oneself, finishing an action is superior, but for the sake of teaching others, study is superior to action. Therefore, we tell him to study. It is obvious that the study of Torah for the sake of teaching others contains two merits. As the *Midrash Tanhuma* states, one who teaches their fellow is like one who restores their soul. When one teaches Torah to another, it is as if they are paying back a soul to them. Therefore, teaching others is superior to a simple action performed alone.

The Talmud asks: if study is greater, why did they prioritize the laws of *Tefillin*? It concludes that for the sake of teaching others, Torah study is a "great study" because it leads to action, but for the sake of the individual's own practice, the action itself is superior. 

And yet, if teaching others is the priority, why did they place the laws of *Tefillin* first? It should have been study first. Based on what I have explained, it should have preceded the study of others since study leads to action, and the act of *Tefillin* is merely a single deed. However, the answer is: "So that the Torah of the Lord shall be in your mouth." By placing the action of *Tefillin* first, it is as if one is reading the Torah. We saw that Rabbi Yohanan prioritized it because whoever reads the Torah is exempt from the physical act of *Tefillin* at that moment. The author of the *Ashur* <note>likely referring to the "Asheri" or Rosh, a 13th-century legal authority</note> wrote that this exemption applies to one reading Torah, but not necessarily one engaged in general study. 

According to the "Way of Truth" <note>original: "Derekh ha-Emet"; a common euphemism for Kabbalah or mystical interpretation</note>, action is indeed great. It is the simple voice that clarifies and establishes the world through the secret of the "Action" <note>original: "Asiyah"; the lowest of the four spiritual worlds in Kabbalah, representing the physical realm</note>. It becomes clear, then, that all the spiritual "virtues" <note>original: "segulot"; unique spiritual properties</note> are contained within the performance of the commandments and their fulfillment in this world. Just as action is greater than study in terms of the "order of the ladder" from above to below, so too is its greatness revealed in the drawing down of divine flow.

<column-break/>

For through study, one intends the performance of the commandments; the fruit of those commandments and their ultimate purpose is the "Union" <note>term: Yichud (Union); the meditative act of unifying the different aspects of the Divine Name through prayer or mitzvot</note> and the cleaving to the Lord. The desire of this book is to explain the matter of "Purpose": to rectify the "Perfect One" through the rectification of the Supernal Glory—the secret of the World of the Crown <note>original: "Sod Olam ha-Keter"</note>—so that the Glory may be rectified through its blessings. That is to say, the Glory is rectified by the blessings that are included within the Supernal Glory, which exist by His blessed Will. This is for the sake of the verse: "Everyone who is called by My name, and whom I have created for My glory." 

This means the Glory is rectified through its blessings, and the beauty of our testimony is taken up, as I wrote regarding the rectification of His Presence above in the chapter on "The Perfect One in His Image." When the lower Glory is rectified by man walking in the straight path, it becomes unified and rises to the height of heights. 

Behold, this is our "Purpose" which shall bloom in the world. Action comes first because the "rectification" must first ascend from below. Afterward, the rectification becomes wise and draws everything closer to the "First Ones." Your sign for this is: "Accompany the people" <note>original: "halveh et ha-am"; a play on words regarding the Levites or the act of accompanying/joining</note>—meaning, through the rectification and engagement of the people, "we shall hear" follows "we shall do." This is the purpose for which we were created: to be a holy nation to the Lord. 

It is clear, then, that the core of our portion is not in abstract study but in the "Part of Action." For this reason, the Torah always commands the performance of the commandments and the observance of the decrees of the Lord. It did not leave us only with theories or research, because elevation and perfection are entirely dependent on the *performance* of the commandments, and not on the many divisions of thought. 

This is perhaps what the Master Teacher <note>original: "ha-Rav ha-Moreh"; referring to Maimonides (Rambam)</note>, of blessed memory, meant in several chapters of his book. His words were intended to provide a firm footing and to prevent the weakening of one's hands from the Torah. If perfection were dependent only on the "demonstrative sciences" <note>original: "chokhmot ha-iyuniyot"; theoretical philosophy/science</note>, as the Master and his followers wrote, then the majority of humanity would be in a state of terminal illness regarding their hoped-for perfection. It is impossible for such intellectual perfection to be achieved by more than "one from a city and two from a family." 

Therefore, the Supreme Wisdom provided the "necessary perfections" <note>original: "ha-shelemut ha-hechratiyot"</note> through the general laws of the Torah which are set before the Children of Israel. Through these, all may merit perfection, for the Torah includes study for everyone—whether one's mind is sophisticated or simple. As the author wrote in Chapter 4, the Sages did not need to seek perfection in any other place. There is no wisdom or perfection except in the Holy Torah, because it is stripped from the Supernal Garment—"Holy, Holy, Holy"—and it gives birth to the world. Therefore, it has the power to radiate light. This is not the case with the intellectual sciences, which are "tangled in the external intellect" <note>referring to secular or non-revealed logic</note> and have no power to sustain or give life to their possessors. 

Beyond the benefit that comes from the agreement to be perfect in good deeds, we are also prepared for eternal happiness and success through the performance of the commandments according to the Torah. This is the meaning of: "And your people are all righteous; they shall inherit the land forever." That is to say, by being "righteous" and meriting through "action," we inherit the Land—not by being "intellectuals" in the demonstrative sciences. If perfection were only intellectual, most of the world would be excluded from it, and they would never merit any soul-completion in the supernal realm. 

However, the performance of the commandments gives perfection to the body in this world and to the soul in its essence. This is the core of the Torah, and its explanation is received by the Sages of the Mishnah, as we see at the end of the chapter in *Kiddushin*: "Anyone who performs a single commandment, it is good for him, his days are lengthened, and he inherits the Land." And they said at the end: "Rabbi Yehuda said, this is what it means: Anyone who performs a single commandment *in addition* to his existing merits, it is as if he fulfilled the entire Torah." From this we see that for one extra commandment, it is good for him and his days are lengthened—meaning in this world—and he "inherits the Land"—meaning the Land of Life in the World to Come. From this we turn to the teaching in *Sanhedrin*: "All Israel has a portion in the World to Come, as it is said: 'And your people are all righteous, they shall inherit the land forever...'"

<summary>This page discusses the classical debate on whether Torah study or practical action (mitzvot) is superior, concluding that while study leads to action, the physical performance of commandments is the ultimate vehicle for universal spiritual perfection and the rectification of the divine Glory.</summary>
<keywords>Study vs. Action, Rabbi Akiva, Rabbi Tarfon, Maimonides, Kiddushin, Mitzvot, Perfection, World to Come, Supernal Glory, Tanhuma, Tosafot</keywords>

<meta>This page continues the author's deep philosophical and Kabbalistic critique of Maimonides' theory of divine attributes. Having previously established the importance of action, Meir ibn Gabbai now argues that God's wisdom and will are intrinsically linked to humanity through the Torah, countering the philosophical view that God is entirely beyond any relationship with the created world.</meta>

<summary>In this chapter, Meir ibn Gabbai critiques Maimonides' "negative theology," arguing that the philosophical denial of any relationship between God and creation undermines the Torah and the Kabbalistic view of divine flow. He asserts that human wisdom, particularly that of the Sages, is a literal "portion" of Divine Wisdom, thereby establishing a fundamental connection between the Creator and the created.</summary>
