# Chapter 67 — The Section on the Purpose — Chapter 68

The exalted secrets, according to their revelation as mentioned from the "High of Highs" <note>A Kabbalistic term for the highest divine emanations</note> upon them, ensure that their wisdom consists of absolute truths. This is not the case with those who "speak into the water" <note>A metaphor for those whose words have no substance, i.e., the philosophers</note>, whose words are forged like counterfeit silver. Their writings indicate to the discerning eye that they are shameful; their strength is weakness, and their "completeness" is actually a lack. Not all who claim completeness possess it. The wisdom of the Sages was derived from the additions of the prophets, peace be upon them, and therefore their writings were perfect. In their indicators and their reductions, you will find insight between those who establish the truth and those who offer mere "abundant" counsel. 

The violence done to the **wisdom of nature** <term>Chokmat HaTeva: Natural science or physics</term> by the philosophers of the nations is contrasted with the wisdom of the Sages of Israel. This sealed wisdom, which was mastered by the "rash" <note>likely referring to those who rely solely on intellect</note> and their compositions through the path of inquiry and proof, is shown to be lacking. Not even a small portion of it was seen by them, for we have made them look foolish through natural proofs using their own natural methods. Despite all their sophisticated investigation and the depth of their inquiry, it is heard and seen that the Sages of Israel possessed what they lacked. This serves as a demonstration that true natural science does not belong to the Greeks, but to Israel. 

A "voice of violence" <note>An expression of theft or misappropriation</note> is heard in chapter 30... <unclear>various obscure Talmudic references follow</unclear>. They were discerning. When Syria grew strong, the ways were lost... But God, being the Knower of natural wisdom through the "Voice" <note>The Divine Word</note>, even in the smallest details of the beginning of creation, was the Actor and Teacher of every creature... It is from this that it becomes clear that their wisdom in nature is not like the natural science of the Greeks. The Sages' wisdom is above the path of inquiry; it is a knowledge that was theirs because they were holy and wise in the Book and the Torah of our pious ones, may they rest in peace.

Furthermore, the Sages said in the chapter *Ha-Maon* <note>Referring to the Talmudic tractate Chagigah</note> regarding Rabbi Hanina and Rabbi Hoshaiah: "They would sit every Sabbath eve and occupy themselves with the **Book of Formation** <term>Sefer Yetzirah: An ancient Kabbalistic text describing the creation of the world through Hebrew letters</term>, and they would create for themselves a three-year-old calf and eat it." This is a testimony to their wisdom—that the natural science known to the Sages of Israel was true and substantial, such that they could perform physical actions with it. Through this, one can discern that God gave perfection to all His creatures according to their nature. This is not the case with the natural science of the scholars of the nations, for its foundation is human inquiry and the intellect. Therefore, perfection is far from it; it contains no "demonstration" or "substance." 

Seek the interpretation of the Torah and the power in these wonderful matters, such as the **Work of the Chariot** <term>Ma'aseh Merkavah: The highest form of Jewish mysticism</term> and the **Work of Creation** <term>Ma'aseh Bereshit: The mystical study of Genesis</term>. Even the aforementioned Rabbi <note>referring to Maimonides</note> admitted that the "wisdom of the purpose" is a wisdom distinct from all [human] inquiry. This wisdom is known and clear to the truly perfect and the true Kabbalists. From all we have written, it is clear that standing upon the measures of the sciences is impossible through the path of inquiry alone. Whatever the intellect of the nations concludes cannot be relied upon, for no true substance was given to their visions. 

Therefore, one must distance oneself from all these theoretical, "demonstrative" sciences of **Aristotle**. One should not be enticed by their false demonstrations, for they have no reality. The evidence for this is that in every generation, opinions change according to the person. Their inquiries and the changes in their divisions are like those who argue about the "Fifth Element" <note>The quintessence or ether</note> which Aristotle brought a proof for its existence, yet others brought proofs for its non-existence. Indeed, the **Master Teacher** <note>Maimonides (Rambam)</note> of blessed memory, brought proof for the eternity of the world according to the laws of the philosophers, yet **Rabbi Hasdai** <note>Hasdai Crescas (d. 1410), a critic of Maimonides and Aristotle</note> of blessed memory, in the third chapter of the third section of the first discourse of his book, brought proof against this. He had the power to push away and remove intellectual speculation and the path of inquiry, showing that one cannot rely at all upon any matter derived from intellectual investigation, for there is no place for them in our tradition. I have already written about this in several places.

<column-break/>

Their argument for this is based on "demonstrative intellectualizing," which they claim is the path to perfection. They claim this is wisdom, but they have testified falsely. For this is only their own opinion; being subjective and non-obligatory paths, one is drawn after them to seek their "perfection."

The first path, in which one truly finds perfection, is revealed through the truth of the Torah, written through the path of tradition and action. It involves knowing the ways of the Divine Attributes, which provide power and the inheritance of established thought. Without these, one cannot acquire true wisdom. This path is the one followed by the Sages of Truth <note>The Kabbalists</note>, who conducted all the laws of the Torah accordingly. The "investigators" are always divided against the "ancients," but upon all these divisions of opinion, the "Voice" <note>Divine Revelation</note> will always remain one. The words of the Living God are the foundation upon which their tradition is built, fixed in a holy place. We have already alluded to this secret sufficiently for those who know the hidden wisdom.

The second path, in which perfection is revealed, is the conduct of those who do not distance themselves from total servitude to God to seek "freedom" <note>intellectual independence</note>. As mentioned in the **received wisdom** <term>Kabbalah</term>, true Kabbalists hold this in their hands. This is what the Sages alluded to regarding a person falling in wisdom. This perfection and completeness of their intellect is grounded in the first path, which relates to the body. This is the path of the pious of Israel, the "mighty ones" who have always been pious. In this second path, there is no disagreement and no witness from the path of human science, for everything is gathered from the Place of Wisdom. Thus, all perfection is dependent upon these paths, according to one's occupation with them. For the foundation is the Honor of God, and through this, all intellectual perfections are attained. 

This is not the case with the "theoretical intellectual" paths, for any occupation that does not have the foundation of Torah in it is forbidden. There is no hope for fruit therein, except in the occupation with Torah, the fulfillment of its commandments, and the occupation with the "Truth of Torah," which is the wisdom of perfection. For occupation with all of this leads to **Unification** <term>Yichud: The mystical act of unifying the divine names/aspects</term>, as has already been explained. This is what we intended to clarify in the body of this chapter.

I will say that this is a distinction from the ways of those who reveal secrets. Thus, one can distinguish between the forged and the true. The great, mighty, and awesome Hillel said to him... <unclear>Hagadic/Talmudic references</unclear>. 

He told him a parable: A king had thousands of thousands of gold dinars, and they were praising him with silver. Was this not a slight to him? And the Rabbi said that Rabbi Hanina corrected him, saying: "Our Sages of truth said..." and he said that the praises we offer are only because they were written in the Torah and established by the Sages of the Great Assembly. Without those, we would not be able to mention them.

So too, when we describe the perfections of the Blessed One, if we use human intellectual "demonstrations," we are like those who praise gold with silver. For His perfections are absolute perfections, and any human description is a reduction. They have merited this through our lack.

As they said in the Midrash of Rabbi Nehunia ben HaKanah <note>The Sefer HaBahir</note>, peace be upon him: "This was the connector of the Torah above; he was connecting it to the Holy One, Blessed be He." Behold, this is a "Connector of Peace" between two lovers. But this is not the specific "Unification of the Unification" of the Shema in its season.

To indicate this, the order of the verses... for the Sabbath to the companions... we interrupt for them. For we rely on... and we interrupt for the Recitation of the Shema, but we do not interrupt for the Prayer <term>Tefillah: Specifically the Amidah or 'Standing Prayer'</term>. Rabbi Yochanan said: "They only taught this regarding people like Rabbi Shimon bar Yochai and his colleagues, whose Torah was their craft <note>meaning they studied constantly</note>. But for people like us, we interrupt both for the Prayer and for the Shema." (Talmud, Berakhot 11a).

And in the chapter "He Who Reads," Rabbi Hiyya said to him: "I did not see 'Rabbi' <note>Rabbi Judah the Prince</note> accepting upon himself the Yoke of the Kingdom of Heaven." Bar Kapara said to him: "At the moment he passes his hands over his eyes, he is accepting the Yoke of the Kingdom of Heaven." From all this, it becomes clear that the Unification of the Shema is more precious and important than [other study], as is known from its matter. As I wrote, the engagement in Torah is specialized, even though it is from the power of the "One," causing the engager to return and connect between "Man and his Wife" <note>The Male and Female aspects of the Divine</note>—the secret of the "Single Face." For regarding her unification, it is said: "You shall meditate on it day and night" (Joshua 1:8), which is to say the "Way of the Day" and the "Measure of Night" in the heads of the Name, which I wrote as the Written Torah and the Oral Torah. For this secret, the engagement must be with precious deep "pulses" <note>rhythms/efforts</note> to connect the whole into one. Especially if the engager intends this, then his Torah is a "Torah of Truth" and perfection, and it rises for acceptance, for everything follows the intention of the Unification. This is the **Second Path** in Unification.

Furthermore, there is a **Third Path** in Unification in its own way, which is the "Fruit of the Torah" and its purpose: **Action**, which is the performance of the Commandments <term>Mitzvot: The 613 religious duties/deeds</term> in practice. This is a path intended for itself, and also a unique property in prayer—the "Atonement and Restoration of the Name" and its Unification in His Glory. For every single Commandment of the Torah's commandments is a part of the parts of the "Upper Perfect One," as we have written in this book. <header>### Chapter 67</header>

Do not wonder, for the secret of the Torah has not been fully revealed, nor the secret of the words of righteousness within them. For they are life, and they are titles and nicknames <note>original: *kinuyim*</note>. Therefore, do not wonder at the opinion of the **philosophers** who wrote that they do not find this literal meaning within the Torah of our people. This is not a "cutting of the shoots" <note>An idiom for heresy or separating the divine attributes from their source</note>, God forbid. It is necessary to grant you the knowledge that the essence of the proof is that they prevent the establishment of the Torah among the nations of the world, lest they share in the "Great Name." This is for the success of the inner aspect. 

For our desire is for His perfect choice and His will regarding prayers and blessings. There is no way to achieve this except through the "Necessary Existent" <term>Necessary Existent: A philosophical term for God as a being whose non-existence is impossible</term>, who is attributed to us as having the power of speech, for He is One with them in absolute simplicity. For they are the witnesses of the world, and everything depends on Him. Without Him, it would be impossible to bow down or listen to Him. This is the path of those who follow the way of **Faith**. 

Our ultimate purpose is the perfection of the Torah, for those who labor in His Torah. Through them, the "Seal" is recognized—to come to Him, to the Name. Just as the tradition teaches regarding His existence and His will in His ways. Regarding what Rabbi Menachem <note>Rabbi Menachem Recanati, a 13th-14th century Italian Kabbalist</note> wrote in his composition: his intent was not to explain what the Rabbi [Maimonides] wrote. Rather, his intent was what he chose regarding one of the "gates." This is known from the path of the **Accepted Faith** <note>Kabbalah</note>: that it is impossible to show a boundary or a measure in the **Unification** <term>Yichud: The doctrine of God's absolute oneness</term>. 

One cannot say that "this attribute is for Judgment and not for Mercy," or "this attribute is for Mercy and not for Judgment," for that would be the intent of error and "separation in the Unification" <note>original: *peirud b’yichud*</note>, God forbid. Rather, one must believe that His attributes are one with His Essence, and they are united in an absolute Unification. It is like the flame bound to the coal; as one gazes at it, the form and the color are one. Because of this, we unify Him with praises, without placing limits on Him. These are His attributes, which emanate from His light, having no limit or measure. This is what we explained in the *Sefer Yetzirah* <note>The Book of Formation</note>: "Ten Sefirot of Nothingness, whose end is fixed in their beginning, and He is one in them." One does not multiply the Essence by them, for He is One in them. One does not describe Him by them as if He and they are separate things. If they were outside of His essence, God forbid, we would not praise Him by them.

The holy author, Rabbi Shimon bar Yochai, peace be upon him, said in the book *Tikkunei Zohar*: 
"Elijah opened and said: Master of the Worlds, You are One but not in number. You are Higher than the highest, Hidden from the hidden; no thought can grasp You at all. You are He who brought forth ten 'Tikunim'—which we call the ten Sefirot—to guide the worlds... You have no known image... And there is no Judgment or Law that grasps You, and no Mercy at all." 

Behold, he explained that Wisdom and Understanding are not additions to Him, nor are they separate from Him. He is One with them, and they are united in Him, and they are not something else. This is unlike human beings, in whom wisdom and understanding are added and separate qualities. This is well known. He is exalted above all His attributes, and they are in Him. What He "fixed" as *Tikunim* <note>Rectifications or Divine Structures</note> was to make known His boundaries and His might to the world, to show how the world is conducted through a measure comprised of Judgment and Mercy for the needs of the world. But the tradition received by the Sages did not find—God forbid—any known or limited Judgment, nor any known or limited Mercy or Law. Rather, all these attributes are united in Him. He is one, unique, and simple in all His attributes. Therefore, we describe Him with these titles and pray before Him using them, provided that we do not attribute "measure" or "limit" to Him. For that would be the intent of "separation in the Unification." After these words of truth, I say that this Rabbi Menachem was correct in his intent... <margin>separation in the Unification, God forbid</margin> regarding the names that are inclusive, such as the thirteen attributes of mercy...

<column-break/>

<header>### The Section on the Purpose — Chapter 68</header>
<sig>27</sig>

"Our portion is the Lord, God is One." For the true Kabbalah, in which we are grounded, relates specifically to the **Emanation** <term>Atzilut: The highest of the four worlds in Kabbalah, where the Divine Light is most pure</term>, which is the "Plain." These are the powers included in the Name. One must speak with intention and repentance, for the purpose of the prayer is to show no "separation" or "division" <note>original: *peirud*</note> at all. We have come to examine and know how He is unified in everything, both in the hidden and the revealed. On this, see the "Great Unification." 

Upon the Lord, He examines the hearts and kidneys <note>A biblical idiom for the seats of emotion and thought</note>, and weighs one's intention and thought in the "Simple Unification." For He is unified according to His greatness, which is the root of the Torah and the secret of Faith. The ultimate goal of man is to reach this level. This is what the entire Torah stands upon, and it is the fruit of the commandments. This is the opinion of the Sages. To know the "Knowledge of Good and Evil," one must say that in the Unification, one knows the faith as it is explained in the portion "You have been shown to know" (Deuteronomy 4:35).

His treasure, as we publicized in the book *Tola'at Ya'akov* <note>The author's work "The Worm of Jacob," a commentary on the liturgy</note>, in all that was said by the mouth of Wisdom: they include the totality of these attributes within each other and their unification. For example: "The Great, the Mighty, and the Awesome" <note>The opening of the Amidah prayer</note>. These are nicknames for the inclusive attribute that encompasses them. For such is the attribute: it is included and bounded by each one, and unified in its end. We call Him by these names to testify to the Unification, even though they are different nicknames, because they are not additions to the Essence, and He is not multiplied by them. 

Because of this, he grew angry and said that our existence is as one in them... and he wrote that you should take for yourself the specific attribute that is found. This is "separation" <note>heresy</note> if it is said. Behold, the intention of the Sages was prayer to the "Great God," and the descriptions are not additions to the Essence. 

He wrote further: This is the Unification. Indeed, we would not permit ourselves to describe Him with these names unless they were explicitly written in the Torah. We rely on the latter sages who permitted us to add these because they do not imply "multiplicity," as they point toward the Unification, as I have written. This is the secret of the "Great Assembly" <note>Anshei Kneset HaGedola</note> who permitted the "Crown of Unification" and established it in prayer to show that they are permitted and that there is no multiplicity in them, nor any addition to the Essence, for they testify to the Unification.

What can we compare this to? To the parable of a king who had millions of gold coins, but he was praised for having millions of silver coins. This would be a diminishing of his honor. For gold includes the value of silver, but silver does not include the value of gold. Similarly, "The Great, the Mighty, and the Awesome" are the "Gold" of the attributes. All the nicknames and titles are included in the ten inclusive Sefirot that represent the attributes and testify to the Unification. Everything is a "Crown" for the King. 

The wise recipient of these descriptions understands that they are limited in the context of Unification. For instance, praising the King for something that is below Him is a slight to His honor. His intention should be toward the "Infinite" <note>original: *Ein Sof*</note>, for He has no measure or limit, but is the cause of all causes. The prayer is founded and bound to all the inclusive "titles" of the Name, such as "Great," "Mighty," etc. Not in a way that creates "separation" <note>peirud</note>. After the Unification, which is the ultimate goal, one reaches the level where there is no limit or measure... until here reaches the purpose of what I intended to write in this chapter.

# Chapter 70: The Section of the Purpose #

It is possible that the Lord will reveal to one a unique treasure and wisdom, and therefore He revealed it to the precious ones of old, and they revealed it in turn. Despite their hiding it, the King disciplined the ancient sages, as we have said. Furthermore, regarding what is written, *The way of life is the reproof of instruction* <note>Proverbs 6:23</note>, this teaches that anyone accustomed to the **Work of the Chariot** <term>Work of the Chariot (Ma'aseh Merkavah): The ancient Jewish mystical tradition focused on the visionary experience of the Divine Throne</term> and similar pursuits in seeking the Lord and His statutes, and who has been revealed the hidden foundation—this "engine" is under your hand. Or, the words of a certain sage might allow one to understand them; otherwise, one might stumble in them and distance themselves from the Torah of "reproof of instruction" intended for all in truth.

And this is for the "way of life," for whoever wishes to merit the way of life is able to, through the wisdom of instruction. And upon the return of the King, who is the "Total One" within them, they return to their paths. "Reproofs of instruction"—there is no reason to complain about them, for one who separates from them is like one who separates from his own life and soul. They are comforted that they have merited the way of life. If one wishes to merit the way of life, let him be drawn toward the path of the **Work of the Chariot**, which is hidden in its existence and revealed in its beginning, which is the secret of the "hollows of the classes" <note>likely referring to the ranks of angels or celestial spheres</note> and the foundation of the "reproof of instruction." Let his hands not be slack regarding them at all, for they are the **elixir of life**, and through them, he will come to know the Honorable and Awesome Name, for this is the "whole of man."

Do not be astonished according to what was written, for because they seek wisdom outside of the law, the judgment is upon them. As our Sages of blessed memory said in their stringency: "Because they treated the holy as profane in the House of the Chariot, their lungs were puffed up and they were exiled," etc. Even for a small dampness or moisture, their wisdom and their "pockets" <note>metaphor for their stored knowledge</note> were occupied. The masters of wisdom protected it more than the masters of Scripture and Mishnah.

In the book of the **Tikunim** <note>Tikkunei Zohar, a central Kabbalistic text</note>, the Holy Lamp, Rabbi Shimon bar Yochai (peace be upon him), spoke in this language: *If a bird’s nest chances before you... you shall surely let the mother go and take the young for yourself* <note>Deuteronomy 22:6-7, interpreted mystically</note>. This "sending" is from above to the earth. These "young" <note>original: banim (children/sons)</note> are the "points" <term>Points (Nekudot): In Kabbalah, these often represent the vowel signs or the initial sparks of divine emanation</term> of the house of our Master, within which the **Divine Presence** <note>Shekhinah</note> dwells with Israel. These "young," it is said, are those lacking in Scripture study, but generally, they are occupied with the Torah. These are her children. They are the "Nest" and the "Divine Presence," and they caused it to be written that they should "inherit and be taught" from there. Hearken to these voices that have fallen; therefore, do not prohibit the reading of Scripture. As for those "hypocrites," they are thin and light... and because of this, she [the Shekhinah] rides upon the "husks" <note>original: chasfis</note>. But regarding the "young," she does not ride upon them as a "smashed gate" <note>unclear metaphor</note> of which nothing can be said. And they are the "wings of a dove"—these are the small ones, and they are the four wings for each one. The "Living Creature" <note>original: Chayah</note> rides upon them, and they are destined to be lifted from their place, for it is said of them: "a cherub of his spirit." They are the "masters of the nest." It is said of her [the Divine Presence]: "she is light," praising the sages of the dwelling place, and she shall never move from them. Until here [is the quote].

The reason is that they are constantly occupied with the **Unification of the Name** <term>Unification (Yichud): The meditative practice of declaring and internalizing the absolute oneness of God</term>, to know the Lord. It is impossible to perceive Him or know Him except through the **Higher Wisdom**. Because their taste for it prevails, it strengthens them until the Prophet is at a higher level. Thus, this writing was revealed from the "Awesome Prophet below," which is the Unification—the glory of their fragrance. And what are these "wings" regarding "knowing Him"? For Unification is the "knowledge of the Lord." He handed over His follies to him. And according to the way I have spread out in this chapter, as I saw in his wisdom, this is the ultimate purpose of all man and the end of the advantage. The levels of the hidden ones are revealed one to the other; as they increase their voice in knowledge and perception of the Unification, they increase their knowledge of the Lord. These levels rise and are exalted, like one who perceives the Knower in His place.

Is it not clear to us that if the matter is good and successful and glorious, it is only to do the will of his Creator, which is his existence and his life? This is the **True Wisdom**. There are those who turn away from His glory... this is a dream and not this. This is the mention of the Prophet regarding "sitting as His strength." This is the level of which the Lord said: *Let not the mighty man glory in his might* <note>Jeremiah 9:22</note>. This intention is that the master of these levels should not think of them for his own needs, for his voice is everything and his reward is written to prepare the "Throne of Glory," etc., as found in the Tikunim. These are like a mother included in the Higher Glory, for she is "Desolation," "Might," and "Crown." From them, the Glory is repaired, both the upper and the lower. The master of these levels is like a "Throne" to them, a "likeness of a vessel" to resemble his Creator and to repair the Glory through these levels included in him, in the likeness of the Higher Glory. Similarly, he comes to his Creator, and moreover, what truth! A great law in His glory, a great abundance. This is the testimony of the intention in his flight, and he shall glory in "attaining" these things for his own sake.

<column-break/>

Through all of them, the purpose of the Torah and the "fruit of the commandments" will be clarified for you, as we have written. With this, we complete what we wished to discuss in this chapter.

## Chapter Seventy ##

The completion of the true perfections, which are the fruit of all the commandments and every desire and every labor of those who strive, is the "Knowledge of His existence" which we wrote. For He knows all, the Life of the Worlds, for He is the Perceiver, the Known, and the Understanding of the **Unification of the Name** and His statutes. The strength of the knowledge of His fear, His hope, and trust in Him is through Him. This is the way to perceive Him—this is the purity of the heart and the refining of thought.

The "engine" is through this; this is the path to this knowledge, which is the existence and the strength of the hand, of which the glory-seeker shall glory: *That he understands and knows Me, that I am the Lord* <note>Jeremiah 9:23</note>. This is the life of the perception of the Glory and the secret of His existence that we wrote. This is a hint to these "buildings of the Lord," as it is said: *And keep the words of this covenant and do them, so that you may prosper [or: understand] in all that you do* <note>Deuteronomy 29:8</note>.

The intention is that the "Teacher" <note>original: Moreh</note>, which is the occupation with the explanation of the Guide, is weighed against the verses of the Bible. All the advantages of this level and their matter relate to the "secret of the existence of the commandments," as is known. Even more than what is written in the "Firstfruits," that which is "pleasant"—this is the hidden fruit. Aside from this part, his existence... to the repair of his existence in the "All" and his Life and in the Creator. In this way, I have already written.

It is impossible for the knowledge of this "Repair" <note>Tikkun</note> and its manner to arise unless the observer is fluent in the **Wisdom of the Torah** and all the **Wisdoms of Tradition** <note>Kabbalah</note> which occupy themselves with "knowing the Lord." Strengthen this Unification, as is known from its matter to those who draw near to His Unification. It is known that it is impossible to see the "Light of Unification," which is the true knowledge, except through the "Tearing" <note>unclear, perhaps 'penetrating'</note> of those who occupy themselves with the **Wisdom of Truth** <note>Kabbalah</note>. This is only to unite toward this perfection. Therefore, strengthen this wisdom to know the Honorable and Awesome Name. 

He who has this wisdom closed before him, it is impossible to know Him. Of him, it is said: *Also, for a soul to be without knowledge is not good* <note>Proverbs 19:2</note>. It is understood by proof that knowledge is far from those who exist truly. Strength is according to how the soul holds on to its ascent from this knowledge while in this body, which has the nature of distance and dust. Knowledge over it is the "Secret of the Spirit" from the understanding there, "David," and there is also the secret of "Life" there, which is "Knowledge," which is the **Holy Spirit**. This is "good," for this soul has no existence except through the Holy Spirit, which is the knowledge of His existence. When it dwells in the body, its existence and perfection are only through the "Super-soul" <note>Neshamah</note>. This is the "Repair of the Teacher" <note>Tikkun HaMoreh</note> through Knowledge, which is the **Wisdom of Truth**. There is no existence or perfection except through it, through this wisdom that allows one to see the "Light of the Knowledge of the Lord."

This is the secret of the division of the levels of the chosen ones and their advantage over one another. For the Wisdom of Truth is inclusive, and its benefits are many and precious. It is known that whoever is heard in it and perceives it can encompass His Name and perceive the secrets of the Torah and the deep "Reasons for the Commandments" <term>Reasons for the Commandments (Ta'amei HaMitzvot): The philosophical or mystical explanations behind Jewish laws</term>. Aside from the "psychic proof" which rules that this is called by the name "Repair of the Soul" and "Cleaving to one's Creator."

Furthermore, the thought of performing the commandments in their name will be strengthened in a "Great Assembly," for this is the craft that the wise know how to perform in its perfection, as is known from their results. From it, one will derive benefit in the matter of Service and Prayers through the "Bond of Unification" and Faith. This matter was received in the book **The Worm of Jacob** <note>Tola'at Ya'akov, a Kabbalistic work by Meir ibn Gabbai</note>... until this point, the occupation with this wisdom rose to the place of "Service" and the spreading of his wisdom before the Place, blessed be He.

In the Midrash of Rabbi... his students asked Rabbi Rachumai: "What is the meaning of that which is written: 'Write it, engrave it, the honor upon the judges of the rock'?" He said to them: "Anyone whose heart's actions are removed from the occupations of the world and who is occupied with the **Work of the Chariot** is accepted before the Holy One, blessed be He." They asked: "Is all the existence of the hidden tradition engraved?" He replied: "It is worthy to be on the paths of the Lord; in true love, you shall return and be in the 'Day of the Work of the Chariot.'" Until here. The secret of the "Work of the Chariot" is the blessing of wisdoms—this is the secret, and this is the Unification and the **Wisdom of Truth** in the truth of the light that shines upon him. And thus, the occupation with it is very attaining, and with the Levite...

# Chapter 69: The Section of the Purpose #

The lower [realm] is established according to the likeness of the Upper, serving as a chariot for the components of the **Divine Chariot** <term>Divine Chariot (Merkavah): The celestial structure of the divine realm, often envisioned as a throne-chariot in Jewish mysticism</term>. For this reason, all the positive commandments are established as parts corresponding to the number of limbs of the **Supernal Man** <term>Supernal Man (Adam Elyon): A mystical concept representing the divine structure in human form</term> and the lower [man], as we have written. By completing [the act] below, one sustains the vitality [above], giving power, strength, and might, thereby upholding and strengthening the "Book" and the "King" in the matter corresponding to that specific commandment. From his strength in his place—and the sign that supports the Throne—we have already written this. This foundation is the strength of the commandments. Some of them are divided into the "hidden," for all the powers desire to engage with the Throne and the Dwelling Place for the **Divine Presence** <term>Divine Presence (Shekhinah): The indwelling, feminine aspect of God that resides within the world</term>, waiting for the Great Name in His glory. This is a supernal example, following the likeness of the "Perfect One" who sits upon the Throne.

This is proven by the **Tefillin** <term>Tefillin (Phylacteries): Black leather boxes containing Torah verses, worn on the head and arm during prayer</term>, as the sages said: "Does the Holy One, blessed be He, wear Tefillin?" <note>original: "מניח תפלין" - a reference to the Talmudic statement in Berakhot 6a</note>. Indeed, He wears Tefillin. For the Tefillin of the head contain four sections, the secret of **Wisdom, Understanding, Kindness, and Might** <term>The Sefirot: These are the divine attributes or emanations through which God interacts with the universe</term>. These are transmitted and placed upon the head to crown it, bestowing the secret and grace found within the Name. The secret of the one who dons Tefillin is that he becomes bound and unified, ascending to the height of the living beings <unclear>as described</unclear>. This is the secret of the four sections... and the Tefillin of the hand are the secret of the "Hand," known as our strength, encompassing these four sections within a single house [compartment] to indicate their endurance. They are unified there, and a voice transmits them through the hand of the **Righteous One** <term>The Righteous One (Tzadik): Associated with the Sefirah of Yesod (Foundation), which acts as the conduit for divine energy</term>, which is the secret of the letter *Yod* and the awakening. And behold, this is the secret of the "Voice" and the "Unification," the foundation of the voice... the secret of the sections of the Tefillin of the hand. Everyone who binds himself to this commandment and places Tefillin on his head and spreads them upon his hand, through this power, awakens the [divine] Attentiveness and the Unification above, just as this action is performed below. I have already written that the action performed below awakens its likeness above. For this reason, one must be very precise in the performance of the commandment and direct the proper **intention** <term>Intention (Kavvanah): The meditative focus required when performing a religious act</term> within it. Through this, it shall rise to [divine] favor, directed toward the "Book" and the "King" who corresponds to it above, ascending in perfection, unified in its standing, and strengthening the ancient decrees. 

In this manner, all the other commandments of the Torah—each and every one—are directed toward this purpose, even with their various differences; they are all good for one single intention: the "Total One" who dwells upon the Throne and the rectification of the Great Name and His unification in His glory. Then, this rectification is hinted at as a "crown" <note>original: "עטרה"</note>... to be included in my commandments, encompassing the action below and the action above. Through the completion of all the commandments in this way, corresponding to the lower man and the rectification of the Upper... and in the Midrash of Rabbi Shimon bar Yochai, peace be upon him <note>The Zohar</note>:

> "Perhaps 'and you shall make them' <note>Leviticus 26:3</note>—whoever performs the commandments of the Torah and walks in its paths, it is as if he made Him above. The Holy One, blessed be He, said: 'All of them and My Shekhinah...' he established it and ascended, 'and he made it' indeed. And He awakens upon them to be joined together, to crown the Holy Name as is fitting. 'And you shall make it' indeed."

Rabbi Shimon did not say this lightly... I have already written this. Because of the sin, this [wisdom] is precious and fallen, and one needs light from above to open the eyes of the blind to see the wonders of the Torah and the commandments. David, peace be upon him, sought this in his prayer: *Open my eyes, that I may behold wondrous things out of Your law* <note>Psalm 119:18</note>. For this we plead when we say [in the liturgy]: *Enlighten our eyes in Your Torah, and let our hearts cleave to Your commandments.* <note>From the blessing 'Ahava Rabbah' preceding the Shema</note>. This stems from the desire of our ancestors to know His unity and to serve Him. In the blessing of the Shema before the Name, before the section on Unification, we mention this love and request of Him to place intention in our hearts to know His unity and to remove all obstacles that prevent this. We are diligent in saying: *With an everlasting love You have loved us* <note>original: "אהבת עולם אהבתנו"</note>, referring to this superior love, so that it may pass to us... that great truth upon us, to bring us under the yoke of Your commandments and to give us life through His loves... in His house. I have already written this. "Our King"—we are His servants, a request upon us for the day we accepted our yoke and His commandments when we served Him, for He created us and brought us out of the **iron furnace** <note>A biblical metaphor for Egypt (Deuteronomy 4:20)</note> from Egypt, from the house of bondage. For this, we are His from among every nation and language, for the sake of Your Great Name, as on the day we praise and Your height—

<column-break/>

—in this way as well. And for the sake of our ancestors who trusted... and let us learn the **laws of life** <note>original: "חוקי חיים"</note>, laws carved from the Source of Life. So may You favor us, etc., and put into our hearts understanding to discern and to perceive, etc., for study leads to action. And it says "to learn and to do," because there are two parts to the Torah: positive commandments and negative commandments. And "to fulfill," for in guarding and doing, there is a preservation above for all the words of the study of Your Torah—the Supernal Torah. The commandments below provide sustenance and teach their likeness above through love, for the complete service is love and unification. We have already written the root of this in the first part at the end of the book. 

After we prepare ourselves through Your commandments, this matter of the truth of the Torah and contemplation ascends. For what did we mean when we said "and put into our hearts understanding... to learn and to do"? This certainly refers to the matter of the Torah and the commandments and their reasons in the world. It is the connection and the acceptance of study and action, which is the perfection of service. For this reason, we asked first for study—that You might grant us the power for action—and then for the commandments that draw forth the Unification, so that through them we may know what the Will is for its sake, its purpose, and its perfection, which is Unification. For this is the rectification and the completion, the final perfection of study and action; without it, they are like a corpse without form. As I have already written, this proves what is requested in the Torah: that both [study and action] should be heard as one thing, a body corresponding to everything else. 

If you look with contemplation, you will always find this. This is why it says: *And let our hearts cleave to Your Torah* and finally, *and unify our hearts* <note>Liturgy: "וייחד לבבנו"</note>, for the end will come to love, and it cleaves even more for the sake of the rectification of perfection. And he will support the intellect to [distinguish] the sweet and the bad for the good, as they understood: *With all your heart*—with both of your inclinations <note>Berakhot 54a: the 'Good Inclination' and the 'Evil Inclination'</note>. This is the ultimate good and the perfection of choice, which is to rectify all internal aspects toward a straight intention, as they were in the perfection of the Voice in thought before they emerged. These will bring existence and sustenance, their intention established for all that is precious and light once the Unification has occurred. I have already written this.

And finally: *So that we may never be ashamed or confounded.* Since through action the preservation of perfection begins, it is as we said: our entire purpose is the intention which is to be perfected in us, which is the rectification of the "Glory" <note>The Kavod/Shekhinah</note>. As we wrote, in everything we shall not be ashamed or confounded forever, all within the rectification of the secret... the matters of our perfection. Perfection is close to the matter... to complete it by His will. For when his [man's] intention is brought—for which he was created—which was the rectification of the Glory and the unification of this Name, it completes and establishes it forever. This is the meaning of: *And open... and circumcise our hearts to fear Your name.* In the way explained there, he prayed: *Return us to You.*

*For in His holy name [we trust]*... through his intention, the rectification of the secret is made, to make us believe that through it we are doing Your will. *We shall exult and rejoice in Your salvation*—now we ask for the Purpose, the place and the movement of the hand to complete this rectification, which is the salvation we hope for. The time will come of which it is said: *For the earth shall be full of the knowledge of the Lord* <note>Isaiah 11:9</note>. Then there will be the capacity to complete the intention for which we were created. *And let us rejoice in Your salvation*—for behold, a King shall come to you, righteous and victorious <note>Zechariah 9:9</note>. We have already explained all of this. *And bring us in blessing and peace from the four corners of the earth*—the "Righteous One" and the "Righteous One," meaning as it is said: *And those who are lost in the land of Assyria shall come* <note>Isaiah 27:13</note>. After that, we ask concerning the orders that prevent and delay this perfection, which refers to the nations who are upon our necks, in the sense of: *O Lord our God, other lords beside You have had dominion over us* <note>Isaiah 26:13</note>. This is what is meant by: *And break the yoke from off our necks.* You have the power to act against the iniquities and to have pity on the souls, just as You acted previously. For You chose us from every people and language, and may the promise be fulfilled for us... and further, that You brought us near to Your Great Name in love, as we wrote. The purpose of all this is to thank You and to unify You, for this is Your will. And You shall be glorified and completed in the attribute of... and You brought us near to Your Great Name in His glory, which is perfection.

### Chapter One ###

Regarding the knowledge of this section and its purpose, the wisdom and the secret of its signature will be explained in this part through an allusion to all the hidden goodness in the "countenance of the world." <term>Countenance of the world (Dikna): A Kabbalistic term referring to the radiating channels of divine mercy and wisdom</term>. One must know before Him that "knowledge" <note>Hebrew: Da'at</note> is like the removal of their deficiency, which receives... and the voice and vision... this one acquires our companionship... for my heart is prepared to honor [God] through these degrees. As the sages said: "Exercise kindness, justice, and righteousness" <note>original: "oseh chesed mishpat u-tzedakah" from Jeremiah 9:23</note>. Behold, these are three specific "Alphas" <term>Alphas: Here used to mean primary principles or divine attributes</term> within the crown of the Tetragrammaton <note>The four-letter name of God, YHWH</note>, and in them He delights. The secret is to establish the Kingdom <note>The Sephirah of Malchut</note> through the "doing" of the preciousness, and to establish the Honor <note>The Sephirah of Tiferet</note> through the correction of the...

And this is the calculation and His will in the creation. This is what is meant by "returning," for at the beginning, because of the power of the Name of the Lord in these defects, the Unification <term>Unification (Yichud): The meditative act of declaring and visualizing the oneness of God's various attributes</term> would become complete and acquired through the Name. This is the meaning of "knowing Me" <note>original: "Haskel ve-yado'a oti" from Jeremiah 9:23</note>. Therefore, the unique path is the knowledge of the Lord, which is the intention and His will, and the connection of all things. When one prays for this completion, it ascends according to its rectitude and its degree in the knowledge of the secret. This is the hint and the reward explained at the beginning of this section: that the ultimate purpose of all created beings is the **Perfect Man** <term>Perfect Man (Adam HaShalem): The idealized human state where physical and spiritual wisdom are integrated</term>, and the ultimate purpose of the Perfect Man is the Secret of Unification and the Knowledge of the Lord.

The absence of this wisdom and knowledge caused the exile. We are in a state of offering where we do not recognize Him, especially in this current exile where the Unification is hidden, and there is no one who knows, understands, or takes it to heart. This is undoubtedly the cause of the exile and the destruction. If the first man had kept the eyes of his intellect open to gaze upon the Supernal Unification, all his focus would have been upward in Wisdom to know his Creator. But after the [act of] Kindness, it is written: "And the eyes of both of them were opened" <note>Genesis 3:7</note>. In the Midrash of Rabbi Shimon bar Yochai <note>The Zohar</note>, it asks: Why were they "opened" to gaze? Because they entered into what they did not know until then. Once they knew, their eyes were opened to hear, and then they knew that their eyes were... to eat from it. They were called "rising" to seek [sustenance] from the mouth of the Most High and to withdraw from His power. They were found to be "naked" of... and concerning this it says: "And the eyes of both of them were opened and they knew they were naked" through the judgment of the world, perceiving what they did not perceive before when they were "open" above.

It is also written there: "I will lead the blind by a way they knew not" <note>Isaiah 42:16</note>. This does not mean opening physical eyes, but rather intending to gaze upon His eternal wisdom and to look at what they did not understand in this world. This is so they will merit to perceive and have the scrutiny to reach His conversation. All that wisdom is our wisdom, and there is no knowledge in the distant secret... for since my intention is for the ultimate purpose of the cause of Unification and clinging <term>Clinging (Devekut): The meditative state of being constantly mindful of and attached to the Divine</term> to Him, and it is not yet found, He is destined to complete it and to be crowned with the Crown of Wisdom, from which we shall know the Unification. When His intention in creation is spread out, it is the meaning of "I will lead the blind," for there are none so blind as those without the wisdom to gaze with Wisdom to know the Name in this way. And know that this is "The Way of the Lord," which is the Unification.

"In paths they have not known I will guide them"—these are the paths of the Supernal Wisdom, the Unification designated in the Name. "I will make darkness light before them"—this is the darkness that darkens the eyes of the intellect, which drew away the eyes of Adam and caused them to leave the Supernal Light. This is the cause of the world, the Unification, the Wisdom, and the Knowledge of the Lord. And for the poverty of man, He will turn that "thick cloud" into "light," so that he will no longer abandon the darkness or abandon perfection. This is the "crooked path" that diminishes the creatures to make them stumble, walking in a way that is not good. But now, through kindness to their uprightness, it says: "I will lead them in a straight way, they shall not stumble," in the paths of the Holy One, which are Wisdom and the Knowledge of the Lord. These are the matters whose contents are immediate to completing the Name and the intention in creation.

By the degree of this staff in the world... to return the ten to their original state, so that the first intention, which is the Unification, may begin. He is destined to clarify this. This is the explanation of what our teacher chose for this chapter and likewise in the reveal of the third part. Behold, I bless the Lord who has answered me... for the sake of the glory of His name.

->**The Part of the Ultimate Purpose is finished and complete: Which points toward the One without end.**<-

<column-break/>

<margin>
In the ancient wisdom received by us from Sinai, the wisdom of the Torah and the secrets of the Torah were specifically entrusted to the Levites. They studied the Torah as a body and a soul. During the time when the "order of the secrets" was sealed, it was not revealed to the world at large, nor was it entirely written down. In every generation, this book of sealed wisdom was passed from the mouth of a King to one who receives the "Solomonic portions of wisdom." It would have been likely that the Levites would not have been moved to stir the heart for those who cover and hide these secrets, and this is an essential reason why the wisdom of our secrets was nearly lost entirely. 

But I have written that because this is a path in the "palace," it is impossible for it to pass away. What greater wisdom is there than that praised by the Prophet, saying the Lord acts through His secret? Indeed, this was because the Name... to do... and in the vision of Rabbi Shimon ben Yochai (peace be upon him): "It is time to act for the Lord; they have made void Your Torah" <note>Psalm 119:126</note>. What does "It is time to act for the Lord" mean? It means when they have "made void the Torah"—the Supernal Torah—by not receiving it, it must not be allowed to pass away into the hands of those who would mock it.

Rabbi Judah said: "It is time to act for the Lord" in order to sustain the Torah and not let it be consumed entirely. Behold, in these matters, a high degree is diminished if it is not acted upon in its specific place, which is the correction of the Glorious Name and the "Special Treasure." One must turn to the Lord to establish the connection for Him, and these are the general principles in this Name—the unification of all in His Glory. Since this correction is impossible without the knowledge of Wisdom in its treasuries, it was written "Seek life" so that the path would not be lost. 

This wisdom was gathered from the mouths of the sages of Israel, such as the *Book of Formation* <term>Sefer Yetzirah: An ancient mystical text attributed to the patriarch Abraham</term> and for the Sages of the Talmud, the *Book of the Brilliant* <term>Sefer HaBahir: A foundational 12th-century kabbalistic work attributed to Rabbi Nehunia ben HaKanah</term>. There are also the many books regarding the identification of this wisdom, such as the book of Rav Meiri Gaon, and the responsa of Rav Hai Gaon concerning the "Roots," and the *Book of the Tikkunim* <term>Tikkunei Zohar: A later commentary on the Zohar focusing on the first word of the Torah</term> which the holy Rabbi Shimon bar Yochai (peace be upon him) composed. This is the great book... Rabbi Shimon bar Yochai... and then the *Book of the Radiance* <term>Sefer HaZohar: The central work of Jewish mysticism</term> was revealed, which was hidden for thousands of years. As it is written in the *Book of the Tikkunim*, it was meant to be revealed through the hand of "this one" to be discovered by those of noble spirit...

I have already written and added these essential reasons why this wisdom was hidden from the nation. I have elaborated in several places on why it was withheld. I have brought it back here to benefit those who seek this wisdom now. For this secret is a book of this wisdom. Even though the knowledge of it was almost entirely lost from the nation, the "Good and Great" [God] has willed that the knowledge which was said to be "His portion" should be sustained. And I have searched through the books received concerning it and added to them...

# Chapter 2: Section on the Secrets of the Torah #

### Chapter 2 — Page 111 ###

->**Chapter 2**<-

...which guards this secret. Furthermore, the matter of "Generations" <term>Generations (Toldot): In this context, it refers to the cosmological outcomes or spiritual lineages emerging from divine emanations</term> contains lofty secrets within it, and the writings testify to the sublime **Secret of Intercalation** <term>Secret of Intercalation (Sod Ha-Ibur): The traditional term for the calculations used to align the lunar and solar calendars, which Kabbalists believe contains deep mystical insights into the nature of time and divinity</term>. Many things in the "Calculation of Yah" <note>Hebrew: Heshbon Yah; likely referring to divine mathematics or the name of God</note> are directed toward this secret. It is said that Maimonides <note>The text likely refers to Maimonides (the Rambam), though using a shorthand title</note> was an expert in the "Wisdom of the Spheres" <note>Astronomy</note>, seasons, and zodiac signs, and knew how to intercalate years and establish months. These secrets were handed down to him along with the order of the **Secrets of the Torah** and their reasons. According to this, what you might think regarding this matter—that knowing how to intercalate years and so on is simply a plain matter—is incorrect. What the Sages said in the chapter "The Judges of the Palm Tree" <note>Reference to a specific Talmudic discussion, possibly Sanhedrin</note> is that it is part of the "Secrets of the Torah" according to the specific secret intended by it, in the way that I have explained.

However, as for why it is forbidden to reveal it to the nations of the world, even if it were derived from the logic of these matters, this is a hidden doubt that needs to be clarified for the discerning. It seems to me that I can resolve this doubt: it is known among those who possess wisdom that through the **Secret of Intercalation**, one can establish times and the authority of changes and the awakening of "likenesses." Through it, the rain and other spiritual transformations and the authority of souls are established. There is no way to understand this principle or to distinguish between truth and falsehood except by standing upon the "Secret of Intercalation," as is known to those who stand within its secret. Furthermore, everything that relies on this Secret of Intercalation is necessary for the preservation of the world and for the Unification of the Unique Lord, for "there is none else besides Him" <note>Deuteronomy 4:35</note>. From this secret, one understands the preservation of the Chosen Nation and the excellence of this Torah which Moses set before them. It is impossible to divide the nation or to exchange this Torah.

Additionally, one can discern the innermost secret of the intercalation. If this were known to the nations, they would undoubtedly convert, for they would realize that their origins are "hard and difficult" <note>original: "kashim ve-kashiyot"</note> and that their ancestors inherited lies. None of them would have a place <note>original: "shel makom"</note> in the miracle which will be revealed to sanctify His great name, which is praised among the nations. The greatness and wonders within it cannot be revealed until the transformation of **Gog and Magog**, as Ezekiel said: "Thus will I magnify Myself, and sanctify Myself; and I will be known in the eyes of many nations, and they shall know that I am the Lord" <note>Ezekiel 38:23</note>. The Prophet (peace be upon him) also said: "For then will I turn to the people a pure language, that they may all call upon the name of the Lord, to serve Him with one accord" <note>Zephaniah 3:9</note>. And it is said: "And the Lord shall be king over all the earth: in that day shall there be one Lord, and His name one" <note>Zechariah 14:9</note.

Behold, at first He will be magnified and sanctified in the eyes of all nations, and afterward He will make His name known, and they will wait for the "Whiteness" <note>Hebrew: Levanot; possibly a metaphor for spiritual purity or the moon/Shekhinah</note>—those who were false in the world—and He will circumcise them. Therefore, He instilled in Israel the nature not to reveal the Secret of Intercalation to the nations of the world. Even among the Chosen Nation itself, it is forbidden to reveal it except to one who possesses these qualities. All this is to demonstrate the preciousness of this secret and its gravity.

It is a rare virtue to find in these generations one who is spoken of as Moses was at the Tower <note>original: "be-babelah"</note>. I too "knew that I did not know" <note>A classic philosophical expression of humility</note>; and if I have strayed with my lips regarding this great secret, I have only repeated what I heard. Even if I haven't grasped the matter in its full clarity, or if I heard it and forgot it due to my distractions, it would have been fitting for me to strike myself so as not to ascend this great mountain, nor to quench my coals in its flame, and not to write a book about the "Secret of Secrets." But because of my spirit and my desire for my chapters and my portions, this thing was in my heart like a burning fire. Because of my longing, I have no rest to sleep. I said to myself, "I will be broken and broken" <note>unclear: "eshaber ve-eshaber"</note>. It is "a time to act for the Lord; they have voided Your Torah" <note>Psalm 119:126</note>—to act to repair this matter. If it is not repaired through this correction, then "Your Torah"—the Torah of Above—is nullified. It was my desire to write down what I received and what I found from the holy, celestial sages who stand in the secret of Greatness: the **Work of Creation** and the **Work of the Chariot** <term>Work of Creation / Chariot (Ma'aseh Bereshit / Merkavah): The two primary categories of ancient Jewish mysticism—the study of the cosmos and the study of the divine throne</term>, with the help of Him who teaches man knowledge.

Before this, I must say that these two commandments do not hinder one another. That is to say, it is possible for a true sage to be expert in one while remaining a void in the other. This was the matter regarding the dispute between the Sages and Rav Yosef, for they were repeating the Work of Creation and were experts in its form and intent, for they had received the ancient traditions regarding the goal of Creation. This is the Secret of the Work of Creation.

<column-break/>

Since anyone who has tasted even a little of the "Wisdom of the Spheres" <note>Astronomy</note> knows that there is no doubt in the world that the sphere is fixed, and this is a matter visible to the eyes, it follows that the calculation of seasons and zodiac signs is not hidden from the eyes of the nations. Indeed, for its practical application, we even need them. However, I know that the **Secret of Intercalation** was a wisdom and understanding "hidden from the eyes of the nations" and part of the "Secrets of the Torah." Regarding the Sabbath, it is said "He gave it as an inheritance to His people, to Jacob," etc. <note>Refers to the idea that the Sabbath and the calendar are unique Jewish inheritances</note>. Therefore, for every nation, the Secret of Intercalation—upon which all things depend—is a unique and precious possession. Through it, the relationship between "Above and Below" is established, and the reasons for the Torah are rooted. Because it is an open matter for those who are upright, we have been warned not to reveal it because of those short of mind and small in wisdom who would treat hidden matters with their own logical speculation and limited tools of attainment.

Such people treat the terrifying and wondrous things hinted at in the Torah and the books of the Sages as objects of mockery, investigating them with external intellect... until our Master explained that in the end, the Intercalation and the reasons of the Torah and its secrets are received traditions, not my own invention. I must rise and inform you that the Secret of Intercalation is *not* merely the calculation of seasons and zodiac signs; Heaven forbid that it should be so. It is difficult to strip away the "external shells" <note>Hebrew: Kelippot; a Kabbalistic term for the layers of mundane reality that hide spiritual truth</note> until they hear that the Secret of Intercalation is actually the calculation of seasons and zodiac signs.

Furthermore, in the chapter "The Judges," Rabbi Eliezer says that when they went out to the Land of Israel, he said: "I will reveal my exile first." For when he was in the war, he fled and they found him involved in the Secret of Intercalation. He said, "I will reveal it first," and his hand was upon the... <unclear/>... in the secret of "My people shall they not be" <note>Ezekiel 13:9</note>. The Rabbi <note>Maimonides</note> wrote on this that it is a clear and distant matter that the Secret of Intercalation is not merely the calculation of seasons and zodiac signs, for no superior wisdom was required for that. One could be a "rider upon a rider" <note>an expert</note> once he knew the calculation of seasons and zodiac signs and knew how to anticipate the new moon and intercalate the year. Thus, there is no greatness in that alone.

Remember what was said in the chapter in Sanhedrin: it implies that "Intercalation" refers to the Secret. We learn there: "In the secret of My people shall they not be"—this refers to the Intercalation. And further, when it was time to intercalate, the Prophet said to him... <unclear/>. Believe with clarity that the Secret of Intercalation is the wisdom and understanding above which there is nothing higher. It is the Secrets of the Torah and its wondrous reasons, as the Rabbi said. However, there is no proof from there, because when it says he was involved in the Secret of Intercalation, it does not refer to the learning and the knowledge, but to the removal of the external... to anticipate the intercalation. For this, one must be ordained <note>Smikhah</note>, and before that, one must have prior knowledge of the calculation. Afterward, they draw him away from the "externals" to intercalate. As we say in the chapter in Sanhedrin: "We do not intercalate the year through 'externals'" <note>meaning those outside the inner circle or unauthorized</note>.

But a difficulty arises: what is the "secret" in this, such that it would be said of it, "In the secret of My people shall they not be"? These secrets of wisdom were known to all, and the sages of the nations were more sophisticated in them than the sages of Israel! One cannot argue that the calculation itself is the Secret of Intercalation. In the Chapters of Rabbi Eliezer <note>Pirkei De-Rabbi Eliezer</note>, they said that the Head of the Academy mentions the Divine Name, and they hear the sound of the announcement, and it speaks in a language of heat <note>possibly "hush" or "vision"</note>, saying: "The Lord spoke to Moses and Aaron... saying, this month shall be to you," etc. <note>Exodus 12:1-2</note>. It is possible that because of this, they called it the "Secret of Intercalation."

It occurred to me to say that for this reason they gave it this name: because this "intercalation" <note>Ibur</note> has a relationship and similarity to the **True Secret of Intercalation**, which is the Secrets of the Torah and its reasons. For "Intercalation" <note>Ibur</note> means to equalize and align the path of the sun and the path of the moon, and joining them together as equals points toward the Unity of their archetypes. This is like the celestial beings who are in a state of equal existence, which is part of the sublime Secret of Intercalation. For this reason, they applied the term "Secret of Intercalation" to the calculation of the year, to point toward this deeper secret. This reason is sufficient for calling it by this name. The holy sages of Israel were aware of this and were directed toward this wondrous secret. To this they aimed when intercalating the year, following the words of our Sages regarding the sanctification of the month and the intercalation of the year.

### Chapter 1

He who wrote and did not repeat said: He who knows the solution to a matter <note>A reference to Ecclesiastes 8:1</note>—they taught him the truth of Man. And they taught that from the knowledge of His will, one finds the wisdom of **hidden grace** <term>Hidden Grace (Hesed Ha-Tzafun): The primordial divine benevolence that is "stored away" in the highest levels of the Godhead</term> which is concealed in the Supreme Wisdom. He draws from that Wisdom toward the Supernal Countenance and returns to it. Through it, the small and the smallest of the judges <note>Likely referring to the lower emanations or human authorities</note> can cause Mercy to return. This is the special quality of the Divine Will: to reveal Grace in the eyes of God for all those who follow the "banner" <note>Hebrew: Degel</note> of miracle. This is why He does not withhold their wisdom, and the knowledge of the end is all in the Book.

The inner foundation of the secrets of the scriptures is that everything is a sealed mystery for the "House of the Wise." They receive his offerings, and no one who inherits it fears the "Seal of Death." All of these matters are derived from the secrets that hint at the **hidden mysteries of the Cup** <note>original: "Sitri Kos"; possibly a reference to the "Cup of Blessing" or a vessel of emanation</note>. Who knows the secret of the hidden secret? Its secret is known to the Living, but there is no understanding for others. When the Living exists in accordance with what is written: "By wisdom He founded the earth" <note>Proverbs 3:19</note>, then we shall know the "solution to the matter." The book recounts the improvement of the wicked and the decree upon Israel. He wrote to the **Grace of the Secrets** <note>original: "Hesdat Seri"</note> regarding mercy for Israel. They hinted that the wisdom of knowledge and the heights of attainment are unique to the "Unique One." One who digs to weigh it in the secret of the burden <note>original: "Sevel"</note> will find it exalted; they shall not explain it further. Here is the foundation of the return: explaining the solution of the matters to Israel through His Torah, just as "He has declared to His people the power of His works" <note>Psalm 111:6</note>.

### Chapter 2

In truth, within the letters of the secrets of the Torah assembly, and to return to its smallness, **Ramban** <note>original: "Ramban" - Rabbi Moses ben Nahman (Nahmanides), a 13th-century philosopher and Kabbalist</note> mentions returning to the "Small Zuta" and the surrounding environment of the "Living." However, these are for the "holy ones who are wise." These secrets were only handed down to the "Pious of the Ages" <note>original: "Vatikim"</note>, and only to a wise man according to his strength. This is because the secret is like returning to grace by way of a parable, like turning bitter to sweet. Thus, he explains the boundary and can come to action and speech.

There are chapters they cannot explain, and for this reason, they do not expound upon the **Chariot** <term>Work of the Chariot (Ma’aseh Merkavah): The most guarded mystical traditions in Judaism, dealing with the divine throne and the nature of the celestial realms</term> at all, unless the student is already a wise man who understands from his own knowledge. In such a case, one may transmit to him the "Heads of Chapters." **Rashi** <note>original: "Rashi" - Rabbi Solomon ben Isaac, the preeminent medieval commentator</note> taught that we do not hand over the secrets of the Torah, such as the **Work of Creation** <term>Work of Creation (Ma’aseh Bereshit): The esoteric study of cosmology and the origins of the universe based on the opening of Genesis</term> and the Work of the Chariot, except to those who have been clarified through these specific qualities. These were already explained in the Talmud. 

The intention is that according to the truth of the wisdom, one must possess these qualities. The reason for this is that he acts as a "supernal example." It is fitting to hand over the secret of the Work of Creation to him, for within the generalities are the **Fifty Gates of Understanding** <term>Fifty Gates of Understanding (Hamishim Sha’arei Binah): The levels of divine insight; according to tradition, Moses reached the 49th gate</term>. And so it is with the "Inner Countenance"—that he should be a man of great deeds in the fulfillment of the commandments, believing in the intent of Mercy. This continues until he can "see the face" in his generation, such as Rabbi Hanina ben Dosa, may peace be upon him, who rose very high in the Gates. He reached the point where he could stand firm in his lineage, as is explained in its place. No man like him exists who can understand the Received Tradition (Kabbalah) and the secrets. 

There are three ways concerning the Work of Creation and the Work of the Chariot. One involves honoring his teachers, as Moses did at the Burning Bush. By this, he recognizes the "power of His works." The second involves merit and understanding.

<column-break/>

The second way involves the choice of laws and rulings. He is like a "spring of water" <note>original: "Berekhah"</note> who bestows strength until he becomes a teacher to the wise, with the truth of his mouth speaking words of Torah. These are the two paths we have written. And this is correct: to "understand one thing from another" <note>original: "Mevin mada’ato"</note>. This is what happens when they tell him the secrets of the Chariot in the form of "Heads of Chapters"—he understands the secret of the words and their explanation on his own and does not need to ask. 

When it is said that one who is crowned with these qualities is worthy of having the words written at the beginning handed to him—those are the **Secrets of the Torah**. These qualities generally include: Old Age (Wisdom), Wisdom, Understanding, and Action. This is the perfection of the Supernal Knowledge. For these are the secret of the Work of Creation, from the beginning until its end. And through this, he performs "Work of Creation," as it is written: "The Lord by wisdom founded the earth; by understanding He established the heavens" <note>Proverbs 3:19</note>. With His "Knowledge," the depths were broken open. The Work of the Chariot depends on this. Thus, it is clear that one crowned with these qualities is an example of the "Supernal Work," and he is the one who "turns his face on high" toward the Work of the Chariot. It is not fitting to hide the "Honor of the Lord" <note>original: "Kavod YHVH"</note> from him. 

The Sages said that "one who knows how to calculate the cycle" <note>The astronomical cycle</note> and establish the calendar is part of the Secrets of the Torah. They stated that he must be appointed to this task before the secrets are handed to him. In the second chapter of the tractate, they mention that the **Secret of Intercalation** <term>Secret of Intercalation (Sod Ha-Ibur): The calculation of the lunar and solar years to set the Jewish calendar, viewed by Kabbalists as a deep mystical secret</term> is among the secrets of the Torah. We must ensure that a "minor" <note>one unlearned or young</note> does not come and reveal the secret of intercalation as a mere "sign" <note>astronomical sign</note>. This is the version of our masters, the **Tosafists** <note>original: "Ba’alei Ha-Tosafot" - 12th-13th century French and German Talmudic scholars</note>. Their explanation is that they should not reveal the "Secret of Intercalation" in common language, for it contains his wisdom. 

However, the version of **Rashi, of blessed memory**, is that they should not reveal the secret to everyone. He calls it "The Secret of Intercalation" and connects it to the "Secret of the Reasons of the Torah." This implies that the Intercalation is indeed part of the Secrets of the Torah. It is written regarding this: "It shall not be among the general words of Torah." We learned in the chapter "One Does Not Expound" <note>Hagigah, Chapter 2</note> that one does not hand over the words of Torah to a gentile, as it is written: "He declares His words to Jacob... He has not done so for any other nation" <note>Psalm 147:19-20</note>. This is because of the "Secret of the Treasures of the Torah."

The holy Kabbalist **Rabbi Todros Ha-Levi, of blessed memory** <note>13th-century Spanish Kabbalist and author of "Otzar HaKavod"</note>, wrote: "From here you learn that the Secret of Intercalation is NOT what our Rabbis meant by the calculation of seasons and zodiac signs." For we do not find that the Sages were overly protective of those calculations; all of Israel were experts in them. In these generations, even school children are experts in calculating seasons and zodiacs. Furthermore, the Sages said: "For this is your wisdom and your understanding in the sight of the nations" <note>Deuteronomy 4:6</note>. What is wisdom and understanding in the sight of the nations? This refers to the calculation of seasons and zodiacs. If there were an "oath" or a prohibition on teaching it, they wouldn't have permission to learn and teach it! Furthermore, the "Sages of the Nations" are more expert in this science than the Sages of Israel. As the Sages said: "The Sages of Israel say the sphere is fixed and the zodiac rotates, while the Sages of the Nations say the sphere rotates and the zodiac is fixed." And the Sages of Israel [eventually conceded] to the Sages of the Nations...

<meta>This page continues the esoteric analysis of the creation narrative from Genesis 1.
