### Chapter 4: Section on the Secrets of the Torah - Chapter 4, 112

All other wisdoms were included within it, spreading forth from it by the power of the **Simple Thought** <term>Simple Thought (Mahshavah Peshutah): In Kabbalistic thought, this is the primordial, undifferentiated divine plan before it takes form</term>, which is supreme within it. It serves as a palace below to sow within it the holy seed of all other generations. Except for the word *Bereshit* <note>original: "In the beginning"</note>, which includes both of them in the secret of "Head of the House" <note>A wordplay on Bereshit (ב-ראשית) as Rosh-Bayit (ראש-בית)</note>, for in it, every primary thing was included in the Holy Light. Still, everything remained within the Thought. And in the spreading of that Thought, it becomes the **First Point**, whether in its hidden or revealed state. Its expansion was for the benefit of the created beings, and it was life itself. This is the meaning of "In the beginning He created" <note>Genesis 1:1</note>, which existed through the power of the First Point—the Thought.

The second stage is the Sanctuary, which is called *Elohim* <note>The Divine Name associated with justice and structure</note>, in which all other desires were included. Their time comes when they spread forth from that seed which includes everything from the beginning. This is the "Generations of the Heaven and the Earth," and it is the secret of all the letters included in the Throne. This is the secret of the letters given to Moses—the Written Torah. And this is the secret of *El* <note>God</note>: it is the letters. "The Heavens" refers to Him and His partner, for in the light they went out. This is the secret of "the Heavens"—male and female. The Holy Name <note>Y-H-W-H</note> is called *Et* <note>The Hebrew particle 'את', often used in Kabbalah to signify the totality of the alphabet from Aleph to Tav, representing the Shekhinah or Divine Presence</note>, the totality of all letters, which was the totality of everything. Afterward, both were included in one another through the secret of "and He completed *Et*." This is the secret of "and He sent forth majesty" <note>referring to divine emanation</note>.

This expansion was done to produce "generations" <note>offspring/results</note> for the preservation of the worlds. This is the secret of **Man**, the secret of *Elohim* in a small measure. For through the entry and expansion of everything within it, that which was supreme existed with this to create worlds in their proper establishment. "And God created Heaven and Earth"—this is the secret of the two *B*'s in *Bereshit* <note>The letter Bet (ב) has the numerical value of 2</note>, representing two worlds.

For the **Upper Elohim** <term>Upper Elohim: Often associated with the Sephirah of Binah (Understanding), the divine womb of creation</term> created the Heavens and the Earth in a state of equality and expansion. But the **Lower Elohim** <term>Lower Elohim: Often associated with the Sephirah of Malkhut (Kingship) or the Shekhinah, the manifest presence of God</term> is the secret of the "Final He" <note>The last letter of the Name Y-H-W-H</note> who builds the heaven and earth and every creature from what was clarified and expanded from the Higher Power. The word *Bereshit* hints at both of them, for everything was made from the first power. When interpreted regarding the upper realms, *Elohim* is the secret of the "First Aleph" in power; when interpreted regarding the lower realms, *Elohim* is the secret of the "Final He." From the power of equality and expansion in the upper realms, there was balance and permanence in the lower realms.

Just as the light of desire and permanence comes from *Binah* (Understanding), *Hokhmah* (Wisdom), and *Binah*—all within the Divine Will—to become the Upper Heaven and Earth, so too everything is clarified and expanded through the power of the "Final Building," the secret of the Lower Elohim, to create the lower heaven and earth with every creature. This is the matter of "These" and "God"—the *El* of these includes all letters, which is the Upper Elohim we began with.

The expansion of all created beings into existence was done through His power, and the action of all the "Work of Creation" in the lower realms comes from the power of the "Work of Creation" <term>Work of Creation (Ma’aseh Bereshit): The study of the origins of the physical universe</term> specifically. Behold, the Upper Elohim sustained heaven and earth through the aspect of *Hesed* (Grace/Mercy). The Lower Elohim, regarding whom it is said "Even my hand founded the earth and my right hand spanned the heavens; I call to them, they stand together" <note>Isaiah 48:13</note>, acts through both the right and the left. The Right created and established the heavens, and the Left created and founded the earth. This is the secret of "I call to them, they stand together."

The Lower Elohim, the secret of the "Final He," created and made the lower realms in the likeness of the upper realms—one corresponding to the other. Everything from the first Thought to its end is connected, and when everything is grasped by the "Last," it becomes a "Beginning" as well, for it is the head and beginning for all that is beneath it.

<column-break/>

The Upper [God created] the heavens and the earth, the lower realms, and every creature. For "In the beginning God created" means the Upper Beginning mentioned, returning to the Upper Elohim in the hidden power. From it, the other "generations" were clarified. The end is reflected in the womb, for from the beginning it was called "Beginning" after His name. In *Bereshit* <note>In the beginning</note>, the Upper Elohim created the lower heaven and earth; in it He created everything and in it He sustains it.

Another matter: *Bereshit*—He created a beginning for Man, founded it, and established it upon its dust. This is the "Written Torah," the secret of the letter *Yod*, which is a beginning for the three later stages. This was created by the Lower Elohim, the secret of the "Final He," [creating] the heaven and the earth. This is the secret of the hint that "the Holy One, blessed be He, looked into the Torah and created the world."

**"And the earth was unformed and void"** <note>Genesis 1:2</note>. The "Earth" is the one mentioned in the first verse. It became "unformed" (*Tohu*) after the creation, meaning the whole world was like wine that had become pregnant <note>fermented</note> with its dregs (*Shemarim*) which were mixed within it. This is the "difficult Tohu." Before it was clarified and set in its place, the dregs went down.

**"And darkness was over the face of the deep"**: This is the secret of the seal that carves out the creatures. It hovers over the face of the deep in Thought. For *Tohu* is the secret of the "Noise of the Multitude" and the dregs that emerge from it. The "Face of the Deep" is the "Face of Evil," which is called "Darkness." This is the secret of the "affliction of the eyes" and the "darkness of the eyes." Why? Because it is the sight and the gaze into the soul of the wicked.

**"And the Spirit of God hovered over the face of the waters"**: This is for His understanding and His joy. The "Face of the Waters" refers to the "split stones" in the deep from which water emerges. In the chapter "One Does Not Expound" <note>A famous chapter in the Talmud, Hagigah</note>, it is taught: "*Tohu* is a **Green Line** <term>Green Line (Kav Yarok): A mystical boundary that surrounds the world and from which darkness emanates</term> that encompasses the entire world, and from it darkness goes out to the world. *Vohu* refers to the split stones sunken in the deep from which water emerges."

The Green Line encompasses the world, and from it comes darkness. From the power of that darkness, the faces of the creatures were drawn. It is impossible to stand upon the depth of these matters unless one has been enlightened by the **Secret of Intercalation** <term>Secret of Intercalation (Sod Ha-Ibur): A dual-meaning term referring both to the calculation of the calendar and to the mystical "impregnation" or reincarnation of souls</term>.

Rabbi Shimon ben Lakish interpreted these verses in the context of the **Exiles** <note>This is a classic Midrashic interpretation linking the chaos of creation to the future history of Israel</note>:
1. **"The earth was unformed (Tohu)"** — This is the Kingdom of **Babylon**, as it is said, "I saw the earth and behold, it was Tohu."
2. **"And void (Vohu)"** — This is the Kingdom of **Media**, as it is said, "And they hurried (*vaya-be-hilu*, related to Vohu) to bring Haman."
3. **"And darkness"** — This is the Kingdom of **Greece**, which darkened the eyes of Israel with its decrees, saying: "Write on the horn of an ox that you have no part in the God of Israel."
4. **"Over the face of the deep"** — This is the Kingdom of **Edom** <note>Rome/the current exile</note>, which is unfathomable like the deep. Just as the deep has no limit, so too Edom.
5. **"And the Spirit of God hovered"** — This is the **Spirit of the King Messiah**, as it is said, "And the spirit of the Lord shall rest upon him."

Who built these? God built them with power and will shepherd them. As the Ramban <note>Rabbi Moses ben Nahman / Nachmanides</note> and the upright ones teach knowledge: "By the word of the Lord they shall be established." Another matter: "And the earth was unformed and void"—Heaven and Earth went out through Grace (*Hesed*). They took on other countenances afterward in their fullness, as seen in Man.

<summary>This page explores the mystical origins of creation, distinguishing between the "Upper" and "Lower" Divine Names (Elohim) and interpreting the chaotic elements of Genesis 1:2 (Tohu, Vohu, Darkness) as both cosmological stages and the historical four exiles of the Jewish people, culminating in the hope of the Messiah.</summary>

### Chapter 3: Section on the Secrets of the Torah - Chapter 3

From now on, regarding those who were burdened and the discussions, etc., according to the order of the Torah portion; I wrote there in the portion of *Bereshit* <note>Genesis</note> about the things assigned and alluded to regarding the secret of the engraving <note>The Hebrew "Kiyuk" likely refers to *Hakikah*, the mystical process of "engraving" or carving out forms within the Divine light</note> within the Divine Thought. This was enacted through the power of the "Beginning of Wisdom" <term>Hokhmah: The first active spark of intellect in the Kabbalistic tree of life</term>, for the Torah portion tells of the existences of the lower realms while alluding to and awakening the existences of the upper realms and their developments, as will be explained further on.

The **Work of the Chariot** <term>Ma'aseh Merkavah: The ancient Jewish mystical tradition focused on the vision of Ezekiel and the inner workings of the Divine Realm</term> is a separate, unique matter; yet, it does not hinder the knowledge of the **Work of Creation** <term>Ma'aseh Bereshit: The mystical study of the origins of the physical universe</term>, even though the Work of Creation was contained within the Chariot, as is known to those who possess the "Grace of Wisdom" <note>A common term for Kabbalists</note>. Even though the specific, detailed order which is called the "Chariot" and the "Work of the Chariot" existed in the world as a blueprint for being, this is no wonder. For the knowledge of the Work of Creation does not depend solely on the secret of the "Unique Voice" in the Chariot, and it would not have been possible for there to be voices in the Work of Creation that were not also in the Work of the Chariot.

And indeed, although Rav Joseph <note>A prominent sage in the Talmud known for his expertise in mystical traditions</note> was not an expert in the Work of Creation in the certain way I described above, he nevertheless needed to know the secret of the ascensions of all existences in general. For if not, it would be impossible to be an expert in the Work of the Chariot, as is known to the "wise of heart." Moreover, he was given permission regarding the Work of Creation in its reality, for they are His messengers, etc. After the discussion of *Hesed* <note>Loving-kindness</note>, it will be explained through what I have written in this great principle regarding the Work of Creation and the Work of the Chariot. Therefore, we shall choose the details of the matter according to the order of the verses in the Work of Creation. This will happen after [explaining] the parts that must be introduced first, dedicating a specific chapter to this, and afterward I shall return to the order of the arrangements of the Work of Creation. From the rest of *Bereshit* <note>Genesis</note>, I shall begin to establish it, for I have remembered to converse with your mouth and your Torah which you shall speak.

### Chapter 3

Before the existence of any created being, upper or lower, the Ancient Existence existed in the essence of His being, in the *Keter* <term>Keter: "Crown," the highest and most hidden of the ten Sefirot, representing the Divine Will</term> of His being—a simple unity. Nothing was included apart from Him, as is alluded to in the interpretation of the Chapters of Rabbi Eliezer <note>Pirkei De-Rabbi Eliezer, an 8th-century Midrashic work</note> when they said: "Before the world was created, there was only the Holy One and His Name alone." By agreement regarding the Primordial Unity that cannot be grasped, everything—in its general principles—was hidden within the Great Name. As of yet, there was no hint or end to anything.

Then, it was revealed in the Primordial Thought, which is hidden from all living things, to create the world. It was being formed and sketched in its powers within the Thought. He said in His wondrous Wisdom that it would be impossible for it to stand if it were to exist according to that Thought without an intermediary. This was because the intention was to judge the unity of worlds as being free from all deficiency; yet, if the creation had come from Him without an intermediary vessel, it would have been nothing but a recipient of deficiency, or it would have been like Him in its purity and infinity. But this was not the intention; rather, the intention was for it to be finite. If it had been created thus, purely from all equilibrium, the finite being could not have endured it. Therefore, its acceptance of finitude was necessary for each of the created beings.

It was impossible for them to be complete unless they had an intermediary aspect containing both sides: from one side it would be finite, and from the other side it would be powerful and perfect. These are the "Generations of the Name," etc., a perfect power and a power of *Hesed* <note>Grace/Kindness</note>. This inclusive power cannot exist essentially in its beginning in a separate thing, for the inclusive grace must be specific and a unity for the created being. For from the side of its being in the specific collective, it includes both perfection and deficiency: perfection in its existence as a recipient of divine flow, and [deficiency] from the side where the flow is withdrawn from it.

Before this, as long as the power was not "clothed," the world could not stand upon the specific quality of the Thought within it. For this secret, they alluded in the Midrash that it was revealed in the Thought to create the world, and He would "blow" <note>or "flicker/propel"</note> the world before Him, but it would not stand. To what is this comparable? To a king who wanted to build a palace: if he does not sketch its outlines on the ground—its foundations, its bases, and its corridors—he cannot begin to build. So too, the Holy One "flickered" the world before Him, and it did not stand until He created *Teshuvah* <term>Teshuvah: Usually translated as "Repentance," but here refers to the cosmic principle of "Return," a spiritual framework allowing the world to exist despite its imperfections</term>. Behold, they explained that He was judging and repeatedly sketching and narrowing the plan of the palace, which is the world, and it would not stand unless He sketched and narrowed the foundations so they could

<column-break/>

endure it—the six hundred last ones—so that it could be created, etc. And as we explained, without them it would not be lacking, for the reason I wrote. This is the secret of the "Four Foundations" and the narrowing of the detail so that it could be created, etc., and the "Voice of Repentance" would return. So too, the developments of the Thought toward manifesting life within it are known. Know that from the Higher Thought, it was bequeathed to the "Primordial Precious Thought." Everything was necessitated, as will be explained.

The Holy Light <note>Likely referring to the Zohar or the author of a mystical text</note>, regarding the return to the foundation, said in this language: "It arose in the deep will of the Holy Ancient One, the Holiest of all Holy, to be rectified through rectifications. For if these rectifications were not found, the worlds would not be established, and everything would be as if it were not." <note>original Aramaic: "סלקא לי עמיקא לעתיקא קדישא לקדישין לא להתתקן בחין תיקונין לא אשתכחו עלמין... וכלה תלייא כלא הוו"</note>. Behold, he explained that the worlds were not established until these rectifications were set—and they are the secret of the Upper Constellations, which are the secret of the Hidden Name that makes Him known through the upper and lower "hangings." For there is no path to the collective perfection of the emanations except in the way I have written.

And in the Midrash of Rabbi Nehunya ben HaKanah <note>Sefer HaBahir</note>: "Until I loved it in your words," implying that before the world was established, it was in the power of the Holy One before it existed, as I have already mentioned. And according to the law of the seekers: "With ten utterances the world was created: with Wisdom, with Understanding, and with Knowledge, with Strength, and with Might, and with Rebuke, etc." And the rest are from the "Remnant of the Thirds" in the Great Name. They are the vessels of our existence through which the world's power was channeled to its limit, according to what I wrote.

We have explained their sum in the "Ten Utterances" through which the world was necessitated, etc. And thus in the Chapters of Rabbi Eliezer: "With ten utterances the world was created," and they are all included in the power of the Lord: "By Wisdom the Lord founded the earth; by Understanding He established the heavens; by His Knowledge the depths were broken open" <note>Proverbs 3:19-20</note>. This encompasses it all. And in the hearing of it, they are included in the words which are arranged according to the order of my teaching. It is impossible for the world to be created and to endure without all of them; everything necessitated His mercy through them. This is why they included "Crown" <note>Keter</note> and "Foundation" <note>Yesod</note> in the Thought of *Bereshit* <note>In the Beginning</note>.

This is what they said in the chapter "One who reads the Megillah": Rabbi Yohanan said they correspond to the Ten Utterances with which the world was created. "And He established it," and "He said," are in *Bereshit*. Is *Bereshit* itself an utterance? Yes, as it is written: "By the word of the Lord the heavens were made" <note>Psalm 33:6</note>. The secret of the creation mentioned in the lower realms is primary and awakens the secret of the Work of Creation in the upper realms. For the great existences are allusions to Wisdom, and that is the secret of the Work of Creation itself. Even if its necessity was in the lower realms, it is for this reason that they asked if the lower ones were above the upper ones. The upper cause is the reason for the existence of the lower ones, for otherwise, it would not be possible for them to exist, for the reason I wrote.

In short, the structure that counts after the engraving of the Thought consists of the necessitated words in the Work of Creation, corresponding to the upper existences. I have prepared this "Work of Creation" to give life. The priority and the inheritance from the beginning was "Divine Wisdom" (*Hokhmat Elohim*), which is a unique and inclusive power in the power of the beginning. From its power came the "Wisdom of Solomon" <note>Ecclesiastes/Proverbs</note> for the Chariot, for it too is an investigation into the mercies of the Upper Name. It is the purpose of the matters in creation and the establishment of the structure in the lower realms according to the source, exactly, without addition or subtraction. These were in the power of the upper realms through the power of creation in the Thought. Therefore, the creation in the Thought was in the likeness of the Upper Engraving, to awaken the idea that creation exists through the Name in its time and its rectification. It is impossible for anything to be created in the power of the upper or lower realms except as has been explained. With this, the intention of my labor is completed, as it is worthy to be established as the Work of Creation, and the Wisdom shall awaken in the explanation of the matter, with the help of Him who teaches man knowledge.

### Chapter 4
The emanation of the messengership <note>Atzilut: The process of Divine Emanation</note> is as we introduced. Everything was within the *Keter* <note>Crown</note> and ascended in the Primordial Return. The power of the design and its being were in the hidden darkness, and there was the Upper Grace. Upon the mark of the Point <note>The first manifestation from the Infinite</note>, which detaches everything and is called "Mercy," the "Small Utterance" was said to all the other utterances. This is what they meant by *Bereshit* <note>In the Beginning</note>, as He said. And in its power were all the rest of the utterances, and it is the gate for all existences, for it was supported by its garment...

### Chapter 1: Section of the Secrets of the Torah — Chapter 153

The excellence between right and left... and the inner secret and the general rule: both the pure and the illuminating light, and the darkness of the *Chashmal* <term>Chashmal: A mystical 'electrum' or glowing energy seen in Ezekiel's vision, often associated with the angelic realms</term> are joined together like a female... and afterwards He separated them to distinguish them. This secret is the conclusion of the Sefirah <term>Sefirah: One of the ten divine attributes or emanations through which God interacts with the universe</term> that includes all. And this "female" aspect... to be "face to face" <note>A kabbalistic term for perfect union and balance, as opposed to being 'back to back'</note> and therefore let all be one for the existence of the world...

"And God called the light Day" because its dwelling is on the Right <note>The 'Right' side in Kabbalah represents the attribute of *Chesed* or Loving-kindness</note>. And he called the darkness Night because its dwelling is on the Left <note>The 'Left' side represents *Gevurah* or Judgment/Restraint</note>, as it is written: "and the darkness He called Night." After He separated them, He called each according to its dwelling. This separation is not a total division... but they are joined together to be one. This is why it is written: "And it was evening and it was morning, one day"—night and day are called "one." To indicate this, it does not say "a first day" <note>original: *Yom Rishon*</note> but "Day One" <note>original: *Yom Echad*</note>. 

And Rabbi Yehuda bar Simon said: It does not say "Let there be evening," but "And it was evening"—from here we learn that there was a chronological order of time prior to this. Our Sages taught that God was "building worlds and destroying them" until He created these and said: "These please me, those did not please me" <note>A famous Midrashic teaching suggesting that our universe is the result of a divine balancing act of previous 'drafts' of creation</note>. This relates to the secret of the "Two Faces" <term>Du-Partzufin: The concept that primordial beings were created with two sides (male and female) joined together, later separated to face one another</term>... the upper ones are the order of time for the lower ones.

And the words of Rabbi Abbahu are wondrous secret words... it is impossible to explain everything here... The shell <term>Klipah: Literally 'husk' or 'shell'; in Kabbalah, it represents the forces of concealment or 'evil' that surround and protect the 'fruit' of holiness</term> is like a peel for the food. The shell exists to be a boundary before the inner light... and the spiritual is closer to Grace... for the Right side is the root of Grace... and because the worlds were created in this way, they endured. For as long as the form of "Man" <note>referring to *Adam Kadmon*, the primordial spiritual archetype</note> was not yet ascended and rectified as male and female "face to face," there was no stability for the Good... therefore He destroyed the previous worlds because they were without this rectification...

<column-break/>

...I have written these hints for the sake of those who must know them... to awaken the hearts of the wise and to search for the word of the Lord, so they may believe and understand that the words of our holy Sages are received traditions <note>original: *mekubalim*</note>... regarding the matter of this chapter:

### Chapter 6

"And God said: Let there be a firmament in the midst of the waters, and let it divide the waters from the waters." From here we learn the secret of duality and separation. It is asked: Why is "It was good" not said on the second day? Because on it, the light of *Gehenna* <term>Gehenna: The realm of purification or 'Hell' in Jewish thought</term> was created. 

Another answer is because on this day, "discord" <note>original: *machloket*</note> was created, as it says "and let it divide between waters and waters." Rabbi Shimi said: If a division or discord is for the rectification and existence of the world, it is ultimately good. But discord for the sake of confusion is not good. Until this point, everything was in the secret of the "Right," which is perfection and our existence; from here on, there is the "Left," where separation and boundaries were created.

God called the firmament "Heaven" <note>original: *Shamayim*</note> to distinguish between the Upper Waters and the Lower Waters, following the secret of the Left, where separation exists... for the "Right" is the unity of all, and when the "Left" was awakened, discord was awakened... 

The secret of the matter: "Let there be a firmament"—let it expand and spread... this expansion was the separation itself. The "Lower Waters" were not yet established... the Third Day arrived, where all discord was turned to peace and the work of the waters was finished. Therefore, "It was good" is said then <note>The phrase 'it was good' appears twice on the third day in Genesis, which the text explains as the resolution of the second day's division</note>. This is because there can be no offspring or continuity for the world until things are separated and each established in its own place... the letter *Vav* <note>The Hebrew letter *Vav* often represents a connecting hook or the bridge between heaven and earth</note> is between them to bring peace and to rest...

It details how the separation of light and dark, and upper and lower waters, allows for the balance of 'face to face' existence.</summary>

<meta>This page continues the exploration of the creation narrative from Genesis, moving from the distinction of Day and Night into the mystical relationship between the Upper and Lower worlds. It uses Midrashic parables to explain why the Earth was initially "unformed and void" and details the specific mechanics of the emergence of the First Light.</meta>

### Chapter 5

A man is above his wife, and he pours out for her [the blessing of] the Earth, and she is fulfilled. Its end is to be attached and to walk together, for she desired the Heavens. This is the secret of the Sun over the Moon <note>original: *chamah* and *levanah*</note> and the Earth that is influenced by his glory and his expanses. They turned "face to face" <note>A state of perfect divine union and harmony</note>, merit corresponding to merit, and they were comforted.

And according to Rabbi Isaac and Rabbi Judah bar Simon and Rabbi Abbahu, they told a parable of a king who had two servants. One he fed from the royal treasury, and to the other he said: "Whatever you toil for and earn, you shall eat." The servant who was fed from the treasury said: "I am fed from the king's bounty." But the other said: "If I do not toil, I do not eat." Thus, the Holy One, Blessed be He, dealt with the Upper and Lower beings. The Upper beings <note>The angels and spiritual entities</note> are fed from the radiance of the Divine Presence <term>Shekhinah: The indwelling presence of God in the world</term>, while the Lower beings <note>Humans and the physical world</term>, if they do not toil, they do not eat.

And Rabbi Judah bar Simon said a parable of a king who had two handmaids. To one, he gave a portion of jewelry and fine clothing, and to the other, he gave nothing. The one who received nothing said: "Is this not because of my conduct?" So too, the Holy One, Blessed be He, dealt with the Upper and Lower beings. The Upper beings live [forever], while the Lower beings [eventually] die. Therefore, "the earth was unformed and void" <note>Genesis 1:2</note>. 

Rabbi Tanchuma said: This is like a king’s daughter who was sleeping in her cradle, and her mother was preparing her clothes and her needs because she was destined to be nourished once she grew up. So too was the Earth, which was destined to nourish the man who was to be created, as it is said: "Cursed is the ground for your sake" <note>Genesis 3:17</note>. Therefore, the earth was unformed and void. 

And behold, each of these parables comes to clarify the King's face—that is, the beginning of the arousal of Wisdom <term>Chokhmah: The second Sefirah, representing the first point of conscious creation</term>. Through it, the Heavens and the Earth were intended. The Upper beings would return to be as one "Countenance" <term>Partzuf: A configuration of divine attributes acting as a persona</term> and would make use of a single Crown <note>The Sefirah of *Keter*</note>. The light upon them was as a drop, and they were both prepared for the Upper Divine Presence. No one was directed except by the hand of his fellow. 

And after they were divided and chosen, the Earth was directed by the hand of the Wise, who is the intermediary between Mercy and Truth. The sustenance was filled for the Heavens, and from it, the sustenance was directed. This too was through the arousal of the Lower beings. As was said in the parable: "Whatever you toil for and earn, you shall eat"—the Heavens are hidden and the Upper is hidden, while the Earth toils and eats. This means that the flow of energy comes through the arousal of the Lower beings, which is a great labor. It is of a hidden nature that if the arousal does not ascend from below through Torah and good deeds, as it were, there is no "sustenance" above. Certainly, regarding the sustenance of the Earth, they must be quenched and aroused by the stars. Regarding this, the Earth was unformed and void.

Indeed, the second [parable] comes to awaken us to the mystery of the Tradition <term>Kabbalah: The received mystical tradition of Judaism</term>, that the hand [of power] is toward the side of death. For when the Divine Presence was straight, there was light and life, and to peace there was no end. But when they were separated, a side of death and darkness was aroused, and the Earth became unformed. This parable is very precise, for the first servant is his [the King's] own and does not move from the Upper Palace; he is within and bound to the Name. But the second is cast out to the place where he was created, which is his place. Usually, the "handmaid" refers to the place of arousal for the "end" <note>A reference to the physical world or the final Sefirah, Malchut</note> which is meant to be guarded. This is why the Earth was unformed and void, in the secret of the arousal of chaos and death.

The third [parable] comes to awaken a wondrous secret: that the Tradition comes from the existence of the Name, but he had not yet given it a place to rule. For there was no power there except for the first [light]. As written in the Portion of the Chariot <term>Ma’aseh Merkavah: Early Jewish mysticism focused on the vision of Ezekiel</term>, they were shaken. This refers to the power of the earth beneath his hand, which was distanced for his sake. The spaces were emptied in that place, becoming a place for the House of the Lord to learn the Place. And because the Earth was opened to all this, and the Place for this was the "void," it was not yet made. Ultimately, it will be so, until it is fulfilled, and "the light of the moon shall be as the light of the sun" <note>Isaiah 30:26</note>, for the deficiency will be filled and the nourishment will be removed, and there will be no more labor in the House of the Lord. This is what was intended in this chapter.

<column-break/>

**"And God said: Let there be light, and there was light"** <note>Genesis 1:3</note>. It is written that he explains the removal of the covering, for when they were in [the state of] unformed and void and darkness, they were separated from the covering and sank into the place I called for them, the rest of the covering. According to the secret of every blemish, he went out to refine the vessels. The secret of the "remover" arrived, and that is the Light. For when the darkness was removed, it was refined, and the hidden Light was revealed, which is the "vessel of distinction." This is the secret of "And the earth was unformed and void, and darkness was upon the face of the deep, and the spirit of God hovered" <note>Genesis 1:2</note>. They were warmed and melted and refined, and the dross was separated—those things that are the "obstruction of darkness" which covers and prevents the light. 

Then the darkness was aroused from the light, and **"God said: Let there be light."** This is the light that emerges from His glory, from the beginning of the creation. From here is the beginning of the differentiation of every structure in its form, how the world was created in detail from the general principle. For all was raised up, and the Hidden One acted with a light that is not [physical] soul. All was in the secret of the parables, and his light was in the secret.

When the sweet spark spread in the Palace, Mercy <term>Chesed: The Sefirah of Loving-kindness</term> was sown within it. There, the things were prepared to be created and to be heard, referred to by the name "God" <note>original: *Elohim*</note>. It does not say "And He was so" <note>original: *Vayehi khen*</note>, because above there is no "becoming" <note>implying change</note>, nor in the middle in detail. And regarding what they said, that "In the beginning" is also a "Saying" <note>Referring to the ten utterances of creation</note>, it is certainly a Saying, for it is the general principle of all. But it does not say "And He said" because all was already prepared in thought. From here is the secret of the worlds, from what is known to be taken and to be heard, the Hidden One in his structure. It was in parables, and now it is revealed and brought forth. Whatever was and was created was done through involvement. 

And this is: **"Light, and God said: Let there be light."** This is the secret of "The Great God" <note>original: *El HaGadol*</note>, the God of Mercy. From it, all that we have mentioned testifies and informs of this secret of the *Mezuzah* and the Crown. It is gathered within it to emerge as light to the first spark, the place of expansion. This shines to the beginnings to satisfy the portion of things to be within it. 

And in this, it is clarified first and revealed. All is girt in sackcloth, and there is blessing and expansion of everything. In this spark is the "Simple Tongue" <note>The pure divine word</note> in which everything exists. If it were not so, it would return to its void. This "Greatness" <note>Chesed</note> acts in every single thing. The secret is that everything is found to be refined by the secret Will, and nothing leaves it. One who knows this secret knows in truth that all these matters of creation are through the arousal of the attributes from the "Sustenance," according to the opinion of those who contemplate from their own knowledge and intend from their hearts. 

And in the words of Rabbi Nehuniah ben HaKanah on the phrase: **"And God said: Let there be light, and there was light."** He said: This is like a king who was... his face was visible and shining upon the oil for him a place, and he placed there two lights. "And there was light" implies it already existed. The secret in this is that the Spark was from the Hidden Light of the Primordial Light <note>original: *Or Kadmon*</note>, which is the secret of secrets. It was visible like the appearance of wine... it was refined and became from it like a parable... which is the light that was already there. 

It is also found that the Spark is also called light, from the secrets of the Primordial Spark, which is the light of the "Upper Path." It was refined for him, and the "beings" were in the "hiding of the spirit." In its hiddenness, it was as if it were in the storehouse that is not refined. To sustain the world, a great light expanded from it. Because the Will was very hidden, this light that expanded was called the "First Light," the foundation of the Right Hand of the Lord, to establish it as Great. This is the secret of the Name of Israel: "There is a God" <note>original: *Yesh El*</note>, which is the beginning. And Understanding <term>Binah: The third Sefirah</term> is Light, the secret of the "Great God" that is drawn from the attribute of "God" (*Elohim*). It is found that "Let there be" (*Yehi*) is the first spark, acting to give existence to the general things as hinted at above. 

"And there was" (*Vayehi*) was the Spark of God. "Light" (*Or*)—in the fullness of its word on the Right. And in this secret "God" (*Elohim*) is included in the Right as well as the Left. Behold, all is girt together, and this word is girt. It is praised on the Left and on the Right to testify to the structure. 

**"And God saw the light, that it was good"** <note>Genesis 1:4</note>. This is the central line, for "that it was good" shines above and below. And for every branch, this is a perfect foundation for everything and fulfills everything. "And God divided the light from the darkness"—in the secret of the qualities, He made peace between the Light and the Darkness.

<summary>This page uses parables to explain the relationship between the Upper (angelic) and Lower (human) realms, emphasizing that earthly sustenance requires human toil and spiritual arousal. It details the emergence of the First Light from primordial chaos through a process of divine refinement and the balancing of the Sefirot.</summary>

# Chapter 7
## Part of the Secrets of the Torah

### Chapter 7

Everything has its source in Him, for He is the origin of all that exists below. From the day of the command "And it was so," <note>original: *vayehi khen*</note> there were divisions. "For it was good" <note>original: *ki tov*</note> was also scrutinized the following day to see if it was indeed good.

The scholars and mystics already know that a portion was set aside for "the good" apart from what was for the "other side." <note>The "other side" (*sitra achra*) refers to the realm of impurity or judgment</note>. He acted upon the "line" <note>original: *kav* — referring to the divine ray of light that began creation</note> and extended it toward the **Upper Jerusalem**. It is written that the "line" extends and reaches the foundations of all that is made. From it, the flow proceeds outward, and all the "waters of mercies" <note>original: *mei rachamut*</note> are gathered beneath it. So too, the purification of the "Living Creatures" <note>original: *chayyot* — angelic beings</note> meets the waters from below. Through the voice that joins and unites them, the "levity" of their offspring is refined, for they are planted in the secret of His divinity. All the waters of mercies and all the waters that descend and satisfy the world are drawn from the "Point of the Altar of All" through Him. 

In my opinion, King David nullified everything <note>meaning he unified the diverse physical needs into spiritual service</note> and divided it among the people, as it is written: "And he distributed among all the people... a cake of bread, a portion of meat, and a flagon of wine." <note>original: *chalat lechem achat, v'eshpar echad, v'ashishah achat* (2 Samuel 6:19)</note> This represents how he distributes what he receives from the Divine Attributes. David is the secret of the "King," and he has nothing except what the Attributes grant him in the secret of the hidden realm. He receives in the secret of "from below to above," including everything within him according to the measure of each attribute. He then brings forth and reveals the secret of what he received from the "Upper One" in the secret of "behold, I will rain bread for you from heaven."

**One** <note>original: *achat*</note> in every place signifies a tongue of unity, to show the oneness of all. **A portion of meat** <note>original: *eshpar*</note> is in the secret of the "head of holiness," the essence of David's reception from what is above. **A flagon of wine** <note>original: *ashishah*</note> refers to the foundations of the world, like the "foundations of the grapes." This is the vessel of reception for the "Upper Life" that is awakened by its foundations—meaning pure goodness and the "joy of wine." This "wine" is the initial power given to Abraham, which David then receives and prepares for all. As it is written: "He gave to them," and regarding the "Woman of Valor," it is written: "She rises while it is yet night and provides food for her household." <note>Proverbs 31:15</note> This "food" is given to those who love her. "Her household" refers to Israel, for they are the ones who reside in her shadow. Afterward, she provides "sustenance for her maidens," which refers to the rest of the angelic hosts.

And God said: "Let the earth bring forth grass." After the waters were gathered and the dry land appeared, His name was fulfilled. Afterward, through the awakening of the "Awakener," she was filled with truth. This is the secret of how the Earth received the "fruits" and "offspring" that return from the hidden to the revealed. Through the power of the "Righteous One," <term>Tzadik: often refers to the Sefirah of Yesod, the conduit of divine energy</term> who is the secret of the Covenant, she brought forth the offspring of her mate. This is the secret of "Let the earth bring forth grass, the herb yielding seed." 

Regarding **grass** <note>original: *deshe*</note>, the term "yielding seed" is not used. Only for the **herb** <note>original: *esev*</note> is it said "yielding seed." This is because grass does not have the same permanence; it is meant for the consumption of the "Beasts" <note>original: *behemot*</note> who are known for their great number. They seek their honor in it and strive for it. The secret of the matter is that "grass" does not yield seed because it represents the angels who were created on the second day. They serve as sustenance for Israel through the taste of the "Righteous One," and they are like an offering to the Divine Presence.

The "Upper Earth" <note>The Shekhinah</note> received them through the power of the waters that descend upon her from above. Because they are for "consumption," they were included at the beginning and preceded the "herb yielding seed," which is mentioned with the term "permanence." These are the "Holy Camps" and the "Chariots" that are under the blessings and prayers. Through the "service of man," they are crowned and prepared. Through the "service of man," they are provided with sustenance for the world, in the secret of "bringing forth bread from the earth." The grass is prepared for the "Beasts," while the herb is prepared through human service, all for the benefit and repair of the world. "To bring forth bread from the earth" refers to the "Land of the Living." The Cherubim are prepared from below, and the blessing spreads upon them from above.

In the fourth chapter of *Pirkei De-Rabbi Eliezer*, it says: "Whatever is produced from the earth... it is the Lord of the Thousand Mountains." Each day, they are renewed by the "Almighty" <note>original: *Shaddai*</note>, and at night they are completed. 

<column-break/>

This is the secret of the Jordan River that waters them. The waters of the Jordan are trusted to sustain the entire Land of Israel, whether above the ground or beneath it. As it is written: "He is confident that the Jordan will rush forth to his mouth." <note>Job 40:23</note> This refers to the reward set aside for the Righteous. 

In the Midrash on Leviticus, regarding the portion *Acharei Mot*, it discusses the "Living Creatures of the Thousand Mountains." Rabbi Yochanan, Resh Lakish, and the Rabbis differ: 
**Rabbi Yochanan** says: It is one animal <note>The Behemoth</note>, and it crouches upon a thousand mountains, and these mountains produce for it all kinds of grasses, and it eats. 
**Resh Lakish** says: It is the "beasts of the field" mentioned in the verse "upon a thousand mountains," and these mountains produce fruit and food for the "Living Creatures" of the Righteous. 
**The Rabbis** say: It is one beast, and its size is over a thousand mountains, and it eats all types of animals. What is the reason? "All the beasts of the field play there." 

Master Tanchuma said: These things are the works of God; how wondrous are His deeds. 
Rabbi Yochanan and Rabbi Simeon ben Lakish further debated: 
**Rabbi Yochanan** said: All that the animal drinks from the Jordan in one gulp would suffice for six months of drinking. What is the reason? "Behold, he drinks up a river and hastens not." 
**Rabbi Simeon ben Lakish** said: All that it drinks in one gulp would suffice for many months. What is the reason? "He is confident that the Jordan will rush forth to his mouth." 
**Rabbi Huna** in the name of **Rabbi Jose** said: It has no "opening of the mouth" <note>meaning its drinking is miraculous or spiritual</note>. How does it drink? **Rabbi Simeon ben Yochai** said: A river comes out of Eden, and its name is **Yovel** <note>The Jubilee river</note>, and from there it drinks. 

Now, we have only written this to clarify the secret and to examine the subtle hints within these divisions. You will find that Rabbi Yochanan’s words clarify the secret of the "grass" that the Earth produces. It is understood as food for the "Beast" according to the details of the verse. The "thousand mountains" represent the secret of the "Flow" <note>original: *mazal*</note> that emanates there. **Resh Lakish** said that they produce food for the "Living Creatures of the Righteous." This refers to the "hidden secret" where the "Upper Righteous" and the "Lower Righteous" meet. The Upper Righteous receives and knows, while the Lower Righteous eats from the goodness of the "Provider." 

The **Rabbis** say that the "grass" is not just for its own sake, but it includes the Names, the Living Creatures, and the Lights, which are all drawn into the Infinite. This is what they meant by "all the beasts of the field play there." The "Jordan" upon which it drinks represents everything that is drawn from the source to the "Place of the Name," which flows to sustain the life force. 

Rabbi Huna’s statement that it has no "opening of the mouth" means that its drinking is never-ending. It does not stop because it comes from the **Source** that flows eternally. It is like the river that goes out of Eden, whose name is **Yovel**, as the holy Zohar explains. 

Regarding what was said in Chapter 4 about how things are "completed"—this is because on that day, the food of the lovers is prepared. In the secret of "In the morning he devours the prey, and at evening he divides the spoil." <note>Genesis 49:27</note> In the chapter "They do not expound," it says that every single day, the Ministering Angels are created from the "River of Fire" <note>original: *Nehar di-Nur*</note>, and they sing their song and then vanish. This is the meaning of "They are new every morning; great is Your faithfulness." <note>Lamentations 3:23</note> 

And in the Midrash on Lamentations: Every day, the Holy One, Blessed be He, creates a new set of angels, and they say a new song and go on their way. Each of these points is part of the "Secrets of the Beginning." In the secret of "Let the earth bring forth grass," the word "earth" is written as *tadshe ha-aretz* rather than *totzi ha-aretz* <note>the former implies a spontaneous sprouting, the latter a bringing forth</note>. This hints at something that returns to its source. For "grass," "yielding seed" is not said, because it is transient and does not have the same permanence as the "herb." The reason is that these beings are like the grass that fades; they exist for their moment and then return to the unity.

<summary>This page explores the mystical meaning of the third day of creation, specifically the difference between ephemeral "grass" (representing angels) and permanent "herbs." It uses the legendary Behemoth and the Jordan River as metaphors for how divine energy flows from the hidden source to sustain both spiritual and physical realms.</summary>

<meta>This page continues the mystical exploration of the Creation narrative, specifically the second and third days. It bridges the discussion from the "Firmament" to the "Gathering of the Waters."</meta>

# Chapter 6

And regarding their engagement with their foundations, a dispute was revealed. Had they only engaged in this dispute, there would be no stability in the world. To indicate their agreement, their stability, and their inclusion together, it is called the **Firmament of Heaven** <note>original: *Raki'a Shamayim*</note>. For the Holy One, Blessed be He, took water and water, placed them into one another, and from them, Heaven was made. In the chapter *Ein Dorshin* <note>A famous chapter in the Talmud (Tractate Hagigah) dealing with forbidden mystical studies</note> in the *Tanchuma* midrash, it says: The Holy One, Blessed be He, took fire and water and mixed them together, and from them the Firmament was made. 

And according to the midrash of Rabbi Nehumia ben HaKanah: What is "Heaven" (*Shamayim*)? It teaches that he took fire and water and mixed them together, making from them the "head" of our heart, as it is written: "The head of Your word is truth." And this is why it is written "Heaven" — Fire (*Esh*) and Water (*Mayim*) <note>The Hebrew word *Shamayim* is traditionally read as a combination of *Esh* (fire) and *Mayim* (water)</note>. There is a secret in the verse "And God called the firmament Heaven": Fire is filled with water from the right and the left, and they conclude the darkness; and the firmament is in its whiteness and its expansion, and it relates to the height and its curvature.

To ensure their stability and inclusion in their foundation, they said in the chapter *Ein Dorshin*: Our Rabbis taught: It happened that Rabbi Joshua ben Hananiah was standing on a step on the Temple Mount, and Ben Zoma saw him but did not stand up before him <note>Standing up for a teacher was a mandatory sign of respect</note>. He asked him: "From where and to where, Ben Zoma?" He replied: "I was gazing between the Upper Waters and the Lower Waters, and there is nothing between them but a mere three finger-breadths." To strengthen the concept of the Divine, it says "The spirit of God hovered over the face of the waters" like a dove that hovers over her young, touching yet not touching. 

Rabbi Joshua returned to his disciples, and Ben Zoma was still "outside" <note>This implies he was in a state of mystical trance or mental instability</note>. For look, the "spirit of God" is written on the first day, but the firmament was created on the second day! And regarding what was said, "Let it divide between water and water," how much space was there? Rabbi Joshua said it was like the thickness of a thread. Mar Zutra, and some say Rav Ashi, said it was like two cloaks spread out. 

Ben Zoma remained "outside"—meaning outside of proper settled mind—because he arranged it so that the "hovering" was written not in the place of the blessing. His nature was confused because he had not yet properly entered the secret of the matter. The wisdom of the other Sages did not differ on the reason for the gap between the Upper and Lower waters, teaching that there is no empty space between them, but rather the entire void is like a pearl <note>meaning solid and continuous</note>, to emphasize the fineness of the Firmament. There is no empty space without them clinging to one another, bound in pure agreement. It is not in any "sides," so it is possible there is no pressure whatsoever. This indicates the length of the generations and the stability that ought to be. If it were all simply "water in water," stability would be impossible, as I have written. For this reason, they mixed them and said this matter is like a drop connected to the womb, and the "word of the waters" establishes the branch and its offshoots. Through this, there is peace in its weight, and this is the "Good Foundation."

Regarding all these matters, it is said: "And God made the Firmament, and divided between the waters which were under the Firmament"—this refers to the body of the Firmament—and "between the waters which were above the Firmament." The Upper Waters were suspended by the Divine Word. To the understanding person, the Upper Waters are revealed through the Word, and their outcomes are in the Heavens, as it is said: "From the fruit of Your works, the earth is satisfied." This indicates that the Upper and Lower waters are not connected in the sense of literal water. 

To further demonstrate this, they said in *Ein Dorshin*: Rabbi Akiva said: "When you enter the place of the pure marble stones, do not say 'Water, water!' For it is written: 'He who speaks lies shall not be established before My eyes.'" The Holy Instructor here distinguishes the name "water" in these realms. He doubled his warning—"Do not say water, water"—to inform them so they would not err regarding the Upper and Lower waters by thinking one is for itself and the other for itself. Rather, in all the laws of the Foundation, it is one unique whole without any division. One who perceives a division is a "speaker of lies" and "shall not be established before My eyes." There is a secret for the person who comes into the count: to show that it is not literal water.

<column-break/>

# Chapter 7

The Absolute Firmament of which they spoke, in which all revelations are established, took the "act of dispute" and they said: "Their evaporation is from the Heavens," and "From the fruit of Your works the earth is satisfied." Blessed be He, who submerged the earth in the waters; this is the secret of the "Ascents," which were guarded for the stability of the worlds. To this secret, He gave the introduction, so that they should be contained in "vessels" and not in a state of confusion, for there is no stability in confusion. 

There is a secret of a "Single Path" by which they called the Upper Waters, the Lower Waters, and the Firmament to stand. It is gathered at the edges of the "Flank" <note>likely a reference to a specific anatomical/mystical configuration of the divine chariot</note> and it follows the secret of adaptation. For the "Upper Understanding" <note>original: *Tevunah*</note> acts as a foundation, and its likeness is found in the lower realms. The secret of the Water and the Firmament for the "Wondrous Ones" is explained in the first part of this book: "And there was evening and there was morning, a second day." This day expresses "twoness" and dispute, in the secret of the Left Side <note>In Kabbalah, the second day is associated with the Left Side/Judgment because of the division of waters</note.

When the multitude, the correction, and the tempering between all things were awakened, the word reached the ultimate stability. This occurred through the paths of **Male and Female**. This is the secret of the spreading of impurity, the smoke of Judgment, and various types of "destroyers" and punishments. From them, the spirit of impurity and the secret of the "foreskin" <note>original: *orlah* — referring to spiritual blockage or evil</note> are born. But in the correction of Male and Female, He acted to establish influence, connecting them in one union. This is the secret of "Her Understanding." 

In every level where the dispute spreads in the world, it is all within the secret of the Left. Both good and evil spread, and the power of the "Line" sustains the world as it seems right in the eyes of the Creator to act according to His wisdom and His eye of holiness. And regarding this, the intention is found in the verse:

->**And God said: Let the waters under the heavens be gathered unto one place.**<-

After the agreement of the blessing between the Holy and the Holy, which was for the stability of the worlds, the first Holy power caused the matter to unfold. Through this agreement, the outcomes and the fruit—which are the purpose of existence—would appear and be drawn forth. A person reaches perfection when he sustains the Light and the four qualities of existence. This is the "Foundation" that rules over matter. This is the law for the day after: "Let the waters be gathered" into the void, and "let the dry land appear." Everything was sanctified by the whisper of the Word, the Source, to equalize the physical reality. It is like a spring to water the garden. Through the letter *Yod*, He established the whole toward the "Place of the Sanctuary" in every corner, including Male and Female, the waters of the worlds. This is the secret of "Let the waters be gathered"—those that emerge from the "Sustenance" in a straight path from "under the heavens." 

The secret of the "One Place" is the supreme secret and the secret of the Creator for Man: thought joined with the body. "And let the dry land appear" is the secret of the final Hand <note>original: *Yad* — likely referring to the Sefirah of Malkhut</note>, which should be secure and longing for its completion. This is why "dry land" <note>original: *yabbashah*</note> suggests a lack of moisture/sweetness, yet it is the basis of things. Behold, the dry land ascends for the wise. The "outcomes" are by the power of the "Side" <note>the divine side</note> from above. Furthermore, "let the dry land appear" so that the clouds will saturate and provide for it, and it will not be like a mother mourning her children, but as a bride to Him, with His face turned toward her, in the secret of the "Union of the Living Creatures." 

"And God called the dry land Earth" — the quality of "running" <note>a play on the Hebrew words *Eretz* (earth) and *Ratz* (run)</note> toward the outside. To the gathering of waters, he called "Seas." This indicates the "Righteous One" <note>the Sefirah of *Yesod*</note>, ensuring that there is no gap between the Upper Waters that descend and those that gather below. From there, they are drawn to water the world. Thus, the sixth day returns to the equality of the Upper Ones in all their formation, and he carries everything.

<summary>These chapters provide a mystical commentary on the second and third days of Creation, focusing on the "dispute" between fire and water and the eventual gathering of the waters into "one place" to allow the dry land to appear. It interprets the physical creation as a manifestation of divine union (Male and Female) and the reconciliation of opposing forces.</summary>

<meta>This page continues the mystical exploration of the Creation narrative, specifically focusing on the Fourth Day and the nature of light. It follows the previous discussion of the Firmament, moving now to the "Hidden Light" and the relationship between the Sun and the Moon.</meta>

# Chapter 8
## Secrets of the Torah
### Chapter 8, Page 115

It is prepared for the righteous in the time to come. And the Zohar, of blessed memory, said: "And more for the light..." These things were hidden in the bond of pure kindness <term>Chesed; the divine attribute of Mercy or Loving-kindness</term> as hinted at, but it was severed from the past. Once this "snow" was cut off like a screen and expanded, the wicked in the future would be excluded from all of it. Yet, the pious one receives it, and through him the world is sustained; the entire millennium of the days of kindness <note>A reference to the messianic age or the "seventh millennium" in kabbalistic thought</note> is said to be supported by it. From this comes a single thread of the Great Kindness through which the world exists, and he is the "Foundation of the World," as it is written: "The righteous is the foundation of the world" <note>original: *Tzaddik Yesod Olam*; a key verse from Proverbs 10:25 used in Kabbalah to identify the righteous person with the divine attribute of Yesod</note>.

And in the chapter "There was a memory," it says regarding the first day: "Let there be light," to be revealed and then hidden. He knew of those thirty [days?] in the firmament of the heavens, and it is written: "And it was evening and it was morning, a fourth day." However, according to the measure of the light, Rabbi Elazar said: From the light created on the first day, a person could see and gaze from one end of the world to the other. But once God looked upon the generation of the Flood and the generation of the Dispersion <note>The generation of the Tower of Babel</note> and saw that their deeds were corrupt, He stood up and hid it from them. From whom did He hide it? From the wicked. And for whom did He prepare it? For the righteous in the time to come. This is the meaning of "And God saw the light, that it was good" — and there is no "Good" but the Righteous, as it is said: "Say of the righteous that he is good." And since He saw that the light was prepared for the righteous, He immediately designated the light for the righteous.

We have written that the light created by the Holy One, Blessed be He, on the first day allowed a person to gaze from one end of the world to the other; these are the words of Rabbi Jacob. But the Sages say: These are the very same lights that were created on the first day, but they were not suspended <note>Set in their fixed positions</note> until the fourth day. There is no real dispute here, for this light was hidden in the secret of all the "branches" mentioned on the first day. These are the two luminaries created on the fourth day, which were included as "two bodies in one" <note>original: *Du-Partzufin*; a mystical concept where two entities share a single back-to-back form</note>. This is what the Sages, of blessed memory, hinted at when they said He "took a portion" and left it as a secret. The Sages revealed it through a hint, referring to the secret in the text of "another day" [the fourth]. It is from the first light that He hiddenly measured and established the "Head of the Mountains" <note>A term for the high spiritual realms</note> in holiness. The inner, pure essence was covered and forgotten in its wisdom, just as some waters are hidden and some are revealed. This revelation occurred on the fourth day, for when the light passes, darkness is found, and when darkness passes, light is found.

In the firmament of the heavens, after the light was diminished, it was said that the secret of the "other" light would be called "in the firmament of the heaven." This is the secret of the Zodiac <note>original: *Mazal*</note> in the firmament of the heavens, which was then covered. "And you shall have no light but from Me." It was the "Conqueror" to distinguish between the day and the night, so that the solar sphere would not dominate, as we hinted above. And "they shall be for signs" — these are the Sabbaths, for they are called "Day Sabbath" and "Night Sabbath," regarding which it is said: "It is a sign between Me and you." "And for seasons, days, and years" — all this refers to the blessings of the fall and the rains, which will be aligned with the "right leg" <note>Symbolizing the attribute of Mercy/Chesed</note>, and for the sanctification of the month and the leap year, as it is known that the leap year aligns the luminary with the House of Judgment. "And they shall be for luminaries" — this time they shall be two in their place in the firmament of the heavens, for everything in the heavens and the earth is balanced. And the moon, in its fullness, sometimes returns to the earth to receive from it its sustenance and likeness.

"And God made the two great luminaries." At the beginning of their creation, they were two "faces" <note>profiles</note> joined as one, and they did not appear great until the end, when the moon returned to its own place. Then it was called "the lesser luminary." In the chapter "These are the torn," it is written: "And God made the two great luminaries," yet it is also written: "the great luminary and the lesser luminary." How is this? The moon said before the Holy One, Blessed be He: "Sovereign of the Universe! Is it possible for two kings to use one crown?" <note>A famous Talmudic midrash from Tractate Chullin 60b</note> He said to her: "Go and diminish yourself!" She said: "Sovereign of the Universe! Because I have said a proper thing before You, must I diminish myself?" He said to her: "Go, and Israel shall count the days and years by you." She said: "What is the greatness in that? They also count by the sun!" He said: "Go, and the righteous shall be called by your name: Jacob the Small, David the Small, Samuel the Small." Still, her mind was not at ease. The Holy One, Blessed be He, said: "Bring an atonement for Me for diminishing the moon." And this is the meaning of the "goat for a sin offering to the Lord."

<column-break/>

This decree of "Let there be the lesser luminary" was in her mouth because I diminished the moon. They were "two faces" when they were joined and identical, but in the end, when there was Kindness <term>Chesed</term> and a Body, they were called by their names. They were to be attached in a single bond, and the light returned at the end to be recognized. She [the Moon] is the "Presence" <term>Shekhinah</term> who is diminished in the one crown. This is the root of the matter that emerged.

She said before Him: "Is it possible for two kings and two faces to use one crown?" This was so there would not be two identical heads for the beginning and the end. She was seeking that her word would be heard, for her statement was divided concerning the six directions [of the world]. He said to her: "Go and diminish yourself and be the head of the foxes" <note>A metaphor for leading lower levels of existence</note>. These are her levels. And this is the deed, for even if there is a head over them, since there is no multitude of excellence and honor, she has no shame with her light in a single foundation. And then her nature was changed, and this foundation was placed in you.

The "Greater Luminary" would remain, and the "Lesser Luminary" would be the end of her being, returning to her former fullness. She would be included in the "Great Name" <note>The Tetragrammaton</note> in the secret of the final letter *He*. They hinted that this "fourth" <note>The fourth day and the moon as the fourth leg of the divine throne</note> is for her dwelling, as a single entity. Thus, she began to be called by the names of the "two" and the "world's edge." To all sides, she is called by the sign of the final letter of the Great Name, though she was not in the "Greatness" and the "Multitude" below. In the perception of the lower beings, she is called by the name "God" <term>Elohim</term>, and "His kingdom rules over all."

She said before Him: "Sovereign of the Universe! Since I have said a proper thing before You, why should I be the one to diminish myself?" He answered: "Go and diminish yourself," meaning this will be a place for the multitude. She said [another] proper thing, but it was withheld from her because they were not "face to face." There is no stability in this, for the blessing only rests on things that are hidden. She was on the level of the "Number" <term>Gematria</term>, which was her intention.

And then they were as they were at the beginning in their intention, which was for the blessing to be upon the "Seven" <note>The seven lower emanations/Sephirot</note> for the sake of the union and the identity. This was for the sake of one protection and inclusion, that they might be blessed with mercy and judgment together, as hinted. This is the ultimate purpose of the union. Furthermore, there is a matter here regarding the "Cloud." We have prepared her intention to be for the luminaries and to shine upon the forbidden, for the three faces of the final desires were there. The final *He* and the *Chayah* [living creature] of the secret of the *Qoph* and the *Loph*. They emerged as two profiles because they are the *L* and so on. And from the side of the *L* and from the side of the *Chesed* [Kindness], they emerged as two bodies, as it is written regarding their union as we have written. And the entire action of God is for His work, to elevate it. He who glorifies himself is like one who grasps at the *Qoph* <note>The letter *Qoph* often symbolizes the "ape" or a mimicry of the holy</note>.

"Go and serve by day and by night." The final letter of the Name is in one luminary. Thus she shines by day, and in the second she is called by the name *Elohim* [God], so she shines by night. This is the secret of the "Great Name" providing in the "Release" <term>Heter</term>. This is one of the "eight" of the "Oil." For in the final letter, she is the "flesh" of that which receives from the vessel of the Greater Luminary.

He said to her: "Go, and the righteous will be called by your name." It is said that they will be in the world of clarity, and He will return to them and turn to them, and they will be a chariot for you, a place of glory and a crown. Their good deeds will gather the "drops" and the rains will start, and they will be called "Good" by your name. For they will store the fat and the smallness, and from it comes the greatness and the multitude. These are Jacob and David, who were as heads and leaders to bear the yoke of the defect and the lack. They would diminish themselves. "And the heel of the threshold" <note>Referring to the humility of Jacob/David</note>. David answered: "I am a worm and no man." He was not appeased.

Then the Holy One, Blessed be He, said: "Bring an atonement for Me." "For Me" specifically, as in "and he prayed to the Lord." This is a path of straightness for the Moon, so that the lack will be removed. This is "for Me," and this is because "I diminished the moon." And the "diminishing" is the loss of the generality of the daughter who stands over them. It requires atonement to satisfy the mind of the moon. However, the "lack" is the cause of the "luck" <term>Mazal</term> for us, for she did not reveal who received them. This is the "goat for a sin offering to the Lord," for the goat is the "hairy man" [Esau], but the goat of the moon is what brings relief. And the sacrifice is offered for her unique holiness when the time is fixed. And in the midrash of Rabbi Shimon bar Yochai, it is all spoken in metaphor. Thus said Rabbi Shimon: The Holy One, Blessed be He, said...

It frames the moon's smaller status as a form of humility shared by figures like Jacob and David, and explains the Rosh Chodesh sacrifice as a divine response to this cosmic shift.</summary>
