# Chapter 21 &emsp; Part of the Secrets of the Torah &emsp; Chapter 21 #

The Chariot <note>original: *Merkavah*; the divine assembly or throne-world</note> is affected when a person sanctifies and purifies themselves, remembering us here below. Indeed, the repair <note>original: *Tikkun*; the mystical process of restoration or rectification</note> of the Voice rises also to the heights, rectifying the Holy Names that correspond to it. In this way, the Great Name is elevated, and the righteous are made from them in their ways from His place in glory. They are like a threshold <note>original: *limutar*</note> that was literally below, and in the end, they become like the Righteous One <note>a reference to the Sephirah of Yesod, the "Foundation"</note> in a literal sense.

This is the secret of what the Sages said in the chapter "One who reads the Megillah" <note>original: *HaKorei et HaMegillah*; Megillah 18a</note>: Rabbi Isaac said in the name of Rabbi Eleazar: "From where do we know that the Holy One, blessed be He, called Jacob 'El' <note>original: 'God'</note>? Do not be surprised, for it says: 'And he called him El, the God of Israel' <note>Genesis 33:20</note>. He called Jacob 'El.' And who called him so? The God of Israel." This is because our father Jacob, peace be upon him, his attribute is Truth—the Torah of Truth—represented by "Israel the Elder" <note>original: *Yisrael Saba*; a higher spiritual manifestation of Jacob</note>. He rectifies and glorifies the Glory above, and Jacob below is just like him; "Israel, in whom I will be glorified" <note>Isaiah 49:3</note>. This occurred at the beginning of his era, and he was called "El."

This is the secret of the Sages' statement: "The Patriarchs are the Chariot" <note>original: *Ha-avot hen hen ha-merkavah*</note>. For they repaired the Glory below, and each one became a specific throne and repair for the Divine Presence <note>original: *Shekhinah*</note>. They represent the multiplication of the Supernal Chariot, the secret of their high qualities. There are a thousand below following the pattern of the supernal ones above. These people rectify the Glory above through the refinement of the "wise-hearted," and those rectify it through their honor below. This is a great level for those in exile—that the Voice involved in this repair has the power in its hand to rectify the Glory from below by being occupied with what is "good and right in the eyes of the Lord."

Even though the hidden wisdom is his, according to this level, even in his smallness, they merited God. This was the expression of the Sages of the holy generation. When Phinehas understood the wondrous secret, he too was girded with this. There were many wise men, and this was great among them. He too was girded to increase and enlarge the matter, for according to the strength and great wisdom... and this is what he would say... that they would merit, and the power is given to the creature under the sun. For by the power of the Supernal Crown <note>original: *Keter Elyon*</note>, the repair of the upper realms is placed in his hand, as well as the unification of the Great Name in its glory. This is a great thing.

This is the wisdom I have used more than anything I have attained until now—from Wisdom <note>original: *Chokhmah*</note> to Sovereignty <note>original: *Malkhut*</note>—because everything was for the purpose of this repair. Therefore, this section was greater than all that preceded it. Furthermore, his intention regarding the deficiency of his world was perhaps there, and he began for himself on a standing, on a connection, rectifying the Glory which is the secret of our existence. It is a great wisdom. And this itself was written literally like "Hezekiah" <note>unclear wordplay in original</note>. In this writing, it is permitted to him because it is the thickening... and it is written: "But let him that glories glory in this, that he understands and knows Me" <note>Jeremiah 9:23</note>, as has already been explained.

And in this comes the whole matter of the cycle of rejection, where he said: "A city of destruction <note>original: *ir ha-pesed*</note>... and wisdom, who is above it?" There came to it a great king who besieged it and built great siege-works against it <note>referring to Ecclesiastes 9:14</note>. In the Holy Midrash on Ruth, they said at the end of the passage: "This small city" is the Wisdom of Israel, which is called a small city. For this city, compared to the Holy One, blessed be He, is like a bride who is "small," for it says of Wisdom, "You are my sister," and this is the Assembly of Israel. She is called "small" just as it says regarding her wisdom, "Rachel" <note>who was the "younger/smaller" daughter</note>.

"And few men in it"—this refers to Adam, upon whom the heavens descended to his threshold, etc. "And there was found in it a poor wise man"—this is the first man, but [wisdom] departed from him. Noah came and brought it down to earth; the generation of the Flood came and it departed from the world. Shem his son came and brought it down; the generation of the Dispersion came and it departed. And so the world went on, and thus "few men in it." Abraham came and brought it down; the wise men of his generation came and it departed. And so it continued. Therefore, "few men in it" so that the foundation of the world might exist for a short time. If they had maintained it for a long time... "And a great king came against it"—this is the Holy One, blessed be He, the King who surrounds us. What does "besieged it" mean? From all sides. "By the Name of the Lord, His wall surrounds," etc. "And built great siege-works against it"—these are the "siege-works" of our iniquities, and the decrees and penalties for our sins. These "siege-works" are for the souls of the guilty to be punished for transgressing the commands of the Torah. "And there was found in it a poor wise man"—this is the King... for no man clung to his mission...

<column-break/>

"Upon my bed" <note>referring to Song of Songs 3:1</note>. Behold, we have explained that the lower stature is aimed at the stature of the Chariot. The Voice of fortune is the measure of the stature of the Ancient Glory <note>original: *Kavod Atik*</note> to give life... and this is the sign. With the right intention, when your hands are open and wide, for by its measure in the "reed of measure" is the secret of these lines of kindness. It is a beam that you wrote as the place of the lower glory, and the power of the measure of everything is in the secret of the upper lines in length and breadth. For it spreads to all sides and understandings to receive corresponding to these upper parallels, the secret of the laws.

And that these should also be until the place of the Altar, also against the upper one, a great vision of might <note>original: *Gevurah*</note>. Help what is written in the secret of "to you is their work." And in this is a wondrous intention, for the secret of the opening of the voice... and the silver. These are the corners of the soul, and so the "diamonds" and kindness in the stretch of the "ten" and its forces in the surrounding. And the silver—for the levels of evil in the eye are the surrounding of the secret of the light action. And the sickness unto the ten and possessions... receiving in the void of the body which is in the fulfillment of the Torah. And its integrity is covered in everything, and as a shield to its teachers, it is a protection for me and for the booths <note>original: *Sukkot*</note>, to stand the crown upon the sickness... and from all the clear paths to the Kingdom <note>original: *Malkhut*</note>.

The intention is for the prophecy to be... in all sides, whether in those from the side of the good or in the seal from the side of the "better than good." And from every material below... to the will, the Voice is removed, and it is bowed over it all the time like a servant before his master. There is the secret of "their work is yours," and it is considered as if actually done. And behold, while we remember and help, and the "master of stature" <note>original: *Baal Komah*; a reference to the mystical dimensions of the divine</note> relates things clearly from himself to the Glory. Behold, from every place... on what I hinted to them regarding perfection... of the prophecy, being included from all perfection in the upper pattern. For according to the prophet, he is rectified with the upper rectifications. The Voice is written as the "Glory" and the "Chariot of God." He awakens them through his breaths, and finally, for from the lines of his direction... and just as they merited... in the chapter... and with this the prayer of the future is completed, and so the intention in this chapter is finished.

## Chapter 21 ##

My second secrets I have separated for the "seeing prophet." According to the vision, to give the kings and the clouds to understand. And the refinement in it is according to the ways of help and assistance aimed at blessing and drawing down [divine flow] in the Hidden Unity. Always their thought is bound... without doubt. And the peace itself is missing in all this, and against the lack... in the statures of the Chariot.

This book compares the Torah to one who descends and is written, for it has no... appearing from its power. For the peace is strong and rectifies what needed to be rectified regarding the Hidden Names which he intended. For it has already been clarified in this book that the "small man" <note>the human being</note> is a repair for the "Large Man" <note>the cosmic divine structure, *Adam Kadmon*</note>, so to speak, to give the Great Name its glory. And in the repair... this is a great power. And in his prayer to rectify the Glory in its smallness... and therefore it included everything that is included in the Supernal Glory and the Supernal Crown above and below.

To know this, they complete and rectify the Glory. And this is the secret of "Everything that is called by My name, and for My glory I created it, I formed it, even I made it" <note>Isaiah 43:7</note>. Since the lower man is included in everything that the upper one includes, for everything is called by the name "All" <note>original: *Kol*; often associated with the Sephirah of Yesod</note>. For the Righteous One... rectifies and establishes his world above, called "All" because everything is in him. So too the righteous one below, in his being, rectifies and establishes the Voice in light. "The Righteous is the foundation of the world" <note>Proverbs 10:25</note>, called "All" in his name. Because he began and was occupied in the building of the upper world below, in the likeness of the Righteous One above, it is fitting for him... like us.

This is the secret of "Everything that is called by My name," and "to the God of Israel"—thus the reason was revealed: "For My glory I created it, I formed it, even I made it." For the reason it is called by His name is because it includes all that is in the Supernal Glory. And it is written that there is Greatness and Might in it. And this is the secret of the vessel to rectify the lower Glory, the Glory of the Lord... so that he too might rectify the Glory below. And behold, through him, the Great Name is unified in its glory. And this is the secret of "remembering us" with intention... to resemble the limbs...

# Chapter 22 &emsp; Part of the Secrets of the Torah &emsp; Chapter 22 &emsp; 127 #

Prophecy is granted according to one's spiritual height and the quality of the Voice reaching the prophet. The Voice reaches each individual particularly, according to the Great Name. We shall explain that for every prophet, the power mentioned is not the same as the Voice heard by Moses. He knew God "eye to eye" <note>Numbers 14:14; a metaphor for direct perception</note> and with a singular Voice. As has been explained, for others, this occurs in a "vision" <note>original: *mar'eh*</note> to prevent them from seeing clearly, or in a "dream" <note>original: *halom*</note>. For Moses, everything was within the general scope of the vision from the start, but for others, it was "from afar." This is the "House of the King" <note>a reference to the Tabernacle or the Divine realm</note> where the order of all prophecy is counted. Even the greatest among them could not ascend to this level or grasp this Great Name. This is what was mentioned regarding the prophecy of the Patriarchs: none could reach this distance. Rather, it is better stated as: "Not so with My servant Moses; he is faithful in all My house" <note>Numbers 12:7</note>. He was told to prepare the Inner Sanctuary <note>original: *dvir*</note>, and his clarity and goodness were unique to him within the House. Moses is called "faithful" because it was explained that he "heard" in "all My house." One should not ask why Moses' habit was to seek proof, for our Sages (may their memory be a blessing) said: "All the prophets looked through a dull mirror <note>original: *aspaklaria she-einah me'irah*; an opaque lens</note>, but Moses looked through a shining mirror <note>original: *aspaklaria ha-me'irah*; a clear lens</note>" <note>Yebamot 49b</note>. This is the secret within all prophecies: others saw through a "rolling mirror" <note>likely a corrupted OCR for *me-urpelet*, meaning "clouded"</note>, perceiving through thought but not fully. They achieved perception through a "rope of logic," whereas Moses achieved it in its literal level through the "Shining Mirror." This means there was a distinct radiance in his prophecy that was not withheld. For him, the "rope" of the walls of prophecy was entirely open. This is the meaning of "in all My house"—it was accessible to him. God said, "Please, do not speak against him," to inform them: "I have known you." Moses achieved a "Great Name" in prophecy that no other prophet ever grasped. The Kabbalists say that "The Beauty of Israel" <note>original: *Tiferet Yisrael*; the sixth Sephirah</note> is the "Covenant of the Tongue" and the "Crown of Beauty." Moses was uniquely connected to this in a single, transformed prophecy. All divine speech to Moses was direct and singular.

"Mouth to mouth I speak to him, clearly and not in riddles" <note>Numbers 12:8</note>. This refers to the nature of the gift given to him (peace be upon him). His prophecy was a direct sight of the matter in its essence and reality, without riddles. This is what is intended by the "Great Name" mentioned in prophecy—it is a sight within a vision. This is the general rule. "And he beholds the form of the Lord" <note>original: *temunat Hashem*</note>; this implies a wondrous level. In the *Sifrei* <note>an ancient legal commentary</note>, it says: "He beholds the form of the Lord"—this refers to the angel who shows him, or to the likeness of the Tablets of the Covenant. These are the four principles that distinguish the level of the Master of all Prophets <note>Moses</note> from the level of all other prophets, as arranged in the verses of the Torah. We have learned that the prophecy of the Holy Patriarchs was described as: "I appeared to Abraham, to Isaac, and to Jacob as God Almighty (*El Shaddai*), but by My name YHWH I was not known to them" <note>Exodus 6:3</note>. At the end of the Torah, it confirms his superiority over all future prophets: "There has not arisen a prophet since in Israel like Moses" <note>Deuteronomy 34:10</note>. As Nachmanides <note>original: *ha-Ramban*</note> (may his memory be a blessing) wrote, this serves as a memorial to the level of Moses our Teacher (peace be upon him), as much as can be understood, to recognize and praise him. This is the intent of this chapter.

### Chapter 23 ###

->Concerning the second level of the appropriate levels of prophecy<-
->The prophecy of the hearts and the rest of the matters<-
->Regarding the level of prophecies attained through vision and the Holy of Holies<-

<column-break/>

Regarding the matters that preceded this and what we have agreed upon here, as we mentioned, we did not expand without reason. The matter is with him and his development over time, opening a window to receive it—meaning everything for his family. Regarding the "Cushite woman" he took, this refers to the level of purity he maintained. This is the source and the cause of their existence, atop the "window" of the scriptures regarding the cessation of physical intimacy that he chose. It mentions Jethro’s daughter to speak of the "Ladder of Life" in the building of our father Abraham, providing him with a vision of the cutting of the covenant and the future. Some wisdoms are so deep their perspective reaches his hand. As it is written: "You shall not give your daughter... and his daughter you shall not take for your son" <note>Deuteronomy 7:3</note>. The same applies to holiness and a pure body. As it is said in the *Sifrei* regarding the law of the High Places: Miriam and Aaron spoke against him... "Has the Lord indeed spoken only through Moses? Has He not spoken through us also?" <note>Numbers 12:2</note>. This is connected to what was said above: "Would that all the Lord's people were prophets!" <note>Numbers 11:29</note>. They thought that because the spirit was placed upon them, they were equal in power and purity. But Moses was chosen by the Spirit of the Lord itself, according to His wisdom. They said, "Has He not also spoken through us?" to include a scholar who is great in his wisdom. But Moses' prophecy was holy and separate. The Lord heard their vision and corrected them.

The general explanation in the *Sifrei* regarding other prophecies is according to the plain meaning of the text. The "Pillar of Cloud" from the Lord descended to speak with them. Moses was "more humble than any man on the face of the earth" <note>Numbers 12:3</note>. This refers to his total submission. Just as he said, "Now I know that you are a woman of beautiful appearance" <note>Genesis 12:11, quoted here likely to compare Moses' lack of physical desire to other figures</note>, Moses surpassed this; he did not awaken to any physical or bodily thing at all due to his great humility and holiness. He did not take Jethro's daughter for physical building but by divine necessity. They should have guarded his honor and not compared themselves to him. The "Voice" says that there was a "burning anger" because Moses’ level was unique through the "Direct Gaze." One should not pray that this level be hidden from the eyes of Aaron and Miriam. These "Secrets of the Torah" are revealed through prophecy. They did not receive it directly from him, and He said to them: "Hear My words: If there be a prophet among you, I the Lord will make Myself known to him in a vision" <note>Numbers 12:6</note>. This is My way with you. But the level of Moses' prophecy is much higher and distinct from yours. His spirit was not distant or clouded. "My servant Moses is not so; he is faithful in all My house." He is precious in God's eyes. They were rebuked for his honor. From here we derive the rule of the level of Moses' prophecy compared to all other prophets. The intent of the "Way of Truth" <note>a common term for Kabbalah</note> is that the Glory of the Lord reached the level of direct prophecy for him, whereas for others, they only grasp it through a vision.

# Chapter 22 &emsp; Part of the Secrets of the Torah &emsp; Chapter 22

And he will further appoint them over all the treasuries of that King, for all his treasuries and his servants are released to do his will, from the small to the great; all are guards of his watch. They do not divide one thing from another, nor do they exchange his goodness. In the passing of the night, they long for this in their knowledge and their piety, the cloud upon them. As it is written: "He will not withhold any good from the righteous" <note>Psalm 84:12</note>, and it is written: "He will guard the feet of His pious ones" <note>1 Samuel 2:9</note>. The general principle is that the Divine Presence <term>Shekhinah: the indwelling presence of God in the world</term> is grace, like a heritage lacking a sword in their matter. And they are like vineyards that have reached maturity over us, and they cover the lack of the degrees of maturity. They are the ones who release and surrender all burdens and arguments, and turn away from the things that prevent petition. This is as far as our efforts have reached in clarifying the matter of the assemblies and the intended purpose written here.

### Chapter 22

The level of this whole matter is according to what the Sages of Truth <note>The Kabbalists</note> have divided into four levels:
1.  The first and highest level of all is the level of the **prophecy of Moses**.
2.  The second is the level of the **prophecy of the other prophets**, peace be upon them.
3.  The third is a level below these, which is the level of the **Holy Spirit** <term>Ruach HaKodesh: a level of divine inspiration lower than formal prophecy</term>.
4.  The fourth is the one that follows it, which receives the **Heavenly Echo** <term>Bat Kol: literally "daughter of a voice," a divine resonance or secondary echo of the divine word</term>.

Understand the general rule: the level of Moses’ prophecy, peace be upon him, differed from the level of the prophecy of the other prophets. Our Sages of blessed memory explained this by saying in the chapter *Ha-Mo'er* <note>Talmud, Tractate Yebamot 49b</note>: "All the prophets looked through a lens that does not shine, but Moses our teacher looked through a luminous lens" <term>Aspaklaria: from the Latin *specularia*, referring to a transparent windowpane or mirror used as a metaphor for prophetic clarity</term>. They clarified these matters with this language: "What is the difference between them?" The Luminous Lens is the difference.

The words of the prophets were many and diverse. Rabbi Yehonatan said: "The prophets saw through five lenses," and that is what is written: "And like the appearance of the vision which I saw..." <note>Ezekiel 43:3</note>. Moses saw through only one lens, as will be explained, and this was his excellence. The Rabbis say: "All the prophets saw through a dirty lens," as it is written: "And I have multiplied visions" <note>Hosea 12:11</note>. Moses saw through a polished lens, for it is said: "And the likeness of the Lord does he behold" <note>Numbers 12:8</note>.

The secret of the matter is that Moses was granted the heritage of knowledge—the secret of the vineyards—the Great Name <note>The Tetragrammaton, YHVH</note>, which is the unique glory. It is the secret of "And the Lord spoke to Moses face to face" <note>Exodus 33:11</note>. The secret of "face to face" is a matter of "Luminous Faces," the secret of the Luminous Lens. In contrast, "faces that do not shine" is the secret of the lens that does not shine in total unity. Therefore, he knew the Great Name and attained his prophecy from within the Glorious Name. This is the secret of: "And the Lord spoke to Moses," intended to help and confirm the speech facing the "Glory," the place of his prophecy to Moses. It was said facing the "Ezer" <note>Helper/Support</note> of the "Seven" <note>The seven lower emanations/Sefirot</note>, to inform that from the unique one within the Seven, Moses would perceive and know.

This is why no other prophet ever rose to this level. For the Patriarchs, the level of their prophecy was through "El Shaddai" <note>God Almighty</note>, which is the secret of the lens that does not shine. They knew the secret of the Great Name that was unified within it, but they did not attain it in their prophecy. This is what the Sages said: "To Abraham, to Isaac, and to Jacob [I appeared] as El Shaddai, but by My name YHVH I did not make Myself known to them" <note>Exodus 6:3</note>. This means the Great Name, the secret of Knowledge <term>Da'at: the attribute of divine connection and consciousness</term>, was not attained by the Patriarchs in their perception, though their prophecy was complete. This is: "And I appeared to Abraham..." through the Great Name in prophecy, rather through this [lower] name, which is the Angel of the Attribute of Judgment. From there, the speech came to them, and through it, He was revealed to them. Regarding what is written about the speech being with them, it was a matter of the "rectification" for Moses at a minor level. When it says "And the Lord spoke to Joshua," it is impossible to say it was the Luminous Lens; it was the lens that does not shine in unity. He had the vision but not the full prophecy. This was the level of the Patriarchs as I have written. However, I have a tradition from my teachers that there was a level of attainment, though I did not receive specific knowledge of the matter. I say the reason is that the speech was the "impediment" of the Written Torah and the Oral Torah. The Written Torah is through Moses, who ascended to the level of eating with the angels and the degree of the "Song." One ascends in holiness and does not descend. But whoever was not so, did not ascend again in his house to the level of "face to face."

<column-break/>

Rather, only Moses, peace be upon him, and the entire path we have written. This was the tradition of all the Sages of Truth regarding the level of prophecy of those prophets and the level of the Patriarchs. This was also the tradition of the holy Sage Rabbi Shimon bar Yochai (Rashbi), peace be upon him, for the truth is given according to the intellect. This is his language in his Midrash <note>The Zohar</note>:

Rabbi Shimon was sitting one day with Rabbi Elazar his son, and Rabbi Abba was present. It is written: "And I appeared to Abraham, to Isaac, and to Jacob as El Shaddai, but by My name YHVH I did not make Myself known to them" <note>Exodus 6:3</note>. How should we understand this? The word "appeared" refers to the secret of the Upper Spirit <note>original: *ruach ila'ah*</note>. There are hues <note>original: *guvanin*</note> that are visible and hues that are not visible. These hues are the Upper Spirit of Faith, which human sons do not know and do not contemplate. And there are lower hues that are not blessed until they are established upon them. And until they are there, it is written "And I appeared." These are the hues that are visible. But those hues [the higher ones] are not like the ones above. Those that are visible [below] are hidden [above] and not seen. No person has ever stood upon them except for Moses. Regarding this, it is written: "But by My name YHVH I did not make Myself known to them." I was not seen by them in the Upper and Lower hues, for they did not know them; they only knew those that are revealed.

It is written: "And those who are wise shall shine like the brightness of the firmament" <note>Daniel 12:3</note>. What are these? They are from the side of Wisdom <term>Chokhmah</term>. He contemplated those things that human sons are not able to speak with their mouths; they are called "The Peering Ones." And there is the "Brightness of the Firmament." This firmament is the exact firmament that stands in the center <note>The central column of the Sefirot</note>. The "Brightness" is the one that is revealed and stands over that firmament to show hues. Those hues are seen in it but do not provide light, for they are hidden hues. Here, there are four lights. One of them is heard but not seen. It is the light that reveals the perfect light. This is the secret of the Sapphire stone <note>original: *sapir*</note>, to give light to the purple light that includes all lights. A light that is not a light, which contemplates these and shines this [light]. And those hues are seen in it according to the knowledge of the one who sees.

These three that we mentioned are hidden and stand upon that which is revealed. This light is "eye to eye." There are hues revealed that stand within it, and although they are there, they do not provide light because they stand in the light that does not shine. These are the hues that are hidden and stand over them, and they are not seen. They are only seen by Moses. He looked into the Luminous Lens which stands over that which does not shine. We see from here and there that there were hues revealed, but the hidden ones stood over them and did not shine. This is why it is written: "And I appeared to Abraham, to Isaac, and to Jacob as El Shaddai"—in those hues that are visible. "But by My name YHVH I did not make Myself known to them"—these are the hidden Upper hues that Moses was privileged to see. The Upper Spirit returns and reveals; it returns and reveals to the Luminous Lens. It was revealed before him, the lens that does not shine. Therefore, this one [Moses] was in the Luminous Lens, as it is known.

And I appeared to Abraham... Rabbi Abba came and kissed his [Rabbi Shimon's] hands. Rabbi Abba cried and said: "And the Lord..." <note>incomplete quote</note>. He stood and was astonished. The world is orphaned without you! Who will contemplate these secrets of the Torah? Until here.

From here, if you examine what I have written, the words of this holy author will be clarified for you, for all of them are one intention. They sit and discuss each and every point in His glory and essence. The levels of Moses' prophecy, peace be upon him, are distinguished from the level of the other prophets. This is what was said in the great rebuke to Aaron and Miriam: "Hear now My words..." <note>Numbers 12:6</note>. And this section is connected and bound to what is above.

<meta>This page concludes the previous discussion on the unique nature of the prophetic word "This is the thing" and transitions into Chapter 24, which focuses on the level of the Holy Spirit, specifically as it manifested in King David and King Solomon.</meta>

As we mentioned regarding the incident of the Golden Calf <note>The sin of the Israelites in Exodus 32</note>, the phrase "The Lord, God of Israel" <note>original: "יי' אלקי ישראל"</note> is used because vengeance belongs to Him when they have been zealous in their iniquities. Judgment belongs to God, and therefore He mentioned "the God of Israel." Furthermore, in the response to Moses regarding this matter, Moses saw that she <note>The Divine Presence, or Shekhinah</note> would be included in the power within it, saying "The Lord in the great vision," and so on. He mentioned the sign in its inclusion within the power, saying "The Lord," and added to them a staff that was included in the language of "**this is the thing**" <note>original: "זה הדבר" (zeh ha-davar) — a phrase often used to introduce a prophecy or command</note>. And in their saying "May He add unto you," he hints at their superiority over them in the prophecy of the secret of "**this is the thing**," which is a secret of pardon and forgiveness. Pardon is specifically through Kindness <term>Chesed: the attribute of divine mercy</term> in the context of "face to face." 

In every place where "**this is the thing**" is mentioned, it also has a directed meaning. In general, in the portion of *Naso* <note>Numbers 5:1-7:89</note>, "this is the thing" is used regarding the intention of the Tabernacle; and in the portion of the *Miluim* <note>the consecration of the priests</note>, "this is the thing which the Lord commanded to do"; and regarding the destruction of Jerusalem, "this is the thing" is said at the end of the Lord’s response, "and the glory of the Lord shall appear to you." Also in the portion regarding Vows, it says "**this is the thing** which the Lord commanded." In all places where "**this is the thing**" is mentioned, it refers to a sublime light, indicating the unity of the Great Name in His glory, and hinting at the secret of the highest level of His glory. This is what I have seen hinted at regarding the level of the *Shekhinah* <term>the indwelling Divine Presence</term> among the levels of prophecy; for these are the levels of all the prophets combined, except for our teacher Moses, peace be upon him. With this, the intention of this chapter is completed.

### Chapter 24

->The Level of Prophecy — The Level of Prophecy<-
->The level of the Holy Spirit, which is below the second level<-

The second level, and all that is written in the Scriptures, even from the songs within the level of prophecy, which is not a dream—all that they wrote and their words alongside the other words of the prophets—is a level of radiance, light, and flavor in the Midrash <note>homiletic interpretation</note> of the Kingdom of the House of David. It is attained through "hearing the name" and is called the **Holy Spirit** <term>Ruach HaKodesh</term> because the spirit comes to it from the Holy, a secret from the side of God. From it, the spirit was included upon those gathered who speak by the Holy Spirit. Regarding this, David said: "The spirit of the Lord spoke through me, and His word was on my tongue" <note>2 Samuel 23:2</note>. 

This is the secret of his writing at this level more than all others who speak by the Holy Spirit. This is also the secret of *Kohelet* <note>the Book of Ecclesiastes</note>, for of all things they said "The Lord has done it there," and with the strength of the "He" <note>the letter He, representing the Shekhinah</note> he performed three prayers. For he is below as a reflection of that which is above, in the secret of "O God, do not remain silent" <note>Psalm 83:2</note>. For the spirit increases for the *Shekhinah*, the secret of the King whose garment consists of songs and praises, which is revealed as a "song for the King" in glory and greatness. He seeks from her and says to her: "Let me hear your voice... for your voice is sweet" <note>Song of Songs 2:14</note>. It is also written: "So that my glory may sing to You and not be silent; O Lord my God, I will give thanks to You forever" <note>Psalm 30:13</note>.

David said, "so that the Glory may sing and chant to You"—this "Glory" is the Bride <note>the Shekhinah</note>. Therefore, "I will give thanks to You forever," without interruption and without a sound, for the Glory above shall not be silent; for just as I awaken it below, it shall be awakened above. It is written: "Awake, my glory! Awake, lute and harp! I will awaken the dawn" <note>Psalm 57:9</note>. This is the secret of David's glory in his place, which rises of its own accord. In the secret of his early rising, "Glory" was an elevation above David's bed. Once night arrived, a northern wind would blow upon it <note>David's harp</note>, and it would play by itself. This watched over the Assembly of Israel <note>Knesset Yisrael</note>, which is the singer. This is the "Harp of David," the harp of the House of Israel, within which was the secret that constantly divides and spreads to be honored above. It is the "Blue Light" <note>the Shekhinah</note> that guards, yearns, and moves constantly to connect like a flame with the "White Light" <note>the divine attribute of Mercy</note>. When these are included and honored within one another, they are refined and ignited as in a furnace. Behold, the Bride is with her Beloved through the pleasantness of song. 

For this reason, I understand "O God, do not remain silent; do not be deaf and do not be still" <note>Psalm 83:2</note>. The awakening of the longing in her toward Him comes from the north wind at midnight, in the secret that "the perfect one shall be refined for mercy." The harp would play of its own accord when the voice awakened. David, who is her silent counterpart below, said: "At midnight I will rise to give thanks to You" <note>Psalm 119:62</note>. All of this was to awaken a spirit from on high upon her, and to refine every dross of vitality and thorns from the power of the Bride. For David has no life of his own, except for what Adam the First granted him <note>a midrashic tradition that Adam gave 70 years of his life to David</note>. He is exalted and does not need to awaken with every kind of melody to draw down the Holy Spirit; it was from the source of life to knowledge, and upon this he marked his levels.

<column-break/>

He knows how to play to awaken the voice and the spirit, and to clarify and draw down the Divine Will to his world, and to herald every evil spirit away from him. For this reason, he played before Saul, and the evil spirit—which is that which diminishes him—departed from him. For when David's harp played of its own accord, in the secret of the awakening of the voice that came to him from the north, it gave birth to a longing "light of the eyes." He would come to her and say: "Let me hear your voice, for your voice is sweet," making the "beloveds" sweet, which is the secret of the Bride. Behold, regarding the kings who were exalted and passed on, they said: "Have they not passed?" In that longing, "no stranger shall interfere."

This was the joy of David below—he knew how to play and knew how to awaken the Holy Spirit and to banish the evil spirit. For the sound of the harp could endure to remove the illness. The words of the Lord are full and complete, and this is a hint to the Kingdom <term>Malchut</term>, which is merit, glory, and majesty. Solomon was wise and "saved the city" <note>Ecclesiastes 9:15</note>—the City of the Lord, as in "the City of our God"—through his wisdom, which is the *Shekhinah*. For in the intention of the "Standing Prayer" <term>Amidah</term>, which is established in the Kingdom, in the secret "and the love of Solomon was sweet," his wisdom was greater "than the wisdom of all the children of the East" <note>1 Kings 5:10</note>, hinting that they shared in the ancient wisdom. 

It is written: "And Solomon became wise." In the statement of Rabbi Joshua ben Korcha: "Solomon is actually the Holy One, blessed be He." Rabbi Yohanan said: "Every mention of 'Solomon' in the Song of Songs is holy, except for one <note>Song of Songs 8:11</note>, for he is the King to whom peace belongs" <note>original: "shlomoh" punned with "shalom," peace</note>. "And I shall place My glory in your name, My daughter"—this refers to the Torah, which was said to be attached to him, as it says: "And the Lord gave wisdom to Solomon." Solomon is named after the Holy One, blessed be He, who is called in the sanctified secret "Solomon," the King to whom peace belongs. 

Since he had the "Daughter" <note>the Shekhinah</note> and all was in his name, he is David and he is the secret of the *Shekhinah*. For Solomon was named with the name of "My Name" <note>the Lord's name</note>. God loved him, letting him walk in His ways and complete the Name that He had designated for him and given to him as a gift. He said to him: "Do as you wish with it." In the statement of Rabbi Phinehas ben Jair: "Therefore, 'And the Lord gave wisdom to Solomon' teaches that He was like a King who married his daughter to his son and gave her to him as a gift, saying, 'Do with her as you wish.'" Because he merited the King's daughter, the Holy Spirit rested upon him, for he was the divine son-in-law of the King's daughter. Everything is included in the "Houses" <note>the Temples</note>, and from the power of "I will teach you," the heart hears. Behold, he asked for her love, and the "water of his days" confused her. He asked for the paths of wisdom, and it is written: "Wisdom and knowledge are given to me." 

According to what our Sages of blessed memory said, "when he asked for one, he asked for all," for he was asking for Wisdom, and everything is included in it. The Spirit is called by seven names, for everything is in everything, and Solomon merited all because she is "Bathsheba" <note>literally "Daughter of Seven," referring to the Shekhinah as the seventh of the lower emanations</note> to him, to Solomon. In the Midrash of Rabbi Shimon bar Yochai <note>the Zohar</note>, peace be upon him: "Three wise men were beloved through Solomon." In seven ways, he spoke with intention to the world, and there she shall live forever—the seven. And besides these, they shall live below, the seven elevations. These are the paths for the prophets, for he is above all prophets. It is written: "May God make the name of Solomon better than your name" <note>1 Kings 1:47</note>—these are the seven crowns for the days of the world to receive. There were seven names used to hold onto the holy consolation. For this reason, he is called by seven names: he is called Jedidiah <note>"Beloved of the Lord"</note> because to the beloved of the Lord, He gives honor. And they had seven names... and he was perfected in the paths of wisdom, being called *Kohelet* <note>the Assembler</note>.

Because he was a reflection of the supernal pattern, included in seven supernal levels, the *Shekhinah* rested upon him and the Holy Spirit covered him as a wise spirit. As it is written, there are friends, and Solomon spoke three books by the Holy Spirit, which is the inner Holy Spirit. In the Midrash of Rabbi Shimon bar Yochai, they said in this language: "To be perfected in the fullness of his completion and as a bride in the wisdom behind." Come and see: he brought three books of wisdom to the world, and they were divided in his wisdom: **Song of Songs**, which is Wisdom <term>Chokhmah</term>, receiving/tradition <term>Kabbalah</term>, and Understanding <term>Binah</term>, drawing to the garden to receive the garden of books. 
- **Song of Songs** corresponds to Wisdom; so it is.
- **Ecclesiastes** (*Kohelet*) corresponds to Understanding; so it is.
- **Proverbs** (*Mishlei*) corresponds to Knowledge <term>Da'at</term>. 
These correspond to the supports, for all these verses are inner crowns and the Foundation <term>Yesod</term>. From this power, the structures were prepared and all was perfected. These verses contain this and those contain that, for it corresponds to Knowledge. To this extent: "The Lord remembered us through it." For in it is Your Name which is written, and it clarifies that every gate is hidden and tires itself with the power of the Supernal Wisdom and in the Foundation of the seven...

<meta>This page continues the exploration of prophetic levels, moving from the specific linguistic framing of Moses’s prophecy ("This is the thing") to the metaphysical source of his authority compared to Joshua and the later prophets. # Torah Chapter 23 | Chapter 23: Secret Part

The spirit of Joshua originates from the heights of Moses in a celestial likeness. This is the secret of the verse, "And I will take of the spirit which is upon you and will put it upon them" <note>Numbers 11:17</note>, for behold, the end of the degree is according to its attainment. The place of Moses’s prophecy transfers light and abundance to all nations, and from him, it spreads to all the prophets. He is the secret that includes all **six directions** <term>The six emotional attributes or Sefirot of the divine realm</term>, and within him, the seventh is perfected. As Moses spreads into the branches below in the secret of the seventy pure levels, this is the secret of "Gather for me seventy men of the elders of Israel." They were chosen and judged by what was emanated upon them from the light and radiance of Moses, and he lacked nothing <note>The light of Moses is often compared to a candle that lights others without losing its own flame</note>. This celestial pattern demonstrates that the prophecy of all prophets was included in and flowed from the spirit of Moses. Therefore, all their prophecy is called "Tradition" <term>Kabbalah: here meaning the received tradition of the Prophets and Writings, as opposed to the core Torah</term>, because of his holiness over them. As the sages said: "We do not learn words of Torah from words of Tradition" <note>original: "דברי תורה מדברי קבלה לא ילפינן" — a legal principle stating that laws cannot be derived solely from the Books of the Prophets</note>. This is because they received their prophecy from Moses, but Moses received only from the mouth of the **Almighty** <term>Ha-Gevurah: a title for God emphasizing His power and the directness of the revelation at Sinai</term>. In this way, no Torah law is learned from their prophecy, but their prophecy is learned from the Torah. For Moses was the master of all prophets; he was the head, and they were the branches drawing sustenance from him.

Because this level is drawn from the Divine Name and is hoped for, and the secret there is that the Holy Spirit never departs. Rather, the fountain is always constant and does not cease, for it is a river and uprightness. A spring shall go forth, but always as the sun in its beginning and its strength; its light shall never be lacking. So too was Moses, peace be upon him, as a celestial pattern. His name was sung above, and so he was below—always prepared and ready in spirit. For he was the beginning of the abundance, crowned in excellence. Therefore, he was sufficient in himself and overflowed to others, dwelling and giving in his likeness above. For this reason, the Name was never hidden from him all his days. He did not require the awakening of intermediate things to complete the spirit of prophecy, for it never departed from him at all. He was always ready and prepared without any hindrance, for in his name below there was no departure of the holy spirit or abundance. In this, he was like the sun.

This was not the case with the other prophets, peace be upon them, who required intermediate means to awaken the spirit upon them and reveal purity. As it is written: "And with a lute and a drum and a pipe and a lyre before them, and they shall prophesy" <note>1 Samuel 10:5</note>. And it is written: "But now bring me a minstrel. And it came to pass, when the minstrel played, that the hand of the Lord came upon him" <note>2 Kings 3:15, regarding the prophet Elisha</note>. The reason is that they had a deficiency; the Holy Spirit and the abundance would sometimes depart from them and their group would be divided. Therefore, to make the spirit dwell upon them, they needed the music to stir the heart and bring comfort so that the spirit could rest upon them. They required a unique preparation from the spirit above. This is the secret of the "Holy Song" with the collective. These matters are explained by Rabbi Shimon bar Yochai, peace be upon him, in the *Tikkunim* <note>The Tikkunei Zohar, a classic Kabbalistic text</note>: If they were worthy in their souls, they stood among the prophets to have the spirit of prophecy rest upon them. It says "and now bring me a minstrel," because by the music they would cast off the "clothing" of the physical and allow the spirit of prophecy to connect to them. So it was with all the prophets, for this "female" level <term>Nukva: the receptive or lunar divine attribute</term>, except for Moses, was divided among all the other prophets of the world. Therefore, they only saw parts. All the prophets, in all their prophecy, saw according to their level of attainment, like one looking through a **dull mirror** <term>Aspaklaria she-einah me'irah: a lens that does not shine or a clouded window, representing indirect prophecy</term>. They would see by reflecting there in the light of the Name. Moses, peace be upon him, did not prophesy in this manner at all, for he was a branch from above, a blessing. His attainment is mentioned in many places in the Torah where the name of the Lord is mentioned. This is a matter for the "wise of heart," for prophecies involve the holy names.

<column-break/>

Thus far, according to our holy tradition, is the portion of the intention of the blessing of our Master, peace be upon him. He wrote in this language: Following Rabbi Shimon, until the blessing was awakened, it was the secret of the holy level of the **Ancient One** <term>Atika: a very high, hidden level of the Divine</term>, drawing into the holy Name from the "constellation," as it is written, "He strengthens the mountains of creation." Below, all the levels were hidden until the final level, and then the Holy One spoke with him and said, "Go for a blessing," and said, "And may He give to you," and Jacob, all of these are the name *Shaddai*. Thus far is the explanation of this matter: the concept of "Kindness to Abraham," and from there all blessings go toward the fulfillment of the level of *Shaddai* <note>original: "שדי" — a divine name often associated with natural boundaries and sustenance</note> until the end of the night. 

**The Secret of the Prophets**
The secret of the prophecy of the Lord is the source of the **Glowing Mirror** <term>Aspaklaria ha-Me'irah: a clear, direct lens of prophecy unique to Moses</term>. Does it not shine as we have written? The teachings of Rabbi Shimon bar Yochai, peace be upon him, hint at this with the name "Israel," the fourth level that was not fully revealed from the "waters" until Samuel came, and of him it is written: "And also the Eternal of Israel will not lie nor repent" <note>1 Samuel 15:29</note>. Furthermore, it points to the source of Moses. The explanation is that their prophecy and attainment were from within the "form," which has three levels. Each prophet attained according to his strength and the level given by the Torah. The sages of truth <note>The Kabbalists</note> received that according to the generation, so was the attainment of prophecy. As Rabbi Shimon bar Yochai revealed in the *Tikkunim*: "All the prophets, their prophecy was through the 'windows' of the King's palace." These windows are the stars, and they are beyond counting. The sages of truth explained that these "windows" refer to levels that are behind the holy curtain. These levels are covered by **Seraphim** <term>A high order of angels</term>, covered in boxes, covered in purity, covered in fire, covered in the night, covered by the "Living Creatures" <term>Chayot: another high order of angels</term>, and covered by the secret of the Covenant and the "Head of the King." It was impossible for them to look directly.

But Moses attained his prophecy in every place. In every place, he was like a "partner" to the prophecy, which was not the case for other prophets. Each of them had to ascend their path to use the "speech" from that lack. Behold, he explained that all the prophecies and attainments of the others were only through the "Dull Mirror." That was the place of their attainment. Their prophecy was according to what was prepared in that hour. But for Moses, the holiness of prophecy was started for him. Moses attained his prophecy everywhere. His excellence over all other prophets was because his form and soul were emanated from above the dwelling of the "White World." Because of this, he was clear and perfected above all levels. Therefore, he attained a chosen vision. This is the meaning of "In all My house, he is trusted" <note>Numbers 12:7</note>. To explain this, they returned to the Midrash of Rabbi Shimon bar Yochai: Rabbi Judah said, "What is there to ask about Moses? No man ever turned back." Rabbi Yochanan said, "He was able to look into ten levels, as it is written: 'In all My house he is trusted,' and not just 'in the vision of My house.'" This was the portion of a man of wisdom.

Therefore, the intention of Moses was to guide them from their level of attainment through the Torah. He was perfected and included all the levels of the human soul. When the glory was divided, Moses’s soul was a "faithful artisan" and did not lack, just as Joshua’s merit was dependent on him. For Moses’s face was like the **Sun**, and Joshua’s face was like the **Moon**. Therefore, when they crossed the land, they were settled by the permanence that Moses established in his soul and spirit. The sages (may their memory be a blessing) clarified this: "The face of Moses was like the face of the sun, and the face of Joshua was like the face of the moon." For the moon has nothing of its own, but only the light that is transmitted to it from the sun. Therefore, Moses was the Sun, the source of light and attainment for him <insert>Joshua</insert>.

# Chapter 25 | Part: Secrets of the Torah | Chapter 26

The generation is deficient in this regard, etc. It is "deep, deep" <note>Ecclesiastes 7:24</note>; we find ourselves wandering and lacking because of their transgression. This is explained beautifully in the statement: "The Name which is in my house, I am departing" <note>original: השם אשר בביתי אני פורש; a reference to the Divine Presence leaving the Temple</note>. The intention concerns the sacrifice of the prophets who came during the deficiency, where everything enters and dwells to subdue that which seeks to bring about destruction. For this is set against that: the strength of the light and the flow against the scrubbing away and the ruin. In the verse of preparation, the light is seen as designated, and according to this, there is no relation to the attributes of prophecy for you, about which you complained. This "withdrawal" is hidden within your power, for this level was not withheld from you because you were unworthy of it—though he does complain about his power. 

I have considered their grievance, for even the level of those "pious ones of the Holy Spirit" <term>Ruach HaKodesh: a level of divine inspiration lower than formal prophecy</term>—who were like the level of the prophets—cannot be reached by a transgressor. If it were only for himself, he would have been worthy, and you would have had everything. For even during the initial exile of the Kings, there was still hope, as the rest of the Tribe of Judah remained and the Sanctuary was on its foundation. In our mercy, a belt is permitted; so too is the greatness in Israel, through which the Supernal Will returns in the morning watches and the lower shepherdings and the practical sisters. For the "Greatness" was like stolen property, hunted in its beauty by the hidden ones of the nation and the consolation. And the Name shall not be severed. 

He <note>likely referring to Maimonides</note> of blessed memory already wrote: "Reflect on the wisdom of their words regarding this generation, that the cessation of prophecy was not to frustrate the soul of the prophet in clinging to all attainment." In the house of prophecy alone, he placed the modes in an easy cause through his exertion. # Chapter 24 | Part: Openings of the Torah

The worlds, both general and particular, and those that serve as foundations, cannot be fully clarified... for within the "General" lies the Godhead, grouped within the "General" according to its power and its levels of greatness. It spreads out through the levels of our own hierarchy, for the Torah corresponds to the Great Name <term>The Tetragrammaton: the four-letter, essential name of God</term>, the secret of the "Splendor of Israel," the encompassing place of the Five Books of the Torah. Above it, there is no higher level, and nothing compares to it. In the world of "Those Taught by the Lord" <note>Isaiah 54:13</note>, the supports of the Torah are written against the "General" which includes everything—the secret of the Holy Spirit <term>Ruach HaKodesh: a level of divine inspiration lower than formal prophecy but higher than human intellect</term>. Everything is contained within the "Thought" and the "Unity." Blessed be those who study and occupy themselves with these matters, making them known so that they may be sustained and warmed by them. However, this is not achieved through wisdom received from the prophets, nor from the mouth of Moses, nor from the mouth of 
<margin>2</margin> the Almighty <note>original: הגבורה "The Power/The Might," a rabbinic title for God</note>. The secrets of "Thought" remain hidden within such knowledge; one might recognize certain logics through the intellect of the spirit of the "All," but it provides no practical benefit. The 
**fourth level**, which is much lower than the level of the Holy Spirit, is the level of the 
**Sanctified Heavenly Voice** <term>Bat Kol: literally "daughter of a voice," an echo of divine will heard after the cessation of formal prophecy</term>. This was diminished even among the pious when the Holy Spirit departed from Israel, as is found in the accounts of the "Messengers of Death," etc. Our Sages taught: Since the deaths of the last prophets—Haggai, Zechariah, and Malachi—the Holy Spirit departed from Israel; nevertheless, they still made use of the **Heavenly Voice**. Once, they were reclining in the upper chamber of the House of Gedi in Jericho, and a **Heavenly Voice** came from heaven and said to them: "There is one among you who is worthy of the Divine Presence <term>Shekhinah: the immanent, indwelling presence of God</term> resting upon him, but his generation is not worthy of it." They cast their eyes upon **Hillel the Elder** <note>A famous leader of the Sanhedrin during the 1st century BCE</note>. Again, once they were reclining in the upper chamber in Yavne, and a **Heavenly Voice** came from heaven and said: "There is one among you who is worthy of the Divine Presence resting upon him, but the generation is not worthy." They cast their eyes upon **Samuel the Small**. So it is said in the Jerusalem Talmud and in the tractate *Berakhot*. From this, you may know that the **Heavenly Voice** makes use of understanding... and the Masters of Truth <term>Kabbalists</term> said of this voice that it is what is referred to in the verse: "The sound of words you heard" <note>Deuteronomy 4:12</note>. It is the eighth level for Israel and is much lower than the Holy Spirit. A spark of the Godhead extends into the understanding from the "Fifth Voice," the "Voice of the Well," which is the **Heavenly Voice**. It establishes its structure because the great Kabbalists said that the "Lot of Glory" is the great destiny of Prophecy, and that the **Heavenly Voice**, the Holy Spirit, and the arrangement of the Divine Presence upon the Ark were dependent on the Ark and the Cherubim. When the First Temple was standing and established, the Light and the Flow of influence would spread out. For as 
<margin>4</margin> the Divine Presence strengthened upon it—may peace be upon it—and as I have written for you there, I remembered the "Kindness from atop the Mercy Seat" <term>Kapporet: the gold cover of the Ark of the Covenant</term> from between the two Cherubim. For the Glory dwelt between the two Cherubim as an earthly example of the "Upper Example." For the Sanctuary below is aligned exactly with the Sanctuary above, and everything in the Upper Sanctuary has a corresponding structure in the Lower Sanctuary. The place where it is said the Divine Presence dwelt below is like the place above, for the dwelling worlds were within it. According to this secret, "The Lord is in His Temple," for the Sanctuary and the Holy of Holies—which contains the Foundation Stone <term>Even Shetiyah: the bedrock of the Temple, considered the center of the world</term>—are the secret of the "Structure" as an upper example of the entire design of the Chariot <term>Merkavah: the mystical vision of God's throne-chariot</term>. When the Divine Presence dwelt there, everything was made according to the example and the design of the Secret. So too the Ark, the Mercy Seat, and the Cherubim—all were empowered by the Glory. Moses saw the Light and the Flow spreading to all the Great Ones. For the Ark, the Mercy Seat, and the Cherubim are like a 
**wick**, and the Glory is like the **flame** that catches and burns upon the wick. Through them, the Light increases and rests upon the Cherubim. But in the building of the Second Temple, the Glory and the Ark were hidden; they were no longer in the House. Even Haggai, Zechariah, and Malachi were confused after the destruction of the House and the coming to the land. This is because Prophecy and the matter of the "Secret" were intended to come from the Sanctuary, but it was held in great concealment and hiddenness. Thus, the vitality was drawn down to a lower level than that of the earlier prophets. For as the Light was delayed and suppressed, the "Structure" became smaller, until it eventually departed entirely due to the absence of the Light and the Flow from the "Almighty." Therefore, when it was withheld from Haggai, Zechariah, and Malachi, the Holy Spirit departed.

## Chapter 25

**Prophecy and the Absence of the Holy Spirit from the Cherubim.** This is mentioned by the examiner of the words of prophecy regarding what was written by **Baruch ben Neriah** <note>The scribe and disciple of the prophet Jeremiah</note> the prophet and Jeremiah... as it is explained: "The Lord God of Israel says concerning you, Baruch: You said, 'Woe is me now! For the Lord has added grief to my sorrow; I fainted in my sighing, and I find no rest'" <note>Jeremiah 45:3</note>. The intention here is that Baruch was praising himself and preparing himself for prophecy, but when he saw that prophecy was not achieved, he fell into a sickness of spirit, returning to the level of those who speak only by the Holy Spirit.

# Chapter 25

Even though the Second Temple stood before the Light was gathered up, and so it was in the latter building. Because it was still found during the existence of the House, a bit of the "Establishment of Light" remained for them—the **Heavenly Voice** which they used—and that is the end. The Light was intended to be a "portion" and a "heritage"... and this is what is found in their statement: "There is one among you who is worthy of the Divine Presence resting upon him, but his generation is not worthy." The intention was not to say that this voice was Prophecy or that they should be "Prophets," but rather that the perfection of the Ark and Cherubim was missing. It means to say that the Voice was very great, even though the Divine Presence had been removed from the Cherubim and the secrets of the Flowing Light were no longer present. They were prepared and yet far from it... they aimed themselves toward the attributes of the Divine Presence so that it might perfect them, yet being "Prophets" was withheld from the many. The perfection that was Moses was withheld... for just as a prophet requires the preparation of his own perfection, so too the greatest among them—the "Captains of Prophecy"—required wisdom and preparation. As we have explained, one needs two "Prophets" to precede him: the perfection of the Building of the House, the Ark, and the Cherubim; and second, the merit of the Light at the center of the Temple. But with the merit of the Light, it is possible for one who prepares himself to reach the level of those who speak by the Holy Spirit, even if they do not ascend to the level of full Prophecy. This was the case in the generation of Hillel and Samuel the Small... and also what I wrote regarding the young man in the four levels of prophecy as explained in the Kabbalah.

## Chapter 25

Indeed, with the destruction of the Sanctuary and the latter building... the great Cherubim of the levels of Prophecy were gone. The intention is that Baruch was preparing himself for Prophecy, and when he saw it was not achieved, he fell into sickness, remaining at the level of those who speak by the Holy Spirit, like David and Solomon. When he saw that he did not even merit this level, the scripture says 
<margin>3</margin> to him: "The Lord has added grief to my sorrow." Meaning: I was trusting that I would merit being among the prophets, and furthermore, the Lord added grief upon the pain that I did not even reach the level of the Holy Spirit. "I fainted in my sighing" refers to the collapse of the mind... as they said, "I fainted 
<margin>4</margin> in my sighing and found no rest." "Rest" includes both of these levels. They said: "There is no rest except Prophecy," as it is said, "The spirit rested upon them" <note>Numbers 11:26</note>, or "The spirit of Elijah rested on Elisha." He worries about these five things... and he says "all the land." The intention is to say it is not found 
<margin>5</margin> established, but from you it shall be established... for the Fountain flows always and is never diminished... the "Structure" is within you... for I am deep to establish the arrangements which are the great cause for the song of Prophecy... also the Upper One which corresponds to these lower ones... and the Light of Prophecy was not hidden entirely. Even if you did not reach the level of the Holy Spirit, this does not mean you are unworthy in your actions, for the Light is not hidden...

# Chapter 27 | Part: Secrets of the Torah | Chapter 26

Above all the holiness and purity we have grasped and our ability in the understanding of the Leader <note>original: "Menaheg," referring to the Divine Guide or the Intelligence governing the world</note>, the body is to matter as all absolute materiality. Through our power and the power of the Leader, and through the lack and physical nature of intent <note>original: "chumro," meaning his physical or material substance</note>, His wisdom is to me like my books, in the brain that moves and gives it eternal life. What is his value compared to the capacity of the lower realm, which is included in that which is from above?

What did he know? What was speaking with him? <note>This refers to the paradoxical comparison between Moses and the pagan prophet Balaam</note>. It is said regarding Moses: "Comfort" <note>This seems to be a corrupted OCR reading of the word "Mofet" or a reference to a specific Midrash</note> names for the material. Below, he did not know what was speaking with with him. Regarding Balaam, he "knew and his life spoke with him from all matter and he knew the knowledge of the Most High" <note>Numbers 24:16; original: "yodea da'at elyon"</note>. 

Moses did not speak with Him except when he was standing, as it is explained: "Mouth to mouth" <note>Numbers 12:8; original: "peh el peh"</note>, and "stand here with me" <note>Deuteronomy 5:27; original: "amod imadi"</note>. Balaam, however, spoke when he was falling, as it is said: "Falling and with eyes open" <note>Numbers 24:4; original: "nofel ve-galui einayim"</note>. 

From what follows, going to a king involves being bound in heresy. Up to this point, the sages have used their words to show the high status of Moses, peace be upon him, and the lowliness of Balaam. The enlightened one understands the difference between one and the other from the perspective of the etched laws of the Leader. This is the purpose of Moses's power and the weeping of Balaam. Far be it from the first speaker <note>Moses</note> that regarding his materiality, he did not know what was speaking with him. It is intended to say that he did not know or grasp the *essence* <term>Essence: the inner "whatness" or true being of the speaker, which Moses in his humility did not presume to "capture" or limit</term> of the one speaking with him. 

But for you, it is said that "what was speaking with him" and "your seal in his matter" refers to the identity of the thing which speaks with him. For the voice, peace be upon him, his broad mind and his reading and understanding would not allow him to grasp and know the missing point. For the lack of power and for his reward, peace be upon him, to grasp the secret of a matter from the supreme thought and its closeness to the simple and the reality of the high levels from the necessary thought, there is no boundary to the goodness of the Leader and his wisdom over the expanse of the Torah. 

Every level of Moses's prophecy, compared to Balaam, was lacking in its source and its zeal. The speaker, the voice, was missing. He did not know what was speaking with him because he leaned on a limited perspective according to his zeal, for the nature of everything—the voice is missing. Thus, because all of Balaam's prophecy was not void toward the All, he was an expert in it and grasped it, knowing what would hinder him. He spoke according to his nature, being one who understands himself and the extension of his thought. Wisdom in a king knows its revealed power like the work of the wise from every body and power, for everything is fixed within nature. 

It hints at the power of the conducting forces from the evil, all the traits of the body. Because all things—the thought from the evil which in its wisdom is the notification of the traits—all the intentions and the vessels are destructive. Regarding the matter of the Leader, the Judge, as the doubt and the end and the courtyard, so that all his dealings are in vain matters, he forgot the abandonment and knows through the proofs of action. Among them are things that the temperament of the soul was appointed over, and he knows from them his ability. 

Moses, peace be upon him, because he was far from physical life, did not have dealings with the "owners" <note>referring to terrestrial powers or astrological forces</note>, nor did he occupy himself with purified substances. He was like a fool in this regard because all his business was with the King at His table. For he is like the son of the house, a member of the household. And the one at the table of the King does not know what is in the King's heart regarding his conduct—only the King himself knows. Therefore, "he did not know what was speaking with him," and he could not grasp the end of His nature or the occurrence at all, to know what all His powers were. For he was on the ladder of the King. 

But Balaam was like a cave, reaching only the level of the "what" of his heavy traits. For the wise and for the destiny of Israel, it was not according to his abilities. For he was among the superior powers explained in his words, except that the supreme providence gave him a "table for a king" to attain this level and rank to be sustained. According to the custom, he knew what was speaking with him, and he intended more so that he would be afraid in his materiality, like one hearing the material of God. After he knew the Leader, for at the time of hearing and speaking, the voice of the opening—the intent in it was even the voice of the speaker—he would hear and know that the speaker of the voice was for the essence of the speaker. 

And Balaam knew *what* was speaking with him, and therefore his materiality was endangered. Moses did not know his vitality speaking with him, for he was prepared and standing, and his mouth was like a straight poem, and his heat was toward the speaker.

<column-break/>

Peace be upon him, he did not grasp His will, and therefore he had no hindrance or separation in his soul between his perfection and his cleaving to his level. Until he decided to understand himself and his essence, he gained profit. The text says "he almost knew" his essence and what spoke with him, and like all he rested himself. He did not rejoice in the emptiness of the spirit of vanity, but sought from the voice of the Holy Spirit. 

Close to this is the voice of the spreading of the soul. In our power and the power of their predecessor, it is written regarding his materiality: "And God happened upon Balaam" <note>Numbers 23:4; original: "Vayikar elohim el bil'am"</note>. Our Rabbis of blessed memory hinted in *Vayikra Rabbah* <note>A collection of homiletic teachings on Leviticus</note> that the language of "happening upon" (*Vayikar*) only refers to the language of impurity <note>original: "tumah"</note>, as we say: "that which is not pure by a chance occurrence <note>original: "mikreh"</note> of the night" <note>Deuteronomy 23:11</note>. 

And his prophecy itself, as written in the power of the voice, he knew the essence upon him of the Holy Spirit, and it was placed, "and he knew the knowledge of the Most High." Our Rabbis explained that he knew the moment <term>The Moment: a technical term for the split second of Divine wrath that Balaam allegedly knew how to exploit</term> in which the Holy One, Blessed be He, is angry. The voice of my sickness did not know one thought of the delayed cold, and it was not prepared at all. 

Regarding all the verses, they said Moses did not speak with Him except while standing, because the "Void" <note>referring to a total spiritual self-nullification</note> took hold of him to be in a heroic prophecy. And in the way we mentioned, this was possible for him according to his level. Regarding the matter of the "standing," it is the World of Standing <term>World of Standing: a spiritual state of stability and permanence, associated with the higher angels and Moses</term>, in his image in its entirety. It is the power of the phrase: "But as for you, stand here with me" <note>Deuteronomy 5:27</note>. 

Balaam, however, spoke when he was "falling," because all his dealings were with the "Missing Voice." He fell from the place of his holiness, as is known to the wise of heart. Thus it is written: "Falling and with eyes open." And all the end of the verse is doubled in his image to show his source. 

The power replaced the inclusive custom, and from it, the power and level of Moses were derived. From within his standing came his strength, while the lowliness of Balaam was evident. In the *Sifrei* <note>An ancient legalistic Midrash</note> at the end of the portion, regarding his voice and "the speaker as one playing music," they said: What is the difference between the prophecy of Moses and the prophecy of Balaam? There are two traits. For Moses, he did not know who was speaking with him, he stood, etc. Moses spoke with Him "mouth to mouth." The speaker spoke "mouth to mouth" with him. 

Regarding Balaam, in his materiality, he "heard the words of God" but He did not speak with him "mouth to mouth." Moses spoke with Him "face to face" <note>original: "panim el panim"</note>, as it is said: "And the Lord spoke to Moses face to face" <note>Exodus 33:11</note>. But Balaam did not speak except in parables, as it says: "And he took up his parable and said" <note>Numbers 23:7; original: "vayisa meshalo vayomar"</note>. 

The power in the part of "mouth to mouth" and "face to face" refers to two traits. They made known what was necessary in the double level of "face to face." And the secret of the power of even the Written Torah and the Oral Torah is here. The Sage of Speech desired to connect the matters. 

From the knowledge that his voice reached the height of his wisdom and Israel, this is the text: "And the Lord spoke to Moses," separating him from materiality. This is the end, and "face to face" indicates the level of Moses's prophecy and his wise zeal. 

But Balaam was in a "fall" to pass over the Holy Spirit... and in his words were parables and hints. They established that "and he said" represented two traits that Balaam possessed... Moses did not know *who* spoke with him, but Balaam knew *who* spoke with him, as he "heard the words of God." This is a hint. 

And it seems to me from the outside that this matter is based on what they said in the *Sifrei* regarding the expression "He spoke with him." For this settled the level of the Torah for us, which is impossible for any intellect to bring down or understand unless from the mouth of the Ancient One from whom all come. Through our grace, he made us merit it. It is impossible to know and grasp who the speaker is... The Midrash points to their secret... for on the level of the Torah, it points to the place of the dominion of words that Moses had... from the level of speech which is "mouth to mouth" and "face to face." And he was forced thus by the level of the Torah that was included in the supreme wisdom. 

Thus, they knew that Moses did not know what was speaking with him... while Balaam, these traits were in the hand of Balaam and not in the hand of Moses.
