# Chapter 27 | Torah Part Two | Chapter 26

The spiritual is first designated as the **Building of the Wing** <term>Binyan de-Kanfata: A mystical structure associated with the Shekhinah or Divine Presence</term>, encompassing **Wisdom and Understanding** from within. From the side of the entrance, the Wisdom that stands upon the ground of this Temple is where one may behold Wisdom and "acquire her hands," as it is written regarding the soul’s preparation for atonement. Because of this, all the words of the prophets are the speech of a prophet, as it is said: "Let them be mixed in the midst." For this reason, the word of the commandment was not snatched away, and "this is in their mouths." 

Within the **Chamber of Will**, turn back toward the inner prophets, who are Metatron <note>The primary archangel and "Prince of the Countenance" in Jewish mysticism</note> over them. They are the **two thighs** <note>original: "triein yerchin," referring to the Sefirot of Nezah and Hod, the sources of prophecy</note> for the altar of incense, and they are categorized as the two lower thighs for the opening, which are the stars of prophecy called the **Oral Torah**. Just as there are standing supports for the Torah that is the **Written Torah**, so too are there standing supports for the Torah that is the **Oral Torah** below. This is the "Challah" <note>Referring to the grain offering or a specific spiritual portion</note> below. When these two supports below are joined as one, they provide the prophets with the power of the "eye-paint" <note>A metaphor for spiritual insight or the ability to see the divine</note>. This is the joy of her existence, like a direct appearance, and all those who are emptied above all else shall be sucked clean. They are eternally in one body, and for this reason, He is one and they are one. 

When all these are joined, she then rules over another power. This is the **Holy Entrance**, which is called "The Building" among the powers. Through these holy matters, everything stands and everything lives from the side of the **Wing**. From afar, God is from the side of the **Wing**, spreading out until the end. 

It has already been explained that the **Writings** <note>Ketuvim, the third section of the Hebrew Bible</note> involve two contemplations: the inner secret of His study, the depths of the Torah—the **Torah of Truth**. Everything is achieved through the **Elders of the Pillars** who strengthen themselves here at the summit. The mouth builds, and even more so through these lower ones who resonate with their higher powers. When these are joined to one another and reveal themselves together, they draw power for the benefit of all through her possession. This is the secret of the day called "Selah" when all these powers are joined through a **sent-forth mirror** that is polished. For through the Elders of these Pillars, they were all strengthened in the branches. From within the **Female World**, they would perceive the **Male World** <note>In Kabbalah, the "Female World" often represents the receptive Shekhinah, while the "Male World" represents the active, radiating Sefirot</note>. This is what the Holy Author said in his Midrash: What is the difference between her power and her strength? One is in the world of the hidden, and "God was" in the world of the Female. 

One yearns to write down the level of the "Cubit of the Building." Thus, one praises it in every height of space—how beautiful! If the Elders of the level of power extend throughout the firmament until the end. When the scribe wrote, he said regarding her power in the **Male World**, "laws." They did not achieve the **Female World**, as it is written: "And may God be," and Isaac blessed him. This is correct: to spread these from the Male World so they are revealed to her, so as not to trespass in a holy place. 

Behold, the nature of the "laws" in the aforementioned world was sent through the "Female" world as we have written. Because they were not strengthened by day, but only in the externalities of the night—which was the station—it is possible their action was mixed with Kindness and Mercy, yet remained unblemished by the eye of a limb whose vision cannot grasp the **Mirror that does not shine** <term>Aspaklaria she-eina me-ira: An opaque or indirect vision, associated with all prophets except Moses</term>. This is the meaning of "it is inscribed." The secret is that there are many "faces" <note>aspects or dimensions</note>. Without the "Rectifications" <note>Tikunim</note>, the place of the permanent Union is according to the "Cup of the Tongue." There, the "Crown of the Sabbath" resides in the house. The Shekhinah is called "Blood" for all forms and images, to hold Ezekiel and all the higher forms.

<column-break/>

The designated reason: Like a string of construction for every light, according to the brain from which all lights emerge. The secret is that this light and abundance shatters and strengthens from the **Source of Light** upon the face of its level through the "thick cloud" <note>arafel</note>. In this way, he [Moses] would suck and draw in his prophecy through the secret of the **Voice**, the power of the inner face. This is the secret of **"Face to Face"**—the Upper Faces which are the Radiant Faces spoken of regarding Moses. The secret of the Lower Faces is that they radiate into one another. Therefore, all words of kindness and the lights within are in wholeness and mercy, existing forever in their strength and revealed. 

Therefore, it is said that the "end of thought" is in the totality, because of the flow from the highest inwardness. It goes without saying that the "Laws, Sayings, and Judgments" which are his body are an essence that contains no systems of parable or imagery; rather, everything is in the **Thought** and the entanglement of these Upper Beings. In the "Songs of his Torah," everything is according to its plain meaning and its usage; there is no parable or imagery in them at all. This was appropriate for the lights of the place from which the Torah was faithfully given: that **Higher Thought** which is clean of all dross. There, no "system" of a thing exists, nor the secret of "backwards" or the "seven stars." The Wisdom of that place is light, and the receiver must receive it according to the order of the **Voice**—the Voice itself. 

For this reason, he [Moses] rose in the level of his prophecy above all other prophets. The place of the Torah's attachment is great. This is the beautiful opinion of the Sages when they said: "No prophet arose in Israel like Moses." For the Torah exists forever, and it contains "two laws." 

In the books, they said: "In Israel, one did not arise, but among the nations of the world, one did arise—and who was it? **Balaam**." In the Midrash of Rabbi Shimon bar Yochai <note>The Zohar</note>, regarding the first proof: "No prophet arose in Israel like Moses." Rabbi Joshua said: In Israel he did not arise, but among the nations he did. Who was it? Balaam. He responded: "You have spoken well!" Rabbi Shimon came and said: If he were still alive, I would open with words of scepters and rods! What is the peace of these? If such a one arose among the nations, it was Balaam, who perceived the "Upper Upper." Just as they worship below, he used the crown of the holy fear above. But Balaam used the **Lower Crowns** that are not holy below. 

It is written of them: "not like these." He was a "diviner." He said: "Let God be," taking more. Rabbi Yose said: "Let God be" implies that the Holy One, blessed be He, is for the upper and lower tablets. He is full of Mercy, Judgment, and Strength. The nations of the world and Israel are spread out: Israel in the **Holy Upper Crowns**, and the nations of the world in the **Lower Crowns** that are not holy. These are to the Right, and those are to the Left. 

In any case, the level of the prophets of Israel is holier than the prophets of the nations. Rabbi Isaac said: Just as there is a distance of a thousand parasangs between various prophecies of holiness, so too is Balaam distant from the side of prophecy, belonging to the lower, unholy side. In any case, Moses rose to the line... and many levels are spread between them. 

The intention of the Sages was to say that just as Moses was exalted in the level of his prophecy through holiness and **Thought**—which is the portion of Israel—above all other holy prophets, so too was Balaam exalted in his level of prophecy above all other sorcerers and diviners who draw from the "hard" levels. Balaam was found with the "strength of the serpent" and with the "sword" in all types of impurities. Between the level of Moses and the level of Balaam, there is the distance between the world and the void.

# Chapter 27 | Secrets of the Torah | Chapter 27

His operation <note>The "operation" or "action" of the Divine Name</note> stems from an internal awakening. For this reason, it is impossible to perceive anything in the word "Blessed" <note>original: "Barukh"</note>, for it is a name of every form and has no visible appearance or likeness at all. Any form or appearance mentioned in Scripture exists only in the prophet's thought, where perception is clearer. For this reason, Daniel’s perception was particularly clear, because his entire perception took place within his thought.

<margin>1</margin> In the *Chapters of the Chariot* <note>original: "Pirkei HaMerkabah," likely referring to Heikhalot literature</note>, I have written on this matter. Let us return to the level of Jacob our Father (peace be upon him), specifically regarding the Unity and his level of perception, which was greater than that of Ezekiel. Regarding Jacob, it is said: "And God spoke to Israel in visions of the night." This implies that his "ascending and descending" <note>A reference to the angels on the ladder</note> served as a memorial for the point of exile. This is explained through the number twelve <note>The twelve tribes</note>. Consider the intent: it corresponds to the **Well of Living Water**, the "Well of the Sabbath," and the daughter <note>original: "Bat," often a reference to the Sefirah of Malkhut/Kingship</note>, which are like the waters that gladden the camp. To Israel, these were given in strength, for the "Living Creatures" <note>The *Hayyot* of the Chariot</note> support from below and sing above. This is the meaning of "He established it with His strength," generating greatness and power. The Divine Presence <note>original: "Shekhinah"</note> was meant to cleave to his father Isaac, which is the attribute of **Awe** <note>original: "Pahad," the Sefirah of Gevurah</note> unique to him, to strengthen and complete it. Through his awe, he was aided, moving from the domain of the "Judges" to provide rest. This rest was for his children who constantly descend through the "crossing," bound like soldiers from the "wine" and "understanding" <note>original: "Binah"</note> that emerges from the womb. Thus, the intention was to cleave to his father Isaac.

"And God spoke to Israel in the visions of the night"—this is the secret of the "Rectifications" <note>original: "Tikkunim"</note> and the attribute of the "Rising" in a great encompassing circle. This is the secret of "in the visions" <note>original: "be-mar'ot"</note>: through the "visions of the night" he would be continuously strengthened. This is why it is said that although he was not the "God of his father" <note>as a separate entity</note>, He is the God of every individual part of his father, who represented the "Line" and the "Continuous" and the "Examination" in its awakening and union. This is the secret of "the God of my father." This is a high level, similar to the level of "Remoteness," as I have written. This is the level of the Patriarchs regarding this vision that is seen.

The matter of prophetic vision and the matter of the angel are closely related, both being included in the refinement toward God. This is what is seen through the angel, as I wrote in Chapter 26. The reason they saw it was because the products of thought and contemplation increased through the strength of the soul’s receptivity. When thought is etched strongly into the soul, the soul is uplifted as if it were a prophecy, even as the body experiences a cessation of its pulse. The "animalistic" part of man is then blessed. This is the meaning of "peace" <note>original: "shalom"</note>, from the language of "dreaming" <note>original: "v’tachlimah"</note>. These are the acts of healing/dreaming that extend and blend as a blessing upon the body and rest for the soul. This perception and the "Mights" <note>Gevurot</note> produce peace through their power. This is further indicated by the "weighing of the heart." As stated in the appropriate chapter, these are not merely "fancies of the heart," as it is said: "Your thoughts came up upon your bed" <note>Daniel 2:29</note>. There it is said that prophecy begins with an awakening to Torah. This is the secret of Jacob’s dreams and the ascending angel. When Jacob our Father (peace be upon him) went to Haran to take a wife, he was being clarified and refined in his "vessels." The Sages said that they changed the word to "peace," referring to the peace of prophecy. Our Sages (of blessed memory) hinted at this regarding the "Creatures of the Chariot." They said regarding the verse "And he took from the stones of the place": Rabbi Yehuda, Rabbi Nehemiah, and the Sages disagreed. Rabbi Yehuda said he took twelve stones, for the Holy One, blessed be He, decreed that twelve tribes would arise. He said: "Abraham did not establish them; Isaac did not establish them. If these twelve stones merge into one, I will know that I am to establish the twelve tribes." When the twelve stones united, he knew he would establish them. Rabbi Nehemiah said he took three stones. He said: "Abraham—the Holy One, blessed be He, unified His name upon him. Isaac—the Holy One, blessed be He, unified His name upon him. If these three stones merge into one, I will know that the Holy One, blessed be He, will unify His name upon me." When they merged, he knew. The Sages say he took a few stones, saying: "From Abraham came the waste of Ishmael and the sons of Keturah. From Isaac came Esau. If these stones merge, I will know that nothing 'unfit' <note>original: "pasul"</note> emerges from me."

<column-break/>

This was the work of the Master's hand. The intention here is that although Jacob our Father’s (peace be upon him) primary journey was to take a wife, he possessed the knowledge of the "Building of the Children" through prophecy. The twelve tribes were ordained by the Holy One, blessed be He, to stand from him, serving as an **Upper Pattern** <note>A microcosm of the divine realm</note>. This is the secret of the "Eye of Jacob," from which twelve prophecies descend, the secret of the "Twelve Permutations of the Name" <note>original: "Twelve Havayot"</note>. These are the "Twelve Diagonal Boundaries" <note>original: "Gevulot Alakhson," a concept from the *Sefer Yetzirah* describing the dimensions of the spiritual universe</note> known to the Scholars of Truth <note>The Kabbalists</note>. Behold, the "Tribes" are the ten [and two] existences that are strengthened through this union and unity. Jacob was the prototype, extending the "Voice" below through the twelve tribes so they would all join into a single unity under the Kingdom of Heaven, mirroring the Upper Pattern. Furthermore, he contemplated that the Name of Heaven should rest upon Israel to bring the spirit of prophecy upon them, so that his children would grasp from him that the tribes are a pattern of the Upper Root. 

He also contemplated that no seed should emerge from him that would prevent perfection or be "waste" like Ishmael or [Esau]. Thus, the "body of the chain" and the receptivity of the unions were formed according to their divisions and their literal meanings in the Name, as if through prophecy. Through this, the understanding increased. In all of this, it can be said that the vision established that which would be; therein the building reached the level of prophecy to receive the Torah. Through this, they were "pressed" into the name of prophecy. This is a wonder of the vessel, displaying a terrible purity and utility. Esau, the "waste," did not merit this. In the name of the Lord it was written: "I am the Lord, God of Abraham your father and God of Isaac." The text does not say "God of my father," but rather unifies the Great Name upon him according to their attribute of **Truth** <note>The Sefirah of Tiferet, associated with Jacob</note>, which is the complete Chariot. This "God of Abraham your father and God of Isaac" means each patriarch was included in this grasp. Jacob is the essence, for in his life he was the body of the "Nothingness" <note>original: "Ayin"</note> to the Divine. He knew he would establish twelve tribes, which is a "constellation" <note>original: "mazal"</note> known to the wise. In this, he spreads out and covers all his divisions. 

Regarding the interpretation of "And it was at the time the flocks conceived," and "I saw in a dream," he sought the "streaked and spotted" among the sheep. The angel of God said to me in a dream, "Jacob," and I said, "Here am I." And he said, "Lift up your eyes and see..." for I have seen all that [Laban does to you].

<margin>2</margin> In the middle of the year, in his haste, according to his glory and righteousness, he was shown a prophetic dream because his actions and intentions were focused on the clarification of his existence. The vision in the dream was a "strike" <note>an impact of revelation</note>; he himself was honored through the visions of prophecy, the secret of the **Upper Levels**. This is explained and divided according to its types in their branches, strengthened by the "Mights of the Mights" <note>Gevurot</note> found in every Chamber <note>Heikhal</note>. His form was purified and refined through them. In this state, he divests and clarifies himself from the "accidents of the body" and its sketches, mingling with the lights of the Holy One and being hidden within them. The spirit is refined into whatever it desires according to its level and perception. In this manner, it is clarified to the prophet through his powers and the preparation of the prophetic spirit, which encompasses spiritual forms. 

It is said concerning the "Withdrawal of the Torah" that it divests from the surrounding environment it was in and reclothes itself in its first form. There is a hint of this in the Torah: "And the Lord went His way as soon as He had left off speaking to Abraham; and Abraham returned to his place"—meaning to his original level <note>his physical state</note> where he was before the inspiration. I saw one of the Scholars of Truth who received from the *Geonim* <note>Leaders of the Babylonian academies, approx. 6th-11th century</note> (of blessed memory), who wrote in this language: "Prophecy and its secret involve all types of powers in dreams, drawing form after form until one is clothed in the form that is speech-like to him, surrounding him like the form of an angel. This form, which was prepared within him, enables him to receive the prophetic power and cleave to his children, encompassing spiritual forms. With a complete awakening, he finishes and concludes his journey toward prophecy, divesting himself of the speech-like form and reclothing himself in the power of his first form. He strips them all off, and it appears to him that all his limbs are woven together and clinging to one another. All his internal powers return to him as they were at the beginning. Then he speaks and is hidden in the likeness of a human being." Thus far his words. And I have already written...

### Chapter 26 | Secrets of the Torah

It was necessary to inform us in the wilderness and at Horeb <note>Mount Sinai</note> that, according to Moses’ explanation, they did not attain nor know [the Divine] in the same way. Regarding the phrase "You cannot see My face" <note>Exodus 33:20</note>, he knew [the limitation], and this was the level of his people. As it has been clarified, "From his own he lacks, and from his own he shall be carved," <note>An idiomatic way of saying one’s limitations define their scope</note> and the sweetness of their mouth. Therefore, he detailed for him... his eyes were like a knife among the fat ones... and because we offered incense... corresponding to the place of His holiness. Just as we study the holy Psalm where it is written, "Until He makes known to us," <unclear>and from years</unclear>. Moses did not know [in advance], yet the Holy One, Blessed be He, would speak with him; but [Balaam] did know to count [the moments] when the Holy One, Blessed be He, would speak with him. For when the "Knowledge of the Most High" was known from his height, it was like a servant who enters before the king... and you know the king from nearby at the table, and he knows the many conducts and powers of the king at his table. So too, Moses knew what the Holy One, Blessed be He, was destined to speak with him. In that same manner, He would speak with him at every hour that he desired, as it is said, "his eyes were covered and revealed," <note>A reference to Numbers 24:4 regarding Balaam</note> he would delight before Him, and his mouth was open-eyed to that which he asked and heard from the Lord. For He would speak with him at any hour he desired, as it is said, "And the glory of Moses <insert>approached</insert> the Tent of Meeting," and he would hear the Voice and so on.

And look at this <term>Sikhlut</term> <gloss>folly/complexity</gloss> which he places in the dispute: the world's debt <unclear>is revealed</unclear> through Balaam and not through Moses. Could this be so? Rather, the explanation of what was said—that "Balaam knew what the Holy One, Blessed be He, was destined to speak with him"—is according to the words found in the <term>Sifrei</term> <note>An ancient legalistic commentary on Numbers and Deuteronomy</note>. Balaam knew *who* was speaking with him, and from this we infer: who among us knows who speaks with him? For this reason, it was proven that this hearing was from the [Divine] thought. To inform us of his merits... and everything told of Balaam's merits and his lowliness was because originally he used the "forces of impurity" <note>original: "kohot ha-tumah," referring to dark magic or sorcery</note>, as I have written. However, afterward, he was elevated by the Holy Spirit for the sake of the benefit of Israel, according to the words of our Rabbis of blessed memory. To that point, the "Sages of the Truth" <note>Kabbalists</note> taught that his tongue and speech were also [divinely directed] at that specific and sweet time, for he was within the <unclear>hidden place</unclear>. And there was then only one time for the benefit of Israel, without him knowing their true stature and praise. He uttered... and he knew the praises of Israel. And the **Ramban** <note>Nachmanides, a famous 13th-century scholar</note> of blessed memory wrote on the verse "And God happened upon Balaam" <note>Numbers 23:4</note> that now, for the honor of Israel, he rose to a higher level to understand the Midrash of the "Great Attribute" which corresponds to Moses, as he wrote there. All of this was for the necessity of the hour and for the honor of Israel. Afterward, he returned to his corruption and his folly, as it is written of him: "And Balaam son of Beor, the sorcerer, the children of Israel slew with the sword." As we have written in the "Letters of Wisdom" regarding its essence and the <term>Pardes</term> <note>The four levels of Torah interpretation: Literal, Allusion, Comparative, and Secret</note>, the explanation concludes the end of the chapter.

## Chapter 26
The Chariot and the Kingship <note>original: "HaMerkabah ve-haMalkhut"</note>. And this intention is in this manner: It has already been clarified that the <term>Kovshim</term> <gloss>conquerors/subduers</gloss> are within your power... from within the level of their sweetness. Just as they entered, so did the masters of illness and dreams... the eye of the sweetened level was the one that brings them in, and they see the <term>Kovshim</term> in their perfection. But not in the "Light of the Day" <note>The clear prophecy of Moses</note> according to the full height of their prophecy; even so, they did not attain it except through the level of the "fallen below." Therefore, Heaven forbid, the Holy One is above the Chariot until their honor, and this is like that. In the Midrash, it is said concerning the "Red Heifer," which refers to the portion of the <unclear>lower strength</unclear> to be eaten from its glory... to go to the feet of the peace... and it is impossible to... to the feet of its opening... from below to the will of the fruit... the understanding that **Metatron, Sandalphon, Uriel, Raphael, Michael, and Gabriel** <note>The primary archangels in Jewish mysticism</note> [govern]. For example, those who are far away... more... and it explained regarding those who are far away until here. And it is written in the [work] *The Crown*...

### The Torah Chapter 26

### Chapter 28 | Part of the Crowns of the Torah | Chapter 28

<margin>And so, from the division of the Seven Sinai [manuscripts] of this book</margin>
By day, according to the way of the <term>Kabbalah</term><note>The Jewish mystical tradition</note>, these movements are called by the name "men." The intention behind this refers to the "Created Glory" <note>Hebrew: *Kavod Nivra*, a philosophical term for the manifested presence of God</note> within the angels. The sages called their precious essence a "garment," for it is a garment for the soul from a higher perspective called <term>H"S</term><note>Likely an abbreviation for *Haskel ve-Sod*—Intelligence and Secret</note>, which are the thoughts. In this word, my soul is the "garment," and the Holy Temple is generally included in this word, which is the garment. You already know that it would be difficult for you to call a human "man" if you only meant the body, for the body is nothing but a garment for the person. Thus it is written: "You clothed me with skin and flesh" <note>Job 10:11</note>. We say that the body precedes the "bringer-forth," but the soul is the true "man" in its thought. This is what is called "Man" in this Torah portion. 

He <note>The author</note> holds, as in other places, that when the movements are called by the name "men," the intention is this "garment." The reason angels are included under the name "men" is that they are prepared for the eyes of the physical body for that specific time. Regarding souls, the matter of the portion is that they sometimes clothe themselves in garments and sometimes as angels. They are "angels" because they are not literally physical garments; they are "men" because they are the angels called "garment." My people, return to your study and awaken to understand this matter. This ends his words. And from the division of the Seven Sinai manuscripts of this book, I have written further from the commentary of <term>Rashbi</term><note>Rabbi Shimon bar Yochai, the 2nd-century sage to whom the Zohar is traditionally attributed</note> of blessed memory regarding this matter.

He said: The light of the secret of the upper world and the lower world are in one <term>aperture</term><note>Hebrew: *Muvka*, a mystical opening or connection</note> and joined together. This is the secret of the three angels. High and low, the dwelling angels—it is written: "He makes His angels spirits, His ministers a flaming fire" <note>Psalm 104:4</note>. If you say they are "higher," then at the time they descend below, they clothe themselves in the garments of this world. For if they did not clothe themselves in garments according to the manner of this world, they would not be able to stand in this world, and the world could not endure them, etc., as I have written there. <insert>And this word was with the letter *He*</insert> even in the eyes of the Supernal ones, for the lower is to the upper like a body and a garment; however, the soul and that which is higher than it are like the form of a soul to it. In this way, all the worlds were established and built, as was explained there.

<margin>And he further wrote</margin>
According to the Midrash of Rashbi, at the end of the passage: "A son of man cannot see <unclear>his own body</unclear> to look upon an angel who has no body." And it is written: "And He rode upon a cherub and flew" <note>Psalm 18:11</note>, and it is written: "He makes His angels spirits." Rather, from here we learn that when they go on a mission, they go like the mortals of this world <margin>6</margin> and go and clothe themselves in a body according to the manner of this world. Until here [is his quote]. 

And in the <term>Midrash Ruth HaNe'elam</term><note>The "Hidden Midrash on Ruth," part of the Zohar literature</note>: "The sons of God" <note>Genesis 6:2</note>—Azza and Azzael—were two angels who brought accusations before their Master, and the Holy One, Blessed be He, cast them down to this world. Once they descended here, they became materialized in flesh and were delayed in it. And you have no other angels among all those who go to mingle among humans except for these. And they were angels called "Sons of God." When the Holy One, Blessed be He, cast them down, they materialized through the powers of the elements of human beings and were clothed in them. Until here. 

And the Master Kabbalist, the Prince Rabbi Azriel <note>Rabbi Azriel of Gerona, a 13th-century Kabbalist</note> of blessed memory, in the book *The Fountain of Gardens*, wrote in these words: "Be careful, O ancient pillars of the world, for the soul, as we said at first, is placed from the quarry of the creative power, which is the Tree of Life and the Well of Redemption, drawn from the light of the Garden of Eden to the level that is beneath this section <margin>E</margin> in that Understanding <note>Hebrew: *Binah*</note>. They join in the Word, and the soul clothes itself in the Spirit and is formed in the image of a shape before the man comes to this world." And they supported this with the verse: "As the Lord lives, before whom I have stood" <note>1 Kings 17:1</note>. It does not say "before whom I stand" but "I have stood" <note>implying the soul stood before God before birth</note>. This is because my teacher explained the matter of the internal lights: when they come before the place of Thought, they are without angels, and it becomes a garment for everything. Therefore, the soul, which is <unclear>almisla</unclear>, is taken in the source of forms, which is the place of Thought. Likewise, internal matters clothe themselves in light matters in their existences, as described. This is what Rabbi Eliezer the Great meant when he said that the soul was created before the heavens in the light, "wrapping itself in light as a garment" <note>Psalm 104:2</note>, and it is written: "You have clothed Yourself in glory and majesty." Until here [is his quote]. 

And the third part of the book, where he wrote further awesome secrets regarding this mystery—it is not proper to write them down or to elaborate on them. But in general, the matters are like the matters

<column-break/>

that passed, and it is certainly our Unity. It is all known by what I have explained to you at the beginning, for with these he himself told me their causes, for he had pity on the honor of His Glory. The one who draws it forth according to our labor—for a divine matter is by the word of the Lord. And also, the truth was hidden in many of my words with a melody—you lack wisdom and more, for the word of the Lord is a voice. He said to him thus according to its literal sense, and he said to him further: "Why did He not permit it to him directly by your hand and not by an angel?" And he said: "An angel spoke to me" <note>1 Kings 13:18</note>, and he did not say "thus says the Lord," but said "by the word of the Lord"—meaning, I know that he spoke to an instrument of the Lord. 

We learn further that the Angel of Glory was in doubt if the word to the angel was for the sake of the Lord’s glory or not. For he <note>the angel</note> said "to His angels He gave charge," but He did not speak to him, for he said "by the word of the Lord." And as I have written further above, he informed us because it was the word of the Lord, as if informing him that it is His way to build with intent and to cancel by means of an angel, as occurred in the matter of the Binding of Isaac <note>where God commanded the sacrifice but an angel stopped it</note>. 

And <term>Ramban</term><note>Nachmanides, the 13th-century sage and mystic</note> of blessed memory wrote at the end of the passage: Here the sages awaken us to say—from where is the prophecy in the first speech? He mentioned that he should remember the second, in which he said that it is the Lord. But for these who are in the way of prophecy, it is built with intent, and He cancels the prophecy through an angel, for he knew that it was the word of the Lord. 

And in the Midrash *Vayikra Rabbah*, they said: "And He called to Moses" <note>Leviticus 1:1</note>—this was not like Abraham. Regarding Abraham it is written: "And the angel of the Lord called to Abraham" <note>Genesis 22:15</note>; from the house the angel calls, and from the back he speaks. But here it says: Rabbi Abin said, the Holy One, Blessed be He, is the One who calls and He is the One who speaks. At that time, Abraham was attaining prophecy until his soul was prepared at first to attain an angel, and he would rise from that level to the level of the Word of Prophecy. But Moses was prepared for prophecy at all times. 

Everywhere, the sages awaken us to inform us that seeing an angel is to enter into the "Intention," and those who see angels and speak with them are not part of the <unclear>past possessions</unclear>. However, angels are found even if those who dwell with them are not among the prophets—this is not so. There are two levels of truth here: one is through the fullness of the intellectual soul, and this catches the distance of prophecy in the matter of <margin>look at where he reached</margin> Daniel, and this is by mistake from the level of prophecy. And the truth is, if one did not reach the level of prophecy, like <term>Balaam</term> or the youth of <term>Elisha</term>, they knew the angels in the "distance of prophecy" with "uncovered eyes" <note>Numbers 24:4</note>. This is the language of hearing from those far away and those who are below the level of the angel of prophecy. There is some proof of this from him. 

And all this place mentioned therein is the taking of an actual angel. But in a place where the sages mention the angel in the soul, as in the portion of *Vayera* and in the verse "And a man wrestled" <note>Genesis 32:24</note> and the verse "And a man found him" <note>Genesis 37:15</note>—this is the "Created Glory" among the angels. He is called "His wrath beneath our King," for even among angels there are various levels; some use these and some use those. Our sages have already hinted at this regarding the angels created on the second day and those on the fifth day. And the <term>Tananim</term><note>Likely referring to high-level spiritual beings or a specific class of angels</note> who are called by the name "men" are those who are materialized in a physical body—not without reason for the pious and the pure of soul and the children of prophecy. This is always without any danger to serve, and the <unclear>waters</unclear> will look upon them as they are. 

And if it is difficult to understand how the "men of Sodom" who were evil and sinners could err regarding angels and not see them—it is possible to say that they did not see them as angels at all, but rather as human men who came to Lot. Some of the sages returned to this, for what did they say to those with "clear bows"? And in Sodom, how could they see them at one time as these and another time as those? To all these, this is the tradition of the Ramban of blessed memory regarding the attainment of angels and the seeing of them in these three levels. And such was the tradition of the holy pious Rashbi <margin>And I already hinted at this in the commentary at the end of Chapter 25</margin> peace be upon him. 

This is because there are some angels who appear to humans in the form of an actual man, and this is a small general rule of the various levels of "uncovering of the eyes" and the level of "visions." There are some who are more internal, and they attain them because they are in the visions of the intellectual soul and in the matter I wrote above. And the precious Rabbi <term>Bahya HaLevi</term><note>Rabbeinu Bahya ben Asher, 13th-century commentator</note> of blessed memory wrote in the portion of *Vayera* that all that is explained...

<meta>This page continues the discussion on the distinctions between levels of revelation, transitioning from the end of Chapter 27 into Chapter 28. ### Chapter 27 | Part of the Secrets of the Torah | Chapter 28

Above, there is a distinct boundary between prophecies. In this same way, there is a distinction between dreams; some are "dreams of prophecy" and others are simply dreams. However, all of them are powerful within the realm of dreams. This is why Pharaoh’s dreams were so troubling, and in general, this serves as an example of the conduct of the prophets for the benefit of Joseph—so that he would rise to greatness—and for the benefit of his brothers to provide sustenance during the famine. This was made known in the dreams at Hebron and through the status of Israel as a singular body. Dreams also have degrees because they function in every action. The reason is that the dream descends and mingles with several degrees, and according to the degree it descends into, so one dreams; according to a person's level, so is their dream. I have already written about this in Chapter 10.

The holy Rabbi Shimon bar Yochai <note>Rashbi, the traditional author of the Zohar</note>, peace be upon him, removed this veil <note>original: *chomer*, referring to a difficult or "material" blockage in understanding</note>, saying in the language of the <term>Zohar</term>: "To them are appointed sixty [messengers] to be established upon the weight of the flanks..." <note>original: *be-lishon shel lachikon mamnan shistin...* This is an Aramaic passage describing the celestial mechanics of how dreams are formed through sixty lower degrees</note>. And he mentions the phrase "revealing to you those appointed over them" to make known through the word "weakness" <note>Hebrew: *chalah*</note> to the kings of the sorcerers. This is the secret of the verse: "And God <note>OCR error reads *Chalkis*; intended is *Elohim*</note> came to Abimelech in a dream of the night" and it is written: "And God said in a dream." His words in the Midrash of Rabbi Shimon bar Yochai, peace be upon him, are: "Thus God prepares to come with the voice of the speaker who proves it to him." And: "God came to Balaam at night with the voice of the speaker to command him."

The reason, as I have written, is that the dream mingles with several degrees and therefore spreads throughout the whole world. However, every prophetic vision has a known place where it spreads, specifically "up to this point." The holy Rabbi Shimon bar Yochai, peace be upon him, removed this veil by saying: "Behold, the dreams of the wise... all connect below. Two degrees spread out from the speaker and the dream, standing in the thresholds... until the feet reach the feet, and there the lower spirit is found..." <note>The author is quoting an Aramaic mystical text describing the hierarchy of revelation from the highest "feet" of the divine realm down to the lower world of dreams</note>. The secret of all these paths and rungs is to look upon one another. All these degrees belong to prophecy, for from there they go out and spread, becoming entangled with the speaker, and from them a dream is made. This is the holy source that said: "He revealed concerning the prophecies"—meaning sometimes through the speaker and sometimes through a dream of prophecy. The reason depends on the place they prepare and mingle, for there the pillars of the degree of prophecy are found, where everything spreads from the place of Jethro <note>possibly a reference to a specific spiritual location or a scribal error for a different name</note>. Sometimes they prepare for this place and it is the "speaker," and sometimes they prepare for that place and it is a "dream." As I have written regarding the secret of the "Work of Prophecy" and the holiness of prophecy in its world, which is the intention of this chapter.

### Chapter 28

I have already written that prophecy spreads out and emanates from the <term>Unification</term> <note>Hebrew: *Yichud*, the oneness of God</note>, and all its wisdoms and prophecies are acts of Kindness <note>Hebrew: *Chesed*</note>, each according to its power, degree, and path. This follows the way I wrote in the "Secrets of Prophecy" and the longing that is prepared from it, for everything is included in the secrets of prophecy to emphasize the Unification and to make its nature known and publicized in the world. This is only possible if the prophet stands as his own voice upon his faith. This would not be possible if people did not challenge him and surround him regarding the Unification itself. It is impossible to understand the truth of the "Glory" <note>Hebrew: *Kavod*, the manifested Presence of God</note> except through the judgment of the King of Glory, His memory, and His numbering.

The prophets would pause at the words of the King. As it is said in the <term>Midrash Tanchuma</term> <note>A collection of homiletic teachings</note>: "And he said to the one completing the path... the prophet said to him: 'Who are you?' He said to him: 'I am a King.' He said to him: 'But it was said to me: "Take now your son" <note>Genesis 22:2</note>.' He himself spoke to me, and he told me to return to the requester." Immediately, "The angel of the Lord called to Abraham a second time." This shows that he was questioning the Torah because it was given by an angel, whereas the <term>Akedah</term> <note>The Binding of Isaac</note> was from the mouth of God Himself. There are matters in the wilderness that touch the heart—the heart of the world in its completion and its Unification—which compel prophecy to reveal its truth. It is impossible to understand them except from the mouth of the "Intentions" and the "Vision of the Levites." Therefore, the one who intends in prophecy requires all of this.

<column-break/>

And he prayed for the prophets, he who sanctified the inner secret of the Unification. Blessed be the King and the Life <note>Hebrew: *Chayot*, also referring to the celestial beings</note> called the "Kingdom of Kings," who appoint the truth of the Glory in this, to publicize His loftiness in His world. For the Glory comes to the prophet not from himself, and He revealed the reason and the secret: so that the Godliness and His Unification would be elevated and publicized to every prophet. This is why it says: "If there be a prophet among you, I the Lord will make Myself known to him in a vision, I will speak with him in a dream" <note>Numbers 12:6</note>. The level higher than this is noted because no specific name was brought in this context; it says "I will make myself known" and "I will speak," meaning the Speaker Himself.

The sanctification of the Glory for the prophecy of the King and its publicity is a strong place for his faith. They stand on the "Horn of Prophecy." This is what Jethro <note>likely an error for another figure, or referring to Moses' father-in-law's realization</note> meant when he spoke to the Master of Prophecies [Moses], peace be upon him: "And I appeared to Abraham, to Isaac, and to Jacob as <term>El Shaddai</term>, but by My name <term>YHWH</term> I was not known to them" <note>Exodus 6:3</note>. Behold, He revealed that the Glory shown to the Patriarchs was not revealed in the same way as to the one who sees through *El Shaddai*. The created being is not called by this name at all without his "making." The Blessed One says that through the "Compassion of the Flames" <note>possibly a reference to the burning bush or angelic fire</note> He built a fortress outside of Himself forever. It is not designated in the language of "And the Lord visited" or "And the Lord said" regarding the angel that appeared to him and was called by the Holy One's own name, as is written in the *Book of Reasons*. But the Blessed One does not build the angel into a name, and the matter is not as the <term>Guide for the Perplexed</term> <note>The philosophical work by Maimonides</note> said.

According to the blessing, every prophet besides Moses our Teacher, peace be upon him, received his prophecy through an angel and the "Degree of the Prophet" which I wrote above. He went according to his intention and said that the prophet, by his own knowledge and will, approaches prophecy through the ancient visions. According to the tradition stated, every place where "Divine Living Beings" are mentioned, it refers to an angel, whether in the Torah, the Prophets, or the words of prophecy. This is true in the Midrash or in the dreams of the ancients. The angels cannot be perceived [fully] because they are not a physical body for the eyes. Therefore, in the "Vision of the Glory," the one who perceives through the sight of an angel sees only the right-side Glory... and similar things have been said about it.

There were prophets who resided in a house with a "simple matter" <note>referring to an ordinary or plain appearance</note>. It appeared to them and... as it is written: "While I was yet speaking in prayer" <note>Daniel 9:21</note>. So too, the vision of the "End of Redemption" <note>Hebrew: *Ketz ha-Geulah*</note> was his blessing with his prophets through the connection and the "Secret of Nature." The sight of an angel and his power is a prophetic vision. Our Rabbis, of blessed memory, included this in the "Seven Living Beings" and the "Clear Tablets." It was not a "service of the voice" as the Guide for the Perplexed said. Therefore, they accepted the tradition regarding the difference between the prophecy of Moses and that of other prophets: "Moses prophesied through a **Glowing Mirror** <note>Hebrew: *Aspaklaria ha-Me'irah*</note>, while other prophets prophesied through a **Dull Mirror**."

A mirror that does not glow is what is used by the prophet who sees by night, without a "nearness" in his prophecy. An angel appeared to Balaam and the young lad, but neither of them was a [true] prophet. Balaam did not rise to the level of a prophet among the degrees of prophecy until the time when it was the Divine Will to conquer for the glory of Israel and their benefit. As for what is written, "I am also a prophet like you" <note>1 Kings 13:18</note>, it has already been decided by the Word of the Lord. The meaning is this: the false prophet who comes to a prophet with things that are... is not the God who speaks. If he has another thought to say, "The voice spoke to me itself from its mouth," as if it were said to me from the mouth of someone other than your Torah... Saul said that the degree of their prophecy is "Truth" and "Shaddai." The Torah was not revealed to him, but this does not diminish it. He said to him, "I am also a prophet like you, I know the level of prophecy that told you 'do not return to walk in the way of the assembly.'" But if a prophet comes to you to permit you because his house is good... he will not permit you anything because he might tell the King that you transgressed the words of God, but when you return by the hand of a prophet, he spoke by the Word of the Lord, and then...

Furthermore, the "guaranty" <note>original: "arevut"</note> hints at the subjugation to which all souls were enslaved when they accepted the yoke of the Kingdom of Heaven and entered the tradition of the Covenant of the Torah. They respond with the hint of "I Shall Be" <note>original: "Ehyeh," the Divine Name associated with Keter or potentiality</note>, which is the Prince of the Supernal Sinai. Just as they accepted the supplications here in the ascent upon Mount Sinai below through Moses, this is the "Covenant of Life" and the Purchaser of above and below, and the Bride in whom they acted.

There is a clarification here: for behold, the Supernal Torah is the Torah written in the "Booth" <note>original: "Sukkah," perhaps a reference to a celestial canopy or the Sefirah of Binah</note> at Mount Sinai, the secret of "Lo, to the remote place." There, all souls destined to be included received it, for the Written Torah and the Oral Torah are in one Unity. Moses, who inclined Israel, received it there in a hidden manner below. This difficulty is found if not from all prophecy, and also upon it, the Leader of all Israel on the day they stood before the Lord at Horeb. All of them were in the lineage of these two Torahs which are known. From the start, the soul was purified in its portion to see the Glory, to be included in it, and to hear His voice. This was their good intention when they said: **"All that the Lord has spoken, we will do"** <note>original: "na'aseh," the famous pledge of the Israelites at Sinai</note>. They desired to remove from their eyes all doubt and the disruption of measurement that continues through the passage of time.

This was clarified in prophecy to confirm for them what they saw with their eyes and heard with their ears. They also desired to stand upon the truth after which there is no doubt, so that they might be established in their faith and in joy in His covenant and its path. They said: "Our will is to hear from the mouth of our King," etc., but it is also said: "Our will is to see our King." (In the *Midrash Chazut* <note>original: "Midrash Chazita," also known as Shir HaShirim Rabbah</note>, Rabbi Simeon bar Yochai taught: Thus did Israel demand in prophecy to confirm for them what they saw in the soul... as with the rescue from Pharaoh. There, Rabbi Levi said: Two things did Israel ask from before the Holy One, Blessed be He: that they might see His Glory and hear His voice. And they saw the Glory and heard the Voice, etc. And it was good in the eyes of the Lord that they asked, and He granted them their request. This is what is meant by: **"And the Lord said to Moses: Behold, I come to you in a thick cloud, so that the people may hear when I speak with you, and also believe in you forever"** <note>Exodus 19:9</note>.) Behold, it was shown that since he went out to meet God so they could receive their answer according to their request, He said His will was to come to him in a "thick cloud." This represents the level of Israel's perception and their prophecy to which they ascended; it was not the level of Moses, which was above their level. Rather, this was necessary both for the heavenly benefits and for those included in their request, which said "so that the people may hear." And again they prayed for the level of prophecy to receive the Torah. Had they been at a higher level, they would not have been able to endure it, and Moses surpassed this benefit. Therefore, he merited the "thick cloud" so that the people would hear. There is another benefit: that they might merit this level of prophecy for their perfection. Had this time been delayed, it might have been used to cancel your words—and know in truth that it would be a lie now—for if it had been at rest... to hand over your words, not to teach them or fulfill them. But this is the beginning... from which one knows and believes that the building is truth and their perfection is truth. There, when they ascended to the level of prophecy, it became your perfection and your glory, and they stood in faithfulness. This is the meaning of: **"and also in you they will believe forever."** It is clear from all this that Israel needed to ascend to the level of prophecy to receive the Torah so they would recognize the level of Moses, peace be upon him, and believe in him. Furthermore, Moses would be strengthened for them, for they would know the Torah contains judgment and doubt to be looked into... both for the body and the soul. For it was clarified from the Unity... just as we did with intention. Furthermore, because it was meant to stand forever and not...

### Chapter Thirty

The Sages of Truth <note>Kabbalists</note>, peace be upon them, received that the Torah in the Heavens is the "Written" one, and it is in the soul. This is fitting, for it is a Voice, as we have written, which the Divine Presence <term>Shekhinah</term> did not direct except from within the fire of the Great Name, as we have written. It prepared and showed the secret of His voice, and this is through the drawing forth of the new Names. This is what is meant by "In the heavens, voices" in the writing of the Torah. Some of our Sages of blessed memory said regarding the beginning of Moses, behold in his Midrash from two perspectives: for the Holy One, Blessed be He, said there: the "Writing," and **"All the people saw the voices"** <note>Exodus 20:15</note>. Are voices then seen? Rather, "all the people saw the voices"—those of which David spoke: **"The voice of the Lord is over the waters..."** etc., and **"The voice of the Lord is in power,"** meaning in the power of my making, and it says **"Even my hand founded the earth."** <note>Psalm 29 and Isaiah 48:13</note> **"The voice of the Lord is in majesty,"** which is the secret of majesty in the clouds. **"The voice of the Lord breaks the cedars"**—this is the fire that purifies the "cedars of Lebanon" <note>a metaphor for pride or high celestial powers</note> by hint. **"The voice of the Lord hews out flames of fire"**—this is the fire that makes peace between the snow and the water... preventing it from learning the water, also preventing his wife. **"The voice of the Lord makes the desert tremble"**—as if He performed a kindness for those who kiss it, for his generation and his seed forever, more than the desert. **"The voice of the Lord makes the hinds to calve and strips the forests bare, and in His temple all say: Glory!"** and it is written: **"I adjure you, O daughters of Jerusalem, by the gazelles or by the hinds of the field."** Behold, the tablets of the Written Torah are "Voices" in the <term>Ashuri</term> <note>the square Hebrew script used in sacred scrolls</note> material and in thought "by the hosts of the field"—these are the tablets that were written, as it is written: "And all the people saw the voices," etc. And in the name of the *Blessings* <note>the Talmudic tractate Berakhot</note> they said the Torah was given with five voices. 

And so it appears from the Midrash of Rabbi Simeon bar Yochai, peace be upon him. They said there regarding the verse: "Behold, Israel, what is for you from what shall be engraved," and in the language: "I will be established in my Supernal, precious Wisdom." Its essence and will are to understand from the radiance of Israel in the <term>Ashuri</term> form and in thought, to understand the pieces of the Torah... from the place of the Voice, as it is written: "the sound of the Shofar," etc. And all is truth, for the Torah was written below with seven voices, and he produces it and contemplates them and hears them. And in the name of the "Ketubot" <note>marriage contracts/tractate</note>, we have placed them in the soft... clearly explained in the scripture. For the seven are explained in the scripture, and they are the "Great Voice," greater than the Written Torah. And the six are the secret of the Oral Torah, the "Voice, Voice" that they mentioned, which was the one that drew Israel near. It was the one in which all the voices were included, and it was what Israel perceived. It is what was said regarding it: **"When you heard the voice from the midst of the darkness"** <note>Deuteronomy 5:20</note>. 

As for what they said in this Midrash regarding the essence and the will to understand from the radiance of Israel, etc.—the intention is not that they perceived the Field, even though they ascended to the level of the "included wealth" with the thought of all the voices. Rather, the secret is that all the voices were included in a single Unity in the Last Voice, and that is the thing that Israel perceived. As it is written, "and all the people saw the voices," it means the voice that was included. And because they perceived... generally from all the voices, they said that they saw specifically, for they did not perceive the other voices. Even if we accept that they perceived according to the plain meaning of the Midrash, it was only through a partition, which was not the case for Moses' perception, for he perceived all of it from Moses. This is what appears from what they said further there: "They showed it at the time they acted out of love, established in the Ashuri form." Except for Moses, all of Israel was like... reaching the form in essence... which was not the case for Ezekiel in this form... its essence to its preparation, voices, faces revealed as one, just as we said, "and all the people saw the voices." But for Ezekiel, the <term>Shekhinah</term> was revealed in the Chariot <note>the *Merkavah*</note> and no more... they explained these from the essences. The reason is because all the voices were included and He included them in the other voice hinted at in what is written, "and all the people saw the voices." The intention is the thing... that they perceived the other voices. Had they merited this level for the sake of receiving the Torah, they would have been at the level itself, established... for the difference between the two perceptions is as great as can be.

# CHAPTER 30 | PART OF THE SECRETS OF THE TORAH | CHAPTER 31

### 52
<sig>G 23</sig>

Regarding Him and "outside the place" etc., meaning to say to you that He who is the "Place of the World" <note>Original: *Mequmo shel Olam*. A rabbinic concept stating that God is not contained by the universe, but the universe is "contained" within His existence</note> can manifest His Glory in a specific place. Because with a dwelling-place, this matter concerning Him, may He be blessed, is hidden from us; yet it is known to Him. Based on this, one should accept and forgive [the difficulty] and not dwell upon it, since the Torah wrote about Him things that point toward Him—even as the High Voice, Heaven forbid, wrote about Himself as if He were a created being, saying "Pardon, I pray Thee, the iniquity of this people" <note>Numbers 14:19</note>. For the Sages said: "Take care for your souls, for you saw no manner of form on the day that the Lord spoke" [Deuteronomy 4:15]. Yet, the Torah also ascribed to Him movement and relocation, writing of Him "And He went up," "And He went down," "And the Lord descended," and "He rested." It even ascribed to Him eyes, a nose, hands, and feet, even though it had already begun to distance all such [corporeal] meanings. I have already written in this book that the requirement to distance physicality <term>Corporeality: The state of having a physical body. Jewish philosophy emphasizes that God has no body or physical form</term> is even greater than what the Torah itself explicitly distanced. Our King did not act without wisdom, nor should we.

The children of the "fifth generation" <note>Likely referring to a specific group of students or a stage in the transmission of Kabbalah</note> waited in silence, for the Glory descended upon Mount Sinai. They began to question the Torah's account of the writing of the "Witness of the Lord" <note>The Tablets of the Covenant</note> in the hidden places, and the mentioning of the Unique Name. Throughout our time, it was by hearing that we were reminded, as it says in the Torah: "Out of heaven He made thee to hear His voice" [Deuteronomy 4:36]. And so it was at Sinai: "And Thou camest down upon Mount Sinai, and spokest with them from heaven" [Nehemiah 9:13]. In this matter, the reception of our holy Sages... until it passed over us.

From the splendor of your wisdom, and according to what they wrote in the *Book of the Glory* attributed to Rabbi Samuel... who wrote about the opinions of the Talmudic Sages according to the Tradition <note>Original: *Kabbalah*</note> that was received from him from generation to generation, a tradition from the mouth of Rav Saadia <note>Saadia Gaon (882–942 CE), a foundational Jewish philosopher who proposed the "Created Voice" theory to explain how God spoke at Sinai</note>. It is written: "And it was on that day, and He descended, and there was thick darkness under His feet." And "The Lord descended upon Mount Sinai, to the top of the mount." Yet elsewhere it says: "Ye have seen that I have talked with you from heaven" [Exodus 20:19]. How can these be reconciled? The reception was that it was a single sound, but the voices were in heaven, as it is written: "Out of heaven He made thee to hear His voice, that He might instruct thee; and upon earth He showed thee His great fire." And what was this "Great Voice"? It was a fire that burned upon the earth, and you heard His words from the midst of the fire.

And the Sages were given visions and spirits of the Voice, as it was said to Israel: "For you saw no manner of form." Not any form at all. This is like a king who speaks to his servants while wrapped in a cloak; they see the royal garments that were received in his kingdom, but the king himself remains distant. They hear his voice, but they cannot see his likeness. Thus the verse says: "No manner of form." And this is what is written: "And the similitude of the Lord shall he behold" [Numbers 12:8]—behold, that is the Voice. For it is written: "Ye heard the voice of words" [Deuteronomy 4:12]. Until here.

Whoever is privileged to understand the essence of the "Standing" <note>The Standing at Sinai (*Ma'amad Har Sinai*)</note> within the Secret of the Lord will understand this teaching. He will contemplate the power of that holy Standing and the Voice, and the truth of Israel will become clear to him, along with the secret of the Glory’s descent to the top of the mountain. One should not reveal the end of this matter any further than what is found in the *Kuzari* <note>The *Kuzari* is a famous work by Rabbi Yehuda Halevi (12th century) defending Judaism, which discusses the national revelation at Sinai as an empirical proof of faith</note>.

The Master Guide <note>Original: *HaRav HaMoreh*, referring to Moses Maimonides (Rambam)</note>, may his memory be a blessing, in Part 1, Chapter 66 [of the *Guide for the Perplexed*], regarding the Splendor <note>Original: *Miph'arei*</note>, said that the Voice—the "Created Voice" <term>Created Voice (*Kol Nivra*): The philosophical idea that the sound heard at Sinai was a physical phenomenon created by God for that moment, rather than an attribute of God's essence</term> which Israel heard... the Torah wrote that it was His speech. He was gracious toward him, for the teaching is one of those transmitted by Rashi <note>Rabbi Shlomo Yitzhaki, the premier medieval commentator</note>, may his memory be a blessing, as is clear and explained in his language.

The intention, according to the writing of the Master, was that if there is "speech" ascribed to the Torah, it is His speech; and since the Torah is in our hands, there is no [other] speech for Him. He further said that the intention of those who distance [corporeality] from speech is because they say His actions are not like our actions. We have established that all these "voices" preceded the prophets who attained them. He said that one must know that these matters reach them from their own thought and from there alone. Behold, these are his words and his reasoning regarding the Voice and the Speech which are of the Torah, through which we have been given life and the world. For all of this is from His mouth, may He be blessed, and it is written: "The testimony of the Lord is faithful" [Psalms 19:8].

<column-break/>

As it is said: "Take heed to your souls." Thus we set the words of the Torah to clarify the matters, and we explain them through our own reasoning as well. His words regarding all human intellect and the Voice were his opinion—that which is refined and investigated by human thoughts. However, it was established according to the opinion of the Sages—a primary opinion—that it is His testimony, may He be blessed, for He is the Supreme One over His unity and His existence. One cannot change this reasoning, for it is like the acceptance of testimony; just as testimony must be established in its simplicity as we heard it. We must not interpret it other than how the Witness intended it. If we do not accept the intention, we have seen no testimony. In this manner, it must be interpreted in connection with the "Supreme Wisdom" <note>Original: *Chokhmah Elyonah*, the second of the ten sefirot</note>. For she [the Torah] was with Him in Wisdom. As it is said: "With the crown of the Supernal One." The Torah and the Name are bound together in His mind. I have not succeeded [in explaining this] except in a simple and lengthy way, bringing proof for all of them.

He had already repeated this potentially damaging opinion three times in Chapter 33.

The words of the Master were meant to hint at the "Palm" and the "Speech" of the clouds and the darkness. This is the Voice that was created for them, which brought Israel to the level of the "Supreme Vision." This is the tradition between us and them: between the Voice and the Speech. They heard the Voice alone, as is the Master's view. There is nothing "created" in the level of the Prophet or the Glory—not to such an extent that it would displace them at the "Standing of the Voice," the level of receiving the Torah.

Regarding this, Moses, peace be upon him, had to bless [God] after the Voice... for those who are perplexed in their souls. He is blessed according to the reception of our Sages, may their memory be a blessing. When He came to give the Ten Commandments, Moses was standing to the side. According to the way I have explained, this is the Master's proof, yet they still struggle with their questions about everything. Even in this life, this is what will be refined—that which was "created."

It is impossible to establish the words of the commentators according to their [limited] knowledge, for it is better [to look] to the prophets in their vision, as explained in the opinion of the Master Guide, may his memory be a blessing. And behold the truth: there is no existence except for the Voice and the Speech... the Master said that the Created Voice is what makes the holy Commandments heard. It was seen and it was also there... many deep things which he arranged and wrote from the "Fifth Section" <note>Possibly a reference to a specific division of the manuscript or a philosophical work</note>. It was in the merit of the Torah received in the "Fifth," after it was clarified at the head with light. Let us stand upon the truth of the Torah in the way I have explained: that the revelation was that specific Voice, seen and heard by the one standing within the Voice.

Regarding that which we shall discuss further concerning the portion of the place <note>Original: *Maqom*. In Jewish philosophy, "The Place" is a name for God because the world exists within Him, rather than Him being contained by the world</note> that was designated, all this is intended to instruct human beings. His will is understood through the phrase "the whole earth is full of His glory," yet His specific will is understood as being between the two Cherubim <note>The angelic figures atop the Ark of the Covenant</note>. Furthermore, in the Midrash Tanchuma <note>A collection of homiletic teachings on the Torah</note> on the portion of *Ki Tisa*, it describes the moment God said to Moses: "Let them make Me a sanctuary, that I may dwell among them" [Exodus 25:8]. Moses replied: "Master of the Universe, behold, the heavens and the heaven of heavens cannot contain You!" God said to him: "It is not as you think. Rather, twenty boards on the north, twenty on the south, and eight on the west..."

God surrounds the world, and the calculation of their mouths <note>Referring to the dimensions spoken of in the text</note> is literal; it is not due to a lack of kindness, Heaven forbid. This matter depends upon our will, and this demonstrates His ability, which is without end or purpose <note>i.e., God's power is not limited by human logic of "cause and effect"</note>. I have already explained previously that even though it is written: "Do I not fill the heavens and the earth?" [Jeremiah 23:24], this can be understood even by one with little understanding. It is without any deficiency. God told him: "Cleanse for Me from afar a great thing." He said: "He desired his own, and eventually gave him permission to say: Cleanse for me from afar small things." He granted him the freedom of "small things" <note>This refers to the "contraction" of the Divine Presence into a small, physical space for the sake of human perception</note>. He said to him: "Does the King desire His glory here?"—meaning in this small space. He said: "What do you have to give, you who are flesh and blood?" rather, from what he spoke with his mouth, in whatever you desire of the material. And in the end, how much more so was it with Samuel? Heaven forbid! "The heavens and the earth I fill," yet in the "prayer of the spirit" He was speaking with Moses. Understand that this is the final word.

The conclusion of the matter is that because the Tabernacle was restricted to the altar, it seems to be a place of distress or confinement. Against this, one might say: how can He who is the end of all things grant us His mercy and His excellence, and how can He write of Himself a "place" that is also limited? But in the place where He is "light," it is because He is the "Place of the World," and the world is not His place. Because it was difficult to understand how the Scripture calls it a "place," this became a difficult matter. Every parable is His own. 

God said: "Choose My Torah." Through the providence of His power, the necessary lack will be seen. He spoke of this "lack" because it was difficult for him to conceive of it in the context of the "Sovereign of Visions" <note>The prophetic experience</note>. This was publicized because he relied on the parable of the vision to understand the depth. We are like those who build small buildings, but the Creator—it is not by means of spending money that He acts. He commanded him to work according to the pattern <term>Pattern: *Tavnit*. The heavenly blueprint shown to Moses on Mount Sinai</term> and His Torah, so that everything would be seen as a vision. Aside from what was written, he saw and understood everything through the vision. 

Since he lacked a "vision" because everything appeared strange, as long as it was not comforted by the written word, it would be impossible to bring it in. Furthermore, the House <note>The Temple</note> informs them through the parable of visions that in a "small thing," He is found. If you desire it to be "small," let it be like the "great vision." You will find that the Tabernacle and the Temple were for the purpose of housing the *Shekhinah* <note>The Divine Presence</note>. As it is written: "I will dwell in every place." Therefore, these were made according to the human pattern because the Indweller fills the whole portion. Just as He is seen in the "Large Vision," He is seen in the "Small Vision." 

Until a certain point, he informs the person of little understanding that in a small choice, He will be divided. As the parable said in the wilderness with Moses: understand that there is no deficiency with the Infinite. Generally, He showed him mercy through the intended kindness, saying: "What have you to give, being flesh and blood?"—meaning a finite being. And yet, I allow you to act with Me in whatever you desire from the material. The world is like a small window, but I am without limit and without end, acting through My words. The finite nature of the world is to show that He has the power over all, and this is the kindness of the Will itself. It is enough to say: "Do I not fill the heavens and the earth?" and in the "prayer of the spirit" He was speaking with little understanding, without any deficiency. This matter is hanging on His will, and He desires life without...

The entire matter is a "partition" <note>A barrier or interface between the human and divine</note>, and it is a beautiful choice. The explanation of the Prophecies according to the intellect adds literal meaning to the "Great Thing," speaking to all of them. Through this, he achieved the "Great Literal Meaning." There they achieved the literal meaning, as it is said: "The Lord spoke to you out of the midst of the fire; you heard the sound of words, but you saw no form; there was only a voice" [Deuteronomy 4:12]. He chose this for them because the "Great Literal Meaning" was revealed to them in a "form," and that part leads to doubt.

And as for what is further in their interpretation: it is a parable for your years, etc. As on the day the Lord spoke to you in Horeb <note>Another name for Mount Sinai</note> from the midst of the fire. Thus, in every place where the "Speech of the Great Fire" is mentioned to you, He chose the "Voice" that was from the midst of the fire to inform them of the place of their attainment. Thus, He informed them there why it was written "And I gave the Sabbath of the Lord" to understand His glory and His greatness, and His voice from the midst of the fire. In its entirety, they said: "You saw the fire," for it was clarified that "the appearance of the glory of the Lord was like a devouring fire on the top of the mount in the eyes of the children of Israel" [Exodus 24:17]. In this "small thing," they bore witness to the Secret of the Unity <note>Original: *Sod HaYichud*. The theological concept of God's absolute oneness and the integration of His various attributes</note>. For God is the ultimate cause, rising to the level of Prophecies, and receiving the verse from the Torah. And as I have written: "To you it was shown, that you might know that the Lord is God; there is none else beside Him" [Deuteronomy 4:35].

The general rule of this is nearby, where it says: "Out of heaven He made you hear His voice, that He might instruct you; and upon earth He showed you His great fire; and you heard His words out of the midst of the fire" [Deuteronomy 4:36]. Just as the sea enters the inlet, so the Unity of the Glory is within the Tabernacle and the Temple, yet He Himself fills...
