Let us return to the higher matters discussed previously, concerning the tradition of our Sages of blessed memory <note>Original: *kdshb"a* – likely an abbreviation for "Our Sages of blessed memory"</note>. It is said that the heart, through the power of the Divine Name, connects with the four masculine forces <note>Referring to kabbalistic emanations or "faces" of the divine</note>. The Sages remarked that the Tablets were formed through the divine Will.

I do not know who brought them to this state, but it is written in the Psalms: "By the word of the Lord the heavens were made" [Psalm 33:6]. Amos also spoke of God’s might. The Master <note>Likely referring to Maimonides or another significant philosopher</note> teaches that our God’s intent regarding the holiness of the Tablets was that they should be a "vessel." On them were written the Ten Commandments. The form of the Tablets was taken from the Heavens, for as it is mentioned, the Tablets were known to be the "Word of the Lord" <note>Original: *Memra d'Yeya* – A frequent Aramaic Targum term for the creative Word of God</note>, the throne of the stars, and all the glory. This was written for those who truly know, and it is inscribed upon the divine.

The matter of the Tablets is a heavenly one, involving the "children of God." This does not merely mean they were physical writing; rather, "the tablets were the work of God" [Exodus 32:16]. Their high status and holiness indicate that these were not works of nature, but a supreme creation that no created intellect can fully grasp. Our Sages of blessed memory taught that the two Tablets of Testimony correspond to Heaven and Earth. They correspond to the two aspects of the Torah—the **Revealed** and the **Hidden**—and they also correspond to **this world** and the **world to come**.

These Tablets teach us of a unique unity, for they mirror the primordial Heaven and Earth. They contain the secret of the "Giver" and the "Bride" <note>Metaphors for God and the Congregation of Israel</note>. The two Tablets were equal; neither was larger than the other. Regarding this, the Midrash says of the Torah: "The world is not greater than it, nor is it greater than the world."

Furthermore, in the Midrash, Rabbi Joshua bar Nehemiah said: "They were the work of God," and they were fashioned in a miraculous way. Rabbi Menachem, in the name of Rabbi Avin, said: "The material was actually taken from the celestial sphere." This corresponds to how the Holy One, Blessed be He, created the Heaven and the Earth. Because the Tablets corresponded to Heaven and Earth, the Giver and the Bride, they were two equal parts—a crown upon a crown. This "work of God" contains the secret of the primordial substance. The writing itself—the "Script of God"—is derived from **Wisdom** (*Chokhmah*) <term>Chokhmah: The first flash of divine inspiration or the "seed" of an idea</term>. From there, the Torah emerges, as it is written that the Torah was hidden and preceded the world, engraved in "white fire upon black fire" <note>A traditional description of the Torah's mystical existence before creation</note>. The script on the page of the Tablets was more recognizable, while the internal meaning remained more hidden. This is why the Holy Spirit is described as being like a story or a book on a vast page. The writing was the Wisdom, and the intellectual capacity within it was **Understanding** (*Binah*) <term>Binah: The analytical power that expands the "seed" of Wisdom into a full concept</term>.

Because the Torah was the "Primordial Torah," the Sages said it preceded the world by two thousand years. This reflects the celestial building process. Things were initially very refined and thin, which is why Wisdom is called the "Book of the King." What was once hidden and concealed eventually moved toward the "Revealed," much like the tongue brings out what is hidden in the mind into spoken action. This is the secret of the Ten Commandments, which are refined and precious words from above. The Tablets were doubled to represent the secret of the refined spiritual realms. They were brought into action through another "tongue," as it were, which is why there were two Tablets, corresponding to the Giver and the Bride, the secret of Israel. They were established as the "lower tablets." This is the secret of the divine work—"and the tablets were the work of God."

<column-break/>

This is a deep and hidden matter, following the opinion of the Holy Zohar <note>The foundational text of Jewish mysticism</note>. When the Sages spoke of the mountain being "hollowed out," it was a visual metaphor. They spoke of the secret of the "hidden pearl" from which the yearning radiance is drawn. From there, it takes shape and becomes more distinct, expanding into the "Crown." It was then refined and included in the generation that received it, which took from it two "good pearls"—the two Tablets.

There is a secret in the "engraving" (*charut*) and the purity within it. They were written and hollowed out like pearls in a crown. Depending on the place where they were engraved, they were seen as red or musical in nature <note>Likely referring to the "colors" or "tones" of the different divine attributes</note>, taking on the likeness of their source. This is the secret of the "Sapphire" appearance. The phrase "the tablets were the work of God" is repeated to emphasize the place from which they were hewn. It is written "he ascended," similar to how it says "Israel ascended from the furnace." The Torah was written and revealed through what we see in the script and the earth.

Therefore, our Sages of blessed memory taught that the Tablets could be read from "both faces," meaning they were like the Heaven and Earth mentioned earlier. They were the "spirit of Israel." It says they were "written on both their sides; on the one side and on the other were they written" [Exodus 32:15]. This means the writing was visible from both sides. This was a miraculous work, for even though the letters were engraved all the way through, the "faces" of the letters remained in place. They said the writing passed from one side to the other <note>Original: *luf* – meaning "through and through"</note>. The engraving was a wonder.

Midrashic sources ask: how did the centers of the letters stay suspended? <note>Referring to the letters *Mem* and *Samekh*, which are closed circles; if carved through a stone, the middle should fall out</note>. This was a miracle. The meaning of "from one side to the other" is that the Torah is fully explained and included within itself. Every part of the engraving was distinct and unique, yet it was all "written by the finger of God." This was not a natural engraving, but a divine one.

This teaches us that every part of the Tablets testifies to the Name of the Creator. Truly, "they are the work of God and the writing is the writing of God." This reflects the way we have explained: the letters were a divine act, attributed to God Himself. They were not "written" in the human sense, for they are above the laws of nature. Nature has no authority over them, for they are from a realm far above it.

The Sages also taught: "Do not read *Charut* (engraved), but *Cherut* (freedom)" [Pirkei Avot 6:2]. This is based on the celestial calculation. The place where they were engraved is the source of all "writing." These "engravings" are etched upon the natural orders, for nature is subordinate to those who fulfill the Torah. As it is said: "You have no free person except for one who occupies himself with the study of Torah." This is also found in the Midrash of Rabbi Shimon bar Yochai <note>Traditional author of the Zohar</note> and all the early masters. They explained that "freedom" (*cherut*) on the Tablets refers to freedom from death and the various "accidents" of the world, as we have written.

The secret of the writing is that it was "soft" and "hard" simultaneously, acting in the way we have explained to show us the wonders of the **Secrets of Unity** (*Sitrei HaYichud*). Every one of the spiritual emanations is included in the Great Name, and each is contained within the other. This is the secret of the matter: each one is woven into the next, and each has many sides and facets.

# CHAPTER 33 | THE PORTION OF SECRETS OF THE TORAH | CHAPTER 33 | 136

For the one who speaks on their behalf <note>referring to Moses speaking for the people</note> and they are for his own words above. And to further instruct on this, it says after the Ten Commandments: **"These words the Lord spoke to all your assembly"** [Deuteronomy 5:19]. And even though it is written: **"And it was when you heard the voice out of the midst of the darkness"** [Deuteronomy 5:20], it had already said afterward: **"This day we have seen that God speaks [with man]"** [Deuteronomy 5:21].

And likewise, what it said: **"Let us not hear the voice of the Lord our God anymore,"** and it is said afterward as a confirmation of this: **"For who is there of all flesh who has heard the voice of the living God speaking out of the midst of the fire?"** [Deuteronomy 5:23]. And regarding **"Moses would speak and God would answer him with a voice"** [Exodus 19:19], it was already written: Not to the voice of your word was it written "and he spoke words," and behold it is written: "from there he will speak these things." But regarding what they said concerning the verse, "and they said to him: 'You speak with us and we will hear,'" it says, "And God answered him with a voice" [Exodus 19:19]—this means so that they would not mistake his greatness for his hearing Moses in his own likeness. Until this point, they have explained that the intention of what is written "Moses would speak" does not refer to the Ten Commandments themselves.

And what comes in the story of the Commandments—the story of the Day of Atonement <note>original: *Yom Kippur*</note>—is to mention that every single one of them was made for the sake of the complaints, for with every one he would speak, and for every word it would say that they should not stray, for it said: **"it is very near to you"** [Deuteronomy 30:14]. And the singular nature <note>Addressing the people in the singular "Thou" vs. plural "You"</note> will be explained with them. This is the opinion of the **Nachmanides** <note>Rabbi Moses ben Nachman, 13th-century commentator and kabbalist</note>, may his memory be a blessing. And in his midrash <note>interpretive homily</note> on the verse, regarding his saying that the Commandments are in the singular language before you: at the Standing at Mount Sinai, all of Israel were like one heart and one will to enter under the wings of the Presence <note>The *Shekhinah*</note>.

And this is what was said regarding the meaning of this closeness: "from the mouth of the Power" <note>term: *mipi ha-gevurah* — a rabbinic idiom meaning directly from God's own mouth</note>. The proof is like a spring and a doubt in my words; for there is no doubt that Moses truly brought to Israel these two "Burnings" <note>likely referring to the first two commandments</note> which are the sources of these, and that is what is meant by the "intellectual proofs" which he said—that they did not become wise through proofs from themselves, for behold, the way of the Lord is to establish for him the "Burnings" <note>the first two commandments</note>. But their greatness lies in the intellectual proofs of their existence as wise men. And as it is explained in the words of the **Rav** <note>Referring to Maimonides, the "Great Eagle" of Jewish philosophy</note> in the *Guide for the Perplexed*, this is their number. And how much more so for the rest of the nation who were not wise, who would need to be taught the proofs so that their faith would be established. For these two Commandments <note>"I am the Lord" and "You shall have no other gods"</note> were found as if they were from the mouth of Moses, peace be upon him. The complaint there is regarding these two Commandments just as it was for all the other commandments, all of them being the 613 Commandments <note>term: *Taryag Mitzvot* — the total count of biblical laws</note>. For all the 613 Commandments were given to us by Moses. If so, it is written: **"Moses commanded us the Torah"** [Deuteronomy 33:4], and the Torah is from him <note>meaning through his agency</note>. And what was our profit? We would need the eyes of a wise man! And if it were not "from the mouth of the Almighty" <note>original: *mipi ha-gevurah*</note> that prevents it, then it would seem that Moses had no hand in them, nor any comprehension, and Israel would be in the proof. And we do not say to Israel that they all became wise by themselves through intellectual proofs by which they would delve into their faith, as I have written. This is for us the great proof of his <note>Moses's</note> peace. And for the awakening of the **Rav** <note>Maimonides</note>, he did not need to receive the proofs and the signs which are from the mouth of the Master of the Universe, blessed be He, to establish His existence; rather, they are from their essence. And as he wrote in the chapter [of the *Guide*] that the nation that rose to the level of prophecy did not know it first from his words there. And for this he said, "and they said to him": they heard the word of God. And before this, the Rav <note>Maimonides</note> has to acknowledge the opinion that these matters of Moses were for us like a proof for the complaints; and behold, the 613 we heard from his mouth. And how will the Rav fulfill what he wrote before this, "and the Torah was from him"? And let not the words of their desire be light! For he already said that even regarding these two words, Israel did not understand them unless he <note>God</note> combined the letters... for he made our hearts simple as it is written in his proof. And our Sages <note>original: *Zal*</note> said that he was hidden. And as is clarified in the *Book of the Torah* which we have, it was given at the end of the days and prohibited from stumbling.

And the philosophers, his students who come after him, established it and accepted it upon themselves, and they added interpretation and "weakness of hands" <note>idiom: loss of resolve or dilution of faith</note> from the Torah. For the account of the Voice which Moses put before the philosophers, his students, was to awaken and to show them the matter of the substance and the faith, to mention and to understand and to complete their days, to strive to seek the cancellations from the way of the *Book of Creation* <note>term: *Sefer Yetzirah* — an ancient, foundational mystical text</note> which was with Moses upon his ascent to the ranks of the Children of Israel. And our Sages <note>original: *Razal*</note> did not explain the statement "it is wise," and let it not be from you

from the "mouth of the Power" <note>the Almighty</note> that prevents it, until he wrote that language: "And I will surely explain to you the tradition of our Sages." Certainly, all the Ten Commandments were heard by all of Israel from the mouth of the Almighty in its literal sense. As it is written: **"Face to face"** [Deuteronomy 5:4]. Regarding the first two commandments, they were hearing the speech and understanding it from Him just as one understands it from Moses. And even so, He would speak with them just as a master speaks to his servant at the time I mentioned. And from here onward, regarding the rest of the commandments, they heard the sound of the speech but did not understand it, and Moses would need to translate for them every single utterance according to his teaching them. And Moses thus opened the heads <note>the beginning of the words</note>: "Moses would speak and [God] would answer him with a voice" [Exodus 19:19], and then they were the words of truth with Moses.

That he <note>Moses</note> would say to them, "I am the Lord your God," and they would say to him <note>in agreement</note>. And the **Rav** <note>Maimonides</note> wanted in his holiness to be a righteous person and say that they did not intend to attribute to the two first commandments any special status to increase themselves, for they did not understand the proof of this matter, but only the later ones. And if so, regarding their essence, these being the foundation of the Torah—also **"Remember"** and **"Observe"** [the Sabbath] which he cast upon the Master of the Universe—He is the pillar of the whole world.

And they saw the God of Israel <note>original: *Elohim*</note>, for they did not understand it in the first two. And if the Rav <note>Maimonides</note> says that the sensory and the intellectual are the two divisions of the world, when he makes them as a covenant of his testimony upon the Master of the Universe, they will not be suspect in it except in the appearance. Even so, when the first utterance, in the opinion of the Rav, is a proof for the eyes to believe that **"there is a Lord,"** as he wrote there: **"I am the Lord"**—and he saw and added to their knowledge so they would believe that the Lord is the foundation. And also the second, which is the unification [of God], they would err in the intellectual matter, and they would not be suspect in them in their natural state. And regarding this, the Rav said that they perceived them through prophecy because they are the foundation of the Torah and the commandments. Even so, every word Moses said—**"Remember"** and **"Observe"**—which he says about the Master of the Universe, they would ponder in his contemplation. And He is the pillar of the whole world who looked into it to establish that they should properly perceive it through prophecy.

And how does the Rav teach that Israel heard all the commandments from the mouth of God? He said that in the "hidden treasure" of the later ones they did not intend to complain, etc., because they heard the sound of the voice. But he says all the commandments were heard from the mouth of God, and this is not the literal meaning of the verse. For if they understood all Ten Commandments, just as it was explained, and they [only] heard the voice in the other commandments—regarding these, it was explained: he said, "they shall believe the Torah." And this is a thing that is not necessary. And if there is yet more power, for the one who questions will say: "Who told us that it was so?" And if they were in the body of the Torah, then the benefit to Israel would be that they might err and doubt in the God of the word. And the "Burnings" <note>the first two commandments</note> and the principles would be hidden. But the entire Torah and the holy writings in this matter all clarify according to the opinion of the Rav, may his memory be a blessing, and according to the matter I wrote above.

And perhaps now, because of the depth of the power in these commandments, which are long words, he speaks on his own behalf, while the later ones are like one speaking. We said that there is the way of the Torah which is revealed from the hidden, as is written elsewhere. And the author of the **Akeidah** <note>Rabbi Isaac Arama (15th century), author of *Akeidat Yitzchak*</note> said that all the commandments were understood by Israel from His mouth, blessed be He, entirely according to the literal meaning of the verses. And this was clarified a little in the language to show the virtue of the first two, as they are the foundation for all the rest. And therefore the language comes as one speaking on his own behalf <note>God saying "I am..."</note>. And when the language comes in the third person, he is not speaking with the listener <note>God being referred to as "The Lord your God" in the third person</note>. They heard and understood from His mouth, blessed be He, without any intermediary. And he said that even they <note>the Sages</note> intended in their saying "from the mouth of the Almighty" <note>original: *mipi ha-gevurah*</note> to mean without an intermediary, even from the powers of that time, elevating them above all the other commandments. Even though they heard from the mouth of the Speech <note>the Divine Word</note>, here they heard from the Power that speaks its own words—this is the summary of his opinion. And with this, it is more correct than all the other opinions recorded here, which suggest that all the commandments were understood from the mouth of the Holy One, blessed be He. They do not agree at all on the intermediary that was between them. And also the language of the statement and its matter should not be confusing at all, for the verse says, **"Face to face the Lord spoke with you"** [Deuteronomy 5:4], testifying that all the commandments were in one vision and one perception, all of them without any intermediary. And also what is written, **"These words the Lord spoke to all your assembly,"** etc. [Deuteronomy 5:19], proves that "I am" and "You shall not have" were not intended to distinguish between the commandments. And that which is written, **"And God spoke all these words, saying..."** [Exodus 20:1].

<summary>This page explores a classic debate in Jewish theology: whether the Israelites heard all Ten Commandments directly from God or only the first two. The author contrasts the rationalist view of Maimonides (the Rav), who suggests only the first two were intellectually perceived, with the more literalist/mystical views of Nachmanides and Isaac Arama (the Akeidah), who argue for a direct national experience of the Divine Voice for all ten.</summary>

<meta>This page continues the philosophical and mystical exploration of the Revelation at Mount Sinai, specifically debating the sensory experience of the Israelites—whether they heard articulated words or a divine sound—and the roles of the Written and Oral Torah in that moment.</meta>

## PART TWO

Indeed, it is therefore part of our tradition to say that that Voice was extraordinary and surpassed the natural limits of any one of them, in order to demonstrate the Divine Unity <note>Hebrew: *ha-yichud*; the concept of God's absolute oneness</note>. For the Source springs and flows likewise into the "upper vessels": Wisdom, Glory, the Ten Utterances <note>The ten commands through which the world was created</note>, the secret of the Ten Sefirot <note>The ten divine emanations in Kabbalah</note>, and the twenty-four letters, Kindness, the Bridegroom and the Bride <note>A common kabbalistic metaphor for the relationship between the masculine and feminine aspects of the Divine, or God and the Assembly of Israel</note>. It is the crown of the Commandments in the "Cutting Constellation" <note>likely referring to the power of the letters to shape reality</note>, following the secret of the movement of the missing elements that are integrated in the "Upper Site." This is the secret of the trembling, the melting, and the mercy, corresponding to Wisdom—the secret of the "window." 

And "Wisdom, where shall it be found?" <note>quoting Job 28:12</note>. Kindness is included in the Torah, which is written in blue <note>Hebrew: *tekhelet*; the sacred blue dye</note>, and within that blue are all the letters. They are guarded and protected, divided, passing through, and completed. They are formed in the final line among them, and there they stay in two statures: the Written Torah and the Oral Torah. These were missing from the place of the Indwelling Presence <note>Hebrew: *Shekhinah*</note> because of the lower tablets <note>the second set of tablets given to Moses</note> among the children and the outer elements. To indicate them, they came "in their door and in their likeness," as a totality of the forty-two letters <note>a mystical Name of God</note>, wanting for the strength of all the Ten Commandments that are within them, among the children and the followers. They are rescued and pass from one strength to another, and this is modeled after the upper realms. And it is called the "Tablets of the Commandments," which were ten in that place to which they were sent, because the Voice itself was within them. For this reason, in the reading of the Torah, it is called "the Testimony of the Lord" <note>Psalm 19:8</note>, as it is a testimony 

<margin>P</margin>

to the Great Name and indicates the Divine Unity. For this reason, it was in our practice and like a cantor <note>Hebrew: *chazzan*</note> to be included in this book, and its voice is our guide to prove this matter to us, etc., according to the portion written in this chapter.

# CHAPTER 33

Regarding the standing at that Voice: it was not merely a voice that moved below until it reached Israel. It was not a voice of dispute, for the mountain was "burning with fire" <note>Deuteronomy 4:11</note> and it "pressed" because it burned below on its own. And the sound of the Voice alone for Israel did not attain Glory at all, for the Voice was a sound that reached them encompassing all the letters. And he <note>Moses</note>, peace be upon him, made Israel hear what he heard. And it says that this is what is meant by the verse: "I stood between the Lord and you" [Deuteronomy 5:5]. And it also says: "Moses spoke, and God answered him with a voice" [Exodus 19:19], and it is written: "so that the people may hear when I speak with you" [Exodus 19:9]. And he said that this shows the speech was for him <note>Moses</note>, and they would hear the Voice, which is peace. It says: "when you heard the voice" [Deuteronomy 5:20] and it says: "you heard the sound of words" [Deuteronomy 4:12]. And everything that implies hearing "words," he said, means they heard the Voice, while Moses was the one who would hear the words and recount them to them. 

And truly, in his opinion, there is a secret proof from the Torah and from the words of the Sages, of blessed memory. Regarding the "proper standing" before Him, the Sages said: "'I am [the Lord]' and 'You shall have no [other gods]' we heard from the Mouth of Power <note>Hebrew: *Gevurah*; a title for God used when describing direct communication</note>." It appeared from this fulfillment that we saw one level gained for Israel just as Moses understood it, and the voice did not reach them through them <note>the Sages</note>. However, from the straight path—which is the meaning of the words in their plain sense and as many agree—it is said that the intention was "from the Mouth of Power" hidden in the mystery. For these ways—meaning the metaphors of the Voice and it being said to Moses "He answered him," like a vision—all that is known by logical proof should be chosen. Whoever knows it well has no advantage, and all who know these ways of the grandeur of prophecy for all, say the Torah gave a vision to know, and so on. These are his words, and this is the summary of his opinion: that the Voice was difficult on the day of the assembly, and it was the mover for Israel; it was a voice for all but did not include articulated letters. And he <note>Moses</note>, peace be upon him, reached the level where the speech was composed of letters, and this he made Israel hear. And he said that in the counting of the Ten Commandments, they were not counted individually. 

But one may question him, for these words of his contradict the verses of the Torah and the established foundations. We must say that He desired to make them hear the wondrous Speech so that they would be established in their faith forever, as has been explained. By hearing a mere sound alone, what would be given to them and what would be added? For one could say, "Who says it was so?" and they would still be in doubt regarding all the matters mentioned in the prophecies of Moses and his prophetic status. What is more exalted than hearing from the Source itself, which removes all possible interruptions and doubts in all those matters? And He, blessed be He, created for them the "tools" <note>senses/perception</note>, as I have written. And from the hearing 

<column-break/>

## THE LIGHT OF THE TORAH

of the voice alone, they would still be rushing after him, and it would be light in your eyes to establish the faith and the preparation and the writing of the Torah that come in this matter. 

The Rabbi's <note>likely referring to Maimonides</note> intention and the wonder of his opinion: if they said, "Behold, I come to you in a thick cloud, so that the people may hear when I speak with you," the language of "hearing" is understood according to its literal sense, meaning the comprehension of the speech. His will was to make them hear our goodness—that which He would speak with him. The intention in this is all the prophecies and visions that he mentioned before the Ten Commandments, for the words were not with them alone, as it will be explained. And there is another reason for "when I speak with you": for His will was to speak with him, and they would hear and understand, so that they would believe in the truth of Moses's prophecy, and by this, doubt would be removed from them. Previously, they were doubtful of his prophecy, but when they reached the point of understanding Him speaking with him, they knew he was truly a prophet. Therefore, the verse supports this: "and they will also believe in you forever" [Exodus 19:9]. 

And in truth, the assembly <note>of Sages</note>, of blessed memory, said: [He gathered] the people and made them hear His words. From here we see that all those days, the meaning of the words was literal—not just a sound, but the inclusion of learning to fear Him by hearing His words. For by hearing the words, they would be strengthened and acquire a heart to fulfill them, and they would be strong and unchanging in them. For the "seal" is that they heard it from His mouth and in His writing. All this is said regarding the hearing of the voice alone. 

And furthermore, the confirmation and seal are found in the verse: "Has a people ever heard the voice of God speaking out of the midst of the fire, as you have heard, and lived?" [Deuteronomy 4:33]. This is a difficult point, for there was a choice made for them as well; "as you have heard" implies further understanding of the matter without any doubt at all. And the cause of the verses will guide us in all this matter. For he said: "Then you said, 'Behold, the Lord our God has shown us [His glory]'" [Deuteronomy 5:21]. For this matter is like a striking blow, the blessing upon him. And truly, the prophets and the dispute are served in the Chariot <note>Hebrew: *Merkabah*; the divine realm</note> against the movers of the world. Behold, the ancient one in name and spirit—no doubt is counted in his name. For he almost approached and clung to the fire. And behold, before the matter and the truth in the vision as is proper for him, which is of those proofs that destroy all doubt in the Name of the Lord. 

"To all that He did for you," etc., "before your eyes" [Deuteronomy 29:1]—meaning we saw it for you not just as a proof, but truly as what you saw. And it stays in the heart, all the things that were at that standing; they understood them in their truth. And I will return: they believed the words, and removed from themselves all prohibition and drawn-out doubt. And he explained the matter in the way proper to its truth and its establishment: it was the "bridging" of the words and the intention, and its opening without any doubt or secret at all. And this matter was also attained through actual sight, and certainly through hearing. And this is exactly what I wrote on "And all the people saw the voices" [Exodus 20:15]—truly as explained, they saw those truths. 

To further indicate this, it says: "Face to face the Lord spoke with you on the mountain" [Deuteronomy 5:4]. This explicitly says that the speech was for them as well, and He did not just leave a voice. For this reason, it says "face to face" to show that they attained both things and their truths. And if it were a voice alone reaching them, this would not be "face to face," but only faith. And to the point where they said: "I stood between the Lord and you at that time to tell you the word of the Lord" [Deuteronomy 5:5]—he did not say this regarding the Commandments, but regarding the laws following the giving of the Torah. Do not be confused by the words of the Rabbi, Rabbi Abraham ibn Ezra <note>A famous 12th-century Spanish commentator</note>. It was already explained: "I stood between the Lord," etc., for he stood at Mount Sinai, and also "He spoke with you on the day of the assembly face to face." And "face to face" would be according to "standing between the Lord and you." And this is the reason for the response: "when you heard the voice," etc., "and now why should we die," etc., "lest the Lord our God [speak to us] anymore," etc., "you go near and hear," etc. [Deuteronomy 5:20-24]. 

And it seems Rabbi Abraham said regarding this: Moses said to them that they said to my heart, "Behold, [God has shown us His glory]," and they were with you on every matter in the way that a mediator <note>Hebrew: *sarsur*; a broker</note> does between a seller and a buyer—the buyer speaks with you on everything. And if it were according to the one who says it was just a sound to you and Moses made them hear with his words, your heart would still be lacking its desire, and there is more.

# CHAPTER 34: PART OF THE SECRETS OF THE TORAH ### CHAPTER 34 [PAGE] 136

In nullifying and removing from my people that which they perceived, it was understood that this was due to the person who restrains himself from nullifying his own power from the beginning, because of the tradition and the law of benefit. One is occupied with believing in the powers of God's will. Therefore, "the fool shall behold it forever" <note>original: *kesel yachazenu le-olam*; a play on biblical phrasing suggesting that those who rely on "folly" or "false confidence" see only a dim reflection</note>, according to the power of the Scripture to uphold all this. His strength is lacking; "acquire wisdom" <note>quoting Proverbs 4:7</note>. This power is divided like a thick cloud, "so that the people may hear when I speak with you, and also believe in you forever" <note>quoting Exodus 19:9</note>. 

This is according to what has already been explained. It is therefore a selection of individual names and secrets, just as the miracle of the Voice was learned from oral tradition. The "Voice" was the lesson received by the wise ones through the affliction of understanding between the letters *Vav* and *Yod* <note>The letters of the Divine Name</note> at the time of the Voice, to comfort the mouth and to speak the *Vav*. It is written that His decree at the end of the *Vav* during the Voice was to teach the wise the "statutes and judgments" <note>Hebrew: *chukim u-mishpatim*</note>, referring to the details of the Commandments and their secrets. 

It has been explained, and we shall further explain the proper reason why these specific utterances were chosen: because they include the entirety of the Torah and all the Commandments. They are the charges and secrets belonging to them. Therefore, the Ten Commandments <note>Hebrew: *Eseret Ha-Dibrot*</note> were the "progenitors," and their wisdoms stem from the secret of the Ten Sefirot <note>The ten divine emanations in Kabbalah</note>, which is why His voice was given to us. Thus, all matters and topics are derived from them. Their relationship is like that of a thinker to his thoughts; they are the source and the foundations for everything. Therefore, the Ten Commandments were, in their form, the specific and precious roots for all types of divine will and wisdom. 

The secret of this "birth" of concepts is that the root contains within it all the branches and connects them to all the foundations. Thus they were built. In the time of the Torah, there are 613 commandments <note>Hebrew: *taryag mitzvot*</note> like a crown, and in the time of the vision of the Ten Commandments, they were missing nothing. The supreme foundation was found to include the 613 commandments, acting as the keys and the "progenitors" generated from the Ten Commandments. They were stamped and engraved according to the Seven Days of Creation. For this reason, the Commandments were concluded with the Name to sanctify the secrets of their praise. 

One part is the "Good Part for Israel" <note>a reference to the Torah</note>, and it is written to include all the other Commandments. Its foundation and essence are hidden within the secret of "Accepting the Kingdom of Heaven" <note>Hebrew: *Kabbalat Ol Malchut Shamayim*; the declaration of God's sovereignty</note>. This is the principle of all the foundations from which all parts of the Torah and the Commandments are derived. For the wise, this descends into their secrets and their practices in deep depths, according to the King's decree. He is the Great King in the Torah, and the "Instructor" <note>Hebrew: *Moreh*</note> indicates the source of all foundations. He alone is the Ancient One, our God, who strengthens the foundation through the resurrection of the higher, lower, and middle levels recorded in the Torah of Witness.

Investigation shows that the "Instructor" indicates comprehension and intelligence. From this root comes the part in the Torah called "Gratitude" <note>Hebrew: *chanut*</note>, which is the bread and salt of the earth, the offspring of the secret of Infinite Power. From it also comes the part called "Judgments" <note>Hebrew: *mishpatim*</note>. These are the noble speech; it is the gate and the foundation for all the Commandments. It is the sign that includes the entire Torah. 

Even though every part of these foundations was a reception of grace and laws, and some of them were perceived through "the sight of the bride" <note>a mystical metaphor for revelation</note>, with all this, the Holy One hinted that His essence is entirely light, and they are assisted by His glory. This begins with the law of "I Am" <note>Hebrew: *Anochi*; the first word of the Ten Commandments</note>, which is the deepest and greatest of all structures upon which everything stands. 

The second Utterance, which is "You shall have no [other gods]" <note>Exodus 20:3</note>, speaks of the "revelation of the face," which is the power of Unity. Its measure "before Me" <note>Hebrew: *al panai*</note> indicates every part of the foundations: eternity, precedence, nature, and power, for He is One. These are, so to speak, internal to Him and not separate from Him. His roots prove that these matters are distinct from anything else; they are not found in any other power or created thing at all. All others are "other gods" <note>Hebrew: *elohim acherim*</note> and are not from Him. They are dependent upon Him and have no existence or life except from Him. 

Therefore, these second things were hinted to the body of Israel as they were heard from the "Mouth of Might" <note>Hebrew: *Mi-Pi Ha-Gevurah*; a Rabbinic term for God's direct speech</note>, as they are the foundation of faith. They did not need a human intermediary to explain them. Even though they heard all the Commandments from the Mouth of Might, as is the simple meaning of the text, what was explained by the mouth of Moses (as will be clarified above) was only for those who reached the level of "the First Face." They reached this in their totality, just as it reached Moses. This is our wonder regarding the "Two from the Mouth of Might." In their portion...

<column-break/>

...to the intellect. "He shall not have," because of the "Might" we heard. This is not a language of lack—far be it from us to say they did not hear! For the verse says, "on that day," because they heard all the Commandments from the Mouth of Might. However, the intention is that the "Essence of the Torah" <note>Hebrew: *Guf Torah*</note>—the commandments included in the image of the words—was perceived by them as a whole. 

But the explanation and details were said to them by the "Body" <note>referring to Moses</note>. For all the commandments were included in the totality, and it was as if they were influenced together, as I have written. But the interpretation and detail were said to be "heard from the mouth of Moses." This applies to all the Commandments, and this is why the "First Ones" <note>The first two commandments</note> did not need any explanation from Moses, as will be clarified. 

Regarding all the other Commandments, they received them, but did not hear their specificities and the fine details of the Torah as I have written just now. Likewise, they were distant from the intention of their "measurements"—meaning the "fruits" of every single utterance—as well as the future grammatical minutiae that would be derived from the generalities and particulars. Not only this, but even their phrasing, their poetic meters, their "reasons" <note>Hebrew: *ta'amim*; also referring to cantillation marks</note>, and their plain meanings. As it is said in the parable: "to the fourth generation" <note>Exodus 20:5</note>, and so on for every single word. All those reasons, those hidden treasures, those crowns and decorations—all were included in the secret of "No" <note>Hebrew: *Lo*; perhaps referring to the negative commandments or the hidden nature of God</note>. 

I have already written about the letter *Vav*. Furthermore, Rabbi Elazar said: "And all the people saw the voices" <note>Exodus 20:15</note>. They saw what was to be seen. If they were mere sounds, they would not be "seen." But these were lights that were seen. It is not written that they saw "the Lord," but rather they "saw the voices." Just as one cannot look at the sun or the earth, you cannot look at the "Voice." 

They did not look at the Lord, but they looked at the "Voice," as it is written: "And his speech was from the earth." They were received in her wisdom, in her joy, and in the "Last Crown" <note>Hebrew: *Keter*; referring to the Sefirah of Malchut/Kingdom</note> that judges the world. This is why there is an extra word *et* <note>a Hebrew grammatical marker often interpreted by mystics to include something additional</note> in the verse "et ha-kolot" (the voices). It indicates all the levels of the soul that they attained in perfection. For so it was fitting for them, as they ascended to the level of prophecy during the reception of the Torah. 

The hearing was dominant. They perceived the Torah in its perfection—its learning, its wisdom, and its reasons—because the "Voice" was what they perceived. It was the "Chariot" <note>Hebrew: *Merkavah*; the divine throne/structure</note> of everything, for it was included in everything. To convey the perfection of this perception, they said in the Midrash <note>traditional homiletic teaching</note>: "At the moment Israel heard 'I am the Lord your God,' the study of Torah was fixed in their hearts, and they would learn and never forget." 

But they came to Moses and said: "Behold, the Lord our God has shown us His glory... now therefore why should we die?" <note>quoting Deuteronomy 5:21-22</note>. They requested that the "Essence" <note>God</note> should not speak to them directly. They turned back and became "learners and forgetters" <note>meaning they would now have to struggle to remember what they learned from a human teacher</note>. For a teacher of flesh and blood passes away, and thus his teaching passes away with him. They said to him: "Moses our teacher, reveal to us the time..." 

I have written about the doubts regarding this. The Torah was received in its way, through many years. He said: "This life is for now, but in the future to come," as it is said, "I will put my Torah in their inward parts, and in their heart I will write it" <note>Jeremiah 31:32</note>. 

The intention is that after they ascended to the level of hearing the Speech from the Mouth of Might, the purpose was to complete them with a double perfection, greater than what they had before. For surely they were not completed in all their aspects except through the "Might" in its totality. However, because of their own will, the "Goodness" was hidden from them. By receiving it from a human intermediary <note>Moses</note>, they lost that perfection which was a gift to the "progenitor." 

Look at how the heavens return to their nature. But their goodness and their perfection will be restored in the future, as it stands before our intellect in their Torah, in their hiddenness. The "Intellect of their study" will return when the "Power of the Lesson" is no longer nullified. Then the "Enlightened Knowledge" will return. He who is occupied with the writing of the Torah should be stringent. The Ten Commandments are the essence. He said: "Before the Holy Name," which was in them to revive this intention.

# CHAPTER 33: SECRETS OF THE TORAH
### CHAPTER 34

These words are said and heard as a single utterance <note>original: *dibur echad*; refers to the tradition that God spoke all ten commandments simultaneously</note>. The meaning is to clarify that when it says "We have heard" and "God spoke all these words," it means—as the Sages of blessed memory said regarding "I am the Lord your God" and "You shall have no other"—that the Holy One, blessed be He, spoke the Ten Commandments in a single utterance, then returned and explained each one individually as a separate word. This is the end of their words. Behold, all ten utterances are as one word, without any separation between them. The rule is: the general is the particular, and the particular is the general. The general includes only what is specified, and the particular is only what is in the general. All were given with one intellect and one understanding, with no difference between them. This is why they were received as a single word.

It tells us there are wonders in the Unity, for the Ten Commandments correspond to the Ten Utterances <note>The ten sayings by which the world was created in Genesis</note> which, according to the secret of Emanation <note>original: *sod ha-atzilut*; the Kabbalistic realm of divine light</note>, are as a single word and a single unity. When spoken by a single "mouth," the secret of Emanation acts as one group where the collective is a unity. Perhaps they were explained and measured according to the order of their form, so that each would be distinct on its own, even while all are tied and unified with one another, "facing each other like sisters" <note>Exodus 26:3</note>, bound together until the Ten Commandments hung as a single word. Then He returned and specified them, for these were nested in those, and those were bound to these.

As stated in the Midrash regarding "I am" <note>original: *Anochi*</note>: when the Holy One, blessed be He, [spoke] with the three [groups] of Israel, the world saw. They are like ten utterances for ten kings. To use a parable: they could not speak with one mouth, but He wrote "I am" and included all ten within it. Thus far the parable: ten utterances for ten kings, and these ten kings are in the Unity of God; in their intellect they are all one. He included them in the single Source. Here it says that the ten utterances are for your "crown" <note>likely referring to the Sefirah of Keter</note>, for it stands to teach and reveal the ten kings that belong to them. Behind "I am" and "You shall not have," nothing of the general principle is lost. According to the generation of Joseph's companions, the Israelites did not receive all the words in this manner, but heard the rest of the gathered names from the mouth of Moses. This is the plain meaning of the matter according to its context. The calculation of Gematria <note>the numerical value of Hebrew letters</note> confirms this, as "Torah" equals 611, while the Holy One, blessed be He, spoke the [other two] directly.

<column-break/>

As we heard "from the mouth of the Might" <note>original: *mipi ha-gevurah*; a rabbinic idiom for hearing directly from God</note>, for the general principles are already simple and revealed in the six days [of creation] and throughout the whole Torah, as we have written. We have already hinted at the words of the Sages in *Midrash Hazit* <note>The Midrash on the Song of Songs</note> where they said: "'Let him kiss me with the kisses of his mouth' <note>Song of Songs 1:2</note>—Rabbi Yochanan said: An angel would take the Word from before the Holy One, blessed be He, for each and every commandment, and bring it around to every individual Israelite, warning him and asking him: 'Do you accept upon yourself this commandment? It contains such-and-such laws, such-and-such punishments, such-and-such decrees, and such-and-such rituals. It has minor and major requirements, and such-and-such rewards.' The Israelite would say 'Yes.' Then the angel would ask: 'Do you accept the Divinity of the Holy One, blessed be He?' and he would say 'Yes, yes.' Immediately, the angel would kiss him on his mouth."

But the Rabbis say: The Word itself <note>The Divine Speech personified</note> would go around to each and every individual, warning and asking: "Do you accept me upon yourself? I contain such-and-such commandments, such-and-such laws..." and so on. He would say "Yes," and immediately the word would kiss him on his mouth. This is what is meant by "the things which your eyes saw" <note>Deuteronomy 4:9</note>—these very words. The Word itself spoke with you. Thus far the Midrash. 

Behold, the words of the Sages show that every single commandment reached Israel through these five [aspects]. Whether the Word itself went around or not, it indicates that the Word reached every person, explaining the roots and the details of the commandments, the laws branching from them, and their rewards. Israel was already in a state of order. Whether it reached them through an angel—and perhaps they would agree that this was necessary so the angel could ask if they accept God's Divinity—the intent is that even if the Word arrived via a messenger, the Divinity of the Holy One, blessed be He, was placed within it. 

It is possible to say further that Rabbi Yochanan agrees the commandments did not reach Israel through a secondary medium, according to the plain meaning of the scriptures. The "angel" he mentioned refers to the "Redeeming Angel" <note>Genesis 48:16</note>, for it is written that God's divinity flows from His way; it is an "Angel" that is Divinity itself. This is what makes the commandments heard by Israel, as it says, "And God spoke" <note>Exodus 20:1</note>. The Sages added that the Word itself was visible to them, like a thread of taste, "and all the people saw the voices" <note>Exodus 20:15</note>. 

As has been explained, we maintain that all the commandments are included within the Ten Commandments. All Israel was bound to them. Furthermore, there is a hint that the ten names of each commandment were written on the first Tablets, and the fine details of the Torah were written in small script. As the verse says, they were "rolls" <note>Hebrew: *gelilim*; a play on Song of Songs 5:14</note>. On the two Tablets of the Covenant, written by the "finger of God," there were these "rolls"—just as between large waves there are small ripples, so between every commandment, the portions of the Torah and its fine details were written. So it is stated in the Jerusalem Talmud, Tractate Shekalim, Chapter 6. There is no doubt that they were written this way for all Israel to hear. 

From all this, it is clear that these Commandments include all the laws. They were written so that all Israel would be bound to them, reaching them without a secondary medium. They are included in the whole Torah and the commandments as a collective. This provides a massive benefit for the prophecy of the Torah; the foundations of Israel remain forever in their faith, and it shall never be broken. No one can claim through prophecy that there is another Torah to follow.

peace be upon him. For the Divine Will was to establish the faith of all Israel. All the portions and properties of the Torah are included in these. This is why the Ten Commandments are counted as containing all 613 commandments <note>original: *taryag mitzvot*</note>. They are the general principles from which the details emerge; they are the roots for all 613 laws that spread out from them. Every power of the letters is brought forth there. After the commandments were completed and they achieved them all, hearing them from the mouth of the Might in a single intellect... afterward, they only received the specific gatherings and the explanations of the commandments from the mouth of Moses.

And after He arranged all the celestial and terrestrial arrays <note>original: *ma'arachot*; referring to the hierarchical structure of the spiritual and physical worlds</note>, this service was required without any cessation forever. Conversely, the movement intended for the attributes of the world ought to be continuous. The reason for this is:
-> **"So that you may remember the day you went out from the land of Egypt all the days of your life"** <-

For among all the generations, and for the preservation of all this, we have been comforted by the reception of the laws of His asceticism, by the telling of its reason with our mouths and hinting at it. Already, from all its paths—the cutting of the hair and the fulfillment of its commandments—it is constant, day and night, not as a fleeting thing. And it shall be for a sign upon your hand and a memorial between your eyes, so that the Torah of the Lord shall be in your mouth. For this is the power of strengthening and the support of the hands of the believers. 

By the power of being a servant, and its form written on the palms, and in our understanding to remember that with a strong hand the Lord brought us out, and not through another. Egypt was like water, and the greatness of Egypt was the essence and the containment of all the commandments. Its memory on the portions is good for us to establish a voice and to taste a good reason. At the time of all the plagues, it was known that they testify to the "underneath" of Egypt, as a memorial upon his hands.

And there, they were written with judgment and wrath, and the reason for the Sukkot <note>Tabernacles</note> is sufficient. Behold, yet another [reason]: to shake the hearts and your thoughts to keep the words of the Lord, lest they be forgotten. Concerning this it says, "Has He not established and written these words?" and includes all the sicknesses of the Torah which Moses set before the children of Israel. This was not for another, but for himself, and for the sake of everything being a thing intended for itself. The end of the matter is a necessity for strengthening everything, to repair the Divine Honor <note>original: *Ha-Kavod*; a term for the Shekhinah or Divine Presence</note>.

Following the path I chose in the book *Tola'at Ya'akov* <note>original: *The Worm of Jacob*; a 16th-century Kabbalistic work by Meir ibn Gabbai that explains the mystical meanings of the prayer service</note>, and this book is also with you. If so, they went out for the sake of the wonders of Egypt. And if not, heaven forbid, it is said that "this is the Torah," and its merits are light. This is for us to believe, for your fathers already received the likeness, for the Torah preceded the world. To make known that its perfection was intended. Therefore, in this place, it was gathered into one matter, for it was intended before our eyes. Do not say it was taken from the Lord's hand. Therefore, upon all this, regarding the end of days, there is a lack of perfection for the soul's truth and for the knowledge obtained. For this Torah is broad and deep, and its words are the fruit of heroisms and its secrets are in the sanctuary and the palace.

And he said that the foundation of foundations and the pillar of wisdoms is to know and to establish that "the Lord is God, there is no other besides Him." At least every researcher should know that prior to the completion of the commandments, the secrets of the Lord God were all things hidden and designated in the Simple Thought. All the powers, the accompaniments, and the choices were souls and spirits of light, species of good and evil. All the opposites were mixed together like the mixture of silver and dross. From one source, everything began to differentiate. 

Just as the noise and the outcry were from the heavy mixtures, so too were the opposites arranged according to the soul and the pure spirit, which is the secret of the Will. There is no opposition there. Its perfection and its likeness and its completion are because it received from one source in unity. 

And because there is no recognition of the Divine Honor when things are in this state, the Will desired to strip the hearts of all their vanities, to divide the waters from all these things included therein. This is the secret of the "Groaning Egypt," for there all the opposites were mixed and confused with one another. There, everyone was refined, whether in the spiritual essence or the light, and the dross remained in its place. The darkness and evil were prepared and separated from the ancient and pure intentions, as in a trial of the place. It was established that the good is the essence, and the shells and externalities <note>term: *klipot*; Kabbalistic term for the forces of evil or "shells" that conceal divine light</note> were refined and nullified in themselves. The perfection of the fruit was refined and hidden, and the separated was entirely completed. This is part of the Great Heroism, the light of strength and law given in greatness and heritage to all things. It became known in truth that the Lord is God, there is no other besides Him.

Thus, the Exodus from the "Groaning Egypt" is clarified and necessitated—to know and remember this, and to publicize it. This is the reception of the Names. He added in the conclusion: from this, they received the Torah. And the secret of this is...

And do not say that the wrath of Egypt was [only] for them. For Israel in the world, the glory of the Holy One, blessed be He, was not recognized until the land of Egypt. For in that state of perfection and time, they received it, and it was not found from anything else. They would teach the world. Because their portion was in deep places, all those signs and heroisms were said [to show] that the Lord is your God from the wrath of Egypt. It was in the looking upon His glory that was hidden in them. This was hinted at in the portion given to the world—a portion of law which was appointed in the land of Egypt for the light of the soul, in their drawing after the land. And the truth was that You did all these things to rescue them from the land of Egypt and its buildings. 

And let it be known now, so that you do not say it was from the beginning. Is it not all His? Thus, the laws were given according to the joy of the gift and the agreement. Jacob, of blessed memory, through the twelve tribes, established the laws of his bed as perfect <note>Refers to the midrash that Jacob's "bed was perfect," meaning all his children were righteous</note>. And the light was more prepared than for his ancestors. For he passed away and caused the spirit of impurity to pass away and be nullified. This is a great principle in the sweetness of the thought. 

Afterward, regarding the divine matter and the reception of the Kingdom of Heaven <note>original: *Kabbalat Ol Malchut Shamayim*</note> in their spiritual place: the perfection was not yet there, because the Holy One, blessed be He, had not yet revealed His kingship to publicize it to all who enter the world through great plagues, signs, and wonders. In the presence of the foundations of the world, for they were like a flock, and Jacob was like a shepherd who was destined to publicize this to all the gentiles. For we have not yet turned to the perfection of every branch from its roots, until the Holy One, blessed be He, completes it. 

For by your hand, peace was found, and His kingship was established in the beginning against the Egyptian perfections. The plagues and wonders were by means of His angels who stood in the depths. For the sake of the book, the hands of the perfect were established. After all the divine matters, He made known to all who enter the world that "I am your God," He said, and "His kingship rules over all." 

This is hinted at in the intention of the dreams and the portions regarding Israel in Egypt, which were in their bitterness. All this was for perfection, and the end was at the beginning of the reception of the Kingdom and the perfection upon you. With this, it was not revealed until the end of the matters: "I am the Lord your God who brought you out of the land of Egypt." And He sighed and said, "And for the Levites, we did not know who He was, or what His name was."

The upper and lower beings were afraid of Him. Therefore, they are portions. After such a notification, no power or force can overcome it. You too are God's portion. And you should know that it is not fitting for you to know and recognize anyone but Him, for He descended from the heights to make known His name and His love against all the gods. For against all the gods of Egypt, He executed judgments. Who among them could make such a thing known? 

In their yearnings, like the power of the upper beings and their commanders, they said to Israel that they would not be under their hands and their labor forever. For just as it was necessary to conclude and descend from their service for eternal generations, so by the power and the law, I have chosen my portions. And you are the ones to whom the Mighty King was revealed, and He notified everyone and said, "Keep and do." 

In the plague and my covenant in the multitude, He overturned the graves of the strong and the great ones from the honor of Pharaoh to the honor of the Lamb <note>Refers to the Passover sacrifice</note>. There are the powers of the upper and lower beings, as known to the wise of heart who, from the time Israel was released from the labor of the ancients, notified and made known His essence. And this is the salvation...

# CHAPTER 34: PART OF THE SECRETS OF THE TORAH

Perhaps it is possible that his actual perfection could not exist without the constant flow of divine emanation <note>original: "shefa"; the overflow of divine energy or wisdom from God to the world</note>. For this reason, his contemplation was meant to bring the study of the Torah close to their hearts, so that it would proceed from his mouth and they would not forget it, remaining forever in their hearts. Thus, when they heard the Second Utterance, they completed the intellectual faculty as a preparation for receiving the Torah. They gained wisdom from the event and established it in the most philosophical language. Through this, the Supernal Will would be divided and ascend within them and within their own books. This is the definition of perfection and the sign of their knowledge. 

When they stood at the foot of the mountain to fulfill the law as servants, as they completed the place of their holiness, they ascended to the level they were at before they returned to being mortal. They became like the heavens, for they were no longer merely students hearing from the mouth of a teacher, but hearing from the study itself. Yet, when they experienced a lack, and the "cord was severed," they returned to their forgetfulness. Initially, their desire was to hear from the source of Perfection itself. It is also possible to prove that all the Commandments reached Israel in the same way they reached Moses.

As explained previously in Chapter 38, the sound of the Voice that made the Commandments heard was not a generic sound, but a unique, distinct voice. It will be further explained that in the spiritual world, there is no physical sound at all. However, Voice and Speech belong to every individual, and it is impossible to have Voice without Speech. Because of His absolute Unity, the Voice is the "Voice of the Great Name" <note>original: "Kol Hashem HaGadol"</note>. The sign of this is "a great voice that did not cease." The Speech is His voice as it spreads through the name of the Lord. One who separates the Voice from the Speech is "cutting the plantings" of the Name <note>a Talmudic metaphor for heresy or causing division within the Divine unity</note>.

This is the secret of the verse: "You heard the sound of words" and it is written "The voice of the Living God" speaking with the Voice and the Speech together. To show the Israelites that the Ten Commandments were not just a sound without the general meaning—which would lead to heresy—they were brought close to the secret of the "Mouth of Power" <note>original: "Pi HaGevurah"; a term for God's direct speech</note>. It has already been explained that a voice without speech has no significance. If they had thought the Voice could exist without the Speech, they would have confirmed their error. According to the received tradition, there is no Voice without Speech. Since there was a Voice in the Ten Commandments, the Speech was also within it. Therefore, the Commandments were both Voice and Speech. This proves without a doubt that all the Commandments reached Israel exactly as they reached Moses.

This addresses the difficulty raised by the great Rabbi, Nachmanides <note>original: "HaRamban"; a 13th-century philosopher and mystic</note>, of blessed memory, from Germany. He questioned the language used, noting that when they heard the divine words, they were overwhelmed, and Moses had to mediate. Some suggest that only the first two commandments reached Israel like they reached Moses, while for the rest they heard the Sound but did not understand it, requiring Moses to explain each word. However, this is not a difficulty at all, for the Torah often uses this style. 

As it is written: "For I have known him... so that the Lord may bring upon [Abraham]..." and "For I will be with you... you shall serve God on this mountain." Look closely: "The Lord gave you the Sabbath." This is a common pattern. The Lord returned to Moses and said: "Go down and warn the people... for on the third day the Lord will descend." And it is written: "The priests also, who come near to the Lord, shall sanctify themselves." All of this contains a wondrous matter regarding the reception of the Torah. In the Midrash of Rabbi Shimon bar Yochai <note>original: "Rashbi"; the traditional author of the Zohar</note>, it says: "If you will diligently obey the voice of the Lord your God..." this refers to the Assembly of Israel. "And do what is right in His eyes"—this refers to the trust and faith in His commandments. 

<column-break/>

# CHAPTER 35

Why did they merit the power of that language? As the Rabbi stated, "And to Moses He said: Come up to the Lord," and "Moses approached the Lord." So too here, in these Commandments, it was as if he were speaking with the Lord in a vision. This was the ultimate purpose until the full revelation, for this is the "Pillar of the Voice." 

The secret of the matter: When they heard the Commandments from the Mouth of Power, they heard the voice of prophecy. This is the secret of "And God spoke all these things." The word "God" <note>original: "Elohim"</note> is used to teach us that "The Lord, He is God" and there is none else. Therefore, the Commandments were spoken in the first person ("I am..."), to accept the Name as the essence of Divinity, accepting His kingship and His unity. This removes the error of those who separate the attributes. 

It is known through the "Path of Truth" <note>a common term for Kabbalah</note> that an oath by the Great Name stems from the attribute of Power (*Gevurah*). This is why one must not take the Name in vain, as it harms the unity of the Name. To demonstrate this, the text says "The Name of the Lord your God" to show it includes everything. Regarding the Sabbath, it is said "The seventh day is a Sabbath to the Lord your God." This includes both the honor of the day and the honor of the night. 

In the commandment "Honor your father and your mother," the text emphasizes "as the Lord your God has commanded you." This links the human parents to the Divine source. As has been explained, the Sabbath is the "Source of Blessing." The pleasantness of the Torah itself speaks here. This reaches the point of the Will to explain the Secrets of the Torah and to connect the day of the Giving of the Torah to its assembly. This is the end of the chapter.

### CHAPTER 35

->**The entire secret of the Torah is founded upon and**<-
->**its core foundation is the Acceptance of the Kingdom of Heaven**<-

The Divine matter is upon us, just as the sages explained regarding the nullification of the monarchy in Babylon. We remember the Name to ensure His presence remains over us. For He said: "For I am the Lord who brings you up from the land of Egypt to be your God." It is written: "I am the Lord your God who brought you out of the land of Egypt to be your God." Upon this foundation, He began to establish His kingdom over us, as it is written: "I am the Lord your God who brought you out of the land of Egypt..." and then follows the order of accepting His decrees.

The Sages said regarding "You shall have no other gods before Me": This is a parable. To what is it like? "I am the Lord your God"—it is like a king who enters a province. The people said to him, "Issue decrees upon us." He said to them, "No. Once you have accepted my kingship, I will issue decrees. For if you do not accept my kingship, how will you fulfill my decrees?" So did the Omnipresent say to Israel: "I am the Lord your God... have you accepted my kingship?" In the Midrash they said: "Yes." "Since you have accepted my kingship, now accept my decrees." Thus, the fulfillment of all the commandments and attributes depends on the Exodus from Egypt. For when they left there, they moved from the dominion of mortals to His kingdom, the power that rules the world and its arrangements.

# CHAPTER 36: PART OF THE PATHWAYS OF THE TORAH — CHAPTER 36 [Page] 139

Regarding all that we have mentioned in this book concerning the **repair of the world** <term>Tikkun Olam: the kabbalistic concept of restoring balance and divinity to a fractured universe</term> and its establishment to be for the purpose and "nourishment" of the Divine Glory. For this reason, man was made in the **Image of God** <note>original: "B’tselem Elohim"</note>, and all the generations of the world, their good deeds, and the Torah are all directed toward completing this repair; as if to say, for this the world was created and made. However, because this [concept] is the wisest of all creations, this was the "great principle" above the principle of **Rabbi Akiva** (may he rest in peace), who stated a general rule: "**Love your fellow as yourself**" <note>Leviticus 19:18</note>.

The explanation and the **secret** <term>Sod: the hidden, mystical layer of Torah interpretation</term> of this law is that a person is naturally close to himself; all his deeds are directed toward himself and his own benefit. This [principle] instructs him otherwise, as it is written for you. This is to say: "Know your fellow," so that your love for your fellows will be like your love for yourself. For one who desires and thinks only of himself will eventually take what belongs to his fellow or sin against them. Regarding these matters of the excellence of love, in my opinion, this is the final decision: that the world stands in a place where one "tears his garments" <note>an idiom for extreme effort or self-sacrifice</note> so as not to cause harm to his fellow, even more than he considers himself. This love grows and ascends until he turns all his deeds toward the benefit of his fellow and his fellow's honor alone, without intending any self-benefit. He should even be satisfied if he suffers a loss of his own honor in order to do good for his fellow. If he does not act with this intention, then he has strayed from the principle of Rabbi Akiva.

Indeed, it is a "fearful power," and regarding this, it is said that through this, his love for his fellow is realized. When he sees and acts in the **Image of God**, he must be with his fellow just as he must be with God—with total trust. For his "Image" creates a bond with God. He occupies his thoughts correctly within the collective, through his will and his leadership. For in all his ways with Israel, [Moses] intended their benefit and honor, even when he feared it would bring him a loss of honor. Then it was incumbent upon them to love Israel, for they are made and ordered in the likeness of His parts, His powers, and His children.

So too, the King, the Almighty, is within the King [Moses], as they will mention his affairs with you—specifically in the matter of the **Golden Calf**, which happened in secret. At that time, [God said]: "I have a great fear... I will make you into a great nation" <note>God's offer to Moses to destroy Israel and start a new nation from him</note>. But Moses did not seek violence; he sought mercy for them, saying: "Why, O Lord..." and "**And Moses pleaded**" <note>original: "Vayechal Moshe"; Exodus 32:11</note> before the Lord. He said: "**And now, if You will forgive their sin—but if not, blot me out, I pray Thee, from Thy book which Thou hast written**" <note>Exodus 32:32</note>. Even when they were in [a state of] his goodness and he was shown mercy in his request at the "Waters of Strife," he did not diminish the sin of the one who blesses, seeking their benefit and honor. This is why it is written: "**Let the Lord, the God of the spirits of all flesh, set a man over the congregation**" <note>Numbers 27:16</note>. All his affection for them was expressed in his leadership before the King, for their benefit and honor, not for his own rest or benefit.

In this same way must be the intention of the **perfect servant** in his service: to be remembered in His Image. All his service in his Torah study and his good deeds should be directed toward the **Repair of the Glory** and the **Supernal Unification** <term>Yichud: the mystical act of unifying the various aspects of the Divine</term> in the world. He should not intend his service for himself at all—not for any benefit or honor—but his intention must be for the purpose of repairing the Great Name in His Glory. This is a "High Necessity" for Him. As explained in the second part of this book, this is the essence of **Grace** <note>original: "Chesed"</note> and the purpose of his creation. For this, he was made in the **Image of God**, so that he would have the power and the capacity that is in the hand of God over us. As it is written: "**Everything that is called by My name, and for My glory I created it**" <note>Isaiah 43:7</note>. In the manner that its secret was explained in the chapters... for God made him in the Image of God. This is a great principle... this was the perfection in his creation... "my soul desired the wilderness..." and this is the purpose of **cleaving** <term>Dveikut: mindful attachment or meditative communion with God</term>. From this, he relates his service... to love... to occupy himself with the Torah out of love and desire. For this holy and perfect purpose, the world was made, to be like a garment for the end, which is the "final thought" of the Supernal Mind. For through his service, he binds and unifies the worlds. The perfection of his intention in this world is that his service

touches the heart. In his heart, he fixes the service at the end of thought, and it accompanies him and returns. If this service is pure, it joins with the Supernal realm. Behold, this servant in this world is an example of the "**Righteous One, the Foundation of the World**" <note>original: "Tzadik Yesod Olam"; a kabbalistic term for the sefirah of Yesod which channels divine flow</note>, who mediates between the upper beings and the "Crowned Bride" <term>The Shekhinah or the community of Israel</term>.
