# CHAPTER 35: PART OF THE SECRETS OF THE TORAH — CHAPTER 36

Within these generalities and decrees of all the laws of the Torah, were it not for the supreme power of the Creator and the **expansion of thought** <term>Hitmashchut HaMachshava: a kabbalistic term for the flow of divine consciousness into the human mind</term>, no person would be able to overcome them—neither those below, nor any action in the decrees, and there would be no memory of anything. Behold, "God has made one thing opposite the other" <note>Ecclesiastes 7:14</note>, and in our hands is the power to distinguish between the physical and the soul, in the laws of the kingdom and the system of beauty within a pure or impure nation, between good and evil, light and darkness. This power drives toward a supreme **treasure** <note>original: "Segulah"</note>, seeking to make His name known and to spread His governance through the great laws and the miraculous statutes. 

All the laws are joined and vowed to Israel, distinguishing them from the nations, so they may be desired, purified, and cleansed from the Western <note>possibly referring to Greco-Roman or secular influences</note> types among them, returning to separate them to be His. As it is written: "And you shall be My portion... to take for Himself a nation from the midst of another nation" <note>Deuteronomy 4:34</note>, to choose them from all peoples to be His. Through this distinction, the portion of **kindness** <note>original: "Chesed"</note> and good is separated from the evil, placing each in its proper place. In all its examinations, it is supreme, great, and holy; a glory, an inheritance, and a freedom. It is the power of the Leader above mirrored by the power of the leader below; the inheritance of souls above and the inheritance of bodies below. 

The Sabbath was the "interrupter" that stands between the rest of these and those, to teach all things. The Children of Israel ascended through it from the portion of Egypt. It is written that through the power of the redemption from Egypt, the Sabbath could serve as the interrupter according to the merit of the "servants." The power of the "inheritance of Egypt" is mentioned multiple times in the Torah, and afterwards it was sealed [at the departure] from Egypt for the tribes on the day they received the Torah, which is comprised of the **Fifty Gates of Understanding** <term>50 Sha'arei Binah: the hierarchical levels of divine insight in Kabbalah</term>. Three hundred and sixty powers received the Torah above, and the bodies corresponded to them below. 

Opposite this, the Holy One, blessed be He, caused them to inherit His nature from Egypt. According to our hearts and our strength, we were enslaved to Pharaoh in Egypt and had not yet received the Torah. Who caused the reception of the Torah? It was the power of Egypt, both above and below, through the force of the heart's kindness. This is the "Holy Power" and the "Dominion." Everything is outside the supreme and lower power of Egypt, and the first "strike" <note>referring to the plagues</note> as mentioned. The distinction between them is spread below, and for the reception of the Torah, there was the **expansion of the supreme thought** corresponding to it through a higher force. There is a secret to the power of the Exodus from Egypt above, and corresponding to it is the Sabbath of the giving of the Torah. The sages hinted that all of life is a "memory of the Exodus from Egypt" and the expansion of the Holy. One who understands this principle that I have written regarding this secret will understand that it is a matter of righteousness and truth. This is the sign to awaken and strengthen the memory of the Exodus. These matters are aimed at life itself in the name of all things, to give and to anoint the Levites among them. Therefore, they were appointed to distinguish, separate, and divide the upper ones below and the lower ones above. There, the "Great Light" shone like the cleaving of piety. This is what I wished to mention in this chapter.

### CHAPTER 36
->Behaving in one’s matters as in the first part of this<-

The portion of man is like a field, and this is the "end of the world"—to extend the "end of thought" into his good deeds. These ways are the "repair" <note>original: "Tikkun"</note> or the "ruin" of this arousal. For this purpose, man came into the world: to decide between the upper and lower realms and to link his deeds to them, holding onto the "First Power" and the "Unique One" within him, which is "Great," as mentioned. This is what the Holy One, blessed be He, desired from the beginning

<column-break/>

in the service of His servants. Like those who know the "hidden things," the servants act out of wisdom and the "building" that was explained in the chapters on Love. This is the power of the heart and the power of the "Receiver" <note>original: "Kabbel"</note>. On this path, the matter of the "Force of the Sages" (peace be upon them) is to strive to merit the Omnipresent and to lack the desire for self-will. For the one who acts out of love is strong, and through it, he is struck by greatness regarding his "treasure" and his wisdom. He exists for the sake of kindness upon kindness. 

However, there is a "double danger" <note>perhaps referring to spiritual pride or burnout</note> and the "Power of Glory." His service stems from the inspiration of the intellect, which is as eager for the Omnipresent as a portion. This thought spreads to all creatures. It is written that one who knows... <unclear>hidden/covered</unclear>... is void, for the "repair" is over the creatures. It is proper that the "building" increases kindness for his law, striving so that all should be lovers of the Omnipresent like him. They said in his book: "And you shall love the Lord your God," which means to look upon the creatures with piety and recognize their merit. From this comes the sign that "His Name shall be beloved through you." The measure of good is from Your mercy, O Lord, to make You beloved to Your creatures and to join Him with all your heart, with both your inclinations: the **Good Inclination** and the **Evil Inclination** <term>Yetzer HaTov and Yetzer HaRa</term>. The Evil Inclination dwells within, but in complete service, it is unified with the Good Inclination and held back for the sake of Love. Thus, he becomes a "builder" for all parts, not one who nullifies, but one who stands upright. 

This is the ultimate purpose of Love. Behold, he fulfills the Torah for their Creator, to <unclear>refine</unclear> them without merit or fitness of the "face," but to enter into [Divine] Will, similar to **Rabbi Akiva**. They said: "This is a great principle of the Torah: Love your fellow as yourself." The servant knows that his boundary is unified, a measure of righteousness, cleansed and descending upon what we have written. We have entered the "curtain of the secrets of service" and the laws of intention within it. For his piety desired peace from the beginning, to subdue his sickness... when they gather at the ultimate end, not to be a "valley," for such a life is meant to refine his law. He relates himself to his fellow as he holds to his own essence. In this way, his love for his fellow must be. They said: "Your friend and your father's friend"—this refers to the Holy One, blessed be He. This is to do His work, the work of the Teacher, the Love, and the Services; to hold Him in the matter of love, never transgressing their will. 

Just as they are "treasures" to Him from all the kindness of the "evil" in joy, one must sanctify Him. From this, my heart received a blessing for the Omnipresent, to bless Him and gird oneself for His service to his fellow. Then his "fruits" ... on this path, one must increase the [love of the] Omnipresent from the "evil" of the love that is thought to distance. One must flee from destruction and endure the burden of the soul for the Omnipresent. Thus He warned in His Torah: "Do not fear," for they are "kindness" upon him. He must purify himself so that all sustenance is in him, and he shall make His word beloved and act upon His will. As they said: "Fill your heart with another portion." 

This is a **Great Principle of the Torah**, and it is the principle of the "treasure of the heart," which is the ultimate purpose of the whole. This was explained through the "generalities of Rabbi Akiva." He was the master of this cycle; he was the master of the "hidden things" in all of this, to pursue and to realize his own "kindness" <note>possibly meaning his own life</note> for the **Sanctification of the Name** <term>Kiddush HaShem: martyrdom or acting in a way that brings honor to God</term>. This is the thought and the secret of "Complete Unity." It is placed at our opening like a word, and this is for the sake of the "Perfection" that comes to complete his spirit and his soul—the end of the supreme thought, the secret of holiness and unity. Within it is the "sweetening" of the distance. 

The Holy One, blessed be He, is for a blessing, as the secret of the sacrifices is known to the "wise of heart." Why was his heart (peace be upon him) divided against him? Because kindness is superfluous in all parts. For this, he sanctified the "existence," as it is written: "And I shall be sanctified in the midst of the Children of Israel" <note>Leviticus 22:32</note>. This is the "evil" to love, and the suffering, and the sacrifice of what is written "his fellow." He did not waste his time. "And you shall not profane My holy name." Up to this point is the ultimate purpose of "turning the evil toward his fellow," to remove the "separating King" who divides between merits, without showing his "face," as it were, so as to cleave to Him alone in time. For this, he surrenders his body, which hinders this "cleaving," to be placed before Him. May it be His will that he cleaves to the spirit of purified will, the kindness of God. These "afflictions" <note>original: "Sigufim"</note> in each one are the essence of the "Great Principle of the Torah." 

**Ben Azzai** says: "'This is the book of the generations of Adam' <note>Genesis 5:1</note> ... in the day that God created man, in the likeness of God made He him." This is a **greater principle** than the other. Ben Azzai raised this "endurance" to the summit of heights. Behold, the voice reaches thus far; he revealed it in his secret.

# The Torah: Chapter 36 | Chapter 36: The Secrets Section
<meta>catchword: Unification | catchword: Book</meta>

It is worthy of observation and requires thorough refinement when mentioned in the Torah, and specifically to merit the Torah [as it stands] against the Great and Holy Name; four camps corresponding to the surroundings of His strength, and this is the complete unification. Even more so, one must unify His name to awaken [the understanding] that He and His great Name are one, as part of His portion <note>original: "chelk ko," likely referring to the Divine energy</note>, and to give permission to give, for the kingdom and the strength are His. As it is written: "For they are sands" <note>original: "cholot," perhaps a reference to the vastness of the Divine wisdom</note> and "Let him who glories glory in this" <note>original: "ve-hithallel ha-mithallel," quoting Jeremiah 9:23</note>. And it is written that he who is wise follows the path of Haifa <note>likely a scribal error or specific mystical reference to a path of purity</note>, as it is written: "The wise man builds his path and with his silver..."

The secret is that "all who know Me," for the unification is intended according to the path we have mentioned, which is the Intellect. And in "knowing the Lord," he said this regarding "all who know Me," learning that the Intellect and knowledge of His Being, according to His nature, is to instruct with a good and worthy heart. This is the language of "Understanding and knowing Me" <note>quoting Jeremiah 9:23: "haskel ve-yado'a oti"</note>. He chooses and says "your laughter" <note>original: "sechakecha," perhaps a reference to Divine play/joy</note> for this unification was the Torah, the Secret of Secrets in its totality, uniquely associated with His name. It consists of portions: 248 <note>the number of positive commandments, corresponding to the limbs of the body</note> lights of action and 365 <note>the number of negative commandments, corresponding to the days of the solar year and human sinews</note> [corresponding to] the "do not do." These are the foundations of the perfect Torah, complete in its service, its peace, its heat, and its integrity toward the Name. That is to say, through the power of His unification, as He said: "For I am the Lord who exercises kindness, justice, and righteousness in the earth" <note>Jeremiah 9:23</note>.

He said that in this order He established a path to this Intellect and Knowledge, which is kindness, justice, and righteousness. He made justice a refuge from the "do" <note>positive commandments</note> and righteousness a sought-after goal. The unification in these foundations is the Torah of Truth in its totality, a decree and a connection in the secret of the letters *Pe* and *Samech* <note>mystical abbreviations or structural markers in the Torah scroll</note>, and the sign of the *Piyut* <note>liturgical poem/structure</note> that ascends and descends between them, as is known to its scholars. Everything is integrated... and prepared through them. According to this model, one needs to be diligent in the business of these [commandments] to dwell in them, for unification is weighed against the Supernal Will. You shall intend in their preparation and their fruit, as He said: "For in these I delight, says the Lord" <note>Jeremiah 9:23</note>. That is to say, the unification is My delight, and finish with these and receive the word of the Lord. Every person should strive as much as they can, and they shall learn from the perfect servant according to the strength he received from Wisdom and the light. The end of the matter is to encompass all the parts... for they said: "This is the whole of man."

Its meaning is this: The end of the matter is the "All" <note>original: "ha-kol," referring to the sefirah of Yesod</note>. And gather from all that the books of holiness have included in what is heard and their rectification, a complete structure from everything. And this is what was said, and he already received it, for his entire book is the intention of the Holy, as it says regarding the inclusion of each of the parts: "Only the Lord your God shall you fear" <note>Deuteronomy 6:13</note>. It is known that "fear" is the source of the negative commandments ("thou shalt not"), and it includes the positive commandments ("thou shalt do"), as it says "Fear God" to indicate the Unification. And "keep His commandments"—in every place "guard yourself lest" and "take heed" refers to a negative commandment. And he said "and keep His commandments" to include the positive commandments within the "keeping" of the negative ones, to indicate their existence, for he received from a single Shepherd <note>Ecclesiastes 12:11</note> that unification follows this path we have mentioned. And by this, the perfection of the Will returns to him.

<column-break/>

And the Supernal Desire, which is sought from all the Divine parts, is determined to be upon the perfect servant who completes this goal. For he is in the Supernal likeness, and this is the Righteous One <note>the Tzaddik</note> who is called "All" <note>Kol</note>. This is also below... for he precedes the one known as the Prince, and his name is "All." He is included in his Being to be called "Complete," meaning he precedes the matter in the likeness of the Righteous One above <note>the sefirah of Yesod</note> to establish the perfection of the Supernal Unification. This is the secret of "For this is the whole [of man]" <note>Ecclesiastes 12:13</note>. The hint is in the name *Shai* <note>numerical value 310</note>, the foundation of the world. And before the King... he establishes the Glory and considers the Unification like Him. This is the secret of "Everyone who is called by My name, I have created him for My glory, I have formed him, even I have made him" <note>Isaiah 43:7</note>. According to the way I have written in its place, everything requires the power of its preparation. Behold, there is a great and unique [station] tied to the perfection of the Unification, and to this the good portion descends and causes the attributes of the arrangement to shine. 

"And may the pleasantness of the Lord our God be upon us" <note>Psalm 90:17</note>; this is the abundance... on the day that Moses finished setting up the Tabernacle <note>Mishkan</note>, which was like a bride entering her canopy. Their faces were toward each other, like a man and his companion, and the work of the holy service was completed. They established the Tabernacle on its base, which is the secret of the breach <note>ha-peretz</note>... they remembered it and he said to them: "It shall be uprooted around it by the work of your hands." Therefore he said, "May the pleasantness of the Lord our God be upon us." Behold, the Tabernacle was established below, and another Tabernacle was established with it above. The Divine Presence <note>Shekhinah</note> was seen below and the Supernal surroundings above, according to the Supernal preparation. This is why it says, "And they finished," regarding the work of the holy service.

The building of the Tabernacle is the perfect Unification in its place. "And they brought the Tabernacle to Moses" <note>Exodus 39:33</note>... indicating a complete thing, the secret of Male and Female in a perfect unification. This is the secret of "And may my soul be upon you" <note>referencing the indwelling of the Spirit</note>. For at the end of the matter, he crowned it and spread it over you in your assemblies in a unique unification. And they said: "And the work of our hands, establish it upon us" <note>Psalm 90:17</note> to hint that the Supernal Intention shall rest and be established through the deed which he did, for they are directed from below corresponding to the form above, in their likeness and their blessing. When they are at this [level of] perfection, then it is "established upon us" through those holy deeds which the Lord our God... as if we had prepared it with our memory and our hands. For if the deeds were not perfectly directed toward the [Supernal] Intention, it would be in its own likeness in its totality... This is the hint: And so, the rectification of the work of our hands, even if it is the good within it, his eyes worked from the structure and the vault. This is what is meant by "upon me, and the work of our hands establish it."

With this, the intention of this chapter is completed, as well as the opening words of this section. The book "Avodat HaKodesh" (The Holy Service) is sealed within the encompassing cycle that unifies everything in the holy service, by the ministering of Glory in Might, and the inheritance in Holiness.

It is a matter worthy of observation and requires thorough refinement whenever it is mentioned in the Torah, specifically regarding how one merits the Torah as it stands against the Great and Holy Name. There are four camps <note>These refer to the four angelic camps—Michael, Gabriel, Uriel, and Raphael—that surround the Divine Throne</note> corresponding to the surroundings of His strength, and this constitutes the complete unification <term>Yichud: the kabbalistic practice of mentally or prayerfully unifying different aspects of the Divine</term>.

It is also written that he who is wise follows the **path of purity** <note>original: "Haifa"; this is likely a scribal variant for a word meaning "pure" or "protected," or perhaps a specific mystical station</note>, as it is written: "The wise man builds his path and with his silver..."

The secret is that "all who know Me" perform the unification according to the path we have mentioned, which is the **Intellect**. Regarding "knowing the Lord," he said this in reference to "all who know Me," teaching that the Intellect and the knowledge of His Being—according to His nature—is to instruct with a good and worthy heart. This is the essence of the phrase "**Understanding and knowing Me**" <note>Jeremiah 9:23: "haskel ve-yado'a oti"</note>. He chooses this and speaks of **your laughter** <note>original: "sechakecha," a mystical reference to the "divine laughter" or the sweetening of harsh judgments into joy, often associated with the patriarch Isaac</note>...
